labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App (ChatGPT desktop, macOS)

### What feature would you like to see?

Summary
We're building a model-independent coordination layer (NuraHarness) that needs one agent to post a message into an existing ChatGPT desktop conversation and confirm it landed. Inside the desktop app this capability clearly exists: send_message_to_thread and read_thread run through the renderer's dynamic app tool dispatch all day for first-party callers. There is no supported way for an external integration to use it with a host-issued caller identity, and failures come back as an opaque -32000 with no reason or request ID.

Environment
- macOS, ChatGPT desktop 26.1106.51428 (build 26605)
- Bundled codex-app-tools plugin 0.1.6
- Desktop-owned app-server runs over stdio; the standalone daemon control socket refuses connections, so no external client can attach to the Desktop runtime

What we observe
- From an integration, read_thread and send_message_to_thread fail with ProtocolError -32000, "Codex app tool request failed". The desktop log shows dynamic_app_tools_request_failed with "The app tool call ended before producing a result".
- Some failures happen before any dynamic_app_tool_renderer_execution_started event, which fits no renderer window accepting the caller. One send reached the renderer and failed 1 ms later, which fits target resolution returning null.
- On 2026-11-14, 71 of 73 send_message_to_thread renderer starts came from first-party callers, so the path works; it just isn't exposed with a legitimate identity for integrations.
- Even a successful send returns only { threadId }, which isn't dispatch acceptance, so delivery can't be confirmed without a separate read.
- send_message_to_thread is approval_mode "prompt" by default, so in headless runs it's effectively hidden unless named explicitly.
- When the call starts from a ChatGPT chat via a connector, it can be stopped by "This tool call was blocked by OpenAI's safety checks", with no category or request ID (see #52095).

What we're asking for
1. A supported, documented way for an authorized integration to send into a specific existing conversation the user owns, bound to a host-issued caller identity rather than one the integration asserts.
2. Typed outcomes instead of -32000: NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_RESPONDING, DISPATCH_ACCEPTED, DISPATCH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, plus the created message or turn ID when available.
3. A request or correlation ID on tool-call failures and on safety-check blocks, so false positives can be reported precisely.
4. If this is intentionally out of scope for integrations, a clear statement saying so.

We are not asking to bypass approvals or safety checks, and we haven't modified the app or its trust checks. Related: #47425, #55023, #52095.

Happy to share redacted logs and timestamps privately.

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.title: Linux voice helper can't open audio devices on NixOS: no /usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf, and NixOS's ALSA plugin config uses `libs.native`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
### What happens

On NixOS, `/voice` fails straight away with:

```
■ Failed to connect voice mode: voice audio devices could not open; check microphone and speaker setup
```

The log shows `voice helper output closed phase=Some(OpenDevices) exit_code=Some(25)`. Audio itself works: PipeWire is running, with a default source and sink.

- codex-cli 0.167.2, from the release archive `codex-package-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.zst`
- NixOS 26.05, PipeWire with `services.pipewire.alsa.enable = true`
- To run on NixOS, the voice runtime's ELF files are patched by autoPatchelf (the helper's interpreter, and the rpaths), and nothing else in `codex-resources/voice` is changed. To rule the patching out, the helper results below come from the unpatched `codex-voice-host` from the archive, started through NixOS's glibc loader with `--library-path` set to the archive's `codex-resources/voice/lib`.

### Root cause

ALSA is statically linked into `codex-voice-host`: it doesn't load `libasound` and contains alsa-lib itself (`alsa_lib` 1.2.9 in `MODULE.bazel`). I talked to the helper directly over its framed protocol (`hello`, then `listDevices` for input and output), with the 10 environment variables codex gives it. That made ALSA's stderr visible, which codex discards (`drop(stderr_rx)` in `client.rs`). There are two separate problems.

**1. ALSA's config file doesn't exist on NixOS.** The helper's ALSA reads `/usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf`. NixOS has no `/usr/share`, and its own alsa-lib finds its config through a Nix store path built into `libasound.so`. So every lookup fails:

```
ALSA lib external/alsa_lib+/src/conf.c:4556:(snd_config_update_r) Cannot access file /usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf
ALSA lib external/alsa_lib+/src/control/control.c:1529:(snd_ctl_open_noupdate) Invalid CTL hw:0
```

`listDevices` returns `[]` for both input and output. Exporting `ALSA_CONFIG_PATH`, `ALSA_CONFIG_DIR` or `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` before starting codex doesn't help, because `child_environment` drops them. I checked the helper's actual environment with `strace -v`: only `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `HOME`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and the seven fixed `GST_*` settings reach it. The `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` probe from #44714 sets nothing either, because none of its three directories exists on NixOS.

**2. NixOS's PipeWire ALSA config uses a field upstream alsa-lib doesn't have.** Given nixpkgs' `alsa.conf`, which includes `/etc/alsa/conf.d`, the helper reads the system's ALSA settings. NixOS's PipeWire module writes `49-pipewire-modules.conf` there:

```
pcm_type.pipewire {
  libs.native = /nix/store/…-pipewire-1.6.6/lib/alsa-lib/libasound_module_pcm_pipewire.so ;
  libs.32Bit = /nix/store/…-pipewire-1.6.6/lib/alsa-lib/libasound_module_pcm_pipewire.so ;
}
```

The `libs` field comes from a nixpkgs patch to alsa-lib, [`alsa-plugin-conf-multilib.patch`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/pkgs/by-name/al/alsa-lib/alsa-plugin-conf-multilib.patch). nixpkgs carries it "to support apps with 32bit sound running on x86_64 architecture". The helper's alsa-lib rejects it:

```
ALSA lib external/alsa_lib+/src/pcm/pcm.c:2578:(snd_pcm_open_conf) Unknown field libs
```

So PipeWire's `default` (from `99-pipewire-default.conf`) can't be opened, and only the null device and the sound cards' own devices are listed.

### Results

`listDevices` results come from the original helper as described above. The `/voice` results are from the TUI.

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| As codex starts it | `Cannot access file /usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf`; no input or output devices |
| `/voice` as shipped | the error above |
| `/voice` with `ALSA_CONFIG_PATH`/`ALSA_CONFIG_DIR`/`ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` exported | the same error; none of them reach the helper |
| `ALSA_CONFIG_DIR` = nixpkgs alsa-lib's `share/alsa`, `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR=/run/current-system/sw/lib/alsa-lib` | `Unknown field libs`; the null device and sound card devices only, no PipeWire, no default |
| The same, with `49-pipewire-modules.conf` hidden | "PipeWire Sound Server" listed, and `default` is the default device |
| Fixes 1 and 2 below, emulated: `ALSA_CONFIG_DIR` set to the `share/alsa` folder of a minimal NixOS system profile built with the settings in fix 1, and `49-pipewire-modules.conf` rewritten from `libs.native =` to upstream's `lib`. No `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR`. | "PipeWire Sound Server" listed, and `default` is the default device |
| The same, without the rewrite (fix 1 only) | `Unknown field libs` again |
| `/voice` with fixes 1 and 2 emulated. The same profile's `share/alsa` is mounted at `/usr/share/alsa`, the helper's built-in path, standing in for codex setting `ALSA_CONFIG_DIR`. No plugin directory. | connects and shows listening |

### Suggested fix

Both are needed, and both are small: fix 1 alone still fails with `Unknown field libs` (the second-to-last row).

1. **Look for ALSA's config in NixOS's system profile.** If `/usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf` doesn't exist and `/run/current-system/sw/share/alsa/alsa.conf` does, pass `ALSA_CONFIG_DIR=/run/current-system/sw/share/alsa` to the helper. It's a fixed path managed by the system, with its files in the read-only Nix store, so it fits `linux_alsa.rs`'s rule of "only fixed system paths". On NixOS it holds `alsa.conf` once the system has:

   ```nix
   environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.alsa-lib ];
   environment.pathsToLink = [ "/share/alsa" ];
   ```

   I built a minimal NixOS 26.05 system profile (PipeWire with ALSA enabled) with and without these lines. `share/alsa/alsa.conf` is present only with both. nixpkgs' `alsa.conf` includes `/etc/alsa/conf.d`, so the helper then reads the system's own ALSA setup. If you'd rather not depend on a system setting, another option is a config shipped inside the package, at a fixed path such as `codex-resources/voice/share/alsa` beside the helper. I haven't tested that option.

2. **Accept nixpkgs' `libs.native` / `libs.32Bit` fields** by carrying [nixpkgs' patch](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/pkgs/by-name/al/alsa-lib/alsa-plugin-conf-multilib.patch) in the Bazel `alsa_lib` build. That's one file in `patches/` and a `single_version_override(module_name = "alsa_lib", patches = [...])`, the same mechanism `MODULE.bazel` already uses for other dependencies. The patch applies to the alsa-lib 1.2.9 tarball that `alsa_lib` 1.2.9.bcr.4 uses (two hunks with fuzz). I built alsa-lib 1.2.9 as a static library, with and without the patch, and linked a small program that opens `default` for capture and playback. I gave both builds the config from fix 1 and this system's unmodified `/etc/alsa/conf.d`:

   - unpatched: `pcm.c:2578:(snd_pcm_open_conf) Unknown field libs`, the same line as the helper's error, and both opens fail
   - patched: both open, as type `IOPLUG`, ALSA's type for external plugins such as PipeWire's (`99-pipewire-default.conf` makes `default` the `pipewire` plugin)

   NixOS's config names the plugin by its full store path, so no `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` is needed: the emulated rows above had none. Adding NixOS's plugin directory, `/run/current-system/sw/lib/alsa-lib`, to `PLUGIN_DIRECTORIES` wouldn't fix this alone: in the fourth row of the table, the helper had a config and that plugin directory, and still failed with `Unknown field libs`.

Separately, diagnosing this was slow because the helper's stderr is discarded and only the generic message is shown, as #46630 also noted. Even a fixed hint for exit 25 on Linux, such as "ALSA could not open its configuration or devices", would have helped.

No MCP errors or warnings appear. The sessions are then cancelled and deleted (`quit_reason=Cancelled`).

- `network_access = true`
- New threads outside any project
- Disabling the GitHub and Cloudflare plugins to shrink the tool list

Remote OAuth MCP tools are available in Desktop threads, the same as in the CLI.

issues.title: Expose privacy-preserving attestation for encrypted collaboration.spawn_agent arguments

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
## Variant

Codex App / app-server / CLI collaboration tools on macOS arm64.

Observed with:

- Codex App `26.727.51351` (`6119`)
- bundled CLI `0.146.0-alpha.9.2`
- `openai/codex` main `ee0247f95a6fe2b094ba2253d82cae2a2b4c2dff`
- model-reserved `collaboration.spawn_agent`

## Feature request

Please expose an opt-in, privacy-preserving, independently verifiable pre-dispatch attestation for encrypted collaboration tool arguments, especially `collaboration.spawn_agent`.

The attestation should let a caller prove that the native invocation delivered to the collaboration backend matched an expected projection without changing the reserved tool schema or persisting plaintext.

A sufficient receipt would bind at least:

- receipt schema and canonicalization version
- function namespace/name and tool-schema identity
- call ID, parent thread ID, child thread ID, and canonical agent path/task name
- requested and effective agent type
- requested and effective `fork_turns`
- requested task name
- SHA-256 and byte length of the decrypted `message`
- SHA-256 of the canonical full argument projection
- dispatch outcome and generation timestamp

The receipt must originate at the authoritative boundary that can observe the decrypted arguments immediately before child creation. It should be platform-signed or otherwise independently verifiable. Plaintext should be omitted by default.

An optional strict mode should fail before creating the child when the receipt cannot be produced.

## Motivation

High-assurance review and compliance workflows sometimes need to prove that an independently spawned reviewer received one exact prompt, role, task name, and no inherited conversation history. Model prose, caller-owned intent capsules, returned task names, or post-hoc child reports cannot prove the actual native invocation.

Codex correctly marks `spawn_agent.message` as encrypted. The local handler receives `encrypted_function_args` metadata and routes the message through the encrypted inter-agent path. That preserves privacy, but it means a trusted local extension cannot compare the actual invocation with a caller-known plaintext digest.

Changing the reserved schema to make `message` plaintext is not viable: the Responses backend rejects a non-canonical `collaboration.spawn_agent` schema. A first-class attestation boundary would preserve encryption and the canonical schema while enabling auditability.

## Minimal reproduction of the capability gap

1. Use the Codex App with the model-reserved `collaboration.spawn_agent` tool.
2. Keep the canonical schema unchanged, including encrypted `message`.
3. Add local instrumentation at the start of the native MultiAgentV2 spawn handler, before child creation.
4. Invoke an ordinary non-sensitive child with explicit `agent_type`, `task_name`, `fork_turns: "none"`, and a known message.
5. Observe that the client can classify `message` as an encrypted function argument and forward it through the encrypted inter-agent path, but cannot independently bind the native call to the caller-known plaintext message digest.
6. If the instrumentation requires locally visible plaintext, it must fail before child creation; no attestation receipt can be emitted.

## Expected behavior

Codex should provide one supported way to obtain an independently verifiable digest/receipt for the decrypted native invocation while preserving encrypted transport and the exact reserved collaboration schema.

This is not a request to disable encryption, expose prompt plaintext in logs, or let clients redefine reserved tool schemas.

## Related issues

- #20204 tracks missing `PreToolUse` coverage for MultiAgent handlers, but a generic local hook still needs an authoritative digest for encrypted fields.
- #31864 shows why the reserved collaboration schema must remain exact.
- #26753 and #33267 document adjacent encrypted collaboration-tool behavior.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows MSIX package: **OpenAI.Codex 26.930.7945.0** (x64), verified with `Get-AppxPackage`. This is the package version, not the About dialog version.

The correlated VM logs identify the desktop client as **Codex Desktop 26.930.61225** and the mobile client as **codex_chatgpt_ios_remote 1.2026.267**.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus.

### What platform is your computer?

- Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9457, x64.
- iPhone: iOS 26.6.2; ChatGPT 1.2026.267 (36747771815).
- Project execution: a remote Linux VM, accessed from Windows through an SSH connection.

### What issue are you seeing?

A conversation created from ChatGPT on iPhone on the remote VM cannot be continued in the Windows desktop app, even after its response has completed.

Windows displays:

> Está aberto em outro aplicativo. Feche lá para continuar aqui.

Meaning: the conversation is open in another app and must be closed there before continuing here. Clicking **Try again** does not recover it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. From ChatGPT on iPhone, create a conversation on the connected remote VM.
2. Send a short message and wait for the response to finish.
3. In the Windows desktop app, select the same VM through its SSH connection and open that exact conversation.
4. Observe the blocked-input message above.
5. Click **Try again**; the conversation remains blocked.

### What is the expected behavior?

Windows should be able to continue the completed conversation through a safe ownership transfer or by attaching to its existing runtime. If an explicit release is required, the UI should identify the owning runtime and provide an actionable way to release it.

### Correlated diagnostics

Controlled reproduction on October 6, 2026; all times UTC:

| Event | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Conversation created by the iOS client | 18:59:49 |
| Response completed (`task_complete`) | 19:00:01.039 |
| Windows `thread/resume` attempts rejected | 19:01:50 and 19:01:51 |

Both desktop attempts, over `unix_socket`, failed with:

```text
thread-store conflict: thread [redacted] already has an active writer
```

The conversation's exclusive kernel lock (`FLOCK ADVISORY WRITE`) is held by a live VM process: **PID 3992516**, the legacy WebSocket app-server on `ws://127.0.0.1:4555`, running **Codex 0.157.0**. The iOS-created conversation also records CLI version 0.157.0. The current VM CLI and separate managed daemon report **0.160.1**.

This confirms a live writer conflict between distinct VM runtimes after response completion. Whether aligning their versions fixes the conflict remains untested. Closing the iOS app was not instrumented in this controlled reproduction, so no release timeout is claimed. Conversation IDs and content are omitted.

### Relationship to the suggested duplicate #50708

I reviewed #50708 in response to the [duplicate-detection comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51429#issuecomment-6021882939). It describes **ChatGPT Chrome extension → VS Code on macOS**, ineffective Retry, history-refresh problems, and a successful fork workaround through the native macOS app.

This report adds **ChatGPT on iPhone → Codex Desktop on Windows with execution on a remote Linux VM**, with correlated resume failures and a live writer identified in a separate VM runtime. The shared blocked-input message may indicate a common ownership/handoff issue, but the available evidence does not establish the same root cause. The macOS fork workaround has not been verified here, and a fork would not demonstrate recovery of the original conversation.

I am keeping this report open pending triage of the remote-runtime evidence. If these cases share an underlying issue, please identify the canonical report so this reproduction can be consolidated there.

### Related reports for triage and traceability

- #44449 — iOS Remote threads remain held by a live Remote Control daemon, blocking Desktop with `already has an active writer`; reported on macOS. This is the closest diagnostic comparison to the live-owner conflict observed here.
- #46647 — mobile/Remote → CLI on Linux: the recovery message does not identify the actual writer owner and asks for an unavailable mobile release action.
- #46652 — reported CLI regression in resuming conversations across windows/machines, with requests for safe ownership transfer or remote release.
- #46924 — VS Code on Linux: existing conversations remain blocked after PC or editor restart; the prior owner is unavailable to close and Retry does not recover them.
- #47977 — VS Code and CLI on Linux: blocked input without a usable recovery path, plus separately reported fork/edit failures whose connection to the lock remains unestablished.
- #51053 — iOS Remote cannot even view a running VS Code task on macOS; a live VS Code writer was identified. This concerns read-only monitoring of an active task, whereas this report concerns continuing a completed conversation.
- #50708 — Chrome → VS Code on macOS; the bot's suggested duplicate, assessed above.

These references connect related symptoms and diagnostics for investigation; they are not confirmed duplicates of this reproduction.

issues.title: bug(windows-os): desktop app "Long-lived" host WebSocket ignores system proxy and HTTP_PROXY, hardcoded URL

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| App | ChatGPT desktop app (Windows, MSIX `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`) |
| Bundled app-server | `codex 0.163.0-alpha.10.2` (windows-x86_64) |
| OS | Windows 11 10.0.26200 x64 |
| Proxy | Clash Verge Rev (mihomo core); Windows **system proxy** enabled (`ProxyEnable=1`, `127.0.0.1:7897`); TUN **not** enabled |
| Network | DNS poisoning present: `chatgpt.com` resolves to random forged IPs |

### Problem

After `remoteControl/enable`, the desktop app also opens a WebSocket to the `hostId=durable` ("Long-lived") host:

```js
// app.asar — hardcoded, no config override
var uue = `wss://codex-cloud-backend.chatgpt.com/`;
function lb(e){ return { id: i.Ai, display_name: `Long-lived`, kind: `local`, websocket_url: uue } }
```

It is issued from the Electron **main process** using the Node `ws` package (not the Chromium network stack), and as a result:

1. it does **not** read the Windows system proxy (WinINET / `ProxyEnable` + `ProxyServer`), even though the HTTP client inside the app-server does;
2. it does **not** read `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY`, even though `codex.exe` in the same process tree does (see the A/B test below);
3. the URL is hardcoded and there is **no setting** to override it.

On any network that requires a proxy — in particular "system proxy on, TUN off", which is the default setup for a very large number of users in mainland China — this connection fails deterministically.

### Reproduction

1. Enable the Windows system proxy (pointing at a local HTTP proxy). Do **not** enable TUN.
2. Use a network where `chatgpt.com` is DNS-poisoned (or any network that requires a proxy).
3. Launch the ChatGPT desktop app, open Settings → Connections → Control this computer, enable "Allow connection".
4. Watch the desktop app log
   (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\`):

```
[AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.websocket_error connectionId=58 errorCode=unknown
  hostKind=durable message="WebSocket was closed before the connection was established" transport=websocket
[AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.closed code=1006 connectionId=58 failureReason=open_timeout
[AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.reconnect_scheduled baseDelayMs=20000 reconnectAttempt=57
```

5. In parallel, `Get-NetTCPConnection` on the main process shows a **direct** connection to a public IP stuck in `SynSent` (the DNS-poisoned address) instead of the local proxy:

```
RemoteAddress    RemotePort  State
127.0.0.1        7897        Established      <- Chromium traffic goes through the proxy
199.16.158.190   443         SynSent          <- long-lived WS connects directly, hits a forged IP
```

### A/B test: the app-server *does* honor proxy env vars

Same machine, same subscription, one variable changed at a time, using `codex remote-control --no-daemon` and looking for `connected to app-server remote control websocket` in the log:

| Group | `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` | Extra flag | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | set | — | ✅ `connected to app-server remote control websocket` |
| E | set | — | ✅ reproduces A |
| B | set | `-c features.respect_system_proxy=true` | ❌ `Error: Remote control is enabled on <name> but the connection is errored.` |
| C | cleared | — | ❌ `os error 10060` (WSAETIMEDOUT) |
| D | cleared | `-c features.network_proxy=true -c network.proxy_url=...` | ❌ `os error 10060` |

So the Rust app-server **does** honor `HTTP_PROXY`, while the main-process WebSocket does not — inconsistent proxy behavior inside the same app/process tree.

Two further observations:

- `features.respect_system_proxy=true` (which reads the Windows system proxy from the registry) makes the app-server WS fail outright with `connection is errored`; the system-proxy path appears to be broken for the WS transport.
- `network.proxy_url` / `network.socks_url` (`features.network_proxy`) only apply to network policy for **sandboxed commands**; they do not cover the app-server's own long-lived connections.

### The endpoint itself works (so this is not a server-side problem)

WS upgrade handshake through the local proxy:

```
$ curl -x http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
    -H 'Connection: Upgrade' -H 'Upgrade: websocket' \
    -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13' -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Key: <random>' \
    -H 'Origin: https://chatgpt.com' \
    https://codex-cloud-backend.chatgpt.com/

User-Agent: (none)                         -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
User-Agent: node                           -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
User-Agent: codex-desktop/26.1013.4894.0   -> HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
User-Agent: ChatGPT/26.1013.4894.0         -> HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
```

As soon as the request goes through the proxy with an acceptable User-Agent, the handshake succeeds — the server and the network egress are fine.

### Isolation: after fixing the proxy env vars, the toggle works but this channel still does not

This pins the problem precisely to the connection described here:

```
# after setting user-level HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and restarting the app
Settings -> Connections -> Control this computer -> "Allow connection"  =>  ON, pairing QR dialog shown  OK
desktop log                                                                   =>  os error 10060 gone,
                                                                                 "connected to rendezvous"  OK

# but the long-lived channel is still connecting directly
codex.exe (app-server) sockets     =>  127.0.0.1:7897  Established        OK
Electron main process "durable"    =>  199.16.158.190:443  SynSent        still direct
```

In other words: the toggle itself is backed by the app-server tunnel (now working), but the channel the **cloud uses to call back into this machine** — issued by the Electron main process — is never taken over by the proxy. **"Allow connection" being on does not mean a remote session can actually be established.**

### Expected behavior (suggestions)

1. Honor `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` for WebSockets opened by the desktop app main process, consistent with the app-server.
2. At minimum honor the Windows system proxy (WinINET), so the very common "system proxy only" setup works.
3. Provide a configurable endpoint override (e.g. `CODEX_CLOUD_BACKEND_URL` or a settings entry) for self-hosted gateways / enterprise environments.
4. Fix `features.respect_system_proxy`, which currently breaks the app-server WS when enabled.

### Impact

In mainland China and any other "proxy required, system proxy only, TUN off" environment, the desktop app's cloud long-lived connection is unavailable, so **remote control sessions initiated from a phone may fail to establish** even though the "Allow connection" toggle turns on and the device shows as online.

```
Desktop app logs:
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\<YYYY>\<MM>\<DD>\codex-desktop-*.log

Codex CLI binary shipped with the desktop app (copied into the user profile):
%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\<hash>\codex.exe
```

*A full local investigation with all raw log excerpts, socket dumps and the A/B test matrix is also available at
https://github.com/Kirito14IT/chatgpt-codex-windows-remote-control-proxy-fix (contains one-click diagnostic scripts).*

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64. Current reported OS version: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

An existing Codex desktop security-review chat stopped with a possible cybersecurity-risk notice while carrying out owner-authorized defensive source review for the owner's own application. The review is a required checkpoint before artifact qualification, controlled recovery validation, and a preview MFA test. The turn failed without a completed review package.

```text
This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try rephrasing your request. If you're doing authorized security work that requires more cyber permissive safeguards, apply for Daybreak access via https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/status-and-access before retrying.
```

The owner opened the supplied Platform access URL and received "Page not found" (404). The owner also reports that the Help Center support chat bubble was not visible.

The owner has already reported submitting in-app feedback. Feedback/session reference supplied by the owner:

`019ec173-c578-70f0-a795-66b6b66fade0`

This is also the affected chat/session ID. It is not being represented as a separate support case number or evidence that access has been restored.

Recorded failed-turn completion: November 13, 2026, approximately 06:31:50 UTC (01:31:50 America/New_York).

The selected model for the failed turn was not independently captured; please correlate it using the feedback/session reference rather than assuming the model used by a different chat.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence, not a verified standalone minimal reproduction:

1. In an existing Windows desktop chat, request an independent review of frozen local source, bounded test/execution contracts, and synthetic/redacted evidence for an application owned by the user.
2. Keep the review constrained: no production/customer access, real credentials, external attacks, live authentication/provider operations, deployment, or safeguard weakening.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please investigate whether this authorized defensive review was misclassified or whether this specific task intentionally requires additional access. If additional access is required, provide the supported product/surface, a working enrollment or support route, and the confirmation that establishes when the original review can resume.

issues.title: [macOS desktop 26.1027.30824] IAB owner not registered for background chats or re-established for resumed subagents

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

issues.body:
## Environment

- macOS, arm64; desktop app 26.1027.30824, build 22943, production channel.
- Configured app updater reports up_to_date on 31 October 2026.
- Bundled in-app browser and supported CUA/browser APIs. No Chrome fallback.

## Problem A: a newly created background chat lacks its browser owner

1. Create a normal local chat through the supported create_thread tool and let it run without selecting it.
2. Ask it to open a neutral HTTPS page in its own hidden in-app browser.
3. It fails with "Browser is not available: iab" and inventory lacks an IAB endpoint for that chat.
4. Select that chat once. Desktop logs show browser owner-sync capturing its route before a page webview exists.
5. The unchanged tool runtime then discovers IAB and opens/reads the neutral page successfully.

Observed twice in existing normal chats. In the independent diagnostic chat, conversation-stream ownership preceded browser-route ownership by several minutes. No restart, runtime reset, or permission change was used for recovery.

## Problem B: completing a subagent removes the browser connection, and followup_task does not recreate it

Three separate diagnostic subagents each opened and read a neutral HTTPS page successfully, then ended a turn with one of these states:

- Only tab explicitly closed; empty tab inventory verified before completion.
- Temporary tab left open without a retention mark.
- Tab marked with markHandoff; presence verified after marking and before completion.

All three lost IAB on followup_task. The preserved browser binding failed, and inventory lacked IAB. In the first two cases, one fresh IAB tab-creation attempt also failed. The marked-tab case did not attempt fresh creation; logs establish that its whole route was disposed and its marked tab closed.

An additional completed file-only turn did not repair the first agent: another resumed turn failed both the preserved binding and one fresh IAB creation attempt.

## Controls

- The ordinary parent survived its own completed turn with zero tabs and the same browser binding, then created and read a fresh page.
- That parent remained usable while the resumed child tests failed.
- Closing the final tab during an active turn returns a valid empty list; a replacement can be created through the existing binding.
- A stale closed-tab handle produces a tab-specific error while another tab remains usable.
- Reading a page with panel visibility false succeeds.

## Read-only packaged-code trace

- The active host browser hook captures child routes on initial subAgentActivity kind="started". Saved followup_task activities are kind="interacted", which this hook ignores.
- Child routes use disposeAfterSessionActivity=true. endSessionActivity disposes the route/backend independently of tab handoff marks. Logs show no route recapture before failed resumes.
- A broader renderer registration hook exists, but its manager initializer has an unconditional false gate in this build.
- The active host thread/started registration path requires a child source with a parent. The ordinary chats' source is "vscode", so that branch performs no registration.
- Selecting a chat invokes browser-sidebar-owner-sync -> syncOwner -> bindSessionRouteOwner, supplying the missing ordinary-chat route.
- Eighteen isolated tests of extracted installed functions support these findings. Those tests use mocked dependencies; the live reproductions above are separate evidence.

## Requested correction and verification

1. Register and await an exact, trusted window/owner association before the first browser-capable turn of an ordinary background chat.
2. Ensure a resumed child's browser route exists at actual turn admission/start using its verified parent association. Preserve handoff-marked tabs when ending a child turn. Recreating an empty route alone cannot restore an already destroyed tab.
3. Preserve per-chat isolation. A generic "interacted" event can also be messaging, so it is not by itself a reliable new-turn boundary.
4. Verify never-selected background creation, all three child cases, an intervening file-only turn, retained original-tab survival, and unaffected parent/unrelated-chat tabs.

Discovery warning counts are not failure counts: probing wrong-session endpoints can produce "No ChatGPT browser route is available" alongside a successful matching endpoint in the same pass.

Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58419 reports IAB discovery failure on the same macOS app version, but its cause and equivalence to these two reproductions are not established.

## Scope and privacy

No installed application files, permissions, security checks, profiles, or unrelated chats were changed. No app restart was performed. Test tabs were cleaned up. This report omits usernames, local paths, chat/session/tab identifiers, private websites, account details, raw logs, screenshots, transcripts, credentials, and proprietary source excerpts. No permanent repair has been applied or verified.

labels.name: priority/p2

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: Important and should be addressed in the near term.

labels.name: area/agent

labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary**: `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even though its own result says it hit the maximum turn limit before doing any analysis.

While using Gemini CLI to investigate two local repositories (`t3code` and `superset`), the agent invoked the `codebase_investigator` subagent and it failed immediately without doing any analysis.

I ran the Gemini CLI on these two local repositories with an objective asking it to understand their architectures and AI agent integrations. The saved session log shows:

- The main agent called `codebase_investigator` with a valid, concrete objective.
- The tool result was reported with `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.
- The embedded result text simultaneously says the investigation was interrupted because the "maximum number of turns was exceeded" before any specific task was identified or initiated.
- `RelevantLocations` was empty and no actual codebase analysis was performed.

This looks incorrect because:

1. The subagent appears to have exhausted its turn budget before performing any actual analysis.
2. The termination metadata is internally inconsistent: the parent tool call is surfaced as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`, but the embedded payload describes a limit-induced early termination with no findings.

Relevant evidence from the session log:

```text
session file: session-2026-03-09T18-34-10479ef5.json

line 50: "name": "codebase_investigator"
line 53: objective: "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset..."
line 61: "Termination Reason: GOAL"
line 61: "The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded)..."
line 61: "\"RelevantLocations\": []"
line 66: "status": "success"
line 79: "The `codebase_investigator` was unable to complete its analysis due to a turn limit..."
```

Full snippet from the saved session:

```json
{
  "id": "codebase_investigator_1773081420202_0",
  "name": "codebase_investigator",
  "args": {
    "objective": "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset, focusing on AI agent integrations.\nSpecifically:\n1. In t3code, how is 'Codex' integrated? Where is the core logic for agent interaction?\n2. In superset, what are the different agent/harness integrations (e.g., Mastra, MCP, Claude, etc.) and how are they implemented?\n3. What are the common patterns or interfaces used in superset that could be adapted for t3code to support multiple harnesses?\n\nIdentify key files, symbols, and architectural patterns in both repositories."
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "functionResponse": {
        "response": {
          "output": "Subagent 'codebase_investigator' finished.\nTermination Reason: GOAL\nResult:\n{\n  \"SummaryOfFindings\": \"The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded) before any specific task could be identified or initiated. As a result, no codebase analysis was performed, and no relevant locations or insights could be gathered.\",\n  \"ExplorationTrace\": [\n    \"Received system notification that the maximum number of turns was exceeded.\",\n    \"Followed emergency termination protocol as instructed.\"\n  ],\n  \"RelevantLocations\": []\n}"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "status": "success"
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these outcomes:

- `codebase_investigator` should actually explore the repositories and return findings.
- If it truly hits a turn limit, it should do so after some visible work, and the tool invocation should be surfaced as a failure or explicit limit condition, not as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.

At minimum, the CLI should not report a contradictory success state for a subagent that says it exceeded its turn budget before beginning analysis. If the subagent hits a system-imposed turn limit before doing useful work, the tool result should be reported as a failure or explicit limit condition (e.g. `status: "error"` with a clear error code), not as a successful `GOAL` completion.


### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Run `gemini` to enter the interactive CLI, then run the `/about` command.

```console
> /about
Gemini CLI package version: 0.32.1
Platform: Windows
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v20.20.0
PowerShell: 5.1.26100.7920
```

</details>

### Login information

Google Account, Pro tier from students promotion

### Anything else we need to know?

- After the failed `codebase_investigator` call, the main agent continued with manual file exploration and eventually produced an implementation plan. So the overall conversation did not fully crash, but the specialized investigator tool clearly failed.
- My current inference is that this may be either:
  - turn-budget state leaking into a fresh subagent invocation, or
  - an incorrect mapping of a subagent limit/error state into a successful `GOAL` termination in the parent session.
- If useful, I can provide the full saved session JSON or a redacted version of it.

issues.body:
# [BUG] Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (e.g., `maxTurns`)

## What happened?
The Browser Agent completely ignores any configuration overrides provided in the global or project-level `settings.json`. While the `AgentRegistry` correctly reads and merges these settings during initialization, the `BrowserAgentInvocation` and its factory (`browserAgentFactory.ts`) skips the registry and recreate the agent definition from scratch with hardcoded defaults.

## What did you expect to happen?
The Browser Agent should respect settings overrides like `maxTurns`, `maxTimeMinutes`, etc., just like other sub-agents (e.g., `codebase_investigator`). For example, setting `maxTurns: 0` in `settings.json` should cause the agent to terminate immediately upon invocation.

## Client information
<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Platform: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
Gemini CLI Version: 0.35.0-nightly.20260311.657f19c1f

</details>

## Login information
Google Account (OAuth)

## Anything else we need to know?
### Root Cause
The Browser Agent's unique invocation flow skips the `AgentRegistry` where settings overrides are maintained. Instead of using the pre-merged definition from the registry, it re-instantiates a fresh definition using hardcoded defaults.

**Relevant Files & Code Snippets:**

1.  **`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`**
    The Browser Agent is explicitly branched out of the standard flow that uses `LocalSubagentInvocation`:
    ```typescript
    if (definition.name === BROWSER_AGENT_NAME) {
      return new BrowserAgentInvocation(this.config, ...);
    }
    ```

2.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentInvocation.ts`**
    The `execute` method calls `createBrowserAgentDefinition`, passing the `config` object but omitting the merged definition from the registry.

3.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentFactory.ts`**
    The factory re-runs the `BrowserAgentDefinition` constructor, which returns hardcoded defaults (e.g., `maxTurns: 50`):
    ```typescript
    const baseDefinition = BrowserAgentDefinition(config, !visionDisabledReason);
    ```

### Suggested Fix
Update `browserAgentFactory.ts` to attempt to retrieve the existing definition from the `AgentRegistry` before falling back to creating a fresh one.

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `browser_agent` (specifically `BrowserManager.ts`) currently employs a restrictive "fail-fast" strategy when encountering a locked browser profile (e.g., when `sessionMode: 'persistent'` is used and an existing instance or orphaned process is active):


```json
{
  "success": false,
  "summary": "The task could not be completed because the browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile.",
  "fullErrorMessage": "The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use --isolated to run multiple browser instances.\nCause: The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use a different userDataDir or stop the running browser first."
}
```

I propose to make it more resilient with the following capabilities:

1.  **Automatic Session Takeover:** If `persistent` mode fails due to a profile lock, the agent should automatically attempt to connect to the existing instance (as if `sessionMode: 'existing'` were specified). This requires a graceful "fallback-and-probe" mechanism in `BrowserManager.connectMcp()`.
2.  **Orphaned Process Recovery:** If an `existing` connection is not feasible but the profile remains locked, the `BrowserManager` should proactively detect orphaned `chrome` or `chrome-devtools-mcp` processes associated with the Gemini CLI profile and offer (or automatically execute) a "Self-Healing" routine (process termination + lock file removal).
3.  **Intelligent Error Remediation:** Replace the current static error messages with an interactive recovery flow. Utilizing the `ask_user` tool, the agent should present the user with a "Choice" menu featuring numbered options to resolve the lock (e.g., **1. Attempt Session Takeover**, **2. Force Termination & Reset**, or **3. Launch Isolated Session**). 
### Why is this needed?

Forcing the user to manually `pkill` processes or close browser windows is a friction point that degrades the autonomous agent experience. The agent has sufficient context (profile path, PIDs) to resolve this internally without user intervention.


### Additional context

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

## Objective
Ensure the Gemini CLI understands its own mechanics well enough to act as its own expert guide. The agent must be able to provide users with accurate facts about how it works, its hotkeys, and the exact CLI flags needed to run itself for specific workflows.

## The Problem
Users rely on the CLI to learn how to use the CLI. If the agent hallucinates flags (like suggesting the deprecated `--yolo` instead of `--approval-mode=yolo`) or forgets UI hotkeys (like `Double Esc` for `/rewind`), it blocks progress and creates friction. The agent needs strict grounding in its own documentation to accurately guide users.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Accurate Internal Facts:** The agent (specifically the `cli_help` subagent) must have flawless recall of its own UI keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, and settings hierarchy.
2. **Flag Construction:** It must be able to tell users exactly how to run it from the terminal for various use cases (e.g., suggesting `gemini -i "prompt" --sandbox --output-format json` for safe, headless scripting).
3. **Self-Execution & Guidance:** It should be able to write the exact commands needed to run itself, restart itself, or execute sub-tasks with the correct environment variables and flags.

issues.title: Leverage model's bash affinity via Zero-Dependency OS Sandboxing & Post-Execution Intent Routing

labels.name: priority/p2
labels.description: Important but can be addressed in a future release.

labels.name: area/agent

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

labels.name: effort/large
labels.description: 3+ days: platform-specific, architecture, memory leaks

type.name: Epic
type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: ci(chained_e2e): don't expose GEMINI_API_KEY to fork-controlled code
prs.body:
## What

`chained_e2e.yml` is triggered by `workflow_run` after `trigger_e2e.yml` runs on a PR; it executes in the base-repo context with secrets and checks out the PR's code via an artifact the triggering run uploaded. This PR gates that artifact — and `GEMINI_API_KEY` — on the triggering run's **head repository** being this repository, and skips the secret-bearing jobs for any triggering run that is not a successful same-repo run. Defense-in-depth for the `workflow_run` + fork-checkout pattern.

## Changes (all in `.github/workflows/chained_e2e.yml`)

1. `download_repo_name` runs for a `workflow_run` only when that run's `conclusion == 'success'` and `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository` — trustworthy event fields, not artifact contents.
2. `parse_run_context` exports a `trusted` output: for a `workflow_run` it is `false` unless `download_repo_name` succeeded and both artifact fields (`repo_name`, `head_sha`) are present. The `set_pending_status`, the e2e (linux / mac / windows), `evals`, the aggregate `e2e`, and `set_workflow_status` jobs are all gated on `trusted == 'true'`.
3. The `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` fallback in the SHA resolution is removed — no silent fallback to an unverified sha.
4. `GEMINI_API_KEY` on the four test/eval steps is passed only when `parse_run_context.outputs.repository == github.repository` **and** (`event_name != 'workflow_run'` **or** `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository`), with the event-field check as the authoritative guard; otherwise the step receives an empty value.
5. The Windows job drops `cache: 'npm'` (it errors on the fork path where no lock file is present) — a small trade-off: in-repo Windows runs lose npm caching.

## Behavior for pull requests from forks

`trigger_e2e.yml` still runs on every PR. But a fork PR's `workflow_run` carries a fork `head_repository`, so `download_repo_name` is skipped → `trusted` is `false` → the chained E2E / evals / status jobs are **skipped**, and no chained-E2E status is posted on the fork commit. **This is a behavior change:** fork PRs no longer get the automatic chained E2E that previously ran — that automatic keyed run on fork-checked-out code is exactly what this PR closes. Maintainers can run E2E for a specific fork commit via the existing `workflow_dispatch` path. If automatic E2E on fork PRs is wanted back, the follow-up is an Environment with required reviewers on the e2e jobs (as `eval-pr.yml` does with `eval-gate`).

## Verification

Static only: the YAML parses, and every job that reads `needs.parse_run_context.outputs.trusted` lists `parse_run_context` in `needs`. Not run end-to-end.

## Credit

The origin-check + trusted-gate design (commits `8a5396d`, `e2433b6`) is from @r-bedekar.

prs.title: feat(core): add model.requestTimeoutMs setting for the API headers timeout
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a `model.requestTimeoutMs` setting so the 60s API headers timeout can be raised. Right now it can only be changed through the `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` experiment flag, which is never fetched for Vertex AI / API key auth, so anyone with long-thinking requests just gets them aborted at 60s and replayed from scratch.

## Details

- New setting `model.requestTimeoutMs` (number, ms, requires restart). Not set = current behaviour, nothing changes by default.
- `Config.getRequestTimeoutMs()` returns the setting when it's a positive finite number, otherwise falls back to the experiment flag like before.
- No changes needed in `fetch.ts`. `refreshAuth` already calls `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()` with whatever `getRequestTimeoutMs()` returns, and that runs for every auth type, so the setting is picked up for Vertex AI too.
- 0 / negative / NaN are ignored instead of being passed on, since `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts` throws on those.
- Regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json` and `docs/reference/configuration.md` with `npm run schema:settings` / `npm run docs:settings`.

I went with a setting rather than the `GEMINI_API_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS` env var from the issue because the other model options already live under `model.*`. Happy to add the env var too if you'd prefer.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29693

## How to Validate

Unit tests:

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/config/config.test.ts -t getRequestTimeoutMs
```

The 3 new behaviour tests (setting used, setting wins over the flag, applied via `refreshAuth` for Vertex AI) fail on `main` and pass here:

```
main:         Tests  3 failed | 5 passed | 247 skipped (255)
this branch:  Tests  8 passed | 247 skipped (255)
```

Also ran the full `packages/core/src/config/config.test.ts` (255 passed), `packages/cli/src/config/{settingsSchema,config,settings}.test.ts` (385 passed, 1 skipped), `npm run typecheck`, eslint and prettier on the touched files.

End to end, I pointed the bundled CLI at a small local server that waits 70s before sending response headers (`GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787`, `gemini -m gemini-2.5-flash -p ping`):

![before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prath47/gemini-cli/pr-assets/requestTimeout-before-after.png)

Without the setting, the request is dropped after ~60s and retried (I killed it at 150s):

```
+2.6s   POST .../gemini-2.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse  (holding 70s)
+63.0s  client closed connection before reply
+68.6s  POST .../gemini-2.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse  (holding 70s)
+129.1s client closed connection before reply
...
Attempt 1 failed. Retrying with backoff... Error: exception TypeError: fetch failed sending request
Attempt 2 failed. Retrying with backoff... Error: exception TypeError: fetch failed sending request
```

With `"model": { "requestTimeoutMs": 120000 }`:

```
+2.6s   POST .../gemini-2.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse  (holding 70s)
+72.6s  replied to .../gemini-2.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse
pong
[cli exit 0 after 72s]
```

Upgrade notes

  • Redirects: the HTTP client transports now follow a redirect only when it stays on the same origin (same scheme, host and port; http to https on the same host is allowed). A deployment whose endpoint redirects to another host or port either configures the final URL or sets redirectPolicy: 'follow' on StreamableHTTPClientTransport or SSEClientTransport. In browsers, a redirected request fails unless that option is set.
  • New options, both off unless you set them: maxToolInputElements on McpServer limits the number of array elements and object members in a tool call's arguments. expectedResource on requireBearerAuth accepts only tokens issued for this server (the token's audience).

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */

mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

}

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

... (truncated)

Updates `lycheeverse/lychee-action` from 2.6.1 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from lycheeverse/lychee-action's releases.

v2.9.0

Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from v0.23.0 to v0.24.2.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee 0.24.x release artifacts. Starting with lychee v0.24.0, the archive layout changed, and the lychee binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. lychee-action now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2

you will get the new version once the floating v2 tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0

What’s new from lychee v0.24.x

Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing #:~:text=.... This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

Sitemap support

lychee can now read sitemap.xml inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

Fixes and reliability improvements

prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #22323

Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS was reported as `status: success` with `Termination Reason: GOAL`, hiding the fact that the subagent was interrupted before completing its task.

## Root Cause

The recovery path in `LocalAgentExecutor` unconditionally overwrote `terminateReason` to `GOAL` whenever the grace-period recovery turn called `complete_task`.

## Changes (16 files, +597/-37)

### Core (4 files)
- `types.ts`: `recovered?: boolean` on `OutputObject`
- `local-executor.ts`: Recovery keeps original terminate reason, sets `recovered: true`
- `local-invocation.ts` + `local-session-invocation.ts`: Non-GOAL -> `SubagentState.ERROR`, llmContent marks `INCOMPLETE`

### Tool hardening (2 files)
- `complete-task.ts`: `looksLikeInterruptionReport()` heuristic
- `codebase-investigator.ts`: Tags empty `RelevantLocations` as `[INCOMPLETE]`

### Telemetry (1 file)
- `AgentFinishEvent` carries `recovered` in OTel attributes

### UI (2 files)
- `SubagentGroupDisplay.tsx`: "Agent Interrupted" header for MAX_TURNS/TIMEOUT
- `SubagentProgressDisplay.tsx`: No spinner for ERROR states

### Tests (7 files, 332 passing)
- 3 existing assertions updated + 17 new test cases

```bash
npm run build && npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- --run
```

prs.title: fix(core): omit null exit code in list_background_processes
prs.body:
## Summary
Hello maintainers, i was looking at minor issue which was not solved from a long time #29167 a small fix can resolve the issue.  list_background_processes was showing `(Exit Code: null)` to the model for any background process that was killed by a signal. Now the exit code only appears when there actually is one.

## Details

When a process is killed by a signal it has no exit code, so its `exitCode` is `null`. The formatter only checks `exitCode !== undefined`, so `null` got through and was printed as text.

The check now prints the exit code only when `typeof exitCode === 'number'`. This still keeps an exit code of `0`, which a simple truthy check would have dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29167

## How to Validate

1. Start a long-running background process, such as `sleep 300`.
2. Kill it with a signal, such as `kill -TERM <pid>`.
3. Call `list_background_processes`. The entry should no longer say `Exit Code: null`.
4. Start a background process that exits normally, such as `true`. It should still show `(Exit Code: 0)`.
5. Run the core test suite. The new regression test should pass, and it should fail if you revert the fix.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation (not needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (none)

prs.title: fix(cli): detect local git clone installation from CLI executable path
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where running Gemini CLI from a source checkout outside of the clone directory causes `getInstallationInfo` to misclassify the installation as a global npm install, triggering an unintended background `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@latest` during auto-update.

Fixes #30209

## Details
In `packages/cli/src/utils/installationInfo.ts`, local git clone detection previously relied on:
```ts
isGitRepository(process.cwd()) &&
realPath.startsWith(normalizedProjectRoot) &&
!realPath.includes('/node_modules/')
```
Because `projectRoot` comes from `config.getProjectRoot()` (which is the current target directory / `process.cwd()`), running the CLI from any other directory caused `realPath.startsWith(normalizedProjectRoot)` or `isGitRepository(process.cwd())` to fail. As a result, detection fell through to the default branch (`PackageManager.NPM`, `isGlobal: true`), spawning `npm install -g` in the background.

This fix:
- Updates the detection to check `!realPath.includes('/node_modules/') && isGitRepository(path.dirname(realPath))`, inspecting where the CLI executable itself is located rather than the user's working directory.
- Preserves the `node_modules` exclusion so package-manager installations (npx, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun) remain unaffected.
- Updates existing tests and adds unit test coverage in `installationInfo.test.ts` for running a local clone from an unrelated working directory.

## Related Issues
Fixes #30209

## How to Validate
Run the unit tests in `packages/cli`:
```bash
npx vitest run src/utils/installationInfo.test.ts --coverage false
```
Expected: All 22 tests pass, including the test asserting that running from an unrelated working directory is correctly identified as a local git clone.

## Pre-Merge Checklist
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [x] Windows (npm run)

prs.title: docs(extensions): stop recommending an excludeTools form that never matches
prs.body:
## Summary

The extension docs tell authors to write `"excludeTools": ["run_shell_command(rm -rf)"]` and promise it blocks that command. It blocks nothing.

Extension `excludeTools` entries are collected into a `Set` in `Config.getExcludeTools()` and compared against each tool's whole name in `ToolRegistry` (`!possibleNames.some((name) => excludeTools?.has(name))`). An entry carrying arguments is never a member of that set of names, so `run_shell_command` stays enabled and no warning says the entry was ignored.

The `toolName(args)` syntax is real, but it is parsed by `mapToolsToRules` for `tools.allowed`, `tools.core` and policy rules, which split it into a tool name plus an `argsPattern`. Extension `excludeTools` never goes through that path.

## Changes

- `docs/extensions/reference.md`: the `excludeTools` entry now states that each value is matched as a whole tool name, shows the working form, and says what the `toolName(args)` form actually belongs to. Command-scoped restrictions point at a policy rule with `commandPrefix` and a `deny` decision.
- `docs/extensions/best-practices.md`: the security example uses `["run_shell_command"]`, with the same pointer for narrower rules, instead of a value that leaves the tool enabled.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/examples/exclude-tools/gemini-extension.json`: the shipped example uses the form that works.
- `packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts`: a test pins the contract, so `run_shell_command(rm -rf)` and `run_shell_command(rm -rf *)` must leave the tool registered. It fails if the matcher ever starts accepting the parenthesised form without the docs being updated with it.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts` — 33 passed
- `npx prettier --check` on all four files — clean
- `eslint --fix --max-warnings 0` via the pre-commit hook — clean

Fixes #28962
