issues.title: Cloud agent: viewing any image ends the session with `CAPIError: 400 The image data you provided does not represent a valid image`

labels.name: triage:needs-human
labels.description: Auto-triage could not classify this issue confidently. Remove the label to re-queue it.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug


## Summary

In a Copilot cloud agent session on a GHEC data residency tenant (`<tenant>.ghe.com`), the `view` tool on any image file ends the session. The tool itself reports success. The next model call is rejected, and the session dies.

The error names the image as the fault. The image is never the fault. A 4 KB, 1280x720 PNG that Pillow reads as a valid RGB image fails exactly like a real screenshot.

## What the session gets

```
Viewed image file at path /tmp/img-720.png
```

then

```
CAPIError: 400 The image data you provided does not represent a valid image.
Please check your input and try again with one of the supported image formats:
['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'image/webp']
```

The session state goes to `failed` and that message is the task's recorded error.

## Reproduction

Any session. No repository state is needed.

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import zlib, struct
w, h = 1280, 720
row = b'\x00' + bytes([200, 40, 90]) * w
raw = row * h
def chunk(t, d):
    c = t + d
    return struct.pack('>I', len(d)) + c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff)
hdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
open('/tmp/img.png', 'wb').write(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', hdr) + chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw, 6)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))
PY
```

Then call `view` on `/tmp/img.png`. The file is 4319 bytes. `PIL.Image.open` reads it as `(1280, 720) RGB`.

## What I ruled out

I made five PNGs of 1280 pixels wide and 720, 1440, 2880, 5760 and 11520 pixels tall, then viewed them one per turn, smallest first. The session died on the **first** one.

| Variable | Tested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Height | 720 through 11520 | dies on the smallest |
| Byte size | 4 KB synthetic, 78 KB real screenshot, 128 KB real screenshot | all die |
| Images per turn | one | dies on one |
| Source | hand-written PNG, Playwright `page.screenshot` | both die |
| Model | `sweagent-capi:gpt-5.6-sol`, `sweagent-capi:gpt-5.6-terra` | both die |

## Why this is worse than it reads

1. **The failing step reports success.** `view` answers `Viewed image file at path <path>`. The agent has no way to know it has just ended the session.
2. **The error blames the file.** Every reader goes and checks the file, and the file is fine.
3. **It kills a session that already did its work.** In our case a session implemented a work item across 24 files, passed 691 unit tests and 6 Playwright end-to-end tests, wrote its screenshots, then viewed three of them and died before it could open the pull request.
4. **It makes your own guidance fatal.** Any instruction that tells an agent to check a screen capture before attaching it now ends the session that follows it.

## What I ask for

1. Make image input work, or say plainly that a cloud agent session cannot take image input on a data residency tenant.
2. If it cannot, make `view` refuse an image with a clear message instead of accepting it and killing the next model call.
3. Fix the error text. "The image data you provided does not represent a valid image" is wrong for a valid image, and it sends every reader to the wrong place.

issues.body:
## Summary

The Code Mode `tools.opencode.worktree_create` and `tools.opencode.worktree_remove` tools execute successfully while Plan mode is active. Plan mode is documented as read-only, but these tools mutate the filesystem and Git state (creating/removing worktree directories and registering entries in `.git/worktrees/`).

Related: `tools.opencode.session_move` likely has the same gap, since it also mutates session state rather than only reading it.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.22621 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: xterm-256color (`TERM_PROGRAM` / `COLORTERM` unset)
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe` (config sets `shell: powershell`)
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none configured (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` has no `plugin` key)

## Reproduction

1. Enter Plan mode in an OpenCode session (the mode that advertises read-only discussion and forbids file modification).
2. From Code Mode (`execute`), call `tools.opencode.worktree_create({ name: "probe" })`.
3. Observe the call return `{ directory: ".../.local/share/opencode/worktree/<id>/probe" }` and the worktree registered via `git worktree list`.
4. Optionally call `tools.opencode.worktree_remove({ directory, force: true })` — note it returns `Permission denied: edit` while `worktree_create` succeeded, so the two tools are gated inconsistently.

## Expected Behavior

Plan mode should block any tool that mutates the filesystem or repository state. `worktree_create` creates a directory tree and writes to `.git/worktrees/`, so it is a write operation and should be unavailable (or require explicit approval) in Plan mode, the same way `edit` and `write` are.

## Actual Behavior

`tools.opencode.worktree_create` ran to completion in Plan mode. The resulting worktree was visible to `git worktree list` as a detached-HEAD entry, and the directory existed on disk. `worktree_remove` was then refused with `Permission denied: edit`, which suggests the permission classification for the worktree tools is not aligned with their actual side effects.

## Additional Context

Observed `git worktree list` output after creating a worktree during Plan mode:

```
C:/.../ai-engineering-os                                    895fcd8 [main]
C:/.../.local/share/opencode/worktree/<id>/probe-worktree   895fcd8 (detached HEAD)
```

Two notes that may matter for the fix:

- **Worktree location and shape.** `worktree_create` places worktrees under `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/<hash>/<name>` in detached HEAD state, with `"strategy": "git"` reported by `worktree_list`. This looks like a sandbox for agent isolation rather than a user-facing feature branch. If that is intentional, it is worth documenting, because it differs from `git worktree add ../dir -b branch`.
- **Stale entries after failed removal.** After `worktree_remove` succeeded for one worktree but failed for another with `Permission denied` (folder locked by another process), `git worktree list` no longer showed either entry, while `worktree_list` still reported both. The Git-side and OpenCode-side registries appear to be able to diverge. `git worktree prune` is the manual fix.

Suggested fix: classify `worktree_create`, `worktree_remove`, and `session_move` as write tools so Plan mode and the `edit` permission gate cover them consistently, and make `worktree_remove` idempotent when the directory is already gone from disk.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Restore the legacy UI with the persistent left sidebar as an option
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

The recent sidebar redesign (#20242) replaced the classic two-panel layout
(persistent left sidebar + session panel) with a Codex-style unified view.
For me this is not a visual refresh — it removed the single most important
part of my daily workflow, and there is currently no way to go back.

**What I want changed / added:**

1. Keep the **legacy UI with the persistent left sidebar** available as an
   option (a `legacy` / `classic` UI toggle or config flag is enough — it
   doesn't have to be the default).
2. If the legacy layout can't be maintained, at minimum restore an
   **always-visible left sidebar** — not hover-only menus or a collapsed rail
   that requires extra clicks.

**Why this matters (the benefit):**

I live inside opencode for hours every day. The left sidebar gives me an
at-a-glance, persistent view of my projects, workspaces, and sessions:

- I can see and switch between projects/contexts without breaking flow.
- Sessions are one click away, not buried behind hover or search.
- Context switching stays fast and predictable.

The new interface hides all of this behind a single unified list with
hover/focus interactions. Every session feels slower and more disoriented.
This is not an aesthetic preference — removing the sidebar with no escape
hatch is a functional regression for anyone who relies on it.

**Related:**

- #4583 asked for a way to go back to the old UI.
- #20242 introduced the sidebar redesign.

Happy to provide screenshots, my opencode version, and platform details if
that helps. Please don't leave those of us who depend on the left sidebar
behind.

issues.title: plugins: RPC registered via ctx.rpc.register returns rpc.unavailable over HTTP
issues.body:
## Summary

RPCs registered by a server plugin (`ctx.rpc.register`) are callable in-process via `ctx.rpc(Contract)`, but every HTTP call to `POST /api/rpc/{rpcID}/{method}` returns `400 {"type":"rpc.unavailable"}` — including a verbatim copy of the `acme` example from the RPC guide. RPC **events** from the same registration do flow through the public event stream (`rpc.<id>.<event>`), so only the HTTP method-call path appears affected.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.3
- OS: Linux 6.14.0-37-generic (linux x64)
- Terminal: TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty, TERM=xterm-ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: local project plugins under `.opencode/plugins/` (a dual-entry server+TUI plugin and a TUI-only plugin, plus the probe described below)

## Reproduction

1. Create a project plugin at `.opencode/plugins/acme-probe/index.ts` containing the verbatim `acme` example from https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc (`Rpc.define` id `acme`, method `search`, event `updated`, registered with `ctx.rpc.register` in `setup`).
2. Trigger a load (touch the file) and confirm it loads cleanly: no "failed to load plugin" in the log, `setup` runs (verified by writing a file as a side effect), and the in-process call `ctx.rpc(Acme).search({ query: "self" })` returns `{ "text": "result for self" }`.
3. Call it over HTTP:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/acme/search --data '{"query":"hello"}'
```

## Expected Behavior

Per the RPC guide ("Call > HTTP"), the endpoint returns the method output (`{"text":"..."}`). A client built with `OpenCode.make({ baseUrl }).rpc(Acme).search(...)` should behave the same way, and so should `context.client.rpc(Contract)` from a TUI plugin.

## Actual Behavior

```json
{"_tag":"RpcError","type":"rpc.unavailable","message":"RPC is unavailable: acme"}
HTTP 400 Bad Request
```

Reproduces consistently:

- before and after `opencode service restart`
- with and without the optional `location` query parameter (also tried `location[directory]=<project path>`)
- from the TUI as well: `context.client.rpc(Contract).method()` resolves to the same endpoint and also receives 400

Working paths for comparison (same registration):

- in-process: `ctx.rpc(Acme).search({ query: "self" })` returns `{"text":"result for self"}`
- events: `registration.events.emit("updated", {...})` arrives on `GET /api/event` as `{"type":"rpc.acme.updated", "location": {...}, "data": {...}}`

## Additional Context

- The plugin completes setup with no errors logged. Registration is clearly validated and executed: omitting the required `events` field in `Rpc.define` produced an immediate `failed to load plugin` (`Object.entries requires that input parameter not be null or undefined`), which we fixed before testing the valid version.
- Verified the call shape against the shipped `@opencode/plugin@2.1.3` types (`dist/rpc.d.ts`) and the guide, so this does not look like an API-shape mismatch on the caller side.
- Real-world impact: my plugin [opencode-contextbar](https://github.com/zyc-bit/opencode-tui-plugins) needs to pass hook measurements from a server plugin to a TUI plugin. Since the documented HTTP method path is unavailable, it ships an events-only transport as a workaround (a per-call event plus a snapshot heartbeat — events are live-only, so a method call would otherwise be needed to bootstrap a late-joining client).

issues.body:
### Description

When updating OpenCode via `opencode upgrade` on an npm-managed installation, the updater spawns npm with `--force`:

```
npm install --global --allow-scripts=@opencode/cli --force @opencode/cli@<version>
```

In `packages/cli/src/services/updater.ts`:
```typescript
const commands: Record<Exclude<Method, "bun" | "curl" | "brew" | "winget">, string[]> = {
  npm: [
    npm,
    "install",
    "--global",
    ...npmPrefixArgs,
    `--allow-scripts=${packageName}`,
    ...((OPENCODE_ARTIFACT === "cli" && !installedPackage?.endsWith("/cli-node")) ||
    (installedPackage && packageName !== installedPackage)
      ? ["--force"]
      : []),
    target,
  ],
```

Because `@opencode/cli` declares 12 native target binaries in `optionalDependencies`, passing `--force` to npm forces it to bypass `os` and `cpu` filtering. Consequently, npm downloads all 12 platform packages (~1.5 GB to 2 GB total) simultaneously instead of only the single ~115 MB package for the current host.

From `~/.npm/_logs/*-debug-0.log`:
```
80 silly reify mark retired [
80 silly reify   '.../lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli',
80 silly reify   '.../bin/opencode',
80 silly reify   '.../bin/opencode2'
80 silly reify ]
81 silly reify moves {
81 silly reify   '.../bin/opencode': '.../bin/.opencode-GjisxTmU',
81 silly reify   '.../bin/opencode2': '.../bin/.opencode2-BL1uIZyH'
81 silly reify }
...
93 http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline/-/cli-linux-x64-baseline-2.3.0.tgz 246068ms (cache miss)
94 http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline-musl/-/cli-linux-x64-baseline-musl-2.3.0.tgz 256299ms (cache miss)
```

Because npm renames/retires existing global binaries prior to fetching dependencies, if the multi-gigabyte download times out or is interrupted, the installation is left with a truncated binary and missing symlinks, causing `command not found: opencode`.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

`@opencode/cli` 2.2.7 (upgrading to 2.3.0)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have OpenCode installed globally via npm: `npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.2.7`
2. Run `opencode upgrade 2.3.0` (or accept update prompt in TUI).
3. Check `~/.npm/_logs/` or network activity: observe npm executing with `--force` and downloading all 12 optional dependency platform tarballs (macOS arm64/x64, Windows, Linux arm64/musl/baseline).

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64, Linux 7.0.0-38-generic), Node v24.18.1, npm 12.2.1

### Terminal

zsh

issues.body:
## Summary

Long-running `opencode serve --service` (v2.3.0) accumulates file watchers and memory: RSS ~440 MB with VmSize ~11 GB, sustained ~10-15% CPU on the main thread, and ~2,368 inotify watches (2,363 distinct inodes). During a session the process is eventually killed by the OOM killer (system shows kswapd active / memory pressure), and prior serve runs end without a graceful `shutdown started` log line.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Linux 7.3.3-300.fc45.x86_64 (Fedora 45, x86_64)
- Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /usr/local/bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest (binary at ~/.opencode/bin/opencode)
- Active plugins: @tarquinen/opencode-dcp, opencode-engram-learning, superpowers, herdr-agent-state, ponytail

## Reproduction

1. Start `opencode serve --service`.
2. Open a session in a git repository (e.g. /home/omar/GuardtowerIQ-version-2).
3. Switch directories / reload locations during the session.
4. Observe in the serve process: `cat /proc/<pid>/fdinfo/* | grep -c '^inotify wd:'` grows; RSS and CPU stay elevated.
5. Eventually the process is killed (OOM) or must be restarted.

## Expected Behavior

Watcher count, RSS, and CPU remain bounded across location switches/reloads within a session.

## Actual Behavior

- Current serve run (run=3c3413ba) logged 56 `watcher subscribe` events but only 21 `watcher started` and 0 `watcher stopped`; the same paths (/, /home, /home/omar, /etc, skill/config/plugin paths) are subscribed 2-3 times.
- `/proc/18001`: 2 inotify instances, 2,368 total watches vs 2,363 distinct inodes.
- RSS 441,560 KB, VmSize 11,334,552 KB, main thread ~10% CPU.
- System under memory pressure (kswapd0 active); prior serve runs terminate without a `shutdown started` line.

## Additional Context

- Related to existing issue #54631 (location invalidation duplicates fff engine / inotify instances not destroyed). This report adds live /proc evidence and the high-CPU / OOM-kill symptom.
- Logs: ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log (run=3c3413ba).
- No `MaxListeners`/`memory leak` warning text present in the log; leak is observable via watcher accumulation and /proc.

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: server: drain replay of pending step fails with Mistral 400 ('str object' has no attribute 'items') and retries every ~15s
issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading to OpenCode v2, long-running sessions on the native Mistral provider (model `zai-glm-5-3`) fail on `SessionRunner.drain` (service-start resume of a pending step) with a provider 400: `'str object' has no attribute 'items'`. Normal sends to the same session and model succeed — only the drain-path replay of the pending step fails. The drain then retries the identical payload roughly every 15 seconds, producing error spam with no self-recovery, re-triggering at each service restart.

## Environment

- opencode version: server 2.0.18 (`@opencode/cli`, bun global, latest release); client 2.0.16 (OpenChamber bundled CLI)
- OS: Pop!_OS 24.04, Linux 7.1.5-76070105-generic x86_64
- Terminal: OpenChamber desktop app (embedded TUI); TERM=linux
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: release channel (bun global) + OpenChamber v2 AppImage bundle
- Active plugins: oh-my-opencode-slim@latest (2.2.25), dcg-guard.js (local, V2 format), openchamber-agent-tool (local); opencode-mem configured but fails to load (pre-V2 release). None of these shape the failing request path (verified).

## Reproduction

1. Run a long-lived orchestrator session on provider `mistral` (native integration `@opencode/ai/providers/mistral`), model `zai-glm-5-3` (variant `high`), accumulating a large reasoning/tool-call history (~973k cumulative input tokens, ~165k output, heavy tool + reasoning usage over several days).
2. Leave a step pending in the session queue across a service restart (in our case: a queued continuation after a background child-task completion, then `opencode service restart`).
3. On server start, `SessionRunner.drain` resumes the pending step and Mistral rejects the request with HTTP 400.
4. The drain retries the same request every ~15s. A second, smaller session hit the same error once at the same restart and then continued normally — the failure is specific to the pending-step replay, not to the session or model generally.

## Expected Behavior

- Drain resume should send a request the provider accepts, or sanitize/refresh the replayed provider state (reasoning/thinking blocks, `providerState` item references) so stale state cannot poison the replay.
- A non-transient provider 4xx should not be retried indefinitely; back off and surface a clear, user-visible error instead.
- The outgoing request body should be logged at DEBUG on provider errors (cf. #29186) so the rejected field can be identified — the provider does not disclose which field was invalid, and opencode's logs do not include the body.

## Actual Behavior

```text
timestamp=2026-09-26T05:17:33.602Z level=ERROR run=65950548 message="Failed to drain Session" cause="AI.Error: ThirdPartyException - {"error":{"message":"'str object' has no attribute 'items'","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}
    at SessionStep.attempt ... at SessionRunner.runStep ... at SessionRunner.drain ... at ServerProcess.start" role=server sessionID=ses_f2456a4b7ffe0kfLCDXgyzSNYp
```

Retries of the identical error: 05:17:33, 05:19:45, 05:20:03, 05:21:29, 05:21:43, 05:21:57, 05:22:05, 05:22:24, 05:23:12 (~15s intervals, 13+ occurrences over ~7 minutes) before stopping on its own. The same failure recurred across consecutive service restarts.

## Additional Context

- The error text is a Python-side error from Mistral's GLM backend: a string arrived where a dict/object was expected. This is consistent with replayed reasoning/thinking state being serialized in a shape the provider rejects on the drain path, while the normal send path (which works against the same model) does not reproduce it.
- Not plugin-related: the only provider-shaping plugin was inert during the first occurrence and only ever targeted a different model (`zai-glm-5-2`) on a different, OpenAI-compatible provider definition; the failing sessions ran plain native-integration `zai-glm-5-3`.
- First observed immediately after upgrading to v2 (OpenChamber v2 bundle); the same multi-day workflow under v1 did not exhibit it.
- Related issues: #45456 (stuck drain retry loop on long sessions; replayed `providerState`/reasoning state rejected upstream; same "no request body in logs" complaint), #39291 (mutated thinking block → permanent 400 retry loop), #44852 (dangling `tool_call_id` poisoning replays), #29186 (log request/response body at DEBUG).
- Workarounds tried: none effective server-side; the loop eventually pauses but re-triggers on the next restart. Upstream report #45456 indicates recovery requires manual session surgery/revert.

issues.title: permissions: built-in external_directory ask never prompts, identical explicit rule does
issues.body:
## Summary

With pure default permissions (no `permissions` key in config), writes to paths outside the session Location/worktree (e.g. `/tmp` from a `~/Desktop` session) complete silently with no permission dialog, even though the built-in base policy resolves `external_directory` to `ask`. Adding an identical explicit global rule (`external_directory * -> ask`) makes the TUI prompt correctly. `deny` rules are enforced correctly.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.25
- OS: Linux 7.2.9-1-cachyos (linux x64)
- Terminal: kitty (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /usr/bin/fish
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Use default config with no `permissions` key. Open a session in `~/Desktop` (non-git dir, project worktree = `~/Desktop`, verified in `project` table).
2. Have the agent create a file in `/tmp` (outside Location and worktree).
3. Observe: no "Permission required" dialog appears; the file is created.
4. Add a global explicit rule: `{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`.
5. Retry the same write. Observe: the TUI now shows "Permission required / Access external directory /tmp" with Allow once / Always allow / Reject. Choosing "Allow once" lets the write proceed.
6. Remove the explicit rule and retry: silently allowed again, no dialog.
7. Sanity checks: `{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "/tmp/*", "effect": "deny" }` blocks the write immediately with `permission.rejected: external_directory`, so rule loading and enforcement work.

## Expected Behavior

Per the V2 permissions docs, a path outside the active Location and project worktree needs `external_directory` approval, and the built-in default for it is `ask` — so step 3 should have shown a permission dialog.

## Actual Behavior

The built-in default `ask` for `external_directory` never surfaces a dialog; the operation proceeds as if allowed. Only user-configured `ask` rules prompt. Verified consistently across multiple attempts, including after `opencode service restart` (rules out a stale-service artifact).

## Additional Context

- TUI is configured with `session.permissions: "prompt"` in `cli.json`, and interactive dialogs render fine (the `question` tool dialog appears normally), so this is not a client rendering problem.
- No saved "Always allow" approvals covered the tested paths (checked the `permission` table; test-created approvals were deleted afterwards).
- Even with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the server log contains no `evaluated permission` lines for these tool calls in 2.0.25, so the evaluation decision itself is not observable from logs.
- Related: #11042 (same symptom class on Windows, closed).
- Workaround: add an explicit global `{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }` rule so all external access prompts as documented.

I did not have a dedicated project folder created, so I initialized/opened the session directly at the root of the main drive (`C:\`) as the project directory. issues.body:
### Description

## Summary

With mouse capture enabled (default `mouse: true`), mouse wheel events always scroll the composer/input box regardless of pointer position. The message transcript (conversation area) never responds to the wheel.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.2.5
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-198-generic (x86_64) — opencode runs on a Linux host accessed over SSH; client machine is Windows
- Terminal: MobaXterm Version 25.2 (2025-05-03); TERM=xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Launch opencode v2.2.5 with default settings (mouse capture on) in a terminal that supports SGR mouse mode (reproduced in MobaXterm 25.2).
2. Have a session with enough messages that the transcript is scrollable (or scroll back first).
3. Hover the pointer over the message transcript (top of screen) and scroll the mouse wheel up/down.
4. For comparison: hover the pointer over the composer/input box and scroll the wheel.

## Expected Behavior

Wheel events are routed by pointer position: transcript scrolls when the pointer is over the transcript; composer scrolls when the pointer is over the composer.

## Actual Behavior

The wheel only scrolls the composer/input box regardless of where the pointer is. The transcript never scrolls.

## Additional Context

- The terminal side has been verified innocent. In a plain shell with SGR mouse tracking enabled (`ESC[?1006h` + `ESC[?1000h`), MobaXterm emits proper SGR wheel sequences whose coordinates track the pointer:
  - Pointer near top (~row 5): `ESC[<64;118;6M` (wheel up)
  - Pointer near bottom (~row 45): `ESC[<65;72;48M` (wheel down)
  So wheel events with correct x/y coordinates are delivered to the foreground process; opencode receives them but does not use the y coordinate to route scrolling to the transcript region.
- Workaround: keyboard transcript scrolling works — PageUp/PageDown (`session.page.up`/`session.page.down`), Home/End (`session.first`/`session.last`).
- Related secondary impact: with mouse capture on, the terminal's native left-click-select-to-copy and right-click paste stop working (events are delivered to opencode). Pasting into the composer still works via Ctrl+V.
- Frequency: reproducible consistently (MobaXterm 25.2_Personal).

issues.body:
## opencode-pty daemon leaks zombie child processes (unbounded growth under a single daemon PID)

Since upgrading to OpenCode 2.3.0, every finished shell command stays a `<defunct>` zombie child of `opencode-pty daemon` and is never reaped. Zombies grow monotonically for the daemon's entire lifetime, holding PIDs and counting against `TasksMax`.

### Reproduction

1. Start `opencode serve --service` (2.3.0) → spawns `opencode-pty daemon` (0.5.2).
2. Run a handful of `shell` tool calls in a session.
3. `ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,comm | awk '$3 ~ /^Z/'`
4. Finished commands are `<defunct>` children of the daemon; the count only goes up.

### Observed (one daemon PID, Debian 13 / Linux 7.3.3-cachyos x86_64)

- 81 total children, 79 zombies: 59 `bash`, 8 `tmux: client`, 6 `ls`, 1 each `tail`, `ps`, `openssl`, `go`, `git`, `curl`
- Oldest zombie ~11 hours old (39,849s) and still unreaped → pool is **not recycled**, it just grows
- Daemon `/proc/2674/status`: `SigCgt: 0000000100000440` (no SIGCHLD), Threads: 97

2.2.7 left no zombies in the same setup; restarting the daemon clears them.

### Related issues (both now closed)

- #63948 — our detailed report, closed as DUPLICATE of #63817
- #63817 — original report, closed NOT_PLANNED for inactivity

Because both duplicates are closed, please **do not close this issue as a duplicate**. The unbounded growth (past 25, under one daemon PID) is confirmed here and by `iehgit` (100 zombies, 2h11m) and `jotenakis2` (aarch64, monotonic past 25).

### Related bot-behavior complaint

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/63975 — opencodejr closed #63948 without checking #63817 was open, and does not respond to reopen pings.

### Expected

Exited children should be reaped promptly (e.g. `SIGCHLD`/`waitid`/`waitpid` in the event loop) so no `[defunct]` children remain after a command completes.

issues.body:
## Summary

The remote-access tunnel serves exactly one HTTPS request after each `opencode service restart`, then stops responding. The mobile client can authenticate but never receives session updates, and ends up stuck on "Reconnecting"/"Couldn't connect".

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0 (desktop app, updater reports "up to date")
- OS: Windows 10.0.26300.9457 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: desktop app (Electron); remote client is Android app `ai.opencode.mobilecode` 0.7.0 on Android 16 (RMX5051)
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none. One MCP server configured: `browse` (local, `browse.exe mcp`)

## Reproduction

1. Enable remote access: `opencode service set remote true` (route becomes `<route>.kz6kl4r2n7zg.opentunnel.xyz`).
2. `opencode service restart`.
3. Request the public URL twice in a row:
   `curl https://<route>.kz6kl4r2n7zg.opentunnel.xyz/api/info`
4. Open the Android app, pick a session and send a message.

## Expected Behavior

The tunnel keeps accepting requests, and the mobile client streams session updates normally.

## Actual Behavior

Only the **first** request after a restart succeeds. Every following request fails at the edge.

```
after restart:
try 1 -> 401   (tunnel alive, auth required as expected)
try 2 -> 000   (~0.2 s, connection reset)
try 3 -> 000
```

Reproduced three times after separate `opencode service restart` runs (23:41, 23:49, 23:52 local). Sometimes the first failure is not an immediate reset but a full TLS timeout:

```
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLS connect error: ... SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL
curl: (35) TLS connect error
```

On the Android device the same URL behaves the same way, and the app shows "Couldn't connect to 1dcf70…" / "Couldn't send · Retry" while the session list itself is cached and visible.

## Additional Context

Control checks made during the same period:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:28894/api/info` (local service) | 401 — healthy |
| `https://<route>….opentunnel.xyz/api/info` right after restart | 401 |
| same URL immediately after | 000 (reset 0.2 s, or 12–30 s timeout) |
| `https://opentunnel.xyz` (provider root) | 200 |
| `https://aaaa.kz6kl4r2n7zg.opentunnel.xyz` (unknown route) | 000 |

- The failure is identical from the Windows host and from a phone on the same LAN, so it is not client-side networking.
- Direct internet, no HTTP(S) proxy configured (`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` empty, WinHTTP direct).
- After `opencode service restart` the tunnel URL and route stay the same in `GET /api/info`, so the route is not re-registered.
- Restarting only the desktop app does not help, because the background service keeps running and owns the tunnel; only `opencode service restart` gives a brief working window (one request).
- Workaround: none usable; the desktop session on the same machine works fine.

Note: route id, hostname suffix and service password are redacted above.

issues.title: permissions: external_directory ask is skipped for shell
issues.body:
### Description

The `external_directory` rule is enforced for the file tools but not for `shell`.

With `{ "permissions": [ { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" } ] }` in the global config:

| Tool | Action | Prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write` | write to `C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\out\a.txt` | yes — "Access external directory" |
| `shell` | `Set-Content "C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\out\a.txt" "x" -Encoding utf8` | no |

Same path, same session, back to back. The docs say shell checks "its external working directory and directories inferred by its scanner" before the `shell` rules, so a literal absolute path passed to a standard cmdlet should be the easiest case to infer.

This is not #54524. There the explicit rule works and only the built-in default does not. Here the rule is present, works for the file tools, and is skipped for `shell`. It also survives `opencode reload` and `opencode service restart`, and `experimental.portable_shell_scanner: true` makes no difference.

Impact: `shell` can read, write and delete files anywhere on disk without an `external_directory` prompt, so the rule is not a boundary on its own. Workaround: `{ "action": "shell", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`.

Related: #56247 (permission evaluations are no longer logged in v2) made this harder to diagnose, since no permission lines appear in the log for either case.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Global config: `{ "permissions": [ { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" } ] }`
2. Start opencode in a workspace (e.g. a temp directory).
3. Have the agent write a file outside the workspace through `shell`: `Set-Content "C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\out\a.txt" "x" -Encoding utf8` -> the file is created, no prompt.
4. Have the agent write to the same path through the `write` tool -> the "Permission required / Access external directory" dialog appears.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

2.0.32

### Operating System

Windows 11 Home Single Language (NT 10.0.26300.0)

### Terminal

Windows Terminal (PowerShell 5.1.26100.9711)

issues.body:
## Summary

Switching a session from an OpenAI Responses model (with hosted `web_search` history) to a Chat Completions model (`opencode-go` / GLM-5.3) makes every subsequent request fail before any network call with `OpenAI Chat assistant messages only support text, reasoning, and tool-call content for now`. The chat adapter hard-fails instead of dropping or normalizing the hosted-tool history.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.7
- OS: Linux 7.2.14-arch1-1 (linux x64)
- Terminal: ghostty (TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: release (latest)
- Active plugins: `./local/chatgpt-native-search`, `@slkiser/opencode-quota`

## Reproduction

1. Use an OpenAI Responses model (`gpt-6.1-sol`) with hosted `web_search` available (here: enabled via the local `chatgpt-native-search` plugin over ChatGPT OAuth).
2. Ask a question that triggers a hosted `web_search` call, so the assistant history contains a `web_search` tool call.
3. Switch the same session's model to a Chat Completions model (`opencode-go` / `glm-5.3`).
4. Send a follow-up message.

## Expected Behavior

The session continues. OpenCode re-normalizes or drops history parts the Chat model cannot represent, or otherwise degrades gracefully.

## Actual Behavior

Every request fails with `Failed to drain Session`:

```
AI.Error: OpenAI Chat assistant messages only support text, reasoning, and tool-call content for now
    at OpenAIChat.fromRequest ...
```

The offending assistant message contains a hosted `web_search` tool part:

```json
{"type":"tool","name":"web_search","executed":true,
 "state":{"input":{"type":"open_page","url":"…"},
 "content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"type\":\"web_search_call\", ...}"}]}}
```

## Additional Context

- This is the Chat Completions counterpart of #29159, which fixed the same hosted-tool history replay for the **Responses** adapter (`OpenAI Responses assistant messages only support ...`). The Responses fix lowers hosted tool history to native Responses input items; the Chat adapter has no native `web_search_call` input item, so it currently throws instead of degrading.
- Related: #55096 (model/provider switch causes a hard history-replay failure for a different content field).
- The model switch is confirmed by two `model-switched` messages: `gpt-6.1-sol` (`providerID: openai`) → `glm-5.3` (`providerID: opencode-go`).
- Workaround: start a fresh session on the Chat model (no search history), or switch the session back to a Responses model.

issues.body:
### Description

OpenCode 2.3.0 still hangs at startup with a blank screen when the user's inotify instances are exhausted (`fs.inotify.max_user_instances`). This is the same failure as #16610, which was closed automatically for inactivity rather than fixed. Two details differ from that report:

- It happens without any `.git` directory: the working directory was an empty folder.
- The hang is at the very first watcher, on the global config directory. The server logs `watcher subscribe path=~/.config/opencode type=directory` and nothing after it. It never logs `watcher started` or `location services booted`, and the TUI never draws. Both processes sit idle in futex/epoll waits indefinitely.

When one instance is free, startup works, and the later `fs.watch` calls fail fast with `EMFILE: too many open files, watch '/etc'` (logged as `failed to watch directory`) without blocking. So only the config-directory watcher blocks on exhaustion. That suggests the inotify backend of `@parcel/watcher` is waiting on a subscription that can never complete.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Exhaust inotify instances for the current user, e.g. temporarily `sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_instances=<current usage>`, or run a process that calls `inotify_init()` until it gets `EMFILE` and keeps the descriptors open.
2. In an empty directory (no `.git`), run `opencode --print-logs --log-level debug`.
3. Observe the blank screen. The last server log line is the `watcher subscribe` for `~/.config/opencode`.
4. Release one instance and run again: OpenCode starts normally.

Same result with `--standalone`.

### Expected behavior

Start without the file watcher (with a warning), or exit with a clear error that names the inotify limit, rather than hanging silently.

### How we hit it

On a headless Linux machine, a long-running process kept spawning `dbus-launch`. Each leftover `dbus-daemon --session` held an inotify instance until the default limit of 128 was reached. Any slow leak of inotify instances can trigger this, which makes the silent hang hard to diagnose.

### OpenCode version

2.3.0

### Operating System

Linux (x86_64, kernel 6.12), headless, `max_user_instances=128`

### Terminal

Any (also reproduced under `script(1)` with no terminal attached)

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Let built-in tools like shell and read be called from Code Mode execute
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Built-in tools (`shell`, `read`, `grep`, `glob`, `edit`, `write`, ...) are registered with `codemode: false`, so `tools.shell(...)` inside `execute` fails with `Unknown tool 'shell'`. #39312 was closed as expected behavior, but the docs do not say why.

This blocks the main use of `execute`: combining calls in one step. For example, run a CLI that saves a screenshot, then read the image, in one call:

```ts
await tools.shell({ command: 'ghosthand screenshot /tmp/s.png' })
return await tools.readMediaIntoContext({ path: '/tmp/s.png' })
```

Today this is two tool calls, because `shell` is not in the catalog.

**Proposal**

- Let built-in tools opt in to the Code Mode catalog, with a config flag or a per-tool setting.
- Nested calls keep their normal permission checks, as other Code Mode tools already do.
- If there is a reason for the current default, document it on the Tools page.

Related: #54826 (direct MCP servers in Code Mode), #55072 (images from `execute`).

issues.body:
## Summary

In the TUI, fenced code blocks tagged `cpp` (and filetypes mapped to `cpp`) lose most syntax highlighting: keywords, comments, strings, numbers and types stay at the default foreground, while a few captures (e.g. struct field identifiers) are colored. The bundled `cpp` tree-sitter query is nvim-treesitter's delta-only file (`; inherits: c`) and the tree-sitter client neither resolves `inherits` nor loads the parent `c` query, so everything defined in `c/highlights.scm` is missing.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: `TERM=xterm-256color` (Windows Terminal / pwsh; `TERM_PROGRAM` unset)
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe` (COMSPEC), working shell is PowerShell 7
- Install/channel: latest (npm `@opencode/cli`, release build, not local dev)
- Active plugins: local TUI plugin `./plugins/mu-highlight` (added as a workaround for this bug; the bug reproduces with this plugin disabled)

## Reproduction

1. Start the TUI and send a message containing a code block:

   ~~~md
   ```cpp
   // sum
   int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
   ```
   ~~~

2. Observe the rendered block: `// sum` is not colored, `int` and `return` are not colored, only some identifiers get a color.
3. Same result when opening a `.cpp` file in the TUI file view.

## Expected Behavior

Standard C/C++ highlighting: keywords (`int`, `return`, `struct`), comments, strings, numbers, operators and types all use the theme's syntax colors.

## Actual Behavior

Most tokens render in the default text color. In a struct, only field identifiers are highlighted, e.g. for

~~~cpp
struct Point {
    int x, y;
};
~~~

only `x` and `y` are colored. That matches the `(field_identifier) @property` rule in `cpp/highlights.scm`; every other capture lives in the inherited `c/highlights.scm`, which is never applied.

## Additional Context

Evidence collected on 2.3.0 / Windows:

- Cached query is delta-only: `~/.local/share/opentui/tree-sitter/queries/cpp-16b846db.scm` is 4904 bytes and starts with `; inherits: c`.
- The bundled parser config for `cpp` (visible in the binary, `filetype:"cpp"`) lists only
  `.../nvim-treesitter/.../queries/cpp/highlights.scm` and `.../cpp/locals.scm`; `c/highlights.scm` is not included, although `c` is a separate filetype with its own entry.
- The cache directory contains `bash`, `cpp` and `python` queries only — no `c` query is ever fetched.
- No `inherits` handling exists in `@opentui/core`'s tree-sitter client/worker, so the directive is treated as a comment.

Confirmed diagnosis with a workaround: a local TUI plugin that calls
`getTreeSitterClient().addFiletypeParser({ filetype: "mulan", wasm: ".../tree-sitter-cpp.wasm", queries: { highlights: [".../c/highlights.scm", ".../cpp/highlights.scm"] } })`
and maps the code block to that filetype produces full highlighting (keywords, comments, strings, types). So the grammar and the queries are fine; only query inheritance is missing.

Related observation, possibly a separate small bug: `RenderNodeContext.treeSitterClient` passed to `context.markdown.registerCodeBlockRenderer` callbacks is always `undefined` in 2.3.0, even though the type declares it and code blocks are highlighted (they fall back to the global singleton internally). A plugin therefore cannot register parsers through the documented context field and has to import `getTreeSitterClient` from `@opentui/core` instead.

Suggested fix: resolve `; inherits: <lang>` when loading highlight queries (load the parent query and concatenate it, recursively), or ship pre-merged queries per language.

### Description

# Bug: Browser skill guidance interrupts successful file reads with local Ollama model

## Environment

- OpenCode CLI: v2.3.0
- Platform: Windows 11 x64
- Client: OpenCode Desktop
- Provider: Ollama, local OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Model: Qwen3:8b (Q4_K_M)
- Active Ollama context: 8192 tokens
- Agent: Build
- Agent step limit: 5

## Description

When using the `read` tool to retrieve a simple text file, the tool successfully returns the correct file contents.

Immediately afterward, OpenCode inserts a system message announcing the availability of the `browser` skill (`core/skill-guidance`).

The model then treats this additional system message as the current task and responds about browser capabilities rather than returning the requested file contents.

This occurs even though the browser tool and browser skill are denied in the agent's permissions.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure OpenCode with Ollama and the local Qwen3:8b model.
2. Open a project containing `test.txt` with one line of text.
3. Use the Build agent and start a new session.
4. Ask: "Read test.txt and return its exact contents. Do not modify any files."
5. Inspect the exported session data after the response.

## Expected behavior

The assistant should return the contents of `test.txt` after the successful `read` call.

Any additional skill availability notifications should not override the user's original request. Denied skills should ideally not be advertised as available to the agent.

## Actual behavior

1. The `read` tool completes successfully.
2. The tool result contains the correct text and reports `truncated: false`.
3. A system message is inserted with `instructionSources: ["core/skill-guidance"]`.
4. The message announces the `browser` skill.
5. The model responds about browser availability and never returns the requested file contents.

## Relevant evidence from exported session

Tool call:

```json
{
  "name": "read",
  "state": {
    "status": "completed",
    "input": {
      "path": "test.txt"
    }
  }
}
```

Tool output:

```text
Read file test.txt, lines 1-1
1: Hello, I am AURA. This is my first independently created file.
```

The line above is translated and anonymized; the original file contains German text.

Subsequent instruction:

```text
Instructions updated: core/skill-guidance

New skills are available in addition to those previously listed:
browser
```

:

```text
The browser skill is now available!
I can use the in-app browser...
```

## Additional observations

- Standard file creation through the `write` tool works.
- Reading the same files directly through Windows PowerShell works.
- The issue persisted after increasing Ollama's context from 4096 to 8192 tokens.
- In other sessions, the model repeatedly invoked `read`, occasionally with identical `offset=1, limit=1` parameters.
- Setting the Build agent's step limit to 5 successfully prevented unbounded execution.
- The diagnostic session confirms that the tool result itself was correct.

## Possible cause

The dynamic `core/skill-guidance` system message may be taking precedence over the active user request after a tool response, especially for smaller local models.

The browser skill announcement also appears despite explicit browser-related denials.

These are hypotheses, not confirmed root causes.

## Suggested investigation

- Check whether skill availability notifications are filtered by effective agent permissions.
- Ensure newly injected skill guidance preserves the active task context.
- Consider whether a skill update should be injected immediately after unrelated successful file operations.
- Test with local Ollama models that support tool calling.

I can provide a sanitized session export containing the tool result and subsequent instruction message.

issues.title: Expose the resolved interpreter/shell on the pre-execution tool hook (V1 tool.execute.before, V2 execute.before)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/plugins
labels.description: Plugins, skills, custom agents

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Problem

The synchronous pre-execution tool hook cannot know which interpreter a shell command will actually run under. In V1, `tool.execute.before` receives `{ tool, sessionID, callID }` and args; in V2, `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", …)` receives `{ tool, sessionID, agent, messageID, id, input }` (verified against `@opencode/plugin`'s published types). Neither carries any shell-identifying field, so a policy hook that must analyze command text per-dialect (e.g. PowerShell vs POSIX shell) cannot attribute the correct dialect and must either guess or treat every command with one tokenizer.

Config cannot substitute for the event: the configured shell is subject to fallback, later mutation and per-call selection, and reading config at hook time proves the *configured* shell, not the *resolved* one. (Source findings: https://github.com/CtrlCarlitos/agent-guardrails/issues/501 — payload evidence for both majors and the config-fallback analysis.)

### Requested API

Add host-owned, read-only **resolved interpreter metadata** to the pre-execution hook event (V1 input and V2 event, as supported): at minimum the resolved executable and a dialect hint (PowerShell/POSIX/cmd or unknown), plus the session and call IDs for correlation. Bind it to the **actual spawn** — after config fallback and per-call selection have resolved. If a later lifecycle event can change the command or interpreter after the hook has answered, invalidate the prior verdict and re-evaluate rather than letting a stale answer govern a different execution.

The mutable V2 shell lifecycle event alone does not provide this contract: observing a shell change asynchronously is not the same as the synchronous, veto-capable pre-execution answer carrying the resolved interpreter.

### Suggested acceptance tests

1. A PowerShell-configured session's `execute.before` event reports the PowerShell dialect; a POSIX session reports POSIX — verified through actual runtime dispatch, not schema fixtures alone.
2. Config fallback (missing/invalid shell entry) and per-call override paths report the *resolved* interpreter, not the config value.
3. A config reload or shell change mid-session is reflected in the next event, and any already-rendered verdict for a pending call is invalidated and re-evaluated.
4. A field of the same name inside the tool input (model-controlled) cannot override the host-owned metadata.
5. `cmd.exe`/unknown interpreters are represented explicitly rather than collapsed into a default dialect.

### Downstream context

Guardrail (CtrlCarlitos/agent-guardrails) uses this to route shell command text through the correct dialect's ruleset; today both opencode majors are documented as "proven shell unavailable" and adapters stay conservative (unknown-dialect commands keep the POSIX reading): https://github.com/CtrlCarlitos/agent-guardrails/issues/501

prs.title: feat(core): turn experimental schedules into automations
prs.body:
**Experimental schedules become automations: a trigger plus an action, which can be a prompt or a Code Mode program that runs with no model.**
Still experimental and behind a flag (on in local and dev builds, off in releases). Nothing outside this feature changes.

💡 **Why**
Schedules could only prompt the Session that created them, gated by `if` / `until` checks and stopped by `ends`. That covered "remind me" but not "watch something and act without spending a model call", and it tied every schedule to one Session. This is the first of two PRs; event triggers come next.

🆕 **Now you can**
- Prompt the creating Session, another Session in the same project, or a fresh Session started with an agent on every run.
- Run a Code Mode program on a timer with no model: it calls the tools it was approved for, keeps `state` between runs, and stops itself with `done: true`.
- Create one without a Session over HTTP (it runs in the given directory) and keep it after the creating Session is deleted. Automations belong to the project.

🚦 **How it ships:** flag `experimental.automations`. The old `experimental.schedules` key and `OPENCODE_FLAGS=schedules` still turn it on when the new key is unset, so existing configs keep working.

```diff
- schedule { when: in|at|every|cron, if?/until?: shell|code check, ends?: {after,at,times}, action: {prompt} into its Session }
+ automation { name, trigger: at|every|cron, action: prompt {to: {session}|{new: agent}} | code {code, args?}, expires? }
- code check returns boolean | { wake, state?, message? }, then a prompt fires
+ code action gets input { state, now, runs, args }, returns nothing | { state?, done? }; it is the action
```

**Decisions**
- `if` / `until` / `ends` are gone. A code action that returns early replaces a condition, `done: true` replaces `until`, and `expires` replaces `ends.after` / `ends.at`. `ends.times` has no replacement; a program can count `runs`.
- Shell conditions are dropped. A code action covers what they did, with tool permissions asked once at creation, and keeping a second runtime and permission path for a background shell was not worth it in this PR.
- `at` accepts `"in 10 minutes"` and stores the resulting instant, so the separate `in` trigger is gone.
- A code action runs with the agent and permissions of the Session that created it, so it needs one. If that Session is deleted the automation pauses with a reason. Prompt actions don't need one.
- It runs in the creating Session's folder, else the folder given over HTTP, else the home folder. A missing folder, a deleted target Session, a target Session moved to another project, or an agent that is gone pauses it and says why in `lastOutput`.
- `to: { new }` takes only an agent that can start a Session (not hidden, not subagent-only), checked after plugins load. Each run's Session id comes from the automation and run number, so a retry after a crash adopts the Session it already started instead of leaking another.
- After downtime, a missed slot runs once, late, never several times (unchanged from schedules), unless the automation has expired by then: a slot that only comes up after `expires` (downtime, a retry, or resuming a past-due `at`) doesn't run and the automation ends with outcome `expired`.
- A run's result is written only if no other process has recorded a run since it started, and the next slot is counted from when the run finished, so a slow run can't trigger a burst.
- Code actions keep the shipped limits (30s, 20 tool calls, 32 KB, no `fetch`). They may now call tools that edit files, since they act rather than check; the automation, Session-move and worktree tools stay off-limits. A failed run keeps the previous state, retries a minute later, and pauses after 3 failures; a program that cannot succeed (parse error, unknown tool, bad return shape) pauses at once. Loading `tools` with `import` or `require` is rejected, so every tool call is visible to the creation-time check.
- Permissions for code actions: creation asks for each tool, plus `execute` unless a tool already asked. A rule scoped to some resources (`{ "*": "allow", "vault:*": "ask" }`) asks too, not only the catch-all. At run time the unattended grant stands in for the catch-all only, so a scoped `ask` or `deny` still applies and that call fails. The shipped schedule checks had the same gap; this matters more now that code actions can edit files.
- `GET /api/experimental/automation` shows only automations whose folder has the flag on, rejects a relative `directory`, and looks up its project without recording one.
- Tools, `/automation` and the HTTP routes (`/api/experimental/automation`, `client.experimental.automation.*`) replace the schedule ones without aliases, per the experimental API rules.

**Storage:** a migration creates the `automation` table, copies over live schedules that mean the same thing as automations (a prompt into their Session, no check, no run limit), and drops `schedule`. Schedules with a check or a run limit, and finished ones, are not copied: without their condition or limit they would run differently.

**Next PR:** MCP event triggers.

↩️ **Undo:** revert isn't enough, because the migration drops the `schedule` table. A revert needs a migration that recreates it; the copied automations would be lost.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/automation.ts`, the two run paths (`runPrompt`, `runCode`) and `settle`: which writes need the automation still active, and which land even after a pause so a run is never counted twice. Then `authorize` and `run` in `packages/core/src/automation/code.ts` for how scoped rules survive the unattended grant. Also the migration's copy query. The rest is a rename plus regenerated SDK.

<sub>Follows a design discussion about turning schedules into automations · no user reports</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `packages/core`: `bun test test/automation.test.ts test/tool-automation.test.ts test/flag.test.ts test/database-migration.test.ts`: 72 pass, 0 fail; `test/config/normalization.test.ts`: 47 pass
- `packages/server`: `bun test test/automation.test.ts`: 3 pass, 0 fail
- `packages/protocol`: `bun test test/experimental-identifiers.test.ts`: 1 pass
- `packages/client`: `bun test test/promise.test.ts`: 41 pass
- `packages/codemode`: `bun test test/scan.test.ts`: 5 pass
- The new permission, expiry, run-count, agent and Session-id tests fail on the previous commit
- `packages/core`: `bun run migration --check`: no ungenerated migrations
- `bun typecheck` in schema, core, protocol, server, client, codemode, sdk: no errors
- `bunx oxlint` on changed files, `bun script/sdk-docs.ts`: 0 problems
- Not run: the full `bun run check` from the root

</details>

### Issue for this PR

Related to #40689 (mention skills in the middle of a prompt).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

Skills could only be mentioned with `@`. This lets a user type `/` anywhere in the prompt (after whitespace) to pick a skill, so several skills can be used in one prompt, for example `review this design with /arch-review and check it with /code-gen`.

Picking a skill replaces the typed `/token` with an `@skill` mention. It goes through the existing `insertPart` skill path, the same as an `@skill` mention or the `/skills` dialog, so it is stored in `PromptInfo.skills` and resolved on submit like those.

Changes, all in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx`:

- `onInput` opens the popup for a whitespace-preceded `/` token past the start of the prompt. A bare `/` does not open it.
- Past the start of the prompt the popup lists skills only. No commands are offered there, because a command only runs when the prompt starts with `/`.
- Skills match by prefix and a skill already in the prompt is not offered again. The popup closes when nothing matches, so Enter still sends a sentence like `tell me about /c`.
- `show("command", slash)` now sets the index in one step. Setting it in two steps let the new auto-close effect fire on an intermediate state.

Behavior at the start of the prompt is unchanged.

### Issue for this PR

Reported in Slack: the count in the beta GUI's "Used 3 Execute" tool-group header looks slightly cut off at the top.

> **Unverified for the reported case.** In headless Linux Chromium at the header's actual size (13px Inter, 16px line height), the mask doesn't touch the digit, so this change makes no pixel difference there. Only 12/14/16px change, by one antialiased row. The reporter is on the beta desktop app, which may position text at fractional pixels where this setup can't. Hold until someone confirms that disabling `mask-image` on the digit in DevTools sharpens the count.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`AnimatedNumber` puts a top/bottom `mask-image` fade (18% each end) on every digit box so rolling digits fade in and out. The mask sat on the box all the time, though, so a still digit also got it. With `line-height: 1em` the cap top of a digit lands about 0.14em below the box top, inside the fade, so the top stroke always rendered partly transparent. The number wasn't clipped, just dimmed.

This moves the mask under `[data-animating="true"]`. Rolls keep their soft edges, and a still number renders at full opacity. Layout, overflow clipping and reduced motion are unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Rendered the component's CSS before and after with Inter at 12, 13, 14 and 16px, counts 3, 18 and 407, on the dark timeline background, using headless Chromium at 1x and 2x.

- `prettier --check` passes. `lint:changed` only covers TS files, so it has nothing to check for this CSS-only change.
- I didn't run the Playwright component tests. No test asserts on the mask.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

N/A

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds experimental support for [MCP Skills](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills/blob/main/specification/beta/skills.mdx), a beta MCP extension that lets a server publish skills. Guarded by the `mcp_skills` flag.

- **Discovery:** when a connected server offers the extension, OpenCode lists its skills with the SDK's `SkillsClient` and shows each one as `<server>:<name>`, for example `team:deploy`. Listing reads no files, as the spec requires.
- **Loading:** the existing `skill` tool fetches only that skill's `SKILL.md`, after the permission check, and the SDK verifies its size, SHA-256 and frontmatter.
- **Supporting files:** the existing `read` tool on `skill://team:deploy/...` fetches and verifies only the requested file. Listing a directory uses the skill's manifest and fetches nothing.
- **`Skill.Service`:** keeps `list`, `get` and `files`. `add` also takes content as an Effect that runs on load; `{ content: false }` returns summaries without loading anything; `files(id)` returns paths and `files(id, path)` reads one file.

prs.title: feat(desktop): offer the OpenCode 2 upgrade
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. OpenCode 1 desktop has no path to OpenCode 2 today; the TUI got one in #54409.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

OpenCode 1 desktop now offers OpenCode 2.0, the desktop counterpart of `/update` in the TUI.

- OpenCode 2 downloads in the background once OpenCode 1 is on its newest release, the way a 1.x update already downloads. A newer 1.x release still comes first.
- Nothing installs until the user chooses: **Restart to upgrade**, **Upgrade on quit**, or **Later** (hidden for 7 days, like Dismiss in the TUI).
- The card names what OpenCode 2 adds, what it keeps, and the one thing that breaks: plugins made for OpenCode 1.
- The card opens by itself once per launch, and only right after the app starts. After that it is one click away on the titlebar update pill, in Check for updates, and in the command palette.
- A failed download stays quiet and is retried at the next 10 minute check.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> unavailable
  unavailable --> downloading: OpenCode 1 is up to date
  downloading --> ready: OpenCode 2 downloaded
  downloading --> unavailable: download failed
  ready --> unavailable: newer 1.x release found
  ready --> scheduled: Upgrade on quit
  ready --> [*]: Restart to upgrade
  scheduled --> [*]: app quits
```

OpenCode 2 desktop keeps the app ID, so its installer replaces OpenCode 1 in place. OpenCode 1 reads GitHub releases and OpenCode 2 publishes to its own feed, so the offer uses a second updater. The OpenCode 1 updater never sees the OpenCode 2 feed:

```ts
// packages/desktop/src/main/updater.ts
const MAJOR_FEED = "https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/"

function majorUpdater() {
  // autoUpdater is already the right updater for this platform and package type.
  const Updater = autoUpdater.constructor as new (options: { provider: "generic"; url: string }) => AppUpdater
  const updater = new Updater({ provider: "generic", url: MAJOR_FEED })
  updater.autoDownload = false
  updater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = false
  return updater
}
```

Upgrade on quit arms `electron-updater` after the fact. It only registers its quit handler when a download finishes, so the cached installer is "downloaded" again, which returns at once:

```ts
installOnQuit: () => {
  updater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = true
  return updater.downloadUpdate()
},
```

### How did you verify your code works?

- Packaged this branch as an unsigned 1.19.5 Windows build and ran it in Windows Sandbox against the live feeds. Restart to upgrade closed OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2.3.0 was running 16 seconds later, with the old app's stores imported.
- Not verified end to end: Upgrade on quit, macOS, and Linux. macOS needs a signed build, because Squirrel only installs over an app with the same signature.
- The card strings are translated for all 61 locales by agents and matched to each locale's existing terms. No native speaker has reviewed them.

prs.title: fix(tui): draw the prompt panel bottom edge with glyphs CJK console fonts have
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55634

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The half-height strip under the prompt panel is drawn with `▀` U+2580 plus a `╹` U+2579 cap on its left edge. Both characters are missing from CJK console fonts (their coverage follows GB2312 / Big5 / Shift-JIS), and the legacy Windows console host paints a missing glyph as a hollow box in the cell's foreground colour — so in `cmd.exe` the strip renders as a row of thin bars. Windows Terminal is unaffected because it does its own font fallback.

This PR draws the same strip with `▄` U+2584 and swapped colours. `▀` paints the top half of the cell with the foreground colour, `▄` paints the bottom half, so setting the cell background to the panel colour and the glyph foreground to the page colour renders exactly the same pixels. `▄` exists in GB2312 (and in CP437, Consolas and Cascadia, so nothing changes in other terminals). The `╹` cap is dropped because no CJK charset has a half-height vertical; that also removes the `promptBg().a === 0` special case, since a transparent panel background now paints nothing by construction.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Captured the row from the console screen buffer: before `▀`×74 (fg 11;37;58 / bg 1;22;39), after `▄`×74 (fg 1;22;39 / bg 11;37;58) — the pixels are identical (top half panel colour, bottom half page colour), so terminals that already rendered this correctly are visually unchanged.
- Pixel analysis of `conhost` screenshots: the strip keeps the same start column and width, aligned with the panel background above it; the bars are gone.
- Glyph coverage check on the default Chinese Windows console font 新宋体 (NSimSun) via GDI `GetGlyphIndicesW`: U+2580 and U+2579 missing, U+2584 present.
- `tsgo -b` in `packages/tui` passes.

prs.title: fix(latex): support the LaTeX control space in math
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55346

Resubmission of #55359, closed by the automated PR cleanup while it waited for review.

The two commits are @shreyanshj10's and unchanged: same SHAs (`7cd5fb2882`, `35056bfa44`), original author and committer, original dates. Nothing was rebased or edited. This branch only re-hosts them because a PR closed by the cleanup bot can only be reopened from the original fork, which I have no way to reach.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A math fence containing `\ ` (backslash-space, the LaTeX control space) printed its raw source instead of rendering.

`spacingCommands` in `packages/latex/src/symbols.ts` covers `\,`, `\:`, `\;`, `\!`, `\quad`, `\qquad`, `\enspace` and `\thinspace`, but not `\ `. `readCommand` returns whatever character follows the backslash unchanged when it is not a letter, so `\ ` reaches `parseCommand` as `" "`, finds no entry in the table, and strict mode throws `Unsupported command \ `. `markdown.ts` treats any `LatexParseError` as "keep the source", so the whole block falls back to unrendered code.

This adds the missing entry with width 1, which is what `\;` and `\enspace` already use for a space. A backslash before a tab, a carriage return or a newline reaches the same table as `"\t"`, `"\r"` and `"\n"`; KaTeX collapses a backslash followed by any of space, tab, CR or LF into the same control-space token (`controlSpaceRegexString` in its `Lexer`), so all four are added and a CRLF source is treated like a plain one. Both the structural parse and the `\text{...}` fallback read that one table, so there was nothing else to change.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/latex/src/parser.test.ts` gains two cases: `a\ b` in strict mode must parse to a space node between the two symbols, and the formula from the issue must not throw; the second case covers a backslash before a newline, a tab and a CRLF.

This branch merges into `dev` (`367d24b70`) without conflicts. On that merged tree, `bun test` in `packages/latex` is green (125 tests across 6 files) and `bun run typecheck:tsc` is clean. With the `symbols.ts` hunk reverted the first new test fails with `Unsupported command \ `.

### Screenshots / recordings

No rendering code changed, so I did not record the TUI. The visible difference is that a block which used to fall back to raw LaTeX now renders; the before state is in the issue.

prs.title: fix(core): let retry hooks handle content-filter finishes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60822

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A step that ends with `finish: "content-filter"` sets `providerFailed`, so `step.ts` never builds `llmError` and the `session.retry` hook is skipped. The same refusal sent back as an HTTP `ContentPolicy` error does reach the hook, which is why a fallback plugin can recover one but not the other, and why a refused subagent job ends as `error`. In v1 both cases ended up on the same path (`prompt.ts` turned a content-filter finish into `ContentFilterError` and published `Session.Event.Error`, like any API error), so plugins could treat them the same way.

This isn't tied to one provider. `content-filter` is the normalized finish the protocols already produce for Anthropic `refusal`, OpenAI Chat and Responses `content_filter`, Gemini safety blocks, Bedrock guardrails and Mistral, so all of them go through the same branch. The change wraps that finish in a `ContentPolicyError` and sends it through the retry decision like other provider failures. The hook receives the same `provider.content-filter` error that `step.failed` carries today. `ContentPolicy` isn't retryable, so the proposal stays `retry: false` and nothing changes without a hook. If a hook switches the model and returns `retry: true`, the runner reuses the existing `Retry` outcome when no output was produced, or `Continue` when part of the answer was already streamed, the same way it handles a mid-stream rate limit. It's 10 lines in `step.ts`.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added two tests in `session-runner.test.ts`, modeled on "retries an unknown finish before output" and "continues after a mid-stream rate limit": a hook turns a content-filter finish into a retry before output and into a continuation after partial output. Both fail without the change. The existing content-filter tests pass unchanged, `bun test test/session-runner.test.ts` is green and `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core` is clean.

I also ran it on v2.2.4 with the patch cherry-picked and a local OpenAI-compatible stub returning `finish_reason: "content_filter"`, using oh-my-opencode-slim's retry hook. A root session and a background subagent both switched model and finished on the fallback, and the parent got `state="completed"` instead of `state="error"`. With no fallback configured the step still fails as before.

### Issue for this PR

Fixes #64100

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

In a collapsed shell tool row, the status badge (Exit 1 / Failed / Timed out) folded onto two lines inside its fixed 16px height, so the second line was clipped and a border segment went missing — and a long command ran into the badge with no ellipsis.
