prs.title: feat(ai): scope HTTP middleware to any call, for every modality
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None. This is the `@opencode/ai` half of making plugin HTTP hooks run for image, video and other non-chat model calls. Core wiring comes in a follow-up.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Only chat calls could take HTTP middleware for a single call. Image, video, decisions, embeddings, speech and transcription couldn't, and neither could polling or downloads. Core needs one per call (per session) so plugin hooks like Azure's Entra ID token reach those calls too. This adds one way to do that for every modality, instead of an option on each method.

```ts
// before: chat only
ai.stream(req, { http })
ai.video.status(model, id)        // no way to hook it

// after: every provider request made inside the scope
yield* Effect.gen(function* () {
  const job = yield* ai.video.start(req)
  return yield* ai.video.result(model, job.id)
}).pipe(RequestExecutor.withMiddleware(http))      // Effect or Stream

await ai.video.start(req, { http })                // Promise: on every call's options
```

How it works:

- `RequestExecutor.CurrentMiddleware` holds the scoped middleware, the same way `CurrentTls` holds the client certificate. `withMiddleware` sets it, wrapping any outer one.
- The executor reads it and sends the request through it. Executor-wide middleware (`RequestExecutor.middleware`) still runs outside it, and per-call middleware (chat's `{ http }`) runs inside it. The executor clears it while the request runs, so a request a hook makes itself, such as a token refresh, isn't wrapped again.
- Promise `RunOptions` gains `http`. `run` and `iterate` apply it, so every Promise method gets it. A transcription handle keeps the `http` of the call that returned it. Chat calls pass `http` once, not twice.

Downloads are the exception. A result URL is often a CDN or presigned storage link, and an auth hook that adds `Authorization` there would leak the token (and S3 rejects two auth methods). So a `url` asset never uses the caller's scope. It downloads with its own `middleware`, which a route sets only for result URLs on the provider's origin, the same rule the route already uses for download headers. That also makes a result downloaded later, outside the scope, still go through the hook.

```text
submit / poll / result / cancel     → caller's middleware
download from the provider's origin → the middleware captured when the result was read
download from any other host        → none
```

`MediaProtocol.PollContext.headers(url)` becomes `credentials(url)`, which returns `{ headers, middleware }` to spread into `Media.url`. OpenRouter video is the only protocol using it.

Guardrails so the APIs don't drift apart:

- `test/http-hooks.test.ts` calls every Promise method with `{ http }` and fails if any request reaches the network without passing the hook. It also lists every method of the client, so a new method fails until it's added there as a provider call or a local helper. Since the Promise client runs the Effect API, this covers both.
- Only the executor can send HTTP. Types already enforce it for Effect code: every route gets the executor's `execute` and returns `Effect<…, AIError>` with no requirements, so reaching for `HttpClient` doesn't compile. Lint covers the rest: in `packages/ai/src`, `.oxlintrc.json` rejects `fetch` and importing `HttpClient`/`FetchHttpClient` outside `route/executor.ts`. (`globalThis.fetch` isn't caught; oxlint has no rule for restricted properties.)
- `test/promise-parity.types.ts` now allows exactly the `RunOptions` keys (`signal`, `http`) as the Promise/Effect difference.
- `AGENTS.md` says there is one way to hook HTTP: no per-method options, nothing that bypasses the executor.

A custom `RequestExecutor.Service` that doesn't build on `RequestExecutor.layer` won't apply scoped middleware. The only ones in the repo are test stubs that fail every request.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/executor.test.ts`: order is executor-wide, then outer scope, inner scope, per-call; nothing scoped runs outside the scope; it applies to a `Stream` and to a request sent through a per-request `fetch`; a request made inside a hook isn't wrapped again.
- `test/openrouter-video.test.ts`: a result on OpenRouter's host downloads through the hook after the scope ended; a result on another host doesn't, even inside the scope. Removing the download change makes this test fail.
- `test/http-hooks.test.ts`: 22 provider methods all go through `{ http }`. Removing `http` from `run` fails 12 of them.
- oxlint flags a probe file calling `fetch` or importing `HttpClient` in `packages/ai/src`.
- `bun test` in `packages/ai` (2217 pass), `bun typecheck` there, and `bun run check` at the root.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### Issue for this PR

Closes #63981

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

OpenCode currently picks between `patch` and `edit`/`write` with a hardcoded model-ID heuristic, and there is no supported way to change that choice or the amount of patch output returned to the model.

This adds `experimental.editing` config with:

- `add` and `remove` deltas over the existing model heuristic, limited to `patch`, `edit`, and `write`
- per-model `rules` matched against `${providerID}/${model.id}`, with the last matching rule winning
- `result_style`: `summary`, `counts`, or `diff`, defaulting to `summary`
- decode-time validation for invalid regular expressions, unknown tools, and overlapping `add`/`remove`

The existing heuristic remains the base. A matching rule replaces the top-level delta rather than merging with it. Other tools are untouched. Without config, the patch result is unchanged. `counts` adds `+N -M`; `diff` adds the applied diff without file headers and caps very large output.

Example:

```jsonc
{
  "experimental": {
    "editing": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "match": "deepseek.*(?:v4|flash-latest|pro-latest)",
          "add": ["patch"],
          "remove": ["edit", "write"],
          "result_style": "diff"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Docs are updated in `config.mdx` and `tools.mdx`.

- `cd packages/core && bun test test/tool-patch.test.ts`: 52 pass, 0 fail

prs.title: fix(server): answer handler defects with a readable 500 instead of an empty one
prs.body:
Requests that crash in a handler used to get a `500` with an empty body. Now that same 500 carries a JSON body: what went wrong with storage when that is the problem, otherwise a ref to find the crash in the server log. Messages never name the database engine.

```text
POST /api/session/:id/prompt   (disk full)
  before: 500  ""
  after:  500  { "_tag": "UnknownError", "message": "Storage is full", "ref": "err_1a2b3c4d" }

any other crash
  before: 500  ""
  after:  500  { "_tag": "UnknownError", "message": "Server failed to handle the request. Check server logs for details.", "ref": "err_1a2b3c4d" }
```

### How it works

```text
handler fails
  defectResponseLayer (global router middleware)
    HttpServerError.causeResponse(cause)    ← what Effect would answer
    not an empty 500?  → unchanged (declared errors, 404, aborts, defects with their own response)
    empty 500?
      log the cause with a ref
      message = StorageFailure.message(cause) ?? generic text
      fail with [original cause + UnknownError response]
        → Effect sends the response
        → the request span and the response log still record the original defect
```

```text
StorageFailure.message(cause)                       core/src/database (the only layer that knows SQLite)
  find the SqlError: a failed transaction, or a drizzle query error holding one
  resultCode(sqlError.reason.cause)                 ← each #sqlite module reads its own error type
    bun:      cause instanceof SQLiteError → errno
    node:     one Schema decode → errcode
    workerd:  undefined (no codes)
  primary code →
    FULL               "Storage is full"
    READONLY           "Storage is read-only"
    BUSY, LOCKED       "Storage is in use by another process"
    IOERR              "Storage couldn't be read or written"
    CORRUPT, NOTADB    "Storage is damaged"
    CANTOPEN           "Storage couldn't be opened"
    anything else      undefined → generic message (a buggy query never sends SQL or data)
```

### A rollback no longer hides the storage failure

```text
transaction write hits SQLITE_FULL → SQLite rolls the transaction back itself
  before: our ROLLBACK then fails ("no transaction is active") and replaces the error → generic message
  after:  body failed with FULL / IOERR / BUSY / NOMEM / INTERRUPT (the codes SQLite documents as auto-rollback)?
          → that failed ROLLBACK is expected, report the body's error → "Storage is full"
          any other rollback failure still fails
```

### Changes

```diff
 packages/server/src/
   routes.ts
+    Layer.merge(defectResponseLayer)
   middleware/
+    defect-response.ts           # empty 500 → UnknownError, encoded with its schema
 packages/core/src/database/
+  storage-failure.ts             # typed SqlError → storage message, engine never named; rolledBack(cause)
   drizzle/effect-sqlite/session.ts
+    skip the expected failed rollback after an auto-rollback
   sqlite.bun.ts / sqlite.node.ts / sqlite.workerd.ts
+    resultCode(cause)            # the driver's own error type, read once
```

### What doesn't change

- Status codes and endpoint contracts.
- Traces: the request span still ends as a failure with the original defect, and the response logger still logs it.
- Anything that wasn't an empty 500.

New: one error-level log line per crash, carrying the ref the client sees.

### Limit

Only some endpoints declare 500 (`UnknownError`), and the generated client only reads the body on those. `session.prompt` doesn't, so the client still reports `UnexpectedStatus: 500` there. Showing the reason in the TUI on a failed send is a follow-up.

### Tests

- `server/test/defect-response.test.ts`: a prompt on a real full disk (`PRAGMA max_page_count`) returns the storage reason, another crash returns the generic message with a ref, and an unknown route still returns 404. Both behavior tests fail without the middleware.
- `core/test/storage-failure.test.ts`: a transaction SQLite rolled back itself still reports "Storage is full" and leaves the connection usable (fails without the session fix); real bun errors, including full disk through a statement and a query, an extended code, and non-storage cases (constraint, bad statement, plain defect, interrupt). The node shape is checked under real Node in `sqlite-node.test.ts`.
- Server suite 129 pass (isolated HOME), core database tests pass, and `bun typecheck` in core and server and `bun run check` pass.

prs.title: feat(server): async video generation API with disk-backed media
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None. This is the HTTP half of the media plan; the agent tool PR (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63666) can rebase onto it.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Clients can now generate a video over HTTP without holding a request open for minutes. I submit the job, return an ID, and the server polls the provider and stores the video on disk. The video is served by hash from the existing media route, which now handles Range requests. It's all behind the `video_generate` flag.

```text
POST /api/experimental/generate/video   { model, prompt, start?, end?, references?, duration?, aspect?, resolution?, sound?, expiresAfter? }
→ { data: { id: "gen_…", status: "running" } }

GET /api/experimental/generate/video/gen_…
→ { data: { id, status: "running" } }
→ { data: { id, status: "completed", media: ["media:<sha256>"], expiresAt } }
→ { data: { id, status: "error", error, reason: "failed" | "cancelled" | "expired" | "unknown" } }

GET /api/experimental/media/<sha256>    (Range: bytes=0-1023 → 206)
```

**How a job runs**

```text
POST
  insert generation row as "submitting"        ← before the paid call
  provider.start → save provider job ID, status "running", reply
  poll status every 5s (2h deadline, then error/unknown)
    completed → stream result into blobs/<gen id>.part, hashing as it goes
                fsync, rename to blobs/<aa>/<hash> (or drop the .part if that file is already there)
                in one transaction: insert blob row (data = X'', bytes, mime, expires_at), mark completed
    error     → delete .part, mark error with the provider's reason
restart
  "submitting" with no provider ID → error/unknown, never resubmitted
  "running"                        → wait for plugins (providers), then keep polling by provider job ID
```

The submit runs in a server-owned fiber, so a client that disconnects mid-request can't cut off a paid call. A download that fails is retried twice, then the job is marked `error`. Videos are never held in memory: `Generate.video.result` now returns a stream instead of bytes.

**Blob storage**

The `blob` table only gets `expires_at`, through a plain `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`. Nothing is rebuilt, so `blob_ref` can't be wiped by the `ON DELETE CASCADE` (that matters on Durable Objects, where foreign keys are always on). A video row has an empty `data` and `bytes > 0`. One private check in `session/blob.ts` (`onDisk`) owns that, and every reader goes through it:

| Reader | File-backed blob |
| --- | --- |
| media route | streams the file, with Range |
| history / `hydrate` (what the model and export see) | not loaded; reads as the existing `[media unavailable: …]` |
| `keepRefs` (clients that fetch media themselves) | keeps the `media:` ref, as for any blob |
| `media:` ref in a prompt | rejected with an attachment error for now |

Retention:

```diff
- readable while a blob_ref exists
+ readable while a blob_ref exists OR expires_at > now
- save: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
+ save: ON CONFLICT keep the later expires_at
- release: delete the blob once no ref is left
+ release: delete it once no ref is left and it has expired; file-backed rows are left to the sweep
```

The sweep runs at startup and hourly. It deletes the row with a statement that rechecks "no ref and expired", then unlinks the file. It holds a per-hash lock that the generation commit also takes. If the unlink fails (say a file is open on Windows), the hash is retried on the next sweep.

**Media route**

The URL, `media:<sha256>` refs and the `"<hash>"` ETag don't change, because shipped iOS sends `If-None-Match: "<hash>"`. 304 is answered before any bytes are read. New: single Range with 206/416, `Accept-Ranges`, and strong-only `If-Range`. The Range parser now lives in `server/src/range.ts` and `fs.ts` uses it too, but `fs.ts` keeps its own ETag. `video/*`, `audio/*` and `application/pdf` get their real Content-Type. Everything else is still `application/octet-stream`, with the same `attachment`, nosniff and sandbox CSP as before. A file-backed row whose file is missing or the wrong size is a 404, logged as an error, and the row stays.

**Choices worth checking**

- Retention is per request: `expiresAfter` in milliseconds like `expiresAt`, 24 h by default, up to 30 days. There's no config key.
- Flag off returns 403 on both routes, the same as artifacts. Generated video storage doesn't depend on `media_blob`.
- A submit error without an HTTP status (timeout, connection reset) is recorded as `unknown`, not `failed`, since the provider may have taken it.
- A completed job past its `expiresAt` reads as `error` / `expired`.
- On workerd, `Generation` is replaced with a layer that answers "not supported in this runtime".
- The plugin context's `experimental.generate` leaves out `video`, so plugins don't get it yet.
- I copied the core `Generate.video` (start/status/result), `resolveVideo` and the `video` model type from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63666. `result` now streams and `cancel` is gone, since nothing calls it. The flag key is the same.
- The SDK generator used to add a deprecated old-path alias for every endpoint in a group that moved under `client.experimental`, so new endpoints got aliases for paths that never existed. It now takes the frozen list of paths that actually shipped (`deprecatedClientPaths` in `protocol/src/client.ts`), so the video endpoints get none and `GenerateApi` stays.

**Limitations and follow-ups**

- The agent tools, and the job recovery they need.
- An async image route on the same `generation` table (`kind = "image"`).
- R2 / Cloudflare storage for videos.
- `path` copies of a `media:` ref.
- How a video reaches the model, export and import. Today history and export don't load file-backed bytes, so a session can't use a generated video yet. The one way to hit this now: attach a video whose bytes exactly match a generated one (with `media_blob` on), which reads as unavailable.
- Accepting a file-backed `media:` ref as a prompt attachment.
- Filling in `width`/`height` for images.
- `blobs/` is shared by every database in a data dir, and the sweep only unlinks files for rows it deleted itself. A second database holding the same hash could lose its file. Stray files from crashes aren't swept.
- Old `generation` rows are never cleaned up.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core`: `test/generation.test.ts` uses a fake provider and TestClock. It covers submitting → running → completed, with the file under `blobs/`, the blob row and no `.part` left. It covers a restart (a `submitting` row becomes error/unknown with zero submits, and a `running` row resumes), a failing download (`.part` deleted, error), the provider's own reason, the deadline, and a rejected submit.
- `packages/core`: `test/blob-store.test.ts` covers the sweep (expired and unreferenced rows are deleted with their files; referenced, unexpired and inline session rows are kept), release vs. expiry, the expiry max on re-save, history not loading file bytes, and reuse of an intact copy.
- `packages/core`: `test/database-migration.test.ts` applies the migration with foreign keys on and checks that the `blob` and `blob_ref` rows are untouched.
- `packages/server`: `test/video-generate.test.ts` runs POST → GET completed, then on the media route: 200 with `video/mp4`, 206 slices including a suffix range, 416, a mismatched `If-Range` getting 200, 304 on `"<hash>"`, a 404 once the file is deleted, and an unknown ID. With the flag off, both routes return 403.
- Existing `media.test.ts`, `fs.test.ts` and `generate.test.ts` pass, along with the full core suite.
- `bun typecheck` in schema, protocol, core, server and plugin, and `bun run check` at the root.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---

Public API: adds experimental POST/GET /api/experimental/generate/video (client.experimental.generate.video.*), Generate.ImageFile, the video_generate flag, Model.Type "video" and Range support on the media route (backwards compatible)

prs.title: fix(mcp): propagate tool-call trace context
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #46856 — partial implementation. Baggage remains deferred.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Propagate the executing caller's `traceparent` and optional `tracestate` on MCP `tools/call`, in `_meta` and the SDK's existing request-local HTTP headers. This lets instrumented MCP servers join the tool execution's trace, including over stdio.

Read context when each call runs, not when its shared connection is created. Preserve configured/auth headers, session/progress metadata, cancellation and stale-definition retries. No dependencies, global instrumentation, propagators or configuration are added. Non-tool client code is unchanged from the pinned upstream base; baggage, catalogs, prompts, resources and Events tracing are outside this PR.

Omit absent, invalid, disabled and propagation-suppressed context, including ordinary built-in spans under Effect's default non-exporting tracer. Genuine OTel parents, direct external parents (sampled or unsampled) and explicitly active custom backends are supported. A NativeSpan carried into the default backend, or a new default-native child of an external parent, is omitted; historical span provenance is not inferred.

Flag: none; this propagates existing traced tool executions rather than enabling instrumentation by default.

prs.title: fix(service): retry Windows pipe spawn on packaged access denied
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #63892

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, a shell command that uses Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 stops before it can run. Process creation fails with OS error -1073283067 (0xC0070005), so the caller gets no command output, in a project directory and in a temporary directory. The same commands still run under Windows PowerShell 5.1. Pipe-mode creation passes PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST to CreateProcessW and retries without a job when that attribute is refused. The retry matches only Win32 error 5. A packaged executable reports the same refusal as 0xC0070005, so the original spawn failure is returned unchanged.

### Type of change

### Issue for this PR

Related: #56386, #56389

#56389 covers the same source change for `run` and `mini`. This PR adds automated regression tests and also fixes the full TUI's location fallback: when `file.list` fails, the TUI used to fall back to the server's active location, which can be an unrelated directory (for example, a stale shared service).

prs.title: fix(core): surface missing session directory as a typed, actionable error (no more silent failure)
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55859

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

When a session's project folder is missing on disk (moved, deleted, drive unmounted), sending a prompt fails silently: the user hears the error sound, the turn completes empty, and nothing in the chat says why. The only trace is an `ENOENT` line in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`.

**Why it happens:** the instance layer resolves the session's working directory with `FileSystem.realPath` and fails with `FileSystem.DirectoryNotFoundError` before any provider call — so every provider fails identically. On the shipped 1.19.x line the server *does* log and publish the real cause, but the renderer only routes `session.error` to an OS notification (gated behind a setting) whose description is the session title, and the message row is never marked as failed. On `dev` the failure reaches `toSessionError`, which has no case for `DirectoryNotFoundError`, so it degrades to a generic `unknown` error with a raw message, and the execution-failed notification still describes the session title instead of the failure.

**Changes:**

- `packages/core/src/session/to-session-error.ts` — map `FileSystem.DirectoryNotFoundError` to a typed `session.location-missing` error: `Project folder not found: <path>. Restore the folder, or move this session to another directory.` The envelope is an open `type` string, so this needs no schema change; the existing timeline error card renders `type: message`, so the failed turn now shows the cause and the location inline.
- `packages/app/src/shell/notifications/notification.tsx` — pass the `session.execution.failed` event's error into the notification handler so its description is the actual failure instead of the session title / `"An error occurred"`.
- `packages/core/test/session-error.test.ts` — case asserting the new mapping.

prs.title: fix(ai): send one max-token field when a body overlay sets its own
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55726

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The OpenAI Chat body builder always emits one of `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens`,
derived from the output limit. The `http.body` overlay is merged on top of that body later,
in the transport. So when the overlay carries the *other* field, both end up in the request
and strict OpenAI-compatible endpoints reject the body.

That is what #54694 exposed: a v1 `max_tokens` model option is not in `COMPATIBLE_KEYS`, so
it now migrates into the model body, and the builder adds `max_completion_tokens` next to it.

Two parts, as suggested in review:

1. `compatibleModel()` no longer migrates `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` / `maxTokens`
   into the body. They are the model's max output in v1, so they become `limit.output` and the
   builder keeps deriving its single field from it. Per-request limits (compaction) still apply.
   A non-numeric value keeps v1's behavior and still goes out in the body.
2. The builder skips its own field when a merged overlay already sets one. This covers what the
   migration cannot: explicit `body` config, and variants, which carry no limit of their own, so
   a variant-level `max_tokens` stays in the body under v1's key.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/ai` — a test drives a real request through the transport with a model body overlay of
`max_tokens: 262144` and `generation.maxTokens: 256000`, then asserts the serialized body. It
fails on `dev` with both fields present (`max_tokens: 262144` and `max_completion_tokens: 256000`,
exactly as reported) and passes here. Full suite: 1812 pass, 0 fail. Typecheck passes.

`packages/core` — `provider-options.test.ts` covers the three option spellings, and
`config.test.ts` covers the migration end to end: a v1 model with `limit.output: 200000` and
`options.max_tokens: 262144` migrates to `limit.output: 262144` with no body, and its variant
keeps `max_tokens` in the body. Typecheck passes. The suite has 29 failures on my Windows
machine (ShellTool / Session.shell / symlinks), and the set is byte-identical with and without
this change, so they are pre-existing here.

prs.title: fix(server): flush SSE headers before streaming events
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #55741, #48771. This PR does not resolve the Kaspersky buffering cause confirmed in #55741.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Explicitly flushes SSE headers when the Node server starts consuming a response body, after `writeHead`. Bun otherwise corks the initial headers and first body write together; flushing first moves that body write onto the already-sent path. This makes headers available even while the response body has no events to send. The event handler still subscribes before emitting `server.connected`.

The reporter subsequently isolated #55741 to Kaspersky buffering requests without `Accept: text/event-stream` ([details](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/55741#issuecomment-6199111277)). This server-only change does not add that client request header.

prs.title: feat(core): offer MCP search tools for the built-in web search
prs.body:
**Title:** feat(core): offer MCP search tools for the built-in web search

### Issue for this PR

Closes #51103

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The first time the model calls the built-in `websearch` tool, OpenCode opens a consent form that only offers the bundled providers (Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Tavily, TinyFish) or disabling web search. A user who already runs their own search MCP server (SearXNG, Brave, Kagi, an internal index, ...) has to reject the prompt and then tell the model to use the MCP tool. The issue asks for that MCP tool to be offered as an option for the built-in search.

This PR does two things:

**1. MCP search tools show up in the consent form.** Connected MCP tools that look like search tools are registered as web search providers with ID `mcp:<server>/<tool>`. Each one is offered as its own option in the first form:

```
Allow OpenCode to search the web for up-to-date information?
  Allow search via Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Tavily, TinyFish
  Choose another provider
  Search with MCP tool searxng/search
  Disable web search
```

Picking one saves it as the web search selection, like picking a bundled provider. The built-in `websearch` tool keeps its permission check, progress reporting, and result formatting, and sends the query to `Mcp.callTool`.

MCP has no marker for "this is a search tool", so a tool counts as a candidate when:

- its name contains `search` (case-insensitive), and
- its input schema has a string `query`, `q`, `search`, or `keywords` property, and
- no other input is required.

That keeps tools like `fetch` out, and also tools such as GitHub's `search_issues` when they need extra required arguments. The list refreshes on `mcp.tools.changed`, so servers that connect after startup appear without a restart.

**2. A `websearch.mcp` config option pins a specific tool and skips the prompt:**

```json
{
  "websearch": {
    "mcp": { "server": "searxng", "tool": "search", "argument": "q" }
  }
}
```

`argument` is the tool input that receives the query and defaults to `query`. Config reloads take effect without a restart.

**MCP providers are never picked automatically.** "Allow search via ..." stores the `random` selection, which spreads queries across providers and fails over on HTTP 429. Random selection now skips `mcp:` providers, so a user's MCP server, or an unrelated MCP tool that happens to match, is only queried after the user picks it.

Changes:

- **`packages/schema/src/config/websearch.ts`**: new `ConfigWebSearch.McpInfo` (`mcp: { server, tool, argument? }`), added to the `Selection` union next to `false` and `{ provider }`. Existing configs decode exactly as before.
- **`packages/core/src/websearch.ts`**: `WebSearch.mcpID(server, tool)` and `WebSearch.isMcp(id)`. Random selection and the random default lookup skip MCP providers.
- **`packages/core/src/config/plugin/websearch.ts`**:
  - Registers a provider for each connected MCP search candidate (`searchTool`), refreshed on `McpEvent.ToolsChanged` with a short debounce.
  - When the latest `websearch` config entry is `McpInfo`, registers that tool and selects it.
  - An MCP result with `isError: true` fails as `Mcp.ToolCallError`, so the tool reports a normal search failure instead of empty results.
  - `toResults` maps MCP output to `WebSearch.Result[]`. A list of `{ url, title?, content? | snippet? | description? }` items, bare or wrapped in `{ results: [...] }`, from `structuredContent` or JSON text, becomes one result per item. Any other text becomes a single result (`mcp://<server>/<tool>`), so free-form search tools still work.
- **`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/websearch.ts`**: the consent form lists MCP providers as direct options. "Allow" and "Choose another provider" only cover bundled providers and are left out when there are none. If the only providers are MCP tools, the form still opens with those options.
- **`packages/web/src/content/docs/tools.mdx`**: documents MCP tools in the prompt and the `websearch.mcp` option.
- Regenerated `packages/protocol/openapi.json` and `packages/client/src/promise/generated/types.ts`, because `Config.Info` is part of the public protocol.

### Design notes

- The selection is stored in the same KV key as bundled providers, so there's no new persistence. After a restart, if the chosen MCP server hasn't connected yet when the first search runs, the provider isn't registered and the consent form opens again. Once the server connects, the stored choice applies. `websearch.mcp` avoids that window because the configured provider is registered without waiting for the server.
- I put discovery in the existing config websearch plugin rather than adding a new plugin. That plugin already owns provider registration and default selection from config, and already depends on `Mcp.Service`.
- `Mcp.callTool` already returns a clear `ToolCallError` when a server isn't connected or needs auth ("Reconnect it from /mcps" / "Sign in from /mcps"), and the websearch tool reports it as a tool failure.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/tool-websearch.test.ts`: new test where an `mcp:searxng/search` provider sits next to the bundled ones. The consent form lists it as its own option. Choosing it runs the query through that provider and stores `mcp:searxng/search` as the selection. Ten `random` queries across separate sessions never pick it.
- `packages/core/test/config/websearch.test.ts`:

issues.title: Bedrock: a new BedrockRuntimeClient is created for every request
issues.body:
### What happened?

`bedrock-converse-stream.ts` does `new BedrockRuntimeClient(config)` inside `stream()`, so every model call gets a fresh client: new credential provider and new HTTP/2 session.

With an SSO profile that means every call does a `GetRoleCredentials` round trip to `portal.sso` plus a new TLS handshake to `bedrock-runtime`. I measured 2 new TLS handshakes per call, around 0.35 s before the request even starts (0.24 s SSO + 0.11 s TLS from eu-west-1). In an agent loop with ~35 calls per run that adds up fast. The old SSO sockets also stay open, I had 29 idle connections to `portal.sso` in one process.

I patched it locally to keep one client per config (region, profile, endpoint, hashed credentials, proxy) in a small LRU with an idle timeout, and dropping the cached clients on credential/auth errors so a refreshed or rotated key is picked up. Time to first byte on EU Haiku went from ~1.25 s to ~0.69 s, and calls after the first one do 0 handshakes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `amazon-bedrock` with an SSO profile (`AWS_PROFILE`).
2. Run any session with a few tool calls.
3. Watch `lsof -i` (or count TLS handshakes): every call opens a new connection to `portal.sso.<region>.amazonaws.com` and `bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com`.

### Expected behavior

The client, credential provider and HTTP/2 connection are reused across requests with the same config.

### Version

1.4.0, still the same on main (cc9c52310)

Happy to open a PR for this if you want it.

issues.title: RPC: deferred prompt gets no response when bootstrap settlement starts compaction

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
> AI-written: this report was drafted and posted by the AI agent that maintains [OAR](https://github.com/botiverse/oar) (a host that embeds pi over SDK and RPC). The reproduction below was run, not inferred.

### What happened?

In RPC mode, a `prompt` sent while a `session_start` bootstrap run is held in an awaited `agent_settled` hook never gets a response if that hook then starts compaction. The deferred prompt is rejected before `preflightResult`, so RPC never writes a reply for its request id; the error goes to the extension's `sendUserMessage` instead. The host cannot tell which input was refused and can only time out.

Two causes in `rpc-mode.js` / `agent-session.js`: RPC subscribes after `bindExtensions`, so it misses the bootstrap `agent_start`; and `get_state.isStreaming` is false while the settled hook runs, so the host cannot avoid this window.

### Steps to reproduce

Extension: `session_start` calls `pi.sendUserMessage("BOOT ...")`; the first `agent_settled` hook waits on a gate, then calls `ctx.compact()` and returns while compaction runs. Send `{"id":"D","type":"prompt","message":"D"}` while the hook is held, then release it. Runnable repro (loopback model, no account): https://github.com/botiverse/oar/tree/98beb26ff76a4107c5b5f70b7e37834da5107410/experiments/pi-bootstrap-admission

### Expected behavior

Every RPC prompt gets a correlated response, including a refusal when a deferred prompt is rejected before preflight.

### Version

pi-coding-agent 1.5.0 (executed), 1.5.2 (same ordering by source reading). Related: #10704.

issues.title: subagent({ workflow: true }) loses code block on some hosts — script fallback undocumented

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# `subagent({ workflow: true })` loses code block on some hosts — script fallback undocumented

## Summary

The `subagent` tool's `workflow: true` pattern requires the model to emit both a tool call AND a code block with language tag `js workflow` in the same reply. On some hosting platforms, the code block is stripped after the tool call is processed, causing the subagent to fail with "block missing" or similar. A working fallback (`options: { script: "..." }`) exists but is undocumented in the tool schema.

## What happens

1. Model emits: `subagent({ workflow: true })` + a code block with language tag `js workflow`
2. Some hosting platforms serialize the tool call and text separately
3. The code block text is lost or not delivered to the tool handler
4. The tool reports "block missing" or the subagent fails to launch
5. Models fall back to implementing the work themselves, losing delegation

## Root cause

From the agent loop (docs/how-pi-works.md):
> The provider streams an assistant response, which can contain text and tool calls. Pi records the response, executes each tool call, and records the results.

The assistant response content is a mixed array: `(TextContent | ThinkingContent | ToolCall)[]`. When providers serialize this, code blocks in `TextContent` may not survive alongside `ToolCall` blocks depending on the provider's message format.

## Evidence

A working fallback already exists in the system:
```typescript
subagent({ workflow: true, options: { script: `const r = ...; return r;` } })
```

And the file-based pattern works reliably:
```typescript
// Reply 1:
write({ path: "./lane.js", content: `...script body...` })
// Reply 2:
subagent({ workflow: "./lane.js" })
```

These are mentioned deep in one SKILL.md file but **not** in the tool's description, so models don't discover them when the primary pattern fails.

## Current tool description (incomplete)

> true: run the one ```js workflow block in this same reply (false invalid).
> String with '/': script file read from request cwd.
> Other string: named workflow resource.
> Raw scripts (true or path) have no runs.host.

The description assumes the code block always survives and doesn't mention the inline script fallback.

## Proposed fix

**Option A (preferred)**: Update the tool description for `workflow` to include the script fallback:

````text
true: run a workflow script. Provide it via a ```js workflow block in the same reply,
or via options.script (a string). Some hosting platforms may strip the code block;
in that case use options.script or write to a file and use workflow: "./path.js".
false: invalid.
String with '/': script file read from request cwd.
Other string: named workflow resource.
Raw scripts (true or path) have no runs.host.
````

**Option B**: Make `options.script` the primary/recommended approach, and deprecate
the code block pattern (or make it a fallback).

**Option C (both)**: Update the description AND update the default tool description
format to include usage notes that models see.

## Impact

This affects all models using the `pi-subagents` skill with `workflow: true`. The
current workaround (documented in SKILL.md) is not discovered by models at runtime,
causing unnecessary delegation failures.

## Related

- `pi-subagents` skill: `.pi/agent/skills/pi-subagents/pi-subagents/SKILL.md`
- Agent loop: `docs/how-pi-works.md`
- Message types: `docs/message-types.md` (AssistantMessage content array)
- Codemode scripts: `docs/codemode.md`

The endpoint is a 25-line Python stub that speaks enough of `/v1/chat/completions` to return one fixed string and counts the requests it receives, so no GPU, model file or real provider is involved. `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` points at a throwaway directory, and the counts below are the stub's counter.

1. `models.json` defines provider `alpha-provider`, `baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8099/v1`, `api openai-completions`, `apiKey "stub"`, one model `probe-model`. `settings.json` `defaultProvider` / `defaultModel` point at it.
2. Start `pi -ne` in an empty working directory and send a prompt: stub counter 0 to 1, answer displayed.
3. Rename the provider key to `bravo-provider`, model id unchanged, while pi is still running.
4. `/model`, then Escape without selecting anything. The selector lists `bravo-provider`, so the file was re-read. The session is still on `alpha-provider`.
5. Send a prompt: `Error: No API key found for alpha-provider.` Stub counter stays at 3, no request leaves the process. Every further prompt in that session fails the same way.

Two controls in the same run. Without opening `/model`, prompts keep reaching the stub after the rename, counter keeps increasing. The built-in `/reload` also leaves the old provider usable and prompts keep working. So the model selector, not the reload, is what strands the session.

### Expected behavior

Closing the model selector should not strand the model the session is already on. Either re-resolve it the way session restore does, or keep a provider that is still configured reachable. And the message should distinguish "this provider is no longer defined in `models.json`" from "no API key": the second reading sends people to hunt for a key on a local server that does not use one, which cost me an hour before I measured instead of guessed.

Unverified pointer, not a claim: `restoreModelFromSession()` in `core/model-resolver.js` does fall back when a saved provider cannot be resolved, which is why a fresh process survives the same rename. I did not trace the selector path.

### Version

1.5.2 (npm @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent), Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.11-arch1-1. Repro scripts and the stub server are on disk here and I can paste them on request.

issues.title: Extension-registered providers: fresh sessions intermittently ignore defaultProvider/defaultModel and start on another provider's default

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

A fresh pi session intermittently does **not** start with the configured
`defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` from settings.json when that provider is
registered by an extension via `pi.registerProvider(name, config)`. Instead, pi
silently falls back to another provider's default model
(`defaultModelPerProvider`) — in our case `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`,
which our Google credential (free tier, quota `limit: 0`) cannot serve, so the
first request fails with a 429.

Measured over repeated fresh launches: ~4 of 10 sessions start on the wrong
model; the rest start correctly on the configured default. Instrumenting
`findInitialModel` (step 3) shows the outcome correlates 1:1 with the
availability snapshot state at resolution time:

```text
step3 <default-provider>/<default-model> -> HIT auth=false  → session starts on the fallback
step3 <default-provider>/<default-model> -> HIT auth=true   → session starts on the configured default
```

Root cause: `createAgentSession` resolves the initial model
(`restoreModelFromSession` / `findInitialModel`) before name+config provider
registrations from extensions are applied to the model registry.

- `pi.registerProvider(name, config)` queues into
  `runtime.pendingProviderRegistrations` while extensions are loading
  (loader.js, "Pre-bind: queue registrations…"); the queue is flushed in
  `bindCore`, which runs when the `AgentSession` is constructed — after
  initial model resolution.
- `findInitialModel` step 3 (model-resolver.js) requires
  `getModel(provider, id)` **and** `hasConfiguredAuth(provider)`; the latter
  reads `snapshot.configuredProviders`, which is rebuilt asynchronously by
  `runAvailabilityRefresh` and can lag the registration.
- When step 3 misses, step 4 returns the first `defaultModelPerProvider`
  match from the available snapshot — silently, with no warning.

Note that `pi.registerNativeProvider(provider)` (object form) is flushed in
`createAgentSessionServices` _with_ an awaited
`modelRuntime.refresh({ allowNetwork: false })` before model resolution — the
name+config form has no equivalent before `findInitialModel`.

Possibly a residual of #6948 / #6922 (async provider model refresh vs startup
resolution, addressed for the built-in llama.cpp provider): model lists now
hydrate from the store at startup, but the configured/auth snapshot can still
lag, and the fallback is silent instead of an error. #2291 is an earlier
instance of the same ordering problem from a `session_start` hook.

Suggested direction: after extension loading completes, flush both pending
registration queues (`name+config` and native) and await
`modelRuntime.refresh({ allowNetwork: false })` before initial-model
resolution — mirroring what `createAgentSessionServices` already does after
extension load. Happy to send a PR if the direction looks right.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a provider from an extension using the name+config form:

```ts
export default function (pi) {
  pi.registerProvider("acme", {
    name: "acme",
    baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1", // never called in this repro
    api: "openai-completions",
    models: [
      {
        id: "acme-model",
        name: "Acme Model",
        contextWindow: 128000,
        maxTokens: 8192,
      },
    ],
    auth: {
      apiKey: {
        name: "acme",
        check: async () => ({ type: "api_key" }),
        resolve: async () => ({ auth: { apiKey: "demo" }, source: "acme" }),
      },
    },
    fetchModels: async () => [],
  });
}
```

2. Add a stored credential for it in auth.json:

```json
"acme": { "type": "api_key", "key": "demo" }
```

3. settings.json:

```json
{ "defaultProvider": "acme", "defaultModel": "acme-model" }
```

4. Launch several fresh sessions back-to-back and inspect each session
   journal's first `model_change` entry:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  d=/tmp/repro-$i; mkdir -p "$d"; (cd "$d" && pi -p "hi" >/dev/null 2>&1)
done
# first model_change per journal: acme-model @ acme on good launches,
# gemini-3.1-pro-preview @ google on fallback launches
```

Measured: 4 of 10 fresh sessions started on the fallback provider; 10 of 10
with the refresh applied before resolution started on the configured default.

### Expected behavior

Every fresh session starts with `defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` from
settings.json — regardless of how long extension loading takes. If the
configured provider cannot be resolved yet, pi should say so explicitly
instead of silently starting on an unrelated provider's default model.

### Version

0.84.4

The left sidebar links on the same pages are correct. Example: on , clicking **"Choose a model"** in the body goes to (404) instead of (200). You land on `https://docs.pi.dev/latest/latest/models`, which returns 404 ("Page Not Found"). Or without a browser: ```sh curl -s https://docs.pi.dev/latest | grep -o 'href="/latest/latest/[^"]*"' | wc -l # 22 curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://docs.pi.dev/latest/latest/models # 404 ``` ## Expected behavior Body links should resolve the same way sidebar links do: `https://docs.pi.dev/latest/models`. ## Scope Not specific to one page - every page has broken body links, while sidebar links work: | Page | Broken body links | |---|---| | `/latest` | 22 | | `/latest/extensions` | 21 | | `/latest/cli` | 17 | | `/latest/models` | 16 | | `/latest/quickstart` | 13 | | `/latest/sdk` | 11 | | `/latest/settings` | 10 | | `/latest/providers` | 3 | The docs content is fine, which points at the site's link rewriting rather than the Markdown: - `packages/coding-agent/docs/index.md` uses plain relative links: `[Choose a model](models.md)`. - The server already resolves those correctly: `https://docs.pi.dev/latest/models.md` → 302 → `/latest/models`. - `https://docs.pi.dev/latest/search-index.json` contains clean paths (`models.md`, `quickstart.md`), so search results are unaffected. So the article-body HTML renderer appears to prepend the version base (`/latest/`) to a slug that has already been resolved to a version-prefixed path (`latest/models`). The sidebar is built through a different code path that prefixes once, which is why the site still feels navigable. ## Version Docs site, `search-index.json` source sha `ede360e4d6548531c008dfd508d7e37f9bd47529` (generated 2026-11-13).

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

On current main (`04fd0897e4df`), the unit test `packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts` — "keeps a coalesced reload alive while another credential reader is waiting" — is flaky. I ran that test alone 20 times and got 8 passes and 12 failures. Every failure is the same: the second `read("anthropic")` returns the cached `"old"` key instead of `"new"`.

The test writes `"old"` and then `"new"` with `writeFileSync`. Those strings are the same length, and two writes in a row often keep the same `mtimeNs`. `getFileRevision` uses `size + mtimeNs + ctimeNs`, so it does not see a change and the second reader hits the cache. This is a unit test; no extension is involved.

### Steps to reproduce

On main, from the repo root:

```
npx vitest run packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts -t "keeps a coalesced reload alive while another credential reader is waiting"
```

Run it repeatedly. It usually fails more often than it passes.

### Expected behavior

The test should reliably exercise the coalesced reload path. After writing `"new"`, the file revision needs to change. Bumping mtime with `utimesSync` by 1s made it stable for me (30/30 on the isolated test, 31/31 for the whole file). I have that test-only fix on a fork and would like to open a PR.

### Version

main `04fd0897e4df`

issues.title: Proposal for solve the builtin:mcp publish server connection status via ctx.ui.setStatus("mcp", …) ISSUE

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Update the MCP status whenever the MCP subscription notifies of changes (connection, disconnection, failure, need for authentication, enabling/disabling), and reset it (to "undefined") when no servers are configured.
(suscribe callback & runAction manager)

(Optional) Also emit a structured pi.events event (e.g. mcp:status) so extensions can react programmatically, not just render a string.

### Why?

Because the lack of a MCP status signal—also no event or API that exposes the state of an MCP connection—any development built on Pi requires redundant work and significant additional effort to query or verify the status of an MCP connector; an external extension cannot compensate for this deficiency.

In the collaborative development of gentle-shell, this issue is causing some "problems" (non-blocking, but annoying for both users and developers), affecting both installation and the integration of features.

The necessary changes are minimal and would bring consistency to PI.

This issue has already been raised by other members of the community at https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10871; this proposal presents an approach

### How? (optional)

Proposal for solve the `builtin:mcp` publish server connection status via `ctx.ui.setStatus("mcp", …)` **ISSUE**
----
>

**Problem:**   `builtin:mcp` tracks full server state (`connected`/`disconnected`/`needs-auth`/`starting`, tool counts, errors) internally for `/mcp`, but never publishes it via `ctx.ui.setStatus()`, so neither the standard footer nor custom footers (pi-footer) can display MCP status — the `FooterDataProvider` channel exists but has no producer.

 `/mcp` shows rich per-server state (connected/disconnected/needs-auth/starting, tool counts, errors), but this state is only visible inside the `/mcp` UI. Extensions and custom footers can render persistent statuses through `ctx.ui.setStatus()` / `FooterDataProvider.getExtensionStatuses()`, yet `builtin:mcp` never publishes one. There is also no event or API exposing MCP connection state, so an external extension cannot fill the gap.

**Request:** have `builtin:mcp` publish a compact status under a documented stable key (e.g. `"mcp"`), updated on every connection state change.

 1. In `packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts`, publish a compact summary (e.g. `mcp: 2/3 servers · 14 tools`, with `auth`/`error` markers) under a documented, stable status key `"mcp"`, via `ctx.ui.setStatus`.
 2. Update it wherever `subscribe` already notifies state changes (connect, disconnect, failure, needs-auth, enable/disable), and clear it (`undefined`) when no servers are configured.
 3. Republish on extension setup so the status survives `/reload` (statuses are cleared by `clearExtensionStatuses()`).
 4. Document the key in `docs/mcp.md`/`docs/extensions.md` so custom footers can rely on it.
 5. (Optional) Also emit a structured `pi.events` event (e.g. `mcp:status`) so extensions can react programmatically, not just render a string.

 No changes to `interactive-mode.ts` or `FooterDataProvider` are needed — the publishing channel already exists.

---

## Problem recap

- `ctx.ui.setStatus(key, text)` is wired end-to-end: it calls `setExtensionStatus`, which writes to `FooterDataProvider` and requests a render.
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L2440-L2443
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L2780

- Custom footers receive `ReadonlyFooterDataProvider` (with `getExtensionStatuses()`) as the third argument of the `setFooter` factory.
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L2664-L2678

- The MCP extension already holds all needed state in `servers`/`connection.state` and already refreshes `/mcp` live via `subscribe`.
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L64
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L998-L1009

- No external extension can observe this state — there is no `pi.on("mcp_*")` event or getter — so the fix must live in `builtin:mcp` itself.

## Proposal

The core change is small and concentrated in `packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts`: add a function that summarizes the state of `servers` (which already exists and is already iterated in `formatStatus()`) and call it with `ctx.ui.setStatus("mcp", …)` whenever the state changes — i.e., inside the `subscribe` mechanism the `/mcp` menu already uses to refresh live.
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L998-L1040

No changes are needed in `interactive-mode.ts` or `FooterDataProvider`: `ctx.ui.setStatus` is already exposed to extensions and already writes to the provider read by both the standard footer and custom footers.
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L2780
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L2440-L2443

---

## Concrete changes

### 1. Producer in `extensions/mcp/index.ts`

Inside `createMcpExtension` 
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L998-L1009
add something like:

```ts
const publishStatus = (ctx: ExtensionContext) => {
	if (servers.length === 0 && configErrors.length === 0) {
		ctx.ui.setStatus("mcp", undefined);
		return;
	}
	const connected = servers.filter((s) => s.connection?.state === "connected");
	const needsAuth = servers.filter((s) => s.connection?.state === "needs-auth");
	const failed = servers.filter((s) => s.connection?.error && s.connection.state !== "connected");
	const tools = connected.reduce((n, s) => n + (s.connection?.state === "connected" ? s.connection.tools.length : 0), 0);
	ctx.ui.setStatus("mcp", `mcp: ${connected.length}/${servers.length} · ${tools} tools` +
		(needsAuth.length ? ` · ${needsAuth.length} auth` : "") +
		(failed.length ? ` · ${failed.length} error` : ""));
};
```

The possible states are already defined in `formatStatus()`: `"connected"`, `"disconnected"`, `"needs-auth"`, `"starting"`, plus `connection.error` and `connection.tools.length`
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L1015-L1040

### 2. Invocation points

- **In the `subscribe` callback**: the `/mcp` menu already receives state-change notifications via `subscribe` (passed to `ui.menu` in both loops)
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L998-L1009
 And call `publishStatus(ctx)` in:
 https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/runtime.ts#L333-L335
 
- **After `runAction`**: manager actions (login, reconnect, enable/disable, exposure) end in `runAction(ui, ctx, server, action)`
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L1003-L1006
 republishing afterwards covers enable/disable changes.
- **At session start**: once the config is loaded and connections started, publish the initial state.

### 3. Guard the non-TUI context

`ctx.ui` in RPC/print mode may have no footer; the call should be defensive (`setStatus` itself is a no-op outside interactive mode, but it's worth verifying). `formatStatus()` already serves the plain-text `/mcp` output without a TUI
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/index.ts#L1015-L1018

### 4. Republish after `/reload`

`resetExtensionUI()` clears all statuses via `clearExtensionStatuses()`
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c3cc91632d0a1950fb122605b190233f2aa0006e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L2604-L2608
Since `builtin:mcp` re-runs when extensions reload, publishing the initial state in the extension setup is enough.

### 5. Documentation and tests

- Document the `"mcp"` key and its format in `docs/mcp.md` / `docs/extensions.md` so pi-footer and others can consume it as a stable API.
- Add a test in `test/` (there's precedent: `interactive-mode-status.test.ts`) verifying the status is published/updated/cleared.

### 6. Optional: `pi.events` event

Emitting `pi.events.emit("mcp:status", {...})` alongside `setStatus` would give other extensions structured access to the state, not just the footer string.

issues.body:
**What do you want to change?**

Publish native MCP connection status through the existing `ctx.ui.setStatus` interface, from the built-in MCP extension.

**Why?**

Custom footers can already render `setStatus` keys, and third-party MCP extensions published server status there. Native MCP does not, so users who migrate lose the indicator and have to open `/mcp`.

The state exists but is unreachable: `/mcp` knows every server's connection state, while `pi.getAllTools()` only proves tools were *registered*. A disconnected, retrying or auth-pending server still looks healthy to any extension reading the tool inventory.

Prior request, auto-closed: #10871.

**How? (optional)**

The built-in MCP extension already tracks per-connection state (`connecting`, `connected`, `disconnected`, `needs-auth`, `failed`, `closed`) and already has a local change hook it calls on every transition.

It could publish one documented key (for example `mcp`) with an aggregate summary such as `3/4 connected` or `1 failed`, and update or clear it on each transition. No new core API and no new connection logic.

I'm happy to implement this if the shape is acceptable — or tell me if you'd prefer a typed snapshot plus a change event instead, and I'll shape it that way.

issues.title: Session restore silently switches to an unrelated model when a provider rewrites model ids

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

Resuming a session can silently start on a **completely different model** than the one the session last used, with no warning. In my case a resumed session ran on `xai/grok-4.7` instead of my default `mistral` model, and the first request rebuilt an 80k-token prompt cache for **$0.16** before I noticed.

Two things combine to cause this:

1. `getBranchSelection()` (`core/virtual-models.js`) prefers the **last assistant message's** `provider`/`model` over the last `model_change` entry.
2. A provider whose `streamSimple` rewrites the model id (common for subscription gateways that must send an upstream model name) records an id in the message that **does not exist in the model catalog**.

Restore then fails, and `findInitialModel()` step 3 picks the first "available" model by iterating `defaultModelPerProvider` in **object key order** — where `xai` precedes `zai`, `zai-coding-cn` and `mistral`. So the fallback is biased toward Grok.

## Repro

Extension that registers a provider with a display id but streams under an upstream id (this is the shape many subscription wrappers use):

```ts
export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {
  pi.registerProvider("myprov", {
    api: "openai-completions",
    baseUrl: "https://api.example.com/v1",
    apiKey: "sk-...",
    models: [{ id: "my-model", name: "My Model", reasoning: true, input: ["text"], contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 }],
    // upstream only accepts the real name, so rewrite it at request time
    streamSimple: (model, ctx, opts) => api.streamSimple({ ...model, id: "vendor-model-20260101" }, ctx, opts),
  });
}
```

1. New session, select `myprov/my-model`, send one message → the assistant message records `provider: "myprov", model: "vendor-model-20260101"`.
2. Quit and resume the session (`pi -c` / `pi --session <file>`).
3. `getBranchSelection()` returns `{ provider: "myprov", modelId: "vendor-model-20260101" }`.
4. `modelRuntime.getModel(...)` → `undefined` → restore fails → `findInitialModel()` fallback → first available model in `defaultModelPerProvider` order (e.g. `xai/grok-4.7`).

Observed: `session_start` reports the wrong model; no `model_change` entry is written for the fallback, so the session file still looks correct on disk. The same session restores fine when the last model belongs to a provider that does not rewrite ids (verified with `zai-coding-cn/glm-5.3`).

## Expected

- Restore should fall back to the session's last `model_change` entry when the recorded message model cannot be resolved.
- If restore still has to pick a different model, print a **visible** warning (currently `modelFallbackMessage` is only surfaced in some paths) — silently switching to a different provider is a cost and trust problem.

## Suggested fixes

1. In `getBranchSelection()`, when `getModel(message.provider, message.model)` misses, fall through to `findLastModelChange()` instead of returning the unresolvable response.
2. In `findInitialModel()` step 3, prefer the user's `enabledModels` order (or the most recently used model) over `Object.keys(defaultModelPerProvider)`, so the fallback is not biased toward whichever provider happens to be declared first.
3. Consider recording the selected model id (not the rewritten one) on assistant messages, or recording both (`model` + `upstreamModel`).

## Environment

### What happened?

With `openai` authenticated through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, Pi 1.3.0 reports a 272K context window for `gpt-6.1-sol`, although the same account's live model catalog reports a 500K default. This gives Pi a smaller context/compaction budget than the server advertises.

An authenticated `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` using the stored `openai` OAuth access token returned HTTP 200 and:

```json
{"slug":"gpt-6.1-sol","context_window":500000,"max_context_window":872000}
```

This is an account-specific catalog check, not an inference test above 272K. [OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) directs this sign-in flow to use `/v1/models` for the account's current catalog.

Related: #10840 and commit 5712b134e corrected `openai-codex` to 500K, but left `openai` at 272K. The static short-context pricing cap also applies when `openai` uses subscription OAuth, not an API key.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to `openai` through Sign in with ChatGPT.
2. Run `pi -ne --no-mcp --list-models gpt-6.1-sol`:

```text
provider  model        context  max-out  thinking  images
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

3. With the same OAuth access token, query `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` and inspect the entry whose `slug` is `gpt-6.1-sol`. The tested account returns `context_window: 500000`.

### Expected behavior

For ChatGPT subscription authentication, use the account's advertised default context window (500K here), rather than inheriting the API-key pricing cap. This report does not request a blanket change to API-key defaults or use of the separate 872K maximum.

issues.title: durable: allow cancellation handlers to wait on signals and deadlines
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let cancellation handlers in pi-durable save their progress and wait for a signal or deadline.

After Stop, a parked tool could request cancellation of a remote job, save its cancellation checkpoint, and wait for confirmation. If the host closes and reopens, the same task would pick up the cancellation without restarting normal execution.

### Why?

Requesting cancellation doesn't always mean the remote job has stopped. A host may need to wait for confirmation before releasing resources or treating the operation as finished.

I want that wait to survive host restarts, while keeping the task's existing ownership and the conversation’s busy state.

### How? (optional)

Extend the existing sleep and signal mechanisms to cancellation handlers, with separate cancellation checkpoints and signal delivery. Leave durable task joins and new owned children out of this change.

Related: #12026.

I'm willing to implement this change.

issues.title: Two prompts that reach an idle session together both start a run (regression in 1.5.1)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

> AI disclosure: drafted with an AI coding assistant. I checked the cited code against 1.5.2 and main (the same at this point), and ran the repro below on main.

Two `prompt()` calls on an idle session in the same tick both start a run, and the second rejects with `Agent is already processing a prompt. Use steer() or followUp() to queue messages, or wait for completion.`, even with `streamingBehavior` set.

Since #9155 (1.5.1), `prompt()` awaits `_preparePrompt()`, which reads `isStreaming` and returns the trigger, and only then calls `_startRun()`, which marks the run active (`agent-session.ts:2186-2195` at v1.5.2). The comment there says "_startRun marks the run active synchronously, so there is no gap", which holds for `_startRun` itself, but the return from the async `_preparePrompt()` leaves a microtask gap between the check and the start. A second prompt that reaches the check in that gap also sees an idle session. In 1.5.0 the check and `_startRun()` ran with no await between them when auth was already configured.

My app embeds `AgentSession`. After a Stop that leaves two prompts held in input handlers, both are released together and both start a run. Plain concurrent prompts with no extensions hit it too.

### Steps to reproduce

```js
// createAgentSession with the faux provider and two replies queued, no extensions
const verdicts = [];
await Promise.all([
  session.prompt("first", { streamingBehavior: "followUp", preflightResult: (v) => verdicts.push(v) }),
  session.prompt("second", { streamingBehavior: "followUp", preflightResult: (v) => verdicts.push(v) }),
]);
// main (and 1.5.2, same code): rejects with "Agent is already processing a prompt. ..."
```

Same when two prompts are held in an async `input` handler and released in the same tick.

### Expected behavior

The second prompt queues into the run the first one started, by its `streamingBehavior`, as it does when it arrives while a run is streaming: one `agent_start`, verdicts `started` and `queued`, both messages answered.

Checking `isStreaming` again right before `_startRun()`, in the same tick as its synchronous start, does it; the queueing `_preparePrompt()` already does can move into one helper both checks use. I have the fix and a regression test (both cases fail on main without it) and would like to send the PR.

### Version

1.5.2 (regressed in 1.5.1 by #9155, still on main)

issues.title: Google adapters reject Gemini 4 Hydrogen's advertised xhigh level

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

 Gemini 4 Hydrogen supports a fourth thinking level, xhigh (Google docs), and models.dev exposes it as low/medium/high/xhigh. A model whose
 thinkingLevelMap contains "xhigh": "xhigh" is therefore selectable via /thinking, but selecting it throws before any HTTP request is sent:

 **_Unsupported Google thinking level mapping for google/gemini-4-hydrogen: xhigh -> xhigh_**

 resolveGoogleThinkingLevel() in packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts only accepts minimal | low | medium | high, and ResolvedGoogleThinkingLevel excludes xhigh/max. Both google-generative-ai and google-vertex go through this resolver. This is reproducible directly in the adapter, with no extension loaded and no network access.

### Steps to reproduce

```
import { resolveGoogleThinkingLevel } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/google-shared";

const model = {
  provider: "google",
  id: "gemini-4-hydrogen",
  api: "google-generative-ai",
  reasoning: true,
  thinkingLevelMap: {
    low: "low",
    medium: "medium",
    high: "high",
    xhigh: "xhigh",
    max: null,
  },
  input: ["text"],
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
  contextWindow: 1048576,
  maxTokens: 65536,
};

resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, "xhigh");
// Error: Unsupported Google thinking level mapping for google/gemini-4-hydrogen: xhigh -> xhigh
```
 The same mapping is what a models.dev sync writes into a custom Google provider, and what models.json accepts for a model override.

### Expected behavior

 xhigh should resolve to XHIGH and be sent as thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel: "XHIGH" for both Google adapters. Models that do not declare
 thinkingLevelMap.xhigh should keep the current behavior. The existing google-thinking-level-map test, which only allows extended levels to map down to high, needs updating for Hydrogen.

### Version

1.5.2. The same resolver is still present on main, which pins @google/genai 2.32.0. @google/genai 3.3.0 added the native ThinkingLevel.XHIGH  enum.

### What happened?

In Pi 1.5.2, switching models mid-session (e.g. from `gemini-4-carbon` to `gemini-3.8-flash` via an OpenAI-compatible / LiteLLM proxy) right after a tool execution causes the next request to fail with HTTP 400:

```json
400: {"error": {"code": 400, "message": "Invalid thought signature.", "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"}}
```

When switching models mid-session (`isSameModel === false`), `transformMessages` drops thinking blocks and strips `thoughtSignature` from previous `toolCall` blocks. 3. Switch model mid-session (e.g. via `/model` to another Gemini model) while history ends on a tool result.
4. Let the agent continue.
5. The request fails with HTTP 400 `Invalid thought signature`.

### Expected behavior

Cross-model replay to Gemini in `openai-completions` should attach the sentinel `"skip_thought_signature_validator"` to un-signed historical tool calls (similar to `google-shared.ts`) or preserve compatible thought signatures so the session does not break.

1.5.2

issues.title: pi auth check cannot see providers from extensions
issues.body:
Seems like `pi auth check` cannot see extension-registered providers and reports a missing model as `invalid_state`. (My interpretation)

`auth check` is the documented way for scripts to gate on provider readiness. Wrapping pi in a non-interactive review pipeline, the check said the provider was broken, the call worked, and the only way to tell was to read `auth-check.ts`.

## Reproduction

```sh
pi auth check --provider cortecs --json
# {"status":"not_ready","provider":"cortecs","reason":"provider_not_found"}

pi auth check --model deepseek-v4-pro --json
# {"status":"invalid","provider":"deepseek-v4-pro","reason":"invalid_state"}

pi -p --no-tools --model 'cortecs/deepseek-v4-pro:high' "Reply with the single word ok."
# ok
```

Core providers behave as expected in the same environment (`mistral` with an API key: `ready`; `anthropic`, `openai-codex` with OAuth: `ready` with `--no-refresh`).

## Where it comes from: Agent summary inspecting `pi`

Fable found this trail in the code to back up the weird behavior:

> `pi auth check` builds its own `ModelRuntime` without loading extensions, so a provider registered by an extension package is invisible to it. The `--provider` form then reports `provider_not_found`, and the `--model` form reports `invalid_state`, while a real `pi -p` call on the same model succeeds.
>
> `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/auth-check.ts`:
>
> - `createAuthCheckModelRuntime` creates the runtime with an `InMemoryCodingAgentModelsStore` and never loads packages from settings, so `modelRuntime.getProvider("cortecs")` is undefined. `provider_not_found` is accurate for that runtime and wrong for pi as configured.
> - With `--model`, `resolveCliModel` fails against the bare store and `checkProviderAuth` throws an `AuthCommandError`. The auth command in `main.ts` catches every throw and reports `{status: "invalid", reason: "invalid_state"}`, so "model not resolvable here" surfaces as a credential failure.
> 
> Related: #8810 (extension-registered providers ignored on fresh sessions) touches the same loading boundary from the session side.

Using pi 0.85.1, macOS 15, provider registered by `npm:@czottmann/pi-cortecs`, credential of type `api_key` in `auth.json` under `cortecs`.

## Expected

Either the check loads extension-registered providers (the same package list a session loads), or it reports the limitation explicitly, e.g. `reason: "provider_not_loaded"` for `--provider` and a model-resolution error for `--model`, instead of `invalid_state`.

I'd prefer it loading :)
