prs.title: fix(coding-agent): kill whole process trees of bash commands on Windows
prs.body:
## Problem

On Windows the bash and PowerShell tools kill a command with `taskkill /F /T /PID <shell>`. `taskkill /T` finds descendants through their parent pid, so it misses every process whose parent already exited:

```bash
(while true; do echo tick; sleep 0.05; done) & sleep 1; exit 1
```

With `timeout: 3`, the shell exits after 1s, `taskkill` at the deadline finds nothing (the shell pid is gone), and the loop keeps writing to pi's pipes. The tool waits until the output pauses, and the loop keeps running after that. The same happens on abort: aborting `sleep 30 & sleep 30` in Git Bash left two `sleep.exe` running. The #11613 regression test was skipped on Windows for this reason.

Unix has no such gap: the shell runs in its own process group, and `kill(-pgid)` reaches every member, wherever it is in the tree.

## Solution

Windows has no process groups. The equivalent is a job object: a process created inside a job stays in it, and so does every process it starts, even after its parent exits, and none can leave unless the job allows breakaway. Node cannot put a child into a job before it runs, so commands now start through a small helper, `pi-job.exe` (plain C, `kernel32` only, no C runtime, about 6.5 KB):

- `pi-job run <name> <command line>` creates a job named `<name>`, starts the shell suspended, assigns it to the job, resumes it, and exits with the shell's exit code when the shell exits. The command line after the name is passed to `CreateProcessW` exactly as Node quoted it.
- `pi-job terminate <name>` terminates the job. `ProcessTree.kill()` runs it and also kills `pi-job` itself (that covers the moment before the job exists).
- `pi-job hold <handle>` (internal): background processes that are still running when the shell exits keep running, as on Unix. `run` starts a detached holder that keeps the job and its name alive until they exit, so a later abort or timeout can still terminate them. The holder has no stdio (pi's pipes still close when the writers exit), no console, and runs in the system directory.

Failure handling:

- If no job can be created or assigned (for example inside a job that forbids it), `pi-job` runs the command without one, and `kill()` reaches it through `taskkill /T` on `pi-job`.
- pi checks once per process that `pi-job` can run (security software may quarantine or block it) and otherwise spawns commands directly, as before.
- `taskkill` only targets children Node has not seen exit: Windows reuses pids quickly, and a stale pid can name an unrelated process tree.
- The holder runs from a copy in `%TEMP%`, so background processes never keep pi's installation in use.

`spawnProcessTree()` in `utils/shell.ts` wraps both platforms (process group on Unix, job on Windows), and tracked children are now tracked as process trees. If the helper is missing, or the shell path does not exist (so Node's ENOENT spawn error is kept), it falls back to the previous direct spawn plus `taskkill`.

The helper follows the existing pattern of `packages/tui/native/win32`: C source, a `build.mjs` (MSVC via vswhere, or MinGW/clang cross-compilers), and committed x64 and arm64 prebuilds. They ship in the npm package (`files`), are copied next to `pi.exe` by `scripts/build-binaries.sh`, and are required in the source archive. The prebuilds are built with zig 0.17.1 (`zig cc`, the default toolchain of `build.mjs` when zig is available), which links deterministically; the new `Windows process trees` workflow rebuilds them and fails if they differ from the committed bytes. MSVC and MinGW still work.

## Testing

Windows 11 x64, Git Bash:

- New `test/shell-process-tree.test.ts` (all platforms): argument and exit code pass-through (`a b`, `q"uote`, `trailing\`, empty, `%PATH%`), a background process that survives the command's exit and is killed by `kill()` afterwards, and a kill while the command runs. With the helper removed, the background test fails on Windows.
- `11613-bash-timeout-after-shell-exit.test.ts` now runs on Windows and passes.
- `bash-close-hang-windows`, `shell-kill-process-tree`, `6596-taskkill-enoent` pass. The bash-related tests in `tools.test.ts` pass; its 4 remaining Windows failures (plus 2 in `sdk-session-manager.test.ts`) fail identically without this change.
- Bash tool by hand: `sleep 3 & echo started` returns after 210 ms as before, `sleep` keeps running, and the holder exits when it ends. Aborting `sleep 30 & sleep 30` leaves nothing running (before: two `sleep.exe`). Overhead: about 12 ms per command (70 ms vs 58 ms for `true`).
- Linux (WSL): the background survive/kill scenario behaves as before; the Unix path is unchanged.
- `npm run check`: clean apart from `check:install-lock:coding-agent`, which fails on Windows on unmodified `main` too (the generator orders one entry differently).

- New workflow `Windows process trees` runs the process-tree tests on `windows-latest` and `windows-11-arm`; both pass.
- Argument fuzzing: 200 random argument vectors (quotes, backslash runs, tabs, `% ^ & | < >`, newlines, Unicode, empty) give the same argv through `pi-job` as with a direct spawn; stdin piping and a 32,500-character argument work.
- New tests: the holder runs from the temp copy, `run` falls back to no job when the job name is taken, and an unusable helper falls back to direct spawn. Overwriting the installed `pi-job.exe` while a holder runs works.

Windows on ARM: the arm64 prebuild is a native ARM64 executable importing only `kernel32`; the tests pass on the `windows-11-arm` runner. x64 pi under emulation picks the x64 helper by `process.arch`.

## Notes

- When pi itself is killed while a command runs, `pi-job` dies with libuv's own job and the whole job closes, so that command's processes die too. Before, only the shell died.
- `packages/durable/src/env/node.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/transports/stdio.ts` have their own `taskkill /T` copies and are not changed here.

closes #11613

issues.title: Agent Collaboration: delegate to agents in different registered workspaces of the same daemon

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Issue needs to be triaged and labeled

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support native Agent Collaboration between **different registered workspaces in the same Qwen Code daemon**. A main session in workspace A should be able to `@` an assistant bound to workspace B, let it execute in B, and receive its progress, questions and final result back in A.

For example, an embedding application has a main workspace and several specialist assistants. Each assistant already has its own registered workspace with its own `QWEN.md`, skills, tools, project settings and sessions. Asking `@SqlAssistant` from the main session should use that assistant's existing workspace context. It should not require switching the main session's workspace or copying the assistant's configuration into it.

The desired contract is:

1. **Bind and address the target.** Provide a supported API to register/bind a native agent to an existing workspace in this daemon, then expose it to an authorized caller's native `@` roster. Resolve the binding by stable workspace/agent IDs; display names alone must not select the execution target.
2. **Execute in the target context.** Create or resume a native session in B using B's effective directory, instructions, skills, tools and configuration. Keep A's context unchanged and enforce existing workspace trust and permission boundaries. Copying a definition into A is not sufficient.
3. **Return progress and results.** Preserve the native collaboration run/session identity and authorship when reporting queued/running/waiting/terminal states, useful progress and the final result to A. Expose a stable target-session/task reference that the embedding application can turn into an openable link. A message-delivery acknowledgement alone is not task completion.
4. **Handle long-running tasks and follow-ups.** Allow A to continue working while B runs, with supported wait/read or event delivery and a way to recover the binding after reconnect or restart. A follow-up or targeted cancellation should affect the intended task in B without starting a duplicate task or cancelling unrelated sessions.
5. **Relay structured user questions.** If B calls `ask_user_question`, make the pending question available to A, including the original request identity, answer keys, all questions/options and free-text or multiple-selection semantics. A host can answer from authorized context it already has, or ask the user, then submit the answer to that same pending request in B. This must resume the original task rather than send a new user prompt. Ordinary questions and tool-permission approvals need separate semantics; this must not implicitly approve tools.
6. **Support the assistant lifecycle.** An embedding application should be able to register and verify the binding when it creates an assistant, and disable/retire or unbind that agent when the assistant is removed. Reconciliation after an unknown API outcome should not create duplicate agents. Retirement should prevent future calls while preserving the appropriate history and attribution.

The API shape is open. Reusing the daemon's existing workspace/session backend through a supported execution adapter would work; a documented existing API that provides this complete flow would also satisfy the request. A separate daemon or remote AgentHost for each local workspace would add avoidable operational overhead to this use case.

### Why is this needed?

Native collaboration already provides useful shared-session scheduling and replies. The missing integration point for our application is selecting an **independent registered workspace as the native agent's execution context** and carrying its interaction lifecycle back to the invoking session.

We currently bridge this using a small on-demand skill that calls daemon session APIs to create a task in B, read/wait for progress, and answer an original pending question. The application also has to maintain task references and continuation state. We would prefer native `@agent` collaboration to own this lifecycle while reusing those session capabilities, without an extra model acting as a relay.

This is a same-daemon use case. The workspaces may be ordinary independent directories and do not need to be linked Git worktrees or remote hosts.

### Additional context

Checked against public `main` at `2366c440a002ba912f565a8c60fed48753d6fd1d`: local agent execution uses the invoking workspace ([orchestrator](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2366c440a002ba912f565a8c60fed48753d6fd1d/packages/cli/src/serve/session-agents/orchestrator.ts#L2263-L2274)), and the [execution configuration](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2366c440a002ba912f565a8c60fed48753d6fd1d/packages/core/src/agents/workspace-agents/types.ts#L167-L180) offers local or managed-host modes without an explicit target registered workspace. The native session-agent question/approval relay accepts an option selection ([route](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2366c440a002ba912f565a8c60fed48753d6fd1d/packages/cli/src/serve/routes/session-agents.ts#L517), [adapter](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2366c440a002ba912f565a8c60fed48753d6fd1d/packages/cli/src/serve/session-agents/adapters/qwen-acp.ts#L413)) but does not expose the full structured answer flow described above. If there is already a supported API or extension point for this scenario, please point us to an example; these observations are not a claim that Qwen Code lacks multi-agent collaboration in general.

Related requests have different execution boundaries:

- #15682 shares user-level agent/squad definitions across workspaces while keeping runtime state per workspace. Here the agent must execute in its bound workspace B when invoked from A.
- #15316 asks for per-session directories under one shared workspace configuration. Here A and B are separate registered workspaces with their own configuration.
- #13785 concerns agent identity and attribution on the public multi-agent contract. This request adds the cross-workspace execution and interaction flow that an embedding application needs.

A minimal acceptance scenario is: register A and B with distinguishable instructions/skills; bind an assistant to B; invoke it from A; verify execution uses B; relay and answer a question without creating a new prompt; receive the final result and task reference in A; retire the binding and verify it is no longer callable.

## What this issue tracks

#17045 moves every surface onto the shared agent loop and the event-bus kernel, turns the defaults on and removes the old loops. This issue collects what #17045 leaves out, so its freeze on 2026-11-21 does not drop it. Each item names where its decision or design is recorded.

### From #17045's scope

- [ ] A surface hands its whole turn to the loop, with no `maxRounds` and no round driver of its own. Headless's main turn does not do this either; it touches when queued input, notifications and Goal turns start a round.
- [ ] Streaming tool dispatch, on the design recorded in [Streaming tool dispatch](docs/design/2026-11-11-streaming-tool-dispatch.md), with `llm.tool_call` and `tool.cancel`, which it publishes. Worth revisiting for a provider path that ends each call during the stream, or for calls that need approval or write.
- [x] The Hosted Harness's model round on the shared loop, as a separate opt-in slice; its journaled tool batch stays ([evaluation](docs/design/2026-11-14-hosted-harness-loop-evaluation.md), #17248) — landed as #17264.

### From the speculation PR 6b decision (#17324)

The [PR 6b decision](docs/design/2026-11-15-speculation-tool-step.md) (merged as #17324) keeps speculation's own tool step and speculative loop; only its model round runs on the shared loop (PR 6a, #17029). It discharges #17045's two speculation decision boxes (the tool-step decision and the unit-parity gate decision). The gated steps and reconciliations it leaves:

- [ ] 6c — speculation on by default, then remove its current round: the record's own label for #17045's unnumbered "On by default" / "Legacy path removed" boxes. The flip must satisfy the five-step model's step-2 criteria in the [unified agent loop](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md).
- [ ] Reconcile the 6c integration gate: the parent design's integration entry expects a run "added when its default flip is prepared", but a deterministic end-to-end speculative round is impractical (a background, timing-dependent optimization). Name a nightly integration signal that satisfies the rule, or record here that the unit parity suite suffices for the default flip too.
- [x] Close the partial-batch boundary coverage before the 6c flip: the existing boundary tests cover only the zero-executed bail on the raw-chunk arm; the partial-batch hand-back and its composition with the shared round's parts have no test on either arm (the path is already reachable through the opt-in setting). Also pin an absolute count in the multi-call parity scenario. — landed as #17399.
- [ ] Reconcile #17045's obsolete speculation entries: the "Kernel on by default, if PR 6b put its run on `runAgentLoop`" box is moot under the decision (speculation keeps its own run), and the 11-18 dated row "PR 6b merged, with speculation's integration scenario" is replaced by the record's unit-parity gate decision.
- [ ] Reconcile the end-state numbers and the removal rule with the keep-its-own decisions: "1 agent loop implementation", "1 `finalizeToolResponses` caller" and #17045's "Legacy loops outside the Hosted Harness" (6 → 0) are not literally reachable — speculation keeps its speculative loop and finalizer, and the Hosted Harness keeps its journaled loop and tool step. The parent's End-state footnote records the shape; the Target cells and the removal rule's wording are this item's to fix.
- [ ] Refresh the parent design's pointers that still route the remaining steps to closed #17045 (the Status line, Goals, the five-step heading and the Follow-up section) to this issue where appropriate.

### From the capability ledger

The [capability ledger](docs/design/2026-11-15-loop-capability-ledger.md) maps each behavior of the 1.0 loop to main. These rows go here:

- [ ] L11 (defect): main collects async hook output and never delivers it to the model; `HookSystem.getPendingAsyncOutput()` has no caller.
- [ ] C10: a Stop hook's `continue: false` continues the model instead of ending the turn.
- [ ] C14, T11: a PostToolUse or PreToolUse `stop` fails only the call instead of ending the turn.
- [ ] C28: headless does not fire StopFailure when a request fails, as the TUIs, ACP and the Hosted Harness do.
- [ ] C32: a detailed terminal reason (`hook_stopped`, `model_refusal`, `prompt_too_long`, …) in the headless and SDK result.
- [ ] C6: a hook output that sets the session title.
- [ ] C11: a Stop hook that clears the context before its continuation.
- [ ] L7: reminders of the turns a bounded run has left.
- [ ] T13: a notice in the result when a hook replaced a call's input.

### Later

- [ ] Ledger rows found after 2026-11-21: the 1.0 loop directories (`event-bus/`, `tool-executor/`, `core/query-*`) are diffed against `v1.0.0-preview` every week, and a change becomes a row here.

## Linked issues

Follow-up to #17045.

prs.title: feat(web-shell): Codex-style managed worktree sessions (default-on, detached, branch & handoff)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Web Shell sessions in a trusted Git workspace now behave like Codex managed worktree chats. A new session defaults to an isolated worktree instead of the user's current checkout; the worktree is created lazily when the first message is sent, starts in detached HEAD so parallel sessions never pollute the branch list, and carries the source checkout's uncommitted changes (staged, unstaged, and untracked) so the agent sees exactly the files the user has on disk. From the branch chip's menu the user can turn the detached worktree into a named branch ("Create branch here") or move the same chat between the worktree and the local checkout ("Hand off"), with the work carried across in both directions. A new `worktree.defaultForNewSessions` setting (default `true`) turns the default off; explicit mode selection always wins, and the daemon API semantics are unchanged for callers that do not opt in.

This is the first five phases (P1–P5) of the Codex parity design linked below; retention with snapshots (P6) and a configurable worktree root (P7) are tracked in #17237. The design document (English and Chinese) records the Codex reference behavior, the consumer census behind the detached-HEAD refactor, and the v1 limitations of the handoff.

## Why it's needed

Today multiple Web Shell sessions in one workspace share a single checkout, so concurrent agents trample each other's edits and HEAD, and an agent's changes land directly in the user's working tree. Codex solves this with managed worktrees that are on by default, detached, and carry the user's uncommitted context. This PR brings that experience to Web Shell: isolation by default without branch pollution, the user's in-progress work visible to the agent, and a safe path to bring the work back to the local checkout or promote it to a branch. The default is configurable so users who prefer the current-branch flow can keep it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Build and bundle (`npm run build && npm run bundle`), then run a daemon against a throwaway Git workspace (`node dist/cli.js serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4199 --require-auth --workspace <repo>` with `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` set). Confirm: (1) `GET /workspace/settings` serves `worktree.defaultForNewSessions` with effective `true`, and setting it to `false` at workspace scope flips the effective value; (2) creating a session with `worktree: {}` yields a worktree whose `branch` is `""`, `git -C <worktree> symbolic-ref HEAD` fails (detached), and `git branch --list 'worktree-*'` in the source repo is unchanged; (3) with a dirty source checkout (one staged, one unstaged, one untracked file), all three appear in the new worktree while the source status is untouched and the worktree HEAD equals the source HEAD; (4) `POST /session/:id/worktree-branch {"name":"feat/x"}` returns 200 and the worktree is on `feat/x`, a second call returns 409 `worktree_already_branched`, a taken name returns 409 `branch_already_exists`, and an invalid name returns 400; (5) `POST /session/:id/worktree-handoff {"to":"worktree"}` on a plain session moves it into a detached worktree carrying local dirty state, and `{"to":"local","name":"feat/y"}` moves it back, checking `feat/y` out locally with the worktree's commits and tracked dirty changes, leaving the worktree detached; a dirty local checkout returns 409 `local_checkout_dirty`. In the Web Shell UI, the composer chip shows Worktree mode by default for a trusted Git workspace, the branch picker offers "Create branch here" only for detached worktree sessions and "Hand off to local" / "Move to worktree" by context, and resetting the chip to the current branch before sending creates a plain session.

Focused unit suites (run from the repo root): `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/gitWorktreeService.dirty-carry.integ.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.detached.integ.test.ts src/services/worktreeSessionService.test.ts`; `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/routes/session-worktree-branch.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-worktree-handoff.test.ts src/serve/branch-worktree-preparation.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-settings.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-settings-i18n.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry-catalog.test.ts src/startup/worktreeStartup.test.ts`; `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/BranchPickerPopover.test.tsx client/components/GitModePopover.test.tsx client/components/messages/SettingsMessage.dom.test.tsx` and `npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t worktree`. On this machine the web-shell suites need `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage` (Node 22+ experimental webstorage shadows jsdom's localStorage) and the git integration suites need `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` to bypass a host-level pre-push hook; neither is a product requirement. The repo-wide drift guards (settings zh coverage, telemetry count/catalog) and the integration capabilities baseline (`cd integration-tests && npx vitest run cli/qwen-serve-routes.test.ts`, after `npm run build && npm run bundle`) migrate with this surface and are part of the focused list.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Daemon-level E2E probes against a throwaway dirty Git repo, before (installed 0.27.3) vs after (this branch's bundle): the settings key is absent before and served with effective `true` after; worktree creation before yields a named `worktree-<slug>` branch with none of the dirty files carried, after yields `branch: ""`, detached HEAD, an empty `worktree-*` branch list, and all three dirty files carried with the source untouched. The handoff round trip (local → worktree → local) returns 200 in both directions with the branch checked out locally, the session's commit present, and the worktree left detached; a dirty local checkout returns 409 `local_checkout_dirty`. Unit evidence on the final head: core dirty-carry + detached + sidecar suites 76/76, cli branch/handoff/journal/settings/telemetry suites green, web-shell App worktree filter 14/14 plus BranchPickerPopover 151/151, GitModePopover 18/18, SettingsMessage 59/59; full App.test.tsx 1508/1508. Build, typecheck (core/cli/web-shell), and bundle all exit 0. UI screenshots: component-tested; visual capture to follow in review.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux runtime: isolated `node dist/cli.js serve` daemons on throwaway ports/workspaces with `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` and bearer auth; real git repositories for the worktree probes. Node 24 toolchain for build/typecheck (the host's default Node 26 lacks corepack).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the default flip changes where a new session does its work — an isolated worktree instead of the user's checkout. Mitigations: the worktree is created lazily on the first prompt (selection alone creates nothing), an explicit composer selection always wins over the default, the touched marker survives transient git-status blips, and `worktree.defaultForNewSessions: false` restores the old default. The detached-HEAD refactor reworks the worktree service's lifecycle gates (branch/tip equality, unmerged-commit detection, reattach, journal identity); a missed consumer would be a silent fail-closed leak, so the change ships with a full consumer census (design P3 inventory) and per-consumer migration tests. Handoff relocates a live session's cwd; its v1 limitations are documented rather than hidden (see the design D6): a clean local checkout stands in for "no other active session owns it" (the bridge has no session-list occupancy probe), and there is no crash-window atomic rollback — a crash mid-handoff leaves a recoverable shape, not a self-healing transfer.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows are not locally validated (⚠️ in the table; the PR-phase CI skips unit tests on both). Visual UI capture is pending (component-tested only). Retention with snapshots/restore (P6) and a configurable worktree root (P7) are out of scope here and tracked in #17237. The base-side `acp-agent-loop-parity` no-AK failure is attributed to `main` (cross-PR control in the PR comments), not to this diff.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: callers that relied on a session worktree sitting on a named `worktree-<slug>` branch now see detached HEAD with `branch: ""` in the session metadata, sidecar, and SDK `DaemonWorktreeInfo`; code that compared against `worktree-<slug>` must tolerate the empty-string detached convention (the daemon's own gates, journal recovery, reattach, and displays were migrated in this PR). Tool-created (`enter_worktree`), agent-isolation, and Arena worktrees keep their named branches — only Web Shell session worktrees change shape. The daemon API is unchanged for callers that do not pass `worktree`/the new routes; `POST /session` without `worktree` still runs in the workspace directory. Users who prefer the previous flow set `worktree.defaultForNewSessions: false`.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-worktree-codex-parity/docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-worktree-codex-parity/docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.zh-CN.md) (decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and the P6/P7 follow-up work are complete and synchronized in both).

## Linked Issues

- Tracks the remaining phases: #17237 (P6 retention + snapshots, P7 configurable root).
- Design reference: `docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.md` (+ `.zh-CN.md`), added in this PR.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

受信任 Git workspace 中的 Web Shell 会话现在与 Codex 托管 worktree chat 行为一致。新会话默认进入隔离 worktree 而非用户当前检出；worktree 在首条消息发送时惰性创建，以 detached HEAD 起步使并行会话永不污染分支列表，并携带源检出的未提交改动（staged、unstaged、untracked），让 agent 看到与用户磁盘上完全一致的文件。用户可从分支 chip 菜单把 detached worktree 转为命名分支（「在此创建分支」），或在 worktree 与本地检出之间移动同一 chat（「Hand off」），两个方向都携带工作。新设置 `worktree.defaultForNewSessions`（缺省 `true`）可关闭缺省；显式模式选择始终优先，未 opt-in 的调用方 daemon API 语义不变。

这是下方链接的 Codex 对齐设计的前五个阶段（P1–P5）；保留策略 + 快照（P6）与可配置 worktree 根（P7）在 #17237 跟踪。设计文档（中英成对）记录了 Codex 参考行为、detached-HEAD 重构背后的消费方普查、以及 handoff 的 v1 限制。

## 为什么需要

当前同一 workspace 的多个 Web Shell 会话共享一个检出，并发 agent 互相踩踏编辑与 HEAD，agent 的改动直接落在用户工作树。Codex 用缺省开启、detached、携带用户未提交上下文的托管 worktree 解决此问题。本 PR 把该体验带到 Web Shell：缺省隔离且不污染分支、用户进行中的工作对 agent 可见、并有把工作带回本地检出或提升为分支的安全路径。缺省可配置，偏好当前分支流程的用户可保留原行为。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

构建并打包（`npm run build && npm run bundle`），对一次性 Git workspace 起 daemon（`node dist/cli.js serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4199 --require-auth --workspace <repo>`，设 `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN`）。确认：(1) `GET /workspace/settings` 暴露 `worktree.defaultForNewSessions` 且 effective 为 `true`，workspace 作用域设 `false` 后 effective 翻转；(2) 以 `worktree: {}` 建会话得到的 worktree `branch` 为 `""`，`git -C <worktree> symbolic-ref HEAD` 失败（detached），源仓库 `git branch --list 'worktree-*'` 不变；(3) 源检出 dirty（一个 staged、一个 unstaged、一个 untracked 文件）时三者都出现在新 worktree，源 status 不被触碰，worktree HEAD 等于源 HEAD；(4) `POST /session/:id/worktree-branch {"name":"feat/x"}` 返回 200 且 worktree 在 `feat/x`，二次调用 409 `worktree_already_branched`，占用名 409 `branch_already_exists`，非法名 400；(5) 普通会话 `POST /session/:id/worktree-handoff {"to":"worktree"}` 迁入携带本地 dirty 的 detached worktree，`{"to":"local","name":"feat/y"}` 迁回并在本地 checkout `feat/y`（带 worktree 的 commit 与 tracked dirty），worktree 留 detached；本地 dirty 时 409 `local_checkout_dirty`。Web Shell UI 中，受信任 Git workspace 的 composer chip 缺省显示 Worktree 模式，分支选择器仅对 detached worktree 会话提供「在此创建分支」、按上下文提供「移交到本地」/「移入 worktree」，发送前把 chip 重置为当前分支则创建普通会话。

聚焦单测套件（从仓库根运行）：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/gitWorktreeService.dirty-carry.integ.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.detached.integ.test.ts src/services/worktreeSessionService.test.ts`；`cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/routes/session-worktree-branch.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-worktree-handoff.test.ts src/serve/branch-worktree-preparation.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-settings.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-settings-i18n.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry-catalog.test.ts src/startup/worktreeStartup.test.ts`；`cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/BranchPickerPopover.test.tsx client/components/GitModePopover.test.tsx client/components/messages/SettingsMessage.dom.test.tsx` 及 `npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t worktree`。本机 web-shell 套件需 `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`（Node 22+ 实验性 webstorage 遮蔽 jsdom 的 localStorage），git 集成套件需 `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` 绕过宿主级 pre-push 钩子；两者均非产品要求。仓库级漂移守卫（设置 zh 覆盖、telemetry 计数/目录）与集成 capabilities 基线（`npm run build && npm run bundle` 后 `cd integration-tests && npx vitest run cli/qwen-serve-routes.test.ts`）随本表面一起迁移，已列入聚焦清单。

### 证据（改动前后）

对一次性 dirty Git 仓库的 daemon 级 E2E 探针，前（已安装 0.27.3）后（本分支 bundle）：设置键前缺席、后以 effective `true` 暴露；worktree 创建前产出命名 `worktree-<slug>` 分支且不携带任何 dirty 文件，后产出 `branch: ""`、detached HEAD、空 `worktree-*` 分支列表、三态 dirty 全携带且源不被触碰。handoff 往返（local → worktree → local）两个方向均 200，分支在本地 checkout、会话 commit 存在、worktree 留 detached；本地 dirty 返回 409 `local_checkout_dirty`。最终 head 单测证据：core dirty-carry + detached + sidecar 套件 76/76，cli branch/handoff/journal/settings/telemetry 套件绿，web-shell App worktree 过滤 14/14 + BranchPickerPopover 151/151、GitModePopover 18/18、SettingsMessage 59/59；App.test.tsx 全量 1508/1508。build、typecheck（core/cli/web-shell）、bundle 均 exit 0。UI 截图：组件测试覆盖；视觉采集待评审阶段补。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地 Linux 运行时：一次性端口/workspace 上的隔离 `node dist/cli.js serve` daemon，带 `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` 与 bearer 鉴权；worktree 探针用真实 git 仓库。build/typecheck 用 Node 24 工具链（宿主默认 Node 26 无 corepack）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与取舍：缺省翻转改变了新会话的工作位置——隔离 worktree 而非用户检出。缓解：worktree 在首条 prompt 时惰性创建（仅选择不会创建任何东西）、显式 composer 选择始终优先于缺省、touched 标记挺过 transient git-status 抖动、`worktree.defaultForNewSessions: false` 恢复旧缺省。detached-HEAD 重构重做了 worktree 服务的生命周期门（分支/tip 等值、未合并 commit 检测、重附着、journal 身份）；漏掉的消费方会是静默 fail-closed 泄漏，因此改动随附完整消费方普查（设计 P3 清单）与逐消费方迁移测试。Handoff 迁移在线会话的 cwd；其 v1 限制成文而非隐藏（见设计 D6）：以本地检出干净代替「无其他活跃会话占用」（bridge 无会话列表占用探针），且无崩溃窗口原子回滚——中途崩溃留下可恢复形态，而非自愈转移。
- 未验证 / 范围外：macOS 与 Windows 未本地验证（表中 ⚠️；PR 阶段 CI 两端单测一律跳过）。视觉 UI 采集待补（仅组件测试）。保留策略 + 快照/恢复（P6）与可配置 worktree 根（P7）不在本 PR 范围，在 #17237 跟踪。base 侧 `acp-agent-loop-parity` no-AK 失败已归因于 `main`（PR 评论中的跨 PR 对照），非本 diff。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：依赖会话 worktree 落在命名 `worktree-<slug>` 分支的调用方，现在会在会话元数据、sidecar、SDK `DaemonWorktreeInfo` 看到 detached HEAD 与 `branch: ""`；与 `worktree-<slug>` 比较的代码必须容忍空串 detached 约定（daemon 自身的门、journal 恢复、重附着、展示已在本 PR 迁移）。工具创建（`enter_worktree`）、agent 隔离、Arena worktree 保留命名分支——只有 Web Shell 会话 worktree 改变形态。未传 `worktree`/新路由的调用方 daemon API 不变；不带 `worktree` 的 `POST /session` 仍在 workspace 目录运行。偏好旧流程的用户设 `worktree.defaultForNewSessions: false`。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-worktree-codex-parity/docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-worktree-codex-parity/docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.zh-CN.md)（决策、约束、验收标准与 P6/P7 后续工作在两版中完整同步）。

## 关联 issue

- 跟踪剩余阶段：#17237（P6 保留 + 快照，P7 可配置根）。
- 设计参考：`docs/design/2026-11-14-web-shell-codex-worktree-parity.md`（+ `.zh-CN.md`），本 PR 新增。

</details>

prs.title: refactor(managed-agent): archive Kubernetes runtime and resident CSI backend
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Moves the Kubernetes Runtime, Resident Workspace, Workspace CSI, and Kubernetes Harness Pool discovery implementations out of the managed agent server into a cold source archive under `packages/sdk-java/managed-kubernetes-archive/`, preserving the original module layout without wiring the archive into the build or CI. The former K2 resident deployment example is archived alongside them. The managed agent server keeps only the general runtime backends (local process, SSH process, external scratch/workspace, static) and static Harness pool discovery. CSI-only database columns, configuration properties, internal broker endpoints, and maintenance entry points are removed; the shared tables and the lock ordering used by ordinary bindings are preserved, and the generic checkpoint/canonical-JSON helpers move onto the contracts that still use them. The branch is merged up to date with `main`, keeping upstream's new web-terminal, external-workspace, and terminal-hold features intact.

## Why it's needed

The Kubernetes/CSI runtime path is being retired in favor of the general backends. Keeping its contracts, schema columns, configuration surface, and verification suites inside the managed agent server added maintenance burden and dead surface to deployments that never use it. Archiving the implementation preserves the design and deployment evidence for reference while leaving the production tree and schema with only the capabilities that remain supported.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Build the managed agent server reactor and run both Checkstyle executions (`checkstyle:check` and `checkstyle:check@runtime-broker-checkstyle`); expect success with no violations.
- Run the managed agent verification unit suite (H2); expect green. The native-media integration cases additionally require the TypeScript worker dist (`packages/core` and `packages/cli`) to be built first; CI builds it before running them.
- Confirm no Maven module references the archive and no production code references the archived classes.
- Confirm ordinary binding control still locks the session root before the binding row, and that dispatch authorization keeps that root-before-binding ordering (the CSI admission classes that previously carried this ordering were archived, so the ordering now lives directly in the binding repository).
- Confirm the external-workspace drain proof reader still rejects non-integral numbers, duplicate keys, and trailing content (`ManagedContextProtocol.parseCanonical`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (refactor; no user-visible/TUI change).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅ tested   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ not tested   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️ not tested   |

### Environment

JDK 21, Maven 3.9.12, isolated local Maven repository. The full managed-agent verification suite passes locally after the merge with `main`; CI additionally builds the TypeScript worker and runs the cross-platform matrix and the approval-gated MySQL/Hosted lanes.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the archive is a cold copy and is not compiled; restoring it later requires re-adding the removed schema columns and SPI hooks documented in the archive README.
- Not validated / out of scope: MySQL integration lanes and Hosted fault/failover gates (approval-gated in CI); the TypeScript worker source is unchanged.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: deployments configuring the Kubernetes workspace provisioner, resident workspaces, or Kubernetes Harness pool discovery will fail closed; those options are removed. The internal CSI batch-read endpoint returns 501.

Design document: [`docs/design/2026-11-13-managed-kubernetes-java-archive.md`](docs/design/2026-11-13-managed-kubernetes-java-archive.md) and [`.zh-CN.md`](docs/design/2026-11-13-managed-kubernetes-java-archive.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

<!-- none -->

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

把 Kubernetes Runtime、Resident Workspace、Workspace CSI 以及 Kubernetes Harness 池服务发现的实现从 managed agent server 中迁出，冷归档到 `packages/sdk-java/managed-kubernetes-archive/`，保留原模块层级，但**不接入构建与 CI**。原 K2 常驻部署示例一并归档。managed agent server 只保留通用运行时后端（local process、SSH process、external scratch/workspace、static）与静态 Harness 池服务发现。CSI 专属的数据库列、配置项、内部 broker 端点与运维入口被移除；共享表与普通绑定所用的锁序保持不变，通用的 checkpoint/规范化 JSON 辅助方法内聚到仍在使用它们的契约上。分支已合并到最新 `main`，完整保留上游新增的 web-terminal、external-workspace 与 terminal-hold 功能。

## 为什么需要

Kubernetes/CSI 运行时路径正在被通用后端取代。把它的契约、schema 列、配置面与验证套件留在 managed agent server 内，给从不使用它的部署增加了维护负担与死代码面。归档实现既保留了设计与部署证据可供回溯，又让生产树与 schema 只剩仍然支持的能力。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

- 构建 managed agent server reactor 并跑两套 Checkstyle（`checkstyle:check` 与 `checkstyle:check@runtime-broker-checkstyle`），应成功且零违规。
- 跑 managed agent verification 单元套件（H2），应全绿。native-media 集成用例还需先构建 TypeScript worker 的 dist（`packages/core` 与 `packages/cli`）；CI 会先构建再跑。
- 确认没有 Maven 模块引用归档、没有生产代码引用归档类。
- 确认普通绑定控制仍先锁会话根再锁 binding 行，dispatch 授权也保持该 root→binding 锁序（原先承载此锁序的 CSI admission 类已归档，锁序现在直接落在 binding repository 中）。
- 确认 external-workspace drain proof 读取器仍拒绝非整数数字、重复键与尾随内容（`ManagedContextProtocol.parseCanonical`）。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A（重构，无用户可见/TUI 变化）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅ 已测   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ 未测   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️ 未测   |

### 环境

JDK 21、Maven 3.9.12、隔离的本地 Maven 仓库。合并 `main` 后完整 managed-agent verification 套件在本地通过；CI 另行构建 TypeScript worker 并跑跨平台矩阵与需审批的 MySQL/Hosted lane。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：归档是冷副本、不参与编译；日后若要恢复，需按归档 README 重新补回被移除的 schema 列与 SPI 钩子。
- 未验证/范围外：MySQL 集成 lane 与 Hosted 故障/故障转移门禁（CI 中需审批后触发）；TypeScript worker 源码未改动。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：配置了 Kubernetes workspace provisioner、resident workspaces 或 Kubernetes Harness 池服务发现的部署会 fail-closed；这些选项已移除。内部 CSI batch-read 端点返回 501。

设计文档：[`docs/design/2026-11-13-managed-kubernetes-java-archive.md`](docs/design/2026-11-13-managed-kubernetes-java-archive.md) 与 [`.zh-CN.md`](docs/design/2026-11-13-managed-kubernetes-java-archive.zh-CN.md)。

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the confirmation question visible when the body overflows
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes a tool-confirmation dialog fit the height it was given, so the question being answered and the answer choices are always inside the visible area — and so the part of the body that was cut away is announced, counted, and reachable.

Round two (review feedback) changed how the body is limited rather than whether it is limited:

- One budget per confirmation type, taken before the option splice and before the auto-mode banner is wrapped in, so the banner is charged exactly once and the dialog's own cap matches the budget its body was sized against.
- Clipping is now contiguous. The capped column pins its rows and owns its own height limit, so a cut removes the tail instead of compressing rows onto one another and leaving a scattered sample of the content on screen.
- Every cut the dialog makes says what it hid, in its own row: `... last 29 lines hidden ...`, `... 29 more URLs hidden ...`, `... 1 more URL hidden ...`, and an announcement when a whole block (a plan, a prose prompt) was dropped.
- The reveal shortcut becomes discoverable. Each cut registers an overflow for as long as the confirmation is on screen, which is the only condition under which `Press ctrl-s to show more lines` appears; the registration is released when the confirmation leaves. This is the inspect path the review asked for: `ctrl-s` lifts every height budget in the dialog, so the whole body — including the destinations behind a `... 29 more URLs hidden ...` — renders into the terminal scrollback without answering.
- Inside the fetch-style confirmation, destinations are costed before the prose that explains them, and the block's own chrome (label, separator, hidden-count footer) is dropped before any destination is. A label over an empty list answers nothing; a host is the thing being authorised.
- The prompt is measured by what it renders, not by its Markdown source, because the renderer strips emphasis markers and turns links into labels.

## Why it's needed

A confirmation is only usable if the user can read what is being asked and can see the choices. The height budget was enforced only by the parts of the body that limit themselves — the diff view, the plan view, the command preview. Bodies that do not limit themselves grew to their full content height: a prompt rendered as inline Markdown, a long list of URLs to fetch, an MCP confirmation whose server and tool names wrap across many rows. The live transcript clips a pending item at the bottom, so the overflow was cut from the bottom — exactly where the question line and the option list live. The user pressed Enter on body text without ever seeing the question.

Cutting the body alone was not enough, and the first round of this PR showed why. An ancestor height limit in Ink does not clip a tail: it compresses rows, so a list can survive as a misleading sample of entries with its headers gone and nothing saying so. A cap computed after the auto-mode banner and the spliced option were already counted charges the same rows twice and hides the command the user is being asked to approve. And a silent cut is indistinguishable from a complete list, which is a worse failure than an overflowing one — the review called this out for the destination list, and it is the reason this round spends rows on counting and on the reveal shortcut.

Earlier work on the same budget: #6867, #7001.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Run the confirmation dialog's component tests: **76 pass**.
- Confirm they are load-bearing. Check out this branch, revert only the dialog component to the PR head (`git stash push -- <the component>`), and run the same test file: **15 of the 76 fail** on the height, contiguity, counting, singular-wording, reveal-registration and overflow-release cases. Restore the file and the same file reports 76 passed.
- Three of the new tests pass at the PR head as well; they pin behaviour this round introduced rather than a defect that existed at the head, and their comments say so: prose measured by rendered rows, a single MCP identity row, and the plan hint keeping its own row.
- Confirm the neighbours are unaffected: the tool message, the history item and the shared height-limited box pass unchanged (184 tests).
- In a real terminal (Linux, tmux at 100×24) drive a fetch confirmation whose prose is long enough to overflow. Expect a contiguous prefix of the prose, a counted hidden-lines row, the `URLs to fetch:` block with its destination, the question, all four options, and the reveal hint — all inside 24 rows. Then press `ctrl-s` and widen: the whole prose appears, the hidden-lines row is gone, and the question plus every option are still selectable; answering still runs the tool.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Component level, one info confirmation whose prose is 40 paragraphs, given a 12-row budget at 50 columns. On `main` the body is neither capped nor announced: the frame is 86 rows for a 12-row budget, and the question line lands on row 82 — below the fold of any real terminal. At this PR's head, the first iteration of the fix, the frame is capped to 12 rows and the question is on row 8, but the cut is silent: nothing on screen says most of the prose is gone. Round two keeps the same 12 rows and announces the cut:

```text
   finding 1

   finding 2

   ... last 75 lines hidden ...

 Do you want to proceed?

 › 1. Yes, allow once
   2. No, suggest changes (esc)
```

The announcement is paid for with a content row: at the PR head the sixth body row reads `finding 3`, where round two shows how many rows were hidden.

Live terminal at 100×24, the same mock model and the same page, current tree:

```text
     Fetch content from http://127.0.0.1:8765/page and process with: Part 1: Summarise this
     page for a maintainer who has never seen it. Cover: what the page documents; which
     subsystems it names; every caveat it states about ordering, concurrency, and failure
     handling; the exact wording of any warning about data loss; the migration steps in order;
      the rollback path; the benchmark table and what each column measures; the deprecation
     notices with their dates; the list of configuration keys it mentions and the default of
     each; the examples it shows and the assumptions they make; anything that contradicts
     ... last 29 lines hidden ...

     URLs to fetch:
      - http://127.0.0.1:8765/page

   Do you want to proceed?

   › 1. Yes, allow once
     2. Always allow fetch from 127.0.0.1 in this project
     3. Always allow fetch from 127.0.0.1 for this user
     4. No, suggest changes (esc)

Press ctrl-s to show more lines
```

The same scenario on the tree before any change of this PR renders the prose region blank with the tool-call header cut off at the top: an over-tall frame loses its own top rows in this terminal too. That is also why the exact symptom in the report — the question below the fold — does not reproduce live at 24 rows; it is demonstrated at component level, where the same frame measures 86 rows against a 12-row budget with the question on row 82, and where reverting only the dialog component turns 15 of the 76 tests red.

Pressing `ctrl-s` while the confirmation is pending, then widening the window to 60 rows, renders all three end markers of the prose, drops the hidden-lines row, and leaves the question plus all four options selectable.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️     |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️     |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅     |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests (vitest, run without coverage) plus one tmux session against a local OpenAI-compatible mock model, no sandbox, no real model calls.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: at a tight budget the explanation loses to the destinations, so a fetch confirmation can show zero prose rows. That is deliberate — the user still sees which hosts are being authorised, how much prose was hidden, and can reveal the rest. The question and the choices are visible with or without the reveal path.
- Known limits, recorded rather than fixed here: pressing the reveal shortcut at a terminal height the revealed frame cannot fit removes the hidden-lines row and shows blank rows, because an over-tall frame loses its own top rows — that behaviour predates this PR and is unchanged by it. A plan cut inside the Markdown renderer carries that renderer's own cue rather than a counted footer from this dialog, and does not light the shortcut hint; the plan's own `o open full plan in editor` row is always rendered instead.
- Not validated / out of scope: the hook-driven long confirmation reason and the pathologically long MCP tool name are covered by unit tests only — no built-in tool produces a multi-URL confirmation and no realistic server names a tool that long. The dedicated question-asking dialog renders through its own component and is untouched.
- Deferred on purpose, to keep this PR at its original scope: the exact clamp arithmetic for a compact `exec` body, the shared helper for registering an overflow, the fifth copy of the hidden-lines label, and the per-render cost of measuring wrapped rows. These are recorded here so they are not silently dropped; each is fine as a follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No option, command, keybinding or public type changes; the only visible difference is what a confirmation renders inside its height budget.

Design document: [English](docs/design/2026-11-14-confirmation-body-height-budget.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-14-confirmation-body-height-budget.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Related, both already closed: #6867, #7001. This PR closes no issue.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让工具确认对话框适配它被分配的高度，从而保证「正在被询问的问题」和「可选答案」始终位于可见区域内；同时，被裁掉的那部分正文会被宣告、被计数，并且可以被调出查看。

第二轮（根据评审意见）改变的是「如何限制正文」，而不是「是否限制」：

- 每种确认类型只取一次预算，且取在「插入额外选项」与「包裹自动模式横幅」之前，因此横幅只计一次，对话框自身的上限与其正文所依据的预算一致。
- 裁切现在是连续的。被限高的列会钉住自己的行并持有自身的高度上限，因此裁掉的是尾部，而不是把若干行压缩到彼此之上、只留下零散样本。
- 对话框每一处裁切都会用自己的那一行说明隐藏了什么：`... last 29 lines hidden ...`、`... 29 more URLs hidden ...`、`... 1 more URL hidden ...`；当整块内容（计划、说明正文）被丢弃时另有宣告行。
- 调出快捷键变得可发现。每一处裁切都会在确认界面留在屏幕期间登记一个溢出，而这正是 `Press ctrl-s to show more lines` 出现的唯一前提；确认界面离开时该登记会被释放。这就是评审要求的「完整查看」路径：`ctrl-s` 会解除本对话框内所有高度预算，于是完整正文——包括 `... 29 more URLs hidden ...` 背后的目标地址——会渲染进终端 scrollback，且无需先作答。
- 在抓取类确认界面里，先核算目标地址的成本，再排解释性正文；并且先丢弃该区块自身的装饰（标题、空隔行、隐藏计数页脚），再丢弃任何一条地址。空列表上方的标题不回答任何问题，而主机才是被授权的对象。
- 说明正文按「渲染出来的样子」计量，而不是按 Markdown 源码，因为渲染器会去掉强调标记并把链接转为标签文本。

## 为什么需要它

只有当用户能看到被询问的内容以及可选项时，确认操作才有意义。此前的高度预算只由正文中自我限制的部分保证——diff 视图、计划视图、命令预览。不做自我限制的内容会按完整内容高度渲染：以内联 Markdown 渲染的提示、较长的待抓取 URL 列表、服务器名与工具名换行成多行的 MCP 确认。实时转录区在底部裁切未固定的条目，因此超出部分正是从底部被裁掉——而那正是问题行与选项列表所在的位置。用户是在只有正文的画面上按下了回车，从未看到问题与选项。

仅仅「裁掉正文」是不够的，本 PR 的第一轮就说明了原因。Ink 中外层的高度上限并不会裁掉尾部：它压缩行，于是一个列表可能以具有误导性的样本形式残留，标题全部消失，且没有任何提示。而在自动模式横幅与被插入的选项已被计入之后才计算上限，会把同样的行重复扣两次，进而把用户正要批准的命令隐藏掉。至于「静默裁切」，它与「列表完整」在外观上无法区分，这是比溢出更糟的失败——评审对目标地址列表正是提出了这一点，也是本轮把行数花在计数与调出快捷键上的原因。

此前针对同一预算的相关工作：#6867、#7001。

## 测试者验证方案

### 如何验证

- 运行确认对话框的组件测试：**76 条通过**。
- 确认这些测试确实有效：在本分支上只把对话框组件还原为 PR 头（`git stash push -- <该组件>`），再运行同一个测试文件：**76 条中有 15 条失败**，涉及高度、连续性、计数、单数措辞、快捷键登记与登记释放等用例；恢复文件后同一文件报告 76 条通过。
- 另有三条新增测试在 PR 头也通过，它们固定的是本轮引入的行为而非头部的缺陷，测试注释中已说明：按渲染结果计量说明正文、MCP 标识只保留一行、计划提示独占一行。
- 确认相邻组件未受影响：工具消息、历史条目以及共享的限高盒子全部通过且未改动（184 条测试）。
- 在真实终端（Linux，tmux 100×24）里驱动一个正文足够长、会在小终端溢出的抓取类确认。预期看到：连续的正文前缀、计数的隐藏行、`URLs to fetch:` 区块及其目标地址、问题行、四个选项，以及调出提示——全部在 24 行内。随后按 `ctrl-s` 并放大窗口：完整正文出现、隐藏行消失，问题与全部选项仍可选择；此时作答仍会正常执行工具。

### 前后对比证据

组件层面：同一个 info 确认，正文为 40 段，高度预算 12 行、宽度 50 列。在 `main` 上正文既未限高也未宣告：12 行预算下帧高 86 行，问题行落在第 82 行——在任何真实终端里都在折叠线之下。在本 PR 头部（即修复的第一版）帧被限到 12 行、问题行在第 8 行，但裁切是无声的：屏幕上没有任何东西说明大部分正文已经消失。第二轮保持同样的 12 行，并宣告这次裁切：

```text
   finding 1

   finding 2

   ... last 75 lines hidden ...

 Do you want to proceed?

 › 1. Yes, allow once
   2. No, suggest changes (esc)
```

这行宣告要用一行正文来换：PR 头部的第 6 行正文显示 `finding 3`，第二轮在同一位置显示被隐藏的行数。

真实终端 100×24，同一 mock 模型与同一页面，当前工作树：

```text
     Fetch content from http://127.0.0.1:8765/page and process with: Part 1: Summarise this
     page for a maintainer who has never seen it. Cover: what the page documents; which
     subsystems it names; every caveat it states about ordering, concurrency, and failure
     handling; the exact wording of any warning about data loss; the migration steps in order;
      the rollback path; the benchmark table and what each column measures; the deprecation
     notices with their dates; the list of configuration keys it mentions and the default of
     each; the examples it shows and the assumptions they make; anything that contradicts
     ... last 29 lines hidden ...

     URLs to fetch:
      - http://127.0.0.1:8765/page

   Do you want to proceed?

   › 1. Yes, allow once
     2. Always allow fetch from 127.0.0.1 in this project
     3. Always allow fetch from 127.0.0.1 for this user
     4. No, suggest changes (esc)

Press ctrl-s to show more lines
```

在本 PR 任何改动之前的同一棵树上，同一场景会把正文区渲染成空白，并在顶部截断工具调用标题：过高的帧在这个终端里同样会丢失自己的顶部行。这也是报告中所描述的现象（问题行在折叠线之下）没有在 24 行的真实终端里复现的原因；该缺陷在组件层面被证实：同一帧在 12 行预算下实测 86 行，问题行在第 82 行；而只把对话框组件还原，就会让 76 条测试中的 15 条变红。

在确认待作答时按 `ctrl-s`，再把窗口放大到 60 行，正文的三个结束标记全部渲染，隐藏行消失，问题与四个选项仍然可选择。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS    | ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows   | ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux    | ✅   |

### 运行环境（可选）

单元测试（vitest，关闭覆盖率）外加一个 tmux 会话，对接本地 OpenAI 兼容的 mock 模型；无沙箱、无真实模型调用。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：预算很紧时，目标地址优先于解释文字，因此抓取类确认可能显示 0 行说明正文。这是有意为之——用户仍能看到将被授权的是哪些主机、有多少说明被隐藏，并且可以把余下内容调出来。无论是否使用调出路径，问题与选项都可见。
- 已知限制（如实记录，本次未修）：在「调出后的帧放不进当前终端高度」的情况下按调出快捷键，会移除隐藏行并显示空白行，因为过高的帧会丢失自己的顶部行——这一行为早于本 PR，且未被本 PR 改变。在 Markdown 渲染器内部被裁切的计划正文带的是该渲染器自己的提示，而不是本对话框的计数页脚，也不会点亮快捷键提示；计划分支改为始终渲染自己的 `o open full plan in editor` 行。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：由 hook 驱动的长确认理由，以及异常冗长的 MCP 工具名，仅有单元测试覆盖——没有内置工具会产生多地址确认，也没有真实服务器会把工具名取得那么长。专门用于向用户提问的对话框由其自身组件渲染，本次改动未涉及。
- 有意延后（以保持本 PR 的原始范围）：紧凑模式下 `exec` 正文的具体钳制算法、登记溢出的共享辅助函数、隐藏行数文案的第五份副本、以及每次渲染都测量换行行数的开销。这些在此登记以免被静默忽略，各自适合作为后续 PR。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。选项、命令、快捷键与公开类型均未改动；唯一可见的差异是确认对话框在其高度预算内渲染什么内容。

设计文档：[简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-14-confirmation-body-height-budget.zh-CN.md) · [English](docs/design/2026-11-14-confirmation-body-height-budget.md)。

## 关联 Issue

相关且均已关闭：#6867、#7001。本 PR 不关闭任何 issue。

</details>

prs.title: fix(web-shell): bottom-sheet model picker on touch screens
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On touch devices and narrow viewports, the composer model control now opens as a bottom sheet instead of a small popover with a nested side submenu. Thinking and effort controls stay visible in the sheet, and a Model row shows the current selection. Tapping that row opens a floating card anchored 8px above it with search, refresh, and full-width model names. Selecting a model dismisses only the card, so reasoning adjustments can continue before the user taps Done or outside the sheet. Desktop popover behavior, including select-to-close, is unchanged.

## Why it's needed

On phones, the model list opened as a right-side popover next to the reasoning panel. The panel took about 262px and the nested list about 108px, leaving roughly 42px for a model label. Entries sharing a prefix (for example different providers of the same model) were visually indistinguishable, and the nested popover could also be pushed off-screen on narrow viewports. The mobile composer already uses bottom sheets for other menus, so this brings model selection in line with that pattern.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Serve the Web Shell and open it in a desktop viewport. Open the model control: the reasoning popover and right-side model list behave exactly as before, and selecting a model closes the popover.
2. Emulate a touch phone (for example 412×915 with touch enabled) and reload so the touch media query is re-evaluated. Open the model control: a bottom sheet appears with Thinking, Effort, a Model row, and a Done button.
3. Tap the Model row: a floating rounded card opens directly above it (8px gap) with search and full model names; long names wrap instead of truncating.
4. Select a different model: only the card closes, the sheet stays open, and the Model row plus the composer chip reflect the new model.
5. Change the effort or toggle thinking while the sheet is open, then tap Done: the sheet closes and the chip shows the updated model and effort.
6. Focused tests: `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/ChatEditor.test.tsx` (295 tests, including a new bottom-sheet case covering expand, select-keeps-sheet-open, collapse, and Done).

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (touch emulation): model labels rendered at ~42px and truncated; same-prefix models were indistinguishable. After: the floating card gives labels ~342px with no truncation, measured `truncated: false` for every row, and the card-to-row gap measures 8px.

Before/after screenshots and the full Playwright log are attached in the E2E comment below. Desktop after-capture confirms the nested popover is pixel-identical in behavior (labels unchanged at 214px).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

`node packages/cli/dist/index.js serve --port 4171` from this branch; Playwright Chromium contexts (touch 412×915 and desktop 1280×900).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the new sheet applies only when the viewport matches a coarse-pointer or narrow media query; the approval-mode popover deliberately keeps its existing presentation.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux were not run locally; other composer menus are unchanged.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. On touch devices, selecting a model now keeps the sheet open (Done closes it) instead of closing immediately; this is the intended interaction change.

## Linked Issues

N/A

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的内容

在触屏设备和窄视口下，composer 的模型控件现在改为底部 Sheet，而不是一个小弹层加嵌套侧面子菜单。Thinking 和 Effort 控件保留在 Sheet 中，Model 行显示当前选中的模型。点击该行会在其正上方 8px 处打开一张悬浮卡片，内含搜索、刷新和完整宽度的模型名称。选中模型只关闭卡片，因此用户可以继续调整推理相关选项，再点击「完成」或面板外部关闭 Sheet。桌面端弹层行为（包括选中即关闭）保持不变。

## 为什么需要

在手机上，模型列表此前以右侧弹层形式开在推理面板旁边。面板约占 262px，嵌套列表约 108px，模型标签只剩约 42px。前缀相同的条目（例如同一模型的不同提供方）在视觉上无法区分，而且嵌套弹层在窄视口下还可能被挤出屏幕。移动端 composer 的其他菜单已经使用底部 Sheet，本次改动让模型选择与这一模式保持一致。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 启动 Web Shell 并在桌面视口打开。打开模型控件：推理弹层和右侧模型列表行为与之前完全一致，选中模型后弹层关闭。
2. 仿真触屏手机（例如 412×915 并开启触摸）并刷新页面，使触屏媒体查询重新求值。打开模型控件：出现包含 Thinking、Effort、Model 行和「完成」按钮的底部 Sheet。
3. 点击 Model 行：在其正上方（间距 8px）打开圆角悬浮卡片，带搜索框和完整模型名；长名称换行而不是截断。
4. 选择另一个模型：只有卡片关闭，Sheet 保持打开，Model 行和 composer chip 显示新模型。
5. 在 Sheet 打开时修改 Effort 或切换 Thinking，然后点击「完成」：Sheet 关闭，chip 显示更新后的模型和推理强度。
6. 聚焦测试：`cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/ChatEditor.test.tsx`（295 个测试，包含新增的底部 Sheet 用例，覆盖展开、选中后面板保持打开、收起和完成）。

### 证据（前后对比）

修复前（触屏仿真）：模型标签仅约 42px 且被截断，同前缀模型无法区分。修复后：悬浮卡片中标签约 342px，所有行实测 `truncated: false`，卡片与 Model 行间距实测 8px。

前后截图和完整 Playwright 日志见下方 E2E 评论。桌面端修复后截图确认嵌套弹层行为不变（标签仍为 214px）。

### 测试平台

macOS ✅；Windows、Linux 未在本地运行。

### 环境（可选）

在本分支运行 `node packages/cli/dist/index.js serve --port 4171`；Playwright Chromium 上下文（触屏 412×915 与桌面 1280×900）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：新 Sheet 仅在匹配粗指针或窄屏媒体查询时启用；审批模式弹层刻意保持原有展示方式。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：Windows 和 Linux 未在本地运行；其他 composer 菜单不变。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。触屏设备上选中模型现在保持 Sheet 打开（由「完成」关闭），而非立即关闭，这是预期的交互变更。

## 关联 Issue

无

</details>

prs.title: test(channels): pin the managed DingTalk lifecycle, settings, and export surfaces
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Lands the test-only residuals tracked in #17173 for the managed DingTalk adapter, each pinning an existing guard that previously had no witness or a witness that could not fail. The CJK byte-clamp witness now lands the byte budget mid-code-point (a leading ASCII byte makes the remainder non-divisible) and asserts the exact maximal-fit result, with a second astral case pinning whole-code-point fits for 4-byte characters; the old self-referential expectation is gone. The adapter's default polling is driven without the `pollLoop` option, the `stop()` abort of a parked ~24.8-day poll delay is exercised (the witness flushes the first tick so the loop is genuinely parked before disconnect), and `controlPlane.disconnect()` on teardown is asserted. The state store's 0600 file inside a 0700 directory is pinned, credential hygiene (embedded CR/LF/NUL, blank values, trimmed edges) and the `privatePolicy: "pairing"` refusal get dedicated cases, the package's managed export surface reds when the export block is reverted, and the channel command tree's registration of both managed subcommands reds when a `.command()` line is dropped.

## Why it's needed

These are the deferred coverage/hygiene suggestions from the #17136 reviews (R2-6/R2-7/R2-9/R2-10/R2-11, R3 export surface, R4 disconnect and state modes). Every one of them described a guard whose removal left the suite green — the exact class of silent regression the mutation-verified approach of the earlier batches exists to prevent. No production behavior changes; the diff is four test files.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/channels/dingtalk` run `npx vitest run` (968 tests) and from `packages/cli` run `npx vitest run src/commands/channel.test.ts`. To confirm a pin is load-bearing, remove its guard and re-run: an off-by-one in the clamp walk reds both clamp witnesses; `pollLoop ?? false` reds the default-polling case; deleting `this.abort?.abort()` makes the shutdown case time out; deleting the `controlPlane.disconnect()` call reds the teardown case; loosening either state mode reds the mode case; dropping the credential control-character check or the pairing throw reds the settings cases; reverting the managed export block reds the export-surface case; removing `.command(managedDingtalkCommand)` reds exactly the dingtalk registration case while email stays green. All were run and observed red, then reverted. One documented equivalent mutation: splitting the clamp walk by UTF-16 units instead of code points stays green because the escaped-byte budget itself rejects any mid-surrogate cut (a lone surrogate costs six escaped bytes, more than the sub-4-byte remainder) — the exact-fit expectation is what discriminates there.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only change. Local verification: dingtalk 968/968 green, the CLI channel suites green, `tsc --build` clean for both packages, ESLint and Prettier clean on all four files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only. Node 22, pnpm 11.24.0. Note: the local CLI coverage toolchain (test-exclude/minimatch) emits a pre-existing brace-expansion unhandled error on this machine, identical on unmodified baseline files and absent with coverage disabled; CI does not exhibit it.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none behavioral — no production code changes. The shutdown witness uses fake timers plus a microtask flush to park the loop deterministically; the default-polling witness uses a 5s wait window against the 2s default interval.
- Not validated / out of scope: the remaining #17173 residuals (stream/deps layer test gaps, the write-failure guard placement, the SDK heartbeat timer cleanup, and the two connect-lifecycle design items) stay tracked on the issue.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #17173 (partial batch; the issue stays open for the remaining residuals). Follow-up to #17136, #17351, and #17396.

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): publish the managed /loop skill variant by profile
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Publishes the Managed `/loop` skill variant that the fixed-interval schedule slice (#17088) and the self-paced wakeup slice (#16835) both deferred as a shared touchpoint. A Managed Session on a loop-bearing tool profile now receives a `loop` skill whose body teaches the same parsing, interval-to-cron table, and subcommands as the bundled local skill, but with Managed semantics (always durable, runs until cancelled, no 7-day expiry) and naming only the creators the profile declares. The variant is injected server-side at creation admission, selected purely by the Session's tool profile.

## Why it's needed

Until now the Hosted skill catalog carried no loop skill, so a Managed Session's model could not drive `/loop` even though the tool surface (`cron_create` / `cron_list` / `cron_delete` / `loop_wakeup`) and the scanner were already merged. The bundled local skill carries local semantics (session-only default, 7-day auto-expiry) that are wrong for a Managed schedule. This closes open question 4 of the schedule design: which carrier ships the variant and how it degrades across profiles.

The design's original "mirror the local BundledSkillLoader" wording could not be implemented literally — the managed skill wire format has no `allowedTools` field and skill admission consults no gate today. Instead the variant is composed from the bundled source by a TypeScript generator (one committed body per profile shape: union / cron-only / wakeup-only), pinned byte-for-byte by a parity test, and selected by profile in Java. The deployment gates are operation gates that leave the tool declaration in place, so they do not condition the body.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Body parity: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/skills/bundled/loop/managed-loop-skill.test.ts` — each committed asset equals `buildManagedLoopBody(profile)` byte-for-byte; the union body uses Managed durable/expiry wording; cron-only never names `loop_wakeup`/`LoopWakeup`; wakeup-only never names `cron_create`/`CronCreate`. Editing the bundled `SKILL.md` shared content reddens all three parity cases (mutation verified, byte-identical restore).
- Selector: `ManagedLoopSkillTest` (verification module) — each loop profile maps to its asset; non-loop profiles (files/1, files/3, shell/1, mcp/1, team-lead/1, read/1, null) receive nothing.
- Admission: `ManagedSessionCreationSkillsTest#injectsTheManagedLoopSkillByProfileEvenWithNoCallerSkills` — a files/4 creation with an empty caller catalog still receives the loop skill (widened save guard); a files/1 creation receives none; a caller-imported local `loop` skill conflicts on the duplicate name. Removing the injection reddens this test (mutation verified, byte-identical restore).
- Real MySQL: the same admission test runs on MySQL 8.4 via the inherited `ManagedExtensionCreationMySqlIT` (11/11 green against a disposable MySQL 8.4 container).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI (skill publication, admission, generated assets, tests, docs).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local H2 + a disposable MySQL 8.4 container (`managed_agent_test?createDatabaseIfNotExist=true`), the Managed Agent checkstyle gate, and the core vitest parity test. No real-model turn.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the variant body is model-facing wording; the parity test pins each generated body to the bundled source, and the admission test pins the injection. The two paths interleave throughout the bundled body, so the composition lives in the TypeScript generator (not Java string surgery); Java is a pure selector.
- Not validated / out of scope: a real `/loop` model-turn E2E remains a separate effort. The shell/3 and shell/4 admission paths are covered by the selector unit test (the shared Harness mock only negotiates the shell/1 lifecycle); files/4 exercises the full injection wiring on H2 and real MySQL.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The injection is additive; existing caller-skill behavior is unchanged (the save guard widens from "caller skills non-empty" to "effective catalog non-empty").

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #17088 and #16835 (the shared skill touchpoint). Resolves open question 4 of `docs/design/2026-11-10-managed-loop-schedule.md`. No closing issue.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做什么

发布固定间隔调度切片（#17088）与自定步调唤醒切片（#16835）共同延后的 Managed `/loop` skill 变体（共享触点）。运行在携带 loop 工具 profile 的 Managed Session 现在会收到一个 `loop` skill，其 body 教授与 bundled 本地 skill 相同的解析、interval-to-cron 表与子命令，但用 Managed 语义（恒 durable、运行至取消、无 7 天过期），且只点名该 profile 声明的 creator。变体在创建准入时服务端注入，纯按 Session 的 tool profile 选择。

## 为什么需要

此前 Hosted skill 目录没有 loop skill，因此即便工具面（`cron_create` / `cron_list` / `cron_delete` / `loop_wakeup`）与 scanner 已合入，Managed Session 的模型仍驱动不了 `/loop`。bundled 本地 skill 携带本地语义（session-only 默认、7 天自动过期），对 Managed 调度是错误的。本 PR 解决调度设计的开放问题 4：哪个载体承载变体、如何按 profile 降级。

设计原文"镜像本地 BundledSkillLoader"无法照字面实现——managed skill wire 格式没有 `allowedTools` 字段，且今天 skill 准入不咨询任何门。改为：TypeScript 生成器从 bundled 源组合变体（每个 profile 形状一个提交 body：union / cron-only / wakeup-only），一致性测试逐字节钉住，Java 按 profile 选择。部署门是保留工具声明的操作门，故不作为 body 的条件。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

- body 一致性：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/skills/bundled/loop/managed-loop-skill.test.ts`——每个提交资产与 `buildManagedLoopBody(profile)` 逐字节相等；union body 用 Managed durable/expiry 措辞；cron-only 绝不点名 `loop_wakeup`/`LoopWakeup`；wakeup-only 绝不点名 `cron_create`/`CronCreate`。改 bundled `SKILL.md` 共享内容会使三个一致性用例红（已变异验证，字节级还原）。
- 选择器：`ManagedLoopSkillTest`（verification 模块）——每个 loop profile 映射到其资产；非 loop profile（files/1、files/3、shell/1、mcp/1、team-lead/1、read/1、null）不得到。
- 准入：`ManagedSessionCreationSkillsTest#injectsTheManagedLoopSkillByProfileEvenWithNoCallerSkills`——files/4 创建即使 caller 目录为空仍收到 loop skill（放宽的 save 守卫）；files/1 创建不得到；caller 导入的本地 `loop` skill 因重名冲突。删除注入会使该测试红（已变异验证，字节级还原）。
- 真实 MySQL：同一准入测试经继承的 `ManagedExtensionCreationMySqlIT` 在 MySQL 8.4 上运行（对一次性 MySQL 8.4 容器 11/11 绿）。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A——非 UI（skill 发布、准入、生成资产、测试、文档）。

### 测试平台

🍏 macOS ⚠️ 未测 · 🪟 Windows ⚠️ 未测 · 🐧 Linux ✅ 已测。

### 环境

本地 H2 + 一次性 MySQL 8.4 容器（`managed_agent_test?createDatabaseIfNotExist=true`）、Managed Agent checkstyle 门、core vitest 一致性测试。无真实模型回合。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：变体 body 是面向模型的措辞；一致性测试把每个生成 body 钉回 bundled 源，准入测试钉住注入。两条路径在 bundled body 中深度交织，故组合住在 TypeScript 生成器（非 Java 字符串外科手术），Java 是纯选择器。
- 未验证/范围外：真实 `/loop` 模型回合 E2E 仍是独立工作。shell/3 与 shell/4 准入路径由选择器单测覆盖（共享 Harness mock 只协商 shell/1 生命周期）；files/4 在 H2 与真实 MySQL 上演练完整注入接线。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。注入是增量的；既有 caller-skill 行为不变（save 守卫从"caller skills 非空"放宽为"effective 目录非空"）。

## 关联

#17088 与 #16835 的跟进（共享 skill 触点）。解决 `docs/design/2026-11-10-managed-loop-schedule.md` 的开放问题 4。无关闭 issue。

prs.title: fix(web-shell): show notification guides only for the browser's OS
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Task notifications popover in the Web Shell lists the system-level setup steps to try when reminders do not appear. It used to render the macOS guide and the Windows guide side by side, unconditionally, so every user saw instructions for an operating system they were not on.

This PR detects the browser's operating system and renders only the matching guide. Phones and tablets get neither guide, because none of the steps exist there. Unrecognized desktop platforms keep both guides rather than showing none, so the change cannot hide help from anyone.

## Why it's needed

Closes #16363. The popover is the place a user lands when notifications are not working, and it is where they are told what to check in their OS settings. On macOS the Windows steps are noise, and on Windows the macOS steps are noise; both point at settings that do not exist on the user's machine. Filtering by the client OS keeps that fallback path direct.

The platform is read from `navigator.platform` and `navigator.maxTouchPoints`, so it reflects the machine running the browser, not the daemon, container or server that hosts the Web Shell. This matters because the Web Shell is commonly served from a remote daemon whose OS is unrelated to the user's.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`packages/web-shell/client/components/messages/BrowserNotificationControl.test.tsx` asserts the rendered guide headings for a given `navigator.platform` and `maxTouchPoints`:

| `navigator.platform` | touch points | Guides shown |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Win32` | 0 | Windows |
| `MacIntel` | 0 | macOS |
| `iPhone` | 0 and 5 | none |
| `MacIntel` | 5 | none |
| `Linux armv8l` | 5 | none |
| `Linux x86_64` | 0 | macOS and Windows |
| unset / empty | 0 | macOS and Windows |

Run the component tests from `packages/web-shell`:

```bash
npx vitest run client/components/messages/BrowserNotificationControl.test.tsx
```

31 cases pass at `2e9be37c`: 15 pre-existing at the branch base (`45cde869`; unchanged at `main` `3ec010e4`) plus 16 added — 12 platform-table rows (including `Linux armv8l`/1 point, and `iPad`/`iPod` at 0), 3 "does not point at steps it does not render" cases, and 1 heading/body pairing case.

### Evidence (Before & After)

I wrote a standalone reproduction against unmodified `main` at `92bed7ee` before touching the component. It rendered the popover with `navigator.platform` stubbed to `Win32` and to `MacIntel` and asserted the guide headings:

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'macOS', 'Windows' ] to deeply equal [ 'Windows' ]
AssertionError: expected [ 'macOS', 'Windows' ] to deeply equal [ 'macOS' ]
```

Both guides rendered on both platforms, which reproduces the issue.

As a negative control for the fix itself, I reverted only the component change and re-ran the platform table:

```
× lists only the guides for Win32 (touch points 0)
× lists only the guides for MacIntel (touch points 0)
× lists only the guides for iPhone (touch points 5)
...
```

The Linux and unset rows pass either way by design, since they keep the pre-existing behavior.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

Linux and Windows were not run locally. Their platform strings are covered by the unit table and by CI's Linux Chromium, not by a local browser on those systems.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests via `vitest` (jsdom). Prettier is clean for the changed files at `f74df684`. ESLint and `tsc --noEmit` were run for the package at `a378b77a` and are unchanged by this head, which touches only a Markdown sentence and an e2e comment.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the rule reads `navigator.platform` (deprecated and frozen in some browsers) plus `maxTouchPoints`, and falls back to "Apple device name says mobile" for a touch-less `iPhone`/`iPad`/`iPod`. After the touch rule, the effective match is Windows by name, Apple by name, and any non-Windows touch device as mobile; everything else keeps both guides, so a wrong or missing value cannot hide the instructions.
- Not validated / out of scope: not verified in a real browser against a live `qwen serve` daemon; verification is at the jsdom unit-test level. Linux and Windows were not exercised locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No new i18n keys, no public API change. The existing translation strings for both guides are reused unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Closes #16363

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

Web Shell 的「任务通知」浮层里，列着「没收到提醒时该检查什么」的系统级设置步骤。此前它把 macOS 和 Windows 两份指引并排、无条件地渲染出来，所以每个用户都会看到不属于自己操作系统的那一份。

这个 PR 检测浏览器所在的操作系统，只渲染匹配的那一份。手机和平板两份都不显示，因为那些步骤在移动端并不存在。无法识别的桌面平台会保留两份而不是一份都不显示，因此这个改动不会让任何人看不到帮助。

## 为什么需要

关闭 #16363。用户发现通知不工作时就会打开这个浮层，也正是在这里被告知要去系统设置里检查什么。在 macOS 上 Windows 的步骤是干扰，在 Windows 上 macOS 的步骤是干扰；两者都指向用户机器上并不存在的设置。按客户端操作系统过滤，能让这条兜底路径更直接。

平台信息读自 `navigator.platform` 与 `navigator.maxTouchPoints`，因此反映的是运行浏览器的那台机器，而不是托管 Web Shell 的 daemon、容器或服务器。这一点很重要，因为 Web Shell 常常由远端 daemon 提供服务，而那个 daemon 的操作系统与用户无关。

## 审阅者验证方式

`packages/web-shell/client/components/messages/BrowserNotificationControl.test.tsx` 针对给定的 `navigator.platform` 与 `maxTouchPoints` 断言渲染出的指引标题：

| `navigator.platform` | 触摸点数 | 显示的指引 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Win32` | 0 | Windows |
| `MacIntel` | 0 | macOS |
| `iPhone` | 0 与 5 | 无 |
| `MacIntel` | 5 | 无 |
| `Linux armv8l` | 5 | 无 |
| `Linux x86_64` | 0 | macOS 与 Windows |
| 未设置 / 空 | 0 | macOS 与 Windows |

在 `packages/web-shell` 下运行组件测试：

```bash
npx vitest run client/components/messages/BrowserNotificationControl.test.tsx
```

`2e9be37c` 上 31 个用例全部通过：分支起点 `45cde869` 原有 15 个（`main` `3ec010e4` 未改动该文件），新增 16 个——平台表 12 条（含 `Linux armv8l`/1 点、`iPad`/`iPod`/0 点）、「不指向未渲染步骤」3 条、标题正文配对 1 条。

### 证据（修改前后）

在改动组件之前，我先针对未经修改的 `main`（`92bed7ee`）写了一个独立复现。它把 `navigator.platform` 分别打桩为 `Win32` 和 `MacIntel` 渲染浮层，并断言指引标题：

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'macOS', 'Windows' ] to deeply equal [ 'Windows' ]
AssertionError: expected [ 'macOS', 'Windows' ] to deeply equal [ 'macOS' ]
```

两个平台上两份指引都渲染了，问题得到复现。

作为修复本身的负向对照，我只回退组件改动后重跑平台表：

```
× lists only the guides for Win32 (touch points 0)
× lists only the guides for MacIntel (touch points 0)
× lists only the guides for iPhone (touch points 5)
...
```

Linux 与未设置两行在两种情况下都通过，这是设计使然——它们保留的是原有行为。

### 测试平台

|     系统   | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

Linux 和 Windows 未在本地运行。它们的平台字符串由单元表和 CI 的 Linux Chromium 覆盖，不是本地这两个系统上的浏览器。

### 环境（可选）

通过 `vitest`（jsdom）运行单元测试。`f74df684` 上改动文件的 Prettier 检查干净。ESLint 与 `tsc --noEmit` 是在 `a378b77a` 上跑的，本 head 只改了一句 Markdown 和一段 e2e 注释，不影响它们。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：规则读 `navigator.platform`（已被废弃，部分浏览器中已冻结）加 `maxTouchPoints`，并对无触摸点的 `iPhone`/`iPad`/`iPod` 保留「苹果设备名即移动端」的兜底。加入触摸规则后，实际匹配是：按名字命中 Windows、按名字命中苹果、其余非 Windows 触摸设备视为移动端；剩下的一律保留两份指引，因此错误或缺失的值不会导致指引消失。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：没有在真实浏览器中对接运行中的 `qwen serve` daemon 验证；验证停留在 jsdom 单元测试层面。Linux 与 Windows 未在本地运行。

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): resolve external execution actor through child session lineage
prs.body:
## What

In a workspace-bound external-files (`hosted-workspace-external-files/1`) deployment, a content-only suite child Session's first Turn fails terminally with 409 `workspace_unavailable` before any Runtime binding is acquired, and the parent Turn waits until its deadline.

## Root cause

`WorkspaceAttachmentAuthorizer.externalExecutionActor` resolved the execution actor with a single-row query pinned to `parent_session_id IS NULL`. A child Session is a real row in the same workspace, generation and storage whose `parent_session_id` is non-null, so the query matched zero rows and admission threw. The resident path (`inheritedExecutionActor`) already walks the committed lineage hop by hop; the external path never did.

## Fix

Walk the committed lineage to the parentless root, keeping the same per-hop tenant / workspace / generation / storage checks as `inheritedExecutionActor`, bounded by a visited set, and preferring the explicit owner with the same `COALESCE(owner_actor_key, creator_actor_key)` the original single-row read used. No admission check is relaxed.

## Verification

- `WorkspaceLifecycleStoreTest` 70/70 PASS (69 existing + 1 new)
- Mutation verification: reverting to the single-row read makes exactly the new test red with the same `workspace_unavailable` verdict; restoring the fix returns 70/70 green.
- Byte-identical restore after mutation confirmed with `cmp`.

Fixes #17407
