prs.title: feat(core): retain the latest complete operation during compaction
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Retain the latest complete operation verbatim after compaction and summarize only the older history. Keep tool calls and results together, preserve subsequent input, and distinguish the retained operation from the generated summary when resuming or rewinding a session. Retained operations keep their original turn ownership so deleting a message group also removes its raw retained replies and tool results.

## Why it's needed

A full-history summary can discard the exact edit arguments, test failure or result the agent just observed. This is a bounded migration of the response-group idea from `v1.0.0-preview`, not a return to the percentage-based tail retention removed in #4599. The retained operation must fit both a 20,000-token cap and 20% of the configured context window; incomplete, ambiguous, ownerless, oversized and overflow-recovery cases retain full-summary behavior.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that both summarization paths receive only older history; complete parallel calls/results and original signatures survive; pending results are submitted once; and unsafe or oversized operations fall back. After checkpoint/resume, delete the owning text or tool message group, with and without a following prompt: raw retained data should disappear while the generated summary and unrelated input remain. Confirm that merged adjacent inputs and repeated compaction retain the correct owner. After fast compression removes restored images, deleting the retained operation must still preserve the generated summary and unrelated input. Verify that prompt-only token accounting includes retained latest output exactly once, that the inflation comparison uses the same before/after basis, and that truly inflated candidates are still rejected.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Review reproduced checkpoint/deletion failures, false-inflation failures and a fast-compression boundary failure. These now pass through the actual compression and persistence consumers with inference mocked. Hosted live-tool-turn resume no longer duplicates a pending result after a retained operation; unowned injected input and coalesced ownership use full-summary fallback. Truncated or failed summaries report the same prompt-plus-output baseline. Existing bounded-retention, pairing, recovery and persistence coverage also passes. No live-model quality or latency improvement is claimed.

The updated tree passed on macOS with Node 22.17.0: 1,458 core tests across nine focused suites, 147 hosted compression/recovery tests, the full repository build, production bundle, aggregate typecheck including integration-test types, and changed-file ESLint/Prettier and whitespace checks. Build used a 6 GB Node heap.

### Tested on

- macOS: focused automated tests and repository verification.
- Linux: required CI passed for the updated head; remaining non-required checks are still running.
- Windows: not tested locally.

### Environment

Local checkout, Node.js and repository dependencies. Deterministic regression tests mock inference; live-provider end-to-end behavior was not tested.

## Risk & Scope

- Main tradeoff: a bounded amount of exact recent context reduces the achievable compression ratio; prefix-only summarization can reuse a shorter cache prefix.
- Not validated: live-model task quality, latency and provider-specific end-to-end behavior. General restoration-budget work in #16895 is out of scope.
- Existing provider anchors can undercount tool results or unanswered input added after the last request until fresh usage arrives; broader anchor accounting remains out of scope.
- No new setting or breaking configuration migration. Existing inflation and hard-send guards remain in place.
- Design: [English](docs/design/retain-latest-compaction-operation.md) / [简体中文](docs/design/retain-latest-compaction-operation.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Related architectural context: #4599. Separate budget work: #16895.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动内容

压缩后原样保留最近一组完整操作，仅摘要更早历史。工具调用及结果成组保留，同时保留之后的输入；恢复或回退会话时，明确区分真实保留操作与生成的摘要。保留操作携带原轮次归属，删除消息组时也会删除对应的原始回复和工具结果。

## 为什么需要

全量摘要可能丢失模型刚看到的编辑参数、测试失败原文或工具结果。这是对 `v1.0.0-preview` response group 思路的有限迁移，不是恢复 #4599 移除的百分比尾部保留。完整操作必须同时满足 20,000 token 与配置上下文窗口 20% 的上限；不完整、歧义、无法识别归属、过大以及溢出恢复场景仍采用全量摘要。

## 审阅测试计划

### 如何验证

确认两条摘要路径只接收旧历史；完整并行调用/结果及原始签名保留；待提交结果仅发送一次；不安全或过大的操作正确回退。检查点恢复后，在有、无后续输入的情况下删除操作所属的文本或工具消息组：原始保留数据应被删除，生成摘要及无关输入保留。确认相邻输入合并和重复压缩后归属仍正确。快速压缩清除恢复图片后，删除保留操作仍应保留生成摘要和无关输入。验证仅含 prompt 的计数只补入一次保留的最新输出，膨胀比较使用一致的前后口径，并且仍拒绝真正膨胀的候选。

### 改动前后证据

审查复现了检查点/删除失败、膨胀误判以及快速压缩边界丢失问题。这些场景现在均通过实际压缩和持久化消费者验证，推理使用 mock。Hosted 活跃工具轮恢复不再重复提交保留操作后的待处理结果；无归属注入输入或合并导致的归属歧义均回退全量摘要。摘要截断或失败时也统一返回 prompt 加输出的计数。原有预算、配对、恢复和持久化覆盖也通过。不宣称已验证实模质量或延迟提升。

更新后的代码在 macOS、Node 22.17.0 上通过：core 九个定向测试文件共 1,458 项、hosted 压缩与恢复 147 项、全仓构建、production bundle、包含集成测试类型的全仓类型检查，以及改动文件 ESLint/Prettier 和空白检查。构建使用 6 GB Node 堆。

### 测试平台

- macOS：针对性自动化测试与全仓验证。
- Linux：更新后 head 的必需 CI 已通过，剩余非必需检查仍在运行。
- Windows：本地未测试。

### 环境

本地仓库、Node.js 与项目依赖。确定性回归中 mock 推理；未验证真实 provider 端到端行为。

## 风险与范围

- 主要权衡：有限的原样近期上下文会降低压缩比例；仅摘要前缀可能缩短可复用缓存前缀。
- 未验证：实模任务质量、延迟与 provider 端到端行为。#16895 的通用恢复预算工作不在范围内。
- 既有 provider 锚点可能低估最后一次请求后追加的工具结果或未回答输入，直到新的用量返回；更广泛的锚点记账不在本次范围内。
- 无新增设置或破坏性配置迁移，现有膨胀与发送硬限制检查保留。
- 设计：[English](docs/design/retain-latest-compaction-operation.md) / [简体中文](docs/design/retain-latest-compaction-operation.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联内容

架构背景：#4599。独立预算工作：#16895。

prs.title: feat(web-shell): resume an interrupted turn when a session loads
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a daemon or environment restart leaves a persisted turn interrupted, the Web Shell used to restore the session idle behind the Continue button, so a task that was running when the machine or container went away stayed stopped until someone opened that session, noticed the banner, and pressed it. Loading a session now resumes an interrupted user prompt through the existing `POST /session/:id/continue` route.

The behavior is opt-in through a new `DaemonSessionProvider` prop, `autoContinueInterruptedTurn`, enabled for the main session and for split-view panes.

The automatic resume is limited to `interrupted_prompt`, the kind the daemon produces when a user prompt was cut off. `interrupted_turn` — a turn cut off mid-tool-call — is deliberately left to the banner: its repair synthesizes the missing tool results and hands control back to the model, which is why the recovery plan marks it `canAutoContinue: false` / `requiresUserConfirmation: true`. A turn the user stopped is never resumed either: the daemon reports it as `clean`, or, when the cancellation reason could not be persisted, attaches a `cancellationConfirmationId`.

The resume is also fenced to the recovery snapshot the load itself published, so a `turn_error` that arrives later and refreshes that snapshot with `canContinue: true` does not re-run the turn the user just watched fail. Each load snapshot is claimed at most once, which keeps a rerender or a StrictMode double-invoke from enqueueing two turns.

## Why it's needed

#6695 records the gap: PR #5030 added `POST /session/:id/continue`, which classifies persisted history and continues an interrupted prompt or dangling tool turn without inserting a synthetic "continue" user message, but `DaemonSessionProvider` never called it. The reporter reproduced both shapes against a deterministic OpenAI-compatible fake model — a SIGKILL during an active prompt, and a model stream that ends with empty text — and both returned `accepted: true` with `interruption: "interrupted_prompt"` once the route was called manually. Only the Web Shell orchestration was missing.

The issue also states the boundary this change keeps: explicit user cancellation must remain terminal, incremental SSE reconnection must not invoke continuation, and completed or already-active sessions must not produce a new model request.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The change is provider-level, so the tests are the reproduction. Run the new suite and confirm the positive case resumes and the four negative cases do not:

```
cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx -t "autoContinueInterruptedTurn"
```

Expected: 7 passed. Each negative case shares the same `replay_complete`-then-idle event stream as the positive case, so a "not called" assertion cannot pass merely because the load never finished catching up. I checked that by deleting each guard in turn and confirming the matching test fails:

- remove `recovery.kind !== 'interrupted_prompt'` → `leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button` fails
- remove `connection.catchingUp` → `does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying` fails
- remove `recovery !== autoContinueLoadRecoveryRef.current` → `does not resume a turn that fails after the load` fails

For a manual check on a running daemon: start `qwen serve` with a persistent runtime directory, submit a long prompt, `SIGKILL` the daemon, restart it, and load the same session in the Web Shell. Without this change the session comes back idle behind the Continue button; with it the turn resumes and reaches a normal terminal state.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Provider-level only, as a transcript of the same command against the commit before and after the fix.

Before, with the effect disabled (the behaviour of the base commit for `interrupted_prompt`):

```
× continues an interrupted prompt once, without a user click
✓ leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button
✓ leaves the turn to the Continue button when the user cancelled it
✓ does nothing when the turn finished cleanly
✓ stays opt-in
✓ does not resume a turn that fails after the load
✓ does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying
Tests  1 failed | 6 passed | 529 skipped (536)
```

After:

```
✓ daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx (536 tests | 529 skipped)
Tests  7 passed | 529 skipped (536)
```

No screenshots: I did not run the Web Shell against a real daemon restart, so I have no captured before/after UI state. That reproduction is listed under "Not validated" below.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests under Node with jsdom; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` for `packages/web-shell` run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384` (the default heap OOMs on this package).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: an automatic continuation spends a model request the user did not explicitly ask for. That is the point of the feature, and it is bounded to one attempt per session load, to `interrupted_prompt` only, and to a snapshot the load itself produced. It is also opt-in per provider.
- Not validated / out of scope: no real daemon-restart reproduction against `qwen serve`, no Web Shell Playwright run, and no full `npm run build`. Whether `interrupted_turn` should ever be auto-continued is left open; the design doc currently says it should not.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The prop defaults to `false`; the two in-repo call sites opt in.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #6695

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

守护进程或环境重启后，被打断的会话在 Web Shell 里原本会停在 Continue 按钮后面等人点，于是机器或容器掉线时正在跑的任务就一直停着，直到有人打开这个会话、看到提示条、按下按钮。现在加载会话时会通过已有的 `POST /session/:id/continue` 路由自动续跑被中断的用户 prompt。

该行为通过 `DaemonSessionProvider` 新增的 `autoContinueInterruptedTurn` 属性选择性开启，主会话和分屏面板都已启用。

自动续跑只针对 `interrupted_prompt`，也就是用户 prompt 被截断时守护进程给出的那一类。`interrupted_turn`——在 tool call 中途被切断的一轮——刻意留给提示条：修复它会合成缺失的 tool 结果再把控制权交回模型，所以恢复计划把它标记为 `canAutoContinue: false` / `requiresUserConfirmation: true`。用户主动停止的一轮同样永远不会被续跑：守护进程会把它报成 `clean`，或者在取消原因没能持久化时附带 `cancellationConfirmationId`。

续跑还被限定在「本次加载自己发布的恢复快照」上，因此之后到达、并把该快照刷新成 `canContinue: true` 的 `turn_error` 不会把用户刚看着失败的那一轮重新跑一遍。每个加载快照最多被认领一次，重渲染或 StrictMode 双调用也就不会排出两轮。

## 为什么需要

#6695 记录了这个缺口：PR #5030 加了 `POST /session/:id/continue`，它能对持久化历史分类并续跑被中断的 prompt 或悬挂的 tool 轮次，且不插入合成的 "continue" 用户消息，但 `DaemonSessionProvider` 从未调用它。提报者用一个确定性的 OpenAI 兼容假模型复现了两种形态——活跃 prompt 期间 SIGKILL，以及模型流以空文本结束——只要手动调用该路由，两种都返回 `accepted: true` 与 `interruption: "interrupted_prompt"`。缺的只是 Web Shell 这一层编排。

该 issue 也写明了本次改动保持的边界：用户显式的取消必须是终态，增量 SSE 重连不能触发续跑，已完成或仍在活跃的会话不能产生新的模型请求。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

改动位于 provider 层，测试即是复现。运行新增的测试套件，确认正向用例会续跑、四个反向用例不会：

```
cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx -t "autoContinueInterruptedTurn"
```

预期：7 个通过。每个反向用例都与正向用例共用同一条「先 `replay_complete` 再空闲」的事件流，因此「未被调用」的断言不会仅仅因为加载还没追平而通过。我逐个删除守卫验证过这一点：

- 删掉 `recovery.kind !== 'interrupted_prompt'` → `leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button` 失败
- 删掉 `connection.catchingUp` → `does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying` 失败
- 删掉 `recovery !== autoContinueLoadRecoveryRef.current` → `does not resume a turn that fails after the load` 失败

在运行中的守护进程上手工检查：用持久化运行目录启动 `qwen serve`，提交一个长 prompt，`SIGKILL` 守护进程，重启之，再在 Web Shell 里加载同一个会话。没有本改动时会话会停在 Continue 按钮后空闲；有了本改动，该轮会续跑并走到正常终态。

### 证据（前后对比）

仅在 provider 层，下面是同一条命令在修复前与修复后的输出。

修复前，把该 effect 禁用（即基线提交对 `interrupted_prompt` 的行为）：

```
× continues an interrupted prompt once, without a user click
✓ leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button
✓ leaves the turn to the Continue button when the user cancelled it
✓ does nothing when the turn finished cleanly
✓ stays opt-in
✓ does not resume a turn that fails after the load
✓ does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying
Tests  1 failed | 6 passed | 529 skipped (536)
```

修复后：

```
✓ daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx (536 tests | 529 skipped)
Tests  7 passed | 529 skipped (536)
```

没有截图：我没有对着真实守护进程重启跑 Web Shell，因此没有截到前后对比的界面状态。该复现列在下文「未验证」中。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

在 Node + jsdom 下跑单元测试；`packages/web-shell` 的 `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` 需要 `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384`（默认堆在这个包上会 OOM）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：自动续跑会花掉一次用户没有显式请求的模型请求。这正是本功能的目的，并且被限制为每次会话加载一次、仅限 `interrupted_prompt`、仅限加载自身产生的快照，同时按 provider 选择开启。
- 未验证 / 范围外：没有对着 `qwen serve` 做真实守护进程重启复现，没有跑 Web Shell Playwright，没有跑完整 `npm run build`。`interrupted_turn` 是否应该自动续跑仍留待决定；设计文档目前说不应该。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。该属性默认为 `false`；仓库内两个调用点选择开启。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #6695

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): make Goal state and session navigation readable at a glance
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR makes the state of a Goal and the way to reach its session readable at a glance in the Web Shell, without touching the daemon, the SDK, or the wire format.

On the Goals page, every goal card now carries two unmistakable ways to open the goal's session in the goal's own workspace: a constant header action tinted in the interactive blue (apart from the grey edit/pause/clear controls), and a footer link that frames the session name with a message icon and an arrow, in the same blue with hover underline and a focus ring. The transcript is the goal's history, so jumping to the session is the primary way to inspect a goal — the first iteration left these affordances in the same grey as the surrounding meta and readers could not find them, so navigation now wears every conventional link cue. The status pill is tinted by lifecycle state using the same execution-status palette the cockpit and the workflow inspector already share: in-flight goals read blue and goals waiting for the user (paused, blocked, usage-limited) read amber; the palette also defines a green done tone, though completed goals are filtered out of both listings by pre-existing daemon policy, so no surface renders one today. Whenever a goal has an armed ceiling — turns, tokens, or active time — the card renders a compact progress bar per budget with the spent/ceiling figure, clamped so a spent budget reads as a full bar; the active-time bar advances with the existing one-second tick. Unbounded goals render no bars at all, and a token ceiling reported by an older daemon without a usage figure is skipped rather than drawn at zero.

The in-session goal strip gains a "View all goals" action that opens the Goals page, on both the main composer and the split-view panes; surfaces where the Goals page is unavailable render no button. The strip's status text uses the same lifecycle tint as the cards, so a goal reads the same colour everywhere. All new strings are localized in English, Simplified Chinese, and Russian.

## Why it's needed

Inspecting a goal meant hunting for the session-name text link at the far right of the card footer, the monochrome pill gave no at-a-glance sense of whether a goal was running or waiting for the user, and budget consumption was plain text among several unrelated meta items — exactly the figures a user checks to decide whether to let a goal keep running. A user who landed in a goal's session also had no way back to the aggregate Goals page without the sidebar. This PR closes those gaps with a display-only change: no new polling, no new timers, no control-semantics change.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the Web Shell against a daemon with at least one loaded session driving a goal (set one with `/goal <condition>`; arm ceilings with `/config model.goalMaxTurns=20` and `/config model.goalMaxActiveMinutes=30` before creating the goal, then restart the daemon). Open the Goals page from the sidebar.
2. Confirm each card shows a blue chat-bubble header action and a blue footer link (message icon + session name + arrow); clicking either opens that goal's session, and on a multi-workspace daemon the session opens in the goal's own workspace (the workspace badge matches). Hovering the footer link underlines the name.
3. Confirm the status pill is blue while the goal is active and amber once it is paused, blocked, or usage-limited; pause a goal from the card and watch the pill change.
4. For a goal with armed ceilings, confirm one progress bar per budget with the spent/ceiling figure, and that the active-time bar advances while the goal runs. A goal without ceilings shows no bars.
5. In the goal's session, confirm the strip above the composer shows a target icon action that opens the Goals page, and that its status text carries the same tint. Split-view panes show the same action (SplitView only mounts where project features are available); on any surface without the Goals page the button is absent.
6. Switch the theme (light/dark) and confirm the tints follow the shared palette in both.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Real browser captures (Playwright + Chromium, mock daemon, identical fixtures on both arms; the before arm asserts the new affordances are absent). Goals page with an active goal (turn/token/time ceilings armed, mid-turn) and a paused goal (turn ceiling), multi-workspace:

| --- | --- |
| ![Goals page before, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-goal-display/web-shell-goal-display/goals-page-before-light.png) | ![Goals page after, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-goal-display/web-shell-goal-display/goals-page-after-light.png) |

Dark theme, same fixture:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Goals page before, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-goal-display/web-shell-goal-display/goals-page-before-dark.png) | ![Goals page after, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-goal-display/web-shell-goal-display/goals-page-after-dark.png) |

In-session goal strip (active goal): the after arm adds the "View all goals" action and the lifecycle tint on the status text.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Goal strip before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-goal-display/web-shell-goal-display/goal-strip-before.png) | ![Goal strip after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-goal-display/web-shell-goal-display/goal-strip-after.png) |

Automated: the two goals E2E suites pass 19/19 including two new @smoke tests (the header action lands on the owning session's route; a paused goal with 3/20 turns renders the attention tint and a 15% turn bar). Unit suites: GoalsDialog 85, GoalStatusStrip 20, i18n parity 40, ChatPane 197 — 342 passed; the App-level gate cases (including click-through navigation) pass in App.test.tsx. Typecheck, ESLint, and Prettier are green on every touched file.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️ not tested   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ not tested   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ tested   |

### Environment (optional)

Local `npm run dev` (vite) with the Playwright mock daemon on Linux x64, Node 24, Chromium headless shell; unit suites under vitest/jsdom. No real-daemon arm is needed because the change is client-only and derives everything from the existing goal payloads.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the header action shares its accessible-name pattern with the existing footer link (both perform the same navigation); no E2E selector queries that name, and the redundancy is intentional for discoverability. Budget bars re-render on the existing one-second tick only while a goal is active — no new timer is introduced.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS/Windows not exercised locally (CI covers them). Goal markers in the sidebar session list are deliberately deferred — they would need a new always-on goals poll or a new session-summary field, beyond a display enhancement. No daemon/SDK change; older daemons without a token usage figure simply show no token bar.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The strip's new prop is optional; surfaces without the Goals page keep their current shape.

Design document (both languages, complete and synchronized): [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-goal-display/docs/design/2026-11-15-web-shell-goal-display.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-goal-display/docs/design/2026-11-15-web-shell-goal-display.zh-CN.md)

## 这个 PR 做了什么

2. 确认每张卡片有蓝色的会话气泡头部操作和蓝色页脚链接（会话图标 + 会话名 + 箭头）；点击任一都打开该目标的会话，多工作区 daemon 上会话在目标自己的工作区打开（与工作区徽章一致）。悬停页脚链接时会话名出现下划线。

6. 切换浅色/深色主题，确认两种主题下色调都跟随共享色板。

prs.title: fix(cli): bound provider-warning URL sanitizing to the URL authority
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`sanitizeProviderWarning` stripped credentials from `/status` provider warnings with two bespoke `indexOf` heuristics over the whole warning segment, with no notion of where the URL authority ends. The warning path now delegates to `sanitizeProviderBaseUrl` for each URL segment, and the authority it computes now ends at whitespace.

## Why it's needed

Both forms of the report follow from the missing authority bound:

- A URL with an explicit port inside prose lost everything after it:
  `Cannot reach https://api.example:8443/v1 — contact admin@example.com`
  became `Cannot reach https://example.com`. The colon of `:8443` was read as the start of a password, and the `@` of the contact address as its end — so the port, the path, the em-dash and the word "contact" were all deleted.
- An `@` inside a password leaked the remainder of that password:
  `Failed loading provider https://user:p@ssw0rd-tail@broken.example/v1` kept
  `ssw0rd-tail@broken.example/v1`, because `indexOf('@')` stopped at the `@` inside the userinfo.

`sanitizeProviderBaseUrl` already computes the authority end and takes the last `@` *within* the authority; it had only ever been reached from the fallback branch that the heuristics pre-empted. The warning path now delegates to it for each URL segment, and the warning-specific helpers (`sanitizeProviderWarningSegment`, `hasCredentialPrefix`, `URL_LIKE_PATTERN`) are deleted.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Delegating alone is not enough. The segment splitter deliberately runs past the URL so a password holding a raw space stays intact, which means a pathless URL followed by prose is handed over whole — and `findAuthorityEnd` only stopped at `/`, `?`, `#`, so the "authority" claimed the rest of the line and a later `@` in an email address was read as userinfo. `findAuthorityEnd` now also ends the authority at whitespace, which cannot appear in a URL. A space that sits after the userinfo colon and before the authority's only `@` is still treated as part of the password, so the space-in-password shape keeps stripping correctly.

```sh
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/utils/acpModelUtils.test.ts src/serve/workspace-providers-status.test.ts
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

The four new cases were checked against the unfixed source first and fail there (`4 failed | 98 passed`); with the change the two files report 102 passing tests. The before/after for the two warning shapes is quoted verbatim above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; no dev server or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the warning path and the base-URL path now share one authority computation, so a change to `findAuthorityEnd` affects both. The whitespace bound is the only behavioural addition and is covered by the new cases.
- Not validated / out of scope: full `npm run build`, the full test suite, and a package-level `tsc --noEmit`. In this fresh worktree the package typecheck fails on `TS6305` for unbuilt `packages/core` output, unrelated to these files. ESLint and Prettier are clean on the changed files.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8136


<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

`sanitizeProviderWarning` 原先用两个自制的 `indexOf` 启发式，在整段警告文本上剥离 `/status` 里的 provider 凭据，完全没有「URL 的 authority 到哪里结束」的概念。现在警告路径对每个 URL 片段改用 `sanitizeProviderBaseUrl`，并且它计算出的 authority 会在空白字符处结束。

## 为什么需要

上报的两种形态都源于缺失的 authority 边界：

- 正文里带显式端口的 URL，其后内容全被删掉：
  `Cannot reach https://api.example:8443/v1 — contact admin@example.com`
  变成 `Cannot reach https://example.com`。`:8443` 的冒号被当成密码开头，联系邮箱的 `@` 被当成密码结尾，于是端口、路径、破折号和 "contact" 一词全被删除。
- 密码里的 `@` 泄露了该密码的剩余部分：
  `Failed loading provider https://user:p@ssw0rd-tail@broken.example/v1` 保留了
  `ssw0rd-tail@broken.example/v1`，因为 `indexOf('@')` 停在了 userinfo 内部的 `@`。

`sanitizeProviderBaseUrl` 本来就会计算 authority 的结束位置，并取 authority *内部*的最后一个 `@`；它此前只从被启发式抢先的兜底分支里被调用。现在警告路径对每个 URL 片段都委托给它，警告专用的辅助函数（`sanitizeProviderWarningSegment`、`hasCredentialPrefix`、`URL_LIKE_PATTERN`）已删除。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

只做委托还不够。片段切分器会刻意越过 URL，以便保持含空格的密码完整，这意味着后面跟正文的无路径 URL 会整体交给它——而 `findAuthorityEnd` 原先只在 `/`、`?`、`#` 处停止，于是「authority」把该行剩余内容全占了，后面邮箱地址里的 `@` 被当成 userinfo。`findAuthorityEnd` 现在也在空白字符处结束 authority，而空白不可能出现在 URL 里。位于 userinfo 冒号之后、且在该 authority 唯一 `@` 之前的空格仍按密码的一部分处理，所以含空格的密码形态仍能正确剥离。

```sh
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/utils/acpModelUtils.test.ts src/serve/workspace-providers-status.test.ts
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

新增的四个用例先在未修复的源码上验证过会失败（`4 failed | 98 passed`）；改动后两个文件共 102 个测试通过。上面引用的两种警告形态即前后对照。

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

仅单元测试；没有启动 dev server 或沙箱。

## Risk & Scope

- 主要风险或取舍：警告路径和 base URL 路径现在共用同一套 authority 计算，因此改动 `findAuthorityEnd` 会同时影响两者。空白边界是唯一的行为增量，已由新用例覆盖。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：完整 `npm run build`、全量测试套件，以及包级 `tsc --noEmit`。在这个新 worktree 里，包类型检查会因 `packages/core` 未构建产物报 `TS6305`，与这些文件无关。改动文件的 ESLint 与 Prettier 干净。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8136

</details>

prs.title: feat(acp): connect durable team reports and session approvals [13902 B/3]
prs.body:
Stack: **[#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) → [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) → [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659)**. This is **B**, based on A (`split/13902-agent-identity`, `3294001f39040a668fcbad20045b64e03dc1b6e6`); base branch: `split/13902-agent-identity`. C (`split/13902-teammate-activity`) depends on B. Split from #13902 at source commit `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`; candidate B: `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`. Review B against A to isolate the coordination change.

## What this PR does

Connects an ACP-hosted leader to Team reports, roster membership and teammate approvals. Reports and join/exit notices enter the existing peer notification path with canonical teammate identity, survive recording and replay, and receive teammate attribution in the Web Shell. Pending reports participate in work holds, reversible close, queue overflow and shutdown flushing.

Teammate approvals reach the host independently of the leader's permission queue. Session scope, request UUIDs, binding epochs, ownership checks and retirement on manager replacement or teammate exit keep approval lifetime tied to the owning session. B includes producer, persistence, bridge, SDK/UI consumers and their tests. It consumes A's shared identity contract without depending on subagent runtime behavior. Tool activity and inter-agent message display arrive in C.

## Why it's needed

Without a leader sink, ACP-hosted teammate reports remain unread and teammate approval events have no consumer. The leader and its client need a delivery path that carries attribution, preserves undrained reports and exposes teammate approval requests.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. At candidate `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`, run `npm run build` from the repository root, then run the package-local commands below serially. Each Vitest command runs from the stated package directory.
2. Deliver a teammate report and roster join/exit, then reload the transcript. Confirm canonical attribution, peer semantics and turn-marker correlation. Exercise reversible close, pending-report holds, overflow, repeat flush and shutdown with undrained reports.
3. Leave a teammate approval unanswered while the leader requests its own tool approval. Confirm the leader request remains visible. Exercise host answer/failure, standalone policy, session ownership, manager rebinding, teammate exit and cancellation; evaluate the inherited feedback below separately.

```sh
# cwd: packages/acp-bridge
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/bridge-workflow-ancestor-trust.test.ts src/bridgeClient.test.ts src/transcript-replay.test.ts
# cwd: packages/cli
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/acp-integration/acpAgent.test.ts src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts src/acp-integration/session/team-sink.test.ts
# cwd: packages/core
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/agents/team/test-utils/coordination-harness.test.ts src/services/api-user-prompt.test.ts
# cwd: packages/sdk-typescript
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/agent-identity.test.ts
# cwd: packages/web-shell
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/adapters/transcriptToMessages.test.ts client/components/messages/SystemMessage.test.tsx
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

On candidate `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`, `npm run build` exited 0. The focused package-local Vitest runs passed **3058 tests in 11 test files**: ACP bridge 356, CLI 2246, core 130, SDK 13 and Web Shell 313. These counts come from this split candidate, not the original PR.

Runtime, UI E2E and standalone typecheck were not run. Matched before/after protocol, persistence and UI evidence is not available. The build and focused tests do not establish that all verification obligations are complete; this PR remains a draft and the unresolved feedback below remains open.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Build and focused tests; runtime/UI E2E and standalone typecheck not run |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

### 本 PR 做什么

将 ACP-hosted leader 接入 Team 报告、成员变更和队友审批。报告及加入/退出通知携带规范队友身份，进入现有 peer 通知路径，通过录制和重放保留，并在 Web Shell 中标注队友。待处理报告参与 work hold、可逆关闭、队列溢出和关机 flush。

prs.title: fix(cli): refresh worktree status and preserve exit cleanup
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Coordinates the existing final-process watcher policy with confirmed interactive exits and restarts, and replaces worktree sidecar directory watching with an exact-file, nonpersistent 500 ms subscription. A changed configuration or session cannot display an old sidecar, and unsubscribe affects only the owning listener.

The review follow-up checks that a supervised in-place restart launcher resolves to a regular file and is executable after cleanup, immediately before the original exec attempt. A known invalid launcher or catchable JavaScript exception produces a best-effort safe error and terminal exit code 42. Without a supervisor, manual restart is required. Successful restart arguments, GC flags and cleanup order remain unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Final exits should apply the existing watcher shutdown policy consistently. Worktree footer updates need to survive sidecar creation, deletion and atomic replacement without depending on directory notifications. Separately, a real owned-copy test showed that removing the launcher could run cleanup and then abort the runtime rather than reach the former catch-based fallback. The new precheck handles this known-invalid-path case; it does not make native exec failure generally recoverable.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the first unconfirmed interrupt still only warns, while confirmed exits retain their existing codes. Enter and leave a worktree and check that the current footer follows the durable sidecar. Switching owners, removing a listener, a failed read after a previously loaded worktree, and a later successful read should not leave stale state or disturb another subscriber.

For restart failure, use only an owned executable copy: start it, remove that copy, and request a restart. Cleanup should run once, the safe error should be reported when writable, and the process should exit 42 rather than signal-abort. Check that valid launchers retain the original arguments and that a closed error stream cannot prevent the catchable-error fallback. Do not remove or modify an installed/global executable.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the real owned Node-copy/unlink reproduction ran cleanup, then native exec failed with ENOENT/SIGABRT instead of 42. After: the real-child regression passed with cleanup recorded, no terminating signal and exit 42. The current follow-up has passed build, typecheck and seven whole CLI files (185 tests). Full lint, formatting and bundle passed. The final test-only compatibility condition was followed by fresh build/type, all 20 tests in that whole file, targeted lint, formatting and bundle; the other six whole files (165 tests) are byte-identical. This is 185 unique current tests, not 205 distinct tests. The initial follow-up run retained an ESM-namespace spy fixture failure after its real child had already passed; only the test mock wiring was corrected, without changing production behavior.

The prior candidate separately passed 181 affected tests and three short-fit public sidecar profiles; those passes belong to its earlier artifact and are not new-candidate public qualification. The retained signal matrix is 5 passed / 1 failed, including the Native first-interrupt hint failure also reproduced on the clean baseline. Separate Bun Trust restart failures/NQs remain unresolved. This follow-up does not claim to repair them.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | Build/type/185 unique affected tests, full lint, format/bundle passed; earlier public evidence scoped separately |
| 🪟 Windows | Current follow-up not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | Current follow-up not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local Node 24 source/build tests, with a separate owned executable child and core dumps disabled. Published commit is `7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c`, tree `1b82b0f10ac4dbccece2746126e71e7adc0823fe`. Build preceded the commit; the later four-design checkpoint preserved every code/test blob and all 1,455 bundle files. Windows or runtimes without execve skip the native-exec fixture; absence of that API retains the legitimate existing exit-42 route and must not be counted as real-exec coverage.

## Current CI

Remote CI update for `7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c`: TUI snapshots/no-flicker and both Managed loop jobs succeeded. Qwen CI remains **failed** at [no-AK shard 2, ACP retry-again round-count assertion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43789339488/job/133046231671), plus its derived aggregate. The three automatic CI attempts recorded differing shared/kernel debug-round counts; requests/updates/stop-reason equality was not reached there. The uploaded failure artifact has JUnit only, without the three-arm dumps/debug logs. A single local Node 24/macOS attempt reached the unchanged assertions with current 0/0, shared 3/0 and kernel 3/3 and equal normalized results; its outer cleanup guard still failed after a SIGTERM to an addressable process group. That is not a full local pass, a Linux reproduction, an infrastructure diagnosis or a waiver of the CI failure. Useful next maintainer/CI-owner evidence is the failed attempt's existing ACP_PARITY_DUMP and retained scratch debug logs, separated by attempt so retries cannot overwrite them. No CI rerun or Core change was made.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: executable checks are observations, not an atomic guarantee. E2BIG, ENOEXEC, noexec mounts, permission changes or mutations after precheck may still cause native runtime abort; the JS catch cannot guarantee terminal42 for all syscall failures. The process-global final marker remains sticky until exec or exit.
- Not validated / out of scope: all exit routes, all filesystems/platforms, installers, native signal handling, Bun post-exec startup and overall migration/stability. No automatic supervisor or retry is introduced. The existing review status is unchanged; no automatic resolution, review request or merge is implied.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no new flags, Core changes or migration requirement. Metadata polling can coalesce intermediate writes. Redundant test consolidation is deferred to preserve unique final-policy coverage and module isolation in this bounded correctness follow-up.

Designs: [exit policy (EN)](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-cli-final-watcher-exit-chain.md), [退出策略（中文）](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-cli-final-watcher-exit-chain.zh-CN.md), [polling (EN)](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-worktree-sidecar-polling.md), [轮询（中文）](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-worktree-sidecar-polling.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to this PR's first review round; no additional issue is closed.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

在已确认的交互退出和重启前接入既有最终进程 watcher 策略，并将 worktree sidecar 目录监测替换为精确文件、非持久的 500 ms 订阅。切换配置或会话不能显示旧 sidecar，取消订阅只影响所属 listener。

本轮审查后续在清理完成后、原 exec 尝试之前，检查 supervised 原位重启的 launcher 是否解析为普通文件并可执行。已知不可用 launcher 或可捕获 JavaScript 异常会尽力安全报告并以代码 42 终止。无 supervisor 时必须手动重启。成功路径的重启参数、GC 参数及清理顺序不变。

## 为什么需要

最终退出应一致应用既有 watcher 清理策略。Worktree 页脚需能随 sidecar 创建、删除和原子替换更新，而不依赖目录通知。另外，真实 owned 副本测试证明删除 launcher 后可能完成清理却直接终止运行时，无法进入此前的 catch 回退。新预检处理这一已知无效路径情形，不使全部原生 exec 失败变得可恢复。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

确认首次未确认中断仍只提示，已确认退出保持原退出码。进入及离开 worktree，检查当前页脚跟随持久 sidecar。切换 owner、移除 listener、已加载 worktree 后读取失败，以及随后读取恢复，都不应保留过期状态或干扰其他订阅者。

重启失败仅使用 owned 可执行副本验证：启动它、删除该副本，再请求重启。清理应恰好一次，输出可写时应安全报告错误，进程应以 42 退出而非信号中止。确认有效 launcher 参数不变，错误输出流关闭不阻止可捕获错误的回退。禁止删除或修改已安装或全局可执行文件。

### 前后证据

修复前：真实 owned Node 副本删除自身 launcher 后完成清理，随后原生 exec 发生 ENOENT/SIGABRT，而非 42。修复后：真实子进程回归通过，清理已记录、无终止信号且退出码为 42。当前后续候选已通过构建、类型检查与七个完整 CLI 测试文件（185 项）。完整 lint、格式及 bundle 已通过。最终仅改测试兼容条件后，又完成新的 build/type、该整文件全部 20 项、定向 lint、格式及 bundle；另六个完整测试文件的 165 项 blob 不变。当前共 185 项独立测试，不是 205 项。首轮后续检查在真实子进程已通过后遇到 ESM namespace spy 夹具失败；仅修正测试 mock 接线，没有改变生产行为。

此前候选另有 181 项受影响测试及三个 short-fit 公开 sidecar 配置通过；这些属于旧产物，不是新候选的公开验收。原信号矩阵仍为 5 通过 / 1 失败，其中 Native 首次中断提示失败也在干净基线复现。另案 Bun Trust 重启失败及 NQ 仍未关闭，本后续不宣称修复这些问题。

### 已测试环境

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | build/type/185 项独立受影响测试、完整 lint、format/bundle 通过；旧公开证据单独保留范围 |
| 🪟 Windows | 当前后续未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | 当前后续未测试 |

### 运行环境

本地 Node 24 源码及构建测试，使用独立 owned 可执行子进程并禁止 core dump。出版 commit 为 `7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c`，tree 为 `1b82b0f10ac4dbccece2746126e71e7adc0823fe`。构建发生在 commit 之前，后续四文档 checkpoint 保持全部 code/test blob 及 1,455 个 bundle 文件不变。Windows 及不提供 execve 的运行时跳过 native-exec 夹具；缺少该 API 时保留合法的既有退出 42 路径，不能计为真实 exec 覆盖。

## 当前 CI

远端 CI 更新：TUI snapshots/no-flicker 及 Managed 两条路径成功；Qwen CI 仍因 no-AK shard 2 的 ACP 重试轮次断言和派生汇总失败。CI 自动尝试记录的 shared/kernel debug 轮数不同，尚未执行后续请求、更新及停止原因比较；上传产物只有 JUnit，没有失败当次三路径 dump/debug。本机 Node24/macOS 单次原场景的轮数与归一化结果一致，但外层清理守卫仍因向可寻址进程组发送 SIGTERM 而失败；不是完整本地通过、Linux 复现、基础设施结论或 CI 豁免。下一步需 CI 维护者保留失败当次既有 ACP_PARITY_DUMP 和 scratch debug，按 attempt 分隔，防重试覆盖。未重跑 CI，未改 Core。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：可执行检查只是一次观测，不是原子保证。E2BIG、ENOEXEC、noexec 挂载、预检后的权限或文件变化仍可能导致原生运行时中止，JS catch 不能保证全部系统调用失败都退出 42。进程全局最终标记在 exec 或退出前仍保持 sticky。
- 未验证及范围外：全部出口、全部文件系统及平台、安装产物、原生信号处理、Bun exec 后启动及整体迁移和稳定性。不增加自动 supervisor 或重试。现有审查状态不变，不自动解决讨论、请求审查或合并。
- 破坏性变更及迁移：不新增 flag、不改 Core、无需迁移。Metadata 轮询可能合并中间变化。本轮有界正确性后续暂缓重复测试整合，以保留独有的最终策略覆盖和模块隔离。

设计：[exit policy (EN)](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-cli-final-watcher-exit-chain.md)、[退出策略（中文）](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-cli-final-watcher-exit-chain.zh-CN.md)、[polling (EN)](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-worktree-sidecar-polling.md)、[轮询（中文）](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7da3f7ccc6012303ba7441ba6b7655995bebe51c/docs/design/2026-11-15-worktree-sidecar-polling.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联问题

对应本 PR 第一轮审查的后续，不额外关闭 issue。

</details>

prs.title: fix(acp): surface failed todo_write calls instead of dropping them
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Failed `todo_write` calls are now reported to the ACP client as a terminal `tool_call_update` with `status: failed`, instead of producing no frame at all. Successes keep the existing plan-only representation, which is what the client renders as the task list.

## Why it's needed

A `todo_write` result is deliberately rendered as a plan update rather than a tool card, and every failure path returned early without emitting anything:

- `ToolCallEmitter.emitResult` returned on `!success`;
- `Session.runTool` skipped the terminal emission for `todo_write`;
- the `earlyErrorResponse` path skipped `TODO_WRITE`;
- a discarded tool-call preparation returned without a frame;
- transcript replay dropped the record the same way.

A failed `todo_write` normally writes no plan, so a failed call was invisible on the wire: no plan frame, no `tool_call` start, no `tool_call_update`. In ACP hosts the plan panel is the *only* progress surface, so the failure was silently swallowed and there was nothing to diagnose from. This was called out as an actionable follow-up in the triage for this issue.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. 3. Optional end-to-end check: make `todo_write` fail (for example by sending a todo list with a dependency cycle) and confirm the ACP stream now carries a failed `tool_call_update` for that call id.

I also ran the whole `packages/cli` `Session.test.ts` suite (1436 tests) — it passes.

Expected: the failure is observable. Observed before the change: nothing was emitted.

I also ran the whole `packages/cli` `Session.test.ts` suite (1436 tests) — it passes.

- Main risk or tradeoff: ACP hosts now receive a `tool_call_update` for `todo_write`, a tool that normally never produces one. Clients that key on the tool name to suppress todo cards could show an extra failed card — which is the intent here, but it is a visible behaviour change.

prs.title: fix(verify-pr): close the context trust refusal's root-tmp and hard-link bypasses
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes the local verification checker's trust refusal fail closed on the layouts it previously let through, and binds the host-supplied verification snapshot by content so a round cannot pass off a file it wrote as the host's record. Three layers: a root-aware containment rule (a trust root equal to the filesystem root contains every path and is rejected as a usage error), applied at both containment sites so they cannot drift apart; a link-count guard that refuses a context retaining a second name (a hard link), wherever the source lives and whether or not it is readable; and a content binding — `verify-pr-prepare.mjs` prints the sha256 of the snapshot it writes host-side, the skill holds that digest outside the clone and passes `--context-sha256`, and the checker refuses a `--context` whose bytes do not match. The refusal message is split by cause so it no longer states a path relation that is false for the alias and filesystem-root cases.

## Why it's needed

Follow-up to #17185, tracked in #17371 (finding R17-1). The waiver-approval trust boundary requires that the coordinates judging a round's waiver come only from a host-held snapshot the round never controlled. The original refusal derived trust from path strings and leaked on a round directory directly under a root-level temporary directory (the computed trust root became the filesystem root and the prefix comparison never matched) and on hard-link aliases. Review and an independent non-root verification round then showed each successive guard was incomplete: an artifact-directory inode walk missed sources outside that directory and failed open on an unreadable subdirectory (R1-1, R1-2); and a link count of one still does not prove the host wrote the file — the round can rewrite the bytes through an in-clone alias then unlink it, or write a fresh single-link file at a writable path (R2-1). The content binding rests on what prepare wrote host-side, which a name cannot fake.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Run the checker with a round directory directly under the system root-level tmp and a genuine one-link host copy outside the artifact dir: it must refuse and name the derived-root cause (remedy: move the dir, not `--context-root`).
- Run the checker against a sanctioned clone layout where the supplied snapshot is a hard link of a round-writable file (the round's own snapshot, the clone's verify-context sibling, or a file under a chmod-000 subdirectory): each must refuse as a hard link.
- With `--context-sha256` bound, rewrite the snapshot's coordinates through an in-clone alias then unlink it, or substitute a fresh single-link file: both must refuse on digest mismatch; a genuine copy whose bytes match the digest must be accepted.
- A genuine host copy outside the trust root, including one that only shares the clone's name prefix, must still be accepted (no false refusal). A `--context-root` of the filesystem root must be a usage error even without `--context`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change: N/A for screenshots. Before: the root-tmp layouts, the hard-link aliases, and the rewritten/substituted single-link snapshots were accepted. After: all refuse, and genuine host copies are still accepted. Locally: the full verify-pr cluster plus the step-7 replay suites pass 654 with 0 failures and 5 container-aware host skips; mutations that revert each guard (predicate, bare prefix, link count, digest refusal, message split) turn the corresponding witnesses red, with byte-level restore verified; a real-filesystem base/head A/B as a non-root operator and a prepare-style digest round-trip confirm genuine→accept and tampered/forged→refuse. Prettier and ESLint are clean.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

The witnesses are Unix-specific (root-level tmp, hard links, mode bits) and skip on Windows; the derived-root witness builds at a literal root-level /tmp (not os.tmpdir(), which CI routes elsewhere) so it is load-bearing on the Linux lane. CI covers all three platforms.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests plus a real-filesystem A/B and digest round-trip as a non-root operator, Node 24.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the content binding is only as strong as its delivery. The digest is computed by prepare host-side and passed by the operator (the round does not run the checker), so it is secure under the isolation premise; `--context-sha256` is optional for backward compatibility, and HELP states that without it the path/link-count form alone is not proof of provenance. The sanctioned skill always passes it.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS/Windows local runs (the witnesses are Unix-specific). A caller that omits the digest gets only the path/link-count heuristics; making the digest mandatory for every `--context` use is a possible follow-up hardening. The other residual risks stay tracked in #17371.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: a trust root of the filesystem root is now a usage error (exit 2) even without `--context`; the local skill now captures and passes the snapshot digest. The CI path (`QWEN_VERIFY_CONTEXT`) is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Tracks #17371 (R17-1). Follow-up to #17185.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

让本地验证检查器的信任拒绝在此前放行的布局下 fail closed，并按内容绑定宿主快照，使轮次无法把自己写的文件冒充宿主记录。三层：根感知包含规则（信任根等于文件系统根即包含一切路径，作为用法错误拒绝），用于两处包含判定使其不走偏；链接数守卫，拒绝保留第二名字的 context（硬链接），无论源在哪、是否可读；内容绑定——`verify-pr-prepare.mjs` 打印其宿主侧所写快照的 sha256，skill 把摘要持于克隆之外并传 `--context-sha256`，checker 拒绝字节不匹配的 `--context`。拒绝文案按因拆分，不再对别名与文件系统根情形陈述失真的路径关系。

## 为什么需要

#17185 的后续，跟踪于 #17371（R17-1）。豁免批准信任边界要求判定轮次豁免的坐标只来自轮次从未控制的宿主快照。原拒绝从路径字符串推导信任，在直挂根级临时目录的轮次目录（算出的信任根成为文件系统根、前缀比较永不匹配）与硬链接别名上泄漏。评审与一轮独立非 root 验证继而表明每层守卫都不完备：产物目录 inode 遍历漏掉目录外源、且在不可读子目录 fail open（R1-1、R1-2）；链接数为 1 仍不证明宿主所写——轮次可经克隆内别名改写字节再删名，或在可写路径新写单链接文件（R2-1）。内容绑定基于 prepare 宿主侧所写内容，名字伪造不了。

## 评审验证要点

- 轮次目录直挂根级 tmp、供产物目录外的单链接宿主副本：须拒绝并点名派生根因（药方：移出目录，而非 `--context-root`）。
- 受认可克隆布局下，所供快照是轮次可写文件的硬链接（轮次自身快照、克隆 verify-context 兄弟、chmod-000 子目录下文件）：各须以硬链接拒绝。
- 绑定 `--context-sha256` 后，经克隆内别名改写坐标再删名、或替换新单链接文件：均须以摘要不匹配拒绝；字节匹配摘要的合法副本须接受。
- 信任根外的合法宿主副本（含仅同名前缀者）仍须接受（无误拒）。文件系统根的 `--context-root` 即便不带 `--context` 也须为用法错误。

证据（前后）：非 UI，截图 N/A。前：根级 tmp 布局、硬链接别名、被改写/替换的单链接快照均被接受；后：均拒绝，合法宿主副本仍接受。本地：完整 verify-pr 簇 + step-7 回放套件 654 通过 / 0 失败 / 5 容器感知宿主跳过；回退各守卫（谓词、裸前缀、链接数、摘要拒绝、文案拆分）的变异使对应见证变红，字节级还原核验；非 root 真实文件系统 base/head A/B 与 prepare 式摘要往返确认合法→接受、篡改/伪造→拒绝。Prettier 与 ESLint 干净。

## 风险与范围

- 主要权衡：内容绑定的强度取决于摘要传递。摘要由 prepare 宿主侧计算、操作者传递（轮次不运行 checker），故在隔离前提下安全；`--context-sha256` 为向后兼容而可选，HELP 明说不带它时路径/链接数形式本身不是来源证明。受认可 skill 总是传它。
- 未验证 / 范围外：macOS/Windows 本地运行（见证为 Unix 特定）。省略摘要的调用方只得到路径/链接数启发；把摘要设为每次 `--context` 必需是可能的后续加固。其余残余风险仍由 #17371 跟踪。
- 破坏性变更：文件系统根信任根现在即便不带 `--context` 也是用法错误（exit 2）；本地 skill 现捕获并传递快照摘要。CI 路径（`QWEN_VERIFY_CONTEXT`）不变。

## 关联

跟踪 #17371（R17-1）；#17185 的后续。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): retain arguments after redirects in permission rules
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Suggested shell rules retain arguments after redirections without granting every subcommand of the executable. For example, `git > /dev/null push origin main` produces `Bash(git push *)` and, when that derived rule alone does not cover the invocation, a reusable original-command rule. Saving the suggestions covers that invocation; redirected reset/clean commands still require their own permission.

Rule extraction restores trailing redirect arguments only on the rule-production path, in source order. This follows [the maintainer direction in #17001](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/17001#issuecomment-6816035580). `getArgumentNodes` and read-only classification keep their existing behavior.

## Why it's needed

tree-sitter-bash stores words after a redirection inside that redirect node. Dropping those words can suggest a root-wide Git rule for a push. Retaining the narrower subcommand alone can then leave the saved rule unable to match the original redirect spelling, so the same command repeatedly prompts. Scheduled gates had the same problem: their blocked notice could suggest a rule that never unblocked the gate.

## Round 3 follow-up

Current head: [`597adc7dd3`](https://github.com/Afloat16/qwen-code/commit/597adc7dd316584f173f1aab6a4e8722f6217b3e), a normal follow-up to `a2112d18`. The changes below address [review 5914963829](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17372#pullrequestreview-5914963829). The R3 numbers refer to the visible inline labels, whose AST/continuation numbering differs from the embedded review ledger.

| Finding | Change | Regression boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R3-1: nested heredoc descriptor | Descriptor attribution includes recursively visited redirects without collecting their trailing arguments twice. | Derived rules for fd 0, 3 and 10 remain `git push *`; they do not grant reset/clean. |
| R3-2: restrictive spelling gaps | Deny/ask rules compare one command-word/file-effect representation using the existing quote-aware tokenizer. Supported fd, clobber, combined-stream, quote and escape forms share the same write effect. | Actual decisions, relevance and citations are checked under a broad allow, with unrelated command, target and read-effect controls. Literal dollars/backticks and valid assignment prefixes retain their meaning. |
| R3-3: line continuations | Bash matching and compound splitting remove executable continuations consistently with suggestion production, preserving literal quoted text. | Saved suggestions are reloaded into a fresh manager and applied to the original continued command for both Bash and Monitor. |
| R3-4: platform and approval policy | Bash syntax checks are gated on Bash. An explicit empty rule list suppresses permanent choices in Ink, OpenTUI and ACP without setting the separate explicit-interaction flag. | Bash/cmd/PowerShell differential tests, empty-versus-undefined option controls, and registered headless/YOLO regressions. |
| R3-5: mixed commands | Safe independent segments keep their suggestions. The helper receives the whole raw command and restricts caller eligibility to actual segments. | Saving the npm rule from a mixed command does not approve its unsupported segment; loops and heredoc fragments do not become grants. |
| R3-6: wrappers and unresolved destinations | The grant guard follows shell wrappers to the tracker's depth bound and rejects variable/glob destinations it cannot resolve. | Wrapper/glued-redirect and three glob forms remain unapproved; quoted and escaped literal targets retain their controls. |
| R3-7: arithmetic | A narrow parser recognizes constant decimal arithmetic arguments with balanced parentheses and `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`. Only substitution detection uses that view; redirect checks still see the original text. | Variables, arrays, nested execution, ambiguous closing syntax and arithmetic redirect destinations still require confirmation. |
| R3-8 through R3-11: test effectiveness | Tests exercise the actual platform gates, prefix-matching substitution guard, compound splitting, configured cwd and explicit context cwd. Direct manager assertions accompany the higher-level helper. | Seven targeted negative controls demonstrate that the protected behavior can actually fail. |
| R3-12: scheduled gate remedy | The runtime gate uses the same suggestion helper as the dialogs and emits a hint only when every segment is covered. | A saved redirected-gate hint permits the next evaluation; unsupported and incomplete mixed gates omit the ineffective remedy. |

The tokenizer's existing file-operation consumer keeps its default token behavior; the restrictive view opts into additional syntax/expansion metadata. Valid descriptor-close input uses a bounded structure-only reparse of AST-identified `<&-` / `>&-` operators, while extraction and grant matching retain the original input. Other parse errors, control flow and heredocs remain excluded from reusable suggestions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

1. Save the suggestions for a redirected push and reload permissions. Check the original invocation, its line-continued form and both Shell/Monitor entry points; unrelated reset/clean commands must remain unapproved.
2. Configure a broad Git allow plus `Bash(git>/tmp/protected push *)` as deny or ask. Test `1>`, spaced redirects, quoted targets, `&>` and `>|`; verify the final decision and cited restrictive rule. Check unrelated targets, subcommands and read redirects.
3. Append command/process substitution after an already-matching `git push *` prefix. Compare Bash with mocked cmd/PowerShell, and check relative targets with cwd outside the project root, both before and after `cd /project`.
4. Save the individual `Monitor(...)` rules from a redirected cron-gate hint and evaluate the original gate again. Unsupported or partially covered gates must not display an ineffective whole-gate remedy. Empty persistent suggestions must not change the existing YOLO policy.

After the frozen workspace installation and normal build, run the complete core and CLI suites with their normal package configuration:

```sh
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
npm run build
npm run typecheck --workspace=packages/core
cd packages/core
CI=true npm exec -- vitest run \
  src/utils/shellAstParser.test.ts \
  src/permissions/shell-semantics.test.ts \
  src/permissions/shell-command-syntax.test.ts \
  src/permissions/command-rule-suggestions.test.ts \
  src/permissions/redirected-command-rules.test.ts \
  src/permissions/rule-parser.test.ts \
  src/permissions/permission-manager.test.ts \
  src/core/permissionFlow.test.ts \
  src/core/permission-helpers.test.ts \
  src/tools/shell.test.ts \
  src/tools/monitor.test.ts \
  src/tools/cron-create.gate.test.ts \
  src/services/cron-gate.test.ts \
  src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
cd ../cli
CI=true npm exec -- vitest run \
  src/acp-integration/session/permissionUtils.test.ts \
  src/ui/components/messages/ToolConfirmationMessage.test.tsx \
  src/ui/opentui/dialogs-confirm.test.tsx \
  src/ui/opentui/live-session.test.ts \
  src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
```

## Current validation

The published 27-file change was checked against a frozen manifest before and after verification. Each published Git blob matches the verified local file exactly. Manifest SHA-256: `637beff263f57f80a3211d1554a785317c0de9fb432acab59957b27ed26e4c56`.

| Executed check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Five complete registered test files in the standalone source harness | **1,199 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**: AST 589, shell semantics 262, redirected permissions 139, shared suggestions 158, syntax views 51. |
| Independent core reproduction | Exact `a2112d18` produced 29 failures and 24 passing controls; the same 53 assertions pass on the candidate, with only the producer call adapted to the new raw-command API. |
| Independent cron/platform probe | Baseline: 9 failed / 3 passed. Candidate: all 13 passed, including one additional complete-safe-compound control. This invokes the real gate runner and PermissionManager with the execution/output boundaries mocked. |
| ACP option builder | Baseline: 2 failed / 4 passed. Candidate: 6/6 passed; the final ACP module blob is identical to that tested candidate. |
| Static checks | TypeScript 5.8.3 syntax checks for all 26 TS/TSX files, repository-configured Prettier for all 27 files, and `git diff --check` passed. This is not a semantic typecheck. |
| Exact-source checks | All 27 byte counts, SHA-256 values and Git blobs match before/after; the changed-file set is unchanged. |

The following isolated in-memory mutations were each applied to the actual source and detected by the named assertions. They produced assertion failures, not import/collection failures. Removing the mutations restored **190/190** redirected-permission/syntax tests with no skips.

| Deliberately broken behavior | Expected assertion failures observed |
| --- | ---: |
| Apply the Bash allow guard on cmd/PowerShell | 4 |
| Apply restrictive Bash normalization on cmd/PowerShell | 4 |
| Bypass the unsupported-syntax allow guard | 6 |
| Stop splitting compound commands | 2 |
| Stop following `cd` for relative targets | 4 |
| Resolve targets from project root instead of cwd | 4 |
| Remove restrictive semantic matching | 22 |

**Environment and limits:** Linux, Node.js 24.22.1 and the existing minimal source-test dependencies. These are actual repository source/test files in an explicitly separate source harness, not the normal built-artifact workspace/globalSetup. The complete original `cron-gate.test.ts` could not collect because this environment lacks `@opentelemetry/api-logs`; its 0 collected tests are not counted as passed. The isolated 13-case gate/platform probe is reported separately. Full workspace build/typecheck, the complete original cron suite, Ink/OpenTUI rendering and headless CLI suites remain for the new head's upstream CI. No native Windows/macOS run or live model/TUI session is claimed. Command examples were parser inputs; no push/reset/clean or protected-file writes were executed.

[Current-head checks](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17372/checks) are the remaining full integration gate. The prior [main CI run on `a2112d18`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43790231412) completed successfully, including 2,361 tests in the previous 11 focused files, both no-AK integration shards and both web-shell smoke shards. Those results belong to the previous head and are not counted as validation of the R3 changes.

## Scope and compatibility

Existing settings and saved rules are not rewritten. Existing prefix/glob and legacy `:*` parsing remain in place. Additional semantic spellings apply only to restrictive rules. Unsupported Bash redirects and expansions cannot inherit a persistent grant; unresolved destinations are not treated as resolved file paths. The documented persistent-rule boundary does not change automatic-approval policy.

This does not implement general shell execution, environment expansion or filesystem alias resolution. File-operation analysis, settings schema and read-only classification retain their existing roles. The separate underlying heredoc-body splitting report and #16870 remain outside this patch; this producer refuses to persist those fragments.

Refs #17001.

prs.title: fix(web-shell): show the copy menu when a selection boundary lands on row chrome
prs.body:
## What this PR does The Web Shell copy menu (Copy plain text / Copy Markdown) is suppressed when the outer boundary of the selection lands on the row chrome next to the message body, even though the whole line is visually selected. `getReplySelectionRange` now clamps that boundary to the body edge on a clone of the range, so the live selection is never mutated. Clamping only happens when the boundary is on the correct side of the body and does not belong to another message's body — cross-message selections are still rejected as before. ## Why it's needed A triple-click on a line (or a drag that reaches the edge of the line) makes the browser park the outer range boundary on the row chrome element (e.g. the timestamp tip) and the range's common ancestor sits above the message body. `getReplySelectionRange` requires both boundaries to be contained in the body, returns null, and the menu is suppressed — the user sees a highlighted line but no copy actions. Reported in #17270. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify Unit: in `packages/web-shell` run `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts --pool=forks utils/selectionClipboard.test.ts` — the new "reply selection range at row edges" suite: trailing and leading boundary on row chrome is clamped to the body edge (both cases RED on the pre-fix code), identity when both boundaries are inside, rejection for a boundary inside another message body, and rejection for wrong-side / ancestor / collapsed boundaries. Manual: open a Web Shell session, triple-click a whole assistant reply line — the "Copy plain text / Copy Markdown" menu appears; drag a selection from inside a line to the right edge of the line — the menu appears; select across two messages — no menu (unchanged). ### Evidence (Before & After) Unit (node:22-bookworm volume, `utils/selectionClipboard.test.ts`, 61 tests): pre-fix code — 59/61, exactly the two clamping cases fail (`getReplySelectionRange` returns null instead of the clamped range); post-fix — 61/61. Live CDP matrix on the 0.27.2 Web Shell with the equivalent patched bundle (same algorithm, issue #17270): triple-click on `

` → menu shown; triple-click on `

  • ` → menu shown; cross-message drag → no menu; double-click on a word → menu shown; the live selection boundaries are not mutated by the clamp. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ✅ | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ | | 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ | ### Environment (optional) Unit tests in a `node:22-bookworm` Docker volume (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile + full build); live CDP verification through the user's Chrome DevTools protocol bridge against a 0.27.2 Web Shell daemon. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: cross-message rejection relies on the message body carrying a CSS-module class containing `contentBody` (`div[class*=contentBody]`); if a boundary ever lands on another such container the selection is rejected (menu suppressed) rather than clamped — the safe direction, no wrong content can be copied. - Not validated / out of scope: Windows/Linux local runs (CI covers them); no change to copy content formatting (plain text / Turndown output is untouched). - Breaking changes / migration notes: none. ## Linked Issues Fixes #17270

prs.title: test(cli): wait for the applied skills selection before navigating
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Deflakes the skills manager layout case that navigates the picker. The case used to accept the first frame that showed the loaded list and immediately send `j`; it now waits for that same frame to also show the applied checkbox state, so the navigation key can only be sent once the list's keypress handling is actually live. The test still asserts the same highlighted row, the same disabled neighbor, and the same `/nine` pick, with one added precondition it already depended on.

## Why it's needed

The case was flagged as flaky after failing and passing on a rerun of the same commit, on a host reported at load ~80. The first loaded frame is painted during the list's first commit, before React flushes passive effects, so `MultiSelect`'s keypress subscription can still be pending when the test writes `j`. A key broadcast in that window reaches no list handler and is never replayed, which is why the existing contended-host wait budget could not save it. Waiting for the frame that carries `[x] nine` closes the window deterministically: that paint is produced by the dialog's own effect, and React flushes a child's passive effects (the subscription) before its parent's.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the layout suite in `packages/cli` and confirm the picker case passes repeatedly on an idle host and on the slow-host budget arm (`RUNNER_NAME=ecs-qwen-...`). To see the mechanism, a temporary probe is not needed: the committed wait adds the `[x] nine` precondition, and the next assertion still requires the marker to move to `nine` after a single `j` press. Removing that precondition and mounting the picker repeatedly makes the single `j` disappear before the selection frame lands.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: with only the `› [ ] eight` wait, a probe pressing `j` on the first loaded frame lost the key in 50/50 mounts — the selection frame then painted `[x] nine` but the marker stayed on `eight`, even 300 ms later.

After: waiting for the same frame to contain `[x] nine` moved the marker to `nine` in 50/50 mounts. The full file passed 37/37 on 5 pre-build runs, 3 post-build runs, and 2 runs on the slow-host arm.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux container, `packages/cli` Vitest with coverage disabled for repeats; build/typecheck/lint from the repository root.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the test now needs the checkbox state to paint before it sends navigation. If the dialog ever stopped applying the initial selection, the case would fail at the new precondition instead of the later assertion — which is the same regression, reported earlier.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real terminal keypress path is unchanged; no product code was touched. Timeout budgets are unchanged.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17404

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

修复技能管理布局用例中操作选择列表的抖动问题。该用例原先一看到展示已加载列表的第一帧就立刻发送 `j`；现在会等待同一帧同时展示已应用的勾选状态，从而保证导航按键只会在列表的按键处理真正就绪后才发送。测试仍然断言同一个高亮行、同一个被禁用的邻居以及同一个 `/nine` 选择，并额外断言了一个它本来就依赖的前置条件。

## 为什么需要

该用例在同一 commit 的重跑中出现“先失败后通过”，被标记为 flaky，上报主机负载约为 80。列表的第一帧在首次提交阶段就绘制完成，早于 React 刷新被动 effect，因此测试写入 `j` 时 `MultiSelect` 的按键订阅可能仍未注册。此时广播的按键不会到达任何列表处理器，也不会被重放——这正是已有的高负载等待预算无法挽救它的原因。等待携带 `[x] nine` 的帧可以确定性地消除这个窗口：该状态由对话框自身的 effect 产生，而 React 会先刷新子组件的被动 effect（即按键订阅）再刷新父组件的。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/cli` 下运行该布局测试套件，确认选择器用例在空闲主机和慢主机预算分支（`RUNNER_NAME=ecs-qwen-...`）上都能反复通过。该机制无需临时探针即可理解：提交的等待条件新增了 `[x] nine` 前置条件，而紧接着的断言仍要求单次 `j` 后标记移动到 `nine`。若去掉该前置条件并反复挂载选择器，这一次 `j` 会在选中状态帧到来之前就消失。

### 证据（前后对比）

修改前：只等待 `› [ ] eight` 时，探针在第一帧按下 `j`，50/50 次挂载中按键均丢失——随后选中帧虽然绘制了 `[x] nine`，但 300 ms 后标记仍停在 `eight`。

修改后：等待同一帧包含 `[x] nine` 后，50/50 次挂载中标记都移动到了 `nine`。完整文件在构建前 5 次、构建后 3 次、慢主机分支 2 次运行中均为 37/37 通过。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

Linux 容器；重复运行时在 `packages/cli` 下关闭覆盖率；构建/类型检查/lint 从仓库根目录运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：测试现在需要先绘制出勾选状态才会发送导航按键。如果对话框不再应用初始选择，用例会在新的前置条件处失败，而不是之后的断言处——这仍是同一个回归，只是报错更早。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：真实终端按键路径未改动；未修改产品代码。超时预算未改动。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #17404

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve literal custom command arguments
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Custom commands now preserve argument text literally in local prompt expansion and hosted extension expansion. Only placeholders in the original template are expanded; placeholder-looking text inserted from arguments is not interpreted a second time. Shell arguments still follow the existing quoting, safety checks, and permission flow.

## Why it's needed

Arguments containing JavaScript replacement sequences currently change before they reach the model or shell: `$$` becomes `$`, `$&` becomes the matched placeholder, and the prefix/suffix sequences duplicate surrounding template text. Hosted expansion also rewrites argument text that happens to contain `$ARGUMENTS` or `${extensionPath}`. This corrupts perfectly valid code, regular expressions, and shell examples passed to a custom command.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Define a custom command whose prompt is `Review {{args}}.` and invoke it with arguments such as `costs $$5 and $&`. Confirm that the submitted prompt contains those exact characters.
2. Repeat with argument placeholders before and after a template shell block, and with both `{{args}}` and `$ARGUMENTS` inside a shell block. Confirm that the permission check and runtime execution receive the same correctly escaped command.
3. For a hosted extension, include `${extensionPath}`, `{{args}}`, and `$ARGUMENTS` in the template while supplying the same strings as argument text. Confirm that only the template's extension path is resolved. The shell regressions cover unquoted, single-quoted, and double-quoted argument placeholders.
4. Run the three focused suites from `packages/cli`:

```sh
npm exec -- vitest run src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.test.ts src/services/command-factory.test.ts src/serve/hosted-extension-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1 --coverage.enabled=false
```

### Original evidence (`6eb41fc4`)

The regression tests exercise the custom-command action and the hosted expansion API with controlled permission/runtime boundaries. A global `qwen` binary was unavailable, so this is automated entry-point evidence rather than a terminal recording.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial regressions plus existing adjacent tests | 13 failed, 46 passed | 59 passed |
| Additional hosted shell extension-path regressions | 3 failed, 10 passed in the hosted suite | All three quote contexts preserve the argument text |
| Final combined suites | — | 62 passed |
| Plain prompt argument `$$` | Collapses to `$` | Preserved as `$$` |
| Hosted shell argument `${extensionPath}` | Rewritten to `${QWEN_EXTENSION_ROOT}` | Argument remains literal; the template path still expands |

Existing controls continue to cover ordinary input, permission rejection, shell escaping, multiline input, opaque injected files, and durable hosted result replay. ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check` passed. `npm run bundle` completed and the built CLI reported version `0.27.3`.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :--- |
| macOS | Not tested locally |
| Windows | Not tested locally |
| Linux | Original `6eb41fc4`: 62 focused tests passed; bundle and CLI version smoke check passed. Current `f3589a78`: upstream Lint & Static, build and both Linux unit-test shards passed, including all 65 tests in the three focused suites. Detailed head/merge-tree results below. |

### Original local environment (`6eb41fc4`)

Linux, Node.js 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 11.24.0 with the frozen worktree setup. The initial full workspace build was killed with exit 137 in the core compiler. A serial 4 GiB-heap core build and the ACP bridge build subsequently passed. Unchanged web/SDK prerequisite outputs were reused after verifying their sources and manifests match the previously built checkout; generated web assets were included in the bundle. A full local CLI typecheck and full repository suite were not completed; upstream CI is still required.

### Current validation on `f3589a78`

This follow-up merges accepted upstream commit [`34ed63fe` (#15959)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/commit/34ed63fe7319455408baf1c6c19ee54d50b1d34a). The two custom-command production files are byte-for-byte unchanged from `6eb41fc4`. The additional changes are confined to three test files:

- R1-1: an independent hosted `@{...}` file-injection case checks the literal path at both the permission boundary and the actual `read_file` call.
- R1-2: two safe-input cases distinguish raw `$ARGUMENTS` from quoted `{{args}}`, checking that permission and execution receive the same command.
- The Unicode publication fixture now registers the real asynchronous verifier and its named scheduler, including normal Spring cleanup. Its timeouts, Unicode rejection checks and execution/capture assertions are unchanged.

The earlier ordinary [Qwen Code CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43725704202) passed on `6eb41fc4`; the subsequent [full Managed Agent gate](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43731660610) failed. Investigation connected the retained-output failure to the asynchronous segment-receipt format and the Broker failure to reading a stale session status after a locking query. Both are addressed by the accepted upstream baseline. On a checkout with the exact same tree as `34ed63fe`, [upstream verification](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43733785106/job/132900917741) passed all 21 Hosted automation cases, all four shell lifecycle recovery cases and the previously failing public deletion case; the full [Broker/MySQL job](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43733785106/job/132900917760) also passed.

That upstream Hosted run still failed the Unicode o2 case. Its manual fixture omitted the verifier required after publication became asynchronous: the data store's default wakeup is empty, while the normal publication configuration is disabled for this fixture. The new test-only wiring addresses that concrete gap. A controlled run of the original fixture followed by the corrected fixture is still needed to confirm the causal diagnosis.

**Validation status (2026-11-16 04:53 UTC):** the two added TypeScript test blocks pass Prettier, and the final diff was checked. The following upstream results have now completed:

- On exact head `f3589a782bdd46216e221e5e4419a4d14e979488`, [Lint & Static](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43797710817/job/133070262813) and [Build unit-test tree](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43797710817/job/133070262875) passed.
