prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a SpecStream section to the "Supported MCP Web Search Services" list in `docs/developers/tools/web-search.md`, after You.com, in the same format as the looot entry (#13999): description with what is sent to the provider, Documentation, Cost, Get API Key and Best for bullets, the tool list, and the CLI and `settings.json` setup for the remote server with a Bearer header. SpecStream runs a remote MCP server at `https://api.specstream.ai/mcp` with web search (`search_web`, each result with its source URL and a published date where the page states one), page reading (`read_pages`, pages and PDFs as Markdown) and a priced research report. I work on SpecStream, so this is a vendor addition.

## Why it's needed

Users on providers that cannot back the built-in `web_search` (OpenRouter, DeepSeek, local models) need an MCP server for search and page reading. This adds one more option that uses the `httpUrl` plus `headers` form the other remote entries already show.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Docs only. Read the new section next to the looot entry, which uses the same `qwen mcp add -t http ... -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."` command and `httpUrl` plus `headers` block. `POST https://api.specstream.ai/mcp` answers 401 when no key is sent. `prettier --check docs/developers/tools/web-search.md` passes. I did not run the qwen CLI against the server.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A, docs only.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none for code, the change is one docs section.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live qwen session against the SpecStream server.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

None. Docs-only addition in the same shape as #13999 and #14000.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

在 `docs/developers/tools/web-search.md` 的 "Supported MCP Web Search Services" 列表中，You.com 之后新增 SpecStream 一节，格式与 looot 条目（#13999）相同：简介（说明哪些内容会发送给服务方）、文档、费用、获取 API Key、适用场景、工具列表，以及远程服务的 CLI 和 `settings.json` 两种配置方式（Bearer 请求头）。SpecStream 的远程 MCP 服务地址为 `https://api.specstream.ai/mcp`，提供网页搜索（`search_web`，每条结果带来源 URL，页面注明时附发布日期）、网页读取（`read_pages`，网页和 PDF 转为 Markdown）以及按价格确认的研究报告。我在 SpecStream 工作，这是服务商自身的新增条目。

无法使用内置 `web_search` 的模型服务（OpenRouter、DeepSeek、本地模型）的用户需要通过 MCP 服务进行搜索和网页读取，本条目提供另一种选择，配置方式与其他远程条目一致。

仅修改文档，未改动代码。未发送密钥时 `POST https://api.specstream.ai/mcp` 返回 401；`prettier --check` 通过；未使用 qwen CLI 实测该服务。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): isolate PowerShell during Windows standalone updates
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Windows standalone updates now isolate the extraction subprocess from inherited PowerShell 7 module paths, allowing Windows PowerShell 5.1 to resolve its compatible Archive module without changing the parent environment or the system-wide execution policy.

Extraction errors are treated as failures and retain bounded, stream-decoded UTF-8 diagnostics. The subprocess also isolates encoding changes from the caller's console. Regression coverage exercises inherited and normal module environments, corrupt archives, and installation preservation after failure.

## Why it's needed

Updating the standalone installation from 0.26.9 to 0.27.3 under Microsoft Store PowerShell 7.7 failed with only `Expand-Archive exited with code 1`. The inherited `PSModulePath` caused Windows PowerShell 5.1 to load a PowerShell 7 Archive module, and discarded stderr concealed the underlying module-loading error.

Adding `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` alone is insufficient: the incompatible module can report a missing .NET overload while exiting 0 without extracting the expected files. Selecting the compatible module and making extraction errors terminating addresses both failure modes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. On Windows, use isolated archive/installation fixtures with the parent `PSModulePath` pointing to PowerShell 7 modules. Confirm that a valid archive is extracted and its manifest is parsed and validated, while the parent environment remains unchanged. Confirm the normal Windows PowerShell environment also works.
2. Supply a corrupt archive. Confirm that extraction fails with the underlying diagnostic, localized text survives UTF-8 decoding, and the existing installation is preserved with temporary extraction state and the update lock cleaned up.
3. In an isolated shared console seeded to input/output code pages 936/936, run the extraction subprocess with the production options. Confirm that the caller remains at 936/936 after child exit. The child may change its own output code page; a zero console-window handle alone does not prove console absence.

### Evidence (Before & After)

**Before:** the reported standalone update failed after download:

```text
更新失败：Expand-Archive exited with code 1
```

A read-only diagnostic in the original terminal exposed `PSSecurityException` / `UnauthorizedAccess` while Windows PowerShell 5.1 attempted to load the Microsoft Store PowerShell 7.7 Archive module.

**After, using isolated fixtures and real Windows subprocesses:**

- Valid archive: exit 0 with extracted contents verified byte-for-byte.
- Corrupt archive: exit 1 with lossless UTF-8 diagnostics, including Chinese text on the reproduction host.
- Native shared-console measurements: caller input/output code pages remained 936/936 before and after extraction. An independent asynchronous subprocess probe also confirmed the encoding change stayed isolated from the caller.
- Targeted updater tests: **86 passed, 72 platform-skipped**. These exercise the actual updater with fixture downloads; the valid archive is intentionally incomplete and reaches the later installation-layout check after successful extraction and manifest validation.
- Workspace build, all declared workspace and integration typechecks, targeted ESLint/Prettier checks, bundle, and bundled CLI version smoke check passed locally.

These results verify extraction and error handling; they do not claim a completed production upgrade.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ Regression tests and real subprocess/console probes |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Windows x64; Node.js 26.8.2 for local builds and probes; Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9818; Microsoft Store PowerShell 7.7.0.0 module directory present. Windows PowerShell's effective execution policy was `Restricted` with all individual scopes `Undefined`. Console verification used disposable hidden consoles and isolated fixtures, leaving the real installation untouched.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Windows extraction now uses a sanitized child module environment and explicit diagnostic encoding. Native console probes verify isolation from the caller; they do not establish the absence of a child console.
- Not validated / out of scope: a full live 0.26.9 → 0.27.3 upgrade, including production download, installation replacement, rollback, and deferred swap; macOS/Linux runtime behavior. Scope is limited to Windows extraction and focused regression coverage.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No new dependencies or system-wide execution-policy changes are required. Existing checksum verification, extracted-path validation, replacement, and failure cleanup remain in place.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17211

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Windows 独立安装版更新时，解压子进程会隔离继承自 PowerShell 7 的模块路径，让 Windows PowerShell 5.1 使用自身兼容的 Archive 模块，无需修改父进程环境或系统全局执行策略。

解压错误会作为失败处理，并保留有长度上限、采用流式 UTF-8 解码的诊断信息。子进程的编码变化也与调用方控制台隔离。回归测试覆盖继承模块路径、正常模块环境、损坏归档，以及失败后保留已有安装的行为。

## 为什么需要

用户在 Microsoft Store 版 PowerShell 7.7 中，将独立安装版从 0.26.9 更新到 0.27.3 时失败，只看到 `Expand-Archive exited with code 1`。继承的 `PSModulePath` 让 Windows PowerShell 5.1 加载了 PowerShell 7 的 Archive 模块，而被丢弃的 stderr 隐藏了实际的模块加载错误。

仅添加 `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` 不足以修复：不兼容模块可能报告 .NET 重载不存在，但仍以 0 退出，且没有解压出预期文件。选择兼容模块并将解压错误设为终止错误，可以同时处理这两种失败模式。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在 Windows 上使用隔离的归档与安装夹具，让父进程的 `PSModulePath` 指向 PowerShell 7 模块。确认有效归档能被解压，清单能够被解析和校验，且父进程环境保持不变；同时确认正常 Windows PowerShell 环境也能工作。
2. 提供损坏归档。确认解压失败时包含底层诊断，本地化文本经过 UTF-8 解码后仍完整可读，已有安装保持不变，临时解压状态和更新锁被清理。
3. 在输入/输出代码页均设为 936 的隔离共享控制台中，使用生产配置启动解压子进程。确认子进程退出后，调用方仍为 936/936。子进程可能修改自身输出代码页；仅凭控制台窗口句柄为 0，不能证明它完全没有控制台。

### 证据（修改前后）

**修改前：** 用户报告独立安装版在下载后更新失败：

```text
更新失败：Expand-Archive exited with code 1
```

在用户原始终端运行只读诊断，确认 Windows PowerShell 5.1 加载 Microsoft Store PowerShell 7.7 的 Archive 模块时，出现 `PSSecurityException` / `UnauthorizedAccess`。

**修改后，使用隔离夹具和真实 Windows 子进程验证：**

- 有效归档：退出码 0，解压内容逐字节核对正确。
- 损坏归档：退出码 1，诊断是无损 UTF-8，复现主机上的中文文本完整保留。
- 原生共享控制台测量：解压前后，调用方输入/输出代码页均保持 936/936。独立的异步子进程探针也确认编码变化未影响调用方。
- 更新器定向测试：**86 项通过、72 项按平台跳过**。测试通过夹具下载执行实际更新器；有效归档被故意设计为不完整，在成功解压并校验清单后，到达后续安装布局检查。
- 工作区构建、全部已声明的工作区及 integration 类型检查、定向 ESLint/Prettier 检查、bundle 和打包后 CLI 版本启动检查均在本地通过。

这些结果验证了解压与错误处理，不代表已经完成真实安装升级。

### 已测试的平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ 回归测试及真实子进程/控制台探针 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |

### 环境（可选）

Windows x64；本地构建和探针使用 Node.js 26.8.2；Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9818；本机存在 Microsoft Store PowerShell 7.7.0.0 模块目录。Windows PowerShell 的有效执行策略为 `Restricted`，各独立作用域均为 `Undefined`。控制台验证使用一次性的隐藏控制台和隔离夹具，未触碰真实安装。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：Windows 解压现在使用清理后的子进程模块环境，并显式设置诊断编码。原生控制台探针验证了与调用方的隔离，但不证明子进程没有控制台。
- 未验证或范围外：真实的 0.26.9 → 0.27.3 完整升级，包括生产下载、安装替换、回滚和延迟替换；macOS/Linux 的运行时行为。本次范围仅限 Windows 解压及对应回归测试。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无。无需新依赖，也无需修改系统全局执行策略。既有的校验和验证、解压路径校验、安装替换及失败清理逻辑继续保留。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #17211

</details>

releases.name: Release v0.27.4
releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

- Managed Agent sessions can access granted local directories and open an interactive Managed Web Terminal without persisting credentials or paths. ([#16844](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16844), [#16866](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16866))
- Send outputs to Feishu and WeCom webhooks, with long managed-channel replies delivered as ordered segments instead of being truncated. ([#17012](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17012), [#17013](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17013), [#17223](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17223), [#17224](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17224), [#17002](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17002))
- Auto Mode now requires explicit authorization for risky actions, reviews classifier timeouts, avoids HTTP(S) URL filesystem lookups, and visibly marks Full Access. ([#16858](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16858), [#17127](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17127), [#17146](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17146), [#17100](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17100))
- Web Shell Goals page can merge goals from trusted workspaces, show workspace badges, and target a selected workspace when creating goals. ([#17230](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17230))
- Manage memory with restored CLI /memory controls, persistent workspace settings, and typed SDK APIs to preview, submit, inspect, cancel, and retry Codex memory imports. ([#17162](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17162), [#17213](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17213))
- Terminal tabs, web previews, local commands, and slash commands keep working over plain HTTP when native UUID support is unavailable. ([#17196](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17196))

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- Managed Agent sessions can use the browser user's local filesystem through temporary directory grants, without persisting credentials or paths. ([#16844](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16844)) by @wenshao
- Long managed-channel replies are split into ordered delivery segments instead of being truncated, with a visible truncation notice if the segment limit is exceeded. ([#17002](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17002)) by @wenshao
- With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop enabled, each AgentCore round runs model and tool batch in one runAgentLoop call, optionally on the event-bus kernel. ([#17059](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17059)) by @qqqys
- feat(cli): run each OpenTUI round in one runAgentLoop call ([#17104](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17104)) by @qqqys
- feat(channels): add Feishu custom bot webhook delivery ([#17012](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17012)) by @jkxiao
- Auto Mode now lets the session model review a fast-classifier timeout once when identifiers differ, allowing or blocking the action under existing policy. ([#17146](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17146)) by @callmeYe
- Exposes a typed workspace-bound SDK API for previewing, submitting, inspecting, canceling, and retrying Codex memory imports. ([#17162](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17162)) by @callmeYe
- Runs each Ink TUI round in one runAgentLoop call when experimental.unifiedAgentLoop is enabled, aligning TUI loop execution. ([#17160](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17160)) by @qqqys
- Adds per-turn Hook execution records, read-only Hook pages, SDK access, summaries, and signed snapshots for session history. ([#17015](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17015)) by @callmeYe
- Makes cancelled runs publish loop.cancelled and finish within a 10-second bound, preserving completed batch results when possible. ([#17145](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17145)) by @qqqys
- Adds a send-only Feishu Webhook connection method with secret URL, optional signing secret, channel control, and scheduled group delivery. ([#17013](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17013)) by @jkxiao
- Adds nightly E2E loop rollout legs for kernel and OpenTUI, including forced parity arms, while push runs keep their current legs. ([#17050](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17050)) by @wenshao
- Enables the serve daemon's PR-state watch to observe and deliver PR updates promptly by provisioning its dependencies and adding resume delivery. ([#17032](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17032)) by @wenshao
- Improves web-shell session search with a dedicated centered dialog, clearer results, keyboard selection, loading and retry states, and responsive layouts. ([#16779](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16779)) by @deggs7
- Adds an interactive Managed Web Terminal to Managed Agent sessions, using a short-lived ticket for authenticated WebSocket access and keeping the runtime active while attached. ([#16866](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16866)) by @wenshao
- feat(managed-agent): fixed-interval /loop schedules for Managed Sessions ([#17088](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17088)) by @wenshao
- With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop enabled, each ACP round runs in one runAgentLoop call; experimental.eventBusAgentLoop uses the event-bus kernel. ([#17181](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17181)) by @qqqys
- When experimental.unifiedAgentLoop is enabled, speculation model rounds now use the shared agent loop; otherwise behavior is unchanged. ([#17029](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17029)) by @wenshao
- Experimental loop switches now resolve per surface and can be forced on or off by environment overrides such as 1, 0, or headless,acp=0. ([#17055](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17055)) by @wenshao
- Adds a send-only WeCom group webhook Channel that can deliver Notify outputs, prompt results, and supported scheduled-task results to a configured WeCom group. ([#17223](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17223)) by @jkxiao
- Adds a send-only WeCom Webhook connection method with group URL configuration, channel control, and scheduled delivery selection. ([#17224](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17224)) by @jkxiao
- Makes PR watch operator-owned by adding the operator-only serve.sessionPrWatch setting and retiring GitHub channel state-transition delivery. ([#17214](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17214)) by @wenshao
- Restored native /memory controls and User/Project file or managed-folder actions in the CLI, with workspace settings persisting across restarts. ([#17213](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17213)) by @chiga0
- Adds multi-workspace support to the Web Shell Goals page, merging goals from trusted workspaces, adding workspace badges, and letting new goals target a selected workspace. ([#17230](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17230)) by @wenshao
- Adds experimental.unifiedAgentLoop hosted surface so Hosted Harness model rounds can use the shared agent loop while the legacy path remains default. ([#17264](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17264)) by @wenshao

### Bug Fixes

- AUTO permission checks now judge explicit user authorization, especially for destructive, discarding, shared-history, or bulk actions, rather than mere relevance. ([#16858](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16858)) by @yanyukang2003-ux
- When Full Access (yolo) is active, the web shell composer mode trigger now shows its icon and label in the destructive color, keeping the risky mode visibly marked. ([#17100](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17100)) by @callmeYe
- Synchronous managed-session rename settlement no longer waits on the stale tenant guard, allowing concurrent first renames to settle independently within or across tenants. ([#17074](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17074)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(web-shell): preserve observer activity during recovery ([#17098](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17098)) by @callmeYe
- fix(web-shell): show timeline on narrower screens ([#16986](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16986)) by @callmeYe
- fix(deps): 修复 MCP、DOMPurify 和压缩请求解析漏洞 ([#17105](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17105)) by @chiga0
- fix(managed-agent): stop the legacy CSI guard from gap-locking other Sessions ([#17069](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17069)) by @doudouOUC
- Updated qs, fast-uri, ip-address, Hono, and Node adapter security dependencies across workspace and Mobile MCP trees. ([#17134](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17134)) by @chiga0
- AUTO mode no longer tries filesystem resolution for HTTP(S) URLs, preventing Windows network lookup delays and session termination before requests start. ([#17127](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17127)) by @callmeYe
- Native Anthropic conversations now omit unsigned thinking blocks from completed history while keeping visible answers, signed thinking, and completed tool exchanges. ([#17031](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17031)) by @callmeYe
- Updated fast-uri and ip-address in the independent Live Host and CUA Electron installations to secure versions, closing remaining URI and IPv6 advisories. ([#17147](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17147)) by @chiga0
- Goal status messages now show a compact one-line objective preview with Expand details, keeping long objectives from filling the chat. ([#17133](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17133)) by @callmeYe
- An unconfirmed send from another conversation no longer locks the composer; it remains editable, but submission is blocked until retry or discard. ([#17140](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17140)) by @yiliang114
- Edit now recovers matches between non-ASCII text and Unicode escape spellings when exact matching fails, preserving the file's original representation. ([#17096](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17096)) by @callmeYe
- Raises the document export renderer size budget to 2,136,000 bytes so current builds pass export validation. ([#17153](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17153)) by @chiga0
- Upgrades glob and minimatch together to secure versions, improving matching reliability and preventing search regressions. ([#17149](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17149)) by @chiga0
- Hover timestamps no longer cover message controls in the web shell, keeping buttons such as Goal details readable. ([#17168](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17168)) by @callmeYe
- Removes obsolete ExcelJS archive dependency paths and updates unzipper to 0.12.5 for cleaner dependency resolution. ([#17163](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17163)) by @chiga0
- Upgrades minimatch and glob dependencies in independent Electron build trees to address security advisories. ([#17165](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17165)) by @chiga0
- fix(external-context): deflake malformed proxy env test (#17176) ([#17179](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17179)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Prevents table toolbar overlap in narrow web-shell views by compacting controls, shortening summaries, and preserving row counts. ([#17020](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17020)) by @Lilian0122
- Clears non-sensitive OpenTUI extension-setting drafts when Ctrl+C is pressed, fixing text accumulation in ordinary setting fields. ([#15951](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15951)) by @chiga0
- Prepares file watchers before final interactive exit so /quit can complete cleanly instead of leaving the CLI process alive. ([#17148](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17148)) by @chiga0
- Fixes Unicode Edit recovery so it no longer damages syntax by matching inside backslash, hexadecimal, or Unicode escape sequences. ([#17152](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17152)) by @callmeYe
- fix(ci): route classify_pr by association and admit dispatch to the fleet ([#17178](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17178)) by @yiliang114
- Terminal tabs, web previews, local and slash commands, and related shell flows now keep working over plain HTTP by generating IDs when native UUID support is unavailable. ([#17196](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17196)) by @wenshao
- Managed Sessions /loop schedules now recover more efficiently and only expose the cron tools declared for the session profile. ([#17197](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17197)) by @wenshao
- Fixes the agent tab context usage meter to use the agent's own model window instead of the main session window. ([#13614](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13614)) by @Shizoqua
- Fixed the CLI feedback prompt to preserve typed input and made newly registered workflow commands appear immediately in the model-facing catalog. ([#17233](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17233)) by @qqqys
- Fixed managed-agent configuration reads to accept PUBLISHED as a settled state for the relevant Agent resources. ([#17207](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17207)) by @yiliang114
- Fixed the memory-manager integration suite so it can choose an output root without requiring a special environment variable. ([#17265](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17265)) by @wenshao
- Returns correlated error responses for Java SDK control callback failures, including request ID, subtype, and error value. ([#17113](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17113)) by @Afloat16
- Fixes release validation failures in interactive memory-manager tests by ensuring fake editor and opener scripts run correctly. ([#17294](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17294)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Fixes managed agent child sessions to use inherited extension configuration at committed state and report failures before Runtime acquisition. ([#17281](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17281)) by @yiliang114

### Performance

- Improves CLI performance in ACP by skipping interactive extension watching, reducing startup contention. ([#17177](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17177)) by @callmeYe
- Speeds up the first native ACP session by overlapping initialization work and deferring unneeded command and dependency loading. ([#17209](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17209)) by @callmeYe
- Improves Java transcript performance by sharing immutable event snapshots instead of duplicating parsed page data. ([#17115](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17115)) by @Afloat16
- Speeds up the Web Shell Daemon Status Usage dashboard by caching per-transcript usage summaries and rescanning only changed transcripts. ([#17239](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17239)) by @wenshao

### Documentation

- Adds bilingual Managed Agent design documentation inventorying lifecycle claim mirrors and tenant guards without changing runtime behavior. ([#17073](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17073)) by @doudouOUC
- Documents streaming tool dispatch decisions in English and Chinese, with opt-in implementation deferred to a follow-up. ([#17171](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17171)) by @qqqys
- README Capabilities now presents a grouped overview of Qwen Code features, with links to user docs and labels for experimental and opt-in features. ([#17226](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17226)) by @wenshao
- Added design documentation evaluating the Hosted Harness agent-loop migration and its separation into journaled tool batch and model round paths. ([#17248](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17248)) by @wenshao
- Updated README availability claims to distinguish default features from experimental or opt-in features and expanded listed chat channels. ([#17263](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17263)) by @wenshao
- Updates README capability labels to avoid repeated pitch text and links /resume to the commands reference. ([#17277](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17277)) by @wenshao
- Updates PR watch design documents to record shipped status, settled review questions, and the removal of the enablement switch. ([#17250](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17250)) by @wenshao

### Internal Changes

- Web shell test now opens Session Overview from the footer entry instead of the More menu, matching single-column layouts. ([#17067](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17067)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Managed Agent schema initialization now uses ManagedSchema.initialize directly after removing the redundant JdbcRuntimeBrokerSchema alias. ([#17075](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17075)) by @doudouOUC
- refactor(managed-agent): drop the catalog probe and repeated root lock from binding control ([#17072](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17072)) by @doudouOUC
- test(cli): compare the kernel off and on in every headless parity scenario ([#17130](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17130)) by @qqqys
- Improves ACP turn handling by replacing host-ownership flags with explicit turn inputs and caller-owned interaction spans. ([#17070](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17070)) by @yiliang114
- Adds an embedding regression test and removes obsolete release repair steps to preserve Managed Agent scheduler isolation. ([#17139](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17139)) by @doudouOUC
- Stabilizes the TUI background notification parity test by normalizing launch size fields and PID-width variations. ([#17114](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17114)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Stabilizes headless and TUI agent-loop parity tests to reduce flaky CI failures without weakening assertions. ([#17172](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17172)) by @yiliang114
- Moves the mid-width toolbar compaction test into the intended container-width band; no product behavior changes. ([#17187](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17187)) by @wenshao
- Stabilizes the managed runtime terminal replay test by attaching the output listener before WebSocket reconnection; no product behavior changes. ([#17194](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17194)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Adds a CI lane that verifies shared-loop and event-bus agent execution across Managed headless, AgentCore, and ACP entry points. ([#17180](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17180)) by @yiliang114
- CI stability improves for large transcript export tests on shared ARM64 runners without weakening regression detection on GitHub-hosted CI or local runs. ([#17205](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17205)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Adds tests verifying Managed Sessions automation handling of null creator keys and tenant isolation, with no production behavior change. ([#17235](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17235)) by @wenshao
- test(external-context): clear lowercase proxy vars in the fail-fast pack test ([#17240](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17240)) by @wenshao
- Internal test change: deflakes the queued-input parity case by treating process-derived shell result size telemetry as volatile. ([#17220](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17220)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Internal test change: strengthens CI coverage for tree-ref encoding guards and corrects misleading test comments. ([#17191](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17191)) by @wenshao
- Internal test change: makes the external-context fail-fast pack test self-contained on proxied runners and adjusts its subprocess timeout. ([#17246](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17246)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Improved web-shell retention tests so wheel events target the transcript and virtualized card restore checks run reliably. ([#17242](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17242)) by @wenshao
- Improved ACP integration tests by counting loop rounds with a dedicated marker for each runAgentLoop call. ([#17227](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17227)) by @qqqys
- Removes an unused per-call client ID override from Web Shell QR-login wiring without changing login behavior. ([#16999](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16999)) by @wenshao
- Moves trusted pull request CI jobs to persistent runners while keeping untrusted PRs on disposable runners. ([#17279](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17279)) by @yiliang114

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/compare/v0.27.3...v0.27.4

issues.title: bug: at 256 retained usage records the next turn fails before dispatch — the capacity handler says it continues, then retain rejects the record

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: os:windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

A local bookkeeping admission failure ends the turn **before the provider request is sent**, with the model never called:

```
Turn failed: provider source admission failed: usage publication has no reserved native journal slot
```

This contradicts the 0.10.3 changelog entry at `CHANGELOG.md:505`: *"Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error... The turn now continues, the receipt keeps the accounting error, and the status line says the cost is uncertain."*

That promise was implemented for the **settlement** path only. The **admission** path, which runs earlier, was never made non-fatal — and it is still fatal on `upstream/main`.

## Observed

Four admission failures between 13 and 15 November 2026, in three different sessions, on `0.10.3 (dev)` built from `5af8a9a24`:

| When (UTC) | Session |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-11-13T20:56:01 | `f80a14df…` |
| 2026-11-15T02:18:35 | `c6d6e81d…` |
| 2026-11-15T03:40:00 | `da9cbd26…` |
| 2026-11-15T15:04:01 | `c6d6e81d…` |

Recorded in `turn_outcomes[].error` with `status: "failed"`.

The turn is what is lost, not the prompt: the prompt stays in history and the next message continues from it. Verified in the same session — the failed turn's prompt is retained and answered by the following turn. What the operator pays is a dead round trip, not retyping.

## Root cause: the usage journal's capacity path contradicts itself

This is not an owner-mismatch race. The immediate trigger is visible in the log, and it lines up with all four failures:

```
2026-11-15T15:03:52.792468Z  WARN codewhale_engine::cost_status:
    native usage journal is at capacity; this request continues without a retained receipt
2026-11-15T15:03:52.793015Z  WARN codewhale_engine::tools::subagent::engine:
    child refusal receipt was not admitted
    error=usage publication has no reserved native journal slot
2026-11-15T15:04:01.367856Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Failed
```

Seven capacity warnings in the log window; every admission failure follows one within seconds:

| Capacity warning (UTC) | Turn failed (UTC) | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-13T20:56:01.736 | 2026-11-13T20:56:01.912 | 0.18 s |
| 2026-11-15T02:18:33.174 | 2026-11-15T02:18:35.642 | 2.5 s |
| 2026-11-15T03:40:00.255 | 2026-11-15T03:40:00.419 | 0.16 s |
| 2026-11-15T15:03:52.792 | 2026-11-15T15:04:01.367 | 8.6 s |

The code path, in `crates/engine/src/cost_status.rs`:

1. `prepare_observed_kind` calls `reserve_retention_slot()` before building the record.
2. `reserve_retention_slot` checks the per-owner cap (`MAX_RUNTIME_USAGE_RECORDS_PER_OWNER = 256`). At capacity it logs *"this request continues without a retained receipt"* and returns `Ok(())` — **before** `slot.active.store(true)` and **before** inserting the slot into `native_slots`.
3. `prepare_observed_kind` continues, builds the record with that same (still inactive) slot, and calls `retain_runtime_usage_record(owner, &record)?`.
4. `retain_runtime_usage_record` checks `proof.slot.active` — false — and returns `WouldBlock` with *"usage publication has no reserved native journal slot"*.
5. That error propagates out of `admit_dispatch`, and the turn fails.

So the capacity handler says "continue without a receipt" and the very next call makes it fatal. The two halves of the same function disagree.

## Why it is a defect and not a policy

- **Nothing was dispatched.** Unlike a stream drop or a timeout there is no unknown provider outcome — the request never left. Nothing was billed, nothing was generated, no duplicate risk exists.
- **It is local.** The provider, the network and the model are irrelevant; a journal slot is Codewhale's own bookkeeping.
- **The behaviour is documented as fixed for this class.** The settlement branch honours that (`turn_loop.rs`: `tracing::warn!(%error, "provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues")`). The admission branch does not. Note the admission path was added in `ccc087723` (2026-11-02) and the later `bc3ad117e` (2026-11-07) fixed only the settlement path; it never touched `model_step.rs`.

## Still present upstream

Checked against `upstream/main` at `b107c4996`, 350 commits ahead of the build that produced these failures:

- `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs` still returns `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed` with `provider source admission failed`.
- `crates/engine/src/cost_status.rs` still has the `WouldBlock` "no reserved native journal slot".
- The three commits that touched `model_step.rs` since the build (Auto-Review intent, RunOrigin minting, DeepSeek parity) do not change this block.

Updating the binary does not fix this.

## Suggested direction

Make the capacity path and the retention call agree. Two options, either is small:

1. **Skip the retain when reservation declined.** Have `reserve_retention_slot` report that it declined (at capacity), and have `prepare_observed_kind` skip `retain_runtime_usage_record` for that record — the handler already decided the request should continue without a receipt.
2. **Make admission non-fatal, like settlement.** Log the admission failure with its code and let the request proceed with cost unknown. The turn is what produces the usage the journal is trying to record; failing it to protect the journal is backwards.

Option 1 is narrower and preserves the existing retention semantics. Independently of either, the capacity branch is worth a second look: 256 records per owner is reachable in a long session, and the branch currently drops retention silently for every request past the cap even when it does not fail the turn.

The `AlreadyExists` guard ("usage source was already admitted") may deserve a fatal path — that one signals a real double-admission bug — but it should be a distinct variant, not shared with a capacity or retention-slot condition.

**Scope note: this block has three fatal returns, not one.** The same pre-dispatch section also fails the turn on a `NativeUsageOrigin::runtime` construction error ("provider accounting admission failed") and on `bind_dispatch`. All three are local bookkeeping that runs before dispatch, so a fix should decide the class rather than patch the one message string this report happens to contain.

## Related

- #7328 — the logging/card defect for provider failures (commented there about this one).
- `bc3ad117e` — made the settlement path non-fatal; this issue asks for the same on admission, or for the capacity path to stop contradicting itself.
- `ccc087723` — added the admission path.
- `CHANGELOG.md:505-509` — the 0.10.3 changelog entry this contradicts. (0.10.3 is not tagged; the latest release is v0.10.2.)

issues.title: Provider failures: the diagnostic log has no cause, and the error card drops the typed code

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
When a provider request dies after dispatch, the cause survives as English prose in two places (the session record and `codewhale receipts`) and **never reaches the diagnostic log**. The prose is also the only machine-readable form there is: no receipt field, no log field, no structured tag.

1. **The session record keeps prose, not a cause.** `turn_outcomes[].error` holds a sentence; the `Provider request receipt` carries `outcome: "open_failed" | "incomplete"` and `coverage: "missing"` but **no cause field**, so a consumer must regex English to tell a header stall from a mid-stream read drop from a proxy reset. `codewhale receipts` re-renders that same sentence, so it inherits the same limitation.
2. **The diagnostic log holds neither.** `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log` records `engine turn completion settled status=Failed` and nothing about the reason: a grep for every provider failure family returns **zero** hits across 62 log files, while the settlement line appears 463 times.
3. **The rendered card drops the typed code.** The card is prose composed from the raw provider string; the typed `code` the envelope already carries (`llm_network_error`, `llm_timeout`, `llm_server_<status>`, …) never reaches the reader, and neither does `RequestTransmission` (`NotDispatched` / `Rejected` / `OutcomeUnknown`) — the one field that answers "did the provider see it".

None of this is a retry-policy complaint, and none of it says the cause is lost — `receipts` proves it is not. It is a "the evidence is not where a support reader looks, and is not structured where a tool could use it" complaint, and it is cheap to fix.

**Stated up front so nobody has to discover it:** `codewhale receipts <id> --format json` already returns the cause (verified live, quoted in § Defect 1). This issue argues the log and the card should carry it too, not that it is unavailable.

---

## What is measured, and how

Two corpora, both from one operator's machine:

- **Session records** — `~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json`, 610 files, 2026-09-15 → 2026-11-12. Each carries a `journal` (`message` + `system` entries) and `turn_outcomes[]`.
- **Diagnostic logs** — `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log`, 62 files, 2026-11-05 → 2026-11-12, 8.4 MB. These files are appended to while a session runs, so the counts below are a snapshot; `Completed` drifts upward between reads while `Failed` stays at 15.

### Where the failures actually are

`turn_outcomes[]` with `status: "failed"` across the whole corpus: **180 records, every one carrying an `error` string**. Grouped by cause:

| Cause (verbatim leading text) | Count | First seen | Last seen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Provider returned an empty response` | 44 | 2026-10-05 | 2026-10-26 |
| `Upstream idle timeout exceeded` | 26 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-11-02 |
| rate-limit / 429 family | 25 | 2026-10-18 | 2026-11-06 |
| `Provider stream connection dropped…` (transport read) | 12 | 2026-10-10 | 2026-11-12 |
| auth family | 10 | 2026-10-xx | 2026-11-09 |
| `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` | 5 | 2026-10-23 | 2026-11-06 |
| `Network error: Request failed: error sending request` | 2 | 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12 |
| `Provider usage settlement failed…` | 2 | 2026-11-11 | 2026-11-11 |
| `Request timed out after 0ns` | 1 | 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12 |
| other (tool, policy, quota, malformed provider text) | remainder | | |

### What survives into the log

Zero. Across all 62 files:

```
$ grep -c "Provider stream connection dropped" ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0 in every file
$ grep -c "error decoding response body"        ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "error sending request"               ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "did not receive response headers"    ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "Upstream idle timeout"               ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
```

What the log *does* contain is the bare settlement line — `engine turn completion settled status=Failed` — 15 times in the same window:

```
394  engine turn completion settled status=Completed
 54  engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted
 15  engine turn completion settled status=Failed
463  total
```

Attributing each `Failed` to the nearest preceding log line gives: 4 × usage-receipt retention, 3 × snapshot prune, 4 × tool failures, 1 × proxy refusal, 1 × turn stall, 1 × session retention, 1 × nothing. The provider failures above are not among them — they did not write a line at all.

### What survives into the session record

Free text only. For a `Provider request receipt` with `outcome: "open_failed"` or `"incomplete"`, the full key set is:

```
source_accounting, accounting_error, session_id, turn_id, request_index, request_id,
source_id, route, primary, transmission, coverage, physical_requests,
physical_requests_dropped, prefix_check, reused_preparation, wire_observations,
wire_observations_dropped, usage, usage_reported, outcome, transport_retries,
elapsed_ms, cache_attribution
```

There is no `error`, `cause` or `failure_class` field. `accounting_error` exists but is `null` for these. So the only machine-readable statement about a failed request is `outcome` (3 values) and `coverage` (`missing`); the cause lives exclusively in `turn_outcomes[].error` as English prose — and that prose differs by code path, so a consumer has to string-match on sentences that are periodically reworded (see § "Why the prose is not a stable key").

---

## Defect 1 — the diagnostic log has no cause for a failed turn

**Claim, verified against `28b755f6e`:** the failure branches that build the user-visible card have no `tracing` call at `warn`/`error` level, and the one line that does settle a turn carries the status but not the cause.

Where the two cards are actually built:

- **Stream-open failures** — `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs:424` calls `initial_stream_error_user_message(...)`, then the `Err` arm runs to `model_step.rs:~486-536` and returns `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed`. That file has exactly two `tracing` calls: `:577` `tracing::debug!` (target `provider_response_diagnostics`) and `:637` `tracing::warn!` (child usage settlement). Neither carries the error.
- **Transport-read failures** (`Provider stream connection dropped…`) — built at `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:5073` via `stream_read_error_user_message(&message, any_content_received)`, in the same shape, also with no `tracing` call.

The umbrella settlement line does exist — `crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs:7961-7968`:

```rust
tracing::info!(
    target: "engine.turn",
    status = ?status,
    event_sent = turn_complete_event_sent,
    "engine turn completion settled"
);
```

(Quoted verbatim from `engine.rs:7961-7968`. The `error` value exists in scope two lines above and is **not** included.)

`info` with `status` — and **no error**, **no route**, **no provider**, **no transmission state**. So the log says a turn failed and cannot say why, which is exactly the question asked after a crash.

**The `debug` line does not rescue this, and that is measured, not assumed.** `crates/runtime/src/runtime_log.rs:137-139` builds the file-subscriber filter as `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or("info")` — so `debug` is dropped by default. In 62 log files / 8.4 MB:

```
grep -c "parent model response settled"  → 0
 grep -c "provider_response_diagnostics"  → 0
 grep -c "engine turn completion settled" → 463
```

That is: the `info` settlement line reaches the file; every `debug` diagnostic does not. Raising `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL`/`RUST_LOG` to `debug` would surface `provider_response_diagnostics` — but it still would not carry the error text, and the default install never sees it.

**What already works, and must be stated or this issue is wrong.** `codewhale receipts <id> --format json` **does** return the cause, because `session_receipt` reads `turn_outcomes[].error` and renders it as a `TurnFailed` action (`crates/engine/src/receipts.rs:142-172`, `:1887-1902`, with `bounded(&redact(...))` for secret hygiene). Verified live against a real session:

```
$ codewhale receipts <session> --format json | jq '.actions[] | select(.tool=="turn" and .status=="failed") | .error'
"Network error: Request failed: error sending request"
"Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. …"
```

So the gap is narrower than "the cause is lost", and the honest statement is: **the cause survives in the session record and (truncated) in `receipts`, and never reaches `tui-*.log`.** A reader who knows to run `receipts` gets the prose; a reader tailing the log — or reading a log shipped by someone else, which is the usual support case — gets `status=Failed` and nothing else.

`receipts` also bounds the sentence: `MAX_ERROR_CHARS = 160` (`crates/engine/src/receipts.rs:50`), and the live output shows the cut — 52 chars for the short one, exactly 160 plus an ellipsis for the long one:

```
52   Network error: Request failed: error sending request
160  Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. Some output had already
     streamed, so Codewhale is surfacing the warning instead of replayin…
```

The truncated tail is where the distinguishing detail lives (`Details: Stream read error: error decoding response body`). So `receipts` gives a *recognisable* cause, not a complete or structured one — a third reason the structured field belongs in the envelope and the log.

**Why the log gap still matters.** `receipts` prints the same free-text `turn_outcomes[].error` sentence, so it inherits the instability described in § "Why the prose is not a stable key" — it can say what the sentence says and nothing structured. It also cannot be grepped across a fleet of sessions without re-implementing the sentence matching. And `not_recorded` / `omitted_actions` mean `receipts` may itself be bounded away from the failure.

**Why there is still no cheap workaround inside the log.** `codewhale_runtime::logging::warn` is stderr-only and gated on `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL` (`crates/runtime/src/logging.rs:106-113`); it never reaches `tui-*.log`. Only `tracing::*` at `info`+ does. Several sibling diagnostics in the same file use `logging::warn` (`turn_loop.rs:5018, 5045, 5097`), so setting `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` still leaves nothing durable.

**Suggested direction.** One `tracing::warn!` (or `error!` when the turn ends) at each failure-card site, carrying the fields the envelope and receipt already have: `code`, `category`, `transmission`, `provider`, `model`, and `http_status` when present. No new event, no new persistence, no behaviour change — the neighbouring `tracing::error!(%error, "provider usage has no durable acknowledgement")` at `turn_loop.rs:4858` is the shape to copy.

---

## Defect 2 — the card drops the typed cause and the transmission state

`crates/engine/src/llm_error_envelope.rs:21-24` sets `envelope.message = display_message`, overwriting whatever the typed mapping produced. The typed `code` survives on the event (`ErrorEnvelope::code`), and `apply_engine_error_to_app` stores only `message` and `severity` into the transcript cell (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:232`). So the reader sees prose and the machinery keeps the code — the two never meet.

Six distinct failures, as the operator sees them:

| Layer | What the operator reads | Says the layer? | Says "provider saw it"? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-dispatch (DNS/TCP/TLS/proxy) | `Connection failed before request dispatch: …` | yes | yes, implicitly |
| Post-dispatch, transport read | `Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. … Details: Stream read error: error decoding response body` | no | no |
| Post-dispatch, request send | `Network error: Request failed: error sending request` | no | no |
| Header stall | `SSE stream request did not receive response headers after Ns; request outcome unknown` | partially | says "unknown" |
| Local idle/timeout ceiling | `SSE stream idle timeout after Ns — no data received (bytes_received=…)` | yes, it's ours | n/a |
| Upstream status | `Server error (503): <provider text>` | yes | yes |

The vocabulary to fix this already exists and is 15 codes wide:

```
llm_quota_window, llm_rate_limited, llm_quota_exhausted, llm_server_<status>,
llm_network_error, llm_connect_before_dispatch, llm_timeout, llm_auth_error,
llm_authorization_error, llm_invalid_request, llm_model_error, llm_content_policy,
llm_context_length, llm_parse_error, llm_other
```

and `RequestTransmission { NotDispatched, Rejected, OutcomeUnknown }` at `crates/engine/src/llm_client/mod.rs:370-374`.

**Suggested direction (composition only):** render a short tag from `code` and the transmission state beside the message — e.g. `provider stream read failed · outcome unknown · resend to continue`. Keep `message` as the detail line. No new types.

---

## Why the prose is not a stable key

The failure sentences are reworded often enough that no consumer can depend on them, which is the concrete argument for Defect 1's structured field:

| Phrase | Present at `28b755f6e`? | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Provider returned an empty response` | **no** (only in a test fixture) | 44 historical failures carried it |
| `Upstream idle timeout exceeded` | **no** (only in a taxonomy test) | 26 historical failures carried it |
| `SSE stream request failed after HTTP/1.1 fallback` | **no** | the fallback error now goes through `h1_fallback_error` (`stream_entry.rs:215-238`) |
| `Request timed out after 0ns` | replaced | now `… (provider request exceeded its transport budget; exact duration not recorded)` — `da201bac8` |
| `Provider stream connection dropped` | yes | `streaming.rs:390-411` |
| `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` | yes | `chat.rs:1732` |

Both rewordings are good on their own — `da201bac8` stopped fabricating `0ns`, and `21c8f86c4` named determinate rejections instead of calling them `internal`. Together they mean the sentence text is not an API, while nothing else carries the same fact.

---

## Corrections to my own earlier counts (so a reader can reproduce)

My first pass over `sessions/*.json` counted **substrings**, which over-counted badly: agent transcripts quoting the failure text, earlier analysis sessions quoting source code, and one conversation describing the same error three times all inflated the numbers. Recounting only `turn_outcomes[].error` — a field the engine writes, never a transcript — gives the 180-record table above. Raw substring counts (e.g. 480 × `error sending request`) are **not** occurrence counts of the fault and should not be read as such.

The distinction matters for one claim I am *not* making: I cannot show that every one of these 180 was recoverable by a single follow-up message. I can show the weaker, verifiable thing: every failure class above except rate-limit and auth was followed in the same session by further successful turns, so the session's work continued.

---

## How to reproduce the counts

A maintainer cannot run my classifier, so here is the exact method. It reads fields the engine writes, never transcript text.

```sh
# Count of failed turns across every saved session.
# -s (slurp) is required: without it jq drops files mid-stream on this corpus.
jq -rs '[.[] | .turn_outcomes[]? | select(.status=="failed")] | length' \
  ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json          # → 180

# The same records, one cause sentence per line, grouped by leading text:
jq -rs '.[] | .turn_outcomes[]? | select(.status=="failed") | .error' \
  ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json \
| sed -E 's/^(.{0,40}).*/\1/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

Two things a reader must know to reproduce these numbers honestly:

- **`-s` matters.** Without slurp, the same one-liner printed 42, 192 and 180 on three consecutive runs over an unchanged directory. The corpus contains multi-megabyte session files, and non-slurped `jq` appears to stop early on this input set. Use `-s`, and expect the total to drift upward while the session doing the counting is itself being saved into the same directory.
- **No deduplication.** A turn that failed twice counts twice. That is intentional: the claim is about how often a reader is left without a cause, not how many distinct faults exist.

Field path: `turn_outcomes[].error` on the session document root, written by `SavedTurnOutcome` (`crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs:2092`).

**The "other 53" bucket is not a junk drawer, and deliberately not expanded.** It decomposes into tool failures, provider plan-quota exhaustion, malformed provider text (`ERROR` alone), a wall-clock ceiling, and a handful of one-off rejections. None of those are transport failures, and none would change the two defects above; expanding them would pad the table without adding an argument.

**What the numbers do not prove.** They are one operator's sessions, from one provider, on one machine, over 59 days. They do **not** establish a rate, a frequency per turn, or that a typical user sees this. They establish only that the failures are common enough in one real corpus to justify a diagnostic line — which is the whole claim.

---

## What this issue does not ask for

- No change to retry policy, defaults, or `[retry]`/`[stream]` semantics.
- No replay of anything after dispatch. The unknown-outcome stop (`92b4900d1`) stays as is.
- No new persistence format — the fields proposed for the log already exist on the envelope and the receipt.

---

## Deferred: the replay knob

The obvious next ask — "give me an opt-in knob that replays these" — was pulled from this draft because its central premise does not survive review:

> **The premise, and why it is wrong.** A header stall or a post-dispatch `NetworkError` means *the client saw no bytes*. It does **not** mean the provider produced no completion. The provider may have generated and billed the entire answer while the client was gone. That is precisely the case `92b4900d1` exists for (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2914-2917`).

Two smaller blockers found while checking it, worth recording here so they are not rediscovered:

- `ErrorEnvelope::recoverable` is not a "resend hint". It drives offline-mode / turn-liveness (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:177-198`) and headless exit status (`exec_error_event_is_fatal` = `!recoverable`, `crates/engine/src/exec_events.rs:206-214`). Repurposing it would change `exec` exit codes and CI behaviour.
- `[retry]` merges **whole-table** per profile (`crates/runtime/src/config.rs:10181`: `retry: override_cfg.retry.or(base.retry)`), unlike `[stream]`'s per-key merge (`:10187`). Any new `[profiles.x.retry]` opt-in would silently discard the base `max_retries`. Also, `crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs` defines **no** `retry.*` keys at all, so `/config` and `config set` cannot reach a new key without schema work.

If it is ever proposed, the honest framing is "replay when the client received no bytes, accepting that the provider may already have billed a completion", with per-attempt cost accounting — not "replay when the provider cannot have answered", which is not knowable.

---

## Related

- `92b4900d1` (2026-11-02) — "stop replaying inference with unknown outcomes". The policy this issue leaves alone.
- #6184 (**open**) — "Engine silently freezes mid-run: user messages are persisted but never answered; no error, no log line, no crash entry". Closest open neighbour; Defect 1 may belong with it.
- #6796 (closed) — "Retry attempts are invisible". Addressed the *retry* banner; the *failure* record is still missing.
- #6843 (closed 2026-10-08) — determinate rejections labelled `internal`. Why prose can be a poor key, and proof the wording moves.
- #6699 (closed) — no retry when the SSE request never received headers.
- #7045 (closed) — SSE retries capped by the stream-open window; HTTP/1.1 fallback returned raw HTTP errors.
- #5769 (closed) — network errors stopping the engine; closed as working-as-intended, which is why this issue is scoped to diagnostics rather than recovery.

## Environment notes (anonymised)

- The local proxy refuses connections on a six-hour cadence (01:54, 07:54, 13:54, 19:54 local), self-heals within ~2 s, 17 times in the 7-day log window: `net: local proxy refused connections; requests go direct until it returns`.
- That window is the environment this issue is written from: a flaky edge, a third-party OpenAI-compatible provider, a model that streams reasoning. Nothing in the report depends on the provider's identity.
- One `Provider plan quota exhausted` cluster (2026-11-09) is the provider's own weekly limit and is not a defect.

issues.body:
Before each model request, `prepare_model_bound_request` (`crates/engine/src/client.rs`) passes every tool result in the conversation through `redact_model_bound_secrets` again, so the redaction cost is paid on every call and grows with the session. Redaction itself is slow on ordinary text: on a 2.8 MB mix of this repo's source, `Cargo.lock` and JSON files, one pass takes about 317 ms here (release build, Windows 11, i7-9700), roughly 9 MB/s.

I have a change ready in `crates/sanitize/src/redact.rs` that brings that pass to about 127 ms (about 2.5x) without changing any masking rule or any output. The old and new code give byte-identical results on every text file in the repo and on fuzzed input, and the existing sanitize tests pass.

Since this sits next to the credential handling that CONTRIBUTING asks to discuss first: would you take a PR for it?

XML fallback tool calls silently lose parameter values containing newlines. A model-generated `write_file` call with multiline content becomes an empty argument object before the engine executes it. The outer invoke matcher already accepts multiline bodies, but both parameter matchers did not.

Enable multiline matching for the two supported parameter forms. The regression exercises the public parser and checks the complete argument object, tool name, and cleaned display text.

prs.body:
## What and why

Adds TrustedRouter as a bundled compatible-host descriptor row, in the same shape as the Opper row (#7131). TrustedRouter is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with one key for models from several labs. `/provider` uses `TRUSTEDROUTER_API_KEY`, `https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as the bootstrap model. Model ids are vendor-prefixed (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`); `trustedrouter/auto` routes each request across models. `GET /v1/models` is public, so discovery is `public_models_endpoint`, like Runcrate and Wafer. Billing stays Unknown in the omission ledger. No new ProviderKind or compiled model roster.

Files: the descriptor row and its test, the compatible-default count and omission row in pricing coverage, the EN and ZH provider docs, and the regenerated `docs/PROVIDERS.md` entries in `web/data/agent-docs.generated.json`. CHANGELOG and credit files are left to maintainers, as CONTRIBUTING asks.

Usage: `/provider trustedrouter` (alias `trusted-router`), or

```toml
provider = "trustedrouter"

[providers.trustedrouter]
kind = "openai-compatible"
base_url = "https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1"
api_key_env = "TRUSTEDROUTER_API_KEY"
model = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash"
```

## Where this came from

Provider addition, no issue needed.

All run with `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9`, so nothing could reach a real API:

prs.title: fix(client): decide the reasoning dialect by endpoint, not by model id
prs.body:
## What and why

A provider row with `kind = "openai-compatible"` (the `custom` identity) that
carries a DeepSeek model id was sent DeepSeek's native `thinking` object on
`/v1/chat/completions`. `apply_route_reasoning_controls` promoted any `custom`
route whose model name matched `requires_reasoning_content` to the `deepseek`
provider kind, and that promotion was unconditional — it never looked at the
endpoint.

Aggregating gateways reject the field. Against a new-api style distributor:

```
400 invalid_request_error  param: "thinking"  code: "unsupported_parameter"
"thinking" is not supported on /v1/chat/completions and was not applied.
Use "reasoning_effort" (or "***.effort") to control thinking.
```

An OpenAI-compatible endpoint's request dialect is not knowable from the model
id alone. That is why every other gateway identity in `reasoning_effort.rs`
(`telecomjs`, `zenmux`, `edenai`, `csdn`, `custom`) already writes neither
`thinking` nor `reasoning_effort`; the `custom` row escaped that policy through
this one promotion.

The promotion stays, because forwarding the configured effort is what `008d21d69`
added it for — custom DeepSeek routes were silently dropping it. What changes is
that the dialect is now decided by the **endpoint**:

- a route labeled `deepseek` speaks DeepSeek's dialect (unchanged);
- a `custom` row pointed at one of DeepSeek's own hosts speaks it too, and keeps
  the native toggle;
- a `custom` row pointed anywhere else keeps the documented `reasoning_effort`
  spelling and loses the native `thinking` object.

`off` on that last kind of route is sent as `reasoning_effort: "none"`, the
compatibility spelling this repository already maps `off` to for other
compatible routes. On the gateway this was verified against, `none` stopped
thinking (`reasoning_tokens: 0`, no reasoning field) rather than merely omitting
the control. This also keeps the reasoning-replay gate self-consistent: it skips
`reasoning_content` for `off`, so sending no control at all would have left a
gateway that forwards to DeepSeek seeing thinking-on with no replayed reasoning
on assistant tool turns.

`a610a8602` fixes a regression the first commit introduced, found by review
before this PR was opened: `translate_prepared_with_usage` passed
`self.api_provider` instead of `chat_shape_provider`, so the named DS4 route (an
`openai-compatible` row that implements the first-party DeepSeek dialect) lost
`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` on its translation requests. Both Chat
Completions call sites now agree on `chat_shape_provider`.

A note on the history: `c0b848807`'s message says the gateway cleanup "used to
sit before nine other shapers". That count is wrong. The correct figure is 11
shaper calls after the original position (local_reasoning, modelstudio, minimax,
inkling, openai, xai, direct_moonshot_k3, kimi_code_k3, zai, mistral, google),
of which 7 write or remove `thinking` (counting the generic effort layer makes 8).
The message is not amended because this fork does not force-push shared refs;
this paragraph is the correction. The code is unaffected either way: the cleanup
is now the function's last statement.

Known limitations, all stated in the code or below rather than discovered later:

- `none` handling depends on the gateway. One that validates the field fails
  loudly; one that silently ignores unknown values falls back to its own default
  while the replay gate skips `reasoning_content`. This mapping is only
  self-consistent on gateways that implement `none`.
- A row declared `kind = "deepseek"` and pointed at a gateway still sends
  `thinking`. That label is the operator stating "this is DeepSeek"; adding
  endpoint awareness to it would change every existing `[providers.deepseek]`
  mirror config, so it is out of scope here.
- `api.deepseeki.com` is in the host set on purpose. `docs/REBRAND.md` records it
  as a historical typo kept for existing configs, and the strict-tools and
  Responses paths accept it too — being inconsistent would make one host DeepSeek
  for those and not for reasoning.
- A `custom` row on an official host written as `http://` (or with a trailing
  dot in the FQDN) now falls into the gateway branch. Narrow, and consistent with
  how `deepseek_base_url_supports_strict_tools` already matches.
- `reasoning_content` replay on assistant tool turns is still keyed on the model
  name for these routes. That predates this change and is deliberate: a gateway
  that forwards to DeepSeek needs it. A gateway that validates message bodies
  strictly could still reject it.

## Where this came from

A bug fix with no issue — reported directly, reproduced against the gateway
before the change.

## How I tested it

Each test below fails against the code before its commit.

```
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::openai_compatible_gateway_gets_no_deepseek_thinking_dialect_from_a_model_name
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::a_custom_row_on_the_official_deepseek_host_keeps_the_thinking_toggle
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::a_lookalike_host_does_not_inherit_the_deepseek_dialect
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::the_deepseek_identity_keeps_its_thinking_toggle
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::tests::deepseek_chat_wire_body_tracks_the_documented_effort_ladder
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::ds4_tests::named_ds4_translation_keeps_the_disabled_thinking_toggle
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib client::ds4_tests::a_gateway_translation_asks_for_none_instead_of_the_thinking_toggle

test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed    (each of the seven)
```

Beyond running them, each assertion was checked by breaking the code it covers
and confirming the test goes red:

- forcing `is_deepseek_chat_host` to `false` → both host-decision tests fail
  (`left: None`, expected `Some("disabled")`);
- deleting `rsplit('@')` → the userinfo case fails;
- deleting `split(':')` → the port case fails;
- making the `none` injection unconditional → the `auto` case fails
  (`left: Some("none")`, expected `None`).

Whole-module run, with the local HTTP proxy unset so mock-server loopback
requests are not intercepted:

```
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib "client::" -- --test-threads=2
test result: FAILED. 676 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 6501 filtered out
```

The one failure is pre-existing and environmental, not from this change:

```
client::stream_entry::tests::refused_connection_names_the_host_and_skips_the_http1_hint
panicked at crates/engine/src/client/stream_entry.rs:628:
nothing listens on the port: Response { status: 503, headers: {"proxy-connection": "close", ...} }
```

It asserts `(connection refused)` while this host reports `(connection failed)`.
Reproduced on unmodified `upstream/main` (`71cab400f`) by stashing this branch
and re-running the same command — it fails identically there. The file it lives
in is not touched by this PR.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` exits 0.

Live check with a CLI built from this branch against the gateway, on the config
that previously returned 400:

- plain turn → `OK` (200)
- `--auto` tool turn (tool call, tool result, `reasoning_content` replay) → 200
- `reasoning_effort = "off"` → `OK` (200)

The gateway was also verified by hand to accept `reasoning_effort: "none"`
(`reasoning_tokens: 0`), `minimal`, streaming, `tool_calls`, and replayed
`reasoning_content`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

Not a new user-facing feature: this fixes the request dialect for an existing
provider identity. No `docs/features.toml` row applies, and no `CHANGELOG.md`
change is included.

## Attribution

issues.body:
### What happens

You switch to another app for a few seconds. While you are away, the Control UI's Gateway socket stops delivering frames without closing. When you come back, the page looks the same as before, and nothing the Gateway sends arrives. In live runs the UI replaced the socket 17.5 s after the return on the chat page, and 41 s and 56 s after it on the model setup page.

### Why

`ui/src/app/gateway-page-activation.ts` runs a recovery check on `visibilitychange`, `focus`, persisted `pageshow` and `online`. It replaces the client only when `needsWakeReconnect` is true: the socket is closed, or nothing has arrived for longer than the silence window (two Gateway ticks, 60 s by default).

A socket that died while you were away for a few seconds fails neither test. It still reports open, and its last frame is only seconds old. Detection then falls to the inbound-silence watchdog in `ui/src/api/gateway.ts`, which waits for the 60 s silence window (or for a request to go unanswered for 5 s) and then gives a `health` probe 10 s to answer. Nothing on return asks the socket whether it is still there. On the chat page the composer reloads its Talk settings on every window focus; on a dead socket those requests go unanswered, so the watchdog probes about 5 s after the return. Pages without the composer send nothing on return, so they wait for the 60 s silence window or for some later request to go unanswered.

Measured on `main` (e970cf66f7b) with the repo's Vitest page-activation harness: a socket that goes silent during a 5 s app switch is replaced 65,000 ms after focus returns. In a live run (Chrome for Testing and an isolated Gateway in a macOS VM, with a proxy that stops forwarding on the open socket during a 5 s switch to Finder), the socket was replaced 41.2 s and 56.1 s after the return on the model setup page. On the chat page, with a stand-in model whose reply finished while away, the reply appeared 17.5 s after the return.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI and wait for it to connect.
2. Switch to another app. While you are away, make the socket stop delivering frames without closing it (for example, a local proxy that stops forwarding but keeps the TCP connection open).
3. Switch back within a few seconds.
4. Nothing arrives until the UI replaces the socket: 17.5 s after you switch back on the chat page, 41 s and 56 s on the model setup page in the live runs.

### Proposed fix

On return, when the socket still counts as healthy, send the existing `health` liveness probe right away, with the watchdog's existing 10 s deadline. Any inbound frame (the reply, an error reply, a tick, a chat event) keeps the socket; if nothing arrives, the existing watchdog closes it and the reconnect supervisor replaces it. A socket already silent past the tick window is still replaced at once, as today.

This costs one `health` request per return to the window while connected.

Related: #198451 covered a connection that had already dropped. This one still looks open.

## Summary

`openclaw configure --section workspace` accepts a regular file, or a path below a regular file, as the workspace directory. Provisioning then fails after the user leaves the prompt. The interactive setup wizard already has a shared path validator that can explain the problem while the user is still editing.

Reuse `validateSetupWorkspacePath` in the configure prompt, applying the same normalization and fallback used when consuming its value. This allows correcting the path in place while preserving the existing protection against persisting a failed workspace.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

The regression runs `runConfigureWizard` with its prompt adapter and real temporary filesystem entries. It checks a file and a child of that file, verifies that neither provisioning nor persistence has started, supplies a corrected directory, and verifies the selected agent receives that directory while the original file remains unchanged.

On base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, the prompt has no validator and the new regression fails. With the fix, all 17 cases pass, including the existing persistence-on-provisioning-failure control:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs   src/commands/configure.wizard.test.ts   --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text

```

## Summary

Inside an existing OpenClaw checkout, the Git installer dry-run displays `~/openclaw`, although the installation path actually selects the current checkout when no destination was explicitly supplied.

## Reproduction

From the root of an OpenClaw checkout:

```sh
bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --dry-run --no-prompt
```

At base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, the observed plan is:

```text
Git directory: <home>/openclaw
Detected checkout: <checkout>
Dry run complete (no changes made)
```

The actual installation target is selected later in `main`, where the detected checkout takes precedence over the implicit default. An explicit `--git-dir` works as expected.

## Expected behavior

Resolve the target once, then use it for both the preview and installation. The dry-run must describe the operation it previews, while remaining free of installation side effects.

I confirmed the before/after output through the actual Bash entry point with network disabled, plus the existing target-precedence test matrix. No installation was performed by the dry-run probes.

## Summary

Doctor correctly inspects a named profile's node service, but its recovery messages print unqualified commands such as `openclaw doctor --fix` and `openclaw node start`. Copying one into a fresh shell targets the default profile instead of the node just diagnosed.

Use the existing `formatCliCommand` owner with the same environment for all three node-service recovery hints: repair, reinstall after preserving custom settings, and starting a repaired but intentionally stopped service. Default-profile commands remain unchanged.

## Reproduction

Run Doctor for a named profile with a legacy node-service launcher. When repair is deferred or the service has custom native settings, the printed repair/reinstall command omits the profile. The start hint after repairing a stopped service has the same problem.

## Evidence and expected behavior

The regression uses actual temporary launchd definition files and the production Doctor/service readers, with the service manager intercepted. It covers deferred repair, custom native settings and a stopped service repaired without activation.

On base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, the three named-profile assertions fail because the messages omit `--profile work`. With the fix, the instructions retain the selected identity:

```text
openclaw --profile work doctor --fix
openclaw --profile work node install --force
openclaw --profile work node start
```

All 14 owning-suite tests pass, including the default-profile, preservation and rollback controls. The named-profile custom/deferred cases preserve the service definition byte-for-byte; the stopped case remains stopped while its stored launcher is repaired.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor-node-services.test.ts \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Summary

The Podman setup script recognizes only `--quadlet` and `--container` and silently ignores all other arguments. As a result, `--help` enters setup and a typo such as `--qudalet` proceeds with the default container mode.

Parse options before loading setup helpers or checking host dependencies. `-h`/`--help` should print usage and exit successfully; unknown options and positional arguments should fail with exit 2 before any provisioning. Existing mode selection and the documented environment override retain their precedence.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

The new tests execute the Bash entry point, with a temporary HOME and intercepted external commands. Both help flags work even when the setup repository path is unavailable. Three invalid-argument cases verify exit 2, a useful usage message, no Podman invocation and no configuration directory.

All five new cases fail on unchanged base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca` and pass with the fix. The existing token/configuration controls also pass:

## Summary

Non-interactive setup rejects `--gateway-bind custom` when `gateway.customBindHost` is missing, then recommends plain `openclaw onboard` to be prompted for the address. That command drops the custom-bind intent and takes the default setup route instead of selecting the promised custom-address prompt.

Keep `--gateway-bind custom` in the interactive recovery command. The config-set alternative and existing profile-aware command formatter remain unchanged.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

The regression calls the actual non-interactive gateway configuration handler. On base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, its diagnostic ends with:

```text
or run openclaw onboard interactively to be prompted for it.
```

After the fix:

```text
or run openclaw onboard --gateway-bind custom interactively to be prompted for it.
```

The strengthened existing assertion fails on base and passes after the fix; all 28 cases in the owning suite pass:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs   src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/gateway-config.test.ts   --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       28 passed (28)
```
