issues.title: [Feature]: Workboard: give each card its own URL so it can be opened directly from a link

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
### Summary

Give each Workboard card its own URL in the Control UI, e.g. `/workboard/<boardId>/<cardId>` (or `/workboard/<boardId>?card=<cardId>`), so a card's details can be opened directly from a link.

### Problem to solve

The only Workboard routes are `/workboard` and `/workboard/<boardId>` (docs/web/urls.md). Opening a card's details is in-page state: the URL doesn't change when a card is open, and the Workboard Control UI reads no card parameter from the URL. So nothing outside the Control UI can link to a specific card.

That breaks a common setup: mirroring Workboard cards into an external task manager (we mirror a board into Things 3 on iPhone/Mac, one to-do per card, with the card's link in the to-do's notes). Tapping the link can only land on the board; the user then has to search for the card on the board. The same applies to links in emails, notes, chat messages, or comments on another card.

Sessions already have this: `/chat/<agentId>/<sessionRef>` and `/sessions?session=<sessionKey>` open a specific session directly. Cards are the one first-class object without an addressable URL.

### Proposed solution

1. Add a card route: `/workboard/<boardId>/<cardId>` (preferred, matches the readable-path style in docs/web/urls.md) or a `?card=<cardId>` parameter on the board route.
2. Opening that URL shows the board with the card's details open. If the card is on a different board than the one in the path, or archived, resolve it anyway (redirect to its board / show the archived card) instead of failing silently.
3. Opening and closing card details updates the URL (push/replace history), so the browser back button, reload and "copy link" work on an open card.
4. Add **Copy link** to the card's menu, using `gateway.publicOrigin` like the session **Copy link** does.
5. Optionally expose the card URL in `workboard.cards.*` responses / `workboard_read` so agents and sync scripts can write it into external tools without building it themselves.

### Alternatives considered

- **Link to the board and search:** what users do today; several extra steps per card, and on mobile the search is awkward.
- **Link to the card's session instead:** works only for cards that have a linked session. Creating a session per card just to get a link adds sidebar noise and doesn't help cards that are only tracked, not worked.
- **#183966** asks for the session-header chip to open the linked card instead of the board. Related, and a card route would be the natural way to implement it, but that issue is about in-UI navigation and doesn't ask for an addressable URL.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone linking to Workboard cards from outside the Control UI (task-manager mirrors, notes, messages, other cards).
- Severity: annoying to workflow-blocking for mirrored setups; every card link resolves to the board.
- Frequency: every time a card is opened from an external link.
- Consequence: manual search per card; external integrations can't deep-link at all.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3, Control UI on macOS and iOS Safari.
- docs/web/urls.md route table lists Workboard as `/workboard` with `/workboard/<boardId>` only.
- Related: #183966 (open the linked card from the session chip), #197180 (board links in nav).

issues.body:
## Summary

The standalone CLI installer accepts `--node-version v24.22.1`, but uses that value literally when constructing its archive URLs. Setup requests `/dist/vv24.22.1/` instead of `/dist/v24.22.1/`. An incomplete future-major value such as `27` also passes validation and reaches `/dist/v27/`.

## Reproduction

On base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, run:

```sh
bash scripts/install-cli.sh --node-only --prefix "$HOME/openclaw-node" --node-version v24.22.1
```

I exercised the actual Bash entry point in a network-disabled sandbox with `curl` intercepted at the download boundary:

```text
--node-version v24.22.1
  Installing Node v24.22.1 (user-space)...
  requested https://nodejs.org/dist/vv24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt
--node-version 24.22.1
  requested https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt
--node-version 27
  requested https://nodejs.org/dist/v27/SHASUMS256.txt
```

## Expected behavior

Normalize an accepted leading `v` once, before using the release as an archive path or runtime directory. Require a complete numeric archive release before preparing installation files. Keep the existing, broader classification of already-installed Node runtimes unchanged.

This is a Simple Setup recovery problem: an accepted option sends the user into a download failure instead of a usable release or an immediate input diagnostic.

## Summary

The CLI installer invokes `os_detect` and `arch_detect` inside arguments to other functions. Their failing status is lost: the error text becomes an argument, and setup proceeds into private Node preparation and downloads.

## Reproduction and evidence

Base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, actual Bash entry point:

```sh
bash scripts/install-cli.sh --json --node-only --prefix "$HOME/openclaw-node"
```

With `uname` reporting `Linux/riscv64` or `SunOS/x86_64`, the observed output starts provisioning rather than surfacing the platform error:

```json
{"event":"step","name":"node","status":"start","version":"24.22.1"}
```

Both cases create the selected prefix and reach a request for `https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt`. I reproduced this using a `uname` fixture and an intercepted `curl` in a network-disabled macOS sandbox; this isolates the installer response to those platform values, rather than claiming execution on those operating systems.

## Expected behavior

Return the existing unsupported-platform diagnostic before preparing files or downloading Node. In JSON mode, emit a single error event. Supported platforms should keep their current installation path.

The detector already knows the problem; preserving its status gives users the actionable setup error instead of an unrelated provisioning failure.

issues.body:
### Summary

Since plugin generation capture landed (#144252, first shipped in 2026.9.6), a Gateway with an external or workspace plugin that has a large package or dependency tree blocks its event loop for minutes. It happens at startup, and again whenever the prepared model runtime republishes. While the loop is blocked the Gateway accepts TCP connections but answers nothing, including `/healthz`, WebSocket RPCs and channel polling.

`capturePluginGenerationArtifact` (`src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts`) copies the plugin package synchronously on the main thread. When no `entryFile` is set, `copyPackage` copies the whole root. It then walks and copies the dependency tree through `capturePluginDependencies` → `linkDependency` → `copyPackage` → `copy`.

### Evidence

**Isolated repro on origin/main `4d4d99d`**, using a synthetic 878 MB context-engine plugin:
- The Gateway stalls for 219 s before it starts listening, then for another 168 s.
- It logs `prepared model runtime startup degraded after 120000ms (workspace plugins; agent main)`.

**Production Gateway on 2026.9.6.** The plugin root is a Bun global install: a 134 MB package whose sibling `node_modules` hold 1.5 GB across 221 packages.
- **Startup:** the process started at T+0 and logged `http server listening` at T+2m20s. `/healthz` timed out until about T+7m.
- **Stacks:** four inspector samples taken during the hang all show the same stack:
  ```
  realpathSync / path.join
  ← pluginNativeNamespaceMemberPath / resolvePreparedSource
  ← copy (recursive)
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← linkDependency ← capturePluginDependencies ← captureDependencies
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← capturePluginGenerationArtifact
  ← bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader ← loadPluginModule ← loadRuntimePluginCandidate
  ```
- **Earlier, during a prepared-runtime republish:**
  - The event loop was blocked for 124 s (`eventLoopDelayMaxMs=124352`).
  - Telegram polling stalled.
  - `config.patch` took 125 s and returned `UNAVAILABLE`, followed by `prepared model runtime reload failed after config commit: prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out; restarting gateway`.
  - The Gateway then restarted, and startup blocked again.
  - Separately, the Control UI's provider sign-in stayed on a blank tab for the whole outage. That is covered by #160954.

A `thinkingDefault` patch alone hot-applies in 50 ms in the isolated repro. The republish in production was probably already pending. Candidate cause: #160120, a refresh loop triggered by an auth profile that fails to resolve. That link is being verified.

### Impact

- Any install with a large external or workspace plugin.
- The Gateway becomes unreachable for minutes on every startup and on every prepared-runtime republish.
- Config hot reloads can escalate into restarts, which block again.
- 2026.7.35 is not affected; 2026.9.6 (npm `latest`/`beta`) is.

### Expected

Capture should not block the Gateway event loop for more than a bounded time. An unchanged plugin should reuse its existing capture instead of being recopied.

**Version:** 2026.11.5-beta.1 (d7e4557), macOS, managed `openclaw` profile, agent tool in code mode.

**What happens:** `browser` `action:"upload"` with a file under the managed downloads directory (`/tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf`) fails with:
`Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (~/.openclaw/media/inbound)`

**Why it's misleading:** `resolveUploadPaths` (`extensions/browser/src/browser/paths.ts`) tries `DEFAULT_UPLOAD_DIR` (`<tmp>/uploads`) first and then the inbound media root, but returns only the inbound check's error. The message suggests only chat attachments can be uploaded. In our case the agent told the user to re-attach a file it had already generated, when copying it into `<tmp>/uploads` would have worked. (`<tmp>/uploads` also isn't created up front, so nothing nearby hints that it exists.)

**Expected:** the error lists both accepted sources, e.g. "must be inside the uploads directory (`/tmp/openclaw/uploads`) or be a direct inbound media file (`media://inbound/<id>`)". Optionally, downloads could be accepted as an upload source too, or there could be a documented way to stage a download for upload.

issues.body:
## Summary
The Discord `edit` message action (the agent message tool's `action: "edit"` and `openclaw message edit --channel discord`) sends the new text to Discord verbatim, while a `send` of the same text goes through the Discord outbound renderer. An edited message therefore renders differently from the message it replaces:

- Markdown tables stay raw pipe text instead of the configured `markdown.tables` mode (Discord default: fenced `code` block), because Discord does not render Markdown tables.
- CommonMark `__bold__` reaches Discord unchanged, where `__x__` means underline. Sends normalize it to `**x**`.
- `channels.discord.mentionAliases` handles (`@alice`) stay plain text instead of becoming `<@id>` mentions.

An agent that sends a status table and later edits it with updated values ends up with a broken raw table in the channel.

## Environment
- Commit: 2775e24f749f7ab823e7278f7837adb5cd112157 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Discord message action `edit` (agent-authored content branch); retained progress edits are a separate branch and not affected

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure Discord with `mentionAliases: { alice: "123456789012345678" }`.
2. Send `| svc | state |\n|---|---|\n| api | __up__ |\n\nping @alice` with the `send` action, then edit that message with the same text via the `edit` action.
3. Compare the POST body of the send with the PATCH body of the edit.

## Expected
The edit PATCH carries the same rendered content as the send POST (fenced table, normalized bold, `<@123456789012345678>`).

## Actual
The edit PATCH carries the raw input text.

## Root cause
`extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.messaging.messages.ts:120-146` reads the agent text and hands it straight to `editMessageDiscord`, which PATCHes it as `content`:

```ts
      const content = snapshot
        ? (buildDiscordTextChunks(/* retained progress compositor text */)[0] ?? "")
        : readStringParam(ctx.params, "content", {
            required: true,
            allowEmpty: true,
            trim: false,
          });
```

Both send transports (`sendMessageDiscord` in `extensions/discord/src/send.outbound.ts:109` and `sendWebhookMessageDiscord` in `extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.ts:101`) run text through `prepareDiscordOutboundText` (`extensions/discord/src/outbound-text.ts:7`), which applies `renderDiscordMarkdown` (table mode plus CommonMark bold normalization) and `rewriteDiscordKnownMentions`. The agent-authored edit branch never calls it.

## Sibling surfaces
Slack (`normalizeSlackOutboundText` in its edit path) and Telegram (`renderTelegramHtmlText` in `send-edit.ts`) already render edits the same way they render sends; Discord is the outlier. The retained progress edit branch (`progressSnapshot`) already carries Discord-ready compositor text sent with `allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }` and should stay as is.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: The Discord edit action PATCHes raw agent Markdown (raw table pipes, `__x__` underline, unresolved `@alice`) while a send of the same text is rendered (fenced table, `**`-normalized bold, `<@id>` mention).
Real environment tested: A tsx driver on macOS (Node 26.9) calling the production Discord channel plugin action adapter `discordMessageActions.handleAction({ action: "edit", ... })` (the entry the message tool and `openclaw message edit` use) and, for reference, the real `sendMessageDiscord` sender, with a real config (`groupPolicy: "open"`, `mentionAliases: { alice: "123456789012345678" }`). Everything inside OpenClaw stayed real: action dispatch, read-target policy (it fetched the channel and guild), account resolution, the Discord REST client and request runner. Only Discord's HTTP API was replaced, by a local loopback server selected through the product's own `DISCORD_API_URL` override, which logged each request body. Captured on origin/main e7fdb9b1770 and with the fix from closed PR #190018 (head 95672b76efb) on identical inputs; reconfirmed on 2775e24f749 (see below).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `DISCORD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:27431/api/v10 node --import tsx drive-edit.mts "$T" send` then `... drive-edit.mts "$T" edit`, with `T=$'| svc | state |\n|---|---|\n| api | __up__ |\n\nping @alice'`, reading the loopback server's request log.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main e7fdb9b1770)
POST /api/v10/channels/222/messages {"content":"```\n| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n```\n\nping <@123456789012345678>","flags":4,"nonce":"7c1d5711d8bd269359b1fbec","enforce_nonce":true}
PATCH /api/v10/channels/222/messages/5555 {"content":"| svc | state |\n|---|---|\n| api | __up__ |\n\nping @alice"}
tool result content: "| svc | state |\n|---|---|\n| api | __up__ |\n\nping @alice"

# EXPECTED (with the fix on closed PR #190018, identical inputs)
POST /api/v10/channels/222/messages {"content":"```\n| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n```\n\nping <@123456789012345678>","flags":4,"nonce":"df0ea4e3f87e1e5c6ebc5e1b","enforce_nonce":true}
PATCH /api/v10/channels/222/messages/5555 {"content":"```\n| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n```\n\nping <@123456789012345678>"}
tool result content: "```\n| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n```\n\nping <@123456789012345678>"
```
Observed result after fix: On main the send body is rendered but the edit body is the raw input; with the fix the edit PATCH carries exactly the same rendered content as the send POST (fenced table, bold markers normalized inside the table, `@alice` resolved to `<@123456789012345678>`).
What was not tested: No real Discord server or client rendering (the Discord HTTP API was a loopback stand-in); the `openclaw message edit` CLI was not driven end to end because the source-run plugin loader failed to load the Discord plugin in that local checkout; retained progress edits were not re-driven; full build not run.

### Reconfirmed on current main
On origin/main 2775e24f749 the offending lines above are unchanged and no commit has touched `extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.messaging.messages.ts` since the PR base. The regression case from closed PR #190018 (`extensions/discord/src/actions/message-bodies.test.ts`, "renders edited content the same way as a send", which drives the real `send` and `edit` actions against a loopback Discord HTTP fixture) still fails there: the PATCH body carries `"| svc | state |\n|---|---|\n| api | __up__ |..."` instead of the fenced table and `<@id>` mention that the send POST carries.

## Proposed fix
Closed PR #190018 (branch `yetval:fix/discord-edit-render`) runs the agent-authored edit content through `prepareDiscordOutboundText(content, { cfg: ctx.cfg, account: resolveDiscordAccount({ cfg: ctx.cfg, accountId: ctx.accountId }) }).textWithMentions`, leaving the retained progress branch untouched. Plain text without tables, `__` spans or known handles is returned unchanged. It includes a regression case in `extensions/discord/src/actions/message-bodies.test.ts` asserting the edit PATCH equals the send POST. Possible overlap: draft PR #165664 (Components V2 edits) touches the same `editMessage` case for a different concern. Anyone is welcome to pick it up.

issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #177387 and #186331, both of which were closed as "already implemented on `main`". That implementation **still has not shipped**: the newest published release, **v2026.10.10 (published 2026-11-03)**, ships the same Preview-only identity check. Every release published since the fix was merged on `main` reproduces the bug.

This issue reports the **new** fact — a release published *after* those closures also lacks the fix — rather than re-reporting the original defect.

## Affected published releases (verified against the shipped npm artifact, not the changelog)

| Release | Published | `MINIMAX_M31_MODEL_ID` in shipped build | Accepts GA id? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v2026.10.8` | 2026-10-27 | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | no |
| `v2026.10.9` | 2026-10-29 | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | no |
| **`v2026.10.10`** | **2026-11-03** | **`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`** | **no** |
| `main` | — | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (+ separate preview id) | **yes** |

### Verification 1 — the published npm tarball for v2026.10.10

```bash
curl -sL https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw/-/openclaw-2026.10.10.tgz -o o.tgz
tar -xzOf o.tgz package/dist/thinking-Dg9lPaiN.mjs | grep -n 'MiniMax-M3.1-Flash'
```

```js
// package/dist/thinking-Dg9lPaiN.mjs  (openclaw@2026.10.10)
const MINIMAX_M31_MODEL_ID = "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview";
...
function isMinimaxM31ModelId(modelId) {
	return modelId.trim().toLowerCase() === MINIMAX_M31_MODEL_ID.toLowerCase();
}
```

### Verification 2 — the release tag source

`extensions/minimax/thinking.ts` at `v2026.10.10` is **byte-identical** to the same file at `v2026.10.9`:

```bash
diff <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/v2026.10.9/extensions/minimax/thinking.ts) \
     <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/v2026.10.10/extensions/minimax/thinking.ts)
# no output
```

### Verification 3 — runtime behaviour of the shipped build

```js
import("file:///path/to/openclaw/dist/thinking-Dg9lPaiN.mjs").then(m => {
  console.log(m.r("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash"));                       // false
  console.log(JSON.stringify(m.i("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash")));       // {"levels":[{"id":"off"},{"id":"adaptive"}],"defaultLevel":"adaptive"}
  console.log(JSON.stringify(m.i("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview"))); // {"levels":[{"id":"low"},...{"id":"max"}],"defaultLevel":"max"}
});
```

The GA id and the Preview id resolve to **different** profiles in the same build.

## Impact (unchanged from #177387, still live)

Two symptoms, one one-line identity check in `extensions/minimax/thinking.ts`:

1. **No level choices.** `resolveMinimaxThinkingProfile("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash")` falls through to the plain-M3 rule → adaptive-only profile (levels `off`/`adaptive`, default `adaptive`). The five-tier ladder MiniMax exposes on M3.1 is unreachable for the GA id.
2. **Effort never reaches the wire.** `wrapMinimaxProviderStream` in `extensions/minimax/stream.ts` gates the Anthropic-compatible payload patch on the same `isMinimaxM31ModelId(model.id)` check, so `output_config.effort` is never sent for the GA id. The request goes out with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` and no effort bound, and the model self-selects maximum reasoning.

The affected id is not a typo — it is the id MiniMax's live catalog returns and the id the bundled catalog documents. `main` already accepts both ids.

### Wire contract (verified live against `api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1/messages`)

- `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` → `200 OK`, `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` varies by level
- `off` → `400` `invalid reasoning_effort: "off" (allowed: low, medium, high, xhigh, max) (2013)`
- `adaptive` → `400` `invalid reasoning_effort: "adaptive" (allowed: low, medium, high, xhigh, max) (2013)`

Both `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` are accepted by the endpoint. Note `adaptive` is **not** a valid `output_config.effort` value — unbounded adaptive behaviour is obtained by omitting `output_config` entirely, which is exactly what the plain-M3 path does.

## Proposed fix

Publish #176955 (`ed5a99e0`). The resulting profile on the GA id:

```
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash         levels=["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] default=max
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview levels=["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] default=max
MiniMax-M3                 levels=["off","adaptive"]                   default=adaptive
MiniMax-M2.7               levels=["off","minimal","low","medium","high"] default=off
```

### Root-cause fix preferred

#182110 proposed keying the profile off the model **family** rather than a fixed id list, so M3.1 Pro and future M3.x get the same five effort levels without needing a release each time. That would prevent this whole issue class from recurring — the id list has now needed changing at least three times (GA id added, Pro added, preview deprecated).

## Note on release-branch divergence

Release tags appear to be cut from a branch that does not contain `main`'s merge commits as ancestors, so a fix merged on `main` does not automatically reach a release. Concretely, for `v2026.10.10` the merge commit of #176955 is *not* an ancestor of the tag, and the shipped artifact still carries the pre-fix check.

This also means the release changelog is **cumulative** — `CHANGELOG/2026.10.10.md` is 3,089 lines versus 88 lines for `2026.10.9.md`, and it re-lists already-shipped PRs. For example it advertises MiniMax OAuth work (#160089 models-list, #160459 regional token renewal, #168957 discovery refresh) whose **content is byte-identical between the 10.9 and 10.10 npm artifacts** — i.e. it was already live in 10.9. The MiniMax OAuth entries in the 10.10 changelog therefore do *not* indicate MiniMax received attention in this release; the GA-id fix is the only MiniMax behavioural delta, and it is absent.

Because of that, please verify release content against the shipped artifact or the tag source rather than the changelog when triaging MiniMax reports.

## Workaround in use

Until the fix ships, operators patch the installed build (one-line id widening, mirroring `ed5a99e0` exactly). This must be re-applied after every `openclaw update`, since an update reinstalls `dist` and reverts it.

issues.body:
> AI-assisted report, requested by the affected user. Personal paths, addresses, account details and credentials have been omitted.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

During a macOS network investigation, two orphaned `ssh ... git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'` processes in an OpenClaw source checkout were found; one was still receiving about 1.95 MB/s and the other had cumulatively received about 3.40 GB. **The process that originally launched them was not captured, so attribution to the OpenClaw updater or runtime is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.** This is a triage request based on an observed process-lifecycle/bandwidth problem, not a claim of malicious behavior or a confirmed current-release regression.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The incident was observed on one machine. The original invoking command/application and the moment the parent exited were not recorded. I have not reproduced this on a clean installation or the latest release, and do not want to present diagnostic commands as reproduction steps.

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Requested outcome: when a caller cancels or exits, any Git/SSH transfers it owns should terminate; update/status checks should avoid downloading unnecessary repository history. Whether the original caller was OpenClaw remains unverified.

### Actual behavior

Read-only process and network sampling showed:

| PID | Parent PID | SSH target / command | Cumulative received bytes, sample 1 → sample 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 17503 | 1 (`launchd`) | `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o SendEnv=GIT_PROTOCOL git@github.com git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'` | 3,399,071,394 → 3,399,071,394 |
| 72834 | 1 (`launchd`) | same command | 332,215,030 → 336,123,532 |

Samples were approximately 2 seconds apart. PID 72834 received 3,908,502 bytes during that interval (~1.95 MB/s); PID 17503 was idle during that interval. The 3.40 GB is a cumulative process counter, **not** an additional 3.40 GB downloaded during the sample and not a measured total VPN charge.

Both processes had the source checkout as their current directory. `lsof` showed stdout directed to `/dev/null`. FlClash independently attributed the active GitHub port 22 connection to an outbound proxy route. That connection's cumulative counter rose from ~104 MB to ~525 MB during the investigation.

### OpenClaw version

Installed npm-global CLI: 2026.6.11.
A separate local source checkout was also present at commit `105a6307cceb`.
Which executable/version initiated the SSH commands: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2, arm64

### Install method

npm global CLI plus a separate Git source checkout. The Gateway launch agent existed but was not loaded when inspected.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

Observed network path: SSH → github.com:22 → FlClash proxy route.
Model/provider path that initiated the operation: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Logs

```text
nettop cumulative bytes_in, about 2 s apart:
ssh.17503: 3399071394 -> 3399071394
ssh.72834:  332215030 ->  336123532

ps:
17503 PPID=1 ssh ... git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'
72834 PPID=1 ssh ... git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The figures above are transcribed from direct `ps`, `lsof`, `nettop` and FlClash observations on 2026-11-12. Raw screenshots include unrelated personal network details and are intentionally not attached.

### Impact and severity

Observed on one machine: sustained background transfer over a metered proxy, manual investigation and termination required. One process had received ~3.40 GB cumulatively; the other was actively receiving ~1.95 MB/s during sampling. Frequency and other affected versions/systems: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information

- Sending SIGTERM to both identified processes stopped them; a follow-up process check showed both absent.
- The user subsequently uninstalled the local installation. This report does not claim that stopping the Gateway alone would have stopped the SSH processes.
- Related but **not established as the same root cause**: #176152 (update checks fetching broad branch history) and #127591 (SSH descendant cleanup on termination).

## Summary

Add an optional Cua Spaces integration through the existing WorkerProvider plugin contract.

## Problem to solve

Operators with Cua Spaces cannot select their existing Cua infrastructure as an OpenClaw worker provider. They need the standard worker execution and desktop workflow while Cua owns allocation and deletion.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional provider for dedicated, disposable Linux x64 Cua Spaces. Keep the Gateway on its existing host. Use Core-owned Node enrollment grants, the existing worker-turn and remote-exec modes, and Core's authenticated desktop viewer.

Keep placement and account selection in explicit trusted configuration. Local placement stays the default. Direct and Relay placement must retain the exact parent, child, account context, and operation ownership. The provider must report indeterminate cleanup when the host API cannot prove physical absence.

The first implementation keeps a pinned container image, runc runtime, no reuse, no public ports, and guest-only desktop control. It adds no general Gateway token or host desktop access. A bundled implementation would live under extensions/cua-spaces-worker and use the current public Plugin SDK. An external plugin remains a supported alternative if maintainers prefer that ownership model.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep a standalone plugin. This already fits the public SDK and avoids another bundled dependency, but maintainers would not own its release or compatibility.
- Reuse Crabbox. Crabbox is the existing bundled WorkerProvider precedent. This request is for Cua infrastructure and its native capabilities, with separate lifecycle and ownership behavior.

## Impact

This affects operators who already use Cua and want to attach a disposable worker to an OpenClaw conversation. The missing integration blocks that workflow until they maintain an external adapter. No outage, account change, paid plan, or automatic migration is implied.

## Evidence/examples

- The current public WorkerProvider contract and bundled Crabbox provider supply the required plugin registration, execution modes, enrollment callbacks, and desktop lease contract.
- An external candidate targets OpenClaw 2026.10.7 and @trycua/cua 0.9.0. Its isolated synthetic suite passed 86 tests with no skips and its package installation was checked. This is evidence for that candidate, not proof of compatibility with current main.
- An earlier local candidate demonstrated same-guest Core execution, files, computer interaction, and the Core viewer with a reviewed task-only Core enrollment repair. Stock Core and the current candidate were not qualified by that run. The existing enrollment work remains separately owned in #159178 and is not duplicated here.
- Genuine remote allocation, guest execution, and teardown remain unverified. A successful host delete response is not physical absence proof.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The goal extends beyond parity with another worker backend. The proposal is phased so OpenClaw can use Cua's native lifecycle, placement, desktop, and storage capabilities through the SDK rather than rebuild them. Later units can evaluate native media streams, stop/resume, checkpoints and forks, volumes, and prewarm where the supported contracts permit them. Each needs its own ownership model and runtime proof. The initial provider does not implement or claim those capabilities.

No Core enrollment repair, new generic manager, paid service, account enrollment, host listener, host desktop, or production deployment belongs in the first slice.

issues.title: [Bug]: exec (zsh) — heredoc on non-first pipeline stage receives upstream pipe output ⊕ heredoc body instead of overriding the pipe → false "Exec failed" NameError alerts

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Marked as stale due to inactivity

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.7.1-2** (launchd gateway, exec host = local/gateway)
- macOS 15.8.2 (x64), `/bin/zsh` **5.9** (x86_64-apple-darwin24, Apple build)
- exec tool with default shell config (zsh)

## Summary

When an agent runs a command that combines a **pipeline** with a **heredoc attached to a non-first pipeline member** — e.g. the very common monitoring pattern:

```
openclaw cron list --json | python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, sys
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
...
EOF
```

the last-stage process does **not** receive the heredoc on stdin (POSIX/bash semantics: an explicit stdin redirection overrides the implicit pipe). Instead it receives **the upstream pipe output concatenated with the heredoc body**. For `python3 -`, the piped JSON gets executed as Python source and dies at the first bare `true` / `false` / `null`:

```
NameError: name 'true' is not defined. Did you mean: 'True'?
```

This produced **6 false "Exec failed" alerts in a single day** in our heartbeat monitoring (the cron fleet itself was fully healthy; each run self-healed same-run via a write-to-file-then-read pattern).

## Root-cause isolation — not an OpenClaw command-mangling bug

- **ps forensics**: exec runs the command as `/bin/zsh -f -c "<shell-snapshot preamble>; export PATH=…; eval '<command>'"`. The command text is passed **intact** (shQuote-wrapped, real newlines preserved). Replaying this exact argv from a plain Python subprocess reproduces the anomaly, so the snapshot preamble and the `eval` wrapper are **not** the cause.
- The anomaly reproduces **entirely outside OpenClaw** with bare `zsh -f -c` and with zsh **script files**: on zsh 5.9 (this build), a heredoc/here-string attached to a **non-first** pipeline member is *concatenated after* the upstream pipe output instead of overriding it. `bash` and `/bin/sh` behave correctly (heredoc wins).
- OpenClaw merely inherits zsh behavior. Filing here because exec is the surface where agents hit it, and a warning/normalization in exec would have saved a day of false alerts.

## Minimal repro (no OpenClaw involved)

```zsh
% printf 'PIPE-CONTENT' | cat <<'EOF'
HEREDOC-CONTENT
EOF
PIPE-CONTENTHEREDOC-CONTENT      # zsh 5.9 actual: concatenated

% bash -c "printf 'PIPE-CONTENT' | cat <<'EOF'
HEREDOC-CONTENT
EOF"
HEREDOC-CONTENT                  # bash: correct POSIX semantics
```

Interpreter-from-stdin hazard (the incident shape):

```zsh
% echo '{"enabled": true}' | python3 - <<'EOF'
print("hello")
EOF
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
NameError: name 'true' is not defined. Did you mean: 'True'?
```

## Probe matrix (subprocess with exact argv control)

| # | Scenario | zsh 5.9 | bash | POSIX expectation |
|---|----------|---------|------|-------------------|
| 1 | `printf P \| cat <<EOF` via `-c`, multi-line | P⊕body ❌ | body ✅ | body |
| 2 | leading `export PATH=…` line + same command | P⊕body ❌ | — | body |
| 3 | `eval '…'` wrapper (exec's exact shape) | P⊕body ❌ | body ✅ | body |
| 4 | script-file mode | P⊕body ❌ | body ✅ | body |
| 5 | 3-stage pipe, heredoc on last member | P⊕body ❌ | — | body |
| 6 | heredoc on **middle** member | P⊕body ❌ | — | body |
| 7 | heredoc on **first** member: `cat <<EOF \| cat` | body ✅ | — | body |
| 8 | standalone heredoc (no pipe) | body ✅ | body ✅ | body |
| 9 | empty upstream output `printf '' \| cat <<EOF` | body only (proves concat, not duplication) | — | body |
| 10 | here-string `printf P \| cat <<< H` | P⊕H ❌ | — | H |
| 11 | `/bin/sh -c` | — | body ✅ | body |

(⊕ = in-order byte concatenation, no separator. The heredoc body always arrives as **data**; a `echo SHOULD-NOT-RUN` probe confirms the body is never re-parsed as commands.)

## Suggested mitigations (OpenClaw side)

1. **Warn** when a command under shell=zsh combines a pipe with a heredoc/here-string on a non-first pipeline member. bash-tools already parses segments/tokens (e.g. the `token.startsWith("<<")` heredoc-approval path), so the hook point exists.
2. Alternatively, normalize heredoc-containing commands to bash-compatible execution, or document that heredocs are only safe **standalone or on the first pipeline stage** when exec uses zsh.
3. zsh upstream will be notified separately (mailing list; the zsh GitHub mirror has issues disabled). This box has no Homebrew zsh to distinguish Apple patches vs upstream, so the zsh-side report will carry that caveat.

## Notes

- Searched existing issues; no prior report of this specific behavior found. (Related but distinct: #114128 literal-`\n` via unquoted heredocs; #179890 `$<digit>` redaction.)
- Local incident log: 6 Exec-failed pushes on 2026-10-31 (03:12/05:12/07:00/09:11/11:43/14:41 GMT+8), all `NameError: name 'true'` from cron-list JSON being fed to `python3 -` as source code.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

A CLI pointed at a Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (`gateway.mode: "remote"`, `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`, no token or password) never opens a WebSocket. `openclaw tui`, `openclaw tui --url <gateway>` and `openclaw gateway call` all stop locally with a "credentials required" error.

In this setup Access authenticates the upgrade and the Gateway runs `trusted-proxy` auth, so there is no token or password to pass. Because the client never dials, the device never files the pairing request an admin could approve.

[Cloudflare Tunnel and Access, Verify](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloudflare-access#verify) already describes the intended flow: `openclaw tui` reaches the Gateway and reports `device pairing required`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"` behind Cloudflare Access, per the Cloudflare Access guide.
2. On another machine, configure the CLI with no Gateway credentials:
   ```json5
   {
     gateway: {
       mode: "remote",
       remote: {
         url: "wss://gateway.example",
         edgeAuth: { "Cf-Access-Token": { source: "exec", provider: "cloudflare-access", id: "token" } },
       },
     },
   }
   ```
3. Run `openclaw tui`, `openclaw tui --url wss://gateway.example`, and `openclaw gateway call sessions.list --json`.

### Expected behavior

The client sends the edge-auth headers, reaches the Gateway, and lets the Gateway decide access. On first contact, `openclaw tui` gets `device pairing required` and leaves a pending request for the admin. After approval, the stored device token covers later `tui` and `gateway call` connections.

### Actual behavior

None of the three commands opens a connection; the proxy sees no request.

- `openclaw tui`: `Missing gateway auth credentials.`
- `openclaw tui --url wss://gateway.example`: `gateway url override requires explicit credentials`
- `openclaw gateway call sessions.list --json`: `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"gateway_credentials_required","message":"gateway sessions.list requires credentials before opening a websocket ..."}}`

Three prechecks do this:

- `src/gateway/call.ts` (`callGatewayWithScopes`): with no `gateway.auth` in the client config, the mode defaults to `token`. With no token, no password and no stored device token, it throws `GatewayCredentialsRequiredError` before dialing.
- `src/gateway/client-bootstrap.ts` (`ensureExplicitGatewayAuth`): a `--url` target requires `--token`/`--password` or a stored origin device token.
- `src/tui/gateway-chat.ts` (`resolveGatewayConnection`): a missing shared credential is fatal unless an origin device token is stored.

None of them accounts for `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` already authenticating connections to that origin.

### OpenClaw version

main @ 3c6bb67f82a (2026-11-14)

### Operating system

macOS

### Install method

Source build

### Impact and severity

Any CLI or TUI user of a Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (or another identity-aware proxy) who has no shared Gateway secret is stuck at first contact. Team guests are the main case, since they shouldn't get the shared token. The only workaround is handing out a shared Gateway credential, which defeats the guest model.

### Additional information

Reproduced against a loopback Gateway in `trusted-proxy` mode behind a small TLS proxy. Like Access, the proxy answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then forwards with identity headers. With the prechecks skipped for that origin, the same `openclaw tui` reaches the Gateway, gets `device pairing required`, and leaves one pending request.

Proposed fix: skip the local credential prechecks only when edge-auth headers are configured for the target's origin. Configurations that work today don't change. Only configurations that currently fail before dialing start connecting, and other origins still require credentials.

issues.body:
### Summary / Problem Statement

`openclaw` resolves user-supplied local paths **lexically** (`path.resolve` via `resolveUserPath`, `src/infra/home-dir.ts:108`) before touching the filesystem. When a parent directory is a symlink and the path contains `..`, the lexical answer differs from what the filesystem actually traverses. Commands then silently operate on a **different, valid neighbor** — reading the wrong source or writing to the wrong destination — and report success.

This is a cross-command pattern, not a single call-site bug. The same root cause appears in every command that takes a local file/directory path and normalizes it with `path.resolve` / `resolveUserPath` before I/O.

### Reproduction (real user-visible harm)

Setup (one-time, POSIX):

```sh
root=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$root/physical/nested" "$root/cwd"
ln -s ../physical/nested "$root/cwd/selected"   # selected -> physical/nested
cd "$root/cwd"
```

A path like `selected/../<target>` reads (or writes) `<root>/physical/<target>` on the filesystem, but `path.resolve` collapses it to `<root>/<target>` — a different, valid resource.

**Example 1 — wrong plugin installs** (`plugins install`):

```text
fixture: <root>/physical/plugin-b (id: plugin-real)
         <root>/cwd/plugin-b      (id: plugin-decoy)
command: openclaw plugins install "./selected/../plugin-b"
```

Base (current main): installs `plugin-decoy` (the lexical sibling), reports success — the operator gets another plugin's code, manifest and capabilities installed under their chosen path.

**Example 2 — diagnostics export to the wrong directory**:

```text
command: openclaw gateway diagnostics export --output "selected/../bundle.zip"
```

Base: archive written to `<root>/cwd/bundle.zip`; the directory the path actually names (`<root>/physical/`) stays empty.

The same shape affects identity import (`identity --source ...`), local image inputs (`--file ...`), and `templates validate/create/archive` — the pattern was demonstrated end-to-end in the PRs below, each with a red-on-base / green-on-fix pairing.

### Why This Matters

- Every affected command **succeeds** on the wrong resource — no error, no warning.
- Distinct valid projects/files make this a silent wrong-operation, not a crash: a decoy plugin, image, identity or project is selected instead of the one the operator's path names.
- The fix is a shared-owner change, not N per-command patches: replace lexical `path.resolve` with physical prefix traversal for user-supplied paths.

### Suggested Direction (open for maintainer decision)

`@openclaw/fs-safe` already ships `resolvePathPrefixSync(input)` (`@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced`, `dist/path-prefix.d.ts`) returning `{ absolutePath, existingPath, unresolvedSegments }` — the physical existing ancestor plus the segments that do not exist yet. It is already used by `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.paths.ts`, `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/file-access-runtime.ts` and 10+ other shipped call sites for this exact class of input.

A possible consolidation: give user-supplied local path resolution a single shared owner (in `@openclaw/fs-safe` or the path-resolution owner) that walks physical parents before lexical collapse, and route all user-input path commands through it. Behavior to preserve: whitespace trimming, `~` expansion, "missing path" diagnostics, and non-`..` paths unchanged.

**Decision requested:** which owner should own user-supplied path resolution, and whether a shared resolver replacing `resolveUserPath` for user input is the right direction? Happy to implement once the owner is agreed.

### Known affected call sites (current main, all still exposed)

| Call site | Command | Wrong-resource effect | Related PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/install-source-plan.ts:102` | `plugins install <local path>` | installs a neighboring plugin | #199874 |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts:439` | `gateway diagnostics export --output`, `stability --export` | archive to wrong directory | #199669 |
| `src/commands/agents.commands.identity.ts` | `identity` import/select | reads wrong IDENTITY.md / wrong agent | #199715 |
| `src/cli/capability-cli/media-input-path.ts` + `media-understanding-command.ts:21` | model runs/editing/describe `--file <path>` | reads a neighboring image | #195363 |
| `src/templates/reader.ts`, `project.ts`, `project-build.ts`, `path-containment.ts` | `templates validate/create/inspect/archive <path>` | validates/creates wrong project | #198814 |
| `src/cli/media-output.ts:29` + `capability-cli/video.ts` | media/video output path | writes to wrong directory | #199632 |

These per-site fixes were reviewed (diamond/platinum, no actionable findings) but closed by maintainers in favor of a single shared-owner fix. This issue is that consolidation.

### Impact

- **Behavior**: user-supplied path commands select the resource the path actually names.
- **Preserved**: whitespace trim, `~` expansion, "Plugin path not found"-style diagnostics, non-symlink and non-`..` paths.
- **Scope**: no new config options, no stored path changes, no containment/policy changes.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw audit --agent ""` (or `--agent "$UNSET_VAR"`) exits 0 and returns **every agent's** audit records — byte-identical to running `audit` with no filter — instead of rejecting the blank value. An operator who scopes an audit query with an empty shell variable silently gets a report covering all agents, sessions, runs, and channels.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Gateway and generate at least one agent_run audit record (`main` agent).
2. Run `openclaw audit --agent ""` (empty value; also reproducible with `--agent "$UNSET_VAR"`).
3. Observe: exit 0, and the output includes the `main` agent's record — identical to `openclaw audit` with no filter.
4. Compare: `openclaw audit --agent nonexistent` correctly returns an empty page (a non-empty value is honored).

Sharpest case: `openclaw audit --execution ""` exits 0 and lists activity, while `openclaw audit --execution xyz` correctly fails with `--execution requires --explain.` — a blank value silently bypasses a validation that a non-blank value triggers.

### Expected behavior

An explicitly passed blank value for `--agent`, `--session`, `--run`, `--execution`, `--channel`, or `--cursor` should fail with exit 1 and a "must not be blank" message, before any Gateway call — mirroring the existing blank-value rejection for `--after`/`--before`/`--kind`/`--status`/`--direction` (added in #137335, merged).

### Environment

OpenClaw main as of 2026-11-16. `src/commands/audit.ts:587` builds `AuditActivityListParams` with truthy spreads (`...(options.agentId ? { agentId: options.agentId } : {})`), so `""` never reaches the Gateway as a filter.

### Anything else

The free-string filters are the inconsistent half: the bounds/kind/status/direction filters already reject blank values (merged #137335), but `--agent`/`--session`/`--run`/`--execution`/`--channel`/`--cursor` still silently drop a blank value.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

MS Teams and Zalo (zalouser) still declare `chunkerMode: "markdown"` while configuring the fence-blind `chunkTextForOutbound` splitter, so an assistant reply crossing the channel text chunk limit (Teams 4000, Zalo 2000 characters) with a fenced code block is split mid-fence: the first chunk ends with an unclosed block and the next starts with bare code lines, so clients render code as plain text and trailing prose inside a stray code block. This is the same defect fixed for Matrix in #196167, Mattermost in #196331, and Tlon in #196430; these two adapters were scoped out of #196430 because shipped-entry proof is not achievable without a tenant (see below), and this issue tracks the remaining repair.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect MS Teams or Zalouser to a Gateway.
2. Trigger an assistant reply longer than the channel chunk limit whose fenced code block crosses the limit.
3. Read the delivered messages in the client.

Chunker-level reproduction on main (executing the configured outbound chunker, the function the Gateway invokes): a fenced reply of (limit + 300) characters splits into two fence-unbalanced chunks on both channels; the fence-aware SDK splitter `chunkMarkdownTextWithMode(text, limit, "length")` produces balanced chunks within the limit for the same input. Transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196429

### Expected behavior

Code blocks survive splitting intact (closed at the boundary and reopened with the original info string), as delivered by Matrix since #196167, Mattermost since #196331, and Tlon via #196430.

### Actual behavior

Mid-fence splits with unclosed blocks and stray closing fences, as described in #196429 (identical chunker behavior; Teams/Zalouser were not part of that fix).

### OpenClaw version

main since 2026.11.2 (verified 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-16)

### Operating system

Linux x64 (channel-side markdown text, platform-independent)

### Install method

pnpm dev source checkout

### Model

Not relevant — channel outbound chunking before any provider send.

### Provider / routing chain

Not relevant — same reason.

### Logs

Chunker transcript in #196429.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: users of the MS Teams and Zalo channels receiving long code-bearing replies.
- Severity: annoying; blocks reading code answers on these channels.
- Frequency: every reply crossing the chunk limit with a fence crossing it.
- Consequence: identical to what #196429 reported for four channels, minus the two already fixed elsewhere.

### Additional information

Why this needs a tenant-backed (or owner-decided) proof, unlike Mattermost/Tlon:
- MS Teams: outbound delivery resolves a Bot Framework `serviceUrl` that `extensions/msteams/src/bot-framework-service-url.ts` restricts to Microsoft HTTPS hosts (`smba.trafficmanager.net`, GCC/GCC-High/DoD equivalents, `botframework.azure.cn`). There is no loopback or self-hosted mode, so a recorded `openclaw message send` proof requires a real Teams tenant.
- Zalouser: sends through the Zalo user protocol via zalo-js with stored account credentials and no configurable endpoint, so the same applies.
- The production change itself is the same one-line adapter swap as the three merged siblings: `chunker: (text, limit) => chunkMarkdownTextWithMode(text, limit, "length")` plus a fence-balance regression test (drafted in the history of #196430 and easy to restore).

The repair + mocked-sender/chunker-level evidence were prepared in #196430 and can be split into per-channel PRs once delivery evidence is obtainable.

issues.body:
## Summary

A Control UI update from 2026.11.5-beta.1 to 2026.11.5-beta.3 stops at `doctor-failed`. The snapshot space preflight passes, then the SQLite read-only worker runs out of space in `TMPDIR` while it makes its private snapshot.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.5-beta.1 (installed), candidate 2026.11.5-beta.3, npm package install
- Debian 13 (trixie), arm64, 16 GB RAM, managed systemd user service
- Debian 13 mounts `/tmp` as tmpfs at 50% of RAM (8 GB). The managed unit sets `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- About 2.5 GB of SQLite stores, the largest about 1 GB

## What happened

- `snapshot-space-preflight`: "Initial snapshot needs 3.0 GiB for 2.0 GiB of known SQLite files and temporary working space." / "explicit-tmpdir /tmp: 3.0 GiB needed; 5.9 GiB free."
- All 16 database snapshots then completed (about 2.1 GB in total).
- The next step failed: `SQLite read-only worker failed while creating its private snapshot: copy_file_range: No space left on device (os error 28)`. The update record shows `os error 2` in one place and `os error 28` in `failureFacts`.
- Two retained `openclaw-update-runtime-*` trees (1.1 GB each) from earlier failed attempts were still in `/tmp` and took part of the space.

## Expected

The preflight counts the worker's private copies and the retained runtimes. It refuses before staging, or picks another candidate directory (the capture directory beside the state directory has hundreds of GB free), instead of passing and then failing with ENOSPC.

## Notes

- Workaround from the docs: `TMPDIR=/var/tmp openclaw update --yes`. An update started from the Control UI can't take that, because it inherits the unit's `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- Failed attempts leave their `openclaw-update-runtime-*` trees in `/tmp`, which shrinks the room for the next attempt.
- Possibly related: #163465, #183091, #194208, #153607.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Control UI turns a bare filename in an assistant message into a clickable file link, but clicking it returns `session file not found` when the existing file is in a nested workspace directory; an explicit full-path link to the same file opens successfully.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.10.1 before any local patch:

1. The workspace contains `labs/file-organizer/output/sorted-copy-001/ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md`.
2. An assistant message contains both an explicit Markdown link to that file using its absolute path and an inline-code mention of just `ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md`.
3. Click the explicit link: the report opens in the Files preview.
4. Click the automatically generated link for the bare filename: the preview shows `session file not found`.

The file remained present throughout; no deletion or move was involved.

### Expected behavior

The explicit full-path link to this same file was observed opening successfully. A clickable reference to it should either resolve to the existing file or explain that its location is unresolved, rather than presenting a bare name as a working link and then returning a generic error. If resolution is attempted, ambiguous names should not silently select an arbitrary file.

### Actual behavior

The bare-filename button has `data-file-path="ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md"`. Its `sessions.files.get` request uses only that name, which is resolved relative to the workspace root. The report is in a nested directory, so the preview displays `session file not found`. Opening the full-path link and reading the correct absolute or workspace-relative path through the Gateway both succeed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1 (e178c39)

### Operating system

Windows host + WSL2 Linux (OpenClawGateway distribution). Exact Windows/Linux release: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

Installed npm package in a managed Node v24.19.0 prefix inside WSL2; Gateway runs as a systemd user service. Original installer invocation: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol (affected session override)

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> Codex runtime (local app-server) -> configured openai/gpt-5.6-sol. Further upstream routing: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No model call is needed to reproduce the file-link click in the existing message.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Local Gateway with token authentication; session placement was local. Workspace root returned by sessions.files.list: `/home/openclaw/.openclaw/workspace`. Explicit agents.defaults.workspace was unset, using the runtime default. An initially suspected missing dot in `.openclaw` was ruled out.

### Logs

```shell
Observed Gateway line (connection/request identifiers omitted):
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.files.get errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=session file not found

Control checks: sessions.files.list returned the correct root; sessions.files.get successfully read the report using both its absolute path and `labs/file-organizer/output/sorted-copy-001/ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md`.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Live browser reproduction before modification: the explicit full-path report link opened the file, while the automatically linked inline-code basename returned the error. DOM inspection confirmed `data-file-path="ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md"` on the failing button. Gateway RPC checks independently confirmed the file was readable at its real path. No screenshot attached.

### Impact and severity

Affected: the observed Control UI conversation on 2026.10.1; scope beyond this installation is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.
Severity: UI/workflow friction; no data loss observed.
Frequency: reproduced repeatedly by clicking the bare-name link before the local patch; exact attempt count was not recorded.
Consequence: an existing readable report appears unavailable through a link generated by the UI, requiring the full-path link or workspace file browser as a workaround.

### Additional information

Related: #150322 (similar error for media:// references; different original trigger) and #152649 (preview errors hiding the Files browser). No exact bare-filename duplicate was identified in the searches performed.

Local modification disclosure: AFTER reproducing the original behavior, a local installed-UI patch was applied. It retries only a missing bare filename by searching the same session workspace, and only uses one exact file-name match when the search is not truncated. The previously failing click then opened the report; the full-path link still worked. This is a workaround, not a claim that recursive filename search is the preferred upstream design. Workspace configuration, skill files, and session data were unchanged.

Only 2026.10.1 was tested; current main and newer releases were not tested. No regression range established.

### Source location and illustrative local workaround

Repository-relative path: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts`, function `openFile()`. Verified against tag `v2026.10.1`: function starts at line 173, `requestPath` at line 179, and the direct file-read callback at lines 192–195.

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts#L173-L195

The local change was made in the installed compiled bundle. The following is a readable TypeScript equivalent of its core logic, NOT a source-tree patch that has been compiled or tested upstream. Change `const requestPath` to `let requestPath`, then replace the direct loader callback passed to `openWorkspaceItem` with:

```ts
async () => {
  try {
    return await state.sessions.getFile(sessionKey, requestPath, { agentId });
  } catch (error) {
    const details = error instanceof GatewayRequestError
      ? error.details as { type?: unknown } | undefined
      : undefined;
    if (details?.type !== "session_file_not_found" ||
        /[\\/]/.test(requestPath) ||
        requestPath === "." || requestPath === "..") {
      throw error;
    }
    const listing = await state.sessions.listFiles(sessionKey, {
      agentId, path: "", search: requestPath,
    });
    if (!listing?.root || !listing.browser || listing.browser.truncated) {
      throw error;
    }
    const matches = listing.browser.entries.filter(file =>
      file.kind === "file" && file.name === requestPath &&
      typeof file.path === "string" &&
      !/^[\\/]/.test(file.path) &&
      !file.path.split(/[\\/]/).includes("..")
    );
    if (matches.length !== 1) throw error;
    requestPath = matches[0].path;
    return await state.sessions.getFile(sessionKey, requestPath, { agentId });
  }
}
```

Keeping the resolved `requestPath` is intentional: the existing save and fetchLatest closures also use it. The local compiled-bundle fix passed a syntax check, five mocked cases (unique/absent/ambiguous/truncated/traversal), and live browser checks of the previously failing basename plus the original full-path link. These checks do not establish upstream TypeScript compatibility or broader session/connection lifecycle coverage; a production implementation should preserve those contracts and add regression coverage.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.3, macOS (launchd service).

## What happens
`gmail-watcher` spawns `gog gmail watch serve` with `detached: true` (own process group). Its shutdown path (`stopGmailWatcher` → `killProcessTree`) only runs on an orderly Gateway shutdown. After `openclaw gateway stop --force` (and after crashes / kernel panics) the Gateway exits without logging `gmail watcher stopped`; the `gog` process is reparented to launchd (ppid 1) and keeps listening on 127.0.0.1:8788. The new Gateway then logs:

```
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind (address already in use); retry 1/3 in 5s
…
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind after 3 retries (address already in use); stopping restarts.
```

and Gmail push delivery stops until someone kills the orphan and restarts the Gateway. Seen on 7 different days in one month on one host.

## Expected
Any of:
1. On startup, if the port is held by a `gog gmail watch serve` with ppid 1 started by this user for the same account/port (i.e. our own previous watcher), terminate it and take over.
2. Record the watcher pid/pgid in the state dir and reap it on next start.
3. `gateway stop --force` should signal the watcher's process group before exiting.

## Workaround
Before `gateway start`: find `gog gmail watch serve … --port 8788` with ppid 1, SIGTERM it, then start.

## Related
#161467 (closed) made the watcher recover when the conflicting listener disappears shortly after a restart. Here it never disappears: the previous Gateway's `gog` is orphaned and keeps the port indefinitely, so the watcher stays down until someone kills it by hand.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When an incognito session expiry job fails to delete its session, the cleanup path catches the error and unconditionally re-arms itself with a fixed 60_000 ms delay. There is no attempt counter, no backoff, no maximum attempt cap, and no terminal/give-up state, and every failed attempt emits exactly one warning log line. Because the only exit paths are "the session entry disappeared" (the sessionId changed, or the memory owner no longer returns the entry) or the sidecar being stopped, a permanent delete failure keeps the entry alive and therefore re-queues the job every 60 seconds forever. The result is unbounded retry pressure and one warning per minute, indefinitely, with no escalation and no signal that the cleanup will never converge.

### Steps to reproduce

Check out the pinned revision and install dependencies.
Exercise the incognito session lifetime path (startIncognitoSessionLifetime -> startIncognitoActorSessionLifetime) with a controllable scheduler and a memory owner that reports one incognito session with an expiry.
Advance the scheduler past the session's expiresAt so the expiry job runs.
Make the delete path fail permanently (the underlying deleteGatewaySession keeps throwing) while the session entry keeps the same sessionId.
Advance the clock by 12 consecutive 60-second windows and count how many times the job re-arms and how many warnings are emitted.

### Expected behavior

Cleanup retries should be bounded. A per-deadline attempt counter should grow, the retry delay should back off, and after a maximum number of attempts the job should stop re-arming, record a terminal state, and emit a single escalation-level (error) line rather than a warning every 60 seconds forever.

### Actual behavior

The catch block around the expiry job (session-incognito-lifetime.ts:69-84) never counts attempts. When the session entry is still present, it logs a warning and re-schedules with the constant retry delay:

session-incognito-lifetime.ts:79 if (active && entry?.sessionId === deadline.sessionId)
session-incognito-lifetime.ts:80 params.logWarning("Incognito session expiry could not finish cleanup; will retry.");
session-incognito-lifetime.ts:81 schedule(deadline, CLEANUP_RETRY_MS);
CLEANUP_RETRY_MS is the fixed constant 60_000 (session-incognito-lifetime.ts:18), and the deadlines map (session-incognito-lifetime.ts:38) stores only the scheduled job reference, not an attempt count. A permanent failure therefore re-arms forever at a constant 60-second cadence.

issues.body:
## Problem

The bundled IMAP trigger already provides useful sender authentication, read-only mailbox access, bounded message fetching, deduplication and contained hook-reader dispatch. I would like to discuss a small, opt-in reliability extension rather than a new email platform.

Some workflows need a durable answer to **“what happened to this mailbox message?”** after a restart. The answer must distinguish:

- source captured or durably referenced;
- agent turn admitted;
- processing completed, failed, skipped or of unknown outcome;
- optional delivery completed, rejected or of unknown outcome.

A successful admission/runId is not evidence of processing completion or delivery.

## Source basis

Reviewed upstream main at **bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8** (2026-10-21). This is source analysis, not a live-provider failure reproduction.

- [IMAP state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/extensions/imap/src/state.ts#L18-L101) persists cursor, claims and a bounded Message-ID ring.
- [Watcher processing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/extensions/imap/src/watcher.ts#L351-L450) claims a UID before dispatch, releases rejected admission through a bounded retry path, and returns success on accepted admission. The [sweep](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/extensions/imap/src/watcher.ts#L284-L349) then advances the cursor.
- The [trusted plugin hook contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts#L462-L479) returns admission success/runId or a rejection reason. The [Gateway facade](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/src/gateway/server/hooks.ts#L620-L712) does not expose its internal completion promise to the plugin and uses a process-local replay map.
- The [IMAP documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/docs/automation/imap.md#L156-L171) already documents the admission/crash limitation and that skipped messages are outside the channel ingress dead-letter queue.

Consequently, an admitted turn that later fails is not retried by the watcher; a crash during unresolved admission can leave a deduplication claim. Those are important existing safety tradeoffs, not an exactly-once bug claim.

## Proposed minimum scope

An **optional durable processing handoff** for IMAP, designed around existing host persistence/queue owners:

1. Persist a bounded, immutable event envelope or validated source locator before advancing intake. Bind it to configured mailbox identity, UIDVALIDITY and UID; retain Message-ID as metadata, not the sole identity.
2. Retain an inspectable lifecycle record linking that identity to admission and terminal processing facts. Where delivery is involved, keep execution and delivery outcomes distinct.
3. Recover pending work across restart only when ownership and prior execution state are known. Preserve an explicit held/unknown state for unresolved admission or sends; do not blindly rerun an admitted model turn or resend after an uncertain ACK.
4. Make failed/skipped/held entries discoverable with bounded retention and secret-free reason codes. Any future operator resubmission should be explicit and must not reset a mailbox cursor or discard delivered receipts.
5. Preserve today's default behavior unless the durable mode is explicitly enabled. Define fresh-install and UIDVALIDITY-reset policy rather than implicitly replaying a mailbox.

The exact API shape is open. If a supported existing queue/outcome API can provide these guarantees, documentation and a thin IMAP adapter may be sufficient.

## Reuse existing infrastructure

OpenClaw already has [plugin state/blob/ingress queue APIs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts#L567-L609), an [ingress lifecycle contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/src/channels/message/ingress-queue.types.ts#L157-L246), and [outbound unknown-send reconciliation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcb386ad34a89bfa11ac70d8ffe95c6f10929dd8/src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts#L559-L643). This proposal should reuse those owners, not introduce a parallel queue or retry framework.

Direct HTTP hooks can wait for completion, but an in-process completion promise or a single HTTP response alone does not provide restart-persistent custody. A small trusted outcome lookup/event seam may be needed; whether it belongs in the SDK or remains IMAP-local needs maintainer guidance.

## Non-goals

- Exactly-once processing/delivery guarantees.
- A new SMTP sender, provider migration or general task orchestration framework.
- Application-specific sender lists, task identifiers, routing/fallback policies, notification schedules or agent roles.
- Automatic execution of attachments or instructions inside mail.
- Treating extraction availability or agent completion as proof a human/model understood every part.
- Automatic Seen mutation; read-only mailbox behavior should remain unchanged.
- Weakening sender authentication, plugin trust, containment or tool policy.

Full-original/attachment retrieval could be a separate extension. The minimum handoff must describe truncation and source availability honestly; it need not ship an OCR/document-processing pipeline.

## Related work / duplicate boundary

- [#137871](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/137871) and [PR #138120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138120): explicit IMAP delivery targets. This discussion is **not** another channel/to request.
- [#173952](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173952) and [PR #176606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176606): execution status versus canceled delivery.
- [#7281](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7281): generic hook fallback; outside the minimum scope here.
- The official [AgentMail plugin's durable receive adapter](https://github.com/agentmail-to/openclaw-plugin/blob/4ae26ff564d59ad9f81e897ca5c9da940ba58d0e/src/channel/src/durable-receive.ts#L150-L210) demonstrates useful reuse of host ingress queues for a different provider. It is an architectural analogue, not IMAP checkpoint compatibility.

## Suggested synthetic acceptance cases

Use a loopback fake mailbox/reader/transport, isolated temporary state and no production credentials:

- Crash before/after persisted handoff, admission acknowledgement and cursor advancement.
- Processing failure after admission; restart before terminal-outcome persistence.
- Repeated same-UID intake, Message-ID collision and UIDVALIDITY change.
- Lost send ACK and restart with an already-started platform send.
- Capacity/retention exhaustion: no eviction of admitted pending work or advancement past unretained input.
- Safe opt-in migration from existing cursor state without mailbox replay or silent baseline gaps.

Every case should identify the retained owner, stage and outcome; “unknown” is valid when it is honest and does not cause blind replay.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is durable IMAP handoff a suitable bundled-plugin extension, or is an existing supported ingress/outcome composition preferred?
2. Is there already a restart-persistent trusted-hook outcome interface this should consume?
3. What is the smallest acceptable operator inspection/recovery surface?

I would like to settle scope and ownership in discussion before proposing implementation.

## Alternatives considered

Keep an external IMAP consumer with its own ledger (works, but duplicates transport and authentication ownership); compose HTTP hooks with waitForCompletion (still requires restart-persistent custody); use AgentMail (different provider, not an IMAP checkpoint migration). Prefer a thin supported composition of existing native queue/outcome primitives where possible.

## Impact

Affected: operators using bundled IMAP for asynchronous agent workflows that need per-message recovery and auditability. This is a reliability/recovery gap around crashes or admitted processing failures, not a claim of routine loss. Consequence: operators must reconstruct outcomes from logs and original mail or maintain a separate lifecycle ledger. No production incident rate is claimed; evidence here is source analysis.

## Implementation intent

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. We plan to review discussion in approximately two weeks before deciding whether to propose a narrowly scoped PR.

issues.body:
### Summary

An opt-in usage budget contract: per-surface (agent / channel / cron job / subagent) token-cost rollups plus a simple enforceable budget hook that can degrade the model, pause a non-critical schedule, or stop the turn when a configured window is exhausted.

### Problem to solve

Cost attribution and cost *control* are currently two different gaps:

- Attribution is fragmented: #102807 shows usage is provider-keyed rather than credential-keyed so mixed API+subscription installs display the wrong billing mode; #90911 notes per-run token accounting exists on `cron_run_logs` but not on `task_runs`/`subagent_runs`; #156999 shows legacy cron sessions land in an "Unattributed" bucket. Operators cannot answer "which of my automations burned the budget".
- Control is essentially absent: a runaway loop, a session-reset re-seeding storm (see #178953), or a chatty channel can consume a full 5-hour plan window in minutes with nothing in the product to stop or downgrade it. Users discover this only at the provider's rate-limit wall.

With recurring autonomous schedules (cron, heartbeats, subagents) being a core deployment pattern, spend needs to be attributable per surface and bounded per policy, the same way tool execution is gated per turn.

### Proposed solution

1. **Attribution rollup contract**: every model call carries the originating surface (agent, channel, cron job id, subagent run, interactive session) end-to-end, and a single queryable aggregate exposes tokens/cost grouped by surface over a time window. This generalizes the parity ask in #90911 and fixes the bucket problems in #102807/#156999 at the data model layer rather than per-UI-widget.
2. **Opt-in budget hook**: a config-scoped budget (per surface or global, per rolling window). On exhaustion the configured action fires: degrade to a cheaper model, skip/pause a schedule with a recorded reason, or fail the turn with a user-visible error — never a silent continue.
3. **Decision-friendly enforcement point**: the budget check belongs at the owning boundary where the next model call is admitted. The recently introduced provider-neutral `decision_evaluate` capability (#155115) is a natural fit for the "what do I do at the limit" judgment, keeping the mechanism generic and opt-in.

Explicitly **not** proposed: a billing system, per-token pricing tables, or provider-specific quota mirroring beyond what exists today.

### Alternatives considered

- Per-provider usage display fixes alone (e.g. #169428's footer template): treats symptoms; no enforcement.
- External monitoring scripts watching usage files: exactly the out-of-tree watcher pattern the project keeps absorbing back into core (cf. #161049 for cron supervision).

### Impact

- Affected: every operator running unattended schedules or multi-agent setups; mixed API+subscription users.
- Severity: cost surprises at "uninstalled it" magnitude are reported; for subscribed plans, wasted 5h windows block real work.
- Frequency: continuous for automation-heavy installs.
- Consequence: unpredictable spend, rate-limit lockouts, and manual post-hoc forensics across session files.

### Evidence/examples

- #90911 (per-run token persistence parity), #102807 (provider-keyed attribution), #156999 (unattributed cron sessions), #7379 (usage footer ask).
- Session-reset re-seeding as a concrete unbounded amplifier: #178953.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

If the attribution layer lands first (it is independently useful), the budget hook could follow as a small policy gate; happy to split this into two requests if maintainers prefer.
