issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
The shipped Kubernetes `init-config` command can fail to copy a required configuration or instruction file and still exit successfully. Its final temporary-directory setup overwrites the earlier failure status, allowing initialization to complete with required files missing.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Use the shipped `scripts/k8s/manifests/deployment.yaml` and an empty state volume.
2. Supply a ConfigMap containing `AGENTS.md` but missing `openclaw.json`.
3. Run the `init-config` command from the manifest in its BusyBox 1.38 image as UID/GID 1000, with writable state and temporary volumes.
4. Inspect its exit status and the seeded files.
5. Repeat with `openclaw.json` present but `AGENTS.md` missing.

### Expected behavior
Initialization exits unsuccessfully when a required seed file cannot be copied. The failure should remain visible at the init-container boundary so the Gateway does not start with incomplete initialization.

### Actual behavior
Both missing-source cases print a `cp` error but return exit code `0`. The missing file is not created. The subsequent successful `mkdir`/`chmod` command determines the overall status.

### OpenClaw version
Source commit `e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f`; affected manifest also compared with current main before reporting.

### Operating system
Linux arm64 container, BusyBox 1.38, UID/GID 1000. Host: macOS 27.0.1 arm64.

### Install method
Shipped Kubernetes manifest; reproduced by executing its unchanged command and paths in the declared container image.

### Model
Not applicable; no inference.

### Provider / routing chain
ConfigMap files → init-config shell → persistent state/workspace files → init-container exit status.

### Logs
Captured from the actual manifest command in a container with isolated temporary fixture volumes:
```text
missing openclaw.json:
  cp: can't stat '/config/openclaw.json': No such file or directory
  init_exit=0
  seeded openclaw.json=MISSING

missing AGENTS.md:
  cp: can't stat '/config/AGENTS.md': No such file or directory
  init_exit=0
  seeded AGENTS.md=MISSING
```

The complete-source control seeds both files and exits `0`. The preexisting-state control retains edited configuration and instructions and exits `0`.

### Impact and severity
An incomplete ConfigMap or failed state-volume copy can be mistaken for successful initialization. The Gateway can then fail later or start without the intended configuration/instructions, making the original deployment error harder to identify.

### Additional information
The [embedded init command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f/scripts/k8s/manifests/deployment.yaml) uses conditional copies but does not terminate on their failure. Its existing explicit guard only covers temporary-directory preparation. The [ConfigMap volume](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f/scripts/k8s/manifests/deployment.yaml) mounts the map without requiring individual keys, so a missing seed key is not rejected by that volume declaration.

The proof executes the exact init-container command/image; it does not run a Kubernetes control plane. Seed-if-missing behavior and protection of existing user files should remain unchanged.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Resolving an SSH identity filename containing two spaces or a tab returns a different filename: `two  spaces` becomes `two spaces`, and `with\ttab` becomes `with tab`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a source checkout at `77f79c00df61326c83f0420948a1959117007104`, create an empty temporary file named `two  spaces` (two spaces).
2. Call the production `resolveSshConfig({ host: "127.0.0.1", user: "proof", port: 22 }, { identity: absolutePath, timeoutMs: 5000 })` from `src/infra/ssh-config.ts`. It runs the installed OpenSSH client with `-G`; this prints effective configuration without establishing a connection.
3. Compare the returned `identityFiles` with the exact path supplied. Repeat with a tab in the filename and with `one space` as a control.

The reproduction used OpenSSH 10.3p1, empty temporary files, and a macOS sandbox denying network access and reads of the user's SSH directory. No SSH server, key material, or model is required.

### Expected behavior
Preserve whitespace inside each identity pathname, as OpenSSH does in its `identityfile` output.

### Actual behavior
The production resolver returned:

```text
input filename     returned filename   exact match
two  spaces        two spaces          false
with\ttab          with tab            false
one space          one space           true
```

The [parser](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/77f79c00df61326c83f0420948a1959117007104/src/infra/ssh-config.ts) splits the whole line on whitespace and rejoins the tokens with a single space. A separate `ssh -G -F <temporary-config>` check also preserved repeated spaces and tabs in quoted `IdentityFile` values.

### OpenClaw version
Source checkout `77f79c00df61326c83f0420948a1959117007104`.

### Operating system
macOS 27.0.1 arm64; Node 26.12.1; OpenSSH 10.3p1.

### Install method
Source checkout with the frozen pnpm lockfile.

### Model
Not applicable; SSH configuration resolution does not invoke a model.

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw SSH configuration resolver → system OpenSSH `-G`.

### Impact and severity
Affects identity filenames containing repeated internal spaces or tabs. The resolver reproducibly changes the pathname. [Gateway status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/77f79c00df61326c83f0420948a1959117007104/src/commands/gateway-status.ts) uses the first resolved identity when no explicit identity override is set, so this result can select a different path for the tunnel. Authentication was not exercised in this reproduction.

### Additional information
#190056 and closed PR #188906 concern trimming whitespace at the ends of configured paths. Their proposed change removes `opts.identity.trim()`; it does not change this output parser. This report concerns internal whitespace in `ssh -G` values. A focused fix can preserve the value after the key separator while retaining the existing blank-value, `none`, and port handling.

issues.body:
# Follow-up: await post-ready maintenance in pending-install lifecycle fixture

The first case in `src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` (hot-applies pending installs without restarting a sibling whose package metadata keys were reordered) can reach `plugins.reload` while real post-ready maintenance holds the plugin/config lifecycle lease. Its startup/config-reload readiness checks do not cover that owner. The later webhook cases already observe and await real maintenance.

## Release evidence
- Frozen candidate/qualification: `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`; FRV 43770476915/1.
- Original failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43770968712/job/132986918056 — `echoed` false, 1 failed / 530 passed. The original assertion did not print the RPC response, so its exact refusal cause remains unobserved.
- Same exact candidate passed this test in prior CI 43759963756/1, job132952700432. A local whole-file replay passed all3 cases; an original-shard replay passed this target but timed out on unrelated HTTP cases, so is not green-shard evidence.
- A bounded private Node24.22.1 diagnostic delayed the REAL `runGatewayPostReadyStartupMaintenance`, held the REAL registry refresh while it owned its lifecycle lease, and invoked the real `plugins.reload` RPC. This reproduced `echoed=false` with `UNAVAILABLE`, retryable=true, retryAfterMs=1000, mutationAccepted=false. No fake RPC/lease response or production change.
- Controlled comparison: release the same real refresh and await the real maintenance promise before the RPC. The unchanged target assertions then passed (1 passed / 2 unselected siblings, 26.16s wrapper; target 11.506s). This changes no production code and is not CI qualification.
- That controlled reproduction proves a missing fixture-readiness boundary; it does not retroactively establish the unlogged original RPC error.

## Requested main fix
Reuse the existing real-maintenance observation helper for the first case, await completion before the explicit reload, and expose the RPC refusal before asserting downstream metadata effects. Add bounded regression proof at the real owner boundary, retaining all sibling ownership/channel assertions. Do not relax the live lifecycle lease or add retries/sleeps to hide contention. Check current main for equivalent fixes before editing.

This is the fix-in-parallel tracking item for a bounded same-SHA release retry, not a waiver. The release candidate and P remain frozen; an unwaived CI failure still blocks publication.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash / run failure

### Summary

On 2026.11.1, sending `/think medium` in the same Telegram topic while an ordinary agent turn is running kills that turn with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` ("SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"). The directive itself is applied and acknowledged, but the in-flight turn fails right after its first model response: the completed model output is discarded, the user gets "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…", and the original request is dropped until the user resends it.

This is #192522 with a different command. PR #192585 fixed only `/status`: it marks status replies `contextFreeCommand` and states that "ordinary commands retain their existing behavior". Directive acknowledgements (`/think`, `/reasoning`, `/verbose`, `/fast`, `/elevated`, `/model`, `/queue`, …) still go through the same delivered-command recorder as context-bearing rows, so typing any of them mid-turn has the same effect.

### Observed sequence

2026.11.1 (`4ffdd20`), Linux, Node 26.12.1, Telegram polling, direct chat with forum topics, built-in `openclaw` runtime, `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, default queue mode. All times UTC, 2026-11-07, from the gateway log:

1. 03:59:46.377 inbound user request (411 chars) in a DM topic; agent turn `runId=0f7a6dbe…` starts on `lane=session:agent:main:telegram:direct:<peer>:thread:<topic>`.
2. 03:59:59.984 inbound `/think medium` (13 chars) in the same topic, ~14 s later, while the turn's first model request is in flight.
3. 04:00:02.880 directive reply "Thinking level set to medium." delivered (`sendRichMessage`) and recorded as a delivered command exchange.
4. 04:00:47.909 the first model response returns (`request=1`, promptTokens≈177k).
5. 04:00:48.821 `lane task error: lane=main durationMs=61856 error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"`, and the same for `lane=session:…`.
6. 04:00:49.065 `Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>`.
7. 04:00:49.400 `message dispatch completed … outcome=error`; 04:00:50.237 the user receives "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…". No answer to the original request; the user had to send "Continue" manually.

The same install hit the same failure on 2026-11-06 11:13 UTC, also on 2026.11.1: a 792-char request, then a 7-char command in the same topic 19 s later (acknowledged within 4.6 s), then the conflict 18 s after that, at the first model response. The command text isn't in the log, but its length matches `/status`. That is consistent with #192585 not having shipped yet (see release status below).

### Why (source)

- On `main`, the only producers of `contextFreeCommand` reply metadata are `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-status.ts` (`markStatusReply`) and the unknown-subcommand branch in `commands-info.ts`. `directive-handling.impl.ts` sets nothing, so a `/think` acknowledgement is recorded by `recordDeliveredCommandExchange` as a context-bearing command input plus reply.
- The active turn's prepared assistant append then fails the transcript fence when the first response is committed. The installed build checks this in the session-turn worker: `append.preparationVersion` against the version read in the transaction, which includes `rawSeq` and `transcript_updated_at`.
- The embedded runner rethrows it as fatal (`if (isSqliteTranscriptMutationConflict(promptError)) throw promptError`), and model fallback classifies it as `coordination`. So there is no retry or continuation, and the already-paid model response is lost.

The throwing call site wasn't instrumented. The timing (failure at the first assistant commit, after the directive exchange was recorded) and the #192522 analysis both point to the prepared-assistant fence.

### Release status

#192585 (merge `c2cb56c665e3c0a84f21f30369731563e05c37fa`) is not in `v2026.11.1` (latest stable) or `v2026.11.5-beta.1`: `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.transcript.ts` contains no `contextFreeCommand` at either tag, and the installed 2026.11.1 `recordDeliveredCommandExchange` has no such handling. Even after it ships, it won't cover `/think`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A Telegram (or any channel) session on an embedded-agent runtime with SQLite transcript storage.
2. Send a request that keeps the first model call busy for 10 s or more (a long answer or a large context).
3. While that call is in flight, send `/think medium` in the same chat/topic. `/think low`, `/reasoning on` or `/verbose on` should behave the same way.
4. Expected failure: the directive is acknowledged, then `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` fires at the first model response, the user sees "couldn't finish this request", and the original request never gets an answer.

Control cases: the same request without the directive completes normally, and the same directive sent after the turn finishes is harmless.

This was observed twice in production, not in an isolated harness. Rough frequency: any directive typed mid-turn by a user who adjusts settings while waiting.

### Expected

A settings directive sent while a turn is running should apply to the next turn (or at a safe boundary) without failing the turn in flight. User-visible commands shouldn't be able to destroy an in-progress answer.

### Suggested direction

- General fix, preferred over per-command marking: let the prepared-assistant fence rebase over delivered command exchanges that land mid-turn, or defer recording those exchanges until the active turn on that session lane settles. Marking commands context-free one at a time is whack-a-mole; there are dozens of slash commands and any of them can be typed mid-turn.
- ~~Narrow fix: treat directive-only acknowledgements like `/status`.~~ Withdrawn: #169026 (`289d859c`) deliberately keeps `/think`, `/model`, `/reasoning` etc. in later model context, and the slash-commands docs keep `/status` as the only exception. The fix should keep the directive exchange in history and context but stop it from invalidating the turn already in flight, for example by recording it after that turn's prepared answer commits, or by letting the fence accept a delivered command pair that arrived after the turn's input.
- Safety net, only if the above is not enough: recover the already-received answer when the sole intervening rows are a delivered command exchange. Not a blanket replay, which could admit unrelated newer input or repeat tool side effects.

### Related

- #192522 / #192585: `/status` variant, fixed on `main` only for `/status`.
- Same error family with other concurrent writers: #184909, #176235, #174994, #145551, #148280.
- Closed-unmerged #185939 ("recover rewrites from concurrent appends") is the general approach.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A Template that maps a `HEARTBEAT.md` larger than 262,144 bytes, or one that is not valid UTF-8, passes `templates validate`, `templates inspect` and `templates build`. The limit is only applied when Add plans the heartbeat automation, where it surfaces as a generic CLI failure: no reason is printed without `--json`, and with `--json` the output is not the Add plan envelope.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Template project `hbbig` whose `CLAW.md` maps the heartbeat file:
   ```
   ---
   schemaVersion: 1
   agent:
     id: hbbig
   workspace:
     bootstrapFiles:
       HEARTBEAT.md:
         source: workspace/HEARTBEAT.md
   ---
   Hello.
   ```
2. Write 324,000 bytes of text to `hbbig/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md`.
3. Run `openclaw templates validate ./hbbig`, `openclaw templates inspect ./hbbig` and `openclaw templates build ./hbbig --out ./hbbig.tgz`.
4. Run `openclaw templates add ./hbbig --dry-run` and `openclaw templates add ./hbbig --dry-run --json`.
5. Repeat with a 15-byte `HEARTBEAT.md` that is not valid UTF-8.

### Expected behavior

`validate`, `inspect` and `build` report the size or encoding problem as a Template diagnostic that names `HEARTBEAT.md`. If it is only found at Add, the preview reports it as a blocker in the normal plan output.

### Actual behavior

`validate`, `inspect` and `build` exit 0. `add --dry-run` exits 1 and prints only "The CLI command failed." `add --dry-run --json` prints a generic `cli_error` object.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3, source checkout of `main` at `159df507ba6` plus two local commits that touch only Gateway Add admission, the Control UI catalog dialog and docs

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Darwin, arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm openclaw`), isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, Templates enabled in Labs.

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
See the captured output under "Screenshots, recordings, and evidence".
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Captured output (temporary directory shortened to `<tmp>`):
  ```
  $ openclaw templates validate <tmp>/hbbig
  Valid Template project: <tmp>/hbbig
  Package: hbbig@1.0.0
  [exit 0]

  $ openclaw templates build <tmp>/hbbig --out <tmp>/out/hbbig.tgz
  Built Template: hbbig@1.0.0
  [exit 0]

  $ openclaw templates add <tmp>/hbbig --dry-run
  [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
  [openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
  [exit 1]

  $ openclaw templates add <tmp>/hbbig --dry-run --json
  {
    "ok": false,
    "error": {
      "type": "cli_error",
      "message": "cron scratch exceeds 262144 bytes (324000 bytes provided)"
    }
  }
  [exit 1]

  $ openclaw templates validate <tmp>/hbbad        # HEARTBEAT.md is not valid UTF-8
  Valid Template project: <tmp>/hbbad
  [exit 0]

  $ openclaw templates add <tmp>/hbbad --dry-run --json
  {
    "ok": false,
    "error": {
      "type": "cli_error",
      "message": "The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8"
    }
  }
  [exit 1]
  ```
- `templates inspect` on `hbbig` also exited 0.
- For comparison, a readable Template gives `add --dry-run --json` an object with `schemaVersion: "openclaw.templateAddPlan.v1"`, `blockers` and `diagnostics`.
- The limit comes from the cron scratch contract (`src/cron/scratch-contract.ts`); the heartbeat file is read when the plan builds the portable automation (`src/templates/portable-automation.ts`).
- Not run: a full Add, or the same Template through the Gateway.

### Impact and severity

An author can publish a Template that nobody can add. The person adding it gets no reason in the default output, and a script reading `--json` gets a shape it does not expect from this command.

### Additional information

Same family as #198559, where the `BOOTSTRAP.md` limit is also applied at a different stage than validation.

prs.title: perf(update): keep update migration attribution off generic database paths
prs.body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the installed package grows toward the 50,000-entry limit that released updaters enforce, because every worker that opens a database copies update/Doctor migration attribution (and the update inspection code behind it) into its private build.

## User Impact

User impact: no behavior change for users. It recovers installed-package headroom (about 56 entries now) and stops future database-opening workers from pulling update inspection code, which slows the drift toward the limit where updates from 2026.9.x stop working.

## Why This Change Was Made

`database-engine/open.ts`, the state DB fast path, current reader, open/maintenance/repair paths and the client-credential store imported `update-doctor-migration-attribution.ts` directly. That module drags in `update-candidate-state.*` inspection and `update-database-generations`. Since #197510 made the fs-safe copy worker host workspace filesystem operations, that worker's graph grew from 292 to 1,124 modules.

`src/infra/update-doctor-migration-context.ts` now owns the capture `AsyncLocalStorage`, the light read helpers (`hasUpdateDoctorMigrationCapture`, `getUpdateDoctorMigrationSource`, `getDoctorMigrationBackup`) and the entry points generic database code calls (`runUpdateSqliteMigration[Async]`, `beginUpdatePostgresMigration`, `beginUpdateSqliteCompanion`). Without an active capture these behave exactly as before: run the operation or return `undefined`, and the async path keeps its abort-signal check and synchronous-callback refusal. Under a capture they dispatch to the attribution owner, which `update-doctor-migration-attribution.ts` registers inside `runWithUpdateDoctorMigrationCapture`, the only place a capture becomes active. Doctor/update callers are unchanged. The new module is added to the PR wrapper source inventory.

## Evidence

- **Worker graphs** (tsdown probe, base `1cb3f179eac` → fix): the attribution module is absent from all 12 probed private worker graphs. Emitted files: fs-safe-copy 136 → 126, disk-budget 59 → 52, service-child-group-anchor 41 → 33, transcript-reconcile 37 → 31, openclaw-state-read 327 → 321, session-transcript 381 → 376, native-hook-relay 218 → 214, sqlite-readonly-location 103 → 102.
- **Installed package** (npm 12 install on Crabbox AWS): base `1cb3f179eac` 46,771 → head `6168a0413fc` 46,715 entries.
- **Bound test**: `keeps database-opening workers outside update migration attribution` (`test/scripts/tsdown-config.test.ts`) builds the fs-safe-copy worker with its real private config. It fails with base sources (update inspection modules in the graph) and passes on head `6168a0413fc`.
- **Native lanes** on head `6168a0413fc` (relabelled 2026.11.30): published 11.3 → fix via CLI succeeded (rc=0, readyz 200, 1 retained runtime, watched strings 0), and a managed `update.run` with a chat requester succeeded (readyz core, active).
- **Checks**: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt clean; test-line ratchet +58 of 400. The attribution, open, Doctor backup/schema, client-credential, state-DB-open and dialect-ratchet suites pass. 25 tests in `update-command-migrated-schema`, `doctor-health-startup.signal` and two attribution cases fail identically on base locally (`rollback-state-unverified`), so they are pre-existing and environment-dependent.
- **Reviews** on head `6168a0413fc`: autoreview scoped-clean at P2; the independent `codex exec` review (read-only) found nothing.
- **Remaining headroom**: this doesn't reverse the overall trend. The structural lever, consolidating tiny shared chunks in the unified graph, is a build-owner decision recorded in the update-reliability ledger.

prs.title: fix: preserve local wait budgets across wall-clock changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local waits can end early or overrun their allowance when the system wall clock changes, affecting accepted exec followups, runtime auth, process exit, Scheduled Task settlement, and managed update handoffs.

## User Impact

These five waits retain their elapsed-time budgets across wall-clock corrections. Existing messages, persisted timestamps, RPC epochs, and helper-owned shutdown settlement are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing monotonic-time owner for local budgets and explicitly select its clock in the handoff scheduler. Keep integer agent.wait timeouts with Math.ceil. Runtime auth converts only its internally created startup budget: upstream command-queue epoch deadlines remain epochs and can still be affected by clock corrections. The handoff closed command still joins its helper without a shorter parent timeout.

## Evidence

- Main 7997daf5ded5 and candidate each ran twice with process-local Date.now steps, plus unstepped controls, at all five sites. The six-minute followup allowance ended after about one second on main and after six minutes on the candidate; no competing direct delivery occurred.
- Source/vitest-source proof used natural performance.now and isolated HOME/state through ocx. Windows daemon cases are explicitly unit-level native-boundary fixtures on macOS, not live Windows proof. Auth uses delayed operations and handoff uses real child pipes; this is not full OAuth, Gateway/model, or installed updater E2E proof.
- 75 initial consumer checks passed. After aligning the Scheduled Task fixture, 55 daemon checks passed, including all three unavailable-settlement cases and 37 additional settlement cases. Production type diagnostics and changed-file formatting/lint were clean.
- [Detailed paired timing results and proof limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199951#issuecomment-6907343993).
- The fixture-only followup leaves all five production owners unchanged from the paired timing head 6a095fb37c2b. Native probe work and mocked sleep now advance the same existing fixture clock; all unavailable-settlement, exact-budget, and no-false-restart assertions remain.
- Full proof at a3e85ac9ba27: ocx build --dts passed, followed by packed tarball integrity validation and isolated packed CLI version/help smoke.
- No new clock framework or test-only production exports. Test changes consolidate reconnect clock-step cases and remove incidental duplicate logging-field assertions. Production: +40/-24 lines (+16); tests: +15/-19 (-4).

## Prior Reports

Supersedes the closed per-site PRs #181942, #195457, #187439, #190976, #199640, and #199665. Thanks to @mikasa0818, @shuisadev, and @SunnyShu0925 for those prior reports.

Two-way door: reverting restores the old local wait calculations; no stored data, configuration, or public protocol changes. Blast radius is limited to these five wait owners.

prs.title: fix(ui): a connection that died during an app switch recovers late after switching back
prs.body:
Fixes #199875

### What Problem This Solves

When the Control UI's Gateway socket stops delivering frames without closing while you are in another app, the page looks the same after you come back, and nothing the Gateway sends arrives. In live runs the UI replaced the socket 17.5 s after the return on the chat page, and 41 s and 56 s after it on the model setup page. On return, the page-activation check only replaces a socket that is closed or already silent past the 60 s tick window. A socket whose last frame is a few seconds old is left to the inbound-silence watchdog: after 60 s of silence, or 5 s after a request goes unanswered, it sends a `health` probe and gives it 10 s to answer. On the chat page the composer reloads its Talk settings on every window focus; on a dead socket those requests go unanswered, so the watchdog probes about 5 s after the return. Pages without the composer send nothing on return, so they wait for the 60 s silence window or for some later request to go unanswered.

### What changes

- On `visibilitychange` back to visible or window `focus`, if the socket still counts as healthy, `GatewayBrowserClient.probeOnWake()` sends the watchdog's `health` probe (`probe: false`) right away. It keeps the watchdog's 10 s deadline.
- Any inbound frame keeps the socket. The activity hook clears the pending probe as soon as a frame arrives, so an answer that lands in the same millisecond as the previous frame also counts.
- If nothing arrives within 10 s, the watchdog closes the socket (`inbound silence probe timeout`) and the reconnect supervisor replaces it.
- Switching back again while a probe is running keeps that probe and its deadline, so repeated focus events cannot hold a dead socket open.
- A socket that is closed, or already silent past the tick window, is replaced at once on return, as before.

### Impact

- Chat page: a reply that finished while you were away appeared 11 s after the return, against 17.5 s on `main` (one live run each).
- Model setup page: a socket that stopped delivering frames during an app switch was replaced 11.6 s and 11.2 s after the return, against 41.2 s and 56.1 s on `main` (two live runs each).
- A healthy socket stays open: in both model setup page runs the return's `health` probe was answered in 0.06 s, and no new connection opened in the 40 s that followed. This path closes a socket only if nothing at all arrives for 10 s after the return, the same deadline the watchdog uses.
- Each return to the window while connected sends one `health` request.

### Evidence

**Live runs, model setup page.** An isolated Gateway (`gateway run`, auth off, channels off, no model configured, so the Control UI opens on model setup) and the Control UI in Chrome for Testing, in a macOS VM. Both builds come from one source tree (this PR's head, `05bc22f`) and differ only in the two changed UI files; the served bundle was checked for `probeOnWake` before each run. A test proxy between the page and the Gateway logged every WebSocket and frame, and on command stopped forwarding on the open socket in both directions without closing it. It also removed the WebSocket compression offer so it could read frames. App switch: Finder brought to the front for 5 s, then Chrome again. Each run did a healthy switch first, then a switch with the socket cut off. Run 2 cut it off 1 s after a tick, so the socket's last frame was recent at the return.

| Build | Run | Healthy return | Dead socket: `health` probe sent | Old socket closed | New connection ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 1 | no probe, no reconnect | 29.2 s | 40.2 s | 41.2 s |
| `main` | 2 | no probe, no reconnect | 45.1 s | 55.1 s | 56.1 s |
| This PR | 1 | probe answered in 0.06 s, no reconnect | 0.03 s | 10.7 s | 11.6 s |
| This PR | 2 | probe answered in 0.06 s, no reconnect | 0.02 s | 10.2 s | 11.2 s |

Times are from the proxy log, counted from the moment Chrome came back to the front ("new connection ready" is the replacement socket's `hello-ok`). On `main`, run 1's probe came 60 s after the socket's last frame; run 2's came 5 s after a page request went unanswered. Screenshots of the page 40 s after the healthy return, 3 s after the dead-socket return and after recovery were pixel-identical in all four runs, so the page itself showed nothing either way.

**Live runs, chat page.** The same setup plus a stand-in model that holds its reply until the socket has been cut, so the reply finishes while you are away. One recorded take per build: send a message, switch to Safari, cut the socket, let the reply finish, switch back (Safari was in front for 32 s on `main` and 27 s with this PR). On `main` the page sent `talk.catalog` and `talk.config` on return, the watchdog probed 5.4 s later, and the replacement socket's `hello-ok` came 17.4 s after the return; the reply was on screen at 17.5 s. With this PR the probe went out on return, the `hello-ok` came 11.5 s after it, and the reply was on screen at 11 s.

<details>
<summary>Proxy trace for the four model setup page runs (redacted)</summary>

Each line is a proxy log entry: UTC time, seconds since the matching return to Chrome (the healthy return first, then the dead-socket return from `dead-away` on), and the event. `MARK` lines are the scenario's own steps. `c2s` frames come from the page and `s2c` frames from the Gateway; `DROPPED` means the proxy received the frame and did not forward it. prs.title: fix(ci): restrict dependency approvals to admins and SecOps
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152415

## What Problem This Solves

Dependency changes can bypass restricted security review when a PR author or approval-command commenter has Maintain access but is neither a repository admin nor a SecOps member.

## User Impact

There is no product runtime change. Dependency changes requiring approval again require repository admin or active `@openclaw/openclaw-secops` authority, whether supplied by the author or by `/allow-dependencies-change`. Sensitive-product Maintain/Admin policy, removal-only exemptions, rollout behavior, dependency versions, and existing merge protections are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restores the dependency policy that preceded `b52d2f08f51840eb386b4829b20656b239d13bee` ("trust maintainer-authored dependency changes") and removes the dependency-command broadening from #152415 without reverting its unrelated sensitive-product review tier. The shared approval owner and native prior-CI clearance now apply the same dependency-specific rule.

SecOps membership uses the existing primary/fallback GitHub Apps with only organization Members-read permission, separate from the workflow token used for repository statuses and notices. This is the route already used by the PR-context and native-proof workflows; no credentials, App grants, static approver roster, or public configuration were added. Membership-token failures are visible and fail closed. As with the existing separately minted cleanup token, a review exceeding the App token lifetime can require a new workflow evaluation.

## Evidence

- Red/green reproduction through the production dependency-guard entry point: a Maintain org-member author published success on the base; the restored rule leaves dependency approval pending. The matrix also covers nonmember Maintain authors, Maintain command commenters, admins, active/inactive SecOps members, bots, and revision-command freshness.
- 353 dependency, sensitive-product, combined-review, rollout, and workflow tests pass (18.52 s Vitest / 19.50 s command). All 120 native prior-CI consumer tests also pass (87.94 s Vitest / 88.83 s command), including dependency Maintain rejection and admin/active-SecOps acceptance. This existing integration suite exercises native Git/CLI admission and retained outcomes, not just a helper predicate; CI job seconds are not yet available.
- Focused lint, formatting, workflow actionlint/zizmor, docs MDX, and link audit pass. Targeted test typecheck passes with Node 24-compatible `ES2024.Promise` declarations for the existing `Promise.withResolvers` test usage; the default ES2023-only declaration set reports that existing library mismatch. No application build is needed for these trusted CI scripts. PR CI remains the broad exact-head proof.
- Independent Codex autoreview (GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2, reviewed base `270b338edea53c5fb8778d60e5ba7f68d36c31fd` through the complete local candidate with supplied owner/caller context: no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout was dirty/ambiguous; one hosted review will be requested on the ready PR.
- Existing Members-read App-token minting succeeded in [PR-context run 43808918001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43808918001). The changed default-branch Security Review workflow cannot execute from this PR before landing; its wiring and credential separation are covered by production-entrypoint fixtures and workflow checks.
- Simplification: Maintain authority no longer doubles as dependency authority. One shared predicate owns both author and command decisions; added machinery is limited to required credential separation and the native reader adapter, with no cache or fallback policy. Against the base: production scripts +60/−23 lines; tests/fixtures +141/−44; workflow +22 lines. The necessary growth preserves SecOps authorization and credential separation while removing Maintain dependency authority.

## Contributor credit

Requested and security-approved by @vincentkoc.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/c97b10d9)

prs.title: fix(release): contribution accounting fails for unavailable historical issues
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release contribution accounting failing when a previously recorded issue becomes unavailable on GitHub, even though its closing PR and covered release work remain verifiable.

## User Impact

Release maintainers can explicitly supply an original historical snapshot and its SHA-256 digest to preserve supported reporter credit. Recovery remains opt-in and fails closed without the frozen contribution row, historical reciprocal relationship, matching current PR identity, and covered source. No migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Historical evidence is read separately from exact-range live caching and cannot alias output paths. One recovery-aware resolution path revalidates every pass and records historical provenance without inventing live authorship or spreading reporter credit to unrelated PRs.

The covered source may be the original merge or one unambiguous release adaptation with an exact matching title and `Source commit` / `Source PR` markers. A missing live closing-issue edge is expected after visibility loss; the complete historical reciprocal relationship is still required. Mixed authorization, rate-limit, and transport failures are not treated as missing issues.

This PR changes only the collector, its owning workflow instructions, and tests. It does not regenerate release accounting or change release notes, releases, tags, assets, or existing historical snapshots.

## Evidence

- Final published head `93ae37cc21697de155f56aa274928a9fe5135864`: [CI run 43808371694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43808371694) completed **success**, with 32 successful and 30 skipped jobs. This is PR-head CI evidence, not main-landed or release qualification.
- Prior candidate `c05d6119c9ca7dbd37b3618a96e3ddd4bf6af026` (tree identical to initial published head `08cb558ef150aa0acae4104bf8829fc7217b0700`): the full collector suite reported **181 passed**. The retained terminal log remains prior-candidate evidence, not a local full-suite rerun on the final head. The original process completion was subsequently observed in native process history as exit 0; its stdout also contains an earlier temporary authentic-proof harness ENOBUFS failure, which must not be mistaken for the final test result.
- Initial CI TS2345 was attributable to the new fixture's unchecked snapshot filename. The exact root-scripts type graph reproduced exit 2, then passed after commit `c7e55a777d659ca0748af3fdb715a406fda82b95` added a runtime assertion. At head `9af6fdac92f5c16460eb3996bbaf6241a6311494`, [run 43806704340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43806704340) confirmed the type check and changed tests passed, but failed the +402/400 test-line budget and an inherited agent-catalog lint defect. The latter file was byte-identical to the base and was not changed here.
- Commit `2eabe87d2ea0e4e2a049e935b9f3a235962655fc` simplifies only fixture setup, retaining every case/assertion. Test-line budget now passes at **+400/400**, without allocation credit. Local focused validation: **17 passed, 164 skipped**, exact root-scripts type graph exit 0, targeted lint/format/diff checks passed. The collector and owning skill remain byte-identical to the previously reviewed candidate.
- The **existing independent read-only reviewer** assessed the complete collector change and then the fixture simplification. Its beginning/end identity checks confirmed base `5dc8071931853986c9a924c2e99996b8b5753a71`, final candidate tree `bb605eb64b1f30b097f9185d95157b245abdca86`, full diff SHA-256 `dda99685dae712b5f83f14161e02cbcbc84c819c181029ccc794e4c1d5c971fa`. **No P0–P2 findings.** This tree matches the committed repair and final published metadata-only descendant. Earlier proxy-stderr and redundant title-reference findings are resolved. The reviewer inspected source and retained validation without starting tests or accounting runs. Earlier autoreview was clean but its retained log alone does not print a diff/tree digest; no retroactive digest-bound receipt is claimed.
- The retained bounded authentic-case proof used the original digest-pinned snapshot, committed ledger and divergent release adaptation. It retained only supported historical reporter credit and asserted exact before/after snapshot byte equality and SHA-256. This was not full release accounting. All three original attachment hashes remain unchanged; original ingestion/before-after receipts for the two auxiliary attachments remain unavailable.
- A later request for a full exact-`d843` accounting proposal was not executed: this checkout lacks the working-tree 2026.11.4 section required by the supported source reader. No notes were initialized/copied, no source view was fabricated, and no accepted analysis was rerun.

Simplification consolidated three resolution passes and removed the superseded title-only unresolved-reference branch. Necessary production growth is bounded evidence/provenance validation; test growth covers distinct failure boundaries. Full repository build and full-range release accounting were not run locally. No merge is requested.

Thanks @hannesrudolph for the report, authentic retained evidence, and implementation direction.

prs.title: fix(install): show the effective Git destination in dry runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `install.sh --install-method git --dry-run` runs inside an existing OpenClaw checkout, the plan prints the default `~/openclaw` directory. Actual installation chooses the detected checkout instead. The preview therefore describes a different destination from the operation it previews.

## User Impact

The plan now names the same checkout that installation will use. Explicit CLI and environment destinations retain their existing precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve `final_git_dir` before displaying the plan and pass that value to both the display and the existing installation call. This moves the existing selection logic rather than duplicating it or changing where installation writes.

## Evidence

Four actual Bash entry-point invocations, network disabled, using a temporary checkout recognized by its package/workspace files. Paths below are sanitized:

```text
base, detected checkout: Git directory: <home>/openclaw
```

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins init @acme/demo --type provider` generates a default model whose provider does not match the generated registration. Model references split at the first slash: `@acme/demo/example-chat` addresses `@acme`, not `@acme/demo`.

## Changes

Derive a slash-free provider ID once and use it throughout new provider scaffolds: registration, auth options, catalog lookup, manifest/setup/activation metadata, and default model. The scoped plugin ID and npm package name remain unchanged. Existing projects are not rewritten; ordinary IDs retain their existing output.

Related: #186901, the earlier scoped-package-name fix. This preserves that fix and corrects the remaining model-reference defect.

## Proof

[Maintainer receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197598#issuecomment-6907907886), including public full-build and packed-smoke qualification.

Maintainer source-tier reproduction through the real `openclaw plugins init` CLI on isolated HOME/config/state:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Main `4ff607aa61f3`, scoped run 1 | `@acme/demo` | `@acme/demo/example-chat` |
| Main, scoped run 2 | `@acme/demo` | `@acme/demo/example-chat` |
| Candidate `a53742b923d5`, scoped run 1 | `acme-demo` | `acme-demo/example-chat` |
| Candidate, scoped run 2 | `acme-demo` | `acme-demo/example-chat` |

Both scoped candidate outputs retain plugin ID `@acme/demo`; their setup and activation providers agree with registration and the model reference. No generated source was patched. This proves scaffold output, not inference against the intentionally placeholder endpoint.

The existing provider-scaffold consumer regression passes. Full owner suite: 30 pass, one inherited macOS symlink-directory mode assertion fails (`1016` versus `2040`); the identical case fails on main `4ff607aa61f3` with the same values. Targeted formatting and lint pass.

Production +17/-14, tests +5/-5 (net 0), docs +5/-0. Existing code-shape assertions were replaced by the real model-reference parser invariant; no test case or allocation file was added.

## Risk

Two-way door for new scaffold output: reverting restores the old generator. Existing generated or installed projects are never modified. Blast radius is newly generated scoped provider projects; model parsing and runtime provider selection are unchanged.

prs.title: improve(ci): avoid unused snapshot supervisor preload
prs.body:
## Outcome: rejected, not landed

The benchmark stopped after measured pair three, as required by the rule published below: maximum-child RSS was 1,625.44 MiB for baseline versus 2,250.64 MiB for the candidate (+38.46%). The experiment exited 12 intentionally. No second VM, replacement sample or threshold change was used.

The full five-pair protocol did not complete, so this is not a qualified performance win. The sample does not establish the cause of the memory variation. The observed regression is enough to reject this candidate under the predeclared rule.

| Measured pair | Baseline wall (s) | Candidate wall (s) | Baseline peak RSS (MiB) | Candidate peak RSS (MiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 36.706 | 32.141 | 2147.49 | 2573.22 |
| 2 | 26.773 | 25.995 | 2251.64 | 2249.54 |
| 3 | 26.770 | 25.962 | 1625.44 | 2250.64 |

Descriptive medians of these three pairs only: command wall 26.773 → 25.995 s (-2.91%); summed crash-case duration 22.744 → 22.227 s (-0.517 s); user+system CPU 24.98 → 23.98 s (-4.00%). These are incomplete samples, not an acceptance result or a CI billing estimate. Broad PR CI was not qualified; the PR remained a draft.

Provider: Boat / ascii-box. Lease: `cbx_7c6d9e1bb797`. Native run: `run_02cbaa769f3f800a06d8a9aee47509d1`. The provider supplied no run URL. Source and all 65,487 tracked blobs matched the published candidate before execution; candidate contents were restored in the benchmark's finalizer.

## What Problem This Solves

Four SQLite crash-cleanup cases start a TypeScript loader in a supervisor that imports only Node built-ins.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. This measures whether removing unused test setup makes CI cheaper while preserving the real crash and cleanup scenarios. Maintainer-directed CI optimization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the outer supervisor preload. Keep the producer's TypeScript preload, child processes, SIGKILL, publication gates, original database-byte checks and survivor assertions unchanged. No new build roots, cache or dependencies. One argument removed from one existing test; no new tests or production changes.

## Evidence

- Normal commit hook/format and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local dependency sharing could not qualify; proof ran on one isolated Boat / ascii-box VM (8 usable CPUs, about 16 GB RAM). The affected format, lint and TypeScript checks passed. All five existing scenarios passed in all eight executions: two excluded warmups and three measured AB pairs.
- Local ClawSweeper0.3.3 reviewed the complete committed range `5dc8071931853986c9a924c2e99996b8b5753a71..70556ebe982b3a1dc4e3bd7813203959f329bc86`, completed with0 reported findings and no priority filter. Review did not execute the tests.

### Measurement rule, published before timing

Baseline: `5dc8071931853986c9a924c2e99996b8b5753a71`. Candidate: this one-argument change.

Workload: `CI=1 /usr/bin/time -v node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-parent-exit.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`.

On one isolated Linux VM with the same source/dependencies, exclude one warmup per side; run five serial alternating AB pairs. Record complete-command wall, sum of the four crash-case test durations, CPU user+system, maximum-child RSS, host load and observed resources. Outer TypeScript preloads must fall from four to zero with unchanged product children and assertions. Crash-case median must fall by at least0.2 seconds; full-command median must improve. P95 command wall/CPU/RSS may not worsen more than5%. Any measured metric more than20% worse stops the experiment; a regressed metric needs explicit acceptance. All five existing scenarios plus affected lint/type/format gates must pass before landing. No whole-job or billing saving is inferred from focused samples.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): reduce worker scope inheritance overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workers inherit a separate shared-memory backing store for every SQLite write scope. Long-running Gateways with many scopes pay that cloning cost again when workers start.

## User Impact

Reduces the memory and startup cost of inheriting large SQLite admission snapshots. Database contents, scope invalidation, worker lanes, configuration, and UI behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allocate each scope's three atomic cells from a 16-scope backing store. Each scope retains its own view and identity. Slots are never recycled, so views retained by older workers cannot alias replacement scopes. One surviving scope can retain at most 180 additional bytes of backing storage.

The production change is 12 net lines. One regression covers backing-store count, independent receipts and retirement; a standalone benchmark exercises the complete allocation/publication owners and actual worker inheritance. Native database operations are excluded from that benchmark.

## Evidence

Five serial, interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on Node 26.13.0, macOS arm64: 40 synthetic databases, 1,000 scopes each, four workers. Acceptance was fewer backing stores and no greater than 20% median regression in worker heap, RSS increase, or startup.

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared backing stores | 40,000 / 40,000 | 2,520 / 2,520 |
| Combined worker heap | 78.87 / 78.87 MiB | 65.15 / 65.16 MiB |
| Process RSS increase | 117.88 / 121.46 MiB | 98.73 / 99.77 MiB |
| Worker startup | 1,639.91 / 1,729.24 ms | 96.99 / 107.33 ms |

Rerun with `node scripts/perf/sqlite-scope-inheritance-measure.mjs "$PWD" /path/to/baseline-receipts.ts 5`, taking the baseline file from the parent commit. A separate run also verified cross-worker atomic writes through nonzero-offset views. The five-pair result used `60bdbf22bfe5312912619cecd5a4e5976772bc9c`. A follow-up renamed the local view to satisfy no-shadow lint; one additional paired run on that final source confirmed 40,000 → 2,520 backing stores, lower worker heap/RSS, and successful cross-worker writes. These are synthetic admission results, not full-Gateway or packaged-RSS measurements.

- Exact PR head: six SQLite/worker test files passed locally, 77/77 tests. The two worker files with Linux CI failures also passed on the recorded main baseline, 16/16 tests.
- The new regression fails with the original allocator (128 backing stores exceed 8); the exact PR source was restored afterward.
- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed, including runtime bundles, SDK declarations, plugin assets and Control UI. Pinned formatter, syntax, whitespace and commit guards passed.
- Earlier final-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43796767735. 62 jobs passed, including production/test types, core lint, primary lint, Windows checks and both unused-file scans. CI remains failed in six separately investigated jobs: unchanged catalog lint, unchanged `fs-safe.ts` exports, two UI timeouts, and two Linux/Node worker test groups.
- The manual-action UI timeout matches the same test in scheduled main run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43798879940. The other UI timeout occurred after all 600 selected tests passed. The worker failures observe synchronous filesystem calls/pump delivery in unmodified, unscoped fixtures; they do not invoke the scope allocator. Bun and the local main/PR runs pass. The Linux/Node failures remain unresolved outside this allocation change; a passing replay is not claimed as their fix.
- All named failed input blobs were verified identical between the CI main baseline and its retained merge snapshot. These failures are recorded for the native attributed-failure landing route; no failed CI is relabeled green.
- Local ClawSweeper completed the full original committed range with no actionable correctness/security findings. Follow-up commits only fix a shadowed local name and loop braces.
- The earlier isolated Boat attempt ran no tests because source sync failed. Its lease was reconciled as absent and removed from local tracking.

- Fresh ready-for-review CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43807253555. 48 jobs passed, including all selected test shards. The sole leaf failure is the same unchanged catalog `prefer-structured-clone` diagnostic at line 118; the downstream CI gate also failed. Required build and security checks passed. The earlier worker failures passing on this run is not claimed as a repair. Native landing evidence is bound to this fresh run.

prs.title: fix(discovery): bound wide-area TXT fields before publication
prs.body:
Fixes #199045

## What Problem This Solves

Wide-area discovery can successfully write and serve a zone whose advertised values are already damaged. CoreDNS splits a TXT field above 255 bytes into multiple wire strings; DNS-SD interprets each string as a separate key/value entry. A long `displayName` or `cliPath` is therefore shortened, and a UTF-8 character can be split between entries.

## Changes

- Check each complete `key=value` field's UTF-8 size before zone-file escaping. Keep 255-byte fields valid, including quoted text and multibyte characters.
- Reject oversized fields with an actionable field-specific error before the atomic replacement. An existing valid zone stays byte-for-byte intact; a first-time invalid publication fails clearly rather than advertising a damaged value.
- Cover the boundary through the unmocked production writer. Keep the existing OS file-size failure test effective by using valid individual TXT fields whose escaped zone text still exceeds the imposed file limit.

The existing Gateway discovery owner reports publication failures as warnings. This changes the wide-area producer, with no new dependency or discovery protocol.

## Evidence

### Production writer → CoreDNS → DNS query

Ran seven cases on the base and the fix, each with a disposable state directory, the actual `writeWideAreaGatewayZone`, CoreDNS **1.15.0** and `dig` against a loopback listener. macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 26.12.1. All 14 server runs completed and their owned processes stopped.

| Complete field | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `displayName`, ASCII, 255 bytes | Intact | Intact |
| `displayName`, ASCII, 256 bytes | Split into field + separate `"a"` entry | Rejected; prior zone preserved and still served |
| `cliPath`, ASCII, 255 bytes | Intact | Intact |
| `cliPath`, ASCII, 256 bytes | Split into field + separate `"a"` entry | Rejected; prior zone preserved and still served |
| `displayName`, UTF-8, 255 bytes | Intact | Intact |
| `displayName`, UTF-8, 256 bytes | Last `é` split between wire strings | Rejected; prior zone preserved and still served |
| `displayName`, quoted text, 255 bytes | Intact after escaping | Intact after escaping |

For each rejection, SHA-256 of the existing zone was identical before and after; a subsequent DNS query still returned the original synthetic discovery data. The proof uses the supported zone-file boundary, with synthetic addresses and loopback-only networking. It does not require a Tailnet or install a system DNS service.

prs.title: fix(infra): decide the history-blobs lock with a kernel lock, not mkdir
prs.body:
## Problem

Two agents running `git log -S` or `git blame` in the same sandbox could fetch into one object store at the same time. `prepare_blobs` guarded that with a `mkdir` directory lock and a `pid` file; on the Ubuntu sandbox images this failed, because a lost `mkdir` race is reported as won, so two callers could both believe they held the lock. The closed branch `fix/lazy-fetch-lock-atomic` tried to repair that with a lease, a nonce and a judged-identity restore. It cannot work while the lock pathname is unlinked and re-created: every reclaim is a window in which a third caller acquires the lock that a second caller is about to restore over.

## Change

The lock is a kernel lock on a file the shim never unlinks:

```sh
lock=$common/openclaw-history-blobs.lock.kernel
exec 9>>"$lock" || return 0
case $(uname -s) in
  Linux) flock -x 9 || return 0 ;;
  *)     lockf -s 9 || return 0 ;;
esac
```

`flock(1)` ships in util-linux, which Debian marks `Essential`, so the runtime and sandbox images have it. `lockf(1)` on macOS and FreeBSD base takes the same kernel `flock(2)` lock on an open descriptor, and its `lockf [-s] [-t seconds] fd` form runs no command; where an older userland rejects that form, `|| return 0` turns it into a skipped prefetch rather than a failure. The descriptor is opened inside the `prepare_blobs` subshell, so the kernel releases the lock when the subshell exits and no trap or cleanup path is needed.

Removed with the protocol: the lease, the per-instance nonce, the judged-identity restore, `restore_moved`, the private `abandoned.$$.N` and `released.$$` names, the `kill -0` reclaim, and the signal traps that existed only to remove the lock. Nothing unlinks the lock file, so there is no reclaim step, and the three interleavings the closed branch patched stop existing rather than being repaired one at a time.

## The legacy marker, and its bound

A directory marker written by an older shim is still read. An in-place upgrade can have an old process holding that directory while new processes start, and the two paths lock different inodes, so the new side serves a live owner first and never reclaims or removes the record.

`kill -0` only shows that a pid exists, never that it is still an old shim, so a leftover `pid` record whose pid was reused by a long-lived process of the same user would hold the lock for good and every other search would queue behind it. The wait is therefore bounded to 300 iterations of `sleep 0.1` ÔÇö the same bound the directory lock itself had ÔÇö and then gives the prefetch up: the kernel lock is released and the search runs unhydrated. A reused pid can cost one prefetch; it cannot wedge hydration.

## Size

| revision | lock protocol | shim lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 20 lines: `mkdir` + pid file + 30 s bound + reclaim | 609 |
| `fix/lazy-fetch-lock-atomic` | 112 lines | 701 |
| this branch | 6 lines of lock, 11 for the bounded legacy read, 19 with comments | 609 |

The file ends up exactly as long as `main`: six lines of kernel lock buy back twenty lines of reclaim protocol, and the bounded legacy read spends them again.

## Tests

New: `admits one history prefetch at a time across racing linked worktrees`. Six linked worktrees of one repository race two disjoint object sets through a `git` wrapper on `PATH` that writes `enter` before every fetch, holds it open for 0.6 s, and writes `leave` after. Exclusivity is the journal alternating; two `enter` lines with no `leave` between them are the overlap the lock forbids.

New: `gives up the prefetch on a legacy lock marker whose pid was reused`. The legacy record holds a live pid that is not an old shim, so the bounded wait has to expire and return instead of holding the lock. It costs about 30 seconds, which is the bound itself.

Dropped: `does not restore a reclaimed lease over a successor that arrived meanwhile`, which exercised the deleted lease protocol.

Kept unchanged: `shares overlapping blob prefetches across linked worktrees and keeps offline reads offline`. The assertion that still catches the original defect is `expect(new Set(wanted).size).toBe(wanted.length)` (`agent-git-shim.history.test.ts:175`): a second caller inside the lock repeats the wants the leader already supplied. Its neighbouring pack-count bound does not fire on this fixture; the duplicate-want assertion is the one that does.

### Results

Ephemeral cloud sandbox: Ubuntu 26.04.1, node 24.22.3, git 2.53.0, 4 vCPU / 8 GiB, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`.

| command | exit | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/agent-git-shim.history.test.ts` | 0 | 5 passed |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/agent-git-shim.test.ts` | 0 | 2 passed |
| `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental` | 0 | |
| `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` | 0 | 58 464 files |
| `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on both files | 0 | 0 warnings, 0 errors, 259 rules, `max-lines: 700` |
| `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` | 0 | |
| `check-max-lines-ratchet.mts` | 0 | |

### Both new tests can fail

Deleting the `case`/`flock`/`lockf` block from a throwaway copy of the shim, never committed and restored afterwards:

```
├Ś admits one history prefetch at a time across racing linked worktrees
  AssertionError: expected [ 'enter', 'enter', 'enter', ÔÇŽ(3) ] to have a length of 2 but got 6
├Ś shares overlapping blob prefetches across linked worktrees and keeps offline reads offline
  AssertionError: expected 11 to be 22   (agent-git-shim.history.test.ts:175)
```

Putting the previous shim `51e4e0f2c39` under this test file reproduces the reported hang exactly: the reused-pid test never returns and the run dies on its 90 s timeout instead of on an assertion. With the bound it returns after the 300 iterations (30.7 s measured).

### Not run here

macOS and FreeBSD: `lockf -s 9` is the documented descriptor form, but only Linux executed in this environment. Windows is not materialised for this shim.

prs.title: fix(configure): validate workspace paths at the prompt
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw configure --section workspace` accepts a regular file, or a path below a regular file, as the workspace directory. Provisioning then fails after the user leaves the prompt. The interactive setup wizard already has a shared path validator that can explain the problem while the user is still editing.

Reuse `validateSetupWorkspacePath` in the configure prompt, applying the same normalization and fallback used when consuming its value. This allows correcting the path in place while preserving the existing protection against persisting a failed workspace.

## Evidence

The regression runs `runConfigureWizard` with its prompt adapter and real temporary filesystem entries. It checks a file and a child of that file, verifies that neither provisioning nor persistence has started, supplies a corrected directory, and verifies the selected agent receives that directory while the original file remains unchanged.

On base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, the prompt has no validator and the new regression fails. With the fix, all 17 cases pass, including the existing persistence-on-provisioning-failure control:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs   src/commands/configure.wizard.test.ts   --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       17 passed (17)
```

This exercises the wizard handler and filesystem boundary with a simulated prompt adapter; it is not a terminal screen recording. The validator introduced for setup in #160373 is reused unchanged.

Formatting, focused lint and diff checks passed.

The owning test typecheck passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json --incremental`.

Closes #199983.

prs.title: fix(discovery): validate expanded wide-area service names
prs.body:
Fixes #199055

## What Problem This Solves

A configured wide-area domain can be valid by itself but too long once the generated service instance and `_openclaw-gw._tcp` are prepended. OpenClaw writes the zone successfully; querying the resulting CoreDNS service returns `bad packet: name too long`.

## Changes

Validate the expanded service name before rendering and replacing the zone. Reuse the existing ASCII domain-length bound, accounting for the final root dot. The service instance is the longest generated name, so this also bounds the shorter host, service type and SOA names.

The same service label is used for PTR, SRV and TXT records. There is no hostname truncation change, new dependency or arbitrary shorter domain limit. Invalid updates leave the existing zone untouched, and an invalid initial publication fails clearly.

## Evidence

Ran the actual production zone writer, CoreDNS **1.15.0** and native `dig` with synthetic data and loopback-only networking on macOS 27.0.1 arm64 / Node 26.12.1.

| Expanded service name, excluding final root dot | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 252 ASCII characters | Valid PTR response | Valid PTR response |
| 253 ASCII characters | Valid PTR response | Valid PTR response |
| 254 ASCII characters | Zone written; `dig` rejects the response as `name too long` | Writer rejects the domain; no zone file created |

The configured base domains were 204, 205 and 206 characters for the actual host used. Each individual label was within 63 characters. CoreDNS remained running in the failing base case; the observed failure was the DNS answer, not server startup. Every server process was stopped after its query.

<details>
<summary>Captured publication/query results and malformed-response diagnostic</summary>

The recorded lengths refer to the original expanded names. Local instance names, paths and the packet hex dump are omitted.

#### base-confirm capture

```json
[
  {
    "target": 252,
    "domainLength": 204,
```

prs.title: fix(agents): plugins tool cannot update an existing ClawHub install
prs.body:
Closes #199721

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an owner cannot update an already-installed ClawHub or official plugin from a conversation, because the agent `plugins` tool can only `install`, and install refuses an existing plugin.

## User Impact

Owners can ask the agent to move an installed plugin to a newer version, such as a ClawHub package from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2. Plugin configuration and enablement are kept, no uninstall is needed, and capability consent and `security.installPolicy` still apply. Plain `install` still refuses an existing plugin, so replacement is never implicit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway's `plugins.install` already accepts `mode: "update"`, the same managed path the `/plugins install --force` chat command uses. The tool now has an explicit `update` action that sends the existing install request with that mode. It accepts the same sources and fields as `install`. An action rather than an option keeps the deliberate replacement visible in the tool call, and leaves `install` unchanged. Docs in `docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md` describe the new action.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, real agent turn.** An isolated loopback Gateway was given a synthetic local OpenAI-compatible provider and a local ClawHub fixture serving `oc-demo-pack` at 0.2.1 and 0.2.2. The provider issued the `plugins` tool call through `openclaw agent`, and each step below is the tool result the agent received:

| Step | `main` (`e692995ce23`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `install` 0.2.1 | installed, enabled | installed, enabled |
| `install` 0.2.2 over it | — | `plugin already exists … (delete it first)` (unchanged) |
| Request update to 0.2.2 | `Validation failed for tool "plugins"`; stays 0.2.1 | `ok:true`, `enabled`, `version: 0.2.2`, `restartRequired:false` |
| `list` | 0.2.1 | 0.2.2 |

On this PR's run:
- After the update, `plugins.entries.oc-demo-pack.config.roster` (set between install and update) was unchanged.
- The install record became `clawhub:oc-demo-pack@0.2.2`, and the installed `dist/index.js` exported `0.2.2`.
- `openclaw plugins info` reported the plugin as `loaded`.
- With the plugin disabled, `update` back to 0.2.1 kept `enabled: false` and the configuration.
- The fixture logged artifact, security and download requests for each requested version, so the normal ClawHub verification path ran.

**Checks**
- `src/agents/tools/plugins-tool.test.ts` adds ClawHub and official `update` routing cases. They fail on `main` and pass here.
- Also passing: the plugins tool, reload handoff and route tests, plus `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `docs:check-mdx`, `docs:check-links` and `git diff --check` are clean.

prs.title: fix(doctor): updates fail after Doctor completes on hidepid /proc hosts
prs.body:
Related: #199559

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update fails with "Doctor complete." followed by "Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped" on Linux hosts that mount `/proc` with `hidepid=invisible` (Debian/Ubuntu hardening).

## User Impact

User impact: updates on `hidepid` hosts complete without adding the service user to the `/proc` gid group. Plain `openclaw doctor` still reports the legacy WhatsApp crontab advisory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Debian's `/usr/bin/crontab` is setgid. Doctor's legacy WhatsApp crontab advisory runs `crontab -l`. Under `hidepid=invisible`, a setgid (non-dumpable) child's `/proc` entry is hidden even from its own user, so update Doctor process custody cannot prove that child exited and fails the run. The advisory reads the live user crontab, which an update does not change, so update Doctor runs (update in progress, post-core convergence, writable-parent lint, or an update rehearsal) now skip it.

Rejected: teaching process custody to accept unreadable processes. That weakens the ownership proof; the failing spawn is an advisory with no update value.

## Evidence

Native Crabbox AWS Linux (Ubuntu, `/usr/bin/crontab` is `root:crontab g+s`), managed `update.run`, `/proc` remounted `hidepid=invisible` before the update:

| Lane | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 2026.11.3 driver -> base main `e1f84d9cf77` | failed `doctor-failed`: `Doctor complete.; Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped` (Gateway stayed healthy on 11.3) |
| 2026.11.3 driver -> this head `94ee79508d9` | succeeded in 220 s, Gateway ready on the new version |
| this head -> this head (relabelled), main driver | succeeded in 245 s |

Root-cause confirmation on main `3e1c0cd8eda`: the same hidepid update failed with the setgid bit present and succeeded after `chmod g-s /usr/bin/crontab`. Under `strace -f` (which drops setgid on exec) it also succeeded. Plain `openclaw doctor` and `doctor --fix` pass under hidepid because they run without update process custody.

Tests: `src/commands/doctor/cron/warnings.test.ts` new cases fail on base `e1f84d9cf77` (2 failed, 8 passed) and pass with the fix (10/10). oxfmt and oxlint clean. Autoreview scoped-clean at P2; independent `codex exec` review: no findings.

Not covered here: on a tmpfs `TMPDIR` smaller than the update runtime plus the largest database family, an update still fails with `ENOSPC` during state schema inspection (no early refusal). That is tracked on #199559 as a separate design decision.

prs.title: fix(gateway): large BOOT.md stalls boot runs and makes boot message sends fail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

BOOT.md is accepted up to 16 MiB, but the boot echo guard creates a Set of every 80/81-unit window. A sufficiently distinct accepted file exceeds Node's Set capacity during message-tool sanitization, so a legitimate non-echo send fails with `RangeError: Set maximum size exceeded` instead of being delivered. The failed construction also creates a large memory spike.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index rolling hashes from the shorter text, scan the longer text, then confirm a hit with an exact search at UTF-16-safe edges. Keep the existing 80/81-unit windows and whitespace normalization. Remove the no-longer-needed per-BOOT window cache. Exact confirmation returns at the first safe occurrence, including on repeated input; no position map or probabilistic suppression decision is introduced.

## User Impact

Large valid BOOT files no longer make message sends fail because of an oversized echo-window Set. Normal echoes are still suppressed and legitimate non-echo text still reaches the same delivery owner. No user-facing message/prompt text, file limit, configuration, grant, transport policy or stored-data format changes.

## Evidence

Paired-proof base `8b94cfb556c3ffa2d52eb9678b51828a31bb2966`; paired-proof candidate `7a8fb6a057bc4b2b253e392e2fef639abd5453af`; final integrated head `d7b5e324b57e9513df62c2d22937f27a69b79a90`.

The natural proof runs the actual Gateway startup boot-md hook and OpenClaw agent runtime. A loopback OpenAI Responses stand-in issues one real message-tool call to the bundled QA channel, which delivers over HTTP to the stock QA bus. The bus begins empty; the tool result's message ID must match its transport-assigned receipt. No held provider reply or injected normalized delivery state is used.

Both sides use built Node artifacts with the same private-QA flags, isolated HOME/config/state/workspace, loopback ports and default application heap settings. Source-loader qualification was excluded; the maintainer approved built artifacts to remove source-loader RSS from the comparison. Idle small-BOOT tree RSS was 1530.1 MiB base / 1634.3 MiB candidate.

All four interleaved large samples use the same accepted 9,511,058-byte synthetic BOOT file (9 MiB distinct-window ASCII filler with bounded line lengths), SHA-256 `c178d9e65cf5180d773e57a204307a0225615b8da816861a9f4701ccfa4b8126`.

| Sample | Message result / deliveries | Peak process-tree RSS MiB | OS max RSS MiB | Correlated tool-window RSS growth MiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base 1 | Set-size RangeError / 0 | 3225.9 | 3149.1 | 751.2 |
| Candidate 1 | matching transport receipt / 1 | 2354.5 | 2255.4 | 95.0 |
| Base 2 | Set-size RangeError / 0 | 3004.9 | 2918.3 | 651.2 |
| Candidate 2 | matching transport receipt / 1 | 2427.8 | 2328.0 | 36.0 |

Large model context still has memory cost; this is removal of the Set-sized send-time spike, not a constant whole-process RSS claim. Candidate tool-window growth is below the pre-recorded 128 MiB target. No accepted run reached the 4 GiB process-tree or 32 GiB host-available safety limit. For this 143-unit send, only 64 shorter-text window hashes are indexed rather than millions of BOOT substrings.

Controls match on both sides: small non-echo delivered; exact 80-unit echo suppressed; an 81-unit surrogate-boundary echo suppressed; a surrogate-half near miss delivered; a large repeated-character BOOT echo suppressed. The repeated-input cold tool observation was 3973 ms base / 174 ms candidate, consistent with first-match return.

Warm small-flow qualification discarded one call and retained five real calls per side on the unchanged artifacts. Non-echo median/range: base 43 ms (38–51), candidate 49 ms (44–52). Surrogate echo: base 17 ms (16–19), candidate 19 ms (17–23). Both medians satisfy the maintainer's 20% or 5 ms rule; **no latency claim**. Raw cold observations are retained, not labelled noise.

Vitest-source is base 1 RangeError failure / 6 passes, candidate 7 passes, retaining 600 surrogate-half comparisons, lone-surrogate, normalization, minimum-length and large-file assertions. Targeted lint, the matching gateway-root test typecheck leaf and formatting pass. Tests +33/-33, net 0; no allocation file.

The synthetic NO_REPLY terminal causes shared tool-free finalization probes in this runtime on both sides; the primary cases still contain exactly one message-tool call. The proof oracle is that call's actual result and transport receipt, not unrelated finalization behavior. Only synthetic BOOT data and bounded/hash-based evidence are used.

Anurag Singh's original human commit and issue #199437 credit are preserved. The maintenance commit keeps exact safe-edge confirmation and consolidates tests without dropping their contracts.

Full artifact proof: the private-QA Node build passed for the natural runs. A fresh public full build and public packed tarball integrity/version/Gateway-help smoke also pass; no service is started by packed smoke. ocx --verify quarantined a cache comparison mismatch (test-cache/tsbuildinfo among the differing files), not a product result; report `99cb4de0542f395d-1794775251165.txt`. Production +114/-34; tests +33/-33, net 0.

The contributor refreshed its branch and merged main while proof was running. That head was merged into this branch without replacing any contributor commit. Guard/test blobs are unchanged from the paired-proof candidate; incoming main changes do not touch boot.ts or the sanitizer, so the algorithm/RSS and warm evidence is reused with maintainer approval. Fresh integrated-head unit/type/lint/format and public full/packed proof pass. A new private-QA built fixture on the final head delivers the large BOOT send and suppresses the small echo through the real transport.

[Natural transport/RSS, decision-control, warm-timing, integration and artifact receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199646#issuecomment-6901562562).

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the old echo matcher and resource-exhaustion behavior without migrating data. Blast radius is substantial BOOT-echo detection during message-tool sends; normal suppression/delivery decisions, public text and delivery authority are preserved.
