prs.title: fix(ollama): uncurated cloud models fail every request with a window-sized max_tokens budget
prs.body:
Fixes #199928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every reply through an uncurated ollama-cloud model is rejected with HTTP 400 (`max_tokens ... exceeds model's maximum output tokens`) when the model's context window exceeds its real output cap.

## User Impact

User impact: uncurated cloud models (any whose context window exceeds the endpoint's output cap, e.g. the 1M-window lineup) become usable again on 2026.11.3+ instead of failing every request with a misleading "lower its reply limit" copy. Curated cloud models keep their curated budgets; authored `maxTokens` caps are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama's API reports no per-model output limit, and a context window is never a safe output budget — hosted endpoints cap output far below the window. The old fallback chain resolved uncurated cloud budgets to `params.contextWindow ?? OLLAMA_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW`; this drops those two fallbacks so uncurated cloud models return `undefined` and take the shared conservative default (`resolveDefaultModelMaxTokens`) that local models already use. Worst case is again a truncated reply, never a rejected request.

A follow-up could consult the hosted catalog's per-model output limits (already refreshed from models.dev) before falling back, restoring full output headroom for catalogued models; that wiring is intentionally out of scope here.

## Evidence

- `extensions/ollama` suite: 551/551 passed locally (`vitest run extensions/ollama/`), including the updated expectations that uncurated remote/cloud rows now resolve to the conservative default (`16_384` with a 262,144-token stub window) across provider-models, app-guided-setup, and setup-model-selection tests.
- Typecheck: `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `format:check` clean.
- Production observation backing the repro is in #199928 (3 gateways, 100% failure through `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; window-sized budget of 1,048,576 vs a 393,216 cap).

Only Skills is missing the hub heading.** This restores Skills to that existing presentation; it does not introduce the two-title pattern. Whether to remove the repeated title across all three tabs is a separate design decision, outside this consistency fix. All three tabs render the same [PluginsHubHeader](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3df082cf325b7105fbf6833faed7f96d04f68bc8/ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-hub-header.tsx#L18). The patch exempts the existing hub header while retaining suppression for ordinary Settings pages. The selected agent also aligns with the page content, and font-metric trimming centers the Back text and page title without a device-specific offset. The loading header follows the same text treatment. The Back icon uses the button's existing flex layout; padding follows the embedded header across all three hub routes. This is presentation only, using existing adaptive colors. Workshop behavior, copy, permissions, external navigation and the broader title design remain unchanged. ## Evidence | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | Captured on the same physical iPhone using local Debug builds before and after this patch, in English and Light theme, with an isolated Gateway. These screenshots document the development implementation; they do not show the App Store release. - Extended the existing browser navigation scenarios: hub headings must be visible, the selected agent must align with the content, and Back must retain a 44×44 minimum. This now covers Skills plus navigation and direct entry into Plugins and Workshop, without new browser setup. The original base fails because Skills is hidden; an intermediate CSS simplification failed the added destination checks with a 21 px offset, which the final patch fixes. - All **13 existing embedded Settings E2E cases passed** on the final repair, covering navigation, offline behavior, search, desktop chrome and three viewport sizes in Light/Dark. Additional local Light/Dark captures of all three hub tabs confirmed icon/label alignment. The physical-device screenshots above show the same visual change before the subsequent asset-size refactoring. The existing outdated `Import Memory` expectation now matches `Import memory`, also corrected on upstream main during preparation. - Real isolated Gateway: Appearance, Skills, Plugins, and Workshop at **400, 820, and 1280 px**, in Light and Dark. No horizontal overflow or layout-shift entries during the observed transitions; this does not cover every later catalog update. Physical iPhone checked in Light and Dark. VoiceOver speech navigation was not tested. - The official base comparison passed with **Node 24.22.1**, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3.0.2 against `3df082cf`: total CSS **+176 B** and chat-boot JS gzip **+86 B**, both within the existing 192 B variance allowance. prs.title: fix(ui): preserve SVG extensions in inline image downloads
prs.body:
Closes #198999

## What Problem This Solves

When a local SVG preview fails, the inline chat image menu saves the original as `parcel flow.svg+xml`, although the same original downloaded from the image viewer is `parcel flow.svg`.

## User Impact

Inline SVG downloads keep the standard `.svg` extension and exact original bytes. PNG/JPEG filenames and the existing image-viewer behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared inline download helper copied the MIME subtype into the filename. Recognize SVG alongside the existing JPEG mapping, and wrap SVG originals in an inert `application/octet-stream` Blob, matching the viewer's file-download treatment from #187235. Filename sanitization and the 30-second object-URL lifetime remain at their existing owners.

The patch changes one existing helper and adds two regression rows in its existing test file. Production +10 net lines; tests +34. No new module, dependency, setting or renderer.

## Evidence

Base `e741fd0d21ff7f9857a9c49f91d95166beaae83f` → fixed `b612d84e0040b6eea49af1a165350d4dddf097b8`, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 26.12.1, Chrome 157.0.8103.51 with its sandbox enabled.

The built Control UI was served by a real, isolated source Gateway on both revisions. A persisted synthetic conversation contained a local inbound SVG and managed PNG/JPEG controls. For the SVG, the browser aborted only the thumbnail request, exposing the shipped failed-preview image menu; metadata and original-file requests still reached the real authenticated Gateway. Clicking **Image actions → Download image** exercised the changed inline owner. PNG/JPEG used their normal inline download buttons.

| Shipped chat action | Before | After | Original bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SVG after thumbnail failure | `parcel flow.svg+xml` | `parcel flow.svg` | 597, identical |
| PNG | `original.png` | `original.png` | 127,437, identical |
| JPEG | `original.jpg` | `original.jpg` | 159,086, identical |

All six actual downloads matched their source files byte for byte. SVG SHA-256 on both revisions: `fef2d9b165321d1d0d7ee71f041d4c80976c6b8a4773167347e731a56ca8d220`. The browser recorded zero page errors and no extra page. The only injected network failure was the SVG thumbnail; no history, metadata or download response was mocked. No model call was needed.

For comparison, ten earlier browser-boundary downloads through the production helpers also covered SVG with a charset parameter and the unaffected viewer action. Those checks preserved bytes and filenames for the viewer, PNG and JPEG; they also verified that a script-bearing SVG was downloaded without executing its marker. The unit regression verifies the inert download MIME and object-URL cleanup.

- Before the fix: two new regression cases fail at the `.svg+xml` filename; four existing controls pass.
- After the fix: **33 tests pass** across the image-download and image-lightbox owners.
- UI production and UI test type graphs, focused lint, formatting, and line-cap checks pass.

prs.title: fix(google-meet): stop Calendar pagination on repeated tokens
prs.body:
Closes #199011

## What Problem This Solves

Calendar listing keeps requesting pages when Google returns a repeated continuation token, leaving the command or meeting lookup pending instead of reporting the broken pagination sequence.

## User Impact

Calendar operations fail with a clear error when pagination stops advancing. Valid multi-page results, including empty intermediate pages, continue to work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Calendar fetch owner now remembers the continuation tokens returned during one operation and rejects a repeat. This also catches longer cycles, without imposing a page-count limit on valid results. The existing Meet artifact pager protects a different API; this repair belongs in the Calendar owner.

The change adds seven production lines and two parameterized regression cases in the existing test file. No option, dependency or additional abstraction is introduced. Self-review and the simplification pass found no further change needed.

## Evidence

Paired runs through the source CLI, `openclaw googlemeet calendar-events --event target --json`, on macOS 27.0.1 arm64 / Node 26.12.1. A local HTTPS Calendar fixture supplies synthetic OAuth credentials and controlled API responses; the CLI uses the guarded proxy route with TLS verification and OS-enforced loopback-only networking.

| Calendar response | Base | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three valid pages, including an empty intermediate page | Three requests; target returned | Three requests; target returned |
| `second` returned twice | Repeated requests until the fixture's safety cap at request five | Two requests; clear repetition error |
| `second` → `third` → `second` | Cyclic requests until the same safety cap | Three requests; clear repetition error |

The fixture cap returns HTTP 503 to terminate the baseline safely. Every final request matched the synthetic authorization and preserved the query filters. This exercises malformed provider responses; it does not claim a live Google Calendar incident.

Two new regression cases fail on the base and pass with the fix. The focused Calendar, Meet pagination, Google API error and timeout suites pass all 22 tests. Production and test TypeScript checks, targeted lint/format and the line-cap check pass. The full Google Meet plugin lane also passes: 303 tests across 32 executed test files, after the official runtime build.

## What Problem This Solves

`install-cli.sh --node-version v24.22.1` accepts the option and then requests a nonexistent `vv24.22.1` archive path. Incomplete versions also reach provisioning. Normalize the optional leading `v` once and require a complete canonical numeric archive release before any preparation.

## User Impact

Users can paste a normal Node release label into `--node-version`. Invalid archive targets fail immediately. Existing runtime detection keeps its support for leading `v`, build metadata and supported future-major prereleases.

## Why This Change Was Made

The download-version validator and the archive URL builder need the same representation. Normalizing at `main` makes the selected runtime directory and URL agree; tightening only the archive validator leaves installed-runtime policy intact.

## Evidence

Actual Bash entry point, base versus fix; network disabled and download requests intercepted:

```text
input             base request                          fixed request
v24.22.1          /dist/vv24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt         /dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt
24.22.1           /dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt          /dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt
27                /dist/v27/SHASUMS256.txt              no request; no prefix created
```

For `27`, fixed output is `ERROR: Node 27 is unsupported; use Node 24.16.0+ or Node 26.1.0+.` The download interceptor exits 79 when reached; invalid input exits 1 beforehand. No Node installation was performed by these probes.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts   --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --maxWorkers=1   -t '^(?!.*(?:with file TMPDIR|originally set: false|alias is retargeted)).*$'
```

prs.title: feat(sessions): show per-session token and cost usage from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #192616

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway records per-session token and cost attribution and the Control UI shows it, but the terminal could not: `openclaw gateway usage-cost` prints one aggregate number, so a headless operator could not see which session, agent, or model burned the tokens.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions usage [sessionKey]` prints one row per session (label, agent, model, messages, tokens, cost) plus range totals, with `--agent`, `--all`, `--range`, `--start/--end`, `--max-rows`, and `--group-family` selectors. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.usage` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `sessions.usage` owner and only shapes output: conflicting selectors are rejected before dispatch, and the report's `partial` status is printed instead of hidden, so a time-budgeted answer is never mistaken for "no usage".
- The row cap flag is `--max-rows` rather than `--limit`, because the parent `sessions --limit` list-row cap owns that name (the sibling search command follows the same naming after review feedback).
- Registration rejects the parent list selectors, matching the other gateway-backed verbs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-usage.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and run against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000 --json
{ ..., "startDate": "2026-10-06", "endDate": "2026-11-04", "cacheStatus": {"status": "partial"},
  "partial": { "reason": "time-budget", "message": "Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; ..." } }

$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000
Session usage (2026-10-06 → 2026-11-04)
No session usage recorded in this range.
Totals: $0.0000 · 0 tokens · in 0 / out 0
Partial report: Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; narrow the date range or select a session.

$ openclaw sessions usage --agent x --all          → exit 1 (conflict)
$ openclaw sessions usage --end 2026-10-31         → exit 1 (missing --start)
$ openclaw sessions usage --max-rows 500           → exit 1 (cap exceeded)
```

The live response's `partial` reason surfacing in text mode is the behavior the review asked to prove: an incomplete answer is labeled, never silent.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, ledger, or config changes.

When a tool the agent expects is missing, the operator had to guess why. - The command forwards the canonical owner and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and transport failures exit non-zero in both output modes.
- Registered under `agents` because the `tools` root is deliberately reserved.
- The command defaults its runtime to `defaultRuntime`, matching the other agents commands that are invoked without an explicit runtime from the registration wrapper.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents-tools.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` → 32/32 passed locally.

```text
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown session key \"agent:main:main\"" },

Tools diagnostics failed: unknown session key "agent:main:main"

```

The Gateway log confirms both live requests (`⇄ res ✗ tools.effective ... errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown session key`). The isolated store has no sessions, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests.

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, tool-policy, or config changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).
- Workflow validation passed, including pinned tooling fallback and zizmor.
- Changed-surface checks passed: formatting, root-test typechecks, dependency/coercion/dead-export guards, and script/test lint. `git diff --check` passed.
- Repair delta: 12 insertions / 37 deletions across workflow and guard test; removed the separate preflight input, scheduling branch, and branch-dispatch route.
- Local autoreview of this repair against `7bf16b8fd47f07612777b4957b1a14bbc66eba42`: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.
- Remaining integration proof: no new credentialed translation run was dispatched. The earlier hosted translation/artifact run predates the current approval checks, so it does not prove approved and revoked-source behavior for this head. That remains an explicit pre-merge validation gap.

### CI integration repair

- Integrated main `1f01f4944d45` to resolve a concrete CI failure: the new non-publishing upload step retained an old action pin while main's canonical workflow helper required the updated pin.
- Both upload steps now use main's existing upload-artifact v7.0.2 pin; the dispatch/security repair is unchanged.
- Focused workflow regression: 1 passed on the integrated candidate. Full workflow validation, including zizmor, passed. `git diff --check` passed.

prs.body:
feat(tencent): add Hy4 Flash model to TokenHub and TokenPlan

## What Problem This Solves

Tencent users can't pick Hunyuan's faster, cheaper Hy4 tier (`hy4-flash`) in OpenClaw on either the TokenHub or the TokenPlan endpoint.

## User Impact

User impact: users can now pick `tencent-tokenhub/hy4-flash` or `tencent-tokenplan/hy4-flash` (or the "Hy4 flash" aliases). The model accepts text and image input, has a 1,048,576-token window, and supports `none`/`high` reasoning effort, so it works well for high-throughput agent and tool-use loops at a much lower cost than `hy4`.

The default model doesn't change: fresh onboarding still selects `hy4-preview`. Existing configs aren't migrated, and Doctor doesn't move anyone onto `hy4-flash`. If an API key uses a limited access scope, the user has to add **hy4 flash** to its allowed models.

## Why This Change Was Made

`hy4-flash` is added to the catalogs and model aliases of both Tencent endpoints:

- It accepts the same image formats as `hy4` and uses the same `none`/`high` effort ladder (default `high`).
- Its context window is 1,048,576 tokens, with a 983,040-token input limit and 65,536 max output tokens.
- Pricing comes from Tencent's published Flash rates: input 0.07, output 0.281, cache read 0.003.

Reasoning-effort handling needs no new code. The existing logic already reads each model's supported effort levels from the catalog. The hy3-specific effort map stays scoped to hy3.

The Doctor allowlist (hy3, hy3-preview, hy4-preview) is left as is on purpose. Doctor shouldn't silently move users onto a model with different pricing and key scope.

The Tencent provider docs now include `hy4-flash` in the model table, the key-scope note and a short description of the tier.

## Evidence

Unit tests updated in `extensions/tencent/index.test.ts`:

- Both endpoints' auth/catalog tests now expect `hy4-flash` in the configured model list.
- The reasoning-effort tests check that `hy4-flash` maps OpenClaw thinking levels to Tencent's effort values like `hy4-preview` does: `off`/`none` → `none`, and `minimal`/`medium`/`xhigh` → `high`.

prs.title: fix: /tools verbose advertises automations scope the turn cannot execute
prs.body:
Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

`/tools verbose` advertises automation creation during management-only turns, even though execution rejects `add`. Inventory construction has no run ID, so deriving its description and schema from an exact-run execution grant incorrectly falls back to the unrestricted surface.

## User Impact

Discovery inside an admitted management-only turn no longer advertises creation. Fresh remote administrator turns retain creation through the existing `callerScopedCreation` distinction. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This fixes the discovery mismatch only; the reported Telegram creation rejection is not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` reads admitted scope, deployment policy, liveness, and any supplied run ID without requiring an execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` reuses that classification while retaining its exact-run, live caller authority and operational-instance checks.
- Automation descriptions, schemas, and compact summaries use the admitted mode. Summary wording stays in the existing description-presets owner, keeping `cron-tool.ts` within its line limit.
- Discovery outside an admitted turn still describes the configuration surface, not per-turn execution authority.

## CI Repair

Rebased onto upstream `24e758688a6db34e1f9079f65faff3269bf15978`, which contains [#181647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181647), `05d779c0c931c8c0bbccf9cce93a47fbb54e6ef9`. That upstream repair distinguishes the admitted restart source ID from the interrupted execution run ID, addressing the three failures previously reproduced on CI's upstream base without this PR.

Removed this PR's duplicate exact action-enum assertion, which had become stale when upstream added `bind`. The real command-handler regression remains; existing schema and authority tests protect permitted actions and the creation boundary. No upstream assertions, skips, retries, or approval gates were changed by this PR.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression covers `/tools verbose` in an admitted management-only scope. Authority coverage distinguishes discovery from execution grants and preserves fresh remote creation.
- 128 focused tests passed using repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 20 restart-continuation cases plus 108 authority, tool, inventory, and prefix-stability cases across the six affected suites.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

prs.title: fix(codex): use the literal bound workspace cwd for plugin discovery
prs.body:
Fixes #190076

## Reopened

Reopened after the earlier quota-driven close. The defect is unchanged on current `main`
(`extensions/codex/src/native-plugin-tool.ts:95-97` still trims `binding?.cwd`), so the
fix is still needed. The fix commit has been replayed onto the latest `main`; the
production change is byte-identical to the previously reviewed head.

Re-verified on the refreshed base (Node 24.22.1):
- Red on `main`: `uses the bound workspace cwd verbatim when it carries edge whitespace` fails.
- Green with this fix: `native-plugin-tool.test.ts` 9/9 passed.

## What Problem This Solves

`createCodexPluginsTool` resolved the workspace for native-plugin discovery with `binding?.cwd?.trim() || options.context.workspaceDir?.trim() || ...` (`native-plugin-tool.ts`). The bound cwd is stored untrimmed (`app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts` persists `cwd: params.cwd` verbatim at session start), so this leaf trim rewrote the session's literal workspace identity before building the `plugin/list` request. The Codex app-server then scanned the trimmed impostor directory for marketplace plugins instead of the real one — discovery silently returns nothing for a workspace whose name carries edge whitespace.

## Solution

Use `readNonBlankString` on each fallback level. Blank or whitespace-only values still fall through to the next source (`context.workspaceDir`, then the configured default workspace), but non-blank values flow verbatim into the discovery `cwds` request parameter. This matches the whitespace-preserving convention already used for the app-server binding `workspaceDir` in `conversation-binding-data.ts`.

## Impact

- Marketplace plugin discovery scans the literal bound workspace directory.
- Fallback semantics for blank/whitespace-only values are unchanged.
- No other consumer of the binding store is affected: the stored record itself already kept the raw cwd.

## Evidence

Red-green on a pristine `origin/main` worktree (remote runner, vitest):

- **Before:** 1 failure — `expected cwds ["/bound/company"] to equal [" /bound/company "]` in the `plugin/list` request.
- **After:** `native-plugin-tool.test.ts` 9/9 passed; consumer regression `plugin-marketplace-discovery.test.ts` 5/5 passed.

Real behavior proof (2026-10-30): the shipped tool, driven against the pinned `codex-cli 0.164.0` app-server (`plugin/list` over stdio, no mocked catalog), returns `literal-ws-bundle@literal-ws` for a session bound to `/tmp/pr188122-proof/ws/company `, while the `.trim()` selection returns the sibling's `trimmed-sibling-bundle@trimmed-sibling`. Full transcript: [#issuecomment-6524133566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188122#issuecomment-6524133566).

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187554 (configured directory identity) and #187739 (session cwd identity). Sibling sweep PRs: #187751, #187766, #187777, #187816, #187825.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes actionable command errors disappearing from stderr when commands using the shared runtime run with `--json`.

## User Impact

JSON-mode failures show the diagnostic already shown in text mode, including command-specific prefixes. Existing message wording, redaction, JSON stdout and exit codes are preserved. Startup failures outside the command wrapper are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runCommandWithRuntime` now uses its existing text diagnostic path in both modes. A reported-error marker prevents the root renderer from printing a second diagnostic, while JSON formatting unwraps the original error to preserve its envelope and structured recovery/run fields. Existing completed exits and expected errors still pass through unchanged.

The unreachable JSON-only triage callback is removed: calling it after this repair would write a second envelope. Existing per-command expected-error classifications remain because changing their direct consumers, prefixes or debug behavior would not be an equivalent cleanup.

The shared regression replaces the redundant docs-search JSON-envelope e2e case; docs-specific failure wrapping remains covered in `docs-cli.test.ts`. prs.title: refactor(agents): replace tool-loop detectors with an arguments-only repeat guard
prs.body:
## Problem

The tool-loop guard was 12 files and about 1,700 lines. It hashed tool outcomes, had name checks for single tools (exec, message, wait, memory_search, computer, progress_card, write, process), and had four separate detectors plus a post-compaction guard. Rolling detection was opt-in, so most installs did not use it.

One part was always on: after 3 identical failing calls, the next identical call ended the turn. The model got no chance to answer, and the user got a stop message in place of an answer.

## Fix

One guard in `packages/agent-core/src/tool-repeat-guard.ts` (105 lines), used by the agent loop:

- It compares each tool call with the call before it. It compares the tool name and the canonical arguments only. It never compares outcomes.
- 3rd identical call in a row: the call runs, and a redirect note is added to its result. The note names the tool and tells the model to change its approach.
- 20th identical call in a row: the call does not run. The turn ends with the typed reason `tool_repeat_limit` and this message: `OpenClaw stopped this turn: the model called <tool> with the same arguments 20 times in a row. Send a new message to continue.`
- Tools declare `repeatable` themselves and skip the check: Code Mode `wait`, `process` poll/log/list, `agents_wait`, `sessions_yield`, `subagents` list/wait, `computer` screenshot/wait. The declaration is plain data (`true` or `{ actions: [...] }`), so it crosses the worker wire.
- Worker turns (cloud and node workers) run the same guard over all their tools. The Gateway resolves `tools.loopDetection.enabled` (agent over global) into the worker tool-surface policy as `toolRepeatGuard`, and each tool definition carries its `repeatable` exemption. Two optional fields are added to the closed worker tool-surface schema (`definition.repeatable`, `policy.toolRepeatGuard`); worker bundles are build-bound to the Gateway.
- Calls to an unknown tool are keyed by name.
- New user input resets the streak.

Removed: outcome hashing, per-tool checks, argument churn, ping-pong, the rolling history, batch admission and recovery state, the post-compaction guard, the "3 identical failures" hard stop and its error code. Repeated identical failing calls now get the same note and cap as any other repeat.

Config:

- `tools.loopDetection.enabled` stays. `false` turns the guard off. Unset or `true` keeps it on. This also folds the rolling detection that was opt-in into the one default rule.
- The Codex `appServer.loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` key is retired. `openclaw doctor --fix` removes it.
- The `tool.loop` diagnostic event stays, with `detector: "tool_repeat"`.

## Proof

| Check | Tier | Base (`5d5ca9d2`) | Head (`ecb05477`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit: note at 3rd identical call, stop at 20th with `tool_repeat_limit`, repeatable tools skip, unknown tool keyed by name, guard off when disabled (`tool-repeat-guard.test.ts`) | vitest-source | n/a (new) | 10/10 pass |
| Regression: 4 identical failing calls, then the model answers | vitest-source | **fails**: turn ends after 3 failures, no answer | pass |
| Real Gateway, mock model repeats one failing read (`tool-loop-global-breaker`, step 1) | dist-nodts | **fails**: Gateway logs `OpenClaw stopped this turn: the same read call failed 3 times`, run ends in error with no answer | pass: note on 3rd read, model recovers with its final answer |
| Real Gateway, mock model ignores the note (step 2) | dist-nodts | n/a | pass: exactly 20 reads, 20th not run, user sees the `tool_repeat_limit` message |
| Regression: worker turn with loop detection on, `progress_card` called 3 times with `{"markdown":"Still working"}` gets the redirect note on the 3rd result; with `tools.loopDetection.enabled: false` it gets none (`worker.runtime.test.ts`, real worker runtime + fake Gateway) | vitest-source | **fails** on `a3f26f46` (worker forced `enabled: false`) | pass |
| Gateway policy: `toolRepeatGuard: false` only when loop detection is off; agent setting overrides global (`prepared-tool-surface.test.ts`) | vitest-source | n/a (new) | pass |
| Upgrade: config written by latest stable `2026.11.3` (`tools.loopDetection.enabled`, Codex `appServer.loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` + `requestTimeoutMs`) plus the old sub-keys (`windowSize`, `historySize`, `warningThreshold`, `criticalThreshold`, `globalCircuitBreakerThreshold`, `detectors`, `postCompactionGuard`, which stable already rejects, as left by older releases); stable Gateway runs turn 1 on a mock model; head `openclaw doctor --fix`; head Gateway starts and runs turns 2 and 3 on the same session (fresh HOME, throwaway ports) | ocx src | | pass: doctor removes every retired key and keeps `enabled` and `requestTimeoutMs`; head Gateway starts on the migrated config; turn 2 answers; turn 3's provider request contains turn 1's reply, so the session survives |

prs.title: feat(system-agent): let the system agent report backup status
prs.body:
Fixes #192657

## Summary

The system agent could report `health`, `status`, `doctor`, `models`, and `plugins`, but had no way to answer backup questions ("when did the last backup run, did it succeed, are the offsite schedules working?"). The Gateway already summarizes that through the canonical `backup.status` projection; only the model-facing surface was missing.

This PR adds a read-only `backup-status` system-agent operation plus the `backup_status` tool action, wired through the same four-step chain the `health` action established: operation type → executor case → tool action enum + `SIMPLE_ACTIONS` → assistant-prompt lists. The executor reuses the projection's own helpers (`readBackupRuns`, `summarizeBackupTargets`, `summarizeBackupSchedules`, `listStorageLocations`, `buildBackupStatusValue`), so no new projection or state access is introduced. The typed-command parser accepts `backup status` / `backup` / `backups`.

Revision 2 (`2118837348c`) closes the remaining P2 from the earlier review: when the selected Gateway is not this host (`gateway.mode=remote`), the loader now asks that Gateway's `backup.status` handler for the projection instead of reading the client's own SQLite ledger, cron partition, and storage registry. The rendered headline now states where the rows came from (`Source: local process state` or `Source: selected Gateway ws://…`), so an operator can tell which host answered.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: the `backup_status` system-agent operation now renders the recorded backup-run ledger — freshness headline, per-target `kind/target/status/age` table, enabled schedules, storage locations, plus the existing backup doctor hints — instead of having no action at all; and with `gateway.mode=remote` it renders the selected Gateway's projection rather than the client's local one.

**Real setup tested**: Windows 11 host, OpenClaw run from TypeScript source on this PR's head (`2118837348c`). Two isolated state directories, no user state touched: Gateway host `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix` (real pre-existing `state/openclaw.sqlite`, 2.0 MB, with two recorded runs) and remote client `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote` whose own ledger holds **0 rows**. The Gateway ran on `ws://127.0.0.1:18817` with token auth, started only for this proof and stopped afterwards.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1, invoked as `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` (no `dist` rebuild, so the tree under test is exactly this branch's source)
- **Selected-Gateway transport**: the shipped `backup.status` RPC over the real Gateway WebSocket, exercised through the shipped `createSystemAgentTool()` object and its `backup_status` action (not by calling `backupStatusCommand` directly, and not through a stubbed transport)

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
# Gateway host: isolated state with real ledger rows, real Gateway on 18817
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18817

# Local mode (no gateway.mode): the same tool object the agent calls
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts     # createSystemAgentTool({surface:"cli"}).execute({action:"backup_status"})

# Remote mode: client has gateway.mode=remote -> backup.status on the selected Gateway
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts

# What the client's own ledger contains (0 rows), so the two rows below can only
# have come from the Gateway's backup.status response
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-ledger-rows.ts
```

The two probe files contain no stubs: they build the shipped tool with `createSystemAgentTool({ surface: "cli" })`, prepare runtime config through `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader`, and print the tool's real text result.

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
# local mode, isolated state with two recorded runs (newest first)
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: local process state
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# gateway.mode=remote, client ledger has 0 rows — rows come from the selected Gateway
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: selected Gateway ws://127.0.0.1:18817
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# the remote client's own ledger, proving the two rows above crossed the RPC boundary
{"clientLedgerRows":0,"targets":[]}
```

The local-mode run took 254.6 s and exited 0; the remote-mode run took 142.6 s and exited 0. Both are real terminal runs, not test output.

**Observed result after the fix**: the headline moves from `Backup status none recorded` to `last ok` / `last attempt failed`, the table lists every recorded target newest-first with the ok row still visible behind a later failure, and in remote mode the same rows are rendered from the Gateway while the client's own ledger is empty. Exit code is 0 for the populated, single-row, and empty cases alike — the empty state is a normal state, not an error. `Source:` makes the answering host explicit in both modes.

**What was not tested**: no live LLM agent turn was run (this host has no model credential wired for a paid run), so the model's own tool-selection step — choosing `backup_status` and formatting its answer — is covered only by the contract assertions in `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts`, not by an executed agent session. Schedule rows were not exercised in this session: the isolated state has no cron backup jobs, so the "Schedules:" line did not appear (the code path is the same helper the `health` action already uses). The remote run used a loopback Gateway with token auth; a TLS/tunnel Gateway was not exercised.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: the runs used TypeScript source via the `tsx` loader rather than a `tsdown`-built `dist`, so the evidence is byte-identical to this branch's source but not to a packaged release artifact. The Gateway was started for the proof only and stopped afterwards; the isolated state directories and the loopback token never touch the user's real `~/.openclaw`.

## Gateway-target fix (revision 2)

| Scenario | Before this revision | After this revision |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.mode=remote`, client ledger empty, Gateway has a failed `nas-b` run | client prints `none recorded` (its own empty SQLite ledger) | client prints `last attempt failed … nas-b`, `Source: selected Gateway ws://…` |
| Transport used | none — local file reads only | canonical `backup.status` on the selected Gateway (`callGateway`, `operator.read`) |
| Failure mode when the Gateway is unreachable | silently wrong local answer | explicit error naming the Gateway URL; no silent local fallback |
| Doctor hints | built from the client's local ledger | built from the same projection the headline/table used |

`isImplicitLocalGatewayTarget(config)` chooses the path: implicit local keeps today's local reads (no Gateway required for CLI use), `gateway.mode=remote` routes to `backup.status`. `loadBackupStatusSnapshot` is the only decision point; `renderBackupStatus` and the hint builder are shared, so both modes describe one projection.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests landed with the PR (recorded when the branch was pushed, not re-run in this evidence session): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` → 114/114 passed, covering the new `backup status` parse rows and the schema/description assertions.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/commands/backup-status.ts src/commands/backup-health.ts` → 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --write` applied to both files.
- Type checking: a workspace-wide `tsgo` run in this checkout is red on pre-existing `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` dependency drift (`src/acp/*`, unrelated to this branch); it reported exactly one error in the touched files on the first pass (`OpenClawConfig` imported but unused), which is fixed in the pushed head.
- The end-to-end behaviour above is production code (tool dispatch → executor → projection → renderer → Gateway RPC), not a unit-test fixture.
- Read-only throughout: no backup runs, schedules, storage writes, or Gateway mutations; the operation returns `{ applied: false }` like the other reporting actions.

## Risk checklist

- **Does this change user-visible behavior?** Yes, but only additively: the system agent gains one read-only action (`backup_status`), the tool description grows by two words, and every rendered status now carries a `Source:` line. No existing action semantics change.
- **What is the release/rollback risk?** Low. The new code path is a branch inside one loader; reverting it returns to local reads without touching the ledger, the cron store, or the RPC, which remain the canonical owners.
- **Could this corrupt state or break an existing surface?** No state is written. In remote mode the command now performs a read-only `backup.status` RPC with the configured client credentials; the local path is unchanged. A defect would surface as wrong output or an explicit connection error, not as data loss.
- **Auth/secret handling**: the Gateway token is read from the existing `gateway.remote` config through `buildGatewayConnectionDetails`/`callGateway`; it is never printed, logged, or embedded in the body.

## Current review state

- **Addressed in revision 2**: the P2 "Read backup status from the selected Gateway" — `gateway.mode=remote` now routes through the selected Gateway's `backup.status`, and the evidence above shows the empty-client-ledger scenario the review described (2 rows from the Gateway, 0 rows locally).
- **Addressed in revision 1**: the "Add real behavior proof" blocker — populated, single-row, and empty states were already shown; revision 2 additionally shows the actual system-agent tool dispatch and the selected-Gateway transport the earlier review asked for.
- **Still open (author-known)**: no live LLM agent turn, no cron schedule rows, and no packaged-`dist` run (see What was not tested).
- **Next step**: maintainer review. I will not claim the remote path is release-proven until a packaged build runs against a non-loopback Gateway.

## Before / After

| State | Before this PR | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Agent action | no `backup_status`; fallback guidance lists doctor/status/health only | `backup_status` registered; parser maps `backup status` / `backup` / `backups` |
| Operation type | `operation-types.ts` has no backup case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | `{ kind: "backup-status" }` (1 hit) |
| Executor | no `backup-status` case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | dispatches to `backupStatusCommand` (2 hits) |
| Rendered output | — | freshness headline + source + per-target table + schedules/locations + doctor hints |
| Remote Gateway | local ledger read regardless of `gateway.mode` | `backup.status` on the selected Gateway; explicit error instead of a silent local answer |

prs.title: fix(cli): escape the docs search link destination so unusual URLs still render as one link
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plain-text output of `openclaw docs` is markdown, and every field of a result line is escaped as literal text except the link destination. A destination that contains a space, a parenthesis or `>` ends the destination early, so the renderer drops the link and prints the rest of the URL as loose text. This closes that gap with the escaper the same command already applies to the title, snippet and query. Honest scope: today's live docs API returns clean slug URLs (measured below: 12 of 12 destinations from a live query carry no markdown-significant character), so this is a consistency fix on a reachable-but-not-yet-observed input, not a report of a URL that is currently broken on the live site.

- Problem: the plain-text output of `openclaw docs` is markdown, and the link destination was interpolated raw while the title, snippet and query were already escaped by `escapeMarkdownText`. A destination containing a space, parenthesis, `>` or backslash terminates the destination early, so renderers drop the link and print the remainder as literal text.
- Solution: pass the destination through the same `escapeMarkdownText` helper that the surrounding lines already use. Its CommonMark backslash escapes are consumed by the link parser, so every destination that is a valid URL keeps exactly the link target it had before.
- What changed: one line in the plain-text branch of the `docs` command (the destination is now escaped), plus the existing `it.each` case for literal search text now feeds a destination with parentheses and `>` and asserts the emitted destination is escaped and still renders as one link.
- What did NOT change: the rich/TTY branch (unchanged), `--json` output (the raw link is still returned verbatim), the heading, title and snippet escaping, the API request, and the escaper itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Best fix**: reuse the existing owner. `escapeMarkdownText` is the canonical CommonMark escaper in this repo and its own doc comment already says it covers URL punctuation; the previous change in this command escaped the title, snippet and query but left the destination raw. Escaping at the interpolation point keeps the fix at one line and removes the asymmetry instead of adding a second escaper.
- **Alternative(s)**: percent-encoding the destination was rejected because it changes what the user sees in the terminal (a raw space becomes `%20`) even for URLs that render fine today; reusing the title's escaped form was not possible because the destination must stay a URL. Replacing the markdown output with a plain listing was rejected as a user-visible behavior change far beyond this bug.
- **Risk**: the escape sequences are visible in the raw terminal line (`https\:\/\/docs\.openclaw\.ai\/…`). That is the same trade-off the title and snippet already made in this output: the terminal line is markdown source, and the escape is what makes it render as one link. One regression is real and accepted: a destination whose value ends in a backslash now terminates at that backslash because the escaper turns it into `\\` and the parser consumes both, which truncates the anchor. No URL from the docs API ends that way today, and the previous output for such a destination was already broken.

## User Impact

This does not change any output produced by today's live docs API. It removes the last unescaped field of a line that is already escaped field by field, so a result whose destination one day carries a space, a parenthesis or `>` degrades to readable text that keeps the full URL instead of turning into a truncated link plus loose title text. Output for ordinary URLs renders exactly as before, and `--json` consumers see an unchanged payload.

## Evidence

| Case | Before (pre-fix / base) | After (post-fix / this head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result URL contains a space (`/cli/docs/a b`), `openclaw docs docs --limit 1` | 1 anchor whose href is truncated to `https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs/a`, the rest of the URL is lost | no link: the line falls back to literal text ending with the full URL `…/cli/docs/a b`, nothing swallowed |
| Result URL contains parentheses and `>` (`/cli/docs?a=(b)&c=d>e`) | 1 anchor, href `https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs?a=(b)&c=d>e` | 1 anchor, same decoded href (escape sequences are consumed by the parser) |
| Control: title and snippet carry `**bold** [x] ©`, plain URL | 1 anchor, href `https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs/plain`, title/snippet render as literal text | same anchor, same decoded href, same literal title/snippet (only the destination source is escaped) |
| `--json` cell for all three cases | raw link returned verbatim | byte-identical stdout (`cmp` exit 0 for all three) |
| Live API, no fixture: `docs configuration --limit 20` on both arms | 12 of 12 destinations already markdown-safe, 12 anchors rendered | identical: 12 anchors, no output difference today |
| Focused unit test `src/cli/docs-cli.test.ts` | 1 failed / 10 passed with the source reverted | 11 passed |

Both arms ran the built launcher (`node openclaw.mjs docs …`, launcher loads `dist/entry.js`) from a full `runtime` build of the same tree, one with the changed line reverted and one with this head; only that single production line differs between them. Each cell used a fresh isolated HOME / `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` with no credentials and no gateway. In the three comparison cells the only external edge replaced was the `https://docs.openclaw.ai/api/search` HTTP call (via a Node `--import` preload that returns a fixed result set), so the command, argument parsing, output formatting and process exit are the shipped ones; the live-API row ran the same arms with no preload and no fixture at all. Markdown was rendered independently (CommonMark renderer + DOM) to count anchors and read the decoded `href`.

Emitted destination, base vs this head (same fixture):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs docs docs --limit 1        # base
# Docs search: docs

- [CLI docs reference](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs/a b) - Usage for openclaw docs

$ node openclaw.mjs docs docs --limit 1        # this head
# Docs search: docs

- [CLI docs reference](https\:\/\/docs\.openclaw\.ai\/cli\/docs\/a b) - Usage for openclaw docs
```

Rendered result of those two lines (1 anchor vs 0 anchors):

```console
base  cell A  links=1  href=https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs/a
head  cell A  links=0  href=null
base  cell B  links=1  href=https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs?a=(b)&c=d>e
head  cell B  links=1  href=https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs?a=(b)&c=d>e
base  cell C  links=1  href=https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs/plain
head  cell C  links=1  href=https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/docs/plain
```

Same two arms against the real endpoint, no preload and no fixture (`docs configuration --limit 20`, isolated state, exit 0 both arms):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs docs configuration --limit 20     # base
# Docs search: configuration

- [Configuration](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/configuration) - Configuration overview\: common tasks\, quick setup\, and links to the Configuration reference
  ... 14 lines total

$ node openclaw.mjs docs configuration --limit 20     # this head
# Docs search: configuration

- [Configuration](https\:\/\/docs\.openclaw\.ai\/gateway\/configuration) - Configuration overview\: common tasks\, quick setup\, and links to the Configuration reference
  ... 14 lines total

destinations scanned: 12   with markdown-significant characters: 0
rendered anchors: base 12 / this head 12
```

Live queries at `--limit 50` for `a b`, `?`, `(beta)`, `route` and `param` returned only clean slug destinations (`/gateway/configuration`, `/providers/clawrouter`, `/plugins/architecture-internals/gateway-routes`, …); `a b` and `?` returned no results at all. Nothing in the live corpus needs the escape today, which is why the before/after difference only appears in the fixed-result cells.

Built bundle excerpts, showing which form each arm actually executed:

```console
# base dist chunk
s.push(`- [${t}](${e.link})${r}`)
# this head dist chunk
s.push(`- [${t}](${escapeMarkdownText(e.link)})${r}`)
```

Focused test, source reverted vs this head:

```console
$ npx vitest run src/cli/docs-cli.test.ts     # base source, new test kept
× renders literal search text with rich=false
Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/cli/docs-cli.test.ts     # this head
Tests  11 passed (11)
```

What was not tested:

- No live occurrence was observed. The real endpoint was exercised without any fixture, twice per arm, and every destination it returned was already safe for markdown, so the truncation cells above are driven by a fixed result set through a preloaded fetch edge rather than by a URL the live site is serving today. Real numbers: a live `node openclaw.mjs docs configuration --limit 20` returned 12 destinations, of which 0 contain a space, parenthesis, `>` or backslash, and base and this head both rendered 12 links from it; live queries for `a b`, `?`, `(beta)`, `route` and `param` at `--limit 50` also returned only clean slug URLs. So this is a fix for a reachable input, not a reproduction of a user-visible failure that is happening now.
- The rich/TTY branch of `docs` does not build markdown at all, so it was only spot-checked for identical output and is unaffected by design.
- The full `build-all.mts runtime` run ends with the UI bundle phase failing in this environment (same failure with the source reverted), after `dist/entry.js` and the CLI bundles are written; every command above ran against those artifacts. A `cliStartup`-only build hits the same UI phase.
- A destination whose value ends in a backslash was not exercised end to end; by CommonMark rules the escaped `\\` terminates the destination there, so such a link would still be truncated.

Open PR collision check: searched open PRs by changed files for `src/cli/docs-cli.ts` and `src/shared/text/escape-markdown.ts` and by keyword for the command; no open PR touches either file. The earlier escaping change in this command (#196565) is already merged and explicitly left link destinations alone, so this is its remaining gap rather than a duplicate.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep repeat updates with current artifacts a no-op
prs.body:
Related: #195653

## What Problem This Solves

A repeat `openclaw update` unnecessarily reinstalls current ClawHub artifacts and reports “plugins updated.” Skipping that installation must still preserve manifest repair and capability-consent review.

## User Impact

Healthy, accepted artifacts produce a clean no-op. Missing/invalid required manifests and stale/missing acceptance follow the ordinary reinstall/review path. Actual installs, host repairs, and record rewrites continue counting as changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub retention requires matching source/artifact identity, present runnable entrypoints, healthy host links, and the consent owner's fresh inspection of valid package manifests and current capability coverage. The consent owner preserves its existing official and disabled-update exemptions. Failed retention checks fall through to the existing staged installer and consent handler; acceptance is persisted after review, and refusal is reported normally.

Artifact identity contracts now live with their owner, removing the helper-to-installer import cycle. The added assertions were removed using the real record/union contracts. No config/schema/dependency/release changes.

## Evidence

- `update-noop.test.ts` now exercises the real updater, ClawHub installer, archive installation, and consent owner using synthetic registry/archive I/O. Cases cover healthy no-op, one npm record rewrite, stale/missing acceptance, declined consent, missing/invalid plugin manifests, changed digest, and missing entrypoint. Successful repairs assert usable manifests and persisted current acceptance. The old contract-incomplete installer stub and duplicate ClawHub table are removed.
- Serial named local test attempts (`update-noop.test.ts`, `clawhub.test.ts`) were stopped at cold worker compilation as required on the production host. No local runtime pass or baseline red/green result is claimed; PR CI owns that proof and test timing.
- Touched-file tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt, whitespace checks, and commit-hook ratchets passed. Exactly 51 net repair test lines are allocated separately; PV's 127 + PV2's 51 = 178 final net test lines. Shared scalar unchanged.
- Fresh final local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, base `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f` through the staged snapshot committed as `2edfa6636fd02434644dcbd07827ff0860bd909f`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Static scoped assessment; runtime/complete graph proof remains CI-owned.

### Prior-head CI attribution

All four failed jobs and the separate failed commit status were inspected through the API. These are the five failing entries, rather than five distinct failed jobs:

| Entry | Cause and action |
| --- | --- |
| [check-guards-architecture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984097873) | PR-caused helper/installer all-import cycle. Removed the back-reference and placed shared contracts with the artifact owner. |
| [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984097877) | PR-caused two uncommented assertions. Removed both; no baseline exception. |
| [checks-node-changed-compact-large-4-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984098173) | Main-owned source-capture import/GC caller-retention failure on Node 24.22.1. Its test is unchanged; a static traversal of 183 value-import/reexport modules rooted at capture-directory and scheduler reaches no changed PR file. Bare/dynamic imports were not expanded. No matching scheduled-main job exists, so identical baseline runtime failure is unproven. No unrelated source/test change or retry masks it. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128986448232) | Rollup of those three failed jobs. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate commit status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42564026955) | Security-review policy correctly propagates failed CI; its review job itself succeeded. |

PV2 exact-head [CI run 42565567225](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42565567225) is in progress; no final runtime/broad-check verdict is claimed. Prior-head results are attribution evidence only. No merge.


### Typed fixture migration

Commit `f28cb3a747a6bfbf90bae36c3f52a727e8cffb13` shares a typed, non-retaining consent fixture between Doctor and onboarding. This completes the new result contract while shrinking the capped onboarding test to 1043 counted lines (prior allowance 1045). Targeted typecheck/lint/format and the normal commit hook passed; no cap or hook exception. The extraction has exactly 7 net fixture lines, separately allocated. Production behavior and the main-owned caller-retention failure are untouched.

prs.title: feat(gateway): connect approved trusted-proxy CLI and TUI devices within their grant
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199698. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199698 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

A device approved for fewer scopes than its client requests, such as a team guest approved for only `operator.sessions.write`, can't know its grant before it connects. Its first connection after approval therefore always files a scope-upgrade request, for scopes the admin already decided not to give.

## User Impact

User impact: with the new opt-in `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.narrowToDeviceGrant`, an approved CLI or TUI device behind the trusted proxy connects within its grant from the first connection. No upgrade request is filed and no audit entry is written. The TUI also keeps a device token, as the CLI already does. When named operator roles are enforced, a human operator identified by the proxy still receives no device token, as before; their CLI and TUI connect within the grant on every connection without storing it.

The option defaults to `false`, so existing Gateways behave exactly as before.

With the option on, `openclaw security audit` reports a new warn-level finding, because the TUI's token, like the CLI's, authenticates a direct Gateway connection without the proxy identity until the device is revoked.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Existing mechanism:** the Gateway already narrows a same-key scope upgrade to the paired grant, with no pairing request or audit entry, for browser and native UI clients when `trustedProxy.deviceAutoApprove` is enabled. This change gives that lane to CLI and TUI devices under its own option.

**Which connections it applies to:** same-key operator devices that authenticate through the trusted proxy and send no browser `Origin`. For those:
- A request that exceeds the grant connects with the intersection, and the hello reply reports the resulting scopes. That is how a newly approved device learns its grant.
- A connection never receives more than the grant. A request that includes `operator.admin` overlaps every grant, because admin implies every operator scope, so it connects within the grant.
- Only a request that shares no scope with the grant, such as `operator.pairing` alone against a session-only grant, still files the upgrade.
- Browser clients and new device enrollment are unchanged.

**TUI device token:** trusted-proxy auth treats the TUI like the Control UI and issued it no device token. Under the option it gets one, so it keeps the grant between runs. With the option off, its default, nothing changes. Named-role human operators stay tokenless either way.

**New audit finding:** `gateway.trusted_proxy_narrow_to_device_grant` (warn). `deviceAutoApprove` already reports a warn finding; this option reported nothing. The finding and `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` tell the admin to keep the proxy as the only Gateway ingress, and to remove a device with `openclaw devices remove <deviceId>` when its user's access ends.

**Config-surface budget, 2654 to 2655:** the option adds one boolean key, so the core count in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` grows by exactly one. It has to be an option rather than a default because it changes which connections file upgrade requests and which clients hold device tokens; existing admins rely on both. No existing key fits: `deviceAutoApprove` also auto-approves new device enrollment, which an admin who only wants guests to stay within their grant should not have to accept. No other config is added.

**Docs:** `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` gains a section for the option, its config reference entry and the audit checklist line. The section says that the option is off by default and that named-role human operators get no device token. `docs/start/multiplayer.md` points guests' admins to it. `docs/cli/tui.md` marks the TUI's trusted-proxy behavior without a device token as the default and links the option.

## Evidence

- **Server tests:** in `src/gateway/server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts` 20/20:

prs.title: fix(gateway): serialize GitHub publication refresh waves across remembered sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

Serialize background GitHub publication fact refreshes per discovery instance (`refreshTail` queue in `startGitHubPublicationDiscovery`) so that `refreshAll` invalidations on config, GitHub identity, or managed profile changes process remembered sessions one at a time instead of starting up to 256 concurrent preparations at `delayMs: 0`.

Fixes #195649

## What Problem This Solves

`startGitHubPublicationDiscovery` caches up to 256 recently read sessions and subscribes to config-scoped `sessionChanges`, `githubIdentityChanges`, and `onManagedGitHubProfileChanged`. When any of those fires `refreshAll(true)`, `refresh(key, true)` schedules every remembered session at `delayMs: 0`. On the next scheduler wake, all queued callbacks start concurrently and call `prepareGitHubPublicationFact`, which immediately enqueues work onto the `"Session target discovery"` worker lane (`maxConcurrent: 1`, `maxPending: 128`). Once more than 129 remembered sessions refresh at once, the discovery lane overflows its 128-pending queue and live user turns that need session target discovery fail with `worker task capacity reached`.

By chaining background preparations sequentially per discovery instance (`refreshTail`), at most one background publication refresh runs `prepareGitHubPublicationFact` at a time, leaving the `"Session target discovery"` lane available for live turns. If an in-flight refresh is superseded by a workspace rebind, removal, explicit re-refresh, or owner shutdown, its slot is released immediately so replacement work is not blocked; queued entries that are superseded while waiting exit before calling `prepareGitHubPublicationFact`.

## Evidence

- Added unit test `serializes config-triggered refresh waves and skips superseded entries` in `src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts` warming 200 remembered sessions, triggering `sessionChanges.emit({ all: true, scope: "config" })`, and verifying:
  - `maxInFlight === 1` across the entire 200-session refresh wave.
  - A session (`wave-1`) superseded by `wave-1-next` while waiting in the serialized queue is skipped without invoking `prepareGitHubPublicationFact` for the stale `wave-1` entry.
- Verified all existing tests in `src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts` continue to pass (including synchronous single-session wake behavior, removed-binding revocation, and workspace rebind replacement).

prs.title: fix(browser): name both accepted upload sources when a path matches neither root
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes [#197015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197015): `browser` `action:"upload"` rejects a path outside both managed upload roots with only the inbound-media error (`Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (~/.openclaw/media/inbound)`). The message suggests only chat attachments can be uploaded and hides the fact that a file staged under `<tmp>/uploads` is also accepted, so an agent that generated a file has no hint of the working recovery path.

`resolveUploadPaths` (`extensions/browser/src/browser/paths.ts`) already tries the uploads directory first and then the inbound media root, but when both checks failed it returned only the inbound error.

## Solution

When the inbound media check also fails, append guidance naming the uploads directory as the other accepted source:

```
<inbound error>. Uploads must be placed in the uploads directory (<tmp>/uploads) or reference a direct inbound media file
```

No permission surface changes; the same two roots remain the only accepted sources.

## Evidence

### Regression test (real tool dispatch)

`browser-tool.upload-rejection.test.ts` drives the shipped `createBrowserTool().execute("upload", …)` path with a file matching neither managed root. No browser, node, or gateway mock is involved; `resolveExistingUploadPaths` runs for real, so the thrown error is exactly what an agent sees in production.

- GREEN (this PR): the test passes — the real error names both sources.
- RED (pre-fix resolver): the same test fails — the real error names only the inbound directory and contains no "uploads directory".

The full `paths.test.ts` suite (which covers the resolver fixture matrix, including the outside-root rejection) and the new real-dispatch test pass together (13/13); related `browser-proxy-upload.test.ts` and `pw-tools-core.upload-paths.test.ts` also pass (34/34 total).

- `tsc --noEmit -p extensions/tsconfig.json`: 0 errors in the changed files (1951 pre-existing errors are all in other extensions).
- `node scripts/run-format.mts` clean; `git diff --check` clean.

Closes #197015
### Real behavior proof — shipped CLI entry point (RED → GREEN)

Executed through the **shipped CLI** (`openclaw browser upload <paths...>`), the real product entry point, with the checkout's browser plugin loaded — no mocks, no test harness, no helper invocation.

**GREEN (this PR's head, `openclaw browser upload /tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf`):**
```
$ openclaw browser upload /tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf
Error: Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (/home/0668000622/.openclaw/media/inbound). Uploads must be placed in the uploads directory (/tmp/openclaw/uploads) or reference a direct inbound media file
```

**RED (same CLI command against the pre-fix resolver):**
```
$ openclaw browser upload /tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf
Error: Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (/home/0668000622/.openclaw/media/inbound)
```

The CLI upload action (`extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.ts:311`) calls `resolveExistingUploadPaths` before any gateway or file-chooser hook, so this is the exact production path a user hits. The error message now names **both** accepted sources — the uploads directory (`/tmp/openclaw/uploads`) **and** direct inbound media (`media/inbound`) — fixing #197015's complaint that the message hid the uploads root. Output contains no IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints.
