prs.title: fix(discord): render agent message edits like sends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord `edit` (message tool `action: "edit"` and `openclaw message edit --channel discord`) PATCHes agent-authored content verbatim, while `send` of the same text runs through `prepareDiscordOutboundText`. An edited message therefore renders differently from the message it replaces:

- Markdown tables stay raw pipe text instead of the configured `markdown.tables` mode (Discord default: fenced `code` block).
- CommonMark `__bold__` reaches Discord unchanged, where `__x__` means underline; sends normalize it to `**x**`.
- `channels.discord.mentionAliases` handles (`@alice`) stay plain text instead of `<@id>`.

Tracking issue: #190479. Prior source PR #190018 was closed in favor of that issue with the defect still on main.

## User Impact

Agents that send a status table and later edit it with updated values no longer leave broken raw tables (or underline/broken mentions) in the channel. Edits and sends of the same text now match.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route only the non-`progressSnapshot` edit branch through the same `prepareDiscordOutboundText(...).textWithMentions` path already used by `sendMessageDiscord` and `sendWebhookMessageDiscord`. Progress snapshots stay on the compositor path with inert mentions.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI `openclaw message edit` (Gateway-owned Discord edit) against a local Discord REST loopback

Environment (synthetic only, no real Discord credentials):

- Isolated Gateway `ws://127.0.0.1:18901` (token auth, proof config/state under `/tmp`), Discord REST base `http://127.0.0.1:36557/api/v10`.
- Same edit input on both runs (table + standalone bold + alias):

```text
| svc | state |
| --- | ----- |
| api | up    |

**bold** and ping @alice
```

`channels.discord.mentionAliases.alice` → `123456789012345678`.

**Before (main source, this PR's base behavior):** CLI succeeded; loopback captured `PATCH /channels/222222222222222222/messages/555555555555555555` with **verbatim** content:

```json
{"content":"| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n\n**bold** and ping @alice"}
```

Raw pipes (no code fence), unresolved `@alice`.

**After (this branch head `81a94379e2f`):** same CLI command; loopback captured PATCH with **send-parity** content:

```json
{"content":"```\n| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n```\n\n**bold** and ping <@123456789012345678>"}
```

Fenced table, alias expanded to `<@123456789012345678>`, bold left as Discord-native `**bold**`. CLI result `handledBy: "plugin"`, `action: "edit"`.

### Red / green regression (production path)

- `message-bodies.test.ts` case `edits agent content with the same outbound rendering as send`: fails when the source fix is reverted (edit keeps raw table / `@alice`); passes with the fix (edit body equals send body).
- Local: `vitest.extension-discord` on `message-bodies.test.ts`, `runtime.test.ts`, `handle-action.test.ts` — 185 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on both changed files.


### Discord message-surface rendering of the exact PATCH bodies (sanitized)

No live guild or real bot token was used. The image below renders the **exact** before/after PATCH `content` strings captured from the shipped CLI run above, in Discord-style message chrome (raw pipes vs fenced table; unresolved `@alice` vs mention chip for `123456789012345678`).

**Before / After**

![Discord before/after PATCH rendering](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f29ebc8-3f3c-40f5-9be0-0e3c61416b9b)

### Review findings addressed

- Patch quality: no findings; production change is one non-progress branch (+16/−5) plus the regression test (+22).

## Merge Danger

- Narrow: 2 files, one production branch (non-progress edit only).
- Snapshot/progress edit path intentionally unchanged.
- No schema, config, or public API changes.
- Discord Gateway websocket identity is not required for the REST PATCH path exercised above; proof loopback is synthetic and contains no real tokens or guild IDs.

prs.title: fix(doctor): name the pending state migration and its database instead of a redacted refusal
prs.body:
Related: #172897

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` reports a required, routine database migration as a redacted refusal, so the operator sees `Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue` and `Failing check session-entry-state (step-refused): OpenClaw agent database [redacted-path]` with no cause, no database and no next step when the state dir was written by an older release (for example 2026.10.10, agent schema 27).

## User Impact

User impact: a read-only `doctor` run against a state dir with pending migrations now says the migration is pending, names the operator's database in home-relative form (`~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`), prints both schema versions, and tells the operator to run `openclaw doctor --fix`. The exit status is unchanged (still non-zero, because this run does not apply the migration), and `doctor --json`, health warnings and persisted failure facts keep the existing path redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal text was rendered from the failure facts, which are deliberately produced by the support-report redactor. That redactor replaces a pathname **and the rest of its line**, and this reason begins with its path, so `OpenClaw agent database <path> uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix ...` reached the terminal as `OpenClaw agent database [redacted-path]`.

Doctor's terminal detail now comes from the same step receipts with local formatting: secrets are still redacted, paths are labelled instead of removed (`~`, or `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` when the state dir is outside the home directory), and the line is bounded. The persisted facts are untouched, so shareable reports keep their current behavior.

The session-entry-state inspection also records `refusal.code: "state-migration-pending"` when the failure is a `StartupMaintenanceRequiredError` for a migration `--fix` can apply (a schema newer than this build stays a hard refusal). That code drives the new summary line and is mapped to `state-migration-failed` in update run causes, so update reports classify the same as before.

## Evidence

Same source checkout, same copy of a 2026.10.10 state dir (agent schema 27, shared state schema 22), only the patch differs.

Before (this branch's `upstream/main` base, patch stashed):

```text
$ pnpm openclaw --profile mig3before doctor
...
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue. Resolve the reported migration failure before retrying. Later repairs were not run.
Failing check session-entry-state (step-refused): OpenClaw agent database [redacted-path]
EXIT=1
```

After (same state, patch applied):

```text
$ pnpm openclaw --profile mig3src doctor
...
Doctor found pending state migrations. Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the same state/config to complete them; later repairs were not run.
Failing check session-entry-state (state-migration-pending): OpenClaw agent database ~/.openclaw-mig3src/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 42 before using it.
EXIT=1
```

The released `2026.11.5-beta.4` prints the same old message with `[redacted-path]` for the same state, so the symptom is not specific to this checkout's schema version.

Focused regression test `src/commands/doctor-session-entry-state.pending-migration.test.ts` (old-schema agent database, read-only repair) fails on the base with the old message and passes with the patch:

```text
$ pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-entry-state.pending-migration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 ✓ names the pending agent schema migration instead of a redacted refusal
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

Related suites, all passing: `state-migrations.schema-diagnostics`, `state-migrations.blocked-receipts`, `state-migrations.agent-owner-guidance`, `doctor-session-entry-state`, `doctor-session-entry-state.update-capacity`, `doctor-session-transcripts`, `doctor-config-preflight.container-upgrade`, `doctor-update-refusal`, `doctor-maintenance.migration-refusal`, `doctor-health.migration-refusal`, `doctor-health.update`, `doctor.refuses-newer-database-schemas.e2e`, `gateway/server-startup-schema-refusal`, `update-run-cause`.

`pnpm format:check` passes, and `pnpm check:changed` (dead-export lane skipped) passes format, changed-file lint, core and core-test typecheck, and the changed test.

Not verified: Windows path labelling, PostgreSQL agent stores, and the separate `doctor --json` exit-code mismatch reported alongside this bug (deliberately not touched here). Running `pnpm lint` across the whole tree reports pre-existing `max-lines` errors in unrelated files; the changed-file lint lane is green.

prs.title: fix(plugins): prevent SDK replies from using retired runtime state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SDK reply dispatch reaching a retired state-database factory when a native SDK module survives replacement of its calling runtime graph.

## User Impact

Reply operations stay with the host that admitted them. Fresh hosts can dispatch replies, while calls retained from a closed host remain rejected. Public SDK signatures, lazy exports, and the shipped standalone path are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing SDK resource host captures the whole lazy ACP/provider dispatch operation, including shared-state admission. Admission and execution therefore share one lifetime. Buffered and plain provider dispatch use one light guarded facade and sanitizer. The runtime-channel duplicate binder is removed.

The private ACP implementation has a distinct core export. Canonical abort, typing, cron, session, and reply-option type owners remove the circular static graph without changing capability validation or runtime bodies. Database lifecycle guards, schemas, configuration, and public operation identities are unchanged.

The native GitHub PR file inventory reports production +418/-277 (net +141, 35 files) and tests +409/-29 (13 files). The production growth implements the per-host captured operation capability and shared lifetime boundary, replacing duplicate dispatch binding and sanitization.

## Evidence

Signed candidate: `b00e62f842843e50211eb3058e05481db372f154`, tree `09e7c4db9a74bc5425a3136aec9010e1f098a98b`. The native workflow integrated only frozen required-CI base `8862ffc735fe6f5e553a69ea2fb7731a6b90fd87` at signed anchor `d4bb8fb2e9b03ee88adc080e33786df25aa8a845`; its tree exactly matches the previously executed CI merge. <details>

Two broader checkers retain historical raw failure receipts, with identical results on the complete frozen base `7ecd67ccfd51e2c5aa6673809b69fb318235dd0a` and candidate `26e88564f23556afbbbdc46882741d1b4a994560`. prs.title: docs: add an Agents and Templates guide
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The docs cover agents and Templates only through reference pages (`concepts/agent`, `concepts/agent-workspace`, `concepts/multi-agent`, `cli/agents`, `cli/templates`). Nothing says when a job deserves its own agent, or why you would package an agent as a Template.

## User Impact

Readers get a short guide, readable in two or three minutes, as the first page of the Agents tab. It explains when to make a new agent, what defines the agent's job, how to package the agent as a Template, and how to start from someone else's Template. Docs only; no runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New page `docs/concepts/agents-and-templates.md`, with the frontmatter neighbouring pages use (`summary`, `read_when`, `title`) and these sections: When to make a new agent, Give the agent its job, Package it as a Template, Start from someone else's Template, Related.
- Navigation: the page is the first entry of the Agents tab. The tab has no group named "Agents", so it sits at the top of the tab's first group ("Agent runtime") and becomes the tab's landing page.
- One link each from Getting started (Related), the Templates CLI reference (See also), and Multi-agent routing, where a short paragraph notes that a second agent can be for a separate job and not only a separate person, persona, or channel account.
- The page says Templates must be enabled in **Settings → Labs** (or `gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates` on a headless installation).

Left out on purpose:

- Specific published Templates. The page points readers to **Pages → Templates** and ClawHub instead of naming packages.
- The team preset and coordinator material, which stays on Multi-agent routing.
- Translated docs. `docs/AGENTS.md` says translations are generated in `openclaw/docs`, so only the English source changes here.

## Evidence

**Statements checked against current docs and source**

| Statement in the guide | Checked against |
| --- | --- |
| An agent has its own workspace, instructions, memory files, and sessions; OpenClaw starts with one agent | `docs/concepts/multi-agent.md`, `docs/concepts/memory.md` |
| **Create new agent** in the agent selector; `openclaw agents add <id> --workspace <dir>` | `docs/web/control-ui.md`, `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-agent-creation.ts`, `openclaw agents add --help` |
| `AGENTS.md` and `SOUL.md` roles; workspace `skills/` is visible only to that agent | `docs/concepts/agent-workspace.md`, `docs/tools/skills.md` |
| Plugins and MCP servers are Gateway-level and shared; per-agent tool policy can restrict them | `docs/cli/templates.md`, `docs/tools/mcp.md`, `docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md` |
| `openclaw automations create "<cron>" "<message>" --name --agent`; the agent can offer to promote a repeated job | `docs/cli/cron.md`, `docs/automation/cron-jobs/how-it-works.md`, `openclaw automations create --help` |
| What a Template can include, what stays out, the "create a new template from this agent" flow, read-only review, `clawhub login`, Publish, Pending and Published states | `docs/cli/templates.md`, `skills/create-template/SKILL.md`, `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-template-creator.ts` |
| Labs switch, **Pages → Templates**, Add is one-way and creates an ordinary agent, **Add** has no confirmation step, flagged Templates need confirmation, `--dry-run --json` preview, first reply lists remaining setup | `docs/cli/templates.md`, `docs/web/control-ui.md`, `docs/web/control-ui/settings.md`, `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`, `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-templates.ts` |

**Checks run on this branch**

- `pnpm docs:list`: lists `concepts/agents-and-templates.md` with its summary and read-when hints.
- `pnpm check:docs` (the CI docs gate): passed. That covers `format:docs:check`, `lint:docs`, `lint:templates`, `docs:check-mdx` (1,444 files), `docs:check-links` (16,797 internal links, 0 broken), `docs:check-config-examples`, and `changelog:check`.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports 14 broken fragments locally, none in files this change touches (they are in a stale local ClawHub mirror, `releases/2026.10.1.md`, and `tools/acp-agents-setup`). The new `/cli/templates#author-locally` link resolves.
- `pnpm docs:dev -- --page concepts/agents-and-templates --build-only` against `openclaw/docs` main: built, and the page was inspected in a browser at desktop and phone widths.

**Before and after: Agents tab navigation (first group)**

```text
Before (main)                      After (this branch)
Agent runtime:                     Agent runtime:
  concepts/architecture              concepts/agents-and-templates
  concepts/agent                     concepts/architecture
  concepts/agent-loop                concepts/agent
  ...                                concepts/agent-loop
                                     ...
```

In a preview built from `main`, `/concepts/agents-and-templates/` returns 404. Screenshots from the local preview follow: the Agents tab before, the Agents tab after, and the rendered page.

Related: #199909

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `check-lint-core-2` fails on `main`, and on every pull request whose lint lanes include `src/agents`, since #199909 merged.

## User Impact

User impact: none. No runtime behavior changes. Contributors stop getting a red `openclaw/ci-gate` from a lint error in a file their change does not touch.

## Why This Change Was Made

#199909 snapshots MCP catalog metadata with `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` on purpose: the comment above the line says the JSON round trip drops `undefined` members that are not valid JSON. `structuredClone` would keep those members, so applying the lint rule's suggested fix would undo the change. This adds the suppression the repository already uses for the same situation (for example in `extensions/deep-research/src/job-state.ts`), with the reason stated on the line.

Before, on unmodified `main` at `59b74af7e1ae`:

prs.title: fix(searxng): bound preflight DNS by the search deadline
prs.body:
Fixes #199063

## What Problem This Solves

A canceled SearXNG search can keep waiting on preliminary endpoint DNS. Its configured timeout starts only after that wait, so even a one-second search budget does not bound a stalled lookup. The same preliminary validation also runs before returning cached results.

## Changes

Use the existing request-deadline pattern already implemented for Brave in #132097:

- Start one timeout combined with the caller's signal before endpoint classification.
- Pass it through both HTTP private-network validation and HTTPS pinned DNS classification. Preserve cancellation instead of treating it as an ordinary classification failure.
- Keep that signal through HTTP, body consumption, category fallback and cache publication; always clean up the timer.

Endpoint trust policy, configuration defaults and response/cache formats stay the same. The shared resolver already supports an interruptible wait, so no new resolver, SDK export or dependency is needed. The underlying OS lookup can finish later; its completion does not resume a canceled request.

## Evidence

### Native provider entry point and HTTP control

Ran five isolated cases on the base and five on the fix through `createSearxngWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, with real Node timers/signals and the production validator/resolver/guarded-fetch code. Only the Node lookup for a synthetic endpoint was held. The successful control used an actual loopback HTTP server. macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 26.12.1; no model calls or external network access.

| Case | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP DNS held, caller canceled | Still pending 250 ms after abort | Rejects with the exact caller reason before DNS release |
| HTTPS DNS held, caller canceled | Still pending 250 ms after abort | Rejects with the exact caller reason before DNS release |
| HTTP DNS held, one-second budget | Still pending 1.4 s after DNS starts | `TimeoutError` before DNS release |
| HTTPS DNS held, one-second budget | Still pending 1.4 s after DNS starts | `TimeoutError` before DNS release |
| HTTP DNS resolves normally | One result, one HTTP request | One result, one HTTP request |

All four stopped cases issued **zero HTTP requests**, including after releasing DNS for cleanup. The control exercised the real request/response path in both versions. These observations concern the DNS wait, distinct from the already-fixed in-flight HTTP cancellation in #104216 and configured defaults in #173467.

prs.title: fix(android): preserve notifications posted in the same millisecond
prs.body:
Fixes #199084

## What Problem This Solves

Distinct Android `system.notify` requests posted in the same millisecond replace
one another. Both requests succeed, but only the later alert remains visible.

## User Impact

Independently requested alerts keep separate entries in the notification drawer.
Existing permission, channel, text-rendering and tap behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a fresh notification tag for each post instead of deriving its identity from
the wall clock. Android already owns the `(tag, id)` identity and dismissal uses
the full notification key, so this needs no persistent counter or new permission.

## Evidence

The regression calls the production `SystemHandler` twice, using separate handler
instances and different bodies while Robolectric's clock stays fixed. On base,
both commands succeed but only `second` remains; with this change both remain.
The clock assertion passes before checking notification contents.

- Base: 12 existing handler tests pass; the new regression fails with
  `expected:<[first, second]> but was:<[second]>`.
- Fix: all 30 focused tests pass across Play and ThirdParty Debug, including
  existing permission/channel rejection, tap intent and multiline-body controls.
- Main/test Kotlin formatting and Android lint for both variants pass.

Executed on macOS arm64, JDK 21, using Robolectric 4.17/API 34. This is JVM
validation of the Android posting owner; physical-device delivery remains the
independent confirmation point.

```sh
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SystemHandlerTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SystemNotificationBodyTest \
  :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SystemHandlerTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SystemNotificationBodyTest
./gradlew :app:ktlintMainSourceSetCheck :app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck \
  :app:lintPlayDebug :app:lintThirdPartyDebug
```

### Independent review focus

On a paired Android node with notifications enabled, send a short burst of
`system.notify` requests with distinct bodies, confirm separate drawer entries,
and check that tapping opens the app and dismissing one leaves the other entries.
Then block the selected notification channel and confirm the existing refusal.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop pending Gateway reads on Ctrl-C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupting a pending read-only Gateway request can leave the CLI connection running until its timeout and print a late timeout report.

## User Impact

Audited read-only calls now inherit the command's cancellation signal without each command forwarding it. Explicit cancellation, writes, node invocations and callback-owned streams keep their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway call read classification now lives at `callGatewayCli`, below both shared CLI RPC facades and their transport/authentication wrappers. It applies before the explicit-scopes branch, so administrative reads are covered too. The classifier follows actual handler behavior, not authorization scopes: `operator.read` also covers mutations. `device.pair.code` is a read only without a decision or request ID; approval/rejection still keeps its receipt.

Removed the forwarding-only cron read wrapper and redundant Gateway, library, users and system signal forwarding. Existing cancellation/publication guards remain. Node diagnostics retains its explicit signal because an authentication fallback deliberately uses backend identity; join-code retains its existing explicit cancellation because it creates a shortcode.

Supersedes the shared read portions of closed #195106, #197970 and #198723. This does not cover #197802 (post-commit publication wait), #198314/#198339 (batch mutation custody), #199436 (secret resolution/fallback), #197327 (local secret processes), #197502 (local MCP processes), #198203 (update inspection scope), or #199623 (deep security probe).

## Evidence

Built Node CLI comparison on base `ef8d709a05a3` (`ocx base`, runtime artifact) and final head `d0e137541658` (`ocx build --dts`). Each read command ran twice against naturally pending `wss://192.0.2.1:21937`, with isolated HOME/state and SIGINT sent directly to the observed CLI PID. prs.title: fix(state): bound startup upgrade copies and pruning to owned state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes startup upgrades copying and pruning unrelated bulk state, sharing SQLite extents with preserved originals, and overwriting uncopied workspace files with Doctor templates.

## User Impact

Large installations copy only migration inputs and get an explicit space check and copy progress. SQLite copies use read/write file handles, with NOCOW directory preparation on btrfs; quiescent WAL/journal content is recovered privately. Uncopied live files remain unchanged with a warning.

Retired startup-migration backups, SQLite `.bak` files, and media-persistence recovery images are deliberately retained, with observed counts and bytes in the upgrade report and log. Their deletion belongs to the operator or Doctor: deleting large shared clones synchronously during startup can stall a CoW filesystem. Older unpinned `.pre-<version>` generations are pruned only beside files this upgrade publishes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is follow-up hardening of feature owner @obviyus's copy-and-swap design in #198389 (ef930ebbad77), alongside #199847. It retains the durable plan, crash recovery, migration chain/generic fallback, pinning, config-admission refusal, and publication boundary.

A large btrfs installation has 81 GB and 26 GB NOCOW databases alongside approximately 3.4 TB of managed worktrees (about 1,300 subvolumes). Reflink sharing forces CoW on subsequent database writes despite NOCOW; observed filesystem commits stalled for 8–18 seconds and queued database writes for up to 14 seconds. The original upgrade would copy unrelated trees and synchronously delete large operator recovery images during startup.

The copy now excludes default/configured worktrees and agent workspaces, nested mount/subvolume boundaries, Knowledge, browser profiles, backups, caches, and media payloads. Legacy outgoing-media record JSON remains because Doctor still imports it; legacy session, push, identity, device, credential, exec-approval, audit, config, and extension inputs remain. Ancillary SQLite families above 64 MiB are omitted; outdated targets and shared state are always included. The cutoff keeps small legacy stores available without copying large current databases or archives. Space accounting includes ordinary files because FICLONE may fall back to byte copying, plus an equal-sized scratch margin of at least 256 MiB.

Production delta: +284 lines (403 added, 119 removed). The necessary growth is the bounded inventory, byte-copy and space/progress handling; recursive whole-tree pruning was removed.

A required database inside a nested mount or subvolume is refused before any copy, with nothing live changed: the swap publishes by rename, which cannot cross filesystem or subvolume boundaries. NOCOW directory preparation is a performance policy and stays best-effort, so a btrfs host without `chattr` still upgrades (with a warning).

Pruning no longer recursively walks the live tree. It uses the swap's file ownership, preserves pins, and never deletes retired recovery artifacts. Replacements require copy-baseline membership in both chain and fallback paths; adds require an absent live path.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced on the base: `diffTree` incorrectly emitted `replace:workspace/AGENTS.md` for an uncopied live workspace file. The focused test passes with the fix.
- Focused tests: 37 passed across `src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts` and `src/state/sqlite-copy-swap.test.ts`. Covers scope, retained recovery count/bytes, old-generation pruning, exact space refusal before copy, SQLite file-handle/NOCOW ordering, and committed WAL recovery without source changes.
- Changed-file oxfmt and type-aware lint passed. Exact-head [CI run 43801195156](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43801195156) completed on `57bf41e57a51f7d20d0034404504df5808ebf995`. All executed test/type jobs and the repaired baseline/import-closure checks passed; CI is **not green** because `check-lint-core-2` fails on the inherited `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone` error at `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118` ([exact-head job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43801195156/job/133083583363)), which also fails the aggregate gate.
- CI found two lane defects, now fixed: the extracted worktree resolver was missing from the PR wrapper inventory, and config parsing used a new raw assertion instead of the existing coercion owner. Both failed import-closure tests and all seven affected state-upgrade tests pass locally after repair. Prior-head CI also found an inherited `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone` error at `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118` ([job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43799836820/job/133078761753)); the same code was verified on fetched main. The final exact-head log confirms the identical inherited error. No failed CI jobs were rerun.
- Synthetic 2 GiB SQLite file with unused trailing pages: buffered byte copy took 0.7 seconds, 3,283 MB/s locally. This is a local copy timing, not btrfs or fsync performance evidence.
- Populated prior-release Gateway E2E: all six fixtures passed (2026.7.1, 2026.7.1-blob, 2026.7.35, 2026.8.35, 2026.9.37, 2026.10.10), plus two forced-fallback cases and config refusal. The full existing seven-case run passed cleanly, then the two newly added July cases passed separately with unchanged production code. An earlier attempt passed its assertions but was rejected by the source-change guard; it was discarded and rerun.
- No production access, deployment, schema bump, new configuration, or new environment controls. Native btrfs extent behavior is not measured locally; the file-handle and directory-policy boundary is tested without requiring btrfs.

Source evidence for exclusions: `state-migrations.doctor.ts` and `state-migrations.doctor-discovery.ts` migrate managed-worktree registry rows, not checkout trees; `state-migrations.managed-outgoing-images.ts` imports `media/outgoing/records`, with payload retention outside the copy; Knowledge's `doctor-contract-api.ts` only normalizes configuration, with its store root owned by `extensions/knowledge/src/stores.ts`; browser profiles are owned by `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`, outside the core migration chain. Workspace paths use the canonical agent resolvers and remain outside the existing startup copy contract. State-relative `backups`, `cache`, `locks`, and `tmp` are absent from the core step/source inventory in `state-migrations.doctor.ts`; nested filesystem boundaries are excluded during inventory before descending. Logs and installed extensions are retained because their migration/import ownership is broader than a simple root exclusion.

- Follow-up commit 8b7ccff5: NOCOW preparation failures warn instead of aborting the copy; new focused test, 38 focused tests passed locally.

prs.title: docs(release): avoid per-commit fetches during closeout audits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release closeout audits can spend minutes fetching historical blobs one commit at a time in partial clones. This documents a bounded alternative for the RRI691 release-ledger finding.

## User Impact

No runtime or end-user behavior changes. Release operators get a pinned, metadata-first audit procedure that avoids implicit per-commit network reads without treating a file inventory as a completed semantic review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing closeout guide says to audit the release branch but does not explain how to do so on `blob:none`. The new section separates pinned commit/parent inventories, explicit bounded missing-blob acquisition through existing Git ownership, and no-lazy content review. It retains deletions and intermediate changes, covers merge parents, and requires semantic comparison against pinned main. No new script, state store, configuration, schema, permission, or publication behavior is introduced.

## Evidence

- Refreshed main at `2159567b9ffc17a770579d7e6487836789c67be5` and checked open PRs for RRI691 and related closeout/lazy-fetch terms; no matching repair found.
- Synthetic disposable `file://` partial clones on Git 2.53.0, six release-only commits including modification, deletion, rename, transient add/delete, and a merge: ordinary per-commit patch reads grew promisor packs from **1 to 6**.
- Pinned metadata inventory made **zero fetches**, retained deletions and intermediate versions, and identified eight missing blob OIDs. A no-lazy content read failed visibly (exit 128) before acquisition. One explicit batch fetched all eight; packs grew **1 to 2** and stayed at two during offline patch reads.
- Executed both documented shell blocks from the Markdown in a fresh clone. All per-parent patches matched the complete source repository with network protocols disabled. Local refs, Git config, and `FETCH_HEAD` were unchanged by acquisition. Relative documentation link/anchor verified.
- `pnpm docs:list` and `git diff --check`: passed. Independent documentation review approved with no blocking findings and independently confirmed offline per-parent patch equality.
- Simplification pass retained one canonical guidance section and link; no production or test code added.
- Initial targeted MDX validation could not start because the task worktree lacked installed dependencies; no shared installation was changed. Repository local-review automation was not run; the review evidence above is the independent documentation review.
- CI run `43798701397`, `check-docs` job `133073709312`, exposed a canonical formatting failure in the changed guide. The parent maintainer reproduced `pnpm format:check` failing, applied canonical `pnpm format`, and verified the format check passing. Repair commit `f049c7780b2cb3023fbf2728162651cb6041b3fb` adds only two blank lines between list items; command blocks and prose are unchanged. The publication owner inspected that exact diff and confirmed `git diff --check` passes. This does not claim the replacement-head CI has completed.

This is an operator-time guidance repair, not a runtime fix or a claimed recreation of the historical 35-minute duration. The fixture used a local promisor server; production network latency, GitHub transport, and batches above 1,024 OIDs were not exercised. The incident text was verified through authorized GitHub API access; the independent reviewer could not access that private source.

## What Problem This Solves

Release preflight told operators to run an isolated npm token probe, but no standalone repository-token probe workflow exists. Both the package-specific bootstrap warning and the token-liveness warning pointed toward unsupported remediation, and the linked release guides repeated it.

## User Impact

Operators now receive an explicit handoff to the repository NPM_TOKEN credential owner for credential readiness and scope/package-creation access. Token liveness remains unverified by preflight; a local login or secret update timestamp is not proof for the actual repository token.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the two diagnostic instructions and their two linked guidance locations with the currently supported owner handoff. Preserve reconciliation of recent publication, bootstrap eligibility, and all existing package/artifact/parent/runtime authorization checks. No workflow, credential retrieval, permissions, publication behavior, or schema is added or changed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `2159567b9ffc17a770579d7e6487836789c67be5`: a synthetic registry 404 flows through the real npm state observer, publication preflight, and report formatter and emits the nonexistent-probe instruction. The new regression fails on the base for that diagnostic, then passes with the repair.
- Preflight, registry-state, and interface suites: **35/35 passed** (8 + 21 + 6), 1.79 seconds combined wrapper wall time. Changed preflight file: 24 ms test time. Hosted CI seconds not available before publication.
- Tooling-test and scripts typechecks, targeted lint, five-file formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation link targets and the retained bootstrap anchor were checked.
- `pr-simplify`: production change is two existing diagnostic strings (zero net lines); one regression covers both warning paths via the real observer and formatter. No new helper, option, export, or test-only production seam.
- Independent narrative review found no actionable correctness or regression issues in the final five-file diff and inspected the unchanged artifact, OIDC, and protected bootstrap routes. The reviewer did not independently rerun tests; the author completed the type/lint checks successfully. Local ClawSweeper/Codex and the bound autoreview route are unavailable; no helper-owned scoped-clean claim is made.

Proof is credential-free and Linux-local. GitHub observations and package inventory are fixture-backed; no repository token was read or authenticated, and no workflow or publication was dispatched. This repairs guidance, not token liveness verification.

prs.title: fix(workboard): dashboard board widget shows the board id and "Default agent" instead of names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Workboard board widget on a dashboard shows the board id (for example `peter-tasks`) instead of the board's name, and its cards say "Default agent" instead of the agent's name, while the Workboard page shows "Product Operations" and "Molty" for the same board and cards.

## User Impact

User impact: Workboard widgets on dashboards use the same board and agent names as the Workboard page and sidebar. The summary widget header gets the same board-name fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The widget headers printed the raw `boardId` prop, and the board widget passed no agents list to the shared card renderer, so every card fell back to the generic label. The widgets now:

- name the board through `workboardBoardName`, the helper the sidebar and page title already use, from the boards list the widget already loads with its cards;
- build the agents list from the host roster through `workboardAgentsList`, a helper extracted from the Workboard page so the page and widget share one builder;
- the widget runtime also redraws when the agent roster first arrives (its default agent id changes), so a cold start where the cards load before the roster no longer leaves "Default agent" in place.

Accepted edge case: later roster edits alone (renaming an agent) show in the widget on the next Workboard change. Detecting them would mean cloning the roster on every host notification.

## Evidence

Reproduced in the Control UI mock (`--fixture workboard`, "Product operations dashboard"), before and after this change:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Board widget before: header peter-tasks, card says Default agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9108ff72-9aa7-4f88-a385-21dbe6aa9be7) | ![Board widget after: header Product Operations, card says Molty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/069bdefa-d6c8-44df-983a-3b1337f1f9e3) |

- New regression test in `extensions/workboard/browser/widgets/runtime.test.ts` checks the board widget header, summary widget header, and the card agent label when the roster arrives after the cards. It fails on `main` (header `ops` instead of `Product Operations`), fails with the widget given no agents list, and fails without the roster redraw; it passes with the fix.
- `vitest run extensions/workboard/browser`: 35 files, 275 tests passed.
- oxlint (type-aware, `tsconfig.extensions.json`) and oxfmt clean on the touched files; `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.

Not covered: the card widget still shows the raw agent id for assigned cards (separate follow-up if wanted).

prs.title: fix(release): retry timed-out plugin source fetches
prs.body:
Related: #133368

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin npm preflight and publication jobs failing immediately when their exact-source Git fetch times out transiently.

## User Impact

Release operators can recover from a transient fetch timeout within the existing job instead of restarting the publication workflow. Fetch attempts remain bounded; no publication is retried by this change. There is no installed-product behavior change or required migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both source-manifest read steps now use the existing Git owner’s retry-capable fetch operation. It preserves the selected immutable SHA, depth-one/blobless fetching, subprocess cleanup, and cancellation behavior, with up to three attempts and a five-second backoff. The manifest read remains outside the retry. The currently pinned action already supports this operation; no action pin or ownership policy changes are needed.

This is a maintainer-directed release-tooling repair. The change removes 20 production lines and adds 19 regression-test lines, without another retry implementation or test-only production seam.

## Evidence

- **Red:** both workflow-entry regression cases failed against unchanged production with exit **124** and no manifest output after the first stalled fetch.
- **Green:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-release-git-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **47/47 passed**, 28.00 seconds in Vitest / 28.85 seconds wrapper wall time. Hosted CI time is not yet measured.
- The regression executes the actual YAML/Python policy entry points with a stalled first fetch followed by success, checks both attempts retain the same SHA, and requires one successful manifest read. Shared fixture assertions check descendant cleanup before subsequent operations and preservation of preexisting locks.
- Passed targeted root-scripts typecheck, changed-test lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check-workflows.mts` (including actionlint and zizmor).
- Fresh native independent source review found no P0–P2 findings on the complete two-file diff based on `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a`, including direct inspection of the pinned action’s fetch/export contract. Hosted fallback review remains pending.**

**Proof limits:** controlled Git subprocess I/O, virtual fetch deadlines/backoff, and accelerated TERM escalation; the harness uses the current local owner, with pinned-owner compatibility source-inspected. No live GitHub fetch, remote workflow dispatch, OIDC, or publication was performed.

prs.title: feat(update): run Git checkout installs from releases behind the release link
prs.body:
## Problem

A Git checkout install runs its Gateway from `<checkout>/dist/index.js`, and `openclaw update` rewrites that same tree. Everything around the rewrite exists to survive it: the updater copies its own runtime first (133–892 s on a 183k-file checkout), builds the candidate in a private repository and imports it through a pack (256 MB cap), stops and parks the serving Gateway, and rewrites the service definition every update.

## Change

Extends #198835's linked package root to Git checkouts, per the #197949 design. Stacked on #198835: the base `stack/update-linked-package-root` is #198835's head `567a560a`, which already contains #198389. It uses #198835's resolver, link switch, leases and 24 h collection unchanged.

- **Layout.** `<stateDir>/git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw -> releases/<id>/lib/node_modules/openclaw`. Each release is `git worktree add --detach` off the developer's checkout (shared object store, no clone or copy).
- **Stage.** The existing candidate preflight (candidate walk, local-commit replay, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, build, candidate checks) runs in the new release's worktree, then `--version` with the service's Node. A same-source no-op requires the serving release to be at the checkout's commit and its artifacts to verify (#158931).
  - Deviation from the design: the worktree is built at `releases/<id>/build`, then moved into place with `git worktree move`. Node refuses to strip types under `node_modules` (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING`), and the build runs `.mts` scripts. The built tree has no absolute symlinks, so the move is safe.
- **Switch.** `switchPackageReleaseLink` from #198835. The serving Gateway keeps its release (Node resolves the entry's real path), so nothing is stopped, parked or verified before the flip.
- **Restart.** The serving Gateway's maintenance tick sees the link move (installation replacement) and restarts itself into the new release. The updater waits for that successor (up to 90 s), then verifies. It falls back to a native restart only if no successor appears. A native restart from inside the service job (`update.run`) would end the updater itself.
- **Service.** Written once, at conversion, to a frozen launcher `<stateDir>/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`. A unit that names the launcher is never regenerated. The launcher is needed because a release that fails while loading never reaches Gateway code.
- **Trial.** The switch writes `releases/.trial`. The launcher counts starts.
  - After two failed starts it switches the link back and restores `*.pre-<version>` state files (#198389's generation names). Each SQLite family is restored together, and trial-created WAL/journal/SHM/seal files without a preserved predecessor are removed. The launcher mirrors #198389's `companionRemovals` list because it must not load release code.
  - The trial ends when the Gateway's first maintenance tick runs, or when the updater verifies the restarted Gateway. The second path also covers targets that predate this PR.
  - Writes made during a failed trial are lost (approved).
- **The layout never fails an update** (#197949 decision 8). If `releases/` cannot be created, or something other than a release link sits at the package path, the update records a warning and takes the in-place runner. The next update tries the layout again.
- **Post-core work** (requested-channel persistence, plugin convergence) runs in the updater, but only after the restarted release verified and its trial ended. A failed trial therefore never leaves plugins that require the release it switched away from. It runs without Doctor maintenance, which the Gateway holds, and without a plugin cohort, because no core rollback exists to pair it with. If plugins changed, the Gateway is asked to restart again (SIGUSR2). Under `--no-restart` the release is unverified, so only the requested channel is persisted and plugins converge on a later update.
- **The developer's checkout** is never written. The first update builds the commit that serves now as the first release, rewrites the unit once, then stages the target.
- **Retention.** #198835's collection, followed by `git worktree prune`. `git-install` is excluded from backups and from the startup state-upgrade copy. The latter is the same change as #199770, included here so the stack stands alone.
- **One owner.** `usesGitReleases` selects releases. Windows checkouts and package-to-Git switches keep the in-place runner, and the in-place CLI tests are pinned to that runner.

For Git releases this skips:
- runtime retention
- the pack transfer/import
- the managed-service stop/park
- the database rollback capture
- the checkout's source-artifact lock
- the native restart from inside the service job
- per-update service regeneration

## Open decision

Windows Git checkouts and package-to-Git switches still use the in-place runner, so the code above is bypassed on POSIX, not deleted. Prod LOC is net **+769**. Refusing Windows Git updates (option b) would let this PR delete the in-place runner, pack transfer, runtime promotion and Git rollback and go net negative. That decision is pending with the maintainer.

## E2E (mbp-m5, launchd, isolated profiles, shared-clone checkout; ≤15 min per run, ≤3 in parallel)

Rows marked ‡ ran at head `8a720e49`, rows marked † at `6032dedf`; the rest ran at `1140b601`, before plugin convergence moved after verification.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| † First update of a checkout install (conversion, head→head+1) | ok, 402 s wall (two builds, three runs in parallel), longest outage 7.6 s, total 13.1 s (unit rewrite, then a restart after plugin convergence); unit rewritten once to the launcher; checkout tree clean; no retention, pack or handoff steps |
| ‡ Release→release (head+1→head+2) | ok, 180 s wall, one outage of 7.2 s; unit untouched (mtime unchanged since conversion); service runs from `releases/` |
| ‡ `--no-restart` on a switched release | the updater leaves the Gateway running and converges no plugins; within the next maintenance tick the Gateway restarts itself into the release, and the trial is cleared; outage 7.5 s |
| † `update.run` via the Gateway (`openclaw gateway call update.run`) | run `finished|succeeded`, 140 s; link moved; the Gateway restarted itself; unit untouched; outage 7.4 s |
| † Release that crashes on boot | two crashes, the launcher switched back to the previous release, Gateway ready again; the update reports `build-id-mismatch`; longest outage 28.9 s |
| kill -9 mid-stage | link and serving Gateway unchanged; the rerun succeeds; a partial release directory left by the killed run is collected after 24 h |
| kill -9 right after the link moves, before restart | the old Gateway keeps serving; the rerun reports `skipped: already-current`; the Gateway restarts itself into the new release and the trial is cleared |
| `env -i` + `umask 077` (conversion, then release→release) | ok, 376 s and 198 s, outages 5.5 s and 7.5 s; launcher `0700` under umask 077 |
| Install whose unit and state were written by 2026.11.3, moved to head, then converted | ok, 229 s, outage 5.9 s; state DB `integrity_check` ok. 2026.11.3's own updater could not reach head on mbp-m5: it walked back to `already-current` (Node 24.21 below head's `engines`), so that hop was done with `git reset` + `ocx build` |
| Production-shaped install (207,229-file checkout, +3 GB SQLite in state), release→release | ok, 145 s, outage 6.9 s, no retention step. Main was not timed on this host. Peanutto's production main run `90c601fc` took 4,150 s, with 892 s retention and a 300 s outage |

Not exercised: a plugin-only restart (SIGUSR2) after npm plugins actually change; the fixtures have no npm plugins.

## Tests

- `src/infra/git-release.test.ts`:
  - trial fallback restores the SQLite family and drops trial-only companions
  - trial settlement
  - launcher mapping
  - a launcher unit is owned without regeneration
  - a non-link package path falls back to the in-place runner with a reason
- `src/infra/update-runner-git-release.test.ts`:
  - a same-commit release with unverified artifacts is rebuilt
  - a current release is reported prepared, so finalization never regenerates it
  - the first release comes from the serving worktree's commit, and the checkout's different target is still built
- `update-command-post-update.test.ts`: a switched release converges plugins only after its restart.
- `update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`: under `--no-restart`, a switched release persists the channel and leaves plugins alone.
- `update-runner-git-release.test.ts`: a successful rebuild of an incomplete runtime reports the new release's verdict.
- `update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`: release convergence runs in the updater, with no fresh process and no Doctor.
- `update-command-verification.test.ts`:
  - a verified release ends its trial
  - a switched release's Gateway restarts itself without a native restart
- `src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts`: `git-install` stays out of the startup upgrade copy.
- Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint/oxfmt on changed files. On mbp-m5 the broad update suite passes 1,438 / 1,442. The four failures are inherited or environmental:
  - `update-runner-git-node-preflight` ×3: mbp-m5's Node 24.21 is below `engines`.
  - `update-cli.candidate-admission` "blocks package updates when the target requires a newer Node runtime": also fails on the base `567a560a`.

## LOC

prod +786 / −17 (net +769); test +589 / −1.

Draft: lands after #198835. #198389 has merged; #199770 carries the same startup-copy exclusion for main.

prs.title: feat(ui): redesign tool-call rendering, grouping, and lifecycle narration
prs.body:
Tool-call history now separates launches, stops, and confirmed completions from ordinary activity. Consecutive lifecycle events of the same kind share a compact row without rewriting earlier launches with a worker’s later status. Completion rows use recorded execution identities and result-time placement, survive output truncation and reload, and deduplicate repeated collection results. Internal coordination payloads stay out of the main transcript. Stopped-agent names remain available after the child leaves the roster when an earlier confirmed launch records the same execution and session.

Command rows remain muted and truncate to one line; expanded details retain the full command and output. Inline command output continues to follow the existing preference. Image inspection stays separate. Script and shell activity share one Commands summary category. Explicit disclosure choices remain shared between panes, while automatic expansion that preserves a reader’s position stays local to that pane.

Questions retain main’s composer placement. Their width and concise labels remain improved, and ask_user narration is standalone rather than wrapped in another question activity summary. Gateway protocol sources have no diff from the integrated baseline ce49266.

Validation:

- Earlier UI-only follow-up: 90/90 tests passed in 3.64 s. Its changes are limited to UI presentation and the test allocation; the backend at that stage remained at d070dd03.
- Latest placement checks: 32 projection/visibility tests passed in 32.47 s (36.76 s including the runner), and 51 UI/incremental tests passed in 7.70 s.
- Earlier focused checks: 18 persistence-writer tests passed in 31.45 s; 71 rendering/purpose/disclosure tests passed in 2.21 s. The question cut passed 150 UI tests in 6.58 s and 35 ask_user tests in 25.80 s. These overlapping runs are not a cumulative test count.
- Regression checks reproduced lost receipts and incorrect ordering before the fixes. Core/UI type checks, targeted lint, validator generation/check, and final advisory review passed.
- The test-line allocation covers the exact +2,644 net lines: the standard 400-line allowance plus 2,244 allocated lines. Distinct owner contracts cover persistence caps, privacy, chronological placement, search, replay, disclosure, and navigation.

The persistent test Gateway serves UI and runtime 726c42eaf33dc2c98b21a2c8f54993c9300ec3e2. HTML, runtime identity and relevant served bundle bytes were verified; conversations, authentication, model configuration and workspace instructions were preserved. Real flows verified fifteen concurrent launches in one row, completions during parent work and after yielding, replay without duplication, name navigation, retained stop names after child removal, consistent spacing, and questions in the composer.

Six compositions below were refreshed using UI e4e46df; the additional typography comparison uses UI 0f5247c. The other ten compositions and the original before/after comparison retain their earlier capture provenance.

Risk and coverage: broad CI qualification and size-budget work remain with the landing review.

prs.title: fix(gateway): accept parameterized data URLs in chat attachments
prs.body:
Closes #199904

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat.send attachment sent as a data URL with media type parameters (e.g. `data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,...`) fails with `invalid base64 content` when the same bytes without parameters upload fine.

## User Impact

User impact: gateway API and Control UI clients can now attach inline images whose data URLs carry media type parameters (such as `;charset=utf-8`, emitted by some exporters and Windows tooling) instead of having the send fail hard on an otherwise valid URL. Parameterless data URLs behave exactly as before, and payload validation, size limits, and MIME sniffing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attachment normalizer strips a leading `data:...;base64,` header before strict base64 validation, but its regex required `;base64` immediately after a bare media type, so a parameterized header was left in place and `inspectBase64` then rejected the whole string because of the `:`, `;`, and `,` characters. The header pattern now allows media type parameters and matches `;base64` case-insensitively, mirroring the agent image/media tool decoder (`decodeDataUrl`, #195652); the payload still flows through the unchanged strict base64 validation and size limits.

## Evidence

Real Gateway proof (node 26.12.1, no network): an isolated Gateway booted by the repo e2e harness (`createChatFixture`, the same fixture as `chat-send-attach-identity.e2e.test.ts`) with a mock OpenAI Responses provider, driven through real `chat.send` / `agent.wait` RPCs. The harness fixture model is text-only in the gateway catalog, so accepted images deliver to agent input through the managed-media path (persisted bytes plus a `media://` reference in the provider request), which is the standard delivery form for models without image support.

Base `main` (`src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts` at `2159567b9ffc`), both attachment forms rejected by the shipped entry point:

```
media-type-parameters:  chat.send accepted=undefined error=Error: attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content
uppercase-BASE64-marker: chat.send accepted=undefined error=Error: attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content
outcomes=["media-type-parameters: rejected (Error: attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content)","uppercase-BASE64-marker: rejected (Error: attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content)"]
```

With this change, both forms succeed end to end (run started, run completed ok with a visible terminal reply, and the provider request carries the delivered media reference; `fixture.errors` empty):

```
media-type-parameters:  chat.send accepted={"runId":"170ee4b8-...","status":"started",...,"serverTiming":{...,"prepareAttachmentsMs":56.451}} error=undefined
media-type-parameters:  agent.wait={"status":"ok",...,"terminalReply":{"disposition":"visible","text":"param-data-url-proof-complete"}}
media-type-parameters:  providerRequestBytes=18660 inlineImage=false mediaRef=true
uppercase-BASE64-marker: chat.send accepted={"runId":"4907094f-...","status":"started",...} error=undefined
uppercase-BASE64-marker: agent.wait={"status":"ok",...,"terminalReply":{"disposition":"visible","text":"param-data-url-proof-complete"}}
uppercase-BASE64-marker: providerRequestBytes=22316 inlineImage=false mediaRef=true
outcomes=["media-type-parameters: delivered to agent input","uppercase-BASE64-marker: delivered to agent input"]
```

Focused unit lane on node 26.12.1 with no network, run against base `main` and with this change:

- Red on base: two new cases in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` (parameterized header `data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,...` and uppercase `;BASE64` marker) both failed with `attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content`; all 39 pre-existing tests passed.
- Green with the fix: all 41 tests pass in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` (`pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`).
- Targeted lint clean: `0 warnings, 0 errors` on both touched files.
- Format clean (`run-format.mts --write` on both touched files). Full-repo `tsc` shows no errors in the touched files (it reports only pre-existing portability diagnostics in unrelated `*.test-support.ts` harness files under the direct-tsc fallback; the pinned tsgo binary cannot run on this host's glibc 2.28).

Exact-head product CI has not completed: this fork PR's workflows await maintainer approval (`action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` currently reports failure from pending checks rather than from executed failures.

## Local review

Self-review of the one-line regex relaxation plus regression tests against the owning module's contracts (`normalizeAttachment` header-only inspection, strict payload validation downstream); no new surface, no ownership changes. Local ClawSweeper/autoreview tooling unavailable in this environment; relying on hosted review.

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).

prs.title: improve(knowledge): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Knowledge copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The Knowledge plugin's Control UI had ~425 user-visible English strings hard-coded across its views, dialogs, session panel, settings, loading/failure frames, and record panels. They didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary (for example "chat"/"conversation" for the session container, "turn" for an agent reply) or style rules (contractions, curly quotes, sentence case, "Couldn’t …" errors with a next step), and the plugin had no translation catalog, so none of it could be localized.

## Solution

- Add plugin i18n on the existing plugin pattern (`extensions/nostr/browser/i18n`): `extensions/knowledge/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `extensions/knowledge/src` (from `openclaw.controlUi: ./src/control-ui.ts`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` discovers the catalog. `activate(host)` binds `host.locale` once; every view reads copy through `t()` when it renders, so the page, session panel, and dialogs all use the host locale.
- The English catalog is split into `en.ts` (shared/page/search copy) plus `en-records.ts`, `en-scribes.ts`, and `en-settings.ts`, merged under one `knowledge.*` key tree. The split keeps each file under the 700-line cap; key paths are unchanged. All keys live under `knowledge.*`, so none collide with shared core keys.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-facing string the lane owns (the 31 changed view modules). Text written for the model (Ask request drafts, the record reference, scribe prompts, scribe session names) is unchanged.
- Small cutovers that came with moving copy:
  - Scribe catalog presentation fields (`blurb`, `cadence`, `startLabel`, `dialogTitle`, `submitLabel`) moved out of `scribes-catalog.ts` into the catalog and were removed from `ScribeDefinition`.
  - `sourceDateNote` moved from the shared `temporal.ts` (also used server-side) into `record-view.ts`, its only caller, so server code doesn't import Control UI copy.
  - Recent activity save badges key on the change id (`created`/`updated`/`observed`) instead of their English label. The one CSS hook (`[data-change="New"]`) moved to `[data-change="created"]`.
  - The page's source-files rail moved to `record-sources.ts` to keep `record-view.ts` under the line cap. It's a straight move with no behavior change.
  - The evidence excerpt eyebrow is sentence case in the catalog. `text-transform: uppercase` keeps its look.
- Docs that quote changed labels: `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` (Session not found, Open session) and `docs/plugins/knowledge/control-ui.md` (Ask starts a new session).
- Follow-up commit 8221620 (maintainer decisions): group and channel copy keeps “group chats”, and `docs/plugins/knowledge/maintenance.md` and `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` now say “reply” instead of “turn” for an agent cycle.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Starts a new chat with {agent}. … | Starts a new session with {agent}. … |
| Chat was not started. Your request is still here. | Couldn’t start the session. Your request is still here. |
| Chat was started but the request was not sent: {error} | Couldn’t send your request. The session started; open it to try again. {details} |
| Can’t reach the vault. … | Couldn’t reach the vault. … |
| Refresh unavailable / Search unavailable | Couldn’t refresh / Couldn’t search knowledge |
| This store couldn’t be opened | Couldn’t open this store (body now ends with “Retry, or check Stores & sharing.”) |
| The scribe was not started. {error} | Couldn’t start the scribe. Your choices and prompt are still here. {details} |
| The assignment was not changed. {error} / Access was not changed. {error} | Couldn’t change the assignment. Your choices are still here; try again. {details} / Couldn’t change access. Try again. {details} |
| The run did not start: the automation is paused | Couldn’t start the run because the automation is paused. Resume it, then try again. |
| In this conversation (session panel) | In this session |
| Open conversation · Conversation not found | Open session · Session not found |
| Which conversations · Active conversations · Conversations in your sidebar. | Which sessions · Active sessions · Sessions in your sidebar. |
| Knowledge will start a conversation called … | Knowledge will start a session called … |
| Each run is an agent turn over every unlinked claim … | Each run is one agent reply over every unlinked claim … |
| Conversation not recorded (claim source, Learned in) · Saved in conversation | Session not recorded · Saved in a session |
| … from owner-direct conversations | … from direct sessions with the owner |
| Group chats see only their own conversation’s knowledge. | Unchanged: “group chats” is kept (8221620) |
| No page is named exactly "x". · Search all text for "x" | No page is named exactly “x”. · Search all text for “x” |
| PREMISE · EXCERPT / EXCERPT | Premise · excerpt / Excerpt (still rendered uppercase) |
| cannot / is not / does not / could not / must not | can’t / isn’t / doesn’t / couldn’t / can’t |

Strings moved into the translation catalog: **823 English keys**. That's the ~425 source strings, plus one/other plural forms and conditional variants that used to be assembled in code.

## Impact

- English copy now follows the glossary and style rules. The layout and controls don't change.
- Knowledge copy can now be localized. The post-merge Control UI locale-refresh job owns foreign catalogs; this PR adds no foreign strings, `translated.json`, or `.i18n` memory.
- Raw technical details in errors (Gateway messages) stay inline after the next step. This surface has no shared host “Show details” disclosure, so I kept the detail visually secondary instead.
- Known gaps, intentional:
  - Scribe titles such as “Knowledge Consolidation” keep their current case. The title is the scribe session’s display name, which the Scribes tab uses to find a scribe’s session, and it also appears in scribe prompts and automation names. Renaming it would orphan existing scribe sessions.
  - There’s no `translated.json` yet, so `locales.ts` returns English for every locale. The translated catalog loader needs wiring once the locale refresh creates that file.
  - A locale change applies on the next render of each view, not instantly. Only English exists today.

## Evidence

The checks, tests and review below were run on bc913e8842dc236. The follow-up 8221620 changes only English copy and docs; it was checked with `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` (green, `plugin=knowledge keys=823`) and `git diff --check` (clean).

- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=knowledge keys=823`)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/knowledge/src`: green
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/knowledge/src docs/plugins/knowledge`: green
- `git diff --check`: clean
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge`: 64 files passed. `scribes-view.test.ts` and `search-date-filters.test.ts` assertions were updated to the new English.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main` (d59f00281eb0216) on head bc913e8842dc236, max priority P1. Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that its empty sandbox couldn’t run a build.
- pr-simplify: the catalog fields, the shared `sourceDateNote`, and the English-label status hooks were removed, and the shared count/plural helpers were folded into the catalog. Remaining growth is the catalog itself plus one-time `t()` call sites.

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge. Before/after screenshots of Recent, Browse, a record page, Scribes (list, detail, start dialog), Settings (all four sections), and the session panel are still needed under the visual gate.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/efff23f5-1c36-4383-806c-137f3ee688bc)
