prs.title: improve(mcp-relay): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Connected apps copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The MCP relay **Connected apps** page (`extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.ts`) hard-coded all of its English in the view. The plugin had no translation catalog, so the post-merge locale refresh couldn't translate it. Some of the copy also broke the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: an all-caps eyebrow label, a passive "is required" sentence, "do not" instead of a contraction, and "embedded browser sessions" (which reuses the product noun *session* for a different concept). Errors showed the raw request message as the whole alert, with nothing saying what failed or what to do next.

## Solution

- Added the plugin's English source catalog at `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, at the path `control-ui-plugin-i18n-catalog.ts` derives from `openclaw.controlUi`. The view now reads every string through `translateControlUiMessage`.
- Added `src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts}` on the nostr/whatsapp pattern. This page is plain DOM, not Solid, so `locales.ts` keeps the translated catalog in module state and the page re-renders when it loads. The page also re-renders on host locale changes; date formatting follows the locale too.
- `src/i18n/locales/translated.json` is committed as `{}`. The brief said to leave it absent, but without the file the plugin's Control UI build fails: the unresolved dynamic import trips "Control UI builds must bundle their browser dependencies". The empty file holds no translation values; the locale refresh bot fills it after merge.
- Errors now follow "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The redacted raw message moves under a collapsed **Show details**. The Control UI SDK has no shared disclosure component for plugin pages, so this uses a native `<details>`.
- Static `innerHTML` templates are now `element()` builders, so translated text is only ever set as text content.
- Manifest config hints: `Default Agent` → `Default agent`, and the help text says "new sessions" instead of "new conversations". I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` to match (only the plugin baseline hash changed).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No read access | Read access is required to view connected apps. | You need read access to view connected apps. |
| Consent eyebrow | CONNECTION REQUEST / CONNECT ANOTHER GATEWAY | Connection request / Connect another Gateway (CSS `text-transform: uppercase` keeps the look) |
| Consent, no permission | …permissions do not allow connecting an app. | …permissions don’t allow connecting an app. |
| Revoke hint | Revoking an app ends its MCP access and embedded browser sessions. … | Revoking an app ends its MCP and embedded UI access. … (matches the existing revoke notice) |
| Load failure | *(raw message)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load connected apps. Try again. + Show details |
| Approve / deny failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t connect {app}. Reopen the app’s connection page. / Couldn’t deny {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Revoke failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t revoke {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Pairing failure | *(raw message)* / Pairing failed. Try again. | Couldn’t create a pairing code. Try again. + Show details |
| Invalid relay return | The relay returned an invalid return address. Reopen the app’s connection page. | The relay returned an invalid return address. (now the detail; the next step is in the summary) |
| Config hint label | Default Agent | Default agent |
| Config hint help | Optional agent for new conversations; … | Optional agent for new sessions; … |

Moved into the translation file: **53 keys** (`ui:i18n:verify`: `plugin=mcp-relay keys=53`). About 9 existing strings changed, 6 are new (5 error summaries and "Show details"), and 2 manifest hints changed. The rest moved unchanged.

Left as is on purpose:
- "Gateway owner": an owner principal, not a role name. See the open question below.
- "Full access, including administration": names an activity, not the role.
- `ui-tunnel*` transport errors.
- The model-facing `recommendedPrompts`.

## Impact

- The Connected apps page becomes translatable through the existing locale refresh. English rendering is unchanged except for the copy above.
- The error alert is now a `div` with the summary and a collapsed details element. It got small margin and details styles, so expect a slight visual change in error states.
- Known limit: the page label in the navigation is resolved once at activation (`registerPage` takes a static string), so it stays English until the next activation.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.test.ts`: 7/7 pass. Assertions follow the changed English. The refresh-failure case now checks the summary and that the collapsed (closed) details hold the raw message.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=mcp-relay keys=53 locales=0 unused_translations=0`).
- `pnpm check:changed` on the committed head: all lanes ok, including typecheck extensions and extension tests, lint extensions, format, the dead-export scan, the Control UI i18n catalog, the bundled channel config metadata and the config docs baseline. One check failed, `changelog attributions`, and it fails the same way on `origin/main` (existing `Thanks @steipete-oai` entries in `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` and `2026.7.1.md`). This PR doesn't touch those files.
- Plugin Control UI build (`scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/mcp-relay`): succeeds.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify pass: I removed an unused `Translator` type export that the dead-export scan flagged. There's no new state beyond the error-detail fields and the locale tracking the re-render needs.
- Local review: local ClawSweeper isn't installed on this host, so I used autoreview, the documented fallback (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, merge base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `2cd7495c4c6`, max priority P2). Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that unchanged SDK and build contracts weren't in its context; the build and verify runs above cover them.

Before/after screenshots are pending and will be added before landing (visual gate).

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.

prs.title: fix(infra): accept Linux kernels without PID namespaces for Gateway state ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since the Gateway state-ownership lease records a PID-namespace identity, `readGatewayLockProcessNamespace` reads `/proc/self/ns/pid`. Linux kernels built without `CONFIG_PID_NS` — Android GKI (Pixel 6 6.1, OnePlus 13 6.6), some embedded configs — have no such link: `ls /proc/self/ns/` shows `cgroup mnt net time time_for_children uts` and nothing else. The read throws, the process identity becomes `null`, and `classifyGatewayOwnerProcessNamespace` answers `unknown` for every previous owner, so the Gateway and `doctor --fix` refuse state ownership ("cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process (different PID namespace); the owner heartbeat is fresh") until the heartbeat is >90 s stale.

## User Impact

Under a supervisor with `RestartSec=5` the heartbeat never goes stale, so on these kernels the Gateway crash-loops (`status=78`, start-limit-hit) after any non-clean exit, and `doctor --fix` cannot run either. With this change the Gateway starts normally; EACCES or a missing `/proc` keep today's cautious `unknown` behaviour, and a different boot id still classifies the old owner as `dead`.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a kernel without PID namespaces every process shares the one initial namespace, so a same-host, same-boot owner *is* this namespace and PID liveness is the right rule. Recording a sentinel (`LINUX_PID_NAMESPACE_UNSUPPORTED`) when `/proc/self/ns/pid` is `ENOENT` but `/proc/self/ns` exists lets the existing comparison yield `same` without touching the classifier.

Changes:
- `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts`: `readLinuxPidNamespaceInode()` with the `ENOENT` + `/proc/self/ns`-present fallback; exported `LINUX_PID_NAMESPACE_UNSUPPORTED`.
- `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.test.ts`: EACCES → unreadable; missing `/proc` → unreadable; kernel without PID namespaces → sentinel, `same` for a prior owner on this boot, `dead` across a reboot.
- `CHANGELOG/Unreleased.md`: Fixes entry.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on OpenClaw 2026.11.2 on a Pixel 6 (LineageOS 23.2, kernel 6.1 GKI, `# CONFIG_PID_NS is not set` in `/proc/config.gz`): `Gateway failed to start: failed to acquire gateway state ownership | cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process (different PID namespace); the owner heartbeat is fresh` on every start, 43 restarts; `doctor --fix` refused the same way, also from inside the container's own PID namespace and after 100 s stopped.
- With the equivalent patch applied to the installed dist: `http server listening` 8 s after a single start, stable since.
- `pnpm vitest run src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.test.ts src/infra/gateway-lock.namespace.test.ts` — all passed; `oxfmt`/`oxlint`/`pnpm tsgo:core` — clean.

prs.title: fix(gateway): bind QR/device-key browser pairings to the shared-auth generation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser device tokens are verified against the live shared-auth generation on every reconnect, and a token without an `issuer` is refused as `legacy-browser-token`. The connect path only stamped the issuer when the session itself carried the shared credential, so a Control UI paired through a **QR/setup-code bootstrap** (`PAIRING_SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE`, i.e. `openclaw qr` — not the `control-ui`/`control-ui-owner` profiles that #118231 covers) or through a **bare device-key pairing approved on the Gateway** received a bare token. It worked until the first Gateway restart; then every reconnect failed with `unauthorized` and the UI discarded its credential.

## User Impact

Anyone who pairs the Control UI with the QR/setup code (or approves a device-key pairing from the Gateway) on a token/password-protected Gateway has to re-pair after every Gateway restart. After this change that pairing survives restarts like a token-login pairing does. Sessions that authenticated with shared auth keep their session-bound generation; node tokens and Gateways without shared auth are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reproduced on OpenClaw 2026.9.6 and 2026.11.2 (Android/AOHP Gateways, two phones): `device_pairing_paired.tokens_json` for the browser had no `issuer`; after `SIGTERM` → listening, the reconnect logged `unauthorized … auth=device-token` and the UI dropped its token. The gateway was refusing a token it had itself issued moments earlier, on the documented pairing path. Passing the live generation into `issueGatewayConnectDeviceTokens` and binding browser-related tokens to it when the session has no generation of its own is the smallest change that makes the issued token pass the verifier's own rule.

Changes:
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-tokens.ts`: new `requiredSharedGatewaySessionGeneration` param; bind browser-related tokens to it when the session is not shared-auth bound.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.ts`: pass `context.handler.getRequiredSharedGatewaySessionGeneration?.()` at the call site.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-tokens.test.ts`: QR/bare-pairing browser gets the live generation; shared-auth session keeps its own; node token untouched; no shared auth → no issuer.
- `CHANGELOG/Unreleased.md`: Fixes entry.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-tokens.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt`, `oxlint` — clean
- On-device: patched the same change into a 2026.11.2 dist on a Pixel 6 Gateway; unpaired/re-paired the Control UI via QR. The stored token now carries `issuer: {kind: "shared-gateway-auth", generation: <live>}` matching the Gateway's live generation. Restarted the Gateway from its supervisor: `SIGTERM 04:08:31 → http server listening 04:08:45 → webchat connected 04:08:46`, no `unauthorized` line, no re-pair prompt.

prs.title: fix(android): distinguish null from text in SMS and call-log commands
prs.body:
Fixes #199095

## What Problem This Solves

Android SMS and call-log commands treat JSON `null` as the literal text `"null"`.
A null SMS message or recipient passes required-field validation, and optional
null search fields become unintended filters.

## User Impact

Invalid send requests are rejected before carrier submission. Optional null
filters behave as omitted; the actual string `"null"` remains searchable text
and a valid message body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing shared `parseJsonString` helper for the seven affected string
fields. It distinguishes JSON null from text while preserving existing trimming
and primitive conversion. Command authorization, Android permissions, numeric
filters and result formats stay at their existing owners.

## Evidence

The existing Android suites run the production SMS send method against its
carrier shadow, the SMS query parser, and call-log dispatch with its recording
data source. Four regressions fail on base and pass with this change:

- Null SMS body is rejected before submission.
- Null recipient is rejected before submission.
- Null SMS text filters remain absent.
- Null call-log text filters remain absent.

All 116 focused tests pass after the fix (112 pass on base). Controls include
literal `"null"` text, missing fields, permissions, multipart segmentation,
query defaults and pagination. ThirdParty source/test Kotlin lint and Android
lint pass. Executed on macOS arm64/JDK 21 with Robolectric 4.17; the SMS send
suite uses API 35. No real carrier or personal records were used.

```sh
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SmsSendTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SmsManagerTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CallLogHandlerTest
./gradlew :app:ktlintThirdPartySourceSetCheck \
  :app:ktlintTestThirdPartySourceSetCheck :app:lintThirdPartyDebug
```

### Independent review focus

For a paired ThirdParty Android node, compare omitted and null SMS/call-log
filters against disposable records. Null required send fields should return
`INVALID_REQUEST` without carrier submission. The automated suite already
checks that the literal string remains intact; normal SMS submission can be
confirmed separately with a controlled recipient.

prs.title: fix(channels): long replies with a code block arrive split into broken blocks on MS Teams and Zalo
prs.body:
Related: #199876

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long assistant replies that contain a fenced code block arrive split into broken blocks on MS Teams and Zalo (zalouser) when the reply crosses the channel text chunk limit (Teams 4,000, Zalo 2,000 characters). This is the remaining scope of #196429 after Tlon was fixed in #196430; #199876 tracks these two channels.

## User Impact

User impact: on these two channels, a long answer with code arrives with the code block intact (closed at the split and reopened with its original info string when the block must be divided), instead of code rendering as plain text and the trailing prose landing inside a stray code block. Every chunk still respects the channel limit, and plain-text chunking is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both channels declare `chunkerMode: "markdown"` but configure the fence-blind `chunkTextForOutbound` splitter, so a chunk boundary inside a fenced block leaves an unclosed fence. They now use the fence-aware splitter the plugin SDK already exports (`chunkMarkdownTextWithMode(text, limit, "length")`), the same one-line swap merged for Matrix (#196167), Mattermost (#196331), and Tlon (#196430). In the MS Teams sender, the direct `chunkTextForOutbound` call in the plain-text payload path is swapped to the same splitter so both delivery paths agree.

## Evidence

- **Chunker-boundary transcript (executed on this head vs main):** running each channel's real configured outbound `chunker` — the exact function the Gateway invokes — with a (limit + 300)-character fenced reply:
  - main (base): `msteams` 2 chunks, both fence-unbalanced (first ends mid-code, second starts with bare code lines and a stray closing fence); `zalouser` identical behavior at its 2,000-character limit.
  - this head: 3 fence-balanced chunks per channel (prose + two fenced segments), each within the channel limit, identical to the SDK fence-aware reference.
- Regression tests: `extensions/msteams/src/outbound.test.ts` asserts the configured chunker keeps fences balanced for a limit-crossing fenced reply and that a mocked-sender `sendPayload` delivery splits a 500-line fenced reply into balanced, ≤4,000-character chunks; `extensions/zalouser/src/channel.test.ts` asserts the configured chunker keeps fences balanced. `pnpm test:extension msteams` and `pnpm test:extension zalouser` pass (`LANG=C`).
- **Delivery-proof boundary, stated plainly:** shipped-entry delivery evidence (recorded `openclaw message send` runs, as supplied for Tlon in #196430 and Mattermost in #196331) is not obtainable without a tenant for these two channels: the Bot Framework `serviceUrl` is restricted to Microsoft HTTPS hosts by `extensions/msteams/src/bot-framework-service-url.ts` (no loopback mode), and Zalouser sends through the Zalo user protocol via zalo-js with no configurable endpoint. A maintainer with a tenant can produce the recorded run in minutes, or accept this evidence level per maintainer judgment (ClawSweeper is advisory). The production change is the same owner-approved one-line pattern as the three merged siblings.
- `pnpm format:check` passes; oxlint on the touched files reports 0 warnings / 0 errors. Net test-line growth (+27) is allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/199876-msteams-zalouser-fence-chunking.txt`; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` passes.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-14T23:42:01.167Z      skill_selection  -         -       observed  main   proof-run-1   skill.selection.observed  skill:proof--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":2,"eventId":"2c71cbfc-…","sourceSequence":1,
"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"proof-session-1","runId":"proof-run-1",
"action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection",
"actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"proof--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 2, `main`/`agent:main:proof`/`proof-session-1`/`proof-run-1`/`proof--demo`) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 3). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. (An LLM-driven variant was attempted with local ollama `qwen2.5:7b`/`gemma4:12b`; the agent loop stalled at the reply watchdog, so the trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool call — every stage after it is production code on a live Gateway.)

### Verification on this head

- `test/scripts/sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence.test.ts` 203/203
- `runtime-skill-selection` + `audit-events.skill-selection*` incl. new upgrade/sequence tests green
- `audit-events` (37), `commands/audit` (36), `gateway/server-methods/audit` (21/21) green
- `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files, line-cap ratchet clean vs upstream merge-base


## Round 4 (re-review findings, head `883b4d8d003`)

Both P2 findings fixed, plus the requested proof/test adjustments:

- **[P2] Buffered run starts retained until acceptance** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path now keeps the buffered start for the existing paired-settlement contract when `writer.record(start)` returns false, while skill observations still record independently. Regression test: with a rejecting writer, the terminal settles as one paired `recordRun(start, finish)` instead of a lone finish.
- **[P2] Companion counts bound to transaction outcomes** (`audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — tentative counts stage `rollback`/`invalidate` hooks through `stageSqliteTransactionState`, as the canonical ledger does. Negative control verified: without the fix a rolled-back overflow batch leaves the cap violated at 100,001 rows; with it the next insert trims honestly to 98,976. Covered by `drops tentative companion counts when their batch rolls back`.
- **Upgrade proof targets v2026.11.3** — confirmed the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 (no companion table), so the regression test builds exactly that layout, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, `schema_meta` intact), and shows the stored audit row plus continued shared sequencing.
- **Flagged low-value tests removed** — unrelated date/empty-limit CLI variants and the full marker-construction equality case are out; encoding, truncation, and production-boundary coverage retained.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains best-effort: local ollama models (`qwen2.5:7b`, `gemma4:12b`) stall at the agent reply watchdog in this environment, so the trigger stays the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it (observer → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) is production code, demonstrated in Round 3.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7 (incl. rollback + v2026.11.3 upgrade), audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 5 (re-review: settlement intent + true v2026.11.3 fixture, head `4fd73e177bc`)

- **Buffered run-start settlement intent documented** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path flushes the buffered start as a best effort so the ledger holds the run before its independent skill rows arrive (readers join by run; legacy run/tool views stay coherent), while rejection retains the start for the existing paired settlement boundary. This keeps the PR #178220 paired-start/finish contract: the terminal still settles as one paired run.
- **Upgrade fixture is the true v2026.11.3 layout** — verified the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 without the companion table (release commit `50330aa9cf5`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 39`, no `audit_skill_selection_events`). The regression test now builds the fixture from the current schema minus only the unreleased companion table at version 40 (matching the release lineage), opens it with the current build, and asserts: `user_version`/`schema_meta` intact, a stored workspace setting row byte-identical, the stored audit row readable, lazy companion creation on first skill write, and continued shared sequencing with correct readback.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains environment-blocked (local ollama models stall at the agent reply watchdog; xAI cloud models need the `xai` extension whose dist build is broken by a pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` resolution from root, unrelated to this PR). The live-Gateway proof in Round 3 (production tool boundary → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) stands as the in-environment maximum.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7, audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 6 (head `a71b0be6d94`)

- **True v2026.11.3 upgrade fixture** — the reviewer correctly noted the published v2026.11.3 is schema v22 (verified: release tag → commit `847611dcaa3`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 22`, no companion table), not v39. The compat regression test now builds the fixture from `getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema(22)` (verified to reproduce the release's `audit_events`/`schema_meta`/`workspace_setup_state`/`config_machine_state` tables byte-identically; only later-dropped device/gateway tables differ, which audit admission does not touch). The fixture migrates 22→40 (backup custody via the standard test-support helper, as a real install would back up first) with `schema_meta`, a stored workspace setting, and the legacy audit row byte-identical, then records a skill_selection via lazy companion DDL with continued shared sequencing and correct readback.
- **Removed the remaining flagged whitespace-only decision-limit variant** in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (restored the upstream single-case form).

Verification on this head: skill-selection 8/8, audit-events + commands/audit green, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 7 — product upgrade run from published v2026.11.3 (head `a71b0be6d94`, no new commits; proof only)

- **Genuine release write**: ran the published v2026.11.3 source (release tag → `847611dcaa3`, schema v22) to create a state dir and record a legacy agent run through its production audit writer (`sequences 1–2, run release-run-1, user_version 22`).
- **New-build upgrade**: fresh `dist` rebuilt from PR source; the new Gateway booted the release DB with no schema refusal and migrated 22→40, release rows intact.
- **New skill write + shipped CLI readback through the running new Gateway**: production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` → observer → recorder → store (`skill.selection.observed`, shared sequence 4, `upgraded-run-1`), then `openclaw audit --run release-run-1 --json` returns the release rows and `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json` returns the new skill row with full attribution. Full redacted transcript kept with the run notes.
- Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked (local models stall at the reply watchdog; xAI needs the `xai` extension whose dist build fails on the pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` root resolution). The trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it is production code on live Gateways, now demonstrated across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary.

- **[P2] Clear schema readiness when lazy creation rolls back** (`src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — `ensureSkillSelectionAuditSchemaOnce` now binds the `skillSelectionSchemaEstablished` flag to the owning SQLite transaction via `stageSqliteTransactionState` (rollback/invalidate drop both the readiness flag and the warm row-count). prs.title: fix: Custom setup exits during memory import after Gateway startup
prs.body:
Closes #199895.

## What Problem This Solves

Custom setup starts its Gateway before memory import. The memory wizard used the offline-only provider loader, so even an empty source list could abort setup with an exclusive offline ownership error before recommendations and handoff.

## User Impact

Setup can import detected memories into the selected agent workspace while its Gateway keeps running. Users can decline import or retry/skip a recoverable Gateway failure inside setup. One unreadable source does not hide healthy sources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runSetupMemoryImportStep` selects the existing local or serving-Gateway owner. The Gateway path uses the existing memory plan/apply API, reviewed fingerprint and one idempotency key per selected operation; retries reconcile that operation without a local fallback. One presenter serves both paths. Offline and hosted provider lifetimes, host authority checks, source preservation, cleanup and confirmed/indeterminate outcome reporting remain with their existing owners. No config option, environment option, schema or Gateway protocol is added.

Implementation: `6e797aea4cacc78b53417aaa566e99b106af5aa4`. Marked Ready on November 16, 2026 to trigger normal CI; full author delivery remains pending.

## Evidence

### Named-base failure

At `210e3c4282c5b3549b239f8c21a6788b08ba9a29`, runtime build passed. The station executed:

```sh
ocpr prove 199895 --phase pre --sha 210e3c4282c5b3549b239f8c21a6788b08ba9a29 --cmd 'python3 /Users/ericstudio/repos/oc-pr-management/.tmp/openclaw-p0-p1/199895-memory-entry-proof.py'
```

The harness prepared synthetic isolated state with real Doctor (exit0), started a real Gateway through the built CLI, and invoked production memory import with scripted answers. The wizard exited1 before offering import:

```text
Cannot admit migrate for migration providers ... This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership. No local mutation was attempted.
```

The task-owned Gateway was stopped afterward. The committed real Gateway/process regression also fails with the exact named-base wizard owner overlaid, at the same ownership refusal; candidate owner bytes were restored afterward. That overlay run is regression validation, not a separate formal exact-SHA receipt.

### Candidate checks

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/wizard/setup.memory-import.test.ts src/commands/onboard-guided-memory-import.test.ts src/system-agent/hosted-setup.memory.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/migrations.test.ts src/gateway/server.onboard-memory-import.test.ts`: 41 passed across five files, four shards, 93.55s. Covers the real Gateway/process boundary, final workspace, decline, repeat/empty import, source preservation, stable-key uncertain retry, interrupted recovery, per-source isolation and affected offline/hosted consumers.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed after the material review repairs. Changed test-graph typechecks, focused project lint, formatting, first-party mock export ratchet and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `PATH=/private/tmp/ocpr-199895-tools:$PATH node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 210e3c4282c5b3549b239f8c21a6788b08ba9a29`: exit1. Its scoped test-lint findings were fixed and their actual guards passed. It also reports inherited unused exports in unchanged `scripts/lib/plugin-prerelease-test-plan.mts` and `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-rollback.test-support.ts`; the full command is not claimed green. Other executed ratchets/typegraphs passed.
- Independent canonical P0-P2 review: scoped-clean with no actionable P0-P2 findings on the complete candidate. The earlier uncertainty and source-isolation findings were corrected and independently re-reviewed; review did not execute project checks.

### Coverage limits and remaining work

The public executable candidate has been rebuilt and the formal exact-head memory-entry controls below pass. The complete Custom-path/TUI/model/native-service proof below also passed. Remaining: exact-head repository CI execution and the final author-delivery/WATCH gate. The current-head hosted review now accepts the real behavior proof and has no actionable findings. Ready is the CI trigger, not author completion.

### Exact-head memory-entry milestone

At `6e797aea4cacc78b53417aaa566e99b106af5aa4`, `pnpm build:runtime` passed in68.5s, then the station executed:

```sh
ocpr prove 199895 --phase post --sha 6e797aea4cacc78b53417aaa566e99b106af5aa4 --cmd 'python3 /Users/ericstudio/repos/oc-pr-management/.tmp/openclaw-p0-p1/199895-memory-entry-proof.py'
```

Exit0. Real isolated built-CLI Gateway, production memory wizard, synthetic Claude memories and scripted prompt answers:

```text
import: completed; Claude 1 migrated, 0 skipped; destination bytes match source
empty/repeat: nothing-to-import; no prompt and no new copy
decline: skipped; newly detected source not copied
owned Gateway stopped after proof
```

The source remains intact. This certifies the production memory-import owner and real Gateway transport at the exact public head, with synthetic source data. Complete interactive Custom-path, native model, macOS service and final TUI handoff are covered separately below; they are not inferred from these scripted memory-entry controls.

### Real Custom path, macOS service and TUI handoff

Executed at `6e797aea4cacc78b53417aaa566e99b106af5aa4` through the rebuilt shipped CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs onboard --tui --accept-risk --workspace <isolated workspace>
```

The station ran `199895-full-custom-proof.py`, followed by `199895-full-proof-closeout.py`, both with `ocpr prove 199895 --phase post --sha 6e797aea4cacc78b53417aaa566e99b106af5aa4`. Both final executions exited0. Real PTY answers selected One agent, Full access, the detected native Codex connection, the isolated final workspace, No embeddings, Retry, and Yes to memory import. Actual trace, with fixture paths and model identity redacted:

```text
AI check: replied in 18.0s
Gateway: running at ws://127.0.0.1:<isolated port>
Set up memory embeddings? No
Claude: EACCES: permission denied, open <synthetic MEMORY.md>
Retry memory import or skip it for now? Retry

Hatching your agent now...
session agent:main:main
assistant: OC199895_TUI_OK
```

The recovery control used a real unreadable synthetic file, restored its permissions at the Retry prompt, then continued through the same running owner. The source and imported bytes match. The TUI received a real model response; a separate Gateway `chat.history` read verified the marker in an assistant message, rather than counting the echoed user prompt.

Executed final receipt:

```json
{"realCustomSetupAccepted":true,"realTuiAssistantReply":true,"realPermissionRetryThenImport":true,"sourceBytesPreserved":true,"canonicalProfileIdentityVerified":true,"serviceUninstallExit":0,"servicePlistRemoved":true,"serviceJobAbsent":true,"listenerStopped":true,"copiedAuthRemoved":true}
```

Fixture and coverage limits: a unique canonical macOS service profile under the existing OS account, synthetic memory roots, and the existing supported Codex `appServer.homeScope=user` setting with an isolated native-account copy. Other profile state was new. This does not claim a separate fresh OS account, Claude inference, browser handoff, cloud embeddings, or successful app-recommendation inference. The optional recommendation stage logged relay errors and continued to the successful TUI handoff. No default/production profile or preexisting service was changed. The initial completely empty-auth fixture required a separate agent login, and the temporary-HOME fixture was correctly refused by native service admission; neither is product acceptance. The final service used the native env-wrapper representation; a separate identity-verified closeout removed only this profile's service and verified that its listener/job/plist were gone.

### Current hosted gate

[CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43803192150), [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43803191885) and [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43803191989) were triggered again by Ready and report `action_required` on this head; each has zero jobs. These are repository execution gates, not green checks or demonstrated test failures. No approval/bypass or maintainer action is claimed. prs.title: fix(release): recover complete qualification across profiles
prs.body:
Stacked on #199110; base: `openclaw/shared-evidence-validation-contract-refactor`. This PR does not modify that PR or perform a release.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: receipt-backed release recovery only handles beta coverage, and successful aggregate jobs can conceal missing required qualification work.

## User Impact

Release operators can recover authenticated beta, stable, full, and extended-stable qualification receipts without rerunning tests or preparing replacement publication artifacts. The original candidate, publication selection, baselines, child attempts, and waiver policy remain authoritative.

`pnpm frv recover` retains one private request before dispatch and reconciles uncertain outcomes rather than dispatching again. Recovery is explicit; this PR does not dispatch a recovery, publish packages, edit a candidate, or alter an active release.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move admitted child-input reconstruction into the shared validation policy owner, and use one required-work completeness check for direct and recovered qualification. Remove the beta-only role/input policy.
- Derive profile, track, child inventory, soak, platform/package coverage, and publication selection from the original authenticated admission. Preserve advisory failures and trusted waiver scope.
- Authenticate existing plans when present; otherwise discover original receipts from exact dispatch/adoption witnesses. Never treat an invalid plan as a missing plan.
- Keep original artifact transport separate from the recovery workflow and adopted child transport. Retain the exact recovery request, selected P, and request witness for read-only reconciliation.

This is the next coherent stage after #199110: both consumers must switch together to avoid conflicting acceptance policies. Added production code implements actual workload completeness and one-shot operator reconciliation; no competing validator or new publication authority is introduced. The net production delta is +1,486/-174 lines, with +1,813/-178 test lines. The beta-only reconstruction policy is removed in favor of the shared admission owner; the larger additions are required leaf validation and durable operator reconciliation.

## Evidence

- Final combined consumer/completeness/boundary run: **82/82 passed**. Recovery tests: **30/30 passed**. Operator/CLI/scope/boundary validation: **163/163 passed** (overlapping suites, not an additive total). Candidate CLI **2/2**, release-ready recovery CLI **2/2**, and standalone plugin receipt recovery **1/1** passed.
- Independent regressions cover omitted required workload families and frozen-Q/current-P policy divergence; these failed before the owner repair and pass afterward.
- Script and tooling-test typechecks, touched-file production/test lint, formatting, workflow checks, documentation MDX checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent recovery/operator and final completeness reviews found no remaining actionable P0–P2 defects. The final local autoreview helper exited without a verdict (`no route retry`); this is not a passing review. This PR remains draft for hosted review.

### Remaining proof gaps and compatibility boundary

- Five `plugin-npm-cli-process.test.ts` cases stop at the manifest archive entry-list boundary because this host lacks `unzip` (`ENOENT`). The same archive-listing dependency and error mapping exist on the base branch. No archive validation was weakened or bypassed. Those process paths still need a qualified host/CI run.
- Frozen-Q package planning is accepted only when its planner and dependency closure exactly match the supported implementation. Divergent Q policy fails closed and needs a reviewed adapter; it is never silently replaced with current-P policy.
- Hosted review and broad PR CI remain outstanding.

Limits: no live workflow dispatch, registry write, publication, candidate mutation, or full release qualification was performed. GitHub API and artifact transports are isolated in the integration tests; broad platform/runtime proof remains PR CI and the release workflows.

prs.title: fix(slack): deliver the final reply when a boundary or msg_too_long hits a native stream
prs.body:
Two scoped Slack native-stream delivery repairs, preserving both original commits by @n1hility. Found while building #143882; independent of that feature.

## What Problem This Solves

1. **A progress boundary can stop the stream under the final reply.** Core fires `onReasoningEnd` and `onAssistantMessageStart` best effort, without awaiting them. With a live model, a draft boundary can arrive while `deliverNativeFinal` is still appending the completion and the answer. By then the pacing loop has stopped and the final is marked started, so `beginNewProgressTurn` reads the turn as over and stops the stream under the final's append. Slack then rejects the append with `message_not_in_streaming_state`, and the answer either degrades to a separate plain post or is lost.
2. **`msg_too_long` leaves the message streaming without the answer.** Slack answers `chat.appendStream` with `msg_too_long` once a streamed message holds as much content as it allows. The plugin did not classify that code. It marked the session stopped without calling `chat.stopStream` and rethrew, so the message stayed in its streaming state and the answer never appeared. A closeout stop rejected the same way also left the message streaming.


On the real QA workspace, the boundary race produced a duplicated final answer rather than the rejected/lost append described above: both baseline runs stored the final marker twice (182 total bytes); both candidate runs stored it once (110 bytes). Those counts include progress text.

## User Impact

- A late progress boundary no longer stops the stream while its final answer is being appended.
- A final answer rejected with msg_too_long is posted through normal delivery before the stream stops.
- A rejected closeout stops without its oversized chunks instead of leaving the message streaming.
- No configuration or presentation change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A non-forced progress boundary waits for in-flight final delivery; forced queued-follow-up boundaries keep their existing behavior. The existing definitive-rejection fallback handles msg_too_long without replaying its rejected buffer. A rejected closeout is stopped without its extra chunks. The internal operator log is retained; no new user- or model-facing message text.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `d8ca23ee45237dd9e95efb0eae175e2731d0b993`. [Real Slack API proof and redacted QA-user readback receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199849#issuecomment-6907007114).

Two baseline and two candidate runs exercise the boundary overlap, naturally full final append and naturally oversized closing stop. All three controls are unchanged: short native reply, forced queued follow-up and non-native preview. No held Slack responses or injected rejections. The real dispatchPreparedSlackMessage and @slack/web-api paths run with scripted agent callbacks, not a model or live Gateway.

no Slack client session was available; outcome is read back through the Slack API.

- Focused tests: 121/121 pass; baseline replay has nine expected regression failures. Matching Slack test typecheck, formatting, scoped lint and mock-export ratchet pass.
- Full ocx build with declarations and packed CLI smoke pass.
- Production +51/-5; tests +297/-303, net -6. No allocation file or second dispatcher test harness. Existing cases were consolidated with exact retained-contract citations in the proof.
- The original two contributor commits remain. All owned Slack messages were removed with readback, including exact-author recovery of four baseline streams; all leases released.

Merge risk: two-way door. A revert restores previous delivery handling without schema, stored-data or configuration migrations. Blast radius is Slack native progress streaming and its existing normal-reply fallback; ordinary short, queued and preview controls passed.

prs.title: fix(cli): request scopes a session-only device grant covers
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199693. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199693 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a device paired with only `operator.sessions.write`, as the multiplayer guide recommends for guests, can't use `openclaw gateway call` or `openclaw tui`. The CLI asks for `operator.read` and the TUI for admin, read, write and approvals, so every connect becomes a scope-upgrade request for the admin.

## User Impact

User impact: a session-only guest can list, read and create its sessions from the CLI and use the TUI within its grant. Once the TUI has stored the grant with a device token, its connections and `gateway call` file no upgrade request. Behind trusted-proxy auth the Gateway issues the TUI no device token and `gateway call` stores none, so there each connection is refused once with a scope-upgrade request and then works within the grant. #199699 removes that refusal as a Gateway opt-in.

Devices whose grant holds the general scope are unchanged, and a device that needs a real upgrade (for example `operator.read` to `operator.admin`) still files one.

In the TUI, a session-only device gets no command list or pending approvals, because those need `operator.read` and `operator.approvals`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Where the client learns its grant:**
- `gateway call` projects its least-privilege scopes through the stored device grant with the existing `projectOperatorScopesForMethod`. It narrows only when the method's session-scoped alternative still authorizes the call.
- The TUI connects within a stored grant that holds `operator.sessions.*` and none of its default scopes, unless `--token` or `--password` is given.

**A device approved before it ever connected:** it has no stored grant, so its first request can exceed it. The Gateway's scope-upgrade refusal already reports `approvedScopes`, and the client uses that:
- The gateway client gains an opt-in `fitScopesToApprovedGrant` hook that reconnects once within the reported grant, which the TUI uses.
- `gateway call` retries once with the session grant.
- The TUI stores the device token it receives with the grant, so its later connections, and `gateway call` reading that stored grant, fit it. `gateway call` keeps its read-only storage mode on the retry and stores nothing.

Until a grant is stored, each connection still files that request first, because nothing tells the client its grant before it asks. Behind trusted-proxy auth nothing is stored, so that holds for every connection. The opt-in Gateway change in #199699 removes it.

**Moves:** two moves keep the touched files within the line-cap ratchet without changing behaviour:
- CLI scope selection, including the existing `sessions.create` cwd escalation retry, moves to `src/gateway/call-scopes.ts`.
- The gateway client's host-dependency defaults move to `packages/gateway-client/src/client-host-deps.ts`. `client.ts` re-exports their types, so the package API is unchanged.

**Docs:** `docs/start/multiplayer.md` and `docs/cli/tui.md` describe the guest behaviour and when the first-connect request remains.

- **New tests:**
  - `src/gateway/call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5. A session-only grant reads with `operator.sessions.read`; a read grant and a method without a session scope keep their request; a refused request retries with the reported grant and keeps read-only storage on both attempts (this case fails without the read-only fix); a grant that can't serve the method does not retry.
  - `packages/gateway-client/src/client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, against a real WebSocket server that refuses with a scope upgrade: reconnects once within the reported grant; pauses without the hook, or when the hook keeps the request.
  - `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, adding session-only, read, `operator.pairing` and `--token` grants.
  - Without this change, the session-only, retry, `operator.pairing` and `--token` cases fail; the keep-behaviour cases pass on both.
- **Existing tests:** `call.test.ts` 91/91, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `client.handshake.test.ts` 22/22, `client.device-auth.test.ts` 25/25, `reconnect-policy.test.ts` 19/19, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Static checks:** typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Restack onto #199693's pairing hint:** this branch now sits on `a675d1b23b7`, which adds the `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device and keeps an explicit `--url` in it. `git range-diff 3411a94ae50..48d8e528f08 a675d1b23b7..74994fa1a99` shows this branch's two commits unchanged, and the runs below were made at `48d8e528f08`, before the restack. prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Template Add waits for every dependency before the agent can speak. Slow setup stalls the opening; the composer handoff can lose queued input. A failed opening also left Retry unable to dispatch after a same-scope Gateway reconnect.

## What changes

Finalize the prepared agent/session before dependency setup, attach chat and start its opening while dependencies settle. The existing continuation serializes checkpoints and reports dependency results after the opening. Retry preserves the same agent, files and settled work.

The retained composer belongs to the account/Gateway presentation scope, not an obsolete transport object. An explicit Retry captures the current connected transport; in-flight result fences and cross-scope guards remain. Existing owners retain drafts, attachments and queued input. No new owner or automatic retry is added.

Source acquisition stays verified. Timing diagnostics use debug severity. Referenced ClawHub plugins remain recommendations, never automatically installed/enabled. Denies, consent and installation policy are unchanged.

Stacked above [setup #198603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198603), above creation. The [foundation #198065](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198065) has merged; this PR has not.

## Evidence

[Inspected paired real-Gateway recovery proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198637#issuecomment-6873005012), including before/after images:

The prior reconnect snapshot passed all30 focused Add/admission cases, targeted formatting/type-aware lint/UI types and canonical full build. That fixture does not prove an ordinary live-provider turn or new Template receipt semantics. The separate recovery run above proves the cold same-agent Retry path. prs.title: fix(cli): connect through gateway.remote.edgeAuth without a Gateway token
prs.body:
Closes #199691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw tui`, `openclaw tui --url` and `openclaw gateway call` refuse to dial a Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (or another identity-aware proxy) when the client has `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` but no Gateway token or password. A guest's device therefore never files its first pairing request.

## User Impact

User impact: a CLI configured with `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` connects to a trusted-proxy Gateway without a shared Gateway secret. On first contact `openclaw tui` gets `device pairing required` and leaves a request for the admin, as the [Cloudflare Access guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloudflare-access#verify) already describes. Configurations without edgeAuth, and targets on other origins, still require credentials as before. A Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential: edgeAuth only gets the connection through the proxy, and the Gateway then refuses the missing token. A device that has never connected pairs through `openclaw tui`; its `openclaw gateway call` now says so instead of answering with a bare `missing scope: operator.read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three local prechecks reject a connection that has no token, password or stored device token: one in `callGatewayWithScopes`, `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth` for `--url` targets, and the TUI's connection resolver. None of them knew that the proxy authenticates the upgrade. Each now skips the shared-credential requirement when edge-auth headers are configured for the target's origin, using the existing `gatewayEdgeAuthValueForTarget` origin match. The Gateway's device pairing then decides access, so nothing new is trusted on the client.

First pairing stays in `openclaw tui`. `openclaw gateway call` is read-only, so on a device that has never connected it has no device identity to pair; the Gateway accepts the connection and refuses the method with `MISSING_SCOPE`. When edge-auth headers are set, the call has no device identity and the Gateway answers `MISSING_SCOPE`, the error now adds `Fix: this device is not paired with this Gateway yet. Run \`openclaw tui\` once to pair this device, ...` (`withEdgeAuthPairingHint` in `src/gateway/call-device-auth.ts`). When the call was given `--url`, the command in the hint keeps it (`openclaw tui --url <url>`), as the existing stored-device-auth recovery message does, because a bare `openclaw tui` can select another Gateway, such as a local one. `call.ts` is over its line cap, so its edge-auth header lookup is inlined, as the TUI's already is, to keep the file from growing.

`docs/cli/tui.md` and `docs/gateway/remote.md` say that, when the Gateway uses trusted-proxy auth, the first connection through edgeAuth needs no token and sends a pairing request, and that a Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential.

## Evidence

- **Tests:**
  - New `src/gateway/call.edge-auth.test.ts` (6 cases) and one new case in `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts`.
  - Pairing hint: an edgeAuth device with no identity that gets `MISSING_SCOPE` now sees the `openclaw tui` hint; without this change that case fails with the bare `missing scope: operator.read`. With `gateway.mode: "local"` and an explicit `--url`, the hint names `openclaw tui --url <url>`; that case fails on `d2fade98ea1` with the bare `openclaw tui` hint. A device with an identity keeps the bare message on both. `call.test.ts` 91/91.
  - On `main`, the edgeAuth cases fail with the same errors users see: `requires credentials before opening a websocket`, `gateway url override requires explicit credentials` and `Missing gateway auth credentials.`. With this change they pass.
  - The case for a remote without edgeAuth passes on both, showing that it still requires credentials.
  - Neighbouring suites pass: `client-bootstrap.auth.test.ts` 6/6, `gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 12/12, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
  - Typecheck and format are clean. Lint reports nothing in the touched files.
- **Live run** at this head (`3411a94ae50`, built with `pnpm build:runtime`): a loopback Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, behind a small TLS proxy standing in for Cloudflare Access (it answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then injects the identity headers). The guest config has only `gateway.remote.url` and `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`: no token, no password, no stored device token. `--tls-fingerprint` is there only because the test proxy uses a self-signed certificate. The output is trimmed, and IDs and ports are from throwaway test state. The admin approves the TUI's request as it was requested.

(admin rejects it, to see the explicit-URL path file its own request)
$ openclaw tui --url wss://127.0.0.1:19742 --tls-fingerprint <test cert>   # explicit URL, no token or password

prs.title: fix(release): freeze published stable version in maintenance notices
prs.body:
## Summary

Extended-stable release notices incorrectly named the publisher tooling package version as the current regular stable release. Resolve GitHub Latest for initial publication instead, then reuse the prepared or already-public notice for later rendering, canonical readback, and fresh-parent recovery. Standalone preflight uses the same distinction.

Main-derived maintenance-line retirement remains separate from the informational published version. Canonical source-body verification, retired-line approval, and docs-publication ownership remain enforced. This reuses existing release-body files; there is no new schema, state machine, retention policy, or release mutation. Existing renderer callers retain their prior defaults.

## Evidence

Validated patch: `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a..e79892e96eb8e84da0316e8a049e00b18d5ce8bd`.

- Before the fix: four real shell/renderer and standalone-preflight regressions failed because tooling and published stable differed.
- Independent review identified fresh-parent recovery after Latest advances; both recovery regressions failed before the follow-up repair.
- Focused publication, preflight, and renderer suites: 57 passed across four files; wrapper wall time 10.06 seconds. Final draft-fixture change: 23 passed in 6.87 seconds.
- Scripts typecheck and tooling-test typecheck passed. Targeted lint, formatting, Bash syntax, and git diff whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent native source review of the complete five-file patch against `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a`: previous recovery finding resolved, no remaining P0–P2 findings.
- Simplification: removed tooling version as notice authority and reused the existing prepared/public body rather than adding persistent context machinery.

## Hosted CI follow-through

At head `4ab8d0e731251109cc26de45611becd754169e69`, CI run [43797970683](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797970683) has a failed lint job [133072637830](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797970683/job/133072637830): `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118:48`, `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone`. The failing source blob is `5226ae58848652825503bb9c0558b70b73c7baf0` at both the original base and this PR head. This is source-based attribution to unchanged base code, not a green CI claim or a waiver. Remaining CI and hosted review are tracked separately.

## Limits and remaining gates

Proof uses production shell/renderer paths with synthetic GitHub responses. No live publication or authenticated Actions recovery was performed.

Native independent review is not local ClawSweeper/autoreview machine certification. Local ClawSweeper and autoreview were unavailable through the supported tools in this execution environment; no completed local machine review is claimed. This disclosure does not waive required review or CI gates.

prs.title: fix(workboard): Open board in dashboard widgets reloads the whole Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking **Open board** in a Workboard widget on a dashboard reloads the whole Control UI instead of navigating to the board.

The full reload throws away in-memory UI state, such as the Dashboards sidebar author filter and remembered sidebar sections. A manual session confirmed it: `performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')` showed the board URL as a fresh document load. It also happens on `main`.

## User Impact

User impact: **Open board** in the Workboard summary and board widgets now opens the board inside the running Control UI and keeps the current UI state. Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt-click and middle-click still open the board in a new tab or window, because the link keeps its real `href`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The widgets rendered a plain `<a href>` from `host.navigation.pageHref(...)` and had no click handler. They now call the documented `host.navigation.openPage(...)` on a plain left click. Other plugin links already use the same pattern (the Workboard session chip and the Knowledge "Open full page" link). No SDK or contract change.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `extensions/workboard/browser/widgets.test.ts`, run for both the summary and board widgets. On the base it fails (`expected false to be true`: the click is not intercepted). With the fix it passes. It checks that a plain click calls `openPage` with the board target and prevents the default action. It also checks that Cmd-click and middle-click leave the native link alone.
- `pnpm test extensions/workboard/browser/widgets.test.ts extensions/workboard/browser/widgets/runtime.test.ts`: 19/19 passed.
- `pnpm -s tsgo:ui`: clean. oxfmt and oxlint on both touched files: clean.
- Gap: I have not run this through a live Control UI e2e. The behavior relies on the existing `openPage` host method, which the session chip and Knowledge links already use in production.
