prs.title: improve(ui): highlight skill references in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #152599 (inline `$skill` references; standalone slash commands are unchanged). Builds on #192242.

## What Problem This Solves

Selected skills remain raw `$command_name` text in the composer, making them harder to distinguish from surrounding prose and person mentions.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show known skill references as highlighted, atomic names with the existing skill icon and no visible `$`. Copying and sending preserve the canonical reference. No configuration or migration is required.

**Still draft; not performance-qualified for shipping.** The repeated scanning and premature editor-loading defects are repaired, and both hosted correctness findings are fixed. The startup asset gate still fails by **448 bytes**. First skill use and skill-only rich editing still cost substantially more than native text; several New Session p95 cells remain higher. These limits are not waived by this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generic native-first editor and extension contract from the final merged #192242, rather than introduce another editor, overlay or dependency. Skills use the existing command catalog and share atomic boundary editing with people. Display labels no longer grant reference identity: only canonical commands and normalized command identifiers are recognized. Unknown references, shell variables, escaped dollars and code remain literal.

Ordinary edits map existing skill decorations instead of rescanning the draft. Token/Markdown-sensitive edits still use the canonical parser; image-bearing drafts deliberately retain full parsing. Atomic editing checks only affected chip boundaries and does not serialize large pastes for single-character separator checks. Literal dollars may load the small parser, but cannot fetch CodeMirror until a reference is admitted. Catalog replacement explicitly refreshes labels/removals and admits unchanged restored drafts; subscriptions end with their native/editor owners. Native undo snapshots, asynchronous handoff, IME boundaries and retired-frame guards are preserved. Skill integration still composes through the mention adapter, not a new feature framework.

## Evidence

### Current repair and review — November 16

Published head `0283e5b68266ebb706dab8a9d74623406693488e` has exactly the tested product tree of implementation `ec4b449ebd8e2e0e468f10da9fec32b8ec9b789b` (`37b3739503d08c1fbe431ff51ae1ba6af24bcb99`); the publisher's final commit is attribution-only.

- **218 browser tests passed in 13 files**, including person/skill editor consumers, native handoff, undo, paste/drop, composition simulation, ref disposal, catalog/command consumers, overflow, height and mobile fixtures. UI and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, controller guard and whitespace checks passed.
- **Both source-server real-UI Chat/New Session flows passed** with a synthetic Gateway. The new network assertion first failed on both routes: `$HOME`/`$unknown` fetched the rich editor. It now passes while actual skill selection and canonical submission still work.
- Both hosted P2 findings on `6d45233` were reproduced red and repaired: display-name aliases could look selected without resolving on submission; unchanged drafts did not react to catalog arrival/rename/removal. The catalog regression verifies stable editor identity, raw text and selection.
- Independent local **autoreview through P2 was scoped-clean** for the final staged repair against `6d45233`, subsequently committed as `ec4b449`. It included the generic editor, mention adapter, import lifecycle, catalog owner, Gateway reference-resolution contract and Markdown parser as context. Static review is not runtime proof. Earlier reviewer findings for indentation, adjacent backticks, native history and literal-dollar loading were repaired; the staged-only loading finding disappeared when the reviewed working-tree fix was committed.
- **900 valid repair timing observations** were collected across explicit source stages: 390 at `08ec3b39`, 270 at `452d63a5`, then **240 on the final product tree**. Completed interrupted work was retained rather than replayed; one restart interruption in the first stage is excluded from valid observations. Earlier-stage measurements are not relabeled as final-head proof.
- Final separate diagnostics found **zero full-draft skill scans for twelve unrelated keys** in both Chat and New Session, down from twelve on the original feature. Ten people/eight skill chips and exact raw text survived; one editor remained mounted and stylesheet rules did not grow during typing. A final bounded 21-round-trip session lifecycle replay also passed on baseline and candidate; this is not a universal no-leak claim.

### Acceptance rule — unchanged

Baseline `491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3` already contains the final merged mention foundation. Compare same-toolchain production builds with at least ten serial rotating baseline/candidate/identical-baseline rounds. Report median, p95, ranges and host load; keep traced diagnostics separate. Require no correctness loss, unexpected RPCs, per-key remounts/owner-echo transactions or unbounded resource growth. Median regression must be at most 5% with no worse p95; unresolved tails need confirmation. A confirmed move above 20% blocks blanket performance acceptance. Existing asset limits remain unchanged. Mock-renderer, live-Gateway and native-device evidence remain separate.

### Final production-build timings

Chromium `156.0.8078.4`, Linux x64, real production UI with a synthetic Gateway. These are **renderer main-thread CPU milliseconds per action**, not per-key latency, INP, total process CPU or live-provider latency. Long typing is twelve trusted characters in a 64 KiB draft; mixed drafts contain ten people/eight skills. Paste is 256 KiB synthetic clipboard input. Catalog size is 200. Each row has ten observations per variant; each cell is **median / p95**. A/A is an identical baseline.

| Flow | Baseline | Final candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat person-only long | 55.567 / 60.265 | 55.551 / 60.269 | 56.480 / 59.302 |
| Chat mixed long | 52.028 / 58.309 | 54.160 / 57.572 | 54.125 / 56.980 |
| Chat literal dollars | 38.862 / 43.498 | 39.343 / 42.133 | 38.111 / 45.286 |
| New Session person-only long | 52.058 / 54.542 | 53.371 / 58.238 | 53.519 / 57.152 |
| New Session mixed long | 45.783 / 50.206 | 46.555 / 55.102 | 46.154 / 49.780 |
| New Session mixed paste | 23.195 / 25.057 | 23.746 / 26.502 | 22.933 / 25.102 |
| Chat first skill, including first dollar | 47.118 / 52.273 | 87.230 / 91.677 | 48.570 / 52.067 |
| New Session first skill, including first dollar | 45.679 / 49.449 | 74.020 / 81.182 | 44.615 / 48.706 |

The original mixed-typing median regressions were +8.39% Chat and +8.97% New Session. Final mixed medians are +4.10% and +1.69% versus baseline, and +0.06% and +0.87% versus A/A. This supports removal of the measured hot-path waste, not universal parity: New Session person/mixed/paste p95 are still +6.78%, +9.75% and +5.77% versus baseline. The complete acceptance rule therefore remains unmet.

**First-use work is not hidden in preparation.** New `first-skill` workloads start from an untouched native draft and include the first dollar, catalog readiness, typing the query, selecting the skill and settling imports. Older `activate-skill` rows measured selection after typing the query; they are selection-only evidence, not cold first-use parity. Native-to-rich first-use cost remains approximately +40.1 ms in Chat and +28.3 ms in New Session. At the earlier `08ec3b39` stage, short skill-only typing was 20.170 → 36.529 ms and 200 occurrences were 64.712 → 127.286 ms. Those are native-versus-rich feature costs, not all attributable to parsing, and are not waived or claimed as final-head measurements.

Final CPU ranges: Chat mixed baseline 49.655–58.309 / candidate 51.451–57.572 ms; New Session mixed baseline 45.098–50.206 / candidate 44.695–55.102 ms; Chat first-skill baseline 46.277–52.273 / candidate 85.950–91.677 ms; New Session first-skill baseline 43.821–49.449 / candidate 70.785–81.182 ms. Final host load ranged 1.95–6.04 on 128 logical CPUs. Complete distributions and per-run manifests remain in the linked task under `catalog-final-summary.txt`, `catalog-final.log.summary.json`, and raw observations. No outliers were removed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, prior evidence and scope</summary>

The committed workload extends `scripts/lib/control-ui-chat-composer-scenarios.ts`, using the existing engine runner. With matched baseline and candidate builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --compare-source-root . \
  --control-source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --engines chromium --viewport desktop --pairs 10 \
  --steps composer-qualification-chat-first-skill,composer-qualification-new-first-skill,composer-qualification-chat-literal-dollar,composer-qualification-chat-person-long,composer-qualification-chat-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-person-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-paste \
  --output .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/rerun
```

Earlier qualification of `6d45233` retained 510 editing/activation and 62 startup observations, 157 browser cases, eight emulated narrow/dark observations, four scan diagnostics, profiles and bounded retention. Its boot CPU and heap results are historical evidence, not a fresh final-head certification. Earlier repairs retained their own exact-source summaries; only the final table above qualifies the current product tree.

The simplify pass preserves the existing foreign-DOM owner and CodeMirror extension contract. No dependency, editor, overlay, global cache, custom Markdown parser or permission change was added. Necessary growth covers the skill feature, selective invalidation, native history and catalog notification/disposal. Versus `491c2944`, production UI is +714/−263 lines, tests +488/−19, and benchmark code +359/−1. Net test growth is 469 lines; the documented per-change allocation is 69 beyond the standard 400 for reproduced handoff, Markdown, lazy-loading and catalog/identity failures. Startup/performance limits were not raised.

</details>

### Startup asset gate — still failed

Final normalized largest-JS gzip is **569,985 → 570,497 bytes (+512)**. The inherited-over-cap differential permits only 64 bytes: **448 bytes remain over the allowed increase**. Original feature growth was +676 bytes; this repair does not claim the remaining failure is harmless. Chat/New boot gzip grows 539/486 bytes; request counts remain 21/17. CSS bytes and request counts are unchanged. The boot manifest was regenerated without a source diff. No unrelated byte-offset changes or budget increases were used.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --dist dist/control-ui --base-dist .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui --json`. The strict comparison exits 1. Inherited absolute CSS/request overages are distinguished from this new differential failure.

### Remaining limits

This is a verified repair update to a draft, not a shipping or zero-regression claim. Startup size, native-to-rich feature cost and remaining p95 regressions are unresolved. WebKit/Firefox could not load the app under the environment's proxy policy on either build; no bypass was attempted. Native OS IME, mobile Safari, real-device/network and live Gateway/provider performance remain unqualified. Composition browser tests simulate events, not a physical input method. No merge or deployment occurred.

The existing inspected visual evidence is retained; this repair changes computation and correctness, not the chip design. Captures use the real UI with a synthetic Gateway; mobile is an emulated 390px viewport.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/124475c8-50a5-40d7-876f-139275c99a14)

prs.title: fix(update): refuse Gateway-started updates on Windows Scheduled Task installs
prs.body:
## Summary

Updates started from the Gateway (Control UI, chat, automatic updates) on a Windows Scheduled Task install never finish. The task ends up disabled, the Gateway stays stopped, and the package is unchanged. This PR refuses those handoffs before any mutation, with a message that points to a terminal update. Terminal `openclaw update` keeps working.

This is a mitigation, not the full fix. Gateway-started Windows updates are refused rather than repaired. See "Full fix needs a decision" below.

Refs #169844
Refs #199617
Refs #164639

## Root cause

The Gateway spawns the managed update helper `detached`, and the helper spawns the updater. On Windows, libuv's detached spawn does not set `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`. Both processes therefore stay in the Scheduled Task's kill-on-close Job: the launcher Job from `bindWindowsTaskLauncher` / proc-safe `bindCurrentProcessLifetimeTo`, plus Task Scheduler's own Job.

During activation the updater disables the task and stops it (`schtasks /Change /DISABLE`, then `/End`). Ending the task ends the Job, and that kills the helper and the updater. Nothing is left to swap the package or re-enable and restart the task.

## Native evidence (Crabbox AWS, Windows Server 2025, Node 24.22.1, Scheduled Task Gateway)

| Installed (updater) | Lane | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.5-beta.2 | `update.run` → npm beta (beta.3) | Validation passed, then stuck at `activating`. Task Disabled, 0 node processes, readyz down, CLI still beta.2. |
| 2026.11.5-beta.2 | Same, with a watcher outside the Job (`IsProcessInJob`) | Helper (parent = Gateway) and updater both show `job`. Within 1.5 s of the task becoming Disabled, every task descendant, helper and updater included, is gone. |
| 2026.11.3 (stable) | `update.run` → npm beta (beta.3) | Same stranding: task Disabled, 0 node processes, run stuck `activating`. |
| this branch | `update.run` | See "Proof on this head" |

Terminal `openclaw update` runs outside the task's Job and passes. It is covered daily by the update matrix's Windows lanes.

## What changed

`admitManagedHandoffSupervisor` (in `update-managed-service-handoff-service.ts`) now owns the admission of Gateway-started handoffs. It throws `UpdatePreMutationError("managed-service-handoff-failed")` for the `schtasks` supervisor, and keeps the existing systemd admission unchanged. `startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff` calls it before any spawn, lease, or service mutation. Foreground (terminal-origin) handoffs skip it, as before.

All three callers surface the refusal without stopping anything:
- `update.run` records `managed-service-handoff-failed`;
- the in-Gateway `openclaw update` handoff reports it;
- the startup auto-update reports it.

## Full fix needs a decision

Gateway-started updates can only work on Windows if the helper and updater run outside the task's Job. The options are:

1. A proc-safe spawn with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`. This also needs `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK` on the launcher Job, and Task Scheduler's Job must allow breakaway.
2. A one-shot Scheduled Task that launches the helper.
3. A WMI `Win32_Process.Create` launch.

Options 2 and 3 replace the helper's stdio control pipes, so the park handshake protocol has to change. Any of them touches the lifecycle authority boundary. Until one is chosen, the refusal turns a guaranteed outage into a visible, actionable message.

## Tests

- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts`: the new test "refuses a Windows Scheduled Task handoff before spawning the updater" fails on base (the promise resolved with a started handoff) and passes with the fix. The launch-metadata case no longer covers `schtasks`. The full file passes 71/71.
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-settlement-control.test.ts` passes.
- `tsgo:core`, oxfmt and oxlint pass.

## Reviews

- autoreview: scoped-clean at P2.
- Independent `codex exec` read-only review: NO FINDINGS. It covered the gate placement, all three callers, foreground reachability and the message.

## Proof on this head

prs.title: fix(memory): prevent Forget worker OOM on large live transcripts
prs.body:
Related: #176243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a worker out-of-memory failure when Memory Forget inspects a large live SQLite transcript containing original messages.

## Memory impact

**Historical matched benchmark: 59.67% lower median sampled process-tree PSS high water** — 2,070,743,040 → 835,210,240 bytes (1.93 → 0.78 GiB; 1,178.3 MiB less). This is the median of five per-run sampled maxima, not steady-state memory or a true peak.

**Current PR candidate: memory reduction NOT MEASURED.** Those five interleaved pairs measured an older pre-extraction candidate, before helper relocation, CI metadata repairs and main integration changed shared worker/dependency inputs. They are historical evidence, not performance acceptance for this head.

- Workload: real compiled offline Memory Forget CLI preview, synthetic ASCII transcript, 34,401 events / 463,059,747 JSONL bytes; Node 26.12.1, unchanged 512/32 MiB worker limits. Nominal 25 ms sampling sums observed process-tree PSS, including the timing wrapper; Worker-thread RSS is not added.
- **Main-isolate heap reduction, whole-process RSS reduction and true-peak reduction: NOT MEASURED by this comparison.** No percentage for those metrics or for general workloads is claimed.
- Tradeoff: a 463,162,950-byte private temporary export (about 442 MiB), removed on normal completion; crash leftovers remain possible.
- The earlier cohort still **FAILED** both wall/CPU STOP thresholds (candidate 27.356 s / 16.74 s CPU versus baseline 6.914 s / 8.60 s CPU). Later pairs do not erase that failure or establish its cause; the original archived incident remains unproved.

Exact historical patch/workload bindings, all five paired values, method limits and retained failures are in Evidence below.

## User Impact

Users can inspect/forget large live-session history without a full decoded worker reply, preserving snapshot/reset/provenance/failure ordering. No heap-limit, schema, config, or retention change.

The operation uses temporary disk proportional to the transcript: the measured fixture needs a 463,162,950-byte private export (463,163,392 allocated bytes, about 442 MiB). Normal completion removes it; a process crash can leave that private export behind. The exact archived transcript from the issue is unavailable, so this PR does not claim to reproduce or resolve every retained-archive failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing export owner captures an immutable snapshot under its fence/version contract. The acknowledged exchange returns a compact descriptor. Native reader settlement and validation precede callbacks. Replay preserves originals/order; archive/incognito/public array contracts are unchanged.

Operation-local writer/reader buffers grow as needed and use initialized prefixes, eliminating per-record churn and combining frame writes. No global cache, mutable-page callbacks, heap increase, or skipped native join.

## Evidence

- Regression proof: the base original-snapshot worker reply exceeded the 4 KiB contract (74,283 bytes); the bounded-source candidate returned a 260-byte descriptor while preserving callback snapshot semantics.
- Pre-buffer product proof: Unicode/equal-byte ASCII sources, each 34,401 events / 463,059,747 JSONL bytes, actual 512/32 MiB limits. Preview/apply/repeat/since/refusal preserved source/control/origins/tombstones. Prior-head evidence, not a revised-head large-Unicode/model/Gateway run.
- Revised-head focused proof: 63 tests across nine affected files passed, including real-worker snapshot, callback/reset/read-hold/custody paths. The new framing regression is red before buffer reuse and green after it: exact independent Unicode framing, long-to-short records, independent yielded objects, short I/O, and a truncated tail. Three frames plus a forced short write used one writer backing store / four writes; replay used header and payload stores / eight reads including short read and EOF. Only the narrow framing test mocks its database I/O source.
- Scoped production/test typechecks, typed lint, formatting/whitespace checks, and the canonical build passed. The build retained its existing nonfatal locale-size diagnostic. Broad exact-head CI is reported separately by GitHub, not inferred from local success.
- Normal hooks moved two helpers byte-for-byte into the already-imported projection sibling; 41 consumer tests, types, lint and hooks passed. Build/cost evidence predates that move and main integration.

- Integration follow-up: merged main `4d294053ad54`, including #180315’s native-subagent expectation fix, and repaired the newer scheduled-turns expectation from #180282. That case failed before the one-line fix; six affected cases and 33 transcript tests then passed, plus targeted types/lint/format. Candidate review: 19 partitioned passes, no actionable findings; static only. Old CI run 39722865071 remains failed; new-head CI is separate.

### Completed revised-candidate cost comparison

Five predeclared interleaved pairs ran once each: no warmups, discarded/replaced samples, or forced GC. Once-seeded variants matched transcript/table/control facts, normalized config/runtime/time/workload hashes. Real compiled offline CLI preview retained worker limits. All functional/protected-state/default-limit/process-settlement/cleanup checks passed.

| Pair | Baseline wall ms | Candidate wall ms | Baseline waited CPU µs | Candidate waited CPU µs | Baseline observed tree-PSS B | Candidate observed tree-PSS B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6656.329451 | 4315.143755 | 8260000 | 6730000 | 2116646912 | 835210240 |
| 2 | 5267.495488 | 4256.881545 | 8080000 | 6800000 | 2051841024 | 837079040 |
| 3 | 5039.606078 | 4209.454111 | 7720000 | 6820000 | 2060108800 | 819704832 |
| 4 | 6039.779969 | 5029.855176 | 8310000 | 7640000 | 2089146368 | 835561472 |
| 5 | 7723.621762 | 5821.617906 | 9260000 | 8030000 | 2070743040 | 789981184 |

Written gate: stop immediately if candidate paired wall or waited CPU exceeds baseline by more than 20%, or functional/default-limit/coverage/cleanup checks fail. Require median and nearest-rank p95 wall/CPU to hold or improve, and median observed-PSS reduction of at least min(5 MiB, 2% of baseline median). All five pairs pass. Median wall improves 28.55% (6039.779969 → 4315.143755 ms), CPU 17.43% (8260000 → 6820000 µs), and observed PSS 59.67% (2070743040 → 835210240 B). Median PSS reduction is 1,235,532,800 B versus the 5,242,880 B floor. Nearest-rank p95 with n=5 is the maximum: wall 7723.621762 → 5821.617906 ms; CPU 9260000 → 8030000 µs; PSS 2116646912 → 837079040 B.

**Limits:** nominal 25 ms sampled tree-PSS is observed high water, not true peak. GNU Time user+system covers waited descendants, not orphan/cgroup-total; Node exit CPU only crosschecks it. Known timing-wrapper PSS is included; Worker RSS is not added. A5 maximum interval was 57.297481 ms versus candidate maximum 26.054988 ms. All gaps/variable loads retained, no filtering/noise waiver. Five pairs do not establish population tails. Both used current Node 26.12.1, not the earlier failed cohort runtime.

### Earlier failed comparison remains failed

Before buffer reuse, a separate first pair measured baseline 6913.909567 ms / 8600000 µs CPU versus candidate 27356.483281 ms / 16740000 µs. Both +20% STOP thresholds fired. That cohort remains failed, never replaced. Excess wall followed an early JS exit marker; later-JS/native teardown cause is unidentified. Two unscored diagnostics did not reproduce it and were not clearance. New qualification does not prove buffers/runtime caused the old tail.

Independent review completed four P0–P3 passes with all 15 pre-extraction files supplied in full plus unchanged owners; context was partitioned, not all modules in each pass. Native findings / exit 1 remains: four P2 entries described ONE qualification gap, addressed by independently crosschecked five-pair evidence. No other actionable functional/security defect established.

### Historical benchmark provenance and cleanup

The task-specific 612-line benchmark harness has been removed from this PR's current diff; production code and product-boundary regression tests are unchanged by that cleanup. Results remain above, including the failed cohort and measurement limits. No replacement benchmark PR or new benchmark run was made.

Cleanup verification: the only source change from pre-cleanup `0794052e2497` is deletion of that harness; every retained production and regression-test blob is identical. Reference/whitespace checks, normal commit hooks and a fresh P0–P3 deletion review passed. The PR shrank from 20 files (+1,432/−125) to 19 (+820/−125). An installed npm 11.20.0 `pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` inventory listed 15,617 files with zero matches for the removed harness or `scripts/perf/`. It ran no lifecycle scripts, wrote no tarball and did not build; it checked the current package manifest against existing older dist artifacts, not fresh release packaging or runtime behavior.

The exact historical harness is retained in [pre-cleanup commit 0794052e2497db6e0c76d47a6d31b02c7b1cea65](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0794052e2497db6e0c76d47a6d31b02c7b1cea65/scripts/perf/memory-forget-measure.mjs), SHA256 `56ec30ac3e7acd02a76184fa4257741f9480d8778251ac8cac00671764e9688f`. That commit preserves the harness, not a claim that its integrated production tree was benchmarked. The measured production patch is bound separately below. Historical raw receipts, the failed cohort and two unscored diagnostics remain retained privately; no private logs or heap data are published.

Measured pre-extraction full-patch SHA256 `1725077016f16ea7c5c4dbbb4bdbc7e934bc8429b0c1ef11457c6aaa4e1e1ea0`; workload `56ec30ac3e7acd02a76184fa4257741f9480d8778251ac8cac00671764e9688f`. Build/cost results predate helper relocation, CI metadata repairs and main `4d294053ad54` integration. Shared worker/dependency inputs changed: these are NOT measurements of this integrated head. Synthetic origins prove purge selection, not model promotion. Populated-vector purge uses existing tests, not this fixture. No new large-Unicode product run, exact archived-incident reproduction, crash-leftover cleanup guarantee, or merge/CI approval is implied.

prs.title: fix(release): qualify frozen candidates with independent tooling
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release-tooling repairs should not require changing the frozen product candidate. This completes the admitted C/Q/P split, including recovery and publication consumers. Related: #193030.

## User Impact

Operators can keep product candidate **C** unchanged while explicitly selecting immutable, reviewed qualification tooling **Q** and trusted admission/publication tooling **P**. Q defaults to C; independent Q must pass main-ancestry verification and P must authenticate the exact C/Q tuple, transport and complete inputs. Nothing silently substitutes moving main.

Product bytes, package/version identity and candidate baselines remain C-owned. Qualification harnesses and publisher-policy checks use their authenticated original Q; P retains admission and publication authority.

## Changes

- Carry distinct C/Q through requests, admission, verified inventory capture/replay, immutable plans, receipts, final verification and retained artifact consumers.
- Correct receipt recovery, plugin npm adoption/readback, supplemental Telegram and isolated Parallels harness selection. Preserve original producer identities rather than relabeling old evidence.
- Permit child reuse only after immutable workload equivalence plus existing provenance, inputs, artifact digests, attempt and candidate-binding checks. Normal CI compares its workflow closure, scripts/actions, root files and complete config/packages/src/test trees. Other roles conservatively compare all workflows and the full root tree.
- Keep admitted release qualification strict: independent Q must not activate historical diagnostic scenario-omission behavior.
- Update release skills with when to change C, Q or P, explicit frozen-Q commands, the prequalified-FRV checklist route, and recovery/requalification rules.

**Tradeoff:** changing shared scripts invalidates every child; changes inside normal CI's conservatively retained harness trees also invalidate that child. This implementation does not establish cross-Q eligibility for the five historical green receipts. Failed workloads remain failures; coverage, soak, platforms, policy grants and successful final-FRV requirements are not weakened.

## Validation

- Original CLI suites: 131 passed; core admission/plan/final verification: 217 passed (two existing skipped); final changed-core replay: 114 passed; sibling identity/search/harness/artifact suites: 172 passed; retained artifact CLI: 42 passed. Groups overlap; no aggregate count is claimed.
- Follow-up audit: checklist 153 passed; artifact/recovery/validation consumers 132 passed; plugin adoption/readback 66 passed; caller/recovery replay 168 passed; candidate CLI 40 passed. Seven new verified-inventory C≠Q≠P acceptance/rejection cases passed.
- Normal-CI harness regression: four new cases failed before the repair; all 67 child-reuse cases passed afterward.
- Production scripts and tooling-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint/format and task diff whitespace checks passed. Documentation: 16,655 internal links, zero broken; 1,443 MDX files passed.
- Strict omission regression: seven intended failures before repair, 17/17 passed afterward; 117 sibling tests passed. Package-workflow suite: 586 passed, one environment failure because this host lacks zip. The earlier local workflow-linter setup was blocked; see the successful conflict-resolution validation below.
- After committing integration, `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` passed. The earlier summary also named a HEAD-versus-worktree inventory parity test without preserving its exact identifier; that separate result remains unverified and is not claimed passing.
- Test budget: +601 net test lines against integrated main, with 201 explicitly allocated extra lines for distinct production-boundary regressions.

- CI follow-up: run 43762755446 at prior head 4d5a20efbc50cec2161ae8b2215204cf965d8727 exposed a stale cross-Q rejection assertion. Reproduced the failure, then corrected only the test label and expected commit-tree validation error; rejection status and blocker remain required. The two affected suites passed all 200 tests, and the CI-selected replay passed (one selected, 132 skipped). Targeted formatting, lint, whitespace and the unchanged test budget passed.

## Review

The original pre-integration autoreview passed. Integration autoreview and one retry failed during execution, not with a verdict. At the author's explicit request, an independent read-only subagent reviewed all 53 changed-file diffs against integrated main abaf2ced62fc8a29426ce69864560196e7b9bec8. It found a normal-CI harness-closure issue; a focused follow-up confirmed the repair. Hosted review independently raised that issue, strict omission mode, and stale documentation-test wording; all are addressed.

prs.title: feat(slack): show streamed reasoning as task rows and roll long native streams into continuation messages
prs.body:
## Summary

Slack's presentation of streamed reasoning (`agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "stream"`) is broken on `main`, and this PR replaces it rather than adding an alternative:

- **Narration keeps only the head of each reasoning burst.** `formatReasoningProgressDisplayLine` → `compactProgressText` keeps the start of the buffer (`chars.slice(0, end) + "…"`), so once a burst passes ~118 characters every later delta yields the same line and nothing further reaches Slack. The code calls it a rolling row; in practice it shows the burst's opening sentence. A recorded run on `main` sent 3,047 characters of reasoning to Slack as two ~120-character rows. The same compacted line is the native path's narration.
- **The fallbacks disagree.** With `nativeTransport: false` the frozen head rows stay on the card after the turn; when Slack refuses native streaming for a channel the fallback card is deleted after the answer, so reasoning shown during the turn disappears.
- **Long turns lose their stream.** Slack documents that "a streamed response has a time limit of 10 minutes" ([agent design guide](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/agent-design/)), and it holds regardless of appends (measured: appends every 20 s rejected ~605–611 s after `chat.startStream`; idle appends accepted at 8 min, rejected at 12 min). After that both `appendStream` and `stopStream` fail with `message_not_in_streaming_state`. `main` has no rollover, so any native turn past ~10 minutes, reasoning or not, loses its progress message.
- **Answers are lost on `msg_too_long`, and a late boundary can stop the stream under the answer.** Fixed by the first two commits, also up on their own as #199849 with a real-Slack trace.

Slack's `plan` block is the structure built for this: collapsible rows with per-row details, rendered in the web client and the iOS app (both checked), and accepted in ordinary `chat.postMessage` / `chat.update` messages as well as streams. So no client or transport needs the text form, and this PR has no presentation setting.

## What changes

- **Streamed reasoning renders as 🧠 task rows** on the native progress card, interleaved in order with tool rows and collapsed under `Thought for <n>s, <k> tool calls` when the turn ends. The compacted reasoning narration line is removed. Model commentary (visible text between tool calls) is unchanged. With reasoning off, the card shows tool rows exactly as on `main`.
- **Every native progress turn becomes a chain of messages when it needs one.** The current message is sealed (`Thinking, continued below`, open rows completed) and the turn continues in a new message in the same thread when the next update would exceed the size budget, 50 rows (Slack stops showing rows past 50), or 8 minutes of stream age (ahead of Slack's 10-minute close). A plan of any size spreads over as many messages as it needs, every step exactly once. Short turns stay on one message: every exact chunk sequence in `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` passes unchanged.
- **The answer always arrives.** It goes under the cards on the last message when it fits, otherwise in its own message; if Slack still rejects it, it is posted through the normal reply path and the stream is closed (commit 2).
- **The quiet card (`toolProgress: false`) shows no reasoning text**; its summary row is otherwise unchanged.
- **No new configuration.** The schema, types, UI hints, plugin SDK surface and generated config files are identical to `main`.

Other visible effects for turns that roll or show reasoning: the detailed card no longer evicts rows (a message that cannot hold more rolls instead), so running rows are not painted complete early and errored rows keep their title.

## Commits

1. `fix(slack): keep the final reply on its stream when a progress boundary lands during delivery` (also in #199849)
2. `fix(slack): post the answer when Slack rejects a native stream with msg_too_long` (also in #199849)
3. `feat(slack): render streamed reasoning as task rows on the native progress card`
4. `feat(slack): roll long native progress streams into continuation messages`

Net production change against `main`: +2,370 / -214 (net +2,156). Tests and the shared dispatch harness: +2,768 / -20, with the remaining growth recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/143882-slack-reasoning-cards.txt` (2,348).

## How it works

- **Rows (commit 3):** reasoning is merged through the compositor's existing merge, split into segments of about 240 characters at word boundaries and pushed as task rows (`reasoning:<n>`, complete except the newest). A tool call or the end of a reasoning phase seals the open segment before the tool row is admitted. Row titles are capped at 250 characters, our own cap below the 256 Slack documents (the API does not enforce 256). The compositor option it uses (`reasoningLine`) stays internal; there is no new public plugin SDK export.
- **Size model (commit 4), measured against Slack:** `chat.startStream` / `chat.appendStream` reject a message with `msg_too_long` once the plan block, serialized as Slack stores it (compact JSON, non-ASCII as `\uXXXX`), plus the markdown text exceeds 13,200 units, and markdown alone is capped at 12,000 characters. Markdown costs one per character except emoji, which cost their `:shortcode:` length (`:+1:` 4, `:brain:` 7, `:white_check_mark:` 18). Row titles, `details` and `output` share that limit; a row adds a fixed ~46 plus its id, each `details`/`output` field a one-off 132; the plan title is not counted. The ledger (`stream-size.ts`) mirrors that model and rounds up where Slack's cost varies (every row counted as in progress, an emoji in markdown as 20, in `details` as 80), so it can only overcount; a test checks that every measured boundary message counts at or above Slack's ceiling. Budgets sit about 20% under: 10,500 total, 9,600 text, 7,000 rows (at least 3,500 left for an answer), plus 50 rows and 8 minutes of age (`SLACK_STREAM_MESSAGE_MAX_AGE_MS`).
- **Message chain (commit 4):** when the next update would not fit, or the message is expiring, the message is sealed and a new stream continues in the thread, and the chain keeps rolling while plan steps remain that have not appeared in their current status. It builds on `main`'s `rotateInterruptedStream` (one `sealStream` operation for human interruptions and rollover; the thread is kept as `interruptedThreadTs`) and keeps `main`'s `nativeFinalThreadTs` / `canFinishNativeFinal`, snapshot reset and rotation paths.
- **Stop:** a Stop during a roll leaves the stopped session current, so nothing new starts, as `main` already does for a turn-level Stop.

Follow-ups, separate because they touch other transports: rows on the Block Kit fallback card via `chat.update` (also ending its delete-after-turn inconsistency) and in the final message when streaming is off.

## Evidence

### This head (local)

Base `main` `e693b3323`, Node 26.13.0, pnpm 12.15.0.

- `pnpm test:extension slack`: 1,976 tests passed (1,959 plus 17 in the second shard), 0 failed. Commit 3 alone: 1,928.
- Size model: every measured boundary message counts at or above 13,194 in the ledger; budget and admission expectations follow the measured costs.
- Plans: a 20-step plan of 120 CJK characters per step (~15,800 units) spreads over at least three messages, each step exactly once, with the answer on the last, both while the turn runs and at closeout; red before the fix (4 of 20 steps were lost).
- Age roll: a slow tool-only turn past 8 minutes rolls and seals its tool rows complete; a slow sparse think rolls and lands the answer; an answer arriving after the age limit streams as its own message; ledger `expiring` unit test. With the constant raised to 80 minutes the dispatcher age tests fail.
- Tool-only turns: a short turn stays on one message; 120-tool turns cover the row-cap and size rolls. Quiet card: no payload carries reasoning text.
- `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts`: every test passes unchanged except the removed narration-variant test.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base e693b3323`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm lint:docs`, oxfmt, oxlint, `git diff --check`: clean. `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` fails with identical numbers on a clean `main`.

### Measurements behind the design (real Slack, 2026-11-15/16)

- Stream lifetime: two streams appended every 20 s were rejected at ~605 s and ~611 s after start (with and without recipient fields); idle streams accepted appends at 4, 5, 6 and 8 minutes and rejected at 12. `chat.stopStream` after the close fails the same way.
- Size limit: exact boundary searches (n accepted, n+1 rejected) on `chat.startStream` and `chat.appendStream`: 12,000 characters of ASCII or of a 3-byte character are accepted alike (so not UTF-8 bytes); emoji cost their shortcode length (3,300 × `:+1:`, 1,885 × `:brain:`, 942 × `:technologist:`, 733 × `:white_check_mark:`, each totalling ~13,200); rows plus text sum to exactly 13,200 at 1, 3,000, 6,000, 8,172 and 11,000 characters of text; a single 20,000-character title and a 20,000-character plan title are accepted.
- `plan` block outside streams: the block a finished stream stores (`plan` with `tasks[]`, `details`, `output`) is accepted by `chat.postMessage` and `chat.update`, and renders as the same collapsible card in the web client and the iOS app (rows open in a sheet; a tool row's details and output expand).
- `main`'s reasoning narration: code trace above, plus a recorded run of stock `main` (Block Kit card, native refused at start and mid-turn, streaming off).

### Live Slack (`cf24f454`, real Slack, 2026-11-15)

Run on `cf24f454`, where the rows still needed `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "cards"` (variant B below); on this head that is the only behavior when reasoning streams, so variant B is what every reasoning turn now renders, and variant A shows the narration this PR removes. That build measured size in UTF-8 bytes (the `weighted bytes` in its log lines); the age roll, tool-only rollover, plan spreading and the measured size model were added after this run and are covered by dispatcher tests.

Gateway built from this head in a Linux x86_64 container, Socket Mode, a real hosted reasoning model with `reasoningDefault: "stream"`, driven from the Slack web client. Variant A is the default config; variant B adds only `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "cards"`.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Default narration | PASS: one message per turn, no `rolled`/`msg_too_long`/fallback lines, answer delivered |
| Cards + continuation | PASS: `message 1 rolled (budget; 5740 weighted bytes, 24 rows)`, `message 2 rolled (budget; 5401 …, 25 rows)`, answer with all 8 pairs on message 3, no `msg_too_long` |
| Stop during rollover | PASS via the text stop trigger (`stop` reply, same abort path) about 3 s after a roll: run aborted, message 2 finalized, no further rolls, no fallback answer. The native Stop button was not testable: the test app does not subscribe to `agent_session_stopped` |
| Final answer | PASS (Case 2): answer streamed under the cards on the last message |

Screenshots are cropped to the thread's messages; sender names and avatars are blurred.

![Default narration (variant A): the long-reasoning prompt stays one message, narration lines around the Exec card, no 🧠 rows, no continuation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case1-narration-c2-2-final.png)

![Cards (variant B): message 1 sealed as `Thinking, continued below` while message 2 `Thinking, continued` streams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case2-cards-2-msg1-rolled-msg2-started.png)

![Cards: two continued messages, then `Thought for 32s, 2 tool calls` with the complete answer on message 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case2-cards-4-final-answer.png)

![Cards, message 2 expanded: 🧠 rows, the Exec row on the message current when the tool ran, post-tool rows below](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case2-cards-6-msg2-expanded-exec-row.png)

![Stop during rollover: message 2 finalized `Thought for 12s`, the stop reply, `Agent was aborted.`, no third message, no fallback answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case3-stop-2-after-aborted.png)

<details>
<summary>Full redacted transcript: config shape, prompts, every screenshot, log excerpts, all attempts</summary>

Run date: 2026-11-15 (UTC). Client: Slack web client (Playwright, Chromium), signed in as the only allow-listed user.
The bot is a Slack Agent View app, connected over Socket Mode. Replies arrive as a thread under each top-level DM.

##### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Host | Linux x86_64 container |
| Node | v24.22.3 |
| OpenClaw | 2026.11.3, built from PR head `cf24f454cfc6c909509b8e7cf68c43aa492342f7` |
| Model | `<provider>/<model>` (OpenAI-compatible endpoint `<model-endpoint>`), `thinkingDefault: high`, `reasoningDefault: stream` |
| Slack connection | Socket Mode. At every gateway start the log showed a single `socket mode connected` with no "2 active connections" warning (see the note on the first attempt below). |

###### Config shape (secrets are env SecretRefs; ids replaced)

The variants differ in one key only: `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning`.

```json5
{
  gateway: { mode: "local", bind: "loopback", auth: { mode: "token", token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}" } },
  models: { providers: { "<provider>": { baseUrl: "https://<model-endpoint>/v1", apiKey: "${MODEL_API_KEY}", api: "openai-completions",
    models: [{ id: "<model>", reasoning: true, contextWindow: 131072, maxTokens: 32768 }] } } },
  agents: { defaults: { model: { primary: "<provider>/<model>" }, thinkingDefault: "high", reasoningDefault: "stream" } },
  channels: { slack: {
    enabled: true, mode: "socket", botToken: "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}", appToken: "${SLACK_APP_TOKEN}",
    dmPolicy: "allowlist", allowFrom: ["<U-user>"], groupPolicy: "allowlist",
    replyToModeByChatType: { direct: "all" },
    streaming: { mode: "progress", progress: {
      nativeTaskCards: true, toolProgress: true,
      // Variant A (narration): key absent (default "narration")

```

###### Prompts

- **N1** (chosen so no host details appear on screen): ``Use the exec tool to run `python3 -c "import math; print(sum(range(10)), math.factorial(5))"`. Then think about what that output says, and reply with three short bullets.``
- **C2** (long private reasoning, one exec call, then more reasoning; full text visible in the screenshots), with one change: the verification command is wrapped in backticks. Without them, Slack's composer turns the straight quotes into curly quotes, which would break the command. The harness checked that the composer held straight quotes before sending.

###### Screenshot hygiene

- Each image is an element-clip of the thread pane's message list. No sidebar, header, search or composer.
- Before each capture the harness blurred, with CSS `filter: blur(8px)`, all avatars, the sender names (user and bot), the thread header, and every element whose text contains either display name. That includes the "<bot> is working" status row.
- For each capture the harness logged how many name-bearing elements were still visible without blur. Every capture logged 0.

---

##### Case 1: default narration (variant A): **PASS**

  ![case2-cards-6-msg2-expanded-exec-row.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case2-cards-6-msg2-expanded-exec-row.png)

7. `slack/case2-cards-7-msg3-expanded-final.png`: message 3 expanded. Final 🧠 rows, a `Recovered: Message failed` row (see caveat), then the answer.

  ![case2-cards-7-msg3-expanded-final.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case2-cards-7-msg3-expanded-final.png)


Log (`cards.log`, redacted):

```
[slack] socket mode connected
slack-stream: native progress message 1 rolled (budget; 5740 weighted bytes, 24 rows); continuing in a new message
slack-stream: native progress message 2 rolled (budget; 5401 weighted bytes, 25 rows); continuing in a new message
[tools] message failed: OutboundDeliveryError: An API error occurred: missing_scope (needed: ...im:write; granted: ...)
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=slack chatId=team:<T-team>:user:<U-user> ... outcome=completed
```

- Thinking volume for this turn (`thinking-size.mjs`): 9,584 bytes before the exec call and 3,705 bytes after it, with 0 bytes of visible text in between.
- `grep -E "msg_too_long|falling back|native progress stream failed"` → **no matches**.
- No `finished at ... streaming the answer as a new message` line: the answer fit under the cards on message 3 (Case 4's first branch).
- The answer was complete: (20,165) (27,164) (45,160) (60,155) (83,144) (88,141) (101,132) (115,120).

Caveats, stated plainly:
- **Tool count.** The final title says "2 tool calls", not 1. The model made one `exec` call. It also called the `message` tool to send the table as a presentation block, and that call failed on a test-app scope gap (`im:write` not granted). OpenClaw recovered and streamed the answer normally. Afterwards the gateway's delivery-recovery kept retrying that failed message-tool send every 5 s until the gateway was stopped. Nothing extra was posted. This comes from the test app's scopes, not from the PR's streaming code.
- **Roll sizes.** Across all cards-mode runs the roll lines read 5740/24, 5401/25, 6025/25, 6080/25, 5018/21, 5026/23 and 5269/22 (weighted bytes/rows). These are that build's UTF-8 byte counts; every roll stayed under its budgets and the 50-task cap, and none hit `msg_too_long`.

##### Case 3: Stop during rollover (variant B, fresh state): **PASS via the text-stop fallback; the native Stop button could not be tested**

Why there is no native Stop:
- On the first streamed update the gateway logged `Slack's Stop button is unavailable until the app subscribes to agent_session_stopped`. The test app lacks that event subscription, so no Stop control is rendered. The DOM search for a Stop button found none.
- Slack's client rejects a literal `/stop` typed in a thread (Slack replied "/stop is not supported in threads"), so it never reaches the bot.
- In the PR build, the Slack message handler runs `isAbortRequestText` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts`). That accepts `/stop` or any word in `ABORT_TRIGGERS` (`src/auto-reply/reply/abort-trigger-text.ts`: "stop", "abort", …). So the fallback used was a plain thread reply `stop`. It reaches the same abort path, but it is not the `agent_session_stopped` / `markSlackStreamsStopped` path that the native button would use.

Attempts (reported in full):
1. **Missed:** harness locator bug, nothing sent. The run completed normally: 1 roll (6025/25), answer delivered.
2. **Missed:** the trigger waited for a `Thinking, continued` title, but message 2 was titled `Exec`. The run completed: 1 roll (6080/25).
3. **Missed:** the thread-open guard never fired. The run completed: 2 rolls (5018/21, 5026/23).
4. **Missed:** `/stop` was rejected by the Slack client (see above). The run completed normally.
5. **Valid run:** below.

Screenshots (valid run):
- `slack/case3-stop-1-before-msg2-streaming.png`: just before the stop. Message 1 complete as `Thinking, continued below`, message 2 `Thinking, continued` streaming, "is working" status shown.

  ![case3-stop-1-before-msg2-streaming.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case3-stop-1-before-msg2-streaming.png)

- `slack/case3-stop-2-after-aborted.png`: after the stop.

  ![case3-stop-2-after-aborted.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/b91a947061caef11a9e1a99e3aca9cb379b36e0c/pr-143882/case3-stop-2-after-aborted.png)

  - Message 1 still `Thinking, continued below`.
  - Message 2 is finalized as `Thought for 12s`: complete, no longer streaming.
  - The user's `stop` reply follows, then the bot's stop confirmation `⚙️ Agent was aborted.`
  - No third message, no further rows, no answer. The thread stayed unchanged for the following 60 s of polling.

Log (`cards.log`, redacted):

```
21:28:22.801 slack-stream: native progress message 1 rolled (budget; 5269 weighted bytes, 22 rows); continuing in a new message
21:28:25.734 [plugins] [hooks] running run_stopped (1 handlers)
21:28:25.743 [agent/embedded] compaction wait aborted: runId=<run> sessionId=<session>
21:28:25.748 [diagnostic] message processed: ... outcome=skipped                                  # the C2 turn, aborted
21:28:25.760 [turn/execution] visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads: ... cause=skipped:reply_operation_aborted
21:28:25.774 [diagnostic] message processed: ... outcome=completed                                # the "stop" message
21:28:25.869 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=13648 error="agent run aborted" errorName=AbortError
21:28:25.870 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted candidate=<provider>/<model>
21:28:25.889 [slack] delivered reply to channel:<D-channel>                                         # "Agent was aborted." confirmation
```

- After the stop, `grep -E "rolled|streamed delivery failed|falling back|failed to finalize|msg_too_long"` → **no matches**.
- The stop landed about 3 s after the roll. The run aborted, no later roll occurred, no fallback answer was posted, and both progress messages ended in a completed (non-streaming) state.

Not covered: native-Stop variants (Stop on the continuation message, and Stop on the message that just rolled, which targets `streaming_message_ts`). Both need the app to subscribe to `agent_session_stopped`.

##### Other observations

- `slack-stream: users.info team lookup failed (missing_scope)` appears on every stream start. The test app lacks `users:read`, and it is harmless here.
- `assistant_app_thread message_changed ... dropped: no sender resolved from metadata` is logged when Slack edits the thread title. It is harmless.
- **First attempt invalid.** On the first attempt (before this run), a second gateway was connected to the same Slack app and answered the N1 message. Those frames were discarded. Every run reported here started with a single Socket Mode connection.

</details>


### Prior head `ea1a10d` (real Slack, 2026-09-09/10)

The live evidence below was gathered on the previous head; the behavior it covers (card rendering, byte budgets, rollover, the answer-rejected path, the late boundary) is carried over unchanged in substance, but it is prior-head evidence; the live run on this head is above.

- Motivating failure, cards without rollover: a scripted 12,010-character think with one `bash` call rendered 48 rows, then the 92-character answer was rejected with `msg_too_long` (11,215 bytes of titles on the message); the plugin rethrew, never called `chat.stopStream`, and the message stayed `in_progress` without the answer.
- Size probes over the raw SDK (superseded by the exact measurements above; the byte interpretation drawn from them was wrong): 250-character rows accepted through the 42nd (10,571 bytes) and rejected at the 43rd; text-only 9,064 bytes accepted / 12,054 rejected; rows with 100 characters of `details` rejected at 8,821 bytes; 50 emoji-only rows with no body text (22,900 bytes) accepted; 24 emoji rows (10,418 bytes, 8,666 UTF-16 units) rejected a 3,045-character answer. Only UTF-8 bytes fit every run (ceiling about 10,600-11,300 once the message carries text).
- Rollover build: the 12,010-character think rendered as three messages in the thread (`Thinking, continued below` → `Thinking, continued below` → `Thought for 35s, 1 tool call` with the answer), 3 starts / 28 appends / 3 stops, no errors, each stop/start about 300 ms. Emoji-only reasoning rolled at 25 rows / 5,950 bytes over six messages and the 3,045-character answer landed on the last one.
- Real model (OpenClaw gateway from source, Socket Mode, `reasoningDefault: "stream"`): short question and riddle on one message (`Thought for 6s` / `Thought for 10s`); a 25-segment think around one `exec` rolled once and finished `Thought for 59s, 1 tool call` with the answer on the continuation. Before the late-boundary fix (now commit 1) the same setup produced the two defects it addresses: a short answer streamed as a separate message after the card was stopped, and a continuation ending under the preamble headline.

Screenshots from those runs (test workspace, cropped to one thread reply), full sets on the fork's [evidence branch](https://github.com/n1hility/openclaw/tree/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots):

![Short think, no tool call: two 🧠 rows under `Thought for 5s`, answer below the card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s1-short-think.png)

![Long think with one tool call, first of three messages: `Thinking, continued below`, all rows complete](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s2-long-think-msg1-01.png)

![Same turn, third message: the last cards under `Thought for 35s, 1 tool call`, followed by the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s2-long-think-msg3-answer.png)

![Real model over Socket Mode, turn with one `exec` call: the continuation ends with `Thought for 59s, 1 tool call` and carries the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/real-model/rm2-long-msg2-answer.png)

### Not tested

- The native Slack Stop button: the test app does not subscribe to `agent_session_stopped`, so Stop during a rollover was exercised live through the text stop trigger, which takes the same abort path but not `markSlackStreamsStopped`.
- Live: the age roll, tool-only rollover and multi-message plans (dispatcher tests with fake timers and the measured size model); the card roll-and-retry path after a `msg_too_long` on a card update.

<details>
<summary>Review findings addressed on the previous head (all carried over, with their tests)</summary>

Sixteen review findings were fixed across earlier rounds, each with a test that failed on the reviewed head; all of those tests are ported to this head and pass. In short: rejected closeout rows, partial-card extensions and same-title tool-row updates carried to the continuation; queued reasoning rows never evicted by the compositor window; raw reasoning kept across deltas (`reasoningLine`); a Slack Stop honored across continuation messages; rejected SDK text discarded before a rollover stop; queued cards drained through budgeted messages before error, media and silent closeouts and before turn rotation; a rejected completion carried to the message that streams the answer; running tool rows kept across rollovers and frozen rows thawed by a later result; bounded admission (a guard charges every accepted start, append and stop to its message and fails any test where a message passes 50 rows or the byte budget); budgeted narration continuations; tool rows never overtaking queued reasoning; continuation capacity held for queued cards behind a full plan.

</details>

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: docs(voice-call): inboundPolicy "pairing" rejects unknown callers without saying why
prs.body:
Related: #164966

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `inboundPolicy: "pairing"` is a valid voice-call setting that reads like the pairing flow chat channels have, but the docs and config help never say that it only screens callers against `allowFrom`, so an operator who selects it expecting pairing requests gets every unknown caller rejected with no explanation.

## User Impact

User impact: the inbound-calls page and the config help now state what each `inboundPolicy` value accepts and that `pairing` currently behaves like `allowlist` (no pairing code, no approval request; an empty `allowFrom` rejects everyone). No behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the narrow clarification recommended in the review of #164966: document the limitation and leave caller admission as it is. Whether `pairing` should later be implemented, warned about at startup, or retired through a migration stays open on the issue; this PR does not decide it, which is why it links the issue instead of closing it.

- `docs/plugins/voice-call/tts-and-inbound-calls.md`: a four-row table of the policies and a note on `pairing`.
- `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md`: the `allowFrom` row names both policies that read it.
- `extensions/voice-call/openclaw.plugin.json`: `help` text for `inboundPolicy` and `allowFrom` (labels unchanged, schema unchanged).
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`: regenerated for the new help text.

## Evidence

The documented behavior, on main `f4b43b4714`:

- Classic calls: `shouldAcceptInbound` in `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.ts` handles `case "allowlist":` and `case "pairing":` in one branch that returns `isAllowlistedCaller(normalized, allowFrom)`.
- Realtime calls: `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-inbound-admission.ts` accepts when `inboundPolicy === "allowlist" || inboundPolicy === "pairing"` and the caller is in `allowFrom`; otherwise only the callbacks path can admit the call, as under `allowlist`.
- Nothing in the plugin creates a pairing or approval request for a caller.

**Running settings form.** Branch build `8e7228d4f3` (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`), `openclaw gateway run` with `plugins.entries.voice-call` enabled (`provider: "mock"`, `inboundPolicy: "pairing"`, `allowFrom: []`), Control UI at `/settings/plugins/voice-call?view=settings`, Inbound calls section.

After (this branch, footer `docs/voice-cal…@8e7228d`): both help strings render under their fields.

![Inbound calls settings on this branch: help text under Inbound policy and Inbound allowlist](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af3d0ea7-1a7b-4289-905d-f16e703b5704)

Before (same Gateway config; a build of main `f4b43b4714` plus an unrelated change outside voice-call, so the footer shows another branch name; `extensions/voice-call` and `docs/plugins/voice-call` are identical to main): neither field has help text.

![Inbound calls settings before: no help text under Inbound policy or Inbound allowlist](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be823597-947d-4e4a-9186-9d7a24b19d61)

**Checks**, in a Node 24.22.1 container on this branch:

```text
$ oxfmt --check docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md docs/plugins/voice-call/tts-and-inbound-calls.md
All matched files use the correct format.
$ pnpm format:docs:check
Docs formatting clean (1422 files).
$ pnpm config:docs:check
OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json
$ pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/config.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  61 passed (61)
```

The help text changes the generated config baseline hash (`config-baseline.json` and `config-baseline.plugin.json` lines in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`); the counts file is unchanged.

Not covered: no live inbound call was placed; the behavior described is read from the source above.


**Rebased onto main `443e973069` (2026-11-16)** to clear a conflict in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`. The docs and help-text commit is unchanged (same `git patch-id`). The hash commit was regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`, and as before only the `config-baseline.json` and `config-baseline.plugin.json` lines differ from main. Re-run on the new head `2cd2c1078d`:

```text
$ pnpm config:docs:check
OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json
$ pnpm format:docs:check
Docs formatting clean (1431 files).
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/voice-call/src/config.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/manager.async-store.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/manager.notify.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.realtime-routing.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  169 passed (169)
```

The cited source is the same on `443e973069`: `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.ts:51-58` (`case "allowlist":` and `case "pairing":` share the `isAllowlistedCaller` branch) and `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-inbound-admission.ts:19`.

prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.
