prs.title: improve(ui): fix core copy leftovers from the copy sweep
prs.body:
## Problem

Two leftovers from the Control UI copy sweep remained in core copy:

- In Settings › Appearance › Tab icon, the notice for a locked lobster read “This lobster is not unlocked in this browser.” The Control UI style rules call for contractions.
- Core Control UI copy spelled “cancelled” the British way, while the product uses American English.

## Solution

- Changed the English source in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-settings.ts` to “This lobster isn’t unlocked in this browser. Using Default until it is.” Updated the matching assertion in `ui/src/pages/config/view-tab-icon.browser.test.tsx`.
- Spelled “Canceled” and “canceling” the American way, as approved by Vyctor:
  - `en.ts` `common.cancelled`: “Cancelled” → “Canceled”
  - `en-chat-session.ts` unsent and cancelled notices: “This agent update was canceled before delivery.” and “Canceled before the agent started it. …”
  - `en-github-connections.ts` GitHub sign-in: “… or try canceling again.” and the “Try canceling again” button
  - `en-openclaw-id.ts` request expiry: “This browser request expired or was canceled. …”
  - Updated assertions in `chat-thread-live-final.test.ts`, `chat-thread-input-order.test.ts` and `chat-composer-outbox.e2e.test.ts`.
- Key names (`cancelled`, `dismissCancelled`, …) are unchanged. Channel plugins and internal error-matching strings are intentionally untouched.

Lobsterdex lore, bottle fortunes and pet hover titles stay an English-only easter egg, as Peter and Ayaan designed them. An earlier revision of this PR moved them into translation files; that change has been reverted.

## Impact

Seven English strings change; no keys or behavior change. Foreign locales are untouched; the post-merge `control-ui-locale-refresh` bot owns them.

## Evidence

- `view-tab-icon` browser test: 5/5 pass.
- `chat-thread-live-final` + `chat-thread-input-order`: 29/29 pass.
- Keyless `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no change) and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: pass.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer.**

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6f3d8cae-3016-4c59-8e2f-ed53302706a0)

prs.title: improve(clawrouter): apply the Control UI glossary and style to ClawRouter copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The ClawRouter pool page (`extensions/clawrouter/src/control-ui.tsx`) hard-coded every English string inline. That made the copy untranslatable, and some of it didn't follow the approved Control UI style: no contractions, sentences ending fragments with periods, passive "is required" phrasing, a raw error message shown as the alert headline, two different names for the same "enabled state unknown" concept, and Gateway status messages pointing at a "Model Providers" page whose actual label is **Models**.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr/Workboard pattern: `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, `src/i18n/locales.ts`, and `src/i18n/index.ts`, using `translateControlUiMessage`. `browserRoot` is `src/` (the dirname of `openclaw.controlUi`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` picks the catalog up automatically.
- Move **70 strings** into `en.ts` (68 under `clawrouter.*`, plus the shared `common.refresh` and `common.refreshing`, which match core English exactly). Composed strings such as "Observed {date} · Policy {policy}", "{used} used / {limit} monthly limit", and "{count} subscriptions with headroom · {unknown} unknown" are now single templates instead of JSX fragments.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-visible string the lane owns, including the four Gateway pool status messages in `index.ts` that this page renders.
- Errors: the alert now reads "Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh." The redacted technical detail is still shown, but as a secondary hint line under the alert. Plugin views have no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main` (`ControlUiComponents` has none), so per the sweep brief the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- `locales.ts` serves English only. This plugin has no `translated.json` yet, and the sweep brief says to leave it absent. A static import of a missing JSON file would break the esbuild bundle, so the lazy loader isn't added yet (see the open question below).

The `ClawRouter` page title and nav label stay as literal product names.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Could not load the pool. Try refreshing. *(only for non-Error failures; otherwise the raw message was the alert)* | Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh. *(raw detail shown below as a hint)* |
| Read access is required to view the ClawRouter pool. | You need read access to view the ClawRouter pool. |
| Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value is not a subscription charge. | Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value isn’t a subscription charge. |
| Enabled state unknown *(grant badge)* | Enabled state not reported *(same as the extra-usage wording; one name per concept)* |
| Not reported. *(extra-usage fragment)* | Not reported |
| ClawRouter pool status is unavailable. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. | Couldn’t load ClawRouter pool status. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. |
| Configure a ClawRouter key in Model Providers, then try Refresh. | Configure a ClawRouter key in Models, then try Refresh. |
| The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Model Providers. | The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Models. |
| This ClawRouter deployment does not expose pool status. … | This ClawRouter deployment doesn’t expose pool status. … |

All other strings moved into the catalog with their English unchanged.

## Impact

- The English copy is the same apart from the rows above. Layout and markup are unchanged, except that a failed refresh now shows a fixed alert plus a secondary detail line.
- No docs quote the changed labels. `docs/providers/clawrouter.md` and the README reference **Refresh**, **Not reported**, and **ClawRouter**, which are unchanged.
- Foreign locales: none yet. The post-merge locale refresh owns parity. `ui:i18n:check` parity is non-strict on PRs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/clawrouter/browser/pool.test.ts extensions/clawrouter/pool-gateway.test.ts`: 3 + 12 passed. The browser test assertions are updated for the new alert headline, the detail line still being redacted, and the "You need read access" copy.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green, `plugin=clawrouter keys=70 locales=0`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>`: no problems.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>`: clean.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/clawrouter`: bundle builds.
- pr-simplify pass: removed duplicate keys (one "Observed {date}", one "Subscription") and collapsed repeated enabled/disabled ternaries into one helper. Production delta: +260/−126 across 6 files. Most of it is the new 90-line `en.ts` plus the line-wrapping of `t(...)` calls.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex engine, gpt-6.1-sol), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `14ab4736fa24`, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.9)", no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up on this host.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge** (the visual gate needs before/after screenshots of the pool page, including the refresh-failure state).

## Open question

Leaving `translated.json` absent means that after the locale refresh writes it, nothing loads it until a follow-up adds the Nostr-style `loadMessages` loader. The alternatives are to commit an empty `{}` `translated.json` with the loader now, or to add both in the first locale refresh.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/a37a5704-38f5-40e9-87b9-fbcec400e40e)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(x): apply the Control UI glossary and style to X replies copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The **X replies** Control UI page hard-codes its English copy in `extensions/x/src/control-ui.tsx`. Several strings also break the approved Control UI glossary and style rules:

- "bot" where the copy means the agent
- "Administrator" as the role name
- "hidden helpers" for subagents
- fragment sentences that end in periods
- raw server error text shown as the only error message

The empty-state hint also put the internal config key `allowFrom` in normal copy.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr pattern: `extensions/x/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `src` because `openclaw.controlUi` points at `./src/control-ui.tsx`. **63 strings** moved into the catalog under the plugin-specific `xReplies.*` namespace, so no key collides with the shared core catalog.
- Translate the page, navigation label, and page label through `translateControlUiMessage`. The view tracks `host.locale` in its existing presentation store.
- Notices are now typed keys (`added`, `removed`, `guestsOn`, …) translated at render time instead of English strings held in state.
- Request failures are wrapped in a small `RequestFailure` that records which action failed. The alert now reads "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." and the redacted server message follows inline as secondary text (`<small>`, muted). The plugin SDK host components (`ControlUiComponents`) on main have no shared "Show details" disclosure, so as the sweep brief directs, the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- Copy that wraps inline elements (`<time>`, the repository link) uses a small `withSlots` helper. It splits the translated string at `{name}` placeholders, so translators control word order.
- `locales.ts` is English-only for now, and other locales fall back to English, which is today's behavior. `translated.json` isn't added, per the sweep brief. The Nostr-style lazy `translated.json` loader can't be wired until that file exists, because the bundler can't resolve a missing import.

### Notable copy changes

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| Choose whose mentions the bot can answer publicly. | Choose whose mentions the agent can answer publicly. |
| Administrator access is required to manage X replies. | You need admin access to manage X replies. |
| Bot account | Agent account |
| Applies to the selected bot account. Guests get repository answers with hidden helpers of the same agent. No writes, commands, visible work sessions, or other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. | Applies to the selected agent account. Guests get repository answers from this agent and its hidden subagents. They can’t write, run commands, open visible sessions, or use other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. |
| Per guest, per UTC day / `3 mentions` | Mentions per guest, per UTC day / `3` (no more "1 mentions") |
| Could not resolve on X: @a, @b. Check the declared profiles. | Couldn’t find @a, @b on X. Check the declared GitHub profiles. |
| No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or set `allowFrom` in config. | No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or in config. |
| *(raw server error)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load X replies. Try again. · Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. · Couldn’t remove this entry. Try again. · Couldn’t change guest mode. Try again. *(the redacted server detail follows as secondary text)* |
| No successful sync yet.Entries update… *(missing space)* | No successful sync yet. Entries update… |

All other strings moved into the catalog with unchanged English. They were already in sentence case, used the single ellipsis character, and had no straight quotes.

### Out of scope / unchanged

- Server-generated text the page displays verbatim: the guest readiness `blockedReason` from `guests.ts`/`monitor.ts` and the GitHub sync `message` from `verified-github.ts`. That text also feeds channel status and the agent path, so it stays with its backend owners.
- Agent-facing and X-posted text (the guest policy prompt, tool text).
- Docs: `docs/channels/x.md` quotes **X replies**, **From GitHub**, **Guest mode**, and **Refresh**, and none of those labels changed.

## Impact

UI copy only. The plugin's operator RPCs (`x.allowlist.*`, `x.guests.set`), state, and authorization are unchanged. Foreign locales keep showing English until the post-merge locale refresh adds `translated.json` and the lazy loader is wired.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/x/browser/control-ui.browser.test.tsx`: 4/4 passed. Assertions were updated for the new admin-required copy and for the error alert (`Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. Rejected [REDACTED]`), which still proves redaction.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=x keys=63 locales=0`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check`: fails as expected with "missing verified translations" for all 22 locales of the new `x` catalog. That CI step is `continue-on-error`, and foreign parity is the post-merge `control-ui-locale-refresh` bot's job. No foreign files were hand-edited.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/x`: pass. The one warning is pre-existing, on an unchanged line.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: pass, no ratchet changes.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/x`: bundle builds.
- `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify: the remaining machinery is the catalog and translator, one `RequestFailure` class (it carries which action failed to the error summary), and `withSlots` (it keeps inline elements inside translatable sentences). A planned slot was dropped once `allowFrom` left the copy.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`, on candidate `e48ff37`. Result: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final head differs only by removing the `allowFrom` slot from the empty-state string. Verify, test, lint, and typecheck were re-run on it.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.** The visual gate requires before/after screenshots of the X replies page before this lands.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0bf8c201-1ee4-45d1-87f1-4556319f55ac)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(workboard): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Workboard copy
prs.body:
## Problem

Workboard's Control UI copy didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules. It had straight apostrophes, a `...` placeholder, "could not" / "cannot" errors with no consistent form, "Board agent" capitalized mid-sentence, the British "Cancelled", and "board conversation" used for what is a session. Its errors also showed internal RPC text: `sessions.create returned no key` and `workboard response did not include a card`. About 19 user-visible English strings were still hard-coded in `extensions/workboard/browser/` instead of living in the plugin's translation source, so they could never be translated.

## Solution

- Rewrote the existing English in `browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the rules. Errors now read "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The copy uses contractions, curly apostrophes and the `…` character, sentence case, and **session** as the container noun.
- Moved the remaining hard-coded English in `browser/` (execution, loading, mutation and normalization errors; the stale-session fallback; the "Workboard is no longer active" message; widget registration labels; the board-kind suffix on duplicate sidebar names) into `en.ts` and called it through `t()`.
- `host.ts` calls `translateControlUiMessage` directly instead of `t()`, because `i18n/index.ts` imports `host.ts` and using `t()` there would create an import cycle.
- Two places that had the same stale-session fallback in different words (normalization and card alerts) now use one key.
- Updated `docs/plugins/workboard.md`, which quotes the sidebar suffix: **Planning (Cards)** / **Planning (Sessions)**.

Notable copy changes (old → new):

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page load failure | Workboard could not load. Check your connection and reload this page. | Couldn’t load Workboard. Check your connection and reload this page. |
| Delete without write access | Connect with write access to delete this board. | Couldn’t delete this board. Connect with write access and try again. |
| Bulk edit stopped | The operation stopped. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. | Couldn’t apply changes to every card. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. |
| Sessions board agent missing | The board conversation's agent is unavailable. Choose a configured agent or update the board's conversation. | Couldn’t open the board session. Its agent is unavailable; choose a configured agent or update the board’s session. |
| Sessions board create failed | The board conversation could not be created. Try again. | Couldn’t create the board session. Try again. |
| Rules help | The Board agent can edit column rules and session scope. | The board agent can edit column rules and session scope. |
| Note placeholder | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note... | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note… |
| Dispatch help | …this board's Ready cards… | …this board’s Ready cards… |
| Refresh status | Refresh failed | Couldn’t refresh |
| Session status | Cancelled | Canceled (American English, same as core approvals copy) |
| Widget card not loaded | This card is not loaded yet. | This card isn’t loaded yet. |
| Start, hard-coded | sessions.create returned no key | Couldn’t start a session for this card. Try again. |
| Card payload, hard-coded | workboard response did not include a card | Couldn’t read the updated card. Refresh the board and try again. |
| Gateway missing, hard-coded | Gateway client unavailable | Couldn’t refresh Workboard. Connect to the Gateway and try again. |
| Scheduled start, hard-coded | Scheduled cards cannot start before their scheduled time. | Couldn’t start this card. Scheduled cards can’t start before their scheduled time. |
| Already started, hard-coded | This card already has an execution. Refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link before starting another. | Couldn’t start this card. It already has a linked session; refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link. |
| Stop, hard-coded | Refresh this card's session details before stopping it, or use Edit to choose its session. | Couldn’t stop this card’s session. Refresh its session details, or use Edit to choose its session. |
| Changed card, hard-coded | This card changed. Refresh its details before starting or stopping it. | Couldn’t start or stop this card because it changed. Refresh its details and try again. |
| Stale fallback, hard-coded (×2) | Session has not reported… / Linked session has not reported recent activity. | Linked session hasn’t reported recent activity. |
| Inactive plugin, hard-coded | Workboard is no longer active. Reload the plugin to continue. | Workboard is no longer active. Reload this page to continue. |
| Unknown error, hard-coded | Unknown workboard error. | Unknown Workboard error. Refresh and try again. |
| Sidebar duplicate name | Planning (cards) | Planning (Cards) |

String count: 12 existing English values rewritten. 19 hard-coded literals moved into translation calls: 14 go to new `en.ts` keys and the rest reuse 3 existing keys (`widget.boardLabel`, `cardsBoard`, `sessionsBoard.kind`). No foreign locale, `translated.json`, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` or `*.meta.json` file was edited. The post-merge locale-refresh bot owns parity.

Raw Gateway error text still shows inline in the existing Workboard error toast. Workboard has no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main`, and the copy written here no longer includes internal names.

## Impact

Only copy and translation sources change; behavior doesn't. Two edge cases are accepted:
- Widget registration labels and the stale-reason fallback are resolved when they're created. A locale switch picks them up after the next refresh or reload; before this change they were always English.
- The session label `buildCardSessionLabel` writes for new card sessions, and agent-facing template drafts, stay as they are. They're stored data or model-facing text, not Control UI copy.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workboard/browser`: 34 files, 265 tests passed (assertions updated in `index.test.ts` and `widgets/runtime.test.ts`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=workboard keys=395 locales=22`).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `oxlint` on touched TS files: 0 warnings or errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is a copy move or rewrite. The only new code is the 4-line `inactiveMessage()` helper in `host.ts`, which avoids the import cycle. One duplicate stale fallback was merged into a shared key. Net production change is small: about +40/−30 lines, mostly `en.ts`.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol, medium), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head of this branch, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.82)", no findings. The reviewer couldn't see unchanged context, so key validity and import cycles rest on the `ui:i18n:verify` and madge runs above.

prs.title: improve(nostr,memory-core): apply the Control UI glossary and style to plugin copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The Nostr profile panel and the Memory overview/search views had copy that didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: Title Case buttons and labels (`Hide Advanced`, `Import from Relays`, `Save & Publish`, `Public Key`, `Edit Profile`), straight quotes and `...`, "Could not" / "does not" with no contractions, lowercase "gateway", internal jargon ("host memory search runtime"), and error messages that didn't use the "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." pattern. Nostr also had one hard-coded English label (`NIP-05`) outside its catalog.

## Solution

- Rewrote the English source catalogs in `extensions/nostr/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the glossary and style rules.
- **Shared-key collision:** Nostr's `common.hideAdvanced`, `common.showAdvanced`, `common.importFromRelays`, `common.saveAndPublish` and `common.publicKey` share keys with the core catalog (`ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`), and `ui:i18n:verify` requires a plugin's English to match the core text for any shared key. These five now live under plugin-owned `channels.nostr.*` keys.
- Removed those five core `common.*` keys from `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`; nothing reads them any more (approved by Vyctor; `ui:i18n:baseline`, `ui:i18n:verify` and `tsgo:ui` pass).
- Moved the hard-coded `NIP-05` profile-fact label into the Nostr catalog (`channels.nostr.nip05`). The truncated public key now uses `…`.
- Nostr save/import failures now show `Couldn’t update/import the profile. Try again.` with the raw detail after it. Before, a failed request showed only the raw server message (e.g. `Invalid profile`). Both paths share one `failure()` helper in `controller.ts`, which also removed the duplicated prefix logic.
- Placeholders are unchanged on every key that keeps its name (`{prefix}`, `{error}`, `{message}`, `{engine}`), so existing translations still pass verification.
- **Raw error detail:** the Plugin SDK has no shared "Show details" disclosure for plugin settings views, so the raw detail stays inline after the sentence. This matches the existing core pattern (`Couldn’t load cloud device profiles. Try again. {error}`).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Surface | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nostr button | Edit Profile | Edit profile |
| Nostr button | Save & Publish | Save & publish |
| Nostr button | Import from Relays | Import from relays |
| Nostr button | Show Advanced / Hide Advanced | Show advanced / Hide advanced |
| Nostr label | Public Key | Public key |
| Nostr label | Display Name | Display name |
| Nostr label | NIP-05 Identifier | NIP-05 identifier |
| Nostr label | Lightning Address | Lightning address |
| Nostr hint | Click "Edit Profile" to add your name, bio, and avatar. | Click “Edit profile” to add your name, bio, and avatar. |
| Nostr placeholder | Tell people about yourself... | Tell people about yourself… |
| Nostr error | Request timed out after 30 seconds; the server may still have applied the change — check the profile before retrying. | Couldn’t confirm the profile change within 30 seconds. It may still have applied, so check the profile before you try again. |
| Nostr error | Profile update failed: {error} | Couldn’t update the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile import failed: {error} | Couldn’t import the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile publish failed on all relays. | Couldn’t publish the profile to any relay. Try again. |
| Nostr public key | `abcd1234...wxyz5678` | `abcd1234…wxyz5678` |
| Memory search placeholder | Search this agent's memories | Search this agent’s memories |
| Memory search error | Memory search failed: {message} | Couldn’t search memories. Try again. {message} |
| Memory file error | Could not load this memory file: {message} | Couldn’t load this memory file. Close and reopen it to try again. {message} |
| Memory file | This memory file cannot be shown as text. | This memory file can’t be shown as text. |
| Memory notice | Update the gateway to search memories from the Control UI. | Update the Gateway to search memories from the Control UI. |
| Memory hero | Host memory search is unavailable | Memory search is unavailable |
| Memory hero | {engine} does not provide a host memory search runtime. … | {engine} doesn’t provide Gateway memory search. … |
| Memory hero | Checking this agent's memory engine and dream cycle. | Checking this agent’s memory engine and dream cycle. |
| Memory hero | The gateway is offline, so memory status is unavailable. | The Gateway is offline, so memory status is unavailable. |
| Memory button | Open Settings | Open settings |

**Counts:** 28 user-visible strings changed (16 Nostr catalog strings, 10 Memory catalog strings, 1 hard-coded Nostr label moved into the catalog, 1 ellipsis in the formatted public key). 1 string moved into a translation file (`NIP-05`). 5 Nostr keys moved from `common.*` to `channels.nostr.*`.

## Impact

- English-locale users see consistent sentence case, contractions and typography, and errors that say what failed and what to do next.
- Foreign locales: translated.json, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` weren't hand-edited. Keys that kept their names still show their existing (now stale) translations. The five moved Nostr keys show English until the post-merge control-ui-locale-refresh bot runs. Their old translations stay as unused entries (`unused_translations=110`, which verify allows).
- No docs quote the changed labels.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/nostr/browser/profile.test.tsx extensions/memory-core/browser/memories.test.tsx extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.test.tsx`: 3 files, 51 tests passed. The assertions on changed English are updated. The Swedish locale-switch test now waits for an unchanged translated label (`Användarnamn`), because `saveAndPublish` moved to a new key.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (memory-core keys=67, nostr keys=62, 22 locales each; no shared-key disagreement; referenced keys resolve).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- `oxlint` on both browser dirs: 0 errors. The 2 warnings are pre-existing, in the untouched `memory-core/browser/components.tsx`.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK. `oxfmt` applied. `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is copy, a key reference, or the shared `failure()` helper, which replaced duplicated prefix logic. No new state or modules.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch`, base `d59f00281eb0216`, head `0e93cfcfc4e6`, max priority P2. Result: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up in this checkout.

prs.title: fix: native Codex oauth/token without a host profile should still forward unlisted models
prs.body:
Fixes #194980

### What Problem This Solves

A native Codex login that has not selected a host auth profile is an `oauth` or `token` account. `resolveCodexForwardCompatModel` forwarded a model missing from the static patch table only when `authProfileMode` was absent. Models already in the static table are unchanged.

### Why This Change Was Made

The unlisted branch now accepts `authProfileMode === undefined || authProfileMode === "oauth" || authProfileMode === "token"`. It still requires `authProfileId === undefined` and `providerConfig?.auth === undefined`. `api_key`, and `oauth` that already has an `authProfileId`, still return `undefined`.

An earlier head also passed that account mode in from agent execution and off-catalog runtime choice. That expansion did not finish runtime selection: the later membership check still reads model scope, and the Codex auth policy does not belong in core. Those callers and the account-scope readiness API are removed. The repair stays on the provider resolver.

The existing spark-routing test moved to `extensions/openai/openai-codex-spark-routing.test.ts` so the provider test file could take the new cases without growing past its line cap. That test's assertions are unchanged.

### User Impact

A profile-free native Codex `oauth` or `token` context can resolve a model id that is not yet in the static patch table when that context reaches the provider resolver. A selected host profile and API-key auth still do not receive that forward path.

### Evidence

Resolver contract, exact command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts -t "delegates an unlisted first-party model|does not extend native model forwarding" --maxWorkers=1` on `bd5140669e8`: parent exit 1 for `oauth` and `token`; head exit 0. `api_key` with no profile, and `oauth` with `authProfileId` `openai:selected`, stay `undefined`.

prs.title: fix: Apple gateway names are garbled when Bonjour escapes non-ASCII text
prs.body:
Fixes #195540

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes garbled gateway names in Apple clients when Bonjour escapes non-ASCII characters, without changing the identities used to reconnect saved gateways.

## User Impact

macOS and iOS display UTF-8 gateway names correctly, while existing profiles, active/connected gateway selections, credentials, and TLS pins retain their original identity keys. No configuration changes or data migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

DNS-SD decimal escapes represent bytes, so display decoding now reconstructs UTF-8. Persisted endpoint IDs deliberately retain the shipped scalar-per-escape mapping and whitespace normalization, including its legacy handling of values above 255. Sharing the corrected display decoder with ID normalization would strand existing saved state; the identity owner now preserves that separate compatibility contract.

## Evidence

- Preserves the original UTF-8 display patch from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/bonjour-escapes-utf8` at `bfaf6ac55a779ed1bff9ec0b9e2520defa6d5390`. The P1 repair appends `680860e6679b20b601e8a46c7236d73d79af0d96` directly to `8315283df8bb3a869e11f6048f2df9684c7c63da`; remote verification confirms only the three reviewed identity/compatibility files changed and the original two display files are unchanged.
- `git diff --check` passes. Added exact-byte endpoint-ID cases and a legacy serialized-registry fixture exercising the real registry, credential, and TLS stores. The fixture checks saved-ID matching, active/connected membership, label refresh without duplicate profiles, credential access, and TLS-pin access. These Swift tests are authored but **have not executed here**.
- The initial source review missed the cross-layer identity regression reported by ClawSweeper. Independent review of this repair traced the legacy decoder, identity owner, iOS/macOS discovery, saved-profile matching, registry persistence, credentials, and TLS keys; no actionable source findings remain in the reviewed delta. This is source review, not runtime proof.
- Simplification: compatibility stays in the existing endpoint-ID owner, with no migration, fallback lookup, new abstraction, or caller-side workaround. Total delta against the original base: production +29/-9 lines, tests +98; the P1 repair alone is production +21/-1 and tests +85.
- **Draft / missing native proof:** this Linux workspace has no Swift compiler, Xcode, SwiftLint, or SwiftFormat. `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter BonjourEscapesTests` cannot start (`/bin/sh: 1: swift: not found`); Xcode is also unavailable (`/bin/sh: 1: xcodebuild: not found`). Swift compilation, regression red/green, `pnpm ios:test GatewayEndpointIDTests GatewaySettingsStoreTests`, native lint/format, and live Apple discovery remain unverified. No supported managed CI-dispatch action or qualified Apple runner is exposed to this session. Keep this PR draft until required exact-head Apple build/test evidence succeeds; automatic CI skips drafts, and no skipped job is counted as proof.

prs.title: fix(migrate): write unattended pre-migration backups to the home folder
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory imports through the Gateway (`migrations.memory.apply`, used by the Control UI memory import page) and migrations started during onboarding write a pre-migration backup archive without an output path. It lands in the process's current directory. A Gateway started from a source checkout drops the user's backup into the checkout, and the migration resource tests leave real archives in the repo root.

Fixes #199888.

## Fix

The backup engine gets a `preferHomeOutput` option (`src/infra/backup-create.ts`). With no `output`, it writes to the home folder unless the home folder is inside a backed-up source (for example, when an agent workspace is the home folder). Otherwise it keeps the existing default: the current directory, or home when the current directory is itself backed up. The check uses the same included-source list as the engine's existing "must not be written inside a source path" refusal.

`applyProviderMemoryImport` and `offerPostInstallMigrations` set `preferHomeBackupOutput`, which `runMigrationApply` passes through to the backup. `openclaw migrate` and `openclaw backup create` keep their documented current-directory default. `docs/cli/migrate.md` says where each one writes.

## Evidence

Captured output is in the proof comment below. All runs are real Gateway or onboarding runs in a clean macOS VM with the bundled Claude import plugin, made-up Claude Code memory and an isolated HOME. `main` is efc03e24624; "this branch" is 709007e4600.

**Gateway memory import** (`migrations.memory.plan` then `migrations.memory.apply` over `openclaw gateway call`):

| Agent workspace | Gateway started from | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HOME/workspace` | a folder outside HOME | imported, archive in that folder | imported, archive in HOME |
| HOME | a folder outside HOME | imported, archive in that folder | imported, archive in that folder |
| HOME | the state dir | fails: "Backup output must not be written inside a source path" | same failure, unchanged |

No case is worse than `main`. The last row fails the same way on `main` and is out of scope here.

**Onboarding:** interactive `openclaw onboard --classic`, started from a folder outside HOME, with Enter pressed at each prompt (the memory import prompt defaults to yes). Both runs report "Claude: 1 migrated". On `main` the archive is written to the onboarding folder; on this branch it is written to HOME.

**Upgrade from latest stable:** 2026.11.3 sets up the state and imports one memory file (archive in the Gateway's folder). Then this branch runs `doctor --fix --non-interactive` (exit 0) and starts its Gateway on the same state. Gateway port, auth, plugin and workspace settings are unchanged. The memory imported on stable is still there and is planned as a conflict instead of being imported again. A new memory file imports, with the archive in HOME.

**Tests:**

- `src/commands/backup.test.ts`: new case for `preferHomeOutput` with the current directory outside home. Workspace inside the state dir: archive in home. Workspace is home: archive in the current directory. Without the source check, the workspace-is-home case fails with the same "must not be written inside a source path" error as the VM run. With it, the file passes (20 tests).
- `src/gateway/server-methods/migrations.resources.test.ts` asserts that `backupPath` is directly under `HOME`. With the test on `main`'s code, 2 of 5 fail (`Received: <repo root>`) and 4 archives are left in the repo root.
- With this branch, all three resource suites pass (5, 3 and 11 tests), and no archives are left in the repo.

Also run: `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on the changed files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json`. All clean.

Not covered by a live run: the post-install migration offered after a Codex harness install (covered by `migrate.resources.test.ts`), Docker, and service installs.

prs.title: fix(sessions): stop archive/delete batch after Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Ctrl+C, `openclaw sessions delete k1 k2 k3 --yes` (and `sessions archive`) keeps resolving, then deleting/archiving every remaining key until the CLI is force-killed.

## User Impact

User impact: Ctrl+C during a batch `sessions delete` now lets the session being mutated finish with its receipt preserved, starts no other lifecycle mutation, and reports the sessions that were never reached as interrupted. Sessions that were not reached keep their state — for a destructive delete this means they are not deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The describe and delete/patch loops resolve one key per Gateway RPC but never read the command's cancellation signal. The CLI now forwards its existing AsyncWorkScope interrupt signal to the **read-only lookups** (so a pending describe cancels), stops starting further mutations once the signal fires (an admitted mutation keeps its reply), reports unattempted keys as `interrupted` rather than a false `not_found`, and marks an interrupted partial batch as `ok: false`.

This follows the admitted-write handling in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197508 (`sessions import`) and the bulk-loop cancellation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198163.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI Ctrl+C proof, synthetic loopback WS peer speaking the real OpenClaw wire protocol (answers `sessions.describe`, **holds then releases** the first `sessions.delete` after SIGINT), source CLI in a real PTY:

- HEAD `8f5546c0f7b0` (this PR): the admitted delete **settles as `deleted`** (receipt kept), s2/s3 are reported `interrupted` (not a false `not_found`), the batch is `ok: false`, and no later mutation starts.
- BASE `c18593cb904d` (mutation carried the abort signal): the admitted delete's receipt is **dropped** (`deletesReleased: 0`) — exactly the defect the review called out.

Discriminant tests: `stops deleting further sessions once interrupted` / `stops describing further sessions once interrupted`, updated to assert the admitted receipt is kept, unvisited keys are `interrupted`, and no `runtime.exit` fires (28 passed).

Evidence bundle (receipts, raw PTY logs, harness): https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/sessions-lifecycle-signal/proof/sessions-lifecycle-signal/EVIDENCE.md

prs.title: fix(outbound): reject reserved placeholder delivery identities
prs.body:
Closes #199070

## What Problem This Solves

A channel adapter can finish a send without a physical platform identity. Two bundled adapters do exactly that:

- **Matrix** returns `messageId: lastMessageId || "unknown"` with an empty native receipt when the homeserver event ids were all falsy (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.ts:377`).
- **iMessage** synthesizes `"ok"` when the bridge acknowledges a send without naming it (`extensions/imessage/src/send.ts:417`), and its own identity owner already classifies `"ok"` and `"unknown"` as non-identities (`extensions/imessage/src/message-guid.ts:9`).

Core held two disagreeing rules for those values:

- `normalizePlatformIds()` in `src/infra/outbound/deliver-core.ts` excluded `unknown` and `suppressed`.
- `resolveReceiptSourceId()` in `src/channels/message/receipt.ts` returned any nonblank `messageId` first, so a placeholder won the identity gate.

Because the placeholder was accepted, `observeDeliveryResult()` treated the send as identified: the delivery entered `results`, `status: "sent"` was recorded for the payload, `onDeliveryResult` persisted confirmed platform evidence, and `recordMessageSentEvent` fired with `success: true`. The record claimed confirmed delivery while the only receipt available was empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/channels/message/receipt.ts` owns receipt/identity semantics, so the reserved-placeholder rule now lives there as `isReservedMessageIdentity()` and both gates consume it:

- the identity gate skips a reserved placeholder in `messageId` and `pollId`, so it falls through to the nested receipt's primary id;
- `normalizePlatformIds()` keeps its existing exclusion by delegating to the same predicate.

A placeholder can no longer outrank a real multipart id, and the two gates cannot drift apart again. The reserved set is the cross-adapter placeholder vocabulary (`unknown`, `suppressed`, and the `ok` ack word that the bundled iMessage adapter documents as a bridge placeholder), so a new adapter does not have to rediscover that an acknowledged send is not an identified send.

The rest of the tree already assumes this rule, which is what made the disagreement visible:

| Owner | Current rule |
| --- | --- |
| `src/infra/outbound/deliver-core.ts` | filters `unknown` / `suppressed` out of platform ids |
| `extensions/imessage/src/message-guid.ts` | treats `ok` / `unknown` as non-identities |
| `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` | lists `{ ok: true, messageId: "unknown" }` among payloads that stay unconfirmed |
| `src/cron/delivery.ts`, `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts` | branch on `reason === "adapter_returned_no_identity"` as the uncertain case |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-outbound.md` | `suppressed` + `adapter_returned_no_identity` is the ambiguous send that must not be resent; adapters should return `sent` "with the actual provider receipt" |

Fix classification: **behavior-completing** — the delivery gate now matches the receipt owner and the documented ambiguity contract.

## User Impact

A send whose transport returned only a placeholder is no longer reported as a confirmed delivery. The payload is recorded as `suppressed` with `reason: "adapter_returned_no_identity"`, the documented ambiguous bucket, so durable delivery keeps pending custody and reconciles instead of claiming success or resending.

Real identities are unchanged: a concrete `messageId`, a multipart receipt (including a case where a placeholder sits beside real event ids), a `pollId`, and `not_sent` all resolve exactly as before.

One existing fixture used the reserved placeholder as a sample *accepted* id (`message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts`, core-mode row). It now uses a real id so that case keeps testing caller-closure retention; the placeholder outcome is covered by the new delivery regression.

## Evidence

Base: `72f0005c889e5cb69a14ba6ef54efb2715c106ab` (current `main`; the five changed files are untouched between that commit and `84579cbdcc63`). Head: this branch.

### Red on base

Production files restored from the base commit, tests kept, then:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts -t "reserved placeholder" --maxWorkers=1
# Tests  4 failed | 7 skipped (11)
#   AssertionError: expected 'unknown' to be undefined
#   AssertionError: expected 'suppressed' to be undefined
#   AssertionError: expected 'ok' to be undefined
#   AssertionError: expected 'unknown' to be '$event:example.org'

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/outbound/deliver-results.test.ts -t "reserved placeholder" --maxWorkers=1
# Tests  1 failed | 3 skipped (4)
#   base returns the placeholder delivery in results and records status "sent"
```

### Green on head

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1        # 11 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/outbound/deliver-results.test.ts --maxWorkers=1  # 4 passed
```

Delivery regression (new): the adapter result is the bundled placeholder shape — reserved id plus `createMessageReceiptFromOutboundResults({ results: [] })` — driven through the real `deliverOutboundPayloadsCore` handler seam:

```
expect(results).toEqual([]);
expect(onDeliveryResult).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
expect(outcomes).toEqual([{ index: 0, status: "suppressed", reason: "adapter_returned_no_identity" }]);
```

### Shipped CLI run through the real bundled adapter and a real transport

The iMessage outbound path spawns `imsg rpc --json` and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio (`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts`). The proof runs the shipped CLI, the real bundled adapter, and that real subprocess transport, against a protocol-compatible bridge stand-in that acknowledges a send without naming the message — the documented path where `send.ts` synthesizes the `"ok"` placeholder.

Isolated state (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `/tmp`), no Gateway process, no network:

  channels: { imessage: { enabled: true, cliPath: "/tmp/proof-receipt/bin/imsg",
                          service: "imessage", allowFrom: ["*"] } } }
```

Bridge stand-in (node script, `argv=rpc --json`, answers `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":…,"result":{"ok":true}}` for `send`; it logs `imsg-stub: request method=send id=1` to prove the adapter drove it):

# exit code 0
```

**HEAD (same command, same bridge stand-in, this branch)**

prs.title: fix(cli): stop the interrupted pairing-code read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves `openclaw pair ` issues a read-only `device.pair.code` Gateway read before it prints the request details or asks the operator to approve. That read was not wired to the CLI work scope, so when the operator pressed Ctrl+C or the process received SIGTERM while the read was pending, a reply that settled during teardown could still be printed (and, with `--yes`, the approval flow could continue after the interrupt). The sibling read commands (`users list` in #197322, session listings in #197758, cron reads in #197315) already stop with the command. Precedent: #197322 (same shape; this PR only moves the point to the pair command's pairing-code read) ## Why This Change Was Made The pairing-code read now passes `getAsyncWorkSignal()` to the existing `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` call (the same owner the sibling fixes use), and `runPairCommand` returns without printing when the scope is already closed or the call rejects during close. The two decision calls (approve/reject) intentionally keep the documented mutation behavior: a decision already sent to the Gateway still waits for its receipt during cleanup. No new validator, option, or lifecycle was added. Production LOC is `+17/-2` in one file. Classification: `behavior-completing` ## User Impact Interrupting `openclaw pair` during the pairing-code read now exits promptly (status 130/143) without printing request details and without approving anything. Ordinary runs (no interrupt) are unchanged; the approve/reject receipts still settle during cleanup as before. ## Evidence ### Exact-head proof receipt - Product head SHA: `90419642b36a` - Current-main RED baseline: `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0` - Production entry: `runPairCommand` in `src/cli/pair-cli.ts` (the `pair` CLI action) - Canonical owner exercised: `callPairCode` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` in `src/cli/pair-cli.ts` - Decision surface: the `device.pair.code` read and the `logRequest`/`writeJson` output that follow it - Recorder/readback boundary: mocked Gateway transport call log (`decisions()`) and human output (`mocks.log`) in the existing `src/cli/pair-cli.test.ts` harness - Acceptance RED: on current main, the new test settles the read after `AsyncWorkScope.beginClose()` and observes `decisions() === [undefined, "approve"]` — the command kept going and approved after Ctrl+C - Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, the same run observes `decisions() === [undefined]` and zero `mocks.log` calls — nothing is printed and nothing is approved after the close - Legal control: the four pre-existing pair tests (approve flow, reject flow, non-TTY refusal, invalid code refusal) all pass unchanged on exact head - Cleanup: isolated vitest temp state only; no production Gateway, session, token, or config was touched ### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace Vitest shard on the real runner with `AsyncWorkScope` (Node 24.22.1, docker `lexiflow-all`): ```text # BASE (76024435027d) + new test, via node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/pair-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 FAIL src/cli/pair-cli.test.ts > prints nothing and approves nothing when the pairing read settles after Ctrl+C AssertionError: expected [ undefined, 'approve' ] to deeply equal [ undefined ] Tests 1 failed | 4 passed (5) ``` ```text # HEAD (90419642b36a), same command Tests 5 passed (5) Duration ~5s ``` ```text # Legal control on HEAD: pre-existing approve/reject/non-TTY/invalid-code tests Tests 5 passed (5) ``` ### Verification - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/pair-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 5/5 passed on exact head; RED reproduced on current main with only the new test - `docs/cli/pair.md` updated with the same Ctrl-C note shape as `docs/cli/users.md` (#197322) - Not tested: SIGTERM (same scope owner as SIGINT). A pty-level SIGINT end-to-end run against a live Gateway was originally out of reach on the proof host, so the shipped-CLI real-behavior proof below was produced on an unrestricted host; everything else about the earlier vitest red/green stands. ### Scope and risk - Production LOC: `+17/-2` (src/cli/pair-cli.ts) - Test LOC: `+13` (src/cli/pair-cli.test.ts) - Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `getAsyncWorkSignal`/`AsyncWorkScope` and the existing `signal` option on `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport`; no new helper or export - Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none ## Real behavior proof (shipped CLI + live Gateway) The review asked for terminal evidence of SIGINT during a pending pairing read. Reproduced end to end with the compiled CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`, dist built from the pinned base/head trees) against a real Gateway (token auth, loopback, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Harness (all synthetic, loopback-only; no product code modified): - Real Gateway (`gateway run --port

`) with token-authenticated isolated state. - A browser simulator files a real pending pairing request through the shipped HTTP route `POST /__openclaw__/browser-pair/start` (fresh Ed25519 device key, signature over the `openclaw-browser-pair-v1\nstart` payload — the same request a Control UI pairing page files). - A loopback hold proxy in front of the Gateway WebSocket holds server→client bytes until 400–600 ms after the pairing RPC frame is observed, so the `device.pair.code` read is still in flight when SIGINT arrives. This deterministically models a slow network. - `openclaw pair --yes --token --url ws://127.0.0.1:`; SIGINT ~0.6 s after the RPC is seen; the process is awaited to its natural exit. Base — current main `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`: ```text Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting. A browser is asking to pair with administrator access to this Gateway. Code QSJY-34HX Browser (reported) proof-browser-sim/1.0 Address 127.0.0.1 Page (reported) http://127.0.0.1:49710 Browser ID edd426e3 Requested just now ... Approved. The waiting browser connects by itself. It is listed in `openclaw devices list`; remove it with `openclaw devices remove edd426e3…` to end its access. ``` - Exit code 130. The late read settled inside the SIGINT cleanup window and continued into the automatic `--yes` approval. - Gateway-side readback (`devices list` on a direct connection): `Paired (1)` — device `openclaw-control-ui` (`edd426e3…`) with operator scopes. The interrupted run approved the browser. - With a longer 2 s hold the same leak printed the post-SIGINT details but the approval RPC was cut by the ~2 s cleanup grace — the leak lives exactly inside the cleanup window this PR closes. Head — this PR `90419642b36ad570582e8ad39a65ad831fd8bc3f`, same harness and timing: ```text Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting. ``` - Exit code 130; process settled ~0.3 s after SIGINT. No pairing details, no approval line. - Gateway-side readback: `No device pairing entries.` The interrupted read could not continue. Ordinary behavior on the fixed CLI (direct connection, no proxy): - `openclaw pair --yes` against a pending request exits 0, prints the request details, approves, and `devices list` shows the new device — unchanged. - Re-running `pair` on the same code exits 1 with `This code was already answered. Choose Pair this browser again to get a new one.` — the already-sent decision receipt semantics are intact. Not tested here: SIGTERM (same signal owner); a physical remote slow network (the hold proxy models it deterministically on loopback). No real browser, credentials, or non-loopback endpoints were involved; all state dirs and tokens were synthetic and removed afterwards.

Maintainer edits - Maintainer edits allowed: yes — address review comments directly on this branch.
Maintainer options - Land-ready: the change matches the already-reviewed cancellation shape from #197322/#197758/#197315 at one more call site; proof is red/green on the real test runner. - Alternative: batch this one-liner into a broader "cancel remaining CLI reads" pass; kept separate because `pair` is its own command owner. - Scope declaration: behavior-completing only; mutations (approve/reject) keep the documented receipt-during-cleanup semantics.

prs.title: fix(doctor): escape terminal controls in gateway-owned channel status issues
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` writes channel status issue text verbatim into the terminal. The `channels.status` RPC `statusIssues` payload carries plugin-authored `message` and `fix` strings; an ordinary plugin error can therefore clear the screen, change the terminal title, or inject misleading extra lines into the human Doctor report.

The human `channels status` command already sanitizes this exact payload through `terminalText` (Alix-007 #198304). The Doctor report renders the **same RPC field** at a second boundary (`doctor-gateway-health.ts` Channel warnings) that was left unsanitized.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `terminalText` sanitizer at the Doctor human rendering boundary, matching the `channels status` command. Raw JSON diagnostics keep their original values; only human display escapes terminal/format controls.

This completes the same-shape boundary gap; no new option, configuration, dependency, permission, schema, protocol or migration.

## User Impact

Doctor Channel warnings display terminal-safe text with visible newline/carriage-return/tab escapes and stripped ANSI/OSC controls. JSON retains the original Gateway diagnostic values.

## Evidence

Product HEAD: `ef881ae367de294c3d5d8ba620c201418957b9c1`; BASE: `186db3a17736cf5dc7cb528c654b27b9af6ae59f`.

| Discriminating test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `escapes terminal controls in gateway-owned channel status issues` | RED (note receives raw `\^[[31m`/`\^[]2;`/`\^G` controls and literal newlines) | GREEN (note receives `Issue text\\nnext (fix\\rrow\\ttab)` with escaped literals) |

- **Command:** `pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts` — full file 23/23 pass on HEAD; the new discriminating test fails on BASE at the intended `note` assertion.
- **Legal controls:** existing 22 tests unchanged and green (plain-warning and structured issue rendering still match verbatim strings when no controls are present). JSON `writeJson` path untouched.
- **Boundary:** terminal human output escapes controls; JSON diagnostics keep raw Gateway values (schema `Type.String()` untouched).

### Shipped CLI proof

Real `openclaw doctor` (Node 24.22.1, glibc 2.39 container, isolated HOME/state/config) pointed at a synthetic loopback WS peer speaking the real wire protocol; the peer answers `connect`/`status`/`channels.status`/`diagnostics.stability`/`doctor.memory.status`, with `channels.status` carrying control-laden `statusIssues`. Full receipts: [EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/EVIDENCE.md), [base-doctor.out](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/base-doctor.out), [head-doctor.out](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/head-doctor.out).

| Head | "Channel warnings" report block (raw bytes) |
| --- | --- |
| BASE | `- signal default: Issue\x1b[31m text\nnext\x1b]2;forged\x07 (fix\rrow\ttab)` |
| HEAD | `- signal default: Issue text\nnext (fix\rrow\ttab)` |

BASE forwards the raw `ESC [31m` red SGR, `ESC ]2;forged BEL` OSC title change + BEL, a real newline after `text`, and real CR/TAB in `fix` into Doctor's report — a plugin could colorize, retitle the terminal, or forge an extra report line. HEAD strips the ESC/BEL sequences and renders the newline/CR/TAB as visible `\n`/`\r`/`\t` literals. Both heads exit 0 and render a second control-free diagnostic identically.

## Not tested

Real channel/provider traffic, `--json` machine output is intentionally raw (by contract), Control UI, Windows/macOS, full repository suite.

## Checks

`pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts` on HEAD: 23 passed.

Precedent: #198304 (same `statusIssues` field sanitized at the `channels status` human boundary).

prs.title: fix(cli): cancel interrupted gateway secret reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw security audit` (and the other commands that resolve command-scoped secrets through the Gateway: `qr`, `directory …`) kept working for up to 30s after Ctrl-C when the Gateway was slow to answer `secrets.resolve`, then printed a `[secrets] … gateway secrets.resolve unavailable` diagnostic and finished local secret resolution and the command body while the CLI was already stopping.

## User Impact

Interrupting that read now exits in ~1.7s instead of ~43.5s on the same harness, with no post-interrupt `[secrets]` diagnostic and no command output after the interruption notice. Nothing changes when the read is not interrupted: the same 30s timeout still falls back locally with the identical diagnostic and report (controls below).

## Why This Change Was Made

`secrets.resolve` is a read — there is nothing to settle after an interrupt — so it only needed to join the CLI's existing cancellation contract:

- `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.ts:168` forwards the command's ambient signal (`getAsyncWorkSignal()`) into the request; `callGateway` already supports it.
- `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.ts:541` stops before the local fallback when that read was cancelled.

Precedent in the same family: #199307 (merged — gateway call reads), #199353 (state-store guard reads).

Classification: **behavior-completing** (interrupted path only). The cancelled read is rethrown rather than swallowed, so the command never starts and the existing top-level failure path prints its usual `The CLI command failed.` / doctor lines — the same shape accepted in #199353.

## Evidence

Head `64d6685a8ceb` removes one redundant mock-shape test that review flagged; the production bytes are identical to `9e1803590f7f`, where the runtime receipts below were captured. Base is this branch's base `99157f8f8c4e`.

### Reproduction with a real Gateway in a wedged state

A **real OpenClaw Gateway** (this repo's own `src/entry.ts gateway run --port …`, isolated state/config, bundled plugins disabled) is frozen with `SIGSTOP` right after it binds the port: up, accepting connections, not scheduling. That is the natural shape of a Gateway stuck in a debugger stop, a swap storm, or a hung loop — the kernel still completes the CLI's TCP handshake into the accept queue, but nothing answers. SIGINT is sent to the recorded CLI pid 250 ms after the CLI's connection appears in `/proc/net/tcp`.

| Run | Interrupt | Exit | SIGINT → exit | Post-interrupt output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BASE | yes | 130 | **45141 ms** | at +43.7s the CLI ran its local exec-approvals work, then printed `[secrets] security audit: gateway secrets.resolve unavailable (gateway timeout after 30000ms); resolved command secrets locally.` and the full audit report |
| HEAD | yes | 130 | **1686 ms** | no `[secrets]` diagnostic, no audit report; only the existing `The CLI command failed.` / doctor lines at +295 ms |
| HEAD control | no | 0 | — (228.6s total) | still waits out the 30s read timeout, prints the identical `[secrets] … gateway timeout after 30000ms` diagnostic and the same report |

So the pending read is not synthetic: it is the CLI talking to a Gateway that is up but not scheduling, and the interruption contract now applies to it. Timing context from these runs: the Gateway bound its port after ~120s (cold `tsx` start), the CLI connected at ~180s.

### Protocol-level receipts

A synthetic loopback WebSocket peer (real protocol: `connect.challenge` → `connect` → `hello-ok`, protocol 4, `operator.admin`) held the `secrets.resolve` reply so the read stays pending for a controlled interval:

| Run | Interrupt | `secrets.resolve` | Exit | `[secrets] … unavailable` | Audit report | Socket closed after SIGINT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BASE | yes | held | 130 | yes (42.7s after SIGINT) | yes | 29672 ms |
| HEAD | yes | held | 130 | no | no | **8 ms** |
| BASE control | no | held | 0 | yes | yes | — |
| HEAD control | no | held | 0 | yes (identical text) | yes | — |
| BASE control | no | answered | 0 | no | yes | — |
| HEAD control | no | answered | 0 | no | yes | — |

SIGINT → exit: BASE **43467 ms**, HEAD **1737 ms** (the residual ~1.7s is the CLI's existing failure/cleanup path; the held read itself ends 8 ms after the interrupt).

### Focused regression

Remote container, Node 24.22.1, same test files, only the production file reverted for BASE:

```text
BASE:   1 failed | 23 passed
        - stops an interrupted gateway secret read before local exec resolution
HEAD:   24 passed
```

BASE's failure is the shape being fixed: the interrupted call resolves through the local fallback, and the recorded diagnostic even embeds the swallowed invariant error — `memory status: gateway secrets.resolve unavailable (expected undefined to be AbortSignal …); resolved command secrets locally.` The regression also asserts the forwarded signal and that no `exec` SecretRef provider runs after the interruption (its marker file stays absent).

Consumers of the changed module in the same container: `command-config-resolution.test.ts`, `qr-cli.test.ts`, `security-cli.test.ts`, `command-secret-gateway.memory-headers.test.ts` → **38 passed**.

Mechanical gates: `check:test-mock-exports` OK (6319 grandfathered factories), `check:test-lines-ratchet` OK (+19, allowance 400), `check:line-cap-ratchet` OK, touched-file `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean.

### Not tested

- SIGTERM (same atomic close path; only SIGINT measured).
- `qr` and `directory` were not driven end to end; they call this same read.
- No packed/dist build for this change: the PTY runs use the source entry via `tsx`, and unit/consumer tiers ran in a container.
- The startup banner tagline is random per run, not a behavior difference.

### Cleanup

Each run used a fresh `mkdtemp` state/config root, an ephemeral loopback port, froze only the scratch Gateway it started, and terminated every synthetic peer. No production Gateway, session, token, or config file was touched.

prs.title: fix(backup): stop removing further schedules after Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Ctrl+C, `openclaw backup disable` (which removes every matching backup cron schedule) keeps removing the remaining schedules until the CLI is force-killed.

## User Impact

User impact: Ctrl+C during `openclaw backup disable` now lets the schedule being removed finish with its removal confirmed, starts no other removal, and reports the schedules that were never reached as interrupted. Schedules that were not reached keep their cron entry — so for a disable they remain scheduled, and the acknowledgement no longer falsely claims "Scheduled backups disabled."

## Why This Change Was Made

`backupDisableCommand` removes one cron job per Gateway RPC in a loop that never reads the command's cancellation signal. The CLI now forwards its existing AsyncWorkScope interrupt signal through the loop and stops starting further removals once it fires. An already-admitted removal keeps its reply (the mutation RPC carries no abort signal, so its receipt settles), and when the loop stops early the acknowledgement reports the not-reached schedules as interrupted instead of printing the all-disabled message.

This follows the admitted-mutation handling and bulk-loop cancellation applied to `sessions archive/delete` (#198314) and `sessions import` (#197508).

## Evidence

Shipped CLI Ctrl+C proof, synthetic loopback WS peer speaking the real OpenClaw wire protocol (answers `cron.list` with two schedules, **holds then releases** the first `cron.remove` after SIGINT), source CLI in a real PTY targeted at the peer via `--port`:

- BASE `c0def7c89648` (review finding on the interrupted acknowledgement unfixed): the admitted removal's receipt is **kept** and the second removal never starts, but the CLI still prints `Scheduled backups disabled.` even though offsite-job remains scheduled — the misleading-success defect the review called out.
- HEAD `8a20a85bc47c` (this PR): the admitted removal settles, the second removal never starts, and the CLI reports `Scheduled backups disabled before completion: 1 schedule(s) not reached (interrupted).`

Both heads show one removal request and one released reply (the admitted receipt is kept; later removals stay unstarted).

Discriminant test: `stops removing further backup schedules once interrupted` asserts only the first schedule is removed, the mutation RPC carries no abort signal, and the interrupted acknowledgement is printed (red on the review finding, green with the fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes local release verification reporting invalid qualification artifact entries when the host is missing `unzip`. Valid remote evidence previously received the same diagnostic as a malformed archive, with the underlying spawn error discarded.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing manifest reader now retains subprocess failures as `cause`, distinguishes missing `unzip` (`ENOENT`), and checks the prerequisite before acquiring manifest evidence. Direct archive reads get the same diagnosis.

The ZIP parser, digest binding, entry inventory and compressed/expanded size limits remain unchanged. There are no new dependencies, configuration options, authority changes, or schema changes.

prs.title: fix: preserve DeepSeek balances when sibling rows are malformed
prs.body:
Closes #199643

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes DeepSeek usage losing valid balances when a sibling response row is null or contains a non-string currency.

## User Impact

Usable DeepSeek balances remain available when another row is malformed. This addresses synthetic malformed input; no live provider incident is claimed. The failure is confined to the DeepSeek usage result, not a Gateway crash.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate each row in the existing single-pass fetcher instead of trusting an asserted response type. Skip non-record rows and rows with a present non-string currency, whose amount cannot be assigned a reliable unit. Missing/null currencies keep their existing formatting and credits fallback. Existing currency formatting, balance components, unavailable-account handling, and billing rules stay intact.

Author simplification review: removed the unchecked response type; production code is net four lines smaller. Regression coverage extends the existing owner suite without new helpers or production test hooks.

## Evidence

Tested against `c99807a541c86cc49ffcc4d9dbabd1219f65bc53` on macOS arm64 / Node v26.12.1. Inputs are synthetic.

- Owner regression: `pnpm test src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.deepseek.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. On the base, the new mixed-row cases throw at `info.total_balance` and `currency?.trim()`. With the fix, the suite passes, including malformed rows around usable rows and exact no-data snapshots. The unchanged mixed-currency and unavailable-account controls also pass. Final command wall time: 2.494s; file duration: 940ms. Upstream CI time is not yet available.
- Real HTTP boundary: exercised the public SDK `fetchDeepSeekUsage` lazy entry point with native Node fetch against a loopback server via its supported `fetchFn` argument. The server checked method, path, synthetic authorization, and Accept headers; the transport asserted the production URL. Five requests per run, no live provider access. The identical proof failed on the base and passed with the patch; listener/connections closed after each run.

  ```text
  BASE
  valid-only: PASS
  null-before: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'total_balance')
  null-after: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'total_balance')
  numeric-currency-before: TypeError: currency?.trim is not a function
  numeric-currency-after: TypeError: currency?.trim is not a function
  HTTP requests: 5; contract failures: 4

  PATCHED
  valid-only: PASS
  null-before: PASS
  null-after: PASS
  numeric-currency-before: PASS
  numeric-currency-after: PASS
  HTTP requests: 5; contract failures: 0
  ```

  Every passing scenario independently asserts `Balance $1.25 · Granted $0.25 · Topped up $1.00` and `[{ type: "balance", amount: 1.25, unit: "USD" }]`.
- Usage loader, plugin/proxy routing, shared HTTP bounds/cancellation, SDK auth helper, and formatting checks pass: `pnpm test src/infra/provider-usage.load.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.load.plugin.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.shared.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-usage.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.format.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (49.953s including cold worker compilation).
- Targeted repository typecheck, type-aware lint, local oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. The targeted typecheck retains repository strict options and the existing qrcode ambient declaration; no configuration or dependency changes are included.
- Local runtime build passes: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_WORKER_DEPLOY_BUNDLE=0 pnpm build:runtime` (100.954s). The emitted `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-usage.js` entry point also passes the same five real HTTP scenarios. This supported runtime-only option omits the sealed worker deploy bundle and package declarations. The default runtime build first failed downloading a worker native asset (`ENOTFOUND registry.npmjs.org`) in the offline environment. The successful local build reports non-fatal Control UI size-budget warnings; full package/release builds and CI formatter parity are not claimed.

Reproduction payload: one valid row `{ currency: " usd ", total_balance: "1.25", granted_balance: "0.25", topped_up_balance: "1" }`, with either `null` or `{ currency: 42, total_balance: "9" }` placed before or after it in `balance_infos`. prs.title: fix(templates): empty workspace overrides silently select a default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `templates add` / `templates dev` accept an explicitly empty `--workspace ""` (or whitespace) override and then **silently select a different workspace path** instead of rejecting it. The user asked for workspace `""`, the plan reports a derived default (for example `~/.openclaw/workspace-<name>`), and the CLI exits 0 — the requested override is dropped without any diagnostic.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator who passes an empty `--workspace` value (empty shell variable, `--workspace="$VAR"` with `VAR` unset, copy-paste error) now gets `exit 1` with blocker code `invalid_workspace` and the message `Workspace path must not be empty.` before anything is written, instead of a plan that quietly points the new agent at a default path. Omitting the option still selects the default; an explicit non-empty path still wins. Whitespace-only input is now rejected as invalid instead of resolving to the current working directory and failing later with a confusing `Workspace "..." already exists.` collision message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI adapters dropped falsy `--workspace` values (`...(opts.workspace ? { workspace: opts.workspace } : {})`), so empty never reached the owner; the lifecycle owner also canonicalized any non-undefined value, so `"   "` resolved to the cwd. The fix forwards the raw value unchanged through both adapters (`templates-cli.project.ts`, `templates-cli.runtime.ts`) and validates it at the existing owner (`src/templates/lifecycle.ts`): `undefined` still means "derive the default path", empty/whitespace is blocked with `invalid_workspace`, non-empty keeps the canonical path logic. The two hardcoded `already exists` blocker reasons now use the workspace-specific message. No new timeout, permission rule, public API or SDK export, no new state/schema; docs sentence added in `docs/cli/templates.md`.

## Evidence

Base `6ae24e93de69d4bac90be25d61e0c6f66a23ed31` → Candidate `eb64358ad0971aed2d735d0f4f7a418cd2ef1350`

Environment: Linux x86_64, Node v24.22.1, normally built `openclaw.mjs` (`pnpm build`) at each commit, isolated `HOME` + `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with `gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates: true`, fixture Template package `proof-tpl` (`package.json` + `CLAW.md`), real CLI invocations (no mocks).

| Command (real shipped CLI) | base result | candidate result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `templates dev ./proof-tpl --workspace "" --json` | **exit 0**, `agent.workspace = <home>/.openclaw/workspace-proof-tpl` (silent default), no blockers | **exit 1**, `agent.workspace = ""`, blocker `invalid_workspace`, "Workspace path must not be empty." |
| `templates add ./proof-tpl --dry-run --workspace "" --json` | **exit 0**, silent default workspace | **exit 1**, `workspace = ""`, blocker `invalid_workspace`, no writes (dry-run) |
| `templates dev ./proof-tpl --workspace "   " --json` | exit 1, but resolves to the **cwd** `/tmp/ws0-proof/work` and reports `workspace_collision` "already exists" | exit 1, `workspace = "   "`, blocker `invalid_workspace` |
| `templates dev ./proof-tpl --workspace /tmp/ws0-proof/newws --json` (control) | exit 0, `agent.workspace = /tmp/ws0-proof/newws` | exit 0, `agent.workspace = /tmp/ws1-proof/newws` |
| `templates dev ./proof-tpl --json` (control, option omitted) | exit 0, default `<home>/.openclaw/workspace-proof-tpl` | exit 0, default `<home>/.openclaw/workspace-proof-tpl` |
| `templates add ./proof-tpl --dry-run --json` (control, option omitted) | exit 0, default workspace | exit 0, default workspace |

Regression tests, remote container (`lexiflow-all:latest`, node 24.22.1, `node_modules/.bin/vitest run <files> --maxWorkers=1`, tests only run remotely):

- Phase 1, candidate: `src/cli/templates-cli.test.ts src/cli/templates-cli.project.test.ts src/templates/schema.test.ts src/templates/gateway-add-plan.test.ts src/templates/add-stateless.test.ts src/templates/application-schema.test.ts src/templates/project.test.ts` → **7 files, 154 passed / 1 skipped, exit 0, 140.05 s**.
- Phase 2, red on base (only the 3 production files reverted to base): **2 failed / 20 passed, exit 1** — `templates-cli.test.ts:234` ("refuses an explicitly empty workspace override") and `templates-cli.project.test.ts` fail on base with `workspace: <default>` + missing `invalid_workspace`, and pass with the fix.
- Phase 3: candidate files restored, `workspaceEmpty` present in all 3 production files.

Negative claims: no Windows or whitespace-normalization behavior beyond rejecting whitespace-only input is claimed; no Gateway runtime behavior is claimed (the plan JSON path is exercised offline); the proof shows the empty-override drop, not that any default-path derivation logic changed.

## Focused Checks and Simplification

Whole-PR delta: production +21/−14 (net +7: `src/templates/lifecycle.ts` +19/−12, `templates-cli.project.ts` 1/1, `templates-cli.runtime.ts` 1/1), tests +24/−0, docs +2/−2, test-lines allocation +2 (`config/test-lines-allocations/templates-empty-workspace.txt` = 24 ≤ +24 added test lines).

Local (static only, no local tests): `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (total 6,509,786 / ceiling 6,509,843), `check-line-cap-ratchet`, `check-max-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm docs:format:check`, `oxlint` on changed files, `git diff --check` — all green.

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous behavior (empty override silently selects the default workspace) without migrations or persisted state changes. Blast radius is the `templates add` / `templates dev` CLI plan path for `--workspace` overrides. Unchanged: omitting `--workspace` still derives the default unused workspace path, explicit non-empty paths still pass through canonicalization, non-templates commands are untouched, and the `already exists` collision detection for real paths keeps its existing messages.
