prs.title: fix(cli): write diagnostics exports to the selected physical directory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`gateway diagnostics export --output selected/../bundle.zip` writes into the wrong directory when `selected` is a directory symlink, and reports success. The command collapses the path lexically before any filesystem call. For `selected -> physical/nested`, the filesystem reads `selected/../bundle.zip` as `physical/bundle.zip`, while lexical normalization produces `<cwd>/bundle.zip` — a different, valid destination.

`gateway stability --export --output` shares the same owner (`writeSupportExportFromCli` → `writeDiagnosticSupportExport`) and had the same behavior.

## User Impact

An operator who exports diagnostics through a symlinked directory gets the archive in the directory the path actually names. Ordinary paths, `~`-prefixed paths, quoted whitespace names, directory-vs-file selection and the existing default location keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the explicit output parent through the existing fs-safe prefix traversal (`resolvePathPrefixSync`) instead of `path.resolve`. That returns the physical existing ancestor plus the segments that do not exist yet, so the result names the same directory the filesystem will use. An input whose parent chain is not fully created keeps the previous lexical result: no symlink can redirect a segment that does not exist, and the existing "missing directory becomes the created parent" behavior stays intact.

`expandHomePrefix` replaces `resolveHomeRelativePath` at this one call site so a `~`-prefixed output is expanded without being collapsed lexically before the physical traversal.

Classification: behavior-completing. The fix reuses the shipped fs-safe owner that `src/cli/media-output.ts` and `src/cli/capability-cli/media-understanding-command.ts` already use for the same class of input.

## Evidence

Actual repository CLI on Linux / Node 24.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (mode 700), synthetic symlink layout, no network and no model:

```text
fixture: <root>/physical/nested, <root>/cwd, <root>/cwd/selected -> ../physical/nested
cwd: <root>/cwd
command: node dist/entry.js gateway diagnostics export --output "selected/../bundle.zip"
```

| Run | Reported path | Archive on disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base `636454ee16af` | `<root>/cwd/bundle.zip` | `<root>/cwd/bundle.zip`; `physical/` empty |
| Head `20b9919813f6` | `<root>/physical/bundle.zip` | `<root>/physical/bundle.zip`; `cwd/` has no archive |

Same layout through the shared caller:

| Run | `gateway stability --export --output "selected/../stab.zip"` |
| --- | --- |
| Base | reported `<root>/cwd/stab.zip`, written there |
| Head | reported `<root>/physical/stab.zip`, written there |

Control (no symlink, no `..`): `--output out/plain.zip` reports and writes `<root>/out/plain.zip` on both base and head.

- Regression test: `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts` adds one case that builds `physical/nested`, links `selected` to it, and exports through `${tempDir}/selected/../bundle.zip`. On base production code it fails with `expected '<tmp>/physical/bundle.zip' to be '<tmp>/bundle.zip'`; on the fix it passes. The file's 22 tests pass with the fix.
- Existing coverage kept green: quoted output directory name, literal leading/trailing whitespace in an explicit file path, blank output path falling back to the default support directory, config-size failure and the stability-bundle cases all still pass.
- Gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `oxlint` clean on both files; line-cap ratchet `OK: 2 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth`; test-lines ratchet `Net test lines: +19; allowance: 400`.
- Not tested: Windows (`path.sep === "\\"` and junction semantics are unexercised; the new test is `skipIf(win32)` like the adjacent whitespace cases), a real remote Gateway, and exact-head hosted CI.

```sh
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.logging.config.ts \
  src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Isolated state only: the proof used throwaway `/tmp` directories with `chmod 700`. No production Gateway, session, config or token was touched, and no files outside those directories were created.

prs.title: fix(plugins): install the local source the selected path names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins install "./selected/../plugin-b"` installs a different, valid neighbouring plugin and reports success. The install plan collapses the local spec lexically (`resolveUserPath`) before any filesystem call. For `selected -> physical/nested`, the filesystem reads that name as `physical/plugin-b`, while lexical normalization produces `<cwd>/plugin-b`.

Distinct valid projects make this a successful operation on the wrong resource: the operator gets another plugin's code, manifest and capabilities installed under their chosen path.

## User Impact

A local plugin install selects, validates, scans and copies the source the supplied path actually names. Ordinary paths, `~`-prefixed paths, archives, `file:` specs, bundled lookups, surrounding-whitespace trimming and the existing "Plugin path not found" diagnostic keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the local spec parent through the existing fs-safe prefix traversal (`resolvePathPrefixSync`) instead of the lexical `resolveUserPath`. That returns the physical existing ancestor plus the segments that do not exist yet, so the result names the same directory the filesystem will use.

Two existing `resolveUserPath` behaviors stay in place, so no previously accepted input changes:

- **Surrounding whitespace** is still trimmed before home expansion. `plugins install "/path/plugin "` continues to select `/path/plugin`.
- **A regular file in the parent chain** still yields the structured `Plugin path not found` plan instead of a raw `ENOTDIR` throw.

Both are implemented by computing the lexical answer with `resolveUserPath` first and only replacing it when the parent chain resolves physically without an unresolved `..` segment.

Classification: behavior-completing. The fix reuses the shipped fs-safe owner that `src/cli/media-output.ts`, `src/cli/capability-cli/media-understanding-command.ts` and `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts` already use for this class of input.

## Evidence

Actual repository CLI on Linux / Node 24.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (mode 700), synthetic fixtures, no network and no model.

### The wrong-source install

```text
fixture: <root>/physical/nested, <root>/cwd, <root>/cwd/selected -> ../physical/nested
         <root>/physical/plugin-b  (id: plugin-real)
         <root>/cwd/plugin-b       (id: plugin-decoy)
command: node dist/entry.js plugins install "./selected/../plugin-b" --force --accept-capabilities
```

| Run | Reported install target | Source actually selected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base (main source, same tree) | `state/extensions/plugin-decoy` | `<root>/cwd/plugin-b` — the lexical sibling |
| Head `44e65317f2a5` | `state/extensions/plugin-real` | `<root>/physical/plugin-b` — what the path names |

The base run prints `Installing to …/plugin-decoy…` and exits 0: a successful install of the wrong plugin.

### The two input contracts

```text
1. trim:    plugins install "/tmp/v3/plain/solo "    -> Installing to …/plugin-solo…
2. ENOTDIR: plugins install "/tmp/v3/file/child/plugin" -> Plugin path not found: /tmp/v3/file/child/plugin
```

Both match main's behavior; the first version of this patch broke both, which is what the review caught.

### Tests

`src/cli/plugin-install-plan.test.ts` adds three cases against the shared planner:

| Case | main | first patch | head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected/../selected-sibling` selects `physical/selected-sibling` | ✗ (lexical sibling) | ✓ | ✓ |
| `"<root>/plugin "` trims to `<root>/plugin` | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| `<root>/file/child/plugin` returns the not-found plan | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |

The file's 9 tests pass with the fix.

- Gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `oxlint` clean on both files; line-cap ratchet `OK: 2 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth`; test-lines ratchet within allowance.
- Not tested: Windows (junction semantics are unexercised; the new tests are `skipIf(win32)`), a live Gateway install of the resulting plugin, and exact-head hosted CI. A bundled-plugin config-validation error appears after the install step in this dist build and is unrelated to the source selection shown above.

```sh
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts \
  src/cli/plugin-install-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Isolated state only: the proof used throwaway `/tmp` directories with `chmod 700`. No production Gateway, session, config, plugin install or token was touched.

prs.title: fix(ci): Control UI E2E shards time out on slow hosted runners
prs.body:
Closes #198524

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes hourly Control UI E2E shards reaching the 20-minute test deadline on slower hosted runners while tests are still making progress.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Every selected test still runs, with the existing four-worker limit and 20-minute step deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run nine compact Control UI shards instead of six, plus the separate browser-extension row. This changes aggregate browser worker slots from 24 to 36 and adds three setups; the existing full-inventory reserve of thirteen rows and registration envelope remain unchanged. The maintainer accepts that capacity tradeoff for the observed hourly timeout family.

Keep `guest-person-identities` with the existing compiled-worker borrowers so they share invocation preparation. The weighted splitter and timing data are unchanged. All four current main borrower entries remain; separate open #197854's additions are not imported or removed.

The contributor's original investigation covered 282 jobs in 47 hourly runs: hosted EPYC 7763 runners timed out in 35 of 63 jobs, versus zero of 102 Blacksmith jobs. Current source run [43763625500](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763625500) again had two aggregate timeouts. Replaying its inventory projects 921.5 seconds of file weight at six shards versus 614.3 at nine, before startup/preparation overhead. Those are historical observations and projections, not a measured final-head speedup.

Thanks @daniel-lxs for the investigation and focused shard/affinity change.

## Evidence

- Approved historical run [43554096226, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43554096226) used nine four-worker Control UI shards; its test steps finished in 540–663 seconds below the unchanged 1,200-second deadline. It used an older 912-file inventory and failed 19 browser cases plus one unit case, so it is not passing current-main qualification.
- The first native baseline integration included #198537, #198546, #198593, #198592 and #198585. On historical head 4610795e703cc31f9a13dbd8b63bb4cdbd87f00c, all 19 formerly failing Chromium cases and the Bun unit case passed locally. This proof is retained, not represented as a fresh replay on the new head.
- That head's subsequent CI run [43780093071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43780093071) failed one WebKit 390px history-preload assertion, not the aggregate shard deadline. Exact merge/main-parent original-case replays passed on both macOS and Linux; those passing replays did not establish inherited failure or a cure.
- Native successor **f2f426b743a33591869360f2288ac2d9879f796b** integrates exact main **ad09e3821ad152870e6915de901dfa108d538a9a**, including separately reproduced history-input owner repair #199890, while retaining the same eight-file +24/-18 product delta. This is a material owner change at the failed entry point, but it is not claimed to uniquely explain the previous WebKit startup failure.
- On this exact successor, eight sharding cases, 23 focused planner/selection scenarios (including newly inherited manual-runtime routing), and the unchanged single WebKit 390px entry all pass. The WebKit case takes 5.395 seconds, with a 28.32-second wrapper. These are local qualification costs, not hosted capacity measurements.
- Fresh independent Codex review through P2 is scoped-clean. Existing thirteen-row reserve, release/noncompact behavior and borrower membership are preserved. Required `pnpm check:changed --base ad09e382…` ran once in 397.57 seconds: every other selected gate passed, but dead-export scanning failed (script 1, production 0, full-tree 2). The known rollback helper export was introduced by #198268 and is now repaired on main by #199897 / ef8d709a05a391011ccb1dd1b2c931d0cf7e8095; this retained local result predates that repair. A newly exposed script export, `resolvePluginPrereleaseExtensionRuntimes`, was introduced by #198278 / 44522c44d695d04a64afc9d89e12de273b2a801c with a real dynamic caller in `plugin-prerelease.yml`; the existing workflow-consumer compiler does not model that call. It must not be deleted as dead code. These are recorded main regressions outside this patch, not ignored noise or a claimed green check. Their inputs are identical to the selected baseline, but no exact-baseline scan/admin waiver is claimed here.

Fresh exact-head hosted CI and final-head Claw zero open remain required. The old WebKit failure is not being waived as inherited or called fixed solely because local replays pass.

prs.title: fix(release): accept freshly published package candidates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Package Acceptance rejecting a just-published OpenClaw release with npm ETARGET because the source checkout applies a seven-day dependency cooldown to the candidate itself.

## User Impact

Release operators can verify the exact package immediately after publication without disabling dependency cooldowns or changing package integrity checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing candidate pack runner now excludes only the root openclaw package from the release-age filter for that download. It still validates the package spec, suppresses package scripts, preserves the selected tarball identity, and runs the existing digest and tarball checks. No repository-wide npm configuration or dependency installation policy changes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the actual source=npm CLI on main f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a: exact openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.4 failed ETARGET under npm 11.20.0 because it was younger than seven days.
- Same CLI with the fix downloaded that exact version and passed the complete tarball integrity checker. SHA-256: 0be5af77a78a5b7860b8e20e5f76267491ed07883ce40c653f9443bd78f47a7d. No publication or hosted acceptance workflow was dispatched.
- Added a real-npm regression using a private loopback registry and fresh package timestamp: red ETARGET on base, green after repair; another fresh package remains rejected under the same configuration. The regression ran using pinned npm 12.2.1 under the repository test runtime.
- Candidate resolver: 45/45 tests; npm runner sibling: 9/9 tests. Combined wrapper wall time 6.16 seconds; changed file test time 2.27 seconds. Hosted CI duration pending.
- Scripts and tooling-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and git diff --check pass.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 narrative review of the complete final diff found no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper/Codex executables were unavailable; local autoreview via the supported OpenClaw engine was attempted but failed native execution (exit 1). This is not a helper-clean review claim; hosted review remains pending.
- Simplification: one scoped argument at the existing pack owner, no new production helper or state; production +11/-1 lines, test +75/-1 lines.

Limits: Linux-local reproduction. This fixes candidate cooldown resolution, not selection of release-specific tooling for older package formats, and does not claim a hosted Docker acceptance run or Windows execution.

prs.title: improve(ci): overlap isolated upgrade baseline probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Published-baseline startup checks delay every package-upgrade validation row while seven independent package installs run serially.

## User Impact

Release validation can admit its upgrade matrix earlier. Product behavior, selected baselines, scenario coverage, failure policy, and evidence ordering are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run probes in pairs on the existing runner, with each probe retaining its private HOME, npm cache/config/prefix, and OpenClaw state. Keep installation, version, and real CLI configuration startup serial within each probe. Await the sole planner caller. No extra runners, cache, pool manager, new configuration, or removed checks. Two installs may compete for disk/network/CPU; the cap deliberately avoids seven-way contention.

## Evidence

- Observed release-check planner [43773667009 / 132997502412](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43773667009/job/132997502412) spent 126.7 seconds on seven serial probes before matrix dispatch. A shorter planner advances this branch; whole-FRV savings depend on its final position relative to other mandatory children and downstream capacity.
- Actual local production-owner replay, seven versions (`2026.11.3`, `2026.11.2`, `2026.9.37`, `2026.6.34`, `2026.9.8`, `2026.9.9`, `2026.9.7`), fresh isolated caches/homes per probe: **89.17s sequential → 61.42s bounded-two**, 27.75s lower in this one sample pair. All seven baselines usable; returned groups and all 21 command/status/signal outcomes identical. Registry installs and actual published `--version` / `config set gateway.mode local` ran, not stubs.
- This is a functional workload/sanity comparison on a shared, loaded Linux host, not an interleaved five-sample benchmark, median/p95 claim, hosted gain, or measured full-FRV gain. OS/registry caching and concurrent host work remain uncontrolled. The log-based decision evidence and bounded operation count are primary; no full FRV was dispatched.
- Real planner CLI regression verifies two probes overlap, a third waits, isolated prefixes, and deterministic evidence. Serial implementation failed the overlap regression; candidate passed. Test waits use filesystem events rather than timing-based polling; timeout only bounds a broken barrier.
- 19 focused tests passed; Node selected sibling suites passed **65 tests** (77.15s wrapper, 75.11s suite including ~50s worker compilation). Final event-based probe suite: **8 passed**, 1.07s test time / 2.65s wrapper. Existing install/launch hard failures and unusable-version/runtime skips remain covered.
- Production scripts and tooling-test typechecks, touched type-aware lint, format, and whitespace checks passed. Final test-only event-barrier refinement also passed its touched typecheck/lint/format checks.

## Simplification and Limits

Retain the existing baseline owner and summary producer. The necessary growth is one asynchronous subprocess adapter plus a two-at-a-time loop, not a scheduler abstraction; the only consumer is migrated. One compact regression extends the existing executable fixture. Against the merge base: production **+41/-15**; tests **+40/-1**. No upgrade or Gateway behavior changes. Full hosted CI and completed ClawSweeper remain outstanding; not yet review-ready. Local independent review is explicitly waived for this task.

Rollback: restore the synchronous probe and its single caller.

prs.title: improve(ci): narrow FRV admission helper checkout
prs.body:
## Summary
- Limit the FRV admission helper checkout to its runtime imports, workflow sources, workspace manifests, and patches instead of materializing the entire repository.
- Keep the same immutable Q, target C, full frozen dependency installation, source checks, publication inventory, and validation coverage. No cache, new scheduler, relaxed admission, or changed dependency owner.

## Wall-time evidence
The helper checkout in the critical `resolve_target` prefix took **31 seconds** in both observed attempts of FRV [43770476915](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43770476915). It gates downstream dispatch; unlike work in a slack lane, any checkout saving advances the critical path. This change does not add a runner or setup phase.

At base `210e3c4282c5b3549b239f8c21a6788b08ba9a29`, an actual sparse checkout retained **35,536 / 65,473 tracked files** and **321,903,260 / 777,473,576 uncompressed blob bytes**: 45.7% fewer files and 58.6% fewer bytes materialized. All **72** publication tooling paths and **213** child workspace manifests (plus the root manifest) remain. Existing full `scripts`/`src`/`packages` trees intentionally avoid introducing a fragile import-closure owner.

**No measured hosted wall-time gain is claimed.** The local shared-object checkout took 1.40s, but it is not comparable with the hosted 31s checkout. Sparse materialization is smaller; Git object transfer, queue time, filesystem/cache behavior, and the unchanged pnpm install bound actual improvement. Expected wall benefit is within that existing checkout prefix, not proportional to removed bytes. No full FRV dispatch was needed or performed.

## Validation
- Existing trusted-checkout regression: fails on base (1 failed / 12 passed), green with the sparse checkout. It still checks immutable refs and disabled persisted credentials; no new test case/scaffold.
- **211 tests passed**: continuation workflow, publication admission, and no-push release workflow suites.
- Isolated actual sparse checkout: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts` passed (6.4s), without reconciling the shared worktree install.
- Actual production qualification preflight passed for same-revision and frozen-C/different-Q inputs; neither selected a parser-required branch, so these alone are not parser proof.
- Actual `full-release-publication-admission.mts` in the isolated sparse Q checkout admitted frozen C `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`: **102 packages / 4 platforms**, inventory digest `185d52d411ca7fcca0d87612cde138a8adf5a5096c2c02ead7887b0ffeb3305c`. This exercised the real retained-object inventory/parser and exact tooling-byte checks, not an import-only stub. Registry observation collection is unchanged and was not rerun in this local proof.
- Tooling typecheck, touched type-aware lint, format, `git diff --check`, full pinned actionlint/zizmor and workflow guards passed. An empty-token environment initially prevented zizmor startup; removing the empty credential environment variables allowed the normal guard to pass.

## Simplification / risk
The smallest change is the checkout declaration, not a filtered installation or new dependency manifest. Production/workflow **+14/-0**; tests **+8/-1** against merge base. Every retained pattern serves imports or the unchanged workspace install. No local independent review was run (explicit task waiver). Hosted ClawSweeper and exact-head CI remain required before calling this review-ready.

Rollback: remove the sparse-checkout declaration. Future admission imports outside these retained trees must extend the checkout and its real-workload proof.

prs.title: fix: retain subagent results through Gateway restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes finished subagent results being suspended or silently removed when a Gateway restart interrupts requester settlement or completion delivery.

## User Impact

Dashboard requesters recover owed results after restart, retries retain the accepted input identity, and every removed registry row leaves a recorded delivered, suspended, or discarded outcome with a reason. No configuration or database schema change is required. Removal receipts use the existing session-state history retention (30 days / 50,000 events).

## Why This Change Was Made

A settled requester can have pending child results without any interrupted-run marker. Startup skipped that requester, then the sweeper and announce cleanup interpreted retired process authority as a permanently replaced store. Recovery now selects those obligations through the existing requester index, and both false failure branches are removed.

An accepted completion replay could retain its operator profile but lose its original sender presentation. That changed the accepted-input identity despite identical content and provenance. Replay now preserves accepted attribution when the freshly admitted profile matches. It retains the complete-request conflict check. This builds on #199695's committed consumption fact: a consumed private result remains delivered and a restored consumed row finalizes without redispatch; accepting an input alone does not prove consumption.

Retryable rows are protected from completed-run cleanup. The single registry deletion owner records a terminal fact atomically with removal, including the terminal postimage when requester settlement or lifecycle expiry immediately retires a row.

## Evidence

Team r337 (`257759ae` → `dd2d58be`) drained at 23:31:19Z, exited at 23:31:27, restarted at 23:31:29, and reached readiness at 23:31:53. Read-only observations at +1/+6 minutes reported 4 lost results among 14 captured successful results: one was suspended as `store replaced` without a delivery attempt; three had accepted-input idempotency conflicts during drain, then failed/retryable rows disappeared. Two additional pending rows disappeared without delivery evidence. Production transcript contents were not accessed; synthetic evidence does not establish which of those three production inputs were consumed.

Related prior fixes: #198905, #199488, #198807, #198843, #199575. Integrated #199695 at `6d7a56de584a`.

Focused native suites passed 160 tests (117 custody/lifecycle cases and 43 requester-coordination cases), including a real-worker lifecycle-expiry regression that was red before the review correction and green afterward. Baseline regressions fail for unmarked requester discovery, false store replacement, six-minute deletion of retryable results, absent removal facts, and restored sender attribution. The real Gateway subprocess harness passes announce-in-flight, private consumption, busy-requester, settled-private-result, unmarked-requester, and private-announce crash cases: **0 lost of 8 explicitly checked completion rows**, with another restart checking each captured result’s delivered receipt and single input (six repeat checks). The unmarked case recreates the observed persisted shape by removing only restart markers from the stopped synthetic requester after real child capture/drain; it verifies the result is pending and absent from the transcript before startup. The provider is synthetic; Gateway processes, SQLite, admission, transcript consumption, shutdown and restart are real.

Published stable `2026.11.3` → candidate compatibility proof passed through the supported `doctor --fix` upgrade: two completed registry rows and the original transcript survived, and a fresh chat completed. Automatic-startup-only upgrade hit a separate secrets-loading `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR` after migration; that failure remains recorded, and is not represented as passing upgrade proof. Stable also hit a prompt-prefix error in the repeated-delegation setup, so pending recovery and stable data compatibility are separate proofs.

`pnpm check:changed` completed after each correction. Own test lint findings were fixed and both affected lint scopes pass. Its remaining dead-export failure reproduces on exact parent `6d7a56de584a`: `resolveRollbackWorkerInputs` in the unchanged rollback test helper became unused when `e4a30936bb35` / #198268 removed its external consumer. This is a main regression, not a passing gate. Format, typechecks, database/import guards and other checks passed. Codex P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable defects.

Production delta: +141/-56, net +85 lines; tests +379 net lines. Growth is predominantly the requested atomic terminal removal facts and explicit removal reasons; the false store-replacement failure path is deleted. No schema, configuration, dependency, or cache change. No Control UI runtime imports of changed modules were found.

Linux/btrfs synthetic measurement: 42,871,726,080-byte agent DB (~39.9 GiB), 10,830 sessions, 4,300 obligations, 62,000 files / 1.116 GB; Node 24.22.1, 4 CPU / 12 GiB container limits. Five interleaved A/B process pairs, each with 20 warmups and 20 trials, plus two A/A pairs and separate allocation sampling. Baseline selects 4,300 sessions; candidate selects 6,046, recovering 1,746 omitted requesters.

| Discovery owner | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median of process wall medians | 172.5 ms | 180.4 ms |
| Median of process CPU medians (all threads) | 290.7 ms | 318.5 ms |
| Pooled wall p95 | 431.7 ms | 586.5 ms |
| Sampled main-thread allocation per pass | 49.79 MB | 51.54 MB |

A/A wall medians were 171.7/170.3 and 170.3/169.7 ms; CPU medians were 287.9/271.8 and 295.3/289.6 ms. Allocation control was 49.72 MB/pass. The added recovery costs work; this is not a speedup claim. These timings cover startup discovery, not full startup or workspace I/O, and sampled allocation excludes worker heaps. No Team data was copied or mutated.

Initial-head CI run 43782742045 failed only when the Bun correlated-recovery shard exceeded its 60-second no-output watchdog (exit 143, no assertion reported). The six selected tests passed locally under Bun with that same watchdog. This is not claimed inherited or fixed; the final head requires its own CI.

CI run 43786635304 exposed an inherited fixture race in five requester-receipt cases. All five reproduce on its exact main parent `6aae38f36ee8` under Linux CPU contention. Normal session maintenance pruned newly created child fixtures because `updatedAt: 1` dated them in 1970; diagnostic tracing reached the committed session-removal owner. The fixture was introduced by `903b5f20eb4a` / #187270. This PR repairs the two fixture timestamps: the same contention run changes from 5 failed to 5 passed, and all 43 affected-file tests pass. Production retention and receipt assertions are unchanged. This is a repaired main test regression, not ignored CI noise.

CI run 43791145697 found a transcript-counting defect in the new private-announce harness. On exact CI merge `dc6c6b3b61d3`, a 1-CPU Linux run reproduces two matching carriers: the actual completion input and a later Recently Completed Subagents summary. Changing only the filter to count completion-event fragments passes under identical contention. No delivery assertion is removed. The final owner correction also has two baseline-red regressions: restored consumed private input must finalize without announcing again, and process-custody retirement must leave undelivered input retryable. Twelve selected lifecycle cases pass, including both regressions. Final Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.

Final Linux proof also passes graceful private announce and busy requester at one CPU, then private announce interrupted by process crash at four CPUs. The one-CPU crash attempt timed out during setup before any crash or completed-result capture; the unchanged case passes at the fixture’s normal capacity (28.17 seconds total), with unchanged timeouts and assertions. It is a recorded setup limit, not a claimed restart failure or inherited defect. All three final scenarios retain delivered receipts and exactly one captured-result input through a second restart.

The consumer sweep caught an additional contract while simplifying the false retirement branch: an actual store replacement observed during an announce must remain terminal even if its selector later returns. The existing test became red with pending instead of suspended. The admission helper now reports its concrete replacement observation to the cleanup owner; ordinary process retirement still does not imply replacement. This retains the existing store boundary without adding a cache, schema, or generic failure classification. Final focused proof and independent review cover this correction.

Final correction verification: 17 selected lifecycle cases and all 8 selected store-replacement cases pass, including the previously failing selector-return case; all 40 requester-completion settlement cases, 3 normalization cases, and 38 requester-wake product cases pass. The latter covers six-child batches, nested completion, overlapping callers, receipt retention, yielded cohorts, cancellation, and descendant settlement. Final Codex P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.

Exact-head CI 43797910391 also exposes a new main lint regression: `unicorn(prefer-structured-clone)` in unchanged `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118`. The exact CI main parent `8862ffc735fe6f5e553a69ea2fb7731a6b90fd87` reproduces the identical diagnostic with the normal focused lint wrapper. Commit `f4d2e45592438dbaae12975e1c4223a991285b7a` / #199909 introduced the JSON snapshot expression. This is an attributed main regression requiring follow-up, not a passing gate or ignored noise; the repair must preserve its intentional JSON normalization. No CI rerun requested. The final-head ClawSweeper review has zero open items and no findings.

prs.title: improve(ci): admit slow package recovery checks earlier
prs.body:
Related: #198925

## What Problem This Solves

Full release validation can leave slow package-recovery checks waiting until the last wave of its capped Docker matrix.

## User Impact

No runtime/product behavior changes. Release operators should get the same coverage sooner when package acceptance is the critical path; no runner capacity or timeout increase.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing stable priority list to admit package-verification and package-publication recovery first. Preserve the earlier first-hop/legacy ordering, every baseline/scenario row, independent failures/retries, and the 32-job cap. This is two list entries, not a new timing planner.

## Evidence

- In [candidate checks 43773667009](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43773667009), [the final verification-recovery job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43773667009/job/132998350655) waited **2,341s**, then ran **1,437s**. The 90-row matrix reached exactly 32 simultaneous jobs and took **3,778s**. Candidate checks, not normal CI, were the final child of FRV 43770476915; its successful parent was a recovery attempt, so total retry elapsed time is not a clean single-run benchmark.

prs.title: fix(tlon): long replies with a code block arrive split into broken blocks
prs.body:
Related: #196429

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long assistant replies that contain a fenced code block arrive split into broken blocks on Tlon when the reply crosses the channel's 10,000-character text chunk limit.

## User Impact

User impact: on Tlon, a long answer with code now arrives with the code block intact (closed at the split and reopened with its original info string when the block must be divided), instead of code rendering as plain text and the trailing prose landing inside a stray code block. Every chunk still respects the channel limit, and plain-text chunking is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tlon declared `chunkerMode: "markdown"` but configured the fence-blind `chunkTextForOutbound` splitter, so a chunk boundary inside a fenced block leaves an unclosed fence. The adapter now uses the fence-aware splitter the plugin SDK already exports (`chunkMarkdownTextWithMode(text, limit, "length")`), the same change #196167 made for Matrix and #196331 for Mattermost (both merged with this exact one-line swap).

Scope: this PR intentionally covers **Tlon only**. MS Teams and Zalouser have the identical one-line defect and fix, but shipped-entry delivery proof is not achievable for them without a tenant — the Bot Framework `serviceUrl` boundary only permits Microsoft HTTPS hosts (`extensions/msteams/src/bot-framework-service-url.ts`), and Zalouser sends through the Zalo user protocol with no configurable endpoint. They are tracked in #199876 with the prepared fix noted. Mattermost remains covered by the merged #196331. The single-channel scope follows the merged Mattermost precedent.

## Evidence

- **Recorded shipped-entry run (red on base, green on head):** `openclaw message send --channel tlon --target '~nec' -m <13,331-char fenced reply>` (1,200 Python lines + trailing `Done.`) through a running Gateway (isolated HOME, `gateway.mode: local`) against a loopback Urbit airlift fixture that records every delivered poke.
  - Head: 3 content pokes — prose `Here is the script:` (19 chars), `code[python]` 9,976 chars (`print(0)`..`print(916)`), then `code[python]` 3,312 chars (`print(917)`..`print(1199)`) plus prose `Done.`. Every poke within the 10,000-character transport limit, both code segments delivered as native code-block verses with the original info string, no fence marker in prose, concatenated code equal to the source exactly. CLI: `✅ Sent via Tlon. Message ID: ~zod/170.141.184.508.251.111.928.028.813.435.724.896.403`. All loopback; no external endpoints, credentials, or personal data.
  - Base (only `extensions/tlon/src/channel.ts` reverted to main's splitter, same transport): the continuation code arrives as plaintext prose — `expected 'plaintext' to be 'python'` — the reported bug.
- Checked-in regression test (`extensions/tlon/src/outbound.loopback.test.ts`, "delivers a long fenced reply as native code-block verses the transport accepts") asserts at the verse level: prose runs carry no fence markers, every code block keeps its `python` info string, concatenated code payloads equal the 1,200-line source exactly, and each poke fits the limit. It fails on base and passes on this head.
- `pnpm test:extension tlon` passes (269/269 with `LANG=C`; the machine default `zh_CN.UTF-8` makes setup-wizard prompt-answer tests fail on unmodified main too — environment locale sensitivity, unrelated to this change).
- `pnpm format:check` passes; oxlint on the touched files reports 0 warnings / 0 errors; extension boundary lint checks pass. The Tlon-only net test-line growth (+114) is allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/196430-markdown-fence-aware-chunking.txt`; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` passes. Note on the remaining baseline-ratchets state: the CI log on the previous head showed `net delta: +141` exactly matching its allocation, with the residual `over by: 293` coming from the base tree already exceeding its ceiling before this change (arithmetic visible in the checker's own output: base total 6,618,989 > base ceiling 6,618,696). This head reduces the delta to +114, fully allocated.


Update (10f702459): dropped the redundant tiny-limit chunker assertion from the plain-text delivery test per the review note (allocation now +112); the relationship is `Related: #196429` since #199876 retains the remaining channels.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits (#187911)
prs.body:
# Recover Guest Tasks After Concurrent Managed-Workspace Edits (#187911)

## Summary of Changes

This PR resolves issue #187911 (`fix: recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits`) by establishing an authoritative, robust, and verified reconciliation pipeline between host canonical files, sandboxed guest task projections, and the CAS baseline manifest, adhering strictly to the Product Owner's Architectural Decisions in `config-state-lifecycle.md`.

---

## Revision 7 Review Findings Addressed

### 1. Advance Acknowledgement Through Projection State's Update Operation [P1]
- **Root Cause & Fix**: Conflict acknowledgement previously read and modified projection row state without advancing through the custody boundary's formal `state.update` operation. We exported `update` on `projectionOperations` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-state.ts`), introduced `acknowledgeConflictInState(state, ...)` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-conflict-acknowledgement.ts`), and hooked `acknowledgeConflict` in `local-workspace-projection.ts` directly into `acknowledgeConflictInState(state, ...)`.
- **Outcome**: Resolving and saving a reconciled version via `sessions.files.set` now updates the projection state through the official mutation boundary, ensuring subsequent calls to `custody.synchronizeProjection()` synchronize without encountering `"Local workspace binding changed"`, copy reconciled content to `projectionDir`, and settle `pending_ref` to `null`.
- **Regression Added**: In `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts`, updated `acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict` with a real prepared git repo and baseline to assert that synchronization cleanly completes and settles `pending_ref` to `null`.

### 2. Use the File Writer's Selected Candidate for Conflict Hash Resolution [P2]
- **Root Cause & Fix**: When saving files in a session with a nested working directory (`spawnedCwd` / `fileRoot`), `sessions.files.set` previously passed the raw relative `filePath` to `resolveReconciledExpectedHash`, while using candidate path resolution inside `setSessionWorkspaceFile`. If a session was executing in a subfolder (e.g. `sub/`), the conflict on `sub/handover.md` was not matched against the expected hash in `conflicts`.
- **Resolution**: Exported `resolveSessionWorkspaceCandidatePath({ root, fileRoot, filePath })` from `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts`. In `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts`, resolved `effectivePath` once upfront and passed it to both `resolveReconciledExpectedHash` and `write(...)`. Updated `resolveCandidateBrowserPath` in `src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-conflict-acknowledgement.ts` to accept the `conflicts` map and match exact candidate paths directly.
- **Regression Added**: Added integration test `resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot` in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts` verifying that nested session candidates resolve and reconcile cleanly.

### 3. Include All Accepted Receipt Changes in the Resolved Baseline [P2]
- **Root Cause & Fix**: When overlaying resolved canonical paths onto the base manifest in `commitLocalWorkspaceReconciliation`, unconflicted modifications, additions, and deletions made by the guest task were previously omitted from the newly committed CAS baseline manifest if only partial resolutions were staged.
- **Resolution**: In `src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-conflict-resolution.ts`, parsed `snapshotBase` (when available) and applied all unconflicted additions, modifications, and deletions from `snapshot.current` to the baseline before overlaying `resolvedCanonicalPaths`, ensuring full fidelity of guest changes alongside resolved conflicts.

---

## Verification & Test Results

### 1. Vitest Test Suites (29/29 Tests Passed - 100% Green)

- **`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts` (14/14 tests passed)**:
  - ✓ allows inspecting canonical files when the managed workspace has a preserved conflict
  - ✓ acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict
  - ✓ resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot
  - ✓ saves a reconciled version when expectedHash matches the inspected guest draft in projection
  - ✓ preserves compare-and-swap protection for unseen canonical edits outside retained conflicts
  - ✓ accepts a newer guest version that the operator actually reviewed in projection
  - ✓ resolves canonical workspace-relative path when saving absolute path candidates
  - ✓ (and all 7 baseline suite tests)

- **`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.conflict.test.ts` (15/15 tests passed)**:
  - ✓ replaces projection symlinks safely without following destination links (Finding 2)
  - ✓ overlays resolved paths onto complete accepted baseline preserving unmutated baseline entries (Finding 3)
  - ✓ preserves newer guest divergence in projection if edited while conflict is pending (Finding 5)
  - ✓ allows explicitly accepted Markdown separator lines (Revision 3 Finding 1)
  - ✓ refuses to resolve when an ancestor directory component is a symlink (Revision 3 Finding 2)
  - ✓ preserves live guest symlink divergence across retries (Revision 3 Finding 4)
  - ✓ accepts an explicitly reviewed newer guest version (Revision 5 Finding 2)
  - ✓ rejects unreviewed newer guest version written after administrator review
  - ✓ preserves guest file mode changes without byte changes as conflict divergence
  - ✓ refuses acknowledgment after worktree reassignment (Security Finding)
  - ✓ (and all remaining unit regression tests)

### 2. Standalone Real-World Verification Proof (5/5 Scenarios Passed - 100% Green)

Executed `/home/masterswords/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/5fec5c34-95c1-4af4-bc25-c6d1b921c299/scratch/verify-revision-7-proof.ts`:
- **Finding 1**: State update mutation boundary & acknowledgement integration — verified conflict hash resolution and `state.update` recording `acknowledgedPaths` and `acknowledgedGuestVersions`.
- **Finding 2**: Writer's candidate path `packages/core/src/index.ts` correctly matches nested session `fileRoot` and translates hash.
- **Finding 3**: Resolved baseline includes all accepted receipt additions, modifications, deletions, and resolved paths.
- **Scenario 4**: Directory ancestor symlink escapes strictly prevented.
- **Scenario 5**: Live guest divergence preserved without byte loss.

### 3. Ratchets & Invariants Passed (Exact 0 Slack)

- `check:line-cap-ratchet`: **PASS** (`Line-cap ratchet OK: 13 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth`).
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: **PASS** (`Test lines OK: 6574567; ceiling: 6574567; slack: 0`).
- `check:assertion-safety-ratchet`: **PASS** (`assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 2381 files, 5408 grandfathered assertions`).
- Full compliance with `config-state-lifecycle.md` Product Owner Architectural Decisions.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord command deployment stops when a changed command is removed after it is listed but before it is updated.

## User Impact

User impact: startup reconciliation recreates the missing command, finishes removing obsolete commands, and saves the deployment hash so the next startup does not repeat the deployment. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A missing-command response now removes the stale listing entry so the existing create loop can restore it. PATCH and DELETE share the same narrow 404/code-10063 classification; other errors still propagate. prs.title: refactor(whatsapp): add canonical target facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WhatsApp sends that can pass a same-conversation restriction for a distinct same-digit LID, and phone-JID sends that can bypass the saved phone-to-LID mapping.

Addresses the [review findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80515#issuecomment-4417267323).

## User Impact

With `crossContext.allowWithinProvider: false`, a phone-bound conversation cannot send to an unrelated same-digit LID, including when the account uses `allowFrom: ["*"]`. Ordinary phone JIDs continue to reach contacts through their saved LID mapping.

Formed device LIDs, hosted addresses, groups, and newsletters retain their transport handling. No configuration changes or operator actions are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Target classification, authorization, session routing, actions, send addresses, and typing decisions now consume WhatsApp target facts. One lightweight parser supplies both shared policy normalization and delivery input: opaque LIDs remain distinct identities, while ordinary phone JIDs become E.164 before forward mapping.

The review repair deletes the duplicate identity parser and reduces production code by 43 lines. The complete PR adds 168 production lines and 391 test lines; the added dispatch fixture protects the reported authorization boundary and final send destination.

## Evidence

Validated head: [`6cd2f8dac6c1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6cd2f8dac6c16a82bb5a3bdfdd5cd659cc081237).

The [dispatch regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6cd2f8dac6c16a82bb5a3bdfdd5cd659cc081237/test/whatsapp-message-action-targets.test.ts) starts the registered WhatsApp account with isolated synthetic credentials and exercises production Gateway-owned `runMessageAction`, shared policy, outbound resolution, durable delivery, and the Web send API. Only the external Baileys socket and version lookup are replaced.

Synthetic trace with `allowFrom: ["*"]`, cross-context sends disabled, and source `+15555550000`:

```text
Before identity fix:
  send 15555550000@s.whatsapp.net -> socket send 987654@lid
  send 15555550000@lid            -> socket send 15555550000@lid (defect)

After identity fix:
  send 15555550000@s.whatsapp.net -> socket send 987654@lid
  send 15555550000@lid            -> Cross-context messaging denied
  native send count remains 1; presence call count is unchanged
```

The formed-phone-JID mapping regression also failed against the previous target-facts implementation: expected `987654@lid`, received `15555550000@s.whatsapp.net`. It passes with the shared parser.

- Focused validation: **129 tests passed** across dispatch, normalization, authorization, routing, reactions, send API, approvals, directory, and setup consumers. After CI feedback, the final dispatch/quote/target-facts run passed **34 tests in 3 files**, and the import-boundary guard passed **13 tests**. The dispatch proof took 2.5 seconds locally (23.15 seconds wall time for the final 3-file command) and [2.767 seconds in CI, 66.17 seconds including the shard wrapper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797315315/job/133069488460).
- Changed-file lint, boundary lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, mock-export guard, and the 400-line test budget passed. Test data was consolidated with every scenario retained.
- Independent local autoreview of `2bbd8c18641c` → the final change snapshot committed in `6cd2f8dac6c1`: no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the quote and fixture corrections.
- [CI for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797315315): all test and type-check jobs passed, including all four checks that failed on the first repair push. No full build or full suite was run locally.

The remaining red check is [core lint stripe 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797315315/job/133070562439): `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118`, `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone`. CI tested merge `c9f53266ab19` against main parent `2159567b9ffc`. The failing file and `.oxlintrc.json` have identical Git blobs in that main parent and the test merge; this PR does not change either file. This inherited lint failure keeps the CI gate red. The separate Darwin tooling workflow is still pending.

Proof limit: this is a production dispatch/socket-boundary integration test, not a live WhatsApp account send. The Crabline provider attempt could not complete its handshake and supplies no behavior evidence.

prs.title: fix: shared accounts are missing from the chat model picker
prs.body:
Closes #167747

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an existing chat's model picker omits alternate shared credentials when the user has no personal saved model accounts.

## User Impact

Users can select another shared account already available to the current agent from the existing chat's Account menu. New-chat defaults and personal credential ownership keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The menu used its scoped shared-auth snapshot only for identity labels, while both selectable rows and click lookup read the personal account inventory. Combine those existing inputs for this presentation, deduplicate profile IDs, omit inactive setup entries, and match credential-provider domains without merging MiniMax API and portal credentials. Preserve selection ownership checks and reject clicks from an obsolete auth snapshot. No new Gateway method, permission, schema, or credential copying is introduced.

## Evidence

- Mounted component regressions reproduce the missing shared-account option on the baseline and pass with the fix. Coverage includes empty/failed personal inventory, provider aliases and domain isolation, duplicate IDs, inactive setup profiles, refreshable expired OAuth, and stale/read-only selections.
- Published head `8d84085719a93ccca4a506446916b7b6459a22f7` is one commit / five files on main `c718c709486dc20d43af2732f0e95cfbcbb3b13d`. Its tree exactly matches the local candidate; `git range-diff` confirms the patch is unchanged from the tested 2026.9.9 fix.
- After moving to main, all 39 tests across the account-control, model-auth, and new-session model-control suites passed with one worker: 3.86 seconds Vitest duration, 4.88 seconds routed shard time. Hosted CI timing: not measured.
- On the original 2026.9.9 base, 44 related tests, UI production typecheck, eight relevant test type graphs, targeted lint, formatting, and `pnpm ui:build` passed (build Vite time: 9.60 seconds). Asset integrity and performance gates passed. These are prior-base results, not a fresh main build. The final main-based diff passes `git diff --check`.
- Two manually switched accounts completed real model requests against the rebuilt 2026.9.9 UI. No private account identities or transcripts are included in this PR.
- Independent scoped review and the repository's Codex autoreview reported no actionable findings through P2 before the patch-identical move to main.

Known validation gaps:

- A fresh UI typecheck on the main-based candidate reports 13 errors in untouched Mermaid, fs-safe consumer, and terminal files under the existing local dependency installation. The exact same errors reproduce on unmodified main `c718c709486dc20d43af2732f0e95cfbcbb3b13d`. The main dependency installation was not reconciled; this is a local validation limitation, not evidence about upstream CI.
- The mounted full-page E2E scenario was added, but its original 2026.9.9 runner fails before assertions while resolving `@openclaw/workboard-contract` from `browser/lib/workboard/types.ts`; a frozen full-workspace install did not resolve it. This E2E was not repeated on main.
- The original broad changed-check run exceeded its deadline during production dead-export scanning, so it is not reported as passing.

Inspected before/after screenshots are [attached in this PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167748#issuecomment-6079294944) and were also delivered in the originating chat. Both images render successfully on GitHub. They use the actual released account-control component and production styles with two synthetic shared credentials and zero personal accounts. The baseline shows only the current row; the fixed component also lists the alternate shared account.



### Redacted observed account-switch completions

The operator manually selected two different shared credentials in the same existing chat using the rebuilt 2026.9.9 UI. The following allowlisted lifecycle facts were re-read from the local Gateway trajectory database on October 9. This export issued zero new model requests. A concurrent read of the shared secret inventory found **0 live personal model-account records**.

Timestamps are UTC. Account and run/session IDs, emails, URLs, prompts, replies, keys, and raw logs are omitted.

| Turn | Recorded transport / auth flow | prompt.submitted | model.completed | session.ended | Outcome | Input / output tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | openai-responses / chatgpt-token-sharing | 2026-10-09T07:53:39.999Z | 2026-10-09T07:53:44.995Z | 2026-10-09T07:53:45.107Z | success; 4996 ms model phase | 1935 / 30 |
| B | openai-chatgpt-responses / codex-oauth | 2026-10-09T07:58:43.315Z | 2026-10-09T07:58:47.575Z | 2026-10-09T07:58:47.663Z | success; 4260 ms model phase | 2130 / 10 |

The per-run credential ID is redacted by the trajectory recorder. Account association was checked against the unique saved authorization matching each recorded transport, as recorded in the local verification receipt; this is an observed successful switch with corroborating metadata, not a provider billing receipt. These observations are on the rebuilt 2026.9.9 base; they do not assert an authenticated provider run on the main-based PR head. The introduced production patch is identical between those bases.

The live operator picker was separately opened and captured successfully with both configured accounts visible; that private image is not published. The synthetic comparison uses the documented full-page capture path. These screenshots exercise the 2026.9.9 component with the same introduced production patch, while the main-based full-page E2E and local typecheck limitations remain as documented above.

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude CLI per-call usage keeps the stream-start output count
prs.body:
Related: #148603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI per-call usage keeps the output count Claude Code reports when a model call starts (usually 1 to 5 tokens) instead of the call's real output, so `lastCallUsage`, and the live usage of single-call turns, undercount output.

## User Impact

User impact: for `claude-cli` turns, `lastCallUsage` now carries each call's real output count. Single-call turns (most plain replies) now show the right output tokens in `sessions.list`, `/status`, reply usage footers and cron run records, because their live usage is that call. Context sizing is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's `assistant` snapshots repeat the usage from the start of their call. The final output count arrives only in that call's `stream_event` `message_delta`, which the stream parser never read (the gap listed under "Not in scope" in #148682 and in the 10-29 ClawSweeper summary on #148603). The parser now keeps each parent call's `message_start` usage and applies that call's `message_delta` output count to it. It merges into that call snapshot rather than the parser's latest usage, because a background agent's records (`task_progress` totals, subagent snapshots) can arrive in the middle of a parent call, and mixing them would under-size context. `message_delta` records with `parent_tool_use_id` (subagents) are ignored. Only the output count is taken from the delta, so a delta that reports only `output_tokens` still works.

This is the second remaining gap on #148603. The first one (live usage uses the latest call rather than the whole turn) is covered by the open #187118; the two changes touch different code and do not depend on each other. With both merged, `usage` is the whole turn and `lastCallUsage` is the latest call, with its real output.

## Evidence

- Tests in `src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts`, red on base `92b32cadcc3` and green with the fix:
  - The existing reparse test of the real Claude Code 2.1 capture `test/fixtures/cli/claude-2.1-thinking-progress.jsonl` pinned `usage.output` at 5 (the snapshot value). It now expects 534, the capture's `message_delta` and `result` value.
  - The real subagent capture `claude-2.1-subagent-forwarding.jsonl`: the last parent call's usage is now output 66 (its `message_delta`), not 4.
  - A new synthetic test: a `message_delta` with only `output_tokens` updates the call started by `message_start`, a background `task_progress` usage record in the middle of the call does not leak into it, and a subagent `message_delta` is ignored.
  - On base: 3 failed, 19 passed. With the fix: 22 passed. Cost: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, about 1 s of test time.
- Consumers: every `src/agents/cli-output*`, `cli-runner*`, `cli-runner/*` and CLI transcript test, plus `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-*.test.ts`: 109 files, 1,379 tests, all passing. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-mock-exports`, `check:assertion-safety` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Runtime proof, built Gateway CLI in an isolated state dir (`openclaw agent --local --json` with the `claude-cli` runtime). A stand-in `claude` on `PATH` replays the real Claude Code 2.1 capture above over the live stdio transport. Same turn, base build vs this branch:

  | | base `92b32cadcc3` | this branch |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | `agentMeta.usage.output` | 5 | 534 |
  | `agentMeta.lastCallUsage.output` | 5 | 534 |
  | `agentMeta.diagnosticUsage.output` (Claude's `result`) | 534 | 534 |
  | session row `outputTokens` (`openclaw sessions --json`) | 5 | 534 |
  | session row `totalTokens` (context) | 41,373 | 41,373 |

  The same turn with a background `task_progress` record (`usage.total_tokens: 9678`) inserted before the parent's `message_delta` gives the same values on this branch: output 534, context 41,373.

AI-assisted (Claude Code).

prs.title: fix(knowledge): report physical line number for malformed JSON manifest rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `source-manifest.mjs` reads a JSONL manifest and one row is malformed, the operator gets V8's `JSON.parse` position instead of a location:

```
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
```

`line 1 column 2` is the position *inside that row*, not the row's position in the file. On a dump with hundreds of rows the diagnostic points nowhere.

- Problem: `snapshot` and `loadManifest` call `JSON.parse` directly inside the line loop; the syntax error propagates to the top-level handler, which prints only `error.message`.
- Solution: count physical lines (blank lines included) while iterating and rethrow as `<file>:<line>: line is not valid JSON`. The raw row is deliberately not echoed: manifests carry private payloads (message text, author fields), and the file plus physical line already locate the fault.
- Changed: `extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/source-manifest.mjs` (both `JSON.parse` sites) and one regression folded into the existing `source-manifest.test.ts` case.
- Unchanged: valid-manifest behavior, output format, exit codes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest tool is the ingest boundary; naming the exact offending line is the minimal correct diagnostic. Wrapping only the two `JSON.parse` sites keeps the change surgical and preserves the existing per-row validations (header checks, `Item N has no stable string id`, ...) that still throw their own messages.

- Best fix: local try/catch rethrow with the counted physical line, reusing the existing top-level `console.error(error.message)` path.
- Alternative rejected: a whole-file validating parser — larger change, different error ordering and timing.
- Risk: only the error text for malformed input changes; it deliberately omits row contents.

## User Impact

A malformed JSON row now reports the file and physical line, e.g. `-:3: line is not valid JSON`, so the offending row is directly locatable without echoing its contents (or others' private payloads) to stderr.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry point: base vs this branch

One capture, real CLI runs. Base = `main` at `28d20f9532f`, whose `source-manifest.mjs` blob is identical to the PR base `4efd662`; head = this branch at `de40cbd80ca`. Fixture `run/bad.manifest.jsonl` is two blank lines followed by `{bad "PRIVATE_LEAK_MARKER_9f3c" json}` — a malformed row on physical line 3. The marker is a synthetic canary: it must never reach stderr.

```text
$ node source-manifest.mjs plan --current run/bad.manifest.jsonl    # base: main 28d20f9532f
exit 1
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
$ node source-manifest.mjs plan --current run/bad.manifest.jsonl    # head: de40cbd80ca
exit 1
run/bad.manifest.jsonl:3: line is not valid JSON
$ printf '\n\n{bad "PRIVATE_LEAK_MARKER_9f3c" json}\n' | node source-manifest.mjs snapshot --input - ...   # base
exit 1
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
$ printf '\n\n{bad "PRIVATE_LEAK_MARKER_9f3c" json}\n' | node source-manifest.mjs snapshot --input - ...   # head
exit 1
-:3: line is not valid JSON
```

`-` is the stdin filename. Same raw log: [terminal-capture.log](https://github.com/shuisadev/openclaw-pr-197722-proof/blob/main/terminal-capture.log).

### Media proof ✨

![source-manifest line number before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shuisadev/openclaw-pr-197722-proof/main/source-manifest-line-number-proof.svg)

### Regression

The existing `source-manifest.test.ts` case already ran the malformed-row check through `snapshot` only. It now runs one fixture through **both** changed call sites and asserts, per case, that the message names physical line 3 and that the canary is absent:

- `snapshot`, stdin — `-:3: line is not valid JSON`
- `plan --current`, file — `malformed.manifest.jsonl:3: line is not valid JSON`

Both assertions use `expect.soft`, so each case reports independently instead of hiding the second behind the first.

Base (main's `source-manifest.mjs`, blob `63f33e4d`, with this test) — both cases fail:

```text
→ expected 'Command failed: ...' to match /-:3: line is not valid JSON/
→ expected 'Command failed: ...' to match /malformed\.manifest\.jsonl:3: line is…/
Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
```

Head — `npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/knowledge/src/source-manifest.test.ts`: `Tests 3 passed (3)`.

Open PR collision check: searched the latest open PRs' changed files for `source-manifest.mjs`; none touched it. The sibling entry about `--input -` UTF-8 decoding errors (`encoded data was not valid`) is a different failure and is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(infra): reject lossy UTF-8 in managed update handoff output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed update handoff lossy-decodes the updater subprocess stdout with `Buffer.toString()`, so bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are silently replaced with U+FFFD. If that lands inside the JSON diagnostics, `JSON.parse(updaterOutput)` consumes corrupted data with no signal that bytes were lost.

- **Problem**: updater stdout is decoded with `Buffer.toString()`, which silently replaces invalid UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD; `JSON.parse` then consumes corrupted diagnostics with no warning.
- **Solution**: decode with the strict `decodeUtf8Input` helper; log a warning when invalid bytes are detected while retaining a lossy copy so the update flow never breaks.
- **What changed**: `update-managed-service-handoff-control.ts` and `update-managed-service-handoff-sealed.ts` now use `decodeUtf8Input` instead of `Buffer.toString()`; the termination test adds a triage case for the 0xFF byte.
- **What did NOT change**: the handoff line reader, JSON diagnostics consumer, child-process kill logic, and the update-operation deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode updater output with the strict `decodeUtf8Input` helper (the canonical approach already used across the codebase, e.g. #180861). When invalid UTF-8 is detected, the corruption is surfaced via a log line ("managed update updater stdout contained invalid UTF-8; retained a lossy copy") while still keeping a lossy copy so the string/JSON contract and the update flow never break.

The decoder binding reaches the spawned helper through the sealed runtime module it already `require`s, so the fix runs in the real child process.

- **Best fix**: use the canonical `decodeUtf8Input` helper (already used in #180861) to detect invalid UTF-8 at the decode boundary, log a warning, and retain a lossy copy so the string/JSON contract never breaks.
- **Alternative(s)**: (a) reject the entire updater output on any invalid UTF-8 — rejected because it turns a diagnostics corruption into a full update failure; (b) re-encode the updater stdout as Latin-1 — rejected because it silently mislabels the encoding and corrupts valid multi-byte sequences; (c) pipe the raw bytes through a streaming decoder — rejected because it complicates the sealed runtime for a rare edge case.
- **Risk**: the lossy copy uses U+FFFD replacement, matching `Buffer.toString()` default behavior for valid-but-undecodable bytes. Boundary left unchanged: the handoff line reader, JSON diagnostics consumer, and child-process kill logic.

## User Impact

No user-visible change for valid UTF-8 output (including multi-byte CJK split across chunks). Invalid UTF-8 is now annotated instead of silently corrupted, making update diagnostics reliable.

## Evidence

| Case | Before (pre-fix) | After (post-fix) |
|---|---|---|
| Invalid 0xFF byte in updater stdout | silently replaced with U+FFFD; `JSON.parse` consumed corrupted data | warning logged; lossy copy retained; update flow continues |
| Valid multi-byte CJK split across chunks | decoded correctly | decoded correctly (no change) |

### Committed regression (head passes, base fails)

`update-managed-service-handoff-termination.test.ts` drives one raw 0xFF byte through the shipped `runOwnedUpdateCommand` decode path as an extra case in the triage settlement table, and asserts the warning is emitted only for that case while the retained output is the U+FFFD replacement. 8/8 green on head; on the pre-fix base that case fails (`expected false to be true`) while the other rows pass (revert → 1 failed; restore → 8/8). No test-line growth: `check:test-lines-ratchets` delta 0.

### Shipped managed-handoff warning trace (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd 255, Node 24.22.1)

The Gateway runs as a real systemd user service and the update starts from a cron command job, so the updater runs inside the Gateway process tree and takes the shipped handoff. A `NODE_OPTIONS=--import` preload appends one raw 0xFF byte inside the updater's JSON stdout, arming only in the handoff updater (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_RUN_HANDOFF=1`).

```
handoff invalid-UTF-8 lines: 1
[2026-10-28T07:52:33.425Z] managed update updater stdout contained invalid UTF-8; retained a lossy copy
[2026-10-28T07:51:15.463Z] managed update ownership transferred; validating while the gateway serves
[2026-10-28T07:51:15.463Z] starting managed update command: openclaw update --yes --tag openclaw --timeout 1200
[2026-10-28T07:52:33.425Z] managed update update command exited code=1 signal=null
injected 0xff into updater stdout pid=3659 offset=21
settings sha256: a4bb27ad…d977e1 (before = after)
workspace marker: proof-data-marker-186033
```

The published 2026.10.8 build stays silent on the same injected byte (`handoff invalid-UTF-8 lines: 0`).

### Published 2026.10.8 → this build: completed update

Candidate packaged from this head with the repository's own packager (`build` + `runtime-postbuild`, 55 plugin modules verified); it bundles the workspace `@openclaw/ai`:

```
openclaw-candidate-2026.10.9.tgz  90,517,411 bytes  sha256 72c11c5c…934031
package.json            "version": "2026.10.9", "bundleDependencies": [ … ]
dist/build-info.json    {"version":"2026.10.9","commit":"090125e25e76ec49fc146e5901f4f6753bc5f099"}
package/node_modules/   645 files, including package/node_modules/@openclaw/ai
```

Version raised 2026.10.7 → 2026.10.9 with the repo's `stampFixtureVersion` helper because the worktree version is below the published driver. Fresh `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.8` in an isolated HOME/prefix (Debian 13, glibc 2.41, Node 24.22.1), state seeded (config, workspace marker, 2 cron jobs), Gateway `/readyz` 200, then:

```
$ openclaw update --tag openclaw-candidate-2026.10.9.tgz --yes --json
status: ok   mode: npm   duration: 517 s
```

prs.title: fix(sessions): honor string archive filters in sessions_list
prs.body:
Closes #199566

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `sessions_list` returning active sessions when a tool caller requests archived sessions using the string `"true"`.

## User Impact

Archive searches now select the requested sessions when boolean values arrive as strings. Unsupported explicit values report an input error instead of silently selecting active sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing boolean parser at the tool boundary. Preserve boolean inputs, the omitted/default active filter, and `"all"`; keep the published schema unchanged.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway: created two sessions via authenticated WebSocket RPC, archived one with `sessions.patch`, then called `sessions_list` through HTTP `POST /tools/invoke`. Both runs used full Gateway source, synthetic state and Bun 1.4.4; no model inference or external channel was involved.

| `args.archived` | Base `2e1b61901c5d` | Fixed `f4f6b0cc0b5c` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"true"` | HTTP 200, active session | HTTP 200, archived session |
| `true` | Archived session | Archived session |
| `false`, `"false"`, omitted | Active session | Active session |
| `"all"` | Both sessions | Both sessions |
| `"invalid"` | HTTP 200, active session | HTTP 400, input error |

The Gateway shut down cleanly after each run. This proves the HTTP/tool selection path; it does not claim a live Claude CLI model reproduction.

- Existing archive test expanded to cover boolean/string/default inputs; unsupported-input cases confirm that no inventory query is sent. Regression on base production code: **5 failed, 5 passed**. Fixed owner/query suites: **44 passed**.
- Targeted format and type-aware lint: **0 warnings, 0 errors**. `git diff --check` passed. Test delta: **+13 net lines**; no new fixtures or test files.
- Final focused test wall time: **35.28 s** (cold initial run: 80.69 s, predominantly imports/transforms). CI time is pending. The normal runner's compiled subprocess preparation hit the 1.5 GiB container limit; the repository-supported standalone Vitest source path below passed without increasing resources.
- Independent full-diff agent review of `2e1b61901c5d..f4f6b0cc0b5c`: no actionable findings. Full-suite CI remains for GitHub.

<details>
<summary>Focused command and HTTP reproduction</summary>

```sh
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-list-query.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On an isolated Gateway, create one active session and archive a second. With an authenticated HTTP client, call `/tools/invoke` using:

```json
{"tool":"sessions_list","args":{"archived":"true","agentId":"main","limit":20}}
```

Repeat with the selectors in the table. The original and fixed runs used identical fixtures and requests. The fix replaces the returned active key with the archived key; invalid input returns `archived must be true, false, or all`.

</details>

prs.title: fix(skills): preserve source files when the output archive is linked
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the bundled skill packager overwriting a source file or an unrelated file when the output `<skill-name>.skill` is a symlink to it. Linking the archive to the skill's own `SKILL.md` makes the command report success while replacing that source file with a ZIP that omits the manifest.

## User Impact

Skill authors can retry packaging without silently destroying the output link's target. The command now fails with a remedy: remove the output symlink before packaging. Normal output files still support atomic replacement; symlinked output directories remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject the final archive symlink before resolving the output target or starting archive creation, matching the existing handling of a linked `SKILL.md`. This is three production lines at the existing packaging owner, plus one 27-line regression using the existing fixture; no new helper, dependency or alternate publication path.

## Evidence

Actual Python CLI on Linux / Python 3.11, isolated with synthetic files, 1 CPU / 384 MiB / no network. Reproduction from a checkout:

```sh
fixture=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$fixture/sample-skill" "$fixture/out"
printf '%s\n' '---' 'name: sample-skill' 'description: Synthetic CLI fixture' '---' > "$fixture/sample-skill/SKILL.md"
ln -s "$fixture/sample-skill/SKILL.md" "$fixture/out/sample-skill.skill"
python3 skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py "$fixture/sample-skill" "$fixture/out"
```

Captured results from the same reproduction on base `c0166c395` and this fix:

```text
Before:
[WARN] Skipping output archive: .../sample-skill/SKILL.md
[OK] Successfully packaged skill to: .../out/sample-skill.skill
{"exit": 0, "sourceUnchanged": false, "sourceIsZip": true, "outputStillSymlink": true}
{"archiveEntries": []}

After:
[ERROR] Output archive is a symlink; remove it before packaging.
{"exit": 1, "sourceUnchanged": true, "sourceIsZip": false, "outputStillSymlink": true}
After removing the alias:
{"path": "normal", "exit": 0, "manifestPreservedAndArchived": true}
{"path": "overwrite", "exit": 0, "manifestPreservedAndArchived": true}
```

- All three regression subcases fail on the base: output linked to the source manifest, an external existing file, and a missing target. With the fix they reject without changing the target or leaving staging files; replacing the link with normal output succeeds.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/skill-creator/scripts -p test_package_skill.py`: all 7 tests pass in 0.034 seconds, including existing atomic-failure cleanup, ordinary replacement, timestamp bounds, input-link rejection and archive-entry behavior.
- Targeted Ruff check using `skills/pyproject.toml`: passed.
- Independent local review of the final committed diff: no actionable findings.

No full repository suite or native Windows run. This handles pre-existing output aliases; it does not claim protection against hostile concurrent path replacement.
