prs.title: fix(gateway): blank --url silently reports the default gateway status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway status --url ""` (or `--url "$VAR"` where the variable is empty) exits 0 and prints the **configured default Gateway's** service/connectivity report instead of rejecting the blank target. The same command with a non-empty `--url ws://…` probes exactly that URL, so an explicitly passed empty value is silently treated as "flag not provided" while any other value is honored.

`openclaw gateway probe --url ""` has the same silent drop: it prints the full `Gateway Status` report for the configured local/remote targets (byte-identical to running `gateway probe` with no `--url` at all).

Root cause: two independent drop points turn `""` into "absent" before any target is resolved.
- `src/commands/gateway-status.ts` (`gatewayStatusCommand`, the engine behind `gateway probe`): `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth({ urlOverride: opts.url?.trim() })` early-returns on an empty override, `resolveTargets()` maps `""` → `normalizeWsUrl` → `null` (no explicit target), and `hasExplicitUrl` reads `opts.url.trim().length > 0` → `false`.
- `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts` (`runDaemonStatus`, behind `gateway status`): `opts.rpc.url` is passed straight through and `status.gather.ts` treats a falsy override as "use the configured target" (`if (opts.deep && !trimToUndefined(opts.rpc.url))`).

## User Impact

User impact: scripts and operators that pass an empty `--url` (typically `--url "$GATEWAY_URL"` with an unset variable) now get a clear error and exit 1 instead of a successful report about a **different** Gateway than the one they asked about — before any probe, SSH tunnel, Bonjour discovery, or service inspection starts. Blank values fail at command entry, so no partial output is produced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 3-line blank check at the top of `gatewayStatusCommand` and a 4-line blank check at the top of `runDaemonStatus`, reusing the repository's existing `must not be blank` contract (the same wording and shape as `agentCliCommand` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`, `account-selector.ts`, `channel-selector.ts`, and the merged `--agent must not be blank` guard from #193336). Each check sits at the entry of the command that owns the `--url` option, before any of its consumers run.

Not introducing: no new error type, no config validation, no shared resolver change, no owner/state/schema/API change, no SDK-visible surface. `resolveGatewayRpcOptions` / `addGatewayClientOptions` (shared by `gateway call`, `health`, `stability`, `diagnostics export`, `exec-policy`, …) are deliberately untouched — that is a wider family with its own blast radius and is recorded as a follow-up rather than folded into this fix.

## Evidence

Base `37706a74a81129f8ec85289399a2703abf98c2b4` (branch base = `origin/main` at branch creation) → Candidate `166efe4ed6ad68a3dceeee079eececc8dbfd564f` (branch `fix/gateway-status-blank-url`).

Environment: Linux x64, Node v24.22.1, normally built `openclaw.mjs` (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build:docker`), isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` + `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (+ isolated `HOME`), no Gateway running, no network dependency, no seed data. Every case below was run **twice**; each pair was compared with `cmp` (exit code + stdout + stderr), not by eye.

### Shipped CLI (each leg run at least twice)

| case | base | candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway status --url ""` ×2 | **exit 0**, stdout+stderr **byte-identical** to `gateway status` with no flag (md5 `358f247acd194509801e9873eed89e45` / `f8cb63b30f259108654742cce8c82c30`) — blank silently dropped | **exit 1**, stderr `Gateway status failed: --url must not be blank` |
| `gateway status` (no `--url`) ×2 | exit 0 | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway status --url "ws://127.0.0.1:9"` ×2 | exit 0, `Check target: ws://127.0.0.1:9` (explicit target honored) | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway probe --url ""` ×2 | **exit 1**, stdout+stderr **byte-identical** to `gateway probe` with no flag (stdout md5 `f930c0cfd768d2f066ce142512e2e10d`, stderr empty `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`) — blank silently dropped | **exit 1**, stderr `--url must not be blank` |
| `gateway probe` (no `--url`) ×2 | exit 1 (`Gateway Status / Reachable: no`) | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway probe --url "ws://127.0.0.1:9"` ×2 | exit 1, explicit target probed | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |

All eight "unchanged" comparisons were byte-identical (`cmp` clean on both streams) between the base build and the candidate build in the same isolated home/state directory.

### Regression RED → GREEN (remote, real vitest)

Remote proof host (Docker `lexiflow-all:latest`, Node `v24.22.1`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`), production files at `37706a74a81` bytes (verified md5-identical to `git show origin/main:<path>` for all four files before the run):

```text
sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts \
  src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts \
  src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **base production + new test → RED.** `commands` shard: `1 failed | 30 passed (31)` — `rejects a blank --url before reading config or probing` fails with `AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting` at `src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts:234` (the blank value silently proceeded past the guard). `cli` shard: `1 failed | 7 passed (8)` — `rejects a blank --url before gathering status` fails with the same `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting` at `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts:140`.
- **candidate production + the same tests → GREEN.** `commands` shard: `31 passed (31)`; `cli` shard: `8 passed (8)` (the new `rejects a blank --url before gathering status` case is green).
- **Siblings/consumers on the candidate (all green):** `src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/register-service-commands.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.install-hints.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts` → `6 passed (6)` files, `156 passed | 2 skipped (158)`; `src/commands/gateway-status/helpers.test.ts` (root matrix) → `1 passed (1)` file, `18 passed (18)`.

### Local gates

```text
oxlint (v1.88.0) src/commands/gateway-status.ts src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts → 0 findings, exit 0
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <those four files> → All matched files use the correct format
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 37706a74a81 → Test lines OK (allocation credit equals this PR's +18 delta)
git diff --check → clean
```

### Line counts

Whole-PR delta: production **+7/-0** (2 files), tests **+18/-0** (2 files), `config/test-lines-allocations/gateway-status-blank-url.txt` = **18** for exactly this PR's net test growth. Shared scalar `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` untouched. On a clean `37706a74a81` the ratchet reports `Test lines OK: 6496704; ceiling: 6496746; slack: 42`, so this branch stays inside the ceiling with the allocation applied.

### Negative claims

- Not claimed: `gateway status`/`gateway probe` against a **running** Gateway — both legs run with no listener, and the proof is exit code + byte-identical output identity, not live capability data.
- Not claimed: the shared `--url` consumers (`gateway call`, `health`, `stability`, `diagnostics export`, `exec-policy`, …). They share the shape but are a wider family; fixing them belongs to a separate, explicitly scoped change.
- Not claimed: whitespace-only `--url "   "` at the CLI (covered by the same `.trim()` expression; the shipped CLI leg exercises `""`, and the unit test exercises both `""` and `"   "` for `gateway probe`).

## Focused Checks and Simplification

- 7 production lines across 2 production files; each guard is a straight-line `if` at the existing command entry, no helper, no wrapper, no new export, no new error class.
- Tests were merged into the two files that already own these commands (`gateway-status.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`), reusing their existing mock-not-called assertions so no new harness was introduced.
- Test-lines: this PR adds an allocation of exactly its +18 growth and leaves the shared scalar alone.

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous silent fallback without migrations or persisted state changes. Blast radius is `--url` validation at exactly two command entries (`gateway status`, `gateway probe`); both fail **before** config reads, probes, SSH tunnels, Bonjour discovery, and service inspection. Unchanged adjacent behavior: omitted `--url`, non-empty valid URLs, non-empty invalid URLs (still probed and reported as before), `--token`/`--password`/`--port`/`--ssh` handling, `--json` output shape for every non-blank case, and every other command.

Collision check (run against `origin/main` minutes before opening): no open PR modifies `src/commands/gateway-status.ts`, `src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts`, or `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.test.ts`; `gh pr list --search "gateway status"` / `"blank url"` and per-file `gh api pulls/<n>/files` checks returned only unrelated work (the one parallel-lane PR touching remote URLs, #193538, edits `src/commands/onboard-remote.ts` only).

## Status

Reopened: this pull request was closed by mistake during a session cleanup on 2026-11-12 while it was still `proof: sufficient` + `ready for maintainer look`. The branch was rebased onto `611bea727f21` (the only conflict was a neighbouring test in `status.test.ts`, resolved by keeping both cases) and the diff is byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. No new behavior was added.

prs.title: feat(templates): finish Add in a retryable setup conversation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Template Add can create the agent but its tools-disabled opening cannot finish the declared setup or recover a failed opening without repeating creation.

## What changes

After creation, one hidden setup turn uses the new agent’s ordinary tools and retained permissions. It greets in the Template’s voice, creates declared automations paused, reports MCP sign-in needs, and shows exact-package plugin cards without installing or enabling those plugins. Explicit tool denies and operator ceilings remain authoritative.

The ordinary session owns the retryable setup continuation. Retry uses the same agent, workspace and conversation without reinstalling dependencies. When its one-shot receipt has already been consumed, Retry returns a truthful partial/unverifiable outcome instead of inventing readiness or creating another agent. Plugin inventory includes canonical package identity so the agent does not infer a plugin ID from its package name.

This layer follows https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198070. Early-opening/dependency concurrency and composer responsiveness remain a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

### Current repair qualification

Head `577e12a6b457945be951b6e97a753b9c2cfebaef`, base `9ed5a58794db142be41f5e142e68a5cd92d72bd0`:

- Promotes the existing stale/concurrent Retry fix into this independently landable layer. Three Gateway regression cases fail before the fix with false complete/ready results. After the fix the complete owning request suite passes **14/14**, exit0 (144.61s wrapper): `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add-chat.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The same agent, workspace, edited files and dependency-install counts are preserved. External registry/model I/O is fixed; admission, config, workspace, session, rollback and retained setup ownership remain real. No new test seam or mock was introduced.
- Moves the unchanged setup input contract into a type-only leaf and updates all three consumers. Both runtime and Madge import-cycle guards now report **zero cycles**. The leaf does not prematurely add the responsive follow-up callbacks.
- Adds the incident reference beside the bootstrap exception, without changing model-facing prompt bytes.
- Six-file **type-aware lint**, formatting and diff checks pass. Test-line ratchet is **+281 <=400**, no setup allocation or global-limit changes.
- Seven existing setup commits were restacked onto the creation allocation-only repair. UI source and performance inputs are unchanged from the prior setup qualification below; prior results are reused, not claimed as fresh executions. Exact-head hosted compiler/build/CI and completed re-review remain required.

### Retained prior qualification

Prior setup `e68f2ecdbc3b54fea242e6ca545d1f0830bc0aff` above `b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08`:

- Complete strict paired production-UI performance passes, exit0: document **14,019 B <=14,026 B**; chat JS **1,315,006→1,315,005 B**, New Session **818,001→818,000 B**, startup **90,860 B unchanged**. Requests and CSS unchanged. Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08`.
- Owning Gateway14/14 and setup prompt6/6, complete two-shard command exit0 (161.15s). Explicit denies and operator ceilings remain authoritative.
- Deletes the old tools-disabled outcome prompt and uses the existing session continuation owner, not a parallel Template ledger.

The prior hosted native Talk and UI failures were compared with scheduled main run43540514362 and have identical failure signatures; they are not passing CI. New-head checks still need reconciliation. No inherited-failure qualification covers an introduced defect.

## Real product evidence and remaining gap

prs.title: fix(knowledge): report malformed chat export rows without a traceback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A chat export containing a malformed JSON line makes `chat-transcript.mjs` crash with a raw `SyntaxError` stack trace instead of naming the offending row. The neighboring input validations (UTF-8 decode in #196398, UTC `occurred_at` in #196440) throw a one-line `Error` identifying the row; `JSON.parse` was the remaining unguarded read.

Precedent: #196398, #196440 (same file, same "reject malformed chat exports with a clean error" shape; this PR covers the JSON parse step)

## Why This Change Was Made

`readRows` parsed each JSONL line with `JSON.parse` in a `.map()` and let any `SyntaxError` escape as a full Node traceback. The parse now runs in a loop that numbers physical lines (before skipping blanks) and throws a one-line `Error` naming the row, and the CLI boundary catches it — mirroring `source-manifest.mjs` — so the process prints only `error.message` and exits 1 instead of a Node stack trace. No validator, option, config, or policy change.

Production LOC is +11/-2, net +9 (1 file); test: +17/-1 (1 file).

Classification: `behavior-completing` (completes the reject-without-traceback shape for the JSON parse step)

## User Impact

A damaged chat export now fails with `Row N of the export is not valid JSON` as the only stderr line (exit 1, no traceback) before any output is written. The row number is the physical line of the malformed JSON even when blank lines precede it. Valid exports are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Shipped `chat-transcript.mjs` CLI with synthetic JSONL (Node v24.13.1). `RED` is the current-main file; `GREEN` is this branch.

```sh
printf '{"id":"m1","occurred_at":"2026-11-09T10:00:00Z","payload":{"author_id":"1","author_name":"A","content":"hi"}}\n{invalid-json}\n' > malformed.jsonl
node extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/chat-transcript.mjs --input malformed.jsonl --output-dir out --channel '#t'
```

RED (current main) — raw `SyntaxError` traceback, exit 1:

```text
<anonymous_script>:1
{invalid-json}
 ^

SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at file:///.../chat-transcript.mjs:48:27
    at Array.map (<anonymous>)
    at readRows (file:///.../chat-transcript.mjs:48:8)
```

GREEN (this branch) — one line naming the row, no traceback, exit 1:

```text
Row 2 of the export is not valid JSON
```

Blank-line case — a blank first line before the malformed row reports the physical line 3:

```text
Row 3 of the export is not valid JSON
```

Legal control — valid export still succeeds, exit 0, expected files written:

```text
{"days":1,"chunks":1,"messages":1}
2026-11-09.jsonl 2026-11-09.txt chunks.json
```

### Committed regression

`extensions/knowledge/src/chat-transcript.test.ts` gains a subprocess case: a valid row, a blank line, then `{invalid-json}` exits 1, prints `Row 3 of the export is not valid JSON`, emits no stack frame (`at ` absent from stderr), and writes no `chunks.json`. It fails on base (raw `SyntaxError` traceback) and passes with the fix.

```sh
pnpm vitest run extensions/knowledge/src/chat-transcript.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: +11/-2 (1 file); test: +17/-1 (1 file)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the neighboring rows' `throw new Error(...)` style; no new validator/option/config
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Cleanup: synthetic fixtures under `/tmp/chat-a-probe/`; no production Gateway, session, token, or config touched
- Not tested: multi-byte/Unicode malformed bytes are covered by #196398's fatal UTF-8 decoder; this PR only changes the JSON parse step

prs.title: fix(skills): prevent missing transcription values from overwriting files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accidental output overwrites when a transcription option is missing its value: `transcribe.sh voice.wav --out --json` currently uploads the audio and overwrites a file named `--json`, instead of reporting the missing output path.

## User Impact

Malformed arguments now fail before uploading audio or writing a transcript, with a diagnostic naming the option. This also prevents silently consuming `--json` as a model, language, or prompt. A trailing value-taking option now prints a useful error instead of silently exiting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject a missing argument or an exact recognized option token before consuming a value; preserve other dash-prefixed literal values. The fix adds eight production lines and focused Python CLI regressions (44 lines); no parser framework or dependency change. There is no existing transcription argument test on this base. The new test uses the skills Python test lane and is outside the JavaScript/TypeScript test-line ratchet.

This follows the same missing-value/file-overwrite category as #196933, an external contribution merged by obviyus on November 11.

## Evidence

Executed the actual bundled Bash script with **real curl**, a synthetic WAV, an HTTP receiver on container loopback, Node response extraction, and real output files. The receiver returns a fixed transcript; this proves argument handling, request counts, and file writes, not hosted speech recognition. No paid API calls or user credentials were used.

```sh
# With a synthetic WAV, a local receiver returning {"text":"Local transcript"},
# and an existing ./--json file containing KEEP ME:
OPENAI_API_KEY=synthetic-local-key \
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 \
  bash skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/transcribe.sh voice.wav --out --json
```

| Actual CLI case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--out --json` | exit 0; 1 request; `./--json` overwritten with `Local transcript` | exit 2; 0 requests; `KEEP ME` preserved; `--out requires a value` |
| `--model`, `--language`, or `--prompt` followed by `--json` | exit 0 against local receiver; 1 unintended request | exit 2; 0 requests; option-specific error |
| Each of those four options at EOF | exit 1; empty stderr | exit 2; option-specific error and usage |
| Default text, `--json`, `--out -out.txt`, `--out ./--json`, or ordinary model/language/prompt values | exit 0; 1 request; expected output bytes | same |

All 15 actual CLI cases passed after the fix, including `--prompt "--- Meeting transcript ---"` and `--out --notes.txt`. Valid requests contained the exact synthetic WAV bytes. The five valid controls passed on both versions. For an intentional filename equal to a recognized option, use an explicit relative path, such as `--out ./--json`.

Focused verification: Bash syntax, repository-configured Ruff lint/format, and the committed Python regression passed. The missing-value regression failed on the original code in all 12 subcases; after the fix, `pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/test_transcribe.py` passed (2 tests, 14 subcases; 0.86 s). Local checks ran in a secretless, network-disabled container capped at 256 MB and half a CPU. No full suite, macOS run, or hosted provider validation was performed. CI timing is pending.

<details>
<summary>Standalone reproduction from either checkout (Bash, curl, Node, Python)</summary>

```python
import os, subprocess, tempfile, threading, wave
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

script = Path("skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/transcribe.sh").resolve()
requests = []
class Receiver(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        requests.append(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        body = b'{"text":"Local transcript"}\n'
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    def log_message(self, *_):
        pass

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp, HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Receiver) as server:
    root = Path(tmp)
    with wave.open(str(root / "voice.wav"), "wb") as audio:
        audio.setparams((1, 2, 8000, 0, "NONE", "not compressed"))
        audio.writeframes(b"\0\0" * 80)
    (root / "--json").write_text("KEEP ME")
    worker = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
    worker.start()
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(script), "voice.wav", "--out", "--json"],
            cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
            env={**os.environ, "OPENAI_API_KEY": "synthetic-local-key",
                 "OPENAI_BASE_URL": f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/v1",
                 "NO_PROXY": "127.0.0.1"},
        )
        print("exit:", result.returncode, "requests:", len(requests))
        print("file:", (root / "--json").read_text())
        print(result.stderr)
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        worker.join()
```

Observed on base: `exit: 0 requests: 1`, `file: Local transcript`.
Observed on this branch: `exit: 2 requests: 0`, `file: KEEP ME`, `--out requires a value`.

</details>

Independent Codex review covered the complete base `8830ff6d8ed6bbbc0ec15698428a7fcaaeb38deb` → head `fc565651b4a80d47f97843d18c8bc0f36f39498f` diff. One literal-value compatibility finding was fixed and covered before submission; final review found no remaining issues.

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve malformed UTF-8 agent documents during edits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: editing an agent document containing invalid UTF-8 can silently replace its original bytes, even when a matching content hash protects the save.

## User Impact

User impact: Malformed agent documents are refused before a checked edit or identity update can damage their contents. The response is INVALID_REQUEST, confirms that the original file was preserved, and tells the operator to convert it to UTF-8 before retrying. Valid UTF-8, BOMs, literal replacement characters and intentional full replacement without a content hash retain their existing behavior. No new configuration, protocol, schema, default, permission or migration choices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the strict UTF-8 decoder for document reads and validate the same pre-write snapshot after its content hash matches. Apply the same invariant to the workspace bridge and identity preread; stale hashes still report conflicts. Catch only the typed decoding error at the existing file/identity RPC boundary and provide actionable recovery guidance without decoder internals.

## Evidence

Product head: `72394c794052d0efe3783c61f3a287e971039fe4`; acceptance-red base: `83872e599d5720c0bc97d313283a2bc245046699`.

- **Real Gateway / CLI / disk:** the normal built CLI calls `agents.files.get`, `agents.files.set` and `agents.update` against an isolated Gateway. On BASE, a CP1252 byte becomes U+FFFD during an ordinary read/edit/checked-save, a cached-hash save and an identity update. On HEAD, all three refuse invalid UTF-8; actual disk bytes remain identical and identity-update configuration remains unchanged.
- **Actionable recovery:** the actual CLI responses for all three refused operations are independently read back as `INVALID_REQUEST`, state that the original file was preserved, and instruct UTF-8 conversion before retry. No decoder error code, TypeError or cause is exposed.
- **Legal controls:** valid BOM/Unicode/literal U+FFFD checked edits read back exactly; intentional replacement without `expectedHash` still succeeds. **5/5 expected outcomes** pass on each version. Actual CLI stdout/stderr/status and file/config byte hashes are published.
- **Checks:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agents-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **33 passed, 1 preexisting skip**, **62.626 seconds** wall time. Targeted types, lint, format, staged exact test-line budget, normal CLI build and fresh independent adversarial review pass; findings: **None**. Existing handler/real shell-bridge fixture startup accounts for the command exceeding 30 seconds; no timeout was increased. No module mock factories were added or changed; full repository mock checking remains for CI.

[Inspect the frozen collector, paired receipts, actual outputs, checks and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/b727ad1649659fd79a14ebf4441652298a8213f1). Evidence assets are outside the product branch.

<details>
<summary>Replay, scope and limitations</summary>

```sh
python3 collect.py --repo CHECKOUT --output NEW_OUTPUT --node NODE26 --expect-head FULL_SHA --expect EXPECTATION
```

frozen collector defc653fcb34afc7ba09b144b4e332e5fb3629900f4657143d596e922aabb795; version and expected-outcome selectors only. Use clean normally built BASE/HEAD checkouts, a fresh output directory, and `red` / `green` respectively.

Three files: production **+47/-11**, tests **+44/-2** (net **42 LF**) and an exact own-regression allocation. Coverage includes local and real shell-bridge reads/writes, stale-hash conflicts, matching-hash malformed edits, exact classified recovery, identity refusal and byte preservation, valid Unicode/BOM/U+FFFD and intentional blind replacement. The existing decoder and bridge semantics are reused; read-only skills preview and the already-strict session editor require no patch.

Cleanup: The collector stops only its own Gateway process group and verifies its absence. Synthetic workspace/config fixtures are retained. Child environments are allowlisted with isolated HOME/XDG/config/state; no real provider, model, channel or user data is used.

**Not tested:** browser UI clicks, a real remote workspace bridge, Windows/macOS and the full repository CI matrix; remote bridge coverage is in the focused suite.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): validate compaction.maxSummaryChars in session settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.compaction.maxSummaryChars` is bounds-checked in `openclaw.json` since #196207 (integer, 1,000–200,000), but the same key in session `settings.json` bypassed the schema: `readSettingsScope` parses raw JSON and `requireSupportedSettings` only rejected retired keys.

- `0` or a negative value inverted the ceiling into *no truncation* (`capCompactionSummary` returns the summary untouched when `maxChars <= 0`) and made the split-turn context budget negative.
- `100000000` crashed compaction: `resolveCompactionRetentionBudget` estimates with `'x'.repeat(maxSummaryChars)` and dies with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.
- A project `.openclaw/settings.json` arriving with a cloned repository carries either value.

**Fix:** validate the key in `requireSupportedSettings` — the gate every global, project, and merged-snapshot load already passes — reusing `AgentCompactionMaxSummaryCharsSchema` from the config surface. One production file (`src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.ts`, +12); regression folded into the existing first case of `settings-manager.test.ts` (net 0 test lines).

## Why This Change Was Made

That function is the single place where settings validity is decided and already rejects retired keys via `createInvalidConfigError`. Reusing the config-side schema keeps one bounds owner so the two surfaces cannot drift, and the error keeps the existing `InvalidConfigError` / `recovery: "manual"` shape while naming the key, the range, and how to restore the default.

Rejected alternative: clamping inside `capCompactionSummary` or the budget estimator — it persists the invalid value, makes each consumer guess, and still disagrees with the config surface.

### Early rejection scope (owner decision requested)

`createPreparedEmbeddedAgentSettingsManager` validates both original scopes before `agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.projectSettingsPolicy` is applied, so a project file the policy would `ignore` still rejects preparation. That matches the retired-key gate's existing placement and fail-closed behavior, but it is a policy choice, not a mechanical consequence. Moving the check below `buildEmbeddedAgentSettingsSnapshot` would let an ignored scope stop failing; say which you want and I will adjust.

## User Impact

A typo'd or inherited `maxSummaryChars` now fails at load with an actionable error instead of unbounded persisted summaries replayed on later requests or a compaction-time `RangeError`. In-range values and an absent key behave as before.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI (`openclaw agent --local -m "say hi"`) against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, with a real `settings.json` at `agentDir/settings.json` (global) or `<workspace>/.openclaw/settings.json` (project), and a loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoint so an accepted turn actually completes. `model_requests` counts hits on that endpoint.

| build | scope | `maxSummaryChars` | outcome | model requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2026.11.3` `847611d` published | global | `0`, `100000000`, `48000`, absent | all accepted — **the bug** | 1 |
| `73b36af` this head | global | `0`, `100000000`, `999` | `InvalidConfigError` | **0** |
| `73b36af` this head | project | `0` | `InvalidConfigError` | **0** |
| `73b36af` this head | global | `48000`, absent | turn completed | 1 |
| `73b36af` this head | project | `48000` | turn completed | 1 |

`model_requests = 0` is the point: the gate fires before any provider call.

```text
$ openclaw agent --local -m "say hi" --session-id head-global-0
  # settings.json: {"compaction":{"maxSummaryChars":0}}
Invalid config at global session settings.json:
compaction.maxSummaryChars must be an integer from 1000 to 200000; remove it to restore the 16000 default.
-> InvalidConfigError; no model request was made

$ openclaw agent --local -m "say hi" --session-id head-project-0
  # <workspace>/.openclaw/settings.json, same value
Invalid config at project session settings.json:
compaction.maxSummaryChars must be an integer from 1000 to 200000; remove it to restore the 16000 default.
-> InvalidConfigError; no model request was made
```

**Recovery:** after the operator rewrites that same file to `48000`, the next `agent --local` run completes the turn — no state reset or reinstall. **Upgrade:** the published build accepted `{"compaction":{"maxSummaryChars":48000}}`, and this head loads the identical file text and completes the turn, so a file already on disk keeps working unchanged.

Regression test, red on the base with the test kept, green with the fix:

```console
$ git show 26b2a3c2a9a:src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.ts > src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.ts
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.test.ts
 × preserves compaction overrides after local setting writes
AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw an error
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)

$ git checkout -- src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.ts   # then rerun the same command
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Consumer suites (`settings-storage`, `agent-project-settings`, `agent-project-settings.bundle`) under `test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`: `3 passed (3)`, `35 passed (35)`. `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` 0 warnings / 0 errors (259 rules); diff is `+12/-0` production and `+6/-6` test (net 0). CI on this revision: the node-core-test, lint-hosted-core, test-types-hosted-core, and additional shards pass; `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` fails on `ui/src/e2e/screen-requester-routing.e2e.test.ts` (`page.waitForFunction` timeout, 1 of 15 files) with no UI file in this diff.

### Not covered

The published `2026.11.3` → this head step also carries a shared SQLite state-schema migration the CLI asks `doctor --fix` to custody before the first turn. That is independent of this PR (no schema or store change here), so the proof holds `settings.json` fixed and does not claim session-store upgrade coverage.

prs.title: fix(worker): reject non-UTF-8 Git paths in the workspace manifest
prs.body:
Related: #191574

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a workspace capture reports success while the worker receives a workspace without a tracked file whose name is not valid UTF-8.

`git ls-files -z` returns names as bytes, and two decodes on the capture path turned them into strings: `bad\xff.txt` becomes `bad\uFFFD.txt`, the `lstat` for that spelling misses, and both owners read the miss as "nothing to do".

- Gateway transfer inventory: `readBoundedGitPathCandidates()` yielded the replacement spelling and `inspectFile()` stat'd it, so the file never entered the rsync `--files-from` list.
- Worker manifest script: `nulPaths()` decoded the whole list, `addEntry()` missed the same way, and the published inventory omitted the file while exiting 0.

On `4045f09b701` a built Gateway and a real node worker show the whole failure: `sessions.dispatch` returns `ok: true` with an `active` placement while the worker's workspace holds 2 of the 3 files.

## User Impact

- An existing tracked file whose bytes cannot be a manifest path stops the capture before any transfer with `worker workspace Git paths must be UTF-8; rename the invalid path before retrying`, the wording and policy [local-workspace-inventory.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/deed97ef3866dd49e6b7029e921d6fef8d7438eb/src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-inventory.ts) already uses; renaming the path and retrying dispatches normally.
- A Git name whose file a reclaim already removed stays a deletion, and an ignored file nothing selects captures as before, even when a valid tracked file carries its replacement spelling.
- Valid UTF-8 workspaces are unaffected. When both `bad\uFFFD.txt` and `bad<0xff>.txt` are tracked, capture refuses instead of transferring one and dropping the other.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `readBoundedGitPathCandidates()` yields each name with the bytes Git reported and `inspectFile()` merges `selected` and `ignored` by those bytes. The refusal runs before the decoded-name dedupe because a valid `U+FFFD` file can claim that spelling first and hide the file holding the invalid bytes; a name whose file is gone stays a deletion.
- [workspace-sync-scripts.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/deed97ef3866dd49e6b7029e921d6fef8d7438eb/src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-sync-scripts.ts) mirrors it in the generated script: `nulPaths()` records undecodable names per list, so only a name the capture admits (the index, or `.worktreeinclude`) fails, while a plain ignored name cannot fail the tracked file spelled the same; a staged input selected out of the ignored list still refuses.
- Both generated assets come from `pnpm runtime:scripts:gen`, never hand-edited; the added test lines are recorded in [undecodable-workspace-git-paths.txt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/deed97ef3866dd49e6b7029e921d6fef8d7438eb/config/test-lines-allocations/undecodable-workspace-git-paths.txt).
- Gap: a complete (`walk`) capture is unreachable through `sessions.dispatch` (session worktree, repository workspace, or a device folder that transfers nothing), so it rides on the committed test.

## Evidence

Each arm builds that commit (`pnpm build`) and runs an isolated Gateway (`node dist/index.js gateway run`) plus a real node worker (`node dist/index.js node run`) paired over the tunnel; a fixture repository commits `README.md`, `tracked.txt` and `bad<0xff>.txt`, and `sessions.dispatch` sends a worktree of `main` to the node.

| | `sessions.dispatch` result | worker workspace holds | outcome |

prs.title: fix(team-reports): bound API response reads before parsing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every GitHub and Discord page a Team Reports run fetched was buffered whole before any budget applied — whoever answers the request decides the run's memory cost, and nothing capped it.

- `extensions/team-reports/src/sources/http.ts:31` on `main` is `const body = await response.text()`, the only place either source turns a response into bytes (`github/client.ts:84`, `discord/index.ts:70`).
- `MAX_REPORT_BYTES = 2 MiB` bounds the rendered report after collection, so an oversized response was materialized first. Reachable without a compromise: `github.apiBaseUrl` is user-settable (`src/config.ts:38`), so an intermediary can inflate any response.

Solution: read through the shared bounded owner `readResponseWithLimit` — already called by the shipped GitHub and Discord clients for these same APIs — with a 32 MiB budget above the largest page they can legitimately return, and report overflow as a size failure naming the cutoff, the size, and a recovery step.

What changed: overflow becomes a `too-large` read failure carrying the bytes read and the host-advertised size (`src/sources/http.ts`); one `describeResponseOverflow` renders that detail for both sources; `src/limits.ts` holds `MAX_API_RESPONSE_BYTES = 32 MiB` and the warning label; `github/client.ts` and `discord/index.ts` warn with the cutoff plus `regenerate the affected days`, Discord escaping the retry loop; `run.ts` propagates roster-failure warnings into the recorded run error; `docs/plugins/team-reports.md` documents the bound and recovery.

Unchanged: SSRF guard options, `finally { release?.() }`, pagination and page size, retry for other failures, report rendering, the 2 MiB report cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 2 MiB report limit bound bytes after rendering, but acquisition was unbounded. The smallest complete repair reuses the existing public SDK reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) at the shared HTTP owner that already bounds these same APIs for the shipped clients — bound bytes before parsing, preserve release, distinguish permanent overflow, retain warnings through run failure.

- Best fix: Reuses the existing public SDK reader; no new mechanism, config option, schema, or core import.
- Alternative: Per-source limits — rejected; the shared owner already exists.
- Risk / non-goals: Budget is per response, so a hostile host paging repeatedly still controls total work (no run-byte cap). Accepted. The bound changes this plugin's collection contract: pages above 32 MiB now fail — the same shape the shipped clients use. `main` already enforces fixed per-response bounds on these APIs (Discord 8 MiB, GitHub 256 KiB); at 32 MiB Team Reports is looser than all four.

## User Impact

An over-budget page fails with a warning stating the 32 MiB cutoff, the page size, and what to do; its collection stops there (remaining pages not fetched), other scopes keep collecting, and a failed day is not published over the last accepted report.

## Evidence

Before/after behavior through the real shipped source functions over verified HTTPS (real `https.Server` on a public-range address the SSRF guard allows, private CA in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, TLS genuinely verified):

| Case | `origin/main` (before) | this branch (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub roster, server returns 200 MiB | accepted, no warning, 209,715,214 B read, +1053 MiB RSS | 32 MiB warning, `host declared 209,715,214 bytes`, client closed, +88 MiB RSS |
| GitHub roster, normal page | ok, 2 people | ok, 2 people (unchanged) |
| Discord messages, server returns 200 MiB | accepted, no warning, 209,715,246 B read, +844 MiB RSS | 32 MiB warning, `host declared 209,715,246 bytes`, client closed, +89 MiB RSS |
| Discord messages, HTTP 500 | 3 requests, 3.4 s, retry warning | 3 requests, 3.4 s, retry warning (unchanged) |

Overflow warnings, verbatim from that run:

```
Load team acme/core: API response exceeded the 32 MiB limit (host declared 209,715,214 bytes); check the API base URL or proxy for oversized output, then regenerate the affected days
Discord messages for channel 20: Discord response exceeded the 32 MiB limit (host declared 209,715,246 bytes); check for oversized API output, then regenerate the affected days.
```

Roster-failure propagation: a roster read that fails on overflow now carries the cutoff, declared size, and recovery advice into the recorded run error, and aborts the entire run before Discord or any other source collects.

Upgrade parity (`v2026.10.10` → this branch): released source created the store and wrote one accepted day; this branch read it back intact (1315 bytes, both logins), wrote a second day, reopened it. Config with every documented option parses to identical JSON (735 bytes, `sha256:81fcc7c1…`); both reject an unknown `maxApiResponseBytes`. The published artifact's worker module reproduces the round trip.

Regression pin: reverting the bounded read to `Buffer.from(await response.text())` fails exactly the three new tests and leaves the other 38 green in `extensions/team-reports/src/sources`; restoring returns 41/41.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/team-reports --run  →  Test Files 20 passed | 1 skipped (21)  Tests 208 passed | 5 skipped (213)
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 1ca0669b…  →  the 26 added test lines are covered by config/test-lines-allocations/team-reports-response-overflow-size.txt; the remaining over-ceiling delta is inherited from that base commit's stale baseline.
```

The trace calls shipped `createGithubSource(...).loadRoster` and `createDiscordSource(...).collect` — real guard, reader, release and retry paths, one process per case, origin logging bytes and how each stream ended (`client closed` is the origin observing cancellation), with a server returning an oversized body no real API returns.

Not covered: the shipped CLI/Gateway process path — this checkout cannot build in this environment (a bundled plugin's `@solidjs/compiler` devDependency is absent, one native asset unpinned); type checking rests on CI's `check-prod-types` / `check-test-types`.

prs.title: fix(cli): show session label column in sessions table
prs.body:
Related to #181160

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions` never shows a session's display label or its named sidebar tint. A user who named a session (and gave it a color via `SESSION_COLOR_IDS`) sees that label and color in the Control UI sidebar, but the text table renders neither — `toSessionDisplayRow` already projects `label`/`color` from the store, yet both are dropped when the table columns are built.

- Problem: the terminal table discards the `label` and `color` already present on each session row.
- Solution: add a `Label` column to the `openclaw sessions` text table that renders the session label, tinted with the same hue the Control UI uses for that named color. The column is shown **conditionally**: it appears only when at least one displayed session carries a non-empty label, so unlabelled listings keep their previous layout exactly.
- What changed: `SESSION_TINT_HEX` + `sessionTint()` in the terminal theme, a `formatSessionLabelCell` helper in the sessions table, a conditional `Label` column in the sessions command, and focused tests.
- What did NOT change: the `--label` filter from #181160. It needs a product decision on matching semantics and is intentionally left for follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

The data is already present in the session row; the terminal table simply fails to surface it. This change makes the terminal match the sidebar: labels render in the default foreground unless a rich terminal can apply the named hue, and sessions without a label keep an empty cell (no invented values, no noise). When a label has no color or the color name is unknown, `sessionTint` returns no tint and the text falls back to the default foreground.

The `Label` column is conditional so that the common case (no session labelled yet) is byte-for-byte identical to today's output — no spurious empty column. The tint hues are a display-only concern, so they live as a local constant in the terminal theme (`SESSION_TINT_HEX`) kept in sync with the Control UI `--session-color-*` palette rather than adding new palette tokens. This is the display half of #181160 only; the filter half is a separate, product-decision-gated follow-up.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions` now surfaces each session's label, and in rich (color-capable) terminals tints it with the same hue as the Control UI sidebar for that session's named color. Unlabelled sessions and sessions without a color render exactly as before — including the hidden `Label` column when no session is labelled — so no behavior is regressed for existing users.

## Evidence

Focused regression in `src/commands/sessions.test.ts`:
- "shows a saved session label as its own column" — a labelled session renders eight columns with `research helper` in the `Label` cell; the unlabelled-table assertion in the next test still pins seven columns with tokens at index 5, so the column cannot appear without a label.
- Test budget: the regression reuses the existing `singleSessionTableCells` helper, so the change adds no net test lines (`net delta: -1` against the merge base) and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passes.
- Red on base / green on head: with the production diff reverted (`5eeafd8`) the new test fails with `expected [ 7, '1m ago' ] to deeply equal [ 8, 'research helper' ]`; on this head it passes.

Real `openclaw sessions` CLI proof (four states: labelled/unlabelled × plain/rich). Each store was seeded through the production session-accessor path into a fresh SQLite store, then listed through the actual CLI (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts sessions --store <store>`, FORCE_COLOR=3 for the rich runs). ANSI escapes are shown as `<ESC>`, and this is a throwaway local store with no credentials or private endpoints (dummy ids `labelled`/`plain`, dummy model `gpt-6-astra`).

**Labelled store, plain terminal** — `Label` column shown, label in default foreground, unlabelled row empty:

```console
$ openclaw sessions --store .../sessions.json
┌────────┬─────────────────────┬─────────────────┬────────┬─────────────┬──────────────┬────────────────┬──────────────┐
│ Kind   │ Key                 │ Label           │ Age    │ Model       │ Runtime      │ Tokens (ctx %) │ Flags        │
├────────┼─────────────────────┼─────────────────┼────────┼─────────────┼──────────────┼────────────────┼──────────────┤
│ direct │ agent:main:labelled │ research helper │ 4m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain    │                 │ 5m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
└────────┴─────────────────────┴─────────────────┴────────┴─────────────┴──────────────┴────────────────┴──────────────┘
```

**Labelled store, rich terminal (FORCE_COLOR=3)** — the label is tinted with the Control UI's purple hue `#b595e8` (`<ESC>[38;2;181;149;232mresearch helper<ESC>[39m`):

```console
│ <ESC>[38;2;255;90;45mdirect<ESC>[39m │ <ESC>[38;2;255;90;45magent:main:labelled<ESC>[39m │ <ESC>[38;2;181;149;232mresearch helper<ESC>[39m │ ...
```

**Unlabelled store (only unlabelled sessions), plain terminal** — the `Label` column is hidden; the table keeps its previous column set:

```console
$ openclaw sessions --store .../sessions.json
│ Kind   │ Key              │ Age     │ Model       │ Runtime      │ Tokens (ctx %) │ Flags │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain │ 11m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
```

**Before (this PR's original unconditional column)** — the same unlabelled store previously always rendered an empty `Label` column:

```console
│ Kind   │ Key              │ Label │ Age     │ Model       │ Runtime      │ Tokens (ctx %) │ Flags │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain │       │ 13m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
```

The rich capture confirms `38;2;181;149;232` matches the Control UI purple `#b595e8`; the before/after unlabelled pair shows the conditional column hiding.

prs.title: test(ui): scope pending-handoff exact-text locators to chat bubbles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scopes the three page-wide exact-text locators in the pending-handoff Control UI E2E test to `.chat-bubble`, so they cannot resolve to the screen-reader announcement span.

Fixes #162620

## Why

The test used `page.getByText(<assistant text>, { exact: true })` to wait for a rendered assistant message. The Control UI also renders the same text inside a `.chat-transcript-announcement.sr-only[role=status]` accessibility announcement (the live-region text is the full trimmed assistant message). When both elements are present the locator hits a Playwright strict-mode violation:

```text
Error: locator.waitFor: strict mode violation:
getByText('Landed the PR. All focused checks passed.', { exact: true })
resolved to 2 elements:
  span.chat-transcript-announcement.sr-only[role=status]
  p
```

This was observed intermittently in CI (actions run 36848731115). The ambiguity is a test defect, not a duplicate transcript message.

Scoping only to `.chat-thread` is insufficient because the announcement lives inside the thread; the visible message text lives in `.chat-bubble`. So the waits are scoped to `.chat-bubble`, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this file (`.locator(".chat-bubble").getByText(...)`).

## Impact

- Test-only change; no product behavior, UI source, or test configuration changes.
- All assertions and the accessibility announcement remain intact — only the locator scope changes.

## Real behavior proof

Reproduced through the shipped Control UI (real Chromium + the existing mock Gateway harness): a completed assistant message delivered over the live channel (`chat.final`) renders **both** a `.chat-bubble` and the `.chat-transcript-announcement.sr-only` live region carrying the same text. Diagnostics captured from the live page:

```json
{
  "finalText": "Landed the PR. All focused checks passed.",
  "pageWideExactTextCount": 2,
  "chatBubbleScopedCount": 1,
  "pageWideWaitOutcome": "FAILED (strict mode violation): locator.waitFor: Error: strict mode violation: getByText('Landed the PR. All focused checks passed.', { exact: true }) resolved to 2 elements:",
  "scopedWaitOutcome": "resolved",
  "dom": {
    "announcementText": "Landed the PR. All focused checks passed.",
    "announcementClass": "chat-transcript-announcement sr-only",
    "announcementRole": "status",
    "announcementAriaLive": "polite",
    "exactTextElements": [
      { "tag": "span", "cls": "chat-transcript-announcement sr-only", "role": "status", "ariaLive": "polite", "insideBubble": false, "insideAnnouncement": true },
      { "tag": "p", "cls": "", "insideBubble": true, "insideAnnouncement": false }
    ]
  }
}
```

Terminal output from the same run (`Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 1 passed (1)`, `[ui-e2e] Chromium exited (code=0)`):

```text
=== PROOF-162620 DOM DIAGNOSTICS ===
"pageWideExactTextCount": 2
"chatBubbleScopedCount": 1
"pageWideWaitOutcome": "FAILED (strict mode violation): ... getByText(...) resolved to 2 elements"
"scopedWaitOutcome": "resolved"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The page-wide wait fails with the exact strict-mode violation while the `.chat-bubble`-scoped wait succeeds — the failing-base / passing-head demonstration for this defect.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-send-pending-handoff.e2e.test.ts` — all 5 tests pass (including the three whose locators changed) against the mock Gateway with a real Chromium:
  - `retires only the local user when older history arrives beside a pending assistant fallback`
  - `does not recreate a consumed prompt outside the visible history page after reconnect`
  - `does not replay a retired user bubble after a later history page omits it`
  - `keeps one submitted turn through the queued image handoff`
  - `keeps one submitted turn through the early session echo handoff`
- `oxlint` on the changed file: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Formatting check passes.
- `git diff --check` clean.
- Test-line allocation added for the net +6 test lines (`config/test-lines-allocations/162620-chat-pending-handoff-locator-scope.txt`).

## Test plan

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_REAL_GATEWAY=1 \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-send-pending-handoff.e2e.test.ts
```

prs.title: fix(markdown-core): stop shattering text for an unusable IR chunk limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` — exported from the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking` surface — ran every non-`Infinity` limit through `resolveIntegerOption(limit, 1, { min: 1 })`. That fallback is `1`, so a `NaN`, zero or negative limit became a one-character step and the chunker emitted one chunk per character. A 95-character reply reached the transport as **80 separate messages**.

`chunkText` in the same package already returns the whole text for the same input: `normalizeChunkLimit` maps `NaN` to `0`, leaves zero and negative alone, and `chunkText` treats a non-positive limit as "no cap". Two chunkers in one package disagreed about what an unusable limit means, and each side's tests pinned its own answer — `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` asserted `[markdownToIR("abc"), Number.NaN, ["a", "b", "c"]]` while `chunk-text.test.ts` asserted `NaN -> ["abc"]`.

The existing comment already described the right contract and implemented half of it:

```
// Callers pass Infinity to mean "no size cap" ... resolveIntegerOption rejects non-finite values
// and would fall back to 1, shattering the text into one chunk per character; emit the whole IR as one chunk.
if (options.limit === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) {
```

It says **non-finite**, but only `Infinity` was special-cased.

## Is this replacing a deliberately retained fallback?

The one open review question. Checked the basis before answering it:

- `#193956` has **`reviews: 0`**, and its `mergedBy` is a merge click — no maintainer statement on that PR describes invalid-limit semantics as a retained contract.
- Its own body calls the behavior a defect and names the goal as removing it:

  > The deliberately **loud** per-character `NaN` behavior of `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` (pinned by `render-aware-chunking.test.ts`) is intentionally left untouched.

  > The sibling helpers in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts` already return whole text for `NaN`, so this also **removes a divergence between the two chunking implementations**.

- "Intentionally left untouched" is scope discipline from a PR that touched two other files, not a ruling that one-character splitting is correct.
- Its stated premise was **incomplete**: *"This is the single owner of the broken normalization."* `chunkText` reaches `normalizeChunkLimit`; `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` never did — it ran its own `resolveIntegerOption`. That is why `render-aware-chunking.ts` still carried the defect after `#193956` merged.

**This PR deletes that second normalization and routes both chunkers through the owner `#193956` introduced. It completes the claimed single owner rather than adding a contract.** Production code shrinks by six lines.

Why the two paths cannot both stand: `src/plugin-sdk/text-chunking.ts:54-58` exports `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` from the **same file** as `chunkText` and `chunkTextRanges` — one public SDK surface, two answers for one input. A plugin passing the same `NaN` gets whole text from `chunkText` and one chunk per character from `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit`.

`#195329` (`src/shared/text-chunking.ts`) and `#193956` (`chunk-text.ts`) already moved two of the three paths to "unbounded"; this is the third. Two independent contributors proposed the same direction (`#193973`, `#194020`); `#194020` was closed for scope bloat — reminder accounting and Windows executable selection — not because the direction was rejected.

If a maintainer does want the one-character fallback kept as a public contract, that is a separate discussion, but it would leave two exports of the same module contradicting each other, with the falling-split side pinned only by a test inside the package.

## User Impact

Plugin and channel-adapter authors calling the exported `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` with a bad computed limit — `Number(envValue)` on an unset variable, arithmetic over an optional setting — got an outbound message shattered across dozens of channel messages instead of delivered once.

`Infinity` already meant "no cap" and keeps working exactly as before; nothing changes for a usable finite limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both chunkers now read limits through one owner, `packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-limit.ts`, which keeps the non-positive path `chunkText` already relied on. `chunk-text.ts` loses its private copy of the function and `render-aware-chunking.ts` drops its `Infinity`-only special case.

The module is deliberately **not** exported from the package barrel, so `normalizeChunkLimit` does not become new public API — `packages/markdown-core` has a root `.` export and `export * from "./chunk-text.js"` would have leaked it.

## Evidence

Real guarded HTTP transport, not a stub client: a `node:http` loopback server receives the actual POST bodies, while `ssrf-runtime` rewrites only the `chat.googleapis.com` hostname and `getGoogleChatAccessToken` returns a synthetic token. Everything from `formatGoogleChatTextChunks` inward is shipped code — `sendGoogleChatMessage` -> `fetchJson` -> `withGoogleChatResponse` -> `fetchWithSsrFGuard` -> real socket.

Same proof file, same transport, only the library files switched:

Before (`origin/main`):


prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node directory listing stops after 32 pages so one oversized directory cannot pin the gateway. Bootstrap discovery used that stop to skip the directory, then still loaded a sibling, but it recorded no diagnostic. A configured `*/AGENTS.md` file inside the oversized directory disappeared with `diagnostics: []`.

## Evidence

Head `b06896ea3a7` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The production trace below was run on `055d09e2943`. `b06896ea3a7` merges current main and adds the 112-line test grant. It does not change the listing or the diagnostic. A real directory held 131073 empty names, which is one past 32 pages of 4096. Its sibling `keep/AGENTS.md` contained `kept instructions`. Production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` listed that tree. Each `dir.list` call went to production `handleDirList` on that directory, not a scripted page payload. `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` then loaded `*/AGENTS.md`.

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. `file.fetch` read the sibling once. The oversized directory is named in the diagnostic and its instructions were not loaded.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bootstrap discovery skips one directory after the real 32-page listing cap, records that skip, and still loads a sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, head `055d09e2943` in `/tmp/oc-165805`, then merged forward as `b06896ea3a7` without changing the listing or the diagnostic. The directory was a local folder with 131073 names. The node command handler and the gateway bridge ran in one process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created the oversized directory and `keep/AGENTS.md`. Called `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` with `invoke` dispatching to `handleDirList`, `handleFileStat`, and `handleFileFetch`. Called `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` for `*/AGENTS.md`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that production path:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 fetch=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sibling file was loaded. The oversized directory produced one `io` diagnostic, `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages`, after 32 real listing pages.
- **What was not tested:** A second OS process enrolled as a node over the gateway websocket. The same handlers ran in-process.

## Summary

A directory past the listing page budget is still skipped, and its sibling still loads. The skip is now a diagnostic instead of a silent omission.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve source files when extension copy paths overlap
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chrome extension asset copying could delete source files when `OPENCLAW_CHROME_EXT_OUT_DIR` points to the source directory or an overlapping tree. The command reported an error only after the destructive cleanup.

## User Impact

Developers and packagers now receive an overlap error before existing files are removed. Separate output directories still replace stale assets and copy the runtime extension files normally. This affects the browser plugin's asset-copy command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve existing source/output paths and compare whole path components before cleanup, retaining the existing copier and asset filters. The change adds 18 production lines and 51 net regression-test lines, with a separate 51-line allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

Existing output symlinks that resolve into the source tree are rejected. This protects stable configured paths; concurrent path replacement is outside the guarantee. Validation is on Linux; physical macOS and Windows execution is not claimed.

## Evidence

**Current submitted head:** `f3dbc982512981339ce3d9aa8451223a4757e5b7`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42463380546) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42463380546/job/128678889300) passed for this exact head. The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195068#issuecomment-6718471074) reports sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Status checked November 11; runtime records below are retained, not new executions.

| Retained production-CLI scenario | Base | Current candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Same, ancestor, or descendant output | Fails after deleting preexisting files | Overlap error before deletion; all preexisting hashes unchanged |
| Separate sibling output | Replaces stale output and copies runtime assets | Same successful behavior and source preservation |
| Relative paths and source-resolving symlinks | Not claimed as new baseline runs | Recorded fixed-source controls reject before deletion |

The subprocess transcripts and source hashes below are retained evidence from November 9, not new execution today.

<details>
<summary>Detailed verification, source receipts and original runtime captures</summary>

- **CI repair:** the previous run failed the test-line ratchet by 16 inherited lines (6,574,087 lines versus a 6,574,071 ceiling). Main `f6c59570fedab6eed7c612a16d9f1c9167067bfc` already resolves that debt and has 27 lines of slack. Both PR commits were rebased onto that exact main; `git range-diff` reports identical patches and all three changed files are byte-identical to the previously tested head `5fc75d6844dcd3b7e61a98b48791c9ef517ffec7`. No additional allocation, shared-baseline increase, or test removal was needed.
- **Rebased head `f3dbc982512981339ce3d9aa8451223a4757e5b7`:** the unchanged native test-line checker passes: `Test lines OK: 6575070; ceiling: 6575097; slack: 27.` The PR still adds exactly 51 test lines and 51 allocation credit.
- **Fresh real CLI verification:** same-directory, ancestor, descendant, relative-path, and symlink cases reject before deletion and preserve the existing fixture files. Sibling replacement and fresh-output controls pass and exclude test/type files. All seven cases pass in an offline, secretless, read-only container with Node 24.19.0 and Git 2.39.5, limited to 256 MiB / 0.5 CPU.
- **Earlier unchanged-code proof:** the hosted browser package suite passed 6/6 tests on `5fc75d6` ([owner job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42455215241/job/128652903746)); both import-boundary checks, types, and lint passed. The owner suite's hosted runner duration was 40.99 seconds (98% transform); the four new CLI cases took 11/9/10/16 ms. Earlier isolated Vitest execution passed all six tests in 692 ms test time / 1.50 seconds runner duration. These remain prior-head test timings; the current rebased combination has since passed hosted CI, linked above and below.
- Node syntax and diff-whitespace checks pass. No full dependency installation or full local test/build suite was run for this patch-identical rebase.

Independent review: a separate read-only Codex reviewer inspected the full final range `f6c59570fedab6eed7c612a16d9f1c9167067bfc..f3dbc982512981339ce3d9aa8451223a4757e5b7`, owning callers and verification evidence; no actionable P0–P2 findings. This was a session-based review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper CLI run.

**Current-head hosted CI:** [run 42463380546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42463380546) passed on `f3dbc982512981339ce3d9aa8451223a4757e5b7`, including the native baseline ratchet, changed extension checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The subsequent Security Review also passed.

The separate sibling output succeeds on both revisions, replaces stale output, preserves source bytes, and copies only runtime files.

```python
    print(f"$ OPENCLAW_CHROME_EXT_SRC_DIR={source} OPENCLAW_CHROME_EXT_OUT_DIR={output} node {script}", flush=True)

    print(f"exit={result.returncode}\nstdout={result.stdout.rstrip()!r}\nstderr={result.stderr.rstrip()!r}", flush=True)
    after = {name: digest(root / name) for name in before}
    print(f"AFTER manifest={digest(manifest)} old={digest(sentinel)}\nall_preexisting_hashes_equal={before == after}", flush=True)
    if case == "sibling":
        copied = sorted(str(p.relative_to(output)) for p in output.rglob("*") if p.is_file())

    elif revision == "head":

    else:
        assert result.returncode == 1 and before != after
```
