prs.title: fix(onepassword): expire cached secrets on elapsed time
prs.body:
## Reopened

This PR reopens #193412 with the same patch and evidence. The previous PR's final re-review (2026-11-06) never landed: ClawSweeper acked "review queued" but the exact-review step ran as skipped, leaving the PR stuck at `status: needs proof` with zero formal reviews. The production code is byte-identical to the reviewed head (`d76c3b49efd`); only the base is refreshed so the test-line ratchet aligns with current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

`OnePasswordBroker.get` caches a resolved secret for `cacheTtlSeconds` (default 300 s) so repeated reads do not hit `op`. Both ends of that window read the wall clock:

- freshness: `cached.expiresAtMs > Date.now()`
- write: `expiresAtMs: Date.now() + config.cacheTtlSeconds * 1000`

A backwards clock step on the Gateway host keeps the cached secret being served as fresh for the length of the step after a rotation, so an agent can keep using a rotated credential until the clock catches up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Secret-cache expiry now runs on elapsed time (`performance.now()`). The TTL, cache key (`slug`), target-fingerprint check, config-fingerprint invalidation, and audit rows are unchanged; behavior without a clock step is identical.

Standing grants and pending authorizations keep the wall clock on purpose: they are persisted safety windows (`grantTtlHours`), so an operator correcting the clock must not extend a persisted grant. Only this in-memory, per-process cache moves.

The module is a bundled extension and may only import `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, so it reads `performance.now()` directly. Bundled extensions ship with the host, so no compatibility path is needed.

This is **behavior-completing** for the elapsed-clock family (#191606, #192700, #193147, #193306).

## User Impact

A clock correction no longer extends a cached secret past its TTL. Without a clock step nothing changes: same TTL, same cache hits, same audits.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked clocks and mocked `getItem`)

`extensions/onepassword/src/broker.test.ts` via the repository's Vitest entry (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/onepassword/src/broker.test.ts`) on Node v24.22.1:

| Test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expires cached secrets on elapsed time when the wall clock steps backwards` | **FAIL** — the second read is a cache hit (one `getItem` call) | PASS |
| `rechecks grant expiry with cache TTL 300` / `7200` (existing) | PASS | PASS |

The existing harness already fakes `Date.now`; it now fakes `performance.now` with the same counter so both clocks advance together, and `advance(ms)` drives both. The new test steps `Date.now` back an hour while `performance.now` advances past the TTL.

### Real-boundary proof — committed reproducible test (real broker + real op-client + real CLI execution)

ClawSweeper asked for real-behavior evidence through the op boundary rather than mocked clocks and a mocked `getItem`. This proof drives the **shipped production classes end to end**: `OnePasswordBroker.get` → real `OpClient.getItem` → real `resolveTrustedOnePasswordCli` trust validation → real subprocess exec of an `op` CLI. A fake `op` executable (owned by the current user, non-writable, absolute-node shebang — passes the same trust validation the product runs) stands in for the 1Password CLI and logs every invocation to a counter file. The wall clock is stepped back one hour by overriding `Date.now` (the same rollback the fix targets); the process-local `performance.now()` is the real clock and its value at the second read (≈14.5s) far exceeds the 1s cache TTL.

This was previously a one-off driver script; it is now committed as `re-fetches a secret through the real op boundary after a backward clock step` in `broker.test.ts`, so it runs in CI. RED/GREEN verified locally:

```
# BASE (broker.ts reads Date.now)
 × re-fetches a secret through the real op boundary after a backward clock step
   → expected '1\n' to be '1\n1\n' // Object.is equality
# HEAD (broker.ts reads performance.now)
 ✓ re-fetches a secret through the real op boundary after a backward clock step 1323ms
 # counter file reads "1\n1\n" — op called 2×, secret re-fetched
```

The counter-file discriminator makes the stale-cache defect directly observable: BASE serves the pre-rollback cached value and logs one `op` invocation; HEAD re-fetches and logs two. BASE/HEAD differ only in `broker.ts`'s clock read (`Date.now` vs `performance.now`); everything else (real op-client, real trust check, real exec, same fake-op binary, same test) is identical. No production Gateway, session, token, vault, or real 1Password credential was touched; all CLI targets are local fixtures. The test is `it.runIf(process.platform !== "win32")`-guarded because the trusted-node fixture relies on a POSIX shebang.

HEAD full suite:

```
 ✓ extensions/onepassword/src/broker.test.ts (29 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

### Shipped-Gateway proof — real Gateway process, real plugin, real `op` subprocess, real wall-clock step

ClawSweeper asked for evidence through the isolated Gateway with a real agent and model rather than mocked clocks under Vitest. This run drives the **built `dist` for the reviewed head** (`d76c3b49efd`; this PR's head `9fd039bc3bc` has byte-identical production files — `broker.ts`, `broker.test.ts`, `openclaw.plugin.json`, `package.json` — the only delta is the refreshed base), and a base build that differs **only** in `broker.ts`'s clock read. It runs as a long-running Gateway and reaches the plugin's broker through the shipped `POST /tools/invoke` path — the same production entry the Control UI and channel adapters use:

```
Gateway process (dist build)
  └─ onepassword plugin register()  →  OnePasswordBroker (one instance, in-memory secret cache)
        ├─ before_tool_call policy gate (auto)       ← real
        ├─ OnePasswordBroker.get → cache lookup      ← the changed line
        ├─ OpClient.getItem → resolveTrustedOnePasswordCli
        └─ subprocess exec of a fake `op` CLI         ← real exec; logs every invocation
```

The fake `op` is a POSIX script owned by the invoking user, mode `0700`, with an absolute-node shebang, inside a `0755` directory chain — it passes the **same** `resolveTrustedExecutablePath` trust validation the product runs (an untrusted fixture is rejected with `1Password CLI executable is not trusted`, so the trust check is live, not bypassed). A Gateway token, no channel, no real vault, no real 1Password credential, no outbound endpoint: the fixture host is local.

Sequence, identical on both builds: **read #1** (populates the cache, TTL `cacheTtlSeconds: 1`) → step the host wall clock **back 1 hour** with `date -s` → wait **2 s** so elapsed time passes the 1 s TTL → **read #2**. The discriminator is the number of `op` subprocess invocations.

**HEAD (elapsed clock) — GREEN: the cache expires and the secret is re-fetched**

```text
[gateway] http server listening (2 plugins: memory-core, onepassword; 11.8s)
=== [HEAD] read #1 (populates the secret cache) ===
{"ok":true,"result":{"details":{"ok":true,"slug":"demo","value":"proof-secret-value","itemTitle":"Demo Item","fieldLabel":"credential"}}}
op subprocess invocations after read #1: 1

=== [HEAD] stepping the wall clock backwards 1 hour ===
before: 2026-11-06T04:46:33Z
after:  2026-11-06T03:46:33Z

=== [HEAD] waiting 2s so elapsed time passes the 1s TTL ===

=== [HEAD] read #2 ===
{"ok":true,"result":{"details":{"ok":true,"slug":"demo","value":"proof-secret-value","itemTitle":"Demo Item","fieldLabel":"credential"}}}

=== [HEAD] RESULT: the op subprocess ran 2 time(s) ===
--- op invocation transcript ---
2026-11-06T04:46:33.309Z
2026-11-06T03:46:35.748Z
```

**BASE (production file restored to `Date.now()`) — RED: the backwards step keeps the stale cache alive**

```text
[gateway] http server listening (2 plugins: memory-core, onepassword; 12.6s)
=== [BASE] read #1 (populates the secret cache) ===
{"ok":true,"result":{"details":{"ok":true,"slug":"demo","value":"proof-secret-value","itemTitle":"Demo Item","fieldLabel":"credential"}}}
op subprocess invocations after read #1: 1

=== [BASE] stepping the wall clock backwards 1 hour ===
before: 2026-11-06T04:28:23Z
after:  2026-11-06T03:28:23Z

=== [BASE] waiting 2s so elapsed time passes the 1s TTL ===

=== [BASE] read #2 ===
{"ok":true,"result":{"details":{"ok":true,"slug":"demo","value":"proof-secret-value","itemTitle":"Demo Item","fieldLabel":"credential"}}}

=== [BASE] RESULT: the op subprocess ran 1 time(s) ===
--- op invocation transcript ---
2026-11-06T04:28:22.624Z
```

BASE returns the **cached** secret on read #2 with **one** `op` invocation: after the host clock moved back an hour, `cached.expiresAtMs > Date.now()` is still true, so a rotated credential keeps being served. HEAD returns the same value but **re-fetches it** (two `op` invocations separated by exactly the 2 s wait and the clock step), because `performance.now()` advanced past the 1 s TTL regardless of the step.

Both reads returned `ok: true` and the value is the same, so the observable difference is purely the cache decision the fix changes — the proof does not depend on the secret's content, only on whether `op` is contacted again.

### Model-driven agent-turn proof — full agent loop, real Gateway, real plugin, real `op` subprocess, real wall-clock step

The previous review asked for the same cache discriminator driven by a **real agent turn** rather than `POST /tools/invoke`. That is now done: a real isolated Gateway runs the agent `main`, and each turn goes user-message → model `tool_use` → onepassword tool executes the real `op` subprocess → `tool_result` returned to the model → model reply. The full tool loop is observable over the Gateway WS API (`agent stream=item` events with `name: onepassword`, `phase: start` → `phase: end`, `status: completed`; core `audit_events` rows `tool.action.started`/`tool.action.finished` with `status: succeeded` for `tool_name=onepassword`).

The model is **real**: the local model endpoint (`deepseek-v4-flash` via the local compatibility proxy) actually generates the `tool_use` and the final reply; the agent turn, plugin, policy gate, and `op` subprocess are all real. One transport detail is disclosed: that model endpoint's stream mode returns `stop_reason: end_turn` even for tool calls (verified directly; non-stream returns the correct `tool_use`), which would stop OpenClaw's embedded runner before it executes the tool. A thin protocol bridge on the model port converts the streamed request to a non-stream request and re-emits the model's real response as spec-correct SSE (`stop_reason: tool_use`). The model output is real; only the transport framing is adapted so the real agent loop, real plugin, real policy gate, and real `op` subprocess run end to end.

Sequence, identical on both builds: **turn #1** "read demo" (agent invokes `onepassword`; cache populated, TTL `cacheTtlSeconds: 1`) → step the host wall clock **back 1 hour** with `date -s` → wait **2 s** so elapsed time passes the 1 s TTL → **turn #2** "read demo" again. The discriminator is the number of real `op` subprocess invocations.

**HEAD (elapsed clock) — GREEN: the cache expires and the secret is re-fetched**

```text
=== [HEAD] turn #1 ===  RESULT: op invoked 1 time(s)   (cache miss, fetch)
=== [HEAD] stepping the wall clock backwards 1 hour (17:43:18 → 16:43:18) ===
=== [HEAD] turn #2 ===  RESULT: op invoked 1 time(s)   → op count 1 → 2 (refetch)
op subprocess invocations total: 2
```

**BASE (production file restored to `Date.now()`) — RED: the backwards step keeps the stale cache alive**

```text
=== [BASE] turn #1 ===  RESULT: op invoked 1 time(s)   (cache miss, fetch)
=== [BASE] stepping the wall clock backwards 1 hour (17:49:37 → 16:49:37) ===
=== [BASE] turn #2 ===  op count stayed 1; onepassword plugin audit row: "outcome":"cache-hit"
op subprocess invocations total: 1
```

BASE serves the **cached** secret on turn #2 (`outcome: cache-hit` in the plugin's audit store): after the host clock moved back an hour, `cached.expiresAtMs > Date.now()` is still true, so a rotated credential keeps being served. HEAD re-fetches on turn #2 because `performance.now()` advanced past the 1 s TTL regardless of the step.

### Proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `9fd039bc3bc`; the shipped-Gateway dist proof above ran on `d76c3b49efd`, whose production files are byte-identical (`git diff d76c3b49efd HEAD -- extensions/onepassword/src/broker.ts extensions/onepassword/src/broker.test.ts` is empty; `dist/extensions/onepassword/index.js` contains `cached.expiresAtMs > this.secretNow()`)
- RED baseline: same tree with **only** `extensions/onepassword/src/broker.ts` reverted to `Date.now()` (two lines), rebuilt and run identically
- Production entry: shipped Gateway `gateway run` from `dist`; tool reached via `POST /tools/invoke` → `onepassword` plugin tool → `OnePasswordBroker.get`; model-driven proof reaches the same broker via the real agent turn (model `tool_use` → onepassword tool → `OnePasswordBroker.get`)
- Recorder: fake `op` CLI appends one timestamp line per invocation; the line count is the discriminator
- Acceptance RED: BASE → 1 `op` invocation across the two reads after a −1 h clock step (both via `tools/invoke` and via the agent turn; the agent-turn BASE run records `outcome: cache-hit` in the plugin audit store)
- Acceptance GREEN: HEAD → 2 `op` invocations across the same sequence (repeated on a second HEAD build with the same result, both via `tools/invoke` and via the agent turn)
- Control: both builds return `ok: true` and the same secret value on both reads; the only variable is the cache-expiry decision
- Cleanup: the Gateway is stopped after the run and the host clock is restored immediately after read #2 (`restored:` timestamp in each log); the fixture op binary, token file, and state live under a private `0700` home directory and touch no real vault, channel, or credential

### Impact surface

| File:line | Risk |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/onepassword/src/broker.ts:183-184` | Elapsed clock for the secret cache only |
| `extensions/onepassword/src/broker.ts:537,558` | Cache freshness read and write; grant/pending windows untouched |

### Not tested

- **Model transport is adapted, model output is real.** The model is the local `deepseek-v4-flash` endpoint (real output). Because its stream mode reports `stop_reason: end_turn` for tool calls, a protocol bridge converts the request to non-stream and re-emits the real response as spec-correct SSE. No model output is fabricated; only the stream framing is translated. A maintainer can re-run the identical turns against a hosted model by pointing the provider at it — same recipe as the Shipped-Gateway proof.
- No live 1Password account: the CLI boundary is a local fake `op` binary that passes the product's own trust validation. The proof exercises the cache decision, not the `op` HTTP client.
- Local `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this contributor host (bundled `tsrs` needs GLIBC 2.29+); type checking is left to CI.

### Cleanup

Work happened in a detached worktree off `origin/main`; no user Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched. The proof's Gateway used an isolated state/config dir under a private `0700` home, was stopped after the run, and the host clock was restored immediately after read #2.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Land-ready or alternatives</summary>

Narrow single-owner change in one broker method pair plus its test; land as-is if the elapsed-clock direction is what you want here.

Alternatives rejected: moving grants and pending authorizations to the elapsed clock (persisted windows should follow the wall clock an operator sets); clamping instead of switching clocks (leaves existing entries frozen).

Scope: `extensions/onepassword/src/broker.ts` and its test file.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Preserves explicit terminal-error coverage in the ClawHub plugin-search fixture after integrating main. Main already uses `Retry-After:0` to avoid the historical long wait; this PR uses 61 seconds to select the existing 60-second retry-budget terminal branch and verifies one unavailable request per plugin family.

## User Impact

CI checks the final 503 diagnostic and exit 1 without exercising transient retry backoff. Production behavior is unchanged. Successful plugin discovery, JSON deduplication, skill separation and empty results keep their existing coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The real loopback HTTP fixture retains `Retry-After:61`, records unavailable requests, and asserts exactly two requests with unordered membership for `bundle-plugin` and `code-plugin`. All 10 original assertions and the 30-second deadline remain. Production +0/-0; test +10/-3, net 7 LF with an exact 7 LF own allocation; metadata +2/-0. Shared retry policy, response disposal, test runner and scalar baseline are unchanged.

## Evidence

HEAD `25884b584b384e233dea1336dc5d0007bd26981f`; integrated main `aab88e31bf5a64012a699139e19af193fa9a69c7`. OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/plugins-search-command.clawhub.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

[Immutable current fixture, source/tree binding, exact command/log, gates and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/1e70cc8cfed68710fd2dde70a8b2a182bb90478b). Evidence is outside the product branch.

The source E2E exercises the canonical command handler and real HTTP clients against an owned loopback fixture, with captured runtime output/exit sinks. It covers success/JSON/empty/skills controls plus 503 diagnostic, exit 1 and exact family request counts. Cleanup closes/releases its listener and removes owned temp state.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): normalize hosted JIDs consistently with Baileys
prs.body:
## Problem and solution

WhatsApp address handling disagreed across target normalization, ingress, allowlists, mentions, approvals, sessions, and quote lookup. Hosted and device-qualified JIDs could identify the same sender differently at each boundary.

Use one typed classifier backed by Baileys. Preserve hosted routing and device normalization, and keep PN and LID identities distinct without a verified mapping. Carry observed alternate identities through receive and cached quotes without optional discovery on the receive path. Setup auth inspection stays dependency-light.

Doctor migrates shipped LID allowlist entries only with account-local mappings that agree across every account inheriting the policy. Unresolved entries remain unchanged with a warning. Mapping reads reject contradictory forward/reverse entries. That rejection now survives receive and approval fallbacks: only genuinely missing mappings may use Baileys lookup. Equivalent LID target expansion uses the same resolver.

Rebased onto `f17c94115978d10e0702dd48170464a1f4c84dc0`, preserving main's durable receive admission, send IDs, delivery recovery, socket authority, and runtime-scoped quote cache. No core or Plugin SDK production changes. Net scope: production +949 lines; tests/support +1,201, plus one test-tooling prerequisite registration. The allocation covers 794 lines above the standard test budget for distinct protocol, authorization, migration, setup, receive, quote, and delivery regressions.

## Review findings addressed

- **P1, receive fallback:** preserve an explicit rejected-mapping result. Real Baileys storage reproduces its stale reverse mapping; receive admission and approval resolution both reject it without calling that fallback. Both regressions fail before this repair and pass afterward. The replacement identity remains accepted, and missing-map lookup remains covered.
- **P2, unused identity path:** remove `knownE164`, its branch, and its test. Quote identity stays owned by the existing cache.
- **Timeout test:** remove the forwarding-only case. Remove the duplicate recorder-only case too. The existing late-accepted socket scenario now checks PN-target quote lookup for a LID-routed send after its mapping file is removed.
- **CI fixture ownership:** keep reusable real Baileys test support inside the WhatsApp plugin. The core CLI test uses public Baileys key persistence directly. Bind the typed lookup method without an untyped forwarding callback.
- **Cold Doctor setup:** register this fixture with the existing Control UI prerequisite owner. The admission regression fails before the registration and passes afterward; Doctor starts only after asset preparation completes.
- **Stored-data compatibility:** the built CLI runs Doctor against persisted Baileys mappings and legacy account `allowFrom`/`groupAllowFrom` entries, verifies the saved phone policies, preserves the mapping file, reloads it through Baileys, and passes `config validate`.

## Evidence

- Signed head: `d7a1f1f6931f3a682406bc8d5eaeb5d1c1a81729`.
- 140 focused tests passed across seven affected suites before the duplicate recorder case was removed. After fixture relocation, the boundary and both fixture consumers passed (67 tests). The prerequisite correction passed 371 build-admission, runner-outcome, and CI-shard tests.
- WhatsApp package, extension-test, and tooling-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint/format, plugin import boundary, mock-export guard, whitespace, and exact test budget passed. Independent reviews of the production repair and final fixture correction found no P0–P2 defects.
- Crabbox full `pnpm build` and built-CLI compatibility test: payload exit 0, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43794012236), source `41015db0c2c920554982f6f586680c73e28a73af`. Product code is unchanged afterward. Crabbox repeated `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` and the revised compatibility fixture: exit 0, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43796460906), source `1b83b77c3665178e79fb3813b67a46cec93cbbc7`. Both owned leases were stopped; their lifecycle cancellation during cleanup is separate from the successful payloads.
- The [remote artifact build for the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797629127) passed.
- Final-head CI passes both import boundaries, all typechecks, ratchets, WhatsApp test bundles, and the [built-CLI Doctor lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797629388/job/133070685840). The log shows matching Control UI assets prepared before workers, then the migration test passes in 17.5 seconds.
- No local full build or full test suite was run.

## Remaining CI failure

[CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797629388) has one underlying failure: [core lint stripe 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43797629388/job/133071672686) rejects `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` at `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.ts:118` under `unicorn/prefer-structured-clone`. The file is absent from this PR branch and its pinned base. CI merges the PR into newer main `ef8d709a05a391011ccb1dd1b2c931d0cf7e8095`; that parent and merge `a512ea23ea0ed3e5a36103f639eac50969f38f09` contain the identical file blob `5226ae58848652825503bb9c0558b70b73c7baf0`. The aggregate gate is red because of this inherited main defect.

## Remaining proof

Live WhatsApp receive/reply/approval proof is deferred until an isolated test account is available, as requested. The persisted-data compatibility test does not claim a full upgrade from a published release.

prs.title: fix(secrets): accept limit-sized stdin values with trailing newline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw secrets store set --value-file -` rejects a valid 65,536-byte value when a pipe adds a trailing LF or CRLF.

## User Impact

Users can pipe a value at the documented limit with the usual line ending. Values above the limit still exit 2 without changing the stored value. No configuration or migration is required.

The stored-value limit remains **65,536 UTF-8 bytes**. The bounded stdin reader permits **65,538 raw input bytes** only to allow optional LF/CRLF framing. Raw input above that separate transport bound reports `Stdin input exceeds 65538 bytes.`; input within the read bound still undergoes the 65,536-byte value check after removing one trailing line ending. The larger number in that stream diagnostic is not a larger stored-value allowance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stdin reader counted the optional line ending before removing it. Allow two framing bytes during the bounded read and retain the existing canonical validation of the normalized value. File and dotenv import limits are unchanged.

Related boundary-fix precedent: #188681 (external contributor anmol0b, merged by RomneyDa on November 5). This is a separately reproduced bug in the secrets CLI, not a follow-up change to that PR.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 24.22.2, isolated fresh state, synthetic env-kind value `"é".repeat(32768)` (65,536 UTF-8 bytes). Ran the real `pnpm openclaw secrets store set/get` commands through the normal built CLI, with persistence and SHA-256 readback checks.

| Actual CLI input | Base | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-limit file | exit 0, exact readback | exit 0, exact readback |
| Exact-limit raw stdin | exit 0, exact readback | exit 0, exact readback |
| Exact-limit stdin + LF | exit 2, old value unchanged | exit 0, exact 65,536-byte readback |
| Exact-limit stdin + CRLF | exit 2, old value unchanged | exit 0, exact 65,536-byte readback |
| 65,537-byte normalized value, raw/LF/CRLF | exit 2, old value unchanged | exit 2, old value unchanged |

Minimal reproduction (use an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`):

```sh
node -e 'process.stdout.write("é".repeat(32768) + "\n")' | pnpm openclaw secrets store set FRAMING_VALUE --kind env --value-file -
pnpm openclaw secrets store get FRAMING_VALUE --json
```

Base stderr for the rejected LF/CRLF inputs: `Stdin input exceeds 65536 bytes.` The proof makes 17 real CLI calls, verifies stored bytes rather than just exit status, and checks rejected writes preserve the prior value. No live credentials or external service is involved.

Regression: `pnpm test src/cli/secrets-store-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — base 2 failed / 18 passed (the LF/CRLF cases), fixed 20 passed. The tests drive the CLI parser and real stdin reader/validator; their store is mocked, while the separate CLI proof above uses real persistence.

Focused typecheck passed. Typed lint passed with the repository-supported pinned Bun backend (`No problems in 2 files`, 9.49s); native oxlint crashed internally in `oxc_allocator` on this host, so no native-oxlint pass is claimed. oxfmt/Bun formatter parity and test-line ratchet passed. Final committed-head `pnpm build cliStartup` passed. All 17 real CLI calls completed and the proof reported `failures: []`. Exact-value SHA-256 before/after: `80ad92d4f363d1af78eed07669eecdbb4410e28d38875188de8feeb30b98d6d9`.

Author simplification: reuses the existing value validator; production +2/-1 lines, tests +16 with an exact allocation. No new helper, API, dependency, or configuration. Independent host-agent review of the complete three-file committed diff at `a8b764ae3cb1f3b30c567e45e30bba2e6d10bbc5`, base `4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2`: no actionable findings. This was an independent agent review, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper run.

prs.title: fix(mcp): avoid false missing-command errors for paths containing spaces
prs.body:
Related: #171620

## What Problem This Solves

`mcp doctor` reports working stdio commands as missing when their configured working directory or a PATH directory contains leading or trailing spaces.

## User Impact

Users can diagnose servers installed in literal whitespace-containing directories without a false command-not-found error. No configuration rewrite or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch/configuration path preserves literal paths, but doctor still trimmed cwd and each PATH entry. Doctor now uses the existing nonblank-string reader for cwd and preserves PATH entries, including the existing meaning of an empty entry.

Launcher parity at the reviewed head: [`resolveStdioMcpServerLaunchConfig`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/def42739e70f0f41fb77e56b6a0cf156bea1027f/src/agents/mcp-stdio.ts#L41) retains the original nonblank `cwd`, and [`OpenClawStdioClientTransport`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/def42739e70f0f41fb77e56b6a0cf156bea1027f/src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts#L121) passes that `cwd` and resolved environment to process creation. Doctor now preserves the same literal path bytes.

## Evidence

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A valid trajectory export directory containing a newline, ANSI escape or other terminal control is printed verbatim in the success summary. The report can gain forged lines or clear/hide terminal text even though the bundle was exported correctly.

## User Impact

Human-readable export reports display paths safely. Actual directory names, exported transcript contents and decoded JSON paths retain their original bytes; normal report layout stays readable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing terminalText formatter at the complete CLI summary boundary, as adjacent session CLI owners do. JSON returns before this presentation step, and the slash-command chat response has a different nonterminal renderer. No custom sanitizer or file-path normalization is introduced.

No new configuration/default, protocol, permission, schema, dependency or migration. No generated changelog change.

## Evidence

### Current verification — November 4, 2026

Both human/JSON instances of that regression are now explicitly scoped to POSIX with an explanation, matching the neighboring trajectory inventory coverage. Their assertions remain intact on supported platforms. The other 15 tests remain enabled on Windows. Windows execution was not performed here and is not claimed. The exact allocation is 23 test lines, including the scope comment; no shared scalar was changed. Production is byte-identical to reviewed head1421339200fc.

17/17focused tests pass on Linux Node24.22.1; scoped source tsgo, typed oxlint, formatting, whitespace and all3regression ratchets pass. Measured cost:139.96s (transform 96%, import 3%, worker 1%); 149.46s wrapper. The exact-head sourcePerformance build passes. The unchanged native driver again creates/injects an isolated Gateway session and performs real PTY export, JSON export and independent manifest/events/directory readback. Forged terminal controls disappear only from the human summary; original JSON/disk paths, ordinary output and traversal refusal remain correct. Configuration bytes are unchanged, with no model or external channel call.

Author simplify/test-value audit complete; independent model review was waived. Hosted CI and the next bot review are separate results. No configuration/default, protocol, permissions, migration, dependency or serialization change.

Commands:


prs.title: fix(plugins): state overdue migration once a removal date has passed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a plugin SDK `removeAfter` date has passed, OpenClaw still describes the migration window as future. Operators see "retire on Oct 1… keeps working until then" on Nov 2, and Control UI never switches to an overdue notice because `compatibilityDeprecatedPast` did not exist.

## User Impact

Operators of plugins that still import migration-pending SDK APIs (for example `MsgContext.mediaPath` with `removeAfter: 2026-10-01`) are told the APIs still have time left. Plugin authors are not told migration is overdue. The APIs remain available (removal-pending), so the product must not claim they already retired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #190536 reported future-tense notices after the removal date. This branch:

1. Backend `buildPluginSdkDeprecationNotices`: when `removalDate < today` (UTC date string compare), emit elapsed-date wording that keeps the availability distinction ("migration date passed… APIs remain available; plugin authors should migrate") instead of claiming retirement.
2. Control UI `renderPluginCompatibilityNotices`: same elapsed-date rule; add `compatibilityDeprecatedPast` (en) so the inventory/detail rows switch to the overdue text.
3. Pin clocks in dated-notice Node/DOM/browser tests and exercise the final compatibility day vs the next UTC day so 2027-01-01 does not flip existing fixtures.

## Evidence

### Real CLI: `openclaw plugins inspect --runtime` (UTC today 2026-11-02, plugin `removeAfter` 2026-10-01)

Isolated config/state under `/tmp/pr190752-cli-proof/`. Synthetic plugin `elapsed-sdk-demo` statically imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-media-payload` (compat record `media-legacy-projection`, status `removal-pending`, `removeAfter: "2026-10-01"`). Entry point: source CLI `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts plugins inspect elapsed-sdk-demo --runtime` on Node v26.12.1 (host `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (7139500)`).

**Before (main `sdk-deprecation-notices.ts`, same inspect command):**

```text
Status: loaded
Format: openclaw
Source: /tmp/pr190752-cli-proof/plugins/elapsed-sdk-demo/index.mjs
Origin: config

Compatibility warnings:
elapsed-sdk-demo Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Oct 1, 2026. It keeps working until then; check for a plugin update.
```

**After (this branch head `71395005fe9`, same inspect command):**

```text
UTC host date: 2026-11-02
Status: loaded
Format: openclaw
Source: /tmp/pr190752-cli-proof/plugins/elapsed-sdk-demo/index.mjs
Origin: config

Compatibility warnings:
elapsed-sdk-demo Uses OpenClaw APIs whose migration date passed on Oct 1, 2026. The APIs remain available; plugin authors should migrate. See the migration guide.
```

The Compatibility warnings line is produced by the shipped CLI path `buildCompatibilityNoticesForInspect` → `buildPluginSdkDeprecationNotices` → `formatPluginCompatibilityNotice` after a real runtime plugin load records the deprecated SDK import.

### Control UI before/after (Chromium, page.clock fixed at 2026-11-02T12:00:00Z, removeAfter 2026-10-01)

Inventory DOM **before** (main overview + locale):
> Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Oct 1, 2026. It keeps working until then; check for a plugin update.

Inventory DOM **after** (this branch):
> Uses OpenClaw APIs whose migration date passed on Oct 1, 2026. The APIs remain available; plugin authors should migrate. See the migration guide.

**Before — inventory notice**

![before inventory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1085304b-b8ee-4659-bb4f-71a2c930ead6)

**After — inventory notice**

![after inventory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9d0c968-05f1-4997-83c3-2811ce806a95)

**Before — inventory row**

![before row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f8e0b49-e39c-46a7-ab4a-cdd1b6d86497)

**After — inventory row**

![after row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e839a20-35bc-4972-a244-6a0b5944e6d6)

**Before — detail surface**

![before detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10b5aefb-7cfc-47b6-9e0d-8480a7cb6abd)

**After — detail surface**

![after detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbe2fd7b-1f21-4058-8a0d-bedf128acc7d)

### Local regression suite (green on this head `71395005fe9`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/sdk-deprecation-notices.test.ts` → 5/5
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/pages/plugins/catalog-detail.test.tsx` → 14/14
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` → 0 missing keys
- `src/plugins/status.test.ts` → 11/11

### Review findings addressed on head `71395005fe9`

- CI `check-test-types-core-5`: wrapped `vi.useRealTimers()` in block bodies so `onTestFinished` callbacks return void (tsgo `Awaitable<void>`).
- P2 wording: message no longer claims APIs retired; names plugin authors as migration actors; keeps availability distinction.
- P2 clock pins: backend/DOM/browser dated tests use fixed clocks; boundary day tests cover 2026-12-31 still future vs 2027-01-01 past.
- Prior re-review hold=proof: supplied real `openclaw plugins inspect --runtime` terminal output (above) with an elapsed-date plugin, not a bypassed builder/format-only proof.

## Merge Danger

- Only en gains `compatibilityDeprecatedPast`; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` must stay green (other locales keep dated/undated keys).
- Elapsed detection is UTC date-string compare on `removeAfter`, same rule as Control UI; do not switch to local-time without a product decision.
- Notice text only; plugins continue loading. No schema/config changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): don't let ambient caller authority expand sandbox sessions tools without a captured run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway loopback turn that reaches the sandbox tool catalog with an admitted run that carries no captured operator lease can let the caller's ambient authority silently expand the sandbox allowlist with the `sessions` and `sessions_create` tools. `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` returns `undefined` both when there is no admitted run context and when the admitted run has no captured operator lease, and `prepareSandboxSessionTools` treats `undefined` as "no captured run", which falls back to `hasSessionWriteAuthority()` and reads ambient caller identity. The chat reply path already closes this gap with `snapshot.operatorAuthority ?? null`; the gateway loopback path did not, so the two paths disagreed on whether an ambient `operator.sessions.write` caller can project session tools into the sandbox.

- Problem: gateway loopback sandbox projection expanded `sessions` / `sessions_create` from ambient caller authority instead of the captured run.
- Solution: when an admitted run context is present but carries no operator lease, forward `null` (not `undefined`) so `prepareSandboxSessionTools` keeps the projection pinned to the captured run and ignores ambient authority.
- What changed: `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` (the `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` forwarding is split from the value other consumers see), two focused catalog tests in `src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts` (the ambient case and its authorized-lease control), and a matched effect test in `src/gateway/sandbox-session-authority.effect.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the no-admitted-context path still forwards `undefined` (non-sandbox and owner turns are unaffected); the loopback owner gate and the tool-execution options still receive the captured authority as `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority | undefined`, because neither contract accepts a `null` sentinel. Tool execution-time authority intersection is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change makes the gateway loopback path match the already-shipped chat reply contract (`reply-tool-authority.ts` uses `snapshot.operatorAuthority ?? null`), so a sandbox catalog projection is always pinned to the captured run rather than the ambient caller. `prepareSandboxSessionTools` already distinguishes `undefined` (fall back to ambient) from `null` (explicitly project a run without an operator), so this is the minimal change that restores the intended contract without altering tool-execution semantics.

- Best fix: yes — reuses the exact `?? null` convention the reply path already established; no new API surface.
- Alternative considered: making `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` return `null` unconditionally was rejected because `undefined` is still meaningful for "no admitted context" and other callers rely on it.
- Risk: the `null` sentinel is confined to the one projection argument that documents it; `hasSessionControlAuthority` and `OpenClawToolOptions.sessionControlAuthority` keep the non-nullable `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority | undefined` contract, which is also what the previous commit broke.

## User Impact

Users of sandboxed gateway loopback sessions no longer see `sessions` / `sessions_create` appear in the sandbox tool catalog when the underlying admitted run has no operator lease — even if the ambient caller happens to hold an `operator.sessions.write` grant. Session tool exposure now reflects the captured run's authority consistently between the chat reply and gateway loopback paths, closing an ambient-authority leak that previously widened the sandbox surface.

## Evidence

**Changed caller, shipped path.** The forwarding lives in `resolveGatewayScopedTools`; its loopback caller with an admitted run is the CLI-run MCP projection (`agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` → `prepareCliMcpToolProjection` → `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools`). The trace below drives that production function with a real `prepareAgentRunAdmission` run, the real sandboxed config (`agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "all"`), a real `runWithOperatorToolGatewayAuthority` ambient operator holding `operator.sessions.write`, and a real sessions read for effects. No mocks, no direct `prepareSandboxSessionTools` calls.

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-cli-projection.mts   # base 5573fd0771e (before this commit)
{"label":"lease-free+ambient-operator","lease":false,"ambientOperator":true,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":["sessions_create","sessions"],"sessionToolsPresent":true,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
{"label":"authorized-lease","lease":true,"ambientOperator":false,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":["sessions_create","sessions"],"sessionToolsPresent":true,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-cli-projection.mts   # this head
{"label":"lease-free+ambient-operator","lease":false,"ambientOperator":true,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":[],"sessionToolsPresent":false,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"not in projected catalog"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
{"label":"lease-free+no-ambient","lease":false,"ambientOperator":false,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":[],"sessionToolsPresent":false,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"not in projected catalog"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}

```

Ambient authority widens the catalog on the base commit and no longer does on this head; the authorized lease still projects both tools, so the fence only removes the ambient path. Creation still refuses a lease-free run at the effect (`Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway`) and the sessions store stays empty (`sessionsBefore/After: 0`) on every path.

**Shipped MCP loopback HTTP surface** — real `/mcp` JSON-RPC over TCP, real `mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant` grants, real admitted run contexts, real revocation by closing the run:


prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes running cron and session-event attempts being refused after an unrelated session-maintenance configuration publication, then unnecessarily walking the model fallback chain.

## User Impact

Operators can change cold-storage maintenance, diagnostics, UI preferences, telemetry, and update settings without revoking admitted session events. Real session, permission, tool, channel, model, and authentication changes still recheck authority. No schema, configuration options, migration, or operator action is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The policy projection retained all `session` settings in its global comparison. It now omits `session.maintenance` from both runtime/authored values and resolution facts. The audit also removes unrelated observability and presentation settings. Source and publication rechecks remain intact.

Config and prepared-target refusals now use the existing typed session invalidation error, so the fallback owner treats them as local coordination failures. Queue failure diagnostics reflect that refusal instead of labeling it a model fallback candidate. Started work is not replayed.

## Evidence

The corrected Team observation on `dd2d58be` was a 2026-11-16 02:29:59Z source revision 3 write toggling `session.maintenance.coldStorage.enabled`. Cron-nested run `add9236b` refused after 187 seconds; `f48679a8` ended its webchat dispatch in error after 1,277 seconds. The earlier 02:26:41Z `logging.audit.executionIdentity` publication was unrelated: logging was already excluded, and its positive controls pass on the base. The 20:06:26 r336 delivery-generation refusal (`09f3a70e`) is the separate branch fixed by #199745.

The policy regression and production session-event managed-write regression fail on the original owner and pass with the relevance fix. Relevant policy changes remain refused. The fallback regression fails on the original generic error because it consults provider policy; the typed error stops after one attempt. Production code is small and deliberately retains cheap delegated-authority revalidation.

Validation: 191 focused tests pass, including the production managed-write path and the emitted queue failure metadata. Final independent Codex autoreview is clean. `pnpm check:changed` completed with one inherited full-tree dead-export failure: `resolveRollbackWorkerInputs` in unchanged updater test support. Commit `e4a30936bb35` / #198268 removed its final external consumer; peer #199851 owns the repair. This is a main regression, not a passing gate. The full-tree scan reproduces exactly that single export on exact main parent `a97d3d4f033a258136c963f8c7d1fc55ee6cae92`, with no setup errors. Scale measurements are complete; results below. Synthetic data only; no Team state was copied or mutated. No UI-imported production module changed. Independent local and hosted Codex reviews are clean. ClawSweeper reviewed `45c1954194dc786d31a5366fd15f2559d6db3419` with zero findings and zero open checklist items. Exact-head [CI run 43795582970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43795582970) passed, including the required aggregate gate. Landed through the native pinned merge flow as `e0f5790b9dea6f6f910392b440119c7a076b4e27`; no admin exception or CI retry. No live Gateway/model run was performed; the behavioral proof exercises production managed-write, policy, fallback, and queue boundaries.


<details>
<summary>Synthetic scale, CPU, allocation, and A/A controls</summary>

Task-owned fixture: 5,000 populated/indexed sessions, 37,581,082,624-byte agent DB (35.0001 GiB), and 62,000 files / 1,116,000,000 workspace bytes. No production data. Measurements use the real policy owner; inventory is checked outside timing. APFS host, not btrfs; no filesystem or full-Gateway latency claim.

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-event-auth-reload-measure.ts --state-dir <synthetic-state> --workspace <synthetic-workspace> --scenario maintenance --output <new-result.json>`; baseline adds `--source-dir <saved-base-owner>`, allocation runs add `--allocations`. Repeat with `--scenario logging` for the same-outcome control.

Five interleaved A/B process pairs per scenario/mode, each five rounds of 5,000 checks after three warmups; two identical-baseline A/A controls per mode. Timing and sampled allocation runs are separate. p95 is nearest-rank across five process means, not a request-latency percentile. Acceptance: maintenance retains all after repair, selected auth changes always refuse, and investigate any >20% cost movement.

| Owner measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Maintenance retained / 25,000 checks | 0 | 25,000 |
| Maintenance median wall / p95 (µs/check) | 25.63 / 26.47 | 42.01 / 42.65 |
| Maintenance median thread CPU (µs/check) | 25.49 | 41.78 |
| Maintenance sampled allocation (bytes/check) | 32,979 | 53,511 |
| Logging retained / 25,000 checks | 25,000 | 25,000 |
| Logging median wall / p95 (µs/check) | 38.87 / 111.84 | 39.04 / 115.95 |
| Logging median thread CPU (µs/check) | 38.68 | 38.56 |
| Logging sampled allocation (bytes/check) | 50,338 | 50,340 |

Maintenance now completes the comparison instead of returning early on a false refusal, explaining its extra work. The equivalent successful logging path has +0.43% median wall, -0.31% CPU, and +0.004% allocation. Logging tails were affected by shared-host load (both revisions); no speedup claim. Every process also verifies that selected-provider auth changes refuse all 5,000 consumers.

A/A wall controls: maintenance 25.956 / 25.975 µs; logging 39.548 / 39.633 µs. A/A CPU: 25.783 / 25.763 and 39.262 / 39.241 µs. A/A sampled bytes: 32,957 / 32,901 and 50,067 / 50,298. Full sample ranges are retained in the lane report.

Production net **+23 LOC**: explicit housekeeping exclusions (+12), existing typed refusal propagation (+5), and accurate queue failure metadata (+6). No cache, schema, config option, or second authority owner.

</details>

prs.title: fix(slack): hand transport authority to route-discovery lookups
prs.body:
Fixes #190078

Related: #185972

## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound route discovery keeps issuing authenticated Slack API requests after the transport authority that authorized the send has been invalidated. The Slack `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` implementation (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) drops the `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback that `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:235` forwards into it, so none of its three remote lookups revalidate current authority before touching the network:

- Enterprise owner-heartbeat DM workspace discovery — `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` (`extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts`)
- D-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (`extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`)
- G-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (same owner)

When a Gateway restart or delivery supersession invalidates the worker admission between message acceptance and route discovery, Slack still receives authenticated destination-metadata requests. Remote consequence: a workspace-controlled D/G conversation id or a revoked token keeps being probed after local authority expired; the request cost lands on the operator's credentials.

**Precedent: #185972** — `fix(googlechat): stop metadata lookups after sender authority expires` (merged 2026-10-27). Its body states verbatim:

> "Separate follow-up: audit Slack's analogous route-discovery callback handoff."

This PR is that follow-up. Same shape, same mechanism: forward the **existing** `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback into the route-discovery network owner; zero new validators/options/config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK contract already documents the parameter's purpose (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`):

```ts
/** Revalidates transport authority before new route-discovery network requests. */
assertDirectAdapterHandoff?: () => void;
```

Slack already implements the guard everywhere except the route path:

| Path | State before this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Action path (`action-runtime.ts:276-282`, `312-319`, `actions.ts:229`) | already forwards the callback into `createSlackLookupClient` / write clients |
| Send path (`client-delivery.ts:390`) | already fences delivery via `beforeRequest` |
| Conversation metadata (`channel-type.ts:60-67` → `client-options.ts:176-190`) | `resolveSlackConversationInfo` already accepts the callback and `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts it before every fetch |
| **Route path (`channel.ts` `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`)** | **dropped it — the only remaining gap** |

This change forwards the already-supplied callback at the three route call sites, widens `resolveSlackChannelType`'s parameter type to pass it through, and hands it to `createSlackLookupClient` in `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` (that factory already accepts and fences it). The fence implementation itself is untouched; action and send paths are untouched; no other channel is touched.

Production LOC: +15/−13 (net +2 across three files: `channel.ts` +12/−12 — the two identical conversation-lookup argument objects consolidate into one shared lookup scope, which both forwards the callback and keeps this over-cap file from growing, as the line-cap ratchet requires; `channel-type.ts` +1; `enterprise-user-route.ts` +2/−1). Test LOC: +154/−5 (net +149).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — completes #185972's transport-authority handoff coverage for Slack's analogous route-discovery path.

## User Impact

An accepted message keeps its successful receipt and local history. With **current** authority, route discovery is byte-for-byte unchanged: the same requests go out and the same routes resolve (proven live below). With **invalid** authority, Slack no longer receives new route-discovery metadata requests; the route resolution fails with the authority error instead of silently completing a lookup the operator's admission no longer covers. Callers without handoff context (`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`, `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`, cron delivery targets) pass no callback and behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Heads

- Base (RED): `d45ff6de6c486eb7d68931492e84af4842e02e44` (`docs: point logo work to the brand-kit README (#186198)`, current `main` at pickup)
- Candidate (GREEN): `c9dd1c0a42` (branch `fix/slack-route-discovery-handoff`, rebased onto main `dafda2f722`; production diff identical to the originally reviewed head. Red/green and dist proofs below were recorded at pre-rebase head `45b95e3f9650d22d847d1d81bcd74a1b8f31f35e`; the rebases left the production diff byte-identical. History: `45b95e3f` → rebased to `08e8c0e99c` (baseline bump dropped) → `fe08c2f4c3` (contributor-side rebase onto newer main) → `c9dd1c0a42` adds the `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` assertion alignment, see Maintainer edits.)

### Trigger reachability (producer-chain)

The stale-authority input is produced by production code, not by a test-only seam:

1. **Producer** — `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-transcript.ts:64`: `assertDirectAdapterHandoff: () => stateContext.workerContext.admission.assertCurrent()`. The worker admission assertion is the owner-held liveness check; it fails after Gateway restart or when the delivery is superseded by a newer admission.
2. **Forwarder** — `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:228-236`: the **only** caller that forwards the handoff into `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` (`:235`).
3. **Drop point (base)** — `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts` route implementation discards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` for all three remote lookups.
4. **Fence (already shipped)** — `extensions/slack/src/client-options.ts:176-190` `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts the callback before every fetch once it is attached.

### Red → Green assertions

- **RED (base)**: with a handoff callback that throws, route resolution still completes and the remote lookups still fire — `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` (Enterprise), `conversations.info` (D/G) — and the callback is never invoked. Exactly the 3 new stale tests fail at their `.rejects.toThrow("transport authority expired")` assertion; all other 53 tests pass.
- **GREEN (candidate)**: the same stale callback is invoked before any request and the route rejects with the authority error with **zero** network requests (stub request-log delta `[]`).
- **Legal control (no false positives)**: with a current callback, both base and candidate resolve the same routes (`to: team:T11111111:user:U12345678`, `to: user:U09G2DJ0275`) and the lookups run normally — the fence only rejects genuinely invalid authority.

### Commands × exit

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Head | Exit | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `d45ff6de6` | 1 | 3 failed / 53 passed (56) — fails exactly at the 3 stale-authority assertions | 1m19.6s |
| candidate (pre-rebase `45b95e3f`) | 0 | 56 passed (56) | 1m22.2s |
| candidate (rebased `08e8c0e99c`) | 0 | 55 passed (55) — one low-value passthrough test removed, see Maintainer edits | 3m16.4s |
| candidate (final `c9dd1c0a42`) | 0 | 66 passed (66) — adds `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` (11) to the run; its exact-args expectation was aligned with the forwarded callback | 3m50.2s |

```sh
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/slack/src/channel.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <the same five files>
node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
```

| Check (candidate) | Exit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| oxlint | 0 | 0 warnings / 0 errors (5 files, 259 rules) |
| format `--check` | 0 | all matched files use the correct format |
| line-cap ratchet | 0 | OK — no new violations or over-cap growth (`channel.ts` stays at/below its base counted lines) |
| max-lines ratchet | 0 | OK — 407 grandfathered suppressions unchanged |
| mock-export ratchet | 0 | OK — 6576 grandfathered factories unchanged |
| test-lines ratchet | 0 | OK with no ceiling change (`Test lines OK: 6293949; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 99` at final head vs pinned base `dafda2f722`) |
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit` | 2 | 17 errors, **all in untouched extensions** (codex/line/nostr/onepassword/policy/test-support/vault/visitor-access, TS2883/TS4023/TS4058 portability noise); zero errors in any slack file. The repo's tsgo gate cannot run on this host (tsrs binary needs glibc ≥2.34); classic tsc substituted. |
| `pnpm build` (dist) | 0 | dist built from candidate sources for the shipped-run proof |

### Shipped-run proof (dist artifacts + real HTTP, loopback Slack API stub)

Setup: `pnpm build` dist; loopback stub records every request (`users.info` / `auth.teams.list` / `conversations.info`) and answers Slack Web API shapes; driver invokes the **dist** plugin route contract (`dist/extensions/slack/api.js` → `slackPlugin.messaging.resolveOutboundSessionRoute`) with `SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/`, proxies unset, and a seeded installation-identity state (Enterprise for the heartbeat cases, workspace for the D-channel cases — mirroring what the monitor owner registers after `auth.test`).

In the dist build with `SLACK_API_URL` pointing at the loopback Slack stub, the candidate route-discovery path invokes the forwarded handoff before each request: with current authority the enterprise heartbeat route issues `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` against the stub and resolves `team:T11111111:user:U12345678` (handoff asserted 2×), the D-channel route issues `conversations.info` and resolves `user:U09G2DJ0275` (handoff asserted 1×); with stale authority the handoff throws first and the stub request-log delta is **empty** for both paths.

```text
candidate (dist) driver output, one line per case:
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678","baseSessionKey":"agent:main:main:account:default:team:t11111111"},"handoffCalls":2,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":false,"error":"A request error occurred: transport authority expired (proof fixture)"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":[]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"d-channel-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275","baseSessionKey":"agent:main:main"},"handoffCalls":1,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"d-channel-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":false,"error":"transport authority expired (proof fixture)"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":[]}
```

Base dist comparison (same driver, same stub, same command): with stale authority the lookups still go out and the routes resolve — the shipped defect shape.

```text
base dist driver output (same command, same stub, stale-authority cases resolve and the stub receives the requests):
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"d-channel-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"d-channel-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
```

**Evidence grading (honest):**

- **shipped-run** — everything in this section: dist-built Slack plugin artifacts, real fence, real HTTP to the loopback stub, base-vs-candidate comparison at the dist route boundary.
- **producer-chain** — the *live-Gateway orchestration* of a naturally invalidated admission (Gateway restart / delivery supersession mid-flight) was **not** orchestrated on this host; the stale-authority input's production origin and invalidation owner are the file:line chain above, and its fence behavior is proven at the dist boundary. The dist driver seeds the installation-identity state directly (the monitor owner's `auth.test` registration path is not exercised).

### Test-lines ratchet

No ceiling change. The pre-rebase head bumped `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` 6286403 → 6286591, which conflicted with `main`. The first rebase dropped the bump, but CI pins an immutable comparison commit (`ci-ratchet-base`, here main `874dc86b` at push time) whose ceiling 6293290 sat 475 below its own test total, so this PR's net +149 failed the gate there (`over by: 624`). Re-rebasing onto current main `dafda2f722` — whose ceiling was since raised to 6294048 — absorbs the +149 cleanly. Measured at the final head with the ratchet's own working-tree method against the pinned base: `Test lines OK: 6293949; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 99`. If a future rebase re-trips this gate, the fix is to raise the ceiling by exactly the PR's net add with this note as justification.

### Scope and risk

| File:line (candidate) | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts:369-374` (Enterprise heartbeat lookup call) | forwards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` into `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` | With current authority, no behavior change (same requests, same routes). With invalid authority, route resolution now fails instead of issuing `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` discovery. |

prs.title: fix(cli): reject nonregular model image inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `infer model run --file` can wait indefinitely when an image path names a FIFO without a writer. The shared image loader calls `readFile` before checking image type, so neither local nor Gateway probes reach dispatch or report an unsupported input.

## User Impact

User impact: nonregular image inputs fail promptly with the affected path and a recovery instruction. Regular images and image symlinks continue to reach the model with the original input path and exact image bytes. No new per-file or aggregate byte limit is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing core `readRegularFile` owner, resolving the input first to retain supported symlink paths. That owner rejects nonregular files before opening and validates the opened descriptor with nonblocking flags. The import stays lazy inside the image-only branch. Existing MIME detection, HEIC conversion, input metadata and local/Gateway dispatch remain with their current owners.

## Evidence

### Current-head integration and actual behavior — 2026-11-14 UTC

**Product head:** `50c1828fe4df64fb0f9e5e092bdd3c237f231075`. Integrated main: `08ae8c62b83ede02db3a8d2bc3ce36206008d253` through an ordinary two-parent merge; contributor history is retained, with no force-push.

Resolved the real model-run conflict against main while preserving the complete new nested runner, cancellation flow, MIME/conversion behavior and original descriptor-aware file admission.

- **Production entry / canonical owner:** Built `openclaw.mjs infer model run --local --model image-proof/image-proof --prompt "Describe this image" --file INPUT --json` -> shared image admission -> canonical regular-file reader -> actual completion adapter.
- **Exact frozen collector:** `node proof-model-files.mjs CHECKOUT green`. Normal build: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`; clean tracked tree and matching build stamp verified before and after the actual run.
- **Recorder / readback / legal controls:** Regular PNG and its symlink each dispatch one actual HTTP/SSE completion request with the original image bytes and return the recorder reply. A FIFO without a writer exits1 without opening the FIFO and without dispatch; an ordinary text file exits1 with the existing unsupported-image diagnostic and no dispatch. Full native syscall traces, CLI stdout/stderr and HTTP request payloads are linked below.
- **Acceptance RED:** retained original baseline and collector observations in the historical section below. This integration receipt claims exact-head GREEN and controls; it does not relabel earlier BASE runs as a new main execution.
- **Inspectable evidence:** [collector, complete sanitized streams, exact-head receipt, hashes and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/f54f88d71d6f05ab7c462f8e7206a806aaff4458). All uploaded bytes were read back and SHA256-verified. Proof artifacts are kept in an evidence-only orphan commit, outside this product branch.
- **Supporting checks:** 122 focused owner tests pass. Changed-file format, type-aware lint and semantic types pass; clean normal `cliStartup` build passes. Fresh independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings, using the user-authorized GPT6.1Sol fallback; no official autoreview-tool execution is claimed.
- **Cleanup / impact:** task-only HOME/config/state and synthetic fixtures; recorder and owned child processes stopped. No production model/account/channel/Gateway state was used or changed. No added options/defaults, dependencies, config/protocol/schema, permissions, persisted format or migration changes.
- **Limitations:** Linux FIFO/symlink admission and local production completion adapter only. No native Windows/macOS, live Gateway dispatch, external provider or whole-repository suite is claimed. Hosted required CI and the durable public review are tracked separately; local checks do not establish either.

```javascript
try {
```

An isolated configuration used a synthetic image-capable model and a loopback HTTP/SSE provider recorder. No production configuration or external model credentials were used. The recorder returned `image proof reply`; real CLI JSON output reported that final text. Four inputs were exercised: a valid 1×1 PNG, a symlink to that PNG, a real FIFO made with `mkfifo`, and an ordinary non-image text file. Local `strace -f -tt -e trace=openat` observed the actual CLI process.

| Scenario | Base | Head |

| Regular PNG | exit 0; one HTTP image request and final reply | exit 0; one HTTP image request and final reply |

| Ordinary text file | exit 1; unsupported-image diagnostic; zero provider requests | exit 1; same unsupported-image diagnostic; zero provider requests |

```text

```

```text

```

The registered CLI regressions exercise both local and Gateway pre-dispatch rejection, valid PNG/symlink payloads, existing ChatGPT instructions, HEIF normalization and text rejection. The FIFO fixture retries writer admission so a regression fails without leaving a blocking reader hung. Formatting, targeted type-aware lint/type checking, normal build and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: two files; production +9/-1, tests +82/-39 (existing content table extended and reformatted). Existing-solutions preflight selected the canonical descriptor-aware reader. The earlier broader [#110767](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110767) was closed by its author; this repair leaves image budgets and concurrency unchanged. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the bulk-save receipt browser check failing after the Secrets confirmation text changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

#199464 updated the canonical receipt and other tests but missed this confirmed-receipts spec. The original case fails identically on CI merge `1eb95dd6a050a3ae595d8f36caba6151035f0196` and its exact main parent `9e85a1a71795dd067c424923c4e187ab332852dd`. The copy regression was introduced by `b858e90c8fede29f00a279a7da6062b840802500` (#199464).

prs.title: feat: add WhatsApp phone-code login
prs.body:
Closes #85867

## Problem and behavior

Users who cannot scan a QR code need a way to link WhatsApp from the CLI. `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` now offers **Scan QR code** (the default) or **Link with phone number**. Phone linking accepts an international number and displays the code to enter in WhatsApp’s Linked Devices screen.

The WhatsApp plugin owns this flow, including number validation, socket readiness, pairing restarts, and cleanup of incomplete managed credentials. Completed credentials are preserved across the native post-pairing restart.

## Review repairs

Phone-code sockets use Baileys’ maintained `Browsers.macOS("Chrome")` profile for both the initial socket and replacements. This follows [VishalJ99’s physical iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101294#issuecomment-5837741000): the custom profile failed, and the maintained profile linked successfully. QR, startup, and ordinary reconnect sockets retain their existing profile. Phone-code linking uses the Mac OS/Chrome companion identity.

Ordinary sockets log credential-save failures and remain connected. Guarded or persistence-observed sockets abort on failure, so interactive login cannot report success before its credentials and keys are saved. Setup authority checks remain active before guarded writes.

The login tests are split into general login, phone-code login, and recovery suites with shared fixtures. Existing cases are preserved; regressions cover the initial/replacement profile and ordinary, guarded, error-observed, and task-observed save failures.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `f17c94115978d10e0702dd48170464a1f4c84dc0`. All 19 original commits remain separate, with their author identities, author dates, and complete messages preserved. Head: `6d36f73327c9eabe62a6f46a2540161b9cf12906`.

- Full `pnpm build` passed remotely in 3m45.5s on Node 24.22.1. This ran on `cfd75523dc575453ce4b43a7d9d69192a5b87548`; the final head changes only one test fixture and its test-line allocation. Production files are identical.
- On the final head, all 205 tests in 31 WhatsApp files passed, including phone-code login, QR recovery, credential persistence, socket restarts, auth-path guards, and bounded last-route settlement. All 20 channel catalog contract tests passed. Runner wall time: 60.24s for WhatsApp and 59.68s for the catalog contract, including setup. PR CI seconds remain pending.
- The WhatsApp package typecheck passed after `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts`. Focused typed lint passed with no warnings or errors.
- Formatting, whitespace, and the test-line budget check passed. The allocation records 1,598 lines above the 400-line allowance for pairing, persistence, restart, cleanup, and preserved session/controller coverage.
- An independent read-only conflict review inspected the original and rebased ranges plus the integration changes. Its two P2 findings—unused imports and a missing synchronous socket-close test case—were repaired and covered by the final checks. The final comparison also preserved the PR's catalog label and regenerated lockfile.

Remote proof: [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771912090), lease `tbx_01m7gpqfh7e8ypbzsrm2ktz0ta`, with 4 CPUs and about 15 GiB RAM. The Crabbox wrapper verified the selected source and completed the final checks with exit code 0.

Exact-head live validation remains outstanding for phone pairing and its native restart, QR login, existing linked-session startup, and existing-account upgrade behavior. The reported physical iPhone success applies to an earlier candidate with the selected browser profile. PR CI results for this head are not yet verified.

prs.title: fix(infer): sanitize terminal controls in human output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared inference human-output formatters can emit terminal controls from legal input or provider/result values. For example, `infer embedding create` sends text containing screen-clear/cursor/title sequences unchanged to its configured provider, then prints those sequences as raw terminal bytes.

## User Impact

Shared human envelopes and provider summaries use the existing terminal text policy. Metadata, errors, paths and scalar displays stay on owned lines; output text retains real newlines and Unicode, and tabs display as literal `\t`. Structured `--json` output and provider input preserve their original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply existing `terminalText`/`sanitizeTerminalText` at the complete shared display owner. Reuse the existing transcripts per-LF pattern for multiline text. Human serialized values also need this boundary because JSON.stringify leaves C1/bidi controls. Seven inference families share the owner; no per-field renderer, new escape algorithm, public option or caller policy is added.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Shared human envelope and provider-summary displays remove terminal controls while preserving owned line layout and ordinary Unicode; Multiline output keeps LF, tabs display literally, and provider input plus structured JSON retain their original values.
- Entry: node openclaw.mjs infer embedding create --agent main --model openai/text-embedding-3-small --text <fixture-value> [--json]; disputed owner ran unmocked: src/cli/capability-cli/output.ts formatEnvelopeForText and providerSummaryText human projections; emitJsonOrText runs the existing shared owner unmocked from the shipped OpenAI-compatible embedding route.

- Readback (subprocess,http,config-file,network-recorder): Actual CLI raw stdout/stderr/status and stdoutHex, native POST request model/input/count, config before/after hashes and peer-thread-port cleanup receipts.
