prs.title: fix(ui): color theme-catalog failure alerts with the danger contract
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Appearance theme-catalog failures render with the orphan modifier `settings-status--error`. Shared settings styles only define `--danger` (and the other tone modifiers); there is no `--error` rule. The alert text therefore falls back to muted gray while only a separately styled dot may carry color, so a failed theme catalog is visually indistinguishable from neutral/muted status copy.

## User Impact

When theme discovery fails on Settings → Appearance, the operator sees a gray “Theme catalog unavailable” message with a Retry control instead of a red danger alert. The failure does not read as an error, and it does not match other failure alerts in Control UI.

## Why

`ui/src/styles/settings.css` owns the settings-status tone contract. Per review design decision, danger text is limited to failure alerts: `.settings-status--danger[role="alert"] { color: var(--danger); }` so only `role="alert"` copy carries red text; routine danger statuses keep the muted label and the red dot (`.settings-status--danger .settings-status__dot` unchanged). Markup moves the theme-catalog failure from the non-existent `--error` class to the canonical `--danger` modifier and keeps `role="alert"`. The existing appearance-catalogs recovery test follows the class rename. No new tone, no parallel CSS path.

## Evidence

- **Still broken on `openclaw/main`:** `view-appearance.tsx` still has `class="settings-status settings-status--error"` and `settings.css` has no `.settings-status--error` rule.
- **Red on base:** with only the markup rename (no CSS text color), alert text computed color stays muted gray; **green with the fix:** alert text uses `var(--danger)` → `rgb(248, 113, 113)` on the running Control UI while routine danger rows keep the muted label.
- **Running Control UI (mock Gateway, `themes.list` → `__mockError` "Theme catalog unavailable"):** e2e navigates to `/settings/appearance`, finds `.settings-status[role="alert"]`, asserts visible alert copy + computed `color: rgb(248, 113, 113)` + class `settings-status settings-status--danger`. Captured via `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`:

| Alert element (red `role=alert`) | Full Appearance page |
| --- | --- |
| ![running alert](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/settings-status-danger/settings-status-danger/running-alert-after.png) | ![running page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/settings-status-danger/settings-status-danger/running-page-after.png) |

- **Static CSS contract (supporting sample page):**

| Before (`--error`, gray alert text) | After (`--danger`, red alert text) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/settings-status-danger/settings-status-danger-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/settings-status-danger/settings-status-danger-after.png) |

![combined](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/settings-status-danger/settings-status-danger-combined.png)

- **Tests green:** `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.appearance-catalogs.test.ts` (4) — recovery path still finds `.settings-status--danger button`. Source-matching node suite from an earlier revision was removed per review (test-lines ceiling; computed-color proof is the running Control UI assertion above).
- **test-lines ratchet:** `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 01a5e160dab --staged` → `Test lines OK: 6515013; ceiling: 6515041; slack: 28`.
- **Duplicate search:** open PR search for `settings-status--error` / `settings-status--danger` (0 hits); code search on main still shows only the orphan `--error` sites in `view-appearance.tsx` + catalogs test.

## Merge Danger

Three files: one class rename in TSX, one selector rename in an existing catalogs test, one CSS rule addition scoped to `[role="alert"]` (`color` only). No gateway, config, schema, or protocol changes. Existing CSS keeps the danger dot rule; routine danger statuses are intentionally not globally red-tinted. Visual change is intentional danger treatment for a real failure state only.

prs.title: fix(ui): align orphan button classes with the shared btn contract
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`btn--small` and `btn--primary` appear on twelve and three Control UI buttons respectively, but neither class exists in the shared stylesheets. The real contracts are `btn--sm` (padding/font compact) and the space-separated `.btn.primary` accent. Every orphan call site therefore renders as a full-size neutral button: board widget retries, MCP stale Remove/Retry, device-pair Retry, logbook actions, and canvas/browser widget controls never pick up the compact metrics or the primary accent.

## User Impact

On a dashboard with a failed widget, Retry/Remove sit at the default 8×14 / 13px size instead of the compact 6×10 / 12px used by every other `btn--sm` control, and the primary action has no accent fill—so the intended “do this next” affordance is missing exactly where recovery is offered. Device-pair setup’s failed-state Retry looks like a secondary button.

## Why

`ui/src/styles/components.css` owns the contract: `.btn--sm` sets compact padding/type, `.btn.primary` sets the accent background/ink. The rest of the UI already uses those names (`btn--sm` ×344, `btn primary` ×81). Renaming the orphan markup to the existing contract is a pure addition of correct selectors at the call sites; no new CSS, no `usage.css`-style parallel rule, and no behavior change beyond the intended visual treatment.

## Evidence

- **Running Control UI before/after (application entry point):** temporary e2e on the running Control UI (mock Gateway dashboard + settings/devices). Board widget initialization failure shows `BoardWidgetError` Retry; pairing lazy chunk fails into `PairingDialogFallback` failed Retry. Base `01a5e160dab` vs fix `1d7964b54b8`:

| Control | Before (orphan) | After (contract) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Board widget Retry | `btn btn--small` · padding `8px 14px` · font `13px` · neutral fill | `btn btn--sm` · padding `6px 10px` · font `12px` |
| Device-pair fallback Retry | `btn btn--primary` · neutral fill `color(srgb 0.957…)` | `btn primary` · accent fill `rgb(189, 69, 49)` |

| Before (running UI) | After (running UI) |
| --- | --- |
| ![board running before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/board-widget-error-before.png) | ![board running after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/board-widget-error-after.png) |
| ![pair running before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/device-pair-fallback-before.png) | ![pair running after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/device-pair-fallback-after.png) |

Full-page running UI frames:

| Dashboard before | Dashboard after |
| --- | --- |
| ![dash before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/dashboard-before.png) | ![dash after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/dashboard-after.png) |

| Pair page before | Pair page after |
| --- | --- |
| ![pair page before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/pair-page-before.png) | ![pair page after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-running/pair-page-after.png) |

- **Real Control UI components, before/after (inspected):** temporary browser harness mounts the real `BoardWidgetError` and real `PairingDialogFallback` (device-pair failed-state Retry) with production `base.css` + `components.css` + `board.css` + `device-pair-setup.css`. Base (`01a5e160dab` / pre-fix markup) vs fix branch:

| Component | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BoardWidgetError` Retry (`btn btn--small` → `btn btn--sm`) | full-size neutral control, element height 143px | compact control, element height 138px |
| `PairingDialogFallback` Retry (`btn btn--primary` → `btn primary`) | neutral fill `rgb(25, 28, 36)` | accent fill `rgb(209, 60, 60)` |

| Before (orphan classes) | After (contract classes) |
| --- | --- |
| ![board before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/board-widget-error-before.png) | ![board after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/board-widget-error-after.png) |
| ![pair before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/device-pair-fallback-before.png) | ![pair after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/device-pair-fallback-after.png) |

![combined real-component before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-real-combined.png)

- **Static CSS contract (supporting):** base page with old classes computes `padding: 8px 14px; font-size: 13px` and neutral primary background (0 reddish pixels); fix classes compute `padding: 6px 10px; font-size: 12px` and `background: rgb(209, 60, 60)` (17,607 reddish pixels).

| Before (static samples) | After (static samples) |
| --- | --- |
| ![static before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-before.png) | ![static after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/btn-contract/btn-contract-after.png) |

- **Regression suites (green):** `ui/src/components/board/` 9 files / 86 tests; `logbook-view*.test.tsx` 2 files / 13 tests; `app-host-pairing-access.test.ts` 19 tests.
- **Static:** `oxfmt --check` clean on all nine files; `oxlint` shows only the pre-existing `solid(reactivity)` warning at `browser.tsx:132` (identical on unmodified main); test-lines ratchet OK (delta 0 — markup only); repo grep has no remaining `btn--small` / `btn--primary` outside `bp-btn--*`.

## Merge Danger

Nine TSX files, string-only class renames (+13/−13). No CSS, schema, config, protocol, or gateway changes. No tests assert on the old class names (grep over `*test*` is empty). Open PR #183395 also touches `canvas-widget-view.tsx` and is already `CONFLICTING` with main; the two renames there are independent of its feature work. Duplicate search before opening (`btn--small`, `btn--primary`, `file:` on the nine paths, all states) found no competing open PR that renames these classes. `btn--subtle` / `btn--secondary` are likewise CSS-less but have no correct replacement name in the stylesheet—left out of this change on purpose.

prs.title: fix(ui): give shared warning callouts the amber treatment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`class="callout warning"` is emitted across Control UI pages that never load `usage.css` — cloud workers, model setup, updates, and the sign-in wizards — but the only `.callout.warning` rule lives in `ui/src/styles/usage.css`, which those routes never import. On every one of those pages the warning renders as a plain neutral panel: no amber background, no warning ink (#128251).

## User Impact

A user on the Cloud workers or Updates page sees a "you need admin access" or failed-save warning that looks identical to an informational note. The warning semantics are lost exactly where failures and permission problems are reported.

## Why

The shared stylesheet already owns the amber treatment: `.callout.danger, .callout.warn` share a gradient built on `--callout-tone`, and `.callout.warn` sets the tone to `var(--warn)`. `usage.css` carries a second, page-local `.callout.warning` rule that only the usage and model-providers routes load. Adding `.callout.warning` to the two shared selector lists gives every page the same amber treatment as a pure addition; `usage.css` is untouched, so its routes keep their existing visuals — the deletion that killed #128253 stays off the table.

## Evidence

- Red on base (`01a5e160dab`): `ui/src/styles/callout-warning.node.test.ts` fails with `gradient rule: expected [ '.callout.danger', '.callout.warn' ] to include '.callout.warning'`.
- Green with the fix: the new test passes; full `ui/src/styles/` suite is 19 files / 81 tests green.
- Live comparison on the mock Control UI (`settings/updates`, non-admin scope): before = `background: none`, `color: rgb(53, 53, 53)` (neutral panel); after = `background: linear-gradient(135deg, ...)`, `color: color(srgb 0.492 0.228 0.068)` (shared amber treatment). Before/after screenshots inspected:

| Before (base) | After (fix) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/ui-callout-warning-images/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/ui-callout-warning-images/after.png) |
- Static checks: `tsgo:ui` clean; test shard `tsconfig.core.test.ui-other.json` clean; `oxlint ui/src/styles/` 0 errors/warnings; `oxfmt --check` clean; max-lines ratchet OK; test-lines ratchet OK via `config/test-lines-allocations/callout-warning-shared.txt` (+41, slack 28).

## Merge Danger

Three files: one shared stylesheet (two selector lists, +4/−2), one new node regression test, and one test-lines allocation (`callout-warning-shared.txt`, +41). No schema, config, protocol, or gateway changes. `usage.css` is deliberately untouched — removing its local rule would restyle the usage/model-providers notices (#128253 closed for that reason). Routes that import `usage.css` load it after the shared sheet at the same specificity, so their local override still wins and their visuals are unchanged. Duplicate search before opening (`file:components.css`, `callout in:body`, `128251 in:body`, all states) found no competing open PR; historical #128253 and #128270 are closed.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): converge NFD titles to the canonical page and preserve released identities
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

An accented memory-wiki title typed in a different Unicode normalization form than the existing page created a **second** page file, so `[[Café]]` in NFC and NFD resolved to different pages. NFC-normalizing the shared `slugifyWikiSegment` helper fixed new vaults but renamed **released** pages on upgrade, orphaning their frontmatter `id` and hand-written Notes. This revision keeps released identity bytes stable and reuses a released page by canonical equivalence: exact NFC/NFD stem, NFC-equivalent stem, or — for hash-truncated long titles — the stored frontmatter `title` as a canonical slug.

## Findings addressed

- Title-fallback reuse is limited to pages the **same producer** wrote (`pageType` / `sourceType`), so an `unsafe-local` import keeps its id, `sourceType`, and `sourcePath` when a look-alike direct ingest arrives. A page at the exact target stem is still reused — it is this writer's own.
- The fallback compares canonical slugs, not raw titles, so a long mixed-form title whose stem is hash-truncated still matches a case or normalization variant.
- The new page `id` is the title's slug; the `-<12hex>` suffix `slugifyWikiPageStem` adds for reserved stems stays a filename concern (`source.index`, not `source.index-e540cdd1328b`).

Not changed: `slugifyWikiSegment` / `slugifyWikiPageStem` output, frontmatter schema and the `id` shape, link parsing. No migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

NFC-normalizing the shared `slugifyWikiSegment` helper was the wrong owner for this fix: it repaired new vaults by rewriting the identity of pages a released version had already written, orphaning their frontmatter `id` and any hand-written Notes. Released identity bytes are the durable contract here, so this revision leaves them alone and instead makes reuse canonical-equivalence aware — exact NFC/NFD stem, NFC-equivalent stem, or, for a hash-truncated long title, the stored frontmatter `title` compared as a canonical slug.

Reuse also has to stay inside one producer. A look-alike title arriving through direct ingest must not adopt a page an `unsafe-local` import wrote, so the title fallback is limited to pages with the same `pageType` / `sourceType`; a page already sitting at the exact target stem is still reused because it is this writer's own. Comparing canonical slugs rather than raw titles is what lets a long mixed-form title match its case or normalization variant even when the stem was hash-truncated. The `-<12hex>` suffix that `slugifyWikiPageStem` adds for reserved stems stays a filename concern, so a page titled `Index` keeps the id `source.index`.

## User Impact

`[[Café]]` typed in either Unicode normalization form now resolves to the same page instead of creating a second file, and a long mixed-form title re-ingested with different casing or normalization reuses its released page rather than duplicating it. Upgrading from a released version keeps every existing page filename, frontmatter `id`, and hand-written Note: no migration, no removed files, and `openclaw wiki lint` stays at `issueCount=0`. An `unsafe-local` import keeps its own id, `sourceType`, and `sourcePath` when a look-alike direct ingest arrives. Slug output, the frontmatter schema, the `id` shape, and link parsing are unchanged, so nothing else about an existing vault moves.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI — new vault (built bundle, isolated state dir)

```console
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title $'cafe\u0301'      # NFD
  -> sources/café.md  id=source.café  created=True
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title $'caf\u00e9'       # NFC, same visual title
  -> sources/café.md  id=source.café  created=False
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title Index
  -> sources/index-e540cdd1328b.md  id=source.index
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title <long mixed-form>     -> …-9197c5785ca8.md  created=True
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title <same, UPPER + NFC>   -> …-9197c5785ca8.md  created=False
```

### Live Gateway + real model (this branch's dist)

```console
# released vault written by openclaw 2026.11.3
  synthesis page: syntheses/cafe<U+0301>.md  id: synthesis.cafe<U+0301>  sha256 8444fbfc…  487 B
  syntheses/: cafe<U+0301>.md, index.md

# isolated Gateway from this branch's dist, model glm-5.2, one agent turn
$ openclaw agent --session-id gw-proof-nfc2 -m 'call wiki_apply create_synthesis, title "café" (NFC)'
  run ok   tools: [wiki_apply, dispatch_action]   calls: 2   failures: 0
  tool result: "Updated syntheses/café.md via create_synthesis. Refreshed 3 index files."
  syntheses/: cafe<U+0301>.md, index.md   id: synthesis.cafe<U+0301>   sha256 f73e904d…  479 B
```

### Shipped CLI — synthesis, lint, cross-form backlinks

```console
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis Menu --source-id source.café --body-file body.md
  # body.md had [café](../sources/cafe<U+0301>.md) and [[cafe<U+0301>]] in decomposed form
  -> syntheses/menu.md  id=synthesis.menu
  menu Related -> Sources: ../sources/café.md
  café Related -> Referenced By: ../syntheses/menu.md
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis Index --source-id source.café
  -> syntheses/index-e540cdd1328b.md  id=synthesis.index
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis $'cafe\u0301' --source-id source.café
  -> syntheses/café.md  id=synthesis.café        # reuses the NFC synthesis page
$ openclaw wiki lint                               -> issueCount=0
```

### Upgrade from released 2026.11.3 (same state dir, same database)

```console
# vault + state written by openclaw 2026.11.3 (npm stable, unfixed); 21 files
  page: sources/cafe<U+0301>.md   id: source.cafe<U+0301>   synthesis: syntheses/menu.md
  hand-written Notes: "UPGRADE NOTE MUST SURVIVE"
# head CLI on that state dir, documented update path first
$ openclaw doctor --fix
  Doctor: database migrations ... pre-migration SQLite backup kept
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title $'caf\u00e9'
  -> created=False  pagePath=sources/cafe<U+0301>.md  id=source.cafe<U+0301>
  same released page: True   same id: True   Notes preserved: True
  sources/: [sources/cafe<U+0301>.md, sources/index.md]   files removed: []   lint issueCount: 0
```

### Regression runs

```console
# this PR's tests on origin/main (base): 5 failed | 10 passed (15)
  × NFD convergence   × released decomposed reuse   × released mixed-form reuse
  × released hash-truncated NFD reuse   × long mixed-form uppercase reuse
# this PR's tests at the previous head f44f987: 4 failed | 14 passed (18)
  × long mixed-form uppercase reuse   × imported page kept out of ingest reuse
  × synthesis/source id for a title "Index": 'source.index-e540cdd1328b' != 'source.index'
# this commit: 8 test files, 109 tests passed
```

### Before / after

| Scenario (real behavior) | previous head `f44f987` | this commit `c539ab5` |
|---|---|---|
| Released decomposed page re-ingested in NFC | reused (`created: false`) | reused (`created: false`) |
| Released long mixed-form page (`…-9197c5785ca8`) re-ingested as UPPER + NFC | **duplicate page** (`created: true`) | reused (`created: false`) |
| Direct ingest of a title an `unsafe-local` import already owns | **import adopted**: id, `sourceType`, `sourcePath` rewritten | separate page; the import keeps its id and provenance |
| File titled `Index` -> page id | `source.index-e540cdd1328b` (CI red) | `source.index` |
| Released slug bytes and frontmatter `id` shape | unchanged | unchanged |

Checks: `oxlint` 0/0 on the five changed files; `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean; `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json` reports nothing in `extensions/memory-wiki` (tsgo cannot run in this symlinked worktree; CI's shard is the authority).

## Not tested

The vault has no UI surface (`openclaw.plugin.json` declares only an id and the plugin registers no Control UI view), so there is no screenshot evidence to capture. macOS/iOS paste normalization is Unicode semantics, not reproduced here: this host is Linux/KVM with no macOS environment.

prs.title: fix(gateway): match canonical Unicode in human mentions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The human mention directory misses a person's display name when the query and stored name use different canonical Unicode forms. For example, `CAFE\u0301` does not find `Café Person`, although a literal `CAFÉ` query does. This affects the `users.mentionable` results used by the chat composer and person-reference lookup.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createHumanMentionPolicy().search` owns the eligible directory and its text matching. Normalize its existing lowercase query, display-name projection, and verified-login projection to NFC. Keep the eligibility/visibility checks, cached directory, stored profile, returned label, profile ID, and response shape unchanged. Built-in normalization is sufficient; no new dependency, option, storage format, or parallel search path is needed.

## User Impact

People can find the same eligible person with canonically equivalent text from different keyboards or pasted sources. Original names remain intact. Accents remain significant; this adds neither fuzzy matching nor accent removal. It does not grant access to additional users or sessions.

## Evidence

Base: `b6d8eb287e0898d2c50d89abaef749e4c25ca66a`. Tested source and native build: `3dc06a37a08a00eac8eaca47cb3f85ef9139fd54` (`2026.11.1`). The owner is also unchanged on the subsequently inspected main `5f84a8166dc524a4eab375b16030239acbefc92b`.

### Real Gateway RED → GREEN

The same frozen driver started the actual built Gateway on an isolated loopback port with a private state directory and two synthetic trusted-proxy identities. It connected through the production WebSocket protocol, set the second user's name with `users.setDisplayName`, queried `users.mentionable` as the first user, and independently read back the stored name with `users.self` as the second user. No policy method, database, search result, or WebSocket response was mocked.

| Stored display name | Actual query | Base result | Head result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Café Person` (NFC) | `CAFE\u0301` | `users: []` | Original profile ID and NFC name |
| `Cafe\u0301 Person` (NFD) | `CAFÉ` | `users: []` | Same profile ID and original NFD name |

`\u0301` denotes the actual combining character in the request. Each literal-name control succeeds on both revisions. Unrelated text and the requesting user do not appear. The head's independent `users.self` read retains the original name in both forms.

Actual head readback, Linux / Node 24.22.1 / November 9, 2026:

```text
users.setDisplayName {displayName:"Café Person"} -> ok
users.mentionable {agentId:"main",visibility:"shared",query:"CAFE\u0301"}
  -> users:[{profileId:"c2027e24-3282-4fd0-afa3-cdfb760c8148",
             displayName:"Café Person",avatarUrl:<existing avatar URL>,online:true}]
users.self -> id:"c2027e24-3282-4fd0-afa3-cdfb760c8148", displayName:"Café Person"
users.setDisplayName {displayName:"Cafe\u0301 Person"} -> ok
users.mentionable {agentId:"main",visibility:"shared",query:"CAFÉ"}
  -> same profileId, displayName:"Cafe\u0301 Person"
users.self -> same id, displayName:"Cafe\u0301 Person"
canonical queries: base 0/2; head 2/2; literal and exclusion controls passed
```

To reproduce, use two permitted identities on a local Gateway; set one display name to NFC `Café Person`; have the other send the first `users.mentionable` request above. Repeat after setting the NFD form. Compare the returned ID with the target's `users.self` response and verify that response's display-name bytes. The proof's trusted-proxy fixture is confined to loopback; it is not a deployment or auth-configuration recommendation.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation, cost, and limitations</summary>

Frozen external driver:

```sh
node ../replace-four-mention-proof-20261109.mjs "$PWD" green ../mentions-green.json
```

The base run changes only `green` to `red` to assert the expected misses. Driver SHA-256: `5ec455e110d1ef67841314a26d23d987d95a3a47ddf0295d90338c0f86ec4cb9`. The green receipt's source SHA and `dist/build-info.json` commit both equal the tested head above.

- Acceptance RED: both real Gateway canonical queries miss on base while literal queries succeed. The two focused regression cases also fail on base.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mention-directory.test.ts src/gateway/mention-inbox.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`: 50 tests passed across the existing directory and inbox suites. The two-file wrapper took 505.56s, including a 114.899s cold worker compilation and SQLite fixture lifecycle work; this is not production latency.
- Scoped source-backed `tsgo`, typed `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Staged test-line ratchet: passed, 6,589,094 lines against a 6,589,126 ceiling; an 18-line allocation accounts for the two parameterized cases without changing the shared scalar baseline.
- Native `sourcePerformance` build of the committed head: passed in 4m24.4s, followed by the real Gateway GREEN proof above.
- Author simplification and test-value audit completed. No independent model review is claimed. Production +6/−3, tests +18/−0, allocation metadata +2; no new helper or call path.

Compatibility/security: no config/default, protocol, permissions, account linking, identity, schema, persisted-data, or dependency change. The same eligibility filtering runs before matching. The UI consumes these directory results; it does not introduce another client-side name matcher.

Not tested: browser rendering, external chat services, model turns, cross-OS behavior, the full repository suite, or upstream PR CI before opening. This proves the actual Gateway mention-directory contract and stored-name readback, not a browser or production deployment.

</details>

prs.title: fix(qa-channel): match canonically equivalent message searches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Channel message searches miss visually identical text when the message or attachment uses a different canonical Unicode form. For example, searching `CAFE\u0301` does not find a message containing `Café`, despite the existing case-insensitive search.

## User Impact

QA message search finds canonically equivalent message text, attachment filenames, alternative text, and transcripts. Message IDs, original text, attachment contents, account/conversation selectors, deletion filtering, and result limits retain their existing contracts. Accents remain significant: this does not introduce accent-insensitive or fuzzy matching.

## Why This Change Was Made

`searchQaBusMessages` is the single search owner behind QA Channel's HTTP search action and the channel client. Normalize the query and its complete lowercase search projection to NFC at that owner; keep storage and returned message objects verbatim. JavaScript's built-in normalization is sufficient. No dependency, option, schema, state migration, or second search implementation is added.

```js
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdir, readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const [repo, phase, output] = process.argv.slice(2);
assert(repo && ['red', 'green'].includes(phase) && output);
const { createQaBusState, startQaBusServer } = await import(
  pathToFileURL(path.join(repo, 'extensions/qa-lab/bus-api.ts')).href
);
const bus = await startQaBusServer({ state: createQaBusState() });
const observations = [];
const failures = [];
async function post(route, body) {
  const response = await fetch(`${bus.baseUrl}${route}`, {
    method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000),
  });
  assert.equal(response.status, 200, `${route} HTTP status`);
  return response.json();
}
try {
  for (const [stored, query] of [['Café', 'CAFE\u0301'], ['Cafe\u0301', 'CAFÉ']]) {
    for (const surface of ['text', 'fileName', 'altText', 'transcript']) {
      await post('/v1/reset', {});
      const input = {
        conversation: { id: 'search-proof', kind: 'direct' }, senderId: 'synthetic-proof',
        text: surface === 'text' ? stored : 'attachment',
        ...(surface === 'text' ? {} : { attachments: [{
          id: 'attachment-proof', kind: 'file', mimeType: 'text/plain', [surface]: stored,
        }] }),
      };
      const { message } = await post('/v1/inbound/message', input);
      const exact = await post('/v1/actions/search', { query: stored });
      assert.deepEqual(exact.messages.map(m => m.id), [message.id], 'literal control');
      const equivalent = await post('/v1/actions/search', { query: ` ${query} ` });
      const actual = equivalent.messages.map(m => m.id);
      const matched = actual.length === 1 && actual[0] === message.id;
      if (!matched) failures.push(`${surface}:${stored}`);
      const distinct = await post('/v1/actions/search', { query: 'CAFETERIA' });
      assert.deepEqual(distinct.messages, [], 'different text must stay different');
      assert.deepEqual((await post('/v1/actions/search', { query, accountId: 'other' })).messages,
        [], 'account isolation');
      assert.deepEqual((await post('/v1/actions/search', { query, conversationId: 'other' })).messages,
        [], 'conversation isolation');
      const readback = (await post('/v1/actions/read', { messageId: message.id })).message;
      assert.equal(readback.text, input.text);
      assert.deepEqual(readback.attachments, input.attachments ?? []);
      await post('/v1/actions/delete', { messageId: message.id });
      assert.deepEqual((await post('/v1/actions/search', { query: stored })).messages, [],
        'deleted messages are excluded');
      observations.push({ surface, stored, query, messageId: message.id, actual,
        expected: [message.id], matched, literalControl: 'PASS', distinctControl: 'PASS',
        accountIsolation: 'PASS', conversationIsolation: 'PASS', originalReadback: readback,
        deletedControl: 'PASS' });
    }
  }
  assert.equal(failures.length, phase === 'red' ? 8 : 0);
  const source = await readFile(path.join(repo, 'extensions/qa-lab/src/bus-queries.ts'));
  const receipt = {
    phase, recordedAt: new Date().toISOString(), runtime: process.version,
    head: execFileSync('/usr/bin/git', ['-C', repo, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim(),

    protocol: 'real loopback HTTP via public qa-lab/bus-api.ts; no mocks',
    matchingCases: observations.filter(o => o.matched).length, failedCases: failures.length,
    observations, limits: 'Isolated in-memory QA bus. No external channel or model behavior claimed.',

  await writeFile(output, `${JSON.stringify(receipt, null, 2)}\n`);
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ phase, matchingCases: receipt.matchingCases,
```

prs.title: fix(cron): match canonically equivalent automation names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`automations list --query` already finds an automation across NFC/NFD spellings, but `automations show` cannot open the same result by its equivalent name. When equivalent names coexist, detail lookup can omit a matching choice and return an arbitrary-looking unique result.

## User Impact

`automations show` and its `cron` alias agree with the existing Unicode-aware inventory. Canonically equivalent duplicate names report all matching IDs; operators can select the intended stable ID. Stored names and ID lookup precedence retain their identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize only the name-comparison fallback in findCronJobByIdOrName to NFC, matching cron listPage. Keep the direct-ID and case-insensitive ID checks before name matching, along with the existing ambiguity error. This completes the sole name-detail lookup owner for both CLI aliases; it does not change scheduler, execution or persistence behavior.

No new configuration/default, protocol, permission, schema, dependency or migration. No generated changelog change.

## Evidence

### Current verification — November 4, 2026

Exact source/build head: `009577090d0b41836bc56a6d61f4542f3ab90c62`. Normal merge of upstream `258d034391ac03a8ee3530ba33552a5cbf2062fc`; reviewed production and regression files are byte-identical to the previous PR head. The unrelated toast mock-export and shared test-budget repairs come from upstream; this PR retains only its own exact test allocation relative to that main. No shared baseline adjustment was authored here.

- 32/32 focused tests pass, plus scoped source types, typed lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line/mock-export/timeout-race ratchets. Effective budget retains42lines of inherited main slack.
- Exact-head sourcePerformance build passes. The unchanged native driver passes: Both equivalent-name queries resolve the real disabled Gateway jobs; a canonical collision reports both IDs. Exact-name/ID, missing-query and unchanged-inventory/config controls pass for both CLI aliases.
- Author simplify/test-value audit complete; no independent model review is claimed. Hosted CI for this new head is reported separately; local proof does not claim a hosted pass.

Commands: `bash maintenance-validate-20261104.sh cron` runs the same explicit test files documented below; `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance`; `node refill-three-cron-native-20261103.mjs <built-checkout> green <receipt.json>`.

prs.title: fix(skills): resolve canonically equivalent metadata keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`skills list` discovers a skill with metadata key `Café`, but `skills info` cannot inspect it using the equivalent `Cafe\u0301` spelling. The reverse normalization direction fails too.

## User Impact

Equivalent Unicode spellings resolve the same installed skill. Exact names and metadata keys retain precedence; a tie at the strongest matching tier still refuses to choose by discovery order. This is a read-only lookup fix, not a new skill naming scheme.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize only the existing case-insensitive comparison tier to NFC. Both the CLI exit-status decision and detail formatting already consume this shared owner. The existing separator fallback remains unchanged. Metadata keys already accept nonempty Unicode strings; canonical skill names in the native fixture stay valid ASCII. This follows the comparison-only normalization used in #190546 without changing persisted keys or adding a library.

No new configuration/default, protocol, permission, schema, dependency or migration. No generated changelog change.

## Evidence

The unrelated toast mock-export and shared test-budget repairs come from upstream; this PR retains only its own exact test allocation relative to that main. - Exact-head sourcePerformance build passes. The unchanged native driver passes: Both equivalent Unicode metadata-key lookups succeed; discovery, exact-name/key precedence and unknown-query controls remain intact. Skill and config bytes are unchanged.
- Author simplify/test-value audit complete; no independent model review is claimed. Hosted CI for this new head is reported separately; local proof does not claim a hosted pass.

```json
  ],
  "configAndSkillsUnchanged": true,
  "status": "PASS_GREEN"
}
```

Replay driver (build each checkout first):

```js
assert.equal(build.commit, head);
const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'leon-skills-canonical-'));

for (const dir of [home, state, workspace]) fs.mkdirSync(dir);

const config = JSON.stringify({ gateway: { mode: 'local' }, plugins: { enabled: false },
  agents: { ownership: 'explicit', entries: { main: { workspace } }, defaults: { systemAgent: { agentId: 'main' } } },
  logging: { consoleLevel: 'error', file: path.join(root, 'runtime.log') } });
fs.writeFileSync(configPath, config);
const env = { PATH: `${path.dirname(process.execPath)}:/usr/bin:/bin`, LANG: 'C.UTF-8', NO_COLOR: '1', HOME: home,
  OPENCLAW_HOME: home, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: state, OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH: configPath, OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN: '1',
  OPENCLAW_HIDE_BANNER: '1', OPENCLAW_SKIP_STARTUP_MODEL_PREWARM: '1' };
const report = { head, buildCommit: build.commit, node: process.version, at: new Date().toISOString(), expectation, root,
  driverSha256: createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(new URL(import.meta.url))).digest('hex'), calls: [] };
function skill(name, key) {

  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'SKILL.md'), contents);

}
function cli(label, args) {
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): report retryable session work-start conflicts from OpenAI-compatible endpoints
prs.body:
Related: #192465

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session work-start conflicts become opaque internal errors or lose their stable error codes when clients use the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses endpoints.

## User Impact

Clients can distinguish `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` and `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED` from internal failures. Nonstreaming requests receive HTTP 409; streams whose headers have already been sent retain HTTP 200 and report the conflict in their failure envelope before `[DONE]`.

This does not add automatic retries or guarantee that replaying an entire request is safe. Session admission, ordering, cancellation and persistence are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared error mapper already has the correct ownership for coordination-error classification. It now uses the existing error-graph traversal and session-conflict guard to preserve conflicts carried directly or in a nested cause, without overriding direct tool-authorization denials. Both Responses failure adapters preserve the stable code, falling back to the mapped type only when no code exists. `incomplete_turn` keeps its existing precedence.

The original three direct mapper regressions are replaced by real-listener HTTP boundary coverage in the existing compatibility suite, rather than growing the oversized Chat Completions suite. The SSE parser is moved unchanged to a dependency-light helper, so this suite does not import unrelated embedded-agent fixtures just to parse frames; existing stream-test facade exports remain intact. The existing mapped-provider expectation is updated because Responses now preserves provider codes too. No configuration or migration is required.

## Evidence

- Before the adapter repair, a Responses SSE request produced `invalid_request_error` instead of `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`.
- The review-driven nested-cause HTTP regression also ran red: a real authenticated Chat Completions request returned **500 instead of 409** before error-graph recognition (1 failed, 22 deselected).
- Updated head: `39727933c52a9f1d19c27a8c70b6b186419c7b0f`.
- All **23 tests passed** in `server-http.openai-compat.test.ts` in the final workflow-bound run, including four endpoint/stream groups and **24 conflict requests**. Coverage includes typed changed/invalidated errors, an outer-code Error wrapper, a code-only object, and genuine typed/serialized nested causes; it checks status/envelope, one failure, one final `[DONE]`, one HTTP agent-boundary invocation, and admission cleanup.
- The listener, authentication, routing, mapper and wire adapters are real; agent rejection is mocked. This is not live-agent/model contention proof and does not establish deeper provider retry behavior. No live model requests were made.
- The final workflow-bound run passed `git diff --check`, formatting and lint on all seven scoped TypeScript files, `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`, and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json`. Committed tree `87160fa55e09e8dd5c17c50b5d3c03136c0739f7` is the exact verified candidate.

### Unresolved results, not claimed green

Before the nested-cause/helper follow-up, the complete three-file run of `server-http.openai-compat.test.ts`, `openai-http.test.ts` and `openresponses-http.test.ts` finished with **185 passed, 10 failed**. It was not rerun wholesale or claimed green for the updated head. A bounded comparison at original PR HEAD `23c896304f7ae554f2c2ce35aa877c67db706327` reproduced the same ten failure signatures (10 failed, 1 passed, 164 skipped):

- Chat Completions initial SSE chunk: the existing 15-second test timeout.
- Three Chat Completions disconnect cases and three Responses deferred-terminal/admission cases: the agent mock was not called before the existing wait deadline.
- Reserved-tool Responses failure: no failure event was observed.
- Mapped-provider and unmapped-provider Responses failures: existing request deadlines.

The comparison establishes that these signatures also occur before this repair; it does not establish their environmental root cause or fix them. No existing timeout, assertion, baseline or failure expectation was weakened.

### Exact CI-base budget attribution

Against CI comparison base `d755a99495e79c0b98ae1ad612511889097b259f`, the updated prospective integration tree `ff08d2103f4a4c55501a730b397d248d98dc223b` passed assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets. Test lines still **failed, 117 over**: total 6,479,360 versus ceiling 6,479,243. This is inherited debt, not a green result. These checks used a genuine merge plus three-way application of the reviewed repair, in temporary indexes; the real index was unchanged.

This PR's measured net regression growth is exactly **102 LF lines**, covered by the separate allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/pr-193205.txt` containing `102`. The increase is justified by JSON/SSE and both endpoint contracts, including nested wrappers; the parser move itself adds one net test-support line. No shared scalar was raised and no inherited-debt waiver was applied. Across the complete PR, production code grows by 20 net lines and tests by 102 net lines.

## Review and Remaining Limits

Canonical local autoreview/ClawSweeper tooling was unavailable in this environment; it is not claimed to have run. The host `code-review` skill reviewed the complete committed range at `db08ea644e1e9a688126bfdec4ef4134e823c224` and identified the nested-cause mapping gap plus the unnecessary stream-fixture dependency. This update addresses both; the nested-cause finding was dynamically reproduced before repair, and no collection-time speedup is claimed for the helper extraction.

The same independent host reviewer then refreshed the **complete seven-path committed range** from `4671dd463e044be350fdbec2169c0444a62678b9` to `39727933c52a9f1d19c27a8c70b6b186419c7b0f`, applying ten static review angles inline and a final gap sweep while reusing unchanged owner knowledge. Both earlier findings were resolved in the actual code; **no actionable remaining findings** were identified. This was static review, not a new runtime, live-model or broad-suite run. Exact reviewed diff SHA256: `389281f9421c2ba51062be9185591ea1b5e018e28c7ec1f9f29c6c87d05ec02c`.

Real agent/model session contention remains unverified. The existing hosted needs-proof feedback is not treated as resolved merely because boundary tests pass. Current-head CI and enforced maintainer reviews remain separate requirements; this update does not merge the PR.

## Live shipped-Gateway conflict capture (2026-11-16 addendum)

Shipped-path evidence captured against a real Gateway process built from this branch tree (dist via `node openclaw.mjs gateway`) with the Chat Completions and Responses endpoints enabled, token auth, a local OpenAI-compatible provider, and `x-openclaw-session-key` routing. The provider holds the first request in flight; the second request on the same session arrives ~6s later.

```
POST /v1/chat/completions (nonstreaming second request, same session)
HTTP 409
{"error":{"message":"Session \"agent:main:conflict-probe\" changed while starting work. Retry.",
          "type":"invalid_request_error","code":"SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED"}}
```

Reproduced twice in independent runs. This is the exact shipped Chat Completions path - real listener, real auth, real routing, real admission, real error mapper and wire encoder, no mocks; the conflict arises from genuine concurrent same-session admission, not an injected rejection.

The Responses endpoint live capture did not stabilize in this sandbox: with the first request held in flight, the second request was admitted normally (HTTP 200) rather than conflicting, so no live 4xx could be captured for it here. The Responses JSON/SSE conflict envelopes (both failure adapters preserving SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED / SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED, HTTP 409 nonstreaming / failed-event streaming) remain covered by the real-listener HTTP boundary suite: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-http.openai-compat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t conflicts` -> 4 passed | 19 skipped on the branch tree (chatCompletions/responses x json/stream), where the listener, auth, routing, mapper and SSE encoder are real and only the agent-command boundary injects production conflict errors.

prs.title: fix(ui): match NFD macOS file paths against NFC preview search queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the file preview modal's search filter fails to find files whose paths contain accented or combining characters when those paths come from macOS (NFD/decomposed Unicode) and the user types the same text in composed form (NFC).

## User Impact

User impact: on macOS, where file paths contain decomposed Unicode (e.g. `plans/resumé.md` stored as NFD), searching for `resumé` (typed as NFC) now finds the file in the preview modal. Previously the file was invisible to the search even though it was listed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filter in `file-preview-modal.tsx` compared raw strings:

```ts
`${file.path}\n${file.contents}`.toLowerCase().includes(query)
```

macOS file paths use NFD (decomposed) Unicode while keyboard input is NFC (composed); the raw `includes()` check fails across the two forms. The fix canonicalizes both sides to NFC — the same approach as #188883 for the session-diff jump search (the sibling UI search site fixed yesterday). No other preview behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main, regression test only: a file with an NFD path (`plans/resumé.md`.normalize("NFD")) is invisible when searching with the NFC form of the same word:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/components/file-preview-modal.test.ts
 × matches NFD macOS file paths against NFC search queries
   → expected +0 to be 1
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — the same file is found, and the full suite passes:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/components/file-preview-modal.test.ts
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Also verified: `pnpm format:check`.

prs.title: fix(slack): match canonically equivalent names in allowlist resolution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An allowlist entry written in NFC form (e.g. `@Renée`, precomposed) fails to resolve a Slack profile whose display name is stored in NFD form (`Rene\u0301e`, decomposed), and vice versa. The two strings compare unequal under `===` even though they are canonically equivalent, so the user is reported `resolved: false` instead of being matched.

The same omission predicate affects the user's exact-name comparison against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, and `profile.real_name`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSlackUserAllowlist` in `extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts` compares the allowlist entry name against profile names with `===` on lowercased strings. Lowercasing does not canonicalize Unicode, so NFC/NFD-equivalent spellings of the same name never match. Both sides of the comparison are now normalized with `normalize("NFC")`.

This is the same shape already accepted for the feishu sticker-search path (`#190043`, `extensions/feishu/src/sticker-catalog.ts`) and the slack/feishu/msteams directory lookups that normalize query and candidate before matching.

**Security guard (P1):** canonical matching is a fallback, never a replacement. Exact (lowercased) spelling stays the primary comparison, preserving the pre-existing principal selection. If two active humans have display names that differ only by normalization form (one NFD, one NFC), the configured name resolves to the exact-spelling match even if the canonically-equivalent user appears earlier in the directory. This prevents NFC normalization from displacing the configured principal with a different Slack user id.

Production LOC is `+28/-3` across one file. No new validator, option, config item, or persistence strategy is added.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Allowlist entries that differ from the stored profile name only by Unicode normalization form now resolve to the correct user id instead of being reported unresolved. Matching for already-canonical names is unchanged. NFC normalization is a canonical-equivalence relation used as a fallback only: it never merges two distinct names, and it can never displace an exact-name match, so it cannot admit a different principal than the one the configured name denotes.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry-point proof (production WebClient over local fixture)

The real exported `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` is exercised through its production `createSlackLookupClient` WebClient path against a local `users.list` fixture, using the existing `SLACK_API_URL` seam the plugin itself supports. No Slack client is mocked: the same code path that ships resolves entries over the fixture.

- Product head SHA: `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`
- Current-main RED baseline: `632dced4affb7a338d0def2b7059c246ed33b0af`
- Production entry: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` (`extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts:99`) over the production `createSlackLookupClient` (`extensions/slack/src/client.ts:47`) and its `users.list` fetch.
- Decision surface: allowlist entry name matched against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, `profile.real_name`.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the `resolved` flag and resolved `id`/`name` in `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` output.

Base (`resolve-users.ts` without `normalize("NFC")`):

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
  - both NFC/NFD cross-form resolve cases fail (resolved: false)
  - both canonical-direction admission cases fail (no derived grant, sender denied)
  - competing-principal case fails (active grant never derives, intended sender denied)
  - removal case fails (first turn never admits)
  - exact-name / accent-stripped / same-form / ASCII controls pass
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Head (this PR):

```text
 ✓ resolves NFC entry against an NFD profile through the production WebClient and local users.list fixture
 ✓ resolves NFD entry against an NFC profile through the production WebClient and local users.list fixture
 ✓ keeps exact-name matches ahead of canonically-equivalent directory entries
 ✓ does not admit a different principal (accent-stripped) through the production path
 ✓ keeps same-form and ASCII controls unchanged through the production path
 ✓ name-derived grant through production admission > admits the canonical sender for NFC/NFD entries through production ingress
 ✓ ... > rejects the competing principal while the canonical grant is active
 ✓ ... > denies a different sender (unresolved accent-stripped name) before any agent/provider I/O
 ✓ ... > denies subsequent messages once the name-derived grant is removed
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
 [test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

### Shipped CLI trace (`openclaw channels resolve`)

The shipped CLI entry point is executed against the same local `users.list` fixture through the plugin's own `SLACK_API_URL` seam (loopback only; the fixture logs every request). No Slack client, transport, or resolver code is mocked or substituted: the command runs the real bundled slack channel plugin (`plugin.resolver.resolveTargets` → `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the production WebClient). One CLI invocation is one directory-query batch; the fixture serves a fixed directory per scenario and logs `POST /api/users.list` for each run.

Setup (synthetic token, loopback fixture, nothing public):

```text
$ export SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47891/api/        # local users.list fixture on loopback
$ export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$PWD/proof/openclaw.json    # channels.slack.botToken="xoxb-synthetic-proof" (synthetic)
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs channels resolve --channel slack --kind user <entries>
$ node --version   # v24.22.1
```

Base (`resolve-users.ts` at current main, same tree minus this PR's slack files):

```text
# directory: one user, display name stored NFD (decomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée' '@Renee'
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match (pre-existing behavior)
@Renée -> unresolved             # cross-form NFC entry vs NFD-stored profile: the defect
@Renee -> unresolved             # accent-stripped distinct name: control
# fixture: [fixture][nfd-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: one user, display name stored NFC (precomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match (pre-existing behavior)
@Renée -> unresolved            # cross-form NFD entry vs NFC-stored profile: the defect
# fixture: [fixture][nfc-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: NFD-stored user listed FIRST, NFC-stored exact spelling second
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_INTENDED (Renée)     # exact-name precedence (pre-existing on base)
# fixture: [fixture][precedence] POST /api/users.list
```

Head (this PR, head SHA `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`; built from a tree whose slack files are byte-identical to the head SHA):

```text
# directory: one user, display name stored NFD (decomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée' '@Renee'
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # cross-form NFC entry now resolves (fixed)
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match unchanged
@Renee -> unresolved             # accent-stripped distinct name still unresolved
# fixture: [fixture][nfd-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: one user, display name stored NFC (precomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)   # cross-form NFD entry now resolves (fixed)
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)    # same-form exact match unchanged
# fixture: [fixture][nfc-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: NFD-stored user listed FIRST, NFC-stored exact spelling second
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_INTENDED (Renée)     # exact-name precedence intact: the canonically-equivalent
                                 # earlier directory entry never displaces the exact-spelling match
# fixture: [fixture][precedence] POST /api/users.list
```

Both NFC→NFD and NFD→NFC directions resolve on head and were unresolved on base; same-form matching, the accent-stripped control, and exact-name precedence are unchanged. IPs are loopback, the token is synthetic, and no non-public endpoint is touched.

### Authority-chain proof: production DM ingress through final effect

The authority chain no longer stops at the resolver return value or a bare admission boolean. `createMonitorTestContext` returns a context whose `readRuntimeContext` is the real `createSlackRuntimeContextReader`, so awaiting it runs the production `resolveWorkspacePolicy` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/runtime-policy.ts:239-250`), which resolves the allowlist names through the real `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the local `users.list` fixture and merges the derived ids into `ctx.allowFrom` via `mergeAllowlist`. The resolved policy context is then handed to the production DM ingress entry point `prepareSlackMessage` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts`), the function the monitor calls for every inbound message; it runs the DM admission gate `authorizeSlackDirectMessage` and, on admission, returns the exact `PreparedSlackMessage` object the monitor dispatches to the agent/provider. No admission helper, Slack client, or dispatch seam is mocked.

- **Both canonical directions admit the intended Slack ID at final effect.** `@Renée` (NFC) against an NFD-stored profile, and the NFD spelling against an NFC-stored profile, each resolve to `U_ACCENT` through production policy reload, the id lands in the allow-from list, and `prepareSlackMessage` returns a non-null `PreparedSlackMessage` for sender `U_ACCENT` — the object that reaches agent/provider dispatch.
- **The competing principal is rejected while the canonical grant is active.** With `@Renée` derived to `U_ACCENT` and present in allow-from, a message from `U_OTHER` — a distinct sender with its own fixture display name and identity, resolved per user id exactly as production resolves sender names (`prepare.ts:381`) — returns null: the DM gate drops the event before any agent/provider I/O. The derived grant admits exactly the resolved principal and never a different Slack user id.
- **A distinct name is denied before any agent/provider I/O.** With the accent-stripped `@Renee` configured (unresolved), `U_ACCENT` never becomes a derived grant and both `U_ACCENT` and `U_OTHER` are dropped before dispatch.
- **Removing the name-derived grant denies subsequent messages on the same runtime policy reader.** First turn `@Renée` resolves and `U_ACCENT` is admitted at final effect. The published config is then replaced with one whose only entry is the stale `@Renee`; the same reader rebuilds policy on its next read (`runtime-policy.ts:116`, `current.cfg !== cfg`), the derived id leaves allow-from, and a subsequent message from `U_ACCENT` is dropped before dispatch — the same live-policy-change path the monitor uses, no reconnect or fresh monitor.
- **Exact-name principal is preserved (P1 regression).** With `U_OTHER` (NFD display name) before `U_INTENDED` (NFC display name) in the directory, `@Renée` resolves to `U_INTENDED`, not the canonically-equivalent earlier entry. This test fails on the pure-canonical head (selects `U_OTHER`) and passes on this head.

Base (`resolve-users.ts` without `normalize("NFC")`):

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Pure-canonical head (without exact-first guard):

```text
 × keeps exact-name matches ahead of canonically-equivalent directory entries
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Head (this PR):

```text

      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

prs.title: fix(zalouser): match canonically equivalent names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `channels.zalouser.allowFrom: ["Nguyễn Văn A"]` while Zalo reports that friend's `displayName` in decomposed Unicode form (NFD) leaves the sender unresolved: startup logs `zalouser users unresolved: Nguyễn Văn A`, and the DM is rejected even though the name is exactly what the operator sees in the Zalo app.

- Problem: every Zalo name comparison lowercased but never normalized, so NFC and NFD spellings of the same name produced different keys. The startup allowlist resolver (`allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `groups` keys), the `friends`/`groups` lookups, and group-name resolution all missed.
- Solution: name matching now compares canonical keys. `extensions/zalouser/src/directory-index.ts` owns `normalizeZaloNameKey` (trim + lowercase + NFC), and the five comparison sites use it.
- What changed: `directory-index.ts` (new key owner, index build), `zalo-js.ts` (`resolveZaloEntries`, `listZaloFriendsMatching`, `listZaloGroupsMatching`), `monitor.ts` (startup name-resolution lookups), `channel.ts` (group name selection).
- What did NOT change: original spellings still flow to logs, prompts and outbound text untouched; numeric `userId`/`groupId` comparisons keep the lowercase-only helper; no config schema, manifest or API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner decides what "same Zalo name" means, and every comparison asks it. Keeping the key inline at each site would have left five copies of the same convention in three files, which is how the gap appeared in the first place.

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- Inline `.normalize("NFC")` at each call site: smaller diff, five duplicated key definitions.
- Normalizing on ingest (rewriting `displayName` when it arrives): would silently change the spellings surfaced to users, logs and captured messages, far beyond matching.
- A shared `plugin-sdk` canonical helper: no such owner exists; the tree keeps this per-channel (feishu, discord, matrix, mattermost normalize inline).

Boundaries:

- `group-policy.ts` matches operator config group keys/substrings exactly; a different contract, unchanged.
- Numeric ids are compared with the existing `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`; only names get the NFC key.
- Production delta is +4 lines: the key function plus comment replacing the four inline lowercasing sites it supersedes.

Same family as merged per-channel fixes #187953, #188003, #187988; no upstream helper was lost.

## User Impact

Operators whose allowlists, group config keys or lookups use a diacritic-bearing Vietnamese (or other composed/decomposed) name now reach the person they meant, regardless of which Unicode form their device or the Zalo server stored. Before this change the failure was silent: the startup resolver logged `unresolved`, the DM was rejected, and `friends`/`groups` queries came back empty with no error.

Users who already match exactly keep identical behavior, because the canonical key preserves every currently-failing-to-match distinction except the composed/decomposed one.

## Evidence

### Regression: red on base, green at head

The four production files were swapped for `origin/main` (`git checkout origin/main -- extensions/zalouser/src/{directory-index,monitor,channel,zalo-js}.ts`), PR tests kept.

```console
# base source, new tests only
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-zalo.config.ts extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.matching.test.ts extensions/zalouser/src/channel.test.ts -t "canonical|unlisted sender|opt-in is off|grant removed"
Tests  7 failed | 6 passed | 20 skipped (33)   # 6 friend/group/allowFrom + group-name pick
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts -t "resolves canonically|unauthorized|grant removed"
Tests  2 failed | 3 passed | 21 skipped (26)   # startup resolve + canonical sender dispatch

# head source restored, same two commands
Tests  13 passed | 20 skipped (33)
Tests  5 passed | 21 skipped (26)
```

9 of the 12 added tests are red on base and green at head; the three rejection cases (unlisted sender, opt-in off, grant removed after restart) pass on both refs by design. Pre-existing ingress-verdict cases stay flaky on both refs.

### Running Gateway, authority chain (head 2df8019 vs origin/main 1e906e9)

Real `openclaw gateway run`, isolated state dirs, same config on both refs: `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, `allowFrom: ["Nguyễn Văn A"]` (NFC), `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching: true`. Only the Zalo network client is a fixture: `require("zca-js")` resolves to a proof file serving a friend stored as NFD (shared `node_modules` untouched), plus a loopback stub model; startup resolution, admission, dispatch and outbound are shipped code paths. No real Zalo login.

```console
scenario        startup resolution  sender 123  outbound
cand-accept     resolved ->123      dispatched  SEND_MESSAGE threadId=123 text=PROOF_AGENT_REPLY
main-accept     unresolved          blocked     none
cand-optin-off  not attempted       blocked     none
cand-revoked    state reused, []    blocked     none

[zalouser] users resolved: Nguyễn Văn A->123
message processed: chatId=zalouser:123 ... sessionKey=agent:main:zalouser:direct:123 outcome=completed
[zalouser] Blocked unauthorized zalouser sender 999 (dmPolicy=allowlist)   # unlisted, same run

# main-accept (origin/main 1e906e9, same config and fixture)
[zalouser] users unresolved: Nguyễn Văn A
[zalouser] Blocked unauthorized zalouser sender 123 (dmPolicy=allowlist)
```

### Ownership, differential, gates

`normalizeZaloNameKey` is the single key owner: `buildZaloNameIndex` builds with it; startup lookups in `monitor.ts` and group resolution in `channel.ts` query with it. Shipped `openclaw directory peers/groups list --channel zalouser`, 9 queries per ref: main returns `[]` for both cross-form cases (NFC vs NFD, peers and groups), head resolves them, same-form/ASCII/numeric-id/negative controls match on both. `oxlint` 0 errors, `oxfmt --check` clean; tsgo here hits the known `Declaration input escapes checkout` limit as on the base, so CI's extension type check is the authority.
