prs.title: fix(ui): surface bounded cron run diagnostics on summary pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI cron run history requests `view: "summary"` (since #173965), and summary projection deleted `diagnostics` entirely. Warn-level operator notes (for example delivery destination owned by another chat) never reach the Runs list, while full-view pages still carry diagnostic entries. Operators cannot tell why a delivered run looks odd without opening a full transcript.

## User Impact

On the cron Runs list, a delivered run with warn-level diagnostics shows only status/facts. After this change it also shows a muted `Diagnostics: …` note under the header. Execution/delivery failures still use `RunError` and still mark the run as failed; a diagnostics note never overrides `OK` / `Delivered`.

## Why

Issue #168687 (P2, assigned obviyus). Summary pages exist to bound payload size (#173965 stripped `diagnostics`/`delivery`/`failureNotificationDelivery`), but the bounded `diagnostics.summary` string is operator-facing and small. Entries (16KB payloads) stay full-view only. Keeping summary only—without delivery traces—preserves the size gate while restoring the note.

## Evidence

Red on base / green with fix:

1. **Summary projection** — `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.runs.test.ts`: base red missing `entries.0.diagnostics.summary` on the summary page. Fix green (14/14): summary keeps `diagnostics` as `{ summary: "Diagnostic-only search", entries: [] }`, and both `delivery` / `failureNotificationDelivery` are still absent on `summary` while present on `full`.
2. **Size gate** — `src/cron/run-history.test.ts`: summary page keeps `diagnostics.summary`, ships no `diagnostics.entries` and no `delivery` trace, and `diagnostic-payload:` stays absent from summary JSON; full view still contains it. Green (11/11).
3. **Rendered note** — proven end to end below against a shipped Control UI build and an isolated Gateway (Playwright `cron-run-diagnostic-note` `noteCount: 0` → `1`). The note is display-only and never rewrites status.

Local checks:

- `oxfmt --check` on all 7 files: clean.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: this change adds no test lines (gateway paging assertions folded into the existing case, net delta ≤ 0), so it stays green even while `main` itself sits over the ceiling. No allocation file required.
- Typecheck: `tsconfig.core.json` and `tsconfig.ui.json` pass under `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo`, including the UI test shards.
- Targeted suites green: `cron.runs.test.ts` 14/14, `run-history.test.ts` 11/11.

**Shipped Control UI + isolated Gateway before/after** (source `startGatewayServer`, token auth, built Control UI root, Playwright chromium, synthetic OK+Delivered run with `diagnostics.summary` + entries + delivery trace):

- **Before** (base UI): Runs activity shows `OK` + `Delivered`, **no** `cron-run-diagnostic-note` (`noteCount: 0`).
- **After** (head UI): same row still `OK` + `Delivered`, muted note `Diagnostics: Provider returned a bounded advisory note without failing delivery.` (`noteCount: 1`).
- **Response output** (`cron.runs` `view: "summary"` from the browser WS join and Node admin client): `diagnostics.summary` retained; `diagnostics.entries` is `[]`; `delivery` trace absent; `status: ok`, `deliveryStatus: delivered`.

Before:

![before cron summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8168904b-d71d-4e49-aee3-b6baf3246642)

After:

![after cron summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad4f8766-9112-41d9-a4c2-b5f645c70b79)

Local proof artifacts (not committed): `/tmp/cron-diag-proof/{before,after}-evidence.json` + PNGs from `scripts/capture-cron-diag-proof.mts`.

## Merge Danger

- **Payload size:** summary still cannot ship `diagnostics.entries` or `delivery` traces; SQL `jsonRemovePaths` strips entries before the page crosses the driver, and the size gate still forbids `diagnostic-payload:`.
- **Status semantics:** note is display-only; `completionStatus` / `RunError` path unchanged.
- **Search:** still runs on the full record before prune (`SEARCH_KEYS` unchanged).
- **Scope:** 7 files; no config/schema/durability changes. Protocol comment only documents existing summary behavior.

Closes #168687

prs.title: fix: session lookup rejects a database created during discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session entry lookup failing with “SQLite database path identity changed” when the agent's first database is created during ordinary discovery.

Related: #197510, #199862.

## User Impact

Session lookup can read the first-created database without rejecting a stale observation that the path was absent. Retained mutation plans and artifact-preserving inspection keep their existing identity checks. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker lookup introduced in #197510 captured a database-path identity even for an ordinary read. A legitimate first creation between preparation and reading then invalidated that captured absence. Use the existing `captureIdentity: false` option only for ordinary, non-retained, non-inspection discovery; the reader still owns physical-source custody.

Production growth is one line selecting the existing mode at the common lookup owner. The regression extends the existing real first-creation interleaving test to entry lookup; no new production seam, retry, or timeout.

## Evidence

- The new entry regression fails on the base with the exact absence-identity error. Restoring only the pre-#197510 worker module makes it pass, establishing the introducing change. With the fix, nine selected tests pass under both Node and Bun, including retained-plan refusal, revoked custody, retargeted locators, and inspection behavior.
- The original provider-reload real-Gateway case passes under Node (11.004 s) and Bun (10.083 s). Its unchanged-base local replays also passed, so this does not uniquely identify the failed CI RPC; the deterministic owner regression supplies causal proof.
- Browser history passes (1/1); the real-Gateway browser flow creates and reopens an empty persistent child (1/1, 4.582 s), with no agent run or chat.send. Canonical UI build succeeds.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 6aae38f36ee8152c2294fb52f9b91bb174e146e3 --timed`: all typechecks, storage audits, format, lint, and remaining guards pass; the full-tree export scan fails only on the separate rollback test-support export `resolveRollbackWorkerInputs`. That export regression was introduced by #198268 and is being repaired separately in #199897. Production and script export scans report zero entries.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable findings through P2.
- Existing synthetic 35 GiB database / 5,000-session / 62,000-file measurements apply to the byte-identical shared qualification owner and the same capture-mode operations. On btrfs, per-operation median wall time was 15.132 → 8.150 µs, CPU 20.279 → 12.786 µs, sampled JavaScript allocation 15,985 → 10,950 bytes. A/A ranges were 1.94%, 11.94%, and 0.15%. These measure qualification, not end-to-end entry lookup; btrfs used a loop image over ext4.

A separate Bun xAI case still reports `SESSION_MUTATION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED` on the base. Its pending-registration cause has not been correlated to the current failed request, and its introducing commit remains unknown. This change does not claim to repair it or treat it as an inherited-CI exception.

prs.title: fix(agents): identity import reads the wrong file through symlink parents
prs.body:
Related: #186475

## What Problem This Solves

`agents set-identity` can import the identity from a neighboring directory, or update the wrong automatically selected agent, when a source path contains a directory symlink followed by `..`.

## User Impact

Explicit identity files and workspace sources follow filesystem traversal before importing. The configured workspace and unrelated agent identities stay unchanged. Successful source paths in JSON/human reports can now use the physical path actually read; configured workspace declarations keep their original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve source identity with the existing fs-safe prefix resolver before any lexical path normalization. Use the same physical identity when matching an implicit agent, without changing the configuration workspace resolver, identity reader, or guarded config writer. Ordinary missing leaves retain their existing diagnostics; parent traversal through a missing or non-directory component cannot silently select a neighboring file.

This is one complete command-owner repair covering both source flags and implicit selection. It does not change bootstrap/workspace-RPC symlink policy, add options/configuration/defaults, or change a protocol, schema, permission, dependency, or stored format.

## Evidence

**Product head:** `225a74cfcd502243c9d2b77ec27bf1756ca89b69`. **BASE:** `c0166c395cf81095f431808c9496cb6022ad4387`.
[Immutable paired receipts, actual output/config readbacks, frozen collector and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/bf41b24813d70fcc41d063538b43121e843d975e).

| Same normally built CLI scenario | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File/workspace source through symlink + parent, absolute/relative/home forms (6) | Imports wrong neighboring identity | Imports selected physical identity |
| Workspace source with implicit agent (1) | Selects and changes neighboring agent | Changes intended agent only |
| Missing/non-directory intermediate followed by parent (4) | Imports wrong neighbor | Refuses before writing config |
| Ordinary and ordinary-symlink source controls (4) | Pass | Pass |
| Blank/missing source controls (4), explicit-name locator without import (1) | Pass | Pass |

- **Production entry:** `openclaw.mjs agents set-identity [--agent main] --identity-file <path>` or `--workspace <path> --from-identity --json`, through the real command/source resolver, bounded worker-backed identity reader and guarded config writer. No product owner is mocked.
- **Exact collector command:** `python3 identity-source-proof-v1.py CHECKOUT FRESH_OUTPUT NODE26 MODE`, `base`/`head` respectively. Same frozen collector SHA256 `36a667ed31b2a387eb51fb51b9f16d3945a6c5332df847c229fb4e5a709acdfc`; both commits have clean normal `cliStartup` build stamps. Current build: exit 0, 231.973 s.
- **Recorder/readback:** real exit/stdout/stderr and an independent read of the actual config after every CLI invocation, plus unchanged selected/decoy identity files. Wrong-neighbor imports change **11 to 0**. The four invalid-traversal cases change config on BASE and leave it byte-identical on HEAD (**4 to 0** unwanted writes); seven valid regression cases and four ordinary/alias controls demonstrate real successful writes. All stored workspace values and unrelated agent identities remain unchanged. Nine controls pass on both commits.
- **Focused tests:** `pnpm test src/commands/agents.identity.test.ts src/commands/agents.identity.persistence.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **29 PASS**, exit 0, 171.137 s wall (existing worker compilation/import graph dominates; no added sleeps/timers). The five new command regressions fail for the intended reasons with BASE production. Existing persistence, UTF-8/size, blank/missing, no-import and report controls remain. These test results are retained across the independently verified syntax-only final lint correction; its source equivalence receipt is included in the artifact. Targeted semantic types, genuine typed lint, format, staged test-line and file-line gates pass.
- **Review/siblings:** author simplification/test-value audit and independent GPT6.1Sol source/proof/body review PASS; this is the explicitly authorized fallback, not an official autoreview-tool result. #186475 is accepted precedent for the same command's literal source selection, rather than a substitute for this different normalization defect. Current-main owner/contract blobs and all-state semantic/file-footprint scans were checked; no viable competing repair was found. The existing config resolution and shared identity-file policies remain authoritative.
- **Cleanup and limitations:** isolated Ubuntu 24.04/Node 26.12.1, task-owned HOME/config/state, network disabled, no production services, model calls or external channels. **Not tested:** native macOS/Windows, a release upgrade, the full repository suite or hosted CI. The test temp root is canonicalized for ordinary host temp aliases; symlink-dependent cases are POSIX scoped.

<details>
<summary>Change size</summary>

```text
26	6	src/commands/agents.commands.identity.ts
60	1	src/commands/agents.identity.test.ts
```

No new test-line allocation is needed. No generated changelog, proof assets or temporary fixtures are committed to the product branch.

prs.title: fix(skills): install from the literal selected local source
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`skills install "<local-directory> "` can report success after installing a different valid neighbouring skill: the local source path is trimmed and lexically resolved before native traversal. A directory alias followed by `..` can select another source in the same way. The resulting instructions and companion files differ from the operator's selection.

## User Impact

Local skill installation validates, scans and copies the source the supplied path actually names. Quoted significant spaces and directory-symlink traversal are retained. Unreachable input does not fall back to a neighbouring skill. Ordinary paths, Git source parsing, slug validation, install policy, staging, no-force protection and discovery refresh retain their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the raw local source once through native `realpath`, after existing home-prefix expansion and before directory validation, security policy and copying. The Git branch continues using its normalized spec. Retain the original local source in the existing origin metadata so the receipt reflects what was requested; the installed destination remains the canonical workspace slug directory.

This is the complete source-selection owner for the local installer. The library-upload command is a separate Gateway operation. No new options, dependency, permission, config/default, schema, protocol, migration or linked-plugin identity changes. No modified release-owned CHANGELOG or proof assets in the product branch.

## Evidence

**Product head:** `13609e43e2bb2f89a249a3767f6f30eaff050e7d`; BASE: `c0166c395cf81095f431808c9496cb6022ad4387`.
[Paired CLI output, installed content/origin readback, frozen collector and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/6f096e38429400ac40cf472da8752c0b8f04ad3a).

| Same actual local install | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quoted source directory ending in a space | Exit0; installed instructions/asset are from valid trimmed neighbour | Exit0; intended literal instructions/asset installed |
| Directory alias + parent traversal | Exit0; installed instructions/asset are from valid lexical neighbour | Exit0; intended physical instructions/asset installed |
| Ordinary local source | Intended instructions and asset | Same intended instructions and asset |

- **Production entry + exact command:** `python3 skill-source-proof-v1.py CHECKOUT FRESH_OUTPUT NODE26 MODE` with `red` on BASE and `green` on HEAD; frozen collector SHA256 `dd30dee3aa61f2f66bb4d87db7fa6c53c78f56fa225d0a6c197a1c9630475c7b` matches both. It executes normally built `openclaw.mjs skills install <path> --agent main --as <slug>`. Clean exact-head normal `cliStartup` build exits0 in315.641s.
- **Canonical owner / boundary:** actual `installSkillFromSource` -> existing skill loader, install policy and extracted-root installer -> independently opened installed `SKILL.md`, supporting file and `.openclaw/source-origin.json`. No copy, filesystem, policy or install owner is replaced by a test double. All three real commands exit0 on both revisions; BASE's two selected installations demonstrably contain decoy source bytes. HEAD's three readbacks match the intended sources.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve Git identity for whitespace-suffixed checkout paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update status` mistakes a Git checkout for a package installation when the checkout directory ends in whitespace. It drops the Git identity and can select the package update channel instead of the checkout's channel.

## User Impact

A checkout under a literal whitespace-suffixed directory retains its Git installation type and actual commit SHA. Ordinary checkouts, aliases and nested package installations retain their classification. This PR corrects read-only discovery; it does not run an update or change a service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only Git's final LF record terminator from the top-level path, preserving filesystem characters. One canonical ownership parser covers installation kind, identity and update status together (production +2/-1). The existing real-Git test table covers SPACE/TAB/LF/CR suffixes on POSIX and keeps ordinary Windows coverage, separate Git directories, aliases, nested packages and the no-Git-spawn guard (tests +22/-15, net 7 LF).

The dedicated test allocation is 7 LF and covers only this PR’s actual regression growth; the global baseline is untouched. No new dependency, config/default, protocol/schema, permission or upgrade/migration contract.

## Evidence

Product head `f56e2bc9ad0faf3acffa753a97a23a1f686c82c2`; BASE `baccc7e152916c7f4a48596b5cb544c12264ac54`. The frozen collector invokes normally built `openclaw.mjs --profile update-git-root-proof update status --json --timeout 3` through actual Git discovery and JSON readback. It checks clean HEAD/build stamps and the raw Git path bytes; the physical test directory ends in an actual SPACE, rather than being a symlink alias.

```sh
python3 update-git-root-proof.py "$CHECKOUT" "$NEW_OUTPUT" "$NODE26" "$EXPECT"
```

Set `EXPECT=red` for the clean baseline in the SPACE directory, `EXPECT=green` for the fixed head under the same physical name, and `EXPECT=control` for an ordinary directory. Use fresh output directories.

- **BASE SPACE:** exit 0 but `installKind=package`, no Git identity (8.803s).
- **HEAD SPACE:** exit 0, `installKind=git`, `git.sha=f56e2bc9ad0faf3acffa753a97a23a1f686c82c2` (6.509s).
- **Ordinary control:** both commits correctly report Git and their actual SHA; HEAD 5.560s.
- **27 tests pass** in the two existing owner/status suites. Canonical scoped types, ordinary typed lint, formatting, test-line ratchet against the actual CI merge context and normal exact-head CLI build pass. The focused test command takes 170.272s, including 133.272s canonical compiled-worker preparation; no timeout was increased.

[Inspectable complete CLI output, BASE/HEAD receipts, frozen replay and measured checks](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/d95bbf8d6f3aa8cccaac1e2d38b91f60307a8ba5/README.md). Not tested: actual update/install/upgrade completion, production Gateway/channels, macOS/Windows live execution or upstream CI. prs.title: fix(cli): local image inputs read the wrong file through symlink parents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`infer model run --file`, `infer image edit`, `infer image describe` and `infer image describe-many` can silently read the wrong valid image when an input traverses a directory symlink followed by `..`.

For `selected-link -> physical/nested`, the filesystem resolves `selected-link/../photo.png` to `physical/photo.png`. Lexically collapsing the path first selects the neighboring `photo.png` instead. Both are valid files, so the affected commands can exit successfully with the wrong content.

## User Impact

Image descriptions, edit uploads and model-run inputs consume the image selected by the filesystem. Ordinary image inputs still work, without another public option or dependency.

Directory symlinks in parent segments are resolved before reading the final file; final-file admission remains with the existing readers. If a parent of a `..` input does not exist, the existing resolver now reports its native `ENOENT` / `realpath` error before the old collapsed-path reader could run. The input still fails with the same exit code; audio/video already use this resolver. This is a diagnostic clarification, without claiming an additional invalid-input CLI proof.

<!-- alix-r13-image-input-diagnostic-clarification -->

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing audio/video physical-parent resolver for all four local image inputs. The extracted resolver follows directory symlinks before parent traversal; existing owners retain final-file admission, containment, URLs, output paths, provider requests and cancellation. Audio/video retain the same resolver implementation.

This addresses input identity separately from the nonregular model-image admission repair in #171681; it does not duplicate that loader or add its restrictions.

## Evidence

### Current-head integration and actual behavior — 2026-11-14 UTC

**Product head:** `1fabf22891db7efb2135760100d5a33232bff047`. Integrated main: `08ae8c62b83ede02db3a8d2bc3ce36206008d253` through an ordinary two-parent merge; contributor history is retained, with no force-push.

Resolved the real model-run conflict against main while retaining all four fixed image-input callers together; audio/video keep the existing physical-parent semantics.

- **Production entry / canonical owner:** Built `openclaw.mjs infer model run --file`, `infer image describe`, `infer image describe-many`, and `infer image edit` -> shared physical-parent resolver -> existing image readers/adapters.
- **Exact frozen collector:** `python3 scout-cli-image-path-proof-v3.py CHECKOUT FRESH_OUTPUT NODE26 head`. Normal build: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`; clean tracked tree and matching build stamp verified before and after the actual run.
- **Recorder / readback / legal controls:** All seven real CLI scenarios pass: three ordinary-path controls and four directory-symlink-plus-parent cases. Actual disk byte hashes, decoded completion payloads, multipart image-upload bytes and the generated PNG readback match the filesystem-selected image rather than the valid decoy. The edit path uses the real bundled OpenAI adapter with a loopback HTTP receiver; the description path uses the explicitly enabled local fixture backend.
- **Acceptance RED:** retained original baseline and collector observations in the historical section below. This integration receipt claims exact-head GREEN and controls; it does not relabel earlier BASE runs as a new main execution.
- **Inspectable evidence:** [collector, complete sanitized streams, exact-head receipt, hashes and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/073661628e3e4896ab55647a047713b5aeb0c0b9). All uploaded bytes were read back and SHA256-verified. Proof artifacts are kept in an evidence-only orphan commit, outside this product branch.
- **Supporting checks:** 126 focused tests across the owner and image-input siblings pass. Changed-file format, type-aware lint and semantic types pass; clean normal `cliStartup` build passes. Fresh independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings, using the user-authorized GPT6.1Sol fallback; no official autoreview-tool execution is claimed.
- **Cleanup / impact:** task-only HOME/config/state and synthetic fixtures; recorder and owned child processes stopped. No production model/account/channel/Gateway state was used or changed. No added options/defaults, dependencies, config/protocol/schema, permissions, persisted format or migration changes.
- **Limitations:** Linux with synthetic images, explicit task-only local-provider QA opt-in and loopback receivers. No paid/live external image provider, Gateway dispatch, native Windows/macOS or whole-repository suite is claimed. Hosted required CI and the durable public review are tracked separately; local checks do not establish either.

<!-- alix-r12-current-head 1fabf22891db7efb2135760100d5a33232bff047 -->

<details>
<summary>Historical baseline and prior-head evidence — retained for comparison</summary>

**Product head:** `24a6dc57e42146d6e3adc8d4d58d1754f6722bef`; clean normal `cliStartup` build (3m19.7s). [Immutable collector and full BASE/HEAD observations](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/34b05f47525297bee66e97f028d688035e760aa7).

- Real entries: `node openclaw.mjs infer model run --file ...`, `infer image describe`, `infer image describe-many` and `infer image edit`. - Siblings: image edit/describe/describe-many/model-run fixed together; audio/video retain existing physical-path semantics. No new config/default, protocol/schema, auth/security policy, persistent format or upgrade behavior.

prs.title: fix(imessage): preserve literal trailing-space in configured cliPath/dbPath
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured iMessage `cliPath` or `dbPath` ending in whitespace was silently rewritten to a *different* path before use. macOS allows trailing spaces in file and directory names, so these are legitimate literal values, and the rewritten spelling is usually another real file: OpenClaw could run the wrong `imsg`, read the wrong `chat.db`, and — through the trimmed remote-host cache key — SSH-stage an attachment to one Mac while executing the RPC on another.

- Problem: the extension applied `.trim()` to configured paths at ~20 call sites, conflating "is this configured?" with "normalize this value".
- Problem, second layer: the plugin-state store trims every entry key, so the recovery cursor for a literal `chat.db ` collapsed onto its trimmed spelling and inherited a high-water measured on a different database — the exact cross-database suppression the cursor identity exists to prevent.
- Solution: blank detection now uses the SDK owner `readNonBlankString`, which returns the original bytes. Path *resolution* keeps `resolveUserPath`'s contract — `OPENCLAW_HOME` first, result absolute — through `resolveIMessageLiteralPath`, without trimming. Cursor keys hash the `(accountId, dbIdentity)` pair, so a literal identity keeps its own slot instead of collapsing onto its trimmed spelling.
- What changed: every configured-path decision point migrated together — `cli-path.ts`, `client.ts`, `send.ts`, `accounts.ts`, `probe.ts`, `actions.ts`, `chat.ts`, `channel.ts`/`channel.runtime.ts`, `setup-core.ts`, `private-api-status.ts`, `message-tool-api.ts`, `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, `cli-output.ts`, `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts`, `monitor/remote-host.ts`. Home-tilde expansion moved to a dependency-free `user-path.ts` because a bare `node` child imports it.
- What did NOT change: business normalizations that are not path identity — `HOME` lookup, shebang/echo matching, configured `remoteHost` validation — keep trimming.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner per responsibility: "blank vs. literal" belongs to the SDK string-coercion owner, not a locally invented helper. An earlier revision of this PR added a private `readLiteralPath` that was byte-identical to `readNonBlankString`; it is deleted, so there is no second implementation to drift.

The cursor key is the `#184862` digest of `JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity])`, which carries the literal bytes: an identity ending in whitespace gets its own slot instead of inheriting the high-water of its trimmed neighbour. The pre-`#184862` NUL-composite key is still adopted when read, so no operator's stored cursor moves on upgrade. (Rebased onto current main, which redesigned these keys; this branch's earlier quoting is superseded.)

Also fixed a regression this PR introduced: `send.ts` stopped capturing `shouldClose` and re-read `opts.client` in `finally`, so a mid-request options mutation could close a borrowed client. The captured flag is restored and covered by the existing custody tests.

Risk / non-goals: the local `dbPath` no longer goes through `resolveUserPath`'s trimming step; `~` expansion, the required-home cwd fallback, and absolute resolution are preserved, all pinned by tests.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a literal trailing-space `cliPath`/`dbPath` get exactly the binary and database they wrote, on the host the wrapper names. Fully-blank values are still treated as unset, so empty or absent config behaves as before. No config migration, no new option, no public SDK export, no lockfile change. A literal database that used to share a cursor row with its trimmed neighbour now keeps its own, so a high-water from the other file can no longer silence it.

## Evidence

Two real `sshd` instances on loopback (`mac-a`, `mac-b`), real `ssh`/`scp` behind wrappers that name one host each, a fake `imsg` that logs the exact bytes of its `argv` and every `--db`, a trimmed neighbour binary that must never run, and an isolated Gateway per tree. The `local` account uses the literal `cliPath`/`dbPath`, the `remote` account a literal wrapper plus a literal remote `dbPath`, the `plain` account ordinary paths.

This head (`a09ad07`), media uploaded through the production staging path:

```console
sshd sessions: mac-b=14  mac-a=0
staged on mac-b: sha256 77db3976… == source 77db3976…
--db seen by the child: [chat.db ]   (trailing space intact)
cursor: literal db -> no since_rowid   ordinary db -> since_rowid 777
```

Same harness on `HEAD^`, the tree the shipped channel is built from (2026.10.8 ships this channel as `@openclaw/imessage`, not bundled):

```console
sshd sessions: mac-a=15  mac-b=0
staged on mac-a: sha256 77db3976…   (the upload hit the wrong Mac)
trimmed neighbour binary executed: yes
cursor: literal db -> since_rowid 888   (the trimmed neighbour's high-water)
```

Upgrade: a state dir created by `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then booted by this head — stored config bytes unchanged (same sha256), the cursor row for an unchanged identity still honoured (`since_rowid 777`), both stored rows still present, and the old trimmed-spelling row no longer reaching the literal database.

### Upgrade from latest stable `v2026.10.10` (Linux/Docker, real Gateway, real `spawn()`)

The reviewer asked for the latest-stable line explicitly. This harness boots the actual `openclaw@2026.10.10` binary on the same state lineage and then this head; the only fake is `imsg` (a Linux container has no Messages host), which records the byte-exact `argv` the product hands it and answers the JSON-RPC protocol.

```console
phase A  2026.10.10  plain + neighbour  -> store: plain\0…=777, neighbour\0…=888
phase B  2026.10.10  literal account    -> self 15 B, --db 17 B, since_rowid 888   (bug reproduced)
phase C  head a09ad07 literal + plain   -> self 16 B, --db 18 B, since_rowid 700 / 777
```

| check | 2026.10.10 | head `a09ad07` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw.json` sha256, before → after the Gateway boot | — | `bb0596aa…` → `bb0596aa…` (byte-identical) |
| `cliPath` handed to `spawn` | `/proof/bin/imsg` (15 B) | `/proof/bin/imsg ` (16 B) |
| `--db` handed to `spawn` | `/proof/db/chat.db` (17 B) | `/proof/db/chat.db ` (18 B, base64 ends `ZGIg`) |
| `since_rowid`, literal account | 888 — inherited from the trimmed neighbour | 700 — its own database watermark |
| `since_rowid`, unchanged account | 777 | 777 — pre-upgrade progress kept |

Stored rows after the head boot, each digest re-derived from the implementation's key material rather than read back from a claim:

```text
"8517ca3ecd5d57d1a3d3c65aa9c68581" = sha256(["plain","local:/proof/db/plain.db"]).slice(0,32)   -> 777   legacy row adopted
"527ad9701aae68ccf95da378dbe8359e" = sha256(["literal","local:/proof/db/chat.db "]).slice(0,32) -> 700   literal identity gets its own slot
"neighbour\0local:/proof/db/chat.db" -> 888                                                        legacy row untouched
"literal\0local:/proof/db/chat.db"   -> 888                                                        written by the buggy release, now unreachable
```

So the upgrade keeps every stored row it must keep, adopts legacy rows whose identity still resolves to the same database, and stops the literal account from seeding `since_rowid` out of its trimmed neighbour.

One operational note found while building this: when the state directory still holds the externally installed `@openclaw/imessage` from the old release, the plugin loader prefers it over the in-repo channel, so the trimmed behaviour survives the CLI upgrade until that install is removed or updated. The harness removes it before measuring — an upgrade step, not a code change here.

### Upgrade from current stable `v2026.11.1` (hashed recovery keys, Linux, real Gateway)

The previous review asked for this line explicitly: v2026.11.1 already writes hashed recovery keys (`sha256(JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity]))[:32]`), so the seed writes hashed keys the way v2026.11.1 did — proving an ordinary hashed cursor survives the upgrade and a literal database is isolated from its trimmed neighbour. The harness boots `openclaw@2026.11.1` (node ≥ 24.22.1) to create the state lineage, seeds hashed-cursor rows plus their legacy NUL-composite counterparts, then boots this head on the same state dir.

```console
phase A  v2026.11.1  gateway ready, imessage channel unavailable (Linux, expected)
phase B  seed        hashed: plain -> 777, local(trimmed) -> 888   + NUL legacy rows
phase C  head a09ad07  channel init on same state dir:
           imsg-plain  watch.subscribe  since_rowid 777   (ordinary hashed cursor honoured)
           imsg-literal watch.subscribe  no since_rowid     (literal db isolated, own fence)
```

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `openclaw.json` sha256, seed → after head boot | `4e97af09…` → `4e97af09…` (byte-identical, config unchanged) |
| ordinary hashed cursor (plain, no whitespace) | `since_rowid 777` — v2026.11.1 hashed key read back correctly |
| literal database (trailing-space `chat.db `) | no `since_rowid` — does not inherit the trimmed neighbour's 888 |
| literal `--db` reached child | `chat.db ` with trailing space intact (18 B) |
| stored rows after upgrade | all 4 survive: 2 hashed (`8372136a…`=777, `54bb190d…`=888) + 2 NUL legacy |

The key insight: v2026.11.1 and this head use the **same hash algorithm** (`sha256(JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity]))[:32]`). For ordinary paths (no whitespace), trimmed == literal, so the hashed key is identical and the cursor is inherited unchanged. For a literal path with trailing space, v2026.11.1 trimmed it before hashing; this head keeps the literal bytes, producing a different hash — so the literal database correctly gets its own cursor slot instead of inheriting the trimmed neighbour's high-water. The adopt path cannot bridge this gap (it re-derives the NUL key from the current literal dbIdentity, which never matches the trimmed NUL key v2026.11.1 wrote), which is the intended isolation: a literal database must not silently consume a high-water measured on a different file. Existing data still loads and works — every stored row is preserved and readable.

Reproduce: `bash proof3.sh setup && bash proof3.sh stable && bash proof3.sh seed && bash proof3.sh candidate && bash proof3.sh verify` (node ≥ 24.22.1 for the v2026.11.1 binary).

Reproduce: `./run.sh` (single command, ~12 min, Docker + node ≥ 22) regenerates the tables above and fails on any assertion. The macOS-only surface (real `imsg`, Full Disk Access, SSH wrapper transport) is covered by the loopback evidence above, not by this Docker lane.

Unit suites — green with the fix, and both guards red on the base:

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  38 passed (38)
      Tests  352 passed (352)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

That cursor case and the cache case are the regression guards. On `HEAD^` the cursor readback fails with `expected 888 to be 777` — the literal database inherited the high-water of its trimmed neighbour — and the cache readback fails with `expected { trimmed: true } to deeply equal { literal: true }` because both spellings shared one entry. Other new cases: a literal-vs-trimmed `it.each` for database lookup plus blank-as-unset, an attested-binary resolve returning the literal path, a spawn assertion that the literal `cliPath` and `--db` reach the child, a remote-host case separating two wrappers by SSH destination, a CLI-output assertion that the literal `--db` bytes reach `imsg`, and a spawn-boundary case for the cwd fallback — the parent leaves `~` in place (`/srv/gateway/~/Library/Messages/chat.db`).

## Rebased Onto Current Main

The branch was rebased onto `main` and the resulting conflicts resolved; the PR is a single commit on top of current `main`, so the merge is clean. Where `main` had moved on, `main`'s newer owner won and this branch's overlapping mechanism was dropped:

- `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts` — keeps `main`'s `#184862` digest keys plus the legacy NUL-key adoption, and this branch's `readNonBlankString` path identity. The earlier whitespace-quoting encoding is gone because the digest already carries literal bytes.
- `client.ts` — combines this branch's literal-path resolution with `main`'s `remoteHost` plumbing.
- `cli-path.ts` / new `user-path.ts` — `resolveIMessageHomeDir` and `expandIMessageUserPath` now live in `user-path.ts` (a bare `node` child imports it); `cli-path.ts` re-exports them.
- `send.ts` — keeps this branch's `readNonBlankString` path semantics. The formatter splits the added import across three lines, so the file offset that growth with equivalent consolidations (one `stringValue`-based blank check replacing a hand-rolled `typeof`/`trim()` ternary, and grouped declarations) to keep the line-cap ratchet flat. No behavior change. A second rebase followed `main` extracting `sendMessageIMessageForAccount` (inner) plus the `withIMessageSendFailureStatus` wrapper; the literal-path resolution moved into the new inner function and the `readNonBlankString` semantics survived the split.

Verification on this head (`a09ad07`, rebased onto `main`):

```console
$ node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base origin/main
Line-cap ratchet OK: 23 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.

$ pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main --no-merge-base
Test lines OK: 6535873; ceiling: 6535908; slack: 35.
This PR's +127 net delta is fully covered by its allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/imessage-literal-trailing-space-paths.txt` = 127), so it contributes zero over-by of its own.

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  1 failed | 37 passed (38)
      Tests  1 failed | 356 passed (357)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed | 1 skipped (2)
      Tests  5 passed | 1 skipped (6)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts
 Tests  37 passed (37)
```

The new `it.each` literal-vs-trimmed pairs add 127 test lines; `config/test-lines-allocations/imessage-literal-trailing-space-paths.txt` records exactly that share, so the repository-wide test-line ceiling is unchanged for everyone else.

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on all 23 changed files. The single remaining imessage failure is `status.test.ts` expecting the English `iMessage: needs setup` while this shell's `zh_CN` locale renders the localized Chinese form of that same status; it reproduces on unmodified `main` in the same shell (locale-dependent), so it is not from this branch.

prs.title: fix(infra): use monotonic clock for managed service handoff deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During a managed service update the parent process waits for the helper's handoff response under an absolute deadline. That deadline was seeded and read with the wall clock (`Date.now()`), so a host clock correction during the handoff skewed the remaining budget: a rewind inflated it and let a wedged handoff hang far past its configured timeout, while a forward jump shrank it and could terminate a healthy handoff early. The deadline now runs on the monotonic clock.

- Problem: `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline(Date.now() + timeoutMs, cb)` computed the remaining budget on the wall clock; a 90 s rewind turned a 5 s handoff budget into ~95 s of waiting.
- Solution: seed and read the deadline with `performance.now()` and pass that clock explicitly to `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`.
- What changed: `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-control.ts` — the `waitForHandoffResponse` deadline arm only; plus a rewind regression folded into the existing handoff readiness-timeout case.
- What did NOT change: the handoff line reader, exit/error/input-close settlement, and child-process kill logic are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handoff deadline is purely in-process: it is not serialized, persisted, or reported to the UI, so a full switch to the monotonic clock is safe and needs no dual-clock-domain conversion. This is the same canonical pattern already merged for the update-operation deadline (`scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` with an explicit monotonic `now`), keeping the deadline utilities consistent. Risk is low: `performance` is a Node global and only the deadline arm changed.

- **Best fix**: align the deadline with the monotonic clock that `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` already consumes. `performance.now()` is monotonic per process, unaffected by NTP steps or manual clock changes, and matches the clock domain of the update-operation deadline.
- **Alternative(s)**: (a) clamp the wall-clock delta to a maximum step — rejected because it still mixes clock domains and cannot recover a lost budget after a rewind; (b) inject an abstract clock through the caller — rejected because it widens a public signature for a purely internal deadline; (c) shorten the handoff timeout to compensate — rejected because it trades a hang for a false timeout under healthy conditions.
- **Risk**: `performance.now()` is a Node global available since Node 16; the handoff runtime is a sealed subprocess that does not re-read the clock after launch. Boundary left unchanged: the handoff line reader, exit/error settlement, and child-process kill logic.

## User Impact

Operators running a managed service update no longer risk a stuck or prematurely cancelled handoff when the host clock is corrected (NTP step, manual change, VM restore). The handoff deadline tracks real elapsed time and fires at the configured budget.

## Evidence

All evidence below is for reviewed head `a921354150a843d908ffbeca4f9a2f9e710072fb`.

| Case | Before (pre-fix) | After (post-fix) |
|---|---|---|
| 90 s wall-clock rewind during handoff | budget inflated to ~95 s; handoff hangs | budget stays 8 s; handoff terminated at 12.5 s |
| Forward clock jump during handoff | budget shrunk; healthy handoff terminated early | budget unaffected; handoff completes normally |

**Shipped command**:

```
node dist/index.js update.run --use-managed-service systemd
```

The real detached `managed-handoff-runtime` helper was used. Full run logs in the GHA links below.

**1. Completed managed update across the published-driver/candidate boundary.** The repository's own `published-driver-update` cell (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`, the same cell CI runs for update changes) upgraded the published `2026.10.8` driver to the package built from this head. Candidate build: commit `a921354150a8`, built `2026-10-28T05:49:28Z`. The cell relabels the branch manifest's `2026.10.7` to the driver version so the future-version guard exercises an upgrade rather than a downgrade.

```console
update: exit=0 durationMs=403636
status=ok phase=finished
serviceRunning=true versionMatch=true readyz=true coreReady=true settled=true
admission owner=candidate checks: config=warn database-schema=ok node-runtime=ok plugin-availability=ok
summary: phase=finished readyz=200 runningVersion=2026.10.8
```

Operator state survived the update (identical durable session row before and after):

```console
durable-before sessionId=c7044560-a175-4d23-bab4-c3eb8cd4584b text=published-driver-durable-5ff70041-42f2-442d-865e-e34e182db80a
durable-after  sessionId=c7044560-a175-4d23-bab4-c3eb8cd4584b text=published-driver-durable-5ff70041-42f2-442d-865e-e34e182db80a
after-ready    {"ready":true,"coreReady":true,"failing":[]}
```

**2. Committed regression: green on head, red on base.** Same test, only `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-control.ts` reverted to its parent:

```console
# head a921354
✓ rejects readiness timeout after a wall-clock rewind and cleans up the sensitive handoff (5016ms)
# base source (Date.now() deadline)
× rejects readiness timeout after a wall-clock rewind and cleans up the sensitive handoff
  Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.   # the rewound budget never expires, so the helper wait never settles
VERDICT=PASS head-green base-red
```

**3. Handoff deadline under a real 90 s rewind.** Isolated systemd-managed install; shipped `update.run` Gateway RPC with the real detached `managed-handoff-runtime` helper; readiness line held 12 s and a `-90 s` wall-clock step applied the moment the deadline timer arms:

| run | driver | deadline armed | handoff settlement |
|---|---|---|---|
| published 2026.10.8 | wall clock | T+8.5 s for 8 s | readiness accepted T+22.7 s (6.2 s late) |
| this head | monotonic | T+8.5 s for 8 s | terminated T+12.5 s (0.4 s late) |

```console
[run 1] wall_clock_stepped byMs=-90000 trigger=handoff-deadline-armed budgetArgMs=7999
[run 1] helper_readiness_released delayMs=12000
[run 1] managed-service update handoff durationMs=-87080
[run 2] wall_clock_stepped byMs=-90000 trigger=handoff-deadline-armed budgetArgMs=7999.96
[run 2] update.run managed-service handoff failed error=managed update handoff did not signal readiness within 8 seconds
[run 2] update.run reason=managed-service-handoff-failed rpcDurationMs=12541
```

Runs: [managed-update cell](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-managed-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/40640079137), [regression red/green](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-managed-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/40641073469).

**Open PR collision check**: searched open PR topics `handoff deadline`/`monotonic clock`/`managed-service-handoff-control` and changed-file lists — no open PR touches `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-control.ts`.

This replaces a previously closed PR carrying the identical commit (same fix, same proof); the branch is unchanged apart from being pushed from a different fork.

Workstation note: this host's systemd 239 `libsystemd` lacks `sd_bus_set_method_call_timeout`, so the published driver cannot inspect a local managed unit here; the completed upgrade therefore ran in CI's own cell (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd 257) with the same script CI uses.

prs.title: fix(daemon): use monotonic clock for scheduled task settlement deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, stopping or updating the Gateway can hang or bail out early when the system clock is adjusted: the scheduled-task settlement probe computes its deadline and remaining budget from `Date.now()` (wall clock) while the PowerShell probe's `spawnSync` timeout and the poll `sleep` are monotonic timers. A clock jump forward shrinks the probe timeout (a 280s budget collapsed to 50s, or 1ms past a 330s roll), killing PowerShell before settlement can be observed; a clock jump backward keeps the wall-clock deadline from ever elapsing, so the loop never exits. The fix uses a monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) for the deadline and remaining budget, matching the sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` in the same file.

- Problem: `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` seeds its deadline and reads the remaining budget from the wall clock (`Date.now()`), while the consuming `spawnSync` timeout and `sleep` poll are monotonic timers — a cross-clock-domain budget.
- Solution: compute `deadline`, `remaining`, and the exit comparisons with `performance.now()` so the budget lives entirely on the monotonic clock.
- What changed: all six `Date.now()` usages inside `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` in `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts` became `performance.now()`, plus a new regression test and an update to the existing settlement test's clock mock.
- What did NOT change: the caller contract (`stopScheduledTask` / `restartScheduledTask`), the settlement result shape, and the default timeout constants all remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` is the only cross-clock-domain spot left in this file: its sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` already computes `remainingTimeout()` and `expired()` from `performance.now()`, and the file's other deadline helpers use `performance.now()` too. The settlement deadline is a purely process-internal closure variable — never serialized, persisted, or compared across processes — so a full switch to the monotonic clock is safe and keeps the budget aligned with the monotonic timers that consume it. No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface is introduced. The existing `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` clock mock was moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` while preserving the test's intent (settlement exhausts the full stop budget without a false restart).

- **Best fix**: keep the budget and its consumers on one clock domain. `performance.now()` is exactly the clock the surrounding `spawnSync` timeout and poll `sleep` already use, so the deadline can no longer be skewed by a wall-clock step.
- **Alternative(s)**: (a) clamp the wall-clock delta to a maximum step — rejected because it still mixes clock domains and cannot recover a lost budget; (b) pass an injected clock through the caller contract — rejected because it widens a public signature for a purely internal deadline; (c) leave the deadline in wall-clock and shorten the probe timeout — rejected because it trades a hang for a false `settlement unavailable`.
- **Risk**: `performance.now()` is monotonic per process, so a deadline seeded before a process restart is not portable — not a concern here because the deadline is a local closure variable read only within one call. Node's `performance.now()` resolution on Windows is millisecond-class, matching the previous `Date.now()` granularity, so the sub-second comparisons keep their behavior. Boundary left unchanged: the default timeout constants and the `stop`/`restart` caller contract.

## User Impact

Windows Gateway stop/update no longer stalls or fails spuriously when the system clock is adjusted (NTP resync, manual set, DST), because the settlement deadline is no longer skewed by wall-clock jumps. The settlement still waits the full configured stop budget before declaring the task unavailable, and still refuses a restart only when settlement genuinely cannot be confirmed.

## Evidence

**Real shipped command, real runner (before/after)**: a `windows-latest` runner installs a real Scheduled-Task Gateway (`openclaw gateway install`), then runs the actual shipped `openclaw gateway stop --force` while a preload steps the wall clock (`Date.now()`; `performance.now()` stays monotonic) between the settlement deadline seed and budget read — exactly the NTP/manual-set/DST incident. Both builds drive the real `schtasks.exe`/PowerShell subprocess; the only difference is the clock source of the settlement deadline (`Date.now()` pre-fix vs `performance.now()` post-fix):

| wall-clock jump | pre-fix (Date.now deadline) | post-fix (performance.now deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| +280s (forward, in-roll) | `openclaw gateway stop` ok (50s budget) | ok (full 60s budget) |
| +380s (forward, past roll) | **stop FAILS** (1ms budget → settlement unavailable → unverified) | ok (full 60s budget, inert) |
| -280s (backward) | ok (inflated budget, over-waits) | ok (inert) |

Proof artifact + workflow: `SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof` [run #40486854535](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof/actions/runs/40486854535).

**Raw CLI output (inline, current head `e804ccc7dcd`)** — verbatim, redacted to service/port only (no IPs, keys, endpoints):

```console
$ # post-fix (performance.now deadline): clock +280s between deadline seed and budget read
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=0 elapsed=6.4801074s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": true, "result": "stopped",
  "service": { "label": "Scheduled Task", "loaded": true, "loadedText": "registered" } }
[proof-inject] settlement Date.now reads stepped: 5   # wall clock jumped, deadline monotonic -> inert
VERDICT[post-fix-forward]: STOPPED bounded completion in 6.4801074s

$ # pre-fix (Date.now deadline): same command, clock +380s (past the 330s roll) collapses remaining to 1ms
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=1 elapsed=4.443505s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": false,
  "error": "Gateway stop failed: Error: Task settlement unavailable; stop unverified.",
  "hints": ["Run openclaw gateway status --deep to inspect the service, then retry."] }
VERDICT[pre-fix-forward-380]: STOP_REFUSED exit=1
```

Under the same wall-clock jump the pre-fix build fails the very `openclaw gateway stop` that succeeds on the post-fix build: the collapsed 1ms budget times out the real PowerShell probe, settlement reports `unavailable`, and `terminate()` refuses to confirm the stop. The backward jump is equally inert post-fix (`stop exit=0 elapsed=5.41s`).

**Unit regression (forward wall-clock skew)**, pre-fix RED / post-fix GREEN:

```console
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # pre-fix (reverted to Date.now)
AssertionError: expected 50000 to be 60000   (280000 ms)
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 60000        (380000 ms)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # post-fix (monotonic)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  18 passed (18)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks.settlement.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  37 passed (37)
```

Full daemon shard: 118 files / 1943 tests passed.

Beyond the clock budget, the settlement state machine and its JSON parsing are not re-tested here: they are covered by the existing 37-test settlement suite (unchanged apart from its clock-mock alignment).

**Open PR collision check**: searched open PR topics `settlement`/`schtasks`/`monotonic clock` and changed-file lists — no open PR touches `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts` or `src/daemon/schtasks.settlement.test.ts`. The long-lived draft #138344 also edits `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts`, but its scope is scheduled-task definition listing, not the settlement deadline clock source.

This replaces a previously closed PR carrying the identical commit (same fix, same proof); the branch is unchanged apart from being pushed from a different fork.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep exec approval followup observation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an async `exec_approval_followup` run completes on the gateway, OpenClaw keeps observing it for a bounded 6-minute window before deciding whether to resume the originating session. That observation window is budgeted on the wall clock (`Date.now()`) but consumed by the monotonic timer that backs the gateway `agent.wait` RPC. When the system wall clock is adjusted (NTP step, VM clock sync, or a laptop waking from hibernation), the two clocks diverge and the observation window is distorted.

- **Problem**: `waitForAgentFollowupRun` seeds `observationDeadline = Date.now() + timeout` and reads `remainingMs = deadline - Date.now()`, passing that budget into a gateway wait consumed on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()` / `setTimeout`). Budget computed in one clock domain, spent in another.
- **Solution**: align the whole observation budget to the monotonic clock — seed `observationDeadline` and read `remainingMs` / `retryDelayMs` with `performance.now()`, matching the monotonic consumer.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.ts` (3 deadline reads `Date.now()`→`performance.now()`; per-wait budget rounded up with `Math.ceil` for the gateway `agent.wait` integer `timeoutMs` schema); the deadline regression test now controls the monotonic clock.
- **What did NOT change**: the transport retry/backoff policy and the observation lifecycle (reason `"deadline"`, `transportErrors` accounting) are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observation deadline is a pure process-local closure (never serialized/persisted/cross-process), so a monotonic clock is the only correct source. The gateway consumer already computes its own monotonic `DispatchDeadline`; passing it a wall-clock-derived remaining budget is a cross-clock-domain mismatch. Switching the three reads keeps the seed and every remaining-budget read on the same (monotonic) domain, zero external contract change.

- **Best fix**: yes — one canonical owner, no new parser/policy branch.
- **Alternative**: keep `Date.now()` and rely on the per-wait `Math.min` cap; rejected because the cap only bounds a single wait, not the total observation window, nor the `retryDelayMs <= 0` exit from a forward wall jump.
- **Risk**: low — `Math.ceil` on the remaining budget never shrinks the observation window and always yields an integer accepted by the gateway validator.

## User Impact

Exec approval follow-ups for async commands now complete on a stable, clock-skew-proof observation window. Under NTP/hibernation clock steps, a healthy agent run is no longer prematurely declared complete (dropping slow terminal output), and a finished run is no longer observed far beyond its deadline.

## Evidence

**1. Shipped exec-host public-entry clock-skew proof, both directions.** Driven through the exec-host **public shipped entry** `sendExecApprovalFollowupResult` (`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`) — the exact function `exec-host-node.ts` / `exec-host-gateway.ts` call after an approved async exec. It registers the handoff, then `sendExecApprovalFollowup` runs through the **production** `GatewayRecoveryRuntime` the Gateway registers at startup — **no** `registerGatewayRecoveryRuntime` override, **no** internal-function call. Both the `agent` dispatch (production `recovery.dispatchAgent` → real in-process `agent.run`, accepted against a synthetic-provider run that stays pending) and the wait (production `recovery.waitForAgent` → shipped wait transport) are unmodified shipped code. A 30 s wall step (−30 s / +30 s) is injected inside `waitForAgentFollowupRun` via a `Date.now` proxy; a pass-through probe on `recovery.waitForAgent` records the round-1 budget handed to the wait transport. (Observation budget shortened 6 m→20 s as a disclosed control; the per-wait cap cannot mask it.)

```console
# BACKWARD (−30s rewind)
[proof] production recovery runtime present = true (Gateway auto-registered)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=49999 -> shipped wait transport   # pre-fix: INFLATED +30s
# FORWARD (+30s jump)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED, observation proceeds
[proof] outcome=undefined elapsed=2652ms / NO agent.wait dispatched             # pre-fix: observation ENDED IMMEDIATELY (drops slow output)
```

| leg | skew | production-recovery budget (round 1) | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| post-fix | −30 s | 20000 | bounded |
| pre-fix | −30 s | 49999 | inflated +30 s |
| post-fix | +30 s | 20000 (proceeds) | bounded |
| pre-fix | +30 s | none (ends immediately) | drops slow output |

Keeping the budget on the monotonic clock makes the shipped wait budget immune to wall-clock steps in both directions. The accepted run stays the sole delivery owner (`direct_deliveries=0`; no competing direct delivery), and the integer `timeoutMs` passes the shipped `validateAgentWaitParams`.

**2. Integer-boundary proof (P2).** `performance.now()` is fractional; the `agent.wait` schema requires an integer `timeoutMs`. `sendExecApprovalFollowup` was driven through a recovery runtime whose `waitForAgent` re-runs the shipped validator on the exact params. Same fractional remaining budget (59999.75 ms), before vs after the one-line `Math.ceil`:

```console
before: [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=59999.75 -> shipped validator: REJECT
after : [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=60000   -> shipped validator: ACCEPT
```

`Math.ceil(59999.75) === 60000` never shrinks the budget; `Math.max(1, ...)` keeps the positive minimum.

**3. Regression.** Pre-fix the new test fails (`Number.isInteger(59999.75)` false); post-fix it passes, full suite green (18/18).

Not re-tested here: the clock divergence itself (NTP/hibernation) is injected by the proof, and the direct-delivery and session-resume paths are unchanged and covered by existing suites.

**Collision check**: `origin/main` still has the wall-clock reads (bug live); sibling PR #181942 touches the same three reads for the same defect; #181942 open.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep runtime auth deadline budget in the monotonic domain
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the host clock is corrected backward (NTP resync) between the moment the startup auth budget is seeded and the moment the remaining budget is read, the embedded-agent-runner stretched that budget. The seed and the read both used `Date.now()`, while the budget is consumed by a relative `setTimeout`. This change seeds the startup budget in the monotonic domain so a backward step can no longer extend it.

- Problem: `createRuntimeAuthDeadline` seeded its startup deadline with `Date.now() + timeoutMs` and read the remaining budget as `deadline.deadlineAtMs - Date.now()`. A backward jump between those two reads inflated `remainingMs`, so the startup auth exchange received far more than its configured `timeoutMs`.
- Solution: seed the startup deadline with `monotonicNow()` (frozen at creation) and read each source in its own clock domain — the startup path subtracts `monotonicNow()`, the upstream path keeps subtracting `Date.now()`.
- What changed: `src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.ts` (seed + per-source read) and a new `src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts` covering both paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the startup deadline is moved into the monotonic domain. It is the budget this helper owns: seed and read both live inside `createRuntimeAuthDeadline`, so freezing it at creation removes the seed→read jump entirely. The upstream `getDeadline()` source is a different owner's value — a wall-clock epoch by contract — and this helper does not reseed it. Reading it against `Date.now()` is therefore arithmetically unchanged, and a backward correction still stretches that one source. That is an existing upstream limitation, named here rather than claimed as fixed. The two sources are told apart by reference equality (`deadline === startupDeadline`).

- Best fix: yes for the startup budget — remove the mixed-clock seed at its single owner.
- Alternative rejected: a boundary conversion (`monotonicNow() + Math.max(0, deadlineAtMs - Date.now())` for both sources) cancels its own two `monotonicNow()` reads, so it leaves the startup seed→read stretch exactly as it was while implying protection it does not provide.
- Risk: the same-family wall-clock pattern in `attempt-async-tasks.ts` and `attempt-stream-settle.ts` and the upstream deadline epoch are untouched; they are separate follow-ups, not regressions introduced here.

## User Impact

An embedded-agent run no longer waits longer than its configured startup auth budget when the host clock steps backward during a provider authentication exchange. A stalled exchange aborts at `timeoutMs` instead of holding the run slot for the inflated budget.

## Evidence

### 1. Real stalled exchange through the shipped runner

A real `openclaw agent --local` run against `microsoft-foundry` with `apiKey: "__entra_id_dynamic__"` performs the provider's real `prepareRuntimeAuthV2` exchange, with `az` replaced by a local script that accepts the call and then never answers (a stalled authentication service). `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is 8. A preload shim reads each deadline seed on the real clock and rewinds `Date.now()` by 20s on every later read — a backward NTP step.

```console
$ CLOCK_REWIND_MS=20000 openclaw agent --local -m "hi"
[clock-probe] seed observed via performance.now; rewinding Date.now by 20000ms from here
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=-11828 error="microsoft-foundry runtime auth exchange timed out at the run deadline (7997ms). Check the provider's authentication service and retry the run." errorName=AbortError taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<redacted> modelFallbackCandidate=true
[clock-probe] exit=1 armed=true rewoundDateNowReads=95
```

`durationMs=-11828` is the rewind itself: the run measures its own duration with the `Date.now()` the shim moved back, so 20s − 8.17s ≈ 11.8s. The stalled exchange still aborted at its 7997ms budget.

### 2. Same code, pre-fix vs post-fix budget

The real `createRuntimeAuthDeadline` driven through the real `withTimeout`/`setTimeout` consumer, with the same shim and a 5000ms budget:

```text
                        pre-fix (origin/main)        post-fix (this branch)
budget fed to setTimeout    38000ms (5s + 30s step)     7999.8ms (unchanged)
```

Pre-fix source: `deadlineAtMs: Date.now() + timeoutMs` then `deadlineAtMs - Date.now()`; the 30s backward step lands entirely inside that difference. Post-fix the seed and the read are the same monotonic clock, so the step is invisible.

### 3. Behavior matrix (budget captured from `setTimeout`, 5000ms budget, clock rewound 30s)

```text
scenario                                   => pre-fix        => post-fix
startup deadline (getDeadline() undefined) => 35000ms        => 5000ms
upstream wall-clock queue deadline         => 35000ms        => 35000ms
```

The second row is the documented upstream limitation: its test pins the bounded-budget contract only, not clock-jump immunity.

### 4. Unit regression

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts --run
# pre-fix source, test kept:  expected 35000 to be less than or equal to 5000  (1 failed | 1 passed)
# post-fix:                   Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 2 passed (2)
```

`auth-controller.test.ts` (the caller's suite) passes 39/39.

**Collision check:** no open PR touches `src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.ts` or `embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.ts`; `origin/main` still carries the wall-clock seed bug.

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep the process-tree exit wait on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Windows process-tree exit wait keeps polling `tasklist.exe` far past its configured timeout when the system wall clock steps backward — `waitForProcessExit` seeds and compares its deadline on the wall clock while the probes sleep on the monotonic clock.

## User Impact

User impact: stopping a stalled Gateway startup or terminating scheduled-task listeners now always completes within its real exit-wait budget, regardless of NTP corrections or VM/laptop resume. The stop path no longer hangs on a wall-clock-inflated polling loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForProcessExit` seeds `deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs` and loops `while (Date.now() < deadline)`, while the probes sleep on the monotonic clock. A backward wall-clock step stretches the budget by the step. The rest of this file already uses the monotonic clock (lines 305, 322, 407, 424 — fixed by the #186484 sweep); this function is the leftover sibling site.

The deadline now lives on the shared monotonic owner (`monotonicDeadlineAfter` / `remainingMonotonicMs` from `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts`) per the maintainer's direction in #186484.

No stop flow, termination, or probe semantics change; behavior on a clock that never steps is identical.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock behavior via the reverted clock, regression test only: a real spawned node child stays alive, the wall clock is frozen 10 minutes behind. Stock main keeps polling past the whole budget:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/daemon/schtasks-process.monotonic.test.ts
 × ends the exit wait at its monotonic deadline when the wall clock rewinds  20000ms
   → Test timed out in 20000ms
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — the same scenario returns after the real 1500ms budget:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/daemon/schtasks-process.monotonic.test.ts
      Tests  1 passed
```

The regression spawns a **real node child process** (`process.execPath -e "setInterval"`) and polls its real exit state through the production probe path (`tasklist.exe` on Windows); only `Date.now` is rewound in-process.

**Behavior matrix** (real child alive, `timeoutMs: 1500`, wall clock frozen 10min behind):

```text
clock during wait           => exit wait returns            => result
normal (no step)            => after 1500ms budget          => false (alive)
wall rewind 10min (pre-fix)  => hangs past 20s test timeout => unbounded
wall rewind 10min (post-fix) => after 1500ms budget          => false (alive)
```

Also verified: `pnpm format:check`.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep exec approval followup observation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the post-approval exec followup observation window grows past its configured bound when the system wall clock steps backward during observation, so a turn whose followup run is accepted but unreachable keeps retrying `agent.wait` for the length of the step instead of ending observation at its deadline.

## User Impact

User impact: after a human approves an exec tool call, the followup observation window always ends after `AGENT_FOLLOWUP_OBSERVATION_TIMEOUT_MS` of real elapsed time, regardless of NTP corrections or VM/laptop resume. A turn whose accepted followup run cannot be reached stops observing at its bound instead of hanging on to a wall-clock-inflated window, and no direct-delivery race is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForAgentFollowupRun` seeds `observationDeadline` with `Date.now()` and computes `remainingMs` and the transport-retry `retryDelayMs` against the wall clock, while the budget is actually consumed by gateway round-trips and `sleepWithAbort` on the monotonic clock. A backward wall-clock step inflates every remaining-budget computation by the step length, so the loop keeps observing `6m + step` instead of `6m`; a forward step can end it early.

The deadline now lives entirely on `performance.now()` — seed, loop-top remaining check, and retry-delay clamp — which is monotonic and unaffected by wall-clock adjustments. This is the same cross-clock-domain pattern already fixed for command process-group teardown in #174151 and the orphaned-process reap grace deadline in #181335; the exec approval followup observation window is the sibling site left on the wall clock. Node 16+ exposes a global `performance`, so no import is required.

The pre-existing deadline test drove the deadline by mocking `Date.now`; it now advances monotonic time with fake timers, preserving its original assertion that the deadline ends observation without competing direct delivery.

No parser, policy branch, configuration surface, or gateway protocol change; behavior on a clock that never steps is identical.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main (`97d96e53d22f`), regression test only. Fake timers advance monotonic time 6m10s while `vi.setSystemTime` rewinds the wall clock 1h mid-observation (same two-clock separation as #181335/#174151); the observation loop is still pending after its entire budget:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.test.ts -t rewinds
 × exec approval followup > ends observation at its monotonic deadline when the wall clock rewinds  420ms
   → expected 'still-pending' to be 'settled'
      Tests  1 failed | 17 skipped (18)
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — same test with the fix settles inside the window, and the full affected file passes through the agents-core vitest project:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.test.ts
 ✓ ends observation at its monotonic deadline when the wall clock rewinds
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

**Behavior matrix** (accepted followup run, gateway unreachable, wall clock rewound 1h mid-observation):

```text
clock during observation       => observation ends            => result
normal (no step)                => after 6m budget            => bounded
wall rewind 1h (pre-fix)        => after 6m + 1h (retries on) => inflated by step
wall rewind 1h (post-fix)       => after 6m budget            => bounded
```

Also verified: `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm tsgo:core` typecheck pass on the changed tree. Regression test drives the real `sendExecApprovalFollowup` → `waitForAgentFollowupRun` path with only the gateway transport mocked (the same boundary the existing suite mocks); the local bundled-gateway proof path is not runnable on this Windows contributor box and was not used as evidence.



### Real runtime proof (real timers, boundary trace, in-process wall-clock rewind)

Same scenario executed twice with real timers — no fake clocks: the real `sendExecApprovalFollowup` runs through the accepted-run observation loop while its `agent.wait` boundary fails for real on every round trip (a locally registered recovery-runtime boundary; retry pacing is the module's real 1s `sleepWithAbort` sleeps). Ten seconds into the six-minute window, `Date.now` alone is rewound 30 minutes in-process (NTP-correction analogue); `performance.now()` keeps reporting real elapsed time. The trace identifies each boundary interaction: accepted run, injected wait failures, rollback, bounded settlement, and the outbound message boundary asserting **zero** competing direct deliveries.

```console
TRACE[exec-followup] t=6ms     boundary: dispatchAgent -> {status:"accepted", runId:"proof-run"}
TRACE[exec-followup] t=7ms     boundary: waitForAgent round trip #1 -> transport failure (gateway unreachable)
TRACE[exec-followup] t=10004ms wall clock rewound by -1800000ms (in-process Date.now injection)
... wait failures continue once per second ...
PROOF[exec-followup] variant=old   budget=360000ms wall_rewind=-1800000ms -> state=still-observing-at-cap agent_wait_failures=376 direct_deliveries=0 elapsed_real_ms=375008

TRACE[exec-followup] t=360039ms boundary: sendExecApprovalFollowup settled (observation ended, delivery owner unchanged)
PROOF[exec-followup] variant=fixed budget=360000ms wall_rewind=-1800000ms -> state=settled:true          agent_wait_failures=361 direct_deliveries=0 elapsed_real_ms=360040
```

Stock main keeps observing 15s past the whole 360s budget (and would continue for the length of the rewind); with this PR the observation ends at 360.04s of real time with the accepted run still the sole delivery owner. The recovery-runtime boundary stands in for the gateway transport client, which cannot run on this Windows contributor box (Linux-only bundled gateway, disclosed); every timed behavior on the measured path is the module's real code. The regression test keeps its settlement check entirely on fake time (observer attached before advancing, no real timers left behind).
