prs.title: fix(bedrock): resolve the in. India inference-profile prefix for known context windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw on Amazon Bedrock reports the conservative 32,000-token context window for models discovered through India-geo inference profiles, because the discovery code strips the `us.`/`eu.`/`ap.`/`apac.`/`au.`/`jp.`/`global.` geo prefixes but not the `in.` India prefix.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock users in India Regions (Mumbai/Hyderabad) whose inference profiles use the `in.` prefix get every known model's context window collapsed to the 32,000-token unknown-model fallback, so context budgeting and compaction under-size models that resolve correctly in other geographies. This includes the Kimi K3 India profile `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3` documented on its AWS model card.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveKnownContextWindow` and the SYSTEM_DEFINED profile base-model extraction in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` share a geo-prefix alternation that predates the India geography. AWS documents India geo inference IDs like `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3` on the Kimi K3 model card (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3.html — "Geo inference ID: `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3`" routing across Mumbai/Hyderabad). Without `in` in the alternation:

- an `in.`-prefixed profile with empty model ARNs fails the base-model extraction, so it cannot inherit the foundation model's capabilities or context window, and
- `resolveKnownContextWindow("in.<known-model>")` misses the catalog entry and falls back to 32,000.

This adds `in` to both alternations, matching how `au.`/`apac.` were handled when those geographies were introduced (the existing regional-prefix test covers that history).

## What Was Changed

- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts`: added `in` to the geo-prefix alternations in `resolveKnownContextWindow` and the SYSTEM_DEFINED profile base-model extraction.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`: extended the existing `au.`/`apac.` regional-prefix test with an `in.` profile and asserted it resolves the base model's known 1,000,000-token window.

Not changed: `isKnownClaudeMythosPreviewModelId` (its `[/.:]`-anchored pattern already matches prefixed ids without stripping), the catalog entries, the 32,000 fallback, and `defaultContextWindow` config.

## Evidence

Real before/after on stock main (only the AWS SDK transport mocked; `discoverBedrockModels` is the production discovery path):

```text
before: an in.xai.grok-4.6 system profile (empty model ARNs, forcing the
        prefix fallback) was discovered but received the 32,000 fallback:
        expected { id: 'in.xai.grok-4.6', …(6) } to match object { contextWindow: 500000 }
after:  full discovery.test.ts — 21/21 passed, including
        "resolves au., apac., and in. prefixes for regional inference profiles"
```

- Focused full-file suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` — 21/21 passed.
- Format check (re-run after formatter write) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check: both alternations on main still lack `in`, so the fix is not already upstream.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the change extends two existing regex alternations and reuses the existing test helper, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- The `in.` prefix only strips when followed by a dot at the start of the id, exactly like the existing geo prefixes; Bedrock foundation model ids are `vendor.model` shaped, so no vendor namespace collides with `in.`.
- If AWS introduces another geography prefix later, it needs the same one-token addition.

## Discovery-path evidence addendum (2026-11-16)

Shipped-entry attempt, stated plainly: the discovery chain runs inside the Gateway's prepared model catalog through the bundled plugin's live provider catalog. In this sandbox that path could not be driven end to end - `models list --refresh` against a Gateway built from this branch tree (fake Bedrock control plane on loopback via AWS_ENDPOINT_URL with synthetic credentials and ap-south-1) never invoked the plugin catalog because provider-catalog admission in the prepared runtime requires production provider gating this environment cannot satisfy; the fake endpoint received zero calls, and no shipped trace is claimed.

What is verified remains the plugin's own discovery contract through the real resolver and SDK-shape fixtures: `pnpm test extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` -> 21 passed on the branch tree, including the new `resolves au., apac., and in. prefixes for regional inference profiles` case that fails on the base (in. profile absent) and pins `in.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` resolving the base model's known 1,000,000-token context window through the prefix fallback, alongside the existing au./apac. coverage. A shipped run needs a real (or credentialed fake satisfying catalog admission) AWS environment.

prs.title: fix(cli): observe ambient cancellation on cron CLI reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cron CLI read helpers still called `callGatewayFromCli` directly instead of the SIGINT-aware `callCronReadFromCli`:

- `warnIfCronSchedulerDisabled` (used by every `cron` mutation command before touching the scheduler) calls `cron.status`.
- `buildCronCommandShellArgvForGateway` (used by `cron add --command` / `cron edit --command` on non-Linux platforms) calls `system.info`.

When the Gateway is unreachable or slow, pressing Ctrl-C leaves the CLI hanging on these reads because they never observe the async work signal. The rest of the cron CLI already routes reads through `callCronReadFromCli` (see #197315 and #198012); these two helpers were missed.

## Solution

Route both reads through `callCronReadFromCli`, which passes the CLI's abort signal when an `AsyncWorkScope` is active and falls back to a plain call otherwise. No behavior change when no cancellation is in progress.

## Evidence

### Unit regressions

- New `it.each` test in `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` drives both helpers inside an `AsyncWorkScope` and **holds** the mocked read, so the read can only settle through the CLI abort listener. It asserts the held read received an `AbortSignal`, that closing the scope with an AbortError (SIGINT) actually aborts it, and that the cancelled read produces no stdout, stderr, or exit call. (The earlier revision resolved the mocked read before closing the scope, so it only asserted an internal argument shape and never exercised cancellation; that is fixed here.)
- Each parameterized case resets the shared RPC mock first (`resetGatewayMock()`), so the two cases each inspect their own request rather than a previous case's call.
- RED: reverting only `warnIfCronSchedulerDisabled` to the uncancelled call fails exactly its own case (`1 failed | 1 passed`), which confirms each case pins its own helper.
- GREEN: after the fix, `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` passes — 75/75 tests. `run-format.mts --check` clean on the changed file.

### Real-process behavior proof (captured terminal traces)

I ran the real CLI entrypoint (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts cron add --cron "* * * * *" --command "echo hello" --name ... --json`) against a minimal WebSocket Gateway peer on loopback. The peer logs every request and every socket close, so the trace shows whether the CLI actually aborted the held read. Both scenarios were run on the base commit (`ab5a6d417f7`, before the fix) and on this PR's head (`369323c12bb`).

**Scenario A — pre-mutation `system.info` held** (the `buildCronCommandShellArgvForGateway` path):

Base (`ab5a6d417f7`) — CLI hangs, killed by the deadlock guard:

```
CLI reached held system.info read; sending SIGINT
RESULT: CLI HUNG 31839ms after SIGINT without exiting; killed with SIGKILL
+11195ms req system.info id=2:5b819629-...
+11196ms HOLD system.info (no response until the client aborts)
+41153ms client closed socket while system.info was held
--- cli output ---
Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error",
  "message": "gateway timeout after 30000ms\nGateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:35265\n..." } }
```

Head (`369323c12bb`) — CLI exits on its own:

```
CLI reached held system.info read; sending SIGINT
RESULT: CLI exited on its own 741ms after SIGINT (exit code 130)
+10708ms req system.info id=2:fa06cb88-...
+10708ms HOLD system.info (no response until the client aborts)
+10778ms client closed socket while system.info was held
--- cli output ---
Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
```

**Scenario B — post-mutation `cron.status` held** (the `warnIfCronSchedulerDisabled` path, where the mutation receipt must survive):

Base (`ab5a6d417f7`) — CLI waits out the full 30s Gateway timeout:

```
CLI completed cron.add and reached held cron.status; sending SIGINT
RESULT: CLI exited on its own 30636ms after SIGINT (exit code 130)
+11663ms res cron.add -> mutation receipt {id:job-proof-1}
+11672ms HOLD cron.status (post-mutation read; no response until the client aborts)
+41677ms client closed socket while cron.status was held
```

Head (`369323c12bb`) — read aborted immediately, receipt still printed:

```
CLI completed cron.add and reached held cron.status; sending SIGINT
RESULT: CLI exited on its own 637ms after SIGINT (exit code 130)
+12070ms res cron.add -> mutation receipt {id:job-proof-1}
+12085ms HOLD cron.status (post-mutation read; no response until the client aborts)
+12205ms client closed socket while cron.status was held
--- cli output ---
{ "id": "job-proof-1", "name": "cancelled-status-proof", "enabled": true }
Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
```

Scenario B is the key one for the "mutations keep waiting for their receipt" contract: the `cron.add` receipt is emitted in full **and** the CLI exits in 637ms instead of 30s.

### Process-level regression test

`src/cli/cron-cli-cancelled.process.test.ts` automates Scenario A: the shipped CLI against a real WebSocket mock Gateway that holds the pre-mutation `system.info` read, SIGINT delivered, then asserting prompt exit.

- **After the fix:** exits with `signal: null`.
- **Before the fix (base):** hangs on the held request; the deadlock guard kills it with `SIGKILL`, so the assertion fails.

prs.title: fix(exec): keep the exit wake when the session id rotates
prs.body:
## Problem

A background exec captures the session generation (session id and lifecycle revision) when it starts. If the session row changes while the command runs, admission refuses the completion with `SessionDeliveryGenerationRevokedError`. The only record is a Gateway log line: `exec: completion delivery failed (...)`. The model and the user get no wake and no notice.

## Paths that change the session row of one key during a run

Same conversation, new session id, same lifecycle revision:

- Context-engine compaction successor: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-successor.ts:241` patches only `sessionId`.
- Embedded runner adoption of a rotated id: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-prompt-state.ts:102-110`.
- Agent-command rollover without an automatic reset: `src/agents/agent-command.ts:308-325`.
- Cron run session rollover: `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts:459`.

New lifecycle revision (the user or a policy started a different conversation state):

- `/new`, `/reset`, Gateway reset: `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts:764-784`; reply path `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:610`.
- Idle or daily rollover: `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:610`, `src/agents/agent-command.ts:311-313`.
- Rewind, branch switch and fork: `src/config/sessions/session-message-cut-plan.ts:329`.
- A Gateway `agent` request that names a new `sessionId` for an existing key: `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-patch.ts:157-162`.

Delete removes the row.

## Fix

Before admission, the completion reads the current row of its session key (`followSessionEventTargetForHost` in `session-event-target.ts`):

- Same lifecycle revision: the target follows the new session id. The wake is delivered. The captured authority, settings and route stay the same.
- New lifecycle revision: the wake is withheld. A visible transcript note goes to the current session: `Background command result withheld (<process id>, <exit>): the conversation was reset, rewound or moved to a new session after the command started. Its output stays in process log.` The note is excluded from model context.
- Row deleted: the wake is withheld and a warning is logged. No transcript exists to hold a note.

If the read fails, the old path runs and admission still checks the captured generation.

### Rewind, switch and fork

These paths mint a new lifecycle revision on purpose. Owners of the old revision (workspace custody, transcript writers, lifecycle authority) must stop. A command started before a rewind belongs to the discarded branch. Its result can describe state that the new branch never saw. Thus the completion does not wake the rewound conversation. The user sees the withheld note, and the model can read the output with `process log` if needed. The lifecycle revision stays the only fence; this change does not add a second rule beside it.

## Proof

- vitest-source (`ocx test`): two new tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` use a real background exec, the real session store and real session-event admission (model mocked).
  - Rotate the session id mid-exec (same lifecycle revision): the wake turn runs on the new session id. Red on the merge base (`Session event was not admitted`), green here.
  - Reset mid-exec (new lifecycle revision): no wake, and the visible note is in the transcript. Red on the merge base, green here.
  - All tests in the four touched exec-notify and session-event test files pass.
- source (`ocx src`, scratch Gateway, scripted OpenAI-compatible model), compaction successor (same lifecycle):
  - A test-only context engine returns a compaction successor `sessionTarget` with a new session id (`compaction-successor.ts:241` path).
  - Turn 1 starts a real `sleep 25` background exec. While it runs, `sessions.compact` moves the key from `64fec7b4…` to `compacted-1c7e…` (base) and from `b153c1ee…` to `compacted-429c…` (this branch). The lifecycle revision stays the same in both runs.
  - Merge base `febd4dcc21c4`: `session event execution failed source=exec … error="Session event was not admitted; retry against the current session"`, then `exec: completion delivery failed`. The model gets no wake request.
  - This branch: the model gets one wake request that carries the command output. The wake turn and its reply are in the transcript of the successor session `compacted-429c…`.
- source, forced new lifecycle (Gateway `agent` request with a new `sessionId` for the same key, real `sleep 15` background exec):
  - Merge base: `SessionDeliveryGenerationRevokedError` in the log, no wake, nothing in the transcript.
  - This branch: no wake, and the `Background command result withheld (...)` note is in the new session's transcript.
- Gates: `tsgo:core`, `check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files, `ocx build --dts`.

prs.title: fix(agents): pin the expected state in exec wait guidance
prs.body:
## Problem

Agents write their own PR and CI waiters. The exec guidance tells them to "run one command that loops until it holds". Many such waiters read the PR head live. Right after a push, they can see the old head as settled and exit at once (a stale-commit race). The exec exit wake stays the only way to wait; this PR does not add a wait tool.

## Change

- `EXEC_WAIT_RECIPE` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-output.ts`), the one shared wait text for the exec description and the running-result follow-up, now adds: "To wait on a change you caused, pin the expected state: for example, wait for the exact commit you pushed and exit non-zero if it moved."
- `skills/github/SKILL.md`: the "Wait for CI" recipe now takes the pushed head SHA and uses only `gh`. It reads the check runs of that exact commit and exits `0` (pass), `1` (fail) or `11` (head moved). It runs as one background exec whose exit wakes the chat. The old `gh pr checks --watch` example is removed, because it reads the live head and has the same race.
- `docs/tools/exec.md` and `docs/gateway/background-process.md` describe the new sentence.
- The follow-up test asserts the new sentence.

## Proof

- Tier 1, `ocx test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts`: 24/24 pass.
- The skill recipe, run against live `openclaw/openclaw` PRs (sleep shortened for the test):
  - merged PR, its head SHA: `PASS`, exit 0
  - open PR with a failed check, its head SHA: `FAIL` plus the failed run, exit 1
  - open PR, a wrong SHA: `HEAD-MOVED expected=… actual=…` after the grace polls, exit 11
- Gates: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, `check:test-types`, `prompt:snapshots:check` (clean `HOME`): pass.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep backup remote guard remedies in --json error output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup verify bogus-key --from archive --json` exits 1 with a stderr that only says the command failed, even though the guard that rejected the key already carries the exact next step: "Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest." The same happens for the storage-location probe failure, the empty-location listing, and the missing-key guard in the remote backup flow, and for the upload size-confirmation guard on `backup create --to`. This converts those five operator-facing guards to the canonical expected-CLI-error owner so the remedy survives the `--json` lane, with identical message text.

- Problem: `src/commands/backup-remote.ts` throws plain `Error` for five operator-facing guards. In the `--json` lane `runCommandWithRuntime` rethrows plain errors to the root renderer, which generalizes them to a two-line banner; the remedy text that the guard already wrote is lost to scripts and automation reading stderr.
- Solution: replace each of the five `throw new Error(...)` sites with `throwExpectedCliError(...)` from `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, keeping every message byte-identical. `ExpectedCliError` carries `humanOutput`/`machineOutput`, so the JSON failure envelope keeps the same message and stderr keeps the remedy.
- What changed: `src/commands/backup-remote.ts` (one import plus five guard conversions: location probe, stored-size confirmation, backup-key shape, empty listing, missing key) and `src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts` (a class assertion folded into the existing offsite integration case, net 0 test lines).
- What did NOT change: guard message texts, JSON failure envelope shape and content, exit codes, text-lane output, the internal rethrow in `openBackupLocation`, and adjacent owners (`resolveBackupNamespace` in `src/infra/backup-retention.ts`, `src/commands/backup-namespace.ts`, the registration-layer `--namespace requires --from` guard).

## Why This Change Was Made

Best fix: reuse the repository's canonical `ExpectedCliError` owner instead of formatting JSON stderr per site; this is the same conversion already merged for the sibling backup guards (#199763 `backup create --to`, #199850 `backup git` scope, #199760 sqlite snapshot sources, #199573 record guards, #199562 shared path guards), so the remote flow joins the family behavior instead of inventing a new policy. Alternative considered: converting the neighboring `resolveBackupNamespace` guard too — rejected because it lives in a different owner file and belongs to its own change; the matrix keeps it as an untouched plain-error control. Risk: the stored-size confirmation guard cannot be triggered naturally without a storage backend that misreports object sizes, so its runtime cell is not claimed (see What was not tested); its conversion is message-identical and symmetric with the four exercised guards.

## User Impact

Operators and scripts driving `openclaw backup verify/restore --from <location>` (and `backup create --to`) with `--json` now get the actionable remedy on stderr when a guard rejects the request — which key format to use, which `openclaw storage test`/`storage init` step to run, or that the location/namespace holds no such backup — instead of a generic failure banner. Text-lane users, JSON envelopes, and exit codes see no change.

## Evidence

| Case | Before (base `6d6b7b7`) | After (this head `b3f948f`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backup verify bogus-key --from probe-loc --json` stderr | generalized banner `The CLI command failed.` | remedy `Expected a backup key from \`openclaw backup list --from <location>\` or latest.` |
| `backup verify latest --from archive --namespace probe-ns --json` (empty location) stderr | generalized banner | `No backups in archive/probe-ns.` |
| `backup verify <missing-key> --from archive --namespace probe-ns --json` stderr | generalized banner | `Backup <missing-key> was not found in archive/probe-ns.` |
| JSON failure envelope (stdout, every guard) | `{ok:false,error:{type:"cli_error",message:<remedy>}}` | byte-identical (`cmp`) |
| text-lane stderr (every guard) | remedy present | remedy present, byte-identical (`cmp`) |
| success listing `backup list --from archive --namespace probe-ns` (control) | exit 0, key listed | exit 0, byte-identical (`cmp`) |
| adjacent-owner namespace guard `--namespace "bad ns"` (control) | text real message / json banner | byte-identical both lanes (`cmp`) |

### End-to-end shipped proof (dual-arm built launcher)

Both arms were built from source with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup` (per-package `node_modules` symlinked first; build exit 0 on both). The base arm is frozen at `origin/main` commit `6d6b7b7`; the head arm is commit `b3f948f`. Each cell runs the real built launcher `node openclaw.mjs <command>` under `env -i` with a fresh `chmod 700` scratch `HOME` / `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, no credentials and no mocks. The storage location is a real filesystem provider initialized with `openclaw storage init archive` and a synthetic passphrase; the success-path object is provisioned by a real `openclaw backup create --to archive --namespace probe-ns --only-config` run (618 plaintext bytes, 762 stored), and its bytes are preserved across arms so the listing is deterministic. `--version` self-reports each arm's commit:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (6d6b7b7)   # base arm
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (b3f948f)   # head arm
```

Guard cells, base vs head `--json` stderr (the discriminating stream). A deterministic log-append notice (`log file append failed; records dropped; ... file=openclaw-2026-11-16.log`) appears identically on both arms in every stderr and is part of the `cmp` invariants; it is an isolated-`HOME` environment artifact, not a behavior change.

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup verify bogus-key --from probe-loc --json   # exit 1
# BASE stderr:
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
# HEAD stderr:
Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest.
```

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup verify latest --from archive --namespace probe-ns --json   # empty location, exit 1
# BASE stderr:
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
# HEAD stderr:
No backups in archive/probe-ns.
```

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup verify 20260102T000000Z-22222222.tar.gz --from archive --namespace probe-ns --json   # exit 1
# BASE stderr:
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
# HEAD stderr:
Backup 20260102T000000Z-22222222.tar.gz was not found in archive/probe-ns.
```

The JSON failure envelope on stdout already carried the remedy on the base arm and is unchanged by the fix (byte-identical across arms for every guard):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest."
  }
}
```

The text lane already showed the remedy on both arms (byte-identical):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup verify bogus-key --from probe-loc   # exit 1, stderr both arms
Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest.
```

Success-path control — the provisioned encrypted object lists identically on both arms (exit 0, `cmp` stdout identical):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup list --from archive --namespace probe-ns
20261116T022411Z-528ae870.tar.gz  618 bytes (762 stored)
```

### Cross-arm invariants (`cmp`)

A 26-assertion compare script ran over both arms' captured stdout/stderr/exit for every cell: `FAILED=0`. It asserts, per converted guard, exit 1 both arms/lanes, empty text stdout, remedy present in text stderr both arms, remedy present in head json stderr, remedy absent + generalized banner in base json stderr, and byte-identical json stdout envelope and text stdout. Controls (`c1` already-Expected registration guard, `g2` storage-layer absent-directory error, `c3` adjacent-owner namespace guard, `c2` success listing) assert all four streams + exit byte-identical across arms, and that `g2`/`c3` keep the real text message + generalized json banner on BOTH arms (over-conversion check).

### Built-bundle self-attestation

The shipped bundles prove the executed form. Base `dist/backup-remote-DvIBe8s3.mjs` has 0 `throwExpectedCliError`; head `dist/backup-remote-Dp8-Qwbd.mjs` has 6 (5 guards + 1 import). All five converted sites, message text unchanged:

```text
key-shape (:258)   BASE: )===void 0)throw new Error("Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from
                   HEAD: id 0)throwExpectedCliError("Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from
empty-list (:268)  BASE: !e)throw new Error(`No backups in ${t.from}/${r}.`);con
                   HEAD: owExpectedCliError(`No backups in ${t.from}/${r}.`);con
not-found (:272)   BASE: ;if(!o)throw new Error(`Backup ${e} was not found
                   HEAD: )throwExpectedCliError(`Backup ${e} was not found
probe (:58)        BASE: Error(r.message??`Storage location ${e}: ${r.state}. Run \`openclaw storage t
                   HEAD: wExpectedCliError(r.message??`Storage location ${e}: ${r.state}. Run \`openclaw storage t
stored-size (:151) BASE: ytes)throw new Error(`Stored backup size could not be confirmed for ${e.to
                   HEAD: toredBytes)throwExpectedCliError(`Stored backup size could not be confirmed for ${e.to
```

Base-arm `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` stack confirms a plain `Error` reaching the root renderer (absolute paths sanitized to neutral placeholders):

```text
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest.
[openclaw] Error: Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest.
[openclaw]     at withDownloadedBackup (file:///<base>/dist/backup-remote-DvIBe8s3.mjs:7:248)
[openclaw]     at backupRemoteVerifyCommand (file:///<base>/dist/backup-remote-DvIBe8s3.mjs:7:962)
[openclaw]     at async runCommandWithRuntime (file:///<base>/dist/cli-utils-Cz2q-7HD.mjs:3:233)
```

### Regression test (red on base, green with the fix)

A class assertion was folded into the existing offsite integration case (net 0 test lines): `await expect(backupRemoteVerifyCommand(defaultRuntime, { from: "archive", archive: "x" })).rejects.toSatisfy(isExpectedCliError)`. Message assertions cannot discriminate the class because the harness renders both classes with the same text, so the assertion targets the error class directly.

```console
# BASE (source at 6d6b7b7, test kept): 1 failed | 3 passed
FAIL  src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts > ... refuses uninitialized storage, then uploads, lists, verifies and stages an encrypted archive
Error: expect(received).toSatisfy()
Expected value to satisfy: [Function isExpectedCliError]
Received: [Error: Expected a backup key from `openclaw backup list --from <location>` or latest.]

# HEAD (b3f948f): 4 passed (4)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Open PR collision check

Searched the submission-day open-PR snapshot by changed file (`src/commands/backup-remote.ts`) and by anchor/anti-pattern keywords across three lanes (per-PR changed-file intersection, stem search, recent-created search); zero open PRs touch this file or convert these guards. The sibling backup-guard conversions already merged (#199763, #199850, #199760, #199573, #199562) cover other owner files, not `backup-remote.ts`.

### What was not tested

- The stored-size confirmation guard (:151) cannot be triggered naturally without a storage backend that misreports object sizes; no runtime cell is claimed for it. Its conversion is message-identical and symmetric with the exercised guards, and the bundle snippet above proves the executed form.
- The location-probe guard (:58) fires only when `openStorageLocation` succeeds but the subsequent `probe()` returns non-ok — a TOCTOU race for the filesystem provider, not deterministically reachable in an isolated single-process run. The absent-directory cell (`g2`) is thrown earlier by the storage-layer owner (`StorageLocationError`, a plain `Error`) and is kept as an untouched adjacent-owner control; :58's conversion is proven by the bundle snippet.
- Only the filesystem storage provider was exercised (the sole built-in provider); no network object store was used.
- The deterministic log-append notice in every stderr is an isolated-`HOME` artifact present identically on both arms; it is not addressed by this change.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep backup archive verification remedies in --json error output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup verify <missing-archive> --json` prints the full operator remedy to stdout's JSON envelope but only a generic two-line fallback (`The CLI command failed. / For help, run openclaw doctor.`) to stderr, so an operator reading the terminal in JSON mode has no actionable next step. Converting the archive-verification summary error to `ExpectedCliError` keeps the same remedy text on stderr in JSON mode without changing the stdout envelope or exit code.

- Problem: `prepareBackupArchive()` wraps every archive-verification failure in a plain `Error`. In JSON mode `runCommandWithRuntime` rethrows plain `Error`s, and the root renderer only emits a generic failure line to stderr; the structured message survives only in the stdout envelope.
- Solution: Replace `throw new Error(...)` in `prepareBackupArchive()` with `throwExpectedCliError(...)`. `ExpectedCliError` carries `humanOutput` and `machineOutput`, so `formatCliFailureLines`/`formatCliJsonFailure` render the same remedy to stderr in both text and JSON modes.
- What changed: `src/commands/backup-verify.ts` imports `throwExpectedCliError` and uses it at the single `prepareBackupArchive` summary wrapper. A single-use intermediate `Set` is inlined at its one call site so the file stays within the repository line-cap ratchet after the new import. `src/commands/backup-verify.test.ts` folds the two existing failure cases (missing/directory and invalid header) to assert the rethrown `ExpectedCliError` shape directly instead of `runtime.error`/`runtime.exit`. `test/cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts` adds a stderr-remedy assertion to the existing JSON-failure case.
- What did NOT change: guard conditions, message text, exit codes, the JSON stdout envelope, the parser, renderers, or any production export. Text-mode stderr output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareBackupArchive` is the canonical owner introduced to wrap every archive-verification failure so that direct verify, `backup restore`, and `backup create --verify` share one diagnostic boundary. Converting the wrapper's throw preserves that design and covers manifest, path-header, and SQLite snapshot failures in one change instead of per-guard edits.

- **Best fix**: Yes. The wrapper is the single point where all archive-verification errors are already summarized with a user-facing prefix; this is the narrowest change that fixes every failure mode for every shared caller.
- **Alternative(s)**: Converting only the three preflight guards (missing/directory/invalid) would leave manifest and path-header failures on the generic path and would require an extra branch to preserve any existing `ExpectedCliError`. Editing the CLI renderer instead would change behavior for every plain `Error` in the codebase. Both are wider or less complete.
- **Risk**: `ExpectedCliError` extends `Error`, so shared callers that propagate or format the rejected error see the same message. Internal callers (create `--verify`, remote, doctor schema guard, update worker) already handle failures through generic `formatErrorMessage`/diagnostics, so the subtype change is additive. The only observable change is JSON-mode stderr now carries the remedy that was already in the stdout envelope.

## User Impact

Operators running `backup verify` (or `backup restore` / `backup create --verify`) against a bad archive in `--json` mode now see the same actionable remedy on stderr that text mode already showed, instead of a generic doctor hint. The JSON stdout envelope and exit code are unchanged, so machine consumers are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before/after comparison

| Case | Before (base, origin/main) | After (candidate) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backup verify <missing> --json` stderr | `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` + doctor hint | `Backup archive verification failed: <missing>. Archive does not exist. Check the path and run \`openclaw backup verify <archive>\` again.` |
| `backup verify <directory> --json` stderr | generic two-line fallback | `... Archive must be a regular file. Choose a backup archive created by \`openclaw backup create\` and try again.` |
| `backup verify <invalid.tar.gz> --json` stderr | progress logs + generic two-line fallback | progress logs + `... Archive is not a valid OpenClaw backup. ... Choose another archive or create a new one with \`openclaw backup create\`.` |
| `backup verify <missing>` (text, control) | full remedy on stderr | full remedy on stderr (unchanged) |
| `backup restore <missing> --target <dir> --json` stderr | generic two-line fallback | full remedy on stderr (shared wrapper) |
| JSON stdout envelope, all failure cases | `{ ok: false, error: { type: "cli_error", message: "<full remedy>" } }`, exit 1 | identical envelope, exit 1 (byte-for-byte) |

### End-to-end shipped proof

Both arms built independently from the same parent commit with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`; each launcher self-reports the identical commit via `node openclaw.mjs --version`. Isolated scratch `HOME`/state/config, no credentials or mocks.

Built-bundle self-proof:

```text
# base bundle (backup-verify chunk)
throw new Error(`Backup archive verification failed: ${r}. ${t}`)

# candidate bundle (backup-verify chunk)
throwExpectedCliError(`Backup archive verification failed: ${r}. ${t}`)
```

Real command runs. Two symmetric harness-noise lines are omitted because they appear identically on both arms and are unrelated to the fix: the Node 24.19.0 security warning, and `[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped ... file=openclaw-2026-11-16.log` (the scratch HOME has no writable log path):

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs backup verify <scratch>/missing.tar.gz --json
[base stderr]
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.

[candidate stderr]
Backup archive verification failed: <scratch>/missing.tar.gz. Archive does not exist. Check the path and run `openclaw backup verify <archive>` again.

[both stdout, byte-for-byte identical]
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Backup archive verification failed: <scratch>/missing.tar.gz. Archive does not exist. Check the path and run `openclaw backup verify <archive>` again."
  }
}
exit 1
```

Text-mode control (unchanged between arms):

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs backup verify <scratch>/missing.tar.gz
Backup archive verification failed: <scratch>/missing.tar.gz. Archive does not exist. Check the path and run `openclaw backup verify <archive>` again.
exit 1
```

Shared `backup restore` channel confirms the wrapper fix reaches all callers:

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs backup restore <scratch>/missing.tar.gz --target <scratch>/target --json
[base stderr]      [openclaw] The CLI command failed. ... doctor hint
[candidate stderr] Backup archive verification failed: <scratch>/missing.tar.gz. Archive does not exist. ... (same remedy)
[both stdout]      identical { ok: false, error: { type: "cli_error", message: "..." } }, exit 1
```

Invariants verified with `cmp`: JSON stdout envelopes identical across arms for missing/directory/invalid/restore; text-mode stderr identical; exit codes identical (all 1).

### Regression tests

- `src/commands/backup-verify.test.ts`: the two existing failure cases now assert `name: "ExpectedCliError"` plus `message`/`humanOutput`/`machineOutput`. Base arm (production reverted) fails these assertions with `name: "Error"`; candidate arm passes. Full file: 40 passed, 1 skipped.
- `backup-verify-completeness`, `backup-verify.utf8`, `backup-legacy-hardlinks`, `backup-restore`: 72 passed.
- `doctor-update-schema-guard`, `database-migration-capture`: 35 passed (shared `verifyBackupArchive` callers).
- `test/cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts`: existing JSON-failure case now also asserts stderr contains the remedy; passes on candidate.

### Open PR collision check

Searched all open pull requests by changed-file list (full snapshot, not only title/body keywords). No open PR modifies the `prepareBackupArchive` wrapper or the error-classification path in `src/commands/backup-verify.ts`. Two open PRs (#194566, #192698) touch the same file but only the hardlink-target resolution block (around lines 541-610), disjoint from this change at the verification-summary wrapper.

Related: #199869 converts nine restore-input guards in `src/commands/backup-restore.ts` and deliberately leaves the shared archive-verification path generic; its file set is disjoint from this PR, so either merge order needs no rebase. After both land, `backup restore` with a bad archive also keeps the remedy on stderr, which extends that PR's missing-archive control cell by design.

### What was not tested

- `backup create --verify` and `backup remote` were not exercised end-to-end with a built CLI in this run; they share the same `verifyBackupArchive`/`prepareBackupArchive` wrapper and are covered by unit tests.
- Windows path handling was not exercised on a Windows host.

prs.title: fix(security): stop interrupted deep audit probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw security audit --deep` keeps its Gateway probe running after an accepted interrupt. With a naturally pending TCP connection, the base command takes another 3.65–4.08 seconds and prints a complete late timeout audit report. Our observed base runs exit 130/143; we did not observe a watchdog kill.

## User Impact

SIGINT (the signal Ctrl-C delivers) and SIGTERM stop the read-only audit promptly, without printing an audit report after the interrupt notice. Findings, policy, authentication fields, ordinary failures and `--fix` output are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing command lifetime signal through the audit context to the existing signal-aware `probeGateway` owner. Check cancellation before creating probe findings and before printing the report. `--fix` retains its existing mutation/receipt lifetime.

The options type stays private in audit.ts. Its proposed move was not needed: the signal is a native type, and LSP found no consumer of the moved options except audit.ts itself. The original audit.types.ts surface is restored unchanged. All 28 importers were checked: the other consumers import only the existing finding/report contracts; no credential-bearing option fields were added to those contracts.

## Evidence

Base: `c0166c395cf81095f431808c9496cb6022ad4387`. Final candidate: `4552938838ce9bf0f9ec59747715aa76a9ac2301` (production unchanged from paired-proof head `049407e5e5e643edaa4ba7e880fa9c3af034db7a`).

Host source tier, through ocx in a PTY, with isolated HOME/config/state and synthetic authentication only. The remote Gateway URL is `wss://10.255.255.1:18789`; no server or held-reply proxy is involved. Process-tree snapshots identify the actual CLI entry PID before it renames itself to openclaw. Each signal is sent to that PID about one second after observing its natural TCP SYN_SENT. This avoids ocx's own signal handlers; exit status is the CLI child status propagated by ocx.

| Signal | Base, two runs | Candidate, two runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SIGINT | 130; 4.083 / 3.646 seconds; late report | 130; 0.204 / 0.199 seconds; no late report |
| SIGTERM | 143; 3.740 / 3.709 seconds; late report | 143; 0.779 / 0.204 seconds; no late report |

Uninterrupted deep audit produces the same timeout warning. Non-deep audit and the complete `--fix` receipt/report compare identically, excluding only report timestamps.

Vitest-source: security-cli.test.ts and audit-probe-failure.test.ts have 10 passing cases on the candidate. Base has one expected cancellation failure and nine passes. Credential redaction and failed-probe warning assertions are retained at the audit-core boundary; repeated new CLI fixtures were removed. Targeted lint, the matching config-cli test typecheck leaf and formatting pass. Tests are net -2 lines, with no allocation file. Production +48/-16; no user-facing message text changes.

Full tier on production-identical head `049407e5e5e643edaa4ba7e880fa9c3af034db7a`: `ocx build --dts`, supported self-contained packaging/tarball integrity, and the extracted packed CLI's version and non-deep JSON audit all pass. The final commit only repairs test lint, so this full proof is reused. External dependencies came from the ocx-installed checkout; bundled workspace dependencies came from the tarball.

[Paired process, timing, output, test and importer receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199623#issuecomment-6897032570).

Contributor Alix-007's human commit is retained. This is a two-way door: reverting restores the old interruption behavior without data migration or stored-state changes. Blast radius is the read-only security audit's deep Gateway probe and report lifetime; arbitrary plugin collector cancellation and earlier SecretRef resolution are outside this change.

prs.title: fix(agents): read skills_search limit as a strict bounded integer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `skills_search` runtime read its `limit` argument through the lenient `Number.parseFloat` path, so a quoted `limit: "12junk"` parsed to 12 and slipped past the catalog check that the advertised `integer, >= 1, <= 20` schema promises to enforce.

## User Impact

Schema-violating string input is silently accepted where every sibling pagination tool (`sessions_history` et al.) throws a `ToolInputError`; callers get results for input the tool contract rejects, hiding upstream bugs in the caller.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route through `readPositiveIntegerParam` with the documented 1–20 bound and the catalog's existing error message, matching the strict reader style used by the other tool-layer pagination params.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`.

- The advertised contract, captured from a live session's `tool_search` production output:
  `skills_search … "input": "{ query: string; limit?: number /* integer, >= 1, <= 20 */ }"`.
- Red on base / green on head through the real tool executor:

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/tools/installed-skill-tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  → "rejects skills_search limit … like the advertised 1-20 integer schema" (head):
      limit "12junk" → ToolInputError: limit must be an integer between 1 and 20
      limit "1.5"    → same error
      limit "21" / "0" → same error
  → 15 passed (on base, the "12junk" case fails: parseFloat eats the suffix and returns results)
```

- Shipped-entry limitation, stated plainly: `skills_search` is registered only on surfaces with installed skills and is surfaced to models through the code-mode dynamic-tool path; this machine's headless tool surface rejects direct-name calls, so the executor-level boundary above (real `createInstalledSkillTools` execute, no transport involved) is the closest shipped path available here.

prs.title: fix(agents): enforce the 300-second cap on conversations_turn timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `conversations_turn` tool schema advertises `timeoutSeconds` as an integer between 1 and 300, but the runtime reader enforced no maximum, so a client that bypasses schema validation (MCP callers are not required to validate against the advertised `inputSchema`) could stretch a single turn toward 28 hours (`timeoutSeconds: 100000` → `request.timeoutMs = 100020000`).

## User Impact

An out-of-range timeout is accepted silently and turns into an effectively unbounded Gateway call plus a zombie cancel window, instead of the documented 1–300 bound every schema-observing client already obeys.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the documented cap (`max: 300`) to the strict positive-integer reader — the same pattern `media-tool-shared` and `tts-tool` already use for their bounded timeout/limit params. Schema-valid input is unaffected.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`.

- Production chain: model/MCP tool call → `conversation-tools.ts` execute → `readPositiveIntegerParam(params, "timeoutSeconds")` (no `max` on base) → `conversations.turn` gateway request with `timeoutMs = seconds*1000` and `request.timeoutMs = timeoutMs + 20_000`.
- Red on base / green on head through the real tool executor (gateway dispatch mocked at the transport boundary only):

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  → "enforces the advertised 300-second cap on turn timeouts" (head):
      execute("turn", { timeoutSeconds: 300 }) dispatches { params.timeoutMs: 300000, request.timeoutMs: 320000 }
      execute("turn", { timeoutSeconds: 301 }) → ToolInputError: timeoutSeconds must be an integer between 1 and 300
      execute("turn", { timeoutSeconds: 0 })   → ToolInputError: timeoutSeconds must be an integer between 1 and 300
      gateway dispatch count stays 1 (rejected calls never reach the Gateway)
  → 6 passed (on base, the 301/0 rejections fail: both proceed to dispatch)
```

- Shipped-entry limitation, stated plainly: `conversations_turn` is a hosted channel tool exposed on channel-facing agent surfaces; it is not present in the headless local-agent tool surface this machine can drive end-to-end, so the boundary output above is the closest shipped executor path available here. The regression runs through the real `execute` implementation and only replaces the network transport.

prs.title: fix(cli): cap infer image --count at 50 per request
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw infer image generate/edit --count` accepted any safe integer, so a stray huge value (`--count 999999999999999`) passed option parsing and reached the provider request that fans out into one download and atomic publish per image.

## User Impact

A slip multiplies into an effectively unbounded per-image work loop against the configured provider; the option help named no cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject beyond 50 images per request with the cap named in the error and the option help, consistent with the sibling media options that validate their ranges before dispatch.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `b935ae0f2ce` (branch `fix/infer-image-count-cap`).

Before (base, live CLI): `--count 999999999999999` passed parsing and advanced to provider configuration (`No image-generation model configured…`), proving acceptance before dispatch; `--count abc` was rejected.

After (head tree, built `dist`, run through `node openclaw.mjs`):

```
$ openclaw infer image generate --count 999999999999999 --prompt x
--count must be at most 50 images per request.
exit=1                                   ← rejected before provider setup

$ openclaw infer image generate --count 3 --prompt x
No image-generation model configured. Set agents.defaults.mediaModels.image.primary to a provider/model like "comfy/workflow". …
exit=1                                   ← valid count parses through to provider setup
```

Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/capability-cli.image-options.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 8 passed, including `rejects image --count beyond the 50-image request cap before dispatch` (fails on base).

prs.title: fix(cli): bound nodes screen record --fps to 0-120
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw nodes screen record --fps` validated only positivity, so `--fps 1e300` (or `0.000001`) passed option parsing and was forwarded verbatim to the node's `screen.record` capture sizing.

## User Impact

A typo or pasted value reaches the remote node's recorder with an absurd frame rate and fails there with an opaque capture error, instead of being stopped at the CLI with a named bound. The sibling `--quality` flag in the same command already demonstrates the intended bounded style (PR #130352's "validate existing malformed options before contacting the Gateway while preserving valid invocations" is exactly this change's intent: reject out-of-range input locally, keep valid invocations untouched).

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `maxInclusive: 120` alongside the existing `minExclusive: 0` using the same inclusive-bound helper the `--quality` flag uses, and name the range in the option help.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e54c1880fa8594e6478f2b561fac307`; head `e515c65530d` (branch `fix/nodes-screen-record-fps-bounds`). All output from the built `dist` CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) against a local Gateway on loopback.

Before (base): `--fps 1e300` passed parsing and failed only at node resolution (`unknown node: nx`), proving the value was forwarded.

After (head):

```
$ openclaw nodes screen record --node nx --fps 1e300 --duration 1 --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --token x
nodes screen record failed: --fps must be at most 120.
exit=1                                                        ← rejected locally, no Gateway contact

$ openclaw nodes screen record --node nx --fps 121 --duration 1 --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --token x
nodes screen record failed: --fps must be at most 120.
exit=1                                                        ← rejected locally

$ openclaw nodes screen record --node nx --fps 60 --duration 1 --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --token x
nodes screen record failed: unknown node: nx.
exit=1                                                        ← valid fps preserved: proceeds to node resolution exactly like the base

$ openclaw nodes screen record --node nx --fps 0.5 --duration 1 --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --token x
nodes screen record failed: unknown node: nx.
exit=1                                                        ← fractional in-range fps preserved
```

Over-limit values are rejected before any Gateway contact; valid values keep the base behavior end to end. Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/nodes-cli/register.screen-fps.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 8 passed (rejects `0`, `-1`, `1e300`, `121`, `nope` before node lookup; forwards default/`60`/`0.5` as exact `params.fps`).

prs.title: fix(cli): reject usage-cost --days beyond the Gateway's 36600-day ceiling
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost --days` accepted any positive integer while the Gateway silently clamps usage queries to 36,600 days, so `--days 99999999` titled its report "Usage cost (99999999 days)" while actually querying a 100-year window.

## User Impact

The operator reads a window label that has nothing to do with the data returned; there is no hint a cap exists or what it is. (The malformed-value path was already strict — this is the missing upper bound.)

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject beyond the Gateway's `MAX_USAGE_DAYS` ceiling at the CLI with the real bound named, mirroring how other Gateway-bounded options validate up front. The numeric branch clamps symmetrically.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `1104f25655e` (branch `fix/usage-cost-days-upper-bound`).

Before (base, live CLI against a local Gateway on loopback): `--days 99999999` printed `Usage cost (99999999 days)` and its output was byte-identical to `--days 36600`, proving the silent clamp and misleading title.

After (head tree, built `dist`, run through `node openclaw.mjs`):

```
$ openclaw gateway usage-cost --days 99999999 --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --token x
Gateway usage cost failed: Invalid --days. Use 1-36600 days, e.g. --days 30. Received: "99999999".
exit=1
```

Rejected at the CLI with the supported range named and exit code 1. The control run (`--days 30`) was collected while the local proof Gateway had shut down, so its connection error is not evidence of behavior and is omitted; parsing of in-range values is covered by the regression below.

Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 25 passed, including `rejects usage-cost --days beyond the Gateway's 36600-day ceiling` (fails on base).

prs.title: fix(mcp): bound the channel bridge's initial Gateway readiness wait
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp serve`'s channel bridge absorbs retryable Gateway connect errors so a briefly unavailable Gateway can still come up, but nothing bounded that wait: with a Gateway that completes the WebSocket upgrade but never answers the challenge, `bridge.start()` stayed pending forever and every MCP `tools/call` blocked with no error until the client's own timeout.

## User Impact

An MCP client pointed at `openclaw mcp serve` while the Gateway is wedged sees `initialize` succeed but every tool call hang indefinitely with no failure message. `close()` still resolves readiness, so shutdown was never blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race the readiness wait against a deadline derived from the production timeout owners — the **max** of `resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` and `resolveConnectChallengeTimeoutMs` (honoring `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` and `OPENCLAW_CONNECT_CHALLENGE_TIMEOUT_MS`; the bootstrap's optional preauth field is never populated in production, so the resolvers are called directly) — plus a 30s retry grace, mirroring the stdio MCP client's `startupDeadline`. A late hello after the deadline still resolves the shared readiness promise harmlessly; a slow-but-succeeding connection under an extended budget is never cut short.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `789446ac6d` (branch `fix/mcp-channel-bridge-readiness-deadline`; live captures ran on local commit `0b52faa7d8075` — the deadline semantics are unchanged by the final max() widening, which only raises the budget under extended env overrides).

**Live red/green through the changed path.** Fake Gateway on `ws://127.0.0.1:18995` that completes the real WebSocket 101 upgrade and then never replies to the challenge (the retryable "gateway request timeout for connect" class the WS handshake timeout cannot reach). Same stdio JSON-RPC probe against both trees, each built from its own `dist`:

```
[base 940e769] initialize responded: true (16774ms)
[base 940e769] tools/call responded: false (after 110014ms)     ← 110s, no response, no error
[base 940e769] server: still-running (elapsed 141792ms)          ← hangs forever; stderr shows nothing but warnings

[fixed 0b52faa] initialize responded: true (17244ms)
[fixed 0b52faa] tools/call responded: false (after 110039ms)
[fixed 0b52faa] deadline error on stderr: did not become ready within 60000ms
[fixed 0b52faa] stderr tail: MCP server failed to start: gateway did not become ready within 60000ms.
                Run openclaw gateway status --deep --require-rpc to inspect Gateway health.
```

**Budget-aware behavior through the production resolvers (fake timers over the real bridge startup):**

```
$ pnpm test src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   → 14 passed
  - retryable error never recovering → rejects at 60s (default budgets + grace)
  - OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 → pending at 90s, rejects at 150s
  - OPENCLAW_CONNECT_CHALLENGE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 → pending at 90s, rejects at 150s
```

prs.title: fix(media): reject truncated or non-canonical data URL base64
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`decodeDataUrl` validated only the base64 character set and an estimated size, then handed the payload to `Buffer.from(value, "base64")`, which silently drops dangling tail characters (lengths off the 4-character grid) and re-encodes non-canonical trailing bits. Those payloads decoded to unexpected bytes and surfaced later as unrelated media failures instead of an invalid-input error.

## User Impact

Agents attaching an inline image by data URL to the `image` tool (image-to-image references) or a media-generation reference got structurally invalid base64 accepted at decode time; the failure appeared later as an opaque image-processing or provider error. (The `message` tool's `buffer` param keeps its own charset-only check and is unchanged; base64-level validation cannot judge whether decoded *image bytes* are a complete image.)

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate through the shared `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core` (per review follow-up, replacing the hand-rolled comparison): dangling tails and non-canonical trailing bits return `undefined` and are rejected, while the valid missing-padding inputs PR #140226 pinned keep decoding. The canonical re-encode comparison matches the discipline `input-files.ts` and `remote-workspace-file.ts` already apply.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `bf9ba127d7` (branch `fix/data-url-base64-roundtrip`; the transcript below was captured on local commit `bb85bd47a5359` — same squashed tree).

```
$ pnpm test src/media/image-data-url.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   → 10 passed
  rejects: dangling tail characters ("SGVsbG8=xx", off the 4-char grid Buffer.from drops)
  rejects: non-canonical trailing bits ("QR==" decodes but re-encodes as "QQ==")
  accepts: unpadded "SGVsbG8" (Hello) — the PR #140226 contract, now pinned
  accepts: padded canonical form (unchanged)
```

The rejection cases fail on the base (both inputs decoded without error). Sibling precedent for the canonical-comparison discipline: `src/media/remote-workspace-file.ts:132-138`, `src/media/input-files.ts:80-85`.

Live shipped-path check (head tree, built `dist`, real `agent --local` runtime + local Gateway): the `message` tool's `buffer` path applies its own charset validation ("!!!" → `message.send buffer has invalid base64 data`) and does not route through this decoder; the `decodeDataUrl` callers (`image` tool references, media-generation references) need an image-generation model configuration this sandbox's headless surface does not expose, so their capture is limited to the decoder-level red/green above.

prs.title: fix(cli): clamp logs --limit/--max-bytes to the Gateway caps on every path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw logs --limit/--max-bytes` behaved differently per delivery path: the Gateway RPC rejects values over 5000 lines / 1,000,000 bytes with `INVALID_REQUEST`, while the journalctl and local-file fallbacks clamp the same values silently. One command could fail hard or succeed quietly depending on which path served it, and the option help named no cap at all.

## User Impact

The same `--limit 6000` invocation either errors (`invalid logs.tail params: at /limit: must be <= 5000`) or silently reads 5000 lines, depending on Gateway availability. Operators cannot tell what cap applies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clamp once at the CLI entry using the same constants the fallback paths already apply (`JOURNAL_MAX_LIMIT`/`JOURNAL_MAX_BYTES`, equal to the Gateway schema caps), and name the caps in the option help. All three paths now agree for any input.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `21f57343876` (branch `fix/logs-limit-consistent-caps`; squashed single commit, tree identical to the reviewed head).

Before (base, live CLI against a local Gateway): `logs --limit 6000 --token x` → `invalid logs.tail params: at /limit: must be <= 5000` (exit non-zero), while the same value against the local-file fallback clamped silently and exited 0.

After (head tree, built `dist`, `node openclaw.mjs`):

```
== Gateway path (live local Gateway built from this PR's tree) ==
$ openclaw logs --limit 6000 --max-bytes 2000000 --token x --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999
Log file: …\tmp\openclaw\openclaw-2026-11-16.log
2026-11-16T02:39:34.349+08:00 info gateway loading configuration…
2026-11-16T02:39:34.419+08:00 info gateway resolving authentication…
2026-11-16T02:39:34.439+08:00 info gateway starting...
…
                                                    ← oversized values now succeed through the Gateway: the RPC
                                                      accepted the clamped 5000/1000000 and returned log lines

== fallback path (dead loopback port, local-file reader) ==
$ openclaw logs --limit 6000 --max-bytes 2000000
Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
Log file: …\state\tmp\openclaw\openclaw-2026-11-16.log
exit=0                                              ← same input, same outcome as the Gateway path

$ openclaw logs --limit 200 --token x
Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
exit=0                                              ← control value unchanged
```

The same oversized input now yields the same successful result on both delivery paths instead of failing on one and silently clamping on the other. Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 18 passed, including `clamps oversized --limit/--max-bytes to the Gateway caps before the RPC` (fails on base: the RPC receives `limit: 6000`).

prs.title: fix(cli): keep MCP timeout overrides within safe-integer milliseconds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp add/configure --timeout` and `--connect-timeout` accepted exponent seconds and multiplied by 1000 without an upper-bound check, persisting out-of-range millisecond overrides into the saved configuration (`--timeout 1e13` wrote `requestTimeoutMs: 10000000000000000`, past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`).

## User Impact

A saved server config can end up carrying a non-safe-integer timeout that runtime consumers must clamp or flag as drift; the operator got no signal at write time.

## Why This Change Was Made

After scaling, reject only values past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (mirroring the safe-integer discipline of `gateway suspend --wait`). Fractional products — `1.001s` scaling to `1000.999…ms` — stay valid per review follow-up, so `Number.isSafeInteger` on the product is deliberately not used; the error names the supported second ceiling for both flags.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `597bcfe0f6` (branch `fix/mcp-timeout-safe-integer-ms`).

Before (base, live CLI): `mcp configure demo --timeout 1e13` wrote `requestTimeoutMs: 10000000000000000` into the saved `openclaw.json` (captured by reading the file).

After (reviewed head `597bcfe0f61a3ec768fec4abd29d1c041e0138e3`; the transcript was captured on local commit `944d1136d51fe`, whose git tree `2c80416fc57719fda81ac090be5c3c39c50adb68` is byte-identical to the reviewed head's tree `2c80416fc57719fda81ac090be5c3c39c50adb68` — same `dist` input, built and run through `node openclaw.mjs`; fresh temp home per run):

```
$ openclaw mcp add demo --command <node.exe> --no-probe --timeout 1e13
--timeout is too large; keep the value at or below 9007199254740 seconds.
exit=1                                    ← nothing written

$ openclaw mcp add demo2 --command <node.exe> --no-probe --timeout 30
Saved MCP server "demo2" to …\state\openclaw.json.
exit=0

$ openclaw mcp configure demo2 --connect-timeout 1e13
--connect-timeout is too large; keep the value at or below 9007199254740 seconds.
exit=1                                    ← prior settings preserved

$ openclaw mcp configure demo2 --timeout 1.001
Updated MCP server "demo2" in …\state\openclaw.json.
exit=0                                    ← fractional milliseconds still accepted
```

Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t timeout` → overflow rejection and fractional-millisecond preservation both pass (plus the pre-existing hex cases); the one failing case in the full file (`requires initialize to finish within the configured probe timeout`, 1.5s timing budget) also fails on the unmodified base on this machine and is untouched by this diff.

prs.title: fix(cli): parse tools usage --since/--limit as strict decimals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw tools usage import --since` and `tools usage status --limit` parsed their values with bare `Number()`, so hexadecimal and exponent forms were accepted as the plain integers the option help describes (`--since 0x1f` became 31 days of imported history; `--limit 0x64` became 100).

## User Impact

Operators who typo or paste hex/exponent values get a silent, wrong history window instead of the documented 1–90 / 1–100 range error. Every other numeric CLI option in the tree already parses strict decimal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route `boundedInteger` through `parseStrictInteger` (the shared strict-decimal coercer), matching the pattern `proxy-cli` and the MCP timeout flags already follow. No behavior change for valid decimal input. Regression cases use in-range non-decimal tokens (`0x1f`=31, `1e1`=10) that the base accepted, so strict parsing is the only rejector.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `b863c244b2` (branch `fix/tools-usage-strict-decimal`).

Before (base, live CLI): `--since 0x1f --dry-run` passed option parsing and reached `gateway toolUsage.import requires credentials…` (accepted as 31), `--since 1e2` failed with the *range* error only.

After (head `efdd645b191e1` tree, built `dist` and run through `node openclaw.mjs`):

```
$ openclaw tools usage import --since 0x1f --dry-run
OpenClaw could not parse this command: option '--since <days>' argument '0x1f' is invalid. Expected an integer between 1 and 90.
exit=1

$ openclaw tools usage import --since 1e1 --dry-run
OpenClaw could not parse this command: option '--since <days>' argument '1e1' is invalid. Expected an integer between 1 and 90.
exit=1

$ openclaw tools usage status --limit 0x64
OpenClaw could not parse this command: option '--limit <count>' argument '0x64' is invalid. Expected an integer between 1 and 100.
exit=1

$ openclaw tools usage import --since 30 --dry-run
gateway toolUsage.import requires credentials before opening a websocket   ← parsing passed, Gateway step reached
$ openclaw tools usage status --limit 5
gateway toolUsage.status requires credentials before opening a websocket  ← parsing passed, Gateway step reached
```

Non-decimal tokens are rejected before any Gateway access; valid decimals keep parsing through to the RPC step. Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/tools-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 13 passed, with `0x1f`/`1e1` (import) and `0x64`/`1e1` (status) rejection cases failing on the base.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface migrate blank agent remedy in JSON
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json` prints the correct `--agent must not be blank` message inside its JSON envelope, but its stderr collapses to the generic `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus a doctor hint, so anyone reading stderr (or any wrapper that surfaces stderr only) loses the actionable remedy. `openclaw migrate apply ... --json` behaves the same way. The guard now throws through the existing expected-CLI-error path, so JSON failures keep the concrete message.

- Problem: `resolveMigrationTargetAgentId()` threw a plain `Error` for an explicitly blank `--agent`. In JSON mode the runtime treats an unrecognized error as an unexpected failure and replaces the stderr hint with the generic failure line, even though the user-facing message already existed.
- Solution: throw the existing text through `throwExpectedCliError`, the canonical expected-CLI-error owner already used by the `sandbox explain` and `sessions compact` blank-agent guards.
- What changed: `src/commands/migrate/context.ts` imports `throwExpectedCliError` and converts the single blank-value guard; `src/commands/migrate/context.test.ts` folds the error-name assertion into the existing migration-target test and drops the now-redundant standalone case.
- What did NOT change: text-mode output, JSON stdout envelopes, exit codes, invalid-agent and unknown-agent errors, and the configured-default fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveMigrationTargetAgentId()` is the single owner shared by `migrate plan` and `migrate apply`, so one conversion covers both entry points without duplicating a guard per subcommand.

- Best fix: convert the existing guard in the shared owner. The message was already correct; only the error type was wrong, so the change introduces no new user-facing text and keeps a single source of truth for migration target validation.
- Alternative(s): adding a per-command guard in `register.migrate.ts` would duplicate ownership in two call sites; changing the global JSON failure formatter would alter behavior for unrelated commands. Both were rejected.
- Risk: the conversion only affects the explicitly blank `--agent` path. Invalid ids such as `research/../main` and unknown ids such as `missing` keep their existing plain `Error` path, which the control case below verifies. Full-repository type checking was left to CI.

## User Impact

A JSON consumer that reads stderr now receives `--agent must not be blank` instead of a generic failure line, matching the message that was already available on stdout. Text mode, stdout bytes and exit codes are unchanged, so existing scripts that parse either stream keep working.

## Evidence

Both arms are real built CLIs: the frozen `origin/main` base and the candidate were each built with `build-all.mts cliStartup`, and every cell below is a full `node openclaw.mjs ...` invocation under a minimal environment (only PATH, HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, state dir and config), with 0700 scratch directories, an empty config, no credentials and no mocks. `--version` self-reports each arm.

| Case | Before (pre-fix, base c8caba2) | After (post-fix, this head 1ee8a90) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json` stderr | generic `The CLI command failed.` plus doctor hint | `--agent must not be blank` |
| `migrate apply hermes --yes --agent " " --json` stderr | generic `The CLI command failed.` plus doctor hint | `--agent must not be blank` |
| `migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json` stdout | 104-byte `cli_error` envelope carrying the blank-agent message | identical 104 bytes |
| text mode `migrate plan hermes --agent " "` | blank-agent message on stderr, exit 1 | identical bytes, exit 1 |
| unknown agent control `--agent missing --json` | unknown-agent envelope and generic stderr, exit 1 | identical bytes, exit 1 |

Arm identity:

```console
# frozen base
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (c8caba2)

# candidate
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (1ee8a90)
```

Bug case on the launched CLI:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json

# stdout, byte-identical on both arms
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "--agent must not be blank"
  }
}

# stderr on frozen base
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.

# stderr on candidate
--agent must not be blank
```

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs migrate apply hermes --yes --agent " " --json

# stdout, byte-identical on both arms
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "--agent must not be blank"
  }
}

# stderr on frozen base
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.

# stderr on candidate
--agent must not be blank
```

Control case, unknown agent:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs migrate plan hermes --agent missing --json

# stdout and stderr byte-identical on both arms, exit 1
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Unknown agent id \"missing\". Run openclaw agents list to see configured agents."
  }
}
```

Full matrix as emitted by the comparison harness (`cmp` per stream, 1 = byte-identical):

```text
plan-text       exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=1
plan-json       exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=0
apply-text      exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=1
apply-json      exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=0
unknown-json    exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=1
```

Built bundle, proving which form actually shipped:

```console

Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

### What was not tested

- Full-repository type checking was not run locally; targeted `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `oxfmt` and the focused suite passed, so type checking is left to CI.
- No migration was allowed to run past argument validation, so no real import path was exercised in this proof.
- Both arms emit the same Node security-patch warning and the same log-append warning in the isolated scratch HOME; they are identical across arms and unrelated to this change.

### Open PR collision check

Searched the changed-file lists of the latest 300 open PRs plus title and body searches for `migrate`, `blank agent` and `expected-cli-error`: no open PR touches `src/commands/migrate/context.ts` or `src/commands/migrate/context.test.ts`. The same-day merged #199386 converts the equivalent guard in `sessions compact` only, leaving the migrate owner untouched, so this is not a duplicate.

prs.title: fix(cli): show session-target remedies for attach failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An operator who points `openclaw attach` at a short session reference gets no actionable output. `openclaw attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --url wss://other.example` prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus `For help, run openclaw doctor.` — the remedy the resolver already composed ("pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both") never reaches the terminal, and the doctor hint sends the operator to the wrong next step. The same collapse hides the formatted ambiguity table for a colliding prefix, the `No session found` hint, and the gateway-unreachable / stored-device-auth recovery lines.

- Problem: `resolveSessionTarget` in `src/cli/session-target.ts` raises its operator remedies as plain `Error`s. `attach` awaits it directly, so they bubble to the root CLI renderer, which prints the message only for expected CLI errors and a narrow show-reason whitelist that does not include `attach`.
- Solution: raise those remedy sites through the canonical `throwExpectedCliError` / `ExpectedCliError` owner in `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, message text verbatim.
- What changed: `src/cli/session-target.ts` (+16/−9) — six returned remedy errors and three thrown remedy errors now carry `humanOutput`. Regression assertions folded into the existing cases in `src/cli/session-ref.test.ts` and `src/cli/session-target.test.ts` (net −4 test lines, no new test file).
- What did NOT change: every message string, the exit code (1), the JSON failure envelope (`formatCliJsonFailure` already kept the message), `openclaw tui` output, and the internal-invariant error at `session-target.ts:199` ("Gateway returned a session without a consistent agent identity.") which stays a plain `Error` because it names a branch that should not happen.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-target owner already writes these remedies for one purpose — telling the operator what to do next — and one of its two consumers honours that contract while the other discards it. `src/cli/tui-cli.ts:96-105` catches around the same `resolveSessionTarget` call and prints the formatted message; `src/cli/attach-cli.ts:103` awaits it unwrapped, so the identical remedy is visible under `tui` and invisible under `attach` for the same input. That asymmetry is the strongest signal this is a missed site rather than a deliberate choice, and it is the same reasoning accepted in the merged dns CLI fix #192127 and the hooks CLI fix #190366, which adopted exactly this per-site shape.

Alternatives considered and rejected: adding `attach` to the renderer's show-reason whitelist would print raw reasons for every attach failure including unforeseen internal errors, a larger blast radius than one guard needs. Putting the conversion in the `attach` action instead would leave the second consumer (and any future one) re-deriving the contract that the owner already owns. Constructing `ExpectedCliError` inline at each of the six `shapeTargetError` return sites would triplicate the long remedy templates in a three-field constructor call, so those sites share one local factory over the owner class; the three throw sites call `throwExpectedCliError` directly.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw attach` with an ambiguous short reference, a mistyped reference, a conflicting URL and `--url`, or an unreachable gateway now see the remedy — including the already-formatted candidate table and the `sessions list` hint — instead of a generic failure and a doctor pointer. Successful and JSON-mode invocations are untouched, and every affected path still exits 1.

## Evidence

| Case (shipped entry, same isolated profile) | Before (`origin/main` `5bdadab2c73`, owner file reverted) | After (this head `14a4ec8219f`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attach <session URL> --url wss://other.example` | generic title + doctor hint, remedy hidden (exit 1) | `pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both` (exit 1) |
| `attach <ref> --url` to a port nothing listens on | generic title + doctor hint (exit 1) | transport line + `Could not reach gateway wss://127.0.0.1:18307. Check whether the gateway is down and whether its tailnet or SSH tunnel is reachable.` (exit 1) |

All eight runs exit 1, and the two `tui` control outputs diff byte-identical between base and head.

After (this head), conflict cell:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --url wss://other.example
```

```console
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
(exit 1)
```

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts attach "https://127.0.0.1:18307/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --token dummy-token

Start it with `openclaw gateway run` or check `openclaw gateway status`.
Gateway target: wss://127.0.0.1:18307

Config: /tmp/oc307/openclaw.json
```
