```console
(exit 1)
```

The ambiguity table is the remedy most worth keeping visible, and it is a multi-line block, so the renderer branch matters: expected CLI errors print `humanOutput` verbatim including newlines. It is pinned at the owner boundary instead — `src/cli/session-ref.test.ts` "prints bounded ambiguity candidates without listing or describing" asserts the candidate rows and the `Pass a longer reference` line arrive inside an `ExpectedCliError`.

Unit invariant, same tests with the owner file swapped (mutation = full production revert, restored by recorded sha256): on base the plain errors carry `message` but no `humanOutput`, so the class pins fail while all 29 message-text assertions pass on both sides — proof the messages are byte-identical and only the envelope changed.

```console
FAIL src/cli/session-ref.test.ts > session target resolution > rejects a second explicit URL
AssertionError: expected Error: pass one target: use either the se… to be an instance of ExpectedCliError

FAIL src/cli/session-target.test.ts > session target connection errors > surfaces identity-proxy remediation without tailnet or SSH tunnel advice
AssertionError: expected Error: gateway rejected websocket upgrade… to be an instance of ExpectedCliError

      Tests  38 passed (38)                                        # this head
```

Consumers of the owner file were run, not reasoned about: every importer of `src/cli/session-target.js` (`attach-cli.action.test.ts`, `sessions-import.test.ts`, the doctor config preflight process test, `run-main.bare-root.test.ts`, `run-main.command-dispatch.test.ts`) — 132 tests green on this head. `attach-cli.action.test.ts` already asserted `error instanceof Error` plus verbatim `message` on the ambiguity case, and `ExpectedCliError` extends `Error`, so that existing contract stayed green without edit.

prs.title: fix(models): surface the auth login device-code conflict remedy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models auth login --device-code --method password` rejects the conflicting flags but prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` followed by a doctor hint — the remedy the guard already composed (`--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.`) never reaches the operator. This change throws the conflict as an expected CLI error so the root failure renderer prints the remedy line directly.

- Problem: the conflict guard in the `models auth login` action throws a plain `Error`. The root failure renderer prints `humanOutput` only for expected CLI errors, and `models` is not on the show-reason whitelist, so the message collapses to the generic failure title plus `For help, run openclaw doctor.`
- Solution: replace `throw new Error(...)` with the canonical `throwExpectedCliError(...)` from `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, keeping the message verbatim.
- What changed: `src/cli/models-cli.ts` (one import, one throw) and a regression assertion folded into the existing `--device-code` mapping test in `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts` (net 0 test lines, no new test file).
- What did NOT change: the guard condition, the message text, the exit code (1), machine/JSON output, and every other command path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer already owns the remedy-printing contract: an expected CLI error carries `humanOutput`, and `formatCliFailureLines` prints it verbatim before any generic fallback. Reusing `throwExpectedCliError` is the established per-site remedy for this exact anti-pattern — the dns CLI fix #192127 adopted the same shape, including the `rejects.toMatchObject({ humanOutput })` guard-test form reused here. Alternatives considered and rejected: adding `models` to the show-reason whitelist would widen reason printing for every models failure (a larger blast radius than this one guard), and constructing `ExpectedCliError` inline would duplicate the owner. The production delta is +1 line (the import); the throw itself is a one-for-one replacement.

## User Impact

Operators who combine `--device-code` with an incompatible `--method` now see the actionable remedy line directly instead of a generic failure and a doctor hint. Valid invocations are untouched, and the command still exits 1 on the conflict.

## Evidence

| Case | Before (base 25559c4) | After (this head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models auth login --device-code --method password` | generic title + doctor hint, remedy hidden (exit 1) | remedy line printed verbatim (exit 1) |
| same command, `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` | `Reason:` + stack: plain `Error` at the guard (`src/cli/models-cli.ts:586`) | remedy line only, no Reason/stack (expected-error early return) |
| `models auth login --help` (control) | exit 0, help text | exit 0, identical help text |

Live runs through the shipped entry point (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts ...`), both sides on the same isolated profile: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` point at a scratch directory with an empty config, so no credentials or configuration are written (the conflict guard is the first statement of the action handler). The service-probe warning and the log-append note in the outputs below are artifacts of that isolated profile and appear identically on both sides.

After (this head):

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts models auth login --device-code --method password
Installed Gateway service state and config paths could not be verified. Inspect the service environment with `openclaw gateway status --deep` before repairing plugin state.
[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped; check that the path is a writable regular file; file=openclaw-2026-11-13.log
--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.
(exit 1)
```

Before (base, owner file reverted via `git show`, test kept):

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts models auth login --device-code --method password
Installed Gateway service state and config paths could not be verified. Inspect the service environment with `openclaw gateway status --deep` before repairing plugin state.
[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped; check that the path is a writable regular file; file=openclaw-2026-11-13.log
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
(exit 1)
```

Before with `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` shows the hidden remedy and proves the plain-Error envelope (excerpt, stack path normalized):

```console
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: --device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.
[openclaw] Stack:
[openclaw] Error: --device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.
[openclaw]     at OpenClawCommand.<anonymous> (src/cli/models-cli.ts:586:15)
```

Unit invariant, same folded test with the owner file swapped: on base the plain Error carries `message` but no `humanOutput`, so the guard assertion fails (1 failed | 21 passed); on this head the full file passes (22 passed).

```console
FAIL src/cli/models-cli.test.ts > models cli > maps --device-code to the provider device-code auth method
AssertionError: expected Error: --device-code cannot be combined w… to match object { Object (humanOutput) }
- Expected
+ Received
- {
-   "humanOutput": "--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.",
+ Error {
+   "message": "--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.",
  }
```

Open PR collision check (submission-day sweep, 2026-11-13): scanned the 60 most recent open PRs plus keyword searches (`device-code`, `throwExpectedCliError`, `expected-cli-error`, `failure-output`, `models auth login`) and compared changed-file lists. #190482 and #198294 also touch `src/cli/models-cli.ts`, but their hunks (fallbacks-list `--agent` rejection near L422; `withModelsRuntime` near L38) are disjoint from this import/guard change and merge cleanly; #191233 and #191237 are sibling per-site fixes of the same anti-pattern in `security-cli.ts` / `worktrees-cli.ts`; #184579 is a headless device-code feature in the commands layer, not the CLI registration guard. No open PR touches `failure-output.ts` or `expected-cli-error.ts`, and the defect is still present on current `origin/main`.

What was not tested: local lint and typecheck. The repo wrapper rejects this worktree's symlinked `node_modules` ("Declaration input escapes checkout"), and the direct oxlint binary fails loading the config's JS plugin because the shared install's `eslint-plugin-solid` peer-hash symlink is stale. Both lanes were attempted; the change is byte-identical to the canonical pattern already compiling on main (the import line matches seven sibling `src/cli` files; the call shape matches `dns-cli.ts`), so lint/type verification is left to CI on this head.

prs.title: fix(update): stop status inspections when the CLI is interrupted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw update status` continuing to wait for a pending inspection after Ctrl-C. With `--timeout 20`, the interrupted CLI kept its Gateway connection open until the request timed out, delaying exit by about 20 seconds.

## User Impact

Users can interrupt a stalled status query promptly. The CLI retains exit code 130 and any partial diagnostics already available; ordinary status results and the existing overall timeout behavior remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status command creates a scope for its own inspection deadline, which hid the enclosing CLI cancellation signal. Forward cancellation into that scope and remove the listener when inspection finishes. This only changes read-only status inspection, not an update, repair, or service restart.

The regression extends the existing deadline suite rather than adding another fixture framework. This follows the same read-only CLI cancellation pattern as the recently merged external contribution #197491, at the separate `update status` entry point.

## Evidence

**Real source CLI before/after**, Node 24.22.2 on Linux, isolated state, with a synthetic loopback WebSocket peer. The peer completes the protocol handshake, observes the actual `channels.status` request, withholds its response, then the harness sends SIGINT to the CLI process. The command is `openclaw update status --json --timeout 20`; source execution uses the repository's CLI recovery entrypoint and runtime-worker loader.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SIGINT while `channels.status` is pending | Connection closes after 19,913 ms; process exits after 20,559 ms, code 130 | Connection closes after 579 ms; process exits after 725 ms, code 130 |
| Immediate valid response, no interruption | — | Exit 0; valid JSON, no inspection errors |
| Valid response delayed by 250 ms, no interruption | — | Exit 0; valid JSON, no inspection errors |

Timing starts when the peer receives the request and sends SIGINT, excluding CLI startup. No watchdog fired. The normal controls are measured from request receipt, with no signal sent.

<details>
<summary>Observed cancellation output</summary>

```text
Before:
  stderr: Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
  inspectionErrors[channels]: Channel inspection unavailable: gateway timeout after 20000ms
  exit: 130
  socket close: 19912.824 ms
  process exit: 20559.447 ms

After:
  stderr: Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
  inspectionErrors[channels]: CLI stopping (SIGINT)
  exit: 130
  socket close: 579.182 ms
  process exit: 724.658 ms
```

The peer is a disclosed protocol fixture, not a real Gateway. Registry access is offline in both runs and reports an unavailable registry in the update subsection. This proves the real CLI dispatch, signal handling, socket teardown, and exit behavior; it does not exercise live channels, an upgrade, or service management.
</details>

- Regression is red on base `96c685be0`: the pending inspection signal remains un-aborted. With the fix, all **7 deadline tests pass**, including partial results at the overall deadline, short check budgets, large valid timeouts, and normal completion under an outer scope. Final focused run: **13.73 s wall time**, approximately **1.2 s test time**; CI seconds pending.
- Touched-file format and lint, focused production dependency-graph typecheck, `git diff --check`, and the native test-line ratchet pass. Net test growth: **21 lines**, within the existing 400-line allowance. No full local test suite.
- Independent host review inspected the complete committed range `96c685be0` → `9173b2c56`, scope/cleanup ownership, tests, and runtime evidence: no actionable findings. Autoreview CLI was unavailable because its local transport preflight rejected an unsupported configuration field; this is not claimed as an autoreview result. Linux JSON output was exercised; other OSes and text output were not separately run.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop the ID rebind publication wait when the command is cancelled
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw id rebind` commits the key rotation first, then waits up to 30 s for Discovery to publish the new binding. Ctrl+C during that wait did not stop it: the loop kept reading `openclawId.people` every second and only reported when the wait ended.

So on a slow publication an interrupted command:

- held the terminal for the rest of the 30 s window,
- kept issuing Gateway RPCs after the user asked it to stop,
- and then printed a result as if the command had finished normally (`Moved to new keys. Devices reconnect by themselves.` / `Discovery doesn't have the new keys yet`), which reads as "the move may still be pending" even though the move was already committed and the keys already rotated.

The read side of the same flow was fixed in #197747 (merged): interrupted `openclaw id status` reads exit promptly. The publication wait in `rebind` was left out, so an interrupted *mutation* still behaved like an uninterruptible one.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForPublication` is the only place that keeps working after a committed move, so this is a targeted change to that loop, its sleep, and the receipt printed when the wait is cancelled:

- `waitForPublication` reads the ambient cancellation signal once, checks it before each Discovery read, and hands it to the sleep. The in-flight `openclawId.people` read now also carries the signal (the read helper gained that parameter in #197747).
- `runRebind`'s publication `catch` distinguishes "the wait was cancelled" from "the wait failed". A cancelled wait reports the committed move once and returns; a genuine failure keeps the existing `Publication check failed` warning and exit code 2.
- `docs/cli/id.md` documents the interrupted-wait receipt next to the existing committed-but-unreadable receipt, so the `cancelled: true` field is not an undocumented output change.
- The new receipt says the move is committed, that Discovery checking stopped because the command was cancelled, and to run `openclaw id status` instead of repeating `rebind` — repeating it would rotate keys again. It does not set an exit code: the SIGINT handler already owns the exit status, and the mutation itself succeeded.

This follows the repo's existing rule for committed mutations under Ctrl+C (see the suspend CLI): a committed mutation still prints its receipt exactly once, it just stops waiting for the follow-up work.

## User Impact

- Ctrl+C during `openclaw id rebind`'s publication wait returns immediately instead of after up to 30 s, and stops reading Discovery.
- The user still learns that the move committed and what to run next, so an interrupt cannot be mistaken for "nothing happened" (which would tempt a second `rebind` and another key rotation).
- No behaviour change when the wait completes normally or fails for a real reason.
- Exit status stays owned by the signal handler; no new exit codes, options, or output fields for successful runs.

## Evidence

### Real CLI against an isolated Gateway

The shipped CLI (`src/entry.ts id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code …`) against the shipped
Gateway (`src/entry.ts gateway`, real loopback WebSocket, real state directory, real key files
and recovery kit). A local Discovery stand-in answers descriptor reads and then refuses the
post-commit descriptor write with `503`, so the Gateway's own publisher cannot finish and the
stored `published_binding_seq` stays behind: the delayed-publication condition this wait exists
for. No Gateway or CLI code is replaced. The harness watches the Gateway log for
`moved to new keys` and sends one SIGINT 1.5 s later.

| Run | SIGINT to settle | Exit | Printed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| current `main` (`src/cli/id-cli.ts` from `origin/main`), `--json` | 30.8 s | 0 | the late wait result, `published: false` |
| current `main`, text | 29.9 s | 0 | the normal "moved" result |
| this branch, `--json` | **0.65 s** | **130** | the committed receipt, `cancelled: true` |
| this branch, text | **0.63 s** | **130** | the committed receipt, three lines |

Before (`origin/main` `src/cli/id-cli.ts`), the interrupt is ignored — 30 s more of Discovery
reads, then a result that says nothing about the move that already committed:

```console
$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code … --json   # SIGINT after the commit
{"moved": true, "bindingSeq": 2, "published": false}      # +30.8 s, exit 0

$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code …           # SIGINT after the commit
Moved to new keys. Devices reconnect by themselves.       # +29.9 s, exit 0
Discovery doesn't have the new keys yet; the Gateway keeps publishing them (openclaw id status).
If you did this because you think a key leaked, also check Your devices and People.
```

With this branch the receipt is printed once and the command stops reading Discovery:

```console
$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code … --json   # SIGINT after the commit
{
  "moved": true,
  "bindingSeq": 2,
  "published": null,
  "cancelled": true,
  "nextStep": "openclaw id status"
}                                                          # +0.65 s, exit 130

$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code …           # SIGINT after the commit
Moved to new keys (committed).
Stopped checking Discovery: the command was cancelled.
Run openclaw id status to check publication. Do not repeat rebind: it rotates keys again.
                                                           # +0.63 s, exit 130
```

### Regression tests at the CLI boundary

In the existing `id-cli.commands.test.ts` suite (production scope gate, ambient `AsyncWorkScope`,
same RPC fixture as its sibling cases). Base = `origin/main` with only `src/cli/id-cli.ts` reverted.

| Check | Base (`origin/main`) | With this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reports the committed move once when the publication wait is cancelled (json=true)` | FAIL — `expected { moved: true, bindingSeq: 2, published: false } to deeply equal { moved: true, bindingSeq: 2, published: null, cancelled: true, nextStep: "openclaw id status" }` (it kept polling, then reported the wait result) | PASS |
| `reports the committed move once when the publication wait is cancelled (json=false)` | FAIL — `expected 'Moved to new keys. Devices reconnect …' to contain 'Moved to new keys (committed)'` | PASS |
| `id-cli` suite (`src/cli/id-cli.commands.test.ts`, `src/cli/id-cli-rebind.test.ts`) | 2 failed \| 10 passed | 12 passed |
| `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on both code files, `oxfmt --check docs/cli/id.md` | clean | clean |

Both new cases assert that no further Discovery read happens after the cancel and that no
failure text or exit code is produced.

Remaining gap, stated plainly: the real Discovery service and the iroh tunnel are not exercised
here — this host has no Rust toolchain, so the bundled iroh binding is unavailable and the
repository's own `src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-rebind.test.ts` skips for the same reason
(`describe.skipIf(!hasBinding)`). The tunnel/key-switch side of a re-bind therefore still rests
on CI and on a machine with `pnpm build:iroh`. `tsgo` also cannot run here (its native binary
needs GLIBC ≥ 2.34), so typechecking is left to CI; the change uses existing typed helpers
(`setTimeout(..., { signal })`, `AbortSignal.throwIfAborted`).

prs.title: fix(mcp): stop interrupted CLI probe and doctor checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupting `mcp probe` or `mcp doctor --probe` during server initialization leaves discovery and its server process running until the CLI launcher forcibly kills the command.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C/SIGTERM now waits for diagnostic cleanup, stops the owned server and exits promptly without a late report. Normal failures and configuration preflight behavior stay covered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind the fresh private diagnostic runtime to the existing command cancellation signal and join its existing cleanup. Add/configure preflight, shared agent catalogs and admitted OAuth refresh owners retain their current behavior. Existing report rendering moves to its existing probe module to respect the registration file's line cap. No new options, dependencies, config/protocol/schema, permissions or upgrade changes.

## Evidence

### Current-head integration and actual behavior — 2026-11-14 UTC

**Product head:** `9fde0dee56b5e5de702a299c108872dbdf1154c3`. Integrated main: `08ae8c62b83ede02db3a8d2bc3ce36206008d253` through an ordinary two-parent merge; contributor history is retained, with no force-push.

Integrated main’s already-landed lazy TLS builtin import for the previously failing help-exit CI path while preserving the original diagnostic cancellation/cleanup fix. No unrelated production change was added.

- **Production entry / canonical owner:** Built `openclaw.mjs mcp probe` / `mcp doctor --probe` -> private diagnostic runtime -> existing native child-process owner -> real local stdio MCP server.
- **Exact frozen collector:** `python3 mcp-diagnostic-cancel-proof-v2.py --worktree CHECKOUT --node NODE26 --out FRESH_OUTPUT`. Normal build: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`; clean tracked tree and matching build stamp verified before and after the actual run.
- **Recorder / readback / legal controls:** All eight real PTY scenarios pass. Three SIGINT/SIGTERM cases exit naturally with 130/143 in 176–182ms, with the direct server absent before collector cleanup and no late diagnostic report. Five controls retain successful probe, provider-error exit1, static doctor with zero server launches, successful persisted configuration, and failed preflight with byte-identical configuration. The frozen collector and stricter receipt oracle both pass.
- **Acceptance RED:** retained original baseline and collector observations in the historical section below. This integration receipt claims exact-head GREEN and controls; it does not relabel earlier BASE runs as a new main execution.
- **Inspectable evidence:** [collector, complete sanitized streams, exact-head receipt, hashes and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/1232b99170864de61956ec2170f71cab0b26f2d2). All uploaded bytes were read back and SHA256-verified. Proof artifacts are kept in an evidence-only orphan commit, outside this product branch.
- **Supporting checks:** The qualified Ubuntu 24.04/GLIBC2.39 runtime passes all 44 MCP tests and all 25 actual CLI-help process tests. The initial host attempt had one initialization failure and is retained in the linked checks; it was not hidden or fixed by changing code, assertions or timeout. prs.title: fix(cli): observe ambient cancellation on approvals reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw approvals pending`, `get --gateway`, `grants list`, and the `approval.get` lookup inside `resolve` called the Gateway without the ambient CLI cancellation signal. Ctrl-C during a slow or unreachable Gateway therefore waited out the RPC timeout and exited 1 instead of the shell interrupt status, and the supervisor's 2 s escalation force-killed the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread `getAsyncWorkSignal()` into those read RPCs, rethrow aborts before the config fallback, and settle cancelled reads silently in `runApprovalsAction` — the custody shape `cron-cli` already uses. Mutations stay outside interrupt cancellation: the native policy write and its settled readback both run without the ambient signal, so an approved write is never hidden behind an aborted read. `loadSnapshot` takes an `ambient` flag so the readback keeps one snapshot cast at the boundary the base already had — no new `SAFETY:` marker and no raised baseline.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C and SIGTERM now exit 130/143 in under 600 ms instead of being force-killed after 2 s. Reads that complete are byte-identical, and a cancelled read prints no summary and no late timeout.

## Evidence

Real CLI signal matrix (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`), loopback TCP blackhole that accepts but never answers, signal 300 ms after the accept, 12 s exit watch:

| Scenario | Signal | base `97fd503` | head `91679704` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slow / unreachable | SIGINT | `SIGKILL` @ 2096 ms | **130** @ 476 ms |
| Slow / unreachable | SIGTERM | `SIGKILL` @ 2096 ms | **143** @ 478 ms |
| Healthy gateway | — | 0, `{"approvals":[]}` | 0, `{"approvals":[]}` |

```text
base2-int     {"exitCode":null,"exitSignal":"SIGKILL","msSignalToExit":2096,"lateOutputBytes":67,"stdout":""}
base2-term    {"exitCode":null,"exitSignal":"SIGKILL","msSignalToExit":2096,"lateOutputBytes":68,"stdout":""}
cand2-int     {"exitCode":130 ,"exitSignal":null     ,"msSignalToExit":476 ,"lateOutputBytes":67,"stdout":""}
cand2-term    {"exitCode":143 ,"exitSignal":null     ,"msSignalToExit":478 ,"lateOutputBytes":68,"stdout":""}
base2-control {"exitCode":0,"stdout":"{\"approvals\":[]}\n"}
cand2-control {"exitCode":0,"stdout":"{\"approvals\":[]}\n"}
```

The 67/68 bytes after the signal are the existing barrier line `Command interrupted by SIGINT/SIGTERM. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.`; `stdout` stays empty on both sides, so no late timeout or summary leaks out.

Regression tests, folded into the existing suites (no new test file):

```text
head : Test Files 2 passed (2)   Tests 50 passed (50)
base : Test Files 1 failed (1)   Tests 5 failed | 15 passed (20)
```

Base fails on `expected undefined to be AbortSignal { aborted: false }`: it passes no ambient signal. The matrix asserts exact signal identity (`call[3].signal === scope.signal`) and silent settlement for `pending`, `get --gateway`, `grants list`, and the `resolve` lookup, plus the opposite direction — `approval.resolve` and the write's readback receive no signal, with `beginClose` fired from inside the Gateway mock while the write is pending.

Mutation check: removing the config-fallback `throwIfAborted` turns only the `get` case red; removing the silent-cancellation swallow turns exactly the four read cases red and leaves the mutation boundary green.

Gates: `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors, `test-lines-ratchet` slack 1 (`config/test-lines-allocations/exec-approvals-interrupt-custody.txt`: net +110, 132 added / 22 removed), `assertion-safety` unchanged, prod and test typecheck green in CI.

### CI status

The previous head's ten red checks were inherited from `main`, not caused by this diff: `7250eb4b8b7` (#195158) made the retention helpers module-private while call sites still imported them. `main` repaired that in `34d5b3fd291` (restoring `forceFullGc` / `expectCollected`) and `72110f30e8d` (exporting `expectLiveObjects`), and every one of those checks — `check-test-types`, `check-test-types-core-*`, `check-prod-types`, `check-lint-core-*`, `check-additional-extension-package-boundary` — was green. This head is rebased onto `da0e0ba8cae` and re-resolves the conflict with `#197257` (the Effective Policy table refactor moved its imports/helper into `exec-approvals-cli.shared.ts`); the rebase keeps both changes. Tests, format, lint and the test-lines/assertion-safety/max-lines ratchets all pass locally.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): use known Qwen3 256K context windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw on Amazon Bedrock treats the Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B, Qwen3 Next 80B A3B, and Qwen3 235B A22B 2507 models as 32k-context models when they appear in the account's model listings, because the extension's known-context-window catalog has no entries for them.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock users selecting these Qwen3 variants now get the documented 256K-token context window in the discovered model metadata, so context budgeting and compaction size the models correctly instead of using the conservative 32,000-token unknown-model fallback (8x smaller than documented).

## Why This Change Was Made

`KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` is the single catalog mapping Bedrock model IDs to context windows; unknown IDs fall back to a conservative 32,000-token default. Three Qwen3 models listed in the AWS Bedrock catalog were missing, while their siblings (`qwen.qwen3-coder-next`, `qwen.qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-v1:0`) were already present — mirroring the gaps fixed in #192927 and the same-day sibling fixes (#193022, #193035, #193045, #193050). This adds the documented 256K value for each with the AWS model card as the source; resolution goes through the existing prefix-stripping and `:0`-suffix normalization.

- Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-qwen-qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct.html — "Context window: 256K tokens"
- Qwen3 Next 80B A3B: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-qwen-qwen3-next-80b-a3b.html — "Context window: 256K tokens"
- Qwen3 235B A22B 2507: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-qwen-qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.html — "Context window: 256K tokens"

## What Was Changed

- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts`: added the three Qwen3 entries to `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` with model-card links.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`: regression test asserting all three base IDs and a `us.qwen.qwen3-next-80b-a3b` inference-profile variant resolve `contextWindow: 256_000`.

Not changed: existing Qwen entries, Claude 5.x / Claude Opus 4.8 special-casing, the conservative 32,000 fallback, and `defaultContextWindow` config.

## Evidence

Real before/after on stock main (only the AWS SDK transport mocked; `discoverBedrockModels` is the production discovery path):

```text
before: red fixture with the three Qwen3 model summaries received
        "contextWindow": 32000 for each (conservative unknown-model fallback)
after:  full discovery.test.ts — 22/22 passed, including the new
        "uses the documented 256K context windows for the Qwen3 Coder 480B, Next 80B, and 235B 2507 models"
```

- Focused full-file suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` — 22/22 passed.
- Format check (`scripts/run-format.mts --check`, re-run after formatter write) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check at `1cd54b32aca0`: the catalog still lacks all three entries, so the fix is not already on main.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the changes only add `Record<string, number>` entries and reuse existing test helpers, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- Data-only catalog additions; no API, config, schema, or protocol surface changes.
- Qwen3 Coder 480B is in AWS "Legacy" lifecycle (EOL 2027-03-30) but still appears in discovery listings; the entry is correct while the model remains listed.
- If AWS revises a window, the entry needs the same one-line update as its siblings.

prs.body:
Closes #199880

Landed as [8e481bae22994e7741df4fe98bebaaff12082019](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8e481bae22994e7741df4fe98bebaaff12082019). [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43793715329) completed successfully: all three PostgreSQL 17 shards, PostgreSQL 16 Gateway cron smoke, and every applicable gate. The watched-session case executed and passed again on the actual PR merge checkout in [shard 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43793715329/job/133058204889). The exact-head hosted review found no issues or before-merge items.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL conformance did not exercise watched-session prompt preparation from a Gateway-role process main thread. Worker-based conformance bypasses the host SQL restriction and cannot prove this boundary.

## User Impact

Regression coverage only. Production LOC delta: **0**; test LOC delta: **+147 / -1**. Schema versions, DDL, migrations, stored formats, configuration, public APIs, retention and durability are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing fork probe and mixed-engine fixture. The child installs the Gateway role and engine, prepares runtime config and publishes the system-event store resolver in startup order, registers an ambient watch, and stores its title. It checks the exact prepared snapshot and rendered prompt, then disappearance after a completed watcher reset. A real admitted query calibrates SQL observation; retained direct SQL must throw, while async preparation/reset emits zero host PostgreSQL statements. Cleanup finishes before the parent can drop fixture schemas.

The qualification initially exposed a fixture initialization error: engine installation does not publish runtime config. Watch registration caught the strict unpublished-config error and returned false. The canonical fix is to await runtime config preparation and publish the system-event store resolver before session producers run, matching Gateway startup. Reported child errors now include captured stderr. No production paths were added, removed or replaced.

## Exact-Head Evidence

Head: `f09d853c17d617b718298f263cab991b786d2bbe`. [Qualification 43791047989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791047989) personally verified the exact workflow and checkout SHA.

| [Build and published artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791047989/job/133049725222) | **Passed.** |
| Production/test typechecks, all six lint lanes, formatting | **Passed** on this exact head; actual formatting step confirmed successful. |
| [Security-fast](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791047989/job/133049725396) | **Passed.** |
| Independent source review / formal autoreview | **GO / scoped-clean**, P0–P3, no findings, confidence 0.87, complete committed range `6aae38f36ee8152c2294fb52f9b91bb174e146e3..f09d853c17d617b718298f263cab991b786d2bbe`. |
| Node syntax checks / `git diff --check` | **Passed.** |

The [hosted review at e0514653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199881#issuecomment-6905312158) had no actionable source finding. Its exact-head PostgreSQL proof rank-up requirement is now fulfilled for the corrected candidate. [Fresh exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/43794320591) completed with no findings or before-merge items. [Normal ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43793715329) succeeded. PostgreSQL 16 proof is Gateway cron smoke, a separate passing PR job; the watched-session case is qualified under PostgreSQL 17.

Earlier runs 43788582803, 43787526916 and 43787248872 are superseded. The first two exposed fixture defects that are corrected here; unfinished/cancelled jobs are not passing evidence. Local dependency-backed execution was unqualified, and supported remote setup refused incompatible shared tooling before execution. No shared installation was changed; the unused initial lease was stopped.

## Broad CI Failures and Follow-Ups

The broad run is not green. Its failed jobs are tracked separately from the passing changed-surface proof:

| Job | Observed failure | Attribution / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [native-i18n](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791047989/job/133049725108) | Missing native.apple translations | Missing entries exist in frozen base; native inputs unchanged. |
| [control-ui-i18n](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791047989/job/133049725382) | Catalog fallback baseline drift | Catalog/verifier inputs unchanged; exact drift component not reproduced. |

Underlying slowdown UNKNOWN; no baseline reproduction or request-budget violation established. |

Fresh isolated contexts use mocked Gateway responses; no path to these PostgreSQL tests. Underlying causes UNKNOWN; no baseline reproduction or flake diagnosis. |
| [checks-node-compact-large-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791047989/job/133049728034) | Plugin finalization deadline fixture: missing events log | Owning plugin/update sources, fixture helpers, dependency pins and CI runners are unchanged. Isolated infra forks exclude this PR's unit-fast probe, with separate envelope processes. No event file existed at the parent read; child startup/cancellation and the underlying cause remain UNKNOWN. |

Named follow-ups: localization artifacts; rollback fixture export cleanup; release-tooling process timeout; UI receipt, history-pagination, suite-duration and synthetic-key latency assertions; plugin-finalization fixture event receipt; cron-repair import teardown. No failure is relabelled green.

Next bounded PostgreSQL proof: the public async harness wrapper with current/revoked authority, plus mixed PostgreSQL/SQLite store pairs. The existing synchronous public wrapper's compatibility window and return type remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(codex): expose advertised paired computer actions in the initial schema
prs.body:
Related: #192990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex exposes only V1 computer actions when a paired node already advertises V2 capabilities before the first tool call.

## User Impact

User impact: new Codex tool surfaces include advertised paired computer actions. Policy, model vision, session-owned desktop and live execution authorization boundaries remain intact. German keyboard corruption is separate and remains unverified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The common async construction owner now reuses host-owned paired capability preparation before assembly, preserving prepared facts, combined cancellation and stable initial definitions. No SDK surface, discovery cache or dependency is added.

The review repair keeps the extension regression on the existing SDK-backed production-host fixture and exercises discovery over loopback Gateway protocol responses. Session-transport exclusions are tested in the owning core assembly suite. Cron fixtures still record every RPC; only `node.list` and `computer.status` are excluded from action assertions, so forbidden cron actions and unexpected methods still fail non-dispatch checks.

## Evidence

- **Committed regression, red/green:** the identical SDK-backed regression file ran on unchanged base `0af3fea539816c517ec8e595905ba1991dee6407` in a separate worktree. Its V2 case failed because the first serialized computer schema lacked `list_windows` (one failed, five unselected; exit 1). On the fix, all six extension cases passed (exit 0). Two core cases separately verify available/unavailable session-owned transport without paired discovery. No private extension-to-core imports or mocks remain; `lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports` passes.
- **Consumer repair:** all 25 cron policy cases pass, including the six reproduced failures. Forbidden own/sibling automation mutations remain checked before dispatch, including revocation during an awaited call. No RPC history is cleared to obtain a pass.
- **Local acceptance:** 208 cases passed across eight files. After replacing raw WebSocket data stringification with the plugin's existing decoder, the affected six-case SDK fixture was rerun and passed. Core agent-test, cron-test and extension-test typechecks, affected lint/format, line-cap and test-line ratchets, whitespace and pre-commit checks pass. The allocation exactly covers 254 net regression lines. CI time is unmeasured.
- **Actual product proof retained:** an isolated Gateway and subscription-backed Codex app-server 0.166.0 used the same normally paired synthetic node advertising `screenshot` and `list_windows`. Baseline first `thread/start` omitted `list_windows`; the model replied `V2_UNAVAILABLE` without a computer call. The fixed snapshot included it before any computer action, invoked `computer.act` with `action: list_windows`, and produced a successful computer receipt and reply `COMPUTER_V2_192990`. Both live phases passed. The snapshot preceded mechanical preparation extraction/test relocation; equivalent inputs/order and subsequent tests/build support reuse. It is not literal final-head live proof, a physical Windows driver test, a keyboard fix, or blanket V2 exposure. This review follow-up changes tests only.
- **Review:** fresh local autoreview of the test repairs and supplied owner context found no actionable P0–P2 defects; the reviewer did not execute tests. `pr-simplify` removed private test wiring while preserving production behavior. The prior isolated runtime build passed; runtime source is unchanged by this follow-up.

<details>
<summary>Passed local commands</summary>

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix(templates): catalog cards jump on load and icons arrive late
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Templates catalog jumps when cards replace the loading placeholders, and card icons appear a few hundred milliseconds after the card text.

## User Impact

User impact: cards now fill their placeholders in place, and first-screen icons paint in the same frame as the text.

Two visible tradeoffs:

- Every card now reserves two title lines and two summary lines, so all cards are the same height. A card with a one-line title is about 20 px taller than before.
- On a cold browser cache the catalog waits for first-screen icons before revealing cards, capped at 500 ms. In six cold loads the first card text moved from about 535 ms to about 775 ms, while the fully painted catalog moved from about 860 ms to about 775 ms. Icons already in the browser cache add no wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

The placeholders were a flat grid of blocks that ignored section headers and card height, so no loaded card landed where a placeholder had been. They now render the same section and card structure as the loaded catalog. Matching exactly requires a known card height, which is why cards reserve their title and summary lines; a matching skeleton with natural card heights still left every card out of place.

Icons were only requested once the cards rendered. The catalog now fetches and decodes the first 24 icons before revealing cards, using the same request mode as the card image so the browser reuses the response. Slow or failed icons stop holding the catalog after 500 ms and load in place as before.

Preconnecting to the registry and eager, high-priority image loading were also measured and showed no gain, so they are not part of this change.

## Evidence

Measured on an isolated Gateway serving each build, against the live ClawHub catalog, entering Templates from Chat with a cold browser cache. Before is `main` at `718a2f8`; after is this change at `1d9bf3b`. Three later commits repair review and CI findings without changing that behavior:

- `b453488` gives section headers one height whether or not they have a "View all" action. Placement was rechecked on that head with the same harness (14 of 14 at 1280 px, 8 of 8 at 820 px, 5 of 5 at 400 px, 16 of 16 for a selected category).
- `081dff2` draws the placeholder bars inline instead of in the stylesheet. The first version added 888 bytes to a stylesheet that is already at its fixed size ceiling and failed `control-ui-performance`. Against the same base the stylesheet is now 18 bytes smaller raw and 10 bytes larger gzipped, inside the 64-byte build variance.
- `3d32dc6` always renders the summary paragraph, so a Template without a summary keeps its reserved lines. Before that commit the new browser case measured the summary-free card at 83 px against a 129.5 px placeholder.

The last two heads are covered by the browser test below rather than a new recording.

| Cold load at 1280 px (6 runs each) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visible cards landing on a placeholder | 0 of 14 | 14 of 14 |
| Section headers landing on a placeholder | 0 of 2 | 2 of 2 |
| Icons after card text (median first / last) | 147 ms / 332 ms | same frame, 6 of 6 runs |
| First card text (median) | 534 ms | 775 ms |
| Everything painted (median) | 858 ms | 777 ms |

Placement is also exact at 820 px (8 of 8 cards) and 400 px (5 of 5 cards), three runs each, and for a selected category at 1280 and 820 px. Placement compares each loaded card and header rectangle with the placeholder rectangles from the last loading frame. The `layout-shift` observer reports zero on both builds because the placeholders are replaced rather than moved, so it cannot show this difference.

Before:

![Before: flat placeholder grid, then cards in new positions with empty icon squares](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a56bc083-48dd-49de-a92f-e26bb8dd13ef)

After:

![After: placeholders mirror the catalog, then cards and icons fill them in place](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/817b83d9-7582-4236-9131-2d64a005239d)

Side-by-side recording, real time and then at one-fifth speed:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfed7d45-129e-48d1-8956-5264ad6a1e85

Tests and checks on `bd176f2` (the branch with current `main` merged in to resolve a conflict with #198070):

- Browser suite `templates-catalog.e2e.test.ts`: 27 passed. The loading test now holds the catalog response at four viewport sizes, plus a summary-free Template on mobile, and asserts that the first shelf header and first card arrive exactly where their placeholders were. It replaces the previous assertion that a measured grid ends near the bottom of the viewport.
- `templates-home.test.ts`, `templates-add.test.ts` and `templates-admission.test.ts`: 53 passed. New tests cover holding the placeholders until artwork decodes or fails, and releasing them at the 500 ms budget.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passed locally on the merged head.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed with the dead-export scan skipped. That scan reported unused exports in `src/state/*` and `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/member-welcome.ts`, which this change does not touch.

Known limit: when the registry is slow, the 500 ms budget expires and the cards are revealed with some icons still loading. That happened in 2 of 16 cold catalog loads across the final builds (and in 1 of 2 category loads during a slow period), and those loads show their text up to 500 ms later than `main` would have.

prs.title: fix(google): preserve medium thinking for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw rejects `medium` for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, or sends `HIGH` when the setting reaches the Google request builder directly.

## User Impact

`/think medium` and `--thinking medium` now select Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview's native `MEDIUM` effort. The default for this reasoning model stays adaptive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model policy, payload sanitizer, and shared Google request builder applied the original Gemini 3 Pro level rules to 3.1 Pro Preview. The policy excluded `medium`, and the payload layers independently mapped it to `HIGH`. Use a shared model check to recognize the documented 3.1 Pro Preview IDs at all three boundaries. Original Pro mappings, fixed-tier routes, and legacy numeric budgets keep their previous behavior. [Google's thinking-level documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking)

## Evidence

- Ran the built OpenClaw CLI against a local Gemini-compatible test server. `agent --local --thinking medium` sent one request with `generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel: "MEDIUM"` and returned the expected fixture response. With no thinking override, the request omitted `thinkingLevel` and returned the same fixture response.
- The regression cases reproduced the missing level in the model policy and the `HIGH` mapping in both request formats before the fix.
- 362 focused tests passed across 10 files on the implementation commit, including GenerateContent, Interactions, provider policy, and prompt-prefix stability. Core and extension type checks, lint, and formatting passed.
- The tests-only follow-up consolidated duplicate table setup and kept all cases. All 68 tests in the touched suite passed. The test-line ratchet passed on the local merge tree with two lines of slack, and the PR now has a net test-line delta of -2.

<details>
<summary>Redacted CLI request capture for 0d900c69e</summary>

The built CLI ran `agent --local` in a fresh session against a local Gemini-compatible streaming fixture. The explicit case added `--thinking medium`. Each fixture response matched the expected synthetic text.

```jsonl
{"case":"candidate-medium","override":"medium","exitCode":0,"expectedText":true,"requestCount":1,"wire":[{"routeMatches":true,"level":"MEDIUM","levelPresent":true,"thoughts":true,"tools":0,"fixtureAuth":true}]}
{"case":"candidate-default","override":null,"exitCode":0,"expectedText":true,"requestCount":1,"wire":[{"routeMatches":true,"level":null,"levelPresent":false,"thoughts":true,"tools":0,"fixtureAuth":true}]}
```

The upgrade check started with published OpenClaw 2026.10.10 in a separate isolated state directory. Stable saved `high` for the test session and sent `HIGH` again on reuse without a flag. The candidate ran `doctor --fix --non-interactive` for the existing migration, then reused the same session with no override. The saved choice still produced `HIGH`.

```jsonl
{"case":"candidate-doctor","exitCode":0,"providerRequests":0}
{"case":"candidate-upgrade-reuse","override":null,"exitCode":0,"expectedText":true,"requestCount":1,"wire":[{"routeMatches":true,"level":"HIGH","levelPresent":true,"thoughts":true,"tools":0,"fixtureAuth":true}]}
{"sameSessionAcrossVersions":true}
```

</details>

The request captures and upgrade check used a local fixture. Live Gemini Developer API verification remains outstanding. The exact model requires a [paid API tier](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing#gemini-3.1-pro-preview).

prs.title: fix(auth): wait for credential publication before inference
prs.body:
Related: #180719

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT sharing inference can fail with a credential-authority error when it starts during catalog credential publication.

## User Impact

A valid request waits for pending credential publication instead of failing transiently. Unknown settlement and retired authority still reject; final credential checks remain enforced. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catch only the existing owner's typed pending-publication error, await its settlement, and recheck the same retained authority. Keep preparation and the scope-derived options helper in the existing runtime reader. The follow-up restores that helper's placement and both consumer imports, removing the primitive scope module's SQLite-reaching type dependency without another owner or relaxed file-size limit.

## Evidence

### 2026-10-26: current head and main synchronization

Current head: `4d59598ca706f323b5806bda8a376b5c8e9dc707`, a normal merge of main `65112cda4acb357a13cd772641ed88acd9bb5759` into the existing PR history. GitHub now reports the PR as conflict-free (`MERGEABLE`), not approved or merged. The single conflict in `credential-authority.test.ts` was resolved by keeping main's lifecycle coverage and the original pending-publication regressions verbatim. The two PR production files remain byte-identical to `fce02957`.

Fresh checks: **92 tests in six affected files passed**, independent parent authority rerun **55 passed**, and the unchanged production-component transport proof passed **all four scenarios in both worker and parent runs**. Normal publication reaches transport once; unknown settlement, retired authority and locally revoked sharing each reach it zero times. Madge reports zero cycles; focused lint, core types, runtime-cycle, line-cap, format and PR-only diff checks pass. Whole staged-merge whitespace warnings reproduce byte-for-byte in pinned main's patch-file changes and were not silently reported as passing.

[Fresh captured results, conflict resolution and scope limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182428#issuecomment-6407829550). This is a new current-source component-integration run, not a new Gateway/native/external-provider run. New-head CI, re-review and maintainer security approval remain separate gates.

### Historical evidence retained for provenance

The remaining evidence below records the earlier `fce02957` head and the explicitly disclosed combined Gateway build. In particular, the historical 93-test count is not the new 92-test result above.

Follow-up commit: `fce02957b1ee242a894831103281d16d3aecaf36`. [Captured redacted output, exact source revisions and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182428#issuecomment-6382698787).

- Canonical madge: original PR head has one cycle; follow-up has zero. Parent independently reran the passing check.
- Six affected test files: 93 tests pass, independently rerun by parent. Focused types, lint, format and file-size checks pass. Fresh independent review of the four-file follow-up found no actionable P0–P2 issue.
- Actual isolated Gateway: a real catalog publication reply was held until preparation entered its existing settlement wait, then released. The same inference request resumed and returned `PROXY_180719_OK` through native Codex. One canary was submitted using the existing task-isolated protected credential owner, without forced refresh, copied credentials or a new login. Processes stopped and nonsecret transient configuration was restored.
- Live source combines this follow-up with the original, separately scoped fixes in #182426 and #182427. Explicit scheduling/observation instrumentation is separate from this PR and does not relax authority checks. This proves controlled overlap, not its natural frequency or an uninstrumented standalone-PR run.
- Earlier synthetic negative controls exercise real SQLite/credential owners with a manually opened publication batch: unknown and retired authority reject with zero continuation-spy calls. These are harness results, not authenticated-provider negative traces. The same three-case harness fails on the pre-PR base and passes on the follow-up.

- New exact-head production-component denial proof: [captured transport-boundary traces and full redacted reproduction fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182428#issuecomment-6383256512). A real HTTP request enters the shipped inference relay and OAuth resolution while the real publication owner is pending. The committed control reaches the real guarded-fetch final authority check and a loopback provider fixture once. Unknown settlement and owner retirement reject in the real wait, before guarded fetch. Sharing eligibility revoked during waiting reaches the final `beforeRequest` authority check and rejects there. All three denial cases have zero transport invocations and zero provider-fixture requests. Worker and coordinator independently pass all four scenarios; tracked PR source is unchanged.
- This new denial proof uses synthetic credentials, DNS and an injected final transport with actual loopback HTTP. It is not a full Gateway/native-Codex/external-provider negative run; the local sharing-eligibility transition is not a provider-side revocation exchange. It closes the earlier continuation-spy observation gap without claiming a broader live test.

Maintainer security approval and reviewer acceptance of the supplemental evidence remain outstanding. Independent proof is not security approval; no merge-readiness claim is made.

Related: #181826
Related: #174109

## What Problem This Solves

When a task needs a new credential, default guidance does not identify an admitted masked-entry tool, including when its schema is deferred.

## User Impact

Agents with the secrets capability receive its actual callable name and guidance to discover the schema, check a supported consumer, list metadata, and request only a missing task-needed credential. Its description explains existing channel-link prerequisites and blocked-flow recovery.

This is limited to admitted masked entry. Callers without that capability retain their previous policy, and supplied credentials remain available for requested use or storage. The opt-in/presentation work in #174109 remains separate. This PR does not enable the tool, expose a Gateway, or change admission, storage or permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt owner receives admitted capability names from embedded, Codex, Copilot and Agents API callers. Native Codex retains ownership of discovery syntax. The published revision preserves the intentional credential policy from #143238 and #157447 by omitting an unconditional chat prohibition. Four static description wording assertions were removed; availability/qualification coverage remains.

Canonical snapshots were regenerated and checked. All six files are current. Narrowing restores the existing fixture bytes, so no generated-file diff remains.

## Evidence

Ordinary merge `f9c32681a8c509edd200c6ee20d4755f35922e2a` integrates live main `9677960bc55dcbdbfb08faa71ed97abb802a7511` into prior head `f1dfa2feb708949a915c22162ff4a5ab876a79ca`. All nine PR-specific file edit scripts remain identical to the previous reviewed delta. Independent comparison of every added/removed line also matches, and the upstream Copilot publication-order correction remains unchanged. No PR-specific production semantics were added by this integration.

Fresh validation on the merged candidate: **178 tests across 10 files**, core and extension production typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and all **six canonical prompt snapshots** pass. Parent independently reran the credential policy/projection, Codex prompt, Copilot order and tool-surface suites on this exact commit: **57 tests passed**. A read-only merge probe against subsequently advanced main `33f1eccb074650900cdfc3694a0c4d736766cb80` is clean, so no additional integration was made solely for main advancement.

These are local new-head results. The successful hosted CI run [40519777504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519777504) belongs to prior head `f1dfa2fe`, not this new merge. New-head hosted CI and review must be evaluated separately. Historical v04/v05 runtime evidence retains its original revision and limitations; it was not rerun or relabeled as new-head live proof. Ordinary merge `f1dfa2feb708949a915c22162ff4a5ab876a79ca` integrates main `a1b7b2f38f0897749d5d8a46c1d96619412831e2`, including that correction. No conflicts or manual source resolutions were needed. Core and extension production typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, six canonical prompt snapshots and diff whitespace checks pass. A read-only merge probe against later main `e4749abd4ec81c727d0c27e5e4c722164ac3ffcc` also passes; no additional merge was made merely because main advanced.

These are new-head local results, not a claim of passing new-head hosted CI or security approval. The earlier red Copilot CI belongs to `d9d4631`; new-head CI must be evaluated separately. The previous ClawSweeper review found no actionable defects and accepted historical v04/v05 proof for verified unchanged guidance. Current-head review, exact-head maintainer security approval, and the product-direction decision remain separate gates.


### Historical 2026-10-27: attribution of the prior-head CI failure

The failing [Copilot CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40434698418/job/121960970739) is tracked separately in #185447. prs.title: fix: subagent image never reaches its parent and a stray child turn posts to chat when a subagent generates media
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a one-shot subagent (`sessions_spawn`, mode `run`) calls `image_generate`, `video_generate` or `music_generate`, its parent never receives the media, and a stray turn runs on the ended child. That turn's reply is posted to the user's chat.

## User Impact

A subagent now waits for its media as the tool result, the same way a cron run does. It reports the media in the result it returns to its parent, and its run ends with no later turns. The parent relays the image, and the chat receives it one time, from the parent.

Tradeoff: on `main`, the host sent the image straight to the chat from the child's late completion, so the user got it without the parent. Now the image reaches the user through the child's result. The child includes it with the normal `MEDIA:` reply directive, and the parent relays it. A child model that leaves out the directive returns text only. The subagent result is still text-only by contract. Carrying media in the completion record would be a durable registry change and is out of scope here.

## Why This Change Was Made

#199529 and #199585 set a rule on `main`: a one-shot run receives background results only while its executor owns it. Exec already applies this rule to subagents through `isOneShotRunSessionKey`. Media detachment (`shouldDetachMediaGenerationTask`) checked cron run keys only, so subagent media still detached. The completion then woke the finished child session. Media now uses `isOneShotRunSessionKey`, which covers cron runs and subagents.

Yielded subagents are not affected. `sessions_yield` waits for spawned children, and inline media gives the child nothing to yield for. Thread-bound subagents (`mode: "session"`) use the same subagent key. Exec already treats them as one-shot, and they now also generate media inline.

## Evidence

New real-Gateway QA-lab e2e: `test/e2e/qa-lab/media/subagent-image-generation.e2e.test.ts` (mock-openai plus a deterministic local image provider, user on qa-channel). The parent spawns a child, the child calls `image_generate` and replies, and the parent relays the result. The test asserts:

1. The child session sends exactly two model requests: the `image_generate` call, then its reply.
2. The only image the chat receives is the parent's relay.

**Red on `main` (b237d3e5c353):**

```
outbound: ["Started an image worker."], ["", ["image"]], ["QA-SUBAGENT-IMAGE-CHILD-DONE"], ["Protocol note: ... Background task started for image generation ..."]
expected [ 'image_generate', 'reply', 'reply' ] to deeply equal [ 'image_generate', 'reply' ]
```

The child's tool result was "Background task started", and its announced result had no image. The image then went to the chat with an empty caption, straight from a late `image_generate:…:ok` turn on the ended child. That turn's reply was also posted to the chat. The parent never received the image.

**Green on this branch:** passed. The child receives `Generated 1 image …` as its tool result and reports it. The parent relay `QA-SUBAGENT-IMAGE-PARENT-RELAY` carries the image, and no turn runs on the child afterwards.

Local gates:
- `ocx test`: touched unit test, mock-openai `server.test.ts`, the new e2e, `cron-image-generation.e2e.test.ts` and `cron-one-shot-run.e2e.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`
- type-aware oxlint and the formatter on the changed files

All passed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Older inactive chat history stays in SQLite unless operators discover and enable cold storage.

## User Impact

Eligible inactive transcripts are now compressed automatically after 30 days, including on existing installations that omit this setting. Explicit `session.maintenance.coldStorage.enabled: false` still disables future extraction, and existing archives remain restorable. Active/admitted work and recovery-owned history remain protected.

Cold files are authoritative history: use supported backups or retain the referenced archive files with direct database copies. As before, text search excludes cold transcript contents until restoration. Retention and deletion policies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler and extraction worker now share the cold-policy resolver, with defaults of enabled and 30 days. Settings reflects the same omitted-setting behavior instead of showing archival as off and disabling Run now. Help and current configuration docs describe the opt-out; no new configuration field or schema migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- [Before/after Settings screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199899#issuecomment-6905840130), using synthetic data with `coldStorage` omitted in both states. The uploaded GitHub assets were read back and inspected.

- 42 focused backend/schema tests passed across cold-storage round trips, default/explicit-false/age selection, active and recovery custody, scheduler hot reload, and schema help. The scheduler default regression failed on the base before the fix.
- All 4 session-storage browser E2E tests passed, including omitted configuration showing On/30 days with Run now available and saving an explicit false opt-out. The omitted-setting browser regression failed on the base.
- A built, isolated Gateway with synthetic 60-, 14-, and 1-day histories proved automatic archival with `coldStorage` completely omitted in warn mode. Only the 60-day history became cold. An explicit false hot-reloaded without restart and refused further manual extraction; production `chat.inject` restored the exact original bytes before appending while extraction was disabled. No live server state or external inference was used.
- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, targeted type-aware lint, generated config-doc baseline/check, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Lint retains an existing unchanged Solid tracking warning. The successful build also emitted advisory UI bundle-budget overages; broad CI admission remains separate.
- Independent local autoreview, P0–P2, found no actionable findings in the candidate based on `7d90a907c0ded71be3f9f89cb3ba799dcca7aceb`. All production bytes in `927bf4ffc136ec54f133e463494375e6a693a685` are unchanged from that review; subsequent changes only renamed a test-local variable and regenerated the config-help baseline.
