prs.title: fix(openai): recover item conflicts before output and across runs
prs.body:
Related: #199757

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes failed or repeatedly wedged turns when Responses reports `item_conflict` before assistant output, or a later internal session-effects run inherits a deferred repair.

## User Impact

Pre-output conflicts retry once within the same turn. Conflicts after text, reasoning, or tool activity remain deferred to avoid repeating work; the saved repair applies after reload and when that history is copied into an internal session-effects run. Successful requests applying a saved repair log `recovered`. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared SSE/WebSocket classifier inferred output from every event outside a short prelude list. Compaction progress and compaction item lifecycle events emit no assistant content, so they must not disable recovery. The replacement checks actual output items, deltas, and tool activity.

Deferred receipts already survive SQLite reopen, but their session identity fence prevented a copied history from applying its repair. Item-repair receipts now follow that history while preserving provider, model, endpoint, and credential fences. Encrypted checkpoints and ordinary compaction suppression remain session-bound. The converter reports when it applies a repair, including prepared-input reuse, so completion logging needs no additional history scan. Production delta: +62/−17, net +45 lines; growth carries the applied fact across conversion and request completion. No new cache or persistence format.

## Evidence

- Team build `dd2d58be`, including #199757 (`d1307e61`), logged `Model request failed` at 2026-11-16 02:07:13.716Z, `item_conflict_recovery outcome=deferred` at .717Z, and `Embedded agent failed before reply` at .760Z (run `e8dafb99`, request 1; dashboard hash `9e428ae0`, recovery hash `sha256:e1dc26a2550b`). The same recovery hash logged `deferred` at 02:13:22Z and 02:13:54Z on request 1 of new internal-session-effects runs. These logs establish recurrence; the incident's preceding wire events were not captured, so exact production attribution remains unconfirmed.
- Loopback integration: four compaction-progress cases fail on exact parent `443e9730695d6fa1549d84d9f45187883e9570f1`; two full compaction-lifecycle cases fail before the review correction. All 21 pass with the fix. Real text/function/hosted-tool output still defers over both transports.
- Real embedded runner with synthetic provider, tools, and SQLite: deferred → close/reopen → new run succeeds without another conflict, including a real internal-session-effects fork. Before the fix, the fork fails again; ordinary cold recovery lacked its completion log. All five cold-prefix scenarios now pass with repaired-prefix stability.
- Focused transport/WebSocket cases, checkpoint isolation, prepared context usage, provider parity, and all 14 agent-tool prefix-stability cases pass. All 5 Chromium browser and 7 UI end-to-end cases pass locally. No live provider or Team mutation was performed.
- Synthetic fixture: canonical agent schema, 5,000 sessions, 35.06 GiB logical SQLite data, 62,000 files/1.116 GB on compressed btrfs; no Team data copied. Five interleaved A1/A2/B repetitions, 30 operations/sample, with separate CPU/timing and sampled allocation. Stream owner (1,003 events): median 6.671 → 4.998 ms, CPU 4.095 → 4.078 ms, sampled allocation 5.593 → 5.614 MB. A/A wall noise −58% to +65%, CPU −20% to +1.2%, allocation −1.1% to +1.7%: no speedup claim. Fork repair (203 messages) now does the previously skipped work: 0.163 → 0.238 ms, CPU 0.277 → 0.370 ms, allocation 307.6 → 388.6 KB.
- Codex autoreview is P0–P2 scoped-clean for the full change and the final lexical-callback correction (`964b8c5b0a5f8567b7e163cd77e83874a276b9e0`, base `443e9730695d6fa1549d84d9f45187883e9570f1`). Its compaction-lifecycle finding was fixed with red/green proof. `pnpm check:changed` found an unbound-method lint error; the arrow callback fixes it, focused type-aware lint passes, and all 21 integration cases pass again. The full `pnpm check:changed --base 443e9730695d6fa1549d84d9f45187883e9570f1` rerun passes every check except the attributed baseline dead export (including corrected lint, core and all 29 test type graphs, formatting, and import-cycle guards). Exact-head [CI run 43794223591](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43794223591) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. prs.title: fix(agents): snapshot shareable MCP catalog metadata as JSON
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Production regression on Team after deploying `ea8bbbb3` (2026-11-15 18:52 PST): subagent runs fail about 2 s after spawn with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'u', ..."e},"mode":undefined}"... is not valid JSON`. Between 18:54 and 18:58 PST there were 12 parse failures and 24 subagent lane errors, and no subagent created after the cutover completed. Main and dashboard turns were unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

#199804 (3d4bd2a7) shares compacted tool catalogs across runs. It keys MCP descriptor metadata with `stableStringify`, which serializes `undefined` members as `undefined`, and then `JSON.parse`s those same key bytes to build the frozen snapshot. An MCP descriptor with an undefined optional field (`mode`) therefore throws on the shareable-catalog path. The snapshot now goes through `JSON.stringify`, which drops undefined members. The cache key is unchanged.

## User Impact

Subagents spawned in sessions with MCP tools run again. No config, schema, or persisted-state change.

## Evidence

- Regression test `src/agents/tool-search-prepared-catalog.test.ts`: on the parent it fails with the production `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "undefined"`, and it passes with the fix.
- Focused: `tool-search-prepared-catalog`, `tool-search-catalog-reuse`, and `tool-search.metadata` tests pass (5/5); oxfmt clean.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean (0.96).
- Team evidence: read-only Gateway log aggregates from the reliability session, `lane=subagent` errors since the cutover.

prs.title: feat(release): request stable and beta Gateway Store delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway betas need to reach the Microsoft Store Development flight automatically, not stop at signed GitHub prereleases. Regular stable releases need the same central, release-manager-approved Store handoff for Production.

## User Impact

After upstream GitHub activation, both release entry points request the exact signed Gateway source:

- **Beta on npm `beta`:** packaging signs and publishes x64, ARM64, and bundle GitHub prerelease assets, never Latest. Core waits for the successful build/publication, validates its source and current-attempt Store witness, then requests central **Development-flight** delivery.
- **Regular stable on npm `latest`:** packaging builds the Store bundle without sideload signing or a packaging GitHub release, then core requests central **Production** delivery.
- Alpha, extended-stable, failed activation, and mismatched channel/tag combinations remain excluded. Native publication stays detached from npm/GitHub completion.

**A queued request is not proof of delivery.** Both destinations require central release-manager approval. Automatic Development requests also require the central owner's operational activation flag and configured flight. Core adds no Store credential, flight GUID, or activation flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one detached `Windows Gateway Release Request` owner for both destinations. Beta retains `release_channel=beta`, exact published `gateway_version`, signed full-SHA `openclaw_ref`, `signing_mode=official`, and `publish_release=true`; it never follows the moving npm beta selector. Stable retains `signing_mode=store` and `publish_release=false`.

Both paths wait for the exact selected packaging-main run, verify the signed upstream source and separately selected release identity, and consume `openclaw-source-resolution/source-resolution.json` plus the current API `run_attempt` artifacts:

- `openclaw-gateway-msix-store-submission-<attempt>`
- `store-release-source-<attempt>/store-source.json`, binding run, attempt, packaging commit, source channel, exact packaging release/bundle identity, and SHA-256.

Core validates this routing evidence; central alone downloads/hashes the bundle and revalidates protected-main source history, signed payload/identity, published beta packaging release, approval, and destination. The central dispatch is `{product: gateway, run_id: <successful build>, channel: development | production, automatic: true}` to `openclaw/releases/windows-store-publish.yml` on `main`.

The existing release GitHub App (`2729701`, `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) needs Actions write and Contents read on core, packaging, and releases for **both** channels. No PAT or new Store secret is needed; installation grants remain unverified. Post-wait authority validation, original-request replay ownership, and ambiguous-dispatch evidence remain intact. Recover retained downstream runs rather than republishing npm or blindly redispatching.

The 45-minute build wait and 55-minute request-job timeout are unchanged. A build that outlasts that budget remains a retained downstream recovery task; core does not create a replacement build.

## Evidence

Head: `af77d00673cffe7ac7a140defa199fae65d56286` (signed; additive commit, no force push).

Reviewed the complete candidate against base `14d9d554f7d04b0c036c543ff2c2b4592faf958c`; reviewed tree `54ffb427a1264bb3852d065467cb5fd8c3c4ab06` matches the signed commit. prs.title: fix(gateway): keep bundle MCP ownership in MCP App tool-policy checks
prs.body:
Fixes #186775
Fixes #186777

## What Problem This Solves

Both MCP App entry points evaluate session tool policy with only the projected tool **name**:

- model-created App tool calls: `prepareModelCreatedAppToolCall` in `src/gateway/mcp-app-operations.ts`;
- the standalone App runtime: `assertTool` in `src/gateway/mcp-app-extension-runtime.ts`, whose name-only map also drives catalog filtering.

Catalog materialization records these tools as owned by `bundle-mcp` (`getPluginToolMeta`). Policy entries that allow tools by plugin ownership, such as the `coding` profile's `bundle-mcp` entry, only match when that ownership is supplied. Without it, an App tool the session's policy permits is rejected, or hidden from the App's available catalog. The MCP server name is not the plugin id, so it cannot stand in.

## User Impact

With `tools.profile: "coding"` and no other overrides, MCP Apps can call and list their bundle MCP tools again, as the policy intends. Deny rules, per-server overrides and `mcpToolsDeny` keep applying exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSessionResourceToolPolicy` already accepts `toolMeta` and forwards it to `isConversationToolAllowed()` (#172678). Both callers now pass the projected tool's registered metadata:

- `mcp-app-operations.ts`: `toolMeta: getPluginToolMeta(projected)`.
- `mcp-app-extension-runtime.ts`: the `(serverName, toolName)` map keeps the projected tool instead of only its name, and passes `toolMeta: getPluginToolMeta(projectedTool)` with `toolName: projectedTool.name`.

Ownership comes from the trusted catalog projection only. Nothing is inferred from names.

## Evidence

### Tests

- `src/gateway/session-resource-tool-policy.test.ts` has a new case, "admits a coding-profile MCP App tool only with its bundle MCP ownership". It uses the **real** policy evaluator with `tools.profile: "coding"`: `demo_show` is rejected without ownership and admitted with `{ pluginId: "bundle-mcp" }`. This shows the harm and the contract the callers must meet. The file passes 16/16.
- The earlier mock-forwarding case in `mcp-app-extension-runtime.test.ts` was removed after review (`cd68ff7`). It only asserted field forwarding into a mocked policy. The behavioral regression evidence for both entry points is the live A/B below: main denies, this branch allows, under `tools.profile: "coding"`.
- Related suites pass 65/65: `server-methods/mcp-app-extensions.test.ts`, `server-methods/mcp-app.view-grant.test.ts`, `agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.identity.test.ts`, plus the two files above.

Checks run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, core `tsgo` and `git diff --check` are clean.

### Live run: both App entry points, real Gateway and real MCP server (Windows 11, Node 26.12.1)

This is a real `openclaw gateway run` with a **real stdio MCP server** (`notes`), built on the repo's `@modelcontextprotocol/server`. The setup:

- `mcp.apps.enabled: true`.
- `launcher` is an MCP App (`ui://notes/app`). Its global quick action targets `write_note`.
- `write_note` (`destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`) appends one line to a log for every call the server receives. That log is the **final MCP effect**, counted below as "writes".
- Calls go through `openclaw gateway call` with token auth.
- Standalone path: `mcp.app.launch` quick action → `prepareMcpAppExtensionRuntime` → `resolveSessionResourceToolPolicy`.
- Model-created path: an OpenAI stand-in model calls `notes__launcher`, which creates a real App view. Then `mcp.app.callTool(write_note)` runs on that `viewId` → `prepareModelCreatedAppToolCall`. `tools.toolSearch: false` is set so that the model sees the MCP tools directly.
- "Revoked on the running Gateway" means the tools policy in `openclaw.json` was rewritten while the Gateway was running. The Gateway logged `[reload] config source revision 4 accepted (file)`, and the same call was then repeated.

![live run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186790/proof-186790.png)

| entry point · tools policy | main `a74f408db7f` | this branch `321bc3af402` |
|---|---|---|
| standalone · `profile: coding` | **denied** ("MCP App tool is unavailable or denied"), **0 writes** | **allowed**, 1 write |
| standalone · no profile (control) | allowed, 1 write | not run |
| standalone · `coding`, then `deny: ["bundle-mcp"]` hot-reloaded | not run | first call allowed (1 write); **next call denied, writes stay at 1** |
| standalone · `coding` + `deny: ["bundle-mcp"]` from start | not run | **denied, 0 writes** |
| model-created · `profile: coding` | **denied** ("The session's current tool policy does not allow this operation."), **0 writes**, even though the model itself was offered `notes__write_note` | **allowed**, 1 write |
| model-created · `coding`, then `deny: ["notes__write_note"]` hot-reloaded | not run | first call allowed (1 write); **same view denied, writes stay at 1** |
| model-created · `coding` + `deny: ["notes__write_note"]` from start | not run | **denied** ("not app-callable"), **0 writes** |

So on both entry points this change only restores the documented plugin allowance under `tools.profile: coding`. An explicit deny still prevents the MCP write, both from the start and after a live revocation. When a call is denied, no request reaches the MCP server.

### Standalone path: revocation while the call awaits approval

In this variant `write_note` has no read-only annotations, so the standalone call waits on a plugin approval. A persistent Gateway client with `operator.approvals` and the `approvals` cap holds the pending approval and resolves it with `allow-once` on cue.

| scenario (branch `321bc3af402`, `tools.profile: coding`) | approval | `mcp.app.launch` | MCP writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| approve while pending (control) | resolved `allow-once` | `note written` | 1 |
| `deny: ["bundle-mcp"]` hot-reloaded **while the approval is pending** (`[reload] config source revision 4 accepted`), then approve | the pending approval was already cancelled: resolve returns "approval already resolved" | "MCP App configuration changed; reopen the App" | **0** |

So revocation during the awaited preparation stops the standalone call before any MCP I/O, through the real standalone owner and the real stdio transport.

### Requester isolation

These checks run outside the lines this PR changes. They pass on this branch, and together with `mcp-app-extension-runtime.test.ts` and `session-resource-tool-policy.test.ts` the six files passed 127/127 at `321bc3af402` (the commit before the mock test was removed):

- `server-methods/mcp-app.view-grant.test.ts`: "does not reuse another requester's grant, including on an unbound shared view", "rechecks policy after approval and before a granted call executes", "revalidates a cached App grant after HTTP transport preparation before writing".
- `server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts`: "isolates requester-bound views, including read and write operations", "withholds resource read results when widget authority is revoked in flight".
- `mcp-app-tool-approval.test.ts`: "rejects requester revocation during review".
- `mcp-app-standalone.test.ts`: "does not downgrade requester-bound views into bearer-only standalone authority".

Requester binding (`resolveMcpAppActiveView` → `requireRequester`) runs before policy and is unchanged. On the model-created path, the execution-time `assertPolicy` in `prepareModelCreatedAppToolCall` re-runs `resolveSessionResourceToolPolicy` right before the effect. It now passes the same `toolMeta`, and it still re-checks live `mcpToolsDeny`, server overrides and the catalog policy snapshot. That re-check is why the hot-reloaded deny above blocks the second call on an already-open view.

**Standalone cross-requester rejection over a real transport** (`mcp-app.view-grant.test.ts`, `c64d942`). The existing real-transport case, "revalidates a cached App grant after HTTP transport preparation before writing", now runs for both entry points (`it.for(["model-created", "extension-runtime"])`). It uses the real `createSessionMcpRuntime` against a real streamable-HTTP MCP server, and the handlers inject requester identities `alice` and `bob` through `authenticatedUserProfile`. For the **standalone (extension runtime) owner**, the checks run in this order:

1. Alice opens a requester-bound view, approves `allow-always`, and the cached grant executes. The server receives 2 `tools/call`.
2. **Bob calls the same view and is rejected with "not authorized". The MCP server's HTTP POST count is unchanged**, so no MCP I/O happens.
3. Alice calls again, and the tool is denied (`mcpToolsDeny`) while that call is paused in HTTP transport preparation (DNS). The call is rejected, the POST count stays the same, and `tools/call` stays at 2.

Both variants pass, and the file passes 20/20.

Not covered live: a second requester *profile* on a real Gateway connection. Gateway user profiles attach only to device-authorized connections, and the live rig has a single token operator. The real-transport test above injects the two requester identities at the handler boundary instead.

prs.title: fix(audit): blank --agent silently returns every agent's audit records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw audit --agent ""` (or `--agent "$AGENT"` where the variable is empty) exits 0 and returns **every agent's** audit records — byte-identical to running `openclaw audit` with no filter at all. The same command with `--agent nonexistent` correctly returns an empty page, so an explicitly passed empty value is silently treated as "flag not provided" while any non-empty value is honored. `--session`, `--run`, `--execution`, `--channel`, and `--cursor` behave the same way: the blank filter is dropped before the query is built.

The `--execution` case is the sharpest: `openclaw audit --execution xyz` fails with `--execution requires --explain.`, but `openclaw audit --execution ""` succeeds and lists activity — a blank value silently bypasses a validation that a non-blank value triggers.

Root cause: `auditListCommand` builds `AuditActivityListParams` with truthy spreads (`...(options.agentId ? { agentId: options.agentId } : {})` and the same for `sessionKey`, `runId`, `executionId`, `channel`, `cursor`), so `""` never reaches the Gateway as a filter. The same function already **rejects** blank `--after` / `--before` / `--kind` / `--status` / `--direction` (bounds added in #137335), so the free-string filters are the inconsistent half.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator who scopes an audit query with an empty variable now gets `--agent must not be blank` and exit 1 instead of a successful report that silently widens the query to **all** agents, sessions, runs, and channels — before any Gateway call is made. Non-empty values, omitted flags, and every other `audit` path behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 13-line guard at the top of `auditListCommand` that mirrors the repository's existing `agentCliCommand` loop in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` (`["--agent", opts.agent], … → ${flag} must not be blank`), covering the six free-string list filters. It runs before the `--explain` branch and before `params` is constructed, so a present blank filter can never be normalized away.

Not introducing: no new error type, no config validation, no Gateway/protocol change, no new owner or export, no schema/API change. The `--limit` blank path keeps its existing `1 and 500` rejection, and `--kind`/`--status`/`--direction`/`--after`/`--before` keep their existing validators — this change only closes the free-string half of the same contract.

## Evidence

Base `37706a74a81129f8ec85289399a2703abf98c2b4` (branch base = `origin/main` at branch creation) → Candidate `daba319ff1d884e144c71126b57548e85023e341` (branch `fix/audit-blank-filters`).

Environment: Linux x64, Node v24.22.1, normally built `openclaw.mjs` (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build:docker`), isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` + `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + isolated `HOME`, and a dedicated isolated Gateway started by this proof (`openclaw gateway run --port 18999 --allow-unconfigured`) so `audit` has something to query. The isolated ledger contains exactly **one real record**, written by the Gateway itself:

```text
TIME                         KIND       DIRECTION  CHANNEL  STATUS     AGENT  RUN               ACTION
2026-11-05T19:00:08.706Z     agent_run  -          -        succeeded  main   d268d961-0f0f-41e… agent.run.finished
```

That record makes the byte-identity comparisons non-trivial: a dropped filter has to return it, and an honored filter has to hide it. Every case below was run **twice** and compared with `cmp` (exit code + stdout + stderr), not by eye.

### Shipped CLI (each leg run at least twice)

| case | base | candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `audit` (no filter) ×2 | exit 0, header + the record above | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `audit --agent ""` ×2 | **exit 0, byte-identical to `audit`** — the blank filter is dropped and `main`'s record is returned although a specific agent was requested | **exit 1**, stderr `--agent must not be blank` |
| `audit --agent nonexistent` ×2 | exit 0, header only (a real value **is** honored) | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `audit --execution ""` ×2 | **exit 0**, returns the record (blank dropped; should have failed the `--explain` rule) | **exit 1**, stderr `--execution must not be blank` |
| `audit --execution xyz` ×2 | exit 1, stderr `--execution requires --explain.` | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |
| `audit --cursor ""` ×2 | **exit 0, byte-identical to `audit`** (blank cursor dropped) | **exit 1**, stderr `--cursor must not be blank` |
| `audit --session ""` (candidate spot check) ×2 | — (covered by the unit test below) | exit 1, stderr `--session must not be blank` |

The decisive pair: on base, `audit --agent ""` returns the record and `audit --agent nonexistent` does not — the same query with an empty value is wider than the query with an explicit non-existent value.

### Regression RED → GREEN (remote, real vitest)

Remote proof host (Docker `lexiflow-all:latest`, Node `v24.22.1`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`); `src/commands/audit.ts` and `src/commands/audit.test.ts` verified md5-identical to `git show origin/main:<path>` before the RED run:

```text
sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts \
  src/commands/audit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **base production + extended test → RED:** `6 failed | 25 passed (31)`. The six failures are exactly the new cases — `rejects invalid --agent / --session / --run / --execution / --channel / --cursor before calling the Gateway` — each with `AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting` at `src/commands/audit.test.ts:76`.
- **candidate production + the same test → GREEN:** `31 passed (31)`.
- **Sibling on the candidate:** `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts` (root matrix) → `1 passed (1)` file, `17 passed (17)`. `auditListCommand`'s only production caller is `src/cli/program/register.audit.ts`, which has no dedicated test file, and no other test file imports `auditListCommand` (grep over `origin/main`).

### Local gates

```text
oxlint (v1.88.0) src/commands/audit.ts src/commands/audit.test.ts → 0 findings, exit 0
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <both files> → All matched files use the correct format
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 37706a74a81 → Test lines OK: 6496710; ceiling: 6496752; slack: 42
git diff --check → clean
```

### Line counts

Whole-PR delta: production **+13/-0** (1 file), tests **+6/-0** (1 file), `config/test-lines-allocations/audit-blank-filters.txt` = **6** for exactly this PR's net test growth. Shared scalar `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` untouched. On a clean `37706a74a81` the ratchet reports `Test lines OK: 6496704; ceiling: 6496746; slack: 42`, so this branch stays inside the ceiling with the allocation applied.

### Negative claims

- Not claimed: `--limit ""` (already rejected by the existing `1 and 500` bound), `--kind`/`--status`/`--direction`/`--after`/`--before` (already validated by #137335 and untouched here).
- Not claimed: records for a **second** agent or a non-default channel — the isolated ledger holds one `agent_run` for `main`, so the widening is proven against that single record, not against multi-tenant data.
- Not claimed: `audit --explain` behavior for blank selectors beyond the guard itself; the guard runs before that branch, but the proof exercises the activity-list path.

## Focused Checks and Simplification

- 13 production lines, 1 production file; the guard is a straight-line loop at the existing command entry, lifted from the in-repo `agentCliCommand` precedent — no helper, no wrapper, no new export.
- Test merged into the file that already owns the contract (`audit.test.ts`) by extending the existing `rejects invalid $flag before calling the Gateway` `it.each`, so the new cases reuse the existing `callGateway`-not-called assertion instead of adding a new harness.
- Test-lines: this PR adds an allocation of exactly its +6 growth and leaves the shared scalar alone.

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous silent fallback without migrations or persisted state changes. Blast radius is `auditListCommand`'s validation of six free-string filters; the guard runs before any option is consumed and before `callGateway`, so no Gateway request, `--explain` branch, or output path changes for non-blank input. Unchanged adjacent behavior: omitted flags, non-empty valid values, non-empty unknown values (still an empty page), `--limit`, all enum/timestamp filters, `--json`, and every non-`audit` command.

Collision check (run against `origin/main` minutes before opening): the only open PR that touches these two files is **#141004** (`feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage`, different purpose). Its `src/commands/audit.ts` hunks sit at lines 63–234 (record type, row rendering, filter helpers, legacy-param mapping) and never reach `auditListCommand` at line 506, so this PR's guard does not overlap them. In `src/commands/audit.test.ts` both PRs append cases to the same `rejects invalid $flag before calling the Gateway` `it.each` array — adjacent-line additions that resolve trivially on rebase, with no shared semantic change. Every other candidate from the per-file `gh api pulls/<n>/files` sweep (#181303, #193525, #191070, #184328) is unrelated to blank filters, and merged #137335 covered only the timestamp/enum bounds.

prs.body:
Fixes #195517

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an in-flight run failing with HTTP 401 after another run rotates their shared OAuth account token, including providers that exchange the OAuth source for a runtime token.

## User Impact

A replay-safe run can recover once using the same account’s canonical credential instead of ending with a sign-in error. Direct OAuth retries require a changed token; runtime-exchange providers can re-exchange an unchanged source when only the runtime token expired. Explicit reconnects and account-identity changes cannot revive the old run. No configuration change or migration is required. Existing outer replay-safety restrictions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical OAuth resolution now has one shared owner for request auth, direct 401 recovery, and runtime exchanges. It omits the captured store, keeps the selected profile locked, settles sibling publication, and retains the run’s captured authorization around lookup and refresh admission. Runtime exchange validates that same authorization before provider egress and again before installing its result. The canonical source and exchanged runtime token remain separate; scheduled refreshes use the same path as auth-error refreshes.

The original fork diff at `462ef9d8d2cff63335a4b4267c45b8a62cc98a96` was applied to main `2995860edbf34e5a4d18793a118a13c273a2bd98`. The exact follow-up commit `a7c0dae964146323bb6eda2b5a1e31aab6b23af8` addressed direct retry authorization. The runtime-exchange correction in `aef09e9b865a3466641dd9ba27d4dcab66439f60` follows PR head `3cfa6cb3fcf5153c690411a3a574b984b3304656` without replacing branch history.

## Evidence

- Original and first follow-up applied/source patch IDs: `2a7abfb7efbd249fbb2ca2d55e09a38e21d045c8` and `bcd093ef4da549c577bfe3bc286bf652252b232f` respectively.
- Runtime-exchange regression coverage: sibling rotation, unchanged-source re-exchange, same-account reconnect rejection before a second exchange, and reconnect during exchange preventing token installation. Existing direct-token cases and one-retry checks remain. Net new test coverage is 76 lines, allocated separately from the original 62-line allocation; production line count does not grow.
- Current correction: targeted formatting and lint passed (0 warnings/errors), `git diff --cached --check` passed, and test-line ratchet passed.
- Current correction: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json` passed.
- Independent local Auto Review against `3cfa6cb3fcf5153c690411a3a574b984b3304656` through P2 returned scoped-clean. The unchanged provider-secret-egress module was excluded by review input policy; its implementation was not independently reassessed.
- [Contributor-reported red/green proof for prior head 3cfa6cb3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195522#issuecomment-6731481071): 25 request-auth tests passed, with reconnect regression failing against the older code. This is prior-head evidence, not execution of the new runtime-exchange cases.
- **Remaining validation gap:** new focused runtime tests/red-green proof and a live Gateway/model-transport trace were not executed here. No qualified secretless fork-code execution route is available in this session. Static checks and source review do not substitute for runtime proof. The PR remains draft.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): interrupting a reply leaves the agent working on the abandoned question
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller interrupts a reply, and the agent keeps working on the question they just abandoned.

Barge-in today is audio-side only: queued telephony audio is cleared and the active reply is
cancelled, so the caller is no longer talked over and no obsolete answer is spoken. But the agent
run behind that turn continues, so the caller waits out work they already interrupted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `bargeIn.abortAgentRun` that also aborts the in-flight run for the call.

**Cancellation is owned per response.** Each response creates its own `AbortController` and passes
it alongside the work-admission signal (`AbortSignal.any([...])`), then hands that abort to the
webhook. Barge-in fires that exact handle. This matters because a session-keyed abort resolves
whichever turn currently occupies the session: with `maxConcurrentCalls > 1` and
`sessionScope: "main"`, that can be another call's accepted work. The locally minted `runId` cannot
select a run either, since the harness never sees it. The controller is therefore the only authority
over this run, and it is retired when the response settles.

The abort is immediate rather than graceful: it does not wait for a tool-call boundary, and a
foreground exec child process is killed as soon as the signal fires.

History handling is delegated, not reimplemented. Tool calls that already completed stay persisted
by the embedded runner, so the next run resumes with that work intact. Tool calls killed mid-flight
are left without results, and the existing transcript repair layer synthesizes the placeholders on
the next run. The interrupted question is deliberately not carried forward: it is already in session
history, and the barged-in utterance becomes the next turn on its own.

Supporting changes, all needed for the abort to behave:

- **`command-queue`**: an `AbortError` is a deliberate cancellation, not a lane task failure.
  Without this, every interruption wrote two error lines for work cancelled on purpose. Added
  alongside the existing classifications rather than replacing them - `isExpectedRunCancellation`
  does not cover a bare `AbortError`.
- **`exec`**: log the killed child on abort so an operator can see which process died with the run.
  **Identifiers only** - session and pid, never command text and never a derived command label,
  because both retain arguments and arguments carry credentials.
- **One registry owner**: `registerRun` returns a cleanup closed over its own run id, so a
  late-settling turn cannot clear the run that replaced it.

## User Impact

- Opt-in and off by default: `bargeIn.abortAgentRun` defaults to `false`, so existing installs keep
  today's audio-only behaviour on upgrade. No stored data or config shape changes.
- With it enabled, interrupting stops both the speech and the work behind it.
- Explicitly backgrounded commands survive the abort; only foreground children are killed, and the
  documentation says so.

**Scope: the streaming path only.** The flag is read where the streaming trigger lives. The realtime
bridge does not consult it, and the documentation now states that explicitly instead of implying
both paths honour it. Streaming and realtime are mutually exclusive (`config.ts` rejects both), so
any one call is only ever on a single path. Realtime is a straightforward follow-up.

## Evidence

Two live outbound Twilio Programmable Voice + Media Streams calls on a build pinned to this PR's
code (`737a5060808`), verified before dialing by the `dist/index.js` build timestamp and its banner
reporting `2026.11.1 (737a506)`. Identifiers are redacted; structure and timings remain.

### Foreground child kill, and abort immediacy

```
11:11:39.396 Outbound call initiated: callId=<redacted> mode=conversation
11:12:06.144 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794327125192
11:12:06.199 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
11:13:03.421 [exec] abort killed child session=<redacted> pid=81432
11:13:03.422 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794327148253
11:13:03.428 Code Mode execution failed runId=voice:<redacted>:1794327148253 failureKind=aborted
11:13:03.490 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
11:13:29.742 Call finalized callId=<redacted> endReason=completed
```

The child dies at `.421`, **one millisecond before** the barge-in line at `.422`, and the whole
chain settles in 69 ms. That ordering is the immediacy claim: a cancellation waiting for a tool-call
boundary could not produce it. The diagnostic carries `session=` and `pid=` and no command payload.

### Completed results survive, and the next turn resumes

An earlier call on the same build:

```
09:51:47.039 Outbound call initiated: callId=<redacted> mode=conversation
09:52:28.321 barge-in aborted agent run runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322335274
09:52:28.335 Code Mode execution failed runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322335274 failureKind=aborted
09:52:28.409 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
09:52:41.127 barge-in aborted agent run runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322351728
09:52:41.184 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
09:53:02.243 barge-in aborted agent run runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322368701
09:53:02.310 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
09:53:25.826 Call finalized callId=<redacted> endReason=completed
```

Three interruptions, three **distinct** `runId` values, each settling within 60-90 ms, with an
in-flight tool call aborted 14 ms after the first barge-in. In session history the killed call's
result slot holds the repair layer's synthesized placeholder ("Tool call interrupted before a result
was recorded; its outcome is unknown"), while the preceding turn's **completed** tool result remains
intact - and the model reasoned over both on the next turn: "The first batch got interrupted before
anything was recorded, so I reran it and all five searches completed." The barged-in utterance
became the next turn on its own; the abandoned question was not carried forward.

No `barge-in agent run abort failed` line appeared in either call, so the guard never had to swallow
a throw.

### Cross-call isolation

Covered by test rather than capture, deliberately: proving it by phone means winning a race on
purpose, whereas the suite asserts it on every run. `webhook.barge-in-abort.test.ts` registers two
calls under one session id, barges in on A, and asserts only A's handle fires while B stays
abortable. That case and replacement-cleanup survival both fail against the previous session-keyed
implementation, so they are regressions rather than restatements.

## Local gates

```
oxlint                 0 warnings, 0 errors
tsgo:extensions        clean
tsgo:extensions:test   clean
tsgo:core              clean
vitest                 2 files, 13 tests passed
config:docs:check      OK
line-cap ratchet       webhook.ts no longer listed - back within baseline
```

### The earlier webhook line-cap failure is resolved

The previous revision pushed `webhook.ts` from 829 to 830 counted lines. Moving the turn's cleanup
ownership into the response generator - where the run lifecycle already lives - **removed** a line
from `webhook.ts` rather than adding one, so the file is back within baseline with no unrelated
decomposition of that file.

### Three remaining ratchet failures are inherited from `main`

```
src/secrets/egress-proxy/proxy-server.test.ts: 1000 -> 1021 counted lines (cap 1000)
src/state/agent-database-startup.ts:            700 ->  708 counted lines (cap 700)
test lines: 6590377; ceiling: 6590318; over by 59; net delta +10449
```

Neither file is touched by this PR, both are byte-identical to `main`, and
`config/max-lines-baseline.txt` and `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` are byte-identical to `main`'s.
The `+10449` test-line delta arrived with the merge from `main`. This PR's own contribution to the
test-line count is **negative**: the withdrawn exec suite and a leaner coordinator suite outweigh
the added webhook cases, and the allocation was recut 398 -> 272 to match the surviving suites.

## Review response

This revision addresses the ownership, logging, documentation, test-allocation and proof findings
from the Codex review. Command arguments no longer reach the abort diagnostic; cancellation binds to
the exact admitted response instead of the current session occupant; the duplicate run registry is
gone and cleanup carries its own identity; the realtime documentation claim is withdrawn; and the
exec abort-kill suite was withdrawn along with the command-label logging it existed to pin.

The product question - whether the preserved-accepted-work split from #133484 is a principle that
should always hold or a default a deployment may opt out of - remains open and is asked separately
in the thread.

## Provenance notes

This branch was ported fresh onto current `main`, not rebased: the source branch sat on a base
24,034 commits behind, on top of a local integration branch carrying unrelated work. Only the
barge-in scope is here. Deliberately excluded: the chunking work (#118727), deepgram changes from
closed PRs, a queued-message-marker removal that upstream has since extended rather than dropped,
and an `isOpenAIResponsesApi` parameter removal that fights the documented Codex-normalization
design.

`main` has since been merged in to clear a conflict; the only conflicted file was the generated
`docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, resolved by regenerating it rather than taking either
side.

prs.title: fix(muse): allow slow starts without missing-install errors
prs.body:
Fixes #195521

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Muse startup on a busy host or a large local store could fail after 30 seconds with misleading install/sign-in guidance. Startup cancellation also failed to reach chat acquisition, could interrupt another caller sharing the starting host, and lost non-Error cancellation reasons.

## User Impact

Muse has up to 120 seconds to initialize, and catalog reads allow that window plus 30 seconds. Startup deadlines report a timeout rather than suggesting a reinstall. Canceling a chat or catalog wait preserves that caller's reason without aborting another live waiter. The starting host is stopped when its last waiter cancels. A genuinely stalled startup takes longer to fail. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep host startup ownership in the existing Muse pool: forward the turn signal, race each caller's wait independently, and track live waiters before aborting shared startup. Reuse the existing SDK abort helper. The catalog owner exports its deadline derived from the startup limit. Test gates stay under the suite cleanup owner, with named pipes on Windows.

The supplied timeout fix and prior test-directory cleanup are retained. Main was integrated only to resolve an actual import conflict, preserving upstream Muse usage reporting; the reviewed base is `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f`.

## Evidence

- [Contributor-reported live proof by @saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195548#issuecomment-6731114716) exercises the earlier timeout fix with delayed Muse startup: main +40s failed after 33s with misleading guidance; the fix's no-delay control succeeded in 18s; +40s succeeded in 48s; +130s failed after 124s with the correct 120-second timeout. These are the contributor's runs, not RoboClaw's, and do not validate this cancellation follow-up.
- Added production-boundary regressions for canceling chat during host startup and retrying, one canceled waiter alongside a surviving shared-startup waiter (one host spawn), and exact Error/string/object cancellation reasons. Tests drive the existing fake MSP process and actual harness/pool rather than mocking acquisition.
- The Muse production leaf typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/muse/tsconfig.json`) passed after correcting a possibly-undefined mutable entry capture in the startup callback. Targeted formatting, extension lint (0 warnings/errors), and staged whitespace checks passed. The staged test-line ratchet passed with the original 50-line allocation plus an explicit 83-line allocation for the cancellation regressions and portable startup gate.
- Independent source-only Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) reviewed the eight-file diff and full affected sources. Its actionable Windows socket finding was fixed with a named-pipe gate and statically rechecked; it reported no other actionable P0–P2 findings. This is not runtime proof.
- **Remaining coverage gaps:** focused automated tests, red/green execution, and Windows execution have not run here because no approved secretless fork runner is available; contributor code was not executed locally. The static production leaf excludes test files, so test-file typechecking remains a coverage gap. Delayed catalog discovery and the new cancellation scenarios still need executable proof. Prior-head CI does not validate these changes; updated-head CI is required.

Contributed by @saariuslystoned (Bobby Bones). ☁️

prs.title: fix(ui): Cmd+K compose forgets the last selected model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cmd+K Compose forgets the selected model when reopened or reloaded. Reopening while the preference save is still pending can also leave the old model displayed after the save succeeds.

## User Impact

With last-used defaults enabled, the chosen model is retained for the next conversation. Configured defaults still use the configured model. Placement remains separately opt-in, and the foreground worktree name is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model selections now use the existing per-agent preference writer independently of palette placement suppression. When this palette's own save succeeds, the existing guarded adoption path updates its defaults, preserving later explicit selections and the configured-default policy.

No storage keys, formats, migration, CAS or connection guards changed. There is no new cache or polling. Existing default adoption may revalidate a restored custom folder on save completion.

## Evidence

Final reviewed head: `1f5132ebec5f2ffa1c0332effa8ac6290684f202`.

- Fresh main `44522c44d695` reproduced the original forgotten-model behavior in the compiled Control UI.
- The incoming PR also failed a controlled save held across close/reopen: storage contained the chosen model, but the picker stayed on the old one. The corrected owner passes that same scenario.
- Both compiled-app Chromium cases pass: last-used and configured policies, delayed save, close/reopen, reload, session creation and preservation of the foreground worktree name.
- 159 focused model, preference, placement and palette cases plus the standard 535 UI canaries pass. UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- The worktree regression now waits for the observable saved model instead of spying on the obsolete writer, retaining the accepted-name assertion. Capture-only code was removed from the permanent E2E.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings.
- These are real Control UI runs with synthetic Gateway responses, not live provider calls. Existing preference decoding/storage code is unchanged and seeded preferences survive reload; no full installation-upgrade run is claimed.
- The previous ratchet CI job received a runner shutdown signal; it reported no code ratchet violation. The new head must pass its current checks.

### After

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(channels): unblock ingress after a transient shutdown release failure
prs.body:
Closes #193019

## Main compatibility refresh — 2026-11-06

Published merge head `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`, integrating main `b11b610d173cc6ff87eb026b6506c20fc7e5fd62` without rewriting PR history. The single `ingress-drain.ts` conflict is resolved preserving upstream failure callback extraction, queue-cap drops, selective custody retirement and test consolidation.

**Updated scope:** main #193423 already mitigates the old indefinite hold by retiring failed drains and permitting recovery of known never-adopted claims after disposal. This PR retains the bounded, token-fenced native cancellation-release retry before disposal; it does not claim current main remains indefinitely blocked. Pinned-main production overlay fails the focused retry regression (one release instead of two). Exhaustion coverage now follows upstream recovery after joined disposal; uncertain outcomes remain fenced.

**New-head verification:** 180 tests across 13 affected files passed; final worker handoff rerun 12 passed, coordinator independent rerun 12 passed. Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, source-line ratchet and scoped whitespace passed. Independent exact-head semantic review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install used target-identical manifests/lockfile. Test-line ratchet retains main's 25-line debt: pinned main is 25 over, candidate is 25 over, and the PR adds exactly its existing 182-line grant. No shared ceiling was changed. New-head CI is not claimed green.

**Proof provenance:** all Telegram/Claude live evidence below remains historical at `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. Writer bytes are equivalent, but upstream custody/disposal, dependencies and test contracts changed; no live-proof equivalence or new-head live run is claimed. No production restart or new Telegram traffic occurred.

Later observed main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e` also merge-probes cleanly; intervening changes are iOS tooling, so no additional merge was introduced.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued channel messages remain blocked when a pre-adoption cancellation release fails once during shutdown and the retained old drain continues holding its claim.

## User Impact

A transient known release failure can recover automatically so a replacement monitor can deliver the queued conversation. Cancellation preserves delivery retry history. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained cancellation after abort now joins at most three token-fenced release attempts, with 1s and 2s backoffs. The existing settlement owner holds custody throughout. Explicit disposal prevents another attempt; failed completion, ordinary abandonment, standalone drains, and uncertain write outcomes keep their existing safety behavior. Exhaustion or an uncertain cancellation write remains observable and retains custody. The bounded retry can add up to three seconds of backoff to shutdown, plus storage I/O.

## Evidence

- A real production ingress monitor stop/restart with an actual isolated SQLite-backed queue fails on the unchanged base and passes with the repair. One known failure is injected before the native release write; the lifecycle callback is invoked only once. The replacement processes same-lane events in order, rejects stale-token writes, and does not replay already-adopted unrelated work.
- Focused drain, monitor, handoff and claim-owner suites: 73 tests passed. Added checks cover exhausted retries, nested uncertain outcomes, explicit disposal during backoff, takeover during retry, standalone cancellation and ordinary abandonment. Existing failed-completion and retry-history controls pass.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, line-cap/test-line ratchets and whitespace checks are recorded in the local handoff.
- Independent shared autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, one pass over the complete uncommitted candidate against `06d4059a3d06` and supplied unchanged owner context; no actionable findings. This is evidence-based review, without a repository mount or test execution in the reviewer sandbox. Subsequent test edits only added required braces and an explicit already-completed return and removed a redundant default type argument. The coordinating parent independently inspected the final source and clean commit and reran all 10 boundary cases successfully.

**Initial test scope (historical; supplemented by the real Telegram/model run below):** proof here is the owning monitor/SQLite boundary with a synthetic pre-write failure. Actual SQLite locking, a complete Gateway process, a real agent/model, and Telegram transport were not exercised; no live outage reproduction is claimed. Exact live Gateway channel stop/restart under an actual storage lock remains a broader integration gap. No external API or transport contract changes here.

The dedicated allocation grants exactly 182 added test lines for this recovery regression and its distinct custody bounds; the shared baseline is unchanged. The change reuses existing owners and removes redundant release wrappers; production code grows by 12 lines. The four-suite run took 41.92s including worker preparation; the final boundary file took 4.63s in Vitest (50.61s wrapper including compiler preparation), and the parent independently measured 4.92s (53.90s wrapper). CI timing is unmeasured before publication.


## Additional shipped-entry-point evidence — 2026-11-05

The earlier Evidence section describes the initial monitor tests. This additional run used the real built CLI/Gateway, its plugin loader, and the public `channels.stop` / `channels.start` RPCs. It was **not another in-process monitor test**. The channel was a task-only local diagnostic plugin (`ingress-proof/default`), not Telegram. Its delivery callback deliberately calls synthetic `onDeferred` / `onAdopted`; **no real agent/model response or external transport was exercised, so this does not claim the root real-agent/model E2E gate is fully satisfied**.

**Isolation and provenance.** Separate task HOME, config, SQLite state, workspace and loopback ports; only the diagnostic plugin enabled; no provider credentials copied, no production Gateway restart/config/state change, no real-channel messages. The same fixture and one-shot fault wrapper ran against head `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2` and runtime inputs from base `06d4059a3d06e1a34a3cacfd3f635b93fe803a38`. For the base run, only the two owner files were temporarily restored byte-for-byte from the base and rebuilt through the CLI; all other runtime inputs matched base (only the new test/allocation differed). This was a documented base-runtime overlay in the head checkout, not a Git checkout whose HEAD changed. Original source was restored afterward.

The external plugin uses public SDK `createChannelIngressMonitor` and `api.runtime.state.openChannelIngressQueue`. It throws exactly once **before** calling the native release operation, logs refresh only after the real queue returns `true`, and reads the committed queue via the public API. There is no SQLite method mock, SQL reset, forced owner retirement, manual second cancellation callback, or claimed actual `SQLITE_BUSY`. The fixture SHA-256 is `d1d039654e952e53eff1e39baa8680360637a26f3e8cf0bad372773df0b7fcb3`.

**Base observation.** Real Gateway PID `95449`: the channel stop RPC reported `stopped: true`, but the internal joined monitor stop rejected the injected error. Starting the replacement channel did not drain its lane. Only `unrelated` was synthetically adopted; `task` remained claimed and `waiting` pending. Committed `claimedAt` values advanced at `2026-11-05T11:03:19.612+09:00`, `2026-11-05T11:03:21.614+09:00`, and `2026-11-05T11:03:58.706+09:00`; heartbeat commit counts were `[4, 6, 43]`. This is a bounded observation of continued old-owner renewal, not an empirical claim that it can never recover.

```text
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":95449,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-abort","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":95449,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-rejected","generation":1,"pid":95449,"message":"Error: Synthetic known cancellation release failure before native write","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback-returned","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:58 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
```

**Head observation.** Real Gateway PID `93148` remained the same across channel generation 1→2. One cancellation callback caused one known pre-write failure, then release attempt 2 committed about one second later and joined stop succeeded. The replacement synthetically adopted `task`, then `waiting`; the already-adopted `unrelated` was not replayed. The old token's release/complete/refresh all returned `false`, the successor token differed, and re-enqueue of `unrelated` returned `completed`. Final pending and claimed sets were empty.

```text
10:58:29 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:58:59 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"unrelated","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":2,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-result","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","committed":true,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"stale-token-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"release":false,"complete":false,"refresh":false,"changed":true}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"waiting","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:14 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"dedupe-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"kind":"completed"}
11:00:37 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
```

**Shipped command path.** Under each task-only environment: `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`; then `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call` with `--expect-url` pinned to that task's configured loopback Gateway, using `ingressProof.seed`, `ingressProof.arm`, `channels.stop`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, `channels.start`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, and `ingressProof.dedupe` (head). Public lifecycle params were `{"channel":"ingress-proof","accountId":"default"}`. All these RPC commands exited 0; the base's reported stop success is distinguished above from its monitor failure. Both task Gateways later handled SIGTERM and exited 0 with clean shutdown. No commit/push was required for this instrumentation.

**Interpretation and limits.** A generally slow model cannot explain this comparison because no model runs; identical fixture, queue, lane and fault behavior plus the advancing native timestamps distinguish a retained old-owner claim from a delayed initial read. However, the fixture deliberately supplies deferred/cancelled work and observes its own callback receipts. Its synthetic adoption is not evidence of agent execution, outbound send, Telegram acceptance, or user-visible response. It does not prove an actual database lock, indefinite blockage beyond the observed interval, every channel adapter, or a whole-Gateway process restart. It proves a real Gateway-hosted local channel stop/replacement through shipped entry points with actual SQLite persistence. Whether this layer satisfies the requested real-behavior gate remains for review; the broader real agent/model/transport gap is explicit.


## Real Telegram and real model recovery evidence — 2026-11-05

**Observed result:** recovery eventually succeeded through the production Telegram adapter, real Claude CLI agent/model, and Telegram Bot API. It did **not** succeed on the first replacement: the task relay refused two overlapping local polls and the adapter automatically restarted twice before both replies completed. The human operator confirmed in the Telegram client that the replies arrived in A → B order. Per-event counts below are backed by the queue, transcript and Bot API receipts; the human confirmation specifically establishes client-visible order.

Pinned PR head: `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. The requesting user confirmed their dedicated bot was unused elsewhere, then sent a fresh exact handshake and prescribed A/B prompts manually in the verified private DM. No automated user account or team QA pool was used. The isolated Gateway had task-owned config/state/workspace/ports. A parent-owned, destination-bound protected HTTPS relay consumed the stored token sentinel; no credential value was extracted or copied into the Gateway. The operator Gateway was untouched.

Temporary instrumentation held only A before real admission and injected one known error before the original claim's native cancellation release write. It never invoked synthetic adoption. Native cancellation, the PR's existing bounded writer retry, real Telegram replay, real agent/model execution and outbound delivery remained production paths. Setup `deleteWebhook` was a recorded local no-op after verified empty webhook; no upstream webhook deletion or queue flush occurred. Command-menu deletion attempts were refused locally.

Measured timeline, KST:

```text
13:31:16.764  A held before native adoption
13:31:58.907  bound B observed by real Telegram poller
13:32:36.938  read-only task SQLite: A claimed, B pending; same lane; attempts=0
13:32:38.283  one known pre-write release failure for original A token
13:32:39.285  second release attempt for that same token (+1002ms)
13:32:40      manual channel replacement starts
13:32:41      local concurrent-poll refusal; automatic restart scheduled
13:32:47–48   first automatic restart also hits local poll guard
13:32:58      second automatic restart starts
13:32:59.308  real A adoption/completion write commits with new claim token
13:33:03.954  Telegram accepts final A response
13:33:04.053  real B adoption/completion write commits
13:33:06.414  Telegram accepts final B response
```

The old long-poll request remained in the relay until its bounded upstream request returned after the downstream client was cancelled. The relay's single-poll guard refused the two successor attempts rather than starting another upstream poller. This was task relay lifecycle behavior, not a second bot consumer or a newly fixed PR behavior. No queue reset, forced retirement, manual second cancellation callback or failed-send retry was used to recover.

Final read-only SQLite inspection found exactly A and B, both `completed`, both attempts=0, with no pending/claimed work. The real agent transcript contains exactly two assistant records matching the prescribed A and B responses in order, both `provider=claude-cli`, `api=cli`, with actual usage: A input10/output181/cache-write11936; B input10/output81/cache-read11936/cache-write710. Telegram returned two distinct accepted message receipts, A then B; no duplicate-send refusal or uncertain-send event occurred. Native launch/probe/maintenance subprocess counts are not misrepresented as exactly two model requests. The separate one-shot provider setup qualification is excluded from this recovery proof.

The native Claude child used its existing login without copying credentials, with global home file writes denied by an OS policy, tools/customizations and native session persistence disabled. Gateway/OpenClaw state stayed task-owned. This was a real provider, not mock-openai or synthetic `onAdopted`. Source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte, Git was clean at the pinned head, and the uninstrumented head build completed successfully. The Gateway logged a clean shutdown in82ms; its launcher group received SIGTERM and reported-15, so that wrapper is not reported as exit0. Parent verified the protected relay ended code0 and both task ports closed. No live task processes remain; persistent review Remote is retained.

**Client observation:** on 2026-11-05 at 13:43 KST the human operator confirmed the replies arrived in order. This is a human client observation, not an inference from Bot API acceptance.

**Limits:** Actual SQLite locking, every transport/provider, and whole-Gateway restart were not tested or required for this known pre-write failure. The earlier base/head Gateway comparison and existing safety regressions are separate supporting evidence. This run establishes eventual real-channel/model/outbound recovery with the explicit transient relay failures above; it is not presented as a clean first-restart run or proof of all client-rendering behavior.
