prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh default-branch sessions can reuse compatible completed ancestor snapshots. Explicit refs and pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages reuse exact aliases, with verified archive installation as fallback. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification; negotiated peers defer verification to first binding with its full timeout. Exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Current status — November 15:** published head `3825a679…` remains proof-purpose, not landing-ready. AUTH-2 and UPGRADE-3 remain open. The upstream #193873 dependency is now merged, but this branch has not yet incorporated current main; the actual pinned composition has two conflicts. Historical November 9 CI is not qualification of that new composition.

**Dependency update:** [#193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873) merged November 13 as `8e6768f91235b7b094f7f8dde96735d727a3f748`. Its commit, and #193749's `21f7dc609de2c28082c056946c0bed5299183a7f`, were verified as ancestors of pinned official main `8b0c798128eda715d7c6b4b9f794fc7c2537531f`. The upstream merge prerequisite is satisfied; integration and installed snapshot/publication acceptance are separate and remain unproven here. Capture normalization and diagnostics in #193776 remain a separately owned scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve the flow. Strict registration excludes receipt-only fields. Negotiated verification preserves old/new peer contracts without a protocol-version bump; actual-base propagation, preparation callbacks, memoization, capture verification and diagnostics remain intact.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparisons decline optional reuse only after access revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

Original PR and contribution: @galiniliev. Workflow recovery and contributor-credit support were requested with @vyctorbrzezowski. Automated repair and qualification: @roboclaw-bot.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev and @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/70153122-6ab4-4eea-96e9-a8b689da6467)
- [Implementation and verification — first-bind and seed-only regressions](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/649d3ef7-7e03-41fc-b728-f1e3cc134da1)
- [Implementation and verification — mixed peers and snapshot lineage](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/acd66058-9c68-4d20-bd3e-3bb4b94b466b)
- [Implementation and verification — comparison fallback boundaries](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b0bc6b4e-8b23-422c-85ab-e11a9c70d9f7)
- [Implementation and verification — main conflict resolution](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2c3657af-b6ae-4a02-9b36-e12ca377884a)
- [Implementation and verification — landed native workflow prerequisites](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4e21df81-705a-4c4f-8051-ce41b210e29d)
- [Verification — authenticated baseline candidate](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/94d52650-602b-4d45-952b-682817c03e9e)

## Evidence

### Published identity and retained proof

- **Head:** `3825a67949692994c8c09733379bcda88992df5e`; **tree:** `d689db82d1bd50a160e0086c818371eace8753ab`.
- Native proof publication fast-forwarded `e67f9b52…` to this exact candidate. The receipt records proof purpose, no replaced ancestry, and pending AUTH-2/UPGRADE-3. Remote head/tree/blob, parent, signature and both exact Galin/Vyctor trailers were verified; earlier hosted ancestry and signed main merges remain intact.
- The sole final blob records the remaining **3 owned LF**: complete PR regression growth **1,019**, prior grants **1,016**. No tests, runtime, checker or shared scalar changed. Exact hosted composition reproduced red **6,593,452 / 6,593,449**, then green **6,593,452 / 6,593,452**, without inherited-debt credit or padding.
- Native baseline `c7266a4…` preserves `b6faccd…` and authenticated `1bc50e0…` as ordered parents, using landed #195476/#195662 tooling without changing signing trust or rewriting history.

The following receipts keep their original executing sources; they are not summed or relabeled as new-head runtime proof:

| Source | Completed proof |
| --- | --- |
| `32b13317…` | **93-test** proof and immutable source bundle. |
| `adbf95d3…` | **175** owner/direct-consumer tests; **321** routing checks. |
| `50ae028d…` | **255 distinct passes**: 238 owner/direct-consumer and 17 supported-Node native cases. |
| `60f2916c…` | **123 distinct passes**; the 82-case replay is not double-counted. |
| `b6faccdf…` | **219 affected passes, one existing skip** and applicable quality gates; **28/28** independent review passes, zero findings. |
| `c7266a43…` | **828 distinct passes**, 32 files, zero failures/skips/todos; generation/lint/format and seven type leaves passed. The remaining type leaf exposed three missing fixture members. Whole-scope review: **29/29 scoped-clean passes**, 206 complete owner bodies per pass, six historical composition datasets. |
| `e67f9b52…` | Fixture members repaired; affected types and **16 contained replay cases** passed. Lint/format/diff and focused independent review passed. Its hosted merge exposed the residual three-LF deficit. |
| `3825a679…` | Exact allocation-only correction independently scoped-clean; native checker red→green on the exact hosted composition and matching repaired merge-tree. Runtime source unchanged. |

Pre-fix cases reproduced verification-stage/budget incompatibility, seed-only rejection, topic-only retention and comparison fallback failures. Repairs preserve strict wire and fail-closed authority behavior. Historical composition datasets are not installed execution proof. A historical pinned-Bun fixture `spawnSync sh ETIMEDOUT` remains recorded; supported-Node replay does not establish a Bun repair.

### Historical hosted CI — November 9

These completed runs bind to `3825a679…` and tested merge `f0376f49490d960bb746b90a5b98c4b89f36372a` (parents `92798ae…` and this head), not November 15 main:

- [Broad CI 42569113831, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42569113831/attempts/2): **success** after a diagnosed Temurin download HTTP 504 prevented ktlint setup.
- [Periphery 42569113955, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42569113955/attempts/2): **success** after a diagnosed Periphery download failure. Recovery produced the iOS report, correctly retained macOS attempt-1 evidence, and passed shared scan/intersection.
- [OpenGrep 42569113927, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42569113927/attempts/2): **success** with scanning and SARIF uploads. Log: **109 rules on 60 files, zero findings**; inspected SARIF: 145 rule definitions, zero results. **Coverage limits:** 10 partially analyzed files due to parser warnings and 23 existing ignore-pattern matches; this is not an error-free full-parse claim.
- Each affected workflow received one diagnosed-infrastructure failed-job recovery, without a source push. Original failures remain retained; passing recovery does not prove a network repair.
- The November 9 complete readback was **124 success, 42 skipped, one neutral, zero failed/pending**, with successful CI-gate/dependency/security statuses. Those dated results do not satisfy a future integrated head's CI.

### November 15 qualification and integration checkpoint

- Pinned current main includes the merged dependency commits above. Actual composition with published `3825a679…` reports conflicts in provider lifecycle and the prepared-workspace test. Proposed resolution artifacts preserve main's recovered-source guards and this PR's retained-source binding/legacy verification intent; they are not yet an admitted, tested, committed or published candidate. Fresh native source authorization, candidate review and affected checks are still required.
- **AUTH-2:** current public production registration/selection owners and available fixture surfaces were inspected again. The setup adapter supplies a fixed fixture credential plus native guards; it is not the deployment-selected repository/account policy and does not prove revocation/reassignment behavior. No real-policy allowed/revoked/reassigned execution trace is claimed.
- **UPGRADE-3:** current npm latest remains **2026.11.3**, published November 10 at **17:59:44.785 UTC**; normal seven-day eligibility is November 17 at that time. No known-ineligible pack attempt or age override was made.
- The documented exact-baseline selector accepted **2026.11.1** as an additional older published baseline. Its canonical npm tarball was acquired under the unchanged age rule and matched registry integrity. It is **not installed or executed**, is not current latest, and does not close the latest-stable case.
- The local survivor harness still requires Docker, which is unavailable in the inspected environment. Podman sandbox support is not a supported survivor-harness substitution. No admitted installed-runtime fixture is claimed and no deployment, privilege or global configuration change was made.

### Remaining acceptance

- **AUTH-2 — IMPORTANT:** through the real selected `RepositoryIntegration.withIdentity` owner and an admitted isolated repository/account, prove allowed provision→bind→prepared-content execution, then zero prepared-content execution after revocation/reassignment during provisioning. Synthetic adapters do not close this requirement; an owner-supported fixture and existing scoped credential delivery are still needed.
- **UPGRADE-3 — IMPORTANT:** complete actual installed retained-state, mixed-peer and provider acceptance, preserving source/settings/private edits and actual-base binding. Acquired package metadata, source builds and historical Node fixtures are not installed acceptance.
- Resolve and qualify the actual main integration, then satisfy final-head independent review, CI/security and native landing requirements. The last published exact-head review remains **1/6 readiness, 1/6 proof, 3/6 patch quality**; no unchanged review request was repeated.

Native assessment remains **NEEDS WORK**, proof-purpose only. No Platinum rating, ready transition or consumer merge is claimed.

prs.title: fix(plugins): avoid blocking foreground work during reload recovery capture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes foreground work being blocked while plugin reload captures rollback source.

## User Impact

Plugin reload can acquire rollback custody without synchronously copying the entire source tree on the Gateway event loop. Existing cancellation, recovery, and custody policies are preserved; no configuration or migration is required. Existing per-entry metadata/native-reference operations remain synchronous, so this is not a universal latency guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

Initial executable binding was merged in #198302, which moved executable artifacts and recovery ownership to the host. Merely resolving the test conflicts would leave this PR's old worker-only asynchronous wrapper unreachable.

This integration awaits asynchronous filesystem copying through the existing host-local source owner before the cancellation checkpoint and drain. Synchronous and asynchronous callers share copy, relocation, native-reference validation, and cleanup semantics. Frozen-source recovery applies the same frozen aliases and closure restrictions to both paths. Retained source custody and recovery forks remain synchronous. The obsolete worker wrapper is removed; there is no second capture owner, new transport, or new timeout policy.

Adapted from Wes (@akmad)'s work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181491 (original head `7d13ecb8bb33dc7d0e2f96ad3dc287a60c8525e6`). The contributor branch was not executed. This is a current-main adaptation, not a stacked PR.

## Current Integration Evidence — November 16, 2026

Head `ec3c8e4803c7adce0058f3f0641dabcb8d1287af` integrates main `d0e09e419d7e2446f13c0277bfaa8a733876c612`.

- Both conflicting test files resolved; main's physical-cleanup, retained-provider, native, and frozen-source assertions preserved.
- **217 tests across 10 files passed**: real host-local copy progress/cleanup, pre-drain cancellation, native and frozen recovery/forks, source-owner lifetime, and changed direct test consumers.
- **Red/green owner replay:** substituting only the source-lookup owner from the pinned main commit made the real foreground-copy assertion fail: the recovery directory was already populated before foreground work ran. Restoring the repaired owner passed. This is an isolated owner replay, not a full-base end-to-end run.
- Plugin-platform and Gateway-server test typechecks, scoped typed lint (19 source/test files), formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation link audit: 16,653 checked, zero broken.
- Independent read-only implementation review against the pinned main found no blocking correctness issues. It checked the local copy owner, native cleanup, frozen wrapping, complete await chain, and preserved main regressions. This was a subagent review, not local ClawSweeper/autoreview; neither local reviewer CLI nor a bound autoreview tool is available in this session. The subsequent documentation-only correction describes the host-local owner.
- The foreground assertion proves that real copying yields at its start, not a worst-case latency bound throughout a large copy. New-head CI is separate from the historical green checks below.

## Historical Proof Before This Integration

The original head `6061ad40beacd4179a814a0d2a0729d50f70e64d` had passing plugin/Gateway tests, runtime build, typechecks, lint/format/docs checks, independent reviews, and green exact-head CI. Those results are historical, not current-head CI.

[November 15 sanitized traces, limitations, and reproducible harness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198262#issuecomment-6901408265):

- Exercised that original head and pre-PR base `9d28854c4322988d1ad1443604e365547b224695` in isolated state through public `plugins.reload`, `health`, and a synthetic plugin RPC. No live Gateway was changed.
- With an identical injected 1,500 ms hold at the then-existing worker recovery-copy boundary, base health took 1,563 ms and completed after capture. Candidate observations were 8 ms and 111 ms, before capture ended. These are instrumented scheduling observations, not an uninstrumented benchmark or measurements of the newly integrated head.
- Failed replacement activation recovered the original frozen dependency in a fresh instance despite mutated disk source. The observed recovery directory was removed after acknowledged clean shutdown.
- Candidate/base builds and 46 focused tests passed; independent proof review verified the evidence and limitations.
- **Remaining live-model gap:** the real agent/model request returned `credit_balance_exhausted` / `insufficient_quota`. No successful model response is claimed, and the attempt was not replaced by a mock. A usable funded credential is needed for that portion of the proof.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.body:
Closes #196396

## Current readiness — November 16, 2026

**Technically ready for maintainer review at `20097c30375e1575620484965e4148f4a9aedb6b`; not green CI and not merge-ready.** This is the authoritative current status. Dated status statements below are retained historical observations, superseded by this section and the terminal-CI supplement.

- The complete four-file npm correction has an independent `READY FOR /prepare-pr` review with no substantive findings. R1 is resolved by the exact-candidate full Node 24 build and 100 passing tests in job 132520903284, run 43619050658 attempt 1. Existing focused npm/archive and Node/Bun package-operation evidence remains historical source evidence, not relabeled new-head execution.
- Native correction-specific `prepare-gates` and `prepare-push` completed successfully on November 15. The active review is validated, `GATES_MODE=github_pending` binds the exact head, and the already-matching remote required no push. Original incoming identity, publication receipt and ancestry provenance are preserved. No additional source repair, repeated full CI, or unrelated native coverage is required for this bounded technical-review readiness decision.
- **Failed evidence remains failed:** `tests.result=fail`; run 43619050658 attempt 1 and aggregate 132558730426 concluded failure. All 18 product-job failures are investigated with the distinct exact-baseline, matching newer-main, partial-match and source-only attribution strengths below. Source-only attribution is not runtime baseline reproduction or proof excluding every indirect timing effect. Unresolved timing/state/setup causes remain disclosed.
- Jobs 132520920774 (private-QA17) and 132527176191 (macOS Swift tests) were cancelled, leaving coverage gaps. The dispatched exact-head proof does not by itself establish normal PR-CI association or security/review clearance. Existing platform, installed-upgrade and typecheck limitations below remain unchanged.
- **Draft state is separate from technical readiness:** the PR is still draft at this observation. Promotion must use the original publication binding and its current receipt; it is not a technical proof gap. No merge admission, CI waiver, merge, backport or release is claimed or authorized here.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's pinned npm 12.2.1 ships undici 6.29.0 inside its own archive, within the affected range of GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx. Downstream dependency overrides cannot replace that bundled copy.

## User Impact

Updates the bundled npm to 12.2.2, which contains undici 6.29.1. No config, schema, or updater protocol changes; existing installations receive the replacement dependency with the next package update. This addresses the verified dependency finding, not a demonstrated reachable OpenClaw exploit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dependency owner approved this focused patch upgrade. Update only the exact npm manifest/lock entry and qualify npm 12.2.2 in the existing authenticated-bundle policy. Its ip-address 10.7.5 and brace-expansion 5.0.12 satisfy current overrides, so only minimatch 10.2.5 needs the existing exact bundled-occurrence exception. Historical policies remain for supported frozen targets. No broad dependency updates or shared installation changes.

## Evidence

- Independently downloaded npm 12.2.1 and 12.2.2 from the official registry and verified archive SHA512 against registry metadata and the lock. Confirmed bundled undici changes 6.29.0 → 6.29.1; npm engine requirements are unchanged.
- Extended the existing bundle-policy and authenticated-archive test tables: **two new cases fail before the policy fix; all 99 tests pass afterward**. File wall time: 33.94 seconds. Existing subprocess/archive integration cases account for the file's runtime; no new test scaffolding or test lines were added.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/generate-npm-package-lock.test.ts test/scripts/npm-runner.test.ts src/infra/npm-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **113 passed**, 47.48 seconds across three shards.
- Generated a real npm 12.2.2 package lock (149 entries) and validated it through OpenClaw's production override/archive-authentication functions against the official archive. The valid lock passes; changing its bundled undici version to 6.29.0 is rejected.
- Actual npm 12.2.2 `--version`, pack, offline install, and update from a synthetic 1.0.0 package to 1.0.1 pass under **Node 26.12.1 and the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork**.
- Frozen worktree-local install, focused type-aware lint of both changed source/test files, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Simplification pass retained four files only: 16 additions / 8 removals, with no new production mechanism.
- Fresh independent OpenClaw reviewer (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`) inspected the complete diff against base `2ef2b2b8466c846ee919f805c864b1936434f70a`, including unchanged archive authentication and negative controls: **no P0–P2 findings**. This is a narrative independent review, not helper-validated Codex CLI or local ClawSweeper; those local review tools were unavailable.
- Historical CI run [43601269848](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43601269848) checks `d98f18ff7c3de4bf46706a71d25705cef346b3ab`, not the original published npm head `f221fdad5007e6baff6565d795aad7183d7688d7`. Earlier attribution of that run as exact-head npm evidence was incorrect; none of its results establish this candidate’s readiness.

### Remaining proof / known limitations

- **Historical baseline build failure; not exact-head candidate proof.** [build-artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43601269848/job/132466838093) failed `check-cli-bootstrap-imports`: `agents/identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`. The Node 24 compatibility job reported the same assertion. These are baseline-run results, not proof of the npm candidate. The worker repair incorporated below leaves the budget unchanged.
- The local Bun plugin-install E2E attempt hit its 240-second outer limit during cold build preparation (before tests). Root tooling test typecheck also timed out waiting for the same build. Neither is reported as passing.
- The scripts typecheck reports an existing, unchanged error at `scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373` (`entry.tasksCompleted` possibly undefined). This file is identical to the reviewed base; no benchmark repair is included.
- No macOS/Windows device proof, full installed-version upgrade rehearsal, or downstream Dependabot reproduction. The unavailable remote/macOS routes were not retried. No merge, backport, or release is requested by this PR.

People sharing a Gateway can add personal Anthropic API keys, but the supported Claude setup-token method is missing from Connected accounts.

A person can save their own setup-token through Profile → Connected accounts, with masked input, then select it for Claude CLI chats. This retains the existing `claude setup-token` prerequisite; it does not add browser-native Claude sign-in or import the host's CLI login.

## Why This Change Was Made

The personal-account owner already accepts token credentials, assigns private account IDs, and ignores shared configuration patches. The provider needs only to opt its existing method into that flow. No storage, refresh, authorization, or account-selection implementation is added. The input is marked sensitive using the existing wizard contract.

Simplification review retained two production metadata lines, two focused regressions, and setup instructions; no new abstraction or dependency. Native CLI login remains excluded from personal discovery.

## Evidence

- Both new regressions fail before the repair and pass after it.
- Upstream-based candidate: 13 focused provider tests passed; 83.56 seconds wall time including cold worker compilation, under one second test execution. Formatting, type-aware lint, and extension types passed.

- Independent local P0–P2 source review reported no actionable findings; it did not run tests.
- Real Claude consent and inference are not claimed. Credentials in tests are synthetic. Hosted CI timing is pending.

prs.title: fix: allow Team deployments after a controller host reboot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Team deployment controller refuses every deployment after a host reboot when it retains a completed controller-adoption gate.

## User Impact

Operators can deploy again after `/run` recreates the deployment-lock inode. Interrupted adoption/bootstrap operations still fail closed, and completed gates still verify the current exclusive FD9 lock and full controller closure. An already affected installation needs complete-pair adoption from a staged fixed library using the documented `steady-successor` path; merging this PR does not install or deploy it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The intent loader compared today's lock inode with the historical adoption-time inode before validating the completion. Completion reads now distinguish immutable history from an active publication, including a completed bootstrap predecessor. The lock owner still checks canonical path, ownership, safe mode, and exclusive flock. No configuration, database schema, cache, or additional scan was added. Executable production LOC is unchanged; one comment explains the reboot lifetime boundary.

## Evidence

- The reported Team reboot succeeded and its Gateway remained ready, but deployment entry exited 2 in 127 ms with `controller adoption lock inode changed`. Read-only inspection confirmed the completed gate and installed closure match, the activation journal is absent, and the tmpfs lock inode changed. No adoption, deployment, restart, or journal edit was performed on Team.
- Real Linux FD9/procfs regressions: completed ordinary and bootstrap-backed adoption fail on the exact parent with the reported inode error and pass with this fix; unfinished operations remain refused. All 76 adoption and historical-adoption tests pass (27.6 s).
- Extended the existing steady-successor recovery/deployment test to recreate the lock inode before successor adoption, including its historical predecessor chain. It fails on the parent at the old inode guard and passes with the fix (37.0 s). Synthetic systemd/Gateway observations are fixture-owned; this is not live Team acceptance. Container prerequisites include `/usr/bin/node`, installed suspension/startup helpers, and an executable filesystem with the controller's required free capacity.
- `pnpm check:changed` and `git diff --check` pass. No Control UI import boundary is touched.
- Actual btrfs fixture: 35.04 GiB synthetic SQLite database, 6,000 sessions, 62,000 workspace files / 1.1 GB; compressible padding, no copied Team data. Recreated-inode A/A median wall: baseline refused 29.36/30.47 ms, fixed admitted 36.46/38.70 ms; CPU 31.74/31.15 versus 39.62/42.33 ms; sampled allocation 2.764/2.600 versus 3.403/3.239 MB. Same-inode controls admit at 35.85/36.76 versus 37.25/37.58 ms. Ten launches per timing set. These are different outcomes, not a speedup: the repaired path performs closure validation that the refusal never reached.
- A fully specified operator recovery packet constructs fresh descriptors/process/pointer bindings under FD9. Its read-only descriptor generator passed on Team. There is no prospective native read-only steady-successor action; historical `context` also checks the obsolete live process, so it is not a dry-run substitute.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, two completed passes over the local candidate against parent `443e9730695d6fa1549d84d9f45187883e9570f1`, with the full controller library as evidence; no actionable findings. Simplification pass retained the existing loader/closure owner and no new helper.

Hosted review caught two obsolete sibling expectations that still required completed-history inode refusal. Both failures reproduced, and the historical-successor and actual retained-prepare shell consumers now assert admission after lock recreation. Mixed-closure, stale-reader, evidence-drift, and unfinished-publication refusals remain covered. This follow-up changes tests only; measured production bytes are unchanged.
The test-only follow-up also passed fresh Codex autoreview through P2 and a second `pnpm check:changed` run. The original head's CI passed; final-head CI is tracked by GitHub before landing.

prs.title: fix(sessions): allow reset of a session paused as a precaution
prs.body:
Related: #178441
Related: #195598

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session paused by a provider review can never be reset, so when the provider re-flags every continuation the session is permanently dead. For `agent:main:main` there is no way out at all.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can now run `sessions.reset` (CLI, gateway call) or send `/new` or `/reset` from a channel to reset a paused session. Reset keeps the session id and its history and starts a fresh context. The reviewed findings are not continued. Continuing the flagged run still requires acknowledging the findings, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reset keeps the session id and starts a new lifecycle generation (a new `lifecycleRevision`). The session write policy already drops `providerReview` when the lifecycle revision changes. But reset ran the same work-start check as ordinary new work, so the pause refused the replacement before it could happen.

Real case: an OpenAI provider review paused our owner's `agent:main:main` on 2026.9.33 and again after upgrading to 2026.11.3. Each acknowledgment resent the same transcript and was re-flagged. `/reset`, `sessions.reset`, `sessions archive`, `sessions delete` and `session.mainKey` were all refused or ignored. The only way out was stopping the gateway and removing `$.providerReview` from `session_nodes.entry_json` by hand.

This adds a narrow `allowProviderReviewReplacement` work-start option. Only the gateway reset service and the reply path's `/new`/`/reset` trigger pass it. Ordinary sends, agent commands, restart resume and Talk still hit the pause unchanged.

Not included: the Control UI composer and its outbox still hold `/reset` locally for a paused session. That's a follow-up. Until then, operators can reset from the CLI or a channel.

## Stuck on a release without this fix?

Symptoms:

- `Gateway call failed: Session "agent:main:main" is paused as a precaution. Review the provider findings in chat before continuing.`
- **Chat paused as a precaution** / **Session paused as a precaution**. Clicking **Acknowledge findings and continue** gets paused again.
- `/reset`, `sessions.reset`, `sessions archive` and `sessions delete` all refuse the session.
- Provider side: OpenAI `misalignment_policy_violation` / "Potentially unintended activity".

Manual recovery. Back up first, and run this as the account that owns the OpenClaw state:

```bash
# 1. Stop the gateway through whatever supervises it (launchd, systemd, terminal).
# 2. Back up the agent database.
cp ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.bak
# 3. See which sessions are paused.
sqlite3 ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "SELECT session_key FROM session_nodes WHERE json_type(entry_json,'\$.providerReview') IS NOT NULL;"
# 4. Clear the pause on the one you need (example: main).
sqlite3 ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "UPDATE session_nodes SET entry_json = json_remove(entry_json,'\$.providerReview') WHERE session_key='agent:main:main'; SELECT changes();"
# 5. Start the gateway, then send /reset in that session FIRST.
```

Send `/reset` before anything else. If you send anything else first, the flagged transcript goes back to the provider, which usually pauses the session again.

## Evidence

- `src/config/sessions/sessions.test.ts`: the pause still blocks ordinary work and `allowPendingWorkspace`. The new option passes the pause only, and an archived session stays blocked.
- `src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts`: `sessions.reset` on a paused `agent:main:main` and on a peer session succeeds. It starts a new lifecycle generation with no `providerReview`, and a second reset also succeeds. Both cases fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md` now explains how to recover when acknowledgment keeps pausing the session, and quotes the exact error text.
- `pnpm test src/config/sessions/sessions.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts src/config/sessions/provider-review-store.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-provider-review.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 71 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (typecheck, lint, format, line-cap ratchet and guards). It ran with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` because the dead-export scan fails on current `main` in `extensions/knowledge/**`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- The commit was made with `--no-verify` because the pre-commit hook's Node version didn't match the local shell. `oxfmt` was run on every changed file by hand first, and `pnpm check:changed` covers the same format and lint checks.
- Not run: a real provider refusal. The live run below pauses the session by writing the same `providerReview` record a refusal writes. The production session that hit this was recovered with the manual steps above.

## Live Gateway proof

Built this branch (`pnpm build`, head merged with current `main`) and ran the shipped CLI against an isolated `--dev` profile (throwaway `HOME`, port 19001, channels skipped). I created `agent:main:main` with `sessions.reset`, stopped the Gateway, wrote a `providerReview` into its `session_nodes` row exactly as a refusal stores it, and restarted the Gateway. The scoped calls use `callGatewayCli` with an explicit `scopes` list.

```text
== 1. paused
state: sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=4d8f5ae3-2d31-411e-a1fd-1151af8ee268 providerReview=review-proof-1
== 2. ordinary send is still refused
Gateway call failed: Session "agent:main:main" is paused as a precaution. Review the provider findings in chat before continuing.
== 3. write-scoped reset
scopes=operator.write sessions.reset: refused: missing scope: operator.admin
state: sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=4d8f5ae3-2d31-411e-a1fd-1151af8ee268 providerReview=review-proof-1
== 4. admin reset
scopes=operator.admin sessions.reset: ok sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=b73a0074-ce38-4f94-8e38-6572464f168e
state: sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=b73a0074-ce38-4f94-8e38-6572464f168e providerReview=none
== 5. second admin reset
scopes=operator.admin sessions.reset: ok sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=205cd255-3f9e-493b-98d4-9ba6edc83507
== 6. send after reset
  "runId": "proof-send-2",
  "status": "started",
```

What this shows:

- The pause still blocks ordinary work (step 2).
- A caller without `operator.admin` cannot reset, and the pause stays in place (step 3). This PR doesn't change who may reset; `sessions.reset` already requires `operator.admin`.
- An admin reset clears the pause, keeps the session id, and starts a new lifecycle generation (step 4). A later reset still works (step 5).
- Nothing is replayed. The message refused in step 2 is stored nowhere in the agent or state database afterward. Only the new step 6 message is stored.

Stored-data compatibility: this PR adds no stored field and changes no schema. The live run starts from the same `providerReview` row shape that real paused sessions already have.

prs.body:
## Current review-readiness qualification (November 16, 2026)

- Published conflict repair head: `a1d535cdcecd825cbee05d1480ffabb7e435f5ed`, preserving original contributor head `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` as the first parent and integrating main `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92`. This is a merge into the existing fix branch, not a merge of this PR into main.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P3 findings. The adaptation preserves main's delivery-only projection envelope/filter and both the existing and added SQLite regression blocks. `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing live/regression evidence below remains prior-head evidence. This conflict-only adaptation has not been executed locally: the supported secretless AWS proof environment could not acquire credentials (no EC2 instance role). Exact-head CI run [43600215086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600215086) completed. Production types, core test-type stripes, lint, and test-line accounting passed; whole CI is not green. Its failures match three existing main defects: identity worker build budget (240 evaluated modules versus 220), TS18048 at scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373, and mock export preservation at src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13. I independently compared the exact failure text with contemporary [main run 43599691199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199), specifically [build job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948967), [type job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461949721), and [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948989). No unrelated repair or retry was added to this PR. All selected changed Node test jobs passed. The [owning SQLite regression job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600215086/job/132463736345) passed all 16 tests, including completed-run steering attribution, identity mismatch, textless-user barriers, and main’s delivery-only restart case. The separate changed-channels job passed 73 tests across 8 files, including runtime context. The original live model proof is still prior-head evidence.
- Attribution and bounded lookup remain separate reviewable fixes under the existing transcript projection/reconciliation owners. Combining them later requires reconciling the shared projector, SQLite append tests, and documentation; neither is represented as testing their combination.

### Readiness boundary

Native review and preparation are now complete for this exact head. The independent P0–P3 conflict review was recovered and its saved attribution patch verified byte-for-byte against the current base-to-head diff. Its conclusions and the retained proof were recorded in the exact-head native review, which validated with `READY FOR /prepare-pr`, while preserving `tests.result: fail` and the attributed CI run 43600215086, attempt 2. The trusted native `prepare-run` then completed with `GATES_MODE=github_pending`, explicitly recording no successful gate proof. It verified that the remote was already at the same head and skipped pushing; no source, ancestry, or test result changed.

This is technical/native preparation readiness, not merge readiness or a waiver of enforced CI/security/review. Current head remains open, non-draft and mergeable but blocked. The existing ClawSweeper comment reviews original candidate `98a2597…`, not current head. GitHub has no submitted reviews or outstanding review requests; the inspected branch rule requires zero generic approvals with code-owner review enabled. No `required402` refusal was encountered during native review validation or preparation; no claim is made that an unobserved gate was cleared. The two required `openclaw/ci-gate` statuses remain failed. No merge was requested.

### Exact-head CI qualification

The four failed jobs in CI run [43600215086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600215086) reduce to three inherited defects, not four independent patch failures:

| Failed job | Observed failure and attribution |
| --- | --- |
| build-artifacts | `agents/identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`; identical assertion in contemporary main job 132461948967. |
| PostgreSQL conformance (3/3) | The same 240/220 build assertion stops runtime preparation before any Vitest shard executes. Schema/trigger parity completed; this is not a failed PostgreSQL behavioral assertion or a conformance pass. |
| check-test-types | `scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts(373,52): TS18048: entry.tasksCompleted is possibly undefined`; same diagnostic in contemporary main job 132461949721. |
| checks-fast-baseline-ratchets | `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13: ../logging/subsystem.js` violates mock-export preservation; same failure in contemporary main job 132461948989. |

The automated failure table labels these jobs new because it compares against older scheduled main run 43594951095, whose matching jobs passed. The attribution above instead uses observed identical failures from main run 43599691199 at `559f68a57d14f997a7e7face4e2d07d574e9747c`. The failing benchmark, mock, worker entry, and budget-check files are unchanged between that main commit and this PR head. No CI result is relabeled green. Both red `openclaw/ci-gate` statuses report the underlying failed CI, rather than another product failure. The canceled PR-context run is superseded by the successful same-head [job 132470881354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43602768456/job/132470881354).

Closes #197994

## What problem this solves

Recent-history reconciliation previously credited a completed assistant answer only to the nearest preceding user row. With full transcript coverage of `original user -> accepted steering user -> completed final`, the steering row received credit but the original could be re-quoted in a later model input, even when the completed run had answered both requests.

This can duplicate an already-answered request in context. Token cost and answer-quality effects have not been measured. The demonstrated case is an attribution problem, not a missing delivered final or insufficient lookup coverage.

## Implemented behavior and owners

The fix reuses producer-owned canonical metadata and the existing reconciliation owner:

- `src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts` adds `runId` and user `steerTargetRunId` only to the private turn-evidence projection. The public SDK text projection does not gain those fields.
- `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts`, `omitAnsweredRecentHistory`, walks the returned chronological rows backward. A completed assistant records its known run ID. A user is attributed to `steerTargetRunId` when present, otherwise its own `runId`, and can be covered by a later completed answer of that run.
- Known conflicting run identities do not qualify through the nearest-user fallback. When either side lacks usable run identity, the legacy immediately preceding-user behavior remains; the code tracks unidentified completed replies separately from known completed runs.
- Every projected user resets the adjacency-only completion state. Private evidence now retains textless/image-only users as `text: ""` barriers, so an unrelated final is not paired across an invisible user row. Public recent text still excludes empty user text.
- Final omission still requires the same transport ID and unchanged trimmed body. Attachments, edits, unseen discussion, incomplete replies, earlier unrelated runs, and missing completion evidence remain eligible in the tested cases. Session/agent scope and the existing completion classifier are unchanged.

This does not remove the conservative reset, mark all consecutive users answered, create a second completion owner, add schemas/configuration, or change steering admission. The branch also documents the run-aware behavior in `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md`.

### What completion and acceptance mean here

This is host-side completed-run bookkeeping, not semantic answer grading. Accepted steering metadata alone is insufficient: the reader must also observe a completed assistant answer with the relevant run identity. Conversely, a host completion flag is not a generic guarantee that an answer's content satisfies every request. No semantic-answer detector was added.

The historical collector separately inspected the combined final's content. The regression fixtures supply canonical metadata and a final classification to exercise reconciliation; they do not themselves prove real steering admission or semantic coverage.

## Evidence: historical observation versus new verification

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197994-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783568/openclaw-197994-evidence.zip)

`historical/observation.json` is a sanitized read-only reinspection of retained production canonical records and the native rollout. Its event date is November 11, 2026, and collection date is November 13. It reports:

- Original input and accepted steering belong to the same completed run.
- The final stopped normally and carries terminal-run metadata.
- The collector inspected two corresponding final-answer sections; the full final body is omitted from the public excerpt.
- The original request was subsequently quoted in a native recent-history input.

Run membership was copied separately from canonical metadata; the baseline projector did not expose these identity fields. The collector used the real retained events as an injected read-only page, not a fresh storage/channel/Gateway experiment. Its installed/source commit labels are provenance fields, not a new attestation that this fix ran on the historical date.

**The original candidate-only live proof passed on `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` before the conflict repair**, completing at `2026-11-13T03:55:07.004Z`. This is prior-head evidence, not a live execution of current head `a1d535cdcecd825cbee05d1480ffabb7e435f5ed`. A synthetic authenticated local channel exercised the real Gateway/core dispatch, canonical storage, native Codex and configured provider. A declared read-only tool held a checkpoint while a second actual inbound request was admitted through native steering; the gate was released only after a correlated steering acceptance. Original `runId`, steering `steerTargetRunId` and completed-final `runId` agree in the persisted transcript. A subsequent request supplied both inputs plus an unrelated ambient candidate: core removed the two answered inputs and retained only the unrelated candidate.

The executed harness required exact submitted-body matches for all three primary native requests and all three newest provider-user inputs. One native conversation and one separate auxiliary recap were observed. The newly appended input does not repeat the answered requests; their earlier retained native history is not deleted. The build completed with exit zero in 354 seconds and exact build/runtime/Codex provenance verified. Fixture and runner cleanup succeeded. `LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` indexes the raw synthetic records, exact executed harness and verification scope. This is a candidate-only synthetic-transport live test, not Discord transport, a fresh live base/fix A/B, or a production deployment.

## Original candidate red-on-baseline and green-on-fix validation

The original integrator ran the then-current 15-test persisted SQLite suite against the two original production owner files from the base, then restored the fixed source. `attribution-persisted-red.log` records **5 failed, 10 passed**:

- Completed original plus accepted steering remained eligible incorrectly.
- Two explicit run-mismatch/steering-target-precedence cases incorrectly omitted a pending input.

These are owner assertion failures, not the earlier compiler setup failure. `attribution-source-restored.json` records the restored production hashes; both match original tested candidate `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134`, not the later conflict-repair head.

`attribution-final-green.log` records **38 passed** across three files on original tested candidate `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` (prior-head evidence):

- SQLite reconciliation: **15/15**. Covers successful shared-run completion; error, abort, truncation, commentary, and unsettled native output; explicit mismatch; steering-target precedence; missing-identity fallback; edited text; attachments; textless/image-only barriers; and unchanged public text projection.
- Provider prefix stability: **14/14**.
- Channel context runtime: **9/9**.

The final wrapper took 274.83 seconds, including 124.87 seconds of cold worker compilation. The SQLite file took 155.47 seconds including preparation/transform; its test bodies totaled about 6.6 seconds. These timings describe the original candidate handoff, before PR CI; current-head CI results are recorded above.

Original candidate `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` has the same four source/doc hashes as the reviewed tested candidate; the commit's formatting hook did not change them. `candidate-review.json` records those hashes and review scope. From the prepared branch with repository dependencies installed according to `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```sh

  pnpm test src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts \
```

For the persisted baseline comparison, use a separate checkout at the base commit and apply only the regression-test file from the prepared commit, leaving production files at the base. Then run the SQLite test file alone. Do not overwrite a running checkout's source or reuse another run's active dependency installation.

## Portable reproduction of the original mechanism

The unchanged bundled baseline helper requires Node 26.12.1+ and no checkout, install, credentials, network, model, or Gateway:

```sh

# Optional baseline checkout comparison:
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw > checkout-observed.json
```

It resolves `source/` relative to itself and was verified after copying the package outside the checkout and running from `/`. `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` pins the bundled owner to `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` (package `2026.11.3`) with its exact hash and MIT license. `current-base-reproduction-output.json` confirms the same baseline owner/behavior on the newer base.

The seven executed baseline cases include full coverage (limit four, all three rows returned, original retained), an ordinary single-input completion, a larger candidate budget that does not repair attribution, incomplete output, an unrelated earlier unanswered request, and independent edit/attachment controls.

prs.title: fix: load earlier chat messages when upward input interrupts Latest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes earlier messages remaining unavailable when an upward wheel interrupts a pending Latest scroll at the top of the conversation without moving the viewport.

## User Impact

Users can load earlier messages with that single upward gesture while their current reading position stays in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

History receives native input before the transcript cancels its pending scroll. The programmatic-scroll guard introduced in #171009 rejected genuine reader intent; a later cancellation without upward movement could never re-arm pagination. Admit that input, then use the existing transcript cancellation owner before arming history. Passive layout and initial-position protections remain. Production line count is unchanged.

This is a separately reproduced interaction defect found while investigating #198526. Its relationship to that PR's original unreproduced WebKit startup failure is unproven; it does not qualify an inherited-red exception for that PR.

## Evidence

- Exact main parent e970cf66f7b357b8b10edf9e36d11b6045123e5a: the real pane/transcript regression fails with zero older requests; the repair makes one request and projects 190 messages. The no-input control remains zero requests/30 messages.
- Independent real-layout Chromium control is red 0/30 before and green 1/190 after; the same later native zero-offset scroll does not cure the base. Inspected synthetic before/after captures preserve the current-message viewport while the earlier-history boundary disappears.
- Focused owner/autofill 16, input/pagination 9, real-browser 3 and bundled E2E 4 pass. E2E includes WebKit 390px history stability, mobile retry, keyboard focus, and hidden-page upward input.
- Fresh isolated Codex review through P2: scoped-clean for the final two-file snapshot against e970cf66f7b357b8b10edf9e36d11b6045123e5a, unchanged in signed head 14959af382058683e668b07e98f6cdd81a62c75d. Required pnpm check:changed ran once: all selected typechecks, lint, caps and other guards passed, but the full-tree export scan fails on unchanged resolveRollbackWorkerInputs in update-command-database-rollback.test-support.ts. #198268 removed its external consumer; #199851 owns the pending repair. This is a main regression, not ignored noise or a claimed green check. Exact-head ci:full run 43789208570 completed with all history-related cases passing. Its sole substantive red is the independently inherited Secrets receipt assertion described below; the authorized native inherited-failure route retains that failed conclusion.

Before: one upward gesture cancels Latest but leaves earlier history unloaded.

![Before: earlier history remains unavailable above the retained current messages](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc669eec-1365-4931-b284-ab9a7bb33626)

After: the same gesture loads the earlier page and preserves the current-message viewport.

![After: earlier history loads and the current-message viewport stays in place](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51d37802-8bda-4e61-988d-5ee87beb5f05)

## Inherited CI failure

CI run 43789208570 tested merge 1eb95dd6a050a3ae595d8f36caba6151035f0196 against main parent 9e85a1a71795dd067c424923c4e187ab332852dd. UI job 133043993823 fails only `secrets-confirmed-receipts.e2e.test.ts` / “does not call a fully acknowledged bulk save an unfinished import.” The unchanged original case fails identically on both exact merge and exact main parent. The successful receipt reads “Entries saved: 1”; the assertion still filters “Saved 1 entries.” #199464 / b858e90c8fede29f00a279a7da6062b840802500 changed canonical English and the main Secrets E2E but omitted this sibling. This is an attributed main regression with a separate test-owner repair, not a history defect or a flaky replay.

The exact-parent replay failed in 19.45 seconds (36.25 seconds CPU), and the merge replay failed in 21.20 seconds (38.57 seconds CPU). No deadline, assertion, or Secrets behavior changed in this PR, and CI was not rerun. The Secrets owner inputs are identical between the tested merge and main parent. Final-head Claw review 6905422180 reports zero findings/open items on 14959af382058683e668b07e98f6cdd81a62c75d. Landing uses the explicitly authorized inherited-failure exception with pinned native evidence; neither failed CI nor the separate local rollback-export check is represented as green.

prs.title: fix: keep steering queued through long-running tools
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted corrections falling out of the active turn when a tool takes longer than two minutes.

## User Impact

A waiting correction stays visible and reaches the next runtime boundary after the tool finishes. Ordinary steering no longer becomes a separate follow-up merely because 120 seconds elapsed. Cancellation, turn closure, handoff, explicit caller deadlines, and uncertain-delivery protection remain intact. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded owner imposed a 120-second transcript-commit deadline independently of the active run's lifecycle. At expiry it withdrew an accepted message and returned it to follow-up custody. The receiving run already owns commit, cancellation and terminal settlement, so ordinary steering can use that lifecycle without an additional timer.

The production report supplied for this task recorded two rejected steers on revision dd2d58be: one reached follow-up custody after 120,016 ms of runAdmission and another after 100.8 seconds. The previous revision also recorded two approximately 120,011 ms waits. These are post-acknowledgment settlement timings, not evidence that the initial acknowledgment took two minutes. Existing Gateway custody publishes pending input before settlement.

Gateway stage accounting is unchanged between 257759ae and dd2d58be: a rejected steer ending as a follow-up is classified as queued. A completed-steer count of zero does not count the two rejected attempts.

## Evidence

The real AgentSession long-tool regression fails on the base at 120,001 virtual milliseconds and passes with this change. Focused Gateway/controller/session tests pass, including visible fallback custody, explicit withdrawal deadlines, cancellation, and handoff.

Measurement acceptance rule: ordinary steering must retain custody beyond 120 seconds and commit once at the first available tool boundary; acknowledgment/acceptance precedes tool completion; cancellation and explicit deadlines still settle. Five baseline/candidate processes were interleaved, 100 turns each after five warmups, plus two unchanged baseline A/A controls per mode. Timing and sampled allocation were collected separately. Each process uses a fresh session in the same generated database and populated workspace. Startup and fixture generation are excluded.

The fixture contains 5,000 session identities, 1,850 histories, 220,250 transcript events, a 39.016 GiB agent database, and 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.116 GB. The bulk generator was capped at the physical-size target before its original logical transcript budget completed; native owners reopened/checkpointed it, full integrity passed, and a clean-close receipt was written. This is synthetic data on APFS; btrfs and live production-model execution are not covered.

| Uninstrumented owner-flow measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Acceptance p50 / p95 | 0.0481 / 0.0715 ms | 0.0456 / 0.0659 ms |
| Commit after a 20 ms tool, p50 / p95 | 29.224 / 31.702 ms | 29.126 / 32.376 ms |
| Complete synthetic turn main-thread CPU, median per steer | 6.715 ms | 6.716 ms |
| Complete synthetic turn process CPU, median per steer | 27.416 ms | 27.464 ms |
| Sampled allocation, separate runs, median per steer | 2,260,273 B | 2,225,702 B |

All 2,400 scale turns committed. A/A timing controls had acceptance p50 0.0530/0.0535 ms and commit p50 30.435/30.475 ms, but CPU varied substantially (main 10.959/8.200 ms; process 57.981/32.341 ms). A/A allocation was 2,262,610/2,255,465 B per turn. No broad CPU or latency speedup is claimed. Allocation-profiler timing had a higher candidate tail (p95 50.256 → 117.228 ms); those instrumented timings are not used as normal-path latency evidence. The uninstrumented tail and CPU measurements are retained above.

All 86 focused tests passed across the affected cases. The added mock-Gateway active-tool case acknowledged the send in 32.427 ms and exposed its pending receipt in 98.625 ms; releasing the tool consumed the correction exactly once in the original run. These are handler/history visibility measurements, not browser paint timings. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Core, test, and script typechecks and targeted lint passed. `check:changed` passed 39/40 gates and found one unrelated full-tree unused export: `resolveRollbackWorkerInputs`, left exported when #198268 removed its external caller. Exact parent 2824b9f5d2f3 reproduces the same sole unused export. Commit e4a30936bb35 (#198268) removed its external caller while leaving it exported; this is an inherited main regression. Peer PR #199851 already owns its repair. This failure is recorded, not described as green.

The runtime delta is +1 line (18 added / 17 removed): conditional construction of an explicitly requested timer replaces unconditional construction and its default constant. No new configuration, schema, cache, retry layer, or UI-imported runtime module is introduced. ClawSweeper’s remaining stale two-minute documentation description was corrected; docs link audit checked 16,653 links with zero broken links, and a fresh Codex documentation review was clean.

The same 39.016 GiB fixture also reproduced the real 120.1-second boundary case: baseline acceptance 0.957 ms, then withdrawal at 120,002.903 ms; candidate acceptance 0.612 ms, then transcript commit at 120,139.635 ms in the original turn. Each used two model requests. These are one wall-clock sample per revision, not percentile estimates.

CI run 43789089297 exposed one PR-caused stale fixture in `chat-steer-now-handler.test.ts`: its fallback setup depended on the removed implicit timeout. It reproduced locally as an unresolved outcome; the fixture now requests an explicit 120-second deadline. All four affected Send now tests pass, along with targeted type/lint checks. This is separate from the attributed inherited unused-export failure. The corrected head is 5e77d76a64ef1c008b8c26ae6d0961bf5ccddc48; exact-head CI verification is in progress.

prs.title: fix(ui): Usage filters change when Enter confirms IME input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Usage filters changing or search focus leaving the input when Enter confirms IME composition. Confirming a provider search can select the first match and silently narrow the displayed usage; a creator picker can select a person and close.

## User Impact

Users can confirm composed text while retaining the search, focus and current filters. A following ordinary Enter still selects the first search result. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing input-local IME helper in the shared value picker, including keyCode 229 and Enter immediately after compositionend. For composition-confirming Enter, stop propagation to the parent menu without preventing the browser default. Clear composition tracking on key-up and blur, as the neighboring query search already does. The shared change covers both multi-value filters and the single-choice creator picker.

Related: #195087, an external-contributor Usage query IME fix merged by @obviyus on November 8. That fix covered the query field; this fixes the separate value-search handler.

## Evidence

Verified candidate: `47acf54bb48cd98a6246c35b29575a51bbb449a6`.

[Real-Gateway browser proof, request counts and sanitized before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199872#issuecomment-6905516379). Two baseline and two candidate runs in Chromium exercise provider and creator pickers with trusted CDP IME events. Both confirmation variants accidentally select on baseline; neither selects or sends a usage request on the candidate. Active-composition Enter, deliberate Enter exactly once, Escape and outside-close controls are retained. This reproduces WebKit's post-composition ordering in Chromium, not a physical OS IME or a WebKit-engine run.

- Focused tests: 28/28 pass; both extended regressions fail on baseline. Matching UI-pages test types and production UI types pass. Focused wall time: 2.49 seconds; CI timing is recorded on this head's checks.
- Full ocx build with declarations and packed CLI/UI smoke pass.
- Official CI-normalized gzip: startup JS 91092 → 91092 B; chat-boot JS 1314555 → 1314555 B; startup + chat JS/CSS total growth **0 B**.
- Production +16/-1; tests +52/-52, net 0. All 28 cases and original assertions remain; reactive fixture forwarding and repeated lookups were consolidated. No allocation file or product-message changes.

Original fix and parent-menu repair by @zhangguiping-xydt; both contributor commits are retained.

Merge risk: two-way door. Reverting restores the old key handling without changing persisted data or configuration. Blast radius is the shared Usage value-picker search, including provider filters and the single-choice creator picker.

prs.title: refactor(ci): centralize independent Node/Bun runtime planning
prs.body:
Related: #197499 — superseded alternative. This PR retains the original implementation and contributor credit.

## Problem and scope

Full manual validation currently executes Node then Bun inside one job. This change makes root-test and plugin-batch runtime results independently schedulable/retryable. It does **not** claim a measured FRV wall-time win yet; candidate qualification and queue-inclusive comparison are required before landing.

## Simplification

- Restore the existing Node planner and its tests byte-for-byte to merge base `5b750071d1d31b2af9c8d2e58d0f65da010845dc`. Remove runtime-weighted repacking, special CLI stripes, executable-selection-to-packing helper, and temporary module-level timing context.
- Use the existing complete-inventory compact plan once; the manifest expands only runtime membership supplied by the existing runtime owner. Retain exact Node exceptions, both-host/native Bun selections, runner classes, worker limits, deadline/failure/retry identities, and frozen-target capability fallback.
- Restrict splitting to full manual validation. Daily/PR colocation and capacity remain unchanged. Keep all three UI jobs colocated: their three-slot cap offers no general extra runtime capacity and does not justify duplicate browser installation.
- Keep necessary timing collector/refit/reader identity changes so a partial runtime cannot overwrite complete historical policy measurements. Remove duplicate timing/planner tests and all three PR-only test-line allowance files; ordinary test budget passes without allocation credit.

## Historical rationale and actual wall-time evidence

Colocation was deliberate, not an accidental missed parallelism:
- #154340, commit `a94962e9ca8926b7bc410798fa9cb88a1e0ff78f`: qualified Bun in existing worker slots, separate caches/timings and Node preparation; UI initially stayed Node because Bun exceeded 16 GiB.
- #173807, `fa86f99a19fa23fb58b22da6b2cdfd859688cac3`: explicit full Node-before-Bun dispatch policy, doubled sequential deadlines and plugin phase barrier.
- #175699, `7f4c63524a63ffc3466b19cfa131e327e36d731f`: five paired trials established Bun/Node aggregate ratios 0.727–0.752; retained existing slots/caps. Those measurements establish Bun efficiency, **not** a split-job wall-time gain.
- #199366, `387042f830d0586ee6c8484d95db648521c3e78b`, cold release balancing, merged November 15 at 01:54:40 UTC. The evening FRV ran a frozen older target without that fix; it is not a valid measurement of current-main balancing. The shared compact plan also needs a fresh queue-inclusive comparison rather than extrapolation from that old run.

Observed FRV [43757970051](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43757970051), November 15 20:25:14–22:13:11 UTC: **6,477s** total, target `2c173a37a48f850246ae2133aa5c02df2ae35953`. Critical [job 132948320578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43758557488/job/132948320578) queued **631s**, ran **5,279s**, with ~226s setup (including 141s build). Its test step ran Node **2,822.14s**, then Bun **2,152.45s**. Across 174 root jobs, maximum queue delay was **1,041s**.

The 35m52s Bun overlap is only a single-job optimistic bound. Other npm/sealing barriers finished around 21:47, limiting the modeled whole-FRV gain to roughly **24–25 minutes** even before extra setup, runner availability, packing changes and queue delay. Full-manual root cap remains 96 and plugin cap 12. Extra setup/capacity contention can erase or reverse the gain. **No measured post-change FRV result yet; do not land on the theoretical bound alone.**

## Size and proof

Compared with previous `8d6aa41fb654f728ed841acab56617e63ff5233f`:
- Implementation/workflows: net **−232 LOC**; now **+250/−64 = +186 net** versus merge base (previous +500/−82 = +418).
- Tests: net **−330 LOC**; now **+415/−18 = +397 net** versus merge base (previous +747/−20 = +727).
- Documentation counted separately. No allocation/baseline relaxation.

Current cleanup head: `62d9307fcfaf82be12b6ea54f1387cb6f3d70969`. Proof:
- **1,039 workflow/planning tests pass** (150.05s wrapper), including full inventory, frozen-target capability fallback, unchanged daily/PR caps and production output-size guards. An initial two-test failure caught an over-broad cap change; fixed in production, not by weakening assertions.
- Timing reader suite: **109 tests pass**; runtime/plugin focused suites pass. Existing independent runner/refit/refresh contracts retained; superseded repacker-only assertions removed.
- Actual production-manifest comparison: daily/PR matrices byte-identical; full dual root 168→158 and full Bun 168→102, UI stays 3; emitted matrices below GitHub's 256-row limit.
- Actual config/glob/runtime-owner multiset comparison passes all four full-inventory scenarios: hybrid and GitHub × bun-all and dual-all. ## Problem

Related: #198259. When commands.allowFrom legitimately rejects a password-authenticated Control UI caller without a matching verified sender identity, plain-text /status previously vanished without a reply.

## Change

Internal WebChat command denials now return a visible refusal with an actionable next step: “Ask your Gateway administrator for command access.” The native-command branch remains first and preserves its existing wording. External /status text and native wrappers retain their existing silence. This changes feedback only: operator.admin does not bypass commands.allowFrom, and verified identity, authorization checks, owner attribution, and scopes are unchanged.

The correction also updates the /learn undo and /loop regressions to expect the visible refusal while retaining no-effect assertions.

## Current corrected candidate

Signed candidate: 683d6c24b54059a95ecfac1354050ea480142ec1. It adds a one-line persisted Workshop /learn undo consumer correction to bddd6464b82dfbefff03179a40470bddf89447f1; earlier corrections fixed the /loop expectation and denial-table type inference. Production remains identical to 66dbaeef42542e6f22616cb20d621c39a0bebdab; baseline remains d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f.

- Exact current Workshop correction: all 34 integration tests passed under Node 24 in secretless, network-disabled Podman. Messaging typecheck, targeted type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and whitespace passed. Independent review of blob 4fd157b30afd3bdc445c0652fa44bfd8e7e6e5e0 is READY with no findings. The persisted feed and both skill-file no-effect assertions remain unchanged. Initial dependency/cache setup failures occurred before meaningful testing; the corrected isolated setup passed.
- Previous exact loop correction: 9 tests passed; messaging typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace passed. The no-rewrite assertion and owner-only denial remain intact. Independent exact-blob review READY, no findings.
- Previous 3817b584: 26 commands-info tests and messaging typecheck passed. These repeat prior coverage, not additional distinct tests.
- Previous 66dbaeef: four focused suites / 70 tests and full build passed (2m 19.6s). Budget warnings are not performance qualification.
- Full-delta and subsequent test-only correction reviews retained. Neither old-head results nor pending/skipped checks establish current-head broad green CI.

One real-Gateway Chromium scenario passed in a secretless, network-disabled Podman container. It uses real browser pairing, a synthetic session, a nonmatching commands.allowFrom identity, and /status entered through the composer. The scenario creates a synthetic session, sets an allowlist identity that does not match the authenticated WebChat operator, and sends /status through the visible composer. Before: the command finishes silently and the refusal assertion times out. After: the original bare refusal is visible. No cloud model is contacted. Both screenshots were inspected and contain synthetic content only.

| ![Before: slash command has no refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/521273ab-3196-4759-b508-c131354291e7) | ![After: visible authorization refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66a96235-52f9-4535-8c5c-353b9586fcba) |

**Technical review-ready; broad CI remains red, not merge-ready.** On November 16, 2026, native exact-head commit validation and correction-review gate admission completed successfully for 683d6c24b54059a95ecfac1354050ea480142ec1; the latter records `github_pending`, not successful CI proof. Full run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43632645107 completed on November 14, 2026, at 21:48 UTC: **269 jobs, 232 successful, 23 failed, 3 canceled, 11 skipped, zero pending**. The 23 failures include the aggregate ci-gate, leaving 22 substantive failed jobs. The corrected Workshop QA4 job 132563023849 passed under both Node and Bun: 63 passed files / 1 skipped in each invocation, including the previously failing persisted unauthorized /learn undo case. The current messaging typecheck passed. All five Windows shards passed. QA10 passed 64 files / 1,150 tests under each runtime. These successes do not erase other failures or incomplete suites.

All substantive failed jobs and all three canceled jobs were examined. Attribution distinguishes demonstrated source defects, exact recurring signatures, and independent boundaries with unresolved dynamic causes:

- **QA16 / QA19:** Node fails respectively while rebuilding a removed symlink fixture without its pruned parent, and while reading a synthetic events.jsonl after the explicit update deadline expires. Bun passes both lanes. The former was traced to fixture reconstruction before GC assertions; the latter matches the preceding candidate. Neither enters chat-command authorization; timing cause remains unproven where applicable.
- **QA17:** canceled at the explicit two-hour limit, with real failures before cancellation. Node completed with 2 failed / 60 passed / 2 skipped files and 2 failed / 888 passed / 2 skipped tests. Both dry-run update tests report UpdateCommandFailure through ExitError(1); the same two tests also failed visibly under Bun, but Bun never emitted a completed summary. **November 15 follow-up closes the baseline-attribution gap:** both exact test names and ExitError stacks occur under Bun in actual scheduled-main run 43604797931 at b27440329b4c450ec4c572e40ed338ed98f3d9c7. Canonical commit d13336516b239a5164dbd1a978e0e131a306f2be repairs exactly these fixtures by creating their claimed source directories before preview, and records both complete files passing under Node and pinned Bun. Candidate source inspection confirms the missing root reaches fs.realpath during interrupted-link destination inspection introduced by #198673; the relevant main/candidate test and admission files are identical. These are inherited fixture failures, not command-denial defects. The canonical commit's recorded passes are not new candidate execution, and the current-head Bun shard remains incomplete.
- **iOS:** the onboarding bootstrap test failed at BootstrapSetupFailureUITests.swift:53 waiting for Enter setup code, before entering a URL or connecting. The detailed artifact shows a permission interruption during Connect Manually and an invalid computed hit point; the precise navigation cause remains unknown. The settings companion and Watch reachability passed. The exact assertion recurs on the preceding candidate; this is not proof of actual-main dynamic recurrence.
- **macOS:** canceled at the explicit 75-minute limit, **not cancellation-only**. The artifact contains 19 issue records across eight functions, including 600-second limits/wait diagnostics and a genuine MacNodeConnectionStatusTests.swift:87 identity assertion. Six functions completed as failed; pairing replacement and speech recovery remained incomplete. Pairing signatures recur on an earlier candidate, with direct-silent pairing also verified on actual main. Dashboard, health, node identity and speech dynamic attribution remains unresolved. Native sources are byte-identical to baseline, which establishes source independence, not blanket runtime recurrence.
- **Real-Gateway E2E:** canceled at the explicit 40-minute limit. Seventy observed module completions were pass/skip and no assertion-failure block was found, but the whole suite did not complete and is **not green**.

No further PR-caused defect was demonstrated after the three consumer corrections. This does not certify every unrelated failure harmless or resolve the outstanding runtime causes and incomplete native/QA/Gateway coverage. Full logs, artifacts, immutable source checks, final job inventory and per-lane reports are retained under the task's local proof directory. No unrelated repairs or additional reruns were made.

## Historical CI receipts

The preceding full run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43625456883 admitted target bddd6464b82dfbefff03179a40470bddf89447f1 with harness 5df28e77efea3a7bd958b19b758b3ea9b964cbbe and baseline d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f.
