prs.title: feat(templates): open Control UI chat and create the agent without a plan
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Template Add waits for a plan, then can leave an empty agent when a declared plugin is disabled.

## User Impact

Add opens pending chat immediately and creates the agent with its original manifest, files, skills, bundled plugins and MCP servers without a plan/review step. Failed dependencies are reported instead of rolling back; source or workspace failure removes the new agent and chat. CLI plan/consent behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Selects the chat path explicitly, reuses ordinary agent admission, preserves effective setup tools within explicit denies and operator ceilings, and leaves referenced plugins and automations for the following setup layer. The original workspace-root CLAW.md is reserved; a conflicting workspace declaration fails before Template writes. Its error now explains that nothing was kept and the publisher must move the conflicting file and publish a corrected release.

Warned skills or bundled plugins remain uninstalled and are reported. This does not bypass dependency trust checks.

## Evidence

### Current allocation-only repair

Published head `9ed5a58794db142be41f5e142e68a5cd92d72bd0` differs from `b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08` only in this layer’s existing test-line allocation record: **211→338** for the actual **738 net test lines** above foundation. The unchanged global allowance is **400**. The actual ratchet fails with the old 211 allocation and passes with 338; no tests, assertions, product source, scanners or global budgets changed. The paired tests and performance inputs below are unchanged, so those results remain applicable rather than being represented as new executions. Exact-head hosted CI and completed review remain required.

### Retained source qualification

Head `b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08` is restacked once above foundation `c1c471f63b56ad6e5908058d4bebf4e87e080454`. Generated validator conflicts were resolved by canonical regeneration, not hand-editing output. The CLI retains main's canonical scoped-package resolution and the leaf result contract. Git omitted the lazy-permission fixture repair because it is already upstream; unrelated source and all original worktrees are preserved.

- The complete strict paired performance command passes against exact foundation `c1c471f63b56ad6e5908058d4bebf4e87e080454`: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts c1c471f63b56ad6e5908058d4bebf4e87e080454`. Document **14,016 B <=14,026 B**. Chat JS **1,314,978→1,315,005 B (+27)** and New Session **817,974→818,000 B (+26)** meet the unchanged 64-byte differential allowance; startup JS stays **90,860 B**. Requests remain chat21/new17/startup3; boot CSS is unchanged, total CSS −14 B. No budgets raised or new lazy boundary. The unnecessary connection-error adapter import is deleted; the existing trust decoder reads the already-typed protocol error directly, preserving synchronous click-to-chat.
- Wrapper inventory now includes `clawhub-trust-error-details.ts`. Existing source-closure and extracted-dependency-context tests pass **2/2** (19.29s), including the actual materialized import graph.
- Gateway manifest-collision regression fails **1/1 before** for the intended generic-message mismatch. After repair the complete request-owner file passes **12/12** (92.84s; real isolated admission/config/workspace/session/rollback, external registry/model I/O fixed). It retains zero workspace writes, clean agent/chat rollback and successful Add of a corrected release, while returning actionable guidance as INVALID_REQUEST. Arbitrary internal exception text remains hidden.
- Protocol validators pass **5/5**. The original 150-second multi-lane wrapper completed those 17 cases but timed out before its CLI lane; it is not a full command pass. The separately scoped CLI state-owner command subsequently passes **19/19**, exit0 (8.58s suite), including reviewed consent and retained outcomes without replay/local fallback.
- Rendered Template Add tests pass **19/19** (5.99s), including card/detail/modal trust confirmation and duplicate-confirm handling. Four-file syntax lint, formatting, diff checks and canonical generated-validator check pass. No new test harness or mock, assertion removal, permission change, or state-schema change.
- Full exact-head hosted compiler, lint, build, architecture, CI and completed review remain required. These bounded local results do not claim full CI or final-stack real-install/video completion.

### Retained earlier proof

These results predate the current restack, not new exact-head executions:

- The reverse result-type import is removed through a leaf contract; incomplete dependency outcomes reach the opening rather than claiming readiness.
- Stored-checkpoint service compatibility: **11/11**. Refused chat retry retains the original entry/session/workspace; the original reviewed retry completes without rewriting SOUL.md. Not historical database-migration/restart proof.
- Paired lazy-permission fixture proof: old creation and unchanged base each pass119/fail1; unchanged assertion with existing settle helper passes120/120. Fixture-settlement proof, not conclusive attribution of the original hosted failure.
- Earlier integrated import boundary **1/1** and Template Add plus history/live/live-before-adoption composition **22/22**. Earlier pending-admission command timed out at150s after preparation and seven passes; not a full suite pass.
- Earlier creation Gateway12/12, integrated boundary13/13 including Retry, UI Add/admission26/26, browser24/24, synthetic-model real-Gateway authority3/3. Earlier aggregate changed-check retained inherited dead exports.

### Real Control UI comparison

Baseline `4ab02e3c0879` opened chat at19.9s, failed on the disabled plugin at35.6s and left an empty workspace without goplaces/model output. Earlier integrated candidate `c23e44d2811` (creation plus following setup layer) opened pending chat in104ms and produced visible output at52.2s.

The created workspace contains goplaces. Original CLAW.md matches source byte-for-byte, SHA-256 `5f8be1c9add44e177fb9f783d09919c377f1f223cbdc994b1f6e322557ef9f99`. That historical recording persisted the setup card but omitted it live until reload. Original `sentBeforeError=false` passed; original `sentBeforeError=true` failed with `OutboundDeliveryError: message failed: MatrixError: [403] M_FORBIDDEN`, created at the pinned test's line 457, rather than returning `delivery_unconfirmed`. Candidate versions of both cases passed in the prior run. Original-owner isolated wrapper wall time: **66.949 s**, launcher exit 1; per-case times 30.257 ms / 12.829 ms.

The continuation job remains **red**: its evidence gate mistook Vitest's ordinary `runWithTimeout` stack-frame name for a timeout diagnostic. The final admission-only correction filters stack frames out of infrastructure diagnostics, preserves real timeout/setup/connection rejection, and requires the exact original-owner error prefix and source location. All six retained JSON reports replay successfully through that corrected gate, with no further product execution. The final workflow disables the completed Matrix job; no completed SDK, candidate, wire, history, audio, permission, or billing stage was rerun.

[Retained artifact 14193046368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/artifacts/14193046368), `goal24-matrix-43791792505`, contains the six source reports, original-owner log, and the original red summary. The corrected admission result is a local replay, **not a new green hosted run**. Fresh independent native review of the final admission/disable delta also found no P0–P2 findings (SHA-256 `f2eeb134d198b733cdd40f441837d580cc4f7c0ddfd4321dc2606e188889a13e`). Final 26/26 admission tests, exact six-report replay, targeted lint/format/syntax, workflow validation, and whitespace checks passed.

**Remaining external gap:** no authenticated Matrix homeserver/recipient credentials are available. Accepted-then-429 recovery through the full Matrix delivery owner, exactly one recipient event/no duplicate, and encrypted recipient delivery remain unproven. The two causal pairs plus isolated Matrix file timings complete the missing causal/timing portion only. That does not automatically make M3 or the PR READY and supplies no merge, main-write, backport, or release authority.

### Historical failures and environmental limits

- Historical head `4aa0faa30907ba9ce07cfaccdaa7dd21c4bbf1b9`: CI run 43606138401 attempt 2 failed on M4 fixture collision and inherited scripts TS18048. It passed message-tool execution (74 tests), scheduled lifetime (18), accepted results (35), production types and lint. None of this is current-head runtime proof.
- Secretless AWS allocation failed before any lease because credentials were unavailable. No AWS tests or credentialed fallback ran; no contributor runtime executed on the trusted local host.
- **Authenticated live Matrix proof remains unavailable:** no homeserver credentials. No accepted-then-429 recipient delivery or no-duplicate claim.

The results below belong to the contributor's earlier head and are retained for attribution/history, not current-head proof.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor description and earlier-head evidence (superseded where noted above)</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

A `message` tool send can pass the point where the channel may already have accepted it and still come back as a failure — #196802 has Matrix answering `/send/m.room.encrypted/<txn>` with `429 Server is unavailable` after it accepted the event. The tool then reported a plain failure (`message failed: MatrixError: [429] ...`), the model did what "failed" implies, and the room got the same text twice. The delivery queue already knew better: it recorded `unknown_after_send` and reconciled the entry as already sent minutes later, but that knowledge never reached the tool result.

The queue's terminal failure already carries it. `OutboundDeliveryError.sentBeforeError` is set when an earlier attempt of the same intent started or its outcome is unknown, which is exactly the "may have landed" state. This projects that one case as a `delivery_unconfirmed` tool result so the model waits instead of minting a second send.

Two facts decide what the model may be told, and both already exist on the error:

- **Who owns reconciliation.** `owner.project(...)` stamps `queueCustody = "held"` while the durable queue still owns the attempt and `"released"` once it is retired; a `skipQueue` send (`message-tool-execution.ts:575`, scheduled direct sends) has no owner at all. Only `"held"` keeps the Gateway-reconciliation wording. Undefined or `"released"` reports `No queued retry owns it, so the send may already have reached the recipient; check it before resending.` — because there is no row to reconcile and promising one would be false.
- **What the provider already proved.** A permanent pre-dispatch rejection can carry `sentBeforeError` evidence from another payload in the same batch. When the error graph holds a `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError{retryable:false}`, the projection returns nothing and the rejection keeps its actionable error and cause.

Everything else keeps its current behavior: a failure that provably never left still throws, and a failure with confirmed platform sends keeps its existing partial-delivery path (`projectScheduledMessageActionPartialResult`), because the projection requires an empty `results` list.

Open question for the Matrix owner: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/transport.ts:269-283` wraps `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` only when the fetch never started, so a post-dispatch 403 is still reported as `sentBeforeError` and is indistinguishable here from an accepted-then-429 send. Classifying those as `retryable: false` in the adapter would route them through `isProvenDeliveryNotSentError` and out of this projection; that policy is not decided inside a tool-result projection.

Closes #196802

## Evidence

Red — both new behaviours fail against the previous projection, test kept (`node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts`):

```
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is undefined
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is released
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > keeps a provider-proven rejection actionable
   Tests  3 failed | 70 passed (73)
```

Green — same command on `937f77cb2`:

```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  73 passed (73)
```

Other checks, on `origin/main` at `584084d77`:

- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` — passed.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts` — 17 passed, 1 failed (`settles provider revocation during send via direct as accepted`). That failure reproduces identically with this change reverted, so it is a pre-existing Windows baseline, not a regression.
- `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on the touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json` — no diagnostics for the touched files (the repo's pre-existing `@openclaw/fs-safe` drift in unrelated files is unchanged).
- `run-format.mts --check` — all files formatted.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/196802-message-tool-unconfirmed-delivery.txt` = 67, matching the +67 test lines.

Diff against `584084d77` is +96/-3 across `message-tool-execution.ts` (rename), `message-action-execution.ts` (projection), the test file, and the ratchet allocation.

Why the proof is not here: this machine cannot build the dist (`@openclaw/fs-safe` in `node_modules` predates `preserve`, so `build-all.mts runtime` dies in `plugins:assets:build`), and the remaining item needs a live homeserver that accepts a message and then answers 429 without an event id. A maintainer proof run only has to assert `status: "delivery_unconfirmed"` with `delivered: false` on the tool result plus one recipient event.

</details>

prs.body:
## Summary

Recovered the missing focused Goal 24 execution evidence without running contributor code on a credentialed operator host, modifying the product branches, or touching main.

Temporary proof-only workflow on `proof/goal24-secretless-20261115`, explicitly authorized by @RomneyDa on November 15, 2026, including billed macOS execution. No merge, backport, release, or main-branch mutation is requested. This draft is an evidence carrier, not intended to merge.

## Verified product proof

### History — PASS

PR #198091, source `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`; tooling `c95caafe0fc52d86bdae05ebba9515085a300b3d`.

[Hosted run 43768728614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610910): 6 transcript recent-text tests and 5 inbound-context tests passed. Includes all physical-row boundaries, oversized-user barriers, shared 64 MiB budget, and the replay-suppression-after-restart regression. JSON reports prove selected test execution.

### Prefix stability — PASS

The earlier 11 history tests do **not** cover `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`. The focused correction at tooling `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` runs that entire suite against the same immutable PR #198091 source `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`, requiring all 14 cases and the completion-handoff authority regression. Zero or partial execution is rejected.

[Hosted run 43771398337, history job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771398337/job/132987885912) passed: all **14 prefix-stability assertions**, 6 recent-text tests, and 5 inbound-context tests (25 total). The downloaded JSON reports and summary agree on the exact source/tooling SHAs above, with every assertion passed. Prefix cases cover browser/CLI/ACP wakes and recovery, GitHub catalog stability, completion/scheduled/message definitions, wake-screen gating, and completion-handoff authority. Ubuntu 24.04 x64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0. This is focused suite evidence, not a real-model end-to-end claim.

Correction validation: 10 synthetic driver/preflight cases pass, including prefix-zero and partial-suite rejection. Against the prior driver, the new selection/zero/partial checks fail as expected (7 pass, 3 fail); this is harness regression proof, not product base-red evidence. Targeted lint/format, workflow validation, and 1,416 workflow/native-launcher regression tests pass. Initial workflow validation hit an empty-token environment error; rerunning with those empty variables removed passed.

Fresh native independent review of the exact correction from `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0` to `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` found no P0–P2 findings. Reviewed diff SHA-256: `28b466d8d024083d844ab23859180ab6441370b42f54ac4c34edf06d5d818cf3`. This is the explicit native fallback, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper result; the configured autoreview service credit failure remains unresolved, and no model or service route was switched.

### Audio — converter regression PASS; shipped delivery remains unproven

PR #198525, source `a9a084486e3df10193dfa9ac5ab9faa9f53a4619`; initial tooling `c95caafe0fc52d86bdae05ebba9515085a300b3d`.

[Hosted run 43768728614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610823): both focused budget cases passed. The exact timeout-removal mutation failed both cases, including the expected `[5000, 5000, 5000]` versus `[5000, 2000, 1000]` assertion. This is mutation evidence, not a base-red claim.

Real unmocked FFmpeg 9.0.2 → afconvert → afinfo control proof passed on macOS 27.0.1 arm64: a two-second synthetic MP3 converted to mono 24 kHz CAF, exactly 48,000 valid frames versus 48,000 independently decoded PCM frames; tiny exhausted-budget rejection and scratch cleanup verified. This control did not reproduce the original segmented-MP3 truncation. Tiny-budget proof does not claim subprocess termination. The production temp resolver selected its standard root outside isolated TMPDIR; both roots were checked for leftovers.

#### Original ten-segment regression — independently reproduced and repaired

[Hosted run 43772299539, audio job 132990706530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43772299539/job/132990706530) passed on November 15, 2026, using tooling `d43289d7095dadf3c3adc9c41792281cb1e67a12`, the same pinned product head, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, and FFmpeg 9.0.2. The job took 5m58s.

The exact committed synthetic fixture is 166,176 bytes, SHA-256 `7b2d8a3b1244383a4cfc3beaa57ba756c0d76c7d485fa80f927a458bdb60c0f0`. It contains ten independently encoded mathematical-tone segments; no private/user audio or provider call was used.

| Measurement | Independently decoded mono 24 kHz PCM | afinfo valid frames |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source MP3 | 1,153,775 frames / 48.073958 s | n/a |
| Original converter | 79,440 frames / 3.310000 s | 79,200 |
| Fixed converter | 1,154,088 frames / 48.087000 s | 1,153,775 |

The baseline is the unchanged production converter module from pre-fix commit `e80a6dd9fdb4c7ce724472dd5d1b216afb4e70a7`, SHA-256 `867e5fd7ad1b477b1f4ab1023e15d440873c6f9d3d98253bfa6ac4240f6b370d`, loaded alongside the fixed checkout's unchanged runtime dependencies. Only the converter, two tests, and fixture differ between that pre-fix commit and the product head. This is causal original-module red/fixed-module green proof, not a full baseline package build: original conversion succeeded, then the preservation assertion failed specifically on decoded frame loss; the fixed module passed. No helper or codec was mocked.

Fixed output differs by 313 decoded frames (13.042 ms), within the 480-frame Opus-padding allowance. Independent frequency checks at all ten segment centers matched 440, 477, 514, 551, 588, 625, 662, 699, 736, and 773 Hz, with non-silent energy. These samples establish segment presence/identity, not whole-waveform or speech-semantic equivalence. Fixed conversion took 731 ms inside the existing five-second budget. Both variants left no conversion workspaces in the product temp root or isolated TMPDIR.

Downloaded summary and separate native logs agree on the source/tooling/fixture identities and exit statuses (baseline 1, fixed 0). The receipt gate rejects missing/duplicate cases, setup failures mistaken for baseline red, incomplete segment proof, and missing cleanup. Earlier budget/mutation/control proof was retained, not rerun.

**Distinct unfulfilled gates:** no installed-package TTS delivery, Messages transport, receiving-device playback, or shipped missing-FFmpeg/original-attachment fallback was exercised. No paired external device is available to this session (`nodes.list()` returned none). The converter result does not satisfy these gates and makes no overall readiness/merge claim.

### macOS permissions — candidate PASS; causal callback failure reproduced

PR #198869, source `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`; tooling `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0`.

[Hosted run 43769449537](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43769449537/job/132981863979): app/tests compiled; all 10 PermissionManagerTests passed. Retained Swift Testing events prove discovery, start, and completion of `speech authorization completion can enter from a background queue`. Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4 / macOS 27.0.1. This is candidate-only regression coverage, not by itself causal base-red/fix-green evidence or interactive signed-app TCC behavior.

The initial permissions job stopped at an overly exact Swift 6.3 preflight on the supported newer Swift 6.4 image, before building or executing tests. The repair enforces the Package.swift minimum (6.3+) and accurately classifies setup failures. Only the missing permissions job was run again; the passing history/audio results were retained. The next history-only matrix collected the missing prefix-stability proof. At that stage, the matrix ran only the newly added segmented-audio comparison; completed history, permissions, and audio-budget proof were not repeated.

#### Off-main callback causal proof — collected November 16, 2026

Final proof head: `9325008d1f891d8539c6ec0155e6388cacf3c95f`. Product code was not changed by this proof: candidate `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e` and full baseline `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1` differ only in PermissionManager.swift and its original tests.

The same added Swift test, `Goal24SpeechFrameworkBoundaryTests.offMainFrameworkCompletion`, is explicitly **transplanted into both immutable checkouts**. It calls the real `PermissionManager.ensure([.speechRecognition], interactive: true)`. An Objective-C fixture intercepts only Speech authorization status/request selectors, dispatches the framework's actual received completion on a global queue, and records exactly one off-main invocation. No Swift production method, package setting, or actor-checking flag is patched. The candidate must return an authorized result, resume on MainActor, and report one request.

| Native execution | Product / tooling | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Candidate, run 43783553823 / job 133026037240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823/job/133026037240) | candidate above / `924b7db5b02bcd42305bcbe3e7f34ed9dc2bdd4d` | Build passed; exactly one selected function started/completed; off-main marker once; test passed in 0.012 s; native launcher exit 0. |
| [Initial baseline, same run / job 133026037588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823/job/133026037588) | baseline above / same tooling | Build passed; same test started; marker once; Signal 5; no completion; launcher exit 1. The job remained red because Swift's crash helper could not produce the required stack. |
| [Baseline stack diagnostic, run 43786255830 / job 133034441205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43786255830/job/133034441205) | baseline above / final tooling above | Build passed; one start, zero completions, marker once; actual SIGTRAP captured; launcher exit 1; strict expected-failure gate passed with executor and original production callback frames. |

The collected crashing-thread stack is: `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail` → `dispatch_assert_queue` → `_swift_task_checkIsolatedSwift` → `swift_task_isCurrentExecutorWithFlagsImpl` → the original `PermissionManager.ensureSpeechRecognition` authorization callback → Speech block bridge → fixture's background dispatch block. This is the required callback-entry actor-isolation failure, not a compilation, setup, or zero-selection failure. The fixture's diagnostic SIGTRAP handler records an actual signal and exits 133; it never raises one. SwiftPM/launcher reports exit 1. Candidate execution was retained, not repeated for this diagnostic.

**Environment qualification:** the paired candidate/initial-baseline jobs both used macOS 27.0.1 arm64. The later hosted baseline diagnostic image had advanced to macOS 27.2 arm64; Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), Swift 6.4 (swiftlang-6.4.0.34.1), Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 were unchanged. The final stack is therefore a cross-image corroboration of the earlier same-image differential, not a claim of same-image stack capture. Both variants' Swift test SHA-256 is `07670b386db7e63744294bfe64193bc2f8a496fc2c78f01c0e73bddcb0159352`. The Objective-C fixture changed only to add diagnostic signal capture; its hashes are `5e2d8fd2ca8a7f26ac5af7376a6bd050c8fdc5a70ba6b2dbdedb47156ef4eec7` before and `6dc25ce0a5952fa911d0f1303f76baf865b7365c9e5738a27fa28cf6fcc37746` after.

Earlier [Swift-seam control run 43780908432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43780908432) did **not reproduce**: both variants executed one function and passed. Its initial event gate counted suite and function events together. Corrected local replay identified candidate success and control nonreproduction; no macOS rerun was spent on that parser correction. [Compiler-only run 43782722861 / job 133023349215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43782722861/job/133023349215) then showed why: the extracted original imported callback has an executor-entry check, unlike the mutated Swift seam. That compiler probe is supporting diagnosis, not exact candidate SIL or runtime proof.

Fresh independent native reviews found no P0–P2 findings: boundary delta SHA-256 `1b697abfba74f7df7ac3d29bd911b8f2a9e6d61e6a983b5521d58092f371e48a`; diagnostic delta `014b0c31ffc0f59fb35c12cef7fc38ec1f511b7e84571b0bf2964f04b2b1cb5f`. Final synthetic gate checks: 26/26 pass, including Signal 5 and rejection of missing/wrong stacks. Targeted lint/format, workflow validation, and 8 files / 1,416 native-workflow guard tests passed (217.82 s wrapper). Retained artifacts were replayed through the final strict gate: candidate pass and expected baseline failure both accepted.

**Limitations:** this is causal native production-callback proof with synthetic OS responses. It does not exercise a signed app's interactive first grant, denial/regrant, Settings navigation, TCC persistence, or a real user's device. Those external gates remain unfulfilled. No merge, backport, release, main write, or rerun of history/audio/billing was performed.

## Safety and validation

- Fresh disposable hosted VMs; read-only repository permission; no secrets/OIDC/environments/shared caches; checkout credentials not persisted. Contributor subprocesses receive an allowlisted environment and isolated HOME/state. These checks are not a process sandbox; the disposable VM is the isolation boundary.
- Immutable source SHAs, fixed commands, 30/45-minute job bounds, bounded subprocesses, seven-day synthetic-only artifacts. No user audio or HOME/state upload. Audio-only Homebrew provisioning was bounded to eight minutes with auto-update/analytics disabled.
- Independent native source/security review and final-delta review found no P0–P2 blockers. Local ClawSweeper/autoreview executors were unavailable; this is explicitly a native fallback, not a claimed ClawSweeper/Codex result.
- The segmented-proof final diff against `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` received fresh independent native review, with no P0–P2 findings: SHA-256 `591f83cb056a99c0550f90032e8e576d49af37564d69c2cf7d4f68049415bb82`.
- Required workflow/macOS-launcher tooling regressions: 8 files, 1,416 tests passed again for the segmented-proof change (241.06 s wrapper wall time). Sixteen synthetic driver/preflight cases pass (about 0.63 s), including zero/partial proof rejection and Swift-version checks.
- Workflow validation (pinned actionlint/zizmor plus repository guards), targeted lint, formatting, native-harness typecheck with repository ambient declarations, and whitespace checks pass.

## Scope

One bounded driver reuses the repository's test wrapper and macOS isolation owner; the native fixture imports the real audio implementation. No product change, generic runner manager, free-form command input, compatibility path, main write, merge, backport, or release. The initial three-lane workflow remains in the first commit and its artifacts remain attached to the first run.

## Billing — paired runtime observations collected

PR #197369: baseline `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` versus candidate `8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c`. Final proof tooling `16f421ebb28694e48f388ce745e6df848af8fad1` (initial harness `935834f61761725baa063fdfc46d6c31a0ae9cc5`); original runtime tooling/Bun pin `b27440329b4c450ec4c572e40ed338ed98f3d9c7`.

Five fixed Linux groups cover the unresolved jobs 132481409032, 132481406074, 132481409054, 132481409138, and 132481420753. Fourteen selected files include all 18 originally failing cases. Each baseline/candidate group receives its own fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0; original pinned Bun is staged without shared caches. Node precedes Bun. Original runtime/private-QA preparation is retained where the original job built it. Per-case/per-runtime failure signatures, nonzero execution, required-case admission, and actual file start-time order are checked. Missing cases/reports and setup timeouts remain failures, not successful observations. Any observed test failure keeps the hosted job red.

**Important limitation:** this is a bounded focused replay with a common fixed serial order, not the original full parallel shard load. It omits sibling files and separates Node/Bun invocations to preserve distinct reports. A passing replay means “not reproduced,” never “fixed” or “inherited.” Candidate-only failures likewise require causal investigation. The upstream runtime-preparation change `7cd145595bf99f4caec9148b85db37bbb9147fab` is not applied or claimed as a fix. No new billing-path causal attribution is claimed.

Validation: 11 synthetic evidence-admission tests pass, targeted lint and formatting pass, `git diff --check` passes, and the unchanged final workflow passes repository workflow validation (actionlint/zizmor and repository guards). Initial lint findings were corrected and the final lint command passed with failure propagation. Fresh independent native source/security review of the complete final four-file delta found no remaining P0–P2 findings after correcting order enforcement, all required state cases, and exact wrapped timeout signatures. The final review hashes match the published files. This is the existing explicitly labeled native fallback, not a ClawSweeper/autoreview service result.

No completed history, prefix, audio, or permission proof is rerun. No main/product-branch write, merge, backport, or release.



### Billing harness boundary correction — November 15, 2026

Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43775844906 completed with all ten jobs failing the nonzero gate: the pinned Vitest 5 accepts a sequencer constructor in configuration, not a CLI module path. The Node reports contained zero executed tests (`TypeError: Sequencer is not a constructor`); Bun was not reached. This is harness/setup failure, not billing regression evidence. All artifacts were collected and retained.

Commit `16f421ebb28694e48f388ce745e6df848af8fad1` narrowly attaches the constructor to the original config export, preserving original config paths, setup, source pins and selection. Synthetic constructor/policy test added (12/12 pass); syntax, targeted lint and diff checks pass. Independent native final-delta review found no P0–P2 findings (delta SHA-256 `c4b7ebefe370ce48ebe244ceb77739b92a7f1afc9dc364ed2bb56ac10b4971bf`).

Changed-harness recovery run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777174095 — completed November 16, 2026, 00:20 UTC; all ten artifacts collected. Eight jobs passed and both state jobs retained actual test failures. No unchanged-job rerun or repeated completed history/audio/permission proof.


### Collected paired results

Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777174095 executed all selected cases on **both exact source pins**, Node then Bun, with identical fixed preparation and admitted file order. Case identities, statuses, and complete failure messages compare identically between baseline/candidate for each runtime/group. **364 executed assertions: 356 passed, 8 failed.** No zero-test or missing-required-case admissions; no incomplete runtime observations.

| Original job / group | Baseline Node / Bun | Candidate Node / Bun | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 132481409032 / state | 14 pass + 2 fail / 14 pass + 2 fail | 14 pass + 2 fail / 14 pass + 2 fail | Same two Beam UNAVAILABLE failures on both pins and runtimes; all other selected state cases pass. |
| 132481406074 / chat | 62 pass / 62 pass | 62 pass / 62 pass | Pending chat.startup metadata assertion did not reproduce. |
| 132481409054 / reload | 1 pass / 1 pass | 1 pass / 1 pass | Original Bun 120-second timeout did not reproduce. |
| 132481409138 / startup | 6 pass / 6 pass | 6 pass / 6 pass | sessions.list and sessions.github.options timeouts did not reproduce. |
| 132481420753 / compaction | 6 pass / 6 pass | 6 pass / 6 pass | backend-not-entered signature did not reproduce. |

The two state failures are in `server.beam-owned-view.test.ts`:
- `HTTP Visitor publications are privately readable by their initial publisher through admitted RPC` (assertion at line 287).
- `preserves model admission and rolls back revoked owned Beam adoption` (assertion at line 559).

All eight failing assertions report `UNAVAILABLE` / `Could not load this Beam. Refresh and try again.` The four **Bun** failures match the original required case/runtime signatures. Node reports the same symptom on both pins, but is deliberately **not** labeled an original runtime-signature match because the original signature was Bun. This establishes that these Beam symptoms also occur before the billing diff under this focused preparation; it is not blanket attribution of the original failing shard.

The ACP-native timeout/catalog-retiring cascade, config.set reread timeout, and sessions.create timeouts were not reproduced. prs.title: feat(cron): back automation off when a provider pushes back
prs.body:
Related: #196859

Depends on #197394, which sizes automation from the agent limit and memory with no setting.

## What Problem This Solves

Automation bursts can keep replacing completed runs at full capacity even when a provider repeatedly rate-limits requests that eventually succeed through retries.

## User Impact

- A provider rate-limit or overload signal halves automation capacity when automation and the hook turns sharing its budget hold more than eight agent sessions, with a floor of eight.
- Each minute without pushback adds one slot back, until the limit is whole again. With runs queued, the scheduler picks up the new slot within about a minute.
- This limit combines with the sizing from #197394: automation runs no more than the CPU share, the backoff ceiling and the memory count allow. Memory can still take it below eight, down to one.
- Conversations stay independent, and running automations finish normally.
- Each reduction is logged as a Gateway warning. There is no setting.

Backoff makes a backlog drain more slowly. The ceiling is process-wide, so pressure from one provider can also slow jobs using other providers and command or script jobs.

Accepted edge case, as in #197394: after a quiet period no recent exec command sets the per-job memory figure, so a burst of jobs whose commands are much larger than 256 MiB can still exceed the exec memory budget. The exec memory guard then stops the largest command with an error naming the budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run-slot owner observes classified model-attempt failures. It reacts to attempts rather than final job status because runtime retries can turn a rate-limited attempt into an `ok` job.

The ceiling is a reduced value plus one slot per minute since the last pushback, so recovery needs no growth bookkeeping and no signal from the run queue. One burst causes one reduction: while the sessions already in flight exceed the ceiling, their further pushback holds it where it is instead of halving it again; pushback once they have come down to it halves again. Pushback that cannot lower the ceiling, with eight sessions or fewer in flight, also holds it, so every step up follows a full minute without pushback.

Accepted tradeoffs:

- Automation and hook sessions together determine reductions, while the resulting ceiling applies to every automation job type; hook turns keep their own lane width within the shared budget.
- Internal session events share the automation lane.
- CLI, ACP, compaction and other model calls that emit no supported failure event do not drive backoff.
- Reductions are not persisted across Gateway restarts.
- Recovery is gradual: returning from eight to 32 slots takes about 24 minutes without pushback.

For automations whose parent has no workspace binding, parent replacement can still permit owner-authorized work on main. The [main prompt executor installs its parent-source guard only for workspace-bound children](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/220ca12e0732ab599c5a9b6434ac699f6750728f/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L212). The slot wait lengthens that interval; these PRs do not introduce the behavior. Maintainers may choose separate hardening.

## Evidence

Targeted tests, all passing: `service.cross-tick-admission`, `service.run-queue`, `store/scheduler-actor.worker`, `server-lanes.hook-group` and `process/child-memory` (78 tests, including every #197394 regression). Core, cron-test and services-test typechecks, lint on all 20 changed TypeScript files, and format pass. Backoff regressions:

- An agent limit of 30 and 32 due jobs: a provider rate limit halves 22 automation sessions to 11, a second pushback from the same sessions does not halve again, a run ending does not hand its slot on, the ceiling rises to 12 after a minute, a pushback holds it for a minute, and it climbs back to the whole 30 without further pushback.
- Nine sessions cut to eight, then another rate limit at eight sessions 50 seconds later: the ceiling stays at eight for a full minute after that pushback before it rises to nine.
- With hooks on and an agent limit of 32, eight automation runs and eight hook turns in flight: a rate limit halves sixteen to eight, failing without its fix.

Cron tests use fixed free-memory and exec-budget readings, and the cgroup case fakes the cgroup root too. Linux test runs of `service.cross-tick-admission` at `8533a104542` (arm64 Docker, Node 24): on a 6 GB host with no container limit the previous fixture let the host's exec budget cap admission at eight, and 4 of 17 cases failed ("expected 10, got 8", "expected 30, got 8"); with the fixed fixture 17/17 pass, also in a 4 GiB container. The cgroup root fix comes from #197394's head, where in a 4 GiB container the cgroup case admitted four jobs, not five, with the fixture fix alone.

Upgrade from the latest stable at `f97bcfb2df3` (Node 24.20.0): stable 2026.11.3 (`847611d`) upgraded to this head with no config differences, all 18 jobs unchanged, and all 19 IDs with their run history kept. With an agent limit of 12, twelve jobs ran while four due jobs waited, then 16/16 succeeded. A cold restart kept everything, and Doctor converted the heartbeat in place. Bun and the installer path were not run.

Populated container at `f97bcfb2df3`: a private Linux VM, an 8 GiB cgroup v2 container with swap off, a resident 5 GiB peer process, and 16 cron agent jobs each running a real 256 MiB command against a synthetic provider. At most 3 jobs ran at once, memory reached the 8 GiB limit with the kernel reclaiming cache and no OOM kills, all 16 commands completed, and the peer stayed up. The same run on main (`e970cf66f7b`) started 8 jobs at once and lost 15 commands to OOM kills (1/16 completed); its peer also stayed up.

Hook turns in backoff, live at `edeb0a8d703` (this head's code; `8533a104542` changes one test file only) on macOS with 16 CPUs, an agent limit of 32 and hooks on: eight cron agent jobs and eight `POST /hooks/agent` turns were held open by a synthetic provider, which then answered one hook turn's request with HTTP 429. The Gateway logged `automation limited to 8 runs at once after provider standin rate-limited a request`. Once the eight jobs finished, 16 more came due 23 seconds after the 429 while the hook turns were still running: at most 8 ran at once through the 57 second mark, and all 24 jobs then completed ok. The same run at the commit before the hook fix (`1cb2ad0be04`) logged no limit and ran all 16 at once.

Live runs on real isolated Gateways with a synthetic HTTP model provider. The 4 GiB memory runs used commit `dba96726cd0`, in a cgroup with no other process in it:

- Real HTTP 429 and 503 responses, run at commit `64b183a80f9` with no hooks configured, so its backoff counted the same sessions as this head: sixteen requests reduced to eight, queued work waited, and a ninth started after about 71 seconds without further pushback; all 24 jobs completed.
- In a 4 CPU / 4 GiB Linux cgroup with swap off and real exec commands: 16 jobs of 256 MiB each 16/16; 16 mixed commands from 16 to 768 MiB in ascending order 16/16 with at most 3 at once; the ten-minute figure kept the still-recent 384 MiB command after a 768 MiB one expired (33/33 jobs); largest first after idle 15/16 with the 768 MiB command stopped by the exec guard (the edge case above). No OOM kills in any run.

## Validation Limits

The provider was synthetic, not a real vendor model. The hook run was on macOS, not Linux. The test suite could not run in a 2 GiB container (vitest's own compile step stalls there), so the 2 GiB example from review was checked at 4 GiB and on the 6 GB host instead. Overload from real services, active config reload, production user data, Windows, Bun, cgroup v1, the installer upgrade path and the full suite were not exercised.

prs.title: feat(cron): size automation from the agent limit and free memory
prs.body:
Related: #196859

## What Problem This Solves

Due automations wait behind a fixed cap of eight runs. A large team server has room for many more, while a Raspberry Pi or a small container can run out of memory with eight. A fixed number, or a setting for it, is wrong on one of those hosts.

## User Impact

- No setting. Automation sizes how many jobs run at once from the host, every time the run queue decides what may start.
- CPU side: automation shares `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent` (default `max(8, available CPU parallelism * 4)`) with conversations. It may run that limit minus the conversation turns in progress, and conversations never take it below eight. Conversations never wait for automation.
- Memory side: automation runs at most as many jobs as fit in half of the memory open to it, counting about 256 MiB per job. Open memory is the memory currently free plus what running exec commands hold. Under a cgroup v2 memory limit, as in a container, it is at most what that cgroup has left, counting every process in it and treating inactive file cache as free; on Linux it is also at most the exec memory budget. A small or busy host runs fewer jobs, down to one at a time; a large host runs up to the agent limit.
- On Linux, the per-job figure is the most memory one exec command has held in the last ten minutes when that is more than 256 MiB, so jobs that run large commands are counted at their real size.
- Due jobs that do not fit stay queued and start when a run ends, or within a minute of a conversation turn ending or memory being freed. Running jobs are never stopped. Condition checks do not use these slots, and hook dispatch keeps its own width of eight.

Accepted edge case: after a quiet period no recent command sets the figure, so a burst of jobs whose commands are much larger than 256 MiB can still exceed the exec memory budget. The exec memory guard then stops the largest command with an error naming the budget. Starting one job at a time after idle until its command is measured would avoid this, at the cost of slowing every burst after idle, so it is left out.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run queue owns admission, so the host hands it one number of run slots: the CPU share above, capped by the memory count. The memory count depends only on open memory and the per-job figure, not on how many jobs are running. Jobs that just started, whose commands have not shown up as used yet, therefore cannot use up the spare half, however often the queue is drained before they do.

Container headroom comes from the Gateway's cgroup v2 and each visible ancestor with a memory limit: the limit minus what the cgroup holds, less inactive file cache, which the kernel reclaims before killing anything. That counts other processes in the same container, such as a browser or a sidecar, without treating cache as used. Commands are measured by the existing exec memory owner (`src/process/child-memory.ts`), which keeps the largest command sample of the last ten minutes for the per-job figure; when that sample expires, the next largest recent one takes its place.

Accepted tradeoffs:

- Only conversation-lane turns reduce automation's CPU share; subagents, restart-recovery turns and hooks do not.
- The eight-run CPU floor can exceed a configured agent limit below eight.
- Processes other than exec commands, such as a browser, count only through free memory, not through the per-job figure.
- Off Linux there is no exec budget, so jobs are counted at 256 MiB.
- On cgroup v1, or where the cgroup files cannot be read, the container bound is the limit minus the Gateway's own memory, which does not see other processes in the container.
- Waiting demand causes a recheck each minute, including when another admission condition prevents a run.

## Evidence

Targeted tests, all passing: `service.cross-tick-admission`, `service.run-queue`, `store/scheduler-actor.worker`, `server-lanes.hook-group` and `process/child-memory` (75 tests). Core, cron-test and services-test typechecks and lint pass. Regressions, each failing without its fix:

- Twelve due jobs with free memory short: one run at a time, two with 1 GiB free, none while exec commands hold the whole budget or while a recent command held 8 GiB, and all twelve once memory is free.
- With 2 GiB free, three drains in a row start four jobs, not seven.
- An 8 GiB cgroup limit on the Gateway's parent cgroup, holding the 512 MiB Gateway, a 5 GiB peer process and 1 GiB of inactive file cache: five 256 MiB jobs start, not fifteen.
- After a large command expires from the ten-minute window, a smaller recent one sets the figure instead of the 256 MiB floor.
- An agent limit of twelve with two conversation turns in progress runs ten automations; a run ending and a turn ending each pass a slot on.
- Cron tests use fixed free-memory and exec-budget readings, and the cgroup case fakes the cgroup root too, so neither a loaded test machine nor its cgroup can shrink the run slots a case needs.

Linux test runs of `service.cross-tick-admission` at `0fe8e935a6a` (arm64 Docker, Node 24): on a 6 GB host with no container limit the previous fixture let the host's exec budget cap admission at eight, and 2 of 14 cases failed ("expected 10, got 8"); with the fixed fixture 14/14 pass. In a 4 GiB container the previous head failed 4 of 14; with the fixture fix alone the cgroup case still admitted four jobs, not five, because it read the container's own limit at the cgroup root; with both fixes 14/14 pass.

Upgrade from the latest stable at `eb15eab540c` (Node 24.20.0): stable 2026.11.3 (`847611d`) upgraded to this head with no config differences, all 18 jobs unchanged, and all 19 IDs with their run history kept. With an agent limit of 12, twelve jobs ran while four due jobs waited, then 16/16 succeeded. A cold restart kept everything, and Doctor converted the heartbeat in place. Bun and the installer path were not run.

Populated container at `eb15eab540c`: a private Linux VM, an 8 GiB cgroup v2 container with swap off, a resident 5 GiB peer process, and 16 cron agent jobs each running a real 256 MiB command against a synthetic provider. At most 2 jobs ran at once, memory peaked at 7.888 GiB, there were no OOM kills, all 16 commands completed, and the peer stayed up. The same run on main (`e970cf66f7b`) started 8 jobs at once, hit the 8 GiB limit and lost 15 commands to OOM kills (1/16 completed); its peer also stayed up.

Live runs at commit `4608a133aae` on real isolated Gateways with a synthetic HTTP model provider and real exec commands, in a 4 CPU / 4 GiB Linux cgroup with swap off and no other process in it:

- 16 jobs each running a 256 MiB command: 16/16, no OOM kills, no guard kills.
- 16 mixed commands from 16 to 768 MiB in ascending order: 16/16, at most 3 at once.
- A 768 MiB command, then a 384 MiB one three minutes later: once the first left the window the figure stayed at the 384 MiB command's size (33/33 jobs).
- The same mixed commands largest first after idle: 15/16, the 768 MiB command stopped by the exec guard (the edge case above), no OOM kills.

## Validation Limits

The provider was synthetic, not a real vendor model. The test suite could not run in a 2 GiB container (vitest's own compile step stalls there), so the 2 GiB example from review was checked at 4 GiB and on the 6 GB host instead. Windows, Bun, x86 Linux, cgroup v1, real channels, the installer upgrade path and the full suite were not exercised.

Teams tests duplicated parts of the inbound runner and attachment policy, while the test isolation guard treated SQLite file URIs as literal paths.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixtures now use the real public inbound runner and isolated session persistence, with dispatch injected at its existing per-turn boundary. Cleanup joins session work and canonical SQLite cleanup before deleting owned roots, while explicit runtime-config reload snapshots remain intact.

Attachment checks assert ordered saved results and adapter forwarding without duplicating media policy or replacing the existing real SharePoint storage path. The SQLite guard checks NUL before canonical decoding and retains physical containment and original opener arguments. Superseded suites and the retired SQLite coordinator remain removed.

The correction is integrated on frozen base 91d08c31d14cd85be17e5ecb4d8a0ec075ef53bb. Final head is f7a21e31e0976f3ea1de083cede24f7965fd8200: 15 test/private-support source files, +500/-197 lines, plus the exact test-line allocation.

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--

and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```

 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra
lane; the two new tests derive their carrier URL from `import.meta.url` so they run on both
platforms. `pnpm tsgo:core` refuses a worktree that shares its install with the main checkout
("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so the typecheck gate was not run locally and is left to
CI. No live Gateway was started on this machine; the log-line half is proven by reading the file
the file transport actually wrote.

CI on head `e129273e8` (server-recorded base `dbb580aed`, which is 171 commits behind current `main`): 129 check runs = 67 success / 59 skipped / 1 neutral (CodeQL) / 2 failure. The two failures are `checks-windows-node-test-5` (completed 2026-10-02T08:19:37Z) and the 2 s aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` that follows it in the same run. The failing case is `test/scripts/write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts > write-unified-entry-dts > reuses unaffected canonical groups while rebuilding runtime after input edits`, and it throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './record-coerce' is not defined by "exports"` from a `package.json` inside that test's own temporary fixture project (`%TEMP%\oc-vt-8AAiWh\openclaw-sdk-declarations-5DFbNf\Project\node_modules\@openclaw\normalization-core`), imported from `src/process/exec-result.ts` in the same temp tree. This diff is two files, both `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.*`: it touches none of `test/scripts/`, `packages/normalization-core/`, or `src/process/`, and `packages/normalization-core/package.json` on this head does export `./record-coerce`.

What is deliberately not claimed here: inheritance is not proven. prs.title: feat(agents): make Tool Search control result character limit configurable
prs.body:
## Summary
- Adds `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` (`number | "auto"`) to configure the pre-wrapper character budget for network-sourced Tool Search control results (`renderToolSearchControlText` in `src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`).
- Preserves the existing `20,000`-character default (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) when `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` is unset.
- Supports `"auto"` to scale with the active model's live tool-result cap (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) minus the external-content wrapper overhead, and clamps explicit numeric limits at or under the active model's live tool-result budget so wrapped results are never cut mid-marker by the outer tool-result guard.
- Consciously raises the `core` config baseline count budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` by +1 (`2638` -> `2639`) and updates `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the new `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` setting requested in #194857.

## What Problem This Solves
Network-sourced Tool Search (`dispatch_action` / `call_tool` and Code Mode) control results were hardcoded to truncate at `20,000` characters (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) in `renderToolSearchControlText` (`src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`) before `wrapExternalContent`, even when the active model's context window and live tool-result budget (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) could safely accommodate larger structured responses (#194857). Operators and high-context agents had no configuration knob to raise or auto-scale that pre-wrapper character limit while preserving the `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT ...>>>` boundary against outer truncation.

## Evidence
- Verified schema, config resolution, and runtime truncation behavior with Vitest unit tests in:
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-gateway-tool.test.ts` (validates `maxResultChars: "auto"` and positive integers in `AgentToolSurfacePresentationSchema.properties.toolSearch`, rejecting `0`, negative, non-integer, and unknown string values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-config.test.ts` (verifies `resolveToolSearchConfig` omits `maxResultChars` when unset and retains `"auto"` or positive integer values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts` (`scales network control output with maxResultChars='auto' or clamps a fixed limit to the live budget`: verifies a `30,000`-char network payload is preserved un-truncated under `maxResultChars: "auto"` with a `200,000`-token context window, and that `maxResultChars: 50_000` on a `32,000`-token context window is clamped prior to wrapping so `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="...">>>` remains intact).
- Verified `pnpm config:docs:gen` baseline artifacts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`).

Fixes #194857

prs.title: fix: show multi-question reply format
prs.body:
Closes #173760

AI-assisted. Substantially follows the shared-guidance and regression shape from #173845 by @D41910; the commit credits Winoren as co-author.

## Summary

- Show one bounded, copyable multiline example in the initial multi-question prompt and invalid-answer recovery notice.
- Document the same accepted reply format.
- Derive the regression's successful reply from the displayed example so guidance and parser behavior cannot drift.

## Issue

Closes #173760.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messaging-channel users can be told to answer every `ask_user` question by number or id without being shown that each answer needs its own keyed line.

## User Impact

User impact: after an incomplete grouped answer is rejected, the user sees a concrete two-line reply template and can fill it in while the same question remains open.

## Root cause

The multi-question parser already accepts one keyed answer per line, but the shared prompt owner and rejection notice exposed only abstract wording. A normal one-line prose reply fills question 1 and leaves later required questions empty, so the recovery path repeated guidance that did not demonstrate the required shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt guidance is the canonical owner for this format. Reusing one bounded constant in the initial prompt and rejection notice fixes both user-visible paths without changing parsing, validation, authorization, custody, or question lifecycle. #190513 remains complementary parser/numbering work; #193400 remains complementary correction-delivery work.

## Verification

- Exact upstream base: `c61a7c0cf6b72f9c35ad8acdc432e132f4d86a50`; the five touched files were unchanged from the reproduced `95363ce54afd893d89cc6bd6645578dba52888d0` snapshot.
- Before source oracle: exit 1. A one-line two-question answer populated `where`, left `game` empty, and found no copyable example in prompt, rejection, or docs.
- After the same oracle: exit 0. It extracted `1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>`, filled it as `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000`, and mapped both keyed answers while confirming the rejection notice and docs use the same format.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --check` passed for all four touched TypeScript files.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Production delta: `+6/-2` (net +4); tests `+13/-6`; docs `+10/-3`.

## Before/after

Before:

```json
{"answers":{"where":"either is fine, and lets do X","game":""},"hasExample":false,"docsExplain":false,"reproduced":true}
```

After:

```json
{"example":"1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>","completeAnswer":"1: Lisbon\n2: 2000","answers":{"destination":"Lisbon","budget":"2000"},"correctionUsesShared":true,"docsExplain":true,"fixed":true}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Multi-question text prompts and invalid-answer recovery now show the keyed multiline reply shape the existing parser accepts.
- **Real environment tested:** Exact current OpenClaw source snapshot on macOS with Node 22.22.3; source-level behavior oracle plus syntax/docs/diff checks.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Node source oracle reading the production prompt, rejection, parser contract, and docs; `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on the four TypeScript files; `node scripts/docs-list.js`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The oracle derived `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000` from the displayed example, resolved both keyed answers, confirmed both runtime messages share the guidance, and exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** The user-visible recovery text now contains a copyable answer that satisfies both questions without changing parser or lifecycle semantics.
- **What was not tested:** No live Telegram account, deployed Gateway, external model/API, or focused Vitest run.

## Risk and scope

Low. This changes shared bounded guidance, one recovery string, one documentation paragraph, and assertions around the existing custody flow. No config, schema, protocol, persistence, parser, validation, authorization, or delivery lifecycle changes.

## Not tested

Focused Vitest did not start. Blacksmith Testbox failed before allocation because the local `blacksmith` executable is unavailable. Local dependency installation failed first because the configured npm mirror lacks `@pnpm/macos-arm64@12.15.0`, then because Corepack's pnpm 12.15.0 cache was incomplete. The repository formatter and autoreview also could not bootstrap through the same blocked network path; no passing claim is made for them.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface backup restore guard remedies in --json failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup restore backup.tar.gz --target ./restored --postgres-connection-env "not a name" --json` exits 1, but stderr prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` and `For help, run openclaw doctor.` — the actionable remedy (`--postgres-connection-env requires an environment variable name.`) survives only inside the stdout JSON envelope, so an operator watching stderr loses the next step. Eight more restore guards behave the same way: state/agent directory containment, file target, non-empty target, disk capacity, unset connection env, `--local-companion` profile mismatch, and a plain archive without PostgreSQL stores. This PR routes those nine operator-input guards through the existing `throwExpectedCliError` owner so `--json` failures keep their remedy on stderr, with messages, exit codes, and the stdout envelope unchanged.

- Problem: nine operator-facing guards in `backupRestoreCommand` throw plain `Error`; the JSON failure path replaces their remedy text with the generic two-line banner on stderr.
- Solution: classify the nine guards through the existing `throwExpectedCliError` owner, retaining their exact messages.
- Production: +10/-9. Tests: +46/-47, net -1; existing cases folded without dropping a distinct boundary.
- Unchanged: guard ordering, restore/extraction behavior, text output, exit codes, JSON stdout, internal runtime-error classification and dependencies.

## Evidence

[Repeated before/after CLI receipts and focused checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199869#issuecomment-6905105789), baseline `a237e95ceb3f`, candidate `69e5e72fa8a7`:

- One real config-only archive, seven refusal conditions, twice per side in both text and JSON modes. All 28 refusals per side exited 1. Candidate JSON stderr reports the existing diagnostic; text streams and JSON stdout remain byte-identical.
- Normal restore succeeds identically; complete reports and every restored-file hash match. Refused targets remain untouched.
- 66 focused tests pass; the same assertions on baseline produce eight expected-error classification failures and 58 passes. Matching test typecheck leaf and targeted formatting pass.
- Full declaration build and clean packed-install CLI smoke pass. Source, tests and packaging ran on the host through ocx; the diff touches no install/lifecycle-sensitive paths.
- File/non-empty errors pass unchanged through the existing non-ENOENT catch. Env diagnostics expose variable names, never values. Capacity and agent-directory containment are regression-test boundaries, not fault-injected CLI claims.

Merge danger: reversible error-classification/test change. Blast radius: JSON stderr presentation of existing backup-restore refusals; no stored-data or public-contract change.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

## Evidence

<!-- forone-current-submission:start -->
### Current main integration — 2026-11-16 UTC

Current head: `489d827617ffc13fda8341d778e1b991ae4fe8c8`; pinned official main: `7d90a907c0ded71be3f9f89cb3ba799dcca7aceb`. The normal merge had one generated config-baseline conflict, regenerated by its canonical owner. The explicit default-off OpenAI native PDF implementation and tests are unchanged.

Focused current-head proof passed 50 config, prepared-runtime, authority, PDF tool, and OpenAI transport assertions. Config docs and staged diff checks pass. No paid provider request or maintainer workflow approval was performed.
<!-- forone-current-submission:end -->

Earlier validated head: `95d83ad28f203ee6ec15ad60f69c06060a7235a5`. Exact-head [CI39994486818](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39994486818) **passed**: 75 jobs (47 success, 28 skipped), no failures or pending jobs.

- **160 distinct relevant tests passed cumulatively**: 128 PDF/provider/sibling/config tests, 26 official subagent-fixture tests and 6 new authority controls. The final-effect follow-up's affected suite is 48/48 (6 authority, 13 opt-in, 29 existing PDF), a subset of that total. Full/runtime builds, affected production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, SDK exports, schema/docs and formal extension/core graph boundaries pass. Independent full-candidate, credential-handoff and final-effect reviews found no actionable P0/P1 defect.
- **Authority red/green:** before the fence, each of four retired-owner cases sent one synthetic HTTP request. After it, operator and physical-credential retirement after provider or DNS awaits each require reached-injection, the correct owner failure, HTTP0 and no completion fallback. Allowed and nearest-forbidden controls also pass. Provider cases use the real bundled callback; DNS cases use the real guarded-fetch lookup seam. These are authority-owner tests, not live credential rotation.
- **Published stable 2026.10.6 saved-config upgrade:** verified official artifact integrity, authored ordered settings with the published CLI, then validated and edited the same isolated saved state with the built candidate CLI. Ordering and limits are preserved, absent remains absent and explicit false remains false. This is configuration compatibility proof.
- **Earlier real OpenAI API proof:** the actual PDF tool/prepared provider/extractor, using synthetic documents only, returned HTTP200 and expected results for native input and four extraction cases (unset, selected page, password/encrypted, configured text-only). An initial HTTP401 exposed the scoped sentinel-handoff error; the corrected native request returned HTTP200, native=true and expected values. Its successful result was reconciled without replay after a harness-only model-label assertion correction. This proof is bound to preceding implementation head `ac5c3699`; the relevant native transport/payload owners remain unchanged. It is separate from the real Gateway proof below.

### Real isolated Gateway, normal agent route

The built official CLI and GatewayClient used real pinned WSS admission, `health` RPC, one durable synthetic profile, normal `agent`/same-run `agent.wait`, `deliver: false`, and actual `users.setRole` plus effective-role readback. The planner model remained allowed while the nearest negative excluded only the PDF model. PDF model/fallback selection was fixed explicitly.

The Gateway ran the actual run-owned PDF tool. Its planner/PDF HTTP used a synthetic loopback sink through the existing runtime-dependency seam, retaining real DNS/Agent/pinned dispatcher and the final synchronous HTTP authority check. Body/auth inspection was in memory only.

| Condition | Planner HTTP | Native PDF HTTP | Extraction PDF HTTP | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Allowed | 2 | 1 | 0 | Expected actual PDF tool result; pinned dispatcher observed |
| Same-profile/scopes, PDF model denied | 2 | 0 | 0 | Actual model refusal while planner remained usable |
| Role retired while PDF input held | 1 | 0 | 0 | Official owner change; original run ended/error and active root work returned 1 → 0 after release before HTTP0 was recorded |
| `pages: "2"` | 2 | 0 | 1 | Selected-page BETA present; excluded-page ALPHA absent |

All four submissions occurred once, and the original runs reached terminal state with backend work settled. The held-input Gateway retirement proves actual operator wiring; precise provider/DNS timing is covered separately by the focused red/green tests above.

The seven planner requests and seven other intercepted requests are counted separately. The latter remain unclassified and are not treated as PDF/fallback proof; there is no all-process external-egress claim. Gateway runtime build `4b0f4c12` was exercised from test-only source head `7c7816f3`, with explicit runtime-owner bindings to this head. The build is not relabeled as a build of the later merge commit. No production service, employee role, customer document or real channel delivery was used. All task-owned Gateway/driver processes and temporary credential/config/profile/TLS/log state, including failed attempts, have been removed.

## CI and Review Follow-through

Earlier CI found the generated config baseline and an inherited subagent fixture problem. Later official main changed that fixture's completion contract, so the borrowed adjustment was retired in favor of the exact official fixture files and its negative assertion. An authority test's private-extension import was also replaced with the existing public bundled-provider facade; both formal boundaries pass. These repairs add no PDF production behavior.

Previous implementation CI [39968310938](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39968310938) and authority CI [39986691358](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39986691358) passed at their respective heads. A final true conflict against official main `53fb615a` was limited to the generated configuration hash. This branch normally merges that fixed main and resolves the hash with the official generator. Independent blob review preserves the feature/authority/Gateway owners; the only tracked help-file change comes from official main. Current-head CI is reported above separately from preceding evidence.

The items in [the prior/current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-5377643651) are covered by explicit consent, bounded fallback, actual conflict repair, a concrete opt-in proposal, published-stable compatibility, the final-effect authority fence and actual Gateway evidence. [The later evidence reminder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-6051721637) is addressed by this refreshed evidence and description. The remaining adoption, setting-placement and merge decisions belong to maintainers.


<!-- evidence-gate-refresh:2026-10-24 -->

### 2026-10-24 current-main integration

- Merged upstream `main` at `05bc4bf5c9fc717841df38d169bb69fa3d88a52a` normally into candidate `f43a6edbca54b5e3ac6d288f0a9e79e919d6e427`; no force push. The only merge conflict was the generated config-baseline hash, regenerated from the merged schemas.
- Revalidated 40 focused PDF/config/authority tests, config-doc and Plugin SDK export/API contracts, core/extension/extension-test typechecks, touched-file type-aware lint and formatting, the full build (157 SDK subpaths), and a fresh P0/P1 autoreview with no actionable finding.
- The prior real OpenAI/Gateway evidence remains applicable because the provider transport and final-effect authority owners are unchanged by the main integration; the changed generated baseline was regenerated and checked at the new head.
