prs.title: feat(skills): add bundled create-blobster skill and CLI renderer
prs.body:
Closes #199162

## What Problem This Solves

Agent authors and Template creators working in chat, CLI sessions, or offline template repositories have no bundled skill guidance or offline CLI renderer to validate and render deterministic Blobster `.svg` and `256×256` `.png` avatars without going through a second Gateway LLM call.

## User Impact

User impact: Agents and developers can now design Blobster avatars directly in context using the bundled `create-blobster` skill and render validated `.svg` or `256×256` RGBA `.png` files offline via `openclaw agents render-blobster <design> --out <path> [--json]`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Extracted `renderBlobsterSvgFromDesignText(text)` and `MAX_BLOBSTER_DESIGN_CHARS` in `src/agents/blobster-generation.ts` so Gateway avatar generation (`generateBlobsterForAgent`) and CLI rendering share one parser, closed schema validator, and SVG renderer without altering `AgentsAvatarGenerateResultSchema`.
- Generalized `readBoundedCliTextInput` in `src/commands/agent-message-input.ts` and added `src/commands/agents.commands.blobster.ts` + `openclaw agents render-blobster` (`src/cli/program/register.agent.ts`, `src/cli/command-catalog.ts`) supporting file or `-` stdin inputs and `.svg` / `.png` (`@resvg/resvg-js` with `font: { loadSystemFonts: false }`) outputs with `configGuard: "skip"`, `loadPlugins: "never"`, and `networkProxy: "bypass"`.
- Added bundled skill `skills/create-blobster/` (`SKILL.md`, `references/design-guide.md`, `scripts/cli.mjs` registered in `config/knip.config.ts`) and CLI documentation in `docs/cli/agents.md`. Maintainer alignment: discussed with `@Patrick-Erichsen` in Discord (`OpenClaw`), who confirmed landing this offline renderer + custom-accessory authoring workflow now ahead of upcoming Blobster updates.
- Opportunistic Pathfinder fix: converted the child `--import` path in `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-avatar.test.ts` to `new URL("../../../scripts/tsx.mjs", import.meta.url).href` so the subprocess test passes on Windows Node 24 ESM (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` on raw drive-letter paths).
- Addressed ClawSweeper review feedback (`2d2f30a5cbfb`):
  - Cited originating issue and renderer/review provenance (`#199162`, `#173762`, `#181917`, `#198229`, `#196427`) beside the rules in `skills/create-blobster/SKILL.md` and removed duplicated coordinate/primitive prose in favor of `references/design-guide.md`.
  - Removed the self-comparing fixture loop in `src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts` in favor of one independent canonical SVG + `--json` output check alongside stdin -> `256×256` RGBA PNG rasterization and invalid-input rejection coverage.
  - Added `"agents render-blobster"` and `expect(loaded.modules).not.toContain("agents-blobster-command")` in `src/cli/help-cold-imports.test.ts` so cold `--help` actively detects eager action imports.

## Evidence

### 1. Offline CLI Bridge Execution (No Gateway, No Model Config, Empty `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`)

Executed the shipped `skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs` bridge in an isolated empty `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` with provider API keys and Gateway env vars unset:

```text
$ # Isolated empty state directory (0 entries before and 0 entries after)
$ ls -A "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR" | wc -l
0

$ node skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster harbor-navigator.json --out avatars/harbor-navigator.svg --json
{
  "id": "harbor-navigator",
  "name": "Harbor Navigator",
  "description": "A crimson Blobster in a navy peacoat and captain's visor holding a brass spyglass.",
  "out": "<work-dir>/avatars/harbor-navigator.svg",
  "format": "svg",
  "bytes": 3422
}
# exit=0

$ cat harbor-navigator.json | node skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster - --out avatars/harbor-navigator.png
Name: Harbor Navigator
Output: <work-dir>/avatars/harbor-navigator.png
Bytes: 10631
# exit=0
# PNG header check: {"pngMagicHex":"89504e470d0a1a0a","chunk":"IHDR","width":256,"height":256,"bitDepth":8,"colorType":6,"bytes":10631}

$ node skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster bad-script.json --out avatars/rejected.svg
Invalid Blobster design: Unsupported SVG element
# exit=1, avatars/rejected.svg exists=false

$ ls -A "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR" | wc -l
0
```

Rendered `256×256` RGBA `.png` artifacts produced offline via `scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster`:

| `harbor-navigator.png` (offline CLI proof above) | `radar-watch` / custom accessory preview |
| --- | --- |
| ![Harbor Navigator Blobster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50a78906-4eb5-4028-bebd-fe648a1e07f6) | ![Rendered Blobster avatar preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71af2b54-ea17-4606-a7af-857c66400b44) |

### 2. Real Multimodal Agent Session Completing `skills/create-blobster`

Ran a live multimodal `gpt-5.6-luna` agent session in an isolated workspace containing `IDENTITY.md` (`Name: Beacon`, `Theme: coastal lighthouse keeper who watches night storms`, `Avatar: avatars/default.svg`) with the built `skills/create-blobster` directory staged. The agent read `SKILL.md` + `references/design-guide.md`, authored `candidate/storm-lantern.json`, repaired a JSON syntax slip after validating through `scripts/cli.mjs` rather than hand-writing `<svg>`, rendered both `.svg` and `.png`, visually inspected the `256×256` PNG, and left `IDENTITY.md` untouched because only a preview was requested:

```text
[exec exit=0] sed -n '1,240p' <openclaw>/skills/create-blobster/SKILL.md
[exec exit=0] sed -n '1,260p' <openclaw>/skills/create-blobster/references/design-guide.md
[exec exit=0] sed -n '1,160p' IDENTITY.md && mkdir -p candidate
  -> Name: Beacon | Emoji: 🏮 | Theme: coastal lighthouse keeper who watches night storms | Avatar: avatars/default.svg
[file_change] add <workspace>/candidate/storm-lantern.json
[exec exit=1] node <openclaw>/skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster candidate/storm-lantern.json --out candidate/storm-lantern.svg --json
  -> caught malformed JSON escape; revised candidate/storm-lantern.json without writing raw <svg>
[exec exit=0] node <openclaw>/skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster candidate/storm-lantern.json --out candidate/storm-lantern.svg --json
  -> {"id":"storm-lantern-keeper","name":"Storm Lantern Keeper",...} (3628 bytes)
[exec exit=0] node <openclaw>/skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster candidate/storm-lantern.json --out candidate/storm-lantern.png --json
  -> {"id":"storm-lantern-keeper","name":"Storm Lantern Keeper",...} (11180 bytes)
[reply] The PNG preview is visually clean: the eyes are unobstructed, the yellow coat strongly separates from the red shell, and the lantern reads as a single held prop without clipping. `IDENTITY.md` was not modified.
```

Rendered `candidate/storm-lantern.png` (`256×256` RGBA, `11,180` bytes) produced and visually inspected by the live agent session:

![Storm Lantern Keeper Blobster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/489f3bfe-ab47-4330-aa7c-73536b7081e3)

### 3. Validation & Local Review

- **LOC split (`cd61ce32dd28..2d2f30a5cbfb`):** Production `+198/-44` (`+154` net across `src/agents/blobster-generation.ts`, `src/commands/agent-message-input.ts`, `src/commands/agents.commands.blobster.ts`, `src/cli/program/register.agent.ts`, `src/cli/command-catalog.ts`, `skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs`, `config/knip.config.ts`) | Tests `+199/-3` (`+196` net across 4 test files; reduced `-5` net lines in `2d2f30a5cbfb`) | Docs & skill markdown `+101/-0`.
- **Focused Vitest suites (`--maxWorkers=1` on Windows Node 24; CI seconds pending hosted run):**
  - `src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts`: 8 passed (`86ms` test body; `83.2s` cold transform/shard wall time on Windows)
  - `src/cli/help-cold-imports.test.ts`: 11 passed (`23.7s` wall time)
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-avatar.test.ts`: 12 passed (`11.9s` wall time)
  - `src/skills/loading/workspace-skill-snapshot.test.ts -t Blobster`: 1 passed (`25.4s` wall time)
  - `src/agents/blobster-generation.test.ts`: 34 passed (`17.8s` wall time)
- **Checks & build:**
  - `python skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py skills/create-blobster` -> `Skill is valid!`
  - `pnpm build`, `pnpm docs:list`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `git diff --check`, `check-database-worker-ratchet.mts --base cd61ce32dd28`, and `check-changed.mjs` typecheck/lint/mock-export/import-cycle lanes passed cleanly on our touched surface.
- **Local review (`autoreview`):** Ran `autoreview` (`codex` engine, `thinking=high`, branch range `cd61ce32dd28..2d2f30a5cbfb`, default `P0` blocking threshold) -> `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported` (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.98`, 0 remaining findings).

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

## Evidence

Earlier validated author head: `02db206611aaf040ab37ea819889b8264483914b`. It normally merges CI-green head `1c771bb8` with official main `0372963434f6a0b79394dbe330abde2ae34f2a89` to resolve one new generated Discord-delta conflict that arose while the prior CI was running.

- This work performs no employee/runtime update, private Core distribution, permission workaround or freshness-only merge. Only actual conflicts blocking this PR's validation are integrated. The maintainer disclosure/implementation-owner decision below is unchanged.

### Prior validation (historical)

The only failed leaf is [UI cold-load case 118626035515](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39421952171/job/118626035515), plus its dependent aggregate. Only fixed proof fields and the test result are retained; no credential, endpoint, IP address, configuration dump, or conversation text is included. prs.title: fix(plugins): keep Gateway responsive during initial plugin loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway stalls when dependency-heavy plugins are initially loaded: executable binding calls back into the preparation worker synchronously while the plugin loader is running.

## User Impact

Initial plugin loading keeps the foreground event loop moving while preserving plugin execution, retained-source ownership, and recovery. No configuration or public SDK change is required. This removes the measured synchronous worker-wait path; it is not a universal startup-latency guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker retains source custody and plain inspection facts. The existing capture owner reconstructs local executable bindings, replaying ordered acquisitions without repeating covered source inspection or retaining a host Jiti compiler. Initial file reconstruction and receipt validation yield cooperatively; synchronous CLI and lazy callbacks drain the same steps synchronously. Frozen recovery, native admission, and worker-exit cleanup remain attached to their existing owners. Obsolete remote source-mapping callbacks are removed.

Related: #176192. Thanks to @ExoHumann (Krzysztof Kisiel) for the original cooperative-capture/local-binding design and investigation. This is a separately implemented, initial-binding-only repair against current source, not a copy of that contributor branch.

Scope excludes the separate failed-reload transaction repair in #198262, broader startup optimization, and the original PR's Windows installed-package claims. The unused asynchronous recovery API and test-only callers were removed; existing synchronous recovery remains. The complete #198262 patch was not composed or retested here. No merge is requested.

## Evidence

### November 15 conflict reconciliation

Merged main `a4cc2adb5d1a746296803f73955e089df98a68df` into the existing PR lineage. Tested local commit: `864eecaa97934addc51268b18e8958f3310a16ae`; tree: `266a9295626f4a05ed61cd49c99e4057eb322ef8`. ### Historical repair evidence

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The historical [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. That earlier integration retained11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; that earlier head's CI supported its integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents in groups need to recognize invitations and useful opportunities without replying to every message when mention gating is disabled.

## User Impact

With Decision assistance enabled and an effective Decision Model, eligible unmentioned group messages receive a pre-generation participation assessment. An invitation or useful opportunity takes the ordinary agent reply path, including its normal permissions, tools, streaming, and delivery. A negative assessment records the message without starting a primary agent run. Explicit mentions, commands, ambient room events, and generic CLI backends retain their existing paths. Unavailable assessments and unassessable media fall back to ordinary replies.

The existing default-off Labs flag opts into current and future Decision Model consumers, including on upgrades with an already-saved enabled preference. No separate participation setting is added. Hosted evaluations receive bounded conversation evidence and may incur provider charges. Opt-out invalidates pending participation judgments; ordinary cancellation and current-turn authority continue to govern execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deciding before generation avoids unnecessary agent runs and keeps sent-message history accurate. There is no private draft generation, post-generation review, revision loop, or special publication queue. Accepted-input and configuration changes invalidate stale preflight decisions before generation.

## Evidence

Updated November 1, 2026. Evidence is scoped to the tested inputs; this is not a merge-ready claim.

- **Earlier published tree:** head `60becc8feacd3aa5d4d7eb149470e25d8cce97b6` has tree `214f54dc7f68c057f47bd66bee5a6a26a6db541c`. Isolated validation of that tree passed **149 tests across nine files**, full `pnpm build`, configuration-doc generation, and generated-file drift checking. The overall run failed `check:changed` on a stale max-lines baseline entry; it was not an all-green run.
- **Saved configuration:** the built CLI accepted fixtures with Decision assistance absent, false, and true, with no warnings and identical before/after configuration SHA-256 values. This proves parsing and byte preservation, **not** runtime rollout, fresh installation, or version-upgrade behavior.
- **Actual-provider rubric smoke:** four bounded TypeSafe calls using synthetic conversations returned the expected invitation, opportunity, chatter, and resolved-conversation categories (`jev-1.13.0`). These used the installed evaluation tool, not the candidate's exact provider adapter or Telegram path; they are a small semantic smoke set, not a reliability guarantee.
- **Telegram prerequisite:** the canonical Test Server doctor now exits 0 with Convex credentials, isolated TDLib state, authorized Test Server user, and verified SUT bot. This was a DM authentication/readiness check, **not** selective group-participation proof. Actual candidate group scenarios remain pending.
- **October 23 rebase:** head `73edfa2d43da3f86d5f27621b2497843c4a31d29` integrates main `c6facd08e4b5aa14c4424a716f097388537f52ae` using Git’s merge-preserving rebase. All 15 original logical PR commits are retained. The preceding 14 commit IDs are unchanged; only the final integration commit was recreated, preserving its original author, author date, and message. Its complete tree is `d4fe891304f55ec637b23d1bf573c406add897d9`, identical to the previously validated candidate. That unchanged tree passed the full build, core/extension typechecks, affected messaging/plugin test typechecks, focused participation/Decision/transcript/queued-turn suites, all 230 reply entry-point tests, and all 8 prompt-prefix stability tests. Targeted lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/mock-export ratchets, configuration-doc generation checks, and documentation links passed. The prior static review reported no actionable P0–P2 finding; it did not execute project code. Validation and review are reused based on exact complete-tree equality. Exact-head GitHub CI remains pending.

- **November 1 rebase (published):** head `38c5e6ff1261f22b2938bcb976e97b8369e84131` integrates main `d43ab9c516e6dd1effeee8cb50ea479be550232e`, with complete tree `af053b6ad4df37c0d560ac1a9f98095915a9ffe5`. The preceding 14 PR commits are unchanged; the recreated integration commit preserves its author, author date, and message. Conflicts now use current-main reply input admission and Decision type owners. On supported Node 24.16.0, core and affected messaging/plugin-test typechecks, targeted lint/formatting, and documentation links passed. Focused participation, Decision consent/admission/V2, plugin-hook, followup execution/admission/delivery, transcript guard, and prompt-prefix tests passed. Local autoreview of the complete candidate against the pinned main at P0–P2 found one mixed-queue participation defect; it was fixed with a regression test that failed on the reviewed candidate and passes with the fix. Still required: full changed-file CI checks; runtime saved-config and persisted-session upgrade proof; actual candidate real-Decision-provider Telegram group send/silence cases; exact-head CI verification. prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `webhooks gmail setup --json` shows a generic Doctor hint on stderr for blank accounts, invalid Tailscale modes and malformed numeric flags, even though the command already knows the specific correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the established expected-error path for the existing local argument messages. Synchronous account/common-option preparation now runs before the setup catch, so those checks reach the root expected-error renderer. No broad expected-error pass-through remains around `runGmailSetup`.

This boundary matters for credentials: dependency discovery, config access, subprocesses and Google/Tailscale setup remain inside the existing redacting catch. Every setup failure still passes through `formatErrorMessage`, even if a downstream error happens to have an expected-error name. The local guards use fixed messages and fixed numeric labels, never the rejected input, hook token or push token.

No new operator-facing text, flags, defaults, JSON envelope fields or exit codes. Text-mode output remains unchanged.

## Evidence

Credential-free source CLI proof covers blank account, invalid Tailscale mode, and malformed port/max-bytes/renew-minutes twice on main and twice on the candidate, in both JSON and text modes. JSON stderr changes from the generic failure/Doctor hint to the existing remedy. JSON stdout bytes, text stderr bytes, empty text stdout and exit 1 are unchanged after normalizing isolated profile names.

Focused tests exercise all local guards before setup and retain downstream credential-error redaction, including an expected-named downstream error. The CLI test typecheck leaf, scoped lint and formatting pass. Full build/packed-entry receipts and exact-head hosted gates are recorded in the proof comments.

Production +9/-8; tests +29/-29 (net 0), no allocation file. Existing tables cover disabled Tailscale and argument variants; duplicate test scaffolding was removed. The original human commit by Leon-SK668 is retained.

Two-way door: a revert restores the generic JSON stderr behavior without changing stored state. Blast radius: argument-error reporting for Gmail webhook CLI commands; successful setup and credential error redaction retain their existing owners.

`openclaw qr --json` prints a generic failure and Doctor hint on stderr instead of the existing remedy when auth overrides conflict, access-profile flags conflict, `--remote` has no configured remote URL, or the pairing resolver refuses the configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing expected-CLI-error owner at the four refusal sites. The messages are unchanged. Pairing resolution, authentication, access grants and setup-code generation are untouched.

## User Impact

JSON callers get the same stdout error envelope and exit code, plus the same useful stderr message text-mode callers already receive. Text-mode diagnostics and successful setup output retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Base: `2c4413a6abbfeb4ac23cd07b775a105586548af1`. Final candidate: `08adaa7f51fe4cf44aceced270a71c5e533b40d8` (production unchanged from paired-proof head `160ae20444bdb47b5077c95b74e14e2ca73cac94`).

- Host source tier through ocx, with isolated HOME/config/state, synthetic credentials and no Gateway: all four required refusals were run with --json and in text mode. Base JSON stderr has the generic failure/Doctor hint; candidate has the existing remedy. JSON stdout bytes, text-mode output and exit code 1 compare identically.
- Redaction condition cleared: validateMobilePairingUrl never interpolates URL credentials/userinfo. Its errors are static or include only fixed source labels. All label producers were checked against the exact PR blobs. A synthetic userinfo URL also produces only a static refusal, without either sentinel in output.
- Real successful controls pass in --json and --setup-code-only modes with exit 0. Only hashes are retained. Fresh bootstrap credentials and expiry necessarily make raw setup-code hashes differ; payload-contract and metadata-envelope hashes match after excluding those two fresh fields. No setup code or credential value appears in receipts.
- Vitest-source: qr-cli.test.ts is 5 forwarding failures / 15 passes on base and 20 passes on candidate. Existing distinct guard/resolver assertions remain; the duplicate new JSON fixture matrix was removed in favor of real root-CLI proof.
- Built-process consumer suite: all 43 cases in test/cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts pass against fresh candidate artifacts, including both qr/clawbot qr spellings and both conflicting option pairs. Its obsolete stderr expectations now require the remedy and reject the generic banner; JSON and exit-status assertions are unchanged.
- Targeted lint (zero warnings/errors), matching config-cli and root-other test typecheck leaves, and formatting pass. Production +5/-4; tests +15/-17, net -2; no allocation file.

Leon-SK668's original human commit is preserved. Both maintenance commits change tests only. No new error wording, config, permission, protocol, dependency or stored-data format is introduced.

Full tier passes on production-identical head `160ae20444bdb47b5077c95b74e14e2ca73cac94`: `ocx build --dts`, supported self-contained package/tarball integrity, packed version entry and packed QR JSON refusal smoke. The final commit changes only consumer assertions, so this full proof is reused. External dependencies came from the ocx-installed checkout; bundled workspace dependencies came from the tarball. The packed refusal emits the same JSON error envelope and existing remedy without generating setup output.

[Paired redaction, renderer, hash-control and test receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199650#issuecomment-6898076491).

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: a revert restores the old generic stderr behavior without migrating state. Blast radius is QR refusal diagnostics; successful pairing/authentication and setup-code output are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(cli): cancel interrupted approvals reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw approvals pending` does not respond to Ctrl-C. All three pending-approval list reads are issued through `callGatewayFromCli` without an abort signal, so a held or slow Gateway keeps the CLI waiting for the full RPC timeout. The same applies to `approvals get`, `approvals grants list`, and the `approval.get` lookup that `approvals resolve` performs before it decides anything.

This is the same defect class that #197315 and its follow-ups fixed for the other CLI reads: a read already dispatched to the Gateway is not cancellable, so the operator waits out the transport timeout instead of exiting.

Measured against a Gateway peer that holds the read:

```
approvals pending  (before)  exited in 11590ms  code=130
approvals pending  (after)   exited in   668ms  code=130
cron get abc123    (control) exited in   726ms  code=130
```

The control is an already-converted read, which confirms the measurement itself is sound: the fixed path exits in under a second, the unfixed path takes the full timeout.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C (or SIGTERM) now stops a pending `get`, `pending`, or `grants list` read, and the CLI exits 130/143 immediately instead of after the transport timeout. Before the fix the CLI also printed a misleading diagnostic on the way out — `OpenClaw took too long to respond.` / `Your request may have completed. Check its result before trying again.` — for a read the operator had just cancelled. That document no longer appears.

Mutations are deliberately unchanged: `resolve`, `set`, `revoke`, allowlist edits, and `exec.approvals.node.set` still go through `callGatewayFromCli` with no signal, so an already-sent write still waits for its receipt during cleanup and reports any failure. Interrupting does not undo a write.

No config, default, protocol, schema, dependency, persistence, auth, or permission change. Validation order, RPC payloads, output shapes, and exit codes for uncancelled runs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing owner for this behaviour is `getAsyncWorkSignal()` plus the root cleanup path, already used by the cron, hooks, id, skills, nodes, and sessions CLI reads. This change reuses it instead of adding a new cancellation mechanism:

- `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.shared.ts` gains `callApprovalsReadFromCli`, the read counterpart of the mutations that stay on `callGatewayFromCli`. It forwards the ambient signal only when one exists, so exported/programmatic callers keep their current behaviour.
- `runApprovalsAction` now treats an aborted read as the outcome rather than a failure. Without this the abort surfaces as a spurious error document on a read the operator cancelled.
- `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts` routes the five read sites through the new owner: `exec.approvals.get` / `exec.approvals.node.get` (`loadSnapshot`), the three `*.approval.list` calls (`loadPendingApprovals`), `config.get` (`loadConfigForApprovalsTarget`), `exec.approval.grants.list`, and `approval.get`.

Three files, production +26/-5, tests +16, docs +4.

## Evidence

**Red → green, unit contract.** The new table test asserts the CLI hands its ambient abort signal to every read call. With the pending-list site reverted to `callGatewayFromCli` it fails on that command; with the fix it passes. `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.pending-resolve.test.ts`: 17 passed.

**Red → green, real CLI against a Gateway peer.** A minimal WebSocket Gateway peer answers `connect` and holds `exec.approval.list`, `plugin.approval.list`, and `openclaw.approval.list`. The shipped CLI is started with a remote Gateway config pointing at it, waits until the peer logs the held requests, then receives SIGINT and the exit is timed:

```
before (main ab5a6d417f7)
  +19915ms HOLD exec.approval.list (no response until the client aborts)
  +29902ms client closed socket            <- ~10s after SIGINT
  RESULT: exited in 11590ms code=130
  stderr: "OpenClaw took too long to respond."

after (this branch)
  +20546ms HOLD exec.approval.list (no response until the client aborts)
  +20773ms client closed socket            <- immediately after SIGINT
  RESULT: exited in 668ms code=130
  stderr: no failure document

control (cron get abc123, an already-converted read)
  RESULT: exited in 726ms code=130
```

**Consumers.** The existing `exec-approvals-cli` suites (`pending-resolve`, `utf8`, and the process-level test) cover the resolve/set/allowlist paths that this change does not touch; their call-argument assertions read positions `[0]` and `[2]` only, and the signal travels in position `[3]`, so no existing expectation changes.

Not tested: a live Gateway with real pending approvals, node-targeted `get`, Windows/macOS, or the full repository suite. The proof covers the local read cancellation contract only.

## Merge Danger

Low. The change is additive at the read sites and leaves every mutation on its existing uncancelled path. The one deliberate visible change is that a cancelled read no longer prints the transport-timeout diagnostic, which is the point of the fix.

The signal is only forwarded when an ambient work scope exists, so callers that invoke these commands programmatically without one — including the plugin host and tests — keep the exact previous behaviour.

prs.title: fix(cli): avoid slow help with empty plugin config
prs.body:
Closes #114067

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw --help` loads the full config/runtime graph for a standalone `{"plugins":{}}` config even though it prints the same cached help as an absent config.

## User Impact

Root and `nodes` help can use the existing fast path with that empty plugin configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher admits only the strict-JSON standalone empty block. Meaningful plugin settings, dynamic config and dotenv side effects continue through the config owner. This removes unnecessary entry/config loading without adding a cache or another plugin policy. The existing startup benchmark now includes the reported workload and an explicitly selected disabled-plugins control.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: identical help output and zero runtime imports for the inert config, at least 20% lower median startup time, and no control median/p95/RSS regression above 20%. Five serial interleaved base/candidate rounds used the same official `cliStartup` build on Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1; one-minute host load ranged 8.09–8.76. Each sample used a fresh process and isolated state; source-launcher compile caching stays disabled by repository policy.

Workload: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-cli-startup.ts --case help --case helpInertPlugins --case helpDisabledPlugins --runs 1 --warmup 0 --timeout-ms 30000 --json`, repeated in A/B order.

| Config | Exit median, base → fix | Exit p95, base → fix | Range, base → fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Absent | 97.4 → 96.5 ms | 103.3 → 99.7 ms | 96.2–103.3 → 95.5–99.7 ms |
| Empty plugins | 2101.4 → 95.0 ms | 2271.6 → 124.0 ms | 2084.5–2271.6 → 89.0–124.0 ms |
| Plugins disabled | 2919.1 → 3052.6 ms | 3095.2 → 3127.3 ms | 2857.1–3095.2 → 2860.6–3127.3 ms |

Empty-config first-output median/p95 fell from 2037.1/2176.2 to 88.3/116.8 ms; median peak RSS fell from 193.2 to 53.8 MiB. The disabled-plugin control's median duration increased 4.6%; both controls satisfy the acceptance rule.

Official `pnpm --silent openclaw --help` checks (pinned Bun fork) separately confirmed 870 → 0 runtime dist modules and 1 → 0 entry loads for the inert config. Its 8,007-byte stdout matches absent-config help exactly. Disabled plugins retains 944 runtime modules and its distinct, unchanged 7,802-byte output. All six base/candidate invocations exit 0. CPU profiles also show runtime module work disappearing.

- Both launcher regressions fail on the base. Candidate launcher suite: 107 pass, one platform skip; startup harness: 15 pass.
- Official startup build, targeted strict types, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Final response contracts and budget comparison against the same-machine base report pass.
- The checked-in x64 fixture gate reports no-config help latency above its historical baseline on both versions: base 96.2 ms and fix 103.7 ms versus fixture 53.1 ms. The gate remains unchanged; the five-round base/fix comparison above records the actual change.
- Independent P0–P3 review of the complete three-file change against `89ee0bd382d16` (local diff `5317025c00bf`): no findings.

### Latest-stable retained-config upgrade check

On Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1 and npm 11.19.1, installed `openclaw@2026.11.3` (the current npm/GitHub stable release) in an isolated npm prefix with `--allow-scripts=openclaw`. Ran installed root and `nodes` help, then replaced that temporary installation with the reviewed source checkout at `11072ba75bd7` using npm's local-source install. The candidate executes the reviewed launcher with the existing official `cliStartup` runtime (build metadata `89ee0bd`).

The same default `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, containing `{"plugins":{}}` plus a newline, stayed byte-identical through installation replacement and every invocation: 13 checks, 15 bytes, SHA-256 `512bc81cb9f83d93d1e3a6668087087468e3c199ed5122a9c7c035b3fef4f65d`. All 10 help/version invocations exited 0 with empty stderr.

| Installed CLI | Root help | `nodes` help | Empty config vs. absent config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Published stable `2026.11.3` | 7,897 bytes | 1,542 bytes | Both byte-identical |
| Candidate launcher `11072ba75bd7` | 8,007 bytes | 1,542 bytes | Both byte-identical |

Between the two installations, `nodes` help differs only in its build header; root help also differs in command inventory, wording and the support link. Each installation preserves its own help output with the retained empty-plugin config. The same-build base/fix comparison above separately verifies byte-identical output for this patch.

prs.title: fix(sessions): transcript facts backfill replays every covered session after a restart
prs.body:
Closes #199614

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after every Gateway restart on a large agent database, the transcript facts backfill re-walks every already covered session from the start, keeping the gateway busy for hours and timing out RPC while it runs.

## User Impact

User impact: restarts on large installs reach new backfill work in minutes instead of hours, and the gateway stays responsive while covered sessions are skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backfill cursor only lives in memory, so a restart rediscovers every session and replays covered ones through 512-row write batches with a 250 ms yield each. A new read-only probe checks coverage in bounded 8,192-row index windows outside the writer. Fully covered sessions are retired with one probe and a short yield that still scales with observed reply cost, so main-thread contention backs it off. Write batches start only at the first uncovered row and still recheck coverage inside their transaction, so a stale probe costs one visit, never a wrong fact. No schema change.

## Evidence

- New focused tests in `session-transcript-active-facts-backfill.test.ts`:
  - probe retires a covered session, stops right before the first uncovered row, and the write batch fills exactly the missing 15 rows
  - restarting over three covered sessions issues `discover` plus three `probe` commands and no write batches
- Existing resume test keeps its delay and single-open assertions.
- Production context: a 12k-session, ~10 GB agent database restarted the pass from session 0 after each restart; RPC timed out while it overlapped a backup `VACUUM INTO`.
- Local vitest was not run: this worktree is code-only and the shared install did not qualify. CI is the test gate.

prs.title: fix(a2a): inbound correlation test fails intermittently on unrelated PRs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the A2A test "correlates interleaved same-context replies from hermes/crew" in `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.test.ts` fails intermittently on PRs that do not touch A2A, and blocks them from landing.

Seen in CI shard `changed-extensions-config-32` (project `extension-database-workers`, job `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-31-1`):

| PR | Job | Failed case | Failed assertion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #198835 | 133002384788 | hermes, crew | line 181: got `[{text:'second reply'}]`, wanted `[{text:'first reply'}]`. Line 175: got `['a2a:crew','a2a:hermes']`, wanted `['a2a:hermes','a2a:crew']` |
| #198835, same job rerun | 133011401108 | crew | line 175 |
| #185851 | 133006876279 | hermes | line 181 |

Neither PR changes `extensions/a2a`.

## User Impact

User impact: none for people running OpenClaw. Contributors stop getting this red check on unrelated PRs. A2A reply correlation in production is unchanged, and the evidence below shows it was never wrong.

## Why This Change Was Made

The case starts two inbound runs with `Promise.all`, then treated `dispatch.mock.calls[0]` as the first run and `[1]` as the second. Nothing guarantees that order. Before a run calls `dispatch` it awaits a session-entry read in a worker (`createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync` calls `readSessionUpdatedAtInWorker`).

Until #198194 (67ecf6bf352, merged 2026-11-14) those reads used the "Session projection" lane, which had one worker, so they finished in the order they started. That commit folded the lane into "Session store", which gets two workers on any host with three or more cores. Two concurrent reads now run on separate threads and either one can finish first.

The case now finds each turn by the message it carries (`ctxPayload.MessageSid`) and asserts that `dispatch` ran exactly twice. The message id reaches the turn through `buildContext`, and the task id reaches it through the delivery closure, so matching on one does not presuppose the other. The rest of the case is untouched: the session-key comparison, the `From` values, replies delivered in reverse order, and the per-task artifact checks.

I left production alone. `docs/channels/a2a.md` promises that replies go to the task that started the turn, including when messages in one context finish out of order. It promises nothing about which of two concurrent requests dispatches first, and `channel.ts` starts each request as independent detached work with no queue.

One cleanup in the same file: the `dispatched` and `createA2aDispatchResult` helpers took a `queuedFinal` argument that every caller passed as `false`. I removed it. The helpers return the same values as before.

This PR is test-only on purpose. The failing check is the defect.

## Evidence

Head f18eecf2548 on base 7d90a907c0d. Local runs use the pinned Bun fork, the runtime the CI shard uses. Every loop runs `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/a2a/src/inbound.test.ts`.

**Red, unmodified main at e970cf66f7b**

- 30 runs in sequence: 12 failed. The hermes case failed in 7 and the crew case in 7.
- 30 runs, three at a time for CPU contention: 5 failed. Hermes 4, crew 1.
- The failures are the two CI assertions, at lines 175 and 181.

**Cause**

A temporary probe, not committed, repeated the two-run scenario in one process and recorded which run reached `dispatch` first.

- On e970cf66f7b the second run got there first in 192 of 400 rounds. Ingress resolution finished in start order in all 400, so the swap happens at the envelope read. With turns matched by message, every reply landed on its own task in all 400.
- `git bisect --first-parent` with that probe, from 9151ac22e00 (good) to b2f57063e73 (bad), 2,431 commits, ends at 67ecf6bf352. Its parent 7f7b16cdc24 swapped 0 of 80 rounds. The commit itself swapped 40 of 80.

So the hermes failure at line 181, where the first task received "second reply", comes from the mislabelled `firstTurn` and `secondTurn` variables. Both hermes runs share a session key and a `From` value, so line 175 cannot notice the swap. The test then hands "second reply" to the turn that owns the first task.

**Green, this change**

The loops ran on df0211ccf84, which is this commit on main at d2bb33537b4. Main then moved eight commits to 7d90a907c0d. None of them touch `extensions/a2a`, session storage, the worker runtime, the channel helpers or the Vitest config, so I rebased and ran the file once more instead of repeating the loops.

- 30 runs in sequence: 30 passed.
- 30 runs, three at a time: 30 passed.
- One run on f18eecf2548: 15 of 15 cases passed.
- `pnpm test extensions/a2a/src/inbound.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed, 42 s wall. Vitest reports 90% of that as transform and 1% as test time.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/a2a/src/inbound.test.ts` and `git diff --check`: clean.

prs.title: improve(talk): live transcription uses a saved Deepgram, ElevenLabs or Mistral API key
prs.body:
Closes #199684 ## What Problem This Solves Live transcription with Deepgram, ElevenLabs or Mistral reads its API key only from the Voice Call streaming config or the Gateway's environment. A key for the same provider that is already saved in OpenClaw, the one voice notes use, is not used there, so it has to be entered a second time. ## User Impact When Deepgram, ElevenLabs or Mistral is the named live transcription provider and has no key in the Voice Call streaming config or the environment, it uses the provider's saved API key. A key saved with `openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider deepgram` (or, for Mistral, in Settings → Models) is then enough. A provider is named by any of these: - `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.streaming.provider` (Talk and Voice Call) - a meeting plugin's `realtime.transcriptionProvider`, for example `plugins.entries.google-meet.config.realtime.transcriptionProvider` - the `provider` a client passes to `talk.session.create` Apart from the two changes listed below, every setup behaves as on `main`: - **Key order.** The Voice Call streaming config, then the environment (`DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`; `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` or `XI_API_KEY`; `MISTRAL_API_KEY`), then the saved key. When the config or the environment has a key, the saved key is not looked up. - **Automatic selection.** With no provider named, the Gateway and Voice Call pick the first ready candidate. A saved key of these three providers does not count there, so the same provider is picked as on `main`, and a provider that has only a saved key is never picked ahead of one that has a config or environment key. - **Preferred transcription model.** A Deepgram, ElevenLabs or Mistral model in `agents.defaults.voiceModel` is tried as a candidate, not as a named provider. With only a saved key it stays "not ready" there, as on `main`. - **OpenAI and xAI.** Untouched. Their live providers count a saved key in every case, as on `main`. What changes: 1. A named provider whose only key is a saved one goes from "not configured" to working, and `talk.catalog` lists it as configured. 2. With no key anywhere, code that creates a session for one of these providers gets "API key missing" when the session connects instead of when it is created, with the same message, because the saved key is looked up asynchronously. The Gateway does not get that far: as on `main`, it refuses the session with "not configured". The Talk relay, Voice Call and the meeting bot all check `isConfiguredAsync` first and handle a failed connect. Plugin SDK, additive only: - `RealtimeTranscriptionProviderConfiguredContext`, the argument of a live transcription provider's `isConfiguredAsync`, gains an optional boolean `selectedExplicitly`. - `resolveConfiguredCapabilityProviderAsync` and its deprecated synchronous twin pass `selectedExplicitly` to their `isProviderConfigured` callback. - The Gateway's Talk selection, Voice Call (through that helper) and the meeting bot set it when a provider is named. Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Mistral count their saved key only when it is true. A caller that leaves it out gets the same readiness as on `main`. Not in this PR: a place in the Control UI to enter a Deepgram or ElevenLabs key, any config option, any protocol change. The saved key is read from the default agent's store, as the OpenAI and xAI live providers do, so a key saved only for another agent is not used. ## Why This Change Was Made One saved key should serve both voice notes and live transcription. The OpenAI and xAI live transcription providers already fall back to the provider's saved API key (its auth profile). Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Mistral take the same lookup, after their existing key sources, and only for saved API keys (not token or OAuth profiles). The saved key counts only for a named provider, so it cannot change which provider automatic selection picks. A provider's readiness is a single boolean and its `autoSelectOrder` is fixed, so a provider cannot tell "I am the named provider" from "I am one of several candidates" unless the caller says so. `selectedExplicitly` is that statement, and it is opt-in: without it, readiness is what it is on `main`. ## Evidence ### Real behavior on a built Gateway An isolated Gateway built from `main` (the PR's merge base) and one built from this branch ran the same scenario script. The Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Mistral endpoints were replaced by local WebSocket stand-ins that log the credential they receive, and every key is made up. No real provider key or service was used. Settings → Talk, with Deepgram named in `streaming.provider` and only a saved Deepgram key: | `main` | This branch | | --- | --- | | ![Speech to text status on main: active provider deepgram, Not configured](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/81ba09722b1045f58f48c02b8119e2b96e5c97ed/images/2026/11/13d2a0f4-e26c-4f82-b8c6-bcc87410e553.png) | ![Speech to text status on this branch: active provider deepgram, Ready](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/81ba09722b1045f58f48c02b8119e2b96e5c97ed/images/2026/11/5516f27f-6a6a-4f87-835e-144fd1ce52c3.png) | What the Gateway did, with the same result for Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Mistral in the first four rows: | Setup | `main` | This branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Named, no key anywhere | Not configured, `talk.session.create` refused, no connection | The same | | Named, only a saved key (`openclaw models auth paste-api-key`) | Not configured, refused, no connection | Configured, session created, endpoint receives the saved key | | Named, a saved key and the provider's environment key | Not run (the unit tests below cover it) | Endpoint receives the environment key | | Named, a saved key, the environment key and a config key | Not run (the unit tests below cover it) | Endpoint receives the config key | | All three under `streaming.providers`, none named, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` set | ElevenLabs transcribes with the environment key | The same | | The same Gateway after a Deepgram key is saved | ElevenLabs transcribes with the environment key | The same, and Deepgram stays "not configured" |
Captured output of the scenario script on main (key lines) ```text Gateway built from: main at the PR merge base 8656c447df0 (its files, built in the PR worktree) deepgram named in streaming.provider, no key anywhere talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "deepgram" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) deepgram: the same Gateway after a key is saved talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "deepgram" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) elevenlabs named in streaming.provider, no key anywhere talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "elevenlabs" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) elevenlabs: the same Gateway after a key is saved talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "elevenlabs" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) mistral named in streaming.provider, no key anywhere talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "mistral" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) mistral: the same Gateway after a key is saved talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "mistral" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) Automatic selection: the three providers under streaming.providers, none named, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in the environment talk.session.create: {"provider":"elevenlabs","mode":"transcription"} stand-in elevenlabs endpoint received: elevenlabs-made-up-env-key Automatic selection: the same Gateway after a Deepgram key is saved (Deepgram ranks ahead of ElevenLabs) talk.session.create: {"provider":"elevenlabs","mode":"transcription"} stand-in elevenlabs endpoint received: elevenlabs-made-up-env-key ```
Captured output of the scenario script on this branch (key lines) ```text Gateway built from: this PR at cb29c520786 deepgram named in streaming.provider, no key anywhere talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "deepgram" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) deepgram: the same Gateway after a key is saved talk.session.create: plus ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in the Gateway's environment talk.session.create: {"provider":"elevenlabs","mode":"transcription"} stand-in elevenlabs endpoint received: elevenlabs-made-up-env-key elevenlabs named, a saved key, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and a key in the Voice Call streaming config talk.session.create: {"provider":"elevenlabs","mode":"transcription"} stand-in elevenlabs endpoint received: elevenlabs-made-up-config-key mistral named in streaming.provider, no key anywhere talk.session.create refused: Error: Realtime transcription provider "mistral" is not configured stand-in endpoint received: (no connection) mistral: the same Gateway after a key is saved talk.session.create: {"provider":"mistral","mode":"transcription"} stand-in mistral endpoint received: Bearer mistral-made-up-saved-key mistral named, a saved key plus MISTRAL_API_KEY in the Gateway's environment talk.session.create: {"provider":"mistral","mode":"transcription"} stand-in mistral endpoint received: Bearer mistral-made-up-env-key mistral named, a saved key, MISTRAL_API_KEY and a key in the Voice Call streaming config talk.session.create: {"provider":"mistral","mode":"transcription"} talk.session.create: {"provider":"elevenlabs","mode":"transcription"} stand-in elevenlabs endpoint received: elevenlabs-made-up-env-key Automatic selection: the same Gateway after a Deepgram key is saved (Deepgram ranks ahead of ElevenLabs) talk.session.create: {"provider":"elevenlabs","mode":"transcription"} stand-in elevenlabs endpoint received: elevenlabs-made-up-env-key ```
### Tests The focused tests (80 in 6 files), run against the production code on `main` and on this branch: | Case | `main` | This branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Named, only a saved key (each of the three providers) | Not configured | Connects with the saved key | | Not named, only a saved key (each provider) | Not configured | Not configured | | A config key and a saved key | Config key sent | Config key sent, saved key not looked up | | An environment key and a saved key | Environment key sent | Environment key sent, saved key not looked up | | No key | "API key missing" when the session is created | "API key missing" when the session connects | | A provider that is ready only when named, through Gateway Talk, Voice Call and the meeting bot | Refused when named | Used when named, not used otherwise | 9 of the 80 fail on `main`'s code and all 80 pass on this branch: the saved-key test and the no-key test of each provider (6), and the named case of each of the three selection owners (3). The other 71 pass on both, including the 7 key-precedence cases (ElevenLabs has two environment variables). The 80 are Deepgram 18, ElevenLabs 15, Mistral 18, Gateway Talk selection 1, meeting bot selection 1 and Voice Call webhook 27. 391 tests in 29 files that consume the changed code pass: the Talk catalog and session handlers, the transcription relay, the meeting bot, Voice Call media streaming, the SDK selection helper and its other caller, the capability catalog contract, plugin loading, and the three plugins' other tests. Typecheck (core, extensions, and the test projects that hold the changed tests), lint, formatting and the test-line budget (+189 lines of the 400 allowed) pass. The full suite was not run locally. Three existing tests assert the "no key" error at connect instead of at creation, following change 2 above: Deepgram's `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` validation case, ElevenLabs "rejects whitespace-only environment keys", and Mistral "requires an API key". prs.title: fix: find Windows listeners after empty PowerShell queries
prs.body:
Related: #195492

## What Problem This Solves

Windows restart checks can miss a listening process when PowerShell succeeds with empty output even though netstat can identify the listener.

## User Impact

The existing netstat fallback now runs after an empty PowerShell census. Populated PowerShell results retain their fast path, and netstat failures remain indeterminate. A genuinely empty port requires one additional bounded native command.

## Why This Change Was Made

A successful empty CIM query is not reliable evidence that no listener exists. This narrowly reuses the existing collector and parsing path, without weakening process-identity or cleanup checks.

This is a partial improvement for #195492: it does **not** solve the broader observed case where both native collectors omit an HTTP-reachable listener, nor the separate idle-CPU problem.

## Evidence

- New owner-boundary regression: original source **2 failed / 2 passed**; changed source **4 passed**.
- Focused Windows infra/daemon run: **66 passed / 34 skipped** across five files. The skipped consumer cases require POSIX CI.
- New regression plus AppContainer sibling: **11 passed** across two files.
- Formatting, supported core type-aware lint, affected infra test-program typecheck, mock-export guard, test-line ratchet, and diff check passed.
- Independent review found no likely/high-impact defects.
- Adds exactly 60 LF regression-test lines with a separate allocation record; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Initial lint configuration attempted unrelated plugin declaration preparation and timed out. The repository-supported boundary-free core lint configuration passed; no preparation checks were bypassed.

Public fixtures use synthetic PIDs/ports. Live package files and private state were not changed by this source contribution. Full build and broader/platform coverage remain for exact-head CI.

### Native proof follow-up — November 9

I tried an isolated real IPv4 loopback `TcpListener` without modifying the Gateway. The exact PowerShell subprocess again exited 0 with empty output, but real netstat also omitted that listener. This reproduces the broader observation reported in #195492; it does not establish this PR's narrower PowerShell-empty/netstat-visible path through shipped service inspection. The cause of the native visibility gap, including possible execution-environment effects, remains unverified. The requested end-to-end proof is still missing; I am not claiming the mocked regression or green CI clears it.

prs.title: test: stabilize hourly Gateway and runtime fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes hourly tests rejecting valid startup, recovery, and asynchronous tool behavior because their fixtures assume obsolete contracts or unowned timing.

## User Impact

There is no runtime behavior change. The checks preserve exact recovery ordering, error shapes, retained guest state, file contents, proxy responses, and deadline-expiry coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Fixture | Cause and repair |
| --- | --- |
| CLI recovery | The one-second real-time fixture budget introduced by e8c7c933f8c124081b2f0844aa8ecb55d751b01d can expire during setup. Control its monotonic clock for the recovery-order scenario; independent owner tests still exercise expiry. Update the already-shared backend object directly, removing a redundant clone and rebind. |
| Rollback test helper | #198268 / e4a30936bb35bc5a3e01a674ed3e43c98945d0aa left `resolveRollbackWorkerInputs` exported despite its sole caller being in the same file. Remove only the unused export, fixing the full-tree analyzer failure. |
| Archived agent | #199575 / 6f8b9fa083f6a6ef12df662d085817aa44eb4a61 added explicit nonretryable errors. Assert the complete current error object. |
| Workspace recovery | #199717 / aaee9202455e7af006778710cf166e953c054aa7 releases guest quiescence before canonical-only acceptance. Peer #199864 / 2824b9f5d2f3b4e82ef91f2c0e372e223c237b98 corrected the pause assertion; retain its comment and assertion, and add the distinct proof that a subsequent guest write survives recovery in both workspaces with an exact changed-file list. |
| Telemetry timers | The snapshot reclaimer from #192368 can reach process discovery after #197510 from a deliberately worker-free timer fixture. Replace only that unrelated operation locally; the real snapshot-maintenance sibling retains worker-backed cleanup proof. |
| Reload steering | #187095 / bca882333b9d285258052ec95febe6a6a339c5f3 assumes the RPC acknowledgment means native admission. Await the actual steering acceptance before advancing the fake provider; preserve all allowed/revoked content assertions. |
| Proxy listener | #186765 / 6769a69319106f2a7aa664def83cfa7a827a4e00 left a gap between port probing and binding. Use the existing listener reservation owner and register cleanup only after binding. A real competing socket regression exercises the original failure and successful proxy request. |

The proxy file already exceeded the hard line cap after #153661 / 99b8d70706649b286fe25a26f450dff6c5f3ce17 (999→1021 counted lines). Move five unchanged fixture helpers to adjacent support, restoring 999 without dropping coverage.

Main #199804 / 3d4bd2a708bc34b6bbef3046cf86c671996dc215 independently repaired the Code Mode warm-up. The correction retains that main file byte-for-byte and removes our duplicate hunk. The final delta contains nine fixture/support files.

Production runtime LOC delta: 0. No timeout increases, new runtime configuration, caches, or weakened assertions.

## Evidence

Original CLI, Code Mode, archived-agent, workspace, and proxy failures reproduced locally. Code Mode, archived-agent, workspace, and proxy failures reproduce under both Node and pinned Bun; CLI also fails under Node, so this is not a Bun-only family. Restoring only the pre-#199434 middleware owner makes the unchanged Code Mode tests pass; the production source was then restored byte-for-byte.

Focused Node and Bun proofs pass for the behavioral fixtures, including both reload permission cases. A controlled real-admission interleaving makes the original reload fixture fail and the candidate pass. Hermetic Bun fixtures use the existing pinned-binary handoff so runtime download time is outside product proof. Telemetry's original local replays passed; its retained hourly CI error and owner trace expose the asynchronous fixture escape. No local red is claimed for telemetry. The real snapshot-maintenance sibling still deletes all 257 eligible synthetic copies and preserves unrelated content after the file-local mock has retired.

The corrected candidate retains main's Code Mode warm-up byte-for-byte; both selected Code Mode cases pass under Node and pinned Bun (2/2 each). The final integration of #199864 changes only the workspace comment relative to the fully tested signed candidate; its guest-write preservation assertions and all other repair bytes remain unchanged. Behavioral and changed-file check proof is reused with that provenance; fresh hosted CI qualifies the published head. The rollback helper cleanup removes only one keyword.

On signed candidate `c17360830660c2e17557f5f05a0092f7093e7258`, `pnpm check:changed --base f905d3f21c94998a77d3a074f7f7ad74dbd81220` passes in 496.45 seconds, including all 26 test type graphs, production types, formatting, lint, line caps and all three unused-export scans with zero entries. Before removing the rollback helper export, the same canonical check failed solely on that unused export; this is a red-to-green analyzer repair. The complete nine-file candidate passed isolated Codex review through P2 with no actionable findings. prs.title: fix(templates): Template Add says a plugin is disabled when it is only missing from plugins.allow
prs.body:
<!-- Title: fix(templates): Template Add says a plugin is disabled when it is only missing from plugins.allow -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when `plugins.allow` is set and a Template brings a plugin that is not on it, Template Add through the Gateway says "This plugin is disabled. Enable it in Plugins; reinstall it there first if needed." It doesn't name the plugin, and the advice can't work because the plugin isn't installed yet (`openclaw plugins enable <id>` fails with "plugin not installed").

## User Impact

User impact: the Add review now names the runtime plugin id and the step that clears the blocker, for example `Plugin "hopper-gtfs" is not in plugins.allow. Add "hopper-gtfs" to plugins.allow, then add this Template again.` Users no longer have to dig the id out of the package. The local preview named the package or bundled folder (`plugins/gtfs`, `openclaw-christmas-themes@0.1.0`) instead of the id `plugins.allow` needs (`hopper-gtfs`, `christmas-themes`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Template plugin preflights (ClawHub packages and bundled plugin folders) already ask the shared activation owner whether the plugin would load. When the only reason is `not in allowlist`, they now return the runtime plugin id with the blocker, and the Gateway review renders that id instead of its generic text. The id is shown only if it is a plain plugin id: it must pass a strict pattern, a length cap and `validatePluginId`. Anything else keeps the previous generic message, and local paths still never reach Gateway clients. Other disable reasons (explicitly disabled, plugins off, denylist, already installed but disabled) are unchanged.

Related, not changed here: if you add the id to `plugins.allow` before the plugin is installed, config validation calls the entry stale ("plugin not found ... remove it from plugins config") until the Add installs it.

## Evidence

- New tests fail on main and pass with the fix:
  - `src/templates/packages.preflight-inspection.test.ts`: ClawHub plugin preflight returns the runtime id and allowlist message; an unsafe id is not echoed.
  - `src/templates/bundled-plugin.allowlist.test.ts`: real bundled plugin preflight. On main it returns `Plugin plugins/gtfs is disabled by host policy (not in allowlist). Enable it in Plugins before adding this Template.`
  - `src/templates/gateway-add-plan.test.ts`: the Gateway review names the id, falls back to the old text without one, and keeps local paths out.
- Removing the id safety check makes the unsafe-id test fail.
- Focused vitest (6 template files, 57 tests) and `pnpm check:changed` pass.
- Live run against a Gateway built from this branch, with `plugins.allow` set and the plugins missing from it:

```
before (main):  templates add @donniefi/hopper
  blockers: [{"code":"plugin_disabled","path":"$.plugins[0]","message":"This plugin is disabled. Enable it in Plugins; reinstall it there first if needed."}]

after:          templates add @donniefi/hopper
  blockers: [{"code":"plugin_disabled","path":"$.plugins[0]","message":"Plugin \"hopper-gtfs\" is not in plugins.allow. Add \"hopper-gtfs\" to plugins.allow, then add this Template again."}]
after:          templates add @mertbasar0/handoff-coordinator
  blockers: [{"code":"plugin_disabled","path":"$.plugins[0]","message":"Plugin \"clawhandoff\" is not in plugins.allow. Add \"clawhandoff\" to plugins.allow, then add this Template again."}]
  (no agent created by either blocked Add)
after adding "hopper-gtfs" to plugins.allow:  templates add @donniefi/hopper --accept-capabilities
  {"agentId":"hopper-2","status":"complete"}, greeting received
```

Found while adding every third-party ClawHub Template to a Gateway whose `plugins.allow` was already set. All 5 Templates with plugin dependencies hit this.


### Maintainer correction and validation

Resolved the overlap with current-main bundled-plugin collision diagnostics while preserving duplicate-plugin blockers and showing the allowlist remedy only for the selected plugin-disabled failure. Kept the generic blocker helper unchanged and attached optional allowlist metadata at the failed package-preflight diagnostic owner.

Prepared head: `2cb28d897c896399ffb97611a1cbeaa1268792fb`.

- Paired static proof: the first integrated candidate failed the existing lifecycle file limit (705 lines, limit 700); the scoped simplification passes that same lint check without changing the limit.
- 45 consumer tests pass across bundled allowlist, Gateway Add plan/privacy projection, and bundled project sources, including two folders that share a plugin ID.
- Core types, scoped lint and formatting for all 11 changed files, and diff checks pass. The unchanged package-plugin preflight consumers also passed on the first integrated candidate.
- The original live Gateway before/after proof above remains applicable. [Incoming CI run 43645442272](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43645442272) is historical evidence for the original contributor head; fresh CI must qualify the published correction.


### Final CI attribution for corrected head

CI [43781682467, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43781682467/attempts/2) completed on `2cb28d897c896399ffb97611a1cbeaa1268792fb`: 99 jobs, with 68 successful, 28 skipped, two failed test leaves and the downstream failed gate. `security-fast` passed. These final results supersede the pending statement above; CI remains failed.

Manual source review attributes both failures to unchanged inputs. The archived-session assertion omits the existing `retryable: false` field; [scheduled main has the same case and diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43774966177/job/132999497670). The cron fixture observed initial `unknown` delivery state before terminal settlement. Its fixture, producer, transport, persistence and runner/dependency inputs are identical from actual baseline `d8964fd1495376d776066011f913efe80c27be29` to tested merge `300dc93eab58248e915ca7e9bfe6ed43e4eae316`, and these fixtures do not invoke the changed Template branches. Exact cron scheduling remains unresolved; no matching-main cron failure, baseline replay or deterministic-flake claim is made. The automated classifier reports unknown because main shard names differ.

The landing coordinator accepted this scoped inherited-failure attribution. Landing will use the repository's exact-head CI exception, subject to native verification of the genuine tested merge/tree, current head, security and writer authority. No CI retry or green-run claim is used; the passing scoped proof above remains the 45 corrected-tree tests and associated checks.
