prs.title: fix(cli): keep backup git scope guard remedies in --json error output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup git create --repository <repo> --json` without a scope flag exits 1 with only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` and the doctor hint on stderr, so machine callers that read stderr never see the `Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>.` remediation that the text lane already prints. The same gap affects all six scope/blank argument guards across `backup git create`, `backup git verify`, and `backup git restore`.

- Problem: the six argument guards in `src/commands/backup-git.ts` (blank `--agent` element, `--all` combined with an explicit scope, missing create scope, blank `--store`, more than one single-identity scope, missing single-identity scope) throw a plain `Error`. The text lane renders its message, but the JSON lane classifies it as an unexpected failure and replaces stderr with the generic failure banner, leaving the remediation only inside the stdout envelope.
- Solution: throw `ExpectedCliError` from the same guards via the canonical `throwExpectedCliError` helper, so the JSON lane renders the same remediation the text lane prints while keeping the envelope untouched.
- What changed: `src/commands/backup-git.ts` routes the six guards through `throwExpectedCliError` (one new import, six `throw` call sites, identical message text). `src/commands/backup-git.test.ts` folds class assertions into two existing rejection tests (a per-row error-name column in the invalid-agent table — the neighboring unknown-agent guard stays a plain `Error` — and `name: "ExpectedCliError"` in the `--all` conflict case), net zero test lines.
- What did NOT change: exit codes, the stdout JSON envelope shape and message, text-lane stdout/stderr bytes, happy-path backup behavior, the neighboring unknown-agent guard, and every other `backup` subcommand.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ExpectedCliError` is the shipped owner for argument-level CLI failures (`src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`), so the fix reuses the existing failure classifier instead of adding a rendering path. This is the same per-site conversion already merged for the sibling backup guards: #199573 (`backup record`), #199763 (`backup create --to`), and #199781 (`backup verify/restore --namespace`).

- Best fix: convert the guard throws in place; the message text, exit code, and machine envelope stay byte-identical, and only the stderr classification in JSON mode changes. All six guards run before any Git work or lifecycle write custody, so no side effects move.
- Alternative: special-case the JSON renderer to print `error.message` for plain `Error` too. Rejected: that would leak stack-y unexpected failures into the expected lane and change every other command at once.
- Risk: the only observable delta is which stderr lines appear in JSON mode for these six invalid inputs; valid scopes, the text lane, and the stdout envelope were verified byte-identical in the shipped-build comparison below.

## User Impact

Operators and CI jobs that run `backup git create/verify/restore` with `--json` now get the actionable remediation on stderr (for example `Choose a Git backup scope: --global, --agent <id>, or --store <id>.`), matching the text lane, instead of a generic failure banner. Scripts that parse the stdout envelope see no change.

## Compatibility

- Preserved: exit codes, stdout envelope bytes, text-lane bytes, and non-guard failures are unchanged (all `cmp`-verified below).
- Related: #161230 also touches `src/commands/backup-git.ts`, but it changes which agent database a snapshot captures (import rename plus the post-guard database resolution and happy-path tests); it does not touch these six guard throws or the two rejection tests folded here. The changes are complementary — whichever merges first, the other needs only a mechanical rebase.
- Not claimed: no behavior change for valid scope selections, no Windows or macOS run.

## Evidence

Both arms were built with the shipped CLI pipeline (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`) and exercised through the real launcher (`node openclaw.mjs <cmd>`) with `env -i` and a fresh chmod-700 scratch `HOME` / `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` per cell — no gateway, no credentials, no mocks. `--version` self-reports both arm identities: base `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (e693b33)`, this head `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (6eb8f16)`. The final `runtime-postbuild` metadata phase fails identically on both arms on a dangling plugin-dependency symlink in the build host's shared checkout (pre-existing environment issue); the launcher and every cell below run on the produced `dist`.

| Case (`backup git ...`, all with `--repository <repo>`) | Before (origin/main e693b33) | After (this head 6eb8f16) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create --agent " " --json` | exit 1; stderr only the generic pair (208 B); remedy confined to the stdout envelope (104 B) | exit 1; stderr `--agent must not be blank`; stdout envelope byte-identical (104 B) |
| `create --all --global --json` | exit 1; same generic stderr pair; remedy only in envelope (149 B) | exit 1; stderr `Use --all by itself, or select --global and --agent scopes explicitly.`; envelope byte-identical (149 B) |
| `create --json` (no scope) | exit 1; same generic stderr pair; remedy only in envelope (150 B) | exit 1; stderr `Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>.`; envelope byte-identical (150 B) |
| `verify --store " " --json` | exit 1; same generic stderr pair; remedy only in envelope (104 B) | exit 1; stderr `--store must not be blank`; envelope byte-identical (104 B) |
| `verify --global --agent main --json` | exit 1; same generic stderr pair; remedy only in envelope (156 B) | exit 1; stderr `Choose exactly one Git backup scope: --global, --agent <id>, or --store <id>.`; envelope byte-identical (156 B) |
| `verify --json` (no scope) | exit 1; same generic stderr pair; remedy only in envelope (146 B) | exit 1; stderr `Choose a Git backup scope: --global, --agent <id>, or --store <id>.`; envelope byte-identical (146 B) |
| text lane, all six invalid inputs (no `--json`) | exit 1; stderr carries the remedy | exit 1; stdout and stderr byte-identical to before (`cmp` reports no difference on all six) |
| control: `backup verify <missing-archive> --json` (non-guard failure) | exit 1; generic stderr pair; 235 B envelope | exit 1; stdout and stderr byte-identical (`cmp`); generic pair retained |
| control: `backup verify <missing-archive> --namespace probe --json` (sibling guard converted by #199781) | exit 1; stderr `--namespace requires --from <location>.` | exit 1; stdout and stderr byte-identical (`cmp`); remedy retained, no generic banner |

Pre-fix JSON lane (base build, representative cell):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup git create --repository /tmp/417-probe-repo --json
# exit=1
# stderr:
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped; check that the path is a writable regular file; file=openclaw-2026-11-16.log
# stdout:
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>."
  }
}
```

Post-fix JSON lane (this head build, identical command):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs backup git create --repository /tmp/417-probe-repo --json
# exit=1
# stderr:
Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>.
[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped; check that the path is a writable regular file; file=openclaw-2026-11-16.log
# stdout: byte-identical to the base envelope above (cmp)
```

The `log file append failed` line is scratch-environment noise emitted identically by both arms in every cell; it is included in all byte counts and `cmp` comparisons.

Invariants across the two builds (104 automated checks, all passing):

```text
six JSON guard cells stdout (envelope)      : byte-identical, exit 1 on both arms
six JSON guard cells stderr                 : generic pair replaced by the single guard message
six text-lane cells (stdout and stderr)     : byte-identical
control A (non-guard failure), both lanes   : byte-identical; JSON keeps the generic pair,
                                              text keeps the real archive-missing message
control B (--namespace sibling guard), both : byte-identical; remedy on stderr, no generic banner
```

Reachability was verified on the base arm with `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` (the plain `Error` prints a stack; the expected error does not). Frame excerpt, paths shortened to dist-relative:

```text
[openclaw] Error: Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>.
[openclaw]     at resolveCreateDatabases (dist/backup-git-BNh8CDrm.mjs:25:475)
[openclaw]     at backupGitCreateCommand (dist/backup-git-BNh8CDrm.mjs:25:2119)
[openclaw]     at dist/register.backup-DmcjqL9g.mjs:3:8420
[openclaw]     at async runCommandWithRuntime (dist/cli-utils-Cz2q-7HD.mjs:3:233)
```

The `verify` no-scope cell shows the analogous `resolveOneIdentity` frame. Serialized shipped bundles of the changed owner prove the executed form on each arm:

```js
// base dist/backup-git-BNh8CDrm.mjs
if(!e.all&&!n)throw new Error(`Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>.`);
// this head dist/backup-git-Mi6yxXq9.mjs
import{n as throwExpectedCliError}from"./expected-cli-error-oDVmXYil.mjs";
if(!e.all&&!n)throwExpectedCliError(`Choose at least one Git backup scope: --all, --global, or --agent <id>.`);
```

The folded regression assertions are red against the frozen pre-fix owner (detached base worktree, production untouched) and green on this head:

```console
# pre-fix owner, folded assertions kept
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts backup-git.test.ts
 FAIL  rejects an whitespace-only Git create agent
 AssertionError: expected Error: --agent must not be blank to match object { name: 'ExpectedCliError', …(1) }
 FAIL  keeps the --all plus explicit-scope conflict ahead of agent validation
 AssertionError: expected Error: Use --all by itself, or select --g… to match object { name: 'ExpectedCliError', …(1) }
 Tests  2 failed | 17 passed (19)

# this head
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts backup-git.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
 Tests  19 passed (19)
```

The unknown-agent row of the same table asserts `name: "Error"` and passes on both arms, pinning that the neighboring guard (a different owner) is not over-converted.

What was not tested: no Windows or macOS run; `backup git restore` shares the `resolveOneIdentity` owner with `verify` and was not driven separately; commander-level missing-value rejections happen before the owner and are not exercised. Both arms' builds fail identically in the final `runtime-postbuild` metadata phase on the shared checkout's dangling plugin-dependency symlink (environment, pre-existing); the `check-cli-bootstrap-imports` guard passed on both arms.

Open PR collision check: on the day of writing, the full open-PR list (3611 PRs) was scanned by changed-file list (GraphQL for the newest 1100, REST per-PR files for the remainder; four empty-diff PRs verified individually). Only #161230 touches `src/commands/backup-git.ts` / `backup-git.test.ts`; its hunks (canonical agent-database selection for `--agent` snapshots) do not intersect the six guard throws or the two folded rejection cases, so it is complementary, not a duplicate (see Compatibility). Same-family merges this week are per-site siblings (#199573, #199763, #199781); none covers the `backup git` scope guards.

## Maintainer validation

Validated `501efb5896f447a998a51963feb031a985c6d4db`: [twice-per-side real CLI scope guards, byte-identical text/JSON/exit controls, unchanged unknown-agent errors, regression, typecheck and packed-install receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199850#issuecomment-6904241226). The contributor production fix is unchanged. The added commit only makes an existing external-root fixture independent of the macOS `/tmp` alias; no case was removed and test growth remains zero.

Merge danger: reversible error-classification/test-fixture change. Blast radius: JSON stderr presentation for six local Git backup scope guards.

prs.title: fix: honor ID agent limits in message action sends without a role default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Message action sends can create a session outside an OpenClaw ID member’s agent settings when `gateway.roles.default` is omitted.

## User Impact

Message action sends honor the same member agent limits as direct sends and session creation. Unrestricted callers can continue sending without selecting an agent. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the effective caller policy before deciding whether agent authorization is needed, then pass it to the existing session-creation check. Unrestricted callers avoid implicit-agent selection, including wildcard ID members in multiagent configurations.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43781982686) is green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. No CI failure or hosted review finding required a fixup.
- The absent-default regression fails on the base with an unintended allow decision; its controls pass. All 105 focused tests across the new regression, send, and operator-role-policy suites pass with the fix. The standalone regression has five passing cases (57.34s wrapper / 39.62s Vitest, including transform/import/verification).
- Targeted formatting, lint, production typecheck, Gateway-method test typecheck, and full runtime build pass.
- Isolated compiled Gateway replay uses local issuer/Discovery enrollment, normal owner approval, and native iroh member connections. Explicit and implicit excluded-agent sends refuse without creating a canonical session or destination effect. Owner, allowed-member, and wildcard-member sends succeed; the allowed member creates a fresh canonical session.
- Local autoreview (P0–P3) of baseline `b2f57063e7319c1df79abcc281895d1bc09c372b` to `e2249b0fc279824efe0e6151796c802f8eb2c044` found no actionable items. Independent source and exported runtime-evidence review are also clean. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199863#issuecomment-6904393204) of the same head completed with zero findings and no before-merge items.

The replay qualifies a compiled source checkout, without deployment or full package/release coverage. A relocated test fixture initially failed before Gateway startup; correcting its task paths allowed the successful replay without a product change.

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

Focused command:

```sh

node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/config/config-page.notifications.test.tsx src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts src/pages/config/notifications-section.test.tsx src/app/native-notifications.test.ts src/app/native-device-settings.test.ts src/app/web-push.test.ts --project unit --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix(agents): continuation-skip turns tell the model its workspace instructions were removed
prs.body:
Related: #196122

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, every continuation turn on routes that pin the system prompt (direct Anthropic, official OpenAI Responses) tells the model that AGENTS.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md and every heading inside them were "(removed)".

## User Impact

On those routes, skipped turns keep the workspace instructions the model already has, without a system update revoking them. Skipped turns still send no workspace files, and an explicit `contextInjection: "never"` still announces the removal. Sessions that already received a false removal from an earlier skipped turn get their files redelivered once on the next skipped turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

A skipped continuation withholds files that the pinned prompt prefix still carries, but the prompt series diffed the file-less prompt against that prefix and reported each Project Context section as removed. The bootstrap stage now reports that it withheld already-delivered context, and the pinned series reuses its own Project Context block for that comparison, placed inside the framed stable region (before `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->`, or the cache boundary when unframed). If the saved comparison state already lost the block, the block comes from the admitted prefix, which still has it.

Scope: this does not change what unpinned routes (OpenRouter, most OpenAI-compatible providers) receive on skipped turns. Whether those routes should keep workspace files under `continuation-skip` is the separate product question in #196122; this PR leaves the #154923 behavior as is.

## Evidence

- Regression in `session-prompt-state.test.ts` built from real `buildAttemptSystemPrompt` output (with STABLE/DYNAMIC framing): on a pinned series, a withheld turn emits no update; redelivering unchanged files emits nothing; a removal without the withheld flag reports `(removed)` for the file and its inner headings; a comparison state that already lost the files redelivers them (`Be brief.`) once.
- Mutation checks: ignoring the STABLE terminator makes the "no update" assertion fail; dropping the admitted-prefix fallback makes the redelivery assertion fail.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: 36 passed. `tsc` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`: no errors in changed files or for `workspaceContextWithheld`. `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with the allocation. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.
- Evidence gap: I have not captured a live provider request on a pinned route. Pinned routes require a direct Anthropic or official OpenAI endpoint with a real key, so the existing loopback Gateway fixture (`gateway.continuation-skip-bootstrap.integration.test.ts`) resolves as unpinned and cannot show this path. `attempt-bootstrap-prepare.test.ts` hits `EMFILE` on Windows for 14 cases, identically on unmodified `main`.

prs.title: fix(signal): reaction approvals do nothing on prompts forwarded to Signal approvers
prs.body:
Closes #195620

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: 👍 / 👎 reactions never resolve exec or plugin approvals that are forwarded to a Signal approver (`approvals.*.mode: "targets"`); the prompt arrives without the "React with:" hint and approvers have to type `/approve`.

## User Impact

Approvers who receive forwarded approval prompts in Signal can approve or deny with a reaction, as they already can for approvals that start in a Signal chat. Setups without reaction approvers keep the same manual prompt text as today.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal's forwarded-prompt renderer returned the reaction runtime's manual fallback payload, which has its presentation stripped. Outbound delivery only calls Signal's `renderPresentation` for payloads with a presentation, so the existing checked hint renderer (approver, route and target-author checks) never ran and `afterDeliverPayload` had no hinted message to register.

Forwarded prompts now keep their command text plus the approval button presentation, so delivery goes through that existing checked renderer and registration. The forwarded render itself still carries no reaction hint, so controls are only advertised when the route is actually bound. When the hint cannot be added, `renderPresentation` now returns Signal's materialized approval text for approval payloads instead of `null`; otherwise the generic fallback would flatten the buttons and repeat the Allow/Deny commands already in the text. Non-approval payloads behave as before.

## Evidence

- New regression in `extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts` (exec and plugin): a Control UI–origin request forwarded to a Signal target renders with the hint, `afterDeliverPayload` registers it, and a 👍 on the delivered message resolves to `allow-once`; without reaction approvers the rendered text equals the manual prompt. On `main` both cases fail at the missing presentation; dropping the `renderPresentation` fallback makes the no-approver assertion fail.
- `core.test.ts`, `approval-native.test.ts` (including the existing "no unbound reaction choices" target-mode check), `approval-reactions.test.ts`, `monitor.approval-reply-delivery.test.ts`: 53 passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files.
- Authority boundary for the forwarded path (`approval-reactions.test.ts`): a target-mode prompt rendered through `addSignalApprovalReactionHintToStructuredPayload` and registered through delivery does not call `resolveApprovalOverGateway` for a reaction from an unlisted actor or from an approver removed from `allowFrom`, and resolves once for a current approver. Existing cases in the same file keep covering wrong conversation / wrong bot identity, missing explicit approvers, and a changed top-level approval route. The resolution and authorization code itself is unchanged by this PR; it only makes forwarded prompts reach it.
- Test-line growth is allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/196419-signal-forwarded-approval-reactions.txt` (79, exact net growth); `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes after merging current `main`.
- The full `extensions/signal` run on Windows has 8 failures in untouched files (Unix socket paths, temp-dir permissions, Windows env names, and a database-worker timeout in `event-handler.partial-delivery.test.ts`); that approval test fails the same way on unmodified `main`. No live Signal round trip was run.

prs.title: fix(templates): inline review and publish fail when ClawHub handle has uppercase letters
prs.body:
Closes #199405

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inline Template review (`templates.drafts.review`) and publication (`templates.drafts.publish`) fail with `"Your ClawHub account needs a personal publisher handle."` (`clawhub_identity_required`) when ClawHub `/api/v1/whoami` returns a mixed-case GitHub OAuth `user.handle` (such as `MertBasar0`).

## User Impact

User impact: Control UI Template creators whose ClawHub / GitHub personal handle contains uppercase characters can now review and publish Templates inline under their canonical lowercase `@<handle>/<slug>` personal namespace without false `clawhub_identity_required` failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub's `GET /api/v1/whoami` returns the GitHub-cased `user.handle` (for example `"MertBasar0"`), whereas ClawHub's publisher and package surfaces normalize personal handles to lowercase (`@mertbasar0/<slug>`, `ownerHandle: "mertbasar0"`, `https://clawhub.ai/mertbasar0/templates/<slug>`).

`personalPublisher` in `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts` is the sole `/api/v1/whoami` caller in `src/` (introduced in `f16e8bc092e7e`, carried through `d1c8d42588a4b` and `#196427`). Normalizing `result.user?.handle?.trim().toLowerCase()` at that producer boundary (net `0` production LOC: `+1/-1`) aligns review tokens, `prepareTemplateDraft`, upload `ownerHandle`, bound attempt status checks, and receipt URLs with ClawHub's canonical publisher handle.

## Evidence

### Live Windows Control UI Proof (Before vs After against live `https://clawhub.ai`)

**Before (`main` at `6001e95c4946`):** Clicking **Create template** in an isolated dev Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + ephemeral port) with a ClawHub account whose `/api/v1/whoami` returns `"MertBasar0"` fails inline during `templates.drafts.review`:

![Before: Mixed-case ClawHub handle fails inline review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ad4ef06-0a2b-4418-a445-91ff8fe21fad)

**After (this PR):** The same live Control UI flow hydrates **Review your Template** (`by @mertbasar0`) cleanly and completes end-to-end live publication (`Unpublished` -> `Publishing…` -> `Pending` -> `Published` at `https://clawhub.ai/mertbasar0/templates/pr-review-radar`, ClawScan `verdict: "benign"`, `scanStatus: "clean"`):

![After: Inline review card hydrated for @mertbasar0/pr-review-radar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/605b909f-70e9-4b39-a0bd-45065fb330ef)

![After: Live ClawHub publication completed in Control UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec792831-9505-491a-ab1f-bed3cdf42801)

Live end-to-end Control UI recording (`recordVideo`, motion-trimmed):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb7217e3-e806-41b3-b702-7718828cfe8d

Redacted live Gateway WebSocket RPC trace:

```text

templates.drafts.review -> durationMs=942 ok=false errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage="Your ClawHub account needs a personal publisher handle."

# After (fix/templates-drafts-mixed-case-handle b761a69120a5)

templates.drafts.publish -> durationMs=6929 ok=true publicationStatus=pending
templates.drafts.review(checkPublication=true) -> durationMs=4843 ok=true publicationStateStatus=published
```

### Tests & Checks

- Added boundary regression test `normalizes mixed-case and padded /whoami handles to lowercase personal publishers` in `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` verifying mixed-case `/api/v1/whoami` handles (`"  MertBasar0  "`) normalize to `"mertbasar0"` across `templates.drafts.review`, `templates.drafts.publish` (`ownerHandle`), and bound attempt status polling:
  - Pre-fix run failed with `{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Your ClawHub account needs a personal publisher handle."}`.
  - Post-fix run: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` -> `31 passed (31)`.
- Production vs test LOC delta (`git diff --numstat`): `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts` `+1/-1` (**net `0` production LOC**); `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` `+36/-1`.

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

Tested on `upstream/main` `20237d956bb` (2026-11-12) before, and `c50d8b26e1e` (this PR head, rebased onto it) after. Real built CLI, local fake MCP servers on loopback, isolated temp HOME and state dir. Ubuntu 26.04, Node 26.10.0.

`node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning|error`. Exit codes: warning threshold / error threshold.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy server (remote or stdio) | no finding; exit 0 / 0 | no finding; exit 0 / 0 |
| Remote outage: connection refused, HTTP 503, HTTP 401, hang past the 10 s deadline | error; exit 1 / 1 | warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 0 |
| Remote invalid catalog (bad tool entry, repeated cursor) | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Stdio failure: crash at start, missing executable, invalid catalog | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Remote 503 and stdio crash in one config | error + error; exit 1 / 1 | error + warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 1 |

Upgrade check (published `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then this build, same temp state dir, remote HTTP 503): at the error threshold 2026.10.8 gave error, exit 1; this build gave no finding, exit 0. State files stayed byte-identical. Not the `openclaw update` command.
Unit tests (4 files, `--maxWorkers=1`): 55 of 55 pass, including the stdio Doctor tests.
Not tested: real `openclaw update`, a running Gateway, real third-party servers, OAuth, legacy SSE, TLS, human-readable Doctor output, Windows, macOS.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. prs.title: fix(gateway): private-home CI checks time out on cold imports
prs.body:
Related: #199565

## What Problem This Solves

The private-home regression test can exceed its subprocess deadline during cold imports in CI.

## User Impact

Test-only change; no user-visible runtime, permission, configuration or migration change. The existing deadline and cleanup checks remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate home-fixture creation from unrelated runtime-reset imports. Existing callers and the subprocess use one implementation, with reference-identity assertions connecting the facade to the tested owner. No retry, timeout increase, skip or weaker assertion is added.

The change moves the existing fixture rather than introducing another implementation: three fixture files, 86 additions and 73 deletions (net +13); runtime reset behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Natural-main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43774966177/job/132999497139): the added child test hit the existing 10-second limit under Bun.
- [Original-only diagnostic](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_93180d1268b447edd20fe517b1239ca8): all three cases passed in isolation. Of 6.778s parent time, helper import consumed 6.542s, setup 46.6ms and cleanup 11.4ms. This measured import overhead; it did not reproduce the remote timeout or establish an original/fix causal pair.
- [Prior-layout candidate validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9dfc6f0ed1aa70023a5e3dc19f862e90): repository-configured formatting, the maintained Gateway compiler leaf covering all three changed files, exact three-file type-aware lint and normal `qaRuntime` build passed. All three Node 24 fixture cases reported passing, with zero pending cases or suite/unhandled errors; the private-home case took 163.975ms. Tested source was `718a2f8d98e1ad44d7b4475035de84a98d1b9111` plus the exact three-file patch, byte-identical to prior local commit `7bed224e5e904bc6a96a862b3aa78ee3fc6ad269`.
- Complete three-file independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defect. Simplification review retained one home-fixture owner and removed the child dependency on runtime-reset machinery.

The first published revision also hit the source-contract checker because its extracted fixture filename did not use the existing `*.test-support.ts` convention. The same unchanged helper is now named `gateway-temp-home.test-support.ts`; only its imports and path changed. Repository-configured formatting and an independent review of that correction passed. The remote runtime receipts above precede this naming correction; current-head CI must validate the new path and remaining runtime coverage.

The remote run itself is **not green**: its collector later collided with the test reporter filename, leaving the final command-exit record unavailable. The passing test/report and scoped-gate receipts are retained; Bun and recovered-output cases had not run. Normal PR CI must supply the missing runtime/integration proof before landing. No new cloud allocation or unchanged replay is needed just to repeat completed checks. All task-owned leases are cleaned.

## Contributor credit

Co-authored-by: obviyus <22031114+obviyus@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: steipete <58493+steipete@users.noreply.github.com>

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

prs.title: feat(agents): let the gateway tool read update status
prs.body:
## Summary

- The agent-facing `gateway` tool can now read the Gateway's update state with `{ action: "update.status" }`, forwarding to the existing read-only `update.status` RPC through the same `callGatewayTool` path that already backs `config.get` / `config.schema.lookup`.
- `update.status` stays available when `allowConfigReads` is false. The restricted tool variant is the one that schedules `update.run`, so it is the one that most needs the read: "why did my update fail?" is a question the restricted agent is expected to answer without handing it config read authority.
- No new RPC and no new write authority: the action is read-only, `update.run` / `restart` / `update.cleanup` admission is untouched, and the change is a single enum + dispatch branch in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts`.
- The tool description and the Codex prompt snapshot that mirrors it (`codex-dynamic-tools.telegram-direct.json`) move together, per the prompt-prefix contract. Both variants were shortened to 165 chars ("Owner/operator:" replaces "Owner request/operator schedule:") so the tool directory no longer truncates the description.

Fixes #188320

## Linked context

- Issue: #188320 — the `gateway` tool could schedule `update.run` and restart the Gateway but could not read the update state it was about to change.
- Review history on this PR: the 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper round raised three P2s (signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit). All three are fixed on this head.
- **This revision answers the one remaining reviewer ask** — *"Provide a successful real agent invocation of `update.status` with configuration reads allowed and withheld; the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body"*. The previous revision's `tools.invoke` capture aborted on agent-database admission, so the new forwarding branch never ran. This body replaces that capture with **two successful executions of the real tool object, one per variant**, against a live Gateway (see below), and explains honestly why the `tools.invoke` wrapper path is still blocked on this host.

## Revision note (rebase)

The capture below was taken at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`. The branch has since been **rebased onto `origin/main` to clear a merge conflict** (`mergeable: dirty`), so the current head is `8862cfd8bddc482a2ddfbe7caa208b2a9d0fbfd2`. The patch content is unchanged — same 8 files, `+63 −22` — and the only bytes that moved were the generated prompt-snapshot fixtures, which were regenerated with `scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write` rather than hand-merged (`Prompt snapshots are current (6 files)`). Because the captured `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is literally the checkout's HEAD at capture time, it reads `3c654c1b48f…` and not the post-rebase sha; that is the expected consequence of the rebase and is called out here instead of being silently edited.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Before this patch the assembled `gateway` tool's action enum contained `config.get`, `config.schema.lookup`, `update.run`, `restart` and `update.cleanup` only, so `{ action: "update.status" }` was rejected at the tool boundary and an agent could not read the update state it was about to change or diagnose a failed update. After the patch the same call forwards to the canonical read-only `update.status` RPC and returns the recorded state, and it does so in **both** variants — including the restricted one that has configuration reads withheld.

**Real setup tested**: Windows host, Node v24.22.1, branch `feat/agent-update-status` at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, TypeScript sources executed directly through `scripts/tsx.mjs` (source runtime, not a packaged dist), **brand-new** isolated state directory `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` (empty before this run, so the agent database is created and migrated from scratch rather than reused), Gateway bound to loopback port 18815 with `--allow-unconfigured`, reaching `post-ready.startup-maintenance` at total 387.0 s before any RPC was issued.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1 + `scripts/tsx.mjs` loader (source runtime); no packaged `dist` build was used for this capture.

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2
export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18815
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18815

# (1) Ground truth: the canonical RPC the new branch forwards to.
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call update.status --timeout 180000 --json

# (2) The changed code path itself, exercised once per variant against the same
#     live Gateway. This is a throwaway harness (NOT part of the patch); it
#     imports the production factory and calls the production tool object.
#     Variant selection is the same input the real assembly passes:
#       src/agents/openclaw-tools.gateway.ts:23 ->
#       createGatewayTool({ allowConfigReads: options?.gatewayConfigReadAllowed === true })
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ./.proof-probe-188321.ts
```

```ts
// .proof-probe-188321.ts — throwaway harness, deleted after the capture
import { createGatewayTool } from "./src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.js";
import { captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader } from "./src/config/config.js";

const variants = [
  { label: "FULL VARIANT (config reads allowed)", allowConfigReads: true },
  { label: "RESTRICTED VARIANT (config reads withheld)", allowConfigReads: false },
];

async function main() {
  const readConfig = captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader({ skipPluginValidation: true });
  await readConfig();
  for (const v of variants) {
    const tool = createGatewayTool({ allowConfigReads: v.allowConfigReads, senderIsOwner: true });
    console.log(`### ${v.label}`);
    console.log(`tool.description = ${tool.description}`);
    console.log(`action enum      = ${JSON.stringify(tool.parameters.properties.action.enum)}`);
    const result = await tool.execute("proof-188321", { action: "update.status" });
    console.log(`RESULT = ${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}`);
  }
}
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
# (1) Ground truth — direct canonical RPC, EXIT=0, elapsed_s=59.2
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call update.status --timeout 180000 --json
{
  "sentinel": null,
  "updateAvailable": null,
  "effectiveChannel": "dev",
  "schedule": {
    "channel": "dev",
    "autoEnabled": false,
    "install": {
      "kind": "git",
      "git": {
        "currentSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d",
        "commitAtMs": 1794477400000,
        "upstreamSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d",
        "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw",
        "status": "current"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```text
# (2) FULL VARIANT (config reads allowed) — elapsed_ms = 8079
tool.name        = gateway
tool.description = Read gateway config/schema and update status. Owner/operator: update.run, restart, update.cleanup. Use runtime-owned actions.
action enum      = ["config.get","config.schema.lookup","update.status","update.run","restart","update.cleanup"]
RESULT = {
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"sentinel\":null,\"updateAvailable\":null,\"effectiveChannel\":\"dev\",\"schedule\":{\"channel\":\"dev\",\"autoEnabled\":false,\"install\":{\"kind\":\"git\",\"git\":{\"currentSha\":\"3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d\",\"commitAtMs\":1794477400000,\"upstreamSha\":\"3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d\",\"repositoryUrl\":\"https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw\",\"status\":\"current\"}}}}" }],
  "details": {
    "sentinel": null,
    "updateAvailable": null,
    "effectiveChannel": "dev",
    "schedule": { "channel": "dev", "autoEnabled": false, "install": { "kind": "git", "git": { "currentSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d", "commitAtMs": 1794477400000, "upstreamSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d", "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw", "status": "current" } } }
  }
}
```

```text
# (3) RESTRICTED VARIANT (config reads withheld) — elapsed_ms = 210
tool.name        = gateway
tool.description = Read update status; owner/operator: update.run, restart, update.cleanup. Cleanup permanently retires eligible rollback copies; dryRun previews. Use runtime-owned actions.
action enum      = ["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]
RESULT = identical canonical status object as (2), same currentSha/upstreamSha/status:"current"
```

```text
# (4) Gateway-side corroboration — one backend connection per variant, both
#     authenticated as an operator, at the moment of the two probes.
[ws] client connected conn=64415c02-… client=gateway-client name=agent mode=backend role=operator auth=device-token
[ws] client connected conn=232a8461-… client=gateway-client name=agent mode=backend role=operator auth=device-token
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `update.status` now executes through the tool object in **both** variants and returns the live Gateway's real update state — `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, which is exactly `git rev-parse HEAD` of this checkout, and `repositoryUrl` is this fork. That SHA is read out of the running Gateway's own install state, so the payload cannot be synthesized by the calling process. The two action enums are the direct, structural answer to the reviewer's question: the restricted schema is `["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]` — `update.status` is present while `config.get` and `config.schema.lookup` are absent — and the full schema is the six-action superset. The restricted variant ran much faster (210 ms vs 8079 ms); the likely explanation is a warm connection on the second call, and I am not claiming more than that — both executions are real calls against the same Gateway, which the per-variant backend connections in (4) corroborate. `lastRun` / `activeRun` are absent because no update was ever run in this fresh isolated state directory; that is the honest shape of a clean Gateway, not a filtered field.

**What was not tested**: a packaged `dist` build of this head (both captures use the tsx source runtime); the **`tools.invoke` wrapper path end-to-end** — it is still blocked on this host by `Agent database execution admission is closed` (see the limitation section below), which fires inside the Gateway's agent-database admission *before* the tool body runs, so it cannot exercise this patch either way; a full model-driven agent turn on Discord/Telegram that selects this action from the model's tool list; a real update run producing `lastRun` / `activeRun` records (no update was deliberately triggered in a throwaway state directory); and any `openclaw update status` CLI surface, which does not exist for this action.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: The `tools.invoke` RPC (which is how the previous revision tried to reach the tool) is gated by the Gateway's agent-database execution admission. On a brand-new state directory that admission still ends in a schema handshake failure — `agent database remains degraded agentId=main … reason="Agent database execution admission is closed"`, with the Gateway log advising `Use the newer install that supports schema 41 or newer`. The `repairHint` is `openclaw doctor --fix`, which is out of scope for this run (it mutates a deliberately throwaway state directory and is not something a contributor should run to manufacture proof). Rather than stop there, the capture above drives the **same production tool object** the assembly builds, so the new forwarding branch genuinely executes and returns Gateway-served data — but it is invoked directly instead of through an agent-mediated turn, and that distinction is stated rather than blurred. Note also that a **successful** `update.status` does not emit a `⇄ res ✓ update.status` line in this build (only failures and the outer `tools.invoke` RPC are logged at that level), so the round-trip evidence here is the backend connection log plus the self-referential `currentSha`, not a `⇄ res ✓` line — I did not fabricate one. No secrets, tokens or real user state were used: every command ran against `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` on loopback port 18815.

## Tests and validation

- Baseline regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this head → **`Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 15 passed (15)`, duration 368.90 s, exit 0**. This is the pre-existing suite around the changed file, so it covers "did the patch break the existing actions" rather than only the new branch; the run includes the pre-existing `preserves update diagnostic Unicode in tool results` case alongside the new `update.status` assertions.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts` → **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the same four files → **All matched files use the correct format.**
- CI on head `3c654c1b48f`: **110 check runs, 0 failures** (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` pass, `pr-failure-report` skipped as expected). The compiled agents-tools suites are covered by CI, not by this Windows host.
- Unit coverage added on this branch: `gateway-tool.test.ts` ("reads update status even when config reads are withheld" — calls the tool with `allowConfigReads: false` and asserts the forwarded method), `gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts` (action present in the coding profile and in the full profiles after `config.schema.lookup`; grants matrix), `tool-search.test.ts` + prompt snapshot (new description text).

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes`)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The risk is the agent tool surface: one more action becomes reachable from a model-driven turn, and that action crosses the Gateway boundary. The action is read-only, but it does expose update channel/schedule state to the restricted tool variant that previously could not read it — the capture above shows exactly that enlarged surface (`update.status` inside a schema that still withholds `config.get`).

How is that risk mitigated?
- The action maps to the existing `update.status` RPC with no parameters and no write admission; it does not touch `update.run`, `restart` or `update.cleanup`. It is enumerated in the schema (no free-form method passthrough), so an unknown action still fails closed at the tool boundary. The restricted-profile availability is intentional and asserted in tests; the full-profile grants matrix keeps the owner/config-read boundary unchanged. The dispatch branch sits *before* the `allowConfigReads` guard rather than inside it, so the read is available without widening the config-read gate.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review (owner decision) on the bounded status action. No author action is pending on the code; this body rewrite is the author action for the proof gap the review named.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
- Waiting on the maintainer decision requested by the review. Open external proof, stated plainly: a packaged `dist` capture, a model-driven turn that picks the action, and the `tools.invoke` wrapper path (blocked by the agent-database schema handshake on this host).

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
- 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper P2s: signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit — all fixed on this head.
- The 2026-11-12 review's single "Before merge" item ("add real behavior proof … the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body") is addressed by the two successful per-variant executions above; the stale "not producible in this checkout" note is retracted.

## Before/After

- **Before**: `{ action: "update.status" }` was outside the tool's action enum in both variants, so the tool boundary rejected it and an agent could only schedule updates, never read their state. The captured "before" is structural — the four-action / five-action enums on `origin/main` — because a live pre-patch build capture would require reverting the patch on a second host.
- **After**: the same call forwards to the canonical `update.status` RPC and returns `{sentinel, updateAvailable, effectiveChannel, schedule}` in both the full variant (6-action enum) and the restricted variant (4-action enum), with `schedule.install.git.currentSha` matching this checkout's HEAD.
- **Boundary**: the action is enumerated in the Zod schema (`stringEnum`), not a free-form method passthrough, so an unknown action still fails tool-input validation before any Gateway call is made — the enum is closed and the new action is an explicit addition, visible in the two enum dumps above.

prs.title: feat(research): show a quiet research card in the chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194780 removed the Deep research chat card so the side panel was the only entry point, with a redesigned card to follow. Without it, a `deep_research` call in the chat shows only a text summary, which never updates as the research progresses.

This brings the card back as one quiet row that matches the other cards in the chat. It builds on Josh Lehman's (@jalehman) original card from #194780 and credits him as co-author. The design was picked by Vyctor from three prototypes rendered in the real chat.

## User Impact

When the agent starts or resumes research, a card appears in the conversation at that tool call:

- **Title:** the research question, two lines at most.
- **Detail line:** the current step while running ("Gathering evidence (round 1)"); otherwise the outcome ("Report ready", "Partial report", "Paused", "Cancelling", "Failed"…). After that come the counts: sources, findings and open gaps.
- **Actions:** **Read report** (or **View progress** before a report exists), plus a quiet Cancel or Resume when allowed.

Only failures add color. The search icon pulses gently while research runs, but not when the user has reduced motion turned on. The line above the card now says "Started deep research" (or "Resumed…"). Before, it repeated the state at call time, so it could say "running" next to a finished card. On narrow screens the actions and counts wrap whole; no count is ever split. The side panel still works on its own, from Explore panels.

## Changes

- Restore the `research-job` inline view, version 1: the backend descriptor, the `api.inlineView` result on start/resume, and the browser registration. The whole result stays under the existing 24 KB limit.
- Fixes for the three findings ClawSweeper raised on Josh's original card:
  - **Errors show on the card.** A rejected Cancel/Resume, or a failed first read, appears as a line on the card instead of failing silently.
  - **Import through the API barrel.** The view contract now comes from the plugin's `api.ts`, not `src/`, which fixes the boundary check.
  - **Read report opens the report.** It opens the panel on the **Report** tab, and View progress opens **Progress**. A one-time tab request is handed from the card to the panel.
- Card views use the research client in a mode that never touches the panel's saved pending-start state, so a card can't clear a start the panel is recovering.
- Header controls and the session-menu action stay removed.

## Evidence

**Before:** Josh's original card from #194780, which was removed before landing.

![Before: original card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d7382b5-ecb4-470b-8a94-d4ccb6c93316)

**After** (real native plugin bundle in the Control UI chat, mock Gateway):

Running:

Report ready:
![Report ready, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05ba8022-a42d-4f96-afbf-12e5ce162d8f)

Cancelling:
![Cancelling, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a823460d-2452-4bfb-a3b3-fa4cfde4f2fd)

Failed:
![Failed, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f14c0863-d4dc-4f21-83c4-0491464d29a0)

Paused (light):
![Paused, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f8d65c5-518b-456c-8986-d72bf3acda50)

Partial report (light):
![Partial, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b545088f-1499-455a-9a56-a5860f83ea3e)

Mobile, 390 px (running, ready):
![Mobile running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e481286-abd3-4f1e-be6e-c199bee2a4d4)
![Mobile ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eb14dd0-d443-4f5e-8801-7ebbd2823817)

I captured running, cancelling, paused, partial, ready and failed in dark and light at desktop width and in dark at 390 px, and inspected every capture.

Tests and review:
- `ui/src/e2e/deep-research-plugin.e2e.test.ts`: 3/3 pass. The card scenario checks:
  - a failed first read shows an alert;
  - the running step appears in the status;
  - a rejected Cancel shows its error and stays retryable;

prs.title: fix: avoid worktree preparation waits behind shared ref writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: preparing a managed worktree can wait behind an unrelated repository ref writer while fetching missing file contents.

## User Impact

Worktree preparation can hydrate missing objects concurrently with removal's recovery-ref publication. Shared ref changes remain ordered. No config, schema, retention, or recovery-format change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hydration already uses private Git metadata, shares only the object store, and disables tags, pruning, FETCH_HEAD and automatic maintenance. Its caller nevertheless replaced the private transport's queue with the source repository's shared ref queue. Removing that override also removes one Git path-resolution subprocess per hydration.

This follows removal fix #199777. Read-only production timing separates the concerns: the supplied slow preparations already used warm btrfs templates (318–395 ms application, about 2 ms provisioning); base refresh and hydration dominated. This fixes demonstrated unnecessary serialization, not all remote-fetch latency. Existing template reuse and freshness policy stay intact.

## Evidence

The real capacity/worker regression times out on parent ea8cc3372de434a1876ab4d0925941d0befebfa4 while a shared ref writer is held. The candidate completes hydration with the writer still held and preserves shared refs. Cancellation and revoked authority remain checked before transport starts.

Performance acceptance, recorded before measurement: use a synthetic 65,000-file, 1.20 GB Git tree with 600,000 unrelated historical blobs, 2,401 additional refs and one missing target blob. Run 20 interleaved A/B pairs and 20 A/A pairs with a modeled 3,000 ms held shared writer, plus matched uncontended controls. Report median/p90/p95 owner wall and process CPU, native Git CPU, allocation and subprocess counts. Require identical checkout bytes and acquired objects; candidate hydration must overlap the held writer, with no CPU/allocation regression beyond matched control spread. Separately report real service creation stages (cold and matching warm templates) on the same 65k tree; those local file:// results do not reproduce production network or btrfs latency. Do not interpret waiting as CPU.

Focused proof: 98 passing tests and two platform skips across capacity, base-ref and git-exec. Codex autoreview P0–P2 is scoped-clean against the parent, with full transport/queue/worker context. Production LOC -10; no UI import boundary changed.

`pnpm check:changed --base ea8cc3372de434a1876ab4d0925941d0befebfa4` passes all gates except inherited dead-code exports. Exact-parent replay reproduces all nine production and seven full-tree findings, with zero candidate-only entries. State-upgrade exports originate at ef930ebbad771ae219e033f8c5b59a12b5445ffb; the rollback test helper at e4a30936bb35bc5a3e01a674ed3e43c98945d0aa (#198268). These are observed main regressions, not noise. Parent graph discovery also reports five additional voice type exports; no claim that this patch fixes them.

Exact-head CI [43780560576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43780560576) passed on bf7c8ca7f76a6ff2a60b3b5b846ebd2f8e1c9a3d. All 160 owner samples and 40 real service creations passed object/ref/checkout verification. The declared contention/control rule is met: candidate owner medians improve and tails remain within A/A variation. Final ClawSweeper evidence review remains required before native landing.

The native-worker regression completes hydration while its shared writer is still held, then verifies every requested object and identical `show-ref`; cancellation and revocation cases preserve admission checks ([capacity.test.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf7c8ca7f76a6ff2a60b3b5b846ebd2f8e1c9a3d/src/agents/worktrees/capacity.test.ts#L283)). This is the real capacity/worker/native-Git boundary, not a substitute Git implementation. The held-writer benchmark and per-command native receipts exercise the same isolated transport, with unchanged refs and exactly one object fetched on every sample.

<details>
<summary>20-pair owner measurements and CPU interpretation</summary>

### Owner performance (20 samples per arm)

All 160 successful samples are retained: 20 A/A pairs and 20 interleaved A/B pairs in each of the held-writer and zero-hold conditions. Nearest-rank p90/p95, medians of central values. Every sample acquired exactly one missing object, preserved shared refs, and returned the same 1,331,200,000-byte checkout budget for the 65,000-file / 1,198,080,000-byte tree. Both arms used frozen owner overlays through the same loader. Node interval CPU excludes Git children; native Git CPU includes local file:// server children.

|Hold|Arm|n|Wall median/p90/p95 ms|Process CPU ms|Git CPU ms|Allocated MB|Git commands|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|3000|AA-a|20|3260.52/3366.43/3713.85|381.92/480.33/491.01|420.00/1060.00/1410.00|38.81/40.14/40.29|[14]|
|3000|AA-b|20|3321.79/4549.64/5338.54|423.85/949.80/952.93|460.00/1930.00/2050.00|39.33/42.69/43.79|[14]|

|3000|AB-b|20|741.57/1268.88/1963.14|56.59/59.93/63.02|440.00/740.00/850.00|33.64/35.48/37.98|[13]|
|0|AA-a|20|726.41/2274.60/3158.25|129.40/440.25/463.75|380.00/1600.00/2200.00|67.69/71.46/71.48|[13]|
|0|AA-b|20|726.88/1713.17/1996.66|130.90/361.50/385.80|380.00/750.00/790.00|67.34/70.85/71.22|[13]|

Held-writer wall median improves 77.46%. Uncontended median wall improves 1.48%, Node CPU 0.65%, allocation 0.75%; those small ordinary-path changes should be read as steady rather than a large CPU win. All candidate p90/p95 metrics remain inside their corresponding A/A ceilings. Native Git CPU has a visible +15 ms uncontended median (335→350 ms), and the held-writer native p95 rises 580→850 ms; neither is hidden. The worst candidate's native CPU is concentrated before the changed hydration branch (HEAD resolution 460 ms + first tree-size scan 580 ms, out of 1450 ms). The same unchanged commands spike in A/A (native maximum 2820 ms). No additional object or command work appears. This is not an explanation of CPU by waiting.

Git subprocesses per ordinary owner invocation: **13→12**. The held-writer fixture additionally performs one untimed common-directory probe to admit its synthetic predecessor, so raw receipts show 14→13 there. The fixture's 3,000 ms hold models queue contention, not production network latency. Source interval CPU in that case is not a whole-process lifetime CPU claim.

The parser initially expected JSON to be the last stdout line. The first successful candidate emitted a late diagnostic after JSON; its saved successful sample was recovered and verified, without rerunning it. The parser now selects the unique JSON record. Source/committed workload remained frozen.

Reproduce setup: `python3 scripts/perf/worktree-hydration-fixture.py <fixture> --files 65000 --extra-refs 2401`. For each fresh seed copy, run `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-size-measure.ts --repo <copy> --hydration-base-file <frozen-owner.ts> --ref-writer-hold-ms <3000-or-0>`. Use the exact parent and candidate object-hydration.ts files; capture native Git time and trace receipts. A/A loads the parent for both labels. Setup/imports/verification are outside timed owner work; load1 spans about 16–75 across this shared-host run. No production data, gc, repack, network service, agent DB, or btrfs result is simulated.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Real service creation stages on the same 65k-file fixture</summary>

Five interleaved A/B pairs plus five A/A pairs, two creations per process: cold template then matching warm template. All 40 creations verify HEAD and clean tracked contents. This source harness deliberately drains workers between creations; worker startup dominates source/admission phases, unlike the warm production process. Prewarm refill is outside creation timing and reported separately. No p95 is inferred from five samples.

These ordinary service timings are steady within the controls, not a claimed general creation speedup. Cold wall rises 1.83% and process CPU 5.71%; warm main allocation rises 5.35%, all disclosed. The cold rise accompanies pre-hydration startup phases (+516 ms source/admission wall) before the changed branch; no operation or object work was added. A/A cold wall ranges 17.83–64.92 s and CPU 8.94–20.79 s; warm wall 8.55–23.46 s and CPU 7.33–12.79 s. A/A main allocation ranges 277.50–313.68 / 285.28–312.18 MB cold and 48.69–55.76 / 48.27–53.44 MB warm. All successful samples remain included, including one slow control whose 30-second default-base freshness elapsed before its warm creation (nine extra metadata calls, still zero fetch/full checkout).

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-creation-measure.ts --repo <fresh-seed-copy> --output <new-output> --samples 2 --default-base --prewarm`, selecting frozen sparse source overlays through `OPENCLAW_BENCH_BASELINE_DIR` for both arms. prs.title: fix(templates): CLI cannot resume an agent kept by a failed Add
prs.body:
Closes #198558

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the CLI cannot continue a Template agent that Gateway Add kept after a later step failed. Rerunning `openclaw templates add <source> --agent-id <id>` is refused as a state conflict, and the failure output does not say how to continue.

## User Impact

After a failed Gateway Add keeps the agent, `openclaw templates add <source> --agent-id <id>` continues setup in the same agent and conversation, and the failure output names that command. A plain rerun still adds a new copy, and `--agent-id` on any other existing agent is still refused.

The rerun resumes only the Template version the first Add resolved. If the catalog's latest version changed in between, the rerun is refused with the existing conflict message and the kept agent is left as it was.

## Why This Change Was Made

`templates.add.apply` already resumes a kept agent through `readRetainedTemplateInitialization`. `templates.add.plan` did not know about it and reported `agent_id_collision`, so the CLI stopped before apply. The Add review now asks the same owner whether the requested agent ID is a kept agent pending for this exact source and, if so, plans it the way apply does. No new option, protocol field, or state; `gateway-add-apply.ts` is untouched.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

`applyTemplateAddForGateway` admits the agent before it resolves the source (`src/templates/gateway-add-apply.ts:137-266`) and returns `partial` with `initializationPending` when a later step fails (`:667`). On a retry it accepts an existing agent ID when the main session holds a matching pending initialization (`:174-203`), then plans with that agent's config entry removed and its workspace passed as `admittedWorkspace` (`:115-133`).

`planTemplateAddForGateway` (`src/templates/gateway-add-plan.ts:156`) planned against the unmodified config, so the kept agent produced `agent_id_collision`, `workspace_collision` and `configured_access_unavailable`. The CLI exits on any blocker (`src/cli/templates-cli.gateway-add.ts:68`). The Control UI is unaffected because its Retry reuses the original review and never sends `agentId` to `templates.add.plan`.

Retained admission came in with #196392, whose description says failures keep "that exact agent/chat for explicit retry". The CLI moved to Gateway Add in #196431 without a way to make that retry.

Verification still happens in apply under its leases; the review only stops blocking a target apply would accept. A non-matching agent (no pending initialization, another source or version, changed config or workspace) falls through to the same blockers as before.

</details>

## Evidence

Built `main` (3588c0514ac) and this branch, started a real Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`) with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and drove it with the shipped CLI. A local stand-in for the ClawHub registry (`OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL`) serves one Template and can return 503 for the archive download during apply; a local OpenAI-compatible stub answers Add's opening turn. Both trees ran the same script.

- Main: after the failed Add keeps `symtpl`, `templates add symtpl --agent-id symtpl` exits 1 with the state-conflict lines. The kept agent stays unnamed and never set up.
- This branch: the failed Add prints `Rerun with --agent-id symtpl to continue its setup.` and that rerun prints `Added agent: symtpl`, exit 0. The session ID of `agent:symtpl:main` is the same before and after.
- Restart: a second kept agent (`drift`) is resumed after the Gateway is restarted, again with the same session ID.
- Newer version: while `drift` is kept at 0.1.0 and the registry reports 0.2.0 as latest, the rerun is refused on both trees. Nothing is switched to 0.2.0.
- Still refused on both trees: `--agent-id symtpl-2` (a completed agent) and `--agent-id main`.
- Unchanged: a plain rerun still allocates the next ID (`Added agent: symtpl-2`). On main it ran while `symtpl` was still kept, on this branch after `symtpl` had been resumed.
- Main only: `templates.add.apply` over raw RPC with the review taken before the failure completes `drift` with the same session, which shows the review was the only thing in the way.

Tests: `pnpm test src/templates/gateway-add-pending.test.ts src/cli/templates-cli.state-owner.test.ts src/templates/gateway-add-plan.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add-authority.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes (96 tests). The two changed files take 50 s together at `--maxWorkers=1`; `gateway-add-pending.test.ts` already dominated that on main. With only the tests applied to main, the three kept-agent cases in `gateway-add-pending.test.ts` (failure at source download, at runtime publication, and at config write) fail on the collision blockers, and the CLI case fails on the old message. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, targeted oxlint, format check and `git diff --check` pass. Net test lines +33 (ratchet OK).

Production delta +34/-4; test delta +34/-1; docs +6/-2.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous refusal with no state or config migration. Blast radius is `templates.add.plan` requests that name an existing agent ID, which among the bundled clients only `openclaw templates add --agent-id` sends.

<details>
<summary>Main (RED)</summary>

The one-line `[ClawHub Security Audit notice ...]` stands for the boxed trust notice the CLI prints.


prs.title: fix(gateway): allow first database creation during session discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat requests failing with `SQLite database path identity changed` when an agent's first database is created during session discovery.

## User Impact

First-use session discovery can read the newly created database without rejecting its earlier absence. No configuration, schema, migration, or user action is required.

A separate Bun `SESSION_MUTATION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED` failure remains unresolved; this PR does not claim to repair it.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197510 moved ordinary Gateway lookup to worker preparation that captures an absent-file identity before the existing worker waits for pending database creation. Legitimate first creation then invalidates that premature identity. Ordinary lookup now selects the existing `captureIdentity: false` mode, restoring its prior path-custody contract. The actual row reader still owns the opened file's generation; mutation, placement, cold-storage, and retained-plan checks remain intact.

Production code grows by one line to select that existing mode at the lookup boundary. One regression adds 38 test lines and forces real first creation between preparation and discovery.

## Evidence

- Hourly run [43763625500](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763625500), source `ce25df37`, reported this identity failure on Bun. The unchanged xAI Gateway case also reproduced it under Node in 45.543 s.
- Deterministic real-worker regression fails on the parent with the exact error (2.101 s), passes with only the pre-#197510 lookup restored (1.510 s), and passes with this fix under Node (1.883 s) and Bun (6.555 s). The unchanged original Node xAI case passes all scenarios (42.315 s).
- Protected candidate/absence/replacement/alias checks: 14/14 on each runtime. Existing default-fallback creation/replacement checks: 2/2 on each runtime. Focused browser history test and real-Gateway synthetic-provider failure/reload E2E pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 39b066a976970b080df4b107b8ba918e250d4f4e --timed`: all stages pass except 12 production / 8 full-tree unused exports. Both exact-parent A/A controls report identical lists. State exports were introduced by #198389 and fixed by #199847; member-welcome exports were introduced by #198491 and fixed by #199789. These are real main regressions already repaired separately.
- Isolated Codex autoreview of the complete local change against `39b066a976970b080df4b107b8ba918e250d4f4e`, through P2: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. The committed change preserves that reviewed snapshot.

Synthetic owner measurements use a real allocated 35 GiB SQLite database, 5,000 sessions, and 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.116 GB. The existing qualification owner runs five counterbalanced samples per variant, 3,000 operations each, with separate A/A controls and sampled JS allocation. Candidate census stays equal; premature identity captures fall from one to zero per operation.

| Per-operation median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| APFS wall / CPU | 41.87 / 46.59 µs | 21.18 / 25.08 µs |
| APFS sampled JS allocation | 18,079 B | 12,432 B |
| Linux btrfs wall / CPU | 15.132 / 20.279 µs | 8.150 / 12.786 µs |
| Linux btrfs sampled JS allocation | 15,985 B | 10,950 B |

APFS A/A controls: wall 43.71/41.80 µs, CPU 49.19/46.21 µs, allocation 18,129/18,334 B. Linux A/A spreads: 1.94% wall, 11.94% CPU, 0.15% allocation. Linux uses a task-owned btrfs loop image on ext4, 8 CPUs/16 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1. These are qualification-owner mode comparisons, not Gateway throughput or native-allocation claims. No production data was copied.

The original Bun xAI case fails before and after this fix with the separate authorization error. An error-path diagnostic traced it to a pending agent-database registry publication during retained authorization; the guard originates in #163030, but the regression's introducing commit and failing publication owner are still unknown. Later diagnostic passes do not establish a fix. All temporary instrumentation was removed. This unresolved local failure is retained as investigated evidence and is not an inherited-CI exception; exact-head CI remains required.

<details>
<summary>Existing before/after terminal evidence</summary>

These are excerpts from the already-completed canonical `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` invocations with explicit `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` or `bun` and `--maxWorkers=1`. Temporary synthetic paths are redacted. The committed head is byte-identical to the tested candidate.

Unchanged real-Gateway xAI case, Node, parent:

```text
× |gateway-server-isolated| src/gateway/server.xai-fallback.test.ts > chat.send preserves xAI rejection priority and recovers statusless failures 45543ms
  → Error: SQLite database path identity changed: <synthetic-state>/agents/fallback/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
Tests  1 failed (1)
```

Same unchanged real-Gateway case, Node, candidate:

```text
✓ |gateway-server-isolated| src/gateway/server.xai-fallback.test.ts > chat.send preserves xAI rejection priority and recovers statusless failures 42315ms
Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Deterministic first-creation regression, parent Node then candidate Node/Bun:

```text
× |gateway-database-workers| src/gateway/session-utils-store-lookup.test.ts > global session lookup ownership > reads a first database created during target discovery 2101ms
  → SQLite database path identity changed: <synthetic-state>/agents/cold/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
✓ |gateway-database-workers| src/gateway/session-utils-store-lookup.test.ts > global session lookup ownership > reads a first database created during target discovery 1883ms
✓ |gateway-database-workers| src/gateway/session-utils-store-lookup.test.ts > global session lookup ownership > reads a first database created during target discovery 6555ms
```
