prs.title: fix(templates): second Template Add blocked once its MCP env var is set
prs.body:
Closes #198541

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: adding the same Template a second time reports `mcp_server_collision` when its MCP server uses an environment reference such as `STATUSPAGE_TOKEN: "${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"` and that variable is set.

## User Impact

A Template that declares an MCP secret the documented way can be added again after the secret is configured: Add reuses the matching shared MCP server and creates another agent. `openclaw templates add`, `templates add --dry-run`, and `templates dev` all stop reporting the false conflict. A Template whose declaration really differs is still blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Template Add now compares a manifest's MCP server with the server as the config file declares it, using the `authoredConfig` that `listConfiguredMcpServers` already returns (`openclaw mcp doctor` reads the same field). No new option, helper, or state.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

A manifest keeps `${VAR}` references. On main, planning (`src/templates/lifecycle.ts:569`), install (`src/templates/mcp.ts:58`), and rollback (`src/templates/mcp.ts:124`) digest it against `listConfiguredMcpServers().mcpServers`, which comes from the config after environment substitution. With the variable unset the placeholder survives substitution and the digests match; once it is set they differ.

The four places that feed existing servers into planning (`templates add`, `templates dev`, and the Gateway `templates.add.plan` / `templates.add.apply` handlers) and the install and rollback reads now use the authored entry. Rollback still passes the substituted entry as `expectedServer`, because the config writer compares that argument against substituted values.

The comparison came in with #102406, whose description says exact declarations are reused and `${ENV_VAR}` references are preserved, so matching by declaration is the intended behavior. The existing reuse test (`src/templates/schema.test.ts:712`) passes the manifest's own server object as the existing config, and `src/templates/mcp.test.ts` uses literal servers, so substitution never ran in tests.

</details>

## Evidence

Built `main` (6d5e2dfb1b8) and this branch, then ran the shipped CLI (`pnpm openclaw`) with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. A local OpenAI-compatible stub answers Add's opening turn; nothing else is stubbed. The Template is the MCP example from `docs/cli/templates.md`.

- Main, `STATUSPAGE_TOKEN` set after the first Add: `templates add --dry-run`, `templates dev`, and `templates add` each exit 1 with `mcp_server_collision`. Same result when the variable is set before the first Add.
- This branch, same commands: all exit 0, `envmcp-2` is created, `openclaw mcp list` shows one `statuspage`, and `openclaw.json` still holds `"${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"`.
- Control, both trees: with the variable unset the second Add plans with no blockers.
- Control, both trees: a Template that declares `${OTHER_STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}` for the same server, with both variables set to the same value, is still blocked.

<details>
<summary>Main (RED), trimmed to the commands and result lines</summary>

```
$ export STATUSPAGE_TOKEN=dummy-value
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp --dry-run
Agent: envmcp-2
MCP servers: 1
  MCP statuspage: npx --yes @acme/statuspage-mcp@1.0.0
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates dev <run>/proj/envmcp
Template dev preview: envmcp@0.1.0
Agent: envmcp-2
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp
Agent: envmcp-2
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
$ grep STATUSPAGE_TOKEN openclaw.json
          "STATUSPAGE_TOKEN": "${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>This branch (GREEN) and the different-reference control, trimmed the same way</summary>

```
$ export STATUSPAGE_TOKEN=dummy-value
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp --dry-run
Template add preview: envmcp@0.1.0
Agent: envmcp-2
MCP servers: 1
  MCP statuspage: npx --yes @acme/statuspage-mcp@1.0.0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates dev <run>/proj/envmcp
Template dev preview: envmcp@0.1.0
Agent: envmcp-2
Blocked actions: 0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp
Added agent: envmcp-2
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-envmcp-2
[exit 0]

$ export OTHER_STATUSPAGE_TOKEN=dummy-value
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/otherref --dry-run
Agent: envmcp-3
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]

$ openclaw mcp list
OpenClaw-managed MCP servers (<run>/state/openclaw.json):
- statuspage
$ grep STATUSPAGE_TOKEN openclaw.json
          "STATUSPAGE_TOKEN": "${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"
```

</details>

Tests:

- `src/cli/templates-cli.state-owner.test.ts` (real config loading): `templates add --dry-run` plans without blockers for an existing `${VAR}` server once the variable is set.
- `src/templates/mcp.test.ts` (real config loading): install reuses the server, a different reference with the same value is rejected, and rollback removes the Template-introduced server.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts` (planner mocked): the `templates.add.plan` and `templates.add.apply` handlers hand the planner the authored entry, not the substituted one.
- With only the production lines reverted, `pnpm test` on those three files: 4 failed (2 failed, 28 passed in the Gateway file; 2 failed, 23 passed in the other two). On this branch: 55 passed.
- `pnpm test` over the touched files and their consumers (Template planning, Gateway Add handlers, Template and MCP CLI, MCP config): 12 files, 258 tests pass. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, targeted oxlint and format, and `git diff --check` pass.

Gaps:

- The Gateway `templates.add.plan` / `templates.add.apply` handlers were not driven live: they accept only ClawHub or bundled sources, and no bundled Template declares an MCP server. The handler test above covers the two changed lines with the planner mocked. Both handlers read the same `listConfiguredMcpServers` result as the CLI; it builds a fresh snapshot per call (`src/config/io.runtime.ts:314`), and a snapshot of an existing valid config always carries `authoredConfig` (`src/config/io.snapshot.ts:282`).
- The rollback comparison is covered by the test only. Add rolls MCP servers back only before the workspace is exposed and the agent config is committed (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:414`), and it installs them after both (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:665`), so the CLI does not reach it with an installed server. The line changed so all three comparisons use the same entry.

Production delta +9/-7; test delta +69/-2 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; no config, state, or schema change, and reverting restores the prior behavior. Blast radius is Template Add and dev planning plus MCP install when an existing `mcp.servers` entry contains a `${VAR}` reference whose variable is set. An authored escaped literal (`$${VAR}`) no longer matches a Template's `${VAR}` reference.


## Maintainer integration and current validation

Integrated this fix with the landed shared Template Add request owners used by Gateway RPCs and the setup helper. Both planning callbacks select authored MCP declarations. The shared permission, request-lifetime, consent, admission, rollback, and non-mutating preview-error behavior remains intact, along with MCP timeout normalization.

Validation on the refreshed candidate:

- 71 tests across four files pass: production setup-helper composition (12 scenarios), Gateway Add handlers, CLI state ownership, and MCP installation/rollback.
- Core type checking, formatting and scoped lint for all seven changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Separately, 83 tests across five files passed on the signed source correction before baseline integration, including authority and inference invariants. These stages overlap; the counts are not unique combined coverage.

The original isolated CLI before/after traces above remain the behavior evidence for the unchanged authored-declaration fix. No new live Gateway/model conversation is claimed. Fresh CI and security checks for the exact published head are required before landing.

prs.title: fix(templates): bundled dependency errors omit the entry and the reason
prs.body:
Closes #198753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `templates validate` reports every bundled `skills` / `plugins` failure at `$.skills` or `$.plugins` with no index, and three common mistakes get a misleading reason: a missing folder prints a raw `ENOENT` with an absolute path, a folder under `node_modules` is called "not package-relative", and an invalid skill name prints only "Invalid skill slug: pdf_tools".

## User Impact

Each bundled-dependency error now names the entry (for example `$.skills[1].path`) and says what to change: the folder does not exist, `.git` and `node_modules` folders are excluded, or the `SKILL.md` name or folder name may use only letters, digits and hyphens. Which Templates are accepted is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Index: `readTemplateManifestFile` reported every bundled failure at the collection (`src/templates/reader.ts:485-490`). It now looks up the entry's index the way the Add planner does (`src/templates/lifecycle.ts:423`) and reports `$.<collection>[i].path`.
- Excluded folders: `snapshotTemplateDependencyDirectory` (`src/templates/dependency-directory.ts:28-36`) folded the `.git` / `node_modules` exclusion into the "package-relative" check. It now reuses its own `excluded` helper for a separate message.
- Missing folder: `assertNoSymlinkParents` with `allowMissing: false` threw the raw filesystem error. It now allows a missing target (it still checks every existing parent) and the `lstat` right after reports a missing folder by its package-relative path.
- Skill name: `inspectTemplateBundledSkill` keeps the native fallback from the `SKILL.md` name to the folder name, and explains the rule only when both are invalid.

## Evidence

Ran `pnpm openclaw templates validate` on `main` (93fdc3d9ada) and on this branch with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, using the issue's three inputs (each folder has a valid `SKILL.md` unless noted) and a valid control.

```
# main
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2a     # skills: [skills/ok, skills/missing], second folder absent
ERROR bundled_dependency_invalid $.skills: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '<run>/d2a/skills/missing'
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2b     # skills: [node_modules/a]
ERROR bundled_dependency_invalid $.skills: Bundled dependency path must be package-relative.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2c     # skills: [skills/pdf_tools], SKILL.md name: pdf_tools
ERROR bundled_dependency_invalid $.skills: Invalid skill slug: pdf_tools
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2ok    # skills: [skills/ok, skills/pdf-tools]
Valid Template project: <run>/d2ok
[exit 0]

# this branch
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2a
ERROR bundled_dependency_invalid $.skills[1].path: Bundled dependency folder skills/missing does not exist.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2b
ERROR bundled_dependency_invalid $.skills[0].path: Bundled dependency path must not be inside a .git or node_modules folder.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2c
ERROR bundled_dependency_invalid $.skills[0].path: Bundled skill skills/pdf_tools needs a SKILL.md name or folder name that uses only letters, digits and hyphens.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/d2ok
Valid Template project: <run>/d2ok
[exit 0]
```

Tests: a new table case in `src/templates/project.bundled.test.ts` validates a project whose second skill entry is each of the three inputs and expects exactly one diagnostic at `$.skills[1].path` with the new reason. All three rows fail with main's reader and directory snapshot. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/templates/project.bundled.test.ts src/templates/project.test.ts src/templates/reader.test.ts src/cli/templates-cli.project.test.ts src/templates/bundled-plugin.preflight.test.ts src/plugins/templates-bundled.test.ts src/templates/packages.preflight-inspection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes (71 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, format check, `git diff --check` and the test-line ratchet (+28) pass.

Production delta +28/-15; test delta +28/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; message and path changes only, no state or config. Blast radius is diagnostics for invalid bundled `skills` / `plugins` entries. #198812 and #198818 also add a case to `project.bundled.test.ts`; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

Closes #198747

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Template whose `agent.identity.avatar` differs from its `workspace.files` destination only by backslashes or letter case (for example `Avatars\Bot.png` for `avatars/bot.png`) validates and adds cleanly, but the agent shows no avatar.

## User Impact

The added agent's config now stores the declared workspace path, so the avatar resolves. Templates whose avatar already matches the destination exactly are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest check (`src/templates/schema.ts:552-563`) matches the avatar to a destination through `portableTemplatePathKey` (backslashes to slashes, lowercase), which is the right test for a portable Template. The value itself was never mapped to the match, and `resolveLocalAgentAvatarPath` (`src/agents/identity-avatar-file.ts:52`) resolves the stored string literally. The manifest schema now ends with a transform that replaces a matched local avatar with the declared `workspace.files` path, so every consumer of the parsed manifest gets the same path the installer writes. The avatar resolver and the match itself are unchanged.

## Evidence

Ran the offline CLI (`pnpm openclaw templates ...`, Gateway stopped) on `main` (e3f1538c6e1) and on this branch with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, Templates enabled in Labs, and a local OpenAI-compatible stub for Add's opening turn. Each fixture ships a 1x1 PNG at `assets/bot.png`, declares it at `avatars/bot.png`, and differs only in `identity.avatar`. `openclaw agents list --json` reports the resolved avatar through `resolveAgentAvatarUrlFromSource`.

- Main, `'Avatars\Bot.png'`: config stores `"Avatars\\Bot.png"`, the file is at `avatars/bot.png`, and `agents list --json` reports no avatar for the agent.
- This branch, same Template: config stores `"avatars/bot.png"` and `agents list --json` returns `identityAvatarUrl` as a PNG data URL.
- Case-only `Avatars/Bot.png`: stored as written on main and as `avatars/bot.png` here. It resolves on both trees on macOS only because APFS is case-insensitive; on a case-sensitive filesystem the main value would not resolve. I did not run it on one.

prs.title: fix(gateway): let delegated OpenClaw changes work from CLI-backend agents
prs.body:
Related: #136036, #137017

## What Problem This Solves

Delegated `openclaw.chat` calls from CLI/subprocess and worker harnesses failed with `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`. Fully in-process agents retained the ambient caller identity, but harness tool calls crossed the Gateway WebSocket boundary, where that process-local identity is intentionally unavailable.

## User Impact

CLI and worker-harness delegated calls retain their signed source ownership and approval guard, including when optional wire delegation metadata is absent. Existing run, tool-abort and worker-lifetime fencing remains fail-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

The approval gate only consulted the process-local Gateway tool caller identity. OpenClaw already has a host-minted, HMAC-signed `agentRuntimeIdentityToken` for trusted cross-process calls, including the exact admitted run authority and worker turn claim, but `openclaw.chat` was not included in that transport.

The first revision attempted to mint replacement authority from the delegated session id. Review identified that as unsafe. The signed-identity revision then exposed two narrower defects:

- Distinct calls in one source run receive distinct tool-bound lease claim ids. Approval reconciliation compared those claim ids, so a later call retired the original pending decision even though its exact lease was still live.
- The wire fallback retained the generic 30-second request timeout although delegated human interaction is budgeted for 900 seconds and the approval owner can wait 600 seconds before staging/application completes.

## Design

This revision carries the existing source-run authority instead of synthesizing or transferring it:

- `openclaw.chat` is eligible for the signed agent-runtime identity token.
- The host binds the exact tool abort signal into the delegated run authority before signing it.
- Explicit host-prepared Full Access is transported only for `openclaw.chat`; model-authored parameters cannot create it.
- On Gateway arrival, signed agent/runtime/session/routing facts establish delegation even when the optional wire field is omitted; model-supplied metadata cannot override or opt out of that binding.
- Ambient in-process identity remains authoritative when present. Wire calls use the verified signed runtime identity.
- Pending-approval reconciliation first validates the original exact application lease, then compares both callers' active canonical source owner plus local/worker kind and exact worker turn claim. It never replaces the authority stored on the pending record.
- The delegated wire call uses the existing 900-second human-interaction budget. The generic Gateway default remains 30 seconds, and the Codex owner retains its separate 30-second completion grace.
- Run release/replacement, original tool abort, Gateway replacement, worker-claim loss, and delegated-session replacement still fail closed.

No new configuration keys, SQLite surfaces, dependencies or retries are introduced. The existing transient signed-identity token carries an optional host-prepared Full Access fact. Existing canonical owner and human-wait helpers were sufficient.

## Security properties

- No authority is derived from a session id or model-authored delegation fields.
- The signed identity can only be minted by the host holding the local runtime-token secret.
- Full Access is a host-prepared restrict-only fact; omission never bypasses approval.
- Reuse grants observation of an existing pending decision only after its original exact application lease is revalidated.
- The original record retains its exact lease, signals, and application predicate. Closing a later sibling lease cannot transfer or cancel that authority; closing the original lease still blocks application.
- Worker authority remains bound to the canonical placement/turn claim.

## Evidence

- Published head `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` integrates GitHub-confirmed current-main conflicts against pinned upstream `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`. Preserves upstream compact delegate-test layout and PR timeout/permission/session-continuation contracts. Production authority changes merged without manual conflict; removed a now-unused moved import and compacted a local parameter name to satisfy changed-file lint. Validation passed: 91 focused authority/identity/delegate tests across five suites (55.731s wrapper), production core types and all three affected test-type shards, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, pinned-main diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets. The newly integrated cron fixture needed a true-or-undefined permission normalization in its test transport only; its affected integration suite and Gateway-method types pass after that correction. Fresh independent scoped review of the frozen production tree found no actionable P0/P1; retained for the final one-line test-adapter correction. No fresh real delayed-human transport proof, replacement-head hosted verdict, or maintainer signed-carrier acceptance is claimed.

- Prior published head `fad89b4b638381fbb5e964c5d0cade97d01b0afc` reconciles a GitHub-confirmed approval-test conflict onto pinned upstream `d1618ccd0b276f985711ff297b1b87a77bdad35d`. Upstream removed a redundant ambient-only parameter case; the later maintained cross-lease wire/ambient approval coverage remains intact. Seventeen patches replay identically; the first differs only in its upstream conflict context. Prior independent review is retained for this mechanical delta, not claimed as fresh review. All 10 local gates passed: 99 tests across five focused suites (56.058s wrapper), production core types, all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods), changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety checks. The initial lint attempt could not load the newly required eslint-plugin-solid; refreshing the isolated installation from the unchanged frozen lockfile resolved it without source or lockfile workarounds. No replacement-head hosted verdict or fresh live-runtime result is claimed. Real delayed-human-decision proof and area-owner signed-carrier acceptance remain outstanding.

- Prior published head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` addresses revision 24’s test-quality feedback: removed the synthetic delayed-decision mock test and unused fake-timer cleanup. The retained relay test verifies the requested 900-second budget and returned approval outcome. All 15 delegate-tool tests passed (`pnpm test src/agents/tools/openclaw-delegate-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 8.655s wrapper / 6.67s Vitest); affected agents-other test types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Production sources are byte-unchanged from the prior validated head, whose exact-head hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 07:13 UTC and durable revision 24 found no production defect. Those prior-head results are historical. That prior head’s hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; durable ClawSweeper revision 25 reviewed that head and reports no actionable findings, with area-owner acceptance still outstanding. No fresh independent production review or live run is claimed for this test-only deletion.
- A real human decision after 30 seconds remains unverified by the historical CLI evidence. The removed synthetic timeout test did not establish that transport behavior; the historical timeout RED/GREEN results below are synthetic test evidence only.

- Prior published `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b` reconciled a confirmed import conflict onto pinned upstream `2f1f73ccb2224bbe7d961b4c0d3b29cfdd51e7f8`. The maintained hosted-routing suite retains the delegated signed-identity case and drops an obsolete Workshop approval import removed upstream. All other patches replay unchanged; delegated authority, method-scoped Full Access and exact approval-lease intent remain unchanged. Fresh validation of the source committed as `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b`: 103 authority tests across five focused suites passed (50.477s wrapper); production core types and all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods) passed. Changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Prior independent scoped review is retained for the mechanically reconciled delta, not claimed as a fresh review. Prior 27-test URL-boundary proof is retained for the unchanged canonicalizer. No fresh live-runtime proof or replacement-head hosted CI result is claimed. Assigned-reviewer acceptance of the signed Full Access carrier remains outstanding.

Tested head: `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` (base `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`).

- Resolved current-main conflicts without changing delegated authority intent. Migrated the one PR-specific signed Full Access wire/lifetime case into the maintained hosted-routing suite; the retired baseline suite remains deleted. Preserved current-main admitted identity reconstruction and inherited permission schema.
- Omitted-delegation RED/GREEN regression: the real `openclaw.chat` handler test failed before the repair, choosing connection ownership instead of signed source ownership. The parameterized regression checks both omitted and spoofed wire metadata, signed session ownership, and delegated-only operator approval. Both regression variants pass after the repair.
- Prior published `c6ab9511e93f586626135c67633e5240db04ea32` validation: 107 tests across five focused suites passed (36.14s wrapper); production core types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap ratchet and assertion safety passed. Fresh independent review: the sole P1 concerned the old index version; the reviewer explicitly recognized this working-tree repair as addressing it and reported no other concrete P0/P1 defect. The corrected index was verified and committed. Affected Gateway-method test types: passed (exit 0).
- Prior published head `bd1287586199249975f6a268ccbf2553686ad3f0` had successful exact-head hosted CI; those are not current-candidate CI results. The earlier 27 core-test compiler shards passed with the documented aggregate-wrapper exit-124 limitation. Current validation reruns affected proof rather than claiming those prior results as fresh full coverage.
- Historical RED/GREEN timeout evidence: test-only `06648dac970` failed at the generic 30-second timeout ([red runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33936113189/job/101224617458)); `537130294ac2e1360700ab2f094df4b8e9a8b05d` passed 241 files / 5,013 tests ([green runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33936776749/job/101226276241)). These are not current-head CI results.
- The earlier real CLI proof below is historical transport evidence, not a fresh live run of this rebased candidate. No serving runtime was changed for this reconciliation. Hosted CI for prior head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; security-owner/maintainer acceptance remains an external gate.

### Earlier real CLI harness proof

Verified against a locally built Gateway through the real `openclaw agent` Codex app-server path:

1. **Active Full Access succeeds:** an admitted `finance-worker` Codex turn invoked the `openclaw` tool over the Gateway WebSocket and changed `update.checkOnStart` from `true` to `false`. The terminal receipt recorded exactly one successful `openclaw` tool call. An independent CLI read observed `false`; the test then restored and schema-validated `true`.
2. **Source abort fails closed after dispatch:** a second admitted CLI turn emitted the `openclaw` tool call, then received `SIGINT` through the CLI's same-connection abort path. The persisted tool result was `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.` and an independent CLI read remained `true`.

## Observer-cancellation ownership

Proposal-failure retirement belongs to the caller that installed the pending approval. A later same-source observer whose distinct lease closes fails its own live-authority check without clearing or force-denying the original owner's still-live approval. Original-owner cancellation remains fail-closed. The current focused approval-authority suite includes this order-sensitive regression.

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: the MCP CLI test harness forgets directories when their removal fails, so a later cleanup attempt cannot retry them.

## User Impact
No production behavior changes. Test teardown retains failed workspace cleanup and finishes attempting the other directories.

## Why This Change Was Made
Reuse the existing `cleanupTempDirs` helper inside the explicit harness cleanup. Keep allocation, the async API, caller hook ordering, mock restoration, and exit-code restoration. All five consumer suites remain: 46 declarations / 57 expanded cases. Test support changes by +2/-3 lines; production and shared helper code are unchanged. The shared helper uses synchronous removal and its existing retry policy.

This continues the maintainer-directed repository test audit recorded in `test/test-audit-ledger.md`.

## Evidence
- A controlled removal failure in an existing MCP CLI Vitest case reproduces the baseline leak: the second cleanup never retries the forgotten directory. The candidate preserves the original error and successfully retries that directory. Both remove the healthy workspace and restore home, environment, cwd, and exit code. Observations precede emergency cleanup; instrumentation was restored byte for byte.
- `pnpm test` on the five `src/cli/mcp-cli` suites (`.test.ts`, `.oauth.test.ts`, `.login-loopback.test.ts`, `.cleanup.test.ts`, and `.path-case.windows.test.ts`) with `--maxWorkers=1` passes on both versions: 56 cases passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped on macOS. Baseline wall time 106.39s; candidate 138.65s (Vitest 121.87s). These are qualification observations, not speed-comparison data.
- `pnpm test test/helpers/temp-dir.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 11 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped.
- Targeted type-aware lint, CLI test typecheck, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent preservation review found no lost contract. Full local ClawSweeper review of `a56ba88e924fad822fd8f447f1b67e82c13c6f42..278051ae1efeb57d2ebac4807532719b17180ffb` found no actionable issues. The subsequent commit records proof only.
- Exact-head [CI run 43782927363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43782927363) passed in 450 seconds. Required CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review gates passed. The Windows CI lane was skipped by the plan; the Windows-only local case remains unexecuted.

prs.title: perf(ci): reuse Knip analysis across reports
prs.body:
## Problem and solution

CI repeated Knip analysis for dependencies, unused files, and exports. Run one analysis for each existing production, full-tree, and scripts scope: seven scans become three, without changing their configurations or severity policy.

The cleanup uses Knip 6.40.0's native compact reporter instead of a new JSON validator/formatter. Existing export/file policy parsers enforce hard-zero findings (including configured warnings); Knip owns dependency severity. Native stdout and stderr remain on their original streams. The process owner still handles timeout, output bounds, UTF-8 and cleanup; a third duplicate combined-output buffer is gone. Frozen targets opt in only when their own package command advertises this complete report; existing public commands remain available.

## Simplification and size

Against the current merge base `5b750071d1d31b2af9c8d2e58d0f65da010845dc`:

| Category | Before cleanup at 7bb4e94 | Current de8de8b |
|---|---:|---:|
| Implementation/workflows | +155 / -14 = **+141** | +106 / -19 = **+87** |
| Tests | +182 / -8 = **+174** | +116 / -14 = **+102** |

Cleanup reduces the previous revision by **54 production lines and 72 test lines net**. Removes the JSON shape validator, category renderer and 77 lines of parser-specific tests. Keeps compact boundary tests for actual child-process failures, hard-zero warnings, stream separation, and parallel admission.

## Proof at de8de8b

- **50 focused tests passed** through the canonical wrapper (three files, 37.29s including compiler setup). Real CLI/launcher/child-process tests cover all three scans starting before any completes; failed scans do not suppress sibling results; nonzero/empty failures and module-resolution failures reject; colored file/export warnings reject; dependency warning severity remains native.
- Root-tooling TypeScript, focused six-file lint, formatting and diff check passed. No baseline or allowance increased. The earlier 895-test workflow/package suite remains applicable to those unchanged files.
- Fresh exact-source native compact/JSON parity: all three scopes matched status and finding identities (12/12, 15/15, 0/0; no missing or added finding). The real `pnpm deadcode:report` exercised all three scans and exited 1 for the same existing export/file findings; no scanner error was hidden. Artifacts: `knip-cleanup-proof/parity.json`, `wrapper.stdout`, `wrapper.stderr`.
- Exact-head hosted ClawSweeper completed successfully: review run https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/43777498585 and terminal acknowledgement https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185851#issuecomment-6903523564 (November 16, 00:05 UTC); no posted findings. The requester waived the separate local independent-review step, not hosted review.
- Exact-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777292363 remains pending. One unrelated failure, job 133006876279, is `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.test.ts` interleaved Hermes replies (expected first reply, received second). The same assertion reproduces locally under pinned Bun (1 failed /14 passed); A2A source/test are unchanged by this PR. Recorded rather than masked or called a Knip failure. Previous-head runner-disconnection failure was a separate infrastructure incident. **Not RFR until remaining related CI gates are verified.**

## Timing: measurement versus estimate

The retained warm-cache screening pair on 32 CPUs measured **91.28s → 65.91s**, a **25.37s / 27.79%** reduction for concurrent legacy commands versus the combined command. Both correctly failed the same existing findings. The failing legacy graph short-circuited one dependency scan (six actual scans); separate parity explicitly exercised all seven. This is one sample, not a clean-CI median or whole-FRV result. Reporter cleanup preserves the three-scan execution graph; no additional timing benefit is claimed.

The dependency-check lane is not the latest observed FRV critical path. Do not add this lane reduction to the modeled Node/Bun overlap in #198278.

## Credit and scope

Original work by @vincentkoc; coordinated pickup: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185851#issuecomment-6902659754. Original commits and credit retained. No new dependency/configuration, public-command removal, merging, or release publication.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): shorten write locks during large vault scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: large Knowledge rescans reserve the SQLite writer while looking up the authors of unchanged records, delaying other writes.

## User Impact

Knowledge keeps the same revision bylines and external-edit/deletion behavior while spending less time holding the database write lock. No schema migration, configuration change, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch exact-revision attribution before `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, including the prior non-conversion writer for converted records. The commit section rereads authoritative observations and validates the prepared revision. Deletion history and tombstones use two set-based Kysely statements instead of preparing statements per missing record.

Knowledge connections now attach the existing shared statement observer through the worker SDK. Kysely alone did not fix diagnostics because this native connection had never been observed. Remaining native statements are timed too. No new data cache or competing state owner is introduced.

## Evidence

Production evidence supplied by the reliability peer: Team r337, `dd2d58be`, reported `knowledge.observe` holds of **1,756 ms at 23:55:41Z** and **1,188 ms at 00:04:43Z**. Both had zero timed statements and all callback duration in `callbackOtherMs`. The synthetic 62,000-record baseline reproduces second-long holds and that diagnostic signature; the completed serial ABBA controls reproduce and reduce that hold.

Warm synthetic 6,200-record fixture, 62,000 retained history rows, 10,000 completed mutation plans, 10% conversion chains and 10% operator-authored records. Serial ABBA, ten observations per arm:

| Arm | Median write hold | Owner elapsed / observation | CPU / observation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline A2 | 113.06 ms | 149.59 ms | 120.62 ms |
| Candidate B2 | 15.14 ms | 43.83 ms | 48.26 ms |
| Candidate B3 | 14.64 ms | 44.67 ms | 48.81 ms |
| Baseline A3 | 96.93 ms | 102.46 ms | 108.91 ms |

Database, returned-record, and edit/rename/delete/restore digests match across all four arms. prs.title: fix: older conversation drops out of the model view when screenshots fill the history byte cap
prs.body:
Related: #159799

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: older conversation silently drops out of the model's view, without any summary, when screenshot or other large tool results fill the history byte cap of an embedded session.

## User Impact

In image-heavy sessions such as computer use, an agent keeps its earlier requests, decisions and replies in context. Old screenshot bodies are replaced with omission notices instead, so token-based compaction can summarize the conversation once the context actually fills. Below the byte cap nothing changes. The stored transcript is never modified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded runtime bounds replayed history at eight bytes per context token. A stored screenshot result costs 0.25–2.5 MB of that bound but only around 1.5k model tokens, so the bound fills long before the token threshold, and older rows fall off the front of the window unsummarized. #177410 and the comments on #159799 show the same thing on several providers.

The selector already has a policy for this: `toolResultOverflow: "omit"` (#171239) replaces tool-result bodies with notices, largest first, before it drops older messages, and restores the newest bodies that fit once a prefix is dropped. Until now only settled-tool finalization used it (#184704). This change applies the policy to every caller of `resolveEmbeddedSessionContextLimits`, so ordinary attempts, recovery, and the preflight estimate all read the same model view, as the resolver's contract requires.

Accepted cost, documented in the code and in `docs/concepts/compaction.md`: above the byte cap, each newly omitted body changes the prompt prefix from that message on. Today the prefix already changes there whenever the window steps, and the dropped history is lost for good.

<details>
<summary>Scope notes</summary>

- The ordinary path already passes the limits object through: `[sessionManagerReadInitialContext]` rereads through `readSessionManagerModelContextAsync` with the manager's full `boundedContextLimits`. The session manager's own writer branch keeps its strict row read, so the truncation and rewrite paths still see real bodies.
- The `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` guard still charges raw transcript bytes. The bounded read in `compaction-transcript-bytes.ts` only locates expired runtime-context bodies to subtract, and omitted tool bodies are never in that set.
- Compaction input is unaffected; it already reads its complete window independently of the hydration cap.
- Not addressed: byte pressure that doesn't come from tool results (for example encrypted reasoning, see the no-image data point on #159799).

</details>

## Evidence

**Regression test through the ordinary entry point** (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-context-limits.test.ts`). A user goal, four `computer` screenshot results, a reply and a new prompt are opened with `SessionManager.openBoundedAsync(scope, resolveEmbeddedSessionContextLimits({ contextTokenBudget: 1_024 }))`, and then `[sessionManagerReadInitialContext]()` reads the history:

- `main` (`913e6ea2944`): fails. The history starts at the toolCall before the last screenshot, mid-turn, and the user goal is gone.
- This branch: passes. The goal, the reply, the prompt and all four tool results are present, the older bodies are notices, and the view stays within `maxBytes`.

**Focused suites, all passing** (113 tests in 11 files): `session-manager-model-context-limits`, `session-manager-bounded`, `attempt-history-prepare`, `run-embedded-agent.finalization-scope`, `settled-turn-finalization.silence`, `attempt-session-boundary`, `agent-runner-memory-transcript-context`, `agent-runner-memory.byte-preflight`, `agent-runner-memory.byte-pressure`, `harness/builtin-openclaw`, plus the new test. `pnpm check:changed` on this head: format, lint, core and core-test typecheck (all 29 graphs), and the guards pass. The only failure is the dead-export scan, which flags inherited exports in files this change doesn't touch (`src/state/*-swap.ts`, `src/state/state-upgrade*.ts`, `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/member-welcome.ts`); the base commit already has them.

**Measured on a real session** (read-only copy of a 2026.11.3 agent database, Anthropic route, 500k-token budget, 4,000,000-byte cap). One afternoon of computer use stored 189 screenshot images (about 84 MB of active branch) after a compaction. Replaying the selector newest-first:

| Run | Stored bytes (today) | Screenshot results charged as notices |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | window starts mid-turn, 47 of 743 rows | all 743 rows since the compaction, about 2.3 MB |
| 2 | 61 of 760 rows, the model got only the summary | all 760 rows |
| 3 | 88 of 787 rows | all 787 rows |

With notices the estimated prompt is about 245–260k tokens, below the session's 375k compaction threshold, so nothing would have been lost. Charging images at `IMAGE_BLOCK_TOKENS × 8` instead would only have reached back about 100 minutes and was estimated over the threshold. Details are in the comments on #159799.

prs.title: fix(ui): Secrets feedback confuses save counts and name rules
prs.body:
Related: #199116, #199414.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Secrets presents pre-error save confirmations as the final saved count, and invalid-name errors prescribe an example instead of explaining the actual rules.

## User Impact

Partial imports now identify the count as **confirmed saves before the error**, preserving the existing instruction to check the list before retrying. Name errors explain the existing 1–128-character grammar. Completed-import and runtime-warning labels also work for a count of one. Validation, write behavior, permissions and secret protection are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A write can already be saved when its runtime refresh fails. The owner counts successful responses, so zero confirmations before that error does not mean zero entries were saved. This change states the fact the owner actually knows instead of parsing error text or inferring protected values from inventory metadata.

Only four English strings change. The branch now includes current main’s read-state and confirmed-write recovery work from #199116 and #199414. That receipt-handling owner is preserved unchanged; its additional partial-count expectation was updated to the new wording.

## Evidence

- Maintainer verification integrated baseline a56ba88e924fad822fd8f447f1b67e82c13c6f42 through the native workflow. The added main consumer failed on its old text; updating that single expectation made the integrated suite pass without changing receipt handling.
- The partial-import flow replays the Gateway’s actual saved-but-runtime-refresh-failed response, receives an inventory containing the entry, and reaches Retry without a second write. This is source-backed synthetic-boundary proof, not a live secret-store mutation.
- Add and Bulk add reject invalid names without writing, retain their drafts and then save valid non-example names. The existing flow also checks a 129-character name and protected/readable/mixed entries. The longer guidance was checked at 390 px as well as desktop width.
- Fourteen focused view/page/store tests and nine public-name boundary cases agree with the UI and Gateway validators, including one, 128 and 129 characters.
- Current integrated validation with one worker: 14 store cases plus 535 standard UI canaries passed in 28.47s; all eight full built-app Secrets browser cases passed in 17.86s. They exercise dialogs, receipt/readback and reconnect behavior.
- Targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Broad checks run on the updated PR head.
- Screenshots use real components and synthetic values. Matched desktop captures are 1280 × 960; surrounding context was inspected. Before source: main 55430c2797d8e3dacc202e1a5bdbd3cc8bd3ce2c. These original matched captures remain applicable to the unchanged messages; the integrated build was tested separately as described above.

prs.title: fix(ui): expired approvals claim an execution outcome
prs.body:
Related: #199100.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an expired approval page says the operation was denied even when its configured timeout fallback can execute it. The same page also tells people a decision was recorded for expired or canceled requests that have no decision.

## User Impact

The page now says the approval request expired without a recorded decision. Terminal pages still say they can be closed, without inventing a decision. Approval policy, timeout behavior, allowed decisions, redaction and execution are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

An approval request’s terminal state is not the operation’s execution result. The Gateway can return an expired request and a null decision, while the exec owner separately applies the configured fallback. Two English strings now describe only facts known to the page. Existing approved/denied headings and descriptions retain the real decision; no new state or conditional rendering is needed.

## Evidence

- Three focused assertions fail on the original copy and pass after correction. The changed approval-page test file passes all 32 cases with one worker: 3.067 s measured command wall time, 1.41 s Vitest elapsed. CI seconds are pending.
- Another 86 focused history, presentation, card and overlay checks pass. UI and UI-test typechecks, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Two isolated exec-entry tests run a harmless fixture command for the full timeout fallback and reject it for the deny fallback. A separate Gateway handler test proves expiry is returned without a decision and settles the waiter to null. No live approval or policy was changed.
- Matched compiled-app flows cover expired and canceled requests, no decision controls/calls, and the existing Open OpenClaw link reaching Chat. A separate native settings flow confirms grants remain revocable when history fails. These flows use synthetic Gateway data, not live decisions.
- Current-main before baseline: bf51b4faeee62bdaf3a7f948160f08c94631dffe. Real components, light theme, emulated 1200 × 900 viewport; the complete card and surrounding page were inspected.

prs.title: fix(k8s): show deployment help without cluster access
prs.body:
Closes #198913

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Kubernetes deployment help failing before it prints usage when deployment tools or cluster access are unavailable.

## User Impact

Operators can read `--help` and `-h` before installing tools, configuring kubeconfig, or restoring cluster connectivity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing help branch now runs before the deployment preflight. Operational modes still require the same tools and a reachable cluster.

## Evidence

- Both help regressions fail on the base and pass with this change. All six tests in `test/scripts/k8s-deploy.test.ts` pass, including the existing teardown cases and an unreachable-cluster deletion control.
- Full-script checks with a temporary, restricted PATH reproduce missing-tool and unreachable-cluster failures on the base. Both help flags now exit 0 with usage and no tool calls. `--delete` still exits 1 in both environments. Kubernetes calls were inert stubs; no live cluster was used.
- Focused lint, the root scripts test typecheck, formatting and `/bin/bash -n scripts/k8s/deploy.sh` pass.

Validated on macOS 27.0.1, system Bash 3.2.57 and Node 26.12.1. The six-test wrapper completed in 2.30 seconds.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/k8s-deploy.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/scripts/k8s-deploy.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental
pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/scripts/k8s-deploy.test.ts
/bin/bash -n scripts/k8s/deploy.sh
```

</details>


## Full-script terminal capture

The following output comes from `/bin/bash scripts/k8s/deploy.sh` itself. For the missing-tools case, the temporary PATH contains only `dirname` and `cat`; `kubectl` and `openssl` do not exist on that PATH. For the unavailable-cluster case, both are inert executables that record calls and exit 1. Each process receives only that PATH and the temporary call-log path.

```text
BASE
missing-tools        --help   exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=0 stderr=Missing: kubectl
missing-tools        -h       exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=0 stderr=Missing: kubectl
missing-tools        --delete exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=0 stderr=Missing: kubectl
unreachable-cluster  --help   exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=1 stderr=Cannot connect to cluster. Check kubeconfig.
unreachable-cluster  -h       exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=1 stderr=Cannot connect to cluster. Check kubeconfig.
unreachable-cluster  --delete exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=1 stderr=Cannot connect to cluster. Check kubeconfig.

FIXED
missing-tools        --help   exit=0 usage=true tool_calls=0
missing-tools        -h       exit=0 usage=true tool_calls=0
missing-tools        --delete exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=0 stderr=Missing: kubectl
unreachable-cluster  --help   exit=0 usage=true tool_calls=0
unreachable-cluster  -h       exit=0 usage=true tool_calls=0
unreachable-cluster  --delete exit=1 usage=false tool_calls=1 stderr=Cannot connect to cluster. Check kubeconfig.
```

Actual stdout for both fixed help flags in both environments:

```text
Usage: ./scripts/k8s/deploy.sh [OPTION]

  (no args)        Deploy OpenClaw (creates secret from env if needed)
  --create-secret  Create or update the K8s Secret from env vars without deploying
  --show-token     Print the gateway token after deploy or secret creation
  --delete         Delete the default namespace, or resources only in a custom namespace
  --delete-resources
                  Delete OpenClaw resources from the namespace
  --delete-namespace
                  Delete the namespace and all resources in it
  -h, --help       Show this help

Environment:
  Export at least one provider API key:
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY

  OPENCLAW_NAMESPACE     Kubernetes namespace (default: openclaw)
```

The deletion controls still stop at preflight. No cluster operation is simulated as successful, and no live cluster is accessed. The base/head comparison changes only the deployment script between `b27440329b4c` and `8869e1987715`; the fixture and invocation remain identical.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): account for large authority receipt payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing authority-component byte totals when a large actor receipt changes V8 serialization size across the native worker boundary. Related: #199767.

## User Impact

Operators can account for every sampled receipt's known bytes, including large reload, prompt-projection and initial-entry results. The six fixed components now include `receipt_value`; the documented PromQL includes failed-attribution receipt samples in its denominator. No changes to authority, worker payloads, persistence or sampling frequency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Worker capture sizes the original facts, then structured-clones them. Native delivery can change packed-array encoding: the 553,033-byte fixture becomes 556,042 bytes on main, and stripping entry fields leaves a **negative 2,985-byte marginal**. Previously that discarded every component's bytes. Each receipt remainder is now bounded by its predecessor, conserving the worker-recorded total exactly. Component attribution remains approximate and shared objects belong to the last remaining reference.

A final marginal removes both the phase result and its aliased transcript append result into `receipt_value`. Serialization exceptions preserve the known total in `receipt_other` with `result="unmeasured"`. Admission behavior and the main-only 1/128 whole-operation sampling decision stay unchanged; unsampled operations do no attribution work.

Production code: **+19 net lines**. This correctness fix needs the bounded subtraction, new result component and exception accounting; it adds no second sampler, cache or configuration. Benchmark tooling: +46 lines; tests: +107 with an explicit allocation record. The requested non-test/non-doc diff totals +68 lines, including the benchmark and three-line allocation record. Author simplification pass completed; independent Codex review is delegated to the coordinating maintainer before merge under the requested workflow.

## Evidence

Node 26.12.1, local synthetic state; base `fc8363bf8b02edeca6c170fbed2fd72ae8e6c509`. All numbers below are bytes, not retained heap. Native capture/delivery regression fixtures each contain 1,024 distinct ~512-byte event records:

| Receipt shape | Worker total | Base component sum | Fixed entry | Fixed events | Fixed value | Fixed other |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| appendedEvents | 553,033 | 0 | 0 | 552,877 | 85 | 71 |
| authorityReceipts | 553,033 | 0 | 0 | 552,877 | 85 | 71 |
| append.value.reload | 553,033 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 552,962 | 71 |
| modelPromptProjection | 553,042 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 552,971 | 71 |
| entryMetadata | 553,062 | 553,062 | 552,869 | 37 | 85 | 71 |
| initialEntry | 553,052 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 552,981 | 71 |
| metadata append with reload | 553,034 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 552,963 | 71 |

Six large-shape conservation regressions fail on base; entryMetadata already worked. A separate serialization-failure regression changes accounted bytes from 0 to 524,288 and verifies that the exception cannot escape. The native delivery test asserts facts rather than serialized byte equality, since the latter incorrectly assumed that cloning preserves V8 encoding. Existing operation-level sampling and shared-entry tests remain covered.

Actual SessionManager appends also ran with a ~544 KB assistant message and synthetic skills/catalog state. The 548,938-byte receipt contains 545,606 bytes in `receipt_events`, 497 in `receipt_value`, 20 in `receipt_entry`, and 2,815 in `receipt_other`. That single-event receipt was already measured by base. The matrix above demonstrates the missing-array cases; it does **not** establish which field dominates an operator's unseen receipts.

Native replay uses AB/BA plus A/A, 8,192 warmup operations and **2,000 measured appends per arm** (4,000 per revision in the paired comparison). Separate timing and allocation passes:

| Owner measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU, normal 1/128 sampling | 55.68 µs/append | 56.91 µs/append |
| Sampled allocation, normal 1/128 sampling | 291,997 B/append | 290,661 B/append |
| Main-thread CPU, every operation sampled | 134.12 µs/append | 201.82 µs/append |

Normal-sampling CPU difference is +1.22 µs (+2.2%); the A/A control was 54.50→56.40 µs (+1.90 µs). Allocation is effectively neutral (−0.46%; A/A −0.30%). Forced sampling adds ~67.7 µs, or ~0.53 µs amortized at 1/128; the candidate's complete sampled delivery costs ~0.20 ms. Host 1-minute load was 22.16 for normal timing, ~20.10 for allocation, and 23.17–25.24 for forced sampling. This is diagnostic correctness, not a claimed speedup.

Reproduction command (run separate `timing` and `allocation` outputs; add `--sample-all` for the sampled-path bound):

```sh
git show fc8363bf8b02edeca6c170fbed2fd72ae8e6c509:src/infra/worker-message-metrics.ts > .local/worker-message-metrics.base.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-append-receipt-measure.ts \
  --output .local/receipt-measure-timing --mode timing --sessions 2 --rows 4 \
  --rounds 1 --text-repeats 32000 --authority --iterations 2000 \
  --compare-metrics-file .local/worker-message-metrics.base.ts
```

Validation: focused Node metrics tests **19 passed** (1.69 s Vitest wall); default-runtime metrics + native admission + Prometheus exporter **85 passed** (68.01 s wrapper including one-time worker preparation); changed-file oxfmt and lint passed; `pnpm tsgo:test:root` and the matching infra test typecheck passed; `git diff --check` passed. No Testbox lease, production load, or full Gateway stress campaign: the requested fast path applies to this sampled diagnostic boundary. Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43779128160) and [artifact build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43779127715) passed at `42343e93f1ddec70b2e043c7cd79f20c132421b8`, including strict test types, selected runtime tests, docs, architecture guards and lint. No CI failures or reruns. The PR remains ready and unmerged for the coordinating maintainer's independent review.

prs.title: fix(gateway): agents.update gives no billing-route warning when it moves an agent to another billing route
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197368

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `agents.update` can move an agent's model to another billing route (for example from a Claude CLI runtime's own credentials to a metered API key) without the `billingRouteWarnings` reply field and Gateway log lines that `config.set`, `config.patch` and `config.apply` give for the same change since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191326.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator or client that changes an agent's `model` or `agentRuntime` through `agents.update` now gets the same billing-route warnings as a config write: in the reply as `billingRouteWarnings`, and as warning lines in the Gateway log. Before, the write succeeded silently, so a move to metered API billing could go unnoticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191326 added the billing-route comparison to the shared config write flow. `agents.update` writes the agent entry outside that flow, so no comparison ran and its reply was `{ ok: true, agentId }` only.

- **Owner kept:** the handler now runs the same comparator on the committed write (the config before and after it) and replies and logs through the same helper as the config writes. No new comparator, reply shape or log path.
- **Protocol:** `AgentsUpdateResultSchema` declares the optional `billingRouteWarnings: string[]`, so the published result schema matches the reply. No protocol version change; the generated Swift and Kotlin models are unchanged.
- **Advisory only:** as for config writes, the warnings never block the write, and a comparison that fails logs a warning and returns no lines.
- **Docs:** `docs/gateway/configuration/config-rpc.md` now says that `agents.update` returns the same field.
- **Not changed:** `agents.create` does not return the field. The comparison only looks at model consumers present both before and after a write, so a new agent has no earlier route to compare. The Control UI and the SDK client do not render the field; this PR changes only the Gateway reply, its schema and the log.

## Evidence

### Independent CI follow-up — November 14, 2026

The original exact-head CI run [43095118341](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43095118341) was cancelled with zero jobs; it did not establish a product failure or a passing test result.

A single manual validation attempt, [43602777226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43602777226), used trusted workflow revision `9161e20e2c4c085ee4fd60bb8243b9c14bb7d38b` and checked out this PR's exact head `8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c`. The preflight log confirms candidate trust `untrusted`, cache mode `off`, and cache writes disabled. Dependency installation completed with scripts disabled.

The attempt failed before build or test execution in `Build CI manifest`: `The main validation tier requires canonical same-revision manual or scheduled validation with full scope`. This is a dispatch-contract mismatch (`validation_tier=main` on a cross-revision target), not a billing implementation failure. The trusted manifest supports `validation_tier=full` for this cross-revision path. `security-fast` passed; the relevant runtime/test jobs were skipped, so this attempt adds no independent behavioral proof. No source changes or duplicate dispatch were made to hide the failure. The author-supplied proof below remains distinct from this attempted independent validation.

The corrected exact-target validation, [43606084942](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43606084942), **completed with failure** on November 14, 2026: 239 successful jobs, 16 failed jobs (including the aggregate gate), 2 cancelled, and 11 skipped. It was dispatched once from trusted main workflow revision b27440329b4c450ec4c572e40ed338ed98f3d9c7 with target_ref=8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c, validation_tier=full, and dispatch_id=fix24-billing-197369-proof-full. Preflight succeeded. The checkout log confirms that exact candidate; dependency installation used --ignore-scripts and runtime setup used cache-mode=off. The earlier dispatch-contract failure remains recorded above.

Independent relevant proof is now available, rather than merely a passing preflight: [gateway-methods shard 10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43606084942/job/132481406155) passed, and its log explicitly shows all four agents-model-selection tests, including returns the billing-route warnings of the committed write, passing on both Node and Bun (the regression itself took 372 ms and 413 ms respectively). [Gateway-methods shard 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43606084942/job/132481406159) also passed with agents-mutate coverage on both runtimes. Build artifacts, production types, both core test-type lanes, core lint, protocol/bundled checks, docs, and security-fast passed. This does not independently reproduce the author's live before/after or stable-upgrade harness below; those remain author-supplied evidence.

The broad run is not green. Observed failures outside the changed billing files include UI read-aloud button lookup, Control UI locale fallback baseline drift, unused delegatedUserSubjectPrefix, CI prepared-workspace capacity/planning assertions, Git worktree compression, chat-startup transcript timing, update activation custody, session/Beam runtime-state and startup timeouts, plugin-reload continuation timeout, worker admission/PG-boundary assertions, a Unix socket path error, and compaction resource timing. The real-Gateway UI lane and iOS test lane were cancelled; the iOS lane was still running focused Apple Watch operation simulator tests before cancellation. These are recorded as unresolved broad-proof gaps, not waived or silently classified as passing. They have not been reproduced against this PR's base, so no blanket pre-existing-failure claim is made. No billing source change, rerun, merge, backport, or release was used to conceal them.

#### Bounded causal qualification — November 15, 2026

Rechecked the remote head (`8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c`), all seven changed paths, the retained failure summaries, and bounded completed-job tails. The PR remains open, non-draft and mergeable with a blocked merge state. The exact-head ClawSweeper review reports no findings; there are no submitted GitHub reviews. No PR-caused defect was established by this pass.

The following classification is source-based, not a claim of passing base reruns:

| Failed job(s) in run 43606084942 | Qualification |
| --- | --- |
| `132481401111`, `132481424955` — native read-aloud test, null `button.click` | Causally excluded from the introduced billing behavior: the assertion renders a local Solid transcript with mocked speech requests and fails before requesting speech. It neither performs `agents.update` nor exercises the added optional result field. No UI source changed. |
| `132481401266` — Control UI locale fallback baseline drift | Causally excluded from this patch's source changes: no locale/catalog/baseline input changed; the addition is a Gateway reply field, not UI text. |
| `132481402365` — unused `delegatedUserSubjectPrefix` | Causally excluded from the introduced source change: this PR neither removes a reference to that export nor changes the delegation module or dependency-check configuration. The newly exported billing comparator has a caller. |
| `132481406197`, `132481406234` — prepared-workspace capacity/planning assertions | Causally excluded from the billing implementation: the inspected assertions operate on fixed workload lists and CI routing/group generation (including expected 8 versus actual 9 groups), not Gateway execution. This PR does not change those lists, planners or workflow inputs. |
| `132481406092` — Git worktree compression; `132481408989` — update activation custody | No demonstrated billing causal path: inspected tests exercise synthetic Git pack maintenance and update-executor custody respectively, not the modified RPC. Their original failures remain recorded; neither was repaired or replayed in this pass. |
| `132481406074`, `132481409032`, `132481409054`, `132481409138` — chat startup, runtime state, plugin reload and startup core | Unresolved. In particular, plugin-reload continuation times out after 120 seconds. Gateway import/initialization or timing interactions cannot be excluded merely because the failing assertions are outside the changed files. Partial job tails do not expose every original failure. |
| `132481411512`, `132481411522`, `132481420753` — worker PG boundary/admission and bundle/compaction lane | Unresolved. The observed worker failures include two unexpected database `prepare` calls and missing prompt/admission values; the bundle lane's bounded tail does not recover its original failure. These are not proof that the billing patch caused them, nor sufficient evidence to waive them. |
| `132524234615` — aggregate CI gate | Consequence of failed/cancelled prerequisites, not an independent product diagnosis. The two cancelled UI/iOS lanes remain coverage gaps. |

Source inspection confirms that the comparator and success-reply helper themselves were not behaviorally rewritten: the comparator was exported, `updateAgentConfigEntry` now returns its existing committed mutation receipt, and `agents.update` compares that receipt before success-only warning delivery. The shared config handler already imports `config-write-flow`; nevertheless, its new direct import from `agents.ts` and the extra awaited comparison are why the unresolved Gateway timing/import failures have not been blanket-attributed to the base.

Readiness: the specific billing regression has independent Node/Bun proof and no actionable review finding, but broad validation is still red. The minimum remaining qualification gap is causal resolution of the seven unresolved Gateway/worker/bundle jobs above (using their original failure records and, only where needed, bounded base/head reproduction under secretless isolation), plus the cancelled coverage. This pass did not dispatch CI, execute contributor code locally, change source, or merge/backport/release anything.

#### Paired failure reconciliation — November 16, 2026

This update supersedes the earlier readiness paragraph's requirement to reproduce every remaining timeout; it does not change or erase the historical failures above. Under the repository test-failure policy, an investigated but unresolved failure is retained with its reproduction attempts and uncertainty; a passing replay is not a repair, and unresolved failures alone do not require another full run.

[Bounded paired run 43777174095](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777174095) completed with failure: eight jobs succeeded and the two runtime-state jobs failed. The retained per-job JSON and logs identify baseline `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` and candidate `8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c`, original tooling `b27440329b4c450ec4c572e40ed338ed98f3d9c7`, and proof tooling `16f421ebb28694e48f388ce745e6df848af8fad1`. These are focused diagnostic jobs, not a new full CI qualification. Across baseline/candidate and Node/Bun there were **364 test-result entries: 356 passed and 8 failed** (repeated executions, not 364 distinct tests). Node was v24.22.1; the staged OpenClaw Bun fork reported 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1.

| Focused group | Executed per source/runtime | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat | 62 | Passed on baseline and candidate under both runtimes; the original timeout was not reproduced. |
| Runtime state / Beam-owned view | 16 | The same two assertions failed on both sources under both runtimes; 14 passed in each execution. |
| Plugin reload | 1 | Passed on both sources/runtimes; the original 120-second continuation timeout was not reproduced. |
| Startup | 6 | Passed on both sources/runtimes; the original timeout was not reproduced. |
| Compaction | 6 | Passed on both sources/runtimes; the original timing failure was not reproduced. |

The Beam failures are `HTTP Visitor publications are privately readable by their initial publisher through admitted RPC` (`server.beam-owned-view.test.ts:287`) and `preserves model admission and rolls back revoked owned Beam adoption` (line 559). Both return `UNAVAILABLE: Could not load this Beam. Refresh and try again.` where success is expected. The Bun baseline/candidate results match the original failure signatures. Node shows the same symptom on both sources, but is corroboration in a different runtime, not a reproduction of the original runtime. This establishes inherited status for these two Beam assertions, not blanket inherited status for every failed job or timeout. Neither assertion was repaired by this PR or this diagnostic run.

The earlier independent investigations of worker admission/runtime selection (fix `8408f1b57558d36d7bb21bf979a6275c46c20099`, #197370) and prepared-worker Gateway-thread SQL (fix `5d3ce03a81d817381824592dde620ec84306b76b`, #197379) remain separate evidence. They do not imply that unrelated Beam or timeout failures are fixed in this candidate.

**Remaining uncertainty:** selected tests and captured order cannot recreate every original broad-run scheduling/resource interaction. Chat, reload, startup and compaction original failures remain recorded as investigated/not reproduced, not passing repair proof. The cancelled real-Gateway UI and iOS lanes remain coverage gaps. The author's live before/after and stable-upgrade evidence remains author-supplied; the independently passing billing regression remains the evidence identified above.

**Readiness versus landing:** no new PR-caused defect is established by the paired diagnostics. The failure policy permits continued review qualification with failed results retained; it does not make CI green or waive required review/security gates. As of this inspection the PR head is unchanged, the PR is open and non-draft, mergeable but blocked, and there are no submitted GitHub reviews. The existing exact-head ClawSweeper comment reports no findings, but is advisory and is not a submitted maintainer approval. The live `openclaw/ci-gate` remains failure; the manual broad run above is also failed. No merge, backport, release, source change or new proof run was performed for this reconciliation.

Native READY is not claimed: workspace preflight resolves the review artifact to `.worktrees/pr-197369/.local/review.json`, but that worktree/artifact is absent in the observed canonical checkout. The retained task checkout `fix24-billing` is clean at `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92`, not this PR head, so it cannot substitute for an exact-head native review. Smallest next internal step: recover the existing exact-head native review/correction artifacts (or have the native workflow owner re-establish the binding), record this investigated-failure evidence while preserving `tests.result: "fail"`, and validate the artifacts. Further full CI or a repeated passing diagnostic run is not required merely to erase uncertainty. Any eventual landing still needs its own authority and applicable native CI/review/security admission; this readiness task supplies no landing authorization.

Tested at `8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c` (base `main` `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b`).

A before/after harness built both checkouts and ran the same script on each, against one isolated Gateway per side (its own state directory and port, no live Gateway). The config, after `openclaw doctor --fix`: `agents.defaults.model` = `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` with the `claude-cli` agent runtime, agents `main` and `work`, and a fixture `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. HOME was isolated and no model turn was run, so no request reached a provider. The script called `agents.update` for `work` and then, for comparison, `config.patch` with the same model change for `main`, through `openclaw gateway call`. The script exits with an error when the Gateway never answers its health check. In the blocks below, the `config.patch` reply is shortened to one line marked `[abridged]`; the rest is verbatim output.

Before (base `489774034984`):

```text
== agents.update work: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (claude-cli runtime) -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
{
  "ok": true,
  "agentId": "work"
}
agents.update reply billing-route lines: 0
```

prs.title: fix(ui): show app-managed guidance for host-owned Gateway updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198506. When a Gateway's install is owned by an external application (the macOS `OpenClaw.app`, a desktop app, or an immutable deployer), the Control UI's Gateway updates panel shows a local "Update Gateway…" button. Clicking it fails with `Update error: Managed by OpenClaw.app` because the update admission layer rejects host-owned installs.

This PR makes the Control UI aware of the owning app and swaps the local update action for guidance to update through that app instead, so the UI never presents an action it cannot perform.

## Solution

- **Protocol**: `UpdateStatusResult` gains an optional `installOwner` object (`schemaVersion`, `owner`, `displayName`, `updateHint`) describing the external app that owns the install, when one is resolved.
- **Gateway handler**: `update.status` surfaces `installOwner` from the resolved install status when present.
- **Control UI**: `update-overlay-helpers` projects `installOwner` into the update snapshot; the Gateway updates row replaces the "Update Gateway…" button with a managed-by note ("This Gateway is managed by {app} and updates are handled there. {hint}") when `installOwner` is present, and the Retry action on a failed update is hidden for host-owned installs.
- **Validator**: regenerated gateway protocol validators (`protocol.generated/predicates.js`) for the new schema field.

## Evidence

- **Protocol schema**: `config.test.ts` validates the `installOwner` marker (accepts the `macos-app` shape, rejects unknown owner / wrong schemaVersion / empty displayName).
- **Gateway handler**: `update-status-schedule.test.ts` asserts `installOwner` is surfaced on an app-owned install (via `lifecycle.initialize()`) and omitted on an unowned package install; the existing host-owned case (`refreshCheckout`) now also asserts `installOwner`.
- **Control UI**: `updates.test.ts` (jsdom) verifies a host-owned install shows no "Update Gateway…" button and renders the app-managed guidance, while non-host-owned installs keep the update action; a host-owned failed install shows no "Retry update" recovery button (replaced by the managed-by guidance) instead of dispatching into the host-owned rejection.
- The `installOwner` test fixture is typed `satisfies UpdateInstallOwner`, so the schema fields stay checked at compile time.
- **Custodian harness**: `custodian-page.test-harness.ts` builds its overlay snapshot against `Pick<ApplicationContext["overlays"], "snapshot">`, so it now initializes the required `installOwner: null` field. Without it the ui-pages test typecheck fails on the new snapshot shape.
- UI tests: 45/45 pass (3 new). Server tests: 42/42 pass (2 new). Custodian page suite: 29/29 pass. `pnpm format` clean on all changed files.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings’ browser notification test does not disclose that it sends to every registered browser on the Gateway, including other people’s browsers.

## User Impact

User impact: the existing action now says **Test all browsers**, with a nearby explanation of its audience before it is clicked. Native macOS **Send test** remains a local test.

This changes presentation only. It does not broaden delivery, change permissions or subscription ownership, send a real notification, or add a confirmation step.

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented browser test deliberately broadcasts to registered subscriptions; ordinary approval and attention notifications have narrower recipient checks. The existing status row now explains that distinction instead of letting its personal/device settings context suggest a local-only test.

The native label is preserved, browser-specific test expectations are updated, and the English notification guide names the actual control. #199223’s notification-agent picker is separate and is not duplicated. No new component, state or delivery policy is added.

## Evidence

- Maintainer verification reproduced the remaining CI failure in the full Config page consumer: it still looked for the browser button named “Send test.” Updating that single expectation preserved the native label. All 68 Config/notification cases plus 535 standard UI canaries now pass, including rejection recovery, permissions, VAPID mismatch, native feedback and navigation during an admitted request.
- Four selected backend checks pass: broadcasting to registered subscriptions and the browser-test handler’s success, failure and empty-recipient outcomes. These are transport fixtures, not live browser-vendor push delivery.
- Complete built-app flows pass at 1360 and 390 pixels: open Notifications, see the audience, issue exactly one unchanged test request, hold its response, and recover the enabled control. No preference or unsubscribe write is issued. Browser subscription APIs and Gateway responses are synthetic; no real notification is sent.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting, the configured documentation lint and diff checks pass. No broad CI or E2E matrix was run.
- Baseline main: `a64758be048909c5c59ef781d5b4f34aaefc34af`. Matched light-theme screenshots use emulated viewports, real production components and same-frame crops. The full page and mobile wrapping were inspected. Simplification leaves one existing presentation owner, two English strings, and maintained tests/documentation.
