prs.title: fix(state): name the state directory when it cannot be made private
prs.body:
Refs #137242

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw onboard` and `openclaw gateway install` stop with "State ownership directory must be a user-owned real directory" or "State ownership directory permissions are not private" when `~/.openclaw` is on a mount that shows files as root-owned or ignores chmod (Apple VirtioFS shares, SMB, NFS). The message does not say which directory failed or what the user should change.

## User Impact

The error now names the directory, the uid that owns it, and that the state directory has to be on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions. Nothing changes about what is accepted: these mounts are still rejected.

This does not close #137242. Making install work on these mounts would mean relaxing the state-ownership lock, the `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock and the 0600 systemd environment file, which is the open security decision on the issue. This PR covers the "name the state directory and a safe local-filesystem recovery path" option from the issue review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ensureOwnerDirectory` (`src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.ts`) owns the check that the state-ownership lock directory (`<stateDir>/tmp/openclaw-<uid>`) is user-owned and mode 0700. It is the first check these mounts fail on current main, before the systemd environment file named in the issue is reached. The ownership and permission checks are unchanged; only the two error messages change. The non-directory error keeps its existing text.

<details>
<summary>Where current main stops on a chmod-less state dir</summary>

- Files shown as root-owned: `gateway install` fails in `ensureOwnerDirectory` on the uid check. `onboard` fails earlier with a bare `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod` from the `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock (`createNativeExclusiveFile` → `fchmodSync`, reached through `withSetupMigrationTargetLock`).
- Files owned by the user but chmod silently ignored: both commands fail in `ensureOwnerDirectory` on the 0700 check.
- The lock directory moved under the state dir on purpose (`resolveGatewayLockDirForCanonicalStateDir`, "clean break" from process temp), so a state dir on such a mount always reaches this check.

</details>

## Evidence

Linux container (`node:24.22.1-trixie-slim`), non-root `testuser`, account home as `HOME`. Main (`e5f1a21`) and the candidate were each packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` and installed with `npm install -g`. `systemctl`, `loginctl` and `busctl` are the shims from `scripts/e2e/lib/doctor-install-switch/shims`, not a real systemd user manager. `~/.openclaw` is a vfat loop mount: with `umask=000` files show as uid 0, writes work and `chmod 600` returns EPERM, the behavior the issue describes for VirtioFS. With `uid=<testuser>`, chmod returns 0 but has no effect. Commands: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-daemon`, then `openclaw gateway install --port 18789`.

Root-owned mount, `gateway install`:

```
main: ... failed to acquire gateway state ownership at /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001/state.<hash>.lock | State ownership directory must be a user-owned real directory. Stop the Gateway and other state owners for this profile, run `openclaw doctor --fix` against the same state/config, then restart the Gateway.
fix:  ... | State ownership directory /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001 is owned by uid 0, not this user (uid 1001). Run OpenClaw as the user that owns its state directory, and keep that directory on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions. Stop the Gateway ...
```

User-owned mount that ignores chmod, `onboard`:

```
main: State ownership directory permissions are not private
fix:  State ownership directory /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001 permissions could not be set to 0700. Run OpenClaw as the user that owns its state directory, and keep that directory on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions
```

Control, `~/.openclaw` on the container's own disk, same on main and fix: `onboard exit=0`, `Installed systemd service: /home/testuser/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service`, `install exit=0`.

Not changed by this PR:
- On the root-owned mount, `onboard` still prints the bare `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod` from `@openclaw/fs-safe`.
- The migration retry text that follows the error still suggests `openclaw doctor --fix`; it is shared by all legacy-migration lock failures.

Tests: `src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.test.ts` (1 test) fails on main's `ensureOwnerDirectory` and passes on the fix. `pnpm test src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.test.ts src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts src/infra/gateway-lock.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.lock.test.ts`: 63 passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` passes (+26).

Production delta +14/-2; test delta +26/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; only error text changes, with no config, state or behavior change. Blast radius is the two `ensureOwnerDirectory` errors, which are surfaced wherever state ownership is acquired.

prs.title: fix(k8s): fail initialization when config seeding fails
prs.body:
Closes #198981

## What Problem This Solves

The Kubernetes init container can report success after failing to seed `openclaw.json` or `AGENTS.md`. Its later successful temporary-directory setup masks the copy error, so initialization finishes with required files missing.

## User Impact

Deployments fail at the actual initialization error instead of proceeding with incomplete configuration. Normal first-boot seeding works, and existing user-edited files remain preserved across restarts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable shell error termination in the existing init command. This covers failed copies and workspace creation while retaining seed-if-missing behavior and the explicit temporary-directory error message. No new configuration, script, dependency or runtime owner.

## Evidence

Executed the exact command array extracted from the manifest in its **BusyBox 1.38** image, pinned to `sha256:a46257e06c82ad85242d0d38077d0a52d9896389ca60a1a59d3463db586e5fa4`. The container ran as UID/GID 1000 on Linux arm64 with isolated fixture volumes, no network and no host filesystem mounts. All command paths were unchanged. This exercises the init-container command rather than a Kubernetes control plane.

| Scenario | Base exit | Fixed exit | Fixed result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both source files available, fresh state | `0` | `0` | Both files seeded |
| Config source missing | `0` | `1` | Initialization stops at failed copy |
| Instructions source missing | `0` | `1` | Initialization stops at failed copy |
| Existing edited config and instructions | `0` | `0` | Both edited files preserved |

Representative terminal output:

```text
cp: can't stat '/config/openclaw.json': No such file or directory
base:  init_exit=0, seeded config=MISSING
fixed: init_exit=1, seeded config=MISSING
```

The same copy error is visible before and after; the fix makes the process status reflect it. Eight container executions covered the before/after matrix, followed by removal of the proof containers and restoration of the dedicated VM to its stopped state.

- Base regression: **2 failed, 5 passed**, specifically the two missing-source status assertions.
- Fixed manifest suite: **7 passed**. The existing mount/temporary-workspace contract remains covered.
- Tooling test types, scoped lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass. Hosted CI remains pending.
- Diff: one production line; 39 test lines added and one import line replaced in the existing manifest suite. The regression executes the embedded shell against temporary files rather than matching source text.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/k8s-manifests.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental --diagnostics
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --format json --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json test/scripts/k8s-manifests.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check scripts/k8s/manifests/deployment.yaml test/scripts/k8s-manifests.test.ts
node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base upstream/main
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(sqlite): TEMP views invalidate sibling readers and worker logs lack timestamps
prs.body:
Related: #188274

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a connection-local TEMP VIEW unnecessarily invalidates other SQLite readers, while worker console lines lack the emit time needed to attribute stalls accurately.

## User Impact

TEMP views preserve sibling MAIN-reader admission. Worker diagnostics carry emitter-side timestamps, and slow transaction-hold warnings include the hold start time. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing TEMP-object classifier to views without suppressing subsequent MAIN DDL. Enable the existing timestamp mechanism in the two worker logging entry points and expose the already-measured hold start.

This does not address the exec-retry, proof-publication, or invalidation-message concerns in issue items a–c.

## Evidence

The retained tests ran on **a7c6ba155379556c1165b765151fe7ace4e00f8a**, based on **7ecd67ccfd51e2c5aa6673809b69fb318235dd0a**. Reconstructed publication candidate **4390ac8c69d9ae01482ee7b1baa97d9c74c645cd** has the identical complete source tree (`286e2e615470debd2e6b3679a78c8ec6bfa8d067`); only commit metadata and required contributor credit differ. Managed publication produced **d381508fea145ac2771671c21048f0e86c90e648** with that same complete tree; its bot-authored commit carries both human co-author trailers.

- Before production changes: four intended regression failures and 52 passes in four files; the wrapper stopped before the fifth file.
- After: **67/67 tests pass across all five changed test files**, including actual compiled worker logging/JSON-stdout paths and sibling-admission tests.
- Additional affected-owner/consumer suites pass **137/137 tests in six files** on the committed candidate: **204 passing tests across 11 distinct files** including the changed suites.
- Changed-file formatting and lint, production types, and the infra, state-logging, and agents-sessions test-type graphs pass under Node 24.22.1.
- Independent whole-candidate narrative source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. A fresh bound AutoReview of the complete local candidate against `7ecd67ccfd51e2c5aa6673809b69fb318235dd0a` also completed `scoped-clean` at its default **P0-only** threshold; it did not execute project code or certify lower-priority findings.
- Limits: no live Gateway/stalled-host demonstration was run. Hold-start timing is covered by deterministic tests; older supplied Gateway logs are not presented as fresh proof. Published-head CI remains separate.

Original patch by Mitchell Etzel.

## Worked on by

- @Patrick-Erichsen
- @etzelm

prs.title: fix(templates): oversized or non-UTF-8 HEARTBEAT.md fails only at Add
prs.body:
Closes #198848

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Template whose `HEARTBEAT.md` is larger than 256 KiB or not valid UTF-8 passes `templates validate`, `inspect` and `build`, then `templates add` fails with "The CLI command failed." and no reason (`--json` returns a generic `cli_error`).

## User Impact

The author sees the problem at `validate`, `inspect` and `build`, with a diagnostic naming `HEARTBEAT.md`, its size and the limit, instead of publishing a Template nobody can add. `add --dry-run` prints the same diagnostic, and `--json` returns the add-plan schema with `valid: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add imports `HEARTBEAT.md` as cron job scratch (`src/templates/portable-automation.ts`), which must decode as strict UTF-8 and fit `CRON_JOB_SCRATCH_MAX_BYTES` (`src/cron/scratch-contract.ts`). The Template reader (`readTemplateManifestFile`) is what validate, inspect, build, dev, CLI Add, Gateway Add and ClawHub artifacts all read through, so it now applies that contract to the `HEARTBEAT.md` source. It reuses the cron constant and the existing `decodeUtf8Input` helper (same `fatal`/`ignoreBOM` options as the planner); no new limit is added. This follows the `package_bootstrap_too_large` diagnostic the reader already returns for `BOOTSTRAP.md` (sibling of #198559).

<details><summary>Root cause and scope</summary>

- The reader checked workspace sources only against the generic 1 MiB managed-file limit (`src/templates/reader.ts`, workspace source loop). The 256 KiB scratch limit and strict UTF-8 decode ran only in `planTemplatePortableAutomation`, as a thrown `Error`, which the CLI reports as `cli_error`.
- The check covers both ways a package maps `HEARTBEAT.md`: `workspace.bootstrapFiles.HEARTBEAT.md` and a `workspace.files` entry with `path: HEARTBEAT.md` (the planner treats both as the heartbeat, by action id).
- Add now reports this as a Template diagnostic, the same way it reports an oversized `BOOTSTRAP.md`, rather than as a `blockers` entry in a plan. The planner's `assertCronJobScratchContent` call is left in place; every Add path plans from a reader-verified source, so it is no longer reached by these inputs.

</details>

## Evidence

Source checkout, Node 24.22.1, isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, real `pnpm openclaw templates ...` CLI, Templates enabled in Labs. Projects created with `templates create`, then `CLAW.md` mapping `workspace/HEARTBEAT.md`: `hbbig` (324,000 bytes), `hbbad` (14 bytes, invalid UTF-8), `hbok` (18 bytes, control).

- Main (`fbdeb6e150e`): validate, inspect and build exit 0 for `hbbig` and `hbbad`; `add --dry-run` exits 1 with only "The CLI command failed."; `--json` prints `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error",...}}`.
- Fix: all five commands exit 1 with `heartbeat_too_large` / `heartbeat_invalid` naming `HEARTBEAT.md`, the source path, the size and the 262144-byte limit; `--json` is `openclaw.templateAddPlan.v1` with `valid: false` and the diagnostic.
- Control `hbok`: validate exit 0 and `add --dry-run` preview (4 actions, 1 automation) identical on main and the fix.
- Edge: a file of exactly 262,144 bytes still reads (`reader.test.ts`).
- `src/templates/reader.test.ts`: the new case (run for `bootstrapFiles` and `workspace.files`) fails on main (`expected true to be false`, 2 failed) and passes with the fix.
- `pnpm test src/templates src/cli/templates-cli`: 22 + 15 + 3 files, 278 + 151 + 31 tests passed. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted oxlint and format check, `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix: report subagent requester waiting and consumption truthfully
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading subagent delivery records while results wait behind a requester, and false failures when a private continuation consumes results before restart cancels it.

## User Impact

The stored registry row distinguishes waiting from consumption and names the requester run. Restart cancellation preserves consumed private results. A separate visible-final obligation remains required. Exactly-once delivery, restart custody, retention, configuration, and SQLite schema are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending handoff used a terminal non-delivery disposition, and cancellation classified the continuation outcome without retaining its already-completed consumption. Waiting now joins the existing dispatch write. After the requester commits its result-bearing transcript input, its existing source owner immediately starts and joins one registry consumption write before settlement. Readers use that stored fact directly; the receipt-backed projection, cold receipt reads, and their tests are removed.

| Event | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Queued behind a live requester | Pending with intentional-non-delivery disposition and handoff error | Explicit waiting with blocking requester run; no terminal disposition |
| Requester transcript consumes results | Pending without a consumption fact | Raw registry records consumed with the consuming run ID |
| Private continuation cancelled by restart | Failed/intentional non-delivery despite retained input | Consumed fact survives; terminal settlement records delivered to requester |
| Separate visible final still owed | Visible final required | Still required; private consumption does not satisfy it |

Read-only aggregate Team evidence supplied by the reliability peer, November 15: r335/292a4253 run4924541e ended at15:44:05Z; direct announce failed at15:44:12Z; its pending row looked intentionally undelivered while waiting behind requester settlement created at15:45:11Z, then delivered once at15:49:17Z. On r334/b09f4a04, a50bec84/e11342db remained pending for over20minutes although the continuation started at11:40:31Z had consumed both; shutdown recorded failed while restart-resume retained the results. No Team mutation or data copy was used.

The maintainer chose direct recording and accepted up to four registry commits per batch in exchange for removing the projection machinery. This implementation uses **three registry commits per two-result batch**, versus two on the exact main parent, plus the same one existing transcript commit in both arms. Final production delta is **+200 lines**; tests are **+336 lines**, with no test-budget exception. The benchmark adds240 lines and documentation11 lines, counted separately. This removes163 net production lines from the rejected projection version and28 from the earlier direct version. Remaining growth records facts at the transcript/registry owners and distinguishes consumption from a separately owed final; it adds no cache or scan.

## Evidence

Baseline: `89ee0bd382d16ec16183a10e81a8930a92ed1909`. Candidate: `fb2fe55a2d61ac1be0edb468b17613f3f14dec56`.

- The retained exact-parent handoff regression fails on the original pending disposition/error mismatch. The final focused run passes393 tests; additional requester-wake and registry-reader suites pass52. The final bookkeeping-failure repair passes26 focused cases. Its regression fails on the preceding candidate: a successful visible reply became a failure when the consumption write rejected. The settlement join now preserves the transport outcome; the original rejection remains owned by transcript diagnostics and source custody.
- Real Gateway tests with a synthetic provider pass the private-continuation restart and in-flight-announcement crash cases, with raw registry assertions and exactly-once input/final-reply checks. The existing native continuation suite passes16 cases, and the native transcript mirror consumes once after persistence.
- `pnpm check:changed` found two fixture type errors and an async-finally lint error. All identified failed type/lint gates pass separately after repair. Every other full-run gate passed. The aggregate command retains its original failure status; no aggregate-green claim is made. The subsequent `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` repair run passes in full. Final Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2, including an independent review of the bookkeeping-failure repair.
- All behavioral readers continue to use the canonical registry row. The existing compact session-list projection includes the new fact for diagnostics/UI; there are no requester-transcript lookups or fallback reads. A grep finds no retired receipt-projection references. Previously completed UI browser3/E2E8 checks cover the unchanged UI-facing shape; final changes add no UI-imported module or Node-only UI import. The supported stable synthetic upgrade proof remains applicable; the schema stays at40.

Production-shaped synthetic fixture: 39.9GiB agent DB, 10,800 sessions, 4,300 retained runs, and62,000 workspace files/1.116GB. Five interleaved A/B pairs and five A/A pairs for timing and sampled allocation,30 two-result batches/process:40 processes,1,200 batches,2,400 results. Every batch asserts the expected commit count and terminal result. The first measured batch is reported separately; no filesystem cache flush was performed. Local APFS does not reproduce Team's btrfs commit waits.

| Owner metric, median / p95 | Exact parent | Direct recording |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm wall, ms | 3.783 / 13.745 | 4.201 / 17.843 |
| Warm CPU, ms | 4.282 / 9.472 | 4.742 / 9.315 |
| First batch wall, ms | 119.398 / 572.445 | 124.193 / 638.960 |
| First batch CPU, ms | 152.012 / 256.089 | 157.594 / 288.895 |
| Sampled bytes/batch | 3,509,593 / 3,511,819 | 3,615,922 / 3,658,887 |

Warm median cost: +0.418ms wall, +0.460ms CPU, and about106KB sampled allocation per batch. A/A paired median differences: wall+0.77% (range−25.05..+104.53%), CPU+0.36% (−8.34..+49.19%), allocation+0.0003% (−1.00..+0.22%). Host one-minute load ranged19.91–52.79; concurrent checks make timing tails noisy. Allocation includes first-call work. These measurements quantify the accepted extra write; no speedup is claimed. CPU profiles are retained for both arms.

Command: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/subagent-requester-delivery-measure.mts <fixture> <output> <baseline|candidate> <exact-parent-overlay|-> <time|allocation>`. Fixture background verification previously could not stage its snapshot due to disk/temp-root limits; no integrity or permission bypass was used. The offline owner benchmark uses normal admission outside measured batches.

The preceding direct head passed [CI run 43772398866](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43772398866) without a rerun. Final-head [CI run 43775439266, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43775439266) passed on `fb2fe55a2d61ac1be0edb468b17613f3f14dec56`. Attempt 1 repeated the known hosted restart `SessionStoreUnavailableError`; the single authorized plain `--failed` rerun passed, without debug flags or source changes. This is not an inherited-failure exception or a claim that replay repaired the intermittent. [Final-head ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199695#issuecomment-6898383090) has zero open items and no findings; the repaired Codex thread is resolved. Earlier projection-head CI exposed a scheduled-command reset test/contract regression reproduced on the exact main parent and attributed by owner history to `3bbf67501123a640c4634f782ba56aac6050dd3c`; that regression is recorded for the lead, not dismissed as noise.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the hourly dependency check failing on state-upgrade internals and dynamically loaded fixture/preload entry points.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change, schema change, migration, or new configuration. State upgrade and Doctor retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The state upgrade introduced in #198389 exposed internal helpers and left historical installed-plugin entries outside Knip's graph. Keep helpers private, exercise rebuild tests through the production entry point, and give the existing Doctor subprocess boundary its own production module. The Doctor implementation is unchanged and all callers migrate together.

Declare the real historical corpus plugin roots and the heap-rig soak preload as analyzer entry points. The preload omission is a newly identified main regression introduced by #199761 (`1e7f1f743c24f9b713ab78a75284c99b0ad05ca7`), reproduced on the exact main parent; it is not dismissed as inherited noise. No ignores or fixture deletions are added. Production LOC is +2 from module imports; tests are -2 and analyzer configuration is +4.

The independent member-welcome export regression from #198491 is owned by #199789 and is outside this patch.

## Evidence

- On exact parent `39b066a976970b080df4b107b8ba918e250d4f4e`, two export-scan controls reproduced identical findings: nine production/six full-tree state exports plus three/two member-welcome exports. The candidate removes every state finding; only the separately owned member-welcome findings remain.
- The unused-file gate failed on all six corpus plugin entries and the heap-rig preload on the parent; the final candidate passes with zero unused files.
- Focused Node and pinned Bun tests each pass 32/32 across the SQLite copy and state-upgrade owners.
- Real Gateway state-upgrade E2E passes 7/7: invalid configuration refusal, four historical corpora, and two forced Doctor failures. All assertions are retained.
- Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2; final source verification passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 39b066a976970b080df4b107b8ba918e250d4f4e` completed: every selected gate passes except the independently owned member-welcome dead exports, reproduced on the exact parent and introduced by #198491 (`cec47fd13f23df46069da1beb65ceaec6e66d04f`). The final full scan reports zero state findings. The coordinator reports #199789 is now merged on main; this candidate intentionally preserves its pinned base proof.

The actual failed analyzer gates provide the red/green regression proof. Export scan wall times were 183.23/209.06 seconds for the two parent controls and 148.65 seconds for the candidate; CPU was 348.72/347.27/340.42 seconds. Unused-file scan wall/CPU was 130.85/285.11 seconds before and 178.02/325.09 seconds after. These are scanner measurements under varying shared-host load, not production performance claims. Maximum RSS is not allocation totals. The unchanged production operation does not warrant generating a large production-shaped database/workspace for this visibility/entry-graph repair.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the invalid-configuration warning promises “Don’t remind me again” even though dismissing it is temporary.

## User Impact

User impact: the button now says **Dismiss warning**, matching what it does. The warning can return after reloading or changing configuration context. Detailed validation issues stay visible.

No validation, persistence, permissions or configuration writes change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing view owns an ephemeral dismissal, not a saved reminder preference. Correcting its label is sufficient; adding persistence would unnecessarily hide future configuration warnings.

The change is one English string and one regression in the existing Config read suite. It checks dismissal, retained validation details, no save or field patch, and reset when the config context changes. No new state, helper or control is introduced.

## Evidence

- The new regression fails on the old label and passes after. 85 focused Config read/raw/navigation/route/write tests pass.
- Matched built-app flows open an invalid Logging snapshot, dismiss its warning, retain the detailed error, reload and see the warning again. They issue no configuration or preference writes. The data is synthetic; no live Gateway configuration was made invalid.
- Three additional built-app flows pass for failed-autosave recovery, schema/raw guarded writes, and rejected-save feedback/discard. These are fixture-backed flows, not live configuration changes.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass. Broad CI is left to the PR.

prs.title: fix(ssh): preserve whitespace inside resolved identity filenames
prs.body:
Closes #198892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SSH configuration resolution changing an identity filename when it contains repeated spaces or a tab. For example, `two  spaces` becomes `two spaces`, which is a different file.

## User Impact

Identity paths read from OpenSSH retain their internal whitespace when OpenClaw resolves a remote Gateway target. Gateway status uses these paths when selecting an identity without an explicit override.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenSSH already emits the correct pathname. Splitting the entire output line into words and joining them again loses information; splitting only at the key/value boundary preserves it. This keeps the existing handling of empty values, `IdentityFile none`, ports, and explicit arguments.

This is separate from #190056 / #188906, which address trimming the ends of configured paths. Their proposed SSH change does not repair this output parser.

## Evidence

- **Native before/after:** production `resolveSshConfig` with real OpenSSH 10.3p1 on macOS 27.0.1, Node 26.12.1. Empty temporary identity files, with network and access to the user's SSH directory denied by the OS sandbox. Base `77f79c00df61326c83f0420948a1959117007104` changes both a double-space filename and a tab filename; this patch preserves both. A single-space control passes in both revisions. This exercises configuration resolution, not an authenticated tunnel.
- **Regression:** the two added cases fail on the base for the changed pathname; all **9 resolver tests pass** with the repair. Official runner wall time: 1.54s.
- **Consumer:** all **30 gateway-status tests pass**. Official runner wall time: 43.50s (Vitest 40.38s, mostly transformation).
- **Scope and review:** author inspected the complete two-file diff and the Gateway status/tunnel consumers. No new dependency, option, exported helper, or test seam. Production delta: +7/−3 lines; tests: +10 lines.

Commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ssh-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/ssh-config.test.ts src/infra/ssh-config.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/infra/ssh-config.ts","src/infra/ssh-config.test.ts"]'
```

Targeted lint and formatting passed. After completing the source checkout, all eight selected typecheck graphs passed: infra, gateway-root, commands, plugins-platform, config-cli, services, other, and cli-update. Updated-head CI is recorded below. A broader local `check-changed` run also reported findings outside this diff: a mock-export guard in `worker-idle-gc.test.ts` (also reproduced on the unchanged base) and unused exports in `status-runtime-shared.ts` and `openclaw-id/member-role-presets.ts`. Those findings are retained for CI comparison rather than mixed into this fix.


### Landing validation

- Reviewed head: `a40668bb8584ba0e18c30660bcd459f32cb0737f`. The branch was updated with main to incorporate the existing benchmark typecheck repair #198912; the SSH change remains the same two-file patch.
- [Exact-head CI run 43777843366, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777843366): passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, security, production/test typechecks, lint, and changed-source/boundary checks.
- Maintainer review found no actionable issues. Existing regression and real OpenSSH CLI evidence below is reused: the parser, tests, and affected Gateway/tunnel consumers are unchanged by the main integration. No authenticated-tunnel claim is made.

## Shipped Gateway CLI proof

The source CLI at the original reviewed head (`dc57cfd86481f808d78258c45820632d0c11a071`) was exercised in a disposable, network-isolated Linux container with Node 24.22.2 and OpenSSH 9.2p1. Its frozen install resolved the checked-in lockfile. Each run used a synthetic SSH alias with an inherited `IdentityFile`; no `--ssh-identity` override was passed.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway probe \
  --ssh proof-alias --port 39741 --timeout 8000 --json
```

`strace -f -e trace=execve -s 4096` recorded the real `/usr/bin/ssh` processes. The first invocation resolved the alias with `-G`; the second invocation received the identity selected by the Gateway command. These are the captured `-i` argument values (`\t` denotes the traced tab):

```text
fixture       original parser argument          fixed parser argument
------------- -------------------------------- ---------------------------------
double-space  /tmp/proof-keys/two spaces         /tmp/proof-keys/two  spaces
tab           /tmp/proof-keys/with tab           /tmp/proof-keys/with\ttab
control       /tmp/proof-keys/one space          /tmp/proof-keys/one space
```

The original parser also produced `Identity file ... not accessible: No such file or directory` in the Gateway's JSON warning for both affected paths. That warning disappears with the fix; the single-space control behaves identically before and after. Both revisions then report the intentionally closed loopback SSH port, so this proves CLI → alias resolution → identity selection → real SSH argument delivery, not authenticated tunnel establishment.

<details>
<summary>Terminal trace excerpts</summary>


prs.title: fix(auto-reply): bound the sandbox scp transfer with a deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox media staging shells out to `scp`, and that spawn had **no deadline**: a hung transfer (dead peer, wedged ssh, a dropped TCP session that never resets) left the child process alive indefinitely and the caller awaiting a promise that never settles — one leaked `scp` per stalled staging attempt, with no bound on how long the turn could hang.

This gives the transfer a bounded deadline **through the shared process-lifecycle runner rather than by owning the spawn directly**, which is the direction #98141 was closed toward: that PR was closed as "superseded by the current process-lifecycle architecture, not because the linked defect is fixed" — so the timeout belongs on the existing runner call, not on a locally-owned `child_process.spawn`.

## Evidence

The change is two files:

```
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts          |  8 +-
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts | 101 ++++++++++++++++++-
```

- `stage-sandbox-media.ts` derives the per-transfer budget (`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()`: size cap / supported throughput, 30s floor, `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` override) and passes it as `timeoutMs` on the existing shared-runner invocation — the runner already owns deadlines and descendant-tree termination.
- The test suite asserts the deadline reaches the runner (`expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: SCP_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MS })`) so the wiring cannot silently regress, and adds a real-process hang case: a fake `scp` on `PATH` that spawns a descendant, ignores `SIGTERM`, and never exits. The assertion is that the transfer is rejected by the deadline and **both the parent and the descendant are gone afterwards** (via the repo's existing `test-utils/process-tree` helpers), plus a negative control that a normal transfer still succeeds unchanged.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed | 2 skipped (15)
```

## Verification

The deadline wiring and the normal-transfer assertions run and pass here; the two skipped cases are the POSIX-only hang cases (`it.runIf(process.platform !== "win32")`) — this machine is Windows, so the process-tree termination assertion itself is **not exercised locally**. I am stating that rather than implying it: it needs a POSIX CI lane to run, and that is the one part of this change I could not observe directly.

Partial fix for #98468: the deadline wiring, the revised budget, and real timeout recovery (process tree + temporary cleanup) are verified here; the remaining unobserved part is a real multi-hour suspend/transfer scenario on a POSIX lane, which CI's Linux lane runs via the committed cases.

## Context worth knowing before review

- Three prior attempts exist on this issue: #98141 (closed as superseded by the lifecycle architecture — see above), #101473 (long review loop, closed), #132552 (merged, but that was the *cancellation* half of staging, not the transfer deadline).
- The issue currently also carries `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`. If the automated fix lane produces a PR for the same deadline, take that one — the intent here is to have the fix available in the architecture the maintainer pointed at, not to race a bot.

## Revision 2 — revised transfer budget + real transport proof (head `8707115c920`)

**Decision answer (the question the review asked): revise the deadline instead of an unconditional 30s cutoff.**
`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()` derives the per-transfer budget from the size cap and the slowest throughput still called supported, keeps it bounded, and is overridable:

| Case | Budget |
|---|---|
| 50 MiB cap at the 256 KiB/s supported floor | **200s** |
| review example: 40 MiB at 1 MiB/s (~40s) | **160s** (the old fixed 30s could never allow it) |
| small transfers | 30s floor |
| `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` | operator override (tests use it to reach the deadline in seconds) |

The deadline remains an absolute, bounded value owned by the shared runner, so an unattended hang still dies; it just no longer kills a slow-but-healthy copy. A deadline kill is also no longer retried (one bounded wait instead of three): retrying a copy that stopped progressing only re-waits the whole budget. If maintainers want a different number, or a config field instead of the env override, name it and I'll switch it.

### Real behavior proof (no mocks: real spawned transport through staging, Windows)

A compiled stand-in transport is spawned through the same argv/PATH path the runner uses, so the real spawn, deadline, tree kill, and temp cleanup all execute:

```
[proof] slow transfer staged=1 elapsed=7965ms
[proof] staged bytes=real transport bytes
[proof] hung transport pid=22892 alive=true
[proof] descendant pid=54128 alive=true
[proof] reaped by deadline: parent=true descendant=true
[proof] surface={"value":{"staged":{}}}
[proof] attempts="attempt\n"
[proof] temp dir removed=true
 ✓ windows real transport proof > publishes a real slow transport that finishes inside the budget 8044ms
 ✓ windows real transport proof > kills a real hung transport tree on the deadline without retrying 8507ms
```

Both Windows-native cases pass (17 passed | 3 skipped with the scratch cases in place) and the same file without them is **15 passed | 3 skipped, exit 0**; `oxfmt --check` clean on both files. The three skips are the POSIX-gated cases (they spawn a shebang script), which is why the Windows run above uses a compiled stand-in. `oxlint` produced no verdict for explicit paths in this junction worktree, so I am not claiming a lint verdict — CI's lint lane judges.

The new committed cases: the derived-budget unit math (including the 40 MiB / 160s case), a real slow transfer that publishes, and the hung tree + descendant reaped on the deadline with one attempt and the temp dir removed.

prs.title: fix(android): keep model names during temporary catalog gaps
prs.body:
Closes #195456

Related: #192252 (delayed-picker behavior is not addressed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android's composer replaces a known model name such as `Beta` with the raw ID `beta` when the catalog temporarily clears, even though the selected model has not changed.

## User Impact

The unchanged selection keeps its familiar name during disconnects and catalog gaps. Fresh catalog metadata replaces that name; changing Gateway, agent, session, or model clears it. Model selection, availability, eligibility, and request ordering remain unchanged.

**Validation limitation — native visual proof remains incomplete.** Local compilation, lint, focused tests, and red/green regression results have now been reported passing; real Android/Gateway before-and-after evidence is still outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a display-only name in the existing composer, keyed by its existing Gateway/agent/session owner and the selected model reference. The current catalog still owns model choices and capabilities. An authoritative blank name clears the remembered name rather than reviving an old alias.

## Evidence

- **Local Linux validation reported by @DonnieFi:** [full results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195473#issuecomment-6869049039), for the current head `6d958f56ff856723a9ce19549de62aa1a4aeb57a` and base `621ea221a4b074868c0d8c1191db783729068bd9`. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Profile’s GitHub help incorrectly says agents always use the shared account and all cloud work must return to the current computer before personal publication.

## User Impact

User impact: the help now respects each agent’s own or inherited GitHub account and does not tell users to move work unnecessarily when a repository checkpoint already supports publication. Personal publishing still requires an explicit choice, session write access and finished, accepted work.

This is a copy-only correction. Credentials, permissions, publication eligibility and cloud-work recovery are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account owner prefers an agent override before the shared account. Personal publication supports accepted repository-only checkpoints without a Gateway checkout; remote work sourced from a Gateway checkout retains its separate stop/reconciliation requirement. The general Profile explanation should not impose the latter restriction on every cloud session or confuse the browser computer with the Gateway.

One canonical English paragraph is shortened. The specific account explanations above it and the existing per-session publication guidance remain the owners of those details. No new controls, state, helpers or compatibility paths are added.

## Evidence

- Maintainer validation: the existing full built-app Chromium personal-account flow passed before (13.97s) and after (12.25s) removing four redundant copy assertions. The final diff changes only the English help paragraph; it adds no permanent tests. It opens and closes the real help, copies a synthetic device code, connects the personal fixture and disconnects it without changing the shared account or configuration. No live GitHub sign-in or external publication is exercised by the test.
- Original implementation verification: 61 focused GitHub UI/controller tests passed. Six selected backend contracts pass: agent-override precedence, selected-versus-effective identity, personal repository-checkpoint publication, and three busy/local-worktree refusal states. These are selected tests, not full backend suites.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass. An initial backend proof invocation was invalidated because I edited the locale during its compilation; it ran no tests. The source was then held stable and the selected tests passed. No broad CI or E2E matrix was run.
- Matched before/after captures below use real components, synthetic responses and an emulated 1280 × 1400 viewport. The affected paragraph is fully visible after scrolling the help panel; its same-frame crop and surrounding Profile context were inspected. Baseline main: `b75177698b1cffd865aac7051237960055fae8d7`.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): edit the bot's own messages
prs.body:
Related: #189815

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp is missing the `edit` message action that Telegram and Discord have, so an agent cannot correct a message it already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can edit their own WhatsApp messages. Turn it off with `channels.whatsapp.actions.editMessage: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `edit` the same way `react` works, behind the host's exact-current chat gate. Editing another user's message is refused when the cache knows the sender. On a cache miss the edit goes out under the bot's own key (`fromMe: true`); WhatsApp applies an edit only when it comes from the original sender, so such an edit has no effect on the other phone. That is provider behaviour, not something this PR enforces. Baileys resolves on the socket write, so the result says `submitted: true, confirmed: false`.

The edit key's chat is pinned to the chat the caller named. The message-cache lookup that quoting uses also matches a message through its sender. Only an entry whose stored peer number is the target's own number counts as this one-to-one chat under its other JID (phone number or LID) and may supply the key's `remoteJid`; anything else (a status update keyed by its poster, a broadcast list, a match through a bare participant JID) is another chat, and the edit is rejected with `message belongs to another chat`.

Caller authority: `edit` is declared in `writeAuthorityActions`, and the host's `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` is passed down the edit chain as a plain parameter. It is checked at the action handler and again inside the queued socket task, right after the socket-identity check and right before the native `sendMessage`. An edit whose originating run lost authority while it waited in the per-socket queue is dropped before any I/O. A revocation is never retried: the caller guard runs at the start of every send attempt, also while the socket is away, so a revoked caller never waits for a reconnect backoff, and the retry path re-checks the caller before classifying an error as a disconnect, so the caller gets the original guard error. Edits now use the ordinary send path, so the separate single-attempt path is gone.

Provider ownership (`fromMe`, the message cache) only scopes which messages are eligible; it does not stand in for caller authority. Both are required.

Scheduled edits stay out on purpose: `edit` is not in `providerOwnedReadGates`, so the host keeps its exact-current chat check and rejects a scheduled edit. A contract test locks that.

Known limitation: for an external install the host compares targets literally (it applies `normalizeTarget` only to bundled plugins), so a delegated edit must name a DM as `+E164`, the spelling the agent's prompt shows, or omit the target; a `...@s.whatsapp.net` spelling is rejected, fail-closed. Changing that is host policy and out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Live proof on 2026.11.1 (latest stable)

**Upgrade.** A real linked WhatsApp install was upgraded from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 with the normal npm install, `plugins update` and `doctor --fix`. Before and after the upgrade, the full config (sorted JSON), the WhatsApp auth creds and the number of files in the WhatsApp auth dir hashed identically, and the cron list count was unchanged. The channel came back `linked, connected, health:healthy` and the agent answered on its primary model. The config has no `actions.editMessage` key.

**Edit.** Then this PR's commit was cherry-picked onto `v2026.11.1`, `extensions/whatsapp` was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, and only the plugin's `dist` + manifest were swapped in (same dependency versions; all 94 `plugin-sdk/*` imports exist in the installed 11.1 core). Afterwards the stock 2026.11.1 plugin was put back. The cherry-pick differs from this branch only where 11.1's file layout differs from main (the action list lives in `channel-actions.ts` there, plus import lines); the edit, authority and socket code is the same as the pushed head, including the final same-chat guard and the no-socket caller check.

Phone number redacted; the message id is a random WhatsApp id.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

$ openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 3"
"action": "send", "handledBy": "core", "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8"
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 4"
"action": "edit", "handledBy": "plugin",
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8" }
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +15555550100 --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "must not arrive"
ToolAuthorizationError: WhatsApp edit blocked: chatJid "+15555550100" is not in the
configured allowFrom list for account "default".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message ""
Error: WhatsApp edit rejected: text is empty.
[exit 1]

# a message the other phone sent earlier; after the restart the cache does not know it
$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A --json \
    --message "must not arrive (not this account's message)"
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A" }
[exit 0]
```

**Receiving side.** On the receiving account's WhatsApp Web (read-only IndexedDB lookup by message id), the received message `3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8` carries `latestEditMsgKey`, with the edit's sender timestamp 4.4 s after the original. So the edit reached the other phone; it is not only a socket write. The last command above targets a message the other phone itself sent: the socket accepted the write (`submitted: true`), but on the receiving side that message has no `latestEditMsgKey`. WhatsApp dropped the edit because it did not come from the message's sender, which is the provider behaviour the Why section relies on for a cache miss.


### Delegated edit from a real inbound turn (2026.11.1)

Same install and plugin port, plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/extensions` (origin `global`, so the host treats it as an external plugin, the same trust class as the integration test below). The owner's phone sent the bot a WhatsApp DM asking it to call the `message` tool twice. The group is configured and allowed (`groups` + `groupAllowFrom`, the bot is a member), so the plugin itself would accept it. Gateway log plus the session trajectory from `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`; numbers redacted, times UTC:

```text
14:19:11  CLI (direct operator)  message send -> +<owner>  messageId 3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19  "...: meet at 3"
14:19:43  web-inbound            Inbound message +<owner> -> <bot> (direct, 494 chars)
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"+<owner>",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"...: meet at 4"}
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"<allowed-group>@g.us",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"must not arrive"}
14:19:49.762  tool.result (group)  error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.
14:19:49.789  tool.result (DM)     {"ok":true,"submitted":true,"confirmed":false,"messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19"}
14:19:52      web-outbound         the bot's text reply with both raw tool results
```

Receiving side (read-only WhatsApp Web IndexedDB lookup by message id): before the turn the received message had no `latestEditMsgKey`; after it, `latestEditMsgKey` is set with edit sender timestamp 14:19:49.783, the moment of the DM tool result. The group call was stopped in `message-action-dispatch` before the plugin ran (gateway log: `[tools] message failed: Error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.`); the only outbound socket traffic in that window is the edit and the bot's text reply.

The earlier `openclaw agent --to ...` attempts were rejected for a different reason: a CLI-started run has no host-minted turn capability, so the gateway receives no tool context or requester account and fails closed before comparing targets. That is the host's design, not this PR.

Not covered live: a second linked account and revocation while queued (one linked account; revocation cannot be timed from outside). Both are covered by the host-issued-guard integration test below.

### Tests on this branch, rebased on current main

- Host-issued caller guard, end to end (`test/whatsapp-message-edit.integration.test.ts`, on the shared `createMessageReadAuthority` harness, reaching the plugin only through `api.js` and a new `extensions/whatsapp/test-api.ts`, the same public test surface the Discord and Slack suites use): a really minted turn capability and run claim, the message tool under the gateway caller identity, the in-process `message.action` handler (which builds `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` itself), the plugin registered as an external install, the real WhatsApp handler and the real socket session; only Baileys' `sendMessage` is a mock. The test never supplies a guard. The config allows both the other chat and the other account, so only the host can refuse them. Cases:
  1. the current chat's edit reaches the socket with the edit key and returns `submitted: true, confirmed: false`;
  2. the same run naming another allowed chat is rejected before the socket;
  3. the same run's identity sent straight to the gateway's `message.action` with another allowed account is rejected by the host before the socket;
  4. `revokeMessageActionTurnCapability` (what the reply run calls when it ends), called after the edit's preflight while it waits behind a busy send, drops it with `agent runtime authority is no longer active`; the socket only ever sees the busy send.

  Red checks: with the in-queue re-check removed, case 4 fails (the edit reaches the socket); with the host's account comparison disabled, case 3 fails. The old vertical test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` is removed; this test replaces it.
- Socket session (unit level, with a test guard): the queued caller check runs after the socket-identity check and before native I/O; a revoked caller is not retried and gets the guard's own error, also when the error text looks like a disconnect; a revoked caller with no current socket is rejected at once, without a backoff wait; a guard rejection leaves no send-ready proof behind for the next send.
- Message cache: ids containing `:` are never cached or found, so the colon-joined cache key cannot collide.
- Contract: a scheduled `whatsapp:edit` is rejected with "requires provider-owned target authorization".
- Through the plugin handler: a target outside `allowFrom`, another account's `allowFrom`, a message cached as foreign, a message cached in another chat (a status update, or another person's chat matched only through a participant JID), and `actions.editMessage: false` all stop before the socket; a message cached under the other spelling of the same chat, with the target's number as its stored peer, keeps its cached `remoteJid` in the edit key.
- Through the host dispatcher: a direct operator's edit reaches the listener, a delegated caller naming another chat stops at the gate, and a chat removed from `allowFrom` stops the next edit.
- Upgrade compatibility: a config without `actions.editMessage` parses and enables edit; the message cache is in memory and its shape is unchanged.

Rebased on `main` at 47c5db59fd6 (16 Nov); the conflicts were the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` (regenerated) and an import line in `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.ts`, where #198428 switched `mediaAccess` to `OutboundMediaAccess` (both imports kept). On that head, `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` passes every lane except the dead-export scan, which fails on `main` itself on files this PR does not touch (`src/state/*-swap.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-rollback.test-support.ts`). The WhatsApp extension, the edit-gate contract, the integration test and the WhatsApp schema tests pass.

Before that rebase: WhatsApp extension: 101 files, 1107 tests passing; the new integration file 4/4; the extension test-boundary suite 13/13. Contract, dispatcher (`message-action-dispatch.registry`) and schema tests pass; `tsgo` (core, extensions, extension tests, root tests), oxlint, format, `config:docs:check` and `check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` are clean.

### Test-line allocation

Duplicated cases were removed (the vertical queued-revocation test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` and its helpers, now replaced by the host-issued-guard test; the duplicate queued-revocation case in `monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts`; the per-dispatch allowFrom case in `channel-actions.test.ts`; the successful-edit case in `channel-actions.test.ts`, which the host-issued-guard test proves end to end; the cached-foreign case in `send.test.ts`); each contract is still proven at an equal or stronger boundary. The attached-listener setup that `channel-actions.test.ts` and the new test both need lives once in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/attached-listener.test-support.ts`, and the shared harness only gained an optional gateway-context resolver. The remaining net growth of 1152 lines is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/whatsapp-edit-own-messages.txt`, shared scalar unchanged. It is needed because this adds a new write action whose authority has to hold across the host gate, the plugin's account/`allowFrom` checks and the queued socket write, and each of those boundaries has its own test.
