prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.3 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, using the same minimatch options as the `extraPaths` matcher beside it in the memory host SDK (so patterns behave the same on Node and Bun), is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). **Portable glob matching (ClawSweeper's 2026-11-09 review on `05585b7`):** the exclusion matcher called `path.posix.matchesGlob`, which Bun implements with `Bun.Glob`: extglobs never match and wildcards match dotfiles, so `["memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md"]` excluded a report on Node but not on Bun. Main's #194912 had just moved the `extraPaths` matcher to minimatch for the same reason. `1463f6e` moves those minimatch options into one shared constant and uses it for `excludePaths` too, with compiled matchers cached per configured list. Results on Node are unchanged; on Bun they now match Node. Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main `11a13b6`: production +89/-21 in 15 files (including moving main's glob options into the shared constant); tests +159/-3; docs +16/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2654 -> 2658 on main `b03fd2f`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `c210875` (on main `c7152f3`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.3` from npm (installed with `--ignore-scripts`; the CLI runs without the package's install scripts). The branch CLI on `c210875` reports `2026.11.2` because main's version string trails the release. Earlier runs from 2026.11.2 on `1463f6e` and on `05585b7` (before the portable-matcher change), from 2026.11.1 on `6d9ace7` and from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.3 and existing data:** 2026.11.3 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.3, v27 -> v41), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.3, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.3 OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.279 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.272 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.266 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.260 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.254 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.3): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.3): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (c210875) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.3 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v41 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.3 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.279 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.272 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.266 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.260 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.254 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~1s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). - `internal.test.ts` "keeps generated dreaming reports out of default and overlapping extra paths" also lists files with `memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md`. With the old `path.posix.matchesGlob` matcher, `listMemoryFiles` under Bun still returns the report: on stock Bun 1.3.14 it lists `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md, memory/dreaming/light/report.md`, and with `1463f6e` only `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md`. On Node both matchers agree, so the Node run passes either way; the CI shard that runs this test (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-6`) sets up the pinned Bun 1.4.4 test runtime. **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +154, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and portable (Node/Bun) glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch merged main `11a13b6` at `2401ff9`, `1463f6e` adds the portable-matcher fix (its CI passed), `c210875` merged main `c7152f3`, `edb9fd1` merged main `aab88e3`, `fc2ef72` merged main `ba6147a`, `5985aa9` merged main `81ca4f4`, and `e768746` now merges main `b03fd2f`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. The v2026.11.3 proof above ran on `c210875`. `edb9fd1`, `fc2ef72`, `5985aa9` and `e768746` add only main's changes. In `5985aa9` and `e768746`, main's #195369 adds an embedding-cache hook to `manager-sync-base.ts` and #197128, #198348, #199226 and #199694 edit other entries in `schema.help.models.ts`; both files merge cleanly next to this PR's lines. In `edb9fd1`, main's #196480 changed session-export paging in neighboring memory-core sync files, which do not call the file listing, the exclusion matcher or the scope hash. Main's #194912 replaced `path.posix.matchesGlob` in the `extraPaths` matcher in `internal.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge kept both, and `1463f6e` then shares main's options with the exclusion matcher. Main's #139230 reworked dirty-index maintenance and the watcher's background sync in `manager-watch-ops.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge keeps this PR's one `excludePaths` line there, and `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts`, `watch-policy.test.ts` and `manager.watcher-config.test.ts` pass on `e768746`. Main's #191749 bounded the realpath deduplication at the end of `listMemoryFiles`; it merges cleanly because `excludePaths` filters files as they are collected, before that step. Main's #192488 moved the search manager types into `search-manager.types.ts`; this PR does not import them. Main's #193952 added provider name and icon help to `schema.help.models.ts`, which this PR also edits; both sets of entries merge cleanly. On `1cc43f3`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `ci-gate`) failed because main `bf10667` was over its own test-line ceiling by 137 lines; main's own scheduled job logged the same overage and passed only because that run added no test lines. Main `d1ffc39` got back under the ceiling, and the ratchet passes locally on `e768746` (net +154 test lines, covered by this PR's 154-line allocation). On `df4f9e6`, `check-prompt-snapshots` failed on three JSON prompt snapshots this PR does not touch: main's #192596 stopped formatting JSON snapshots without regenerating the committed ones (the content was identical, only the layout differed). Main fixed it in #192628, `5d93337` merged that fix, and `prompt:snapshots:check` passes locally on `e768746`. On `0a3aa17`, 19 CI jobs failed in setup before running any check because downloading the pinned Bun runtime from the `openclaw/bun` release returned HTTP 504; `pnpm test:ci-failed 188294` found no test failures, and CI on `5858e44` passed. On `b0f8904`, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-6` failed in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file.test.ts` (`scopes extra-path EACCES/EPERM/EIO errors to the requested file`), a file this PR does not touch. Main's #194560 updated fs-safe to 0.28.0, which now re-checks the root directory with `lstat` and reports a failure there as `path-mismatch` ("root path changed during operation", with the native error as its cause); `readMemoryFile` maps `path-mismatch` to `not_found`, so the test's explicit file entry no longer reads. The same three tests fail on main `748f3dc` with this PR's files reverted; CI runs them here only because this PR touches `packages/memory-host-sdk`. Main rolled fs-safe back to 0.27.1 in #194589; `05585b7` merges that rollback, and `read-file.test.ts` passes locally (19/19). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `config:docs:check` pass, and the touched tests plus `memory-files-worker.test.ts`, `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` and `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` (files main also changed) pass. `checks-node-changed` on `a63b2b5` failed in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` after main's #188833 referenced an untyped SDK entrypoint in a guide; main fixed it in #188937, and that test passes locally on `e768746`. On `5a03cd1`, `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3` (and so `ci-gate`) failed in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-publication-admission.test.ts` because main's #189247 changed seal-less agent-database opens while that memory-core test still expected the synchronous integrity check; it failed the same way on main `f8e492f` without this PR. Main fixed the test in #189449. On `fc2ef72`, `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3` and `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-7` (and so `ci-gate`) fail on three memory-core tests in files this PR does not touch: `manager-publication-admission.test.ts` (`retains reindexed memory admission with a invalid seal without skipping required integrity`: after an invalid seal, the restarted process finds no `sqlite.full-verification` admission fact), `manager.borrowed-connection.test.ts` (`rejects shared integrity failure before exposing a manager`) and `cli.test.ts` (`fails index --force when the memory index has orphaned provenance`). All three expect an integrity failure to surface when the agent database is opened. They fail the same way without this PR on main `0e966cc` (#194484, which changed when owed full verification runs), on `ba6147a` and on `4092d35`, and pass on the parent of `0e966cc`. The rest of CI on `fc2ef72` passed (72 checks). Main reworked these test fixtures in #197543; `5985aa9` merged that, and `manager-publication-admission.test.ts` (7/7) and `manager.borrowed-connection.test.ts` (22/22) pass locally on `e768746`. Locally, `cli.test.ts` still fails one test as rewritten by #197543 (`fails index --force after full verification records orphaned provenance`): its setup finds no `SqliteIntegrityError` quarantine record after corrupting the database. It fails the same way with this PR's files reverted to main `81ca4f4`. CI on `5985aa9` and `e768746` has not run yet: its workflows wait for a maintainer to approve runs for this fork PR (`action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` reports failure until CI completes. On `3bb1a2e`, `check-lint-core-5` failed on two `typescript(no-unnecessary-type-arguments)` errors in `src/skills/workshop/experience-review.test.ts` (lines 167-168, `createDeferred()`), which main's #190158 (`22c1060`) added; this PR does not touch that file. Main's push CI skips the full core lint stripes, so main did not flag it. Main removed the type arguments in #190292; `8866f78` merged that fix and its CI, including `check-lint-core-5` and `ci-gate`, passed. **Local review:** autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `upstream/main`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.87). It ran on `685db0c`, before the rebases onto `200afde` and `f980e01`, which changed only the base and the generated baseline files. Not covered: Windows paths (the matcher normalizes `path.sep`) and a live remote node workspace (the harness test checks that list and watch requests carry `excludePaths`).

prs.title: fix(ui): Profile recovery points to unavailable actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Profile recovery messages send users to nonexistent controls when an OpenClaw ID is already linked elsewhere or their profile cannot load.

## User Impact

User impact: both messages now point to supported next steps. The account conflict explains unlinking from the other profile and administrator merging only when both profiles belong to the same person; the load failure points to the existing Refresh button.

This is an English copy correction only. It does not merge or unlink profiles, change permissions, or alter sign-in or recovery behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stock Control UI has no Users merge view or Set identity control. The existing merge owner requires administrator access, while the actual Profile header already offers Refresh. Two canonical English strings are corrected rather than adding controls or another recovery path.

## Evidence

- Maintainer validation passed 36 Profile cases plus 535 standard UI canaries. The conflict-to-success regression remains; duplicate copy assertions and exact total/Nth RPC assertions were removed. Targeted lint and formatting pass, and an independent review found no actionable issues. Production changes remain limited to the two English strings.
- Two real built-app browser flows pass: Link → linked-elsewhere explanation → later successful Link; and failed profile read → Refresh → loaded account controls. They use synthetic Gateway responses and a noncredential account fixture, not live authentication. No profile merge or unlink is performed.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, i18n verification and diff checks pass. No broad CI or full E2E matrix was run.
- Simplification pass: two production strings only; regression coverage stays in existing owner suites. No new production helpers, state or compatibility paths.

Matched current-main before/after screenshots below show the actual Profile components in an emulated 1280 × 1000 light-theme viewport. Baseline main: `5025db61e9482d95f29956f266496f32f4f94f72`; relevant Profile owners and English strings are unchanged at observed main `005850723d3c65028f8ded0580c0ba8bea4bc18d`. Crops come from their corresponding full frames; full-page context was also inspected. The refresh recovery row excludes an unrelated random test Gateway port. The linked-account example grows by one line to explain the existing administrator boundary.

### OpenClaw ID conflict — Before

![Before: account conflict points to an unavailable Users merge view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e9146fb-1341-4026-be72-2df41e2e02f6)

### OpenClaw ID conflict — After

![After: account conflict explains unlinking and administrator merging of the same person's profiles](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2476b51-a599-4ebc-9263-e100ee3a9a67)

### Profile could not load — Before

![Before: recovery suggests a nonexistent Set identity control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30ea7edf-fabe-4d4d-a127-f1bdcfef127d)

### Profile could not load — After

![After: recovery points to the existing Refresh button at the top of Profile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bc68f3a-6d6e-4e91-bc58-4c94ce6a254c)

Requested by and co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/27ab8da9-7856-4f25-9b62-91d8138f1a1c)

prs.title: fix: avoid repeated transcript copies during manual compaction
prs.body:
Related: #199561

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary transcript copying when manual compaction prepares a session, adding work on the Gateway's main thread before summarization begins.

## User Impact

Manual compaction preparation no longer requests writable copies of immutable transcript payloads merely to inspect them. Performance acceptance remains pending. This PR does not fix automatic warm-session compaction or all main-thread stalls. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing internal read-only branch accessor for synchronous manual preflight, instead of requesting writable copies immediately before context projection. Public SDK mutation isolation, model-context filtering, extension behavior, and writer/cancellation checks are unchanged; no worker or cache is added.

Requested and guided by @RomneyDa.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5e28e403-d17b-4ca9-afd8-1851a62198b3)

## Evidence

- Real composition regression fails on exact base `9f0f89522a633826aa5c64483cca3bec3dacca34` at retained payload ownership and passes with this change. Delegate suite: **30/30 passed**; unchanged codec siblings: **27/27 passed**.
- Targeted format, lint, agents-other test type graph and `git diff --check` pass. CI-only pinned-Bun parity was not run locally. Canonical local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) found no actionable findings in the exact-base/final local snapshot. Published head `54617a8c765a8672c1459da190ad08567e38bb0e` has the same tree as reviewed/tested signed commit `7bcfe0a3b7757a50ee0a759add452b620b54989a`.
- Exact baseline and published-head `sourcePerformance` builds pass. Workload `f30da43971c6b210df2e89962d0af639bc04107e` passed **17 isolated admission/control-flow contracts** and fresh canonical local P0–P2 autoreview. All **four separately tagged real-Gateway qualifiers passed and were audited**: native compaction, physical-session 8192-byte continuity, matched two-request summary work, default limits, CPU brackets and cleanup.
- [ClawSweeper's review of the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199840#issuecomment-6903144771) lists **no code findings** and requests the declared end-to-end performance evidence. That evidence is not yet complete.
- The original frozen twenty-slot comparison was **interrupted by a Gateway restart** after six native-valid cold observations (three pairs). The seventh slot was interrupted before measured compaction; thirteen slots were unattempted. Original receipts and all outcomes are retained unchanged. This is not a completed five-pair population, a warm comparison, or performance acceptance. The interrupted task container is stopped. No failed tag was replayed and no observations were pooled or relabeled.
- The earlier single profiled baseline remains exploratory only. Prior setup failures, the corrected invalid module-registry oracle and the receipt-shape admission refusal remain recorded separately.

### Prospective performance rule — published before comparison timing

Real manual compaction through isolated built Gateways, the same private long-session fixture, native import and same-physical-session 8192-byte follow-up. Compare exact base `9f0f89522a633826aa5c64483cca3bec3dacca34` against exact published head `54617a8c765a8672c1459da190ad08567e38bb0e`. Workload `f30da43971c6b210df2e89962d0af639bc04107e` preserves the five canonical rig/turn/mock/importer/observer files from `007777bbf9917bdc62a488b9e348990fc06c6a04`. Successful exact builds, fixture/workload/protocol hashes, native admission and the complete order are frozen before accepted runs. Qualification timings are excluded.

Five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs cold, then five pairs process-warm, without profiling. Report every outcome, median, nearest-rank p95 (=maximum at n=5), min/max and spread for compaction/follow-up latency, whole-process and independently sampled main-thread CPU, RPC/lifecycle RSS and heap, and main-thread pulse gaps. Include bracket overhang and host load; all native integrity and cleanup checks must pass. No selective reruns, pooling or outlier removal.

A win requires copying reduction and measurable real-flow improvement without worse user-facing metrics. After each complete five-pair population, a **20% or greater adverse median or p95 in any measured cell stops before another population**. Missing measurements block; zero-baseline/positive-candidate values stop. Smaller adverse cells remain visible and require explicit informed owner acceptance before landing. With no measurable gain, do not land as a performance improvement. Recovery must retain the interrupted original cohort and use separately declared fresh tags/bindings, never rewrite its receipts or silently combine populations.

<details>
<summary>Evidence reuse and measurement limits</summary>

The successful exact-base build is reused, not rebuilt. A separate audited schema supplement retains original install/build receipts and hashes. Whole-tree/dist fingerprints were observed at prior diagnostic admission/end and rechecked, not retroactively observed at build completion; that observation gap remains explicit. The candidate install/build binds the exact published head. Literal probe/install shell-child decoding preserves the actual recorded command without repeating the successful install.

The unchanged nominal 100 ms main-isolate sampler gives a coarse maximum adjacent gap over the inclusive RPC bracket, including overhang. It cannot resolve sub-100 ms blocking or replace other-session RPC latency. Process CPU/RSS include workers; worker-only zero counters do not mean zero main-thread parsing.

Process-warm manual compaction is not resident automatic compaction. Unrelated-session RPC probes occur after compaction, so concurrent responsiveness remains unproven. The fixture is one whole observed generation with fixed mock summaries, not a broad corpus or provider-quality test.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa
- @vincentkoc
- @jalehman

prs.title: fix: unblock carrier-backed releases within a 12k request budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes beta.4 publication being refused when the 101-package carrier-backed release reserves 26,880 GitHub requests despite needing substantially fewer.

Maintainer-requested active-release tooling repair: set a 12,000-request target without changing the qualified candidate or rerunning FRV.

## User Impact

Release operators can publish the already-qualified candidate within the approved request budget. C/Q, the signed release tag, package bytes, and successful FRV 43757970051/1 remain unchanged. This does not raise GitHub's quota or weaken live authorization checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reduce the carrier-backed consume/authorize transport ceiling from 128 to 54 requests per command. Admission uses the same enforced ceiling: 101 × 2 × 54 + 1,024 headroom = **11,932**. The carrierless limit is unchanged. Final permission/ref/parent checks, pagination, and retry accounting remain in place; exceeding the cap still fails closed.

The regression runs each package through separate real CLI consume/authorize processes for ordinary and receipt-recovery carriers. The recovery fixture now emits actual 100-item artifact pages instead of an invalid oversized first page.

## Evidence

- Both 101-package cases fail on original tooling at admission: 26,880 required versus 12,000 remaining.
- Patched full flows: **4,900 ordinary requests; 7,792 recovery requests**, including all 101 consume/authorize pairs. Each command checks its enforced 54-request cap. The complete process and transport suites passed: 29/29 tests in 213.69 seconds, including retained final-authority/tamper and carrierless coverage.
- Focused lint, tooling-test typecheck, formatting, diff check, and test-line budget passed.
- Local ClawSweeper unavailable. Local autoreview attempted against the full working delta on base 113d6243f36094de453622a9e5cbb25da029b83c, P2 coverage, but returned reviewer_unavailable (engine exit 1), with no report. This is not a clean review. Hosted ClawSweeper fallback requested when ready.

The full-topology process tests intentionally exceed the usual unit-test duration: admission-only or shared-process tests cannot prove that every separately launched consumer fits the enforced transport budget. Responses are synthetic; these are CLI-boundary request counts, not production network measurements. The 12k target covers the current 101-package topology, not arbitrary future package growth. Larger graphs/retry bursts can exhaust the cap and stop safely. No new cache or authorization shortcut.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Start agents, Workboard counts worker-start failures without showing their cause and describes triage cards awaiting planning as “organized.”

## User Impact

User impact: the receipt shows the first worker-start failure alongside the full failure count, and describes planning candidates as marked for planning rather than completed work. Readiness updates and released claims are named separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher already returns each start failure’s title and reason, but the browser normalization discarded them. The existing receipt projection now retains the first failure and the existing toast formats it through the host redactor. The preview is deliberately labeled “First start failure” rather than growing an unbounded error report; all counts remain visible.

The orchestration owner only records an idle protocol state awaiting specification or decomposition. The summary now describes that effect. Admission, execution, retry behavior, scheduling, permissions, refresh handling and model selection are unchanged. No new helper or renderer is added.

The current #194983 diff retains the affected dispatch summary. #199288 owns disabled-automation wording and #199295 owns label selection; neither is duplicated here.

## Maintainer Verification

Reproduced the CI type error in the new test, then replaced its ad hoc client with the existing Workboard test-client adapter. The test repair adds no cast and does not change the production interface. The test now observes actual view notifications instead of forcing a render, while retaining failure counts, first-cause-only display, redaction and recovery.

The final dispatch/editor selection and standard UI canaries passed (559 tests), and the full extension-test typecheck passed. Focused lint and formatting passed, including the documentation. Independent static review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Production code and the inspected author screenshots are unchanged by this test repair.

## Evidence

- The new real-view action regression fails on the original copy and dropped failure detail. **37 focused UI/owner tests pass** with redaction, multiple-failure counts, bounded preview and cleared failure after a later successful receipt.
- **Two production-owner contracts pass**: triage cards remain triage and await planning; an unsandboxed target produces a start refusal before claiming work. Backend code is unchanged.
- Full built-app flow through the packaged Workboard plugin passes before/after: Start agents, planning-only receipt plus refused start, close feedback, then a successful second dispatch after simulated external preflight repair. Exactly two dispatch requests; no card creation or direct chat.send. This is synthetic transport evidence, not live worker/configuration execution.
- Both existing native lazy-page cases pass, including actual chunk-load failure and reload recovery.
- Workboard and full UI typechecks, scoped lint, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. No broad local CI run.

Baseline: current main 92016ce978f0f638369ecd0d10fcaa9212e591ce at capture; affected owners are unchanged at observed main e4f55593741ed56f9bac9196847bb079f25c8d75. Real controls, synthetic data, emulated 1280 × 900 viewport. The clock is paused only for the receipt capture and resumed for recovery.

After

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Template detail page in the Control UI has no right-hand rail, so a Template shows no security audit, version, dates, downloads or categories, while the plugin detail page shows all of them.

## User Impact

User impact: before adding a Template, people can see its ClawHub security audit (linked to the full report), the release version, when it was updated and published, its download count and its categories, in the same rail and position as on a plugin page. On narrow windows the rail moves below the contents, as it does for plugins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Template page already used the plugin page's detail shell but never supplied its sidebar, and the Template detail read did not carry the facts the rail needs.

- The Template detail read now returns the exact release's audit (verdict and audit link), the package's publication date and its categories. The audit is optional context for the page: if that read fails, or the report describes another package or release, the detail still loads and the rail shows no audit rather than a guessed one. Add continues to enforce trust through its own check.
- The rail renderer is shared between the plugin and Template pages, so the two cannot drift apart. The plugin rail's markup and output are unchanged.
- While the release loads, the rail shows the version, updated date and downloads already known from the catalog entry, and placeholders for the rest, so the layout does not shift when the detail arrives.

The unused optional `scanStatus` field on the Template detail result is replaced by `security`. It was never populated, and the Gateway and Control UI ship together. The catalog result types moved to a sibling module only to keep `clawhub-source.ts` within its line cap.

## Evidence

Screenshots are from two isolated Gateways on loopback with separate state directories, each serving its own built Control UI and reading the live `myfitnessclaw@0.2.5` release from ClawHub. prs.title: feat: localize model failure notices in English and German
prs.body:
Closes #199735
Related: #113105 (localization tracking), #193641, #167341

## What Problem This Solves

German-speaking conversations still receive fixed English recovery notices when a model request fails, including on WhatsApp.

## User Impact

Operators can select English or German for supported model-failure notices through `messages.locale`, with a WhatsApp channel/account override via `messageLocale`. A verified person's `messages.locale` preference, set through the existing `users.prefs.set` RPC, takes precedence in direct messages. Groups use channel/account and global defaults. English remains the default and the fallback for unsupported client locales.

This is a bounded localization slice for model-failure notices, not complete localization of every command or status message. It does not add a language picker or translate ordinary model answers. The feature adds no database schema migration.

## Implementation

The reply owner captures language once per request and carries it through execution, followups, and transcript metadata. Queued messages with different languages are not collected into one turn. Personal choice reuses the authenticated profile preference store; WhatsApp supplies its resolved account setting through the existing inbound context.

Failure producers render from classified facts. The captured language also reaches combined tool/provider failures, subscription lifecycle events, shared harness lifecycle events, and failures without an assistant message. Error categories are recorded before translation and survive deferred delivery; replacement failures clear obsolete categories. Raw diagnostic classification, provider codes, cancellation, and provider-refusal handling retain their semantics. The existing Gateway text fallback remains for older lifecycle producers.

A narrow subscription parameter projection keeps forwarding explicit and the preparation module within the existing size limit. No lint threshold or test assertion was weakened.

## Validation

- Initial feature validation: 376 tests in 18 files covered English compatibility, returned/thrown failures, personal preference persistence, Gateway client locale, queue separation, transcript metadata/write hooks, WhatsApp configuration/inbound propagation, and prompt-prefix stability. Subsequent original-feature review regressions also passed; those runs overlap.
- Follow-up repair validation: 271 tests in 14 affected runner/lifecycle/dispatch/prompt suites passed. After the parameter projection was extracted, all 45 subscription-owner tests passed again.
- Final category/recovery checks: 16 Gateway tests passed, including German immediate and deferred failures with preserved error categories and provider codes; 59 observation/lifecycle/recovery tests passed. These totals overlap earlier runs.
- The combined tool/provider regressions, personal-language Gateway regression, incomplete-turn regression, and shared-harness language regression failed before their respective fixes.
- Core typecheck, type-aware lint over every changed TypeScript file, formatting, and the test-line budget check passed. A fresh independent static review returned no actionable P0–P2 findings in the selected repair scope; runtime validation was run separately.

- Transport-copy follow-up (`e3c9ca299f49`): 107 focused presentation/formatter tests and all 10 native Gateway error-event tests passed. New regressions reproduced the incorrect German timeout copy for connection/DNS failures and generic internal errors before the fix; genuine timeouts retain timeout copy. The Gateway regression also preserves the existing structured timeout retry category. Core typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and test-line budget passed again; a fresh independent static review of this small delta returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. The built-Gateway/restart/upgrade evidence below is retained from the preceding revision and was not rerun for this renderer-only correction.

### Built Gateway and latest-stable upgrade

The committed `test/gateway-localized-failures.e2e.test.ts` drives a built Gateway over real RPC/WebSocket and HTTP model transport, with a local deterministic Responses fixture and an actual failed read tool. It verifies German defaults, personal English overriding German, durable preferences, and English fallback after restart.

The optional upgrade lane was run from the official `openclaw@2026.11.3` package (commit `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`). prs.title: fix(templates): catalog shows image files in a Template as garbled text
prs.body:
Closes #198767

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the Templates catalog, image files a Template ships (avatars, icons) appear in the detail with a 2,048-character garbled excerpt, and previewing one returns the image bytes decoded as text.

## User Impact

Binary workspace files are still listed by name in the catalog detail, now without an excerpt, and previewing one answers "This workspace file is not text, so it has no preview." Text files keep their excerpts and previews.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readClawHubCatalogPreview` (`src/templates/clawhub-preview-content.ts:61`) decoded every verified workspace file with `toString("utf8")`, and the detail builds each excerpt from that preview (`src/templates/clawhub-source.ts:507`). The preview now checks the verified bytes with `isUtf8` and declines non-text files with a `clawhub_preview_not_text` source error. The detail reads excerpts through `readClawHubCatalogExcerpt` in the same module, which lists such a file without an excerpt instead of failing the whole detail; every other preview error still fails it as before. Showing images inline would need a new preview kind and UI rendering, which the issue left as an alternative.

## Evidence

Started a real Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`) from `main` (93fdc3d9ada) and from this branch with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, Templates enabled in Labs and the default registry (clawhub.ai, read only), and called the catalog methods for `meta-ads-agent@0.1.1` with `openclaw gateway call`.

```
# main
templates.catalog.detail meta-ads-agent 0.1.1, workspace files
  AGENTS.md                   | excerpt chars: 1807 | starts: "Working records Read dat"
  avatars/meta-ads-agent.png  | excerpt chars: 2048 | starts: "�PNG \u001a \u0000\u0000\u0000 IHDR..."
  assets/icon.png             | excerpt chars: 2048 | starts: "�PNG \u001a \u0000\u0000\u0000 IHDR..."
  templates/config.json       | excerpt chars:  539 | starts: "{ \"schemaVersion\": 1, \"a"
templates.catalog.preview instruction assets/icon.png
  kind: instruction | content chars: 181044 | starts: "�PNG\r\n\u001a\n\u0000\u0000\u0000\rIHDR..."
templates.catalog.preview instruction AGENTS.md
  kind: instruction | content chars: 1820 | starts: "# Working records\nRead d"

# this branch
templates.catalog.detail meta-ads-agent 0.1.1, workspace files
  AGENTS.md                   | excerpt chars: 1807 | starts: "Working records Read dat"
  avatars/meta-ads-agent.png  | excerpt chars:    0 | starts: ""
  assets/icon.png             | excerpt chars:    0 | starts: ""
  templates/config.json       | excerpt chars:  539 | starts: "{ \"schemaVersion\": 1, \"a"
templates.catalog.preview instruction assets/icon.png
  {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"gateway_request_error","code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"This workspace file is not text, so it has no preview.","retryable":false}}
templates.catalog.preview instruction AGENTS.md
  kind: instruction | content chars: 1820 | starts: "# Working records\nRead d"
```

The other five files (`IDENTITY.md`, two JSON and one Markdown template, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `SOUL.md`) have identical excerpts on both trees.

Tests: the new case in `src/templates/clawhub-source.test.ts` adds a PNG workspace file to the verified fixture and checks that the detail lists it without an excerpt and that its preview fails with `clawhub_preview_not_text`. With main's preview and source modules it fails (the listed entry carries an excerpt). `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/templates/clawhub-source.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/templates.test.ts src/templates/clawhub-source-artifact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes (68 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, format check, `git diff --check` and the test-line ratchet (+22) pass.

Not verified: the Control UI document modal in a browser; it now receives the error above instead of image bytes.

Production delta +21/-1; test delta +22/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; no state or config. Blast radius is catalog detail excerpts and previews of workspace files that are not valid UTF-8.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents cannot install a published ClawHub Template through the OpenClaw setup helper, even though the Gateway already supports reviewing and adding it.

## User Impact

Agents can request `template_review` and `template_install` without gaining shell access. Installation retains exact-plan and dependency consent, the original administrator/request lifetime, cancellation and revocation checks, and the existing delegated-change approval policy. Missing authority, consent, or Templates enablement returns an actionable blocker. Trust warnings require exact human approval even under Full Access.

Results disclose the actual agent and workspace, complete/partial state, readiness requirements, dependency installation/reuse receipts, and automation outcomes. A failed automation is not reported as enabled. No live Gateway configuration was changed during this work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper now hands Template operations back to its host. UI RPCs and the helper share the same typed Template request owners and installer, rather than introducing another installation path. The host presents the full reviewed plan in its exact-operation approval and retains the requesting administrator through deferred decisions, including native/MCP-backed helper turns. No new configuration or persistent state is introduced.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(skill-workshop): show what whole-file SKILL.md writes and drafts drop
prs.body:
Closes #194826

_Prepared for Cosmin Toma (RUF agentic team)._

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent silently wipes most of a live skill when it sends a short change note as the content of a whole-file `SKILL.md` write or draft.

## User Impact

User impact: when a `SKILL.md` rewrite or draft would drop most of a live skill, the agent (and the user reviewing drafts) now sees how much is removed and which sections disappear, before anyone relies on it. Nothing is blocked; writes still land and can be undone with `restore`.

## Why This Change Was Made

In #194826 (on 2026.7.1-2) an 87-line change note replaced a 387-line skill through the old proposal flow, and nothing showed the loss. On `main` that flow is gone, but `write_file` of `SKILL.md` and `draft` still replace the file whole, and the tool contract never says so.

This PR:

- adds `skillReplacementReport(before, after)` in `skill-lint.ts`: body line count before/after (`SKILL.md body: 387 → 87 lines (-78%).`), up to 8 removed `##` sections (code blocks ignored), and a non-blocking advisory when the new body is under 60% of the old one;
- shows that report on `patch`/`write_file` of an existing `SKILL.md`, on `draft` for a live skill, and on `view draft`;
- adds a `change-note` lint advisory when the title starts with Fix / Proposal / Change(s) / Changelog (only when the write introduces it, like the other rules);
- states in the tool description, the `/learn drafts` prompt and `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` that `write_file`/`draft` content is the complete file and replaces it whole.

Advisory rather than blocking: writes are versioned with `restore`, and the codebase has no override-flag pattern for this. The Control UI already shows a diff before applying a draft.

Known nits: a legitimate title such as `# Change management` gets the change-note advisory; every `SKILL.md` patch now carries a one-line size summary; with the shrink advisory a write can end with four advisory lines instead of the documented three.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: `skill_library` `update` with `proposal_content` also replaces `SKILL.md` whole.

## Evidence

On `main` at d44c9ad92 with this commit applied:

- `pnpm test extensions/skill-workshop`: 16 files, 140 tests passed.
- New tests: `skill-lint.test.ts` (report and `change-note` rule) and `tool.test.ts` ("shows what a whole-file SKILL.md rewrite or draft drops from the live skill"), which reproduces the incident: a 65-line skill rewritten with a `# Fix: …` note via `draft`, `view draft`, and `write_file`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `oxlint extensions/skill-workshop`, and `git diff --check` pass. (On the original base 1ad3ec3d2 also oxfmt, `lint:docs` and the pre-commit hooks.)
- Gap: no end-to-end run against a live Gateway with a real agent; the change only adds text to tool results.

prs.title: feat: let the memory slot owner report its own dreaming status
prs.body: Related: #138366 ## What Problem This Solves A memory plugin that owns the memory slot and does its own consolidation has no way to describe its dreaming on the Memory page. The page reports dreaming as disabled or unscheduled while it in fact runs every night. Two host assumptions cause this: - `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` gives all three phases the same expression, so a plugin whose REM and deep passes run on separate schedules, or whose light pass is event-driven, cannot say so. - The promotion counters come from memory-core's own store, which stops advancing once another plugin takes over consolidation. The workaround is worse than the symptom. Setting `dreaming.enabled: true` on the slot owner makes memory-core create its managed promotion cron at the same frequency, so the same workspace gets two consolidation passes in the same minute. ## Why This Change Was Made `MemoryPluginCapability` already has this shape once. `publicArtifacts` lets a non-`memory-core` slot owner contribute data through an optional provider, while the host keeps ownership of semantics. This PR applies the same pattern to dreaming: ```ts export type MemoryPluginCapability = { publicArtifacts?: MemoryPluginPublicArtifactsProvider; dreaming?: MemoryPluginDreamingProvider; // added // … }; ``` The contract is reporting-only. Lifecycle, memory-core's managed sweep cron and the dream actions stay with memory-core. The full rules are in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context.md`: - **Overlay.** `doctor.memory.status` overlays the report field by field on the host resolution. Without a provider the response is unchanged. - **Every status path.** The provider is consulted with a search runtime, without one, and when the plugin answers through its own `providerRuntime` (new in this revision, see below). - **Owner lock.** Any report arrives as `reportedByProvider: true`. That locks the page's switch against turning the host sweep on, since both would dream at once. A running host sweep can still be turned off. The Off confirmation then says that the orphan-cron cleanup from #156667 (now on main, at plugin reload and at startup) removes the promotion job memory-core already scheduled. - **Switch and scene.** Reported `enabled` arrives as `reportedEnabled`. The switch keeps showing the memory-core configuration it writes. The Dreams scene lights while the owner reports running, or while a phase is enabled and scheduled. - **Counters.** Reported counters arrive as `reportedStats` next to memory-core's figures, not in their place. The Dreaming status line and Settings > Memory › Activity show the owner's counters, with n/a for any it omits. The Review lists keep memory-core's figures, entries and actions, together with a note that says so. - **Schedule rows.** Settings > Memory › Sleep schedule takes each phase's state from its own `enabled` and `scheduled` flags while an owner reports. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main and resolves the two P2 findings of the last review: - **Provider-runtime slot owners.** A plugin that registers both `providerRuntime` and `dreaming.getStatus` took the provider-runtime branch, which returned before the dreaming lookup. That reply now carries the same composed dreaming section. `respondProviderMemoryStatus` keeps its authority checks, health and close. Test: `doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts` › "composes the slot owner's report into a provider-runtime health reply". - **Admitted-plugin value contract (#163818).** The report now crosses by reference. The validator and copier helpers, their tests and the matching docs are gone. A throw or a `null` report still keeps memory-core's resolution. - **Ported onto main's new owners.** The payload fields now live on the `gateway-protocol` `DoctorMemoryDreamingPayload` type. The Dreams controls, review and confirmation dialog are now Solid. Settings > Memory › Overview is memory-core's packaged browser view (`extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.tsx`). Main's phase chips no longer show times, so the earlier "last run" chip helper was dropped. `lastRunAtMs` still appears in the Overview schedule rows. ## Evidence **Before / after on current main** (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`). Both runs use the same `doctor.memory.status` fixture: slot owner `acme-memory` reports REM/deep schedules, an event-driven light phase and `promotedToday: 4`, while memory-core's own count is 2 and the host switch is off. | | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | Overview: phases and counters | | | | Dreams: scene and switch | | | **Live.** The previous revision of this change, on a 2026.10.10 build, has been running in a production installation since 2026-11-05 with a third-party memory slot owner that dreams on its own schedule. The Memory page shows the owner's schedule and counters, and memory-core's sweep stays off. **Patched Gateway (sandbox, 2026-11-09).** A Gateway built from this PR head (`5c7facacab3`, `pnpm build:runtime` plus the Control UI) ran isolated on loopback with no channels. The memory slot is held by a small **fixture** plugin, `acme-memory-fixture`, which registers `dreaming.getStatus` per this PR's contract and reports clearly fake data: REM 01:15, deep 04:00, an event-driven light phase, 4 promoted today / 139 total / 9 waiting. memory-core's own store was seeded with 1 waiting and 2 promoted today, so the two sets of figures stay visibly apart. Fixture source, seed script and the redacted config are in [`fixture/`](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/tree/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/fixture); the [README](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/README.md) maps every file to a scenario. | Owner reports, host sweep off | Host sweep on: Off confirmation | |---|---| | | | - `reportedStats` separation and the Review comparison: [RPC](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/01-owner-reports-host-off.rpc.txt), [Review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/01-owner-reports-host-off.dreams-review.png) and [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/01-owner-reports-host-off.overview.png) screenshots. prs.title: improve(ui): reduce scrolling stalls during tool-heavy replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scrolling stalls while a reply runs many tools with live output. Each event can republish session and child-roster presentation, repeatedly preparing the same growing turn.

## User Impact

This candidate makes tool-heavy replies cheaper to render while keeping output live, complete, and ordered. **Draft: the current head failed input-tail qualification and will not be landed.** A revision is in progress. The independent PageUp correctness fix already landed in #195441.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing run owner's animation frame for session and child-roster presentation notifications. Authoritative state and event handling stay synchronous; terminal, hidden-page, and no-animation-frame paths still publish immediately. Reuse immutable source preparation, while resolving run ownership and consuming attachments afresh on each pass. Remove duplicate bundle bookkeeping.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before running: 20 rotated base/head/base-control triplets in Chromium 1× and 4× and Firefox, with unloaded and text-streaming controls. Require at least 5% better frame p95 or meaningful input delay at both Chromium speeds, no worse Firefox tails, no mutation storm, and exact final 200-tool results/order/completion/anchors. No size ceiling increase. WebKit is unavailable because of the host WindowServer failure.

The frozen run uses the corrected committed benchmark at `c82980d7a598449351e314edf8a71a012b1e29c1`, with all 46 harness sources and the loader verified, fresh browser processes, and source/bundle identity checks. No failed or interrupted sample is replaced. Base is #195441 (`253a985ed9effefd1e1124a543c386d6e47e6b76`).

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chromium 1×, 20 triplets | Frame p95 median 133.4 → 66.55 ms; all 60 correctness outcomes pass |
| Input responsiveness — fails acceptance | Run-tail p95 input delay 17.6 → 22.8 ms; input-to-frame 19.6 → 25.6 ms. Remaining cells stopped; these regressions are not accepted. |
| Owner tests | 39 pass across three changed files; 17 affected assertions pass after final simplification |
| Typecheck, focused lint, format, native precommit | Pass |
| Production Knip and test-line ratchet | Pass |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Visual proof | Before/after synthetic final transcript attached; layout and typed draft preserved |

| Normalized gzip surface | Base | Head | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 90,867 B | 90,867 B | 0 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Startup CSS | 38,662 B | 38,662 B | 0 B |
| Chat JS | 1,296,952 B | 1,296,964 B | +12 B |
| New Session JS | 802,959 B | 802,959 B | 0 B |

Strict same-machine size comparison passes; the 12 B Chat difference is within the checker's 64 B build variance. No ceiling changed.

Production LOC: 2,653 → 2,750 (+97). Tests: +163 net, allocated exactly for frame delivery/cancellation and cached-source replacement/ambiguity/attachment retention; shared scalar unchanged. Overall diff: 379 additions / 116 deletions in nine files. The production growth owns pending callbacks and reuses parsed source facts; it adds no second scheduler or event protocol.

prs.title: fix: reduce clean worktree removal stalls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary recovery-capture work when removing a clean managed worktree with a large tracked tree.

## User Impact

Clean removals retain HEAD directly and skip building a redundant recovery commit. Tracked files, edited provisioned files, and the existing 30-day recovery window remain recoverable. Dirty and exact-state captures retain their existing behavior. New `clean-v1` refs require this version or newer for automatic restore; existing ordinary and exact recovery refs remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot owner already runs one read-only Git status against the cached index. Dirty captures already update only changed/new paths. Clean captures nevertheless enumerated the whole HEAD tree, budgeted it, checked every blob a second time, and wrote a synthetic commit. Reuse the owner's clean result, retain HEAD with an atomic ref publication, and teach restore, interrupted removal, eviction and retirement that this recovery point is HEAD itself. Provisioned bytes retain their separate recovery owner. No schema, configuration, cache, or retention-policy change.

The existing slow-removal diagnostic gains one bounded `recovery` field (`head`, `capture`, `none`). Existing logs cannot establish the clean fraction: 35/36 had no untracked files, but `tracked` was total tracked files. 97.2% is only an upper bound, not a measured skip rate. The field distinguishes recovery kinds among logged removals; the existing slow-log threshold still applies.

## Evidence

- Team r336, 2026-11-15: 36 slow removals returned successfully without deferral. Capture was 184 ms for 671 tracked files versus 1.6–4.1 s for about 65k; this scales with file count, not uptime. The snapshot is a Git recovery ref, not a filesystem snapshot.
- State-DB writer holds of 4.38 s, 4.05 s and 3.39 s coincided with removals despite batch execution ≤5 ms; one maintenance-task main-thread stall was 465 ms. This change removes demonstrated capture work; it does not claim that the writer-fsync coincidence or that production stall has been causally resolved. Rename-before-background-deletion and serial CPU-niced deletion already exist.
- Native Git, 65,000 synthetic tracked files, packed objects, warm index, two identical-code controls and five serial interleaved pairs: capture Git subprocesses **14 → 7**, synthetic commits **1 → 0**, full HEAD-tree inventories **1 → 0**, duplicate blob-validation batches **1 → 0**. Both arms perform one **65,000-file Git stat pass and zero content scans**. Initial host object availability/hydration remains.
- Median / observed p95 owner time **878 / 1,432 → 304 / 583 ms**; Node CPU median **294 → 48 ms**; exact V8 allocation median **232 → 54 MB**. A/A controls: 1,614 and 1,866 ms, 278 and 313 ms CPU, 235 and 229 MB allocation. Shared-host wall-time variance is retained in these figures; CPU excludes Git children.
- Full-service removal/restore and performance acceptance: see the completed 20-pair table below.
- Built CLI proof on final production source: `pnpm openclaw worktrees create/remove/restore --json` in an isolated profile preserves HEAD, tracked bytes and an edited provisioned file for clean-v1. Two additional records were created and removed by exact parent `8656c447df05`; the new built CLI restores both legacy-clean and legacy-dirty records, preserving original HEAD, dirty tracked/untracked contents and provisioned edits. No row/ref rewriting or migration was used.
- Regression fails on exact parent `8656c447df0528d32df66616d71ffeb1cc9ec1e6` because recovery is a new commit rather than HEAD. Focused proof covers 141 distinct tests across recovery, eviction, GC/retention, provisioned files, hidden flags/missing objects, exact-state retirement and diagnostics. Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. First exact-head CI exposed four capture-lifecycle fixture assumptions and one clean-recapture OID assumption; these are fixed in `ea47a46f83df`. The three affected files pass locally (34 passed, one platform-dependent skip), and the repair has a fresh scoped-clean Codex review.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes passed except existing unused exports. Exact-parent reproduction has the same 12 production / 8 full-tree findings: state-upgrade exports introduced by `ef930ebbad771ae219e033f8c5b59a12b5445ffb`, and member-welcome exports introduced by `cec47fd13f23df46069da1beb65ceaec6e66d04f` (#198491). These are main regressions, not ignored noise. The final benchmark setup change also passed targeted script types/lint.
- Retention audit: pruning of expired removed records is implemented and tested, including preserving within-retention recovery and retaining both refs when a pending-ref lock blocks retirement. 4,184 total rows minus 1,827 live means 2,357 removed; therefore at least 40 of the 2,397 snapshot-bearing rows are live. Restore clears removedAt while retaining snapshotRef. Of 2,401 refs, 1,933 are loose and 468 packed-only; update-ref normally creates loose refs, and expiry deletes either representation. All loose-ref files inspected were younger than 30 days (oldest 22.68 days), but mtime is not removedAt and packed-ref ages were not read. The four-ref surplus remains unexplained by the permitted aggregates. No pruning defect is demonstrated; no production cleanup, gc or repack was performed.

Production LOC: +94; tests: +27. Growth is the versioned recovery representation's complete consumer cutover and diagnostic field. The expensive clean path is removed; the full capture machinery remains necessary for dirty, hidden-flag and exact-state recovery. No Control UI import boundary changed.

### Expanded owner acceptance: 20 pairs

**owner accepted: tail within A/A spread at n=20**

The performance owner prescribed acceptance when full-removal wall and process-CPU medians improve and p90/p95 remain within A/A spread. Twenty serial interleaved A/B pairs followed 20 A/A pairs, all on frozen code and the same 65k-file / 1.1 GB workload. Every one of the 80 samples passed recovery verification. Nearest-rank quantiles: p90 is rank 18 and p95 rank 19 of each 20-sample arm; maxima are reported separately. No successful sample was dropped.

| Arm (20 samples each) | Wall median / p90 / p95 (ms) | CPU median / p90 / p95 (ms) | Wall range (ms) | CPU range (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| aa20-a | 1693.329 / 2380.011 / 2759.766 | 1326.003 / 1556.214 / 1565.369 | 1450.303–3214.336 | 1093.843–1615.285 |
| aa20-b | 1926.076 / 3329.498 / 3339.491 | 1459.341 / 1788.941 / 2050.857 | 1430.050–3947.275 | 1138.811–2733.506 |
| ab20-a | 1688.132 / 3202.687 / 4939.154 | 1405.481 / 1916.850 / 2892.395 | 1436.118–5431.384 | 1235.088–3377.264 |
| ab20-b | 1401.071 / 3109.671 / 3139.856 | 1152.539 / 1611.989 / 1650.321 | 1205.605–3869.295 | 965.717–2649.468 |

Wall median improves **17.00%** and CPU median **18.00%**. Candidate p90/p95 are below the upper corresponding A/A quantiles, not merely below the single worst control. Candidate CPU p95 is 1.650 s versus baseline 2.892 s; the previous five-pair CPU-tail increase is not reproduced as a candidate regression. Waiting is not used to explain CPU. Baseline-only controls themselves reached 2.734 s CPU, and the A/B baseline reached 3.377 s; candidate maximum was 2.649 s. Node process CPU includes all workers and excludes Git children.

Full-removal Git calls were consistently **45 → 39** in all pairs. Capture wall median/p90/p95: **853/1734/2050 → 551/1322/1353 ms**. Main CPU: **138/177/210 → 126/165/176 ms**. Main V8 allocation: **40.73/50.63/53.75 → 36.49/47.23/47.89 MB**. The per-sample maximum event-loop-delay median/p90/p95 was **14.50/28.88/46.60 → 14.89/63.44/66.62 ms**, while the worst observed delay fell **184.29 → 70.39 ms**. The higher event-loop-delay quantiles remain visible; this is not a claim that the production 465 ms scheduler stall is resolved. The owner's acceptance criterion for this rerun was full-removal wall and process CPU. Host one-minute load ranged approximately 12–60 across the A/B run.

The earlier five-pair wall p95 (2.48 → 3.58 s) and CPU p95 (1.65 → 2.92 s) were insufficient for tail acceptance and prompted this larger run. They remain in the detailed report. A failed setup attempted an old-runtime restore of a new clean-v1 fixture before measurement; it produced no sample. Both A/A labels then used the baseline fixture, retaining the first successful control. A/B fixtures kept their matching code throughout.

Reproduce each arm with the committed `scripts/perf/worktree-removal-snapshot-measure.ts`: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-removal-snapshot-measure.ts --output <arm-fixture> --tracked 65000 --files 1000 --file-bytes 1100000 --clean --reuse-fixture --warm-index --report <unique-sample>.json`, with `OPENCLAW_BENCH_BASELINE_DIR` selecting the pinned source overlay. Setup and restore verification are outside the timed window. Separate diagnostic profiles are excluded from acceptance timings. This fixture does not simulate a 35-GiB agent DB, thousands of sessions, or competing state-DB fsync.

The 85 net test lines cover HTTP/WebSocket rendering and CSP, HEAD responses, retry timing, navigation cancellation, and slow recovery. prs.title: perf(ci): overlap independent npm source checks
prs.body:
# Problem

FRV npm source validation runs the full canonical check graph serially. The latest completed successful FRV (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43757970051, target `2c173a37a48f850246ae2133aa5c02df2ae35953`) spent 70m55s in this check. Its npm producer was https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43758536481, source job 132947975817.

## Change

Select existing canonical check stages with repeatable `--stage`; no second command inventory. Run preflight/typecheck/policy and lint/format on two isolated source workers, retaining each runner’s current memory/concurrency limits. Preserve the exact `Check npm release source` aggregate receipt owner and require both workers to succeed before sealing. Source/tooling SHA identity, ancestry, plugin compatibility, all validation coverage and downstream phase contracts remain unchanged.

The target’s own CLI must successfully advertise support; frozen pre-selector targets run their original full check exactly once, with an explicit no-op sibling. Probe or selected-check failure cannot fall back to a clean result. No target inventory is replaced by current harness code.

## Timing evidence and limits

Measured stage spans: preflight 16m06.842s, types 12m00.796s, lint plus format 38m01.373s, policy about 4m45s. Non-lint work totals about 32m53s. Ideal same-capacity overlap changes the compute tail from 70m55s to about 38m01s, roughly 32m53s shorter before setup, queue and reducer overhead; around 30 minutes is a hypothesis, not a measured gain.

The latest FRV was CI-dominated: npm finished 25m10s before its CI receipt. This change does not claim to shorten that particular parent by 30 minutes. It removes a substantial latent critical path and helps source/candidate validation when npm is critical. The extra checkout/setup and reducer can increase aggregate runner work; old frozen targets gain no overlap and retain that bounded overhead. Queue effects and whole-FRV wall time still need hosted measurement.

## Proof

- Real `pnpm check --stage lint --help`: rejected on base, accepted with the patch.
- Managed-command traces prove the exact full command union, canonical order, flag/base preservation, deduplication, invalid input rejection and failure status.
- Extracted production worker/reducer shells prove supported and historical target routing, harness restoration, no fallback after failures, and success-only evidence.
- Combined touched workflow/receipt suite: 687 passed; the sole failure was missing `zip` in PATH, not an assertion. Reused the existing isolated Info-ZIP installation and reran that exact test successfully (688 cases covered). The 12-test check suite also passed after test-only lint corrections; 226 workflow guards passed.
- Both new partition cases fail on base production, and pass with the stage selector.
- Canonical scripts/root-tooling TypeScript, targeted production and test lint, formatting, pinned actionlint/zizmor, full docs checks and `git diff --check` passed. Net +237 test lines stays within the unchanged 400-line allowance.
- No receipt schema or npm-prepared-bundle production changes; existing verification tests retained.
- The first exact-head CI exposed TS2488 in the new check trace: managed-runner arguments are optional in its public type. prs.title: fix(ui): Debug replies show the next method instead of the one called
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Debug labels an earlier RPC reply with a method selected for the next call, and its Call button remains enabled without a method or connection.

## User Impact

User impact: responses and errors visibly name the method that was submitted, while the next method and JSON draft stay editable. Call is disabled until it can make a request. No Gateway permission, execution, retry or concurrency behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing manual-call owner now retains the submitted method with its outcome instead of deriving that label from the editable draft. Its current epoch and connection checks still reject stale replies. The existing full-width result layout and shared status/code components are retained; no new helper, renderer, CSS or request manager is added. Production change: +21/-4 lines, with three behavioral regressions in the existing suite.

#199144 already corrects the generic retry advice; that copy is preserved. #199268 separately proposes retiring the security-audit row and is not duplicated.

## Evidence

- Three new cases fail on current main for result/error attribution and unavailable Call controls; all **22 Debug-page cases pass** after the fix. They cover editing the next method and parameters during a request, submitting that next call, connection loss/recovery, and existing stale-result/client-change behavior.
- **45 focused Debug/overlay/shared-system-info checks pass.** UI typecheck, scoped lint, keyless i18n baseline/verification, formatter and diff checks pass. No broad local CI run.
- Native built-app proof: submit health, hold its reply, choose status as the next method, then receive health. The response remains visibly and accessibly health. A mocked cron.run timeout retains its own method after the draft changes. A disconnected Call is disabled; reconnect preserves the draft and a subsequent valid status call succeeds. No real cron job or other live RPC was executed.
- Matched real-component captures below use synthetic responses and an emulated 1280 × 1000 desktop viewport. Success and error layouts were inspected. Baseline main `03b9bea8ec0780bb18ac5ca111f0673eae900925`; the affected owner is unchanged at observed main `1fff14f6019cc12177e54e265d07ee8de38a6695`.

Before — health reply with status selected; no visible original-method label, and the response’s accessible name incorrectly says status.

![Before: the health reply is shown beneath a status draft without its own method label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5544b33-85d6-4703-8c03-d1b2541a503e)

After — the draft remains status; the response is explicitly health.

![After: the response keeps its submitted health method while the next draft remains status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bfc422a-1480-4bc4-85b1-310c3b2fdfb3)

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed the comprehensive wording and interaction audit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/27ab8da9-7856-4f25-9b62-91d8138f1a1c)

> **WIP draft.** Part 17 of 24 in the Settings reorganization series. Implementation not started yet; this PR holds the scope.

## What Problem This Solves

Sibling Settings pages each take a sidebar entry, and Settings has no way to group existing pages as tabs.

## User Impact

Privacy & security shows Overview and Secrets as tabs of one entry; old URLs keep working.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reorganization only moves, groups, renames, removes duplicates and states scope. It adds no new controls or data and changes no config keys.

Scope of this PR:

- Hub mechanism for Settings: owner entry highlight, Escape/Back not treating a tab as a subpage, search by tab title, native title, per-tab visibility, hub tab bar replacing the section bar.
- First hub: Privacy & security (Overview · Secrets).

Depends on: #199799, #199805.
