prs.title: fix(browser): stop sending credentialed CDP wsUrl to the model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #158966.

With a loopback CDP profile whose `cdpUrl` carries HTTP Basic credentials or a query token (as used by Browserless/Browserbase-style endpoints), `browser action=tabs` and `browser action=open` hand the model a fully usable, credentialed `wsUrl`. Every tool action addresses tabs by `targetId`, so the model never needs the connectable socket URL, and its credentials leak into model-facing (and page-adjacent untrusted-content-wrapped) output.

This carries forward the unresolved problem from #137756, whose implementation PR was retired at the author's request without the underlying defect being fixed. Independent code reading against current `main` confirms the same root cause the retired PR identified, at the same two call sites (line numbers shifted slightly since that PR's base commit, behavior identical).

## Root cause

- `formatAgentTab` (`extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts`) explicitly copies `source.wsUrl` onto the agent-visible tab it builds for `action=tabs`.
- `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata` (`extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts`) is documented as removing internal metadata before model output for `action=open`, but only stripped `ownership`/`resolvedProfile`, leaving `wsUrl` and its paired `wsLookup` intact.
- `normalizeCdpWsUrl` (`extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.ts`) deliberately propagates the configured endpoint's credentials onto the per-tab socket URL — that part is correct, it's needed for the runtime's own connection. The defect is only that the derived value then reaches the two model-facing formatting paths above.
- The declared output contract (`BrowserToolOutputSchema` in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.ts`) does not include `wsUrl` at all, and `client.types.ts` already documents `wsLookup` as "omitted from model-facing summaries" — `wsUrl` was never supposed to survive to model output either.

## Fix

Stop copying `wsUrl` in `formatAgentTab`, and strip both `wsUrl` and `wsLookup` in `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata`, matching the class of internal CDP connection metadata that already gets removed for other fields (`ownership`, `resolvedProfile`) and already gets redacted elsewhere in the codebase (`chrome.diagnostics.ts` calls `redactCdpUrl` before diagnostics output).

No other call site reads `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` back off a tool result — every consumer (screenshot capture, snapshot, page sessions) reads `tab.wsUrl` internally before the tool formats its result — so removing it from the two output paths changes nothing else.

## Evidence

New regression test `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts` drives the real, unmocked `executeTabsAction` and `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata` production functions with a synthetic credentialed CDP URL built through the real `normalizeCdpWsUrl`, then asserts the credential and the `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` keys are absent from the serialized model-facing result.

Confirmed the test fails without the fix — reverted the two source files to `HEAD~1` (pre-fix) and reran:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 × browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=tabs model output
   → expected '{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"\n…' not to contain 's3cr3t-pass'
   Received: ...\"wsUrl\": \"wss://admin:s3cr3t-pass@chrome.example.net/devtools/page/AAA111?token=<redacted len=22>\"...

 × browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=open model output
   → expected '{"targetId":"AAA111","title":"Inbox",…' not to contain 's3cr3t-pass'
   Received: {"targetId":"AAA111","title":"Inbox","url":"https://mail.example.com","type":"page","wsUrl":"wss://admin:s3cr3t-pass@chrome.example.net/devtools/page/AAA111?token=<redacted len=24>...

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

Restored the fix and reran — both pass, plus the full existing browser-tool suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 ✓ browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=tabs model output
 ✓ browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=open model output
 ...
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  277 passed (277)
```

Lint, typecheck and format on the changed files:

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo
(clean)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
(clean)

$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

## What was not tested

No real Chrome/CDP proxy end-to-end run — this fix and its test operate at the same production-function boundary (`executeTabsAction`, `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata`) as the issue's own real-behavior proof, using a synthetic credentialed URL built through the real `normalizeCdpWsUrl`. The retired PR #137756 previously ran a full real-Chrome/authenticating-proxy round trip proving the same before/after behavior; that evidence is preserved in its history for reference.

# Proposed title: improve(ci): overlap release evidence lookup with source readiness

## What Problem This Solves
Full Release Validation serializes a read-only evidence lookup behind source readiness even though the lookup consumes no readiness output. Every downstream validation lane waits for both.

## User Impact
Removes an avoidable common-prefix wait without removing a check or adding runner jobs. With unchanged runner admission, the observed trace models approximately 56 seconds less FRV wall time. No post-change hosted FRV saving is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made
Start the existing evidence lookup after target resolution, alongside source readiness. Preserve all direct fanout readiness dependencies and their success conditions, including package preparation, so failed/cancelled/skipped readiness cannot dispatch validation or prepare release artifacts. Explicitly require successful readiness as the first final-summary step before evidence publication, including the reused-evidence path. Keep existing source admission, frozen qualification identity, evidence checks, plan schema, and diagnostic collection unchanged.

## Timing and Critical-Path Evidence
- Most recently finished successful FRV observed: [43757970051](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43757970051), November 15, 2026, 20:25:14–22:13:11 UTC (1h47m57s), target/workflow `2c173a37a48f850246ae2133aa5c02df2ae35953`.
- Source readiness: 20:28:04–20:30:13 (129s). Evidence lookup: 20:30:16–20:31:12 (56s). Their dependency, not data, serialized them. Modeled common-prefix reduction: about 56–59s before downstream runner queue effects; total runner work remains the same. Extra work is accepted only when readiness fails: the existing read-only lookup may already have run.
- The actual longest CI child was [job 132948320578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43758557488/job/132948320578): 631s queue, 5279s runtime, 5049s test step. Node/Bun runtime independence and cold-shard balancing are already covered by other PRs, so this change does not claim their savings.

## Validation
- Existing workflow regression fails on the base dependency (red), passes after the change (green). It retains the existing fanout rejection checks and executes the production summary shell with success/failure/cancelled/skipped readiness: only success passes. Final readiness is asserted to be the first summary step.
- Complete package-acceptance-workflow suite: **587 passed**, 114.35s, with workspace-local Info-ZIP.

Remove one unnecessary dependency rather than adding caches, dispatchers or a new stage. Production +14/-2 lines; tests +22/-3, extending the existing regression without new scaffolding.

prs.title: fix(templates): duplicate bundled plugin id passes preview, fails Add
prs.body:
Closes #198750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Template that bundles two plugin folders with the same plugin id passes `templates validate` and the Add preview, then Add creates the agent, installs the first folder and fails on the second with "changed after planning; review the Template again". Reviewing again repeats it.

## User Impact

The Add preview and Add now report `bundled_plugin_collision` at the second folder, naming both folders and the plugin id, and nothing is created or installed. Templates with one folder per plugin id are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`planBundledTemplateDependency` already blocks bundled skills whose identity collides with another declaration (`src/templates/bundled-dependency-plan.ts:36-42`), but had no equivalent for plugins. Both folders preflighted against the same absent install, so both planned as installs, and the installer's per-action check (`src/templates/bundled-plugin.ts:243-272`) only noticed after the first one had installed. The planner now keeps a map from bundled plugin install ID to the first folder that declared it, next to the existing skill sets, and blocks the second.

`templates validate` still passes: it does not run the install preflight that resolves the plugin id. The issue's minimum (block in the Add plan before anything is created) is what this covers.

## Evidence

Ran the offline CLI (`pnpm openclaw templates ...`, Gateway stopped) on `main` (e3f1538c6e1) and on this branch with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, Templates enabled in Labs, and a local OpenAI-compatible stub for Add's opening turn. The fixture Template declares `plugins/one` and `plugins/two`, both minimal plugins with manifest id `tpl-dup`; the control declares only `plugins/one`.

- Main: the dry run has no blockers; Add prints `Plugin installed: tpl-dup.`, `Added agent: dup`, then `Plugin plugins/two changed after planning; review the Template again. The agent was already made available and was kept.`, and `agents list` shows `dup`.
- This branch: the dry run and Add report `ERROR bundled_plugin_collision $.plugins[1]: Bundled plugins plugins/one and plugins/two both have plugin id "tpl-dup"; keep one of them.`; `agents list` shows only `main` and `tpl-dup` is not installed.
- Control on this branch: the one-folder Template installs `tpl-dup` and adds `single`.

[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/dup --dry-run --json   # blockers

Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-dup
Actions: 5
Packages: 2
  Requirement bundled:plugins/one: missing-installable
  Requirement bundled:plugins/two: conflicting

prs.title: docs(templates): nested CLAW.md fails validate and build as documented
prs.body:
Closes #198847

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Templates CLI docs say `package.json.openclaw.template` may point to `nested/CLAW.md`, but `templates validate` and `templates build` reject such a folder with `project_not_found` when an author follows that layout.

## User Impact

An author reading `docs/cli/templates.md` now learns that `validate`, `dev` and `build` need `CLAW.md` at the package root with `openclaw.template: "CLAW.md"`, and that a nested selector is read only by `inspect` and `add`. Behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue offered two fixes: make the project commands follow the selector, or document the root-only rule. The history shows the root-only rule is intended, so this PR documents it.

<details><summary>History</summary>

- `validateTemplateProject` rejects any selector other than `"CLAW.md"` with `A Template project must set openclaw.template to "CLAW.md".` (`src/templates/project.ts:270`), and `discoverTemplateProjectRoot` looks for `CLAW.md` beside `package.json` (`src/templates/project.ts:111`). Both came with the project lifecycle (#117037, `7422222788c`) and were kept through the rename (#186457) and the legacy-format removal (#192279).
- #192279 is what made the package reader (`src/templates/reader.ts`, `parsePackageJson`) accept a nested selector for packages and downloaded archives, and added the `nested/CLAW.md` example to the docs. It did not change the project commands.
- `templates build` stages `CLAW.md` at the artifact root, and the project tests pin a golden artifact digest for that layout, so following the selector in project commands would change the built package shape, not just discovery.

</details>

## Evidence

Docs-only change. The behavior it describes is the issue's capture (source checkout, isolated `HOME`/state/config): `validate` and `build` exit 1 with `project_not_found` for a folder whose `package.json` selects `nested/CLAW.md`, while `inspect` and `add --dry-run` exit 0. `src/templates/project.ts` and `src/templates/reader.ts` are unchanged between that checkout and this base.

Not re-run on this base: the current `main` tip does not build locally (`check-cli-bootstrap-imports`: `agents/identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`), unrelated to this change.

Checks: `node scripts/run-format.mts --check docs/cli/templates.md` and `git diff --check` pass.

Merge risk: two-way door; docs only. Blast radius is the Templates CLI page.

prs.title: fix: reuse compacted tool catalogs between agent runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated tool-catalog compaction when Code Mode starts another run, session, subagent, or retry with the same effective tool definitions.

## User Impact

Agent runs reuse identical catalog text and immutable metadata while keeping tool execution bound to the current run. No configuration or schema migration is required. This reduces catalog preparation CPU and allocation; it does not establish that catalog builds caused the reported production heap growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old reuse boundary was a run-local catalog reference, and execution/prompt preparation followed fresh entries-array identities. The new owner keys detached metadata by ordered, finalized descriptors and schema fingerprints, sharing bindings, prompts and worker metadata across runs. Executable tools and lifecycle state remain run-local. Raw and published copies of the same native schema have the same key; opaque client schemas stay with the live describe/call path. MCP publication preserves schemas that cannot be published losslessly.

The shared owner is bounded to 32 catalogs, 1 Mi-character input per catalog and 4 Mi-character aggregate inputs, with bounded prompt variants. It replaces duplicate per-run preparation; the net +167 production lines supply the previously missing cross-run lifetime and bounds (282 added, 115 removed). Related: #199346 separately makes MCP output-validator compilation lazy; this change preserves its validation boundary.

## Evidence

Production motivation supplied by the TS peer: Team r336, 2026-11-15, 19:57–21:30Z recorded 176 builtin Code Mode catalog reuse misses against 77 webchat turns (~2.3×). The turn denominator excludes subagents, cron and recovery/retry attempts, so this is an upper bound per run. Windows with 27–29 builds coincided with +73–91 MB after-GC floor steps; quiet windows with 5–9 builds ranged from −36 to +7 MB. This is correlation, not a demonstrated leak. No Team data was copied and no Team runtime was changed.

- Five paired synthetic owner samples, 109 tools and 1,000 measured warm attempts: builds 1,000→0; median CPU 911.256→336.343 ms; allocation 1,549,322,752→500,435,056 bytes. Unchanged A/A variation was 2.7% wall time and 0.03% allocation. Cold construction was 5.338→5.706 ms; these are owner measurements, not user latency claims.
- Prompt bytes remain identical (8,096 bytes; SHA-256 `a4d4aa4417a8964a62754143ac1b90ea4bfd29b00b7cc1fa95027d86de99d32d`). Prefix and affected consumer tests pass. Native/MCP/client regressions execute through the real headless bridge with current-run results. The original three cross-run regressions fail the intended reuse assertion on exact parent `913e6ea294413887fc9bb71a70a5e24a53936fbf`.
- After 10,000 stable-input turns: one retained descriptor catalog and zero executable entries/tools/run payloads. After 1,000 distinct versions: exactly 32 descriptor catalogs and zero executable survivors. The baseline also releases executors; this repair removes repeated work rather than claiming to fix an established executable-state leak.
- Actual source Gateway dispatch with a deterministic loopback model completed on a synthetic btrfs fixture: 35.20 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions, 200,640 transcript messages and 62,000 project-worktree files (~1.1 GB). Seven requested-path attempts built seven catalogs on the baseline and three with reuse: initial interactive, smaller subagent tool set, and cron-specific descriptors. Both fallback attempts reused the interactive catalog. A separately counted recovered child-completion turn rebuilt on the baseline. All cron runs completed successfully. Final A/A baseline owner spans were 25.681–29.165 ms wall / 108.800–118.107 ms process CPU / 8.64–8.99 MB sampled allocation. Candidate spans were 22.196–24.478 ms / 51.582–76.735 ms / 6.99–7.03 MB, including two additional completion-notification attempts that both reused metadata (nine observed attempts, three builds). Allocation per observed attempt was 1.23–1.28→0.777–0.781 MB. Baseline A/A allocation spread was 4.0%; candidate 0.6%. Concurrent worker CPU and differing completion counts limit full-Gateway speedup inference; there is no live-provider claim.
- Codex local autoreview and focused checks are recorded with the final candidate. `pnpm check:changed` found unrelated unused exports, reproduced on the exact parent and introduced by `ef930ebbad771ae219e033f8c5b59a12b5445ffb` (state copy/swap upgrade) and `cec47fd13f23df46069da1beb65ceaec6e66d04f` / #198491 (member welcome). These are existing main regressions, not ignored noise. Exact-head CI remains required.

CI on the first head exposed an old metadata test equating shared preparation with execution-session identity; the updated test preserves policy-driven lifetime replacement independently. It also exposed an inherited immediate-reply fixture regression from #199434 (`37d977fd28b0`): the exact parent fails, and substituting that owner’s preceding version passes all 20 parity tests. The fixture now completes asynchronous first-call middleware discovery before asserting immediate replies, retaining the existing single-execution, memory, call-count and cleanup assertions. Both affected files pass locally (36 tests), with type/lint/format checks and fresh Codex review. ClawSweeper reviewed final head `9244bf780b745318caef052e9685227e80f02e72` with zero findings and zero open checklist items. Exact-head CI remains required before landing.

The measurement model now scopes markers to each sample so pending completion notifications from a reused synthetic fixture cannot replay old spawn commands. This final follow-up affects only the measurement script; it passed script type/lint/format checks and Codex autoreview. Earlier diagnostic-heavy profiles and replay-contaminated samples are excluded from the final timing comparison.

prs.title: fix: Scribe setup assumes a new conversation and default model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Scribe setup promises a new conversation and the agent’s default model even when it reuses an existing conversation, while the overview assumes every visible Scribe belongs to the viewer.

## User Impact

User impact: setup explains conversation reuse and the conversation’s model settings, without suggesting that viewing a shared Scribe transfers ownership or private access. Actions, prompts, model selection, permissions and schedules are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The start owner already reuses a saved conversation and sends the prompt without a model override. The scheduler’s visibility rules also permit administrators to inspect other people’s automations. The copy now describes those existing behaviors instead of assuming a new, viewer-owned conversation. The obsolete store-name input used only by that claim is removed; no new state or helper is added. Documentation is aligned.

This is separate from the queue wording in #199259, control wording in #199267, and the history-error correction retained in #199298.

## Maintainer Verification

Re-ran all 45 Scribe view/state tests after the test cleanup; they passed, including creation, reuse, archive restoration, retries and generated prompts. Focused lint and formatting, including the changed documentation, passed. Independent static review found no actionable P0–P2 defects.

Removed unused model data from the test fixture and two weak negative phrase checks. Positive setup guidance and behavioral coverage remain. Production and documentation are unchanged by this cleanup. The four author screenshots were inspected; the original built-app proof remains synthetic and does not establish live model selection or cross-person execution.

## Evidence

- Two regression assertions fail against the original copy; **45 Scribe view/state tests pass** after the correction, retaining creation, reuse, archive restoration, retries and exact generated-prompt coverage.
- A full built-app flow through the real packaged plugin passes before/after on baseline 3049d421c9514b143e4632de911daf8f9b1e8cd8. It opens the Scribes list and setup dialog, expands the real prompt disclosure, starts setup, and verifies exactly one chat.send to the existing conversation, zero sessions.create calls, identical prompt bytes and no model override or schedule update.
- Scheduler visibility/ownership and Scribe discovery/start owners inspected. This does not claim live cross-person execution or access transfer testing.
- Scoped lint, browser typegraph, full UI typecheck, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. No broad local suite.

Real components with synthetic sessions, an administrator-visible job owned by a different fixture profile, and mocked transport; emulated 1280 × 1100 viewport. No live Scribe, model call or private store was changed.

After

prs.title: fix(swabble): transcript history ignores transcripts.maxEntries
prs.body:
Closes #194843

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `transcripts.log` keeps 100 entries no matter what `transcripts.maxEntries` is set to.

## User Impact

User impact: swabble keeps at most `transcripts.maxEntries` transcripts (default 50), as the README documents.

## Why This Change Was Made

`TranscriptsStore` had a hard-coded `limit = 100`. `serve` now passes the configured limit to `append`. The store also takes an optional file URL so it can be tested without touching `~/Library`.

## Evidence

- New `TranscriptsStoreTests.testAppendKeepsConfiguredNumberOfEntries` checks the in-memory entries, the file on disk, and a reload.
  - It fails when the old fixed cap of 100 is restored.
  - It passes with the fix.
- `swift test --package-path apps/swabble`: 13 passed, 0 failed (macOS 26, Swift 6.4.2).
- `apps/swabble/scripts/lint.sh` (SwiftLint strict): 0 violations. SwiftFormat lint: clean.


**Behavior proof.** Live speech can't be captured in a headless shell. Instead, a throwaway (uncommitted) harness fed 8 `"clawd phrase N"` segments through `ServeCommand.consumeTranscripts`, the same loop `serve` runs, with `transcripts.maxEntries = 5`. The real `~/Library/Application Support/swabble/transcripts.log` lived under a temp home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME`). The shipped `swabble tail-log` then read it back in a new process:

```
## main (before)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 8
$ swabble tail-log
phrase 1 … phrase 8

## this PR (after)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 5
$ swabble tail-log
phrase 4
phrase 5
phrase 6
phrase 7
phrase 8
```

**Existing data compatibility:** the log format (newline-separated text) is unchanged. A 100-entry `transcripts.log` from an older build loads, and the next append trims it to the newest `maxEntries`:

```
seeded transcripts.log with 100 lines from an older build
serve loop fed 8 wake phrases (maxEntries=5)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 5
$ swabble tail-log   # new process
phrase 4 … phrase 8
```


**Upgrade from the v2026.11.1 release, with existing config and history.**
- A `config.json` is created by the release binary and customized.
- History is written by the release's own `serve` transcript loop.
- This branch then loads the same `config.json` through `ConfigLoader.load` and appends through the same loop.
- The shipped `tail-log` reads the result back in a new process.

```
## v2026.11.1
$ swabble-v2026.11.1 setup --config config.json
# customized: wake.word=robot, transcripts.maxEntries=5, hook.command=/bin/echo
serve loop (config loaded from config.json) fed 8 "robot release phrase N" segments
transcripts.log lines: 8   (release ignores maxEntries=5)

## upgrade to this PR (same config.json + transcripts.log)
serve loop (config loaded from config.json) fed 3 "robot pr phrase N" segments
transcripts.log lines: 5
$ swabble-pr tail-log   # new process
release phrase 7
release phrase 8
pr phrase 1
pr phrase 2
pr phrase 3
config.json sha eb04c83bdeffc974 -> eb04c83bdeffc974 ; wake.word/maxEntries/hook.command: robot 5 /bin/echo
```

**Gap:** the shipped `swabble serve` cannot run live microphone input here. In a non-interactive shell, its Speech.framework pipeline aborts on authorization (`Abort trap: 6`) before any audio arrives, on `main` and this branch alike. So the speech-to-segment step is replaced by the synthetic segments above. Everything after it (config load, wake gating, the `serve` consumer, the on-disk log, CLI readback) is the shipped code.

Fixes a local Gateway continuing to start when first-run macOS onboarding chooses **Connect to an existing Gateway**.

The saved profile and its approval/retry behavior keep their existing owner; no authentication or approval policy changes are introduced.

prs.title: fix(sessions): Telegram transcript echoes are not recorded on explicit multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #194829

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a gateway with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` and several agents, a delivered Telegram transcript echo (`tools.media.audio.echoTranscript`) is never added to the conversation history. Instead it logs `result was delivered but was not added to the conversation: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, even though the Telegram account is bound to one agent.

## User Impact

User impact: confirmed sends that have no producing turn, such as transcript echoes, are recorded once in the destination conversation of the agent the channel/account binding selects, as the [conversation transcript ownership](docs/refactor/conversation-transcript-ownership.md) rules require. The missing-owner warning goes away for bound destinations. Single-agent and unbound setups behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` (`src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts`) chose the history owner as `producer?.agentId ?? resolveDefaultAgentId(config)`. A preflight transcript echo has no producer, and explicit ownership has no default agent, so `AgentSelectionRequiredError` was thrown before destination lookup could consult the binding. The ownership doc says destination lookup does not need a producer: carried route, producer context, exact local binding, then plugin resolver.

Without a producer, the owner now comes from `resolveAgentRoute` for the destination's channel and account. That reuses the routing owner's binding tiers, and unbound destinations keep the old default-agent fallback, which is the same error when no default exists. Peer-level bindings are still enforced: the existing `belongsToAgent` check re-resolves the route with the destination peer and skips with the documented "belongs to a different agent" diagnostic.

The fix lives in the shared recorder, so other producer-less confirmed sends benefit as well; Telegram code is untouched. This does not overlap #194783, which covers the durable `sendPayload` final mirror.

Accepted edge: the owner is chosen from channel/account bindings before the peer is known. A destination covered only by a peer-specific binding to a different agent than the account binding is skipped with the cross-agent diagnostic, not recorded under the peer's agent.

## Evidence

- New regression `records a producer-less send under the agent its account binding selects (#194829)` in `confirmed-visible-message.integration.test.ts`. It uses explicit ownership, two agents, account bindings and no producer, and the echo lands in `beta`'s conversation.
- Red on `origin/main`: it fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner…`, the same text as the issue's warning. Green with the fix (11/11).
- Consumer suites green: `deliver` 86, `outbound-send-service` 24, `delivery-queue.transcript` 14, `deliver-confirmed-visible` 3, `outbound-send-service.accepted-outcomes` 2, `echo-transcript` 4, `echo-transcript.integration` 2, `audio-preflight` 5, `apply` 29, `media-understanding-runtime` 7, `subagent-announce-text-delivery` 5, `subagent-completion-mirror.integration` 1, `voice-call realtime-handler` 37.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Telegram voice-note round trip, which needs a bot account and an audio provider. The integration test drives the real recorder against real session storage.

prs.title: fix(templates): agent kept by a failed offline Add has no AGENTS.md
prs.body:
Related: #198744 (this restores the default files; recovering the held package `BOOTSTRAP.md` after a failed offline Add stays open there)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when offline `openclaw templates add` keeps the new agent after a later step fails, the agent's workspace holds only the Template's `SOUL.md`, and it stays that way after every turn. The failure message says "Continue setup in this agent", but the agent runs without `AGENTS.md`, `IDENTITY.md` or `USER.md`.

## User Impact

After a failed offline Add keeps the agent, its workspace also gets the default `AGENTS.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md`, the same files an agent gets on its first turn after a successful Add. The Template's own files are not replaced, and the operator's `agents.defaults.skipBootstrap` and `skipOptionalBootstrapFiles` are honored exactly as ordinary CLI preparation applies them (`src/agents/command/prepare.ts`). The package `BOOTSTRAP.md` is still held back, because its first-run instructions can depend on the plugin, MCP server or automation whose setup failed. Successful Adds and Gateway Adds are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#196392 holds a Template's workspace bootstrap while Add runs: it sets `bootstrapDeferred` and `ensureAgentWorkspace` returns early while it is set (`src/agents/workspace.ts:592`), so no turn can seed defaults or a generic `BOOTSTRAP.md` ahead of the package one. The deferral is cleared when the package `BOOTSTRAP.md` is seeded, which is the last Add step (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:674`). When a later step fails and the agent is kept, nothing clears it. Gateway Add resumes that agent through Retry, which reaches the seed step. Offline Add has no resume, so the hold never ends and every turn skips the default files.

Holding the package `BOOTSTRAP.md` is intentional, and `conversation.workspace.test.ts` keeps proving that a later seed still applies. So this change does not lift the hold. A new `seedDeferredWorkspaceDefaults` in `workspace-preparation.ts`, beside the deferral it respects, writes only the default instruction files that ordinary preparation would write under the current `agents.defaults` (nothing with `skipBootstrap`, minus any `skipOptionalBootstrapFiles`), with the existing exclusive-create publisher, and leaves `BOOTSTRAP.md` and setup state untouched. It does nothing when the workspace is not held. The offline CLI, which owns offline custody, calls it after a partial result with `agentRetained`.

It is not called from `applyTemplateAddPlanStateless` itself: Gateway-kept agents carry a configured checkpoint whose `workspaceIdentity` covers every file in the workspace (`src/templates/add-checkpoint.ts`), so adding files there would make Retry report that the workspace changed.

Accepted edge: if writing the default files itself fails, the CLI reports that error instead of the partial result. The agent is still kept and the next failure message names the cause.

## Evidence

### Current integrated candidate: `7b69a60f36cdd3661b29cfe3dfc7a52dd3aeb126`

The conflict repair preserves contributor ancestry and incorporates main at `355e5ae57e4eef2d39d1afa765613f2981d8d62c` through the native baseline workflow. The retained-defaults caller now passes the workspace preparation owner's captured filesystem evidence to the existing exclusive publisher through `WorkspaceStateGuard`. The complete product diff against that baseline remains four files, **+83/-2**; permitted defaults, suppression settings, existing-file preservation and package `BOOTSTRAP.md` custody retain the original repair's behavior.

- **Exact integrated candidate:** all **97/97** focused tests passed across `conversation.workspace.test.ts`, `templates-cli.test.ts`, `templates-agent-conversation.test.ts` and `agents/workspace.test.ts` (73 infrastructure + 24 CLI). The fresh-process custody regression, both suppression controls, existing `SOUL.md` preservation and subsequent package bootstrap seeding pass with the current filesystem owner.
- Core typecheck, scoped production lint, formatting of all four changed files and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review of the complete integrated delta found no actionable findings. The existing ClawSweeper review covers incoming head `edab73ce2d97d08edb92aa723262608ade9b9b11`; its original correctness findings were already resolved. This paragraph does not claim a new hosted review of the integrated head.
- **Paired behavior proof:** the real isolated offline CLI captures below show baseline `SOUL.md` only after a failed retained Add and later turn, versus permitted default `AGENTS.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md` with this repair; package bootstrap stays held. Those captures are reused for unchanged CLI behavior. The new exact-candidate test/typecheck run specifically validates the filesystem-owner integration; no new model-backed CLI session was run for that mechanical adaptation.

Hosted CI for this new candidate is pending publication; the earlier head's CI is not new-head evidence. The broader package-bootstrap recovery in #198744 remains open.

Offline CLI from `main` (de200490f82) and from this branch, Gateway stopped, isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, a local OpenAI-compatible stub for the model. The failing Add is a Template with a package `BOOTSTRAP.md` whose opening model turn fails after the agent is committed (the stub is stopped during Add, then started again). This trigger does not depend on #198743.

- Main: Add exits 1 with "The agent was already made available and was kept. Continue setup in this agent". The workspace is `SOUL.md`, and still `SOUL.md` after `openclaw agent --local --agent kept --message hello`.
- This branch: same Add result; the workspace is `AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md` after Add and after the turn. No `BOOTSTRAP.md`.
- This branch with `agents.defaults.skipBootstrap: true` in the config: the same failing Add leaves only the Template `SOUL.md` in the workspace, as ordinary preparation would.
- Control on both trees: the same Template with the model up adds normally, has `BOOTSTRAP.md SOUL.md` after Add and all five files after one turn.

<details>
<summary>Main (RED) and this branch (GREEN)</summary>

```
# main de200490f82
$ openclaw templates add <run>/kept
Added agent: kept
Couldn't connect to the AI service. ... The agent was already made available and was kept. Continue setup in this agent; do not add another copy.
[exit 1]
$ ls -A <state>/workspace-kept
  SOUL.md
$ openclaw agent --local --agent kept --message hello
[exit 0]
$ ls -A <state>/workspace-kept
  SOUL.md

# this branch
$ openclaw templates add <run>/kept
[exit 1]   (same message)
$ ls -A <state>/workspace-kept
  AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md
$ openclaw agent --local --agent kept --message hello
[exit 0]
$ ls -A <state>/workspace-kept
  AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md

# control, both trees
$ openclaw templates add <run>/control
[exit 0]
$ ls -A <state>/workspace-control
  BOOTSTRAP.md SOUL.md
$ openclaw agent --local --agent control --message hello
$ ls -A <state>/workspace-control
  AGENTS.md BOOTSTRAP.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md
```

</details>

Tests: "retains package bootstrap custody through a fresh process after setup fails" in `src/templates/conversation.workspace.test.ts` now gives the kept agent its defaults the way the offline CLI does, runs `ensureAgentWorkspace` in a fresh process, and expects `AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md`, the Template `SOUL.md` unchanged, no `setupCompletedAt`, and that `seedTemplatePackageBootstrap` still seeds the package `BOOTSTRAP.md`. With the helper doing nothing (main's behavior) it fails with `expected [ 'SOUL.md' ] to deeply equal [ 'AGENTS.md', 'IDENTITY.md', …(2) ]`. Two more rows defer a workspace and seed it with `skipOptionalBootstrapFiles: ["USER.md"]` and with `skipBootstrap: true`; with the helper from e15f0864cfd they fail with `expected [ 'AGENTS.md', 'IDENTITY.md', …(2) ] to deeply equal [ 'AGENTS.md', 'IDENTITY.md', …(1) ]` and `… to deeply equal []`. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/templates/conversation.workspace.test.ts src/cli/templates-cli.test.ts src/cli/templates-agent-conversation.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes (91 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, targeted oxlint, format check, `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `git diff --check` pass.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting brings back the bare kept workspace with no state or config migration. Blast radius is offline `openclaw templates add` runs that end partial with the agent kept and a held package bootstrap.

### Current-head CI qualification

CI run [43770661392, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43770661392) completed with one inherited updater-test failure. Its candidate-admission test still expects the old joined `Failing check node-runtime` output; upstream `764761ee6450` intentionally changed this path to a one-line refusal plus recovery steps and updated the analogous target-schema test, leaving this assertion behind. The refusal and no-side-effect checks pass before that formatting assertion.

The actual tested merge `f182b244ade18deffa10e28c083da923dd9973d0` has protected-main parent `5b750071d1d31b2af9c8d2e58d0f65da010845dc` and this exact PR head `7b69a60f36cdd3661b29cfe3dfc7a52dd3aeb126`. Its complete four-file delta leaves the failing updater, report, fixture, runner and dependency inputs unchanged. All other independent CI leaves passed or were normally skipped. The failed run remains failed; the 97 focused tests and type/lint/format proof above passed. Landing uses the repository's narrowly scoped inherited-CI qualification, preserving security and enforced review gates.

prs.title: fix(agents): agent denies finished setup after BOOTSTRAP.md is removed
prs.body:
Closes #196403

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent says setup is unfinished, and that it deleted `BOOTSTRAP.md` without reading it, on the turn after it followed and removed that file.

## User Impact

After a custom or stock bootstrap finishes, the agent no longer asks the user to restore `BOOTSTRAP.md` or redo setup that was already done.

## Why This Change Was Made

While setup is pending, `BOOTSTRAP.md` reaches the model through the system prompt. Once OpenClaw records setup as complete, the prompt drops the file and the "Bootstrap Pending" section, but the earlier turns that followed it stay in history, so the model sees a codeword exchange with no visible source. Since #196411, a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` reliably stays pending until the agent removes it, which is exactly this state.

Routing (`resolveWorkspaceBootstrapRouting`) now reports recorded completion (`setupCompletedAt`) for primary sessions, and the bootstrap prompt section replaces the pending text with a two-line note. The note states OpenClaw's recorded state and does not claim each step was verified.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- The note depends only on recorded completion and the session key, never on the turn trigger or run kind, so the prompt prefix stays stable within a session. It appears in place of the pending section, so completion changes the prompt once, as it already did.
- Workspace preparation (`ensureAgentWorkspace`) records completion before routing on both turn paths (`command/prepare.ts`, `reply-workspace.ts`), so the first turn after the file disappears already carries the note.
- The bootstrap section builder moves from `system-prompt.ts` into `bootstrap-prompt.ts`, unchanged apart from the new branch, because `system-prompt.ts` and `cli-runner/prepare.ts` are over the line cap. The CLI helper takes the routing result instead of a separate mode for the same reason.
- A failed state read is not swallowed: `ensureAgentWorkspace` reads the same row earlier in the turn and would fail first.
- Cost: two fixed lines in the system prompt of primary sessions whose workspace completed setup. Removing a completed `BOOTSTRAP.md` from the prompt (#82463) is unchanged.

</details>

## Evidence

Live run of the reporter's flow through an isolated loopback Gateway (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, session `agent:main:main`) on main `8ae9d35bd53` and on this branch `ba176e52584`. A fresh baseline workspace gets a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` (ask for the lighthouse codeword, delete this file, confirm). Then: greeting, Gateway restart, another message, the codeword, "Thanks. Is your setup finished?". Model inputs were captured with a logging proxy between the Gateway and the model server.

The model is the built-in runtime on a local Ollama model (`ollama/qwen3:4b`), not `claude-cli`: the Claude CLI login was unavailable on this host. The prompt code changed here is shared by both runtimes.

On both runs the model asks for the codeword on turns 1 and 2, deletes `BOOTSTRAP.md` with a tool call on turn 3 and replies "Setup complete. Codeword received: HALCYON-42". Turn 4's preparation records `setup_completed_at`. The built-in runtime keeps the first system prompt for prefix caching and sends later section changes as a "System prompt update" on the turn. Turn 4's update:

```text
main (8ae9d35bd53):
  System prompt update. The sections below replace their earlier versions; everything else in the system prompt is unchanged.
  ...
  ## Bootstrap Pending
  (removed)

  ## <workspace>/BOOTSTRAP.md
  (removed)

this branch (ba176e52584):
  System prompt update. The sections below replace their earlier versions; everything else in the system prompt is unchanged.

  ## Bootstrap Complete
  OpenClaw recorded workspace setup as complete; earlier BOOTSTRAP.md instructions are no longer shown.
  Missing BOOTSTRAP.md is expected. It and blank optional profile files do not mean setup was skipped.
  ...
  ## Bootstrap Pending
  (removed)

  ## <workspace>/BOOTSTRAP.md
  (removed)
```

On main the model is told only that the bootstrap instructions were removed; with the fix it is told setup was recorded complete. The omitted `...` lines are unchanged `## Related` doc-link sections, identical in both runs.

`qwen3:4b` answered turn 4 "Yes, your setup is complete" on both main and this branch, so this model does not reproduce the reporter's Claude denial; the evidence here is the model input, not a changed reply. Turns 1 to 3 and Gateway restart behave identically on both.

<details><summary>Turn transcript, this branch</summary>

```text
>>> USER: Hello! Who are you?
<<< Before we begin: what is the secret codeword for the lighthouse?
    [workspace: AGENTS.md BOOTSTRAP.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md] [completed=-]
--- Gateway restart before setup finishes ---
>>> USER: Hi again. Can you list the files in your workspace?
<<< Before we begin: what is the secret codeword for the lighthouse?
    [workspace: AGENTS.md BOOTSTRAP.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md] [completed=-]
>>> USER: The lighthouse codeword is HALCYON-42.
<<< Setup complete. Codeword received: HALCYON-42
    [workspace: AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md] [completed=-]
>>> USER: Thanks. Is your setup finished?
<<< Yes, your setup is complete. I'm ready to help with your next task!
    [workspace: AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md] [completed=2026-11-13T23:03:37.558Z]
```

</details>

Tests and gates on this head:

- `pnpm test src/agents/bootstrap-routing.test.ts src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`: 3 failed / 71 passed with the production changes reverted, 74 passed with them.
- 277 tests across 13 affected files pass, including `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `system-prompt.cache-prefix`, `session-reset-prompt`, `helpers.system-prompt`, and the embedded bootstrap and CLI `prepare` suites.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, scoped oxlint, format, line-cap ratchet, test-lines ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.
- Not run: the same flow on `claude-cli` (login unavailable on this host). `prepare.existing-session` and `prepare.native-compaction` hit the warm Claude session host-memory check on main and on this branch.

Production delta +71/-29, of which 22 lines move the existing pending-section builder; test delta +20/-10; docs +5.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior prompt with no state or config change. Blast radius is the system prompt of primary sessions in workspaces with recorded setup completion.

## Maintainer validation

Correction `d4604e1d4508e7d2b9a6097a670d4d56f94dcd1a` updates two fixture consumers without changing production code or prompt equality assertions: the performance fixture declares incomplete setup, and the existing workspace mock supplies that same completion fact. The obsolete pending-state override in the bootstrap-files mock is removed; its correct workspace override remains.

Before the correction, the scripts typecheck failed with missing `bootstrapCompleted`, and the exact prompt-preservation test failed while trying to open a database broker absent from the fixture. Afterward, scripts typechecking passes and that original test passes. The attempt sibling group passes 36 tests; bootstrap-routing and tool-prefix stability pass 20 tests. Targeted lint, formatting, diff checks, the line-cap check, and independent review of the complete fixture correction pass. The existing Gateway/model-input proof above covers the unchanged production patch. Current-head CI/security qualification remains required.

prs.title: fix: Knowledge reader labels misstate evidence and file outcomes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge’s reader calls additional citations “source files,” displays “1 files,” and describes company identity matches as people. The completed file-writer path also needs an accurate saved-file confirmation.

## User Impact

Citation controls describe the entries being loaded. Identity explanations and editable requests work for companies and other subjects, not only people. Completed file writes say “Original file saved.” The browser handoff keeps main’s existing “Download started. Check your browser downloads.” guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing result already supplies citation and file counts. Identity candidates are records of different types, and the writer confirms completion when its close operation succeeds. This change aligns the feedback with those facts.

## Maintainer Review and Validation

- Integrated main while preserving its browser-download guidance.
- Fixed the core typegraph failure by removing the private Knowledge schema import from the core browser test. The boundary check failed before the repair and now passes, without relaxing the guard or adding casts.
- Consolidated permanent browser coverage into two flows: citation pagination and the company identity card plus editable request. Reused the existing writer success, failure and cancellation tests; removed duplicate cases and optional screenshot plumbing.
- All 13 existing Knowledge UI/evidence tests passed. Three built Chromium flows passed: the two permanent cases plus a temporary file-save probe that read back exact bytes through a real browser-private file handle. Focused lint, formatting and diff checks passed; independent static review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Real components with synthetic records and Gateway replies. The save probe substitutes a browser-private file handle for the OS picker; it does not test the native save dialog. No live Knowledge records or user files were changed.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest refactor in 2c4413a6abbfeb4ac23cd07b775a105586548af1 regenerated the probe without refreshing its reviewed digest. prs.title: fix(browser): keep authenticated CDP URLs out of tool results
prs.body:
Related: #158966. Follow-up to #159036 and #137756.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: listing or opening tabs exposes CDP connection credentials to the model when a loopback browser profile uses Basic authentication or a query token.

## User Impact

Browser connection credentials stay inside the runtime instead of appearing in tool text and structured details. Tab metadata and target-ID-based control remain available. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries forward the output-only fix proposed by @chelsealong in #159036, following @yetval's earlier #137756. The existing PR is still open but conflicts with the current dispatch implementation and lacks current-implementation end-to-end proof. The linked issue was closed administratively, not because the defect was fixed.

Fresh main still copies `wsUrl` when formatting tabs and leaves `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` in open results. Remove those fields at the existing model-output boundary, after internal ownership tracking. Do not strip credentials from CDP normalization: the runtime needs them to connect. This is one output-boundary fix, not a browser authentication change.

**Merge gate:** credential-handling changes require the repository's maintainer security approval; this PR does not claim that approval.

## Evidence

### Real behavior: Chrome through an authenticated loopback proxy

Ran the same isolated source driver before the fix on `cc5c2914c58bde53e0ef708620071213bce06ce8` and after the fix (candidate `2d42547dce845288e60a5af3ed07dda1e70eefa4`; production file byte-identical to the recorded after-run). macOS, Node 26.13.0, real headless Google Chrome with a fresh user-data directory; no operator browser or Gateway state used.

The proxy required **both** synthetic Basic credentials and a synthetic query token on HTTP and WebSocket requests. An unauthenticated `/json/version` probe returned 401. The actual `createBrowserTool` called a real token-authenticated browser-control HTTP server, which reached Chrome through that proxy. No browser responses or transport functions were mocked in this proof.

Sequence: `tabs → open(about:blank) → tabs → focus(returned targetId) → close(same targetId) → tabs`. Confirmed the opened target was listed, focus/close returned success, and the closed target disappeared on readback.

```text
                              before       after
 tabs content credentials     present      absent
 tabs details credentials     present      absent
 open content credentials     present      absent
 open details credentials     present      absent
 tabs/open wsUrl              present      absent
 focus with returned targetId success      success
 close + absence readback     success      success
 authenticated HTTP requests  19           19
 authenticated WS upgrades    13           13
 unauthenticated probe        401          401
```

Driver entry: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof.mts`, with isolated config/state and Chrome directory. It imports this checkout's `startBrowserControlServerFromConfig`, `createBrowserTool`, and runtime-config snapshot publisher. Browser profile: attach-only CDP at a loopback authenticating proxy. Tool calls use the authenticated HTTP bridge (`sandboxBridgeUrl`) rather than a production Gateway. All credentials were synthetic; the comparison checks the entire returned content and details. All task-owned listeners and Chrome were stopped after the run.

### Regression and static checks

- Two tool-entry regression rows fail on pre-fix production for the intended synthetic credential leak and pass with the fix. They assert no credential strings or `wsUrl` in serialized results, no `wsLookup` in structured tab/open details, and preserved page metadata/target IDs.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.structured-output.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-binding.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **5 files, 112 tests passed**; wrapper wall time 10.86s, Vitest 9.09s including transform/import; CI timing pending.
- Extension production and test typechecks: `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`: passed.
- Targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and test-line budget: passed. The +43 allocation is exactly the focused regression growth; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Author simplification completed: no new production helper/state/API. Independent clean-context read-only Codex review of the final diff: **no P0–P2 findings**. CLI autoreview was unavailable (no executable); the independent review used a native reviewer instead.

**Not tested:** hosted Browserless/Browserbase, screenshot/snapshot operations, a provider/model turn, or a packaged release. The real-browser proof covers the actual tool/server/CDP path, not those broader claims. Revert this output-only commit to roll back.

prs.title: fix(plugins): Gateway heap grows with every plugin rebuild
prs.body:
<!-- template: .github/pull_request_template.md at openclaw/openclaw 05aaca51d99 -->
Related: #198802

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained native namespace/member maps when repeated plugin inspection replaces an admission receipt, including when a native file is renamed between inspections.

This addresses demonstrated retainers, not every retention path in #198802. That issue remains open for changed receipt keys, invalidated admission views, and other unqualified lifecycle paths.

## User Impact

Repeated catalog inspection after an in-place native-file rename no longer accumulates obsolete namespace maps and file facts in the same process cache. Plugin configuration, native-root custody, and on-disk capture retention are unchanged.

The proof measures retained objects, not a normalized heap slope or the reported 80–110 MB/hour. Native capture roots still accumulate under their existing custody policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original same-key receipt cleanup pruned namespaces only when no receipt or file fact still named them. Renaming a native file left its old file fact reachable, so that fact kept the obsolete namespace alive.

The complete admission inventory now retires replaced-receipt file hints that no current receipt names, then uses the existing namespace pruning. Preparation workers explicitly retain their partial-inventory status: their global dependency indexes do not imply that they received every plugin's receipts. This preserves cross-plugin reuse. Existing per-admission recovery and republication behavior remains intact; roots, pins, live borrowers, and publication ownership are not released by this change.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway path:** isolated full Gateway with a synthetic native plugin; rename/edit its native file and companion in place, then call authenticated public `tools.catalog`. Cache and admission-state identities stay constant. Baseline `c5afbbde556` retains 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 namespaces/file facts; the repair retains 1 throughout. Namespace members grow 6→30 on baseline and stay at 6 with the repair. Receipts stay at 1. Public `plugins.reload` is the control: it replaces the cache and returns counts to one. Counts are inspected inside the test, not through a new public diagnostic API.
- **Regressions:** native-path replacement fails on c5 in direct capture (five retained namespaces) and real preparation-worker adoption (two). The repair passes both. Existing cross-plugin inode sharing caught an early incorrect retirement and passes with the complete/partial inventory distinction.
- **Focused tests:** 77 passed, 1 failed across nine files. The failure reproduces on unchanged c5: the fixture selects 64 MiB `/dev/shm`, capture requires at least 512 MiB and correctly falls back, then the fixture asserts the old device. It was not skipped, weakened, or claimed passing.
- **Targeted validation:** core and plugins-test-leaf typechecks, targeted lint, format, line-cap ratchet, and whitespace checks pass. Simplification pass completed.
- **Full build: failed on candidate and unchanged c5:** `PLUGIN SDK DTS TOO LARGE: 5315890 bytes exceeds 5315536 bytes.` Candidate also reports eight UI budget warnings; the baseline reused the UI content cache, so those warnings are not independently attributed. No budget or gate was changed.
- **Fresh independent review:** native Auto Review, full local candidate from `05aaca51d99f7bff18128b322ef425b0a9c7ba58`, including base-to-index and index-to-working-tree changes; P0–P2 coverage; `scoped-clean`, no findings. The reviewer inspected tests but did not execute them. The transferred four-file repair and resulting source hashes were independently verified. Published head `114c2c6e9f5155b637c610c239942b3ffba71be1` exactly matches reviewed tree `ac90b428bffe8a724ab443a709991929216171e6`.

- **Hosted CI:** [CI run 43741910473](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43741910473), attempt 2 for head `114c2c6e9f5155b637c610c239942b3ffba71be1`, passed: 33 jobs succeeded, 31 were skipped, and none failed. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and sensitive-change review passed in the same-head readback at 23:13 UTC on November 15. At that readback, both CodeQL workflows, Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep, and macOS Periphery still awaited separate approval; their completion is not claimed.

Contributor: @etzelm.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b16fb173-603a-441d-a9e2-b3cfb9d19093)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9fecc898-d88d-4699-9e11-821fe1b305e5)

prs.title: perf(sandbox): compress oversized reconcile checkpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reconciliation sends megabyte checkpoint documents to the SQLite worker even when only two workspace files changed. The previous 32 MiB compression threshold leaves these requests uncompressed.

## User Impact

A 25,000-file reconciliation fixture now sends about 246 KB instead of 1.52 MB for its checkpoint reservation (83.8% less). Persisted checkpoint/journal bytes, crash recovery, custody, and authority checks are unchanged. No migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rollback journal already contains changed paths only. The reproduced large field is `checkpoint_json`: retained build inputs and fingerprint blobs remain necessary for recovery. Compress process-local mutation payloads above 1 MiB and use the shared zstd codec across both mutation producers and the worker decoder. The separate content-preparation channel stays unchanged. No alternate mutation decoder or persisted format is introduced.

Add one numeric-only oversized-mutation warning per minute per process. It uses the serialization already required by the transport, reports field byte counts and journal dimensions, and never logs paths, identifiers, or document contents. Runtime production delta: **+70 lines**; the requested diagnostic accounts for most growth. The non-test/non-doc diff is **+144 lines**, including measurement tooling and the allocation ledger. Net test growth: **+44 lines**, explicitly allocated.

## Evidence

Baseline: `90af47b0178a5244bec0572507ebf40bbf88be69`, which includes #199683. That acceptance optimization remains intact. The latest-main rebase did not change the measured owner files.

Acceptance: preserve real reconcile results and exact persisted input bytes; reduce the oversized request below 1 MiB; report main CPU, total process CPU, and allocation separately. Byte instrumentation is separate from timing. Warm store measurements used AB/BA plus one predeclared extra pair after CPU deltas changed sign, 1,024 cycles per arm (**3,072 per side**).

| Store cycle, 25k paths | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 8.533 ms | 9.153 ms | +7.3% (+0.620 ms) |
| Process CPU, including workers | 44.208 ms | 48.125 ms | +8.9% |
| Main-isolate allocated bytes | 4,445,909 | 4,477,774 | +0.7% |

This is a wire-size improvement with modest compression overhead, not a CPU or allocation reduction claim. Pair CPU signs were mixed; host load changed substantially. Base/candidate 1-minute host loads were 18.53/16.02, 10.87–13.48/14.13–16.76, and 10.14/15.52. Source fingerprints and individual results are retained in the local evidence report.

Real projection-owner proof used **25,000 physical files** (24,997 retained build inputs plus three ordinary files), two edits per cycle, real Git and SQLite workers, and synthetic container-engine I/O. Three byte-attribution cycles per side verified the canonical result after every reconcile:

| Per request / journal field | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Checkpoint `localWorkspace.mutate`, full wire request | 1,520,518 B | 246,399–246,403 B |
| `checkpoint_json`, uncompressed field | 1,520,000 B | 1,520,004 B |
| `journal_json` | 1,002 B | 1,002 B |
| `journal_pack` | 187–188 B | 187–188 B |
| Journal base/applied entries | 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 |
| Journal base/applied directories | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| `baseTree` reference | 40 B | 40 B |

Field-size differences across fixture runs reflect regenerated observations; the regression checks exact input JSON equality after closing and reopening SQLite. A plain 25k-file fixture without retained build inputs sent only 346,587 B per checkpoint. The reported production 6 MB burst has not been exactly reproduced; the new diagnostic is needed to attribute that burst rather than assuming the journal holds a full manifest.

Separate uninstrumented real-reconcile AB/BA runs used eight cycles per arm (**16 per side**):

| Real reconcile | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU/cycle | 118.683 ms | 119.073 ms (+0.3%) |
| Main-isolate allocation/cycle | 81,478,576 B | 81,212,363 B (−0.3%) |
| Process CPU/cycle | 1,527.1 ms | 1,653.3 ms (+8.3%, mixed paired signs) |
| Total main GC/cycle | 8.014 ms | 7.866 ms |
| Main GC seconds/minute, mean | 0.331 | 0.359 (+0.028 s/min) |
| Event-loop p99, arms A/B | 38.80 / 33.44 ms | 37.42 / 40.37 ms |
| Event-loop samples, arms A/B | 697 / 1,179 | 822 / 928 |
| Max single GC pause, arms A/B | 4.24 / 23.05 ms | 17.12 / 5.05 ms |
| End RSS, arms A/B | 1.312 / 1.180 GB | 1.259 / 1.169 GB |
| End main heap, arms A/B | 170.829 / 170.821 MB | 170.585 / 170.398 MB |
| Host load at arm start | 11.31 / 16.40 | 10.27 / 15.58 |

Tail counts are insufficient for paired p99 gates; each arm had seven major GCs. GC/time rose only 28 ms/min while GC/work fell. These are owner-flow measurements, not a ten-minute dist-Gateway/model/WebSocket stress run; sessions.list/server-handler latency was not measured. No production load or production state was used. The initial deflate prototype was replaced after its extra compression CPU motivated a cheaper codec comparison.

Validation:

- Byte-budget regression failed with the main compression policy: **1,165,236 B > 1,048,576 B**. It passes with this change and verifies exact durable checkpoint JSON after reopen.
- `local-workspace-store.test.ts`, `local-workspace-cas.test.ts`, `workspace-reconcile-recovery.test.ts`: **58 passed**, final invocation 56.55 s including worker preparation.
- Projection-owner persisted recovery selection (`recovers durable state`, interrupted base refresh, accepted unindexed inventory): **10 passed**, 26.69 s. Includes reservation/acceptance/cleanup interruption recovery.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, gateway-other test typecheck, changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Initial CI caught one remaining deflate decoder in `local-workspace-manifest-scan.test.ts` (five repair cases). That test consumer now uses zstd; all **12 tests in that file passed** locally (123.37 s including worker preparation). The repair typecheck and lint passed. Production measurements remain valid: this follow-up changes only the test decoder and its line allocation.
- Broader exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771956450) and [artifact build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771956352): **passed** at `01aae2bb9f27c7043a450917c87f67c24f29f2e1`. Independent review is owned by the coordinating maintainer before merge; this ready PR is intentionally left open.

Reproduction (freeze complete base/candidate sources for codec comparisons; `--revision` on the store microbenchmark only substitutes host owners):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-request-bytes-measure.ts --output .local/owner-arm --instrument timing --iterations 1024 --paths 25000 --workspaces 1
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts --output .local/reconcile-arm --mode reconcile --requests 8 --burst 1 --files 3 --build-input-files 24997 --file-bytes 32 --reconcile-changed-files 2 --instrument timing
```

Add `--reconcile-traffic` only for byte attribution; reuse a fixture serially with `--reuse-fixture --report <arm>.json`. The benchmark header documents complete-source freezing.

Exact warning format (fingerprint count means encoded blobs; bytes count UTF-8 strings / raw byte views):

```text
Local workspace oversized mutation: kind=<create|update|delete> serializedBytes=<n> wireBytes=<n> fieldBytes={<field>:<n>,...} manifestFingerprintCount=<n> manifestFingerprintBytes=<n> journalBaseEntries=<n> journalAppliedEntries=<n> journalBaseDirectories=<n> journalAppliedDirectories=<n> journalBaseTreeBytes=<n>
```

prs.title: feat(cron): make automation inspect links configurable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Implements #150029 by adding the strict config option `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with values `always`, `errors`, and `never`. The default is `always`, preserving existing behavior. This supersedes #175817, which was closed unmerged. The approach is rebased onto current `main` and additionally proves that the policy applies to isolated agent-run announcements through the shared delivery append path. ## Behavior - `always`: include Control UI `Inspect` links on successful completion announcements and failure alerts (backward-compatible default). - `errors`: include links only on failure alerts. - `never`: omit links from both successful completion announcements and failure alerts. - Applies to isolated/direct cron completion delivery, successful completion announcements, failure alerts, and isolated agent-run announcements that share `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`. - Webhook delivery is unchanged; the setting only governs chat announcement links. ## Changes - Add `src/cron/inspect-links.ts` with the policy resolver and `shouldIncludeCronInspectLink`. - Add the strict `cron.announce.inspectLinks` schema under `cron`. - Apply the policy at the shared delivery append path in `src/cron/delivery.ts`, with an explicit completion/error kind for failure alerts. - Gate link generation in `server-cron-completion.ts`, `server-cron-notifications.ts`, and isolated agent delivery dispatch. - Document the option in `docs/gateway/config-automation.md` and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`. - Refresh generated config baseline hashes/counts. - Add `config/test-lines-allocations/194794-cron-inspect-links.txt` (126 lines, exact measured net test LF growth) for the test-lines ratchet. ## Evidence Focused tests: ```text pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 59 passed (59) ``` Schema / generated baseline: ```text pnpm check:base-config-schema [base-config-schema] ok pnpm config:docs:check OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json ``` Type checks: ```text pnpm tsgo:core # passed node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json ... node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json ... # passed ``` Formatting / whitespace: ```text oxfmt --check All matched files use the correct format. git diff --check # passed ``` ## Review notes - Branch is one commit on top of base `56eb6f3fe2e6b3056727094d22add3c02322215d`; current head `67123e2245a348373f2d3a01df041fc3e739a82c`. Only generated baseline outputs changed during this rebase. - No merge is requested here; this PR is ready for maintainer review. ## Shipped-entry-point proof: 2026-11-08 Sanitized extract. Originals remain local. Contains only synthetic fixture data and `control.example` URLs. Placeholders replace credentials, ports, identifiers and paths. ### Scope Proves on the real shipped CLI entry point (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`) that the cron scheduler appends the Control UI run-inspection link according to `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with default `always`: | Mode | Completion | Failure alert | | --- | --- | --- | | `always` (explicit) | link present | link present | | `errors` | link absent | link present | | `never` | link absent | link absent | | omitted (default) | link present | link present | Transport is a **local simulated Bot API over loopback** implemented for this proof. It is **not** real Telegram, not Telegram's network, and not a real bot account. The Gateway, cron scheduler, delivery queue and channel adapter code are the shipped production paths; only the remote Bot API endpoint is simulated. ### Observed revision and build provenance - Branch: `feat/cron-inspect-link-policy-v2` - HEAD: `a89f9f80afff1db14d8135a25f0cc11fac4228fd` - `dist/build-info.json`: `{ version: "2026.11.1", commit: "a89f9f80afff1db14d8135a25f0cc11fac4228fd" }` - `dist/entry.js` sha256 `33b9d9b167163e877b373cf38dfc514dbdda460d489238e5c10980d66ba8917d` - `dist/index.js` sha256 `159f854af966f37f377090380c3c52314a27265e1f4f4f1056edf5fdece44356` - Shipped dist rebuilt from HEAD: bundler exit 0, post-build stamps exit 0. One optional plugin-asset copy step exited 1 for an unrelated plugin whose own build output was absent; it is not used by this proof. - `git diff --check`: clean. ### Reproduction (placeholders) ```bash export REPO= export PROOF_ROOT= export OPENCLAW_HOME=$PROOF_ROOT/state/ export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$OPENCLAW_HOME export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$PROOF_ROOT/configs/.json export NO_PROXY= # 1. prs.title: fix(discord): preserve interactive cards when editing messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord card updates being ignored by the message edit action, and lets native interactive plugins update a source card without reconstructing its unchanged buttons.

## User Impact

Agents can replace a card's structured component specification through the existing edit action. Native plugins can inspect the source component tree and update it without sending retained mentions again. Live callback registrations retain their original session and agent routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The edit action currently drops `components` before dispatch. This change forwards it to the existing component writer and recovers routing from live registrations. Native handlers receive `interaction.messageComponents`; that snapshot is not added to agent prompts.

Component edits suppress mention parsing. Converting a classic message to Components V2 clears its incompatible classic fields, as required by the [Discord edit-message contract](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message#edit-message). The structured edit specification replaces the whole card. Omitted components retain the ordinary text-edit path; native handlers can still clear components with an empty array. Expired or missing registrations cannot recover an unavailable source route and use normal channel routing.

## Evidence

- Added a message-action loopback regression covering card replacement, live callback routing, mention suppression, retirement of buttons, and action/input gates.
- Added a native-interaction regression covering source-tree access, retained buttons, webhook update payloads, and no agent dispatch. Extended existing component-writer assertions for classic-field resets.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent read-only code review covered the complete local change and a follow-up repair delta. Two findings, classic-to-V2 clearing and incorrect test payload assertions, were fixed and re-reviewed with no remaining actionable findings. The shared autoreview helper was unavailable; this was a native subagent review, not a validated helper report.
- **Draft: regression execution is not verified.** The focused test command failed during compiled-worker setup with exit 137 before any tests ran (157.17 seconds total). This is not a passing test result or a reproduced product failure. Test runtime and CI seconds remain unavailable.
- The targeted lint command also failed before reaching lint: SDK declaration preparation exited 13 with an unsettled top-level-await warning. Lint/type validation and a full build remain unverified. No live Discord interaction, client screenshot, or red-on-base/green-on-fix proof is claimed. Complete exact-head build, focused regressions, and relevant CI before marking ready.
