prs.title: fix(templates): ClawHub Template Add says the manifest is invalid without saying why
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Adding a published ClawHub Template with an invalid CLAW.md fails with only "Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.", in the CLI, the Control UI and the Gateway log.

## User Impact

User impact: users and Template publishers now see what is wrong (for example a retired `packages` key or a missing `openclaw.template` selector) and what to change, instead of a reason-free error. Nothing else about the failure changes: same error code, still fails closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest reader already returns specific diagnostics with fix text, but the ClawHub download path dropped them. The error message now carries up to three of them (code, path, message) plus a count of the rest. Reader messages that name a file by its absolute Gateway cache path are rewritten relative to the package root (realpath and link path, longest first), so clients do not see the Gateway host's home directory. Diagnostics can quote publisher-controlled text, so each reported diagnostic goes through `sanitizeTerminalText` before it reaches Gateway RPC clients and the CLI (local and Gateway-owned Add).

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/templates/clawhub-source-artifact.test.ts`: a retired `packages` key is named in the message; an unparsable CLAW.md is named as `CLAW.md` without the cache path, also when the cache root is a symlink whose realpath contains the link path (as `/private/tmp` does `/tmp` on macOS). All fail on origin/main and pass with the fix.
- `src/cli/templates-cli.test.ts` (local Add) and new `src/cli/templates-cli.gateway-add.test.ts` (Add through a running Gateway, real `templates.add.plan` handler): a manifest key containing U+202E and U+009B is named in the error, and neither control character reaches the CLI output. Both fail without the sanitization.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/templates/clawhub-source-artifact.test.ts src/templates/clawhub-source.test.ts`: 58 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: everything passes except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on origin/main in files this PR does not touch.


In a sweep of the 28 third-party ClawHub Templates, 7 failed this way (5 retired format, 2 missing selector) and none of them said why.

### Real CLI runs

Built from source: before = merge-base `82123cd17bd` (main), after = this PR (`91c887117db`). Each run used a fresh isolated state dir with Templates enabled. Mode A has a Gateway running, so the CLI routes the Add through it. Mode B has no Gateway, so the CLI does the Add itself. The state dir path is shortened to `<state dir>`.

**Published Template with a retired `packages` key** (`@etzelm/job-application-coordinator` 0.1.2 on ClawHub)

Mode A, before (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator
Gateway owning <state dir> on local port 19583 could not complete templates.add.plan for Template configuration and provenance: Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.. The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
```

Mode A, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator
Gateway owning <state dir> on local port 19583 could not complete templates.add.plan for Template configuration and provenance: Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. retired_template_configuration at $.packages: Move native settings into CLAW.md agent and exact ClawHub references into skills/plugins. Use automations for scheduled work; remove packages, profiles, cronJobs, and metadata.openclaw.config; keep schemaVersion: 1.. The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
```

The Gateway log line for the failed `templates.add.plan` carries the same reason after the change.

Mode B, before (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator --acknowledge-clawhub-risk
Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.
```

Mode B, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator --acknowledge-clawhub-risk
Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. retired_template_configuration at $.packages: Move native settings into CLAW.md agent and exact ClawHub references into skills/plugins. Use automations for scheduled work; remove packages, profiles, cronJobs, and metadata.openclaw.config; keep schemaVersion: 1.
```

In mode B the local Add asks for `--acknowledge-clawhub-risk` before it downloads this release, so the flag is passed in both runs. Nothing was installed.

**Reason text with control characters** (local test package served by a loopback registry stub)

The package's CLAW.md has an unknown key `evil` + ESC `[31m` + `key` + U+202E (right-to-left override) + U+009B (C1 CSI) + `31m`.

Mode A, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @acme/demo-agent
Gateway owning <state dir> on local port 19583 could not complete templates.add.plan for Template configuration and provenance: Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. invalid_manifest at $: Unrecognized key: "evilkey". The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
```

Mode B, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @acme/demo-agent
Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. invalid_manifest at $: Unrecognized key: "evilkey"
```

A byte check of the captured terminal output and the Gateway log found no ESC, U+202E or U+009B in the reason line. Before this change, both modes stopped at "Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid." with no reason for this package.

The "outcome may be partial" wording in mode A is a separate issue and is not changed here.

prs.title: feat: recommend agent tasks during template setup and new chats
prs.body:
Related: #196643

## What Problem This Solves

Template authors can describe an agent, but users have no way to choose a first task during installation. New chats also show generic suggestions for purpose-built agents.

## User Impact

Agent authors can set an optional description and up to three recommended prompts. Users can select a prompt when adding a Template or in a new chat with the installed agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the user selects a task and approves installation, OpenClaw installs the agent and creates its `BOOTSTRAP.md` file. It then starts a chat with instructions to **complete bootstrap first, then handle the selected task in the same conversation**. If bootstrap requires user input, the agent is instructed to ask and wait for answers before continuing.

This ordering relies on model instructions, not a separate workflow engine. The user can continue chatting after the agent’s first reply, which may be a setup question. If that first reply fails, the installed agent and chat are kept so the user can try again.

### Template configuration

In `CLAW.md` frontmatter:

```yaml
agent:
  id: project-briefing
  description: Follows your repositories and briefs you on meaningful changes, proposals, and decisions.
  recommendedPrompts:
    - Set up a repository
    - Brief me on recent changes
    - Show my tracked projects
```

## Evidence

- **Upstream audit and refresh:** integrated `355e5ae57e4e` and published `b8c69022fb75`. That upstream revision still has no agent `recommendedPrompts`, install-page prompt selection, or selected-task handoff; its generic welcome and existing description metadata are reused, not duplicated. Rechecked newer upstream `39b066a97697`: it still lacks this feature; its intervening Template changes concern preview error receipts and project entry accounting. The sole conflict was the generated config hash, regenerated canonically.
- **Latest-stable upgrade proof — passed:** installed official npm `openclaw@2026.11.3` with registry-integrity verification and its normal lifecycle. The released CLI wrote synthetic agent settings and a real released Gateway created SQLite state. This refreshed candidate then opened the same disk in a new Node process. Test body **45.6s**, complete runner **57.4s**; disposable processes/state cleaned up. No inference is claimed for this compatibility case.

prs.title: fix(templates): Template Add fails on MCP servers that declare a timeout
prs.body:
Closes #198536

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates add` fails after the agent is already created when the Template's `CLAW.md` sets `timeout` or `connectTimeout` on an MCP server.

## User Impact

A Template that declares an MCP timeout now adds completely: the server is saved with `requestTimeoutMs` / `connectionTimeoutMs`, and the Template's automations are scheduled. A server that already exists with the same timeouts in milliseconds is reused instead of being reported as a conflict.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CLAW.md` takes the two timeouts in seconds, under the names OpenClaw config no longer accepts. Add now converts them at the Template MCP boundary with the existing `migrateLegacyConfiguredMcpServer`, both for the config write and for the digest that decides whether a declared server matches a configured one. The manifest schema, the Add review, and the config writer's validation are unchanged. `docs/cli/templates.md` now states the unit.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- `src/templates/schema.ts:351-355` accepts `timeout` and `connectTimeout` (added with the manifest schema in #101328).
- `src/templates/mcp.ts` passed the declaration to `setConfiguredMcpServer` unchanged, and `src/config/zod-schema.mcp-server.ts:76-91` rejects both keys. Add installs MCP servers after the agent is committed (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:665`), so the result is `partial` and automations are skipped.
- `digestTemplateMcpServer` used `canonicalizeConfiguredMcpServer`, which does not touch the timeout keys, so `timeout: 30` never matched a configured `requestTimeoutMs: 30000`.
- Seconds is the unit the rest of OpenClaw uses for these names: `openclaw mcp configure --timeout <seconds>` (`src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:157-167`) and the config migration (`src/config/mcp-config-normalize.ts:140`).

</details>

## Evidence

Built `main` (211bc77) and this branch with Node 24.22.1 and ran the offline CLI (`pnpm openclaw`) with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. A local mock OpenAI-compatible server answers Add's opening turn. The Template declares one MCP server with `timeout: 30` and `connectTimeout: 5`, and one automation. `<run>` is the isolated run directory; output is trimmed to the relevant lines.

- Main: `templates validate` passes, `templates add` exits 1 with the config error, the agent is listed, no MCP server is saved and no automation is created.
- Main, server already configured with `requestTimeoutMs: 30000` and `connectionTimeoutMs: 5000`: Add stops with `mcp_server_collision`.
- Main control, same Template without the two timeout keys: Add exits 0.
- This branch, same three runs: all exit 0. The server is saved with `requestTimeoutMs: 30000` and `connectionTimeoutMs: 5000`, the pre-configured server is left as it was, and `Automation created: Daily summary.` is printed each time.

<details>
<summary>Main (211bc77)</summary>

```
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/proj/mcptimeout

[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout

Config invalid after MCP set (mcp.servers.s: Unrecognized key: "connectTimeout"). The agent was already made available and was kept. Continue setup in this agent; do not add another copy.

$ openclaw mcp list
No OpenClaw-managed MCP servers configured in <run>/state/openclaw.json. Add one with openclaw mcp set <name> '{"command":"uvx","args":["context7-mcp"]}'.
[exit 0]
```

Server already configured in milliseconds:

```
$ openclaw mcp set s {"command":"node","args":["s.js"],"requestTimeoutMs":30000,"connectionTimeoutMs":5000}
Saved MCP server "s" to <run>/state/openclaw.json.
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.s: MCP server "s" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>This branch</summary>

```
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Valid Template project: <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Package: mcptimeout@0.1.0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Ready.
Automation created: Daily summary.
Added agent: mcptimeout
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-mcptimeout
[exit 0]
$ openclaw mcp show s
OpenClaw-managed MCP server "s" (<run>/state/openclaw.json):
{
  "command": "node",
  "args": [
    "s.js"
  ],
  "connectionTimeoutMs": 5000,
  "requestTimeoutMs": 30000
}
[exit 0]
```

Server already configured in milliseconds:

```
$ openclaw mcp set s {"command":"node","args":["s.js"],"requestTimeoutMs":30000,"connectionTimeoutMs":5000}
Saved MCP server "s" to <run>/state/openclaw.json.
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Ready.
Automation created: Daily summary.
Added agent: mcptimeout
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-mcptimeout
[exit 0]

OpenClaw-managed MCP server "s" (<run>/state/openclaw.json):

  "connectionTimeoutMs": 5000
}
[exit 0]
```

</details>

Tests and checks:

- `pnpm test src/templates/mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 passed in 9.75s. The two new cases write through the real config writer. With the `mcp.ts` change reverted they fail with `Unrecognized key: "connectTimeout"` and `already exists with different configuration`.
- `pnpm test src/templates`: 36 files, 408 passed, 3 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the touched files, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` (+20) and `git diff --check` pass.

Not covered: Add through a running Gateway or the Control UI was not run; `src/templates/gateway-add-apply.ts` applies the plan through the same `applyTemplateAddPlanStateless` the CLI uses. A timeout too large to express in milliseconds is dropped by the existing migration rather than rejected.

Simplification: reused the existing seconds-to-milliseconds migration; no new helper. Production delta +5/-3; test delta +22/-2; docs +4/-2 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is Template Add for manifests whose MCP servers set `timeout` or `connectTimeout`, which could not complete before.

prs.title: fix(node-host): Windows node commands cannot use the allowlist or auto-review because of the cmd.exe wrapper
prs.body:
Closes #157930

## What Problem This Solves

On a Windows node host, every `system.run` command is wrapped as `cmd.exe /d /s /c <command>`. The node intentionally treats that wrapper as an allowlist miss (`windowsShellWrapperBlocked`), because cmd.exe changes the meaning of quotes and builtins. As a result, no allowlist entry or durable approval can ever apply on a Windows node: every command needs a human approval, even an absolute-path executable that is explicitly allowlisted.

## User Impact

An operator can now allowlist an executable on a Windows node (for example `C:\Users\me\.local\bin\claude.exe`) and the agent can run it with varying arguments without an approval each time. Commands that genuinely need cmd.exe (operators outside quotes, builtins, `.cmd`/`.bat` scripts) keep the existing wrapper and the existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

#157930 suggests binding and reviewing the inner command of the canonical wrapper. This PR takes the narrower route of not sending the wrapper when it is not needed: when a Windows command has no cmd.exe operator outside quotes, no builtin as its first word, and no `.cmd`/`.bat` target, the Gateway sends it to the node as a direct argv. The `windowsShellWrapperBlocked` rule is untouched, and the node's existing direct-argv path, allowlist and approval binding apply unchanged.

Splitting follows both Windows command-line rules (`CommandLineToArgvW` and the current C runtime) and only accepts a command when both yield the same argv; otherwise it keeps cmd.exe. Characters such as `& | < > ^ ( ) % !` and newlines are literal inside quotes and stay on the direct path; `%VAR%` is not expanded there, and the approval card shows the exact argv that runs. The Gateway approval precheck evaluates that same argv, so it never authorizes more than the node does.

## Evidence

- Unit tests for the splitter: eligible commands, every cmd.exe metacharacter inside and outside quotes, escaped quotes and backslash runs, doubled quotes, newlines inside quotes, builtins, `.cmd`/`.bat`, shell wrappers.
- Gateway tests for the argv sent to the node on both paths and for equality between the approved text and the executed argv.
- Real Windows integration test through the node handler: the child receives `a & b | c < d > e ^ f (g) 50% %PATH% !x! say "hi"` plus a newline exactly; `allow-always` is offered for an ordinary executable and reused.
- Real behavior proof: on a Windows 11 node paired with a Linux Gateway, with `claude.exe` in the node allowlist, the agent ran `claude.exe -p "<prompt with ( ) & % ? and accents>" --permission-mode plan` with no approval prompt, and Claude Code answered the full prompt. Before this change, the same calls required an approval each time and logged `Exec auto-review skipped: dispatch chain cannot be bound`; after it, that line no longer appears.
- Not run locally: the full test suite.

prs.title: fix(telegram): durable final deliveries skip the channel-final transcript mirror
prs.body:
Closes #194783

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: delivered Telegram final replies get no `channel-final` delivery mirror in the session transcript when live preview is off, for example when a plugin registers a modifying `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending` hook.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram finals record the same `channel-final` delivery receipt in the transcript whether they go out through preview finalization, the plain fallback, or core durable delivery. Control UI history and other tools that read the receipt now see it after preview is disabled. Delivery itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable `handled_visible` branch in the Telegram final sender returned before any mirror ran. Core durable delivery also reported the provider-visible `content` only on partial failure, so the channel had no confirmed text it could mirror. ClawSweeper's review pointed out that mirroring the original payload would record text that a message hook may have rewritten.

- **Core (`src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts`):** collects the post-hook text from each confirmed payload's `message_sent` event (`onMessageSentEvent`, already threaded through the durable send) and reports it as `content` on `handled_visible`. `ChannelDeliveryOutcome.content` is already documented as the "final provider-visible text … for this logical payload's terminal observation", so this fills a documented field on the success path instead of adding a new one.
- **Telegram (`bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`):** the `handled_visible` branch writes its channel-final mirror from that confirmed text. It uses the same `hasReplyPayloadFinalDeliveryCapture` guard (dispatcher-owned replies keep their own transcript owner) and the same idempotency sequence as the preview and fallback paths.

Ownership: core durable delivery owns the confirmed post-hook text, and Telegram keeps owning its channel-final receipt. The deprecated `sendBatch` `mirror` parameter is ignored, and automatic destination history deliberately skips the producing conversation, so neither could own this. Each final takes exactly one of the three paths, so it is mirrored once.

## Evidence

- New `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.delivery-transcript.test.ts` › "mirrors a durable final with the confirmed post-hook text": the durable send returns `handled_visible` with hook-rewritten content, and the test asserts exactly one `channel-final` mirror carrying that text. **Red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- New `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.test.ts` › "reports the confirmed post-hook text on a visible final": **red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- Related files, all green: Telegram `final-delivery-lifecycle` 12, `preview.telegram-http` 40, `recovery.telegram-http` 8, `reply-targets.telegram-http` 24, `fallback-topic-media` 4; core `durable-delivery.reload` 25, `run-channel-turn.delivery` 17, `run-channel-turn.finalize` 9, `run-channel-turn.settlement` 3, `delivery-result` 6.
- oxlint (type-aware, tsconfig), oxfmt check, the import-cycle check (0 cycles) and the whitespace diff check are clean.

Gaps: I did not run a live Telegram E2E (it needs bot and user credentials I don't have here), and I did not run a full local typecheck (CI covers it). Other channels' durable `handled_visible` results now also carry `content`. I found no consumer that treats its presence as a partial delivery, and the lifecycle's terminal observation already prefers `content` over `payload.text`.

prs.title: fix(codex): Codex turns fail when a plugin MCP server shares a configured server's name
prs.body:
Closes #194825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Codex-harness turn fails with `url is not supported for stdio in mcp_servers.<name>` when a plugin bundles an MCP server with the same name as a server in `mcp.servers`.

## User Impact

User impact: a configured MCP server now wins a name collision with a plugin's bundled server for Codex turns, as it already does for the merged static surface. Codex turns start, and fallback chains ending in a Codex model work again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex receives MCP servers from two projections: the bundle thread patch and the user-server (configured) projection. The bundle patch kept bundled names that an enabled configured server already owns, so Codex merged both into one `mcp_servers.<name>` table carrying the plugin's `command` and the configured `url`. That combination is rejected at `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:321` (`throw_if_set("stdio", "url", …)`) in the sibling `../codex` checkout.

The bundle patch now drops entries shadowed by an enabled configured server, using the same enabled/session-override rule as the user-server projection. This happens before plugin data dirs are prepared, so a shadowed plugin server no longer gets a data dir either.

Cutover: the bundle path projected durable "Allow Always" grants only for configured names (#136019). Those names can no longer appear in the bundle patch, and the user-server projection already projects their grants (`bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts`), so that dead filter and its test are removed. The optional `agentId` field stays on the exported `LoadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigParams` SDK type, because removing it would change a public contract.

Accepted edge: when a configured server is enabled but excluded for the agent by `isCodexMcpServerAllowedForAgent`, the bundled copy is still dropped. The operator configured that name, so it is not silently replaced by the plugin's server.

## Evidence

- New regression `leaves a same-named bundled server to the enabled configured server (#194825)` reproduces the issue's shape (bundled stdio `gbrain` plus configured HTTP `gbrain`). The patch now holds only `notes`, and `gbrain` is in `userStaticServerNames`.
- Updated `lets user config disable a same-named bundled server unless the session enables it`: a session override enables the configured server, which now owns the name rather than shipping the bundled copy alongside it.
- Red/green: both cases fail against `origin/main`'s `codex-mcp-config.ts` (2 failed / 5 passed) and pass with the fix (7/7).
- Sibling suites green: `bundle-mcp-codex.user-config` 12/12, `run-attempt.configured-mcp` 23/23, `thread-lifecycle.configured-mcp-ownership` 5/5, `attempt-startup*` (20, 9, 4, 3), `mcp-app-session-preparation` 4/4, `run-attempt-client-prewarm` 5/5.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Codex app-server turn. It needs a ChatGPT-authenticated codex-cli plus a plugin bundling a same-named stdio server. The reporter verified the equivalent local patch on 2026.11.1 with codex-cli 0.167.0.

## Exact-head readiness update (November 15, 2026)

- **R1 resolved; native correction recommendation: READY FOR /prepare-pr.** Product source remains `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9` (tree `85c33b6fd00340e5b14124706b8d5f3f9004d04b`). No source changes or new source review were needed for this evidence-only qualification.
- Supplemental secretless [hosted run 43771398337, history job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771398337/job/132987885912) completed **success**, using proof tooling `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` against that immutable product source. Independently inspected original summary, Vitest JSON reports and prefix log show **25/25 passed**: all **14 prefix-stability**, **6 bounded-projector** and **5 persisted SQLite/inbound-context** cases; zero failures. This closes the exact-source prefix execution gap left by the November 14 CI run. The proof workflow's head is the tooling commit, not a new product commit.
- Broad exact-head-attached CI remains [43624048246, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246): **55 successful jobs, 28 skipped**. It executed GitHub's merge checkout, whereas the supplemental proof executed the raw candidate source. The scopes are not interchangeable.
- On November 15, the remote product head was unchanged, the PR was non-draft and **MERGEABLE / CLEAN**, and both checks reported by the required-check query (`openclaw/ci-gate`) were **SUCCESS**. This is readiness evidence, not a merge or an assertion that future main changes cannot require reconciliation.
- Existing independent exact-candidate source review found no actionable P0–P3 defects. The original baseline-red and candidate-only synthetic-channel live evidence below remain **prior-head evidence**. No fresh exact-head baseline/fix A/B or live Gateway/model run is claimed. No autoreview rerun, source rebase, push, merge, release, main change or production-service change was performed for this qualification.

## Historical exact-head proof update (November 14, 2026)

The missing-prefix status in this section records the November 14 observation; it is superseded by the successful November 15 exact-source proof above.

- Current native-published candidate: `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`, tree `85c33b6fd00340e5b14124706b8d5f3f9004d04b`, refreshed against baseline `976a4fb8784a326579108e03d0df4356dad501a3` including the landed `d43de8` worker fix. Workflow source: `8e961de3f838e9bc16c37c148c3364ed958ab810`. Independent exact-candidate source review found no actionable P0–P3 defect.
- Secretless [CI 43624048246, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246) completed **success**: 55 successful jobs, 28 skipped. Runtime setup, build artifacts, production/test types, lint, docs, baseline ratchets and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. This supersedes the runtime-setup gap for this candidate, not the historical outcome below.
- Actual assertion logs verified: [persisted SQLite job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246/job/132536373207), **5/5** (internal-pair absent/present, aborted false/true reconciliation, delivery-only restart); [projector/consumer job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246/job/132536373205), **6/6** bounded projector, **46/46** transcript facade, **12/12** memory-reader; [inbound-context job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246/job/132536373103), **9/9**. The projector cases cover 250/9,999/10,000 newer physical rows, 0/1-row contiguous suffixes after an omitted oversized barrier, and the shared 64 MiB budget. The executed persisted fixture asserts prepared-channel rendering and retention of edited, attachment-bearing, unseen, incomplete and image-barrier requests.
- **Remaining required proof:** the full available CI log contains no execution of `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`. CI success must not be represented as that suite passing; its recorded 14/14 below is prior-head evidence. Native R1 is narrowed to this missing exact-head execution and remains open; recommendation remains **NEEDS WORK**, not READY. No fresh exact-head live baseline/fix A/B or Gateway/model run was performed in this pass; the original baseline and candidate-only synthetic-channel evidence retain their stated scope and source identities.
- No merge, release, backport, main change, local contributor-code execution or production-service change was performed. The earlier CI failure below is retained as historical evidence.

## Historical conflict-repair review update (November 14, 2026)

- Published conflict repair head: `d8caf07f9c97fbfadccf74a24e7649e0bf1c6d32`, preserving original contributor head `9b62025151d3f823522144895d26c17e9c1abfaa` as the first parent and integrating main `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92`. This is a merge into the existing fix branch, not a merge of this PR into main.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P3 findings. The adaptation preserves main's delivery-only projection envelope/filter and both the existing and added SQLite regression blocks. `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing live/regression evidence below remains prior-head evidence. This conflict-only adaptation was not executed locally: the supported secretless AWS proof environment could not acquire credentials (no EC2 instance role). Historical CI run [43600201582](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600201582) completed. Production types, core test-type stripes, lint, and test-line accounting passed; that run was not green. Its failures matched three existing main defects: identity worker build budget (240 evaluated modules versus 220), TS18048 at scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373, and mock export preservation at src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13. The exact failure text was independently compared with contemporary [main run 43599691199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199), specifically [build job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948967), [type job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461949721), and [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948989). Its affected Node test jobs stopped at the inherited runtime-build failure; that historical run remains build-blocked, not runtime proof.
- Attribution and bounded lookup remain separate reviewable fixes under the existing transcript projection/reconciliation owners. Combining them later requires reconciling the shared projector, SQLite append tests, and documentation; neither is represented as testing their combination.

Closes #197995

## What problem this solves

Recent-history reconciliation previously requested `candidate count * 2` projected canonical text rows. Candidate messages, physical platform rows, and projected canonical text rows are different units. An internal user-role runtime input plus assistant `NO_REPLY` can consume that evidence budget without adding a channel-history candidate. A selected, unchanged, previously answered request then resurfaces in later model context because its completion evidence fell outside the lookup.

The conservative behavior on genuinely unavailable evidence is intentional and remains. This is not a missing-final-answer report or a requirement to suppress unproven input. Token cost and answer-quality effects have not been measured.

## What the branch changes

- The recent-history omission owner passes the selected transport message IDs to its existing private canonical turn reader instead of prescribing a two-row ratio.
- The shared SQLite/memory transcript projector follows those IDs until each has been encountered, the active transcript ends, or an existing safety ceiling is reached: 10,000 physical canonical message rows and 64 MiB of captured serialized transcript data.
- Both ceilings are reused from the existing transcript reader constants. The byte count bounds captured payload data, not process heap usage; parsed objects and page metadata add overhead.
- A byte-limited page can contain older sparse rows. Only its newest contiguous suffix is used, and lookup stops at the first omitted physical row. It never bridges a potentially missing user barrier.
- All intervening user rows remain barriers, including image-only/textless users represented as `text: ""` only in the private turn-evidence projection. The public SDK text reader retains its old nonempty-text behavior.
- The private facade captures options and clones candidate IDs before awaiting acquisition. Caller mutation cannot silently change the evidence request after it starts.

The final omission decision still requires exact transport-ID/body equality and completed-answer evidence. Attachment-bearing, changed, unseen, unfinished, and unproven requests remain eligible. Existing active-session/agent scoping and snapshot/worker ownership are retained. There is no new schema, index, configuration, background archive, public SDK option, or arbitrary larger multiplier.

### Performance and bounded fallback

An unseen or too-old selected ID can require searching the whole permitted tail, unlike the old short heuristic. The explicit row and cumulative byte ceilings cap that additional work, and lookup stops early once all selected IDs are found. A missing ID, oversized barrier, unavailable transcript, or exhausted bound can therefore still leave an answered request quoted conservatively. This is an accepted bounded-evidence limitation, not an assertion that every historical answered request will disappear.

The direct projector's 10,000-row synthetic scans ran in 2-3 ms in the supplemental test run. These pages contain already decoded small fixture rows; this is not a SQLite/JSON-decoding benchmark, a production latency guarantee, or a memory measurement.

## Reproduce the original failure independently

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197995-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783640/openclaw-197995-evidence.zip)

Use Node 26.12.1+; the portable helper was executed with Node v26.13.0:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs > observed.json
```

No repository checkout, npm install, credentials, network, model, or Gateway is required. The helper resolves its bundled source relative to itself, not the current directory. Copying the package outside the checkout and running it from `/` produced the identical output.

`SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` pins the bundled baseline owner to `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` (package version `2026.11.3`) with exact source hashes and its MIT license. `reproduction-output.json` is the fresh baseline result. `current-base-reproduction-output.json` confirms the same baseline owner/behavior at the fix branch's newer upstream base.

The helper's optional checkout argument is for reproducing this baseline contract:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw > checkout-observed.json
```

It prints the actual checkout commit/hash and does not label differing source as the pinned baseline. Its assertions intentionally encode the old behavior, including the bug. It is not a green-on-fix acceptance script; use the branch's real owner tests below for the new reader contract.

The executed fixture has exactly six unchanged ID-bearing channel candidates, each with a directly following completed answer. There is no steering fixture:

1. Six ordinary U/A pairs: 12 projected rows, requested limit 12, retained `[]`.
2. Add one internal U/NO_REPLY pair after the oldest answered pair: 14 projected rows, same candidates and requested limit, retained `[target]`.
3. Give the unchanged algorithm all 14 rows: retained `[]` again. This reader override isolates coverage; it is not a repair.
4. Separate controls retain all candidates without evidence and preserve independently edited text, attachments, and incomplete answers.

These are synthetic production-function probes with an injected chronological reader. They do not exercise the real projector, persistence, channel/Gateway, prompt renderer, or model. Passing them must not be called a live end-to-end result.

## Prior-head evidence

`persisted-baseline-red.txt` records the actual pre-fix SQLite/reconciliation failure on the then-current upstream base: three tests passed; adding the internal U/NO_REPLY pair retained `target` and failed the expected-empty assertion. This was a real owner assertion failure, not the earlier cold-compiler infrastructure failure.

The prior implementation passed:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/coverage-final-cache \
  pnpm test src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- SQLite owner: 4/4. Real persistence and `runPreparedChannelTurn` rendering cover the six-candidate control/failure, edited text, attachments, unseen discussion, incomplete output, unrelated internal text users, image-only user barriers, and unchanged public text projection.
- Private projector: 5/5. Covers paging past 250 rows, the exact 10,000-message edge, candidates beyond it, and zero/one-row newest-contiguous suffixes after oversized omissions.
- Provider prefix stability: 14/14, prior head only.
- A supplemental cumulative-byte-budget regression was added after that integration run; the updated projector suite passed 6/6 in 3.36 seconds (7.69 seconds including the wrapper). Production source was unchanged. The new case uses two contiguous pages reporting 32 MiB each, verifies requests of 64 MiB then 32 MiB, and prohibits a third read. Its config-cli test-leaf typecheck, dedicated-core lint, formatting, and diff check also passed. This is a private byte-budget contract, not a SQLite memory benchmark.
- Prior final command: 23 tests passed across three shards, 413.35 seconds including a 160.54-second cold worker compilation. SQLite test bodies totaled about 7.6 seconds; projector bodies about 37 ms. No PR CI was run during that original implementation work; current CI evidence is recorded separately above.
- An earlier candidate passed the unchanged non-recent channel suite, 9/9; that unaffected-path evidence was reused, not presented as an exact-final-head rerun.
- Core production typecheck, plugin-sdk/config-cli test-leaf typechecks, dedicated-core targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `FIX-VERIFICATION.json` records exact tested source hashes and verification scope.

Independent review found and corrected the textless-user barrier and pre-await request-capture defects. Re-review found no further material findings in the reviewed scope. This is not a claim of an automated scoped-clean review.

## Owner and upstream implementation pointers

Pinned baseline source prefix: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/>

- `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts`, `omitAnsweredRecentHistory`: selected candidate identities and conservative final omission.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, `readRecentUserAssistantTurnsForSession`: private active-session/agent facade; public text projection stays separate.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts`, `readRecentTranscriptConversationText`: shared SQLite/memory projection and candidate stopping/coverage.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-visible-cursor.ts`: existing 10,000-message/64 MiB ceilings.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-active-events-read.ts` and `session-actor-memory-history-facts.ts`: byte-bounded page and contiguous-suffix contracts.
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.recent-history.ts`: physical platform-row budget, distinct from filtered candidates and canonical rows.
- `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md`: bounded completion confirmation and conservative retention contract.

## Evidence and submission files

`LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` indexes the successful November 13 candidate-only run. A real isolated Gateway, native Codex runtime and configured provider produced one older answered request followed by seven non-platform user-source RPC turns with seven `NO_REPLY` responses. These are real persisted turns, not fabricated transcript rows, but they are not internal-system events or scheduled automation. Historical production evidence separately covers the original internal-event example.

With six selected history candidates, core dispatch removed the older answered request and retained all five unrelated unanswered candidates. The newly submitted native input contains each retained candidate once and does not quote the older request again. Independent review matched all nine submitted bodies to native and provider requests, verified the 16-row pre-lookup canonical transcript, and separated eight auxiliary recap calls. Retained native conversation history is intentionally not erased.

The canonical `build:runtime` command passed; exact source/build/runtime/Codex provenance is in `live/build-provenance.json`. The fixture uses a restricted native-tool profile and a synthetic authenticated local channel, not Discord transport. Both disposable homes were removed. This is not a fresh live baseline/fix A/B comparison or a full package/declaration/PR-CI run.

The ZIP includes the headerless `fix.patch`, verified `BRANCH.json`, regression receipts, original baseline helper/source/license, sanitized historical observation, live observations, and exact executed harness source. `SHA256SUMS.json` covers the payload. The separate Markdown was byte-identical to the original submission text inside the ZIP; subsequent readiness updates above are not part of that original archive. The original branch was based directly on the stated upstream commit, not on another fix branch; native proof-baseline refresh is identified above.

## Exact limits

- A separate shared-renderer API migration renames `buildInboundUserContextPrefix` to `buildInboundUserContext` returning `{ text, hasHistory }`. If that migration lands first, migrate this branch's added SQLite rendering-test call to the new API and select `.text` where the old string result was consumed. A mechanically clean merge does not establish type compatibility; rerun the focused tests and typecheck after rebasing.
- This is a standalone branch, not a pre-integrated series. A mechanical combination with the separately prepared completed-run attribution change conflicts in the shared projector, SQLite tests and Discord documentation. If that change lands first, rebase and reconcile those owners before landing this branch; combined behavior has not been tested here.
- Recorded historical observations and the prior synthetic-channel proof are separate. Neither implies this branch was installed on the production Gateway.
- No regression-from-known-good release, population-wide incidence, or end-to-end performance rate has been established. The historical observation and deterministic fixtures do not prove such claims.
- The original submission changed only the requested fix branch. Subsequent authorized work published the native proof candidate and updated this existing PR body; no merge, issue comment, release or production service change was performed.

prs.title: feat(ios): add built-in theme and accent preferences
prs.body:
Related: #199394

## What Problem This Solves

iOS cannot apply the same built-in theme and accent preferences as Android and the web Dashboard, so native and embedded screens can present different appearances.

## User Impact

Adds the 11 built-in theme families, System/Light/Dark mode, and accent selection to iOS, with Gateway-profile synchronization and offline/local preference handling. Existing iOS controls, typography, and Dynamic Type remain native. Plugin-provided themes and extra fonts are not included.

This is a **draft stacked on #199394**, targeting **openclaw/amber-krill-3**, not main. It requires the parent fix and matching patched Gateway web assets for embedded-page parity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Projects the Android-owned built-in palettes into generated iOS tokens. One resolved appearance feeds native presentation and the embedded Dashboard's document-start/live appearance rather than keeping separate theme choices for each surface.

Also incorporates Jacqueline's simulator-discovered accent-menu correction: UIKit receives always-original colored swatch images so it cannot template every option with one shared tint.

## Evidence

### Verified native-check repair

The original published head `699dde45476a8ac39737cccde18d42bcae5f9fd2` failed native SwiftFormat/build and SwiftLint. Jacqueline's [verified repair and isolated Mac validation report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199741#issuecomment-6901411221) is now incorporated without further source changes: repair SHA-256 `c3f5cea65c1001a8b0634b5bc7b5752c5a644b49fb274423d8160b9c042e396a`; resulting source tree `8fd229d3ac46ae637d5624ba6fae555509d88c0a`. The native passes below apply to that exact repaired source, **not** the original head.

- **Supplied Mac results, not independently executed here:** repaired native build passes; full iOS SwiftLint and SwiftFormat pass (0/552 files need formatting); 20 native tests pass with 0 failures/skips, including System/Light/Dark migration; generator check/test and i18n pass.
- **Supplied simulator observations:** real stable `v2026.11.3` / `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f` over-install retained old Dark, Keep awake=false and pairing against a conflicting remote Light/Tide/yellow profile, including a second launch. New native choices reached server readback; original-scope offline replay retained the latest blue and retired the queue; unpaired local-only choices survived relaunch. Native and actual WebKit Tide/blue were inspected in Light/Dark and System modes. Logs, recordings and xcresult remain local and are not linked artifacts.
- **Independently run on the exact repaired tree in this Linux publication checkout:** `pnpm ios:themes:check`; the focused generator test (1 passed); `pnpm native:i18n:verify` (`changed=false`); targeted generator Oxlint, JavaScript syntax and non-Swift formatting checks; complete diff whitespace checks. Native Swift/Xcode build, tests, lint and format tools are unavailable here. No TypeScript inputs changed in this repair; the changed generator is JavaScript.
- **Fresh independent review:** Auto Review, P0–P2, reviewed the complete 11-file repair from `699dde45476a8ac39737cccde18d42bcae5f9fd2` to tree `8fd229d3ac46ae637d5624ba6fae555509d88c0a`; `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. This is not ClawSweeper clearance.
- **Simplification:** kept the existing appearance/sync owners and queue semantics; split the compiler-heavy generated tuple switch into mode/family branches and kept its reusable seed emitter in the generator. No duplicate palette owner, new state, rule/baseline weakening or launch-surface repair was added. The repair is +551/−395 across 11 files, mostly formatting/generated output; the added migration cases protect persisted modes and subsequent scoped edits.

### Earlier parity checks and visual evidence

- The implementation owner reported 36 focused web theme/palette/accent tests, UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, i18n, unused-file scans and production web build passing on the earlier parity candidate. Those web sources are unchanged by this native repair; this is not a new full-build claim.
- Earlier performance measurements: web document 14,014 / 14,026 gzip bytes; other largest-JS/CSS and chat-request budget violations also occurred on the paired base, while chat JS grew 294 gzip bytes. Budgets were not changed. This is **not** an all-green performance claim.
- Jacqueline supplied the simulator images below. They illustrate the controls, theme accents and swatch correction; they are not exact-head native logs or proof of every native system surface.

**Remaining verification and limits:** no second real authenticated profile, read-only identity, cross-Gateway switch, forced stale network response, or separate fresh-install profile synchronization was qualified end to end. The supplied full Gateway declaration build failed on external `undici-types` resolution; the runtime-only Gateway/UI proof worked, so declaration/package build is not claimed green. Keep this PR **draft** pending remaining validation and hosted CI; simulator/source-build proof is not physical-device, TestFlight or App Store proof.

**Startup flash remains outside this repair:** a saved-Dark cold start showed a white startup/launch surface; fixed-mode recordings sampled at 4 fps are not an all-frame no-flash pass. Source inspection found the same empty `UILaunchScreen: {}` in [reviewed 699](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/699dde45476a8ac39737cccde18d42bcae5f9fd2/apps/ios/project.yml#L169) and [stable 847611d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f/apps/ios/project.yml#L166), with both applying the saved mode via root SwiftUI `.preferredColorScheme(...)`. This repair changes neither `project.yml` nor `OpenClawApp.swift`. Those unchanged-source facts do **not** establish that the observed flash is inherited; no comparative recording establishes causation.

### Accent-menu swatches — user-supplied iOS simulator

| Before — options all share a red tint | After — options retain their individual colors |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: accent-menu options all rendered red](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9430250-d34e-4dae-9455-9b525a5b3f12) | ![After: accent-menu options retain distinct colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2776806-de6f-46f6-b1c2-c3ed3836bce8) |

<details>
<summary>All 11 theme families — light and dark simulator galleries</summary>

Light:

![Eleven built-in themes in light appearance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab7b6d10-6148-4165-aa05-df825241fb73)

Dark:

![Eleven built-in themes in dark appearance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c630baff-a92b-4ae3-a253-821afc7cd04c)

</details>

## Contributor credit

Reported and scoped by Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen), who also supplied the accent-swatch fix, verified native-check repair and simulator screenshots.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @jjjhenriksen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7c87f5d7-9cb1-4e8e-83a2-d4541e46c06d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b50413f3-678c-43d7-8bcf-c54e7e5a9ec3)
- [Stacked publication verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/38d84dbe-e9b1-44de-933a-08af21dfef1b)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix: Scribes report failed history reads as empty history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Scribes report an empty run history when the history request actually failed.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed history read now shows an error and a way to retry by reopening the Scribe. An empty successful response is described as unavailable recent history, not proof that the automation never ran. No scheduler action or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history owner now keeps its read failure separate from an empty result and passes that fact to the existing detail renderer. Reopening performs the same read again and clears the error when history is available.

This PR has been narrowed to that distinct history correction. Queue/start wording is already covered by #199259, and enable/disable/removal wording by #199267; the overlapping portions of this PR were removed rather than retaining duplicate fixes. Conversation-context wording is separate in #199321.

## Evidence

- Maintainer runtime comparison: main `fc652ec7686410ffcac5f4f502e885032a64a9cc` versus GitHub's integration candidate `b804d6b044197fae21582b027a6ba065f8aaa051`, containing PR head `3429a6d149a8c272b285e29c0f3461e412daf6cf`. Both builds used the same fixture and viewport, including the same main UI changes.
- In the full built Control UI and actual Knowledge plugin, the first history read fails. Main reports “No runs yet.”; the PR reports the read failure. Returning to Scribes and reopening through the visible controls shows “9 filed · 2 pages created.”
- Both runtime cases passed, each with two history reads and zero `cron.run` calls. All 46 focused Scribe view/state tests, lint and formatting passed. Independent static review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- No source repair was needed during maintainer review. These fresh screenshots replace the unavailable previous After image. [Maintainer verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199298#issuecomment-6902728709).

Chromium on macOS, 1280 × 1100, real built components with synthetic Gateway responses and data. No live Scribe, automation or model was run.

### Before

![Main reports a failed history read as no runs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd3b7cef-dced-4436-89a5-f00ef84a5307)

### After

![The integrated PR reports the history read failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82b37a3d-ba23-4cd5-b1b2-46701deabebf)

<details>
<summary>After reopening: recovered history, without starting a run</summary>

![The existing history is visible after reopening](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2411ae7-89fd-4c5b-86a2-06ddd51888ca)

</details>

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed this audit and the user-facing correction.

prs.title: fix(gateway): first chats fail during cold storage startup
prs.body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

First chat requests can fail with storage-unavailable errors while an agent database is starting. Permissive fixture umasks also prevent Gateway tests from reaching that behavior.

## User Impact

Cold chat requests retain the existing database preparation instead of rejecting its first registration. Filesystem permission, routing, lifetime and source-identity guards remain enforced. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait only for an already-running first-use creator before capturing the registry witness, and classify existing-file registrations against physically qualified identities. Readiness stays in the existing fact-acquisition owner; the caller retains its lifetime and routing checks. This adds no retry or timeout increase.

Create fixture-owned `.openclaw` with mode `0700` before publishing its selectors. The native writable-ancestor guard is unchanged; no chmod, skip, quarantine or permission override is added.

## Evidence

- **Current-head integration:** PR CI [43754726962](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43754726962) and Security Review [43754726935](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43754726935) completed successfully for `d8b5dc1572f7f53a0169de4a2d30cd9aabc9c4ef`.
- **Real first-chat flow:** [fresh isolated Gateway run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7c4c71169b62464332a11dfd9e812814) passed the additional selected case in 19.355s. A real first-use creator was paused before opening the absent target database; the same real WebSocket chat request observed a canonical startup refusal before handler work. After releasing the real creator, authorization acquired the target, `agent.wait` returned `ok`, history contained exactly one expected assistant answer, and the tracked local HTTP provider received one request. The native run ended with no suite or unhandled errors, and one-release AWS cleanup completed.

The first-chat test issues **one SDK chat intent, not one wire attempt**: the unmodified SDK made five wire attempts (four normal startup refusals, one handler start). No test retry wrapper, database prewarm or request-timeout change was added. This qualifies the current user flow with an explicit observation overlay; it is **not an original-versus-fixed Gateway RPC RED/GREEN comparison**. The owner-level causal regressions below provide that separate evidence. The provider is local and deterministic, not a live external model.

<details>
<summary>Selected first-chat native receipts and source scope</summary>

Projected from the actual selected-case and native run-end receipts; the immutable pre-release snapshot is the pause witness:

```text
published parent: d8b5dc1572f7f53a0169de4a2d30cd9aabc9c4ef
clean observation commit: 67ff49e8d5f7a748f2b180a73e0a3333e9dff550
observation tree: 319129caca8f11801330a816a249f2519f325ed9
store absent before first use: true
before release: matching target opens=1, creator paused=true
before release: canonical startup refusals=1, handler starts=0
post-release native factory increment: 1
post-release matching target increment: 3
SDK intents=1; wire attempts=5; total startup refusals=4
handler starts=1; agent.wait=ok
persisted expected answers=1; provider requests=1
selected case=passed; suite errors=0; unhandled errors=0
```

The clean native observation commit is a child of this PR head, with four explicit observation/test-path changes. The production preparer is byte-identical to the PR; the fact-reader algorithm is unchanged apart from scalar publications. It is not claimed to be the unmodified published tree. Pinned Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` both passed the tiny native-channel/correlation control before product work. The selected first-chat case passed; the five existing recovery cases were intentionally not selected in this additional run and are covered by the 70-case qualification below.

Only the immutable pre-release snapshot establishes the held creator. Later open counters include a normal second open; the auxiliary post-open pause flag is not a liveness observation and is excluded from qualification. Earlier probes that timed out before the required observation were rejected, not counted as causal RED.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Owner regressions, fixture isolation and scoped checks</summary>

- [Current normalized-source qualification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e2c94863fd1bece84bef822f7c950e59): maintained Gateway-root compiler leaf passed with all five changed files in the actual compiler program; exact five-file type-aware lint and normal `qaRuntime` build passed; all 49 owner, 16 creation/settlement and five original recovered-output cases passed (70 total, zero pending).
- [Exact first-use causal RED and original repair GREEN](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_832e9fbc61a11d78e4d264b4891c0bf5): baseline executed the first-use regression and failed with actual registry-error provenance; the initial repair passed. The normalized run requalified the later owner/readiness simplification rather than borrowing that earlier GREEN. The separate existing-store cold-registration regression also has retained original RED/fix GREEN evidence.
- [Fixture-isolation proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7b92ea0a99a98574bed11207ae2637d3): permissive-umask regression failed on `0775` versus `0700`, then helper 3 + recovered-output 5 + encrypted 1 cases passed. Both fixture files remain byte-identical to that qualified source.
- Repository-configured formatting and fresh complete five-file independent review passed. All task-owned runtime leases completed one-release cleanup.

The normalized proof used failed CI merge `3449e444e4a8733541d828e894d86ce74f83705d`, with all five changed-file bytes matching this revision. Its `97dd78cc2cbd4f9dff1add734a2b316ac8d8bf31` main integration was a different whole tree; the subsequent successful current-head PR CI above, not file-byte equality, supplies integration validation.

</details>

Full-main qualification, release packaging and manual Windows/live-external-model proof are not claimed. Current-head ClawSweeper satisfaction and the native landing workflow remain required; nothing has been merged by this update.

prs.title: perf(sessions): charge shared actor entry fields once in the replica pool
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session actor replica budget charges each session for large skills snapshots that are already shared on the main heap. Repeated immutable prompt-report sections are also retained separately. This causes avoidable eviction within the existing 8 MiB / 128-replica limits.

## User Impact

More session replicas fit within the existing memory budget. Stored entries, model context, authority checks and all wire encoders remain unchanged. Existing resident-entry references may be used more often because fewer replicas are evicted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Charge each interned field once per replica pool, counting resident references and releasing the shared charge when the last resident reference goes away. Extend the existing bounded weak interner to immutable report sections while keeping session-specific report provenance separate.

The full wire-reference proposal is held separately at `steipete/perf-actor-entry-wire-refs-20261115`, commit `e60041e30a5da06f5f6c21afdadb75b26e2e31f5`. This PR contains no advertised field keys, command pins, worker field references or admission restoration. The coordinating maintainer will decide whether to revive that proposal after production component counters are available.

## Evidence

Measurement acceptance: run the existing native append fixture on current main and the residency-only candidate at 2, 100, 200 and 400 sessions; record resident replicas and pool bytes, then measure post-GC main heap at 100 sessions. Compare resident and evicted native request/admission/receipt byte counts with identical fixture paths. Five actual-append rounds of 100 sessions per side measure main-thread CPU and allocation separately, including replica updates and excluding wire-capture instrumentation. The expected win is residency and memory accounting; per-append CPU/allocation should remain neutral or improve. Preserve model-context hashes and the existing wire shapes.

Baseline: `987c04a0086963d301cb4e440c758acc7178c7b6` (current main when measurement began). The synthetic entry contains a ~110 KB skills snapshot and a ~20 KB prompt report. Across 100 sessions there is one skills snapshot, 100 reports with distinct session provenance, and one value for each of four immutable report sections.

| Active sessions | Resident replicas, before → after | Accounted pool bytes, before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 2 → 2 | 626,376 → 334,270 |
| 100 | 27 → 100 | 8,125,902 → 2,633,858 |
| 200 | 27 → 128 | 8,126,388 → 1,427,546 |
| 400 | 27 → 128 | 8,126,388 → 1,427,430 |

Pool bytes are the owner's heap estimate, not physical heap measurements. The separate 100-session post-GC pass measured main heap **146.880 → 143.306 MiB** (−3.574 MiB), and whole-process RSS **1,520.474 → 1,444.718 MiB**. RSS includes native workers and is contextual.

| Actual native append workload | Main CPU per append, before → after | Sampled main allocation per append, before → after | Samples per side per mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 active sessions | 1.582 → 1.381 ms (round medians) | 588,993 → 369,651 B (mean) | 5 × 100 appends |
| 200 active sessions, AB then BA | 1.580 → 1.622 ms (paired means) | 623,841 → 610,710 B (paired means) | 2 × 5 × 200 appends |

At 100 sessions, fewer replica misses also reduce append work through the existing resident-token protocol. With 200 sessions, both sides still miss during sequential churn. Allocation fell 2.25% and 1.96% in the two cold-path pairs. CPU changed +201 µs then −117 µs per append (+12.8%, −7.3%); the signed absolute mean is +42 µs (+2.7%), so CPU is inconclusive rather than an adverse result. One-minute host load varied roughly 15–24. Untraced GC at 100 sessions fell 0.0381 → 0.0120 ms/append (10 → 5 collections; max 2.885 → 1.849 ms). At 200 sessions, total GC was effectively flat at 0.06375 → 0.06348 ms/append, 70 collections per side across both pairs, with maximum pauses 4.950 → 4.079 ms. No percentile gates are claimed from these small collection counts.

**Wire equality:** with matching residency, every captured admission/receipt byte count and every model-context hash matches main. Main→worker totals also match. At 2 resident sessions, per-append mean request/admission/receipt sizes are **1,931 / 1,990 / 5,260 B** on both sides. At 200 evicted sessions they are **1,922.66 / 133,195.6 / 5,564.45 B** on both sides; the 400-session comparison also matches. At 100 sessions, retaining all entries uses the existing resident-token path more often: admission bytes fall 133,191.2 → 2,003.4 B, request bytes rise 1,918.02 → 2,169.82 B, and receipts remain 5,553.05 B. This is a change in existing path selection, not an encoding change. All admission, command, worker, receipt and authority implementations are unchanged from main. The current authority Prometheus byte counter omits ordinary native admissions; no production counter improvement is claimed.

Reproduction (same `--output` path for both arms, move each completed report aside before running the other):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-append-receipt-measure.ts \
  --output .local/residency-run --mode census --sessions 100 --rows 4 --rounds 1 --text-repeats 20
# Census: repeat with 2, 200 and 400 sessions. Heap: --mode heap, 100 sessions.
# Actual append work: --mode append-timing / append-allocation --rounds 5,
# at 100 and 200 sessions; reverse launch order for the second 200-session pair.
```

The existing pool-budget regression fails on main because replicas with a shared large prompt are evicted before reaching 128 entries. It also exercises retiring distinct shared values before admitting the next cohort. The former 16 KiB admission-budget regression is removed from this PR and remains on the held branch.

Runtime production delta: **+86 LOC**. Growth implements explicit shared-value accounting and immutable report-section interning; the former skills-only sharing path is replaced. The interner retains at most 256 weak lookup entries, and resident pool references are released with their last cell. No persisted shape, schema, configuration, or public contract changes. Author simplification removed command pinning, advertised keys, worker projections, admission restoration, wire-only tests and replay tooling from this PR. The remaining benchmark measures actual native appends.

All 106 focused tests passed: 68 actor/replica/worker tests, 14 prefix-stability tests and 24 eager-import/wrapper-closure tests. The matching session test typecheck and `pnpm tsgo:test:root` passed, as did changed-file lint/format, the assertion-safety and export-collision guards, and `git diff --check`. The test delta is +7 lines with an exact allocation entry. Runtime source is +86 LOC; the prescribed non-test diff including benchmark tooling is +196 LOC. On final head `bcc0e285c84422a45f0aa06a1d3033110ade3e5d`, [CI run 43763608489](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763608489) completed with one infrastructure failure: [check-test-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763608489/job/132964687005) timed out during all five checkout attempts and never ran TypeScript. The other required build, lint, typecheck and test jobs passed, including PostgreSQL conformance and its PostgreSQL 16 smoke. `pnpm tsgo:test:root` was rerun locally on this exact head and all four scopes passed (4.6/4.8/4.8/5.5 seconds). The local retry command was refused; no CI rerun was executed. The aggregate CI gate therefore remains red and needs checkout-job recovery by the coordinating maintainer. No production load or full Gateway stress was run; this is the requested residency-only owner/native-transport comparison. Independent review and merging remain with the coordinating maintainer.
