prs.title: perf(update): replace the candidate canary with a runtime contract check
prs.body:
## Problem

Before activation, `openclaw update` rehearses the candidate. It copies all SQLite state and plugin payloads into a scratch directory, runs the candidate's `doctor --fix`, `doctor --lint`, `config validate` and `plugins list` against the copy, then boots a private Gateway on it. On Peanutto's production-sized state this took 10–15 minutes of a 26-minute update (about 46%).

#197851 made that rehearsal redundant. Post-activation rollback now always has a pre-activation SQLite schema baseline, and `--no-restart` updates boot the activated release once (`activated-gateway-startup`) and roll back when it cannot become ready. Doctor and Gateway startup are proven on real state after activation, with rollback.

## Change

The driver no longer rehearses. Before activation it runs only the candidate's recovery worker once: `update-migrated-finalize --check` (step `candidate-recovery`). That one stateless call already produced every canary output used later:

| Canary output | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `candidateSchemaVersions` (activation schema baseline, PostgreSQL baseline gate, post-Doctor schema check) | `--check` `state`/`agent` |
| `gatewayRestartCompletion` | `--check` `gatewayRestartCompletion` |
| `doctorConfigWrites` (delegated Doctor config writes) | `--check` `doctorConfigWrites: "pid-start-v1"` |
| `doctorConfigChanges` | Removed. Activation Doctor reports its own `configChanges` and refusal keys. |
| `validatedConfigSnapshot` | Unchanged: the config read before the check |
| Observed canary Gateway startup ms (previous-Gateway readiness window) | Removed; the existing five-minute floor or `--timeout` applies |
| Missing worker → "uses the current updater" advisory | Kept as-is |

Call sites:

- `openclaw update` (`validateUpdateCandidateWithProgress`) calls `checkUpdateCandidate`. The progress-writer and state-worker scaffolding that kept WAL readable during the copy is gone.
- `openclaw update preflight` (external supervisors) reads config and runs `--check`. Its receipt `coverage` changes from `isolated-core-startup` to `candidate-runtime`, so a supervisor can tell the weaker proof apart. `--source-root` is still accepted.
- Immutable activation runs `--check` before drain and before rollback. The post-start private canary and its second observation are removed; live readiness verification and rollback are unchanged.
- `snapshot-space-preflight` keeps only the activation database backup/rollback space check.
- Automatic-update backoff keys on repeated identical activation failures (`openclaw doctor`, `post-update verification`, `activated-gateway-startup`) instead of `candidate-doctor`, which no longer runs. It counts runs recorded as `rolled-back` as well as `failed`, because a failed activation usually restores the previous release (ClawSweeper finding; the `rolled back` campaign case fails without it).
- The previous-Gateway readiness budget uses the existing floor (5 min, 90 min on Windows) or `--timeout`.
- **Fix found by E2E:** `captureUpdateDatabases` retires idle state-read workers before acquiring capture ownership. A reader started before activation lazy-imported `gateway-owner-lease.worker` by its old hashed chunk name; when the target rehashes that chunk the ownership check fails and automatic restore is disabled.
- **Fix found by E2E:** the no-restart `activated-gateway-startup` boot (#197851) writes boot bookkeeping to real state, after which database rollback saw "changes after Doctor" and refused. `adoptUpdateBootDatabaseWrites` attributes the boot's own writes to the update when nothing else wrote since Doctor. Accepted edge case: a foreign write during the boot window is attributed the same way. Covered by the `activated-boot` case of `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` (settlement and restore, not helper output).
- Restore uses the plugin-cohort binding captured before Doctor, because the previous build cannot open a state database Doctor migrated to a newer schema (`newer-schema` case).

### #197922's delegated rehearsal is removed

#197922 (merged 11-14) made the candidate run its own rehearsal (`openclaw update rehearse`, package marker `openclaw.updateRehearsalProtocol: 1`) when the installed updater supports delegation. This PR removes the rehearsal, so it also removes the delegation: the driver-side delegated rehearsal, the candidate-side `update rehearse` command, the rehearsal contract and the marker (−1,803 lines of #197922).

- **No released version depends on it.** `git tag --contains 3ab80aba158a` lists only `release-publish/*` cuts of 2026.11.3; `v2026.11.3` (npm `latest`) and `v2026.11.5-beta.1..3` do not contain it, and `npm view openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.3 openclaw.updateRehearsalProtocol` is empty. Per AGENTS.md, main and beta are not shipped contracts.
- **Updaters built from main since #197922 fall back.** When the target lacks the marker, they run their own rehearsal (the path #197922 kept for unsupported targets). Proven below: a main updater (merge base, which contains #197922) updated to this branch, rehearsed it itself and finished `ok`.

### Rollback no longer runs without the retained runtime

Runtime retention copies the running updater so its lazy imports and workers keep working after the package or checkout is replaced. Since #185178 a retention failure only logged "continuing update without a verified retained rollback runtime". With the canary gone, rollback is the only safety net, and it loads code from that retained runtime.

Reproduced (package install, retention fault injected, then a migration that commits and a Doctor that fails): Doctor committed the migration, `database rollback` failed with `Cannot find module …/dist/update-candidate-state-<hash>.mjs`, the update ended `state-migrated-no-rollback` and **left the target release active**. The same faults without the retention failure roll back the databases and the package.

Chosen behavior: **every retention failure now stops the update before staging or activation**, with "Could not retain the running updater (<reason>). The update stopped before changing the installation; retry it." Cancellation and uncertain subprocess cleanup still propagate unchanged.

- Least complex: it deletes #185178's fallback (−26 production lines) instead of making rollback independent of the copy, which would mean preloading every lazy rollback import and pinning every worker entry, a second retention mechanism.
- Measured cost on large installs: #185178 was motivated by a worker output cap that #184958 has since fixed. Peanutto (183k entries, ~4 GB retained) completed retention on all 17 updates since 2026-10-27, so this refusal would not have fired once. The remaining causes are a source file changing during the copy (retry) and a host-owned plugin link (documented fix in `docs/cli/update.md#runtime-retention-failures`).
- Retention itself goes away with Git releases in a later slice; this does not redesign it.

### What was removed

- Driver: `update-candidate-canary.ts`, `update-candidate-canary-commands.ts`, canary-only lint/failure/config helpers, Git startup-runtime selection, the validation wrapper scaffolding, and #197922's delegated rehearsal.
- Candidate: `update rehearse`, `update-rehearsal-contract.ts`, the `updateRehearsalProtocol` marker.
- #185178's retention fallback.
- Tests: the canary suites and their test-support, and the delegated-rehearsal tests.

Against the merge base: **production +383 / −2,198** (net −1,815), tests +648 / −6,140, docs +111 / −134, config −18.

### What stays, and why

Released updaters, including stable 2026.11.3, still rehearse whatever candidate they install, using **the candidate's** state-copy worker, rehearsal-aware Doctor and lint, `update-candidate-rehearsal`/`-snapshot`, plugin-tree copy and `--update-canary` startup progress. Deleting those would break upgrades from every shipped version, so the candidate side stays until no supported update source runs the canary. Historical step identities (`candidate-doctor` etc.) stay so existing `update_runs` history renders.

## Review findings

- **Config-convergence test** (`update-cli.config-convergence.test.ts`): the stateless check no longer receives config, so the test now asserts what the check does receive at its boundary, the owning profile's `stateDir` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, keeps an explicit `candidate-recovery` refusal through the result contract, and asserts authored config bytes are unchanged.
- **Data-model compatibility:** no schema, config or stored-data shape changes. Existing state from 2026.11.3 (state schema 22 → 40) and Peanutto's production databases (3.3 GB) load through the real update path below.
- **Boot-writes test:** replaced by the `activated-boot` settlement-and-restore case in the database rollback matrix; it fails when boot-write adoption is disabled.

## Evidence

Harness: real `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --json --tag <packed tarball>` from an npm-global install on isolated `env -i` state (cloned per run with `cp -c`), run on mbp-m5, three at a time. Base = merge base `1e64efd` with inert env-gated faults; head = this branch on the same base (`8065ed6`; the "with fix" rows use `097a6ba`, the retention fix before its refusal wording). The current head `fc813bb` is that change rebased onto `7310fc2`; the rebase only adopted commit `764761e`'s "Update refused: …" wording in the snapshot-space refusal. Fault targets are the same tarball plus env-gated faults: `gateway-crash` (Gateway throws at boot), `plugin-crash` (acpx throws at load), `migration-broken` (state v41 adds a column then throws), `committed-migration` (v41 commits, then Doctor throws), `retention` (runtime retention throws after the native helper is bound). "Gateway after" = a fresh Gateway on the post-update state reaches `/readyz`. Schema = state `user_version` after the run (base 40, fault target 41).

| Case | main (canary) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| clean update | ok; validating 65 s (retention 18, candidate Doctor 7, candidate Gateway 6) | ok; validating 52 s (retention 32, `candidate-recovery` + admission ~20); **no candidate Doctor/Gateway phase** |
| gateway crash | refused at `candidate-gateway-startup`; base kept | activated, `activated-gateway-startup` failed → **database rollback + package rollback**; base active; Gateway after ok |
| committed migration + failed Doctor | refused at `candidate-doctor` | v41 committed, Doctor failed → **database rollback (state back to v40) + package rollback**; base active; Gateway after ok |
| broken migration | refused at `candidate-doctor` | Doctor failed → database + package rollback; state v40; Gateway after ok |
| plugin crash | ok (plugin failure recorded) | ok (plugin failure recorded) |
| retention failure + gateway crash | refused at `candidate-gateway-startup` | before fix: rolled back; **with fix: refused before activation** |
| retention failure + committed migration | refused at `candidate-doctor` | before fix: **`Cannot find module`, rollback failed, `state-migrated-no-rollback`, target left active, state stuck at v41**; with fix: refused before staging, base active, state v40, Gateway after ok |
| 2026.11.3 → head | — | ok (2026.11.3's own canary against the kept candidate surfaces); state schema 22 → 40; Gateway after ok |
| main updater (contains #197922) → head | — | target lacks the marker → updater ran its own rehearsal → ok; Gateway after ok |
| Peanutto-shaped clean update (3.28 GB SQLite: Peanutto's state + 3.1 GB agent DB, its plugin set) | ok; **validating 236 s** (retention 50, candidate snapshot 47, candidate Doctor 64, lint 22, candidate Gateway 27); update 949 s | ok; **validating 68 s** (retention 50, `candidate-recovery` + admission ~18); update 839 s; Gateway after ok |

Peanutto-shaped: the validating phase drops by **168 s** (236 → 68 s), all of it the four rehearsal steps (160 s). Those two runs overlapped each other, so their activation and total times are not a clean comparison; small-state wall times are likewise not comparable across rows (runs overlapped three at a time). The ~950 s mean saving estimated from Peanutto's live history (where the candidate Doctor took 200–670 s) is unmeasured here.

Tests: 31 touched update test files plus the admission test pass (mbp-m5, `ocx test`, 957 s). The retention suites pass (50); 7 of them fail on the previous head because retention resolved instead of stopping. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxfmt clean. oxlint reports one inherited `max-lines` on `update-command-service-maintenance.ts` (750 lines here, 756 on main).

### CI notes

- `update-cli.candidate-admission.test.ts` > "blocks package updates when the target requires a newer Node runtime" still asserted the multi-line diagnostic that `764761e` moved into the saved report; it fails the same way on main `f24c2097`, whose changed-lane CI does not select this suite. Updated to assert the one-line refusal and the recovery steps.
- `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.test.ts` (interleaved same-context replies) failed in an earlier run of this PR and fails locally on main `f24c2097` too; this PR does not touch that plugin. The branch now includes main through #199736, the fix for the earlier memory-core `manager-shadow-write.test.ts` failure.
- `src/gateway/github-pr-workspace-preparation.test.ts` > "recovers an interrupted initial exact install (bound runtime=true)" (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-22`) fails 3/3 locally on both this head `97ca0de5` and main `e182b8d5`, also fails on main `a1dd4938`, and failed again on the rerun of the failed job (run 43763967024, attempt 2), with the same `expect(runtime?.isPaused()).toBe(true)` assertion at line 884. This PR does not touch `src/gateway`.

## Accepted edge cases

- Problems only Doctor or Gateway startup reveal are found after activation. The update rolls back the release and the pre-activation database baseline instead of refusing first: one activation/rollback cycle (with restart, a brief Gateway outage) in exchange for skipping the rehearsal on every successful update.
- `--no-restart` with a Gateway still running the old code: the activated release is not booted (reported), as in #197851.
- External supervisors using `update preflight` get less proof (`coverage: "candidate-runtime"`) and must verify readiness after activation.
- A retention failure now stops the update; the user retries or fixes the named cause.

## Gaps

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` on `dffdf91` reported `database-worker`/`database-dialect` failures after a runner shutdown signal. Both ratchets pass locally against the merge base (`SQLite T1 live calls: 166 -> 166`; dialect: no construct-group growth).

- The Git-checkout path was not re-run in this round (the m5 repository was mid-repack). Retention and rollback share one owner across package and Git installs, and the earlier Git runs are in this PR's history.
- The fixed refusal message was proven in unit tests; the E2E refusal ran on the fix before the message wording was added.
- The main updater at the merge base refuses a relocated state directory in its canary snapshot ("Restored client credentials do not match the captured shared database": the credential receipt pins the shared database inode). The harness repoints the receipt after each `cp -c`; head never runs that snapshot.

prs.title: improve(ui): show the Blobster for Templates without artwork
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Templates without artwork appear in Templates search results as a generic box, which reads as a package rather than an agent and does not match the Templates icon used in navigation.

## User Impact

User impact: a Template without artwork, or whose artwork fails to load, now shows the Templates Blobster outline in the same accent color the box used. Templates that ship artwork are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`TemplateArtwork` owns the fallback for every surface that shows a Template's icon, so the search card, the detail header, the preview, and chat Template references all change together. It now renders the existing `blobster` icon, which is the same artwork as the Templates navigation icon. The icon strokes with `currentColor`, so it inherits the accent color already set on each artwork container, and no CSS or icon data changes. The Template creator's draft header has its own hard-coded box and is not changed here.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the production Control UI bundle built from each revision, in Chromium at 1280x800 and 2x scale, with a mocked Gateway and the same synthetic catalog on both sides. Before is `origin/main` at `29b1f65e7970`; after is `a4918a7ac496`.

Search result card, dark and light:

![Before and after of the Template search card in dark and light themes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c52348b9-b453-49d9-a8fb-b80a0eccc465)

Search results. The middle card has artwork and is unchanged:

![Before and after of Templates search results in the dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/217f9672-00ba-44f9-b2a5-12b7d34021b8)

Template detail header:

![Before and after of the Template detail header in the dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b21c60c-4bb8-476b-9491-43d05222db32)

The fallback's computed color equals `--accent` on both revisions: `rgb(255, 92, 92)` in dark and `rgb(189, 69, 49)` in light.

Tests and checks:

- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/agents-home/templates-home.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed. The updated fallback test covers both a Template with no artwork and an artwork load error, on the card and the detail header. With the source change reverted, both cases fail (`expected to have a length of 2 but got 0`).
- `pnpm check:changed`: formatting, lint, UI and core typechecks, the Control UI controller guard, and the i18n catalog pass. The dead-export scan fails on exports in `src/state/*` and `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/member-welcome.ts`, which this change does not touch.

prs.title: fix: Knowledge claims interrupted settings changes did not apply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge says a store assignment or conversation-access change did not happen when its response is interrupted.

## User Impact

User impact: the error now describes an unconfirmed outcome and directs users to reopen Stores & sharing before retrying. It no longer claims nothing changed when a later read can show the change was saved. Known refusal and successful-save messages remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed response does not establish whether the write committed. The existing owner returns explicit outcomes when it can, but the browser’s catch-all path previously made an unconditional “not changed” claim. Both settings surfaces now preserve that uncertainty without changing writes, permissions, retries or storage.

Related: #195010 is a broader glossary/localization pass. Its current diff changes these messages to “Couldn’t change … Try again,” so it does not resolve this outcome distinction.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both paths through the real built Knowledge plugin on main at 18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15: select a shared store or change conversation access, receive an interrupted response, then reopen Stores & sharing. The synthetic Gateway’s readback confirms that the change applied, despite the original “not changed” message.
- Both committed browser regressions fail on the original copy and pass with the correction. They exercise the existing readback control and verify exactly one mutation, not a retry. Five existing Knowledge UI tests also pass.
- Source inspection confirms that successful assignment and access writes can be followed by a failed snapshot read, and the feature client can throw for an interrupted or invalid response. No new backend outcome or recovery mechanism was introduced.
- Focused lint, browser/E2E typechecks, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks passed. No broad local test suite or live Knowledge configuration change was performed.

### Maintainer verification

Re-ran both built-app Chromium scenarios on the final candidate: assignment and conversation access each report an unconfirmed result, display the saved state after reopening Stores & sharing, and issue exactly one mutation (2/2 passed). The 5 existing Knowledge UI tests also passed. Focused lint, formatting and diff checks passed; independent static review found no actionable P0–P2 defects.

The test fixture now accepts only the expected mutation for each scenario. Removed optional screenshot capture and a redundant internal-state assertion while retaining both readback cases. Production behavior and the screenshots below are unchanged. The applied-write/lost-response condition remains simulated at the Gateway boundary; no live store or access grant was changed.

### Before

![Before: an interrupted assignment reply claims nothing changed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d80d7a59-7802-4959-ac50-b0da552318e1)

### After

![After: Knowledge preserves uncertainty and names the readback step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc8977f3-ff2c-4376-bbe9-e06201a97b3c)

<details>
<summary>Conversation-access feedback</summary>

Before:

![Before: interrupted conversation-access reply claims access was unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a1cbe50-7300-4ef6-9e9e-585098836496)

After:

![After: conversation-access feedback asks for readback before retrying](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aebd1fd-5544-413d-9328-19c1783a99d6)

</details>

Real built app and native plugin components; synthetic agent, store, conversation and Gateway replies; emulated 1280 × 1000 viewport. The applied-write/lost-response condition is simulated at the Gateway boundary. No live store assignment or access grant was changed.

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed this audit and the user-facing correction.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/27ab8da9-7856-4f25-9b62-91d8138f1a1c)

prs.title: fix(agents): skills_read cuts the middle out of large skill companion files
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/199782

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `skills_read({ name, relativePath })` on a skill companion file larger than one tool result gives the model the file's start and end with the middle cut out by the generic tool-result cap, and nothing in the result tells it how to read the cut part.

## User Impact

User impact: a companion file larger than one tool result now pages like `SKILL.md` does since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197564. The `skills_read` result shows its first lines and ends with the `read` call (the companion's path and the next line `offset`) that continues it, so the agent can read all of it.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197564 made `formatSkillInstructionsForModel` fit `SKILL.md` text to the model output budget, and its notes named `relativePath` companion files as a follow-up. That function returned a companion whole before the budget check (`instructions.relativePath !== undefined`), so a companion up to the documented 256 KiB took the generic cap path.

The short-circuit is gone. Companions take the same fitting. The continuation names the companion's own path, `path.join(dirname(<SKILL.md location>), relativePath)`. Companions are read only from local skill directories, whose `location` is the absolute `SKILL.md` path. Delivery bookkeeping (`rememberSkillInstructionDelivery`) still records only whole `SKILL.md` reads, as before. The docs paragraph on companions says how a large one pages.

Changes against `main` (`git diff --numstat`): `installed-skill-tools.ts` +13/−6, `installed-skill-tools.test.ts` +9/−7 (the existing paging case now also runs with a companion), `docs/tools/skills.md` +6/−3.

## Evidence

Tested at `5ef3eb9ebc6` (base `main` `e5f1a21c0b0`).

One driver script ran both sides: it checks out the commit, forces `pnpm build`, starts an isolated Gateway (its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and config, loopback port, token auth from the config), and runs one turn with `pnpm --silent openclaw agent --agent main --session-id proof -m 'Use the companion-proof skill: read its references/big.md companion and tell me the code word.' --json 2>&1 | tee <proof-dir>/runs/<run>/logs/agent.json` (`<proof-dir>` is the local directory holding the driver and run logs; `<run>` is `before-4` or `after-4`). The workspace holds a skill `companion-proof` whose `references/big.md` has 1,601 lines (139,728 bytes), with "The code word is AMBER-HERON-4417." at line 881.

Raw captures: [before-raw.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261115-197564-1-skill-companion-paging/before-raw.txt) and [after-raw.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261115-197564-1-skill-companion-paging/after-raw.txt). Each holds the driver's transcript and then the mock provider's request log. The driver prints each command on a `$` line from the same string it then runs, followed by its stdout and stderr (including the agent's `--json` output) and its exit status (the two background commands, the mock and the Gateway, have no exit line); the build output and the Gateway's log stay in their log files, apart from the lines `tail` and `grep` print. Both captures are verbatim apart from placeholders for the worktree, the proof directory, the run's state directory (`<live-dir>`), the branch name and the two loopback ports. The Gateway's ready line keeps its terminal color codes as printed. `wait` reports exit 143 because the driver stopped the mock with SIGTERM.

What is real and what is injected: the Gateway built from source, the agent runner, the deferred-tool dispatcher, `skills_read`, `read` and the tool-result budget are real. The model is a local OpenAI-compatible mock, not a real model. It calls `skills_read` for the companion, follows any `read` continuation named in the last tool result, and answers `CODE-WORD: <word>` if a tool result contained the code word, else `MISSING-CODE-WORD`. A run with a real model is not included: no provider key was available to this run.

Reading aid, not raw output: each run's `result.txt`, rendered whole by the driver's report script from the request log, with the same `<live-dir>` placeholder. "omission marker" means the tool result contains `middle content omitted`, the generic cap's marker; "tail" is the last 260 characters of the tool result as JSON.

Before (`main` `e5f1a21c0b0`):

```text
request 1: model calls dispatch_action {"id":"skills_read","args":{"name":"companion-proof","relativePath":"references/big.md"}}
  tool result before request 2: 32000 chars, code word absent, omission marker present
  tail: ".\\nLine 1599: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\\nLine 1600: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\\n\"}]}}[... 109536 more characters truncated; rerun with narrower args if needed]"
request 2: model answers MISSING-CODE-WORD
agent reply: MISSING-CODE-WORD
```

After (this PR):

```text
request 1: model calls dispatch_action {"id":"skills_read","args":{"name":"companion-proof","relativePath":"references/big.md"}}
request 2: model calls read {"path":"<live-dir>/workspace/skills/companion-proof/references/big.md","offset":357}
  tool result before request 2: 31603 chars, code word absent, omission marker absent
  tail: "ps.\\n\\n[Skill instructions incomplete: showing lines 1-356 of 1602. Before acting, read the rest with read({\\\"path\\\":\\\"<live-dir>/workspace/skills/companion-proof/references/big.md\\\",\\\"offset\\\":357}) and follow each continuation until the end.]\"}]}}"
request 3: model calls read {"path":"<live-dir>/workspace/skills/companion-proof/references/big.md","offset":723}
  tool result before request 3: 31914 chars, code word absent, omission marker absent
  tail: " later steps.\nLine 721: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\nLine 722: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\n\n[Read output capped at 50KB for this call. Use offset=723 to continue.]"
request 4: model calls read {"path":"<live-dir>/workspace/skills/companion-proof/references/big.md","offset":1089}
  tool result before request 4: 31951 chars, code word present, omission marker absent
  tail: "ter steps.\nLine 1086: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\nLine 1087: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\n\n[Read output capped at 50KB for this call. Use offset=1089 to continue.]"
request 5: model calls read {"path":"<live-dir>/workspace/skills/companion-proof/references/big.md","offset":1451}
  tool result before request 5: 31929 chars, code word absent, omission marker absent
  tail: "ter steps.\nLine 1448: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\nLine 1449: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\n\n[Read output capped at 50KB for this call. Use offset=1451 to continue.]"
  tool result before request 6: 13288 chars, code word absent, omission marker absent
  tail: " 1598: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\nLine 1599: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\nLine 1600: reference detail that the skill keeps in its companion file for later steps.\n"
request 6: model answers CODE-WORD: AMBER-HERON-4417
agent reply: CODE-WORD: AMBER-HERON-4417
```

Observed result: on `main`, the `skills_read` tool result the model receives is 32,000 characters, does not contain line 881, and ends with the notice that 109,536 more characters of that result were truncated. With this change, it receives lines 1-356 and the `read` call, follows it through four `read` pages, and answers with the code word.

The tails are the tool result text as the model received it. `dispatch_action` returns the `skills_read` result inside a JSON string, hence the `\n`, `\"` and closing `"}]}}`; the truncation notice counts characters of that escaped result, not of the file. The page count says "of 1602" because the file ends with a newline: splitting on `\n` yields a last, empty line. Both runs used the same `<live-dir>` path, and their agent output reports the same system prompt (47,874 characters, same hash).

Regression: the existing paging case in `installed-skill-tools.test.ts` now runs for `SKILL.md` and for a companion, each with and without a callable `read`. Both companion cases fail on `main`. Each changed line was reverted on its own: keeping the short-circuit fails both companion cases, naming the `SKILL.md` path in the `read` call fails the `read` case, and naming it in the no-`read` notice fails the other.

Checks: the touched test file passes at the head (13 tests); every test file of the changed function's callers passed at the previous head `a0a2431ea70`, whose production code is the same (only this test file changed since): 12 files, 220 tests (`installed-skill-tools`, `installed-skill-usage`, `code-mode.skill-read`, `code-mode`, `code-mode.result-budget`, `agent-tools.finalize`, `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools`, `skill-runtime.workspace`, `attempt-client-tools`, `attempt.skills-policy`, `skill-resource-transfer`, `worker-tool-authority`). Against `main` (`pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`, where `upstream` is the openclaw/openclaw remote), every lane passed (typecheck core and core tests, lint, format, guards) except the tree-wide dead export scan. That scan flags exports in `src/state/` (`sqlite-copy-swap.ts`, `state-upgrade.ts` and siblings) and `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/member-welcome.ts`, files this PR does not touch. Net test lines are +2, within the test-lines ratchet's per-PR allowance: "Test lines OK. Net test lines: +2; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0." The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/tools/installed-skill-tools.test.ts` | 1.8 s |

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base e5f1a21c0b0165536706fccb2492ee691baaeeff to head 5ef3eb9ebc64bf09580cb8b37a750eee2aa58d4d, priority P0–P1, with `installed-skill-catalog.ts`, `skill-instruction-result.ts`, `installed-skill-runtime.ts`, `agent-tools.read.ts` and `tool-result-limits.ts` as source context: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"e5f1a21c0b0165536706fccb2492ee691baaeeff","head":"5ef3eb9ebc64bf09580cb8b37a750eee2aa58d4d","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

Not covered: no real model provider; the mock plays the model (see Evidence). The following were read in the source, not run. Code Mode's `skills.read` renders from the tool result's `details` (`code-mode-bridge.ts`), which hold the whole text, so this change does not reach it. Placements without a local resource root (sandbox enabled, a remote workspace reader, workspace-hosted skill files, the harness's required-workspace view) reject `relativePath` as instruction-only before this function runs. Under `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, the `read` guard adds each resolved non-workspace skill directory as an extra read root (`core-coding-tools.ts`, `agent-tools.workspace-paths.test.ts`), and the companion's continuation path lies inside its skill's directory.

Accepted edge cases: the continuation is a `read` of the companion's host path, the same as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197564's continuation for `SKILL.md`. When no `read` tool is callable, the notice keeps https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197564's wording, including its advice to "move detail into references/ files", which also shows for a companion.

prs.title: fix: Knowledge mistakes empty filters for an empty store
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge’s Browse view tells users to save new knowledge when an active filter simply has no matches.

## User Impact

User impact: a filtered empty result now suggests changing or clearing filters. Genuine first-use empty views retain their existing guidance. No search, filtering, paging or saving behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory result is already filtered by the current query, type and—in Claims—assertion origin. An empty filtered result does not mean the store is empty. The view now selects its message from those existing inputs; it does not treat an inactive claim-origin filter as active while browsing pages.

Related: #195010 is a broader copy/localization pass whose current diff retains the unconditional first-use message.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main at b37978a42bdf6363e42c7f5cdee922bb1ffe7753 through the real built Knowledge plugin: browse an existing project, enter a nonmatching name, then clear the filter. The sidebar still counts the saved project while the original result claims “Nothing here yet.” Clearing the filter restores it without a write.
- Three filter regressions fail on the original copy. All **9 Knowledge UI tests pass**, including first use, inactive claim-origin state, retained views and inventory paging.
- The full-app filter → no match → clear → existing record flow passes. Only read operations were issued.
- The inventory producer, filter request and broader copy overlap were inspected. Scoped lint, the affected browser TypeScript graph, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. No broad local suite was run.

### Before

prs.body:
Closes #198569

## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub catalog links cannot currently open the matching plugin, skill, or published Template review in the desktop companion.

## User Impact

Users can open a catalog item in their selected Gateway, then make the existing explicit installation/Add decision there. Opening a URL never installs or enables code, selects a Gateway, supplies authentication, enables Labs, or creates an agent. Skill review retains agent selection; Template review retains Labs and Add consent.

**Platform limits:** macOS handoff is proven; shared Tauri source is only parser/URL-builder qualified, not Linux/Windows OS dispatch or live installation qualification. Full Tauri compilation was blocked by the offline cache missing locked `mdns-sd 0.21.6` (0.21.5 cached), with no dependency/lock changes. Separate native Windows Hub is unchanged/unverified. Cold-start Tauri links require connecting a ready main-window Gateway and reopening the link.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add identity-only adapters for `openclaw://{plugins,skills,templates}/install?name=<encoded identity>` and reuse the existing dashboard navigation owners. Validate one bounded package identity, reject external commands/Gateway/authentication parameters, and retain the selected Gateway base path and trusted auth session. Tauri receives normalized URLs, so raw empty-userinfo/dot-segment spellings are not always available; decoded package traversal remains rejected.

Simplification: the old dashboard-only inline Tauri parser/test moves into the single adapter; no new installation owner, state store, dependency, URL registration, or settings UI. Necessary growth covers the three family mappings and authority/identity regressions (whole change: +565/-39 lines including tests/docs/generated source inventory). A Clippy boolean simplification was applied and revalidated. Required native-source inventory was regenerated with the repository command (one source row; no locale/translation-memory edits).

## Evidence

Before first push, Patrick was shown inspected real browser/native screenshots and approved landing with these qualification limits. This PR changes navigation, not rendered UI appearance; the companion ClawHub PR owns the CTA/layout changes. Existing isolated proof is reused; no new installation was performed for publication.

- **Before → after, real macOS:** browser CTA previously had no native catalog review route; the new link opened the matching Hello World review with Install still awaiting consent. Only an explicit click then installed **and enabled** `openclaw-hello-world@0.1.0`. Final native UI and explicitly port-scoped Gateway RPC confirmed installed/enabled. Existing TypeBox runtime/provenance warnings remained; this is not warning-free runtime/provenance qualification.
- **Review-only siblings:** `@steipete/weather` opened the Weather skill review with Install awaiting consent; `@donniefi/hopper` opened the published Hopper Template with files and bundled items and Add awaiting consent. Neither was installed/added.
- Six sandboxed macOS parser/navigation XCTest cases passed (0 failures), including exact scoped identity, invalid-link rejection, trusted Gateway base path and fragment preservation. Swift build passed; isolated signed task app startup/handoffs passed after using the existing SwiftPM resource-lookup packaging helper. Normal installed app/config and default handler were preserved.
- Six tests importing the actual Tauri production parser/URL builder pass offline. Regression proof initially caught trusted-fragment loss (4 pass/2 fail), then all 6 passed. Re-run on the published source: 6/6 pass; offline Clippy `--tests -- -D warnings` passes; Rustfmt (edition 2021) passes. These do **not** compile the Tauri integration/application.
- Targeted SwiftFormat: 0/3 files need formatting; targeted SwiftLint passes; native i18n verification and normal commit hook pass; `git diff --check` passes. Shared Control UI review regression evidence: 85 tests pass; original plugin consent-routing regression: 3 pass.
- Local `pnpm check:changed` broad app checks are not claimed complete; exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate.
- Patrick-selected automated review route: hosted ClawSweeper only (no duplicate autoreview); review findings and exact-head CI will be reconciled before native landing.

No private configs/state, generated binaries, screenshots, or proof archives are committed. No installed-app replacement, normal URL-handler/config changes, shared restart, or dependency changes.


## Review repair and exact proof limits

ClawSweeper's review of `3a5fd51f30afe69cb39cf9defbd536362dc904d2` identified one actionable P2: denied OS notification permission hid the Tauri cold-start recovery instruction. Commit `0d1615d81ef7512127730016cab5432c215bfacc` routes this error through the existing in-window notice owner instead. This is a two-line repair; no new error/state owner or permission request.

A temporary Rust caller probe compiles the production handle_deep_links body and real production URL parser, with desktop I/O simulated: Gateway-not-ready returns the existing recovery instruction and OS notification delivery is denied. Independent expected output is a notice addressed to the focused main window for each catalog family.

```text
Before (3a5fd51f30af):
FAILED: plugins: focused window received no recovery instruction
left: []
right: [(main, Connect to a Gateway in the main window, then open the ClawHub link again.)]

After (0d1615d81ef7):
unavailable_gateway_has_visible_recovery_without_os_notifications ... ok
All three families checked. Existing production parser tests: 6 passed, 0 failed.
Rustfmt edition 2021 (changed modules, skip_children=true): pass

```

This probe verifies caller dispatch, **not** a real WebView/OS notification-denial interaction. No permanent source-string or mock-echo test was added: the live Tauri notice seam needs a desktop/WebView. Full local compilation remains unavailable under the documented offline cache limit. Prior-head hosted Linux companion build and macOS companion tests passed, but those results do not qualify this repaired head; fresh PR CI is required. Windows packaging was still running at the last prior-head observation. Linux/Windows OS-link dispatch/live installation and separate Windows Hub remain unverified.

The earlier macOS runtime captures were inspected and shown privately before Patrick authorized landing; they are not publicly attached here. Those described handoffs are therefore not independently inspectable public media proof. This PR makes no rendered appearance changes, and no new live Tauri/macOS install or broader platform claim is added by this repair.


## Landing status — current head

Reviewed/prepared head: `0d1615d81ef7512127730016cab5432c215bfacc`. The type/file exists at main baseline de0ea1efe5f9, is absent from this PR head, and is outside all nine changed paths. This is an inherited shared-library report, not a catalog-adapter failure.
- Native preparation and review validation passed. Native merge admission stopped **before dispatch** on MERGEABLE/UNSTABLE: its rollup guard requires GREEN, including this non-required report. No merge request/outcome was recorded. The native inherited-failure validator currently supports the primary ci.yml failure route and the specific optional build-artifact workflow, not this Periphery report; no exception evidence or green result has been fabricated, and no raw merge/guard bypass attempted.

Landing remains blocked on an authorized supported native route for this non-required inherited report (or its baseline-owner resolution and resulting qualification). No unrelated source repair, dependency change, or speculative rebase was made to chase green.

prs.title: fix(agents): Template greeting logs every tools.allow entry as an unavailable core tool
prs.body:
<!-- Title: fix(agents): Template greeting logs every tools.allow entry as an unavailable core tool -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every time a Template is added on a CLI backend (for example Claude CLI), the Gateway logs `tools: agents.<id>.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (read, write, edit, exec, ...). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.` for the new agent, though its config is fine.

## User Impact

User impact: adding a Template no longer leaves a false warning that sends operators looking for a broken tool config. Real unknown-entry warnings on turns that grant tools are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Template greeting turn runs with an explicitly empty tool grant (`toolsAllow: []`). On the loopback tool surface used by CLI backends, that grant mediates no coding tools, so every entry in the agent's own `tools.allow` looked unknown to the policy pipeline. Gateway tool resolution now skips the unknown-entry analysis for an explicit empty grant. Tool filtering is unchanged; the flag only gates the warning analysis. The analysis is skipped rather than its output dropped, so the warning dedupe cache isn't filled by a tool-less turn and the same warning still appears on a later turn that does grant tools.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/tool-resolution.toolless-warning.test.ts`. The tool-less case fails on main with the exact production warning and passes with the fix. The follow-up case checks that a later unrestricted turn with the same allowlist still warns.
- Mutations: disabling the empty-grant check fails the tool-less case. Silencing the logger instead of skipping the analysis fails the follow-up case.
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts` and `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` pass (64 tests with the new file). `pnpm check:changed` passes.
- Live run, Claude CLI backend, same Template on the same Gateway state:

```
before (main):  templates add @donniefi/hopper
  WARN tools: agents.hopper.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (read, write, edit, search_transit_systems, ...). Some entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config; ...
after:          templates add @donniefi/hopper --accept-capabilities
  {"agentId":"hopper-2","status":"complete"}, greeting run agents.create:hopper-2:template-greeting
  allowlist warnings for hopper-2 during Add and greeting: 0
```

Before the fix, 17 of 23 third-party ClawHub Templates logged this warning on their greeting.

prs.body:
Related: #199745, #189144

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: embedded-runner fault-sequence tests abort during authentication on a slow or contended CI CPU, before exercising the expected fallback chain. This is a maintainer-requested follow-up to the inherited CI failure recorded in #199745.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. CI continues to verify the same fault ordering, retries, profile rotation, cooldowns, exhaustion, admission invalidation, and compaction/transcript behavior without an unrelated 250 ms run-deadline race.

## Why This Change Was Made

These event-driven fixtures now explicitly select the existing unlimited run deadline (`timeoutMs: 0`). This removes the wall-clock race instead of enlarging a finite timeout. Vitest still bounds the tests, and no assertions or production behavior change.

The separate auth-controller suite retains deterministic fake-clock proof: credential lookup and token exchange each take 60 ms against a shared 100 ms budget; authentication is cut off and late credentials are never installed. Its hung credential, token-exchange, and AWS cases also remain intact.

The 250 ms fixture originated in #121399 (`cebb63081342`); #162398 only moved it. #189144 (`7bd53ff28f69`) correctly made authentication share the run deadline, exposing this fixture race. No production defect was established.

## Evidence

- Unmodified base `8656c447df0528d32df66616d71ffeb1cc9ec1e6`: local full fault suite failed a profile-rotation assertion with `credential resolution timed out at the run deadline (250ms)`; isolated Linux baseline failed 6/15 cases, including the header-only 429 auth-profile case.
- Repaired full fault suite: 15/15 pass; separate auth-controller suite: 39/39 pass. Fault-suite Vitest wall time: 26.58 s; combined wrapper including preparation: 135.68 s. Cold baseline setup is reported separately, not used as a performance comparison.
- Linux btrfs proof uses the prior reproduction's Docker CPU quota (`50000/100000`, 0.5 CPU), synthetic state and the pinned test runtime. Bounded campaign completed without retries: original fixture failed 20/20 runs (134 failed cases out of 300); repaired fixture passed 20/20 runs (300/300 cases). Median wrapper wall/CPU: 99.16/47.81 s before, 106.21/51.21 s after. Repaired wall range was 90.08–189.92 s. Baseline aborts early, so this is a correctness contrast, not a speedup claim. Median per-run peak reported heap was 450 MB before / 445.5 MB after; heap snapshots are not allocation totals.
- Codex autoreview (P0–P2), complete local diff against `8656c447df0528d32df66616d71ffeb1cc9ec1e6`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. The committed patch is `d27b1d3d57557362ac60cab66e3a15c8dbd2b90d`. All changed-file checks pass except the dead-export scan, which reports 12 production / 8 full-tree entries in untouched state-upgrade and member-welcome code. The exact base reproduces identical entries: state-upgrade exports were introduced by #198389 (`ef930ebbad77`), member-welcome exports by #198491 (`cec47fd13f23`). This is a separately actionable main regression; no scan is skipped. Exact-head CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763781283 (17 successful jobs, 32 skipped; changed Node test step 117 s). No inherited-CI merge exception is needed.

- Production LOC delta: 0. Test diff: +5/−2. No new config, cache, dependency, or schema. No UI-imported module changed.

Open #198966 proposes deleting this suite; this focused repair preserves its assertions and should remain distinct from that coverage-removal decision. #190976 changes the auth clock domain separately; this PR does not touch it.

prs.title: fix(discord): replies show an empty or broken code block when it starts at a message split
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord reply shows an empty code block, or loses its code formatting, when a fenced code block starts right at the point where the reply has to be split into a second message.

With the default limits (2000 chars, 17 lines), a reply with a 14-item list followed by a fenced block is split so the first message ends with the opener and a synthetic closer and nothing between them (`buildDiscordTextChunks`, the send path, on `main`):

```
"...14. Step number 14\n```bash\n```"   <- empty code block in Discord
"```bash\nnpm install\nnpm test\n```\nDone."
```

When the opener lands one to three characters short of the 2000-char cap instead, the opener line itself is cut in half:

```
"aaaa...a\n``"
"`ts\nconst x = 1;\n```\nafter"   <- `ts is prose, and the closing ``` opens an unclosed block
```

## User Impact

User impact: Discord replies with a code block near a message boundary no longer show an empty code block or render the code as text and the rest of the message as code. The opener now starts the next message together with its code.

## Why This Change Was Made

The range helper already keeps a fence opener with its body (`cutBoundary`), but `flush` only used it when the chunk overlapped an inline code span. A plain-text chunk ending on or inside an opener line went through `boundary`, which doesn't know about fences. `flush` now always uses `cutBoundary`.

## Evidence

Current verification on `01e53f1bda1a3cb6ff0f395caa667b65b6c80e6e` (2026-11-12):

It checks the default 17-line boundary (15 prose lines followed by an opener/body) and the 2,000-character boundary (1,993 prose characters before the opener), without overriding either limit.

The read-only Discord QA readiness probe failed during Convex lease acquisition before any Discord checks or fixture messages; the QA broker must be available to complete that evidence.

prs.title: fix: avatars and backgrounds fail on Tailscale-authenticated connections
prs.body:
Related: #182689, #188268, #162252

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent/user avatars and saved backgrounds fail to load when a same-origin Control UI connection authenticates through Tailscale but receives a device token rejected by the HTTP image route.

## User Impact

These images use the confirmed Tailscale identity without first presenting an incompatible Bearer credential. Other authentication methods and cross-origin connections retain their existing credential selection. Geolocation retains its ordinary Bearer credentials.

This is a bounded client image-read repair. It does not change server token issuance, revocation, pairing, scopes, rate limits, writes or explicit file-access approvals. Wider media/icon loaders remain in the separate #182689 discussion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select image identity before sending the request, never by retrying an HTTP denial under a different identity. Reuse the Gateway owner's current-client/current-hello check and retire pending reads on disconnect/stop. Keep the background loader's profile, revision, cancellation, size and MIME checks.

### Review follow-up

- **Geolocation regression fixed:** the shared connection context now retains separate ordinary and image credential lists. Only image callers select image credentials. The new real geolocation-consumer test fails on the first revision and passes with this split. Its transport fixture calls the production HTTP authentication function, which requires a token for this non-image route.
- **Real image HTTP boundary evidence:** a managed-Tailscale Gateway server fixture serves agent avatars, user avatars and the current person's private background without Bearer. The same routes reject the invalid Bearer, and another profile's private background is denied. Only the external Tailscale whois response and image normalization are fixture-controlled, not the authorization decision.
- **Retirement evidence:** the actual registered background route withholds private bytes after role reduction or profile reassignment, for both managed Tailscale and trusted proxy. Existing actual avatar authority tests also cover role/alias changes before bytes are returned. No server permission broadening was added.
- **Owner decision still open:** this evidence supports the bounded selection, but does not grant the requested human authentication-owner approval or establish that a changed HTTP principal is the same identity as an earlier WebSocket hello. Review of the intended preselection/reassignment contract remains required.

## Evidence

Current repair head: `fc379be4db71ef198474964d63e0e8571530941e`.

- Refreshed onto upstream `826999cd5`. It includes the core test-type fix and missing upstream test allocation. The former was classified as pre-existing by the failed-check tool. This branch's allocation covers only its own 358 net TypeScript test lines.
- Original real-loader and production-bundled Chromium red/green evidence remains valid for the original failure. The first-revision geolocation regression independently reproduces (1 failed / 5 passed), then passes after the credential split.
- **254 focused tests passed across 11 files:** the final changed/affected UI and registered-background selection is 154/154, plus 100/100 in the actual avatar, agent-response and HTTP authentication suites. No full-repository test run is claimed.
- Targeted type-aware lint, UI production types, UI app/component and gateway-root test types, formatting, whitespace, the exact-base test-line ratchet and UI production build passed. Tested and publishing diffs match (`18b90d09596fc74a5bf913dd9bf788a8dcde036abbda86abff9449f2a2009c85`).
- The final production-bundled Chromium regression passed: one image request without Authorization and a decoded rendered image. This intercepts the network response, so it complements rather than replaces the separate actual HTTP authorization tests.
- Source tests ran on macOS / Node 24.22.1 with isolated synthetic state. The HTTP tests use the production registered routes, profile store and authorization code with a controlled external identity lookup. This is not a live Tailscale daemon/proxy test or native companion acceptance test.
- Direct author review and `pr-simplify` completed. Narrowed the helper name to image authentication and retained the existing connection/cache owners. Whole diff versus refreshed base: production +63/-23, tests +375/-17. No generic post-denial identity fallback or new credential persistence was added. No independent local reviewer is claimed. Current-head CI and human security review remain required.

### Before

The synthetic agent image is rejected and the existing mascot fallback renders.

![Before: mascot fallback instead of the configured synthetic avatar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4d79444-98e9-475a-b2fb-05b040e3fa36)

### After

The same synthetic image renders as a teal avatar. No user photos, real credentials, or production data are present in either capture.

![After: the synthetic teal avatar renders through the confirmed identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6ff49bf-314b-44db-aeed-518252a6c77c)

prs.body:
<!-- Title: fix(templates): failed Template Add preview warns the Add may be partial -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when `openclaw templates add` runs against a Gateway and the preview fails, the CLI says "The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying", although a preview never changes anything.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed preview now reports that no local mutation was attempted, so users retry or fix the Template instead of inspecting state for a partial Add that cannot exist.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI routes Add through the Gateway that owns the state dir and treats any error reply without `details.mutationAccepted: false` as an unknown outcome. `templates.add.plan` is read-only but sent no marker on either failure branch. Both its UNAVAILABLE and its FORBIDDEN (Labs disabled) replies now carry `mutationAccepted: false`, as other read-only owner methods already do. Error codes and messages are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts`: new cases assert the marker on UNAVAILABLE for a ClawHub source error and a generic error; the existing "Labs switched off mid-request" case now also asserts it on FORBIDDEN. They fail on origin/main and pass with the fix.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts src/cli/templates-cli.state-owner.test.ts`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: everything passes except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on origin/main in files this PR does not touch.
- Live run, `openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator` against an isolated Gateway (preview fails on an invalid manifest):

```
before: ... could not complete templates.add.plan ... The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
after:  ... could not complete templates.add.plan ... No local mutation was attempted. Update the Gateway or fix authentication and retry. ...
```

Known gap: the "after" recovery text still suggests updating the Gateway or fixing authentication, which is the CLI's generic owner-refused wording. Changing that text is out of scope here.

prs.title: fix: Memory reports an unavailable provider as awake
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Memory says it is awake when the selected provider reports that it is unavailable or degraded.

## User Impact

User impact: Memory shows the provider’s actual health and explanation instead of a false healthy state. Provider-native engines no longer show an unsupported embedding test or an inferred hybrid-search mode. Refresh still checks the current provider; legacy embedding engines keep their existing controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already returns native provider health separately from legacy embedding readiness. It deliberately skips the embedding probe for native providers. The overview previously ignored the health result and interpreted the skipped probe as no known problem.

This is a presentation correction using the existing payload, not a provider, protocol, search or permissions change. It adds no state or helper. Related: #194982 covers a separate copy/style pass and does not consume provider health.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the built app’s Settings → Memory page on main at 5328b2754d84472b6c6e05fe80c2fc4513fd7e2e, using the real packaged Memory Core fallback view and synthetic native-provider responses. Ready, degraded and unavailable all previously showed “Memory is awake,” inferred hybrid search and an embedding Test that could not check the provider.
- All three native-state regressions failed before the correction. All **40 focused Memory overview/search tests pass**, including legacy embedding checks, disabled engines, no search runtime, failed reads, retry, offline transitions and result presentation.
- **Seven full-app browser cases pass**: three native-health states with refresh-to-ready recovery, plus the existing packaged overview and search flows. The final simplified branch was rechecked with all 40 tests and the three native browser cases. No live provider, embedding request or paid inference was used.
- Source inspection confirms the native Doctor handler returns provider health and intentionally skips legacy embedding probing. The existing browser-safe payload already declares this health field.
- Scoped lint, the actual Memory browser TypeScript graph, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. Broad checks are provided by this PR’s CI. Current-main reconciliation found no intervening changes to the affected owners.

Maintainer validation on `340f51f7ed49`: removed only the new mascot-pose assertion, preserving all health/message/control checks. The overview/search run plus standard canaries passed (575 tests); the final overview run plus canaries passed (562 tests). I18n and formatting passed, and independent static review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Production code is unchanged by the cleanup, so the inspected visual proof below still applies.

### Before

![Before: unavailable native memory is incorrectly shown as awake](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44d0729b-97fd-43ea-b04d-2c1cfae2decd)

### After

![After: Memory shows the unavailable provider and its explanation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a692eac9-6446-4d1b-b744-131ebd6aff77)

Real built components with a synthetic “records” provider and an emulated 1280 × 900 viewport. The existing mascot rerolls its color/accessories on page load; the reading-versus-attention pose reflects the displayed state. No product imagery was replaced for the capture.

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed this audit and the user-facing correction.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/27ab8da9-7856-4f25-9b62-91d8138f1a1c)
