### Summary

The Feishu/Lark WebSocket client (lark-oapi 1.6.8) can wedge **forever** on a half-dead TCP connection — the socket is ESTABLISHED but data stops flowing (e.g. a VPN tunnel flap). The receive loop blocks in `SSL_read` (and the handshake blocks in `SSL_do_handshake`) with **no socket read timeout**, so the SDK's auto-reconnect never fires. The gateway process stays alive and healthy-looking, but the agent is **silently deaf**: no messages in, no errors logged, nothing recovers until an external restart.

This is distinct from the known silent-death issues (#53477, #64712), where the receive loop *exits* and reconnect *fails or is exhausted*. Here the reconnect loop itself is **permanently blocked** by a stalled SSL read: the last log line is "trying to reconnect for the Nth time" and nothing is ever logged again.

### Observed incidents (production, macOS)

Two independent incidents with the same signature:

**Incident A (2026-11-05):** gateway PID 1730 stuck for 16.5h. Last log: reconnect attempt #7 at 21:31:48. `sample` stack: main thread in `SSL_do_handshake → ssl3_read_bytes → BIO_read → sock_read`. `lsof`: one ESTABLISHED TCP to `98.96.213.145:443` (tunnel egress) — TCP connected, but the server hello never arrives.

**Incident B (2026-11-16):** accept-profile gateway PID 1718 stuck for 2 days. Last log: "trying to reconnect for the 1st time" at 21:45:18. `sample` stack: `SSL_read_ex → ssl3_read_bytes → BIO_read → sock_read`. `lsof`: one ESTABLISHED TCP to `98.96.242.53:443` (tunnel egress). Meanwhile the main gateway on the same host was healthy (active message traffic all day) — ruling out a network-wide outage.

Both recovered instantly with a manual `launchctl kickstart` (SIGKILL + restart).

### Root cause

`lark_oapi/ws/client.py` (v1.6.8) has no timeout anywhere in the receive path:

- `_receive_message_loop` (~line 213): `msg = await self._conn.recv()` — `websockets.Connection.recv()` takes no timeout argument. On a half-dead TCP connection this blocks forever in `SSL_read`. The loop never exits, so `_reconnect()` is never reached.
- `_connect` (~line 200): `conn = await websockets.connect(conn_url, **_ws_connect_kwargs())` where `_ws_connect_kwargs()` returns only `{"proxy": None}` — no explicit `open_timeout` (websockets 15's 10s default did not fire for these stalled handshakes; the 16.5h block was observed inside `SSL_do_handshake`).
- `_ping_loop`: a failed ping is only logged as a warning; it does **not** tear down the connection or trigger reconnect. And the receive loop is blocked anyway, so nothing can recover.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Feishu gateway (profile-based or default) behind a VPN/proxy tunnel.
2. Cause a mid-session tunnel flap so the WS TCP connection becomes half-dead (ESTABLISHED, no data flowing). The SDK starts reconnecting.
3. Wait. The log stops at "trying to reconnect for the Nth time"; the process stays up, messages stop arriving, no new errors are logged.

### Expected behavior

A stalled handshake or receive should time out (socket read timeout), tear down the connection, and continue the reconnect loop — or at least surface a state an external supervisor can detect (e.g. emit an error / heartbeat the process state).

### Suggested fix

- Wrap `recv()` with a read timeout (`asyncio.wait_for(conn.recv(), timeout=...)`) in `_receive_message_loop`; treat a timeout as connection death → `_disconnect()` + `_reconnect()`.
- Pass an explicit `open_timeout` to `websockets.connect()` in `_connect`.
- Make consecutive ping failures trigger a disconnect + reconnect instead of only logging.

### Environment

- macOS, Hermes gateway (default and accept profiles)
- lark-oapi 1.6.8, websockets 15.0.1, Python 3.11
- Traffic via Astrill VPN tunnel; half-dead connections observed at tunnel egress IPs

issues.title: [Bug]: Multiplexed gateway: session reset plugin check (doctor + startup warning) runs only in root scope, but pre_gateway_dispatch is dispatched per message profile

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
### Bug Description

In a **multiplexed host gateway**, plugin hooks such as `pre_gateway_dispatch` are dispatched through the plugin manager of the **message's profile** (each routed message runs inside that profile's runtime scope, and `get_plugin_manager()` is cached per resolved `HERMES_HOME`). However, `session_reset_retirement.reset_plugin_enabled()` is only ever evaluated in the **root/host** scope:

- **`hermes doctor`** (`hermes_cli/doctor_config.py` L558-568, `_check_retired_session_reset`) reports `session_reset.mode: both is applied by the session reset plugin` whenever the plugin is enabled on the root profile.
- **Gateway startup** (`gateway/run_startup.py` L966-976, `_start_log_retired_session_reset`) iterates every served profile to collect hits, but calls `reset_plugin_enabled()` **once, in root scope**. If the plugin is enabled on root, the `... is no longer applied` warning is silenced for **all** profiles.

Net effect: if the session reset plugin is installed/enabled only on the root profile (which typically has no messaging adapter of its own in a multiplex setup), the plugin never sees a single inbound message, yet both `hermes doctor` and the startup log say everything is fine. Configured idle/daily resets silently do nothing on the routed profiles.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Multiplexed host gateway serving two profiles:
   - profile **A** = root profile, no messaging adapter;
   - profile **B** = Telegram adapter, `session_reset: {mode: both, idle_minutes: ..., at_hour: ...}` in its `config.yaml`.
2. On the root profile only: `hermes plugins install hermes-session-reset-policy --enable` (the command suggested by the retired-policy notice).
3. `hermes gateway restart`.
4. `hermes doctor` → `session_reset.mode: both is applied by the session reset plugin`. Gateway startup log → no "is no longer applied" warning for profile B.
5. Send a message to profile B's bot after the daily boundary / idle threshold has passed.
6. No reset happens. The plugin's session metadata stamp (`srp_last_user_inbound`) is never written on B's routing entries, i.e. the plugin's `pre_gateway_dispatch` hook never ran for B.

**Workaround (confirms the cause):** also install/enable the plugin on the routed profile (`hermes -p B plugins install hermes-session-reset-policy --enable`) and restart → the hook fires for B's messages and resets work.

### Expected Behavior

Either:

- `reset_plugin_enabled()` is evaluated **per served profile, inside that profile's runtime scope**, in both `hermes doctor` and `_start_log_retired_session_reset`, so a profile whose own plugin set lacks the plugin still gets the "is no longer applied" warning (and doctor does not report it as applied); or
- it is documented (and reflected in the notice text) that hook plugins must be enabled per profile in multiplex mode.

### Actual Behavior

Doctor reports the policy as applied and the startup warning is suppressed for every served profile based solely on the root profile's plugin set, while the routed profiles' plugin managers (the ones that actually receive `pre_gateway_dispatch`) do not have the plugin. Resets silently never happen.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram (the issue is platform-agnostic; it is about multiplex profile scoping)

### Debug Report

Not attached: `hermes debug share` uploads config and logs from a private install. The relevant code paths are cited below; happy to provide sanitized excerpts on request.

### Operating System

macOS (Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.21.6+387.gdce1e9b (2026.9.24), commit `dce1e9b375`

### Root Cause Analysis

Hook dispatch path (per message profile):

- `gateway/run_adapters.py` L1704-1715 `_make_profile_message_handler` → wraps `_handle_message` in `async with ... _async_profile_runtime_scope(profile_home)`.
- `gateway/run_inbound.py` L73-87 `_hm_pre_gateway_dispatch_hook` → `hermes_cli.lifecycle.ainvoke_hook("pre_gateway_dispatch", ...)`.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py` L1878 `ainvoke_hook` → `_delivery_manager()` (L1847) → `get_plugin_manager()` (L1701), which is cached **per resolved home**, so inside B's scope it is B's plugin manager.

Check path (root only):

- `hermes_cli/session_reset_retirement.py` L36 `reset_plugin_enabled()` → `discover_plugins()` + `get_plugin_manager().list_plugins()` — "this process's plugin set", i.e. whatever scope is active at call time.
- `gateway/run_startup.py` L966-976: `hits` is built per served profile via `profiles_to_serve(...)`, but `if hits and not reset_plugin_enabled():` is evaluated once, outside any profile runtime scope.
- `hermes_cli/doctor_config.py` L558-568: same check, root scope only (and only for the active profile's config).

### Proposed Fix

In `_start_log_retired_session_reset`, evaluate the plugin check per hit inside that profile's runtime scope, e.g. (pseudo-code):

```python
for name, home in profiles_to_serve(...):
    found = retired_reset_policy(read_yaml_layers(home))
    if not found:
        continue
    with _profile_runtime_scope(home):
        enabled = reset_plugin_enabled()
    if not enabled:
        logger.warning("Profile %s: %s", name, format_notice(*found))
```

and make the doctor check use the same per-profile evaluation (or at least note when it runs against the root profile of a multiplex host). Alternatively, document that hook plugins are per profile under multiplex and have `format_notice` suggest `hermes -p <profile> plugins install ...`.

Minor, related debugging note: plugin loggers named `hermes.plugins.*` do not match the gateway.log component filter (`hermes_logging.py` L286 uses the prefix `hermes_plugins`), so a plugin's own "armed"/diagnostic lines land only in agent.log, which makes this misconfiguration harder to spot from gateway.log.

issues.title: fix(tools): plain-type coercion fabricates disallowed enum/const members

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Summary

The shared argument-coercion layer (`tools/arg_coercion.py`) coerces a string to a property's
declared type without validating `enum`/`const` membership. On the **plain-type path** this
fabricates disallowed values that reach handlers.

## Reproduction (on `main`)

- `{type: integer, enum: [1, 2, 3]}` + `"5"` → `5` (5 is not a member).
- `{type: boolean, const: false}` + `"true"` → `True` (const permits only `false`).
- Live built-in example: `discord.auto_archive_duration` coerces `"90"` → `90` even where the
  declared enum does not include 90.
- `strip_nullable_unions` / `collapse_const_unions` (in `tools/schema_sanitizer.py`) route
  constrained unions onto the plain-type path, bypassing the union-path guard added in #156337.

## Scope / why this is separate

#156337 guards the **new type-less union path** (bail on `enum`/`const`/composition at both the
branch and the union-node level). The plain-type path's same fabrication is **pre-existing**
(present on `main` before #156337) and repo-wide, so it is split out here to keep the union PR's
regression surface small.

## Proposed fix

Validate membership **after** coercion at the shared entry (plain + union): coerce as today, then
keep the coerced value only if it belongs to the declared `enum`/`const` set, using a type-aware
comparison (so `True` is not treated as `1`); otherwise return the original string. This also
re-enables repair of *valid* members that the presence-based union guard currently leaves
unrepaired (a documented limitation in #156337).

## Acceptance

- Regression tests: plain `type: integer` + `enum` non-member left alone; valid member repaired;
  `const` member; shapes routed through `collapse_const_unions`.
- Range/format keywords (`minimum`/`maximum`/`pattern`/`multipleOf`) remain unfiltered (the handler
  enforces them); parity with current behavior preserved.

Refs #156337, #123345.

issues.title: credential pool: one model entitlement 400 benches a Codex login for a year for model-less callers

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: provider/openai
labels.description: OpenAI / Codex Responses API

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Authentication, OAuth, credential pools

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
Seen on main e96221fa73.

What happens
- A request for another vendor's model id (e.g. `claude-*`) reaches `openai-codex`, for example from a
  `delegation.routing` rule. Codex returns 400 "The '<id>' model is not supported when using Codex with a
  ChatGPT account."
- The classifier maps this to `model_entitlement`. The pool records `model_cooldowns[<id>]` for
  `MODEL_ENTITLEMENT_BENCH_SECONDS` (365 days).
- `model_cooldown_until(entry, None)` counts any active model cooldown as blocking. So `peek()` and
  `_available_entries()` with no model (usage readers, status, diagnostics) see no usable credential
  for a year, until someone runs `hermes auth reset`.

Proposed fix (3 small changes, one commit, rebases clean on main e96221fa73)
1. Do not record a model cooldown when a single-vendor first-party provider gets another vendor's model
   (catalog vendor check).
2. Store the cooldown kind (entitlement or window) with the entry. Model-less lookups skip entitlement
   benches, because a plan property is not a rate window. Calls for that model stay blocked until expiry.
3. Cap window cooldowns (429 / usage-window) at 8 days, so a bogus reset_at cannot bench a login for months.
   The auth.json disk merge takes the kinds from the merge result, so a stale kind cannot outlive its cooldown.

Tests: new tests/agent/test_model_cooldown_scope.py (15 tests). Targeted run on the rebased branch:
70 passed (test_model_cooldown_scope, test_credential_pool, test_fallback_dynamic_credential). Wider run
(credential pool, fallback and auth suites): 105 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (macOS-only).
Docs: user-guide/features/credential-pools.md.

issues.title: [Bug]: A2A inbound requests hang with zero trace after a container stop/start — no response, no audit, no admission, no log line

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Bug Description

After a Docker **container stop/start** (we stop and start the Hermes container around a nightly backup), inbound A2A `message/send` requests are accepted at the TCP level but never answered: the remote peer blocks until its client timeout (150 s). On our side the request leaves **zero trace** — no `gateway.log` line, no `session_admissions` row, no A2A audit row (`~/.hermes/a2a_audit.jsonl`), no conversation file (`a2a_conversations/ctx-*.jsonl`), no task. Other platforms (Telegram) keep working normally in the same state, and outbound `a2a_call` round-trips work. Two incidents on two consecutive container boots:

- An in-container gateway-backend restart heals it (verified after incident 1).
- After incident 2 the path also recovered by itself within a ~19-minute window, without any restart — candidates: a live-session context reset, the first plain user turn, or the first outbound `a2a_call` (outbound alone did **not** heal it in incident 1).

Corroborating signal: runtimes started by a container boot also never write `gateway_heartbeats` rows (details under Actual Behavior), while a runtime started by an in-container backend restart beats every ~30 s until the next container stop. This looks related to the "after a gateway start, wakeups don't fire until a plain user turn" family (#149169) — but plain user turns did not reliably revive A2A inbound here (incident 1: user turns and an outbound A2A turn at 09:18 — inbound still dead at 13:43).

## Steps to Reproduce

Not deterministic on demand yet (we cannot force the broken state), but it reproduced on both of the last two nightly backup cycles on this box:

1. Hermes in Docker, A2A platform enabled (port 9900, `A2A_PEER_TOKENS` + `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS`, REMOTE bind), gateway run by the bundled multiplexer, default profile plus several bot profiles.
2. `docker stop` / `docker start` the container (backup pre/post hooks; the gateway comes up ~10 s later, log shows `A2A: serving Agent Card + JSON-RPC …` and `✓ a2a connected`).
3. From a remote peer, send `message/send` any time within the following ~1–13 h, before any healing event.
4. Observe: TCP connect accepted, no HTTP response, peer times out client-side; our side logs nothing at all.

A fast, side-effect-free probe that distinguishes the state (verified against the code path): an authenticated `message/send` with an **empty text part** and a fresh `contextId`. Healthy → immediate `TASK_STATE_REJECTED / "Empty task — nothing to do."` (0.01 s here; it leaves no audit row, no ctx file and no task, because `_prepare_task` rejects empty text before `security.audit`/`persist_message`). Broken → hangs. We plan to run this probe nightly after the backup window and bring the backend up fresh on failure.

## Expected Behavior

A request that reaches the HTTP listener should either be dispatched or answered with a fast error — auth, rate-limit, trust, method, anti-loop, empty-text and "gateway not ready" all answer fast today. If a post-boot internal state prevents dispatch, the request should fail quickly with a diagnostic instead of hanging silently until the peer's client timeout.

## Actual Behavior

**Incident 1 — 2026-11-15** (container boot 03:01/03:03, v0.23.1):
- 03:03:12 `✓ a2a connected`. Telegram turns fine all morning; 09:18 outbound `a2a_call` round-trip fine.
- 13:43 peer `message/send`: TCP accepted, peer aborts after 150 s. Our side: no log line, no admission row, no audit row, no ctx file for the attempt.
- 14:34 in-container gateway-backend restart → 14:38 peer `message/send` processed normally (18 s turn); heartbeats resumed.

**Incident 2 — 2026-11-16** (container boot 03:01/03:03:56, same version):
- 03:04:07 `✓ a2a connected`.
- 04:56:54 peer `message/send`: TCP accepted, no HTTP error, peer aborts at 150.14 s (`urlopen error timed out`). Our side: hour 04 of `gateway.log` is completely empty; the first `session_admissions` row after boot is a Telegram message at 05:15:16; no audit row, no ctx file.
- 05:15:44 an Agent Card GET answers normally (so accept loop and handler threads were alive by then); 05:17:46 the peer's next `message/send` is processed normally (18.2 s turn) — no restart happened in between.

**Heartbeat rows** (`gateway_heartbeats` in `state.db`): the runtime started 14:34:18 on Nov 15 (in-container restart) beat every ~30 s until the container stopped at 03:00:25 on Nov 16. The runtimes started by the container boots at 03:03 (Nov 15) and 03:03:56 (Nov 16) have **not written a single row** — today's runtime has been up for 3+ hours, processes messages, and still has zero rows. The same absence follows the Nov 13→14 night boots (no row between the 03:00 stop and a 20:40 evening restart). Only an in-container backend restart brings the writer back.

## Code-level narrowing (why the request appears to die before `_prepare_task`)

In `plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py`, `_prepare_task` calls `security.audit("inbound", …)` and `protocol.persist_message(…)` **before** dispatch (`asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(self.handle_message(event), self._loop)`), and every earlier gate answers immediately (401/429/403/method/anti-loop/empty-text, and `self._loop is None or self._message_handler is None` → fast `failed`). Both failed attempts produced neither an audit row nor a ctx file, so they never reached the audit line — they hang somewhere in the HTTP worker path before task creation, with nothing logged. The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`, and a card GET succeeded 20 min after a failed POST and 2 min before a successful POST on the same morning, so the accept loop and handler threads were alive by then.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.1 (upstream 3b421578), Docker install (Unraid), gateway via the bundled multiplexer
- `platforms.a2a` enabled: port 9900, bearer auth, `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` set (REMOTE bind)
- default profile + 5 bot profiles
- peer: another Hermes instance over a WireGuard mesh (Tailscale)
- `hermes doctor` reports a2a healthy; we are on the latest release, so updating cannot change this yet

## Related

#149169 (wakeups dead after a gateway start until a plain user turn — same family for the heartbeat-writer symptom), #147302 (startup-queued A2A requests), #136428 (its notes state: "any A2A task that arrives during startup restore completes empty today — separate pre-existing bug"), #155519 (planned stop silently loses platform inbound, v0.23.1), #155371 / #155688 (restart-lost admissions), #145789 (reply-timeout discards the late reply).

We can provide `py-spy` dumps of the gateway taken inside a dead window (scheduling that tonight), `hermes debug share` output, or any further logs on request.

issues.title: [Feature]: Attach to a Kanban worker session as a normal conversation - read the full transcript and continue the thread

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

labels.name: desktop/sessions
labels.description: Session management in the desktop app: session list and sidebar, creating, switching, resuming, rena

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Attach to a Kanban worker session as a normal conversation — read the full transcript and continue the thread

### Problem or Use Case

Kanban is where the autonomous work happens, but the conversation that does the work is unreachable from the surface that shows the card.

Observed on Hermes Desktop (build 2026-09-22, `hermes-agent` v0.22.2, Windows 11, single default profile, `kanban.auto_decompose: true`, dispatcher-spawned managed workers):

1. The dispatcher spawns a worker that runs in a real Hermes session — persisted in the profile's `state.db` with `source='kanban'`, first user message `work kanban task t_<id>`. Every retry, re-dispatch or re-claim opens a **new** worker session for the same card, so a card that keeps getting respawned accumulates several of them.
2. That session is not reachable as a conversation:
   - it is excluded from the sidebar / project tree (`_PROJECT_TREE_EXCLUDED_SOURCES`; behavior introduced by #75583);
   - the Desktop session picker (Cmd+K / `/resume`) *finds* the row but selecting it loads nothing — no transcript, no error (#85219);
   - the only remaining view is the card drawer, which carries card-level data (description, comments, run history, worker log) and never the agent's message / tool trajectory (#144334, #143004).
3. "Intervening" is a degraded channel at best: the drawer's "Message the running worker…" is `agent.steer()` and only lands after the current tool call returns (#149745); a `kanban_comment` is not seen by the running worker at all (#64447); killing the worker loses the entire run (#148701).

Net effect: when a card behaves unexpectedly, the operator cannot answer the first question — "what did it actually read, and why did it decide that?" — without leaving the UI and reading `hermes kanban log` or the session DB by hand. And there is no way to continue the conversation the agent was already having.

This is the missing half of #85219 (which reports the broken open path) and of #109743 (which makes worker sessions visible at all). Visibility alone is not enough: a visible session that still only loads as a card drawer cannot be read, and cannot be continued.

### Proposed Solution

Treat the worker session as a first-class conversation with explicit *attach* semantics, instead of a private execution record.

Minimum, in layers — each can land independently:

1. **Surface it.** `kanban.show_worker_sessions` (already implemented in #109743) plus titling worker sessions after their card, so two runs of the same card are distinguishable.
2. **Open it from the card.** An "Open session" action on the card / drawer that deep-links into the existing conversation page (`hermes sessions` / Desktop chat). If the row cannot be opened, say why (source excluded, session pruned, belongs to another profile) instead of failing silently.
3. **Transcript in the drawer.** Show the last N messages plus a condensed tool-call trace for the active run, so the common case ("why did it do that?") never requires leaving the board.
4. **Continue the thread.**
   - While the worker is `running`: read-only transcript + steer, with honest delivery semantics in the UI (queued until the current tool batch ends — see #149745).
   - Once the run is terminal (`done` / `blocked` / `crashed`): "Continue in chat" forks the session history into a normal `source='local'` conversation the user can talk to freely. The fork must not re-enter the card lifecycle: no `kanban_complete` / `kanban_block` authority, and the card's `session_id` pointer stays on the original run.

Constraints worth stating explicitly:

- attaching must never grant write authority over the card lifecycle — that stays with the worker, or with the operator via the board;
- no silent transcript replay into a running worker (that is a different feature: resuming a run);
- the attach surface should be opt-in and grouped (a dedicated "Kanban sessions" section, as proposed in #85219) so boards that spawn hundreds of runs do not flood recents (#49991).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Only a full-screen task detail view (#85149)** — fixes information density, but it is still a card-level view: the agent's reasoning and tool trajectory stay invisible, and there is nothing to continue.
- **Only render the worker log in the drawer (#144334, #143004)** — process output is not a conversation: no message boundaries, no tool/result pairing, no follow-up.
- **An external terminal / tmux window per worker (#57552)** — gives visibility, loses everything the session UI already provides (search, copy, resume), platform-specific.
- **Put every worker session back into the sidebar (revert #75583)** — that is exactly what #49991 complains about; the fix has to be opt-in and grouped, not default.

### Feature Type

Other (Desktop UI + session lifecycle)

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Related

#85219 #109743 #85149 #49991 #64447 #149745 #148701 #144334 #143004 #75583

issues.body:
> **Status:** 🟡 fix PR open. **Fixed by #145072.** ✅ **Checked live:** a plugin on the serving host's disk renders in a real browser tab, and a new folder loads within seconds. Follow-ups from its review: #145539 (hot reload, ✅ checked live) and #145549 (desktop halves on a headless host, ✅ checked live).

### Bug Description

The Webapp (the browser-hosted Desktop a gateway serves) loads no desktop plugin from disk, and nothing says so. Plugins in `<root>/desktop-plugins/<id>/plugin.js`, including the desktop half of an agent+desktop package, never appear in a browser tab. Plugins built into the renderer (Radio, hermes-bots) and agent plugins work.

The runtime loader finds disk plugins through the bridge's `desktopPluginsRoot` (`apps/desktop/src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts`, `diskRoots`). Electron provides it (`apps/desktop/electron/fs-ipc.ts`). The browser bridge (`apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-desktop-bridge.ts`, `browser-bridge-stubs.ts`) does not, nor `readPluginSource`. `diskRoots` then returns no root and the scan returns before reading anything.

The fix is in #145072.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Put a desktop plugin at `<root>/desktop-plugins/<id>/plugin.js` on the host that runs the gateway. Any plugin that renders something works, for example a status-bar item.
2. Turn the Webapp on (`webapp.enabled: true`) and open it with `hermes webapp`.
3. Look for the plugin's contribution, or for its row in **Capabilities → Plugins**.

### Expected Behavior

The Webapp loads the desktop plugins installed on the host that serves it, as native Desktop on that host does.

### Actual Behavior

No disk plugin loads and there is no error or row for it. The same plugin loads in native Desktop on that host.

### Affected Component

Other (Webapp: the browser-hosted Desktop served by the gateway)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (not a messaging platform)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not a hermes debug share upload. Reproduced on main daec3cd4c6, Windows 11:
- apps/desktop: npx vitest run src/lib/browser-desktop-plugins.test.ts (from #145072) installs the
  real browser bridge and runs the real loader against a server that serves one plugin. On main:
  "expected undefined to match object { kind: 'disk', status: 'loaded', ... }", nothing loaded.
- tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_desktop_plugins.py: on main the Webapp has no route that serves
  the plugins folder (404).
- Live, with the #145072 build: a plugin in desktop-plugins/ rendered its status-bar item in a
  Webapp tab, and a second plugin folder added while the tab was open loaded within seconds.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

main daec3cd4c6

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Native Desktop reads the plugin folder from its own machine on purpose, never from the backend (#66899). The Webapp has no machine of its own, and its bridge was given no way to reach the folder. The `/api/fs` readers it does have are the wrong ones for this: they follow the profile's SSH workspace, and `read-text` cuts off at 512 KiB, which the loader refuses to evaluate.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

The change in #145072. Webapp-only `/api/desktop-plugins/{root,list,read}` routes serve the server's app-level `desktop-plugins` folder, limited to the folders, `plugin.js` and `.hermes-package.json`, and read whole. The browser bridge gives the existing loader `desktopPluginsRoot`, `readPluginSource` and its folder reads from them. The loader and Electron are unchanged.

What that still leaves out: hot reload of an edited `plugin.js` (the loader's poll picks up new and removed folders, and **⌘K → Reload desktop plugins** reloads edits), copying unified packages' desktop halves on a server where native Desktop never runs, installing and removing plugins from the browser, and `ctx.files`. The planned Webapp Content-Security-Policy (WA-11 in #144705) also needs to allow the loader's `blob:` module imports.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: `sessions repair-profiles --legacy-main rekey` leaves gateway_routing rows and local/API session receipts on `agent:main:`, so profiles folded into the multiplexer lose open sessions and chat continuity

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/slack
labels.description: Slack app adapter

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
Version: hermes-agent 0.23.1 (macOS, launchd). Seven named profiles moved from per-profile gateways into the multiplex host.

What happened
After folding the standalone profiles into the multiplexer, the host refused saved local sessions at boot:

    WARNING gateway.session_local_recovery: Local session local-… receipt refused: ValueError: route mismatch at _checked_entry

Running `hermes sessions repair-profiles --legacy-main rekey --apply` first (all gateways stopped) re-keyed the `sessions` rows from `agent:main:` to `agent:<profile>:` correctly. On the next multiplexed boot local sessions were still refused, and the repair reported nothing left to repair.

Why
The repair re-keys `sessions.session_key` but not:
1. `gateway_routing` rows. The multiplex host loads routing from the default store under scope `<default home>/sessions`, keyed `agent:<profile>:…`. A served profile's rows stay in its own store, keyed `agent:main:…`, so its Slack DMs, threads and API sessions miss and start fresh. The stale rows also linger where `gateway_routing_entry_for_session` (any scope) can still return them.
2. Session receipts in `state_meta` (the `local_policy` half is also reported in #143150; the API binding receipts are affected the same way) (`gateway.local_policy.v1:<sid>`, `gateway.api.binding.v1.<id>`). Their `route` and `entry.session_key` stay `agent:main:…`, and `session_local_recovery._checked_entry` compares `route` against the multiplexed route and refuses the session.

Expected
`--legacy-main rekey` (or `gateway migrate --multiplex` itself) also moves the profile's routing rows into the host index (default store, host scope, `agent:<profile>:` keys, newest row wins) and re-keys `route` / `entry.session_key` in its local and API receipts.

Workaround that worked for us
A one-time re-key, run with every gateway stopped, doing exactly those three things per profile. On a full copy of the live stores and then live: 0 refused sessions at multiplexed boot, and every old chat link resolved to the same session afterwards. The reverse (back to per-profile gateways) also verified with 0 refusals. Happy to share the script.

Also noticed (smaller, separate)
- Under the multiplexer, `/p/<profile>/health/detailed` reads the host's `gateway_state.json`, which records a served profile's adapters only on failure (as `<profile>:<platform>`); successful connects show only in the log. External health checks can't confirm a served profile's Slack is up.
- After the move, the terminal lifecycle guard refuses a whole helper script that both reconnects a sibling profile and (in another branch) restarts the host, so an operator profile loses sibling restarts too. Splitting the host restart into a script run outside the gateway works.
- A plugin that hands work to a fresh thread (`ThreadPoolExecutor().submit(...)`) loses the routed profile's context (the `hermes_constants` home override), so it falls back to the default home. For us `vision_analyze` then failed with "No LLM provider configured for task=vision". Running the work under `contextvars.copy_context().run` fixed it; worth a note for plugin authors or a helper.

issues.title: [Bug]: Sandbox Chromium is never stopped — the stop's identity check fails on Chromium's rewritten /proc cmdline

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/browser
labels.description: Browser automation (CDP, Playwright)

labels.name: backend/docker
labels.description: Docker container execution

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With Bot Desktop placed in the terminal backend's sandbox, the Chromium that `browser_exec` launches inside the sandbox is never stopped. Every stop attempt (idle janitor, per-turn cleanup, gateway shutdown) is skipped with:

```
INFO tools.browser_session_sandbox: browser: not signalling sandbox pid 40538: it is gone or no longer the Chromium launched on /home/pn/.hermes/bot-desktop/browser-profile
```

while pid 40538 is alive and is exactly that browser. The browsers then live as long as their container. On a long-lived gateway with persistent sandbox containers they pile up: I found 19 containers each holding a 3–11 day old Chromium (383 chrome processes in total), several tabs burning 20–60% CPU each, which saturated a 4 vCPU host (load average ~20, 15 GB swap) and made outbound message delivery time out.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Terminal backend `docker`, Bot Desktop placed in the sandbox (image `nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop`, Playwright `chromium-1248`).
2. Have the agent use `browser_exec` once.
3. Wait past `browser.inactivity_timeout` (or end the turn / stop the gateway).
4. In the container, `ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep 'chrome --remote-debugging-port'`: the browser is still running, and the agent log has the `not signalling sandbox pid …` line above.

### Expected Behavior

Once the last session on the sandbox browser is torn down, the Chromium Hermes launched there receives SIGTERM, as the lifecycle module documents ("sandbox → SIGTERM inside the sandbox once no other session uses it").

### Actual Behavior

The stop script's identity check exits with `_NOT_OURS_RC`, no signal is sent, and the browser keeps running until the container is removed.

### Root Cause Analysis

`_STOP_SCRIPT` in `tools/browser_session_sandbox.py` proves the pid is still the launched browser by reading `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` as NUL-separated arguments and requiring one of them to equal the exact `--user-data-dir=<dir>` token:

```bash
while IFS= read -r -d "" a; do [ "$a" = "$3" ] && ok=1; done < /proc/"$p"/cmdline
```

Chromium on Linux rewrites its process title, which leaves `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` as **one space-joined string**, not NUL-separated arguments. Measured on the live browser from the log line above:

```text
bytes=396 nuls=1
args_read=1
arg1=[/opt/playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome --remote-debugging-port=0 --user-data-dir=/home/pn/.hermes/bot-desktop/browser-profile --no-first-run …]
```

So the loop reads a single "argument" (the whole command line), the exact-token comparison never matches, and the stop is always refused for a real Chromium. The pid and the start time recorded at launch are correct (the start-time check passes); only the argv check fails.

The host launcher does not have this problem because it reads the argv through `psutil.Process.cmdline()`, which splits a single-argument cmdline on spaces for exactly this case.

`tests/tools/test_browser_sandbox_stop_identity.py` passes because its stand-in Chromium is a Python script whose `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` keeps its NUL separators.

Running the released stop script against the live browser with the final `kill` replaced by an `echo` gives exit 4 (`_NOT_OURS_RC`); the same script with a single-argument cmdline matched on the space-delimited token gives exit 0, and still exits 4 for a pid that is not the browser.

### Proposed Fix

In `_STOP_SCRIPT`, when the cmdline reads back as a single argument, match the `--user-data-dir=` token as a space-delimited word of that string. The pid + start-time check stays as it is, so a reused pid is still never signalled. PR to follow, with a regression test whose stand-in rewrites its argv block the way Chromium does.

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 host, Docker terminal backend, sandbox image `nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop`
- Hermes: v0.23.1 (`tools/browser_session_sandbox.py` is unchanged on `main` at e96221fa73)
- Python: 3.14

prs.title: fix(tools): tell the model a spilled skill_view preview is missing rules, with a section outline (salvage #151416)
prs.body:
When a skill's SKILL.md is close to the 100k cap, the `skill_view` result is too big to stay in context, so Hermes saves it to a file and shows the model only the first 1,500 characters under a generic "this tool result was too large" note. The model then acted as if it had read the whole rulebook. Now the note says **SKILL RULES INCOMPLETE** and lists each `##` section with the line range where it sits in the saved file, so the model knows rules are missing and can read the section it needs.

Fixes #151283. Salvages #151416 by @ree2507: their commit is cherry-picked unchanged, so the authorship stays theirs.

## What #151416 does (kept)
- `RULE_BEARING_TOOLS = {"skill_view"}`: a spilled `skill_view` result gets a "rules incomplete, do not act from the preview" notice in place of the generic one. Every other tool keeps the old text byte for byte.
- Adds a section outline built from the unwrapped text, giving line ranges because `read_file` pages by lines.
- `Full output saved to:` stays in the notice, so `extract_persisted_path` and the stub guard in `agent/tool_guardrails.py` keep working.

## What we changed on top (separate commit)
- **Turn-budget path:** `enforce_turn_budget` spilled every result under the name `__budget_enforcement__`. A `skill_view` result spilled by the per-turn aggregate (several mid-size results in one turn, or a model with a small context window and a scaled budget) therefore still got the generic notice. The tool's own name is now passed through for rule-bearing tools.
- **Trimmed code:** removed the frontmatter name/description scraper (those fields already appear in the preview's `tool-result-metadata` block) and the per-section character counts, and folded the separate builder into `_build_persisted_message`. The `tools/tool_result_storage.py` diff is now +54/−5 lines, down from +84/−3.
- **Trimmed tests:** cut the 8 tests to 2 invariants.
- **Review follow-up (c1d41017a81):** headings inside fenced code are skipped, titles are clipped to 80 chars so the outline stays bounded, and lines are split on `\n` like `read_file` (U+2028 no longer shifts the ranges).

## Design call
Why a warning plus an outline, and not an exemption from spilling: a 100k skill kept inline costs about 25k tokens every time it is viewed, and it would get around the context-scaled per-result budget (#23767) that protects small-window models. With this change context stays bounded (the spilled notice is about 3.1k chars) and the model is told plainly that rules are missing. The write-side cap (`MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS`) is unchanged here; lowering it is a separate decision.

**Prompt/schema delta: 0 tokens.** No tool schema or system-prompt text changes. The new text appears only inside a spilled `skill_view` result.

## Tests
`tests/tools/test_tool_result_storage.py::TestRuleBearingSpill`:
- `test_skill_view_spill_says_rules_incomplete_and_outline_lines_hit_headings`: **red on main**, green on head. It also checks that `terminal` keeps the generic notice, that `extract_persisted_path` still resolves, that each quoted line range starts on its heading and ends on that section's last line, and that the outline stops at 20 sections plus an "N more sections" line.
- `test_turn_budget_spill_keeps_the_skill_rules_notice`: **red on main and red on #151416 alone**, green on head.

Whole file on head: 63 passed. Related suites (30 files: skills, skill_view, tool storage, guardrails, cron, gateway hygiene, ACP): 774 passed. `tests/agent/test_tool_batch_segmentation.py` plus the guardrail tests: 61 passed. `scripts/check --only health`: ok. These runs came from a `git ls-files` copy of the tree under a scratch HOME, because the `.worktrees/` checkout trips the home-I/O guard.

## Live evidence (real `hermes chat -q` turns, scratch HOME, tree pinned with PYTHONPATH, Nous inference, results read back from each run's `state.db`)
The fixture is a 99,444-char SKILL.md (under the 100k write cap) with 47 `##` sections. The last section is a binding rule ("before any write, reply with codeword PINEAPPLE-7731"). The prompt asked the model to call `skill_view prod-ops` once and say what is required before a database write.
- **main @ acdc8f1ba65:** the stored tool result was 2,162 chars: `This tool result was too large (100,190 characters, 97.8 KB)` followed by a 1,435-char preview. Neither the binding rule nor any outline was in context, and nothing said rules were missing.
- **head:** the stored tool result was 3,133 chars and opens with `⚠️ SKILL RULES INCOMPLETE — showing 1,435 of 100,190 characters. / Do NOT act on this skill from the preview` plus `- ## Section 0: routine procedure 0 — lines 24–45` … `… 27 more sections`. The model answered: "The skill content is incomplete in the preview … I cannot answer what must be done before running a database write based on this incomplete result."
- **Control:** a 97k-char skill (result 98,947 chars, under the threshold) went in whole on main, and the model quoted the codeword.

## NOT_COVERED
- Remote-sandbox spill (the `_write_to_sandbox` route) was not driven live. It uses the same `_persisted()` builder, so it gets the same notice.

## Infographic
![Big skill, honest preview](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1ae31/QrLZwsuSDCecx3-Mc7szt_7zuCx8zK.png)

Related open PRs touching the same spill path (not duplicates): #151194 (skill_view dedup entry for a preview-only view) and #151198 (keep the tail of a spilled command result's preview).

prs.title: fix(gateway): exit 75 on missing core dep import under supervision
prs.body:
## Summary

When the live env loses a core dependency — an env swap from an interrupted `hermes update`, or a service started on a stale env — the gateway raises:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to initialize OpenAI client: No module named 'openai'
```

on **every turn** while looking perfectly healthy to systemd. Because `openai` is imported lazily per turn (not at startup), the failure is never a process exit, so the unit's `Restart=always` / `RestartForceExitStatus=75` machinery never fires, and nothing self-heals. Worse, restarts issued *while the env sync is still in flight* come up on the same incomplete env, so a single manual restart often "doesn't take" and has to be repeated.

This makes the import failure fatal under supervision: when `openai` fails to import and `HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD` is set (non-interactive), log the cause and exit with the existing supervised-handoff code `75`. `RestartForceExitStatus=75` restarts within `RestartSec=5`, each fresh start re-resolves the env, and the gateway comes back on its own as soon as the new env is complete — no human intervention needed mid-update.

Foreground/interactive runs (e.g. `hermes chat` in a terminal) keep the normal `ImportError` — no behavior change outside the supervised unit.

## Behavior (verified against a live gateway on Linux)

- Supervised (`HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1`), openai blocked via `sys.modules['openai'] = None`: process exits with code **75**, logs `Core dependency import failed (openai); live env is stale or mid-swap` with traceback, no further execution.
- Unsupervised, same block: normal `ModuleNotFoundError` propagates, exit code 1.
- Healthy env: `import agent.process_bootstrap; _load_openai_cls()` resolves `OpenAI` unchanged.

## Notes

- Reuses the exit code the unit already special-cases (`RestartForceExitStatus=75` / `SuccessExitStatus=75`), so no unit-file change is required.
- The `sys.flags.interactive` guard keeps interactive REPLs from being killed mid-session even if the env var leaks into one.

Fixes the recurring "gateway up but every turn fails with `No module named 'openai'` after update/reboot" class of incidents.

prs.title: fix(kanban): reject whitespace-only summary/result in kanban_complete
prs.body:
`_handle_complete` gated on `summary or result`, a truthiness check. A whitespace-only string like `"   "` or `"\t\n  "` is truthy in Python, so it slipped past the guard and completed the task with an effectively empty handoff — the check exists to require real content, not just a non-empty string.

This fix strips both fields before the truthiness test so whitespace-only input is rejected the same as an empty string, while a normal non-blank value (even with incidental leading/trailing whitespace) still succeeds.

Scope (2 files):
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`
- `tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py`

Tests:
- Red (before fix): 2 failed, 1 passed
- Green (after fix): 3/3 passed
- Mutation testing: guard mutant killed
- Negative cases: 8/8 passed

Regression note: one flaky failure was observed in an unrelated shared-`basetemp` test race during parallel runs; it is a pre-existing test-infrastructure issue, not caused by this change.

Related: #87569 tracks the same class of gap in the CLI completion path; it is a separate code path and is not fixed by this PR.

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: chore(plugin-catalog): re-pin ctx_checkpoint to 0.13.0
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Re-pins the `ctx_checkpoint` entry (rule 4 SHA bump) from `9f98ff65a51831ca72739c095b134f543e59bc32` (GottZ/ctx v5.29.6, plugin 0.6.2, #147170) to `ebd67053fc9d0c950a008a2c6c38623a25e13414` (tag v5.46.0 on the default branch `root`, plugin 0.13.0). This PR first proposed 0.7.0 to 0.12.0; none of those pins was merged, so the range under review is 0.6.2 → 0.13.0.

The entry changes in four fields:

- `sha` and `version`;
- `requires_hermes`: `">=0.20.4"` → `">=0.23.1"`, the floor `plugin.yaml` declares at the pin (rule 14);
- `description`: the disclosure follows the code (see *Disclosure*).

Capabilities, `docs_url`, maintainer, tier and category stay as they are.

Upstream diff to review: https://github.com/GottZ/ctx/compare/9f98ff65a51831ca72739c095b134f543e59bc32...ebd67053fc9d0c950a008a2c6c38623a25e13414

The range holds 393 commits, most of them in the ctx server. Twelve touch the plugin subdirectory (34 files, +8410/−509); without Markdown and tests that is 12 files, +2668/−350. New files: `config_schema.py` (the Desktop memory form, data only) and `memory/status.py` (connection test, checkpoint outcome, status report). Outside the subdirectory the range changes the ctx workflow `.github/workflows/hermes-ctx-checkpoint.yml`, `README.md`, `integrations/hermes/README.md` (the page `docs_url` points to), `integrations/hermes/scripts/install.sh` and two Go integration tests; none of them is installed.

The full per-version account is the plugin's changelog at the pin: https://github.com/GottZ/ctx/blob/ebd67053fc9d0c950a008a2c6c38623a25e13414/integrations/hermes/plugin/ctx_checkpoint/memory/CHANGELOG.md

## What changed in the plugin

- **0.7.0** (GottZ/ctx#184). Over the default MCP transport, retrieval-only recall (the prefetch before each turn, `ctx_query` without synthesis) calls ctx's `query` tool with `synthesize: false` instead of the lexical `search`; a ctx server older than v5.36.0 refuses those arguments and the plugin falls back to `search`. With the memory layer on, recalled block text (at most 5 rows, 500 characters each, `untrusted` rows labelled or dropped) now reaches the prompt over MCP too.
- **0.8.0** (GottZ/ctx#292). Settings → Memory in Hermes Desktop (`config_schema.py`, `storage=provider`) and six keys under Settings → Plugins. Saving a changed URL or key, and turning the operating mode `compression.checkpoint_required` on, runs Hermes' own MCP probe of the entry; the plugin writes that one compaction key only on an explicit change. Every checkpoint records its outcome in `ctx_state/checkpoint-status.state`; `hermes memory status` and `hermes ctx_checkpoint status` test the connection; failed or skipped checkpoints are named through Hermes' `warning_callback`. `checkpoint_*` values from `ctx.json` apply again. `requires_hermes` `>=0.23.1`: the first release whose `delegate_task` children keep the memory provider under the required mode.
- **0.9.0** (GottZ/ctx#296). Once a checkpoint head is known for the session root, the provider's system prompt block ends with a short pointer to it (head id and title, the read tools, an "untrusted" note), with the memory layer on and off; the outcome file also keeps the head id of each root (at most 512). The compaction receipt gains the same read path.
- **0.10.0** (GottZ/ctx#298). A transcript longer than `max_parts` parts is paced over ctx's 60 s write windows instead of being refused, so the compaction can wait about a minute per further window; a retry of the same transcript reuses the parts already stored; a rate-limited write waits for a free slot, and the second refusal in a row ends the chain, below Hermes' per-server MCP circuit breaker.
- **0.11.0** (GottZ/ctx#300). The redaction of everything stored removes the ctx key on the MCP transport (the key the `mcp_servers` entry signs in with, resolved through Hermes' config and env lookups), runs Hermes' `redact_sensitive_text` in its strict mode, and judges the value behind a credential name by its shape, so code and prose stay and more secret forms are masked. A conversation checkpointed again starts a new chain next to the old one.
- **0.12.0** (GottZ/ctx#302). Under the required mode with the memory layer on, `checkpoint_chain: false` is refused (it used to pass on extracted facts alone) and named at session start and in the status; once the transcript chain is stored, a failed fact no longer fails the checkpoint and is kept as pending for a later compaction; a head that lost `latest_manifest_id` is replaced instead of blocking its root; error texts of chain, fact, mirror and digest stores are redacted before they are raised or logged.
- **0.13.0** (GottZ/ctx#306, closes GottZ/ctx#294, #297, #304). The Desktop form turns the required mode on only after a passing connection test, also on a Hermes that cannot run one. MCP tool names follow Hermes' registration rule, so an entry like `ctx-prod` works; an entry whose tool names another enabled `mcp_servers` entry could also register makes the provider unavailable, naming both. Errors are raised without the unredacted original as `__context__`, and the agent tools redact error text and code in the tool result and the log.
- **Tests shipped in the plugin directory** (GottZ/ctx#305, #306): new test files, a shared answer fixture (`memory/tests/mcp_answers.json`, ctx MCP answer templates, no credential) and the end-to-end driver `tests/e2e_real_ctx.py`, which is no pytest module and runs only when started explicitly (see *Network*).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

The merged 0.6.2 description said "the plugin never writes compaction settings" and "secrets redacted twice"; both are no longer true, so the description changes. Its new clauses: the connection test on setup and status; the write of `compression.checkpoint_required` only on a change of the operating mode, "turning it on needs a passing connection test; otherwise nothing is written"; what the redaction masks and what passes ("the ctx key the server entry signs in with and credentials in known shapes are masked, while unnamed values, plain-word passwords, card numbers and IBANs pass"); the reading of the entry's key for masking; "of the other mcp_servers entries it reads only the names and enabled flags, to refuse one whose tool names would collide with its own"; the outcome file with up to 512 head ids; the pointer in the system prompt; and the full list of core modules. Item by item at 0.13.0:

- **Network.** No new host. The plugin talks only to the ctx server named in `mcp_servers`: through Hermes' MCP dispatch, or through its own REST client with `transport: rest` (which redacts its key from every error text it produces and follows no HTTP redirect). New since 0.6.2 is the connection test: Hermes' probe (the function behind `hermes mcp test`) opens a short connection to that same entry, only from the Desktop form, the terminal setup and the two status commands. There the entry under test carries the URL and key being saved, inlined as a Bearer header; that candidate entry is never written. The entry setup writes keeps the `${CTX_API_KEY}` reference, or the entry's own auth. For a `command` (stdio) entry the probe starts the entry's command, as `hermes mcp test` does (read, not run). Nothing on the session or compaction path tests a connection: `is_available()` reads config only. The pointer is read from the local outcome file; key resolution and the collision check read config only. The chain calls `search`, `get` and `store` on the entry (plus one `get` of a manifest when a retry meets its own transcript).
  - The compaction can take longer: a transcript above `max_parts` parts (default 80 per 60 s window) is written over several windows, and the compaction waits for it in both modes. Hermes runs `on_pre_compress` inside the in-agent compaction worker under a progress-aware idle window of 300 s by default (`agent/conversation_compression.py:1170`, `:3771`; `agent/conversation_compression_deadline.py:20`). At the default `budget_s` (60) and `max_parts`, a chain of 327 parts or more has a deadline beyond that window; Hermes then detaches the worker and retries the compaction once, while the first chain can still be writing; the retry meets the same titles. Read, not run.
  - The installed `tests/e2e_real_ctx.py` connects to the URL in `CTX_E2E_URL` when someone runs it. On import it only defines constants and functions, `main()` sits behind `if __name__ == "__main__"`, and it stops unless `CTX_E2E_URL`, `CTX_E2E_KEY` and `HERMES_REPO` are set; nothing in Hermes or the plugin starts it, and `__init__.py` imports nothing under `tests/`.
- **Files.**
  - `HERMES_HOME/ctx_state/checkpoint-status.state` and `checkpoint-status.lock`, mode 0600, in every mode. The JSON file is replaced atomically and holds no transcript text: the last outcome (time, mode, session kind, head id, part count, a redacted error of at most 300 characters or a skip reason), the last failure, and `heads` (root session id, head id, binding digest and time for the 512 roots checkpointed last; measured at 0.9.0: 94,233 bytes with 512 roots of Hermes' longest id form; its layout is unchanged since). The `ctx_state` pruning (30 days) removes only `*.json` and temporary ledger or digest files, so these two stay.
  - With the memory layer on, as at 0.6.2: small ledger and digest state files in the same directory; the fact ledger (`ctx_state/<root>.json`) also keeps `pending` dedupe keys, capped like `keys`.
  - `state.db` is read read-only in every mode (the compression-lineage root is resolved there; 0.6.2 already did this, the old text said "with the memory layer" only).
  - No other file: after the probes in *How to Test* step 3, `ctx_state` held the two outcome files plus ledger files of the memory-layer cases.
- **Config writes.** All through Hermes' `save_config(..., merge_existing=True)`; a package-managed install refuses them with `ConfigReadOnlyError`.
  - `mcp_servers.<name>` and `memory.ctx_checkpoint` (setup; an engine key that already stands next to its plugin key gets the form's value too); `memory.provider` from terminal setup only.
  - `compression.checkpoint_required`, only on an explicit change of the operating mode. Turning it on needs a passing connection test: the terminal setup offers the mode only after one, and the Desktop form refuses the save and writes nothing when the test fails or cannot run (`ok: None`, a Hermes whose `_probe_single_server` is missing or has no `connect_timeout` parameter; on this tree and at v0.23.1 it exists with that parameter). The web dashboard's form leaves the mode out.
  - Compaction thresholds: never written.
  - `plugins.entries.ctx_checkpoint.settings`: written by Hermes' own Plugins form, read by the plugin.
- **Credentials.**
  - Terminal setup stores the key with Hermes' `save_env_value` as `CTX_API_KEY`; for the Desktop and dashboard forms Hermes saves the secret field to `.env` after the provider's write returns.
  - The status report and a failed checkpoint read `CTX_API_KEY` through `hermes_cli.config.get_env_value` (scope-aware), only to redact it.
  - On every connect, in both transports, the plugin reads the key its `mcp_servers` entry signs in with: the `Authorization` / `X-Context-Key` header values from `config.yaml` (as written and as Hermes loads it), and the `${VAR}` / `${env:VAR}` they reference through `get_env_value` (secret scope, then the profile's `.env`). No other header, no `.env` read of its own, no Hermes function beyond `read_user_config_raw`, `load_config` and `get_env_value`. Values under 8 characters are not bound. The values stay on the provider instance (at most 16 earlier ones kept after a rebinding), are not in the `repr()` of the provider or chain writer, and are used only as the strings the redaction replaces (the metadata names the pass `bound-ctx-key`, never a value). An entry that signs in with `auth` (OAuth) or runs a `command` has no key to resolve.
  - Of the other `mcp_servers` entries the plugin reads only the names and the `enabled` field, for the collision check (`colliding_servers()`, `memory/mcp_client.py:153-175`).
  - With `transport: mcp` the plugin holds no credential of its own; Hermes' dispatch signs the calls in.
- **Redaction of what is stored.** Parts, mirror, facts and digests pass through the same `redact_text()` with the bound keys: Hermes' `redact_sensitive_text(force=True, redact_url_credentials=True)` (present at v0.22.0, v0.23.0, v0.23.1 and on `main`; it also masks every URL parameter named `key`, `code`, `session` or `auth`), then the plugin's rules, which judge the value behind a credential name by its shape. The part header says "credentials in a known shape, and this profile's ctx key where its server entry names it, are masked as [REDACTED]". Known limits (named in the plugin README): a credential without a name (so also the key of an `auth` or `command` entry), a plain-word password, a letters-only value with word shape, a value in prose without a digit, a value the name does not directly precede, a mixed-case `Pin`, a markdown table cell, card numbers and IBANs pass; Hermes' own pass still rewrites some code lines (`api_key: Optional[str] = None` → `api_key: *** = None`). Parts stored by older versions are not rewritten.
- **Error texts.** Errors the plugin raises or logs and the agent tools' results are redacted with the bound keys and the rules, raised without the original as `__cause__` or `__context__`; DEBUG lines carry a redacted traceback instead of `exc_info`. ## Notes for the reviewer

- **`requires_hermes` moves to `">=0.23.1"`**, the current release, with the same floor in `plugin.yaml`. An install by catalog name refuses on an older Hermes; per rule 14, `hermes plugins update` keeps an installed copy at its current pin until Hermes is updated.
- **Writing `compression.checkpoint_required`.** The plugin still leaves the compaction thresholds at Hermes' defaults. This key is not a threshold: it decides whether compaction may run without the checkpoint this plugin exists for. The plugin offers it only as an explicit choice, turns it on only after a passing connection test, writes it only when the choice changes, and writes only that one key.
- **The pointer in the system prompt** is new for users who never turned the memory layer on: after their first checkpoint the prompt gains about 740 characters per conversation root, ids and tool names only, byte-stable across later compactions of that root.
- **Pacing** trades a refused checkpoint for a longer compaction: above `max_parts` parts the compaction waits about one minute per further window instead of losing the checkpoint. Below that size nothing changes.
- **Reading the entry's key, rule 11.** The plugin reads the value its `mcp_servers` entry signs in with, including a variable that entry references, which it does not declare in `requires_env` or `config_schema`. It reads it only through Hermes' own lookups and never opens `.env` itself; the value only feeds the redaction. Without it, the default MCP transport stored the ctx key whenever a conversation contained it. If you prefer another route, say so.
- **Existing installations:** the stricter redaction gives a conversation checkpointed again a new chain next to the old one; old parts stay as stored. A profile with the required mode, the memory layer and `checkpoint_chain: false` now fails every compaction closed until the setting is removed (session start and status name it). A profile with two entries whose tool names Hermes would merge (`ctx-prod` and `ctx_prod`) loses the provider until one is renamed.
- **The disclosure sentence comes from the review commit `d1d2be3ad0`.** I changed only what the new versions make untrue or incomplete, plus two corrections that already applied at 0.6.2 (`state.db` in every mode; `agent.memory_provider` and `utils` in the import list). Trim or reword as you prefer.
- **Name, tier, ownership:** unchanged; I own the plugin repository (rule 5).

prs.body:
Fixes #155032

### Problem

`hermes gateway install` fails in SSH sessions: `schtasks /Create /XML` rejects the generated task XML with 「帐户名与安全标识间无任何映射完成」 (`(17,8):UserId`). Root cause: `_resolve_task_user()` trusted `USERDOMAIN`, which is `WORKGROUP` over SSH, and `WORKGROUP\\user` maps to no SID. Full repro in the issue.

### Fix

`_resolve_task_user()` now prefers the real logon token reported by `whoami` (new `_whoami_user()` helper; POSIX `whoami` prints a bare name so it safely yields None cross-platform) and only falls back to the previous env-var spelling when `whoami` is unavailable or fails. No behavior change on normal console sessions, where `whoami` returns the same `DOMAIN\\user` the env vars produced.

### Verification

- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_windows.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_runtime_service.py tests/hermes_cli/test_install_cua_driver.py` → 110 passed, 23 skipped (Windows-only skips), including 4 new tests: whoami parsing, bare-name/failure rejection, whoami-beats-env (`WORKGROUP` scenario), and the env fallback ladder (`DOMAIN\\user` → bare user → None).
- Pinned `ruff==0.15.22` via `scripts.code_health.ruff_runner` → All checks passed.
- Live check on an affected workgroup machine over SSH: `USERDOMAIN` overridden to the machine name, `hermes gateway install --force --start-now --start-on-login` → task created, `hermes gateway status` → registered + running. (The live install predates this patch — it used the manual env override; the patch removes the need for it.)
