prs.title: fix(tools): coerce type-less anyOf/oneOf union args
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Repairs the **shared argument-coercion layer** so properties declared as a type-less
`anyOf`/`oneOf` union are coerced like any other schema shape.

`coerce_tool_args()` read only `prop_schema["type"]`. A union without a top-level `type`
— `terminal.notify: anyOf[boolean, array]`, a non-nullable MCP union (e.g. Pydantic
`Union[bool, list[str]]` → `anyOf[boolean, array]`), or a plugin tool registered with a raw
`anyOf` — produced `expected=None` and was skipped at the
`if not expected and not _schema_allows_null(...)` guard. String-typed args therefore
reached handlers uncoerced: a model emitting `notify="true"` got the literal string,
and the terminal handler refused it (`notify must be true/false ...`). This is the
Discord/terminal notification bug reported in #123345, still reproducing on `main`.

The fix derives the union's branch types in the shared layer (`_union_branch_types`),
**desugared to the equivalent `type`-list** so `anyOf[X, Y]` reuses the existing
wrap / null-guard / union-coerce machinery unchanged. This is a class fix (AGENTS.md:
"fix the class, not the instance"), not a terminal-specific special case — it covers every
type-less union property that survives schema normalization (built-in tools, non-nullable
MCP unions, raw plugin schemas).

Conservative by construction — the helper returns `None` (value untouched) when:
- Any branch accepts `string` (`"007"` stays `"007"`, not `7`).
- The union node **or a branch** is constrained by `enum`/`const` (even with a plain type):
  type coercion does not validate members, so coercing could fabricate a disallowed value
  that reaches the handler (e.g. `anyOf[{type:boolean,const:false},{type:array}]` + `"true"`
  must not become `True`).
- The node **or a branch** composes constraints (`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`not`/`if`, or both
  `anyOf` and `oneOf` on the node) — same fabrication class, guarded symmetrically.
- A branch has no plain scalar type (nested type-list, `allOf` wrapper, dangling/cyclic `$ref`).
- `$ref` branches resolve per branch against the parameter root.

A single remaining branch collapses to its scalar (`anyOf[array]` wraps a bare string like
`type: array`); `anyOf[array, null]` stays a list and does **not** wrap, exactly like
`type: [array, null]`.

**Deliberate guard boundary:** only membership (`enum`/`const`) and composition stop coercion.
Range/format keywords (`minimum`/`maximum`/`pattern`/`multipleOf`/`minLength`…) do **not** —
parity with the plain-type path, which also coerces through them and leaves enforcement to the
handler. A known cost of the presence-based guard: a *valid* member of a constrained union is
left unrepaired too (`"2"` stays `"2"` for `enum:[1,2,3]`). Validating membership after coercion,
and the **pre-existing** plain-type path's same fabrication, are tracked in #156378 (not here).

It also parses integer literals with `int()` directly instead of round-tripping through
`float`, so large integers (Discord snowflakes, Telegram ids) keep full precision
(`"1550136568038035536"` no longer corrupts to `1550136568038035456`). This guards integer
branches newly coerced via type-less unions and fixes a pre-existing precision loss for
plain `type: integer` (which already corrupted large ids on `main`). Nullable MCP
`Optional[X]` unions are collapsed to `{type: X, nullable: true}` by
`_normalize_mcp_input_schema` before registration, so they already coerce as a plain type
and are unaffected by the union change.

**Supersedes #123356 and #137623** (see Credit). No `terminal_tool.py` changes — the
handler already does the right thing once its args are coerced.

## Related Issue

Fixes #123345

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/arg_coercion.py`:
  - New `_union_branch_types(schema, root_schema)` helper; wired into the coercion loop
    (`expected = prop_schema.get("type") or _union_branch_types(prop_schema, parameters)`).
    Symmetric node-level and branch-level guards bail on `enum`/`const`/composition; `$ref`
    resolved per branch; string-union and non-plain-type branches left alone; single branch
    collapses to scalar; canonical type ordering.
  - `_coerce_number()` parses integer literals with `int()` first (exact precision beyond
    2**53); float path retained for non-literal/decimal forms.
- `tests/tools/test_arg_coercion_union.py` (new, 43 tests): dispatch-level contract for
  `terminal.notify` through the real `handle_function_call` → `coerce_tool_args` →
  terminal handler (executor stubbed, no command spawned), plus class invariants
  ($ref/cyclic/dangling, string-union, typed enum/const at branch and node, composition at
  branch and node incl. `if`/`then`, $ref→const, valid-member pin, range/type-list parity,
  non-nullable union, nullable desugar, single-branch, oneOf, snowflake precision for
  integer/number/plain).

## How to Test

Canonical runner (CI parity), from a checkout of this branch:

```bash
# 1. Red on the base: revert the fix, the coercion tests fail (14 failed, 29 passed)
git checkout origin/main -- tools/arg_coercion.py
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_arg_coercion_union.py -q
#    -> background notify "true"/"false"/'["ready"]', foreground notify "false" no-op,
#       $ref branches, range parity, nullable integer, single-branch wrap, oneOf,
#       snowflake (integer/number/plain), nullable list  == 14 FAILED on main
#    (the constraint/parity pins pass on base: main skips the union, value stays intact)

# 2. Green with the fix
git checkout HEAD -- tools/arg_coercion.py
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_arg_coercion_union.py -q     # 43 passed
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_tool_arg_coercion.py tests/tools/test_arg_validation.py -q  # no regression (72 total)

# 3. Blocking checks
just check                                  # == python scripts/check : 19 checks ok
python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --diff origin/main        # 0 footguns
```

Manual reproduction of the reported bug (real registered terminal schema):

```python
import tools.terminal_tool                      # registers the real schema
from tools.arg_coercion import coerce_tool_args
coerce_tool_args("terminal", {"command": "echo hi", "background": True, "notify": "true"})["notify"]
# main: 'true' (str)  ->  this PR: True (bool)
```

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(tools): ...`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (see Credit — this supersedes #123356 / #137623)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (arg_coercion.py + its tests; no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run the canonical test runner (`scripts/run_tests.sh`, equivalent to `just test`) on the changed code; passes
- [x] `just check` passes (`python scripts/check`: 19 checks ok)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (43 tests; 14 proven red on the base; 6/6 mutants killed)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu Linux (kernel 7.0, Python 3.14)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] N/A — no config keys added/changed (`cli-config.yaml.example` untouched)
- [x] N/A — no architecture/workflow change (`CONTRIBUTING.md`/`AGENTS.md` untouched)
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — `check-windows-footguns.py --diff origin/main`: 0 footguns; pure-Python coercion, no platform syscalls
- [x] N/A — no tool description/schema change (the `notify` schema is unchanged; only coercion of its values)

## Credit

This consolidates the community effort around #123345 (the salvage wave #130139):

- **@webtecnica (#123356)** — the wave's A/B-verified carrier (PASS 10/10), closed by its
  author. This PR carries the same class fix forward on fresh `main` with a `$ref`-aware
  helper; the carrier's inline union block informed the approach. Not a cherry-pick (our
  helper resolves `$ref` per branch and desugars to the type-list), so credited here rather
  than via `Co-authored-by` on a verbatim hunk.
- **@kvnloo (Kevin Rajan, fork PR #155)** — the dispatch-path regression cases (foreground
  `notify="true"` still refused, unrecognized values fail closed) are adapted to the real
  `handle_function_call` entry point. `Co-authored-by` on the test commit.
- **#130139 (salvage wave)** — the A/B contract and consolidation methodology.

Supersedes #123356 (closed carrier) and #137623 (our earlier PR, stale base). #123448
(instance-level, fails the foreground `notify="false"` no-op case) and #123389 are
left to the wave's disposition; this PR does not close others' PRs.

## Behavior notes / scope (for reviewers)

- **One boolean truth table.** `_coerce_boolean` accepts `true`/`false` (case-insensitive,
  stripped) only. `"1"`, `"yes"`, `"on"`, `"maybe"` are **not** booleans and fail closed
  (the handler refuses them). We deliberately do not widen the vocabulary to shell-ish
  tokens — that would change every boolean param in the registry and give `notify` a
  different truth table than its neighbour `background`.
- **Constraint guard (addresses Copilot review).** A union node or branch carrying
  `enum`/`const` or composition (`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`not`/`if`) is left uncoerced: type
  coercion validates neither members nor composed constraints, so coercing could fabricate a
  disallowed value. The guard is symmetric (node and branch). Range/format keywords are
  intentionally **not** filtered (parity with the plain path; the handler enforces them).
- **Blast radius (measured).** Sweep of all 68 registered built-in tool schemas: exactly
  **one** top-level type-less union property changes — `terminal.notify`
  (`anyOf[boolean, array]`). `spotify_playback.state` (`oneOf[string, boolean]`) is left
  alone by the string rule. The broader effect is on non-nullable MCP unions and plugin tools
  with raw `anyOf`. Nullable MCP `Optional[X]` is normalized to a plain type before coercion
  (already coerced on `main`); synthetic fixtures cover the union branches that survive.
- **Pre-existing, not touched here (one PR = one fix):**
  - The plain-type path's `enum`/`const` fabrication (e.g. `discord.auto_archive_duration`,
    and shapes routed by `collapse_const_unions`) is pre-existing and repo-wide → **#156378**.
  - `type: ["string", "integer"]` already reinterprets `"007"` → `7` on `main`. The
    conservative string rule applies only to the new `anyOf`/`oneOf` path; that asymmetry
    is pre-existing and deliberately left unchanged.
  - `terminal_approval_batch.py` compares a pre-coercion args snapshot against
    post-coercion args; coercing `notify` joins `background` in that pre-existing mismatch
    (desktop, ≥2 terminal calls in one batch). Declared pre-existing; follow-up, not patched here.
  - Native-container normalization under unions (the `:72` guard) is left as-is: irrelevant
    to `notify` (items are strings) and changing it would also alter `type`-list behavior.
- **Related, not fixed here:** #109115 (Vertex/Gemini rejects the `anyOf` *schema* with a
  400 — a provider schema-sanitization layer, different root cause); #142509 / #142642
  (`watch_patterns` substring semantics); #141138 (`notify_on_complete` not declared in the
  terminal schema). #23213 (MCP double-encoding) is related; this class fix may help but is
  not claimed to fix it without a dedicated test.

## Screenshots / Logs

Red on base → green with fix (canonical runner):

```
# base (origin/main, fix reverted):
=== Summary: 1 files, 29 tests passed, 14 failed ===
FAILED ...TestNotifyDispatchContract::test_background_notify_true_string_notifies_on_exit
FAILED ...TestNotifyDispatchContract::test_background_notify_false_string_stays_silent
FAILED ...TestNotifyDispatchContract::test_background_notify_json_array_string_becomes_watch_patterns
FAILED ...TestNotifyDispatchContract::test_foreground_notify_false_string_is_a_silent_noop
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_ref_branches_resolve_per_branch
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_range_constrained_branch_matches_plain_type
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_non_nullable_union_coerces
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_nullable_integer_union_coerces_and_null_becomes_none
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_pure_single_branch_array_wraps_bare_string
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_oneof_union_coerces
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_nullable_integer_union_preserves_snowflake_precision
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_nullable_list_union_coerces_json_string
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_plain_integer_preserves_snowflake_precision
FAILED ...TestUnionClassInvariants::test_plain_number_preserves_precision

# with fix:
=== Summary: 1 files, 43 tests passed, 0 failed ===
# regression (existing coercion + arg_validation + new): 72 tests passed, 0 failed
# python scripts/check: 19 checks, ok
# check-windows-footguns.py --diff origin/main: 0 footguns
# git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD: rc=0, no conflict (rebased onto fresh main)
# contributor-email gate: all mapped (author uses GitHub noreply)
```

### Mutation testing (test-quality evidence)

Six targeted mutants of the core fix were each killed by the suite (a surviving mutant would
mean a test gap):

| Mutant | Breaks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | drop the string-union guard (`"007"`→7) | KILLED |
| M2 | skip per-branch `$ref` resolution | KILLED |

prs.title: fix(tools): cap the pre-exec guard wait at 90s, and test the ceiling
prs.body:
fix(tools): cap the pre-exec guard wait at 90s, and memoize only a confirmed identity verdict

The guard deadline had a floor and no ceiling: a long command's own timeout became the
guard's budget, so with a wedged identity probe a 420s command waited 420s before the
refusal — while the refusal itself is identical either way. The ceiling bounds that at 90s.

The root cause of the wedge is the supervised-gateway identity probe, which does real
filesystem and kernel-process work and is called on EVERY terminal command, so each
abandoned guard thread parks in the same `open()`. Memoize it — but **only a confirmed
True**, per `@kvnloo`'s review of the earlier attempt (#151792): the gateway PID file is
written after the process starts and can briefly name the previous pid, so freezing an
early False would answer "not the gateway" for the rest of the process's life and silently
disable the self-kill/ownership guards (#113667). The negative path is still free — the
`_HERMES_GATEWAY` marker test returns before any gateway import — so re-probing it costs
nothing per call, while the positive path (the one that actually did the I/O) is paid once.
A probe that raised is never cached either.

Evidence from `~/.hermes/logs` on 2026-11-16, before the cap was in effect there: 241 guard
refusals (each is logged twice; 362 raw records), 191 of them (79%) longer than 90s — 446
records at 180s, worst 420s — and 661 minutes of dead wall clock. A 420s refusal cannot
happen when `min(guard_timeout, 90)` is live, which is how the cap was confirmed absent
rather than merely ineffective.

Two test files, both two-sided:

- `test_terminal_pre_guard_cap.py` pins the sizing rule, not the constants' existence. With
  the ceiling all five pass; with the ceiling removed — reproducing the code this replaces —
  exactly the three ceiling tests fail and the two floor tests still pass.
- `test_supervised_gateway_verdict_cache.py` is the control for the memo. Against the parent
  commit, `test_transient_false_does_not_freeze_the_verdict` fails with "a cached False
  survived a pid file that now names this process" and `test_unsupervised_launch_is_not_memoized`
  fails on a memoized negative, while the five that pin the positive-path memo pass. With
  this change all 7 pass, and 12 pass together with the cap tests (7.66s).

prs.title: fix(terminal,process-registry): cap the pre-exec guard budget + cache the gateway identity verdict (board #497)
prs.body:
## Supersedes #150829 — rebased onto current `main`, and it carries back the half that was dropped on a wrong premise

#150829 landed only the guard-budget cap. Its sibling #148828 was closed on the claim that `_is_supervised_gateway_process()` "no longer exists on `main`" — it does (still the gate for `gateway_lifecycle_block`, `execute_code`'s pre-exec block, and process ownership), it is still called per tool call, and it still has no memo. So the leak half of board #497 was simply dropped, not fixed. This PR is both halves, rebased onto `8422e54df3` (979 commits ahead of #150829's base), with the missing module-level cache symbol actually declared — the previous attempt would have raised `NameError` on first call, which the new tests catch.

## Symptom (macOS, long-lived supervised gateway)

`sample <gateway-pid>` shows one more parked `deadline-terminal.pre-exec-guard` thread per terminal command that trips the pre-exec guard, never decreasing: 17 → 36 → 140 → 364 across successive observations of the same pid. Every sampled one sits in the same place:

```
Thread_<id>: deadline-terminal.pre-exec-guard
  ... os_open -> open -> __open (libsystem_kernel.dylib)
```

`ps` says 0.1–1% CPU, so it is not a spin — it is a parked thread per event, plus a refused command.

## Cause

1. `_is_supervised_gateway_process()` runs on **every** terminal command (and every `execute_code`, and every process-ownership check). It imports `gateway.restart`/`gateway.status` and does real filesystem + kernel-process work. On macOS one `open()` in that chain can block indefinitely: the guard's deadline worker is abandoned mid-`open()` and stays parked forever. The verdict, meanwhile, is invariant for one process with one environment.
2. The guard's budget is floor-only — `max(plan.effective_timeout, 30s)` — so a wedged probe inherits the *command's* whole timeout. A 600s command spends 600s before failing closed, with the same refusal a 30s detection would have produced.

## Fix

- `tools/process_registry.py` — memoize the verdict on `(os.getpid(), _HERMES_GATEWAY, HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD)`. The `_HERMES_GATEWAY != "1"` early-out is cached too, so non-gateway CLIs do zero I/O. **A probe that raised is never cached**, so a transient failure is retried rather than frozen into a wrong "not the gateway" answer — that answer would silently disable the self-kill guards (#113667). `_reset_supervised_gateway_verdict_cache()` is exposed for tests.
- `tools/terminal_tool.py` — `_PRE_EXEC_GUARD_MAX_TIMEOUT_S = 90`, applied as `min(max(effective_timeout, MIN), MAX)`. The cap budgets only the guard chain; the command keeps its own timeout.

## Verification

```
tests/tools/test_supervised_gateway_verdict_cache.py   5 passed
tests/tools/test_terminal_pre_guard_deadline.py        5 passed
ruff check (3 files)                                   clean
```

New coverage: 25 repeated calls → 1 probe; a changed marker or a verdict cached under a different pid → re-probe; a raising probe → 2 probes (never cached); a 600s command with a wedged probe → refuses in <0.5s instead of 600s.

`tests/tools/test_process_registry.py::TestSystemdCgroupIsolation` shows 11 failures **both with and without this patch** — byte-identical `pytest -q | grep FAILED` output with the diff stashed, so they are pre-existing and unrelated.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Starts the WhatsApp bridge on Windows when the gateway runs inside a job object that forbids breakaway.

A gateway started by the Desktop app, a scheduled task or a service wrapper has no `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK`. `windows_detach_flags()` includes `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`, so `_spawn_bridge_process` fails and keeps failing on every reconnect:

```
ERROR hermes_plugins.platforms__whatsapp.adapter: [Whatsapp] Failed to start bridge: [WinError 5] Access is denied
```

The spawn now retries once without the breakaway bit. That is what the `windows_detach_flags` docstring prescribes and what `gateway_windows._spawn_detached`, `gateway/run_shutdown.py`, `hermes_cli/gateway.py` and `hermes_cli/default_plugins.py` already do. Only `winerror == 5` is retried (errno 5 on Windows is EIO, and a spawn that genuinely failed must keep failing loudly), and the retry logs a warning.

### Why one more PR for this site

This spawn site already has five open PRs: #65990, #87777, #125117, #125531 and #132463. **Every one of them now conflicts with `main`**, they disagree on the exception filter, and #137621 tracks the open choice between them. This PR is the same retry rebased on `main` (fd8a6c41ac), kept to one function and verified against a real job object. The approach is the one #87777 (retry on access denied) and #125531 (winerror-only predicate, warning log) arrived at; thanks to their authors. Once this lands the other five are duplicates of it. `gateway/slash_commands.py::_spawn_detached_update`, the other row listed in #137621, is left to #125117 or a follow-up so this stays reviewable.

## Related Issue

Fixes #68128, #145318, #155492. Part of #137621 (the WhatsApp bridge row).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`: `_spawn_bridge_process` retries once with `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()` when the first spawn fails with winerror 5, keeping `purpose`, stdio, `env` and `umask`.
- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_bridge_breakaway.py`: five unit tests (retry, no retry when breakaway is allowed, other errors are not retried, a second refusal is raised, stdio and umask are kept) and one Windows-only test that reproduces the failure for real.

## How to Test

Unit tests, any OS:

```
python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_bridge_breakaway.py
```

On Windows the last test puts a child process into a job object created without breakaway rights, like the Desktop app's. In it a plain spawn with `windows_detach_flags()` fails with `WinError 5` (the test asserts that, so it proves the job really blocks breakaway), and `_spawn_bridge_process` then starts. All six tests fail on `main` without the change.

Seen in the wild: on Windows 11 with Hermes Desktop v0.23.1, the gateway the Desktop starts logs the error above on every reconnect attempt (every 5 minutes), while the same gateway started outside the Desktop starts the bridge normally.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (it consolidates five, see above)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (one function and its tests)
- [x] I've run the tests for the code I changed: all 27 `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_*.py` files, 228 passed and 15 skipped
- [x] `ruff check` passes on both files. `python scripts/check`: 18 of 19 checks pass and code health reports 0 blocking; `shims` (`.gitattributes` differs from what `generate_shims.py` writes) fails the same way on pristine `main` on Windows, because the generator rewrites the file with CRLF line endings
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docs, config keys, architecture, tool schemas: N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact: the retry keys on `winerror`, which only Windows sets, and `windows_detach_flags()` is 0 elsewhere, so POSIX behaviour is unchanged

Prepared with Claude (Anthropic) and run and verified on Windows by the submitter.

prs.title: fix(execute_code): keep the runtime site-packages out of a cell's child env
prs.body:
Fixes #155952.

**The damage path.** A session kernel inherits the runtime venv's `site-packages` on `PYTHONPATH` so a bare bundled Python can import the generation's dependencies. Everything a cell spawns inherits it too, and pip treats a `site-packages` directory on `PYTHONPATH` as an environment it may uninstall from — so a foreign env's `pip install "pydantic<2.10"` inside a cell can remove the gateway's pin from the runtime venv, and the next gateway start crash-loops.

**What this changes.** Two halves, both small:

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/code_execution_env.py` | `_build_child_env` names the tree it injected: `HERMES_CHILD_STRIP_PYTHONPATH=<runtime site-packages>` |
| `tools/code_kernel.py` (generated runner) | before the first cell runs, drop exactly that entry from `os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]`, and drop `PYTHONHOME` |

**Why the entry stays on the startup path.** The issue's first suggestion is to stop re-injecting it. I did not do that, because the re-injection is what makes a bare bundled Python able to import the generation's packages at all: `sys.path` is built from `PYTHONPATH` at interpreter start, so removing it breaks `import pydantic`/`numpy` in cells, not just in children. The harm the issue describes is not the kernel having the path — it is *children inheriting* it. So the kernel keeps it on `sys.path` and stops handing it onward: same imports, no installable tree in a child's environment.

**Scope, stated rather than implied.** Only the exact tree the launcher injected is removed. An operator's own `PYTHONPATH` entries (a project venv, a user lib dir, the repo root in strict mode) are preserved byte for byte, because those are what `import user_probe` and `import tools.*` in a cell depend on — the existing contract in `tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py` still passes unchanged.

**Tests.** `tests/tools/test_execute_code_child_pythonpath.py`:

- the parent names the directory it injected, and does not name one it did not inject;
- end to end through a real session kernel (`run_code`, strict mode): a cell still imports a module that only exists in that `site-packages`, while `os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]` in the cell and in a subprocess it spawns no longer carries the tree, and the marker itself is not visible to the cell.

RED with either half reverted (only that file reverted, tests unchanged):

```
# kernel-runner half reverted
FAILED test_cell_and_its_children_do_not_inherit_the_runtime_site
# parent half reverted
FAILED test_build_child_env_names_the_runtime_site_path
FAILED test_cell_and_its_children_do_not_inherit_the_runtime_site
```

GREEN: 3 passed. Existing suites unchanged: `tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py` 16 passed.

**What this does not fix, on purpose.** `PYTHONPATH` in strict mode still carries the Hermes repo root so cells can `import tools.*`; if that checkout is an editable install with metadata at its root, a foreign `pip` could still uninstall it from there. Removing the root would break the documented import contract, so it needs a separate decision rather than a silent behaviour change. The per-call (non-kernel) path has the same inheritance question and is not touched here.

prs.title: fix(bot-desktop): identify the launcher by process start marker, not wall clock
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Bot Screen records the launcher as `<pid> <psutil create_time>` and accepts that record only when the
create time still matches within 0.01 s. psutil derives `create_time()` from `/proc/stat` `btime` plus the
process start tick, and `btime` is not a constant: WSL2 re-syncs it repeatedly, and a host does whenever its
clock is corrected. Once `btime` moves, the recorded stamp no longer matches the live process, so Hermes
stops recognising its own screen:

- `status()` reports "installed, not running" and `published_env()` returns `{}` while `Xvnc` is healthy;
- `computer_use` keeps the inherited `DISPLAY=:0` and drives the wrong desktop, and the browser loses the
  bot's own profile;
- `_idle_due()` sees a different identity token on every call, so an abandoned screen never reaches its
  idle stop.

This changes the identity to the kernel's process start marker, which is fixed for the life of the process:
`hermes_cli.web_server_lifecycle._process_start_marker` already returns `linux:<starttime ticks>` on Linux,
`win:<FILETIME>` on Windows, and `ps:<lstart>` elsewhere. New records are written as `<pid> marker:<token>`
and compared by equality; legacy `<pid> <create_time>` records keep the old comparison, so running screens
are unaffected until their next start. `_idle_due()` now compares tokens by equality as well, which restores
the idle stop that the drifting stamp had silently disabled.

## Related Issue

Relates to #128527. It also supersedes #128529, which makes the same change against an older `runtime.py`:
that PR now conflicts with `main`, because `_launcher_identity()` and the `_idle_due()` comparison were added
after it was written, and it only changed `_launcher_pid()`, so the idle-stop path kept the drifting float.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change)

## Changes Made

- `tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py`: `_launcher_identity()` returns `(pid, token)` where the token is an opaque
  incarnation marker for new records and a float create time for legacy ones; `_spawn_and_wait()` writes
  marker records with a create-time fallback so a start never fails on the identity write; `_idle_due()`
  and `stop_if_idle()` compare tokens by equality.
- `tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_runtime.py`: a marker record stays recognised when `_create_time` reports a
  wildly different wall clock, a mismatched marker reads as not running, and a legacy float record still
  matches on create time.
- `tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_idle.py`: `_idle_due()` returns the idle value when the tokens match and
  `None` when they differ.

## How to Test

```
cd hermes-agent
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_runtime.py tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_idle.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_bot_desktop_screen_status.py tests/hermes_cli/test_bot_desktop_screen_stop.py -q
```

On Linux: all pass. On this Windows host: `25 passed, 14 skipped, 4 failed`, and those four are pre-existing
there, failing in `runtime._flocked` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` (Linux-only runtime,
gated by `is_supported_host()`); they fail identically on unmodified `main`.

`python scripts/check` on this branch reports two failing checks that this PR does not touch: `shims` names
`.gitattributes: differs from what scripts/move/generate_shims.py writes` (Windows line endings on this
checkout, file not in this diff), and `health` reports 24 blocking findings against the pinned baseline
`ab84eb7aa0cc`, all in `cron/`, `gateway/`, `tools/registry.py` and `tui_gateway/`. Ruff is clean on the three
files this PR changes and no health finding names a file in it.

Reproduced on a real WSL2 screen: with `btime` moving from `1794676978` to `1794676976` to `1794676962` inside
one minute, `hermes computer-use screen status` said "installed, not running" with `Xvnc` alive at pid 2228,
and `published_env()` returned `{}`. After storing the marker, the same screen is reported running and
`published_env()` keeps returning `DISPLAY=:20` across those `btime` changes, and a one-shot agent turn
captured its own Xfce desktop through `computer_use`.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs/issues to avoid duplicates (#128527, #128529)
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix

prs.title: fix(bot-desktop): bound the launcher's X readiness probes
prs.body:
## What this fixes

`hermes computer-use screen start` fails with

```
Bot Desktop did not publish its display within 15s (see ~/.hermes/bot-desktop/launcher.log)
```

on a host where `Xvnc` is perfectly healthy. `launcher.log` ends right after `created VNC server for screen 0`, with every Xfce banner missing.

## Root cause

The launcher waits for the X server with a probe that has no timeout:

```sh
for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
  xdpyinfo -display "$DISPLAY" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  kill -0 "$XVNC_PID" 2>/dev/null || { echo "Xvnc exited during startup" >&2; exit 1; }
  sleep 0.1
done
```

If that first probe reaches the X socket while `Xvnc` is still coming up, the connection is accepted and never answered, so `xdpyinfo` blocks with no timeout. The launcher never reaches the line that publishes `HERMES_BD_ENV_FILE`, `runtime.start()` hits its 15s deadline, and the screen is reported dead while it is running fine.

Measured on a WSL2 host that loses this race on every start:

- `bash -x launcher.sh` with the `HERMES_BD_*` variables the runtime passes stops dead at `+ xdpyinfo -display :31` and never advances.
- The same `Xvnc` on the same display answers `xdpyinfo` normally one second later, so the server is not the problem.
- With the bound below, that host's start went from a 15s failure to 3s.

The window-manager wait has the same shape (`for _ in $(seq 1 50); do xprop -root _NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK …`), so a hung probe there keeps the panel from ever starting.

## The change

Bound the wait as a whole, not per attempt. A per-attempt timeout is not enough: 100 attempts at 2s each still blows the caller's 15s budget.

- **X readiness:** `READY_BUDGET=$(( SECONDS + 8 ))`, `timeout 1 xdpyinfo` per attempt, `timeout 5` on the final check. Worst case 13s, inside the 15s `start()` allows.
- **Window manager:** `WM_BUDGET=$(( SECONDS + 10 ))` with `timeout 1 xprop`, same deadline break. The env file is already published by then, so this only affects how quickly the desktop becomes usable.
- Same messages, same exit codes, same order of operations; the only new binary is coreutils `timeout`.

`tools/bot_desktop/launcher.sh`: +8 / -4.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_launcher_xvnc.py` already runs the real launcher with stubbed binaries, so the two new tests reuse that harness.

- `test_x_readiness_timeout_bounds_blocking_probe` stubs `xdpyinfo` to sleep 30s and requires a nonzero exit with `Xvnc did not become ready` inside 15s.
- `test_readiness_probes_are_timeout_wrapped` is a static guard: every `xdpyinfo -display` or `xprop -root` probe line must be wrapped in `timeout`, so a later edit cannot quietly reintroduce a blocking probe.

## Verification

- Without the fix, the behavioural test hangs and dies at the subprocess timeout (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` after 20s). With the fix, the module passes in 15.7s.
- `bash -n tools/bot_desktop/launcher.sh` clean.
- `ruff check` clean.
- `tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_runtime.py` has 4 pre-existing failures on a Windows host (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` in `runtime._flocked`), identical on unmodified `main`.

The tests keep the module's existing `platforms("linux")` gate, since the launcher is a Linux script.

prs.title: fix(desktop): decide the ownership reservation with a kernel lock, not mkdir
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`buildSpawnCommand` serialises "one backend per ownership id". Two things were wrong on the real
binary:

1. ownership was decided by `mkdir`'s exit status, and Ubuntu 26.04 ships uutils coreutils
   0.10.0, whose `mkdir` reports a create it lost as a success;
2. the stale-reclaim branch removed the whole reservation with `rm -rf`, so several waiters that
   judged the same dead pid each deleted it ÔÇö and a delete could land after another caller had
   created its record. A live holder lost its record and a second backend spawned.

Both have the same root cause: the mutex is a filesystem object that can outlive its owner or be
taken away from a live one, and every repair in shell needs a compare-and-delete that POSIX does
not have. Earlier revisions of this PR tried two of those repairs (an `O_EXCL` owner record, then an
`ln`-published reclaim marker); the marker one still had the hole this revision removes, because a
delayed waiter's `rm` deletes whatever path holds the marker name, not the marker it judged.

The reservation is one critical section whose whole lifetime is this shell's lifetime: it starts
when the caller decides to spawn and ends when the lockfile is published. So the arbiter is one
kernel lock on one file this code never unlinks, taken with `fcntl.flock` on an inherited
descriptor:

    python3 -c <reservation> "$spawn_lock" "$1" <body> "$lock"

The kernel releases the reservation when all descriptors referring to the locked open-file
description close. The detached backend closes its inherited descriptors; terminating an SSH channel
alone is not proof that every holder has exited. So a dead holder leaves nothing behind: no owner
record, no `pid:nonce` to judge, no ~2 s grace for a record created before it is written, no marker,
no `mv` takeover and no put-back. A waiter either blocks on the lock (bounded at 30 s, then
`EX_TEMPFAIL` 75) or finds the published lockfile and answers `EXISTING` ÔÇö the existing "already
reserved" behaviour, unchanged.

### Why not `flock(1)` or `lockf(1)`

The previous revision shelled out to a CLI and picked one per platform: `flock -x -w 30 9` on Linux,
`lockf -s -t 30 9` on Darwin. Neither can be assumed:

- `flock(1)` is util-linux. It is not POSIX, and a BusyBox build without the applet does not have it.
- Apple's `lockf` in [`shell_cmds-309.120.3`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/shell_cmds/blob/shell_cmds-309.120.3/lockf/lockf.c)
  has **no descriptor mode**. It ends with `if (argc - optind < 2) usage();` and its usage line is
  `lockf [-kns] [-t seconds] file command [arguments]`, so `lockf -s -t 30 9` is a usage error. On
  such a host the Darwin branch could never reserve and every spawn was refused.
- That the payload already runs Python is not by itself an argument that a *different* util exists ÔÇö
  which is why the lock no longer goes through any util at all.

`fcntl.flock` is the same kernel primitive with no CLI in between, and it adds no dependency:
`withRemoteUpdateMutex` wraps *every* spawn in `python3 -c <marker gate>`, so the spawn shell cannot
be reached at all on a host without one. The platform branch is deleted rather than defended: there
is no Darwin path and no Linux path, only one.

## Windows: this payload never runs there

- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` chooses the lifecycle by probed platform:
  `const lifecycle = platform.os === 'Windows' ? connectWindowsRemote : remoteLifecycle.connect`.
- Windows remotes go through `windows-remote-lifecycle.ts`, whose reservation mutex is already a
  kernel object: `[IO.File]::Open(lock, OpenOrCreate, ReadWrite, FileShare.None)` with a bounded
  10 s retry. Same design, different syscall.
- `probeRemotePlatform` (this module) runs `uname -s` and accepts only `Linux`/`Darwin`
  (`SUPPORTED_REMOTE_OS`), so a Windows remote cannot reach `buildSpawnCommand`.
- The suite skips on a **win32 host** only because the payload is executed on the remote POSIX
  shell, not because the remote can be Windows.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue: the mkdir defect is a uutils coreutils 0.10.0 behaviour observed on Ubuntu 26.04
and reproduced locally; the reclaim defect is the same family of "judge then delete" races. Nothing
here names a user-visible symptom beyond "two backends for one ownership id".

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts`
  - New `REMOTE_SPAWN_RESERVATION_PY`: opens `<ownership dir>/.connect.spawn.lock` with
    `O_RDWR|O_CREAT` (never truncating, never unlinking), waits up to 30 s for `LOCK_EX` with
    `LOCK_NB` polls, then `exec`s the reservation body as `sh` with the descriptor still open, so
    the lock lives exactly as long as the spawning shell. The body gets the marker descriptor as
    `$1`, the reservation descriptor as `$2` and the lockfile path as `$3`.
  - The platform branch and both CLI invocations are deleted, along with the `platform` option that
    existed only to choose between them.
  - The owner record, its `pid:nonce`, the unpublished-record grace (`incomplete`/40), the `set -C`
    `O_EXCL` create, the `.reclaim` marker, its hard-link publication, the `mv` takeover, the
    put-back and the `HUP`/`INT`/`TERM` traps are deleted. `mkdir -p` remains only as idempotent
    container creation.
  - The spawn child closes both inherited descriptors (`$1` and `$2`) before `exec`, so the backend
    cannot inherit ÔÇö and therefore extend ÔÇö the reservation.
  - `connectReservationPath` is replaced by `connectSpawnLockPath`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle-spawn.test.ts`
  - **The spawn fixture's payload PATH now contains neither `flock` nor `lockf`.** A payload that
    shelled out to either would exit 75 here instead of reserving; the previous revision does
    exactly that (row 1 below).
  - The lock probe that proves "no second holder while I am inside" is `fcntl.flock` too, so the
    suite tests the exclusion property rather than the presence of a util.
  - Racers run the shipped reservation program with their own critical section (`reservationRacer`),
    so the lock, its 30 s bound and its fail-closed exit are the shipped bytes and only the body is
    the test's.
  - **New deterministic regression** for the reclaim-marker interleaving (see How to Test). It fails
    on `4bbcfec371` and passes here.
  - The `mkdir`-race test is kept as the guard against ever going back to a directory create; it now
    runs the kernel-lock payload.
  - `K callers on one ownership id take the spawn reservation in turn` ÔÇö 8 real callers ├Ś 4 rounds,
    no overlap, and a non-blocking lock probe taken from *inside* each hold must fail.
  - `a holder killed with SIGKILL releases the reservation at once and leaves nothing to reclaim`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts`
  - The composed-payload shape test asserts the `fcntl.flock` reservation call instead of the
    deleted `exec 9>>` opening, and asserts that no `flock`/`lockf` command survives in the payload.
    The file is line-capped by the code-health ratchet, so that edit is net zero lines.

## How to Test

Environment for every line below: Ubuntu 26.04.1, Linux 6.12.114, 4 vCPU / 8 GiB cloud sandbox,
`dash`, python3 3.14.4, `mkdir` uutils coreutils 0.10.0. `/usr/bin/flock` exists in the image, but
the spawn fixture builds a restricted PATH for the *payload*, and that PATH deliberately contains
neither `flock` nor `lockf`.

| revision | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `a5f11a38e3` (previous head) | `npx vitest run --project electron electron/remote-lifecycle-spawn.test.ts -t "returns only the detached child PID"` | **FAIL**, the two `ownership=true` variants ÔÇö `hermes-update-mutex: 1: flock: not found`, then `the spawn reservation is unavailable`, exit **75**. The two `ownership=false` variants pass: they take no reservation. |
| `62412fbde` (this commit) | same | **PASS**, 4/4 variants |
| `a5f11a38e3` | `npx vitest run --project electron electron/remote-lifecycle-spawn.test.ts` with the previous (CLI) fixture | 14 passed |
| `62412fbde` | `npx vitest run --project electron electron/remote-lifecycle-spawn.test.ts` | **14 passed**, exit 0 |
| `62412fbde` | `npx vitest run --project electron electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle-spawn.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle-gate-transport.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle-profile-missing.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle-v2-marker.test.ts electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts` | **156 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0 |
| `62412fbde` | `npx tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `62412fbde` | `npx eslint electron/remote-lifecycle.ts electron/remote-lifecycle-spawn.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts` | exit 0, 0 warnings |
| `62412fbde` | `python scripts/check --base origin/main` | exit 0 ÔÇö 11 checks ok, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory |

Row 1's tree was `a5f11a38e3` plus one line, `export const REMOTE_SPAWN_RESERVATION_PY = ""`, so the
shared test file imports; the line is inert and no behaviour of that revision was edited.

The regression, step by step ÔÇö gates, not sleeps:

1. seed the state the old protocol judged: `<reservation>/owner` = `<dead pid>:<nonce>` and
   `<reservation>/.reclaim` = the same dead pid (a real reaped pid);
2. waiter W reaches its `rm -f .reclaim` and stops there (it has already read the dead pid);
3. reaper R removes the stale marker, wins the `ln` publication of its own marker and stops before
   its `mv`;
4. W's delayed `rm` now runs and deletes R's marker; the test waits for that delete to land;
5. caller L judges the same (still dead) record, its `ln` now succeeds, and it enters the section
   while R is still inside Ôćĺ the `mv` shims record an overlap.

On this commit the marker does not exist: the seeded files are inert, no gate fires, and the three
callers take the one lock in turn ÔÇö same assertions, nothing to overlap.

Exit codes this payload can produce:

| condition | exit |
| --- | --- |
| reservation taken, backend started (`stdout` = child pid) | 0 |
| a live owner's lockfile is present | 0 (`EXISTING`) |
| the lock file cannot be opened | 75 |
| `LOCK_EX` not granted within 30 s | 75 |
| update marker still present after the spawn | 75 |
| lockfile publication (`mv`) failed | 76 |
| `sh` missing at `execvp` | 1 (the marker gate already requires `sh`) |

The full project suite: `npx vitest run --project electron` completed here ÔÇö 372 files, **361
passed, 7 skipped, 4 files failed**, in this 4 vCPU / 8 GiB sandbox. All four failures are missing
host tooling in this container, not this change: `ws` was not installed at the time of the run,
there is no `python` binary on `PATH`, `ruamel.yaml` was absent, and `source-backend.test.ts`
asserts a prepared Python dependency environment. None of the four imports this module. On the
earlier 2 vCPU sandbox the same suite stalled on both revisions with no CPU and no child processes;
**the cause remains undetermined** ÔÇö matching stalls on two revisions are not a diagnosis, and this
run does not establish that vCPU count was the cause.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(scope):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -q` ÔÇö not run: no Python file is touched
- [x] `python scripts/check --base origin/main` passes (exit 0, 11 checks ok)
- [x] I've added tests for my change, and the regression fails on the previous head
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Ubuntu 26.04.1, `dash`, python3 3.14.4). The payload no
      longer depends on a lock CLI, so there is no per-platform command to test separately.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: the reservation is one code path on every POSIX host;
      macOS is **not** executed here (see below)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (the `buildSpawnCommand` comment block and the comments
      next to the reservation describe the lock and the primitive, not the deleted CLIs) ÔÇö no
      user-facing docs mention the reservation
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` ÔÇö N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`AGENTS.md` ÔÇö N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: `exec 9>>` is gone; the descriptor is opened by python and
      inherited by the body shell, which is POSIX
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas ÔÇö N/A

## Notes for review

**Not verified, stated plainly**

- **macOS is not executed.** I have no Mac. What is guaranteed is that no macOS-specific *program*
  runs: there is no `lockf`, no `flock`, no version sniffing. `fcntl.flock` in CPython calls
  `flock(2)` on a platform where `HAVE_FLOCK` is defined (it is on macOS and the BSDs; CPython only
  falls back to emulating it with `fcntl(F_SETLK)` on systems without `flock(2)`). Caught lock-open
  and lock-acquisition errors exit 75 before spawning. Import failures and other uncaught Python
  exceptions may instead exit 1; this review does not establish exclusion semantics on platforms
  using an emulated flock implementation.
- The exact macOS release where `lockf` gained a descriptor mode is **not established**, and is
  deliberately not relied on. Earlier shell_cmds required `file command...`; that is enough to know
  the old branch could not be trusted, and the chosen route needs no version boundary.
- The 30 s timeout path is not exercised (it needs a holder that outlives it).
- A host without `python3` is not exercised, because it cannot reach this code: the marker gate that
  wraps every spawn is already `python3 -c`.
- `flock(2)` semantics on NFS and other network filesystems are unchanged by this PR (the primitive
  is the same as the previous revision, only the caller differs) and are not tested.

**Disclosed limitations (this design)**

- The host needs `python3`, which the spawn path already required. If it is somehow absent, the
  spawn fails closed and no backend starts.
- The lock file is never unlinked. A lock path that is removed and re-created is a new inode, and a
  second exclusive lock on it would succeed while the first holder is still live (#112974). Nothing
  in this code removes it; the ownership directory itself is never removed.
- The wait is bounded at 30 s (the same budget as the 600 ├Ś 50 ms loop it replaces). A holder
  wedged longer than that makes the other callers exit 75 rather than spawn a second backend.
- `SIGKILL` between the spawn and the lockfile publication still orphans a backend, exactly as
  before; this PR changes the reservation, not that window.

**Corrections against the previous revision of this description**

- The Darwin branch is **gone**, not feature-detected. The previous revision claimed
  `flock`/`lockf` was "portable everywhere this shell runs"; `lockf` in
  `shell_cmds-309.120.3` has no descriptor mode, so on older macOS it was a usage error and every
  spawn failed closed with 75. Review found this; the CLI route was removed rather than patched.
- The claim that "the payload already runs Python, so the util is portable" is wrong reasoning and is
  not used. The reason `python3` is admissible here is narrower: the spawn shell is *already*
  unreachable without it.
- The suite-stall sentence is corrected. "Stalled on both revisions in this sandbox" does not
  establish a 2 vCPU limit; the cause remains undetermined, and the suite now completes on a larger
  sandbox with the four tooling failures listed above.
- The Linux-skipped test was **not** pre-existing: commit `43f125c60e` introduced
  `the ownership reservation admits one holder when a mkdir reports a create it lost` in this PR,
  and its racer was written without a mode. Fixing it was fixing my own test, not repairing an
  inherited one.
- The earlier tables (`13/20`, `14/20`, `38/50`, `34-35/50`, `67/400`, `0/400`, `0/40`, the ~33 s
  wedges) came from a throwaway harness that is not in this PR and cannot be re-run from the
  repository. They are removed rather than restated; the table above is everything that is
  reproducible from a clean checkout, with SHAs and commands.
- The mixed-version sentence is **dropped**: an older Desktop build (`mkdir` reservation) and this
  build use different primitives, so on a host where both run they do **not** exclude each other.
  That is a one-time rolling-upgrade window, disclosed here rather than argued away.
- `just check` is not a recipe in this repository; the template's item is `python scripts/check`.
  It was run (exit 0, 11 checks ok).

prs.body:
## What this is

SHA bump for the existing `antemuse` entry: **0.10.44 → 0.11.16**.

| | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| pin | `b19cca81d5a5ff90553e1ad715f042b9a3564a83` | `66173382600525f0dc82d816fb637b7deb91b398` |
| version | 0.10.44 | 0.11.16 |
| commits in range | — | 62 |

One file changed: `plugin-catalog/antemuse.yaml`. `sha`, `version`, the four screenshot/banner URLs, and one added sentence in the description. Tier, category, capabilities and every existing disclosure are unchanged.

## Delta worth reviewing (`b19cca81..66173382`, 62 commits)

Most of the range is release plumbing and test work. The user-visible changes:

- **The cockpit is now a tab of the Antemuse pane**, not a separate surface: `State | Cockpit`, deep-linkable at `/antemuse/cockpit`.
- **`/explore` is flown by hand.** The pane draws the same `GET /graph` payload the map draws; the reticle names the concept under it, the trigger picks, keeps and trashes are recorded, and `tools/hit_rate.py` counts them.
- **Escape hands the mouse back and stays.** Capture is sticky — one click takes the pointer, moving steers with no button held, a `mouse captured · esc frees` badge says so. The drawn `exit · esc` button in the pane's own chrome is the exit. Pointer lock is still requested but nothing depends on it: the packaged host refuses it (`SecurityError` / `WrongDocumentError`), so steering rides ordinary pointer events.
- **Leaving the cockpit files the flight** — the ordered trail plus keeps/trashes is posted as a note (residue for two turns, no turns spent, `active` untouched) and shows in the idle pane as `last flight · N concept(s) · kept K`.
- Walk fixes: the rim is two steps out and a far hop is never a neighbour; a walk stops at its dose; a cursor that names nothing restarts instead of crashing; a state whose conversation is gone ends instead of hanging at "0 hops left". The tool no longer recommends actions that do not exist.
- Packaging: drafts and the working copy are no longer shipped; WordNet is not re-downloaded on every run.

## Surfaces

- Tool: `state` (unchanged capability block — one tool).
- Hooks: `pre_llm_call`, `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, plus the walk/return hooks already declared. No middleware, no required env vars.
- Desktop: two panes — the concept map (now with a Cockpit tab). Terminal gets the same text record; **no terminal takeover** since 0.10.30.

## Disclosures (unchanged, restated)

- Once per session, by default, reads the last 14 days of Hermes session messages **read-only** so a walk steers away from concepts already met (`session_scan` turns it off); it also reads `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` as daydream and dream material.
- `dream` reads commit subjects from the current git repo, or from the repos listed in `dream_projects`.
- `doomscroll` fetches public RSS feeds from fixed news and comedy sites.
- No model calls anywhere on the state path.
- The exploration library (spark, keep, collider, selection) is present but runtime-gated behind `experimental.enabled` and makes no quality claim.

## Known issues (unchanged)

- The picture is the desktop pane only; chat and terminal carry the text record.
- **Windows:** installer and runtime are pure Python (no bash/rsync/symlink needed) and the suite passes on Linux; there is no Windows-specific path, so the pane is expected to work but is still unverified there — mouse capture in particular has not been confirmed on Windows hardware by me.
- The cockpit's flight note needs a gateway that has the `POST /flight` route; on a gateway started before the plugin was installed, the pane records the refusal as `window.__flightPost = {ok:false, detail:"404 …"}` rather than failing silently. It clears on restart.

## Verification at the pin

```
suite (extracted tarball)   574 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed
tools/desktop_harness       exit 0, 12 properties PASS
tools/cockpit_harness.py    35/35 (real Chromium, refuses pointer lock as the app does)
hermes plugins validate .   Validation passed
package                     no bytecode, no local state, no work copy
```

The entry also parses through this repo's own loader: `load_catalog()` returns antemuse at `0.11.16`, 40-char pin, 3 screenshots, image present.

## Screenshots

Pinned to the new commit (all four URLs return 200):

- banner: `docs/screenshots/banner.png`
- `pane-walk.png`, `return-account.png`, `blocked-tool.png`

No self-update in the catalog build: nothing here fetches or replaces its own files. The standalone distribution's installer is a pure-Python file copy.

prs.body:
# Catalog submission: IaC Genius CE (iacg-desk + iacg-board)

Adds two community plugin entries from the public monorepo **RajaRenga/iacgenius-ce**, pinned to
commit `dd897541cf571a25e2ad4a3d717038cf3ea36f60`. Both are part of IaC Genius Community Edition: turn a plain-language infrastructure
request into **validated Terraform/OpenTofu and a reviewable PR**, on Hermes. The model proposes; the
deterministic toolchain decides. Apache-2.0.

## Entries

### `plugin-catalog/iacg-desk.yaml`
- subdir `profiles/iacgenius/plugins/iacg-desk`
- Tools: `iacg_mission` (structured desk access), `iacg_templates` (read-only grounding guidance).
- Hooks: `on_session_start` (mission board snapshot), `pre_tool_call` (the hard apply/cloud-write boundary).
- No middleware. No core override.

### `plugin-catalog/iacg-board.yaml`
- subdir `profiles/iacgenius/dashboard-plugins/iacg-board`
- A web dashboard tab (`/iacg-board`) rendering the desk's mission board snapshot. Registers no agent
  tools/hooks/middleware. The committed `dashboard/dist/index.js` is readable, non-minified React built
  from the dashboard source (no build step at install), inside the dashboard SDK surface.

## Rule-13 disclosure (full)

**iacg-desk**
- Talks to a local Unix socket (`/run/iacg/desk.sock`) served by the `iacg_desk` desk service; falls back
  to `python -m iacg_desk` as a subprocess when no socket is configured.
- Reads its own `local.json` (gitignored) + `IACG_*` env for socket path / data dir / interpreter — config
  paths, not secrets. Reads no credential store.
- The desk service runs the validation toolchain: `terraform init` fetches providers read-only from the
  public registry into a shared cache; `tflint`/`checkov` run locally; the secret scan reads the mission tree.
- Hard-refuses `terraform apply` / `tofu apply` / `destroy` and cloud write commands (`aws`/`gcloud`/`az`/
  `kubectl` writes) at `pre_tool_call`. Holds no cloud credentials; never changes cloud state.
- GitHub delivery uses a desk-held token only after the gates pass and a named human approval; reads the
  commit back. No other network writes. No telemetry. No self-update.

**iacg-board**
- Read-only. Reads the desk's `board.json`/`board.html` over the local socket / shared data dir. No network
  calls, no subprocess, stores nothing. Reports only what the desk recorded; empty state until a snapshot exists.

## Platforms
`linux` only — the desk API uses `AF_UNIX` and `/run/iacg`, `/data/iacg` paths. The CLI fallback is portable,
but the service + pinned toolchain deployment target Linux. Declared honestly in both entries.

## Validation
- `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` run inside the pinned image `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.23.1`
  (the native CLI predates the 0.23.1 capability probe). Result: **both PASSED** — manifest,
  `requires_hermes >=0.23.1`, loadable, capability probe (register ran), declared tools/hooks/middleware
  match registrations, no built-in tool collisions, security scan safe, no core override.
- Desk unit suite: 77 passed (decision ledger, intake resolver, build-sheet freeze, validate hard gates +
  secret-scan precision + lock-race retry, workspace package, plugin apply/cloud-write boundary).
- Generation product tested with a repeatable SkillOpt-style loop over 15 complex chained-resource AWS
  requirements (real LLM + real terraform/tflint/checkov): see the repo evidence. Hard gates = correctness;
  checkov soft findings are accept-or-fix-by-name, never auto-passed.

## Screenshots
Banner (1200×600) + a clean mission-board capture committed at the pin under `docs/media/` (synthetic demo
data; no real account ids, ARNs, buckets, tokens or tunnel URLs).

## Notes for the reviewer
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.1"` floor in both manifests and entries (the profile `distribution.yaml` pins
  `==0.23.1` for the standalone Spot/Docker distribution; that `==` is a distribution pin, not the catalog floor).
- No `.pyc`/native binaries in the pinned tree (gitignored). The board `dist/` is reviewable text source.
- The `iacgenius` profile, SOUL and skills registry are the standalone distribution, not catalog entries;
  this PR lists the two plugins only.

prs.title: fix(termux): fall back when os.link does not exist
prs.body:
Android/bionic CPython builds omit `os.link` entirely, so every hard-link publish path fails with `AttributeError` at attribute lookup — not the `OSError` a filesystem without hard links raises. The handlers caught only `OSError`, so the documented exclusive-create fallbacks were dead code on Termux. Confirmed on device: `hasattr(os, "link")` is `False` on Termux Python 3.14.10, both the system interpreter and the APT package venv (`$PREFIX/lib/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python`).

This supersedes #140083 by covering all remaining production sites in one change, including the three that PR does not touch:

| Site | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway/platforms/helpers.py` (`_read_or_create_log_hash_salt`) | `except OSError` | widened — runs on every gateway start |
| `gateway/hosted_room_peer.py` (`_gateway_room_grant_secret_for_home`) | only `FileExistsError` | exclusive-create fallback added (also fixes #141111) |
| `cron/cancellation.py` (`_publish_first`) | `except OSError` | widened |
| `hermes_cli/update_lock.py` (`_publish_exclusive`) | `except OSError` | widened |
| `hermes_cli/update_cmd_zip.py` (`_hardlink_backup`, `_link_or_copy_artifact`) | `except OSError` | widened |
| `hermes_cli/web_routers/local_models.py` (sideload) | `except OSError` | widened |
| `hermes_cli/macos_tcc_anchor.py` (libpython provisioning) | `except OSError` | widened (future-proofing, as suggested) |

Successful hard-link behaviour is untouched: the fallback branches are only reached when `os.link` raises, and the new handler is additive to the existing `OSError` case.

## Tests

Two focused modules, `tests/gateway/test_os_link_unavailable.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_os_link_unavailable.py`, remove `os.link` from the `os` module (monkeypatched, restored afterwards so later tests are unaffected) and call each helper. Per the review note, they assert the fallback **produced the target file with the expected content**, not just that no exception escaped — a handler that swallows the `AttributeError` and does nothing would fail these.

Evidence on a real Termux interpreter that has no `os.link` at all (not just a monkeypatched one), same assertions as the tests:

```
note: this interpreter has no os.link at all - the real Termux condition
FAIL  helpers salt: AttributeError("module 'os' has no attribute 'link'")   # before
...
5 FAILED
```
```
PASS  helpers salt
PASS  room grant secret
PASS  cancel marker
PASS  update lock marker
PASS  zip backup/artifact
all checks passed without os.link                                          # after
```

Also verified in the field: on an APT-package install (hermes-agent 0.23.1, Android 17) the gateway fails to create its log hash salt without this change and starts normally with the widened handler.

Happy to split this if you would rather take #140083 first and rebase the remaining three on top.

prs.title: catalog: deepseek-web-tools 1.0.6 (file input, honest disclosure)
prs.body:
## Why

The catalog entry for `deepseek-web-tools` pins `2402ccd` (`1.0.3`), which is **four releases behind**
the plugin's `main` (`6e639be`, `1.0.6`). Two things are wrong for anyone installing from the catalog
rather than from git:

1. **Missing the file input.** 1.0.4 added a `files` parameter (ask the question over local documents)
   and 1.0.5 is the release that makes it work: documents cannot be inlined in a chat request,
   so each file is uploaded to the DeepSeek Files API (`purpose` per type: `rich_layout_recognition`
   for PDF/Word/PowerPoint, `user_data` for spreadsheets, text and images) and referenced by
   `file_id`. A catalog user on 1.0.3 gets a tool without any of it.
2. **The disclosure no longer matches the code.** The pinned description ends with *"no other network
   host, no shell commands, no files written"*. 1.0.5 uploads documents — whose bytes are kept by the
   vendor, there is no delete call — and writes exactly one local file: a cache of upload ids and
   timestamps (no path, no file name, mode `0600`) used to avoid re-uploading the same document.

`requires_hermes` stays at the low end deliberately: an earlier draft raised it to `>=0.23.0` on the
assumption that the `register_tool` kwargs arrived there, and a real 0.22.2 install proved otherwise
(`PluginContext.register_tool` already takes `check_fn`/`emoji`/`override`, and `get_config` is
present). The entry pins the **oldest version actually verified**, `0.22.2` — 1.0.6 is the release that
corrected the same over-conservative floor in the plugin's own manifest.

## Changes

One file, four keys — nothing else in the entry moves.

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `sha` | `2402ccd6ad2…` | `6e639beac714b57328de2b39035071b2a488b5ec` |
| `version` | `"1.0.3"` | `"1.0.6"` |
| `requires_hermes` | `">=0.22.5"` | `">=0.22.2"` (verified on 0.22.2 and 0.23.1) |
| `description` | …`no files written` | documents uploaded via the Files API and kept by the vendor; one local id cache, `0600`, no path/no file name |

## Verification

- `hermes plugins list` on the maintainer's host: `deepseek-web-tools 1.0.6 enabled`, installed from
  `6e639be` (= the `sha` above).
- **Live acceptance, not unit tests**: a `web_research` call over a real uploaded `.txt` returned the
  token that exists only inside that document (`ZXQ4711`) — endpoint, `purpose` field, `file_id`
  reference and the vendor's parse all exercised in one call. (An earlier iteration of this feature
  passed 58 unit tests and was rejected live with `HTTP 400 file_data only accepts images`; the release
  carries `scripts/live_accept.py --files-probe` so the check is repeatable.)
- `uv run tests/test_client.py` → 66 tests, py3.11 and py3.13 in the repo's own CI (GitHub-hosted
  runners, no key, no network); `hermes plugins validate .` → Validation passed, on a 0.22.2 and a
  0.23.1 host.
- `SECURITY.md` and `README.md` reviewed against the code for claim parity (the cache, the permanence
  of uploads, the credential-path guard, the injection surface of an uploaded document).

Plugin repo: https://github.com/fedebyes/hermes-deepseek-web-tools · release notes in `CHANGELOG.md`.

prs.title: fix(vault): sync Bitwarden on demand so items shared after bw login are fillable
prs.body:
## Summary

The Bitwarden login backend reads `bw`'s local cache, which only `bw sync` refreshes. Hermes never runs it, so a login added or shared into the vault after `bw login` (for example, into a collection the agent's account can see) never reaches `browser_vault` until the user runs `bw sync` by hand.

This PR makes the backend sync on demand: on unlock, on a stale listing, and once on a missing handle. There's no polling and no background thread.

## Changes

`agent/vault_backends/bitwarden.py`

- **Sync on unlock:** runs `bw sync` once right after a successful unlock, using the session token already held in memory.
- **Sync on listing:** `list_items()` syncs when the last successful sync is older than `vault.bitwarden.sync_on_list_seconds` (default `60`). Set it to `0` to turn on-demand sync off.
- **Sync on miss:** `get_meta()` for a handle that isn't in the cache syncs once more (debounced to 5s) and retries.
- **Non-fatal failures:** a failed sync (server offline, timeout) logs a warning and falls back to the cached items. A locked vault still raises `UnlockRequired` as before.
- **Shared sync clock:** the last-sync timestamp lives at module level, keyed by the `bw` binary path, because `enabled_backends()` builds a fresh backend object per call.

### Config

```yaml
vault:
  bitwarden:
    sync_on_list_seconds: 60   # 0 disables on-demand sync
```

## Security

`bw sync` runs through the existing `_run` path, so `BW_SESSION` goes only to that one child process. It never enters Hermes' own environment, argv, or any other child. `test_session_token_reaches_only_the_manager_call_that_uses_it` now asserts this for the sync call too.

## Tests

Six new tests in `tests/agent/test_vault_backends.py`:

- [x] Unlock syncs once and never exposes the master password
- [x] Listings sync at most once per interval
- [x] A stale clock triggers a re-sync
- [x] `sync_on_list_seconds: 0` disables sync
- [x] A missing handle triggers a re-sync and finds the newly shared item
- [x] A failed sync falls back to cached items

```bash
pytest -q tests/agent/test_vault_*.py tests/tools/test_browser_vault*.py
# 117 passed, 2 skipped
ruff check agent/vault_backends/bitwarden.py tests/agent/test_vault_backends.py tests/agent/test_vault_unlock_tokens.py
# All checks passed!
```

## Notes

- Vaultwarden and Bitwarden also offer push notifications, but the CLI doesn't expose them. A long-lived listener felt like more surface than this needs.
- No behavior change for users who never share items after `bw login`, apart from one extra `bw sync` per unlock.

prs.title: Mid-chat model switches now say which model, provider and effort took over (Inspired by Amp, salvage #139137)
prs.body:
After you switch models in the middle of a chat, the chat now records which model took over, through which provider, and at what reasoning effort. Before, every surface showed just "model changed", so in a multi-model setup you had no record of what answered from that point.

**Outcome:** the model-switch notice names the model, provider and effort on Desktop and in the classic CLI's resume recap.

This builds on @liuhao1024's #139137 (cherry-picked with authorship kept; it stamped `{model, provider}` on the switch row and taught Desktop to read it) and widens it the way Amp's new model selector does ("Switched to GPT-6.1 Sol · High").

## What changes

| Surface | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop chat timeline (live switch, then reload) | `model changed` | `model changed to gpt-5-mini via openai-api · high` |
| `hermes --resume` recap (classic CLI) | `model changed` | `model changed: gpt-5-mini (openai-api) · high` |
| Rows written by an older backend | `model changed` | `model changed` (unchanged fallback) |
| What the model sees | marker text | marker text, byte-identical (metadata is display-only) |

- `tui_gateway/server.py::_append_model_switch_marker`: the row's `display_metadata` also carries `effort`: the explicit `--reasoning` level of the pick, else the live agent's current `reasoning_config`.
- `tui_gateway/model_switch.py::_commit_agent_switch`: passes the pick's `--reasoning` level in, because that level is applied after the commit (reading the agent there would record the old effort).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/hydration.ts`: appends ` · <effort>`.
- `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py::_collect_resume_entries`: the resume recap reads the same metadata instead of the bare catalog label.

The Ink TUI shows no switch row in a resumed transcript at all: the gateway's history projection hides every `[System:` row by design (62bfba521d7), so there is nothing for this PR to label there.

Root cause: the switch row's facts lived only in model-facing marker text, which every UI correctly refuses to show.

## Live repro

Real `tui_gateway.entry` process + real OpenAI (`gpt-5-nano` → `/model gpt-5-mini --provider openai-api --reasoning high` via `config.set`, one turn each side), read back from that run's own `state.db`, then the REST projection Desktop loads, the real Desktop `toChatMessages`, and the CLI recap builder:

| | main (`e96221fa73d2`) | head |
|---|---|---|
| `state.db` `messages.display_metadata` (model_switch row) | `NULL` | `{"model": "gpt-5-mini", "provider": "openai-api", "effort": "high"}` |
| Desktop render of the stored transcript | `["system","model changed"]` | `["system","model changed to gpt-5-mini via openai-api · high"]` |
| CLI resume recap event | `model changed` | `model changed: gpt-5-mini (openai-api) · high` |

Cost: 4 nano/mini turns (< $0.01).

## Tests

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_role.py`: the replacing marker carries the explicit effort; the effort falls back to the live agent's reasoning (2 invariant tests, trimmed from #139137's 3).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages.test.ts`: #139137's test, extended to the effort suffix.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_role.py tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_display.py tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py`: 32 passed, 0 failed. Desktop vitest `chat-messages.test.ts`: 87 passed. `scripts/check --only health`: ok.

## Inspired by Amp

Source: [Bye Bye, Dial](https://ampcode.com/news/bye-bye-dial) (Nov 12, 2026) and the [Model Selector docs](https://ampcode.com/docs/model-selector#switch-models-in-a-thread). Amp replaced its 4-mode Dial with a per-thread model + effort selector, allows mid-thread switches, and records each one in the transcript as "Switched to GPT-6.1 Sol · High".

Ours vs theirs: Hermes already had mid-chat switching with `--reasoning`, and goes further than Amp on the model side (the marker tells the model which runtime it now is, and the size/cost guard warns before an expensive switch). The gap was the human-facing record, which this closes. Amp's other half, "who pays" badges in the picker, overlaps the existing provider/free-tier badges in `model-picker.tsx` and is not part of this PR.

**Not covered:**
- No running-Electron screenshot. The Desktop leg is the real `toChatMessages` run on the real stored transcript, not a rendered window.
- Picks committed through the session-authority `session.mutate` path (`hermes_state_mutation_prepared.py::model_in_transaction`) write no switch row at all, on main or here: that path keeps the transcript byte-stable on purpose. Giving it a notice means adding a display-only row (`active=0, compacted=1`) inside the authority's mutation transaction. That shifts display ordinals and rewind targets, so it needs a design call; it is not in this PR. This PR labels every switch row that does get written: a live gateway switch via `config.set model` / `/model`, the path probed above.

Fixes #139125
Supersedes #139137 (credit: @liuhao1024)

## Infographic

![Model switch notice](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2a6f0/d-N9e16p4edupwis9P6JK_KOSl0AXF.png)

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep bounded control reads off the serial queue
prs.body:
## Problem and behavior

`session.control.read` can miss the client's 30-second deadline while it waits behind a slow request on the same WebSocket. Switching from native Desktop to the gateway-hosted Webapp does not remove that transport queue. The ordinary dispatcher still awaits each serial request before taking the next frame; even existing concurrent reads were admitted into that queue before they could start.

Start the two allowlisted read projections at admission instead: `session.context_breakdown` and the pure `session.control.read` snapshot. Existing bounds remain **2 running + 8 waiting**; a flood still parks the reader. Mutations retain their arrival order.

## Ordering and profile boundaries

These snapshots are deliberately unordered relative to queued mutations. A client needing read-after-write consistency must await the mutation's reply. Desktop/Webapp `session.control` already awaits and consumes the returned snapshot; Ink's explicit control read hydrates the session once and receives later updates as events.

A read naming a hot-starting profile waits within the existing 20-second profile-start budget before taking a running read slot. It still counts against admission, cannot starve ready profiles' running slots, and is dropped when its viewer disconnects. Profile-bound grants naming another profile still fail immediately through the unchanged authority checks. The serial mutation hold lane is preserved.

Completed slow dispatches now log peer, request ID, method and elapsed time at a fixed 5-second threshold. IDs and methods use escaped repr; no request parameters or response bodies are logged. Cancellation and dispatch-crash paths keep their existing diagnostics. A handler that hands work to a pool is timed only through that handoff, not until its eventual reply. No new environment setting is added.

## Verification

Refreshed against upstream snapshot `8112254f8a934626032579cae967b25b7795836d` on 4 November 2026, preserving the published branch's history with a normal merge. Final head: `f41ee761ab98f1e0ab9c245d182a8aa0e59e9838`.

- **80/80 tests passed** across the concurrent-read, real ticketed profile-start, session-control, orphan-race and socket-send-deadline suites, using `scripts/run_tests.sh` with pinned Python 3.14 and two workers.
- The control-read regression fails on unmodified upstream: the read starts only after the gated mutation finishes. With the patch it replies while that mutation remains blocked, while a later mutation stays ordered. Both `prompt.submit` and `session.control` are exercised.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: **14 checks passed**, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude code/security/concurrency review: no remaining blocker or major for PR publication, conditional on passing the revised tests. The 80-test run above is that revised run. An earlier Gemini review raised the same profile-wait and ordering questions; the follow-up Gemini call hit quota and is not reported as a pass.

The first broader worktree run hit the repository's real-home I/O guard when bootstrap inspected its Git metadata under the live install. Verification was moved to an isolated clone outside the live home; the guard remained enabled.

## Limits

This proves the serial-queue regression, not the exact blocker on every naturally timed-out socket. Later independent-socket controls answered in 26–1685 ms while the user's original 30-second failure remained valid evidence. GIL pauses, database waits, read-lane saturation and full `session.resume` cost remain separate possible limits. See the new cross-surface evidence comment on this PR.

No live installation has been patched or restarted by this refresh. Installed activation and sustained real-use validation are outstanding. GitHub reported no configured CI checks; local test success is not a claim that GitHub CI ran.
