prs.title: feat(mcp): bearer_refresh_cmd — re-mint a static bearer on 401 without restarting
prs.body:
Some HTTP MCP servers sit behind a short-lived bearer: an OAuth `client_credentials` grant, or a token a vault mints, usually with about an hour of TTL. The usual config renders it once from an env var (`Authorization: "Bearer ${MY_TOKEN}"`). When the token expires, every request returns 401. The server then parks: current main parks exhausted reconnects and self-probes them, so the process no longer exits. But it keeps replaying the same dead header until someone restarts Hermes or edits the config.

`bearer_refresh_cmd` is an opt-in, per-server command that prints a fresh bearer. When the server answers 401, Hermes runs the command, sends the new token, and retries that one request. A routine rotation stays inside the request. It never shows up as a connection failure, so it spends no reconnect attempts and never reaches the park.

## Config

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  internal-api:
    url: "https://mcp.internal.example.com/mcp"
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${INTERNAL_MCP_TOKEN}"   # optional starting token
    bearer_refresh_cmd: "~/bin/mint-mcp-token --audience mcp"   # or an argv list
```

The command contract is documented in `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md` under "Bearer refresh command":

- It is not run through a shell. A string is split into argv with the repo's `split_command_line` (quotes honoured, no pipes, `$VAR` or globs), and only `~` in the first word is expanded. A list is used as given. It runs with the serving profile's own env and secrets via `served_profile_child_env(inherit_credentials=True)`.
- Stdout must be the bare token and nothing else. Output is rejected if it is empty, under 16 or over 8192 characters, contains whitespace or non-printable characters (a `Bearer ` prefix, CR/LF injection, two values smeared together), or starts like an error (`error…`, `fail…`, `{`, `[`, `<`). A non-zero exit, a rejected output, or a run past the 10 s timeout (the process tree is killed) keeps the current bearer.
- Runs are limited to one per 60 s per server, and concurrent 401s share one run.
- The token stays in memory only and is registered for redaction. The log line names only the server and the fact that a refresh happened.

## Changes

- **`tools/mcp_bearer_refresh.py` (new):** the command runner (`bounded_probe_run`, no shell), the output validator, a per-server `BearerRefreshState` (token, generation, cooldown), and an httpx `Auth`. The Auth sends the latest minted bearer. On a 401 it refreshes once and retries that request. The `Authorization` header is replaced case-insensitively. If no `Authorization` is configured, the command runs before the first request.
- **`tools/mcp_tool_transport.py`:** a new `_request_auth()` picks OAuth, the bearer refresher, or nothing, for both Streamable HTTP and SSE. `bearer_refresh_cmd` with `auth: oauth` is refused with a clear error. The refresh state lives on the task (`MCPServerTask._bearer_refresh`), so a reconnect starts from the last minted token. It resets if the command changes.
- **`tools/mcp_tool_server_run.py`:** the unauthenticated content-type preflight is skipped for these servers, as it is for OAuth. `bearer_refresh_cmd` is also a rebind key, so editing it in `config.yaml` rebuilds the connection.
- **`tools/mcp_tool_registration.py`:** the key is part of the connection identity. A server using it is never adopted across profiles, because its token is minted in the owner's scope.
- **`hermes_cli/mcp_security.py`:** `bearer_refresh_cmd` gets the same malware/backdoor scan as a stdio `command`.
- **Docs:** a row in the server-keys table and a "Bearer refresh command" section.

`run()` and the reconnect ladder are not modified.

## Changes since review

The old diff no longer applied after `tools/mcp_tool.py` was split into `tools/mcp_tool_*`, so the feature has been re-implemented on current main:

- **Initial-auth guard.** The refresh moved out of the reconnect loop and into the request (an httpx `Auth`), so `run()`, `_on_initial_connect_error` and the park logic are unchanged. No exception to the initial-auth contract is needed:
  - If the command heals the 401, `run()` never sees an auth failure.
  - If it cannot (non-zero exit, bad output, cooldown, or the minted token is also rejected), the original 401 reaches `run()` exactly as it does without the key.
- **Token in logs.** Nothing from the token is logged, not even a suffix. The success line is `MCP server '<name>': bearer refreshed via bearer_refresh_cmd`. Failure messages carry the reason and redacted stderr, never stdout.
- **Docs.** `bearer_refresh_cmd` is in `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md`, including the no-shell execution and the stdout-token contract.
- **`run()`-level lifecycle tests.** These run against a real local MCP server and a real mint script, covering:
  - a stale initial bearer, healed with one command run, one transport attempt and no park;
  - a mid-session rotation, healed inside a tool call with the same session and no reconnect;
  - a failing or useless command (two cases): same error class and same transport-attempt count as the same server without the key, the command run exactly once, and the server parked rather than exited.
- **Rationale.** Current main parks and self-probes exhausted reconnects, so the old "systemd restarts Hermes" motivation is gone. The remaining problem is a server stuck on a dead static bearer until a restart or a config edit.
- **Command execution.** Changed from `create_subprocess_shell` to argv without a shell, matching how the repo runs other operator commands.
- **`_is_auth_error`.** The `BaseExceptionGroup` unwrapping commit was dropped. Main already unwraps groups before classifying, and the request-layer design does not depend on it.

## Relationship to #151617

#151617 (`headers_command`) covers the general case: any set of headers, printed as JSON or `Name: value` lines. It credits this PR. This PR keeps the narrower `bearer_refresh_cmd` key, scoped to the `Authorization` bearer with a bare-token stdout contract. It follows the same request-layer approach (refresh on 401 inside an httpx `Auth` and retry the request), and it does not depend on #151617. If both land, the two keys would be mutually exclusive alternatives, and that is easy to enforce.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_mcp_bearer_refresh_cmd.py` (30 tests):
  - output contract;
  - runner (real subprocesses: success plus redaction, no shell, non-zero exit, timeout kill, missing executable);
  - auth flow (single retry, case-insensitive header replacement, no token in logs, cooldown, failed refresh, concurrent 401s sharing one run, no configured header);
  - wiring (OAuth exclusivity, state reuse across reconnects, security scan, connection identity);
  - the `run()` lifecycle tests above.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_tool*.py tests/tools/test_mcp_*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp*.py`: 1411 passed, 3 skipped (platform-gated), 0 failed.

prs.title: feat(display): per-tool label overrides + reversible path-trim previews
prs.body:
## Summary

On chat platforms, tool-progress lines for MCP and plugin tools show the raw tool name (`⚙️ mcp_gbrain_query: "…"`), which looks like an internal ID to non-technical users. Path previews are also fixed to a basename with no way to show the full path. This PR adds two display settings that work alongside the curated friendly labels already on main.

### `display.tool_labels` (default `{}`)

A map from raw tool name to a label you choose.

```yaml
display:
  tool_labels:
    web_search: "Looking things up"           # replaces the curated "Searching the web for"
    mcp_gbrain_query: "Searching information"  # MCP/plugin tools have no curated label
  platforms:
    whatsapp:
      tool_labels: {mcp_gbrain_query: "Looking up"}  # replaces the global map on WhatsApp
```

**How it works with `display.friendly_tool_labels`:**

- An explicit entry wins. It replaces both the raw name and the curated verb, and the argument preview stays the same:
  - gateway progress: `🔍 Looking things up: "weather in NYC"`
  - CLI spinner: `Looking things up: weather in NYC`
  - Slack live status: `is looking things up: weather in NYC…`
- With no entry, output is the same as today: the curated label when one exists, the raw name otherwise. The default empty map changes nothing.
- Entries also apply when `friendly_tool_labels: false`. That switch still controls only the curated labels.
- `verbose` tool progress keeps raw names, because it is a debugging view.
- The setting is resolved per platform through `resolve_display_setting`, so `display.platforms.<platform>.tool_labels` replaces the global map for that platform. A malformed value (not a map) is logged once and the next level up is used. Blank labels are ignored.

### `display.trim_path_previews` (default `true`)

`true` keeps today's behavior: `read_file` previews show only the basename. `false` shows the full path. The trim now happens inside the `read_file` preview builder, the only place a path is shortened to a basename. Every surface that renders that preview therefore honors the setting, including the gateway's `prepare_tool_preview` rebuild. `tool_preview_length` still caps the result and keeps the end of the path. The setting can be overridden per platform.

## Changes since review

- **Path trimming can now be turned off.** The previous version trimmed in a gateway formatter that ran after `agent/display.py` had already reduced `read_file` to `Path(...).name`, so `false` could never bring the full path back. Trimming is now gated by `display.trim_path_previews` inside `_preview_read_file` itself. There is no second, gateway-side trimming step.
- **Works with curated labels instead of replacing them.** The old placeholder `_CURATED_TOOL_LABELS` and `apply_tool_label` helpers are gone. Overrides plug into the code that `friendly_tool_labels` already uses:
  - `agent/display.py`: `build_tool_label` (CLI) and `build_status_phrase` (Slack status)
  - `gateway/run_turn_progress.py::_progress_build_message`: gateway progress lines, including the terminal code-block header
  - `gateway/run_turn.py::_run_agent_display_settings`: per-turn resolution, in the same setter loop as `friendly_tool_labels`

  When no mapping exists, output is unchanged. A test confirms that the default-config gateway output on main still passes.
- **Gateway-level tests.** The new tests in `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_topics.py` write `config.yaml` and run the real `GatewayRunner._run_agent` turn with a fake agent. They check:
  - the default config keeps curated labels and basenames
  - an override beats the curated label, and an MCP tool gets its mapped label
  - an unmapped built-in keeps its curated label
  - a per-platform map wins
  - `trim_path_previews: false` shows the full path

  Resolver tests in `tests/gateway/test_display_config.py` cover the defaults, per-platform replacement, malformed-map fallback and YAML string booleans. Unit tests in `tests/agent/test_display.py` cover the helpers. The new gateway and resolver tests fail on main and pass on this branch, except the one that checks default output stays unchanged.
- **Configuration docs.** The new keys, and the previously undocumented `friendly_tool_labels`, are added to the Display Settings block in `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`, under a new "Tool labels and path previews" section.
- Both keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and the gateway `_GLOBAL_DEFAULTS`, and the classic CLI loads them at startup.
- Dropped from the original PR: the `format_tool_event` changes in `gateway/platforms/base.py` (that path no longer renders these lines on main), and the plan to trim `write_file`/`patch` previews, which would have changed default output.

## Tests

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_display.py tests/gateway/test_display_config.py tests/gateway/test_run_progress_topics.py <related display/progress/slack/config suites>
```

All pass. The only collection errors are for modules missing from the local environment (`aiohttp`, `acp`), and they also occur on main.

prs.title: fix(gateway): honor WATCHDOG_PID and keep systemd watchdog pings under the deadline
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR first added opt-in `sd_notify` / `WatchdogSec` support. While it was open, `main` got the same plumbing from another contributor: `gateway/systemd_notify.py` (`SystemdWatchdog`), the runner lifecycle in `gateway/run_shutdown.py`, and generated units that switch to `Type=notify` + `NotifyAccess=main` + `WatchdogSec=` when `gateway.systemd_watchdog_seconds` is set (`hermes_cli/gateway.py`, documented in `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/index.md`).

So I rebased the PR onto `main` and removed its own copy of the module. What's left is the reviewer's correctness fixes, applied to `main`'s code.

## Changes since review

| Review point | Status |
|---|---|
| Heartbeat floor `max(1.0, ...)` turned a 500 ms watchdog into a 1 s ping | **Already fine on main.** `SystemdWatchdog._run()` pings every `interval / 2` with only a 10 ms floor. This PR adds a test that pins this down (below). |
| `WATCHDOG_USEC` read without checking `WATCHDOG_PID` | **Fixed here.** `watchdog_interval_seconds()` now follows `sd_watchdog_enabled(3)`. If `WATCHDOG_PID` is set and doesn't match `os.getpid()`, or can't be parsed, the watchdog is off. A process that inherited the service's systemd environment therefore can't ping for the main PID. |
| Editing the unit by hand doesn't survive `refresh_systemd_unit_if_needed()` | **Already on main.** `gateway.systemd_watchdog_seconds` in `config.yaml` is the supported, lasting way to turn it on. The generated unit is rebuilt from config, and the docs cover it under "Optional Linux event-loop watchdog". The PR's original env-var route and direct unit edit are dropped. |

## Tests

New file `tests/gateway/test_systemd_watchdog_interval.py` (it runs on every platform because it stubs the notify socket):
- `WATCHDOG_PID` absent → enabled; matching → enabled; mismatched or invalid → disabled, and no datagram is sent.
- Sub-2 s cadence with `WATCHDOG_USEC=500000` and `1500000`. It uses a fake clock and delays every wake-up by the full lag budget, then checks that every ping, including the first, arrives before the advertised deadline.

The mismatched and invalid PID cases fail on `main` without this change.

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_systemd_*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_systemd_*.py tests/tools/test_child_env_supervisor_identity.py -q
```

prs.title: feat(gateway): home_channel_startup_notification — startup ping on unplanned restarts (closes #27870)
prs.body:
## What Adds a per-platform `home_channel_startup_notification` setting that decides when the home channel gets "♻️ Gateway online" on startup: | Value | When the home channel hears "Gateway online" | |---|---| | `restart_only` (default) | Only after a planned restart, meaning the `.restart_pending.json` marker exists. This is today's behaviour. | | `always` | On every start. That includes unplanned ones: a crash, an OOM kill, systemd `Restart=on-failure`, a host reboot, a cold start. | | `off` | Never. The shutdown notice and the `/restart` requester reply are unaffected. | `gateway_restart_notification: false` is still the master switch and silences every lifecycle notice on that platform, whatever the new key says. Closes #27870. ## Why The shutdown side already notifies home channels. The startup side only did so when the planned-restart marker was present, so after a crash, an OOM kill or a supervisor respawn after an unclean exit, the operator never heard that Hermes came back. A boolean can't express "keep the shutdown notice but drop the startup one", so the setting has three values and composes with the existing switch: | Use case | `gateway_restart_notification` | `home_channel_startup_notification` | |---|---|---| | Default (unchanged behaviour) | `true` | `restart_only` | | Notify on every bounce, planned or not | `true` | `always` | | Silence everything | `false` | (ignored) | | Keep the shutdown notice, drop the startup one | `true` | `off` | ## How - **Config** (`gateway/config.py`, `gateway/config_loader.py`): a new `PlatformConfig.home_channel_startup_notification` field. It is parsed like `reply_to_mode`: values are case-insensitive, a bare YAML `off` (which YAML reads as `False`) means `off`, and an unknown value logs a warning and falls back to `restart_only`. It is a typed key, so it does not leak into `extra`. It is bridged from nested `gateway.platforms.

` blocks along with `gateway_restart_notification`. Platform blocks are read raw by the gateway loader, so `DEFAULT_CONFIG` needs no change. - **One predicate** (`_startup_notice_wanted` in `gateway/run_notifications.py`) decides whether a home is owed the notice, from the master switch, the mode and whether this boot is planned. - **Planned boot** (marker present): the existing marker path is unchanged except that `off` homes are skipped and are not part of the owed set, so they cannot keep the marker alive. An `always` home is covered by this path, so it does not get a second notice. - **Unplanned boot** (no marker): `_await_startup_boot_sends` records which `always` homes are owed a notice (in memory, per process) and sends to them after the requester notice. `_replay_restart_notices` and `_schedule_restart_notice_replay` also resend to any still-owed home, so a platform that was down at boot gets its notice exactly once when it reconnects or its send path heals. The owed set clears once every owed home has been reached. - **No duplicates**: delivery uses the existing `_send_home_channel_startup_notifications`, so a chat shared by several served profiles gets one notice, and a Telegram private chat stays keyed per bot. The chat that sent `/restart` is passed as `skip_chats` (keyed by profile, taken from the requester marker the boot pass read) and counts as delivered, so that chat or topic gets only the "restarted" reply. This holds whether the reply goes out at boot or later through the reconnect replay. ## Changes since review - **Double send on chat `/restart` when that chat is the home channel.** The `always` path no longer calls the home sender with `skip_targets=None`. The `/restart` requester's chat is carried into the home sender as `skip_chats`. This covers more cases than the reviewer's suggestion of passing only the target that `_send_restart_notification()` returns: it also holds when the requester's platform was down at boot and its reply goes out later through the replay, and when the requester is in a secondary profile. Regression test: `test_restart_from_home_chat_sends_one_message`, run for a chat and a forum topic, each with the platform live at boot and with it replayed on reconnect. It asserts that exactly one message (the "restarted" reply) reaches the chat. Turning the guard off makes all four cases fail. - **Tests went through the helper only.** The new tests run the real boot pass (`_await_startup_boot_sends`) and the real reconnect (`_install_reconnected_adapter` → replay). Only the adapters are fakes. - **Undocumented key.** The "Restart notifications" section of `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/index.md` now documents the three values, the default, a YAML example, how the key interacts with `gateway_restart_notification`, and the once-per-start, no-duplicate guarantees. - **Rebuilt on current `main`.** The old branch predated the split of `gateway/run.py`. This version sits on the planned-restart marker bookkeeping in `run_notifications.py` and on the reconnect replay from #112109 instead of adding a separate post-startup helper. ## Tests `tests/gateway/test_home_channel_startup_notification.py` (15 tests, all through the boot path): - Unplanned boot: `default` and `restart_only` send nothing, `always` sends one notice, `off` sends nothing, and `gateway_restart_notification: false` together with `always` sends nothing. A later reconnect never repeats the notice. - Planned boot: `restart_only` and `always` each send one notice, `off` sends none, and the marker is cleared in every case. - An `always` home that is down at boot gets exactly one notice on reconnect. - `/restart` from the home chat or topic sends one message; `/restart` from another chat still notifies the `always` home. - Two profiles sharing a home chat get one notice. `tests/gateway/test_config.py`: parsing of each value, case handling, bare `off`/`False`, the warning plus fallback for unknown values, the round trip, and bridging from a nested `gateway.platforms` block. The existing restart, notice-replay, planned-restart multiplex and config suites pass unchanged.

prs.title: feat(gateway): inline shutdown-reason clause in the shutdown chat notification
prs.body:
## What

Adds a short reason clause to the outbound "Hermes is shutting down" chat notice when the gateway is stopped by an **unplanned** external signal, so users can tell why it went down without checking the operator's terminal. The clause comes from the shutdown-forensics snapshot (`snapshot_shutdown_context()`) that the signal handler already takes.

## Why

Today every external stop produces the same generic notice:

> ⚠️ Hermes is shutting down — your current task will be interrupted. When it is back online, send any message and I'll try to pick up where we left off.

Users on WhatsApp / Discord / Slack can't tell whether an operator deliberately stopped the gateway or something else killed it. In production that "something else" is most often `systemctl restart`, a package upgrade going through `needrestart`, or unattended-upgrades restarting a gateway that holds a stale library. All of these look the same in chat.

## Message shape per scenario

| Scenario | Notice |
|---|---|
| Chat `/restart`, SIGUSR1, `hermes gateway restart` (unchanged) | `⚠️ Hermes is restarting — your current task will be interrupted. Send any message after the restart …` |
| `hermes gateway stop` / systemd `ExecStop` planned-stop marker (unchanged) | `⚠️ Hermes is shutting down — your current task will be interrupted. …` |
| `--replace` takeover marker (unchanged) | `⚠️ Hermes is shutting down — your current task will be interrupted. …` (active chats only; the home broadcast stays suppressed) |
| Foreground Ctrl+C / SIGINT (unchanged; main classifies it as a planned stop) | `⚠️ Hermes is shutting down — your current task will be interrupted. …` |
| Unmarked SIGTERM under systemd (`systemctl restart` by an admin, needrestart, unattended-upgrades) | `⚠️ Hermes is shutting down (external stop from systemd) — your current task will be interrupted. …` |
| Unmarked SIGTERM outside systemd (bare `kill`, `pkill`, a non-systemd orchestrator) | `⚠️ Hermes is shutting down (external stop) — your current task will be interrupted. …` |
| No forensics snapshot captured (unchanged fallback) | `⚠️ Hermes is shutting down — your current task will be interrupted. …` |

The reason clause only appears for stops that main already treats as unplanned.

## What changes

- `gateway/run_bootstrap.py`: the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler now stores its forensics snapshot on the runner (`runner._shutdown_ctx`).
- `gateway/run_shutdown.py`: new `GatewayShutdownMixin._shutdown_reason_hint()`. It returns a reason only when the runner's existing classification says the signal was unplanned: `_signal_initiated_shutdown` is set, `_planned_takeover_shutdown` is not, no restart was requested, and the snapshot shows SIGTERM. `under_systemd` picks between the two reasons. `_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown()` uses the new `gateway.shutdown.notice_shutdown_reason` string when a reason is present. The same message goes to active chats and home channels.
- `locales/*.yaml`: new keys `gateway.shutdown.notice_shutdown_reason` (with a `{reason}` placeholder), `reason_external_systemd` and `reason_external`. They are added to every locale because `tests/agent/test_i18n.py` requires every locale to have the same keys and placeholders as English.

## Changes since review

- **Marker-confirmed planned SIGTERM paths were classified as `external stop`.** The reason is now based on the planned/unplanned decision the signal handler on main already makes, not on `_restart_requested`. The handler consumes the planned-stop marker (including the `planned_stop_seen` latch for the CLI's own follow-up SIGTERM) and the `--replace` takeover marker. It sets `runner._signal_initiated_shutdown` only when neither marker claimed the signal, and sets `runner._planned_takeover_shutdown` for takeovers. `_shutdown_reason_hint()` gives no reason unless `_signal_initiated_shutdown` is set, and also returns `None` when `_planned_takeover_shutdown` is set. Planned stops, takeovers and SIGINT therefore keep the plain notice, even under systemd.
- **Notification-level tests for both marker paths.** `tests/gateway/test_shutdown_reason_notice.py` sends a real SIGTERM/SIGINT through the real `_start_gateway_make_shutdown_signal_handler`. The resulting `stop()` runs to completion and the test checks the notice an active chat actually received. It covers the planned-stop marker under systemd, the takeover marker under systemd, unmarked SIGTERM under systemd, bare SIGTERM, and SIGINT. Two direct tests cover a restart (notice unchanged) and a missing snapshot (plain notice).
- Ported to the restructured gateway (`run_bootstrap.py` / `run_shutdown.py`) and the locale catalogue. Message strings now come from `t()`.

## Backward compatibility

- Restarts, planned stops, takeovers, SIGINT and stops with no snapshot all send the same text as current main.
- The only new text is the parenthesised reason on unplanned SIGTERM.

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_shutdown_reason_notice.py`: 7 new tests (systemd vs bare external stop, planned-stop marker, takeover marker, SIGINT, unchanged restart, missing snapshot).
- Also run and passing: `tests/gateway/test_restart_notification.py` and `tests/agent/test_i18n.py`, `test_i18n_languages.py`, `test_i18n_layers.py` (locale key and placeholder parity) — 86 passed, 0 failed across the 5 files.

## Related

Sibling to #55008 (opt-in "gateway back online" startup ping) and #55018 (`sd_notify` / `WatchdogSec` integration). Together they tell users why the gateway went down, that it went down, and that it came back up.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add alphagrowth plugin
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/alphagrowth.yaml`, pinning [alphagrowth/alphagrowth-mcp](https://github.com/alphagrowth/alphagrowth-mcp/tree/1fb99ff5fec9e61b6dba843f9c0532b1e4d10287) at `1fb99ff5`.

## What it does

AlphaGrowth publishes free, read-only crypto data: project metrics and TVL history, chains, fees and revenue, funding rounds and investors, DeFi yield pools, stablecoins, token unlocks and DAO treasuries. This plugin connects Hermes to AlphaGrowth's hosted MCP server and bundles three skills that route questions to the right tools:

- `alphagrowth:crypto-project-research`: one project's metrics, TVL trend, fees, community growth, funding and unlocks
- `alphagrowth:defi-market-scan`: rankings of projects, chains, fees, volumes, yields, stablecoins, unlocks and DAO treasuries
- `alphagrowth:crypto-funding-research`: recent rounds, top investors and investor portfolios

Submitted by the repository owner (AlphaGrowth).

## Hermes surfaces

Portable Agent Plugins v1 package only: `plugin.json`, a root `mcp.json` with one `streamable-http` server (`https://alphagrowth.io/mcp`, no auth), and `skills/*/SKILL.md`. No Python, no Desktop code, no hooks, no env vars, no stdio process.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Network:** every tool call is an HTTPS request to `alphagrowth.io/mcp`. The returned data joins the session context and so reaches the user's model provider.
- **No writes:** all 37 tools are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`; none trades, moves money, sends messages or changes an account.
- **Logging by the server operator:** AlphaGrowth logs each call (tool and arguments, client name and version, user agent, IP and approximate location). After 30 days the arguments and location are deleted and the IP is replaced by a keyed hash; records are deleted after 180 days. Calls are rate-limited per IP. The same text is in the README's "Data and privacy" section.
- **No local state:** the package stores nothing and needs no credentials.
- **Tool list is server-side:** it comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate` was not run locally; relying on the catalog CI job. `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.0"` matches other portable packages that carry a `streamable-http` server.

prs.title: fix(desktop): name the switched-to model in the timeline notice
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

After a live model switch, the chat timeline notice was a content-free hardcoded English string (`model changed`). The gateway's pivot marker row already knows exactly which model/provider took over — `_append_model_switch_marker` writes the full facts into the marker text — but `timelineDisplayContent` in the Desktop hydration pipeline discarded them, so in multi-model setups (e.g. two quantizations of the same base on different endpoints) the user had no trustworthy record of which runtime took over from which point.

This PR surfaces the facts through the existing display-metadata channel (the same one `async_delegation_complete` and `process_complete` rows already use):

- The gateway stamps `{"model": ..., "provider": ...}` as display-only metadata on the pivot row — both the in-memory history entry and the durable `append_message` row (the projection layer and the DB read path already carry `display_metadata` through untouched).
- The Desktop timeline renders `model changed to <model> via <provider>` (or `model changed to <model>` when no provider is set). Rows persisted by backends that predate the metadata keep the old `model changed` string as the fallback.

Scope note: the localization half of #139125 (moving all timeline notice strings behind i18n keys, which also affects `auto_continue`, `personality_switch`, and the `background … finished` fallbacks) is a separate cross-cutting change across the i18n catalog; this PR fixes the information loss, which is the functional gap.

## Related Issue

Fixes #139125

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_append_model_switch_marker` now stamps `display_metadata={"model": ..., "provider": ...}` on the in-memory pivot entry and passes it to the durable `db.append_message` row.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/hydration.ts` — the `model_switch` branch of `timelineDisplayContent` reads the model/provider from `display_metadata` and renders `model changed to <model> via <provider>`, falling back to the previous `model changed` for metadata-less rows.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_role.py` — three regression tests: metadata lands on the entry, follows the replacing marker on a second switch, and an empty provider is kept as an empty string.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages.test.ts` — regression test covering the both-fields render, the no-provider render, and the REST form where `display_metadata` arrives as raw JSON text.

## How to Test

1. Backend: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_role.py -q` → 8 passed (Observed result: 8 passed in 1.44s on this machine).
2. Frontend: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/lib/chat-messages.test.ts` from `apps/desktop` → Observed result: 87 passed (1 test file).
3. End-to-end shape: run a session, switch the model mid-chat (`/model`); the timeline card should read `model changed to <model> via <provider>` instead of `model changed`, and the same full text should reappear after resume/reload because the durable row carries the same metadata.
4. `python scripts/check --staged` → Observed result: `scripts/check: 12 checks, ok` (0 blocking).

prs.title: fix(browser): the sandbox Chromium's stop recognises a browser that rewrote its process title
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes the sandbox browser's stop actually signal the Chromium Hermes launched there.

`_STOP_SCRIPT` proves the pid is still the launched browser before signalling: same start time, and an argv entry equal to the launch's `--user-data-dir=<dir>` token, read from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` as NUL-separated arguments. Chromium rewrites its process title on Linux, which leaves that file as one space-joined string, so the comparison never matched a real Chromium: every stop exited with `_NOT_OURS_RC` ("not signalling sandbox pid …: it is gone or no longer the Chromium launched on …") and the browser lived as long as its container. Details and measurements are in #156366.

The fix keeps the check where it is and handles that one shape: when the cmdline reads back as a single argument, the token is matched as a space-delimited word of that string. This is what `psutil.Process.cmdline()` does for the host launcher's equivalent check (`_cmdline_names_dir`). The pid + start-time check is untouched, so a reused pid is still never signalled.

## Related Issue

Fixes #156366

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/browser_session_sandbox.py`: `_STOP_SCRIPT` matches the `--user-data-dir=` token inside a single-argument (title-rewritten) cmdline.
- `tests/tools/test_browser_sandbox_stop_identity.py`: the stand-in Chromium can rewrite its argv block in place the way Chromium does; new test `test_stop_signals_a_chromium_that_rewrote_its_process_title`.

## How to Test

1. `just test tests/tools/test_browser_sandbox_stop_identity.py` — 3 pass. On `main` without the fix the new test fails (the stand-in is not signalled), the two existing ones pass.
2. Against a real Chromium in a `nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop` container (Playwright `chromium-1248`), with the script's final `kill` replaced by an `echo`:
   - released script: exit 4 (`_NOT_OURS_RC`) for the live browser
   - this PR: exit 0 for the live browser, exit 4 for pid 1 with the browser's start time

prs.title: Migrate the remaining npm projects to pnpm; bump pnpm and node
prs.body:
Follows #1 (the website + bridge lockfile migration), which moved the lockfiles but left three runtime installers and the last npm project on npm.

## What changes

**WhatsApp bridge → pnpm** (`d55fd6a7fbd`)
The bridge's three installers (adapter, `hermes whatsapp` wizard, dashboard) called `npm`, so they ignored `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides; the wizard's staleness check read a `package-lock.json` that no longer exists and reinstalled on every run. All three now run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and the install is stamped with a hash of `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` so a lockfile bump reinstalls too.

The last npm project. `package-lock.json` is replaced by `pnpm-lock.yaml` + `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; the npm `overrides` field moves into the workspace file (pnpm does not read it in `package.json`), and a `publicHoistPattern` keeps `@spectrum-ts/imessage` at the top level so the postinstall patch still finds `dist/index.js`. `pm.workspace.install_node_sidecar`, the Photon adapter/CLI, the Docker bake, osv-scanner, the lockfile CI helpers and the update smoke tests all move to pnpm.

prs.title: feat(google-workspace): named Google accounts with --account
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets one Hermes profile use more than one Google account (personal + work) through the bundled `google-workspace` skill. Today the skill reads a single `<HERMES_HOME>/google_token.json`, so the only way to reach a second account is a whole second Hermes profile, which also splits memory, sessions and config.

`--account EMAIL` on `setup.py`, `google_api.py` and `gws_bridge.py` selects a token of its own at `<HERMES_HOME>/google_tokens/<email>.json`. Leaving the flag out changes nothing: same token path, same output, same gws environment.

This is deliberately the small core the triage on #15602 asked for when it pointed at the closed #30686 ("split out the core multi-account token resolution and CLI plumbing that can be reviewed independently"): no migration, no default-account pointer, no aliases, no new env var, no new scope logic.

### Design decisions

- **No fallback for a named account.** `--account work@x.com` with no token for it exits 1 with the setup command to run. It never reads the default token, because that would answer a request about one account with another account's mail (the data-boundary concern raised in #15602).
- **Wrong-account guard at consent time.** `--auth-url` passes `login_hint`, and `--auth-code` asks Google which account actually granted the token (Gmail `users.getProfile`, or the primary Calendar id when only Calendar was granted). If it differs from `--account`, the token is not written and the message names both accounts. If the granted scopes can't reveal the account, the token is saved with a warning.
- **Separate gws config dir per named account.** gws caches access tokens per config dir without keying on `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CREDENTIALS_FILE` (googleworkspace/cli#572, #134966), so two accounts sharing the default dir would silently run as whichever filled the cache first. Named accounts get `<HERMES_HOME>/google_tokens/gws/<email>` (0700); an explicit `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` from the caller wins. The default-token path is untouched, so this doesn't conflict with #134967's fix for that path.
- **Account names are validated as plain email addresses** (lowercased, no path separators), so `--account` can't escape `google_tokens/`.
- **No new `HERMES_*` env var**, per the contribution rubric; selection is by flag only.

## Related Issue

Fixes #15602

Related: #30686 (closed, larger version of this), #44057 (auth contexts: broader, overlaps in intent), #134967 (gws cache for the default token).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/_google_account.py` (new): account validation, `--account` argument, per-account token / pending-session / gws config paths, `list_accounts()`.
- `scripts/setup.py`: `--account` for `--check`, `--check-live`, `--auth-url`, `--auth-code`, `--revoke`; `--list-accounts`; `login_hint`; identity check before saving a named token.
- `scripts/google_api.py`: global `--account` (before the service); per-account gws config dir; setup hint names the account.
- `scripts/gws_bridge.py`: optional leading `--account EMAIL`; refreshes and writes only that account's token.
- `SKILL.md`: "More than one Google account" section, agent rule to ask which account when ambiguous, remote-backend note (`terminal.credential_files`); version 1.3.0. Website page regenerated with `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`.
- `tests/skills/test_google_workspace_accounts.py` (new): 10 behaviour tests.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_google_workspace_accounts.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_api.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_setup.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_setup_deps.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_credential_files.py -q` → 28 passed.
2. Manual, with a second Google account added as a test user on the OAuth client:
   ```bash
   setup.py --account work@example.com --auth-url      # consent screen pre-selects work@example.com
   setup.py --account work@example.com --auth-code "<redirect URL>"
   setup.py --list-accounts
   google_api.py --account work@example.com gmail search "is:unread" --max 3
   google_api.py gmail search "is:unread" --max 3      # still the default account
   ```
3. Approve with the wrong account on step 1 → `--auth-code` prints `ERROR: You authorized ..., but --account is ...` and writes no token.

The tests cover: named account uses its own token and gws cache; omitting `--account` leaves the env exactly as before; a missing named token fails instead of using the default; path-like `--account` values are rejected before anything is created; the bridge refreshes only the named token; `--auth-url` hints the account and keeps the default pending session untouched; a token granted by a different account is never saved.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#30686 is closed; #44057 and #145124 take broader, different shapes)

- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (one reviewed `# health: allow HX006` on the pre-existing interactive `gws` passthrough in `gws_bridge.py`, whose argument list changed)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (aarch64), Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (SKILL.md + regenerated website page)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no config keys)
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A

prs.title: fix(a2a): resolve startup tokens through the profile secret scope when the env is scrubbed
prs.body:
## Summary

On a systemd-installed gateway, inbound A2A authentication silently degrades to localhost-only / no auth: `_startup_env()`'s unscoped rung read `os.getenv` alone, but by the time `A2ASecurityContext.capture()` runs at gateway startup the `A2A_*TOKEN*` variables have been loaded into the secret store and are no longer authoritative in `os.environ`. `capture()` therefore yielded no tokens, `localhost_only()` was `True`, and every request through a tunnel or reverse proxy — with or without an `Authorization` header — was served unauthenticated while the audit log recorded `peer: "ip:127.0.0.1"` (#148961).

## Fix

The unscoped rung of `_startup_env()` now resolves through the shared `get_scoped_secret(..., external_fallback=True)` accessor in `gateway/platforms/_shared.py` — the same startup-gate read the adapter already uses for `A2A_PORT` / `A2A_PUBLIC_URL` — so a token written to the profile `.env` by `hermes gateway setup` (or supplied by an external secret source) is visible at startup even after the env var is gone. This also revives the documented setup path, which previously never worked on single-profile installs.

Fail-closed is preserved: a token that exists neither in the env nor in the profile's secret scope still yields `""`, so `localhost_only()` stays `True` exactly as before. Profile-scoped (secondary multiplex) behavior is unchanged.

`capture()` additionally logs one WARNING when `A2A_PEER_TOKENS` is set but parses to zero `name:token` pairs (e.g. a bare `vibe_<hex>` value) — the same silent localhost-only trap, now diagnosable from the log instead of only from a tunnel probe.

## Testing

- New regression tests in `tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py::TestStartupEnvSecretScopeFallback` against a real temp profile home: token in the profile `.env` only (env scrubbed) → `capture()` authenticates per-peer and rejects missing/wrong tokens; no token anywhere → `localhost_only()` and the `ip:<addr>` identity unchanged; unparseable value → WARNING logged.
- Sensitivity-verified: the token-resolution regression test fails on the pre-fix code (`localhost_only()` stays `True` with the token present in the store).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over all nine A2A-related test files (plugin, no-token guards, tools gate, rejected resend, forwarded cancel retry, phase23, reason roundtrip, session A2A, hosted create): all pass.
- Full suite verified on CI (fork dispatch run of the `Tests` workflow — all test files, 3 slices; the E2E lanes are dispatch-skipped by design); locally only the affected directories were run per #146467 (macOS, 16 GB).
- The only failures in that run — `tests/gateway/test_journey_compress_restart_fifo.py::test_followers_survive_compression_and_restart_in_order_exactly_once[graceful]`/`[crash]` (`AssertionError: FOLLOWER_1`) — reproduce identically on a control dispatch of unmodified upstream main on the same runner: pre-existing timing sensitivity on 4-vCPU shared runners, untouched by this change.
- `python scripts/check`: ruff clean; the code-health ratchet reports only pre-existing violations in files this change does not touch.

Fixes #148961

prs.title: ci: ratchet new syntactic thread-handoff sites
prs.body:
## ELI5

When Hermes hands a job to a background thread, that thread can forget which profile it is working for. It may then read another profile's settings or keys. Every place that hands work off this way is a spot to check.

This PR keeps a list of the 378 spots that exist today. If a change adds a new one, lint fails until the author either fixes it or writes a comment on that line saying why it's safe. Existing spots stay as they are; the list can only shrink.

**What this does NOT check:** reads of settings, profile or secrets through `os.environ` / `os.getenv`. That is a separate hazard (the code gets the launch profile's value, not the turn's) with its own ratchet: #156039.

| | This PR (thread-hops) | #156039 (raw env reads) |
|---|---|---|
| Hazard | work moves to a thread and loses the turn's profile | code reads `os.environ` and gets the launch profile's value |
| Flags | `Thread(target=)`, `Timer`, `.submit`, `.run_in_executor`, pool `.map` | `os.getenv(...)`, `os.environ.get(...)`, `os.environ[...]` |
| Fix it points to | copy the context (`spawn_context_thread`, `ctx_bound`) or a reasoned marker | read through the profile's config/secret owner |

## Context

Tracking: #152308. Part of #151791 (step 0b-3).

#151791 gives each of three questions one owner: which profile a turn runs as, what a setting's value is, and where a secret comes from. Today the answers live in module globals, `os.environ` and context variables. A context variable does not follow work onto a new thread unless the code copies it, so every thread or executor handoff is a place where a turn can fall back to the wrong profile. Step 0b-1 (#154670) fixed known handoffs one by one.

## Why we need this

Fixing sites one at a time does not stop new ones arriving: main added 16 recognized handoffs while this PR was open. A per-file count can't see when one handoff is removed and an unrelated one added in the same file. This ratchet fingerprints each site, so every new one gets an explicit context-propagation decision from its author, and the review for the remaining sites can work down a fixed list instead of a moving target.

## What changes

```diff
 scripts/check  (pre-commit hook, pre-push hook, lint CI)
   detached-spawns
-    file list: old copy of the scan roots
+    file list: production_scan.production_files()  # follows MOVES, skips generated old-path files
+  thread-hops                                       # new
+    production_files() -> parse files that mention a handoff word (after NFKC, as Python reads names)
+      Thread/Timer(target=...), .submit, .run_in_executor, pool .map
+      fingerprint = (pre-move path, enclosing scope, call AST, occurrence)
+      "# thread-hop: ok — <why>" exempts the first handoff visited on its line
+    fingerprint not in thread_hops_baseline.json -> fail
+    baseline entry no longer present               -> fail, run --update to prune
```

```text
scripts/ci/
├── check_thread_hops.py       # the ratchet
├── production_scan.py         # production file list + reasoned-comment parsing, shared with detached-spawns
└── thread_hops_baseline.json  # 378 existing sites on main fd8a6c41ac
```

- A real comment `thread-hop: ok — <why>` on the call line, or on a comment-only line just above it, exempts one handoff. Wrapping a callback does not exempt it, and a reason made only of separators is rejected.
- The guard judges the requested commit or staged tree, including that tree's own baseline. A baseline may only shrink relative to its base; working-tree runs include new nonignored files and handle deletions.
- Both guards find files through `hermes_agent/compat/moves.py`. Sites are keyed by their pre-move path, so a pure module move keeps its baseline entries. An undeclared old-path copy beside its moved file is refused until it is marked generated or deleted. Explicit paths outside the repository are refused.

## Relation to HX012

Code health already has HX012 ("raw threading.Thread"), a warning for `threading.Thread(...)` calls that don't run in a copied context (237 hits on main). thread-hops covers the same hazard more broadly (`Timer`, `.submit`, `.run_in_executor`, pool `.map`) and blocks new sites, so it supersedes HX012 for this purpose. Follow-up #156038 retires HX012 or points it at thread-hops; this PR leaves HX012 unchanged.

## Scope and limits

This is a syntactic non-regression guard, not proof of context propagation. The baseline holds safe and unclassified existing sites alike. Dynamic aliases, subclasses, unknown executor receivers and indirect dispatch can escape detection; harmless matches need a reasoned exception. Renaming the enclosing function or class changes a site's fingerprint. No runtime production handoffs change.

The baseline must be regenerated if recognized production sites change on main before this lands.

## Credits

- @kvnloo: one marker exempts one handoff (cherry-picked, authorship kept).
- @BearHuddleston: blob reads by object id for Git before 2.38, POSIX-only fixtures, and tests for four surviving mutants (from the review, authored as Bear).

## Verification

- Tests: CI on this head.
- New guards fail on the previous implementation and pass now: marked-twin substitution, `*`/`**` expanded constructors, moved-tree scans for both guards, detached-spawns' marker rules (trailing comment above, string literal, a file that does not tokenize), full-width identifiers, outside-root paths, an undeclared old-path copy and a git timeout in detached-spawns.
- Moving `tools/` to `hermes_agent/tools/` with a matching MOVES entry keeps thread-hops green (378 present, 378 baselined). A new unbound thread and a detached `Popen` in the moved tree are both flagged; before this change detached-spawns reported the moved tree clean.
- `scripts/check --staged --only thread-hops` rejects an unmarked handoff in a hook fixture. That test fails if thread-hops is removed from `scripts/check`.
- Ruff clean. ty adds no new diagnostic kind against main.

No auto-merge is requested.

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Platform: Linux.

prs.title: fix(cli): withdraw a prompt fenced behind a lost turn after submit, and say when it waits on a running turn
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Upstream now covers the main lost-turn path in the classic CLI: `_prepare_submit` refuses a prompt
when the session already holds an `unknown` admission, and `/discard <admission_id>` acknowledges it
(4e35169b2b, 342a55ebad). This PR was rebased onto that work and narrowed to the two cases it does
not cover. The `/discard` route, the pre-submit refusal and the related tests that this PR originally
carried were dropped in favour of upstream's.

1. **Fence lands after submit.** If the owner restarts while a prompt is being submitted, the
   pre-submit check passes, the prompt is admitted, and the restarted owner then fences the turn
   ahead of it as `unknown`. The new prompt sits `queued` behind it and the CLI waits for a
   `message.complete` that never comes (`Initializing agent...` with no end). `_pump` now watches
   the `pending` list from `session.info`; when its own admission is `queued` behind an `unknown`
   one, it withdraws the prompt with `prompt.cancel` and returns `failure_reason="unknown_execution"`
   with the same `/discard` recovery copy, instead of hanging.
2. **Queued behind another running turn.** When the prompt is queued behind an admission that is
   still running (for example an automation turn the restarted owner drains first), the CLI prints
   once that the message is queued and should not be resent. Previously it stayed silent, which is
   what led users to resend the same message into the queue.

Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing is replayed, and no turn is discarded without an explicit `/discard`.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532 (CLI + gateway paths; ACP is #139541)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: `_pump` returns `_BLOCKED` when this turn's admission is queued
  behind a lost turn (`_queued_behind_lost`); `run_conversation` withdraws it with `prompt.cancel`
  and returns the `/discard` recovery. `_running_ahead` drives the one-time "Queued: another turn is
  still running" notice.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`, `agent/error_surface.py`: `unknown_execution` is a gateway-layer
  site failure code, so the CLI shows the recovery copy as written instead of classifying it as a
  provider failure.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`, `gateway/session_ingress.py`: the `Session … paused:
  unknown_execution` log warning names the exact operator command (`hermes [-p <profile>] sessions
  discard <id>`) instead of an unnamed operator.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_cli_lost_turn.py`: 2 passed. With this PR's
  `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py` reverted to base, the file never finishes (stopped by a 200 s outer
  timeout, rc=124): the fenced prompt waits on a completion that never comes.
- Affected suites: `test_gateway_agent.py`, `test_gateway_cli_commands.py`,
  `test_native_pause_notice.py`, `test_failed_turn_site_codes.py`, `test_failed_turn_chat_copy.py`,
  `test_session_authority*.py`, `test_unknown_automation_settles.py`, `test_commands.py`,
  `test_gateway_command_parity*.py`, `test_desktop_slash_registry.py`: all pass (116 passed).
- `scripts/check`: 13 checks, ok.

- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this is not a duplicate.
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore reasoning display after gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Restore the classic CLI's reasoning display preference when its existing connection reconnects to the gateway.

The gateway's `live.show_reasoning` flag is intentionally session-scoped and in-memory. `GatewayAgent.reasoning_callback` sends it and caches the last `(session_id, enabled)` pair. After a gateway restart the CLI keeps that cache, but the new owner has no flag. `GatewayConnection._resubscribe` restores the subscription without restoring the preference. Replies still stream, but live reasoning no longer does; the CLI can subsequently render `last_reasoning` in its end-of-turn fallback box, below the streamed reply. Restarting the CLI masks the problem by sending the flag again.

Keep the preference in this viewer's per-session state and replay it after a successful resume, before the reconnected socket becomes ready. Use the asynchronous client already on that loop, not the blocking `connection.call`. Preserve explicit hidden preferences too; sessions without a preference are untouched. A restore failure follows the existing reconnect failure path, so no prompt is silently admitted before restoration. No prompt replay, persistent config write, transcript mutation, or new protocol/config field is introduced.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (classic CLI reconnect regression).
Related: #139470 restores the same live flag on ACP reattachment. This PR changes the classic CLI only; it does not duplicate ACP, Desktop, reasoning-effort persistence, or commentary routing work.

Searched open and closed/merged issues and PRs for the symptom, `show_reasoning`, reconnect/restart, and the cache symbol; checked the tracker body and comments. No existing classic CLI fix for this path was found.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: remember the callback-derived preference on the session's shared viewer state.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: restore that preference after resuming each retained session, before readiness/new requests. A refused resume is still skipped, with no config write for that session.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py`: exercise shown/hidden preferences, first-turn ordering, same-connection write deduplication, and independent preferences for multiple sessions. Update the existing lost-turn test for the added restore request.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py`: use a real disposable gateway daemon and a loopback fake model, restart the daemon, and verify the same CLI connection/agent receives reasoning before answer deltas on its next turn.

## How to Test

Interactive reproduction:
1. Start a classic CLI session with streaming and `/reasoning show`.
2. Finish a turn, then restart its gateway while keeping the CLI open.
3. Ask another question in the same CLI. Expected: live reasoning still arrives before the reply, without restarting the CLI. On the base, the owner loses its flag and reasoning falls back to the end-of-turn box.

Automated validation on Linux, Python 3.14.7:
- Base: `0f3eac0b8f7ccef9c469c9e9469c5b08e538d8f4`.
- New regression cases on the unchanged base: **3 failed**, at missing reasoning callbacks / missing restore writes (not collection failures).
- The real-daemon restart test also fails on a clean archive of the base: the second turn returns the answer but receives no reasoning (`'' != 'REASONING-BEFORE-THE-ANSWER'`). With the fix it passes, retaining the same connection/agent and receiving all reasoning before the first answer delta. No production gateway or external model is used.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_agent.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_session_store.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_disconnect_outcome.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tools.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_chat_blocking_controls.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py --file-retries 0 -j 2`: **126 passed, 0 failed** (7 files, no retries).
- `python scripts/check --base origin/main`: **12 checks passed**.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep a session's subagents visible after its cached parent agent is rebuilt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A session's delegated children disappear from `subagent.list` once the gateway rebuilds the cached agent for that route, while the children are still running. `subagent.tail`, steer and interrupt then report the child as unavailable, so the Ctrl+T monitor and the dock show an empty roster for work that is still in progress.

Root cause: `gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` ties a child to the session only through the parent agent object (`registry._is_descendant_of(record['agent'], parent)`). A child keeps a weakref to the agent that spawned it. After a cache rebuild, `authority.agent(ref)` returns the replacement agent, the old weakref no longer matches it, and the roster comes back empty. The lineage fallbacks don't cover this either, because they only list rows read-only.

The fix carries the gateway's own `LiveSession` record, which survives a parent rebuild but not a replaced conversation, and matches on that exact object:

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`: `wire()` binds the turn's `LiveSession` on the agent as `_canonical_session_owner` (added to `_TURN_ATTRS`, so `restore()` puts back the previous value).
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `_build_child_agent` copies it onto the child when it is built, because a detached child can register after the parent turn has unwired.
- `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`: `_register_child` stores that record as `owner_session_record`, and nested children inherit it.
- `gateway/session_ancillary.py`: `_owner_objects` passes the session's `LiveSession`, and `subagent_records` checks `record['owner_session_record'] is session_owner` before the existing parent and lineage matches.

This keeps the existing rule that an identical durable session id never transfers access to old objects. The match is object identity on `LiveSession`, so a different `LiveSession` that reuses the same id gets an empty roster. A child that carries no token is still invisible after the rebuild (`owned` in the fixture).

Overlap checked: #114420 carries owner authority across a background-thread hop, #116204 shares the roster across processes, and #135874 lists sibling sessions in `delegate_task(action=list)`. None of them covers a parent cache rebuild within the same process.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. The searches I ran are listed under Overlap checked above.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`, `gateway/session_ancillary.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`, as described above.
- `tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py` (new, 2 tests):
  - The roster and controls keep the owned child after a parent rebuild and after the parent is gone. A foreign token and an unstamped child stay hidden. Reusing the durable id with another `LiveSession` returns nothing.
  - A child registered after the parent unwired still records the session owner.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/ancillary_reads_peer.py` (real gateway daemon probe used by `test_session_ancillary_reads.py`): adds a `rebound` child stamped with the session's `LiveSession` under an old parent. It is listed and tailable, and after `_agent_cache[route]` is replaced with a new generation it is still the only child listed. `owned` (no token) stays hidden, as before.

## How to Test

1. Plant only the test hunks on `main`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary_reads.py` gives 3 failed, including `assert [] == ['owned']` and `test_activity_snapshot_requires_current_owner_objects`.
2. Same command on this branch: 4 passed.
3. Related files (`tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary*.py`, `test_subagent*.py`, `test_local_viewer*.py`, `tests/tools/test_delegate*.py`, 51 files): 418 passed, 0 failed.
4. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks ok, 0 blocking health findings.

I've been running this change on a long-lived gateway since mid-October. Before it, a rebuilt parent left the CLI subagent monitor empty while its children kept running. With it, the children stay listed and steerable.

## Summary

Consolidates the terminal approval work from #98868, #99201, #99260 and #100111 into this existing PR, together with the terminal `.git-credentials` portion of #99182. Rebased onto main `e96221fa73d2dac7ba9f3bc5a8b866b3d0fc188e`.

- Share the shell startup inventory with file safety; add credential-directory write targets and `.git-credentials`, with exact filename boundaries for the added files and subtree boundaries for directories.
- Recognize `.envrc` and structurally parse sed options, programs and operands, including long-option abbreviations, reordered options, executable shell carriers and bounded IFS forms. Keep inert quoted text, reads and ordinary operand controls safe.
- Require independent consent for sed findings alongside unrelated dangerous actions in a mixed command; a remembered sed approval does not suppress another action's prompt.
- Extend the existing HOME normalizer with shell-word provenance, supported POSIX/Windows spellings and lexical normalization. Preserve literal quotes and unresolved expansions rather than guessing runtime paths.
- Extend the existing Hermes credential-store inventory and restrict global-root folding to credential-store tails. Preserve current upstream protections and profile behavior.
- Retain the original source PR regression matrices and add approval-caller, carrier, filename and consolidation controls.

The media-delivery changes remain on #99182. No workflow files changed.

Used `scripts/run_tests.sh` with an isolated PM-built test interpreter and disposable Hermes home/runtime directories. Classified command strings were never executed.

prs.title: feat(telegram): plugins can send HTML widgets and receive their taps (Bot API 10.4)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Telegram Bot API 10.4 (9 Nov 2026) added HTML widgets: a message with sandboxed HTML/CSS/JS, two data packets of up to 1 KB the bot rewrites in place, and taps that reach the bot as a `widget_query` update. A Hermes plugin could not use them through public surfaces: the adapter subscribes with `Update.ALL_TYPES`, and python-telegram-bot 22.8 (Bot API 10.0) does not list `widget_query`, so Telegram never delivers a tap; the three new methods exist only as raw `do_api_request` calls on the adapter's private `_bot`.

This PR adds the missing pieces along the lines that already exist:

- the adapter asks Telegram for `widget_query` too (polling and webhook), on top of PTB's own list;
- a tap becomes a `gateway_platform_event` with `event_type="widget_query"` and `query_id`, `chat_id`, `message_id`, `data`, `thread_id`, `type` and `widget_id`, through the same group-99 observer and gateway authorization as reactions and edits: the source is the sender in the widget's chat; a widget in an inline message has no chat and is dropped. `type` is Telegram's `WidgetQueryType` object as sent (`data`, `sign_data` or `sent_transaction`, with the TON wallet fields Telegram adds to them), `widget_id` names a shared widget;
- a query carries no topic id, so the adapter remembers the topic Telegram reports in `sendWidget`'s reply (in process, bounded, keyed by chat and message) and puts it in `thread_id` and in the authorized source, which keys a private-chat or forum topic as its own session; a widget sent before a restart or by another process gets `None`;
- `ctx.platform_actions` gets three Telegram verbs behind the existing `gateway.platform_actions` capability: `send_widget` (returns the `message_id`; optional `thread_id`, `width` and `height`), `edit_widget_data` (`modified: False` when Telegram answers "message is not modified"), `answer_widget_query`. Other platforms answer `unsupported_platform_action`.

Nothing changes for plugins that do not use widgets; the one behaviour change is an extra update type in `allowed_updates`, which PTB routes to no core handler, only to the observer. A PTB release that models the type works unchanged: its list is not extended twice and a native `widget_query` object is read through `to_dict()`.

A dashboard plugin on a production bot already runs this round trip (send, rewrite the data periodically, answer a "Refresh now" tap), today through private calls; this PR is what lets such a plugin stay on public API.

## Related Issue

Implements #152092

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_widgets.py` (new): the update types with `widget_query`, the query out of an update (`api_kwargs` today, a native object later), the `widget_query` event envelope and the sender/chat identities, the bounded topic memory of sent widgets, and the three Bot API calls
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: `allowed_updates` at both polling and webhook start; a `widget_query` branch in `_normalize_platform_event` and `_source_for_platform_event_auth`, with the widget's topic; `send_widget` (remembers the topic Telegram reports) / `edit_widget_data` / `answer_widget_query`
- `hermes_cli/platform_actions.py`: the three verbs; `hermes_cli/plugin_capabilities.py`, `hermes_cli/plugins_context.py`: capability text and facade docstring

prs.body:
## Summary
- avoid calling `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()` for capability-only config reads on macOS
- report macOS Keychain-backed encryption as available without initializing the `Hermes Safe Storage` item
- preserve the guarded runtime probe on Linux and other platforms

## Why
Electron documents/implements `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()` on macOS by creating the app's Safe Storage Keychain entry. Desktop calls the probe while sanitizing connection settings and the connection registry, so users with plain owner-only cockpit tokens can get a new Keychain item—and repeated password prompts—without saving any encrypted secret.

Reference: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/45328
