prs.title: fix(security): fold single-segment POSIX homes so /root writes are flagged
prs.body:
## Reviewed fresh-base update

Exact head: `ee3c326dbccdc852f5bea8e707ba9405e62139de`. Tested base: `10c6188de188871f64a88dd95bc6b262adb0c307`. This section supersedes earlier heads, bases and verification claims below.

### Scope

Use the shared shell-word scanner to fold whole HOME operands, including single-component POSIX homes. Preserve quote/escape provenance and supported drive, UNC and mixed-separator spellings using one shared projected word. Keep literal reads/copy-out, unresolved expansions, ordinary names, outside-HOME boundaries and the existing Windows SSH fallback unchanged. Preserve quoted/spaced copy destinations.

### Actual verification

Exact-head canonical HOME gate: **2,950 passed, 0 failed** (2 files: 2,949 committed HOME cases plus one task-owned execution-contract test). The combined preservation matrix covers QH1 literal18, QH2 unresolved-native4, QH3 read9, mixed12, paired ordinary/read/mutation controls and original root exclusions. Independent component SPEC and QUALITY passed on source `4dd7df97566626a32cdf444e485a4867f63b9a29`; the rebased source/test files are byte-identical. Reproduce the committed matrix with `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_approval_home_paths.py`.

The six-component local composition passed independent SPEC then QUALITY on `78cff3273037320926303d12ddcf285adf99c5dd`. The conflict-free newer-main replay `1f7edb4d85529693c55bd328badeee1e6620a65e` preserves every reviewed source/test byte and every upstream byte. Its completed canonical **44-file** run records **5,852 passed, 18 failed, 1 skipped**, exit 1. The fresh pristine **10-file media/adjacent** comparison records **353 passed, 18 failed, 1 skipped**, exit 1. Complete failure-node sets are identical. Different selections mean the pass totals are not a like-for-like full-suite comparison. Changed tool-batch and runner tests passed in both arms. These are local results, not GitHub CI or a native-Windows certification.

### Limits

Inherited limits remain explicit: the 18 synthetic `/root` media/cron fixture failures, downstream nested copy-in detection, conservative single-quoted `$HOME` classification, and the existing normalization performance advisory. Media identity checks do not eliminate TOCTOU, inaccessible-store identity or unavailable remote-hardlink identity. Displayed shell strings are classifier inputs, not executed payloads. No merge or workflow rerun is part of this update.

### Exact-head GitHub workflow snapshot

At publication read-back, all listed workflows required repository approval and had zero jobs. No workflow executed this head, and no rerun was requested.

- [CI run 36980466129](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36980466129): `action_required`, jobs `0`.
- [Docker Build, Test, and Publish run 36980464937](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36980464937): `action_required`, jobs `0`.
- [Nix flake check run 36980465073](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36980465073): `action_required`, jobs `0`.

<details>
<summary>Historical description and earlier verification (superseded)</summary>

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #84639.

`_home_prefix_fold_regex` required at least two path components below the root, so `/home/alice` folded to `~/` but `/root` did not. Detection folds absolute home paths *before* pattern matching precisely so the `~`-anchored sensitive-path patterns also catch absolute spellings. Without the fold, running as root left absolute-path writes unmatched while the `~` and `$HOME` spellings were caught.

Measured with `HOME=/root` on unmodified `main` — absolute flagged **0/3**, tilde **3/3**:

| Command | `dangerous` |
|---|---|
| `echo ssh-rsa ... >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` | **False** |
| `echo ssh-rsa ... >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` | True |
| `echo key \| tee -a /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` | **False** |
| `echo key \| tee -a ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` | True |
| `cp /tmp/evil /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` | **False** |
| `cp /tmp/evil ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` | True |

**The scope is wider than SSH.** Sweeping twelve sensitive families found five bypassed: `.ssh/authorized_keys`, `.ssh/id_rsa`, `.netrc`, `.bashrc`, and `.profile`. The last two are shell-rc persistence vectors that execute on next login, not just credential reads. After this change, **0/12** families differ between absolute and tilde spellings.

**An existing test already caught this.** `TestSensitiveRedirectPattern::test_redirect_to_sensitive_target` asserts `Path.home() / ".ssh" / "authorized_keys"` is flagged; it fails on unmodified `main` under `HOME=/root` and passes here. The suite has been detecting this on any root-homed runner, which may be why it went unnoticed on normal-user CI.

## Approach

A new `_is_posix_absolute_home()` lets a single-segment POSIX home fold while preserving the guard's original purpose — a degenerate root must never fold, or folding would rewrite every absolute path in the command.

| Path | Folds? | Changed? |
|---|---|---|
| `/root` | yes | **← this fix** |
| `/home/alice`, `/Users/alice`, `C:\Users\alice`, `C:/Users/alice`, `//server/share` | yes | no |
| `/`, `//`, `""`, `C:\`, `C:/`, `\\server`, `/C:` | no | no |

Only single-segment POSIX homes change behaviour. All 14 boundaries are asserted in the new tests.

## How Has This Been Tested?

`tests/tools/test_approval.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_approvals_suggest.py` → **135 passed, 0 failed** via `bash scripts/run_tests.sh`.

Two controls, because a security fix that only ever answers "dangerous" is not a fix:

- **Positive** — reverting `tools/approval.py` to `main` while keeping the new tests fails **4** (three new, plus the pre-existing redirect test). The tests discriminate rather than merely passing.
- **Negative** — eight ordinary commands under `/root` (`cat /root/notes.txt`, `cp report.txt /root/reports/out.txt`, `git -C /root/repo status`, `echo hi > /root/tmp.log`, …) stay unflagged **0/8**. The fold does not turn routine work into an approval prompt.

Five new tests in `TestSingleSegmentHomeFolding` cover: absolute sensitive writes are flagged; absolute and tilde verdicts agree; ordinary `/root` paths stay unflagged; degenerate roots are still refused; real homes still fold.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🔧 Refactor

## Related Issue

Fixes #84639 (`type/security`, `P2`, was labelled `needs-repro` — repro posted on the issue).

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective (with a positive control proving they fail without it)
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] Comments explain the non-obvious part (why a degenerate root must still be refused)

## Note on scope

Deliberately limited to the approval fold. Two `tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py` cases also fail under `HOME=/root`, but through a different mechanism — `validate_media_delivery_path`, where the tests use `/root/...` as a *container* path that collides with the real host home. That is a test-fixture issue rather than a guard hole (called directly, the denylist correctly refuses `/root/.hermes/auth.json`), so it does not belong in a security fix. Happy to file it separately.


</details>

prs.title: fix(config): preserve surviving YAML list entry formatting
prs.body:
Removing a YAML list entry can transfer its quotes and comment to a surviving sibling. This pairs surviving values with their original nodes before merging changed entries. Integers, floats and booleans stay distinct, including inside nested lists and mappings.

This preserves PRATHAMESH75's [offered fix](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/147594#issuecomment-6560303318), authorship and source trailer. The regressions exercise the public config writer, removal and restoration, unrelated state, scalar kinds, and a second unchanged save. Fixes #147594.

Rebased onto main `4162ecf11f61`; signed head `1b097bb34d26` preserves all three patches, authors and commit messages. On macOS arm64 / Python 3.14.9:

- All 38 tests across the round-trip writer, public list-survivor and config-comment suites pass through `scripts/run_tests.sh` on this head.
- All 19 native `scripts/check` checks pass on this head, with no blocking or advisory health findings.
- The seven public-writer regressions previously failed on main `bc62aec38d61`: surviving entries inherited the removed entry's comment. That RED receipt predates this rebase.

The existing PM test interpreter was reused without changing its dependencies or the project's lockfiles. A fresh dependency build, Linux/Windows and the full suite remain unverified; the running installation is unchanged. [Hosted checks](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/147999/checks).

Pairing takes O(old length × new length) time and memory. Restoring an entry already removed from disk still needs a saved preimage.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add sol-pi (SoL-Pi ObservationPack + Action Fusion)
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/sol-pi.yaml`, which lists [kvnloo/sol-pi-hermes](https://github.com/kvnloo/sol-pi-hermes/tree/6ee9dab731c1f4c719e93ae6f9ab7ad3a5f01dca) pinned at `6ee9dab7`. The plugin ports two mechanisms from NVIDIA's [SoL-Pi](https://github.com/NVlabs/SoL-Pi) (MIT) to Hermes' public plugin surface.

## What it does

| Mechanism | Behaviour | Hermes surface |
|---|---|---|
| **ObservationPack** | A tool result over 10 KiB goes to the model in full on two requests. After that, the outgoing request carries a placeholder with the id, size and a 1 KiB head/tail excerpt, and the model pages the full text back with `obs_recall`. The stored transcript keeps every byte. | `llm_request` middleware (rewrites only the per-call request copy), plus the `obs_recall` tool |
| **Action Fusion** | `sol_pi_write` / `sol_pi_patch` call Hermes' own `write_file` / `patch`. With `then_run` they also run one follow-up command, so an edit and its check take one model turn. | Tools dispatched through Hermes' registry, so commands run via `terminal` and its approvals |

Both mechanisms are off until the user enables them in `sol-pi.json` in the Hermes home.

The placeholder is decided by a fixed boundary: a row gets it once two later assistant turns exist. It carries no timestamp, so it is byte-identical on every later request and comes back the same after a restart or resume. This is the cache-boundary property that [teknium's note on #107731](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107731#issuecomment-5798362641) asks for.

## Related work

- #107731 by @lorencato23 proposes the same wire-only projection in core, as an opt-in `assemble_api_request` pass. This listing doesn't compete with it. The plugin lets people use the SoL-Pi design today through public hooks. If #107731 lands, ObservationPack becomes redundant and I'll drop it from the plugin.
- [`cmi`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/plugin-catalog/cmi.yaml) and [`breadcrumbs`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/plugin-catalog/breadcrumbs.yaml) are context engines. sol-pi registers no engine and leaves Hermes' compressor in charge.
- I searched open issues for related feature requests (ObservationPack, large tool output, tool-result placeholder/recall, fused write+run) and found none.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Writes:** archived tool results and an append-only `ledger.jsonl` under `<hermes home>/sol-pi/<session>/`, with directories at 0700 and files at 0600. The home comes from `get_hermes_home()`, so each profile gets its own archive.
- **Reads:** `sol-pi.json` in the Hermes home, and, for `then_run`, the file the tool just wrote.
- **Commands:** `then_run` executes the model's command through the `terminal` tool, so Hermes' approvals apply to it.
- **Network, telemetry, credentials:** none.

## Checks at the pin

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes plugins validate <checkout> --install-deps` | Validation passed. Security scan `safe`, no core override, declared tools and middleware match. |
| `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/sol-pi.yaml` | `OK: 1 file(s) valid` |
| `hermes plugins install kvnloo/sol-pi-hermes --ref 6ee9dab7…` in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, then `enable` | Installs at `6ee9dab731c1f4c719e93ae6f9ab7ad3a5f01dca` and is listed `enabled 0.2.0` |
| End-to-end check on the installed copy (`discover_plugins()` + `apply_llm_request_middleware()`, one 16 KB tool row, 4 requests) | Tool content bytes per request: `16000, 16000, 1421, 1421`. Stored copy untouched. `obs_recall` returns the first 7,960 bytes with `next_offset`. |
| Plugin's own suite (`python -m unittest discover -s tests`) | OK |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_catalog*.py`, `test_plugins_catalog_requires_hermes.py`, `test_plugins_cmd_catalog.py`, `tests/ci/test_plugin_catalog_ci_confinement.py` | 76 passed, 44 errors, the same counts with and without this file. The 44 errors come from my `env -i` sandbox (git fixtures), not from the entry. |

> [!NOTE]
> At `0.23.1` the runtime manifest loader logs `unknown manifest field(s) ignored: provides_middleware` for `plugin.yaml`, but `plugins validate` fails without the field ("undeclared middleware registered"). I kept the field because validate is the admission gate. The warning is harmless, and I can open an issue for it if that helps.

`requires_hermes: ">=0.23.0"` matches `plugin.yaml`. `llm_request` middleware exists at `v0.22.3` too, but I only tested 0.23.x.

issues.title: [capability] Rootless Podman as a session driver skill (/add-podman) on the driver seam

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New capability or improvement

labels.name: delivery/skill
labels.description: Delivered as a skill; independent of kind

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Running NanoClaw on Linux with Docker means the host user is in the `docker` group, which is root-equivalent. Rootless Podman removes that, but the open Podman PRs (#332, #2230, #2292, #2421, #2667) all predate the session driver seam and patch core paths or setup instead.

### What should be possible?

An `/add-podman` skill that installs a Podman session driver the same way gateway providers install: code and tests in the skill's `payload/`, plus one registration in `src/drivers/installed.ts`. A user picks it at setup; Docker users carry no Podman code.

Before writing the PR: is a driver skill the shape you want, and should it live in `payload/` like the gateway skills?

### What kind of skill is this?

Unsure

### Who benefits?

Linux operators who do not want a root-equivalent `docker` group, and hosts that already run Podman (Fedora, RHEL, hardened servers).

### What have you tried?

I have run a rootless Podman driver on my own install (podman 5.7, Linux). It wraps the existing Docker driver and translates the CLI dialect at the process boundary, so it does not fork the Docker realization. Differences it has to handle, each of which fails silently if untranslated:
- `ps --format '{{.Label "x"}}'` is a template error on Podman (containers/podman#20957); `{{index .Labels "x"}}` works.
- `events` documents use `Status` and top-level `Attributes`, and the terminal statuses are `died`/`remove`; untranslated, every event parses to null and supervision falls back to the 60 s sweep.
- `events --filter label=` ORs repeated label filters (`ps` ANDs them), so one install receives another install's container events.
- Error text differs, so `normalizeDockerError` classifies a missing runtime or image as `unknown` instead of retryable.
- `--userns=keep-id` is needed so session DBs written in the container stay readable on the host.

### What would this change?

New skill folder only: `.claude/skills/add-podman/` with `SKILL.md`, `REMOVE.md`, and `payload/` (the driver, about 620 lines, plus about 540 lines of tests). Core changes: none, if the driver registry already covers driver selection; otherwise a small seam change, discussed first.

### How could we test it?

The driver runs the existing driver conformance suite (`src/drivers/conformance.test.ts`) through `fake-cli`, plus dialect-translation unit tests. A fresh-clone apply/remove check per the skill guidelines

### Can you help maintain it?

- [ ] I can help maintain this skill.

issues.title: fix(setup/onecli): restrict OneCLI admin API and Postgres to loopback after install

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Maintainer-set

labels.name: PR: Fix
labels.description: Bug fix

issues.body:
## Summary

On bare-metal Linux, OneCLI's installer auto-detects the `docker0` bridge IP and binds all three of its published ports to it — including the admin API (`:10254`) and Postgres (`:5432`), not just the proxy gateway (`:10255`). Because NanoClaw runs agent containers on that same bridge by design, every agent container can reach the unauthenticated admin API and Postgres without any misconfiguration on the operator's part.

From any NanoClaw agent container:

```
$ curl http://172.17.0.1:10254/api/agents
HTTP 200 — returns every agent's access token, no auth required

$ (echo > /dev/tcp/172.17.0.1/5432) && echo "postgres reachable"
postgres reachable  (default creds: onecli/onecli)
```

This is tracked upstream at **onecli/onecli#268**.

## Proposed fix

Add a `hardenOneCliBinds()` step to `setup/onecli.ts` that runs after the OneCLI installer completes. It rewrites `~/.onecli/docker-compose.yml` to pin `:10254` (admin API) and `:5432` (Postgres) to `127.0.0.1`, while leaving `:10255` (proxy gateway) on the bridge IP so agent containers can still reach it. Then restarts the OneCLI containers to apply.

- **Idempotent** — a marker comment prevents double-patching on setup re-runs
- **Fail-safe** — if the compose layout doesn't match the expected pattern (i.e. OneCLI changed their file), logs a warning and skips rather than silently mangling the file
- **`--reuse` mode** — does not rewrite; detects the unsafe bind and emits a warning instead
- Adds `HARDENED` + `HARDEN_NOTE` fields to `status.json` so it's observable

## Scope

~80–100 lines including vitest unit tests covering: vanilla compose patched correctly, already-patched no-op, unknown layout no-op-with-warning, missing file no-op-with-warning.

## Related

- Upstream issue: https://github.com/onecli/onecli/issues/268
- Upstream auth hardening issue: https://github.com/onecli/onecli/issues/263

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

306fd1b7

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

`deleteSession()` in `src/db/sessions.ts` runs a bare `DELETE FROM sessions`. `pending_questions.session_id` and `pending_approvals.session_id` reference `sessions(id)` with no `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and foreign keys are on. So the delete fails with `SqliteError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` whenever the session still has an unanswered `ask_user_question` or a pending approval.

The caller I can reach on a normal install is `ncl tasks delete`. For a task with its own isolated session, it removes the session mailbox and folder first, then calls `deleteSession()`, which throws. On a retry the mailbox is gone, so the command reports `no live task matched`. The `sessions` row and its pending rows stay in the central DB for good.

### What did you expect?

`deleteSession()` removes the session's pending questions and approvals with it, the way `ncl groups delete` (#2525) and `ncl messaging-groups delete` (#4103) already cascade these rows.

### How can we reproduce it?

Smallest reproduction, as a test in `src/db/db-v2.test.ts` (fresh migrated test DB):
1. `createSession({ id: 'sess-1', ... })`
2. `createPendingQuestion({ question_id: 'q-1', session_id: 'sess-1', ... })`
3. `await deleteSession('sess-1')` → `SqliteError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`

Same with `createPendingApproval({ session_id: 'sess-1', ... })` instead of step 2.

End-to-end: schedule a task whose prompt calls `ask_user_question`, let it run, do not answer, then run `ncl tasks delete <task-id>`.

A fix with a regression test follows as a PR.

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64

issues.title: Setup can't fetch the hardened image after a Node upgrade: the docker credential helper points at the old Node

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main `62dc09057`. Same code in v2026.10.0 and v2026.11.0-beta.1.

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

Setup stopped at the sandbox step while it fetched the hardened image:

```
error getting credentials - err: fork/exec /Users/<user>/.local/bin/docker-credential-nanoclaw: no such file or directory, out: ``
```

Setup then said "Couldn't fetch the sandbox image. Check your connection and that authentication finished". Neither is the cause: Docker fails before it uses the connection or the sign-in. The helper file is there too.

Reproduced on macOS (arm64) and on Ubuntu 24.04 (x86_64).

### What did you expect?

The fetch works after a Node upgrade. If the helper really cannot start, the error says so and how to fix it.

### How can we reproduce it?

On a test machine or VM. No account is needed, because Docker fails before it asks for a credential.

1. Copy Node into a folder with a version in its name, for example `~/versions/node/v1.0.0/bin/node`. With Homebrew Node, also copy `lib/libnode.*.dylib` into `~/versions/node/v1.0.0/lib/`.
2. Install the helper with that Node: `PATH="$HOME/versions/node/v1.0.0/bin:$PATH" pnpm exec tsx setup/install-cred-helper.ts --registry-host registry.invalid`
3. Add to `.env`: `NANOCLAW_HARDENED_IMAGE=true` and `NANOCLAW_AGENT_IMAGE_REF=registry.invalid/nanoclaw/agent@sha256:` followed by 64 zeros.
4. Rename the folder, as an upgrade does: `mv ~/versions/node/v1.0.0 ~/versions/node/v1.0.1`
5. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step container`. It fails with the error above.

### Cause

Setup writes the full path of the Node it runs on into the first line of `docker-credential-nanoclaw` (`setup/install-cred-helper.ts`, `renderHelper` with `process.execPath`). With Homebrew that path has the version in it, for example `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node@22/<version>/bin/node`, and Homebrew removes that folder at the next Node upgrade. Docker then cannot start the helper.

Setup only writes the helper at sign-in, and it skips sign-in on a machine that is already signed in. So nothing repairs the helper before the next fetch.

The same happens when a version manager removes the old Node, or when two systems share one home folder. A Node at a fixed path, such as `/usr/bin/node` from apt, is not affected.

### Workaround

In the NanoClaw folder, re-create the helper, then run setup again:

```bash
pnpm exec tsx setup/install-cred-helper.ts --bin-dir "$HOME/.local/bin"
bash nanoclaw.sh
```

### Fix

#4341 makes the installed helper find Node itself: it runs on the Node setup ran on while that is there, else on the Node on PATH. Setup and updates rewrite a helper written by an older version.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Reproduced on macOS 26.6 (arm64) and Ubuntu 24.04 (x86_64)

### Install or update path

Standard setup with nanoclaw.sh

### Docker version

Docker 29.9.3 (macOS), 29.1.3 (Ubuntu)

### Channel or interface

Not channel-specific

### Agent provider

Not provider-specific

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
Pulling <registry>/nanoclaw/agent@sha256:<digest>...
error getting credentials - err: fork/exec /Users/<user>/.local/bin/docker-credential-nanoclaw: no such file or directory, out: ``

Pull failed for <registry>/nanoclaw/agent@sha256:<digest>.
  If the registry needs credentials, run `docker login <registry>` and
  retry — this script deliberately has no credential handling of its own.
ERROR Container image pull failed exitCode=1 errorCode="image_pull_failed"
```

issues.title: [bug] A chat turn that acknowledges, works, then ends with only an `<internal>` note never answers and is not nudged
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit
dad1aadf (main, 2026-11-14). First seen on an older install.

### Host platform
Linux

### What happened?
A user asked a question in a channel. The agent:

1. sent "Checking… one moment." with `send_message`,
2. ran web lookups and a memory update,
3. ended the turn with a final output that was only
   `<internal>I answered them. Not free yet; open 9:30 to 4.</internal>`.

The whole answer sat in the `<internal>` note. The user received only the acknowledgement. No nudge fired and nothing was logged as undelivered.

The wrap-nudge cannot see this case: it fires on unwrapped final text, and an `<internal>`-only final has none after stripping. An empty final behaves the same way.

### What did you expect?
The agent is prompted once, the way it is when the final text is unwrapped prose after a tool send (the informed nudge from #3918), so it can send the answer or reply `<internal>done</internal>`.

### How can we reproduce it?
Stub events through `processQuery` (mid-turn delivery on), destination `discord-main` seeded. `M` is `<message to="discord-main">`.

| Events | Delivered | Nudges |
|---|---|---|
| `send_message` row "Checking. One moment.", text and result `<internal>I answered them: not free yet.</internal>` | the ack only | **0** |
| text `M + "Checking. One moment.</message>"`, then text and result `<internal>I answered them: not free yet.</internal>` | the ack only | **0** |
| text and result `<internal>The answer is 9:30 to 4.</internal>`, nothing sent | nothing | **0** |
| control: `send_message` row "Checking. One moment.", text and result `Not free yet; 9:30 to 4.` (unwrapped) | the ack only | 1 (informed nudge) |

All four were run against dad1aadf.

### Note on fixing it: the obvious trigger has false positives
I tried a fix and closed the PR (#4354). It nudged when a user-chat turn's final had no `<message>` block and no reply row was written after the agent's last non-delivery tool call, using a new `tool_use` provider event. An independent review found it also fires on turns that were answered or rightly silent:

- a full reply, then a bookkeeping tool call (memory save, todo list), then an `<internal>` final: structurally identical to "ack, work, silence";
- replies sent with `send_card` / `ask_user_question`, which write `chat-sdk` rows that a `kind === 'chat'` check misses;
- reaction-only turns, which the agent instructions allow as a complete response;
- native slash-command turns such as `/compact` with an empty result.

So this is a policy question more than a patch. Options I can see:

- **Narrow trigger:** nudge only when the turn sent something, then did non-delivery work, then ended block-free. This leaves silent and reaction-only turns alone, and still pays one round trip for "reply, then bookkeeping".
- **Reuse the informed nudge:** quote what was sent and offer the `done` exit, as #3918 does for unwrapped text.
- **Prompt-only:** tell the agent that an acknowledgement does not replace the answer and that `<internal>` is never sent. #3918 already added a reminder along these lines; in this incident the agent's note said "I answered them", so it believed it had.

### Channel or interface
Slack

### Agent provider
Claude

issues.title: [bug] A reply that mentions `<internal>` is withheld, and the retry is dropped without notice
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit
dad1aadf (main, 2026-11-14). First seen on an older install.

### Host platform
Linux

### What happened?
The agent wrote a normal, complete reply that talked about its own scratchpad tag, e.g.

```
<message to="dm">Then I wrote the reply inside an `<internal>` note, which never gets sent.</message>
```

The user never received it. Nothing in the host log shows a failure.

What the runner does (Claude provider, mid-turn delivery):

1. `unresolvedTailStart` treats the `<internal` in the body as an open scratchpad span, so the block is buffered for the rest of the turn and never delivered mid-turn.
2. At the result, the block is counted as missed and one nudge is pushed. The nudge says the response "was not wrapped in `<message to="name">...</message>` blocks". That is not the cause: it was wrapped.
3. The agent re-sends the same text. It parses the same way. The retry turn already used its one nudge, so the reply is dropped with no log warning and no notice to the user.

Two variants are lost with **no nudge at all**: the block with the mention is in a non-final assistant message and the final message is an `<internal>...</internal>` note, with or without an earlier delivered block.

A variant that mangles instead of losing: `wrap notes in <internal>...</internal> tags` inside a message body delivers `wrap notes in  tags`.

### What did you expect?
Either the reply is delivered, or the agent is told the real reason so the retry can succeed, or the user sees that a reply was lost. Not silence.

### How can we reproduce it?
Stub events through `processQuery` (mid-turn delivery on), destination `discord-main` seeded, as in `poll-loop.midturn-resultdoor.test.ts`. `M` is `<message to="discord-main">`.

| Events | Delivered | Nudges |
|---|---|---|
| text `B`, result `B`, text `B`, result `B` where `B` = ``M + "That sat in an `<internal>` note.</message>"`` | nothing | 1 ("not wrapped") |
| same, after an earlier `send_message` row "On it." | "On it." only | 1 ("Your final text was not delivered — not wrapped") |
| text ``M + "Notes live in `<internal>` tags.</message>\n<internal>done</internal>"``, same as result | nothing | 1 ("not wrapped") |
| text `M + "On it.</message>"`, text ``M + "Notes live in `<internal>` tags.</message>"``, text `<internal>done</internal>`, same as result | "On it." only | **0** |
| text ``M + "Notes live in `<internal>` tags.</message>"``, text `<internal>done</internal>`, same as result | nothing | **0** |

All five were run against dad1aadf.

### Note on fixing it: relaxing the parser leaks scratchpad
I tried two parser changes and closed both PRs (#4353). An independent review with differential fuzzing found each delivers private `<internal>` content that `main` never delivers:

- **"An `<internal>` inside a complete `<message>` block is body text."** Leaks when an unmatched `<message>` open precedes an unclosed `<internal>` whose notes quote a draft: ``M + "part one "``, then ``"<internal>SECRET draft: " + M + "DRAFT</message> not sure"`` delivers the scratchpad.
- **"An inline-code `` `<internal>` `` is text."** Leaks when code spans sit next to a real tag (``ran `foo()`<internal>`/etc/shadow` SECRET</internal>``), when a backtick-quoted open is followed by a real close, and when a segment boundary falls at the backtick.

The text cannot distinguish a literal mention from a scratchpad the model forgot to close, so the fail-closed hold looks right. What seems fixable without touching the parser:

- **Name the cause in the nudge.** When the turn ends with a `<message>` open or close stuck in the unresolved tail, say that text after an unclosed `<internal>` is private, and to write "the internal tag" without angle brackets. Let the agent answer `<internal>done</internal>` if it was only notes.
- **Cover the two no-nudge variants** above.
- **Do not end silently on the second miss.** A fixed-text notice to the user, or at least a warning in the log.

### Channel or interface
Slack

### Agent provider
Claude

prs.title: fix(cross-session-context): mark cross-session copies in ncl sessions history
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes `ncl sessions history` show cross-session copies (`session-echo` rows) as copies, so an agent stops reading a sibling session's delivered reply as an unanswered message.

- **Problem**: history rendered every inbound row the same way. A copy of a reply that another session had already delivered looked like an incoming message with nothing after it, and a copy cut at the echo cap ended in a bare "…". An agent checking whether a request had been answered concluded it had not and told the user the answer was "still pending".
- **Fix (writers record, readers read)**: `fan.ts` and `backfill.ts` now record `echo.truncated` and `echo.delivered` in every copy (`delivered` is true only for the delivery hook's copies, written after `markDelivered`), and backfill records the sibling session each entry came from.
- **Fix (history)**: inbound history returns `channel_type` and `source_session_id`. A copy gets `echo: { fromSession, label, self, delivered, truncated }` in `--json`. In the human view its **kind** column reads `copy-delivered`, `copy-earlier` or `copy-received` (from the row, so message text cannot forge it), and its text starts with `[from <session>, <label>]`, plus `copy shortened, full text in that session (--json)` when cut. The marker sits outside the 200-char text cap.
- **Older copies**: consumed echo rows are never pruned, so copies written before these fields existed get a permanent fallback: the two old cut shapes (500 + "…"; backfill's newest entry at exactly 4000) and the delivery-hook surfaces, with those caps fixed as literals.
- **Out of scope**: the container formatter does not yet show `truncated` in the agent's prompt; the module's three echo-content parsers could be merged later.

<details><summary>Example</summary>

```
2026-08-01 10:00|in|copy-delivered|Pixel|[from sess-sibling, another thread with Alex] The answer is 42.
2026-08-01 10:01|in|copy-earlier|Pixel|[from sess-old, this DM, while this conversation was idle; copy shortened, full text in that session (--json)] …
```
</details>

## Related work

No issue filed. Found while tracing a false "your answer hasn't reached you yet" message: a scheduled check read a sibling session's history, saw the copy of a delivered reply as an unanswered inbound, and invented "the rest is still pending" from the echo's "…".

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

## Summary

A long reply that the bridge hard-cuts through an emoji now posts, instead of failing on Slack and never posting.

- **Problem**: `splitForLimit` cuts text with no space or newline near the limit at exactly the limit, which can land between the two halves (a surrogate pair) of an emoji. - **Out of scope**: #4322's other follow-up (a retry re-posts parts that already posted). A separate test-only PR pins it; the fix waits for #4227.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): send_message stamps the destination agent's own message
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes an agent's relayed reply return to the session that asked: `send_message` / `send_file` stop stamping an agent destination with another conversation's message.

- **Problem**: A asks B, B asks C, C answers, B passes the answer to A with `send_message`. The tool stamped `in_reply_to` with whatever started B's turn, C's message. The host's return path (`resolveTargetSession`) looks up that row's `source_session_id`, finds a session of C, rejects it, and falls back to A's newest active session. The answer lands in an unrelated conversation of A, and the session that asked never sees it.
- **Fix** (`resolveRouting` in `mcp-tools/core.ts`):
  - agent destination: the turn's stamp only when the turn is answering that same agent; otherwise `null`, so the host places the message by peer affinity (the session of A that last wrote to B, which for a relay is the one that asked);
  - channel destination: unchanged, the turn's stamp. Adapters read `in_reply_to` for email threading and chat quoting, so it must not change there.
- **Why now**: the stamp was a no-op until #2942 made it reach the host. Before that, these replies used peer affinity and routed correctly.
- **Second commit**: the first commit stamped every destination with its own latest inbound row. Review found that this let a new mail join the last mail's thread and a chat quote an unrelated message, and that it made new requests look like explicit replies. The second commit narrows the rule as above and pins both regressions with tests.
- **Out of scope**: if a second session of A messages B while B waits on C, peer affinity sends the relay to that second session. Fixing that needs B to remember which request it is answering.

<details><summary>Host doc comments</summary>

`RoutableAgentMessage.in_reply_to` and `getMostRecentPeerSourceSessionId` said the stamp is the batch's first inbound and that affinity covers a missing stamp. Both now describe the rule above.
</details>

## Related work

No issue filed. #2331 (closed) is the original wrong-session report, fixed by the three-layer return path. This is a case that path misses. The change is one function plus tests.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test src/mcp-tools/core.test.ts` in the agent image: 16 pass, 0 fail.
  - Against `main`: 2 fail (relay stamps the third agent's message; a new agent request from a chat turn stamps the chat message).
  - Against the first commit alone: 6 fail (channel sends take the channel's latest row, including the mail-thread case; agent sends take the agent's latest row).
- New container tests: relay, reply with a mid-turn follow-up, new request from a chat turn, no turn (agent); reply to the answered channel, send to another channel, send outside a turn, mail from a chat turn (channel). `sendBoth*` now checks both tool results.
- Existing `in_reply_to plumbing` tests renamed and re-seeded for the new contract (the stamp is kept on a reply to the agent that asked).
- Host: new `relay` test in `agent-route.test.ts` (a relay with no stamp lands in the asking session, not A's newer session); `agent-route` and `session-db` tests 34 pass; `pnpm run build` passes.
- Full container `bun test`: 675 pass, 1 fail: `agent mailbox context > treats an unreadable context like a pre-seam host`, which fails only when run as root (passes as `node`). Unrelated.
- CodeRabbit review of the same two commits (mirror PR in the author's fork, drsmk238/nanoclaw#1): one finding, the interleaving case already listed under **Out of scope**; no code change.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Fixed: when an agent passes another agent's answer back with send_message, the reply now reaches the session that asked instead of the newest session.
```

No image rebuild or host change: the agent-runner source is mounted read-only from the checkout at `/app/src`, so the fix takes effect when each agent container next starts.

## Security and trust boundaries

Agent sends now carry either the asking agent's own message or no stamp, so a relayed answer goes to a session of that agent that itself wrote to the sender, not to an unrelated channel session that happened to be newest. Channel stamps are unchanged.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Names `@types/node` in the root `tsconfig.json`, so TypeScript 6 and 7 keep Node globals in builds that extend it.

- **Problem**: TypeScript 6 makes `types` default to `[]`, so it stops loading `@types/node` on its own. The root build keeps Node globals only by luck: `src/` imports better-sqlite3, and its types reference node. add-opencode's `scripts/tsconfig.opencode-auth.json` extends the root but has no such import. prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a group mount of NanoClaw's own runner code, skills or plugins from silently stopping that group's agent from starting.

- **Problem**: only NanoClaw may mount those folders, read-only, and the driver's guard enforces that. But `ncl groups config add-mount` stores such a mount without complaint, and the guard then refuses every start. The only trace is a once-a-minute warning, and the person gets no reply.
- **Fix**: the guard's rule moves into `requiredMountClass` in `drivers/types.ts`. `validateSpec` and `add-mount` both call it, so there is one rule, not a copy. `add-mount` judges the path the way the mount check resolves it, and refuses a reserved path with the reason.
- **Fix**: a start refused with `denied-by-policy` or `spec-invalid` also logs one error naming the cause. The existing retry warning is unchanged, because installed skills anchor on that exact line.
- **Out of scope**: a mount of a parent folder, such as the whole checkout, read-write. That needs a new guard rule and changes behavior for some installs, so it comes as its own PR.

## Related work

No issue. Found in a live install's logs, where two sessions went silent for about 10 minutes after a group mount of the runner code.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests fail on main and pass here: `add-mount` refuses the runner code and the group's plugins folder and stores nothing; a policy refusal keeps the warning and adds the error. A retryable failure logs no error.
- Existing guard tests (`drivers/`, `mount-composition`) pass unchanged against the shared function.
- Full suite: 331 files pass; 6 `scripts/` files hit 5 s timeouts under load and pass alone (184/184). `tsc`, eslint and prettier are clean.
- No existing line is edited in `wakeContainer`'s failure path or in `groups.ts`'s imports, so downstream skills that patch those lines still apply.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Follow-up to #4341: the three points from its approving review. The first is a regression #4341 introduced.

- **Owner cannot be kept**: writing the docker credential helper keeps the old file's owner, group and mode. With a root-owned helper in a bin directory the user can write, the write gave up: setup kept the stale helper and the install at sign-in failed with EPERM. Both replace it again, as a 0755 file of the user's own.
- **Needless rewrite**: setup rewrote the helper before every pull, even one it had just written. A helper identical to what setup would write is left alone.
- **Linked source**: a helper linked to another checkout's `setup/registry/credential-helper.mjs` was rewritten at its target, a tracked file. A target that still begins with the source's own first line was never installed: the link is replaced with a copy and the source is not written. This replaces the same-inode check, which covered only this checkout.

## Related work

Follow-up to #4341. Review: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4341#pullrequestreview-5910287624

- Manual, macOS, real Docker: an older helper is rewritten once through `--step container`, `--refresh` and `container/build.sh pull`; a second run leaves the file's inode unchanged.

prs.body:
## Problem

When a Claude Code session ID becomes invalid (e.g. after a server-side expiry), `isSessionInvalid()` correctly detects it and clears the stored continuation — but the raw error was still delivered to the user as a visible chat message before the next poll could retry fresh.

After clearing the stale continuation, immediately retry the query with `continuation: undefined`. Only surface an error to the user if the retry also fails. This makes stale session recovery invisible to the user in the normal case.

## Changes

- `container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.ts` — retry fresh on stale session; only write error message if retry also fails

prs.title: fix(claude): rotate on missing transcript instead of resuming into a dead session
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code

## Description

**Impact:** when a stored continuation's transcript file no longer exists, the next
message to that session dies with `No conversation found with session ID: <uuid>` —
and every later message dies the same way. The batch is acked `completed` before
the error surfaces, so the user's message is lost, not retried. The session is
permanently bricked until something else clears the continuation.

**When:** any time a transcript disappears out from under a stored continuation —
external cleanup, a deploy that didn't carry session files over, manual deletion.
On the install where this was diagnosed, 22 sessions across 6 agent groups were in
this state.

**Cause:** `maybeRotateContinuation` treats "transcript not found" (and a failing
`stat`) as "nothing to rotate, resume normally". The SDK's resume failure then
arrives as a **result event**, not a thrown error, so `isSessionInvalid` — which
only inspects thrown errors — never fires, and the dead continuation is never
cleared (#2669 has the analysis of why result-event errors bypass the catch path).

**After this change:** the pre-resume check returns a rotate reason for a missing
or unreadable transcript, so the existing rotation path clears the continuation
and starts a fresh session — same silent fresh-start behavior the size/age
rotation already has. No archive is attempted (there is no file to archive), and
fresh sessions get the memory tree injected on startup, so this is the existing
first-class path, not a degraded one. The 11-line core is textually disjoint from
the three open rotation/recovery PRs.

**Test:** the `returns null for an unknown session id` assertion (from #2586) is
inverted — it was locking the bug in as a contract. Its defensive spirit is kept
by the replacement's extra assertions: no crash, no `conversations/` archive
written, no `.rotated-*` residue. Verified red-first (reverting the source change
fails the new test). Container suite failure set identical to base (one
pre-existing flaky timeout that passes standalone); host suite unaffected (1262
passed). The docs paragraph claiming `isSessionInvalid` handles missing
transcripts is corrected — it cannot see result-event errors.

**Related:** #1216 reports this exact symptom; #1761's own "possible fix 2" (eager
validation before resume) is what this implements. #2184 fixes the error catch
path and is complementary (prevention here, cure there); #2864 / #2865 extend
rotation the same direction and touch different files — no conflicts, happy to
rebase whichever lands second.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Starts a fresh session when the stored session's transcript is gone, instead of replying "No conversation found".

- **Problem**: Claude Code deletes transcripts after `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 days by default), but the session keeps the old continuation. The next resume fails: the raw `No conversation found with session ID: <uuid>` is sent as the reply, and the message is acked completed. `isSessionInvalid` then clears the continuation, so only that first message is lost.
- **Fix**: the pre-resume check (`rotateClaudeContinuation`) treated a missing `.jsonl` as "nothing to rotate". It now returns `transcript not found`, so the existing rotation path clears the continuation and the turn runs fresh. Only ENOENT/ENOTDIR count as missing. Any other lookup error keeps resuming, so an unreadable folder never drops a valid session. Docs updated.
- **Out of scope**: if Claude Code's cleanup deletes the file in the seconds between this check and the resume, that turn still fails as it does today. Keeping transcripts longer (#3183) is a separate retention choice.

## Related work

Fixes #1216.

Same approach as #3184 by @OowhitecatoO (credited as co-author), ported to where the check lives now, plus the two lookup guards. It would supersede #3184 and #2184. Ported onto main, #2184's retry still sends the error before the fresh reply.

prs.title: fix(setup): let the docker credential helper find Node after an upgrade
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Fetching the pre-built sandbox image no longer fails with `error getting credentials` after Node is upgraded or replaced.

- **Problem**: the docker credential helper's first line named one exact node binary (`process.execPath`, often a versioned folder). When that folder goes away, docker cannot start the helper and the pull fails before any credential is asked for. Setup rewrote the helper only at sign-in, which it skips on a machine already signed in.
- **Fix**: the installed helper starts with a `/bin/sh` header: it runs on the node setup ran on while that starts, else on the node on PATH. A path with a space or a quote works. Setup rewrites a wired helper before it pulls (container step, `--refresh`). On the update path `container/pull.sh` asks the installer to do it, and never writes or runs the file itself.
- **Out of scope**: `--step registry` status does not test that the helper starts.

## Related work

Closes #4342. Reported by a user whose setup stopped at the image fetch; reproduced on macOS and Linux.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/install-cred-helper.test.ts container/pull.test.ts`: 20 pass on macOS (bash 3.2), Node 22 and 26. Real helper source: old Node gone, a space and a quote in the path, an older helper rewritten in place and on the update path, docker's config untouched.
- `setup/` and `container/` suites: 825 pass.
- Manual, macOS, real Docker: an older helper whose Node is gone is rewritten and starts through `--step container`, `--refresh` and `container/build.sh pull`. The header also runs under Linux `sh` (dash).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

```release-note
Fetching the pre-built sandbox image no longer fails with "error getting credentials" after Node is upgraded or replaced. The docker credential helper now finds Node on its own, and setup and updates rewrite a helper from an older version.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The helper uses the `node` on PATH only when the node it was installed with is gone or cannot run; docker starts it with the caller's environment. The rewrite touches only the helper binary, never docker's config, and only when a registry is already wired to the helper. `pull.sh` reads the helper's first line and marker, then calls the installer. No credential is read, stored or sent.

prs.title: fix(cli): groups restart --id <other group> from an agent restarts the target (#3911)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`ncl groups restart --id <other group>` from an agent now restarts the target group instead of the caller.

- **Problem**: the agent branch of the restart handler ignored `--id`. It killed the caller's session and wrote the `--message` on-wake row to `<target group>/<caller session>`, a folder no session row points at. A global-scope agent got `{ restarted: 1 }` while the target never restarted (#3911).
- **Fix**: take the calling-session branch only when `--id` is the caller's own group. A foreign id goes through `restartAgentGroupContainers(id, …)`, the same path a host call uses, which already handles `--message`.
- **Out of scope**: who may target another group. Group-scope agents are still denied a foreign `--id` by `src/cli/guard.ts`, and the command stays approval-gated.

## Related work

Closes #3911

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/resources` -> 100 passed.
- New `src/cli/resources/groups-restart-foreign.test.ts`: own `--id` kills only the calling session; a foreign `--id` with `--message` calls `restartAgentGroupContainers('ag-b', …, 'check in')`, kills nothing in the caller, writes no orphan row. The foreign-id case fails on `main` without the fix.
- `pnpm run build` -> clean.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
`ncl groups restart --id <other group>` run by a global-scope agent now restarts that group instead of the agent's own session.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None changed. Reaching the foreign-id branch still needs `cli_scope: global` and admin approval; the fix only makes it act on the group the approver saw on the card.

prs.title: fix(mailbox): keep one task payload per recurring series
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops recurring tasks from growing a session's `inbound.db` by one full copy of the task payload per run.

- **Problem**: every re-arm copies the full content (prompt + script) into the next occurrence, and finished occurrences are never trimmed. Size grows as payload × runs, without bound. On a real install, one 21 KB prompt on a `*/10` cron reached 238 MB over 11k runs.
- **Fix**: inside the existing `armNextTask` transaction, the content of the series' older finished occurrences (`completed`/`failed`, recurrence already cleared, `seq` below the new occurrence) is replaced with `{"superseded":true}`.
- **Why rows stay**: `getTaskStats` (runs, failed runs, last run) and `trailingFailedRuns` (script-failure auto-pause) count rows by status. Deleting rows would change both; replacing only the payload changes neither.
- **Why nothing notices**: once a later occurrence exists, every content reader resolves to the newest row of the series: `getTask`, `listLiveTasks`, `findTaskBySeriesSlug`, `updateTask` (future rows only), and the re-arm itself (it reads the just-completed row before compacting). Retries only touch `pending`/`processing` rows. `sessions history` already renders task rows as empty text, because task content has no `text` field.
- **Existing installs**: a series' backlog is compacted on its next re-arm. No migration is needed.
- **Out of scope**: reclaiming file size. SQLite reuses the freed pages, so the file stops growing. `VACUUM` is left to the operator.

<details><summary>Only observable difference</summary>

`ncl tasks get <id>` with the row id of a *superseded* occurrence (not the series id) now shows an empty prompt. The series id and the live occurrence still show the full content.
</details>

## Related work

No existing issue. Searched open and closed issues and PRs for inbound.db growth, retention, prune and recurring tasks. #3289 / #3291 are about the pending backlog, not finished rows.

Open PRs in the same area, all compatible:
- #3696 and #3741 add fields to task content. They read them from the just-completed row at re-arm time, or from the live row at spawn. Neither row is compacted.
- #2915 and #3247 touch the pre-`armNextTask` recurrence path.
- #3594 is container-side.

Happy to rebase whichever lands second.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/mailbox/sqlite/arm-next-task.test.ts` -> 7 passed. 5 are new:
  - a payload is kept once per series, and every row, `getTaskStats` and `trailingFailedRuns` are unchanged;
  - a cancelled series keeps its payload;
  - a pre-existing backlog is compacted on the next re-arm;
  - other series and non-task rows are untouched;
  - when the insert fails, the compaction rolls back with the pair.
- Same file without the one-line call in `armNextTask` -> the two compaction tests fail. The three guard tests still pass, as intended.
- `pnpm run build` -> ok.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 4242 passed, 1 skipped. The clean base had 4237 passed, 1 skipped, so the 5 new tests are the only change.
- Copy of the 238 MB production `inbound.db`, through `wrapSqliteInbound`:
  - stats identical before and after;
  - 203 MB of pages freed;
  - first re-arm 105 ms, which compacts 11k rows once;
  - steady-state re-arm 8 ms.
- Live install, same patch:
  - after the next sweep re-arm, all 11,072 finished rows of the series hold the marker;
  - the pending occurrence keeps its full 12 KB payload;
  - `ncl tasks get <series>` shows the full prompt and an unchanged `completed_runs`;
  - no new host errors.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Recurring tasks no longer grow the session database by one copy of the task prompt per run.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Host-only write to the session's `inbound.db` (its single writer), inside an existing transaction.

issues.title: Support failover between registry providers (e.g. Ollama → Ollama)
issues.body:
Problem
NEARAI_FALLBACK_MODEL only works for the NEAR AI backend. When the primary provider is a registry provider like Ollama, the failover path in crates/domains/ironclaw_llm/src/lib.rs builds the fallback via create_llm_provider_with_config(&fallback_config, ...), which always constructs a NearAiChatProvider from NearAiConfig — so there is no way to fail over from one Ollama model to another Ollama model (or to a second Ollama instance).

This matters for local-LLM setups: if the primary local model is unavailable, overloaded, or OOMs, the only resilience options today are retries against the same model — there is no fallback to a smaller/secondary local model.

Request
Allow the fallback provider to be built from the registry provider config, the same way create_cheap_provider_for_backend already does for the cheap model: it clones RegistryProviderConfig, swaps model, and calls create_registry_provider_inner — keeping the same base_url, protocol, and request_timeout_secs.

Concretely:

When config.backend is a registry provider (e.g. ollama) and a fallback model is configured, build the fallback via create_registry_provider_inner instead of create_llm_provider_with_config.
Ideally also allow a different base_url for the fallback (e.g. LLM_FALLBACK_BASE_URL) so failover can target a second Ollama instance, not just a different model on the same server.
Keep NEARAI_FALLBACK_MODEL behavior unchanged for the NEAR AI backend; a generic LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL env var (mirroring LLM_CHEAP_MODEL) would make the intent clearer for non-NEARAI backends.
FailoverProvider itself is backend-agnostic — only the construction of the fallback provider is NEAR-AI-specific, so this should be a contained change in the provider assembly path.

Environment
ironclaw 1.4.1, Windows, ironclaw serve (Standalone profile)
Provider: Ollama → llama.cpp, primary model NEMOTRON-BOLT-ironclaw:latest (9.6 GB)
Desired fallback: a smaller local model on the same or a second Ollama instance
Workaround
None today. Pointing NEARAI_BASE_URL at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (http://localhost:11434/v1) might approximate it, but it routes through NearAiChatProvider with NEAR-AI-specific auth/session handling and is not a supported configuration.

issues.title: [QA] Make PRIMARY_MODEL_CALL_IDLE_TIMEOUT configurable for slow local LLMs

labels.name: qa-bug
labels.description: Bug found during QA testing

issues.body:
### Environment

hosted-staging (crab shack)

### Version / Commit Hash

1.4.1

### QA Test Date

2026-11-15

### Feature Area

Agent loop → model call idle watchdog (HostManagedLoopModelPort / LLM provider timeout)

### Steps to Reproduce

1.Configure a local Ollama provider in providers.json pointing to a llama.cpp-backed model (e.g. NEMOTRON-BOLT-ironclaw:latest) with a large context (num_ctx ≥ 32k).
2.Set LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS=3000 in the environment and start ironclaw serve.
3.Open the WebChat at http://127.0.0.1:3000 and send a message that triggers an agent turn with a large prompt (~30k tokens: tool catalog schemas + history).
4.Observe the llama.cpp server log: prompt evaluation runs >75 s before the first token, then the request is cancelled — [GIN] ... | 500 | 1m10s | POST "/api/chat" followed by srv stop: cancel task.
In the IronClaw log, the complete_model_request span for that model_call=N ends with a retryable Unavailable / "model gateway timed out" error.

### Expected Behavior

A model call whose backend is slowly processing a large prompt (but not hung) should not be cancelled at 75 s. PRIMARY_MODEL_CALL_IDLE_TIMEOUT in crates/kernel/ironclaw_turns/src/host_managed_ports/model.rs should be configurable (e.g. via env var), or prompt-eval progress should count as progress so the watchdog only trips on a genuinely stalled stream — while preserving the invariant that it stays below DEFAULT_PROCESS_LEASE_DURATION (90 s).

### Actual Behavior

The hardcoded 75 s idle watchdog in await_with_progress_timeout cancels the gateway call because prompt evaluation emits no text deltas; the error maps to AgentLoopHostErrorKind::Unavailable ("model gateway timed out") and the client disconnect makes llama.cpp abort the task.

### Logs / Screenshots

_No response_

### Pre-submit checklist

- [x] Title is specific (not "fix Google Suite" but "Google Suite install throws invalid_grant on OAuth step")
- [x] Commit hash is filled in
- [x] Steps are numbered and reproducible

prs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds **Lynxce Omni AI** (灵策全能AI) to the MCP marketplace as a one-click entry. It also lets local registry entries declare MCP OAuth in a generic way, so future OAuth entries need no extra code.

> **Depends on #2874** (remote MCP OAuth sign-in), and this branch is stacked on it. Until #2874 is merged the diff also shows its commits. The changes for this PR are the last two commits, `ec9c7b86` and `0017bce7`.

**Disclosure:** I work on Lynxce. The service is commercial: usage is billed to the signed-in user's Lynxce account credits. It is kept in a separate PR so #2874 can be reviewed on its own.

## Related Issue

None.

## Changes Made

- **Generic OAuth registry entries** (`types/mcp.ts`, `mcpRegistryPresentation.ts`)
  - `McpRegistryEntry` gets `auth?: 'oauth'`. For remote entries, `command` holds the URL, the same convention the Qichacha entry uses.
  - `mergeMarketplaceRegistry` keeps such entries as app-managed local entries, the same way it keeps `oauthProvider` entries. The server-provided marketplace list stays the single source for everything else.
- **One-click connect** (`McpManager.tsx`)
  - An OAuth entry has nothing to fill in, so **Connect** adds the remote server straight away.
  - The server is saved under the entry id, which keeps the OpenClaw server key ASCII and stable.
  - It is saved with `auth: 'oauth'` and `registryId`, and then the browser sign-in from #2874 starts.
  - While waiting for the browser, the button reads *Waiting for browser…*.
  - The marketplace card and the detail dialog share one label helper.
- **Entry** (`data/mcpRegistry.ts`)
  - Lynxce Omni AI, `https://web.lynxce.cn/api/mcp`, Streamable HTTP, in the Design category, at marketplace position 5 (Qichacha stays at 4).
  - A bundled SVG icon.
  - zh/en description.

- **Bundled skill** (`SKILLs/lynxce-omni/`, commit `0017bce7`)
  - A `lynxce-omni` skill that teaches the agent how to use the server's `lynxce_*` tools:
    - check the balance before videos or batches
    - pick the aspect ratio by use
    - map requests to edit-image operations
    - poll long video and music tasks instead of spinning
    - handle sign-in, credit and moderation errors honestly, never inventing result URLs
  - Registered in `skills.config.json` **disabled by default** and given a display name in `bundledSkillNames.ts`.
  - Registry entries get an optional `skillId`. Connecting the entry turns that skill on, so users who never connect Lynxce never load it.

## Expert kit (not in this PR)

The kit store is delivered by your kit-store config, so a kit cannot be added through the repo. We have prepared a ready-to-list **Lynxce Omni AI Studio** kit in the same format as the current catalog:

- 5 skills: poster and product images, photo retouching, short videos, songwriting, and Douyin script breakdown
- zip bundle
- 512px icon
- catalog entry JSON

If you're open to listing it, I can send the files, or host them wherever you prefer.

## What the server offers

After sign-in, the server exposes tools for:

- text-to-image and image editing: upscaling, background replacement, cut-out, old photo restoration, in-image text translation
- text- and image-to-video
- music generation
- extracting the voice-over script from a Douyin share link

The server implements the MCP authorization spec:

- protected-resource and authorization-server metadata
- dynamic client registration
- PKCE S256
- loopback redirect URIs with any port

Users authorize with their Lynxce account and choose a daily credit cap on the consent page. No API key is pasted anywhere.

issues.title: cron 任务执行的 token usage 未写入 turns.jsonl，与对话 channel 路径不一致
issues.body:
## 现象

QwenPaw 控制台「用量」面板展示的 token 账单来自 `turns.jsonl`。该文件由通道层在每个轮次结束后通过 `_commit_turn_usage` 持久化。

实测发现：cron 任务（`crons/executor.py`）执行期间产生的 token 用量**没有进入 `turns.jsonl`**，导致用量面板统计缺失 cron 任务的消耗，归因口径不完整。

## 根因

对比两条路径的实现：

- **对话路径**：`app/channels/base.py` 的 `consume_one` / `_stream_with_tracker` 在成功完成或异常时均显式调用 `_commit_turn_usage(session_id, ...)`，把当轮的 prompt/completion/token 等信息写入 `turns.jsonl`（见 `app/channels/base.py:2034-2100`）。
- **cron 路径**：`app/crons/executor.py` 的 `execute()` / `_run()` 通过 `self._workspace.stream_query(req)` 拉取事件并直接向 channel 投递，**全程未调用** `_commit_turn_usage`，也未有等效的 usage 持久化逻辑。

也就是说：
- cron 任务会建立 session、发起 model request、返回 token 计数
- 但这段计量数据没有落盘到 `turns.jsonl`

差异在两条路径的处理不对称，且没有任何注释说明为何要跳过。

## 影响面

1. **账单口径有缺口**：`turns.jsonl` 的累计 token 仅含对话轮次，cron 任务的模型调用全部被排除在外。cron 任务（每日早报、定时拉取、自动化提醒等）在实际使用中往往占相当比重，缺口不可忽略。
2. **归因不完整**：现有 `turn_usage.resolve_turn_usage` 能按 session 区分用户聊天 vs cron session，说明数据模型本就具备区分能力——只要 cron 路径补齐 `_commit_turn_usage` 调用，即可让账单自然覆盖 cron 任务。
3. **可观测性偏差**：依赖 `turns.jsonl` 做用量分析/告警/计费的下游都会少算 cron 部分。

## 复现

1. 配置一条 `task_type=agent` 的 cron 任务（使用任意 model slot，开启用量记录）；
2. 触发执行；
3. 观察 `{workspace}/sessions/<session_id>/turns.jsonl`：正常对话 session 每次轮次结束后都有新行，但该 cron session 在请求完成后无任何新增行；
4. 对照 `console` 日志中已打印的 `Usage for session <id>` 条目（说明 model 已返回用量），确认是持久化路径缺失而非模型不返回。

## 修复建议

在 `app/crons/executor.py` 的 `_run()` 内，于 `stream_query` 收敛后（成功或异常分支均需覆盖）补一次 usage 持久化。推荐复用 `base.py` 已有的 `_commit_turn_usage` 机制，例如：

- 选项 A：把 `_commit_turn_usage` 提取为 workspace/channel 的公共方法，供 executor 调用；
- 选项 B：在 executor 内 import 并重用 `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage.resolve_turn_usage` + `qwenpaw.token_usage.persist_turn_usage`，传入本次 cron 的 `session_id` / `user_id` / `channel`。

两种方案任选其一即可；关键是 **cron 路径与 channel 路径保持用量落盘的一致**。若出于设计考量认为 cron session 本就不应写 `turns.jsonl`，建议在 `executor.py` 补一行注释说明原因，避免后续维护者误以为遗漏。

## 补充说明

- 此 issue 仅针对框架行为本身，不涉及任何第三方插件（如 `ledger_ingest` 等消费模块）；插件只是暴露了此缺口，非问题来源。
- 当前框架版本为 v0.3.17。

issues.title: [Bug]: Attachment path truncated to drive root ("C:\") passed to the model since 2.3.0-beta.1 - file saved fine but images fail to load

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0-beta.1 (introduced) / beta.2 / **beta.3** - still reproduces on beta.3, tested 2026-11-10 12:13 (`qwenpaw --version` = 2.3.0b3)

## Description

Since 2.3.0-beta.1, the local path of a user-uploaded attachment is truncated to the **drive root** before it reaches the model. The file itself is downloaded and saved correctly into `media\`, but the model only receives the root, so images can never load and the agent cannot see attachments.

Actual message content received by the model:

- Console / WeChat: `已经下载到 C:\` - the real path `C:\Users\<user>\...\.copaw\workspaces\<agent>\media\<uuid>_<name>` is cut to `C:\`
- QQ channel: `已经下载到 \` (backslash only)
- Console tool side also shows `saved into file:///C:/.`
- Images render as: `[Image unavailable: Error:  is not a valid image: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'C:\']`

**Related PR(s):** none found (searched; unrelated to #8585 which was about recall SQLite URIs)

**Security considerations:** none (local path only, no credentials involved)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0-beta.1 (introduced) / 2.3.0-beta.3 (still present)
- **OS:** Windows 10 & Windows 11
- **Install method:** Desktop installer
- **Python version (if applicable):** bundled

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, upgrade QwenPaw Desktop to 2.3.0-beta.1 or later
2. Send any image/attachment to the agent (console, WeChat, or QQ channel)
3. Observe the model-side message: the saved path is truncated to the drive root (`C:\`), and images fail with `[Image unavailable: ... No such file or directory: 'C:\']`

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** model receives `已经下载到 C:\` (drive root only) plus `[Image unavailable: ... 'C:\']`. Clean time boundary at the beta.1 upgrade moment (2026-10-29 15:05): 258 attachment messages before the upgrade -> **0** truncations; 12 messages after -> **12/12** truncated (last OK 14:12:27, first failure 15:43:08). The file body is **always saved correctly**: 14/14 attachments found on disk as `media\<uuid32>_<original name>`, cross-checked against history.db records. Re-verified on beta.3 (2026-11-10 12:13, console): PNG uploaded -> `C:\` truncation again, file on disk intact (19,397 bytes).
- **Expected:** the model receives the full absolute path (`...\media\<uuid>_<name>`), and no `[Image unavailable]` for files that exist on disk.

## Logs / Screenshots

Model-side rendering of a console upload (beta.3, 2026-11-10):

```
测试看看 [Image unavailable: Error:  is not a valid image: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'C:\']
用户上传文件，已经下载到 C:\
```

The same file on disk: `media\33514bf61c5242e9bcfa40cdf8bce0c3_image.png` (19,397 bytes, saved 12:13:53) - download/save layer is fine; the path value is already truncated when passed back into the message pipeline. Message rendering and image freezing consume the same bad value; the `file_url_to_local_path()` helper in `channels/utils.py` behaves correctly on known-good inputs, so the corruption happens upstream, at the "return URL/path" stage.

## Additional Notes

- Workaround in use: a read-only helper re-finds the real path in `media\` by (filename fragment + time window), then the agent calls view_image/read_file with the reconstructed path. Works 100% so far, but without it every attachment is effectively invisible to the agent.
- Truncation artifact differs by channel: console/WeChat keep `C:\`, QQ keeps `\` - consistent with a string cut at a fixed offset rather than a per-channel bug.

issues.title: [Bug]: Scheduled task fails with APIConnectionError on 2nd model call while manual run of the same task succeeds
issues.body:
## Summary

A daily scheduled task (`daily-web-patrol`) has failed on all 4 scheduled runs (Nov 13-16, 2026) with a model connection error, while manually triggering the exact same task — same task text, same model — succeeds every time. The instance stays awake and the task stays enabled, so this looks like a difference between the scheduled-trigger execution path and the manual-trigger path, not a task configuration problem.

## Environment

- Deployment: AgentScope Platform hosted instance (platform.agentscope.io), QwenPaw console v2.3.0, agent "Default" status Running
- Task: `daily-web-patrol`, enabled, runs daily 09:00 Asia/Shanghai (01:00 UTC); timeout 600 s; miss window 600 s; max concurrency 1; execution model = default; dispatch stream; inbox enabled; target session `default`
- Execution model: `cohere/north-mini-code:free` via OpenRouter (the default model)
- Login: GitHub account nyboyscn-del

## What the task does

Fetches the top 5 headlines from three sites (aihot.news, news.ycombinator.com, www.v2ex.com) and appends them to the workspace file `patrol-log.md`.

## Scheduled runs (from the task execution history)

- 2026-11-13 01:01:21 UTC — FAILED, `APIConnectionError('Connection error.')`, 12 steps
- 2026-11-14 01:02:00 UTC — FAILED, `TimeoutError: timed out after 120s` (timeout was 120 s at the time), 22 steps
- 2026-11-15 01:01:33 UTC — FAILED, `APIConnectionError('Connection error.')`, 20 steps, no summary, nothing written
- 2026-11-16 01:00:32 UTC — FAILED, `APIConnectionError('Connection error.')`, only 2 steps: a Thinking step plus one `get_current_time` call (returned `2026-11-16 01:00:06 Etc/UTC (Monday)`); the next model call failed. No `web_fetch`, no file read/write, no inbox notification.

`patrol-log.md` was not updated by any of the four scheduled runs.

## Manual runs of the same task (same model) — all succeed

- 2026-11-12 15:14:18 UTC — manual trigger succeeded
- 2026-11-14 14:02 UTC — manual run completed and wrote the file
- 2026-11-14 14:07 UTC — manual run completed in 47 steps (~1 min); all three sites fetched, headlines independently verified 5/5 on each site

## Ruled out

- Not a missed trigger: every scheduled run has a trigger entry in the execution history at 01:00 UTC.
- Not instance sleep: the instance has been Running since the WakeUp event on 2026-11-12 10:55:02, with no Sleep event since. Storage 17.43 MB / 5 GB.
- Not the task text: the 2026-11-16 run used rewritten task text (web_fetch-first, with strict tool-use rules) and still failed before reaching any fetch step — the new text never got a chance to execute. (Earlier rounds also hit invalid generated browser-tool code; the 2026-11-16 round isolates the connection error from that.)
- Not rate limiting: no 429 / finish_reason text appears in the execution history.

## Question

Is there a known difference between the scheduled-trigger and manual-trigger model-call paths (different routing, connection handling, or retry behavior)? The pattern — 3 of 4 scheduled failures are the same `APIConnectionError` within the first few steps, while manual runs with the identical model never hit it — suggests the scheduled path is more prone to dropping the model connection. Any guidance on what to check, or a fix, would be appreciated.

issues.title: [Bug]: Same-host reverse proxy bypasses API authentication on 2.3.0 (loopback whitelist + empty trusted_proxies)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0

## Description

With `QWENPAW_AUTH_ENABLED=true` and at least one registered user, every request that reaches the backend through a same-host reverse proxy is treated as a local CLI request and skips bearer-token validation.

Root cause, `qwenpaw/app/auth.py`:

- `AuthMiddleware._should_skip_auth()` calls `resolve_client_ip(request)` and skips auth when the result is in `security.allow_no_auth_hosts`.
- `_resolve_client_ip()` only trusts `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP` when the direct TCP peer is in `security.trusted_proxies`. With the default `trusted_proxies: []`, it returns the direct peer.
- For nginx / Caddy / 1Panel on the same host, that peer is `127.0.0.1`, which is in the default `allow_no_auth_hosts: ["127.0.0.1", "::1"]`.
- The loopback defense-in-depth check also passes, because the peer itself is loopback.

So the default configuration is unauthenticated for the most common deployment shape. `check_proxy_config_sanity()` does not warn here: it only fires when `allow_no_auth_hosts` contains non-loopback entries.

Impact: an unauthenticated `GET /api/agents/<id>` returns the full agent config, including plaintext `embedding_model_config.api_key`, `channels.matrix.password` and channel tokens. Tool endpoints such as `execute_shell_command` are reachable as well, i.e. command execution as the account running QwenPaw.

**Related PR(s):** #2840 (open, Under Review since 2026-04; removes the generic localhost bypass). This report confirms the bug is still present on 2.3.0.

**Security considerations:** CWE-306 / CWE-288. Auth bypass, credential disclosure, command execution.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- **Install method:** pip in a uv-managed venv
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable auth and register a user: `QWENPAW_AUTH_ENABLED=true qwenpaw app`.
2. Put a same-host reverse proxy in front: `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8088;` with `X-Forwarded-For` set. Leave `security.trusted_proxies` at its default `[]`.
3. From another machine, request a protected route without any token:
   `curl -sk https://<proxy-host>/api/agents/<agent-id>`

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** HTTP 200, full agent JSON (23 KB in this deployment), including unmasked credentials.
- **Expected:** HTTP 401.

Setting `security.trusted_proxies: ["127.0.0.1"]` makes the same request return 401, while `curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/agents/<id>` stays 200 (CLI path preserved).

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
# via reverse proxy, trusted_proxies = []
HTTP 200, 23291 bytes
{"id":"...","running":{"reme_light_memory_config":{"embedding_model_config":{"api_key":"sk-..."}}},"channels":{"matrix":{"password":"..."}}}

# via reverse proxy, trusted_proxies = ["127.0.0.1"]
HTTP 401

# direct loopback
HTTP 200
```

## Additional Notes

Suggested fix (or merge #2840): do not treat a loopback peer as local when the request carries `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP`, or require `trusted_proxies` to accept loopback before the no-auth skip applies. Extend `check_proxy_config_sanity()` to warn on the default loopback-allowlist + empty-`trusted_proxies` combination.
