issues.title: [Bug] WeCom channel: every file/image send fails with UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID on 2.3.0 (chunk ack carries no body)
issues.body:
## Summary

On QwenPaw **2.3.0**, sending any file or image to a WeCom (企业微信 AI Bot) conversation always fails with `ChannelDeliveryError: UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID`, and the whole reply turn is aborted (`persisted interrupted turn`). Text-only replies are unaffected.

The same bot worked on 2.2.x, where outbound media went through the built-in `qwenpaw/app/channels/wecom/channel.py` (HTTP media upload). 2.3.0 replaces it with the bundled `qwenpaw_channel_wecom` plugin (generation-based worker process + WebSocket chunked upload), and the new upload path rejects a valid platform ack.

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.3.0 (pip, Linux x86_64, Python 3.11.17)
- channel plugin `qwenpaw_channel_wecom` 0.1.0.dev0 (bundled; loaded from `PLUGINS_DIR` = `WORKING_DIR/plugins`)
- `wecom-aibot-python-sdk` 1.0.2
- WeCom AI Bot, long-connection (WebSocket) mode

## Reproduction

1. Configure the WeCom AI Bot channel (`bot_id` / `secret`, WebSocket mode) and let it reach `platform_state=connected`.
2. In WeCom, ask the agent for anything that ends with `send_file_to_user` — a `.docx` / `.xlsx` / PDF, or an image.
3. The agent completes its work, but the attachment never arrives and the reply is cut off. Server side:

```
ERROR | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID, session=wecom:...
ERROR | task_tracker: run error
qwenpaw.app.channels.isolated_proxy.ChannelDeliveryError: UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID
INFO  | cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn
```

100% reproducible on every send attempt, for both `file` and `image` media types. No attempt ever reaches the `finish` step.

## What the wire actually looks like

Ack frames captured from the WeCom WebSocket (`req_id` shortened, upload ids masked):

```json
{"headers": {"req_id": "aibot_upload_media_init_<ts>_<rand>"}, "body": {"upload_id": "<upload_id>"}, "errcode": 0, "errmsg": "ok"}
{"headers": {"req_id": "aibot_upload_media_chunk_<ts>_<rand>"}, "errcode": 0, "errmsg": "ok"}
```

Note the second frame: the ack for `aibot_upload_media_chunk` carries **no `body` field** at all.

The SDK routes it through `WSClient._ws_manager.on_message`, and `platform.py` intercepts it by `req_id.startswith(_UPLOAD_CMDS)` — so the frame does reach `_upload_ack()` and resolves the future correctly. It is the body validation afterwards that fails.

## Root cause

`qwenpaw_channel_wecom/platform.py`, `_send_ws_cmd()` (around line 606):

```python
ack = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(future), _UPLOAD_ACK_TIMEOUT)
self._check_epoch(epoch)
if ack.get("errcode") != 0:
    raise WeComDeliveryError("PLATFORM_REJECTED")
body = ack.get("body")
if not isinstance(body, dict):
    raise WeComDeliveryError(
        "UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID",
        side_effect_possible=True,
    )
return body
```

One helper serves all three upload commands (`aibot_upload_media_init` / `_chunk` / `_finish`) and requires **every** ack to carry a dict `body`. But WeCom only returns a body for `init` (`upload_id`) and `finish` (`media_id`); `chunk` acks are `errcode`/`errmsg` only. So `body` is `None`, `isinstance(None, dict)` is false, and the upload dies while sending the first chunk.

The call site does not even consume the chunk return value:

```python
await self._send_ws_cmd(
    _UPLOAD_CMD_CHUNK,
    {"upload_id": upload_id, "chunk_index": index, "base64_data": base64.b64encode(chunk).decode()},
)
```

## Suggested fix

Treat a missing body as an empty ack, and keep the existing structural checks for `init` / `finish` (both already validate `upload_id` / `media_id` after the call):

```diff
             body = ack.get("body")
+            if body is None:
+                # WeCom answers aibot_upload_media_chunk with errcode/errmsg only,
+                # no body. Treat a missing body as an empty ack: INIT/FINISH are
+                # still validated by their upload_id / media_id checks.
+                body = {}
             if not isinstance(body, dict):
                 raise WeComDeliveryError(
                     "UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID",
                     side_effect_possible=True,
                 )
             return body
```

An alternative is to validate the body per command (only `INIT` / `FINISH`), which is arguably cleaner since the chunk ack is not meant to carry data.

## Local validation of the patch

- Replayed every captured ack frame through both variants of the check: the current logic fails on 100% of `chunk` frames, the patched logic fails on none (`init` frames behave identically in both).
- Applied the patch, then let the channel worker respawn (`generation` bumped to 1, `platform_state=connected`). **End-to-end verified against a real WeCom conversation:** three consecutive deliveries completed the full handshake

  ```
  init   -> body.upload_id
  chunk  -> errcode/errmsg only   (previously fatal)
  finish -> body.media_id
  ```

  each `finish` ack returned a `media_id` and the attachments arrived in the WeCom client. After the fix there are zero `UPLOAD_ACK_INVALID` records and zero aborted turns, where before every single attempt died on the first chunk.

## Secondary observation

Because the exception escapes `send_content_parts`, the entire turn is cancelled — the user loses the accompanying text answer as well, not just the attachment. A per-part failure (degrade to "attachment failed" while still delivering the text) would be a more graceful behavior. Happy to split that into a separate issue if you prefer.

## Version check

PyPI still lists 2.3.0 as the latest, so there is no released build that contains a fix for this.

issues.title: WeChat channel: silent inbound polling death - error-ret loop has no logging or recovery, cursor never resets
issues.body:
**Environment**
- QwenPaw 2.3.0 (Desktop, Windows 10), official `qwenpaw_channel_wechat` plugin (`platform.py`).

**Symptom**
- Inbound WeChat messages silently stop arriving. The channel worker process stays alive, channel health reports healthy, and there are zero errors in the log. Outbound (e.g. cron sends) still works.
- The only effective recovery is rebuilding the worker (agent hot reload) with the same token — no QR re-scan needed. This proves the failure is in the worker's runtime polling state, not credentials/model/send path.

**Occurrences (local time, Asia/Shanghai)**
- 2026-11-14 13:14 -> 2026-11-15 18:43 (~29h silent window)
- 2026-11-15 20:24 -> 2026-11-16 00:56 (~4.5h silent window)
- Similar silent receive deaths also observed 2026-10-25/10-26.
- In each window: no inbound rows in history DB, no `consume` log lines, no worker stderr at all.

**Code analysis (`platform.py::_poll`)**
```python
data = await self._poll_client.getupdates(cursor)
...
if data.get("ret", -1) not in (0, -1) and not messages:
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
```
- When `getupdates` returns a non-zero `ret` (other than -1) with empty `msgs`, the loop just sleeps 3s and retries forever with the same cursor: no logging, no failure counter, no recovery.
- The exception path logs and backs off, but the error-ret path is completely silent — matching the observed zero-log dead windows.
- `cursor` is only updated from `get_updates_buf` and never reset; a stale cursor / half-dead long connection / server-side subscription lapse cannot be distinguished because `ret` is never logged.

**Related but different:** #4697 (poll thread crash during zero-downtime reload, v1.1.7, closed inactive). This report involves no reload, no exception and zero logs on current 2.3.0.

**Suggested fix**
1. Log abnormal `ret` codes (throttled, numeric only).
2. Track last successful poll; after sustained abnormal ret (e.g. 10 minutes), rebuild the poll client and reset the cursor.
3. Optionally refresh the poll client after a long inbound silence (e.g. 6h) to cover the "ret ok but empty forever" mode.
4. Expose polling freshness in channel health so external monitoring can detect silent death.

**Local mitigation**
A minimal patch implementing 1-3 has been applied locally and is under observation. Diff below; happy to turn it into a PR if useful.

```diff
--- original
+++ patched
@@ -170,2 +170,11 @@
         cursor, failures = "", 0
+        # Local poll-resilience patch (2026-11-16):
+        # log abnormal ret codes (numeric only, throttled) and rebuild the
+        # poll client when polling stays unhealthy, instead of looping
+        # silently forever on a stale cursor/connection.
+        last_ok = time.monotonic()
+        last_msg = time.monotonic()
+        last_rebuild = 0.0
+        last_ret_log = 0.0
+        logged_ret = None
         while not self._stopping:
@@ -174,2 +183,9 @@
                 failures = 0
+                ret = data.get("ret", -1)
+                now = time.monotonic()
+                if ret in (0, -1):
+                    last_ok = now
+                elif ret != logged_ret or now - last_ret_log >= 300:
+                    logger.warning("WeChat poll abnormal ret=%s", ret)
+                    logged_ret, last_ret_log = ret, now
                 if data.get("get_updates_buf") is not None:
@@ -177,2 +193,4 @@
                 messages = data.get("msgs") or []
+                if messages:
+                    last_msg = now
                 for message in messages:
@@ -184,3 +202,19 @@
                         logger.warning("WeChat inbound message failed")
-                if data.get("ret", -1) not in (0, -1) and not messages:
+                reason = ""
+                if now - last_ok > 600:
+                    reason = "abnormal_ret_10min"
+                elif now - last_msg > 21600 and now - last_rebuild > 21600:
+                    reason = "no_inbound_6h"
+                if reason and now - last_rebuild > 60:
+                    logger.warning(
+                        "WeChat poll recovery: rebuild client reason=%s",
+                        reason,
+                    )
+                    await self._rebuild_poll_client()
+                    cursor = ""
+                    last_ok = last_msg = time.monotonic()
+                    last_rebuild = time.monotonic()
+                    logged_ret = None
+                    continue
+                if ret not in (0, -1) and not messages:
                     await asyncio.sleep(3)
@@ -192,2 +226,14 @@
                 failures += 1
+
+    async def _rebuild_poll_client(self):
+        # Fresh HTTP client + cursor reset reproduces the empirically
+        # effective worker-rebuild recovery without touching login state.
+        old = self._poll_client
+        new = ILinkClient(old.bot_token, old.base_url)
+        await new.start()
+        self._poll_client = new
+        try:
+            await old.stop()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
 

```

issues.title: [Bug]:  [2.3.0] WeChat channel cannot start (`ACCOUNT_IN_USE`) and successful sends are reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Environment

| item          | value                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| QwenPaw       | 2.3.0 (PyPI latest at time of report; no 2.3.1 available)    |
| agentscope    | 2.0.10                                                       |
| openai SDK    | 2.33.0                                                       |
| Python        | 3.12.13                                                      |
| OS            | Linux (Manjaro, x86_64), systemd system service              |
| wechat plugin | `wechat` 0.1.0.dev0 (bundled with 2.3.0, `publish: false`)   |
| Channel setup | single agent `default`, wechat enabled with an existing iLink bot token (`bot_token`, no `bot_token_file`) |

## Bug 1 — WeChat channel never starts: `ACCOUNT_IN_USE` (critical)

### Symptom

On every boot (6+ restarts, always identical — unrelated to restart count):

```
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'wechat' Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:1076 | Failed to start new workspace instance for default: Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'wechat' failed: default@...:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
```

The plugin then gets unregistered (`Unregistered channel 'wechat'`), so the workspace no longer has a wechat channel at all and the bot is silently offline.

`GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `404 {"detail": "Channel 'wechat' is not running."}`

### Traceback

```
manager.py:1602  start_one
manager.py:1671  _start_one_unlocked
manager.py:1342  _reserve_channel_auth
wechat_auth_custody.py:117  _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence
    raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

Line 117 is the loop that treats **another agent profile** as a competing owner of the same WeChat credential:

```python
scopes, others = evidence
for runtime_key, configured, other_scopes in others:
    if (
        configured or any(lease.key == runtime_key for lease in leases)
    ) and (scopes.intersection(other_scopes)):
        raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

### Root cause

`_read_wechat_auth_evidence()` skips "myself" with a case-sensitive id comparison:

```python
for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
    if agent_id == workspace_id:
        continue
```

but the workspace id that `manager._reserve_channel_auth()` resolves and passes in is **`Default`** (capital D), while the profile key in `config.json` is **`default`**. The guard therefore never skips itself and evaluates `default` as "another profile". Instrumenting the guard shows the conflict is with the very same workspace, with identical scope hashes:

```
BLOCK workspace_id=Default other=<WORKING_DIR>/.copaw/workspaces/default
      configured=True lease_hit=True overlap=True
      own=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
      other_scopes=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
```

Note also that with `bot_token_file` left empty, `wechat_auth_scopes()` derives the token paths from `WORKING_DIR`, so **any** profile is guaranteed to hash to the same scopes — meaning a second (even dormant, non-wechat) agent profile is enough to trip this check once the id comparison fails.

### Suggested fix

Normalize identity instead of comparing raw strings; e.g. casefold both sides and/or compare resolved workspace directories. A `workspace_dir` parameter is already available at both call sites.

```python
if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
    continue
if own_dir is not None and Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve() == own_dir:
    continue
```

## Bug 2 — Plugin recovery deadlocks on a leaked custody-only lease (critical)

### Symptom

After the plugin has been probed once in a process, it can never be (re)enabled:

```
ERROR loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: ...
POST /api/plugins/wechat/enabled {"enabled": true}
→ 500 {"detail": "Failed to update plugin enabled state: Plugin 'wechat' recovery failed; needs_restart: Recovery has runtime resources; unload first"}
```

`POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` returns `clean: true, quiescent: true`, yet the next enable still fails, and the `_recovery_blocked` entry is never cleared for the lifetime of the process.

### Root cause

`loader._has_runtime_custody()` is just `bool(registry.runtime_owners.leases(plugin_id))`. Probe reservations are made with `custody_only=True` and **no stop adapter**, and `RuntimeOwners._invoke()` refuses to attest a stop for them:

```python
async def _invoke(entry):
    if entry.stop is None:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

`release()` then returns `False` for that lease, so the entry stays in `_entries` forever → recovery sees "runtime resources", blocks, and caches the error.

### Suggested fix

A custody-only reservation owns no process, so it can always be released:

```python
if entry.stop is None:
    if entry.custody_only:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
    return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

## Bug 3 — Successful sends reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`; replies dropped (critical)

### Symptom

Inbound works and the agent produces a reply, but the user never receives it:

```
INFO  channel _consume_with_tracker: chat_id=... session=wechat:...        (message received)
INFO  builder: built agent for session=wechat:... model=...
INFO  Usage for session wechat:...: {'input_tokens': 142422, 'output_tokens': 102}
ERROR base.py:1040 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
WARNING isolated_proxy.py:637 | Channel diagnostic: RESPONSE_FINISH_FAILED
qwenpaw.app.channels.isolated_proxy.ChannelDeliveryError: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
```

`qwenpaw channels send --channel wechat ...` fails the same way (`500` on `/api/messages/send`).

### Reproduction of the platform side

Calling the iLink API directly with the same bot token and the stored `context_token`:

```
POST https://ilinkai.weixin.qq.com/ilink/bot/sendmessage
{"msg": {"to_user_id": "...@im.wechat", "message_type": 2, "message_state": 2,
         "context_token": "<token>", "item_list": [{"type": 1, "text_item": {"text": "test"}}]},
 "base_info": {"channel_version": "0.1.0"}}

→ HTTP 200  {"message_id": <MESSAGE_ID>}
```

**A successful send returns only `message_id` — no `ret`, no `errcode`.**

### Root cause

`plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py:406`:

```python
@staticmethod
def _check_result(response, sent):
    if not isinstance(response, dict) or not (
        {"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()
    ):
        raise WeChatDeliveryError(
            "PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN",
            side_effect_possible=True,
        )
```

Every successful send is therefore classified as an unknown result and the reply is discarded (the proxy also marks `_reply_unknown`, so there is no retry).

### Suggested fix

Accept `message_id` as success (and/or fall back to the HTTP status):

```python
if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
    return
```

## Bug 4 — `top_k` / `repetition_penalty` from per-model `generate_kwargs` crash the model call (major)

With an OpenRouter model whose stored `generate_kwargs` contain `top_k` and `repetition_penalty`:

```
TypeError: AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'top_k'
  File ".../openai/resources/chat/completions/completions.py", line 2714, in create
```

OpenAI-compatible endpoints generally expect these in `extra_body`; the SDK signature does not accept them as top-level kwargs. Removing them from the model's `generate_kwargs` (`PUT /api/models/{provider}/models/{model}/config`) fixed it. Suggestion: filter known-unsupported keys into `extra_body` in the OpenAI-compatible wrapper instead of passing them through.

## Observation (not necessarily a QwenPaw bug)

While testing, `openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` repeatedly returned an empty stream while its connection test reported `status=available, verification=live`:

```
WARNING retry_chat_model.py:1201 | LLM stream failed (attempt 1/4):
        LLM stream for openrouter:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free produced no content
```

Switching the agent's chat model to `deepseek-custom/deepseek-flash` produced normal replies, so this looks model/provider-specific, but the retry loop silently consumed 4 attempts without surfacing a user-visible error.

## Minimal patch set that made the channel usable (for reference)

```diff
--- a/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
 def _read_wechat_auth_evidence(config, workspace_id, working_dir,
+                               workspace_dir=None):
     for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
         if agent_id == workspace_id:
             continue
+        # NEW: the resolved workspace id may differ in case from the profile key
+        if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
+            continue
+        # NEW: or point at the very same workspace directory
+        if workspace_dir is not None and (
+            Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+            == Path(workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+        ):
+            continue

--- a/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
     async def _invoke(entry):
         if entry.stop is None:
+            if entry.custody_only:
+                return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
             return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")

--- a/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
+++ b/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
     def _check_result(response, sent):
         if not isinstance(response, dict) or not ({"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()):
+            if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
+                return
             raise WeChatDeliveryError("PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN", side_effect_possible=True)
```

After these three changes (plus removing `top_k`/`repetition_penalty` from the model's `generate_kwargs`):

- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `{"channel":"wechat","status":"healthy"}`
- plugin → `status: active, diagnostics: ["channel_validation_passed"]`
- inbound messages are consumed, replies are delivered, no `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

## Additional notes

- A zero-downtime agent reload (triggered by any config change) can leave the previous wechat channel handle undelivered: subsequent `POST /api/config/channels/wechat/restart` returns `CHANNEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` indefinitely, and a stale `shared_worker.py` keeps polling (reported `platform_state: connected`) while its messages no longer reach the app. Killing the stale worker unblocks the drain.
- Plugin source edits require `POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` + `enabled=true` to take effect; `channel restart` fails with `SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH`.
- With a large wechat session (142k input tokens per turn) replies take 60–90 s end-to-end, which may be close to the iLink reply window.

issues.title: [Bug]: Upgrade does not migrate built-in channel plugins; installed Matrix stays on old source and 2.3.0 fixes never apply

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (PyPI, released 2026-11-11)

## Description

Upgrading from an earlier release to 2.3.0 leaves `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix` on its old source. The Matrix fixes in 2.3.0 — #8559 (install E2EE dependencies with the channel), #8558, #8584, #8599, #8411 (session and device-key recovery) — exist only in the bundled `official_channels/matrix-0.1.0.dev0.zip`. Nothing installs it over the existing plugin directory.

The upgrade completes, the plugin does not, the fixes never apply, and there is no update entry point: `qwenpaw plugins` has no `update` subcommand, and both Console's update check and the extension market exclude built-in channel plugins.

In this instance the old plugin's `state.py` imports `qwenpaw.plugins.matrix_legacy`, which 2.3.0 removed, so it fails at startup with `ModuleNotFoundError`. Three agents with Matrix enabled fail to start.

Mechanism:

- `plugins/official_channels.py:455` seeds a bundled channel only when `loader.find_installed_plugin_dir(plugin_id) is None`.
- `plugins/official_channels.py:312` does the same during `prepare-upgrade`; an installed plugin only goes through `preflight_backend()`, which checks and installs dependencies but does not replace source.
- `plugins/loader.py:3518` raises `Official source already exists` when a seed is attempted for an existing directory. The comment at `plugins/loader.py:3531` states the intent: `Reuse A first-copy/publication, never replacement.`
- `official_channels/index.json` records matrix as `version: 0.1.0.dev0` with `sha256: 114e9e32...`. No code compares that hash or version against the installed directory.
- Console → Installed plugins → check updates queries `https://download.qwenpaw.agentscope.io/metadata/plugins/index.json` (31 entries, no `matrix`). The extension market has no entry for it either.
- `qwenpaw plugins` has no `update` subcommand; `install --force` is the only entry point.

**Related PR(s):** #8559, #8558, #8584, #8599, #8411

**Security considerations:** None. No credentials or auth paths are involved; the failure is confined to local plugin loading.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-42-generic
- **Install method:** one-line install (`curl -fsSL https://qwenpaw.agentscope.io/install.sh | bash`)
- **Python version:** 3.12.14 (uv-managed venv at `~/.qwenpaw/venv`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On 2.2.x, enable the Matrix channel for at least one agent and confirm it connects. `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix` now exists with `matrix-nio>=0.25.0` in `requirements.txt`.
2. Upgrade to 2.3.0 with the official installer.
3. Start the service and open Console → Channels → Matrix.
4. The channel fails to start.
5. Stop the service and run `qwenpaw plugins prepare-upgrade`. It exits successfully, but `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/requirements.txt` is unchanged.
6. Open Console → Extensions → Installed plugins → check updates, then the extension market. Matrix is not listed in either.
7. Only `qwenpaw plugins install /path/to/unpacked/matrix --force` restores it.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** After upgrading to 2.3.0, the installed Matrix plugin remains on its old source and the 2.3.0 channel fixes are not applied. This instance fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'qwenpaw.plugins.matrix_legacy'`, and all three agents with Matrix enabled fail to start. `prepare-upgrade` does not fix it, Console's update check and the extension market provide no entry for the plugin, and the CLI has no update command.
- **Expected:** Upgrading QwenPaw should migrate built-in channel plugins. At minimum, compare `official_channels/index.json` `sha256` against the installed directory (`version` is currently fixed at `0.1.0.dev0` and cannot serve as a criterion), replace it after backing up, and preserve channel configuration. Alternatively, include built-in channel plugins in Console's update detection and provide an entry in the extension market for one-click update.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'qwenpaw.plugins.matrix_legacy'
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/execution/worker.py", line 230, in connect
  File ".../.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/qwenpaw_channel_matrix/driver.py", line 41, in start
  File ".../.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/qwenpaw_channel_matrix/platform.py", line 204, in <module>
  File ".../.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/qwenpaw_channel_matrix/state.py", line 15, in <module>
```

```text
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'matrix' marked FAILED after startup:
channel 'matrix' failed: job@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED;
jiuhu@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED;
fairy@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
```

After force-reinstalling the bundled source, the same three agents connect within two seconds, and the new plugin logs the recovery path that only exists in the 2.3.0 source:

```text
MatrixChannel: homeserver lost E2EE device keys; re-uploading the existing identity
platform_state: connected
```

## Additional Notes

This is not Matrix-specific. `official_channels/index.json` contains 18 bundled channel plugins; 17 of them are versioned `0.1.0.dev0`. Whenever a release changes their code or the host APIs they import, the same stale-source problem applies, and none of it is covered by the current update detection.

Recovery for affected users is a manual `qwenpaw plugins install <unpacked plugin directory> --force`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Official channel plugin workers crash on Linux — neither the launcher nor the worker bootstrap delivers HOME / QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR required by qwenpaw.constant
issues.body:
## Summary

After the WeChat channel is provided by the **official plugin** (instead of the built-in implementation), the plugin worker process crashes at startup on Linux with:

```
RuntimeError: Could not determine home directory.
```

The channel platform state becomes `failed` and the hub reports `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`. This is not a token/configuration problem: the worker environment contains neither `HOME` nor `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR`, while the official plugin imports `qwenpaw.constant` at module level, which requires one of them. **Two independent sanitization points** both drop the variables; fixing only one is insufficient.

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0** (pip wheel), Linux x86_64 (Debian 12 base, fnOS NAS), Hub deployment
- Official WeChat channel plugin (`qwenpaw_channel_wechat`), local (bubblewrap) provisioner
- The failure is in the launch/bootstrap path itself, so it is independent of the provisioner.

## Symptom (worker log)

```
component_failed | RuntimeError: Could not determine home directory.
worker.py:234 connect -> driver.py:37 start
 -> platform.py:21 <module> -> constant.py:90 <module> -> pathlib.py:1406 expanduser
```

## Root cause (code path, all in the 2.3.0 wheel)

1. **The launcher never delivers the variables.** `qwenpaw/plugins/execution/process.py::_open` (lines 663-682) builds the worker subprocess environment from `os.environ` through a hardcoded whitelist (`PATH`, `SYSTEMROOT`, `TEMP`, `TMP`, `TMPDIR`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_MAINTENANCE`, proxy vars, ...) and then explicitly adds only the custody variables (`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`, reader scope, capability). **`HOME` and `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` are not in that whitelist**, so they never enter the worker process — even though the parent runtime has both (set by `runtime_environment()`).
2. **The worker bootstrap strips the environment again.** `qwenpaw/plugins/execution/worker.py:157` calls `boot._clean_environment(())`, keeping only `_STARTUP_ENVIRONMENT` plus declared passthrough (`qwenpaw/plugins/execution/bootstrap.py:527-539`). That whitelist also lacks `HOME` / `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` (it does include `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`, which is why custody itself passes). Note: a passthrough-only fix here cannot work, because passthrough preserves existing variables — it cannot create ones the launcher never delivered.
3. **The launcher cannot compensate via `private_env` for WeChat.** `qwenpaw/plugins/official_execution_context.py::project_official_execution` builds `private_env` per channel; the `wechat` branch leaves it an **empty dict** (only `qq` injects environment variables). Moreover `validate_private_environment` (`bootstrap.py:91-140`) rejects any `QWENPAW_*` name, so `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` can never be delivered via `private_env`. (`HOME` would be allowed, but nobody sets it.)
4. **The official plugin needs one of them at import time.** `qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py:21`:
   ```python
   from qwenpaw.constant import DEFAULT_MEDIA_DIR, WORKING_DIR
   ```
5. **`qwenpaw.constant` raises without them.** `constant.py:86-94`: with no `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR`, it falls back to `Path("~/.copaw").expanduser()` / `Path("~/.qwenpaw").expanduser()`; with no `HOME`, `expanduser` raises `RuntimeError: Could not determine home directory.`

The built-in implementation never hit this because it ran inside the runtime process, which has a full environment. Migrating the channel into the official plugin worker moved the same imports into the doubly-sanitized environment, where they cannot succeed.

Other official channel plugins that import `qwenpaw.constant` (e.g. QQ) are affected by the same gap.

## Suggested fixes

Both sanitization points must deliver the variables (any equivalent combination):

1. **Launcher:** in `process.py::_open`, carry `HOME` and `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` from `os.environ` into the launch environment (the runtime always has them).
2. **Worker bootstrap:** add `HOME` and `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` to `_STARTUP_ENVIRONMENT`, or call `boot._clean_environment(("HOME", "QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR"))` in `worker.py`.

With both in place, `constant.py` takes the explicit-env branch and the worker's `WORKING_DIR` equals the runtime's working directory — consistent by construction.

Alternatives: have `project_official_execution` include `HOME` in `private_env` for official channels (passes validation) **and** whitelist it in the worker bootstrap; or make official plugins avoid module-level `qwenpaw.constant` imports.

We applied the two-point fix as a downstream packaging patch (idempotent, re-applied on every start) and verified end-to-end: a subprocess spawned with the patched launch environment runs the real worker bootstrap cleaning and imports `qwenpaw.constant` successfully.

## Reproduction

1. Deploy QwenPaw 2.3.0 Hub on Linux (any service account; the variables are stripped from the worker env regardless of the passwd home).
2. Install/enable the official WeChat channel plugin.
3. Observe the worker crash above and `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED` in the console.

---

Related worker-startup reports with different root causes: #8644 (Desktop frozen build, identity probe AttributeError), #8669 (startup race in `_wait_connected`).

issues.title: [Feature]: 希望内置「千问AI平台」（qianwenai.com）供应商预设，原生支持按量付费与 Token Plan
issues.body:
## Summary

希望为 **千问AI平台**（[www.qianwenai.com](https://www.qianwenai.com)，控制台 platform.qianwenai.com）增加内置供应商预设，原生覆盖其**按量付费**与 **Token Plan**（个人版/团队版）两类端点。千问AI平台是千问官方的企业级模型服务平台，QwenPaw 由千问实验室 AgentScope 团队打造，两者同属千问产品生态，期待能开箱即用地打通；目前用户仍需按平台文档手动修改 base_url 或手写自定义供应商配置才能接入。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Documentation (website)

## Problem / Motivation

千问AI平台提供 400+ 模型（Qwen3.8 系列、qwen4-max-preview、DeepSeek、GLM、Kimi 等），兼容 OpenAI / Anthropic / DashScope 协议，并提供官方 DashScope SDK（Python/Java）。平台文档已把 QwenPaw 列入官方接入指南，但当前接入方式依赖手动配置：

1. **内置预设端点与平台当前官方端点不一致**。我在本机核对了 QwenPaw 桌面版内置供应商目录（`providers/data`，catalog_version `2026.10.28.1`）：
   - `dashscope` → `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`
   - `aliyun-tokenplan` / `aliyun-tokenplan-intl` → `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` / `https://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`
   - `aliyun-codingplan` → `https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1`

   均不指向千问AI平台当前的官方端点：
   - 按量付费：`https://maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1`（Anthropic 兼容：`https://maas.qianwenaiapi.com/apps/anthropic`）
   - Token Plan：`https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1`（Anthropic 兼容：`https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/apps/anthropic`）

2. **平台官方 QwenPaw 接入指南目前引导用户"借用"现有预设**：按量付费需要在内置 DashScope 供应商设置里手动把基础 URL 改为 `https://maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1`；Token Plan 的配置文件方式则要手写 `~/.qwenpaw.secret/providers/custom/<provider-id>.json`（自行维护模型列表、max_tokens、supports_image 等字段）。对普通用户门槛偏高，也容易填错。

3. **密钥与端点必须配套使用**（平台文档明确说明，不可混用）：按量付费 API Key 为 `sk-ws-` 开头（早期密钥为 `sk-`），Token Plan API Key 为 `sk-sp-` 开头。没有专用预设与提示时，用户容易把密钥填进不配套的端点。

4. **模型目录与能力声明滞后**：平台指南中的 `qwen4-max-preview`、`deepseek-v4.1-flash` 等新模型不在内置目录中；思考参数声明缺失的问题已在 #7990 中单独反馈。

## Proposed Solution

新增千问AI平台内置供应商预设（命名与拆分方式尊重维护者设计，例如 `qianwenai` + `qianwenai-tokenplan`）：

1. 默认 base_url 直接指向平台当前官方端点，按量付费与 Token Plan 分开；OpenAI 兼容优先，可选支持 Anthropic 兼容端点。
2. 内置模型目录覆盖平台当前主力模型（`qwen4-max-preview`、`qwen3.8-max`、`qwen3.8-flash`、`qwen3.7-plus`、`deepseek-v4.1-flash` 等），并按平台「思考模式」文档声明 `thinking_param_style`（可与 #7990 一并处理）。
3. 在密钥输入处给出格式与配套提示（`sk-ws-` 对应按量付费、`sk-sp-` 对应 Token Plan），避免混用。
4. 同步官网供应商文档；平台侧的 QwenPaw 接入指南也可随之简化为"选择预设 → 填入 API Key"。

如果维护者认为更合适的做法是把现有 `dashscope` / `aliyun-tokenplan` 预设的默认端点迁移或别名为新域名，也完全可以接受。核心诉求是千问AI平台在 QwenPaw 中开箱即用。

## Alternatives Considered

- 按平台指南手动配置（修改 DashScope 预设的 base_url，或手写 custom provider JSON）：可用，但每个用户都要自行查询端点、密钥配套规则和模型参数，且享受不到内置模型目录的能力门控（思考控件、多模态声明等）。
- 手改安装目录下的 `model_catalog.json`：升级会被覆盖（#7990 中已提到）。

## Additional Context

- 千问AI平台官网：https://www.qianwenai.com
- 快速入门（含 OpenAI 兼容示例与 base_url）：https://platform.qianwenai.com/docs/developer-guides/getting-started/introduction
- API Key 与端点配套规则：https://platform.qianwenai.com/docs/developer-guides/administration/api-keys
- 平台官方 QwenPaw 接入指南：https://platform.qianwenai.com/docs/developer-guides/clients-and-developer-tools/qwenpaw
- 通用接入指南（两类端点 URL 出处）：https://platform.qianwenai.com/docs/developer-guides/clients-and-developer-tools/other-tools
- 相关 issue：#7990（Aliyun Token Plan 模型 `thinking_param_style` 声明）
- 内置端点信息核对于本机 QwenPaw 桌面版 `providers/data`（catalog_version `2026.10.28.1`），未做任何修改。

感谢团队的维护与审阅，期待千问自家平台在 QwenPaw 中的原生支持。

## Willing to Contribute

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

issues.title: [Feature]: Multi-user support

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Context

QwenPaw 2.3 appears to be single-user by design: setting `QWENPAW_AUTH_ENABLED=true` and calling `POST /api/auth/register` once creates a single account>

We confirmed this from the source in `/app/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/qwenpaw/app/routers/auth.py`: after the first registration, `has_registered>

In a PoC with a couple of trusted users this is acceptable, but it blocks several real-world patterns:

- confidential drafting (client reports, HR letters, personal correspondence) leaks into the shared chat history
- accumulated agent memory becomes a mix of multiple users' context, degrading personalization and introducing surprising cross-talk
- provider API keys added by one user (e.g. a personal OpenAI key for occasional frontier calls) become usable by anyone else authenticated

## Requested feature

Per-user data isolation under a single running instance. A possible shape:

- Multiple registered accounts (lift the `has_registered_users()` single-user gate)
- Each account has its own workspace directory (e.g. `working/users/<username>/`) with separate `history.db`, `MEMORY.md`, `PROFILE.md`, `SOUL.md`, uplo>
- Provider configurations configurable as either per-user or shared (admin-controlled)
- Optionally, role-based access (admin vs standard user) for managing providers and plugins instance-wide

## Alternatives we've considered

- **One container per user** behind a reverse proxy with path-based routing. Works for ≤5 users but doesn't scale (plugin/model setup becomes N× the wor>
- **Fork and patch** `auth.py` + workspace discovery to be user-aware. Too invasive to maintain against upstream for anything but a short-term bridge.
- **External SSO with per-session scoping** (OIDC in front of QwenPaw). Doesn't help because the underlying data layer is still single-tenant.

## Deployment details

- Version: QwenPaw 2.3.0 (`agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`, deployed 2026-11-11)
- Backend: self-hosted vLLM (Qwen3.8-27B GPTQ Int4 on 2× RTX 3090 NVLink), tool calling via `qwen3_xml` parser
- Current workaround: a single shared account with the whole user cohort fully informed that the workspace is non-private
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Docker 29.1

Happy to refine the spec, help review design proposals, or test preview builds against a real multi-user cohort. Thanks!

issues.title: [v2.3.0] 控制台侧边栏丢失「检查点」入口：checkpoints 导航的 parentId 指向已移除的 core.agent-group
issues.body:
### 环境

- QwenPaw Desktop **v2.3.0**，Windows 10 x64
- v2.3.0 桌面安装包随附的控制台入口 bundle：`assets/index-OpgHLVkg.js`

### 问题现象

升级到 v2.3.0 后，控制台侧边栏（选中智能体后的 agent-scoped 区域）**找不到「检查点」入口**。页面本身（`/checkpoints` 路由）和后端 API（`/api/workspace/checkpoints/status|graph|auto|snapshot|restore|gc`）都正常工作，只是导航项不渲染了。

### 根因（来自随 v2.3.0 发货的前端 bundle）

v2.3.0 中 agent-scoped 侧边栏的分组只有：

```js
{ id: "core.control-group",   ..., isGroup: true, order: 20 }
{ id: "core.workspace-group", label: nav.agent, isGroup: true, order: 30 }   // 子项：files/skills/tools/mcp/acp/agent-config/agent-stats
```

`core.agent-group` 这个分组在 bundle 里已不存在（搜不到定义），但「检查点」导航项注册时仍指向旧父分组：

```js
{ id: "core.checkpoints", location: "primary.agentScoped", parentId: "core.agent-group", route: "core.checkpoints", order: 80 }
```

父分组被移除/改名后，该项成为孤儿节点，侧边栏渲染时被丢弃。对比 assets 目录里保留的旧版本 bundle（如 `index-CANC2e5e.js`）仍定义了 `core.agent-group`，所以升级前入口是可见的——据此判断是 v2.3.0 重构分组 id 时漏改了这一处引用。

### 修复建议

将该导航项改挂到现存的分组，例如 `parentId: "core.workspace-group"`（order 80 排在 agent-stats 之后），或者恢复 `core.agent-group` 分组定义。

### v2.3.0 用户的临时绕过

直接访问检查点页面：`http://127.0.0.1:<backend-port>/checkpoints`（桌面端后端端口，例如 `12095`）。

issues.title: [Bug] Shared frontend, two agents, two WeChat accounts: upgrade duplicates the credential and only one channel can run
issues.body:
## Scenario

One QwenPaw installation (one desktop frontend) is shared by **two family members**, each with their own agent:

| agent | owner | WeChat account |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | person A | A's WeChat bot |
| `VRPUDS` | person B | B's WeChat bot |

This is the same installation, the same UI, two agents — not two installs. `channels.wechat` is a per-agent config, so this looks supported on paper; in 2.3 it is not.

## What happens on 2.3.0

**1. The upgrade re-creates the duplicate credential**

`VRPUDS/agent.json` was rewritten during the upgrade (22:59:22, right after `config.json` at 22:58:51) with `channels.wechat.enabled=true` and the **same 58-character `bot_token`** that `default` already had. Because an inline credential hashes to `domain + token`, both agents then claim the same account:

```
channel 'wechat' failed: default@1979294902288:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE;
                        VRPUDS@19794…:  Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
```

**2. Independent per-agent credentials still collide**

Clearing the inline token and giving each agent its own `bot_token_file` (`<workspace>/wechat_bot_token`) does not help, because custody resolves *other* agents' scopes against the process-wide directory:

```python
# app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
others.append((
    runtime_key,
    configured,
    frozenset(wechat_auth_scopes(other, working_dir=WORKING_DIR)),
))
```

`wechat_auth_scopes()` falls back to `working_dir / "wechat_bot_token"`, so every agent without an explicit file resolves to the **same** path and the **same** `wechat_context_tokens.json` → identical scope hashes → `ACCOUNT_IN_USE`. (Fix proposed in the linked PR.)

**3. Only one WeChat channel can run per installation (blocker)**

Even with distinct credential files, a second agent cannot start its channel while the first one runs. Its channel page returns 500:

```
GET /api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode  (X-Agent-Id: VRPUDS)  -> 500
qwenpaw/app/channels/qrcode_sessions.py:555 in fetch
qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:621 in execution_source
qwenpaw.plugins.ownership.RuntimeSourceBusyError: RUNTIME_SOURCE_MUTATING
```

The channel plugin has a single execution source, so the running `default` channel keeps the source leased and the second agent cannot even fetch a login QR code.

## Why this matters for the shared-frontend use case

`#8187` moved channels into plugins with subprocess isolation for good reasons (less SDK in the host, isolated channel failures, credential/SSRF hardening). But the result is that a *per-agent* channel configuration behaves like a *per-installation* one:

- two family members on one frontend cannot each bind their own WeChat account;
- the migration silently copies one member's credential to the other, which is a **privacy problem** in this scenario, not just a startup error;
- the failure mode is a whole-plugin `failed` state, so neither member's channel works.

## Expected

1. **Migration must not duplicate a credential**: when copying/creating agent profiles, a WeChat identity should stay with exactly one agent (`active_agent`), the others get `enabled=false` and no token (log it: `credential already owned by <agent>`).
2. **Custody should resolve each agent's credential against its own workspace** (the linked PR): two agents with different token files, or no explicit file, must not share scope hashes.
3. **Two channels of the same plugin should be able to coexist** across different agent workspaces — isolation is already per workspace for runtime keys; the execution source should follow that, or the constraint should be documented and reported as a clear `MULTI_AGENT_CHANNEL_UNSUPPORTED` instead of a 500 while another agent's channel is up.

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0** (Windows desktop), two agents, `channels.wechat` enabled on both.
- Related: `#8187` (channels → plugins, subprocess isolation), `#8653` (dependency dir stability).

## Workarounds today

- Keep exactly one agent with WeChat enabled per installation (the other member gets no WeChat), or
- run a second installation with its own `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` (one account per instance — which defeats the shared-frontend model).

issues.title: [Bug]: Subagent completions incorrectly trigger the "Reply completion" desktop notification
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`). Also verified against `main` (`__version__ = "2.3.1b1"`) — `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py` is identical there, so the bug is not yet fixed upstream.

## Description

With Console → Notifications → "Reply completion" enabled, **a desktop notification ("The agent has finished a reply") is also fired every time a subagent finishes** — i.e. when the main agent calls `spawn_subagent`, `submit_to_agent`, or `chat_with_agent`.

The user only cares whether *their own* turn has finished. A subagent is an internal child task of the main agent; its completion should never produce a user-facing reminder.

When one task dispatches several subagents (especially with `batch` or `background=true`), the user receives multiple unrelated "The agent has finished a reply" notifications in quick succession — often while the main task is still running — which is misleading and looks like their request has already been answered.

**Related PR(s):** None

**Security considerations:** None (notification noise only; no auth, config, or credential exposure)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

> The event is published by the backend; the frontend only renders it. The root cause is backend-side, so only Core is checked. The `systemNotifications.conversation` toggle itself behaves correctly.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Linux (Docker container on a 6.6 kernel host)
- **Install method:** Docker (`agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Console → Settings → Notifications, enable "Desktop notifications" and the "Reply completion" (`conversation`) category, and grant browser notification permission.
2. Send the main agent a task that makes it spawn a subagent, e.g.:
   - "Use `spawn_subagent` to count files in directories A, B and C separately, then summarize."
   - or let it call `submit_to_agent` / `chat_with_agent` to talk to another agent.
3. Keep the Console tab in the background (or minimized) and watch system notifications.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** One "The agent has finished a reply" notification per subagent completion. N subagents → N notifications, sometimes before the main task finishes. Also reproduces with `spawn_subagent(background=true)` and `batch` mode.
- **Expected:** The "Reply completion" notification should fire only when a turn **initiated directly by the user** completes. Subagent runs, background child tasks, and inter-agent internal calls must not trigger it.

## Logs / Screenshots

The notification is published unconditionally at the end of `stream_one()` in `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py` (~lines 545–556; identical in v2.3.0 and `main`):

```python
if (
    not err_msg
    and last_response is not None
    and last_response.status == RunStatus.Completed
    and session_id
):
    publish_notification(
        category=f"conversation",
        agent_id=getattr(self._workspace, f"agent_id", f"default"),
        title=f"QwenPaw",
        body=f"",
        session_id=notification_session_id,
    )
```

A comment in the same function states that `stream_one` is **the single executor for every path**:

> `stream_one is the single console executor for the web streaming, background-task, and terminal CLI paths`

Subagent requests travel through the very same path via `POST /console/chat` and `POST /console/chat/task`:

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`
  - `stream_agent_chat()` / `collect_final_agent_chat_response()` → `POST /console/chat`
  - `submit_agent_chat_task()` → `POST /console/chat/task`

So a finished subagent also satisfies `status == RunStatus.Completed` and also reaches `publish_notification`.

## Additional Notes

### Root cause

1. `stream_one()` publishes the notification **without inspecting the request origin** — any completed response triggers it.
2. The codebase already has a way to identify subagents; this call site just doesn't use it:
   - `spawn_subagent` sets `_spawn_subagent: True` in `request_context` (`_build_spawn_request_context` in `agent_management.py`), with session ids shaped like `sub-xxxxxxxx`;
   - `_chat_registration_fields()` in `app/routers/console.py` uses it to tag the chat with `source: "subagent"`;
   - `services/session_thinking.py`, `app/approvals/service.py`, and `hooks/request_setup/contextvars_hook.py` all read the same flag.

### Suggested fix

Filter before publishing the `conversation` notification:

```python
request_context = getattr(request, "request_context", None) or {}
is_internal_call = (
    isinstance(request_context, dict)
    and request_context.get("_spawn_subagent") is True
)
if not err_msg and not is_internal_call and last_response is not None and ...:
    publish_notification(...)
```

### Coverage gap worth noting

Checking only `_spawn_subagent` is **incomplete**:

- `chat_with_agent()` / `submit_to_agent()` go through `build_agent_chat_request()`, whose `request_context` currently carries only `root_agent_id` — **no** `_spawn_subagent` — with session ids shaped like `{from}:to:{to}:{ts}:{uuid}`.
- Those paths would therefore still leak notifications. Either:
  - **(a)** add a shared internal-call flag (e.g. `_agent_internal: True`) in `build_agent_chat_request()` and check both, or
  - **(b)** additionally check the session-id prefix (`sub-` / `:to:`) at the publish site as a fallback.

### Related issues (not duplicates)

- #7107 [Feature]: System notification when a response or task completes while the Console/Desktop app is not focused — the feature this notification implements; this issue is an edge-case defect in that implementation.
- #5797 [Feature]: 定时任务结果弹窗提醒应加开关 — about a user-facing toggle for cron reminders; unrelated.
- #6084 Desktop 任务完成或审核请求的弹窗通知 — feature request; does not cover subagent filtering.

---

## 中文版（Chinese）

### QwenPaw 版本

2.3.0（Docker 镜像 `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`）；同时已核对 `main` 分支（`__version__ = "2.3.1b1"`）的 `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py`，问题代码一致，说明上游尚未修复。

### 描述

当 Console 的「桌面通知 → 回复完成（Reply completion）」开启后，**子智能体（`spawn_subagent` / `submit_to_agent` / `chat_with_agent`）完成任务时也会弹出「Agent 已完成一轮回复」的桌面通知**。

用户只关心自己发起的对话轮次是否完成。子智能体属于主智能体的内部子任务，其完成不应产生面向用户的提醒。

在一次主任务派发多个 subagent（尤其是 `batch` 或 `background=true`）时，用户会在短时间内连续收到多条互不相关的「Agent 已完成一轮回复」，实际到手时主任务往往还没结束，容易被误导为「我的请求已经答完了」。

**关联 PR：** 无

**安全影响：** 无（仅通知噪音，不涉及权限、配置或凭据暴露）

### 影响组件

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

> 说明：通知事件由后端发布、前端仅负责展示，根因在后端，故只勾 Core。前端 `systemNotifications.conversation` 开关本身行为正常。

### 环境

- **QwenPaw 版本：** 2.3.0
- **操作系统：** Linux（Docker 容器，宿主机内核 6.6）
- **安装方式：** Docker（`agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`）
- **Python 版本：** 3.11

### 复现步骤

1. 打开 Console → 设置 → 通知，开启「桌面通知」与「回复完成」（`conversation`）类别，并允许浏览器通知权限。
2. 向主智能体发送一个会让它调用子智能体的任务，例如：
   - 「用 `spawn_subagent` 分别统计 A、B、C 三个目录的文件数，再汇总」
   - 或直接让它 `submit_to_agent` / `chat_with_agent` 与其他智能体通信
3. 保持 Console 页面在后台（或最小化），观察系统通知。

### 实际 vs 预期

- **实际：** 每个子智能体完成时都会弹出一条「Agent 已完成一轮回复」。N 个子智能体 → N 条通知（甚至主任务还在跑就先弹了）。`spawn_subagent(background=true)` 与 `batch` 模式下同样会弹。
- **预期：** 只有**用户直接发起**的那一轮对话完成时才弹「回复完成」通知；子智能体、后台子任务、跨智能体内部调用的完成不应触发该通知。

### 日志 / 截图

通知由后端在 `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py` 的 `stream_one()` 尾部无条件发布（约第 545–556 行，v2.3.0 与 `main` 一致）：

```python
if (
    not err_msg
    and last_response is not None
    and last_response.status == RunStatus.Completed
    and session_id
):
    publish_notification(
        category=f"conversation",
        agent_id=getattr(self._workspace, f"agent_id", f"default"),
        title=f"QwenPaw",
        body=f"",
        session_id=notification_session_id,
    )
```

而 `stream_one` 的函数注释里明确写着它是**所有执行路径的统一入口**：

> `stream_one is the single console executor for the web streaming, background-task, and terminal CLI paths`

子智能体的请求同样经由 `POST /console/chat` 与 `POST /console/chat/task` 走这条路径：

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`
  - `stream_agent_chat()` / `collect_final_agent_chat_response()` → `POST /console/chat`
  - `submit_agent_chat_task()` → `POST /console/chat/task`

因此子智能体跑完同样满足 `status == RunStatus.Completed`，同样会 `publish_notification`。

### 补充说明

#### 根因定位（供参考）

1. `stream_one()` 发布通知前**没有区分请求来源**，只要响应完成就发。
2. 系统里其实已经有识别子智能体的机制，只是这一处没用上：
   - `spawn_subagent` 的 `request_context` 带 `_spawn_subagent: True`（`agent_management.py` 的 `_build_spawn_request_context`），session id 也是 `sub-xxxxxxxx` 形态；
   - `app/routers/console.py` 的 `_chat_registration_fields()` 已用它把 chat 标记为 `source: "subagent"`；
   - `services/session_thinking.py`、`app/approvals/service.py`、`hooks/request_setup/contextvars_hook.py` 等多处也都在读这个标记。

#### 建议修复方向

在 `stream_one()` 发布 `conversation` 通知前增加过滤，例如：

```python
request_context = getattr(request, "request_context", None) or {}
is_internal_call = (
    isinstance(request_context, dict)
    and request_context.get("_spawn_subagent") is True
)
if not err_msg and not is_internal_call and last_response is not None and ...:
    publish_notification(...)
```

#### 需要注意的覆盖盲区

仅判断 `_spawn_subagent` **覆盖不全**：

- `chat_with_agent()` / `submit_to_agent()` 走 `build_agent_chat_request()`，其 `request_context` 目前只有 `root_agent_id`，**不带** `_spawn_subagent`，session id 形如 `{from}:to:{to}:{ts}:{uuid}`。
- 因此这两个工具触发的通知仍会漏过过滤。建议二选一：
  - **(a)** 在 `build_agent_chat_request()` 里也补上统一标记（如 `_agent_internal: True`），过滤时一并判断；
  - **(b)** 在发布处同时判断 session 前缀（`sub-` / `:to:`）作为兜底。

#### 关联 issue（不重复）

- #7107 [Feature]: System notification when a response or task completes while the Console/Desktop app is not focused —— 本通知功能的需求来源，本 issue 是其实现的一个边界缺陷。
- #5797 [Feature]: 定时任务结果弹窗提醒应加开关 —— 讨论的是 cron 提醒开关，与本问题不重复。
- #6084 Desktop 任务完成或审核请求的弹窗通知 —— 需求类，未涉及子智能体过滤。

issues.title: [Bug]: Feishu channel uploads percent-encoded filenames for non-ASCII names since 2.3.0 — file card shows %E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-…docx
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (pip, site-packages). `feishu` channel plugin `0.1.0.dev0`, `agentscope` 2.0.10, Python 3.11.17.

Re-verified against `main` @ `f47dd19bd1442b989eeb8df8d146cbbab572d0b1`: the relevant code is byte-identical, the bug is still present.

**Related PR(s):** #4600 (identical bug fixed for DingTalk — merged), #7192 (same class of bug fixed on the Console side only)

**Security considerations:** none.

## Description

After upgrading to 2.3.0 (where the Feishu channel was rewritten as an out-of-tree channel plugin), any file sent to a Feishu chat via `send_file_to_user` whose filename contains non-ASCII characters (e.g. Chinese) is uploaded with a **percent-encoded** `file_name`, so the Feishu file card shows `%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-%E4%B8%BB%E8%A6%81%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%B7%A5%E6%97%B6%E5%AF%B9%E6%A0%87%E6%B5%8B%E7%AE%97%E6%83%85%E5%86%B5.docx` instead of `附件-主要工作工时对标测算情况.docx`.

- The file content is fine — it downloads and opens normally, only the displayed/uploaded name is mangled.
- ASCII-only filenames are unaffected (percent-encoding is identity for them), which is why this went unnoticed for a while.
- Images are unaffected (uploaded by bytes as `image.png`, `image_key` path).

This is a regression: in 2.2.x the in-tree Feishu channel resolved the `file://` URL through `file_url_to_local_path()` (which calls `unquote`) and then uploaded `path.name`, so Chinese names were delivered correctly.

### Root cause

1. `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/send_file.py` returns a `DataBlock` with a readable `name`:

   ```python
   DataBlock(source=URLSource(url=file_url, media_type=mime_type),
             name=os.path.basename(file_path))
   ```

2. `URLSource.url` is typed `AnyUrl` (`agentscope/message/_block.py:72`), so pydantic normalizes the URL and **percent-encodes non-ASCII path segments**:

   ```json
   "url": "file:///app/working/workspaces/<agent>/documents/.../%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-...docx",
   "name": "附件-主要工作工时对标测算情况.docx"
   ```

3. `src/qwenpaw/runtime/envelope.py` (`TOOL_RESULT_DATA_DELTA`, lines 541–558) rebuilds the media block for the completed tool-result message with **only `type` + `source`**:

   ```python
   blocks_dict[block_id] = {"type": block_type, "source": source}
   ```

   The display name is structurally unavailable here: `agentscope`'s `ToolResultDataDeltaEvent` (`agentscope/event/_event.py:378-396`) has no `name`/`filename` field. So `DataBlock.name` is dropped before any channel sees it.

4. `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/renderer.py:292-295` therefore renders `FileContent(file_url="file:///...%E9%99%84…", filename=None)`.

5. `plugins/channel/feishu/qwenpaw_channel_feishu/platform.py:1231-1232` falls back to the URL basename **without decoding it**, and passes it to the upload API (`…:1256` `.file_name(Path(filename).name)`):

   ```python
   filename = str(
       part.get("filename") or Path(locator).name or "file.bin",
   )
   ```

   `Path("file:///…/%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-….docx").name` → `"%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-….docx"`.

Every other media plugin already decodes the URL basename — DingTalk `transport.py:1745` (`base = unquote(os.path.basename(path))`, from PR #4600), onebot `media.py:171`, slack `sender.py:60`, azure_bot `platform.py:538`. The new Feishu plugin is the only one missing it.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 (pip install)
- **OS:** Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), Linux 6.8.0 x86_64
- **Install method:** pip (into a venv, `site-packages`)
- **Python version:** 3.11.17
- **Channel:** `feishu` plugin 0.1.0.dev0 (`process_mode: runner_process`), `domain: feishu`

## Steps to Reproduce

**User-level**

1. Configure the Feishu channel and connect a bot.
2. Ask the agent to send any local file with a Chinese filename:
   `send_file_to_user("/path/to/附件-主要工作工时对标测算情况.docx")`
3. Open the resulting file card in the Feishu chat.

**Deterministic, no Feishu credentials needed** (this is what the pipeline actually computes):

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from qwenpaw.schemas import Message, DataContent, MessageType
from qwenpaw.app.channels.renderer import MessageRenderer, RenderStyle

# block shape produced by runtime/envelope.py TOOL_RESULT_DATA_DELTA (no "name")
blocks = [{
    "type": "data",
    "source": {
        "type": "url",
        "url": "file:///app/w/%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-%E4%B8%BB%E8%A6%81.docx",
        "media_type": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
    },
}, {"type": "text", "text": "File sent successfully."}]

msg = Message(type=MessageType.FUNCTION_CALL_OUTPUT, role="assistant",
              content=[DataContent(data={"name": "send_file_to_user",
                                         "output": json.dumps(blocks, ensure_ascii=False)})])

for p in MessageRenderer(RenderStyle()).message_to_semantic_parts(msg):
    if getattr(p.part, "file_url", None):
        locator = p.part.file_url
        # what plugins/channel/feishu/.../platform.py:1231 does
        print("filename =", p.part.filename)
        print("uploaded =", Path(str(p.part.filename or Path(locator).name)).name)
```

Output:

```
filename = None
uploaded = %E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-%E4%B8%BB%E8%A6%81.docx
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `file_name` sent to `POST /open-apis/im/v1/files` is `%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-主要工作工时对标测算情况.docx` (fully percent-encoded); the Feishu card shows the encoded string.
- **Expected:** `附件-主要工作工时对标测算情况.docx`, i.e. the `DataBlock.name` (or, failing that, the decoded URL basename).

## Logs / Screenshots

Observed in the recipient's Feishu client (sent by an agent on 2.3.0):

```
%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-%E4%B8%BB%E8%A6%81%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%B7%A5%E6%97%B6%E5%AF%B9%E6%A0%87%E6%B5%8B%E7%AE%97%E6%83%85%E5%86%B5.docx
```

The persisted tool result in the sending agent's `history.db` still carries the correct display name and the encoded URL — the loss happens downstream of it:

```json
{"type": "data",
 "source": {"type": "url",
            "url": "file:///…%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6-%E4%B8%BB%E8%A6%81%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%B7%A5%E6%97%B6%E5%AF%B9%E6%A0%87%E6%B5%8B%E7%AE%97%E6%83%85%E5%86%B5.docx",
            "media_type": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document"},
 "name": "附件-主要工作工时对标测算情况.docx"}
```

The `feishu` worker currently logs neither the received part nor the upload filename at INFO level, so the mangled name is invisible in `qwenpaw.log`.

## Additional Notes

**Workaround:** send files with ASCII-only names (or rename before `send_file_to_user`). Non-ASCII names always surface encoded.

**Proposed fixes** (either one fixes this report; I would suggest 1 now, 2 to follow):

1. **Plugin (minimal, mirrors DingTalk PR #4600)** — decode the fallback in `plugins/channel/feishu/qwenpaw_channel_feishu/platform.py::_send_file_part`:

   ```python
   from urllib.parse import unquote
   filename = str(
       part.get("filename") or unquote(Path(locator).name) or "file.bin",
   )
   ```

   Note `locator` may also be a `data:` URL; `media_basename`/`unquote` should be guarded the same way the other plugins do it.

2. **Core (removes the root cause for every channel)** — stop dropping the display name when the tool-result message is built: give `ToolResultDataDeltaEvent` (or the envelope's rebuild at `runtime/envelope.py:555-558`) a `name`/`filename` field carried from `DataBlock.name`, so channels receive `filename` and never need to reverse-engineer it from the URL. Today the URL basename is treated as the name, which is only correct for ASCII paths.

**Related / precedent**

- #4600 — same symptom fixed for DingTalk (`unquote(os.path.basename(path))`), merged 2026-05-22.
- #7136 → #7192 — same class of bug on the Console file card; that fix touched only `console/src/components/Chat/ToolCards/shared/utils.ts`, so the channel path stayed broken.
- #6510 — related family (Feishu + URL-encoded Chinese paths, inbound `FileNotFoundError`), different code path, still open; this report is the outbound half.
- Not affected: 2.2.x in-tree Feishu channel (`file_url_to_local_path()` decoded the URL before upload) — hence "regression in 2.3.0".

Happy to send a PR for fix (1) with a regression test on `_send_file_part` if the direction is acceptable.

issues.title: [Bug]: Automatic Memory Search 开启后同一轮重复调用 memory_search，拦截后无法正常回复

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2

`python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('qwenpaw'))"` → `2.2.2`

## Description

开启 **Automatic Memory Search（自动记忆搜索）** 后，同一个用户回合内，模型会以相同或几乎相同的 query 反复调用 `memory_search`。

达到第 4 次重复调用后被重复搜索保护拦截，但**拦截之后的正常回复仍然无法生成**：收尾（finalize）与一次受控恢复（recovery）产出的内容被判定为 `tool_block` 或 `raw_tool_markup`，最终向用户返回固定兜底文案，而不是基于已有记忆结果的正常回答。

关键对照：

- **关闭 Automatic Memory Search 后，同一段对话可以正常继续。**
- 更换模型（本地 35B 与云端 Qwen3.8-Flash 等）后**仍可复现**。

因此这不是单一模型的工具调用能力问题，更像是自动记忆注入内容与工具调用循环之间的交互问题。

预期：自动搜索在同一用户回合最多执行一次，结果作为参考上下文提供；即使模型仍重复搜索，也应拦截工具调用并**基于已有结果生成正常回答**，而不是返回兜底。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Windows 10 (AMD64)
- **Install method:** 本地 venv 安装（`pip install qwenpaw`，启动脚本 `启动QwenPaw-2.2.2.bat`）
- **Python version:** 3.11.9
- **Memory backend:** ReMeLight
- **Automatic Memory Search:** enabled
- **Relevant config:** `auto_memory_search_config.enabled = true`
- **Channel:** WeChat / Console

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 在记忆设置中开启 Automatic Memory Search，并确保该 agent 已有可检索的历史记忆。
2. 在一个已有较长上下文的会话中正常提问，使自动记忆搜索被触发。
3. 观察同一用户回合内模型的工具调用：会以相同或等价 query 再次调用 `memory_search`。
4. 重复到第 4 次时被重复搜索保护拦截，停止继续执行工具。
5. 观察最终回复：收尾与恢复生成的内容被判定为 `tool_block` / `raw_tool_markup`。
6. 最终用户收到固定兜底文案（"本轮检测到重复搜索……请重发一次"），而不是正常回答。
7. 对照组：关闭 Automatic Memory Search，同一会话可正常回复。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:**
  - 同一用户回合内 `memory_search` 被重复调用多次，参数相同或高度相似；
  - 第 4 次被拦截后，收尾/恢复的输出被判定为包含结构化工具块或原始工具标签，判为无效；
  - 用户最终只收到固定兜底文案；
  - 该行为跨模型复现；关闭自动搜索后不再出现。

- **Expected:**
  - 同一真实用户回合只自动搜索一次；
  - 自动搜索结果作为明确的"系统提供的参考上下文"进入模型，不表现为模型刚刚发起的一次工具调用；
  - 若模型仍然重复搜索，拦截工具执行，但允许基于已有结果生成纯文本回答；
  - 已存在可用记忆结果时，不应返回"请重发一次"这类兜底。

## Logs / Screenshots

日志中可观察到的关键序列（示意，已去除会话内容）：

```text
MemoryMiddleware: memory_search repeated (same query, same params)
MemoryMiddleware: repeated memory_search blocked (4th call)
MemoryMiddleware: memory_search finalization — answering without tools
MemoryMiddleware: finalization rejected (reason=tool_block)
MemoryMiddleware: attempting one recovery answer
MemoryMiddleware: recovery rejected (reason=raw_tool_markup)
MemoryMiddleware: returning fallback reply
```

另一模型复现时出现的预算分支：

```text
MemoryMiddleware: recovery skipped (reason=budget_unknown, no output limit)
```

说明：被拒绝的具体模型原文未落盘，因此无法提供逐字内容；但拒绝原因码与"返回兜底"的结果可稳定复现。

## Relation to PR #6120

PR #6120（`fix(memory): restrict automatic memory to external user queries`）解决的是**另一层**问题：只有带 `external_user_query` 标记的真实外部用户消息才能触发自动搜索，内部注入的 `loop_continuation` 等 `user` 角色消息不再被误认为新用户问题。

该修复在 2.2.2 中已存在且生效：本地实测中，加入一条 `loop_continuation` 警告后，自动搜索次数仍为 1，且搜索使用的是原真实用户消息。

因此本 issue **不是 #6120 的回归**，而是剩余的一层：

- 自动搜索**结果本身**在上下文中仍以「assistant 文本 + thinking + `memory_search` tool_call + tool_result」的形态呈现；
- 该结构可能被模型当作"自己刚发起的、可继续重复的工具交互"来模仿；
- 重复调用被拦截后，收尾/恢复阶段仍可能产出工具块或原始工具标签，导致最终没有可用正文。

## Suggested Fix (compromise, keeps the feature)

保留 Automatic Memory Search 与完整检索结果，只改变"结果的呈现方式"，并给收尾阶段一个明确的成功出口：

1. **区分自动证据与真实工具调用**
   为自动注入结果增加内部标记（例如 `auto_memory_evidence`），并在构造时不再复用 assistant 工具调用形态；以系统参考上下文的身份呈现，保留完整结果正文与来源信息。

2. **保持注入去重与回合隔离**
   同一真实用户回合只搜索一次；多次 model call 复用同一份证据，不重复叠加；跨回合不串用；关闭自动搜索时完全不注入。

3. **不要让它冒充真实用户消息**
   证据消息不得携带 `external_user_query` 标记，避免影响用户问题识别与自动记忆批次边界。

4. **拦截后必须能给出正文**
   重复搜索被拦截时，使用已有证据生成纯文本回答；若首次收尾被判定无效，允许一次恢复，且恢复请求不得重新注入可被模仿的工具调用示范。

5. **失败要可诊断**
   在拒绝时记录原因码与被拒绝内容的类型（是否为结构化工具块、命中哪类标签、是否 final 帧），便于区分"模型真调用工具"与"校验误杀"。

## Additional Notes

- 临时规避：关闭 Automatic Memory Search 后问题消失（已实测）；agent 仍可在需要时显式调用 `memory_search`。
- 相关历史 issue：#6113（一直卡在搜索记忆）、#6241（`memory_search` 死循环）。两者均已关闭，本 issue 描述的是**#6120 之后仍然存在的剩余部分**：重复搜索被拦截后无法产出正常回复。
- 本 issue 不涉及安全或凭据问题。

issues.title: [Bug]: feishu channel reconnect supervisor exits permanently when disconnect cleanup raises
issues.body:
**Title:** `[Bug]: feishu channel reconnect supervisor exits permanently when disconnect cleanup raises`

## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0, bundled Feishu channel plugin `0.1.0.dev0` ("instance-owned connection lifecycle"). macOS arm64. Upgraded 2026-11-14 09:02 (Asia/Shanghai).

## Description

On 2026-11-15 02:22 the Feishu server rotated our long-lived websocket connection (a routine ticket refresh; the connection had been established ~17.3 h earlier). The channel transitioned `connected → disconnected → failed` within ~6 seconds and **never reconnected**, going silent for ~8.5 hours until a full application restart. The app core process stayed alive the whole time: crons fired, agent turns executed, and outbound delivery failed with `RuntimeError('CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED')`. `grep -E 'PLATFORM_START_FAILED|CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED' launchd-stderr.log` shows the state machine stuck in `failed` (`last_error=PLATFORM_START_FAILED`) with no retry attempt in between.

**Code path.** The plugin sets `auto_reconnect=False` on the Lark SDK and relies on `FeishuDriver._supervise()` (plugins/channel/feishu/qwenpaw_channel_feishu/driver.py) as the only reconnect supervisor. After waking on `wait_disconnected()`, it calls `platform.disconnect()` **outside** its retry loop. That cleanup deliberately raises on incomplete teardown (5 s timeout, thread not stopped, socket handle not cleared), and on the server-kick path those conditions are common: the receive loop tears the ws loop down first, and the shielded SDK close may finish after the supervisor's timeout. Any raised exception lands in the outermost `except Exception`, which only publishes `failed` — **the supervisor task itself then terminates and is never respawned**, making the exponential-backoff reconnect loop unreachable. The observed ~6 s disconnected→failed gap matches `_WS_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT * 1.2`. A second unprotected `disconnect()` call in the reconnect failure handler has the same terminal effect.

Timings are operator-reported and the exception is inferred from the state machine and timeout arithmetic; the precise traceback was not persisted by the worker log ring buffer.

**Expected behavior:** a cleanup failure after disconnect must not terminate the reconnect supervisor; the channel should retry (with backoff) until it reconnects.

**Component(s) Affected**
- [x] Channels (Feishu)
- [ ] Core / Backend — no
- [x] Tests (regression tests accompany the fix)

**Distinct from:** #2336 (legacy built-in channel reconnection, different implementation) and #8669 (startup-state race, already fixed in 2.3.0). This is the **established-connection cleanup path** in the preview plugin.

**Security considerations:** none; this issue contains no credentials, tickets, access keys or device identifiers.

## Related PR(s)

Fix PR to be linked (`fix/feishu-supervise-cleanup-exit`).

issues.title: [Bug]: Tasks submitted during background startup are silently swallowed — agent builds but never calls the LLM, no error logged

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop 2.3.0 (Windows 11 Pro, x64)
- Installed at `D:\QwenPaw\QwenPaw Desktop`
- Affected channels: Console (web UI), Feishu channel
- Models tried: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro` — behavior identical, so model-agnostic

## Description

If a chat message is submitted while background startup is still in progress, the task is accepted (HTTP 200) but silently swallowed. Every subsequent message sent to any chat — including brand-new chats and other channels — is accepted, the agent is built, and then the run dies silently before any LLM call. No error is surfaced in the UI or logs. Restarting the app or the machine is the only recovery.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start QwenPaw Desktop.
2. While startup is still running (backend logs `Background startup completed` only after ~90–100 s), submit a task in the Console (or send a Feishu message).
3. Observe: UI spinner stays forever, no response, no error.
4. Stop the stuck chat, try again in a new chat, switch models — all silently swallowed.

## Actual Behavior

- `POST /api/console/chat` returns 200 OK.
- Log shows: `builder: built agent for session=... model=... tools=1`
- Then nothing: **zero LLM inference requests, no errors, no exceptions**. Session file records turns with `turn_state: canceled` / `finished_at: null`.
- Affects ALL subsequent runs across sessions/channels (Console and Feishu verified), not just the chat that raced startup.

## Expected Behavior

Either (a) queue the submission until the runtime is ready, or (b) reject it with a clear error (e.g., 503 "runtime starting") instead of accepting and silently dropping it.

## Key Log Evidence (`desktop.log`, timestamps local)

```text
12:33:26 POST /api/console/chat 200 OK
12:33:26 builder: built agent for session=sub-f2b42fae agent=default model=haike/deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=1
12:33:26 scroll: compact timing outcome=at_or_below_trigger ...
12:34:44 Background startup completed in 92.905 seconds
   (no LLM call, no error, chat stuck in "running")
12:37:51 cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=sub-f2b42fae reason=user): CancelledError   <- only after manual stop
12:38:50 builder: built agent for session=sub-f2b42fae agent=default model=tokens1688/deepseek-v4-pro tools=1
   (again silent - new model, same result)
12:41:18 builder: built agent for session=c82227a2 agent=default model=haike/deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=1
   (Feishu channel message also swallowed)
```

For comparison, runs completed **before** this startup (11:46, 12:04, same provider) worked normally, including 97%+ cache hit rate.

## Additional Notes

- During the same startup, the Feishu plugin also failed: `Failed to activate plugin 'feishu': Projection channel failed: STARTUP_TIMEOUT` (occurred 32+ times across restarts), and `failed to load persisted envs: Permission denied on .qwenpaw_restore.lock` appears on every start — possibly related to the same racy startup path.
- Restarting the whole machine restored normal operation; a full process-level restart also recovered the pipeline.

## Impact

Silent task loss with no user-visible error — easy to misdiagnose as model/provider issues (I initially suspected model rate limits).

prs.title: fix(console): prevent adjacent conversation backgrounds from overlapping
prs.body:
## Description

On a mouse-only browser, selecting one sidebar conversation and hovering the next paints a darker overlapping strip between their backgrounds. `SidebarSessionList` allocates 38px per conversation, but the 32px action button plus 6px top/bottom padding makes `SessionItem` 44px tall. The backgrounds therefore overlap by 6px.

Give the conversation background an explicit 36px height and 2px vertical padding, retaining the existing 2px bottom margin. This fits the virtual row, centers the label and 32px desktop action button, and keeps the existing 44px touch target and its negative margin unchanged. The existing touch media rule already produced a 36px background, explaining why this is not visible in every browser environment.

This PR changes one stylesheet only and is independent of the sidebar drag/group PRs.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

- `npm run test:run -- src/components/SessionItem/SessionItem.test.tsx src/layouts/SidebarSessionList.test.tsx src/components/SessionGroupDnd/SessionGroupDnd.test.tsx` — 3 files, 54 tests passed.

Measured browser geometry:

| Input mode | Before background / row | After background / row | After gap | Action target after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse | 44px / 38px | 36px / 38px | 2px | 32px |
| Touch emulation | 36px / 38px | 36px / 38px | 2px | 44px |

Eight screenshot/geometry cases passed for mouse/touch × light/dark × 14px/20px UI font settings. Screenshots were captured and visually inspected. Text and button centers align with the row center. The production-build checks also opened the action menu, entered/cancelled inline rename (25px input within a 36px row), and activated/cancelled the real drag preview without saving changes.

The same production assets were additionally loaded in Electron 22.3.27 / Chromium 108 on Windows: mouse/touch × 14px/20px all measured 36px backgrounds in 38px rows, with 2px gaps and unchanged 32px/44px action targets. This was a Windows desktop check, not a physical touch-device or Windows 7 execution test.

Reproduce manually: use a mouse-only browser, open Chat with at least two conversations in the same expanded group, select the first, and hover the second. Before this patch their backgrounds overlap; after it they remain separated. Repeat with touch emulation to confirm that the existing touch layout remains separated.
