prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before. ZeroCode and Telegram wait the full 10 minutes; ACP waits the shorter of 10 minutes and `acp.session_timeout_secs`, because the ACP channel uses the trait's default timeout; other chat channels keep their own `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s by default), so there the shorter wait applies.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is kept in memory only. It ends at the next UTC day or month rollover, or when the daemon restarts, and a restart restores enforcement. Nothing is written to `state/cost-overrides.json`; a file left by an earlier build is ignored.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it. If the daemon refuses the answer (for example `FORBIDDEN`), the notice comes back with the error so the user can answer again; a timeout shows the error without bringing the notice back, because the daemon may already have the answer.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the #11589 row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` covers `src/agent/{approval_bridge,cost}.rs`, `src/agent/turn/{approval_gate,mod,provider_call}.rs`, `src/rpc/approval_channel.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`. It doesn't yet cover the RPC enforcement adapter in `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local}.rs`, or the attribution-only edits in `src/agent/agent.rs`, `src/daemon/mod.rs` and `src/integrations/registry.rs`. The ancestry, admission and binding rules themselves live in `zeroclaw-config` (`cost::override_grant`). A row amendment that covers these files and states the memory-only grant is drafted on fork branch `docs/runtime-exception-11589` (`e7868ca2a`, on `master` `1c1cd118a`). Like #11697, it needs its own Core Team-approved PR; this PR can't grant it.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends or the daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot ask still stop at an enforced limit on their own, but they benefit from a grant made elsewhere—the lift is daemon-wide for every session, delegation, and unattended scheduled or cron job using that shared tracker. Other shared limits and per-agent or per-hop ceilings still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a daemon restart the limit is enforced again and the next turn asks again. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

- **Authority recheck after the peer lookup (head `5d2ca670b747`):** `session/approve` for a cost-override prompt now rechecks the admitted session, the caller's current `SessionApprove` grants and ownership, and the pending request's session binding after the peer-process lookup. It holds the authority lease through delivery, so no await sits between the last check and `resolve_from_operator`. A caller who lost `sessions:update` during the lookup gets `FORBIDDEN`, the prompt stays pending and no override is granted. New tests: `rpc::dispatch::tests::cost_override_approve_rechecks_authority_after_peer_lookup` pauses the lookup, revokes the grant and checks for no approval and no grant. `cost_override_approve_accepts_unchanged_authority_after_peer_lookup` is the control: the approval is acknowledged and the real budget gate grants the override. With only the test commit applied to `ab919d606c`, the revocation test fails (the old handler answers `acknowledged: true`) and the control passes. On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5902 passed; 2 failed`, the two being the `relay::local_dial_tests` loopback-stall tests that also fail on the base; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no automated end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate. The gate tests use a scoped tracker with a scripted channel. The live run above covers that path by hand at the current head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** historical focused run on `2830dc912` (superseded by current head `fb2af71c36ed`) (`d01ad8eb1ad9` plus two ZeroCode-only fixes. Greptile 4429329518: a refused cost-limit answer brings the notice back and shows the error. Greptile 4429693704: a restored notice is cleared when its turn ends, so a refusal that also stopped the turn doesn't leave it up), Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree):
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → lib `52 passed`, bin `1566 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`, including `refused_cost_limit_answer_restores_the_notice_and_shows_the_error` (the daemon answers `FORBIDDEN`; the notice and request id come back, and the error text is shown; a following `TurnComplete` then clears the notice).
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check` → clean.
  - The runtime, config and api crates are unchanged since `d01ad8eb1ad9`, so the results below still apply to them.
- Previous head `d01ad8eb1ad9` (`d0297b2c4` narrow-pane fix plus a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`), Linux x86_64:
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --lib` → runtime `5905 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, config `1834 passed; 0 failed`, api `322 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode` → lib `52 passed`, bin `1564 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on `master` on this host. `cost_limit_notice_keeps_full_scope_timeout_and_buttons_visible` passes at widths 30, 40, 76 and 100.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt --check` → clean.
  - CI for this head is pending. The Security job may fail on the new wasmtime advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424) until #12129 lands. This PR doesn't touch wasmtime.
  - The earlier head `5d2ca670b7` had a green CI Required Gate.
- **Greptile round 3 (on the master merge `e7c4aa6b3f68`):** the typing wrapper now resumes typing when another session's grant releases a waiting prompt, and keeps it off for a cancelled turn (`abandoned_approval_resumes_typing_unless_the_turn_was_cancelled`, which fails with the guard disarmed). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-runtime`; channels `approval_typing abandoned_approval approval_wait_resumes unsupported_approval_resumes` 5 passed; rustfmt and the comment hygiene gate pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; a restart restoring enforcement (grants are memory-only), cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** historical live run on `d01ad8eb1ad9` (not exact-head for `fb2af71c36ed`) (real X11 window captures, daemon and ZeroCode from the same debug build, priced local stub provider). [Manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/MANIFEST.txt):
  - [Cost-limit prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L01-cost-limit-prompt-150x42.png); [Stop ends only that turn, no further provider call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L02-stop-ends-turn-150x42.png).
  - **Child-client IPC:** the daemon's `shell` tool opens a ZeroCode client (pid 3991336, a descendant of the daemon; see [ancestry](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/child-ancestry.txt)). Ctrl+O there [is refused and the turn stops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L05-child-client-ctrl-o-refused.png). The trace records `RPC cost override refused: independent operator process required` (`cost_override_untrusted_process`, `peer_pid` 3991336).
  - **Cross-session release:** with the child and a second, independent client both waiting, [Ctrl+O in the second client releases both turns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L07-grant-in-second-releases-child-desktop.png). It emits one `Approve` event, and [the main turn continues under the same grant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L08-main-turn-continues-under-grant-150x42.png).
  - **Narrow pane:** in a pane about 42 columns wide, [Stop and Override stack on separate rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L09-narrow-pane-stacked-buttons-42col.png), and [clicking the stacked Override continues the turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L10-narrow-pane-override-click-continues-42col.png).
  - Earlier macOS screenshots of `ab919d606c`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6514704152. Earlier build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6160109618.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current head `fb2af71c36ed52d5adf267727410d3e374f6460b` (includes this morning's master merge). Historical ZeroCode tests were on `2cd669c27`; historical runtime tests and the live X11 run linked above were on `d01ad8eb1ad9` / `2830dc912` (ZeroCode Chat pane over local RPC, `zeroclaw daemon`)—those captures remain labelled historical, not exact-head proof of this SHA. Older local runs on `225c52bb636f` (master `f12da7462a0f`, remote macOS arm64 builder). Earlier live run: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the captures, trace lines (`trace-child-refusal.jsonl`, `trace-grant.jsonl`), stub request log and config excerpt are all in the manifest folder linked above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (grants are memory-only; no new file is written)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one new key, `channels.telegram.<alias>.cost_override_operators` (numeric Telegram user IDs allowed to override in group chats; defaults to empty, which denies group overrides; no wildcards or usernames). Also one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`. Before merge, do not revert master merges. Current head is `fb2af71c36ed52d5adf267727410d3e374f6460b`. Earlier feature commits on this branch (for example `a8857fb9b1`…`d0297b2c4`, `2cd669c27`, `2830dc912`, `a4f77e75a7`) are historical; use the live head when naming rollback targets.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.allow_override = false` restores the hard stop without a revert.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** turns stuck waiting at the limit; grep the runtime trace for `cost limit overridden by the operator` and `cost limit override prompt failed`.

prs.title: feat(goal): add accounted Goal execution lifecycle [Goal V1 proposal 4/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> Goal Mode V1 proposal 4/12. This is a staged foundation, not an enablement or merge request. The whole-PR review and its evidence closure are complete with advisories; failed validation observations remain disclosed below. Core runtime-placement approval is still required before merge.

- **Base branch:** `master`; local comparison base `5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9`, candidate `0fe9867dfc6a46d0b9eac65b6c2891547249d41f`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Moves canonical task types into `zeroclaw-api` and adds the separate `zeroclaw-goal` contracts/controller/execution foundation, keeping the existing SQLite task store and usage ledger as the durable owners.
  - Adds session/epoch fencing, deferred-control records and Goal accounting at ordinary attempt/tool boundaries. Known usage is retained; incomplete accounting prevents another Goal-owned call. The accounting contracts preserve ordinary daily/monthly limits alongside Goal limits with one ledger writer; production host wiring is a later slice.
  - Makes shared editor validation compare the pre-edit state: unrelated existing errors remain visible without hiding newly introduced errors. Valid edits preserve their values through persistence/reload.
  - Preserves unset optional numeric values through both dashboard Save actions instead of turning a cleared field into explicit zero. Missing Goal budget defaults remain distinguishable from explicit zero/unlimited choices.
  - Retains valid attempt usage when pricing fails, including its original error and actual provider/model attribution; unknown accounting outcomes are never weakened. Each parent candidate is durably persisted before verification-driven continuation or transition.
  - Rejects edits to inputs of an existing cross-field configuration error, and bounds verifier blocker payloads before persistence. Invalid or oversized verifier output remains a protocol failure, not a silent conversion or truncation.
  - Includes an approved test-only plain-HTTP loopback webhook fixture repair. Production TLS/client construction is unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** No complete production Goal admission, Matrix/ZeroCode integration, restart/session-disposal workflow or full-stack transport parity is claimed by this prefix. Typed `/goal` contracts are not proof of an end-user command path. No provider router, credential policy, dependency upgrade, deployment or live-room behavior is changed or claimed validated.
- **Blast radius:** Public task/cost/Goal Rust APIs, shared configuration editors, generated config schema consumers, runtime accounting/tool attribution, SQLite control-plane schema/boot reconciliation and the dashboard's shared numeric-field serializer.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8303 and tracker #10341. Depends on #11880. This prefix does not close the RFC or tracker.

### What this does, simply

A long-running Goal needs to know which session owns it, what it has spent and whether it may safely make another model call. This proposal establishes those contracts without creating a second task store or budget ledger. It also repairs shared config editing so clearing an optional budget means “not configured,” rather than silently choosing unlimited operation. The remaining stack supplies the production entry points and presentation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the shared dashboard conversion. Use a disposable instance/configuration; do not start a Goal.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, configuration editor; no messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A disposable dashboard with an optional integer or float field populated with a finite value. The browser evidence below uses the real `goal.default_token_limit` field and a synthetic `Option<f64>` field, with intercepted API fixtures rather than an operator installation. The real Goal cost-default path is `goal.default_cost_limit_usd`; the generic float renderer is driven by `type_hint`, not the synthetic path spelling.
- **Steps to run:** Clear the optional numeric field, use section **Save**, and inspect the outgoing `/api/config` PATCH. Repeat with global **Save all**. Reload the editor. Repeat with explicit `0` and a finite value.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Clear sends JSON `null`; explicit zero sends `0`; finite values remain numeric. Reload reflects the saved value.
- **Prior behavior on the frozen comparison base (before):** Static tracing of its shared number parser shows `Number("")` produces `0`; clearing therefore cannot preserve unset. No separate base-browser run is claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** All 58 reported checks are terminal on `0fe9867dfc6a46d0b9eac65b6c2891547249d41f`: 50 succeeded, eight were skipped, and none failed. [Quality Gate run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40933193861) passed the main test suite, repeated parallel runtime tests, lint, formatting, docs, dashboard, channel/tool tests, plugin backends, MSRV and Linux/macOS/Windows checks. **Security and CI Required Gate both passed.** The earlier remote and local security failures remain recorded observations; this success does not relabel them or establish why the advisory result changed. No dependency or ignore-policy change was made by this follow-up. Skipped conditional/advisory jobs are not passing coverage. This proposal is ready for review, not for merge or deployment; Core runtime-placement acceptance and the remaining stack obligations are still required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full-stack Matrix/ZeroCode execution, both ZeroCode transports, live-provider fallback and deployment are not proved by this foundation prefix. Required CI and Core/CODEOWNERS approvals remain separate from local review.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Final-candidate validation is bound to `0fe9867dfc6a46d0b9eac65b6c2891547249d41f`. The complete unfiltered workspace run reached the required targets and retained the same five failed test forms listed below. Required Goal host-contract tests passed (62/62), as did the session contract (26/26). Formatting, strict workspace Clippy, firmware protocol tests (28/28), comment scanner fixtures (58/58), worktree comment hygiene, fresh Web generation/typecheck, permission tests (40/40), context tests (73/73), SOP tests (5/5), and SOP-editor tests (10/10) passed. `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` remain **FAIL** for RUSTSEC-2026-0414; no ignore policy or dependency was changed. A local quality-gate attempt was interrupted without a terminal receipt; the guarded rerun passed, and the incomplete original remains recorded, not PASS.

  Earlier baseline receipts below are bound to `598ca014ff0bc14ca322b8fa84ff22d93fff698c`, not rerun results at the final candidate. The unchanged dashboard numeric serializer retains its recorded browser evidence; the new follow-up commits do not modify that code. The independent review composes that unchanged evidence with final-candidate regressions rather than claiming a fresh browser run.

  | Command/check | Observation |
  | --- | --- |
  | `cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast` | **FAIL**, five failures detailed below. Runtime library: 5,901 passed/9 ignored; Goal host contract: 51 passed; session Goal control-plane contract: 26 passed. The full run reached the remaining suites. Desktop was excluded, not tested. |
  | `./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` | PASS: three runtime repeats (5,901 passed/9 ignored each) and three channel repeats (2,015 passed/2 ignored each). This does not erase other failed runs. |
  | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS with default features; desktop excluded from Clippy, not a claim about every feature/target combination. |
  | `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh`; `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` | PASS: scanner fixtures 58/0; worktree gate passed. |
  | `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`; `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` | PASS: one changed Markdown file, zero lint errors; six link-collector tests passed and zero added links. No HTTP link checking was needed. The original link run's exit was not recovered; an unchanged repeat supplied the observed exit 0, with both observations retained. |
  | Web generate/typecheck/permissions/contexts/SOP tests | PASS within their recorded scope. Unit/serialization tests alone are not browser evidence. |
  | `cargo deny check`; `cargo audit` | **FAIL**, RUSTSEC-2026-0414 in locked `pulldown-cmark 0.13.4`; audit reports one vulnerability and six allowed warnings. The package entry is unchanged from the comparison base. Dependencies and ignore policy were left unchanged. |
  | Isolated actual-dashboard browser matrix | 12 PASS: both Save actions × optional integer/float × clear/zero/finite; exact PATCH and saved-value reload assertions. API responses are test fixtures, not proof of a live gateway or authorization. |

  Literal receipt excerpts from `598ca014ff0bc14ca322b8fa84ff22d93fff698c`:

  ```text
  test result: FAILED. 1868 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 9.00s
  test result: FAILED. 1975 passed; 4 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 15.18s
  test result: ok. 5901 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 32.41s
  test result: ok. 51 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.31s
  test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.24s
  PASS Save: goal.default_token_limit clear -> null
  PASS Save all: goal.default_token_limit zero -> 0
  Summary: 0 error(s)
  Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```

  **Five retained workspace failures:**
  1. `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`: `File exists` in the case-collision fixture, tracked by #11959. This is filesystem-dependent, not a claim that every macOS volume is case-insensitive.
  2. `grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant`: child leader PID startup timeout.
  3. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults`: missing `choices`. The earlier upstream comparison timed out instead; that exact signature is not proved upstream-reproduced.
  4. `openai::tests::responses_model_listing_carries_header_only_profile_and_surfaces_auth_failure`: expected response data absent.
  5. `openai::tests::responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config`: 4 requests observed versus 2 expected; an earlier comparison observed 3 versus 2. Exact causal interleavings remain unproved.

  These remain failed observations with attribution limits, not blanket upstream clearance. An earlier ZeroCode `sigterm_exits_idle_zerocode_and_restores_connected_terminal` failure at `terminal_disconnect.rs:229:13` (“idle-loop readiness deadline”) did not recur in current runs; its cause remains unresolved. Earlier advisory observations, including RUSTSEC-2026-0385/0386, were not reproduced at this candidate; their historical failures are not retroactively PASS. Original review FAIL reports are retained alongside the completed whole-PR/evidence closure; neither tests nor security policy were weakened. One known staged-engine advisory can replace an original error when its failure transition is fenced; that engine is not yet production-wired, and error preservation must be corrected no later than adapter wiring.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the final clear/zero browser images and actual outgoing PATCH records. No live daemon, provider, Matrix room, ZeroCode transport or deployed service was tested.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output from the actual dashboard renderer with service-boundary fixtures. This changes numeric-value semantics, not layout or styling. No React-internal mock or replacement form. Representative screenshots were also inspected locally; no public screenshot attachment is claimed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Browser matrix at `598ca014ff0bc14ca322b8fa84ff22d93fff698c`; the numeric serializer and renderer path are unchanged through `0fe9867dfc6a46d0b9eac65b6c2891547249d41f`. No fresh browser run at that final candidate is claimed. Interface: `/config/goal`, Chrome 156.0.8078.73, en-US, 1440×1000. External font CSS was blocked locally; fallback fonts were used. Local retained browser receipt records all 12 actions and source hashes.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The twelve-case browser check reached the real rendered `/config/goal` inputs, clicked each actual Save button, checked the outgoing PATCH, reloaded, and asserted the input value returned by the browser. In both Save modes, the observed integer values after reload were `""`, `"0"`, `"321"`; float values were `""`, `"0"`, `"4.25"`. The rendered footer after reload was `No unsaved changes`. Exact PATCH examples: `[{"op":"replace","path":"goal.default_token_limit","value":null}]` and `[{"op":"replace","path":"goal.default_token_limit","value":0}]`. This is final-interface observation, not just the parsing helper's return value. The fixture/receipt and representative clear/zero images are retained for independent text/evidence review.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Both Save actions emitted the correct value and reload displayed it. Save-all's section-local dirty indicator remains until reload; this is supported by the second attempt's settled screenshot and static refresh-path trace, not the final matrix's still-in-flight pre-reload snapshots. That shared refresh path is unchanged from the frozen base and is not claimed fixed here. The first browser setup attempt failed before app launch; the second fixture attempt timed out on that common-indicator assumption. Both failures remain recorded separately from the final stateful-fixture matrix.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No desktop build/test, live-provider call, deployment or live-room test. No repeated Cargo runs solely to restyle a review verdict. Existing failed/ignored/unrun observations remain distinguished.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No new generic grant.** New Goal records/scopes use the existing authorized task/session store and ledger; production ingress is staged later.
- New external network calls? **Yes, staged parent/verifier execution through the ordinary provider path.** No new destination authority or transport; no live-provider proof is claimed.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** Existing provider handling remains the owner.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No known introduction.** Browser evidence uses neutral synthetic data and an isolated test token.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Goal objectives/responses remain untrusted; typed control and schema-validated verifier decisions, not ordinary prose, govern transitions. Authorization stays with ordinary hosts.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Session/epoch fences and pre-call accounting admission guard continuation; failures remain explicit. The required Core runtime-placement decision is still open before merge. Strict ledger admission can block every Goal if ledger records are unreadable; operator recovery documentation remains a later-stack obligation.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No, not fully Rust source-compatible.** `TaskRecord` adds public fields, although existing runtime task-type paths are re-exported and old serialized records receive defaults. Goal/accounting interfaces and async settlement require downstream caller updates.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Optional Goal defaults distinguish unset from explicit zero; typed Goal commands/config are added without claiming complete end-user wiring. Shared editor validation preserves unrelated pre-existing errors but rejects newly introduced or related invalid edits. The existing authorization ordering can expose HTTP 400 before 403; that ordering is unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No declared floor change.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Add `session_id`/`execution_epoch` to external `TaskRecord` literals (`None`/`0` match legacy defaults); existing import paths remain usable. Adapt Goal registry/accounting/pricer implementations, async `settle`, the persistence-only `GoalSessionExecutionLease::append_parent_candidate` contract (replacing `append_verified_candidate`), `CostRecord.provider_ref`, and callers of removed `BuiltinCommandId::Goal`/`CommandExecution::GoalAdmission` to the dedicated typed Goal contract. Back up the control-plane database before schema version 14; older binaries are not promised to read the migrated store. Nonterminal legacy Goals without required bindings are failed during reconciliation. Keep Goal admission disabled until complete host wiring and required gates are accepted.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Keep admission disabled; stop/drain Goal work if later enabled, preserve database and usage ledger, then revert this stack in reverse dependency order. For an incompatible schema rollback, restore a pre-upgrade backup rather than editing/dropping durable records or assuming an automatic downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Goal admission remains staged/default-disabled; no rollback-only bypass of accounting is introduced.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected config 400/403 responses, task/epoch or accounting divergence, strict-ledger admission failures, or Goal recovery/status inconsistent with durable records. Do not retry through uncertain accounting.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

prs.title: fix(providers): send drop_block so edited history no longer fails Anthropic thinking requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A replayed Anthropic thinking block is bound to the conversation that preceded it. ZeroClaw edits earlier history in several places (history trimming drops the oldest turns and adds a breadcrumb; `keep_tool_context_turns` collapses old tool rounds; a changed system prompt). On accounts the API checks, every request after such an edit fails with `400 invalid_request_error: … The block is bound to a different conversation`. Fable 5.2 checks every account; Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 check accounts created on or after 2026-08-31.
  - Adaptive-thinking requests to Anthropic's own API now send `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior = "drop_block"` with the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta. The API then drops the blocks that no longer verify, and the thinking blocks after them, instead of failing the request.
  - This is one change at the adapter that covers every history-editing path, including ones nobody has found yet. Each response's `input_transformations` is recorded as counts by type and reason, so the paths that cost reasoning show up in the trace and can still be fixed one by one.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The history edits themselves are unchanged: trimming, the tool-context collapse (#12437 handles that path) and the system prompt.
  - Bedrock (`bedrock.rs`) and the OpenAI-compatible passthrough (`compatible.rs`) are unchanged.
  - Budget (`enabled`) thinking never carries the field: the API accepts it only with `adaptive`.
- **Blast radius:**
  - Requests from the native `anthropic` provider with adaptive thinking, to `https://api.anthropic.com` only. A custom `uri` (an Anthropic-compatible proxy) keeps the pre-beta request byte for byte.
  - **Behaviour change on accounts the API doesn't check:** setting the field opts the request into the check. A block whose history was edited, which those accounts pass through to the model today, is dropped instead. After a trim or collapse the model loses that earlier reasoning rather than reading it against a changed prefix. Nothing fails either way.
  - The `thinking` object changes once, at upgrade, so the first request of each conversation after the upgrade can miss the prompt cache.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12401

### What this does, simply

Claude's thinking blocks are signed against the conversation they were written in. ZeroClaw shortens long conversations: it drops old turns and collapses old tool rounds. Anthropic notices the change, and on accounts it checks (now every account on Fable 5.2) it refuses the whole request, so the chat breaks until it's reopened. This PR asks Anthropic to drop the thinking blocks that no longer match instead of refusing. The chat keeps working, and the model only loses the reasoning in those older blocks. The log now says how often that happens, so the edits that cause it can be fixed separately.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the API-side behaviour, which a mock can't show.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `web` (dashboard chat) on the native `anthropic` provider.
- **Setup / preconditions:** an Anthropic account the API checks: any account on `claude-fable-5-2`, or an account created on or after 2026-08-31 on `claude-opus-5-5`. Default `keep_tool_context_turns` (2).
- **Steps to run:** a dashboard chat with several tool-using turns, past the point where the oldest tool round collapses (the #12401 reproduction).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the turns keep answering. The runtime trace shows `anthropic dropped or flagged replayed thinking blocks` with `by_kind` `thinking_dropped:prefix_binding_mismatch`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** every request fails with `400 invalid_request_error … The block is bound to a different conversation` until the chat is reopened.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc, comment hygiene) and the provider tests cover the request body, the header and the response parsing.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none of the tests calls the real API, so they can't show the API dropping blocks. That is the manual test above; the #12401 reporter offered to run it.
- **Commands run and tail output** (worktree at `90f1dcd767`, on master `3a3f2e3586`):

```text
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -j2
test anthropic::tests::adaptive_thinking_sends_drop_block_to_the_anthropic_api ... ok
test anthropic::tests::budget_thinking_never_sends_block_binding ... ok
test anthropic::tests::chat_sends_drop_block_with_its_beta_and_reads_drops ... ok
test anthropic::tests::custom_uri_leaves_block_binding_out ... ok
test anthropic::tests::chat_without_binding_keeps_the_pre_beta_wire_format ... ok
test anthropic::tests::stream_chat_sends_drop_block_on_both_thinking_paths ... ok
test result: FAILED. 1996 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 4.77s
# the 1 failure: openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults
# "Connection refused" from its own mock server; passes alone 3/3; pristine master
# 3a3f2e3586 with the identical invocation failed it in 1 of 2 runs (1989 passed; 1 failed)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -j2 -- -D warnings
    Checking zeroclaw-providers v0.9.0 (…/crates/zeroclaw-providers)
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 5.97s   # at 90f1dcd767

$ RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-providers
   Generated …/doc/zeroclaw_providers/index.html

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check        # exit 0
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **The new tests:** the body field and the beta header on all three request paths (non-streaming `chat`; `stream_chat` without `display`, which uses the non-streaming fallback; `stream_chat` with `display`, which streams), read back by a capturing mock.
  - **Unchanged paths:** a custom `uri` and budget thinking keep the old wire format.
  - **Responses:** both response shapes carrying `input_transformations`, including an entry type the code doesn't know, parse without error.
  - **Existing test updated:** `resolve_thinking_emits_adaptive_shape_for_4_7_families_and_decorated_ids` now expects `block_binding` on the default (Anthropic API) provider.
  - **Not verified:** the live API, Bedrock, gateways.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace `cargo test`. The change is confined to `zeroclaw-providers`, whose full lib suite ran.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. Same endpoint, one more beta value in the existing header.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The log records counts by type and reason; message paths and block content stay out.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The API can only drop the model's own earlier thinking blocks; no text is added.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. On accounts the API doesn't check, see the behaviour note under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none. A custom `uri` already leaves the field out.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a 400 naming `block_binding` or `thinking-binding-controls` would mean the API rejects the beta. Grep the trace for `anthropic dropped or flagged replayed thinking blocks` to see how often blocks are dropped.

prs.title: feat(providers): adapt Anthropic and Bedrock to adaptive-thinking Claude models
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Anthropic's current Claude generations (Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 4.7, 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5) think adaptively: they reject the fixed thinking budget, and they reject a temperature other than 1 while thinking is active, which on these generations is the normal state. The Anthropic and Bedrock adapters now read the model generation from the alias `model` and pick the request shape from it, so a new release needs no code change. Earlier models keep the fixed budget and their temperature.
  - The thinking level maps to `output_config.effort` on those generations, sent together with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. A configured temperature is dropped with a warning naming the value, and a warning fires when the output cap is still at the 4096 baseline, because reasoning now counts against it.
  - The streaming parser never read thinking blocks (a long-standing TODO), so streamed tool loops dropped the reasoning the model had signed. They are now captured as one record per block and replayed only within the tool round that produced them, which keeps every existing history-trim path valid under the preserved-thinking rule.
  - New optional `thinking_display` field on the `anthropic` slot (`omitted`, `summarized` or `updates`) so an operator can read the reasoning per provider entry; the runtime shows only the readable text, never the signed record. The generation matrix also carries a display axis: generation 5.1 and later accept only `summarized` and `omitted`, so a configured `updates` is sent to them as `summarized` with a warning naming the substitution (option (b) of #10617), whichever knob it came from.
- **Scope boundary:** No typed provider-refusal handling: that work is consolidated in #9272 and was removed from this branch (see "Relationship to #9272"). No global default changes for output caps or timeouts. No reasoning display on Bedrock. No doctor checks for these aliases. No quickstart auto-fill of `context_window`. No capture of `redacted_thinking` blocks. RPC sessions (zerocode) still send no thinking level, so they run at the model's default depth. No behavior change for temperature on the adaptive generations beyond the existing drop-with-warning; only the wording was narrowed.
- **Blast radius:** Every Anthropic and Bedrock alias (request shape changes only on adaptive-generation models), the config schema (one additive optional field), the runtime's reasoning display forwarding, and the display value sent for `agent.thinking.display = "updates"` on generation 5.1 and later (now `summarized`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10617 (this PR implements its option (b) for both display knobs; closing it is the maintainer's call). Related #9272 (owns typed provider-refusal handling; see below).
- **Labels:** live snapshot: `enhancement`, `docs`, `core`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `gateway`, `provider`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `provider:reliable`, `provider:anthropic`, `channel:core`, `provider:bedrock`, `tool:delegate`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `channel:acp`, `cli`.

## Relationship to #9272

This PR carries no refusal code. Commit `4dfc2b985e` removed everything this branch had added for declined requests, so there is one implementation of typed provider refusals to review and carry forward, and it lives in #9272. What went: `RefusalCategory`, `ProviderRefusal`, `is_provider_refusal` and `StreamError::Refusal` in `zeroclaw-api`; the refusal stop-reason parsing, the stop-details struct, the category classifier and the fallible `parse_native_response` shape in the Anthropic adapter; the whole refusal layer in `ReliableModelProvider`; the typed cause on `StreamErrorWithUsage`, the category message keys and the `Refused` render arm in the runtime; the seven refusal keys in all five `cli.ftl` catalogues; and the one docs sentence about classifier declines. `grep -ri refusal` over this PR's diff against `origin/master` returns nothing.

Until #9272 lands, a `stop_reason: "refusal"` is not special-cased: the response has no text and no tool calls, so it takes master's existing semantic-empty terminal path, which retries twice and then delivers the invalid-semantic-completion message. That is the behavior on `master` today, unchanged by this PR.

This PR keeps what it is for: adaptive request shaping, effort and display compatibility, and signed-thinking replay.

## Reconciliation with #10542

#10542 (merged, shipped in v0.8.5) landed the shared `ThinkingDisplay` wire enum, the optional `display` field on `NativeThinkingParams`, the beta header plumbing, and streamed thinking capture on the display path. This branch merges master and keeps all of it: the two adapters resolve one `display` value per request, the beta header `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18` goes out whenever the request carries a display field (master's rule since #10542), and this PR's broader generation matrix and Bedrock work sit on top. The one behavior this PR adds on the shared path is the generation gate on `updates` described above.

## Precedence decision

Both display knobs stay. The order, highest first:

1. An explicit session-level display (the RPC `session/configure` control added by the stacked PR #10636).
2. `providers.models.anthropic.<alias>.thinking_display`, whenever it is set. `omitted` on the entry means the API default: no display field is sent, whatever the profile says.
3. `agent.thinking.display`, applied only when the entry leaves its knob unset.
4. The API default (no display field).

This is the same entry-overrides-profile pattern that `temperature` and `max_tokens` already follow. Before this revision an entry set to `omitted` mapped to no value and fell through to the profile's setting; an explicit entry value now always wins. #10636, which stacks on this branch, implements the session-level step at the top of that order and so reflects the same decision; it is refreshed on this head.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` (zerocode)
- **Setup / preconditions:** An `[providers.models.anthropic.<alias>]` entry with `model = "claude-fable-5-1"`, `max_tokens = 32000`, `timeout_secs = 900`, `context_window = 1000000`, `thinking_display = "summarized"`, `fallback_models = ["claude-opus-5"]`; a second alias with `temperature = 0.2` and `max_tokens = 2048` as a negative control; a third on `claude-sonnet-4-5` with `native_thinking = true` in its runtime profile as a regression control; a fourth on `claude-fable-5-1` with `thinking_display = "updates"` as the display-fit control; a runtime profile with `[runtime_profiles.<alias>.thinking] default_level = "high"`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --verbose --log-level debug agent -a <agent> -m "Use the shell tool to run ls, then summarize what you found."`
  2. Send the same with a `/think:max` prefix, then `/think:low`, then `/think:medium`.
  3. Run one turn on the negative-control alias with `-p anthropic.<bad-alias>`.
  4. Run one tool turn on the regression-control alias.
  5. Run one turn on the display-fit alias.
  6. In zerocode from this branch (`./target/release/zerocode`, so it spawns the sibling `zeroclaw`): pick the Fable alias from the title bar, run a tool task with the thought panel open, then switch to `claude-opus-5` from the title bar and send another message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The `anthropic streaming provider request prepared` debug event reports `"thinking": "adaptive"`, `"effort": "high"`, `"stream": true`, no `budget_tokens` and no temperature; the second tool round succeeds. Step 2 changes the logged effort to `max`, `low`, then none. Step 3 logs `temperature dropped: this model generation only accepts temperature 1 while thinking is active` and `max_tokens is at the baseline; reasoning counts toward it on this model generation, so raise it on the provider entry`. Step 4 still sends `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 10000}` with `temperature: 1.0`. Step 5 logs `thinking display fitted: this model generation accepts only summarized or omitted, so updates was sent as summarized` and the request succeeds with `display: "summarized"` on the wire. Step 6 shows prose in the thought panel, and the request after the model switch succeeds.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** With `native_thinking = true`, master (since #10542) sends `claude-fable-5-1` the adaptive shape with the temperature pinned to 1 and no `output_config.effort`, so `/think:` levels change only the prompt prefix and never the request depth; with it off, a configured temperature goes out unchanged and is rejected while thinking is active, and no thinking object is sent at all. Streamed tool loops replay no thinking blocks unless a display value is set. `agent.thinking.display = "updates"` on `claude-fable-5-1` returns 400 (`thinking.adaptive.display: Input should be 'summarized', 'omitted'`), and an entry-level `thinking_display` does not exist. The thought panel shows nothing or raw JSON records.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `cargo nextest` workspace job covers the provider, api, config and runtime crates changed here; `Docs Style` (docs quality and links gates) covers the two changed Markdown files; the comment hygiene gate covers the Rust comments this branch adds.
- Hosted CI on this head (`d74778eb1396736869780c431995c56de43a2ac3`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34560876208. `Advisory Windows nextest (scoped, plugin-host=true)` failed (non-required; maintainers attribute it to an inherited CI-script problem, not this PR).
- **Historical hosted CI:** the previous exact-head run for `22d912be378a10b30b5d998e1da7d989e2d83a60` ([run 34164949852](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34164949852)) reported `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, along with `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, `Security`, `Docs Style`, `MSRV (declared floor)` and the per-target `Check` jobs.
- **Advisory Windows nextest:** that run's non-required `Advisory Windows nextest (full, plugin-host=true)` job failed. Maintainers attribute this to an inherited CI-script failure (blank `--package` arguments and the `../../web/dist` packaging assertion) rather than to this PR; it is not claimed as passing here.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI job calls the live Anthropic API, so the adaptive request shape, the streamed thinking capture, and the fitted `summarized` request on generation 5.1 are verified by unit tests and SSE fixtures rather than a real response. The 5.1 display boundary rests on one live probe of `claude-fable-5-1` (by the reviewer, 2026-09-04); `updates` was not probed on Opus 4.7, 4.8, Opus 5 or Sonnet 5. Whether Bedrock forwards `output_config` through `additionalModelRequestFields` is likewise unverified. The removal in `4dfc2b985e` carries no regression test of its own: a test for the post-removal `stop_reason: "refusal"` path would reintroduce the vocabulary the removal is meant to clear from this branch, and that path is master's existing semantic-empty terminal behavior, already covered by master's tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. Same endpoints; the `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18` beta header goes out whenever a request carries a display field, the rule master has followed since #10542, and never when no display value is resolved.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Reasoning text returned by the provider is shown as its own event and is never folded into the draft or chunk text surfaces, and the signed record is never rendered.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one additive optional field, `providers.models.anthropic.<alias>.thinking_display`. No migration needed; unset inherits `agent.thinking.display`, and with both unset the API default applies.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade notes: No steps required. ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the merge commit (or the range). No data migration to undo.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Unsetting `thinking_display` and removing `temperature` from the affected aliases returns the request to its previous shape on adaptive-generation models; older models are unaffected either way.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** 400 responses from Anthropic mentioning `thinking`, `budget_tokens`, `temperature` or `display`; the `anthropic provider request prepared` / `anthropic streaming provider request prepared` debug events; the `temperature dropped`, `thinking display fitted` and `max_tokens is at the baseline` warnings.

prs.title: fix(agent): strip stale Anthropic thinking after tool-context collapse
prs.body:
## Summary

- Strip stale `reasoning_content` from retained Anthropic tool-call messages after tool-context collapse removes earlier transcript rows.
- Apply the transformation only to the provider-facing collapsed copy; preserve durable conversation history and all other providers.
- Add a regression test that retains reasoning on ordinary assistant messages while removing it from Anthropic tool-call carriers.
- Scope boundary: this does not change tool-call payloads, user-visible answer text, history persistence, or non-Anthropic requests.
- Blast radius: Anthropic requests after configured tool-context collapse; saved transcripts remain unchanged.
- Linked issue: Fixes #12401.

### What this does, simply

Anthropic thinking signatures are tied to the conversation that came before them. Once ZeroClaw removes older tool turns from a long request, replaying a signature created for the old transcript can make Anthropic reject the request. This change removes that stale reasoning metadata only from the shortened request while leaving the stored conversation and tool calls intact.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

Run the focused regression and the neighboring collapse tests from the repository root.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted CI has not run yet. The focused runtime unit tests exercise the serialized message transformation and existing collapse behavior.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** The full workspace/integration suite was not completed locally. The initial all-target test build exceeded this Windows machine's paging-file limit; the targeted runtime library tests completed successfully.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -j 1 strips_anthropic_thinking_only_from_retained_tool_call_messages` — 1 passed.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -j 1 collapse_tests::` — 12 passed.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
  - `git diff --check` — passed.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -j 1` — passed with existing warnings in runtime/config code; no warning points to changed lines.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -j 1 -- -D warnings` — blocked by existing dead-code and collapsible-if warnings in `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The regression checks the provider-facing message copy behavior directly: regular assistant reasoning remains present, tool-call reasoning is removed, tool calls remain intact, and plain assistant text is unchanged. No live Anthropic API request was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cc8f39a7ac87e935e20817d30ad181f2711b43bc`; unit tests in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/history_trim.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** No rendered interface changed; unit tests observed the expected serialized provider-message fields.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests and all-target Clippy were skipped after the all-target test compile exceeded available Windows paging memory. The changed runtime library and its focused unit tests were validated separately.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Low-risk change; revert commit `cc8f39a7ac87e935e20817d30ad181f2711b43bc`.

prs.title: fix(runtime): surface exit status and stderr on failed shell runs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Failed `shell` tool results now put `exit status N` plus stderr into the `error` field, so the model and run logs can see why a command failed.
  - If stderr is empty, the error falls back to stdout; if both are empty, it still reports `exit status N` instead of `"error":""`.
  - Successful commands are unchanged: stderr still goes only to `error`, with no exit-status prefix.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change command validation, sandboxing, output size caps, credential scrubbing in the tool dispatcher, or how success-path stdout/stderr are captured.
- **Blast radius:** Only the failed-`shell` `ToolResult.error` / `output` shape. Downstream, `tool_execution` already folds `error` and `output` into the model-visible tool result and scrubs credentials there.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12390

### What this does, simply

When the shell tool ran a command that exited non-zero, it treated `error` as “whatever landed on stderr.” A command that printed its failure on stdout, or that failed silently, produced an empty `error`. Run logs then showed `tool failed: shell` with `"error":""`, and the model often could not see the exit status or the diagnostic text.

This change always records the exit status on failure, appends stderr when present, and uses stdout only when stderr is empty. If stdout is used as the failure detail, `output` is cleared so the dispatcher does not show the same text twice. Successful commands that write to stderr still behave as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the behavior is covered by focused unit tests on `ShellTool::execute`; there is no new UI or manual click-through.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

Focused checks on Linux with the CI toolchain (`1.98.0`), in crate `zeroclaw-runtime` only. I did not run the full workspace `cargo test --locked`, `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh`, `cargo doc`, `./dev/ci.sh all`, or Windows jobs.

    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 50s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib tools::shell::tests:: -- --test-threads=1
    Finished `test` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.37s
     Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/deps/zeroclaw_runtime-27c940ef742be463)

running 68 tests
...
test tools::shell::tests::shell_captures_exit_code_and_stderr_on_failure ... ok
test tools::shell::tests::shell_captures_stderr_output ... ok

The new tests use unrestricted `allowed_commands = ["*"]` so `exit` is not rejected by the default command policy. They check: non-zero exit + stderr (`exit status 2: fail_msg`), stdout-only failure (`exit status 3: fail_out` with empty `output`), and silent failure (`exit status 4`). prs.title: fix(security): accept a mid-argument @ in the PowerShell command grammar
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `split_powershell_pipeline_syntax` returned `None` for any unquoted `@`, so an allowlisted command with an email address argument (`himalaya message compose --to user@example.com ...`) was refused as "Command not allowed by security policy" before the risk gate ran (#12005).
  - PowerShell only starts splatting (`@args`), an array subexpression (`@(...)`), a hashtable (`@{...}`) or a here-string at `@` where a token starts: at the start of an argument, after a `-Name:` parameter, or after a `,` array separator. Inside a bare argument it is literal text.
  - The grammar now accepts `@` inside a bare argument and keeps rejecting it in those three token-start positions. `@(`, `@{` and `@"` inside an argument are still rejected by the `(`/`{` arms and the mixed-quoting check.
- **Scope boundary:** only the `@` arm of the bounded PowerShell grammar. No change to the POSIX or cmd.exe dialects, the allowlist, the risk classifier, or the trusted wildcard opt-out.
- **Blast radius:** PowerShell commands that contain a mid-argument `@` now reach the allowlist and risk gates like any other command, and simple ones also get the UTF-8 setup prelude (`powershell_command_supports_statement_prelude` uses the same grammar).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12005

### What this does, simply

On Windows the shell tool checks PowerShell commands with a small, strict grammar and refuses anything it does not understand. It treated every `@` as PowerShell syntax, so any command with an email address or a `user@host` argument was refused with a message about the allowlist, even when the command was allowlisted. PowerShell itself only gives `@` a special meaning at the start of a word (and right after `-Name:` or `,`), so this change accepts it in the middle of a word and still refuses it in those positions.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: the change is a pure grammar decision covered by unit tests at the `SecurityPolicy` boundary.

### How I tested

I checked PowerShell's own tokenizer (Windows PowerShell 5.1, `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput`) for where `@` starts a new token:

| Input | PowerShell tokens |
|---|---|
| `Write-Output user@example.com` | `Generic<user@example.com>` |
| `Write-Output --to=@x` | `Generic<--to=@x>` |
| `Write-Output -InputObject:@x` | `Parameter<-InputObject:>` `SplattedVariable<@x>` |
| `Write-Output a,@b` | `Identifier<a>` `Comma<,>` `SplattedVariable<@b>` |
| `Write-Output @x` | `SplattedVariable<@x>` |

New tests in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs`:

- `powershell_grammar_accepts_at_sign_inside_a_bare_argument`: mid-argument `@` is accepted; `@` at token start, after `-Name:`, after `,`, and `@(`, `@{`, `@"` are still rejected.
- `validate_treats_powershell_email_argument_like_any_other_argument`: through `validate_command_execution_for_shell`, the command with `--to user@example.com` gets the same result as the same command without it, with and without approval.

Before the fix (fix lines reverted, tests kept):

```text
test policy::tests::powershell_grammar_accepts_at_sign_inside_a_bare_argument ... FAILED
test policy::tests::validate_treats_powershell_email_argument_like_any_other_argument ... FAILED
a mid-argument `@` is literal text: himalaya message compose --to user@example.com --body test
assertion `left == right` failed: approved=false
  left: Err("Command not allowed by security policy: himalaya message compose --to user@example.com --body test")
 right: Err("Command requires explicit approval (approved=true): high-risk operation")
```

After the fix:

```text
test policy::tests::powershell_grammar_accepts_at_sign_inside_a_bare_argument ... ok
test policy::tests::validate_treats_powershell_email_argument_like_any_other_argument ... ok
```

```sh

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets
```

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` interface `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` (`wake(target-agent, prompt) -> result<_, dispatch-error>`) and gated `import dispatch;` on `world tool-plugin` (`wit/v0/tool.wit`), gated by `PluginPermission::AgentDispatch` (`agent_dispatch`).
  - Adds `AgentWakeBackend` / `AgentWakeService` on `PluginHostServices` (`zeroclaw-plugins`), `OptionalImports::dispatch` linker gating + coherence checks, `PluginState::wake_agent` (enforcing `ToolExecute` call-frame phase, host-call budget, grant, and target/prompt grammar), and host-owned `WasmTool::caller_alias`.
  - Adds operator grant fields `PluginEntryConfig::{dispatch_agents, dispatch_rate_per_min}` in `zeroclaw-config` (default-closed `[]` and `30`/min, strict alias/padding/bounds validation), `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` in `zeroclaw-api`, and `manifest_owns_instance_state` row seeding so `agent_dispatch`-only manifests receive a `[[plugins.entries]]` row on install.
  - Implements `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/plugin_wake.rs` and wires `plugin_host_services_with_wake` / `register_plugin_tools` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` under the ADR-016 exception approved in #12417: live-config target authorization, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance continuous token bucket, per-`(instance, target)` wake coalescing, `AgentExecutionCapability` admission, `TaskKind::PeerInbox` durable `TaskRecord` registration/settlement, and `CostTracker` scoping.
  - **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):** Increments the hardcoded `wit/v0/` input-inventory assertion in `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`Run runtime plugin admission regressions`, line 1241) from `17` to `18` to account for the new `wit/v0/dispatch.wit`, matching the `expected_inputs` update in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs`. No workflow triggers, runner labels, permissions, pinned actions, secrets, or step logic changed.
  - Adds `tool-dispatch-fixture` WASM guest + `dispatch_plugin_e2e`, unit tests across all touched crates, and documentation (`plugin-protocol.md`, `plugin-manifest-fields.md`, `writing-a-tool-plugin.md`, `CHANGELOG-next.md`).
- **Scope boundary:** `tool-plugin` world only; `channel-plugin` and `memory-plugin` do not import `dispatch`. No synchronous plugin-to-agent RPC, no ambient target grants, no edits to `send_message_to_peer.rs`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes only the 1-line `len(inputs) != 18` inventory count. `wit/v0` remains experimental (no `.frozen` marker); `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` keeps existing `wit/v0` plugins linking unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Additive WIT import, optional `PluginEntryConfig` fields, `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool`, runtime adapter wiring, and the `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` inventory entry in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Default-closed (`dispatch_agents = []`) until an operator explicitly grants target aliases for an `agent_dispatch` plugin.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12416, Related #12417

### What this does, simply

Tool plugins run in a fresh store per call with no network listener or access to the agent loop. This adds a gated `dispatch.wake(target-agent, prompt)` host import so an operator-authorized tool plugin can nudge a target agent into an asynchronous turn—coalescing burst wakes onto at most one queued follow-up turn, capping recursion at 2 hops, and enforcing live per-instance rate limits and target allowlists. It also updates the runtime plugin admission step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and its matching `r5_namespace_tests.rs` list) to expect 18 WIT input files instead of 17 now that `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` exists.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated WASM component E2E (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and runtime mock-provider coalescing/panic/cost tests (`plugin_wake`) exercise the full boundary directly.

### How I tested

Local `dispatch_plugin_e2e` was run explicitly below.
- **Commands run and tail output (on head `f72f78a8ff` / prior `8ac25c5f9b` before the 2-line inventory update):**

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Verified compiled `tool-dispatch-fixture` (`wasm32-wasip2`) end-to-end through both `WasmTool` (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` (`wasm_tool_dispatch_reaches_the_runtime_backend_end_to_end`).

prs.title: feat(ssh): add a native Rust task broker
prs.body:
## Summary

Opt-in Linux Rust implementation of the task-owned OpenSSH broker. It uses ZeroClaw's existing encrypted configuration and secret store, provides Fluent diagnostics, and eliminates Python, tomli and cryptography dependencies when selected. OpenSSH continues to own transport, authentication and host-key verification.

Depends on #11869, #12408 and #12418. This follow-up does not gate the approval or merge of those PRs. The Rust binary is intended to replace the Python helper after review and parity validation. The existing helper remains available for rollback during the preview.

## Vault integration

Retain the operator-managed bao CLI and its service credentials and TLS configuration. Discrete arguments, bounded execution/output and suppressed stderr limit the integration surface. Upgrading the CLI alongside OpenBao can absorb wire-protocol changes while its supported commands and output remain stable. Apply the same criterion to Azure and other vaults. Prefer verified HTTPS when a concrete CLI security limitation makes it safer and the API can preserve authentication, TLS and least privilege. This draft changes no other vault transport.

## Testing and rollout

The following checks support review of the opt-in preview. Formatting and diff checks passed. The current head passed the required CI gate. The combined Jarvis integration built the Linux executable in release mode and staged it for opt-in testing. The production SSH helper remains the Python implementation. The required gate passed on the published head. Live integration evidence is recorded below.

## Security, compatibility and rollback

New opt-in native executable, same existing external trust and destination rules. No new network listener outside the private Unix socket. Switch the service helper and shell wrapper together. Point both back to the original helper to roll back. The Rust executable is available for opt-in testing on the integration host.

## Live integration evidence

The Linux release executable from integration revision 6e1043009, which includes PR head cac915722, ran as the ZeroClaw service account in a separate task state directory. Its existing OpenBao-backed SSH credential authenticated to a real managed host. Two read-only remote commands reused one OpenSSH master PID. The private signer socket was gone after authentication. An unknown alias and an ungranted login were rejected. Expiration at a three-second test timeout closed the idle master and allowed a fresh connection. Graceful shutdown removed the task directory and master, and forced broker death also closed the master.

A disposable OpenSSH server and a real disposable OpenBao server listened on loopback. With both the local encrypted source and a scoped OpenBao read token, a real remote command succeeded after grant, was denied after revocation, stayed denied while replacing the key, succeeded with the replacement after re-grant, and was denied after deleting the alias. The fixture changed the server's accepted public key to verify replacement. All temporary material and services were removed. The production helper stayed on Python throughout.

For rotation of an existing vault reference, revoke the destination, replace the key, and re-grant, as exercised above. Close an active task when an already authenticated transport needs immediate termination.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep a tool-result envelope intact when a follow-up turn follows it
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `normalize_cached_channel_turns()` no longer merges a `user` turn into a preceding `role=tool` turn. Tool content is a structured result envelope, so the merge produced invalid JSON; the OpenAI-compatible adapter then emitted `role=tool` without `tool_call_id`, and strict providers rejected the entire request (DeepSeek: `422 ... missing field 'tool_call_id'`). Because the damaged pair is replayed from the persisted transcript, every later message in that conversation failed the same way.
  - The OpenAI-compatible adapter now recovers the id from the leading JSON value of a tool-result content string (tolerating trailing bytes) and falls back to the most recent assistant tool call, so one damaged envelope can no longer take down a whole request.
  - Two regression tests: `tool -> user` normalization keeps the envelope intact and keeps the user turn; the id recovery handles trailing content.
- **Scope boundary:** does not change the alternation merging added by #1057 for consecutive `user` / `assistant` turns, does not rewrite or drop the follow-up user turn, and does not touch the tool loop, persistence, or provider retry policy.
- **Blast radius:** channel cached-turn assembly (shared by all messaging channels) and OpenAI-compatible request serialization. ACP, ZeroCode, gateway sessions, and non-compatible provider adapters are untouched.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12187

### What this does, simply

A channel keeps the recent turns of a conversation and replays them to the model. When a turn is interrupted, or hits the tool-iteration cap, the stored conversation can end up as `assistant asked for a tool -> tool result -> the user's message again`. The code that restores strict user/assistant alternation handled that by appending the later turn to the previous message. When the previous message was a tool result, prose was appended to a JSON object, and a strict provider answered `missing field 'tool_call_id'` — failing that message and every message after it in the same conversation, which looks like a credential or model problem to the operator.

This PR keeps the follow-up turn as its own message (providers accept `assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> user` directly), and adds a small safety net in the request builder: even if some other path hands over a damaged tool result, the id the result belongs to is read from the beginning of the object and included on the wire.
