- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel`
- **Setup / preconditions:** any channel that keeps tool turns in its cached history (`keep_tool_context_turns`, default) plus a conversation whose stored history contains `assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> user`. A strict OpenAI-compatible provider makes the failure loud; this was reproduced against DeepSeek's official API (`https://api.deepseek.com`, model `deepseek-flash`).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On `master`: obtain a conversation whose stored turns end with a tool result followed directly by the user's request (a tool-capped turn does this), then send a follow-up message.
  2. On this branch: replay the same conversation data and send the same follow-up message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the request carries the tool message with its `tool_call_id` intact and the follow-up user message as a separate turn; the provider answers 200.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the tool message content is `<envelope>\n\n<user text>`, the adapter emits `role=tool` with no `tool_call_id`, and the provider answers `422 ... missing field 'tool_call_id'`; every later message in that conversation fails identically.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): configure and select canonical provider models
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Use the canonical registry RPC editor and exact model references in Zerocode configuration, Quickstart and chat selection; retain masked edit baselines, add text navigation and update independent Fluent catalogs.
- **Scope boundary:** Backend and protocol contracts are provided by the parent. Web dashboard changes are a separate child.
- **Blast radius:** TUI onboarding, configuration save/reload, model selection and validation feedback.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 10; reference implementation `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`. Depends on #12450.

### What this does, simply

The terminal setup and configuration screens need to edit the same connections and models that the backend resolves. This change switches Zerocode to exact registry keys and adds connection/model editing, replacing the old provider-profile workflow. Fresh interactive evidence for this split head remains pending.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the interactive workflow below supplements the passing required CI gate.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `tui`. Not exercised interactively at this revision.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run Zerocode unit/feature tests in CI; use `cargo zerocode` with a V5 configuration to edit the registry, select an exact model key and complete Quickstart.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The TUI reads and writes V5 registry documents, preserves complete model names and reports edit failures without discarding the draft.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The TUI edits provider-family tables and derives selections by splitting profile references.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c`, CI Required Gate, Test, Lint and Zerocode RPC Boundary pass. These cover compilation, automated tests and RPC boundary checks; they do not establish the pending interactive terminal result. The report-only risk workflow fails on file-evidence/head binding.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Actual ZeroCode interaction evidence remains pending. Current-head automated checks are available; original #9809 CI is not substituted for them.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no formatting diff. `git diff --check`: exit 0, no whitespace errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected ownership, imports and the incremental diff against the parent. Runtime/network behavior has not been re-executed locally.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot; inherited reference evidence is documented below and must be refreshed against this head.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c`; source formatting only. TUI screenshots/final-interface verification must be captured for this new head before readiness; no old image is claimed as exact-head evidence.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Fresh screenshots/final-interface evidence for this split head are pending. Any retained #9809 artifacts are reference evidence only.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** No interactive action performed; manual runtime checks remain pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Cargo build/test/clippy were intentionally skipped at the author’s request to use GitHub CI instead of repeated heavy local compilation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No additional permissions.
- New external network calls? No additional provider endpoints; existing backend RPC remains the transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; editors preserve masked connection fields through the backend registry-edit contract.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No additional model-visible input path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A masked value must never overwrite a real credential. The editor carries the backend edit baseline and uses the same validated persistence path; interactive verification remains pending.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Requires the parent V5 backend and its registry-edit RPC contract.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; terminal onboarding and editors use connections and exact model keys.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Merge dependencies first, migrate existing configuration to V5, and rebuild Zerocode against the matching backend. Old profile editing is not retained in the new UI.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this client layer together with dependent UI layers; retain the matching server and V5 config or restore the V4 backup for a full downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 remains the reference PR and is not superseded or closed.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/b46ac874c036def0c6da63856eb0200492c8ec5f...904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c).

prs.title: feat(providers): support multiple models per provider profile
prs.body:
## Summary

Reference status: The author has split this implementation into eleven dependent PRs, listed in [the split map](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9809#issuecomment-6891881340). This branch retains the original V4 layout change; the split introduces the separate V5 boundary.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Separate schema-v4 connections, capability models, presets and fallback graphs. Complete TOML keys are opaque, including dots and case. Historical profile/section and embedding inputs are normalized only in `zeroclaw-config`; V3→V4 migration retires profile-local fallback with actionable notices. Loading and disk migration share route conversion, including older V4 input, and loading converts historical model lists and speech bindings before any consumer receives Config.
  - Centralize chat, embedding, TTS, ASR and native decision protocols in `zeroclaw-providers`, behind capability contracts in `zeroclaw-api`. Share wire implementations across vendor adapters; model-specific text reasoning/tool extraction runs before empty-response validation, independently of native structured calls.
  - Make runtime, channels, memory, delegation, SOP, Doctor, CLI, gateway and UI consume canonical models. Gemini OAuth selects connection-owned credentials through a connection or model key, preserving implicit historical OAuth clients at the input boundary. Quickstart locality and route validation/display use the same admitted canonical registry as construction; model-switch and factory guidance use canonical model/connection names. Model identity is the exact ref plus upstream ID; every route, fallback and switch rematerializes the target model's full policy while connection descriptors may be reused within construction.
  - Use one validated registry editor for exact-key changes, secret restoration/encryption and dangling-reference validation. Editors no longer migrate historical source tables. Provider CLI CRUD manages connections/models/presets/fallback; renames update config consumers and refuse environment-owned references. CLI writes hold exclusive offline ownership; live edits use the daemon's existing transaction. Config deserialization and schema migration share one provider-input normalizer, with generated transient fields from the Config declarations. Historical driver, nested-model, OAuth and memory environment names are adapted at the same input transaction; file migration and environment input share driver field mappings. Environment snapshots follow relocated fields; external op:// references use the same exact-key secret traversal as encryption and survive unchanged saves or connection renames, while edited/deleted references are pruned.
  - Keep model bindings, RPC session refresh and embedding refresh in the admitted config generation lifecycle. Canonical Quickstart/Web/Zerocode pickers and Doctor/pricing use exact keys; context-window discovery addresses `/api/config/models/{model_ref}/refresh-context-window` and rechecks the target after network I/O.
- **Scope boundary:** Provider/model configuration and its consumers; no unrelated dependency/security upgrade or tool-permission expansion.
- **Blast radius:** Config migration/loading, provider construction/protocols, model routing/rebuild, agent turns, gateway sessions, channels, voice, memory embedding, delegation, and summaries.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A connection owns one endpoint and credential. Several independently named models can reuse it, including models for different capabilities. Consumers select a complete model key; model names may contain dots without becoming a path.

```toml
[providers.connections."gateway.prod"]
kind = "openai-compatible"
uri = "https://gateway.example.com/v1"
auth = { mode = "api_key", api_key = "<API_KEY>" }

[providers.connections."gateway.prod".api.chat]
wire_api = "chat_completions"
preset = "chat.balanced"
request_timeout_secs = 120
read_timeout_secs = 300

[providers.model_presets."chat.balanced"]
capability = "chat"
options = { max_tokens = 4096, extract_text_reasoning = true, extract_text_tool_calls = true }

[providers.models."chat.fast.us"]
capability = "chat"
provider = "gateway.prod"
model = "gpt-4o-mini"
options = { temperature = 0.2, extract_text_tool_calls = false }

[providers.models."chat.backup"]
capability = "chat"
provider = "gateway.prod"
model = "gpt-4o"

[providers.fallback]
"chat.fast.us" = ["chat.backup"]
```

An agent selects `model_provider = "chat.fast.us"`. Its model options override inherited preset values. Each selected fallback or switched model applies its own extraction policy; disabling text tool extraction does not disable native structured tool calls. Existing channel delivery sanitization and permission checks still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli` and `surface=web`; gateway/channel consumers use the same admitted model registry.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A synthetic test account or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a connection and two models as above, and an existing agent/risk profile with `model_provider = "chat.fast.us"`. Use a deterministic local fixture when checking textual extraction rather than relying on a model to repeat markup.
- **Steps to run:** Load the config, run `zeroclaw doctor`, then `zeroclaw agent -a assistant -m "hello"`. Repeat with each extraction option enabled/disabled, a native structured tool response, and a failed primary followed by the configured fallback. Switch the selected model and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Exact dotted model keys resolve, including in `llm_task`; model presets and invocation overrides apply. Route credentials override the primary only; backups use their own credentials. Fallback and switching use complete model settings. A tool-bearing request explicitly rejects a fallback chain mixing native and text protocols before dispatch; homogeneous chains and scalar calls remain supported. Registry Save all locks editing until its masked server baseline is refreshed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The canonical connection/model/preset arrangement and per-model extraction switches are unavailable; text tool parsing is controlled by a runtime-profile `strict_tool_parsing` setting and reasoning markup is stripped unconditionally.

### How I tested

- **Historical follow-up (2026-11-12, `da09279218`):** Formatting, working/staged diff checks, migration-fixture TOML parsing and static call-site audits passed. Local compilation, Clippy and tests were intentionally deferred; no historical result below is claimed for this head.
- **Current CI evidence:** At `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`, [Quality Gate run 43674156542](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43674156542) passed `Format`, `Lint`, `Test`, `Test (opt-in tools)`, `Parallel Runtime Test` and `CI Required Gate`. The Test log includes passing child-ownership and session-acknowledgement regressions. These results cover this reference head, not later stack refreshes or live-vendor behavior.
- **Known evidence limits:** Current-head CI is recorded above. The retained screenshots and manual observations below cover their stated historical revisions; no current-head live-vendor or manual terminal result is claimed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** For follow-up commit `dd2116a081`, `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` completed successfully. Source checks cover moved API call sites and test-only fixture boundaries; standard TOML parsing checked the new admission fixtures. No Rust build, test or Clippy was run locally for this follow-up; those results remain pending in CI.
- Added CI regression cases for V3/older-V4 route migration equivalence and idempotency, legacy-only model lists, speech namespace normalization/promotion/rename, explicit capability rejection, selected-connection key inheritance, heartbeat preset/options/clear behavior, and Gemini OAuth connection/model references plus active-profile selection. Follow-up cases also cover projected local models in mixed configs, route validation without canonical fixture injection, implicit Gemini OAuth clients across V3 migration/editor save/reload, masked secrets, and explicit API-key priority. These cases have not been executed locally.
- Added regression coverage for exact dotted keys, complete temporary model policy/fallback inheritance, canonical/legacy environment override restoration and promotion, exact rename/delete atomicity, environment-owned consumer refusal and canonical provider CLI parsing. These tests have not been run locally for this follow-up.
- The preceding CI run identified an exact-model pricing test expectation; the fixture now expects independent entries for both configured models. An inherited dependency advisory and a Landlock tool-install timeout remain outside this PR's scope.
- **Historical evidence:** Earlier revisions passed the targeted provider/config/gateway/Zerocode and Web checks recorded in the PR history. They do not establish compilation or behavioral correctness of this consumer refactor. The existing Web screenshots below cover the earlier UI revision; this follow-up does not change Web layout.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Chrome rendered the production Web bundle against isolated synthetic API fixtures. Selecting `chat.fast.us`, clearing and selecting `main`, following an exact model key into the registry Models tab, and requiring Azure `extra.resource` before staging all passed, with zero page script errors. This is interface evidence rather than real-backend/vendor evidence.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Six existing screenshots and the browser record are in [`.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110`](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/tree/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110). The older registry-save captures in the parent evidence directory are historical.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `surface=web`, production bundle routes `/quickstart` and `/config/providers.registry?model=chat.fast.us`, Chrome `en-US`, desktop 1280×900 and mobile 390×844. The [browser record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/observations.json) records the tested Web tree and bundle digest.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Quickstart desktop](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-desktop.png), [selected model](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-selected.png), [Azure required field](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-azure-required.png), [Quickstart mobile](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-mobile.png), [registry desktop](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/registry-desktop.png), and [registry mobile](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/registry-mobile.png). All data is synthetic and credentials are masked.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** HTTP and RPC configuration navigation expose one registry editor. UI and catalog consumers keep complete opaque model keys. Cost accounting reads canonical model metadata, response-cache identity includes connections/presets, and channel/voice consumers construct canonical ASR/TTS managers without legacy enable flags. Quickstart, factory dispatch, embedding construction and semantic-search diagnostics consume normalized definitions; the production family factory no longer accepts an optional Config for historical profile lookup. Doctor enumerates canonical chat models, retains single-part cache keys, and recognizes Codex authentication on connections. Quickstart writes typed connections plus models and validates required connection fields before publishing. CLI flag prefills, authentication prompts, and subscription login use the same canonical field names; Anthropic setup tokens update the exact connection and use the existing encrypted persistence lifecycle. Existing model selection no longer derives a provider kind from name segments.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local compilation, Rust tests and Clippy were intentionally deferred to CI at the requested validation scope. No unrelated dependency/security upgrades were added. Live-vendor and manual terminal checks require their configured environments.


## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, provider capability support and authenticated registry editing.** The whole-registry editor requires Config read/create/update/delete grants and root `providers` write scope; narrower scopes cannot use replacement to bypass existing restrictions. Native decision and shared audio protocols are available on supported provider adapters; this does not grant new tool permissions or filesystem access. Model capability admission and configured connection restrictions remain enforced.
- New external network calls? **Yes, supported native protocol endpoints.** Requests use the selected configured connection, authentication, transport policy, and timeouts; native decision calls are not synthesized through chat.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Typed connection authentication and all `extra_headers` values follow the existing credential encryption policy. Both editors receive masked snapshots and restore unchanged masks under the config commit lock. Models reference connections rather than duplicating credentials.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Examples use synthetic credentials and endpoints.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Text tool instructions/extraction now follow the selected model's boolean policy. Only admitted tools can execute, and existing approval, permission, and channel delivery sanitization boundaries remain in place.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Selecting the wrong connection or protocol can send a request to an unintended configured provider or expose incompatible model output. Exact-key resolution, capability/type validation, admitted generations, explicit factory errors, encryption, and unchanged execution authorization constrain those changes.

## Compatibility (required)

- Provider CLI CRUD now addresses canonical registry sections and complete keys; legacy category/family/alias arguments are removed. `models set` edits the selected model's upstream ID. These writes require offline ownership; use the running daemon's configuration editor for live updates.
- `ModelIdentity` exposes exact `model_ref` and effective `model_id`; ASR manager construction accepts full `Config`. Context-window discovery uses the exact-model HTTP route documented above; the family/alias route is removed.
- Registry rename updates in-config model/connection/preset bindings and fallback edges, and refuses environment-owned changes. External SOP files must be updated separately. Config loading retires historical source tables before internal consumers run; registry writes edit only those admitted definitions, so deletion cannot regenerate removed models. Historical fixture adapters live in the config migration module and are gated to tests/test-helpers.

- Backward compatible? **No for removed config fields; historical provider input is normalized at the config boundary, including legacy route input in already-versioned V4 files.** Canonical exact keys take precedence when both forms are admitted.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Canonical provider tables and boolean extraction options are available; `strict_tool_parsing` is removed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: This PR is part of schema v4, not a v5 change. Run `zeroclaw config migrate` for v3 input, review retirement notices, define shared connections and capability models, and update consumers to exact model keys. Replace an old `strict_tool_parsing = true` intent with `options.extract_text_tool_calls = false` on the corresponding chat model/preset. Omit a boolean to inherit; use `true`/`false` to override. The two extraction booleans do not accept the `"null"` clear sentinel used by nullable request options.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the PR commits through a reviewed branch. Keep a pre-migration config backup when evaluating the new layout.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No feature flag. Textual extraction can be adjusted per model/preset through the two boolean options.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Config admission/capability mismatch errors, unresolved exact model keys, provider construction or model-switch failures, exhausted fallback chains, and voice/embedding initialization failures. Text extraction regressions appear as unexpected markup in replies or missing textual tool calls.

prs.title: feat(tools): send files through send_via under the read policy
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_via` gains `attachments`, a list of file paths, for an immediate send (`target` + `body`). Today an agent on the email channel cannot send a file at all. Since #9993, outbound attachment bytes come only from `MediaAttachment.data`, and nothing loads a workspace file explicitly for the agent.
  - **Loading.** A new helper (`helpers/outbound_attachment.rs`) checks each path in this order:
    1. Refuse an empty path, a NUL byte or a `..` component.
    2. `is_path_allowed`, then `resolve_tool_path`, then canonicalise.
    3. `is_resolved_path_readable`, the read check `file_read` uses. It is deliberately not the write check the upload tools use, which admits write-only roots.
    4. Refuse runtime config files, and require a regular file.
    5. Open without following symlinks and read with a bounded reader, so the size check applies to the bytes actually read.

    It then builds the `MediaAttachment` directly. `MediaAttachment::from_file` is never called, so the file isn't opened a second time after the check.
  - **Gates, all checked before any file is read.** Any failure sends nothing:
    - the call is an immediate send;
    - the channel declares the new `Channel::supports_outbound_attachments()`;
    - the recipient's peer group sets `attachments_enabled` (default `false`);
    - the call stays within the `[tools.send_via]` limits (default 10 files, 10 MiB each, 20 MiB per call).
  - **Capability.** `Channel::supports_outbound_attachments()` defaults to `false`. Email (IMAP+SMTP), Slack and Matrix return `true`, and `PacedChannel` forwards it. Every other channel, including WASM plugin channels, is refused by name rather than silently dropping the files.
  - **Text in a `send_via` body never becomes an upload.** `SendMessage` gains `inline_attachments` (default `true`, so ordinary replies keep their markers). When it is `false`, every channel that turns message text into uploads sends the text as text instead: Slack, Matrix, Telegram (markers, and its bare-path and `file://` fallback), WeChat, QQ, Lark, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Cloud and Discord. Explicit attachments are unaffected. `send_via` sends with it off, so files go through `attachments` and the gates above, and nowhere else. This replaces a body detector, because channels parse markers in too many ways to mirror: rescanning inside unrecognised brackets, joining text after stripping tool-call tags or embeds, and uploading a body that is just a path.
  - **Approval prompts go out with inline attachments off** too. They are built by a shared `approval_prompt_message` helper on Slack, Discord, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Cloud and Matrix. Their text includes a tool's arguments, so a file marker in an argument is now shown, not uploaded.
  - **Plugin channels** receive the body as written: the plugin interface has no field for the switch, and adding one changes the plugin ABI. Plugins run with no access to host files. The docs say so.
  - The refusals this change adds use Fluent keys, and the attachment load runs in one `spawn_blocking`.
  - **Slack checks its own limits before posting.** That means at most 8 explicit files, none empty and none over 20 MiB. Before, it posted the text and then failed on a bad file, or silently dropped files beyond 8.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No attachments on a routed reply (`send_via` without `body`).
  - Telegram and the other chat channels are left for later. Telegram already has `send_document_bytes`, so it can opt in by returning `true` and sending `SendMessage.attachments`, with no change to `send_via`.
  - No HTML body (#11992), no CC (#9506), no inbound attachments (#11745, #11746).
  - Recipients stay limited to peer groups.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-api`: one trait method with a default, and `SendMessage.inline_attachments` (default `true`) with a builder.
  - `zeroclaw-config`: `PeerGroupConfig.attachments_enabled`, and `[tools.send_via]` inside `BuiltinToolsConfig`. Because that struct denies unknown fields, `migration.rs` now drops a malformed `[tools.<name>]` table on its own instead of the whole `[tools]` table. The tool selection survives a bad limit value.
  - `zeroclaw-tools`: `send_via`, the helper, and `detect_mime` made `pub(crate)`.
  - `zeroclaw-channels`: the three capability overrides, the `PacedChannel` forward, Slack's checks before posting, the `inline_attachments` gate in nine channels, and the approval-prompt helper.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`: the registry passes the limits to the tool.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11996. Related #9993, Related #11992, Related #11990

### What this does, simply

An assistant can now send a file with a message it sends to a known contact, for example "email the client the report", as long as the operator allowed it for that contact. The file has to be one the assistant may read anyway, configuration files are refused by path, sizes are capped, and if anything is wrong nothing is sent at all. Channels that can't carry files are refused up front, not silently dropped. Text the assistant writes in such a message is always sent as text, so a `[FILE:...]` code or a bare path in it can't make the channel upload a file. Every file goes through the checks above.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. The unit tests cover every gate with a channel stub that records what it was asked to send.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`email`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an IMAP+SMTP email channel, a peer group for it with `attachments_enabled = true`, and a PDF in the agent's workspace.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to send the PDF to that peer with `send_via`. Then ask it to send `config.toml`, and to send the PDF to a peer group without the opt-in.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The PDF arrives as a real attachment. The other two are refused, and nothing is sent.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `send_via` has no way to attach the file. The agent pastes text or says it cannot.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on the five touched crates, and Docs for the two pages.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` can't run on my machine (no Node); CI's docs job covers it.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                          ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib                                  ok. 1378 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                 ok. 1817 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration                      ok. 99 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-api --lib                                    ok. 323 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features "channels-full channel-matrix channel-wechat whatsapp-web channel-telegram channel-email"
                                                                    ok. 3815 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::                     ok. 767 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo check -p zeroclaw --tests                                     ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-plugins -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps --features "<same as above>" -- -D warnings    ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools   ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                             passed
# after the review changes, at 718aed5636
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                 ok. 1819 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration                      ok. 99 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings     ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config   ok
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new tests cover:
  - **`send_via`, success:** delivery through a capable, opted-in channel, with file name, MIME and bytes checked; an empty list sends a plain message.
  - **`send_via`, refusals, with nothing sent in each case:**
    - an incapable channel, and a group that hasn't opted in. Both ask for a missing file, which proves the check runs before any read;
    - the opt-in through the channel-alias target path;
    - routing mode, and a wrong argument type;
    - each of the three limits;
    - the read policy: outside the workspace, `..`, a directory, a symlink pointing outside, and a runtime config file;
  - **`send_via` sends its body with inline attachments off:** `"report [FILE:/x]"`, a tool-tag splice and a bare path all arrive as unchanged text with no attachments.
  - **Each gated channel:** a marker body (and on Telegram and WeChat a bare path or `file://` URL) with the switch off goes out as literal text with no upload, while explicit attachments still go out. Slack and Matrix check this end to end against a mock server.
  - **Approval prompts:** a file marker in a tool argument stays in the prompt text and is not uploaded (Slack end to end, WhatsApp Web through its send hook, Matrix and the shared helper directly).
  - **Schema:** the description shows the configured limits.
  - **The loading helper:** 4 unit tests.
  - **Slack:** more than 8 files, an empty file and an oversized file are each refused before any request reaches the mock server.
  - **Config:** a malformed `[tools.send_via]` value, or a misspelt key such as `max_attachment_byte`, drops that table on its own and keeps the tool selection. The drop counts as degraded security, so the daemon won't start without `--allow-degraded-security`: the defaults can be looser than a tightened limit such as `max_attachments = 0`. The same holds when this table is set and a mistake elsewhere drops the whole `[tools]` table.

  Not verified: a live send through a real mailbox on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the commands above at `bbbac5a019`, and the `zeroclaw-config` tests, clippy and docs again at `718aed5636` after the review changes. Tool and channel unit tests, and the Slack and Matrix mock servers; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A, as above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A; the behaviour checks are the tests listed above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `markdownlint-cli2`, because Node isn't installed on my machine; CI's docs job runs it. A live send through a real mailbox wasn't run on this branch.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. A model-called tool can now read files to send them. This is limited to `file_read`'s read policy, with runtime config refused by path (a copy or hard link inside the workspace is not recognised, and `file_read` could read it anyway), a per-group opt-in that is off by default, and size caps. The read is bounded, happens once after the check, and doesn't follow symlinks.
- New external network calls? No. Files go to recipients the agent could already message.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Runtime config files are refused explicitly.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (`example.com` and temp dirs).
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, and this narrows the risk. An injected instruction can no longer get files out through text in a `send_via` body or in a tool's arguments shown in an approval prompt, and the explicit path is off by default per recipient. #11990 lets an operator remove `send_via` from an untrusted channel's turns entirely.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with two changes in behaviour. A `send_via` body is now always sent as text: a file marker or bare path in it is no longer uploaded. And approval prompts show file markers from tool arguments as text instead of uploading them.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Two new optional settings: `attachments_enabled` on peer groups (default `false`), and `[tools.send_via]` with three limits. Existing configs load unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`, or leave `attachments_enabled` off, which is the default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `attachments_enabled` per peer group.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A `send_via` refusal naming the channel ("cannot carry attachments"), the peer group ("not enabled"), a limit, or the path.
  - A file marker or path showing as plain text in a `send_via` message or an approval prompt is the intended behaviour.

prs.title: feat(mcp): expose local configuration controls with deferred writes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (extracted on `a66cc98a4`).
- **What changed and why:** Add an optional Python standard-library stdio MCP server for the existing local gateway configuration API. An explicitly authorized agent can discover settings, inspect non-secret values, apply edits and request a daemon reload.
- Mutations made inside a running conversation return an accepted job before applying the edit; an owned worker waits for observed idle state from the canonical runtime admission coordinator. The authenticated running-sessions API derives a `busy` boolean in the gateway using existing lifecycle accessors and canonical configured aliases, across channel, web and RPC callers, including when persistence is disabled. Alias deletion already refuses outstanding work. No runtime holding-crate addition is needed. No parallel activity registry is added.
- Idle polling uses the authenticated `activity_only=true` projection without enumerating sessions or reading transcripts. Full session-list responses sample live activity after metadata enumeration. The helper also explains named-entry leaf writes and refreshing separately installed copies.
- Credentials are read from an owner-only regular file at use time. Responses avoid echoing submitted values; HTTP 408 and lost mutation responses are uncertain and never blindly retried. Private completed job metadata is bounded to 100 records and seven days; active jobs are preserved.
- **Scope boundary:** Optional script, documentation, tests, and a gateway-owned activity projection using existing lifecycle accessors on the authenticated session endpoint; no runtime holding-crate changes. No configuration fields, history migration, provider changes or new public listener.
- **Blast radius:** Installations that configure and grant this MCP integration; the existing running-session response gains an additive `busy` boolean.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. This is independent of the unmerged session-history foundation.

The branch is synchronized with upstream master at `b98b67bed` using a merge; original topic commits remain intact. Its PR diff contains only the feature/fix files, with no Cargo.lock change relative to the updated base.

### What this does, simply

An administrator can grant a personal assistant the same supported configuration controls used by the local gateway. The assistant can request an edit while answering a conversation and have it applied once that conversation becomes idle. This is an explicit administrative capability, not a restricted worker tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; deterministic tests need only Python 3 and loopback networking.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, real stdio MCP subprocess, HTTP configuration requests to a mock gateway.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Unix Python 3.12 or newer; no real provider, bot, key or operator data.
- **Steps to run:** `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/mcp -p 'config_control_test.py'`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** MCP discovery works; read/patch routes work; an active calling session defers writes/reloads; workers complete after idle evidence. Denied requests, credential rotation, malformed frames and uncertain responses fail safely.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** This optional configuration MCP integration is absent.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Focused local MCP transport tests, gateway route regressions, strict owning-crate Clippy, formatting and documentation gates. Required CI on this updated head is pending; previous-head CI is not presented as current-head evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** HTTP fixtures replace a real operator installation. No real configuration, model, account or credential was changed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local Cargo used Rust 1.98, one build job and `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`.
  - `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/mcp -p 'config_control_test.py'`: `Ran 27 tests ... OK`.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_sessions_running`: `4 passed; 0 failed`. The actual Axum route uses real admission leases; activity-only requests never enumerate the backend, retain bearer authentication and report current activity. The full-list regression starts work during enumeration and requires the final busy signal to observe it.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `BASE_SHA=a4431d2386eaf201f44d399d9f13ad6731688e9c scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`: `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
  - `BASE_SHA=a4431d2386eaf201f44d399d9f13ad6731688e9c scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: six collector tests passed; no added links in this follow-up.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The committed fixtures exercise the real stdio process and queued workers against loopback HTTP, plus the authenticated gateway handler. Source review confirms that the lightweight projection returns before touching session persistence. No live operator mutation was attempted.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; structured MCP/API responses, with no graphical layout changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `aa2e6614c62ed474873804975c6d36f8995cd19c`; CLI/stdin MCP and authenticated gateway routes; `scripts/mcp/config_control_test.py` and `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `27 tests ... OK`; `4 passed; 0 failed`. Route tests assert exact activity-only JSON `{"busy":true}` and `{"busy":false}`, zero backend enumeration calls and HTTP 401 without authentication.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Real turn admission changes the probe's busy value without reading history. Deferred writes wait on that signal; stale persisted running rows cannot keep the worker blocked.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests and live account/config mutations add no coverage to this bounded follow-up. Required upstream CI will validate its configured platform matrix.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Explicitly granting this integration gives administrative configuration authority, including permission changes. Documentation restricts grants to the intended administrative agent and identifies tools to exclude from delegates.
- New external network calls? **No new external service.** Only explicit loopback HTTP endpoints are accepted; redirects and proxy inheritance are disabled.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes for this optional client.** Paired-device credentials are read from a private regular file at each request, never from model arguments or returned tool results. Symlinks and loose permissions are refused. Queued request data is owner-only.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Synthetic values only.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Configuration metadata becomes tool-visible data. It does not manufacture authority or become a shell command; existing MCP grants and gateway authentication remain authoritative.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: This is intentionally powerful administrative access. Revoke its paired device or remove its bundle grant to withdraw authority. Workers reread credentials, never replay an uncertain mutation, expire requests without idle evidence and do not claim that idle proves all outbound audio finished.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes; opt-in.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes for the optional script and additive API query:** `--gateway-url`, `--token-file`, `--state-dir`; existing MCP server/bundle configuration is reused. `GET /api/sessions/running?activity_only=true` returns only the live `busy` field; omitting the query preserves the session-list response.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Upgrade the daemon together with the script; older daemons without the runtime `busy` signal are refused for mutations. Install the script at a stable local path, provision a dedicated private paired-device token, configure the stdio MCP server and explicitly grant its bundle. Follow the documentation example. No native history dependency or storage migration is required.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Remove the bundle grant, revoke the dedicated paired device, then remove the script and owned local state after queued jobs stop. Previously applied configuration edits are reversed individually through normal controls.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing MCP server definitions, bundle grants and tool exclusions.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Stable `gateway_rejected_request`, `gateway_request_failed` or `configuration_control_failed` results and failed/expired job records.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A.

prs.title: fix(channels): re-apply the system prompt cap after per-turn skill refreshes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The channel-turn system prompt is modified after the initial `max_system_prompt_chars` finalization (skills refresh splice on fresh sessions or mode changes, per-message signal block, peer-map append, thinking prefix prepend), so the operator's cap silently stopped applying exactly when the prompt was largest.
  - Re-apply `finalize_system_prompt` with the agent's cap as the last step before the system message enters history (message-processing path), and at the provider-switch retry path (`refresh_channel_history_skills`) and after the startup builder's own post-finalize additions (tool instructions, deferred section, receipts addendum), so startup and refreshed prompts share the budgeting path. Mandatory additions are preserved whole even when they alone meet or exceed the cap; that case logs a warning and can exceed the budget.
  - `finalize_system_prompt` now strips trailing `TIMESTAMP_ORIENTATION` copies before head-retention truncation, preserving user-authored quotes. An older runtime orientation can still repeat when later channel additions leave it inside the retained head.
- **Scope boundary:** no new settings, no canonical-source duplication; the no-op path of `finalize_system_prompt` (prompt within cap) is untouched; compaction/history trimming behavior unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** channel system-prompt assembly only. Agents whose prompts already fit the cap see no change (finalization is a no-op for them). Complete-section skill refreshes are capped when the reserved additions fit. A truncated skills section is replaced in place when its header survives, and channel delivery instructions are reserved independently of text-tool headers. If startup truncation removes both the skills and Workspace headers, refreshed skills are inserted before the earliest mandatory block so optional content remains subject to the cap.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12044 (deferred bootstrap sections), Related #12056 (separate identity-head truncation work; this PR uses the current head-retaining finalizer).

### What this does, simply

`max_system_prompt_chars` is the operator's system-prompt budget. This implementation preserves mandatory additions whole, with a logged overflow when those additions alone meet or exceed the budget. It was enforced only when the prompt was first built at startup. Later, on the first message of a new conversation (or after a skills-mode change), the runtime replaces the skills section with a freshly rendered one — in Full injection mode that is every skill's full instructions — and appends per-message extras. None of those steps re-checked the ceiling, so a fresh conversation could dispatch a system prompt several times larger than the configured cap. In production this surfaced as a hard refusal for brand-new conversations (`system prompt and tool definitions (148706 tokens) exceed context budget (100000)`) while long-lived conversations kept using the older, capped cached prompt and worked fine. This PR reapplies head-retaining truncation after those modifications while reserving the detected tool-protocol or channel-delivery tail. It removes trailing runtime timestamp-orientation copies before truncation; interior copies can still repeat.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the provider-capture regression covers oversized skill refresh into an initially small cached prompt and text-tool retention. Added helper tests cover replacement of an already-truncated startup skills section and native-tool channel delivery retention; they are not additional provider captures.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (telegram path in the repro test, mechanism is channel-generic)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

- New `process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh` (zeroclaw-channels): builds a real startup prompt under a 4000-char cap, drops a ~26KB-body skill on disk in Full mode, and asserts (1) the refresh splice really exceeds the cap (incident reproduction), (2) the refreshed history prompt is ≤ cap with exactly one timestamp orientation, (3) end-to-end, the provider receives a system prompt ≤ cap with one orientation.
- New `refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation` (zeroclaw-runtime): re-finalizing an already-finalized prompt does not duplicate the orientation.
- Before the fix the e2e assertion fails (~26K chars vs cap 4000 reaching the provider); after, green.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI on this PR (build/test/clippy across feature matrix) — the change touches the channel orchestrator and system-prompt finalization used by all channels.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** local run covered lib targets of the two touched crates; full-workspace integration binaries were not built locally (CI covers them).
- **Commands run and tail output:** both new tests and neighbors (`final_prompt_budget*`, `timestamp_orientation_respects_budgets`, full `agent::system_prompt` module — 35 tests, `process_channel_message_refreshes_available_skills_after_new_session`) pass; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` exits 0 with no new warnings in the changed lines.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Idempotence of the added finalization on under-cap prompts (no-op path) via the orientation-count assertions; not verified: full workspace integration binaries and non-Linux platform runs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (No)

prs.title: feat(web): manage scoped HTTP credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch `master`. Depends on #12402.
- Related #12373. Adds separate Secrets tabs for HTTP Basic credentials and API tokens alongside plugin TLS.
- Authenticated operators can create, replace, and delete encrypted credentials. The catalog returns alias, type, and origin.
- The HTTP request tool accepts an alias for Bearer, X-API-Key, or HTTP Basic authentication. The alias is scoped to one HTTPS origin and the existing HTTP policy still applies. Browser form sign-in is outside this change. The catalog also stores TOTP, SSH-key and service-password records; those require compatible consumers. SSH transport integration is tracked separately in #12418.

### What this does, simply

An operator can register an API token as INVENTORY_API and ask the agent to use that alias with the inventory endpoint. The HTTP tool adds the token during the request.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- With secret encryption initialized, open Settings → Secrets and register a disposable credential against an allowed HTTPS test endpoint. Use its alias in an HTTP request. Try another origin and then delete the credential and retry.
- This branch should show metadata in the editor, authenticate only at the configured origin, and refuse use after deletion. The corresponding tabs and scoped argument are absent on master.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked --release -p zeroclaw-gateway -j2` completed successfully.
- `npm ci` and `npm run build` completed successfully.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Added targeted tests for refusing HTTP, another host, and another port. Authenticated live observations, the tested integration revision, and the redacted Secrets editor capture are linked below.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. The HTTP tool can use an operator-created reference within the existing tool and network policies.
- New external network calls? Yes. Opt-in external secret providers are resolved through their installed CLIs and service identities before the existing HTTP tool sends the origin-scoped request. Other providers use simulated CLI-output tests; OpenBao live observations are recorded below.
- Secrets handling changed? Yes. Values are encrypted at rest, omitted from the catalog, and sent only to the registered HTTPS origin. Redirects remain disabled.
- PII in fixtures or documentation? No.
- New untrusted model-visible content? No. HTTP responses continue to be untrusted. Common reflected credential strings are redacted.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible with existing config and requests. The optional credential map defaults to empty.
- Config surface changed. Existing installations require no migration. The editor requires an initialized encryption key.
- Toolchain floor unchanged.

## Rollback

Delete the new aliases to disable their use. Before reverting to a binary without the new config field, remove its entries and retain an encrypted backup as needed. Existing HTTP auth references continue to use their established config.


### Live integration evidence

An authenticated operator registered disposable Basic, X-API-Key, and Bearer credentials through the WebUI. The protected HTTPS fixture returned 200 for each applicable credential. The X-API-Key continued working after replacement, and a deleted alias was refused before dispatch. OpenBao certificate authentication was limited to the scoped KV paths. The agent authenticated to a protected endpoint using an OpenBao alias, with the endpoint confirming HTTP 200. The SSH keys tab was opened in an authenticated browser and a scoped OpenBao SSH reference was registered. The broker integration and live transport validation are tracked in #12418. External providers other than OpenBao use simulated CLI output tests.


## Operator authorization and exact live evidence

Enabling HTTP use for an alias authorizes any caller already permitted to use http_request at the configured HTTPS origin. This implementation has no per-agent or per-principal credential grants. The broader cross-consumer authorization contract is under discussion in #12422. The mutually exclusive HTTP credential arguments now return a Fluent-localized error. The [follow-up integration evidence](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12408#issuecomment-6880721152) records protected HTTPS and SSH endpoint observations before and after grant changes.

The authenticated Jarvis WebUI at integrated revision 77c0b647d was used to provision disposable HTTP and SSH credentials, revoke both grants, rotate their values while revoked, and grant access again. The live catalog returned the expected permission metadata at each step and both records were deleted afterward. This run verified the editor and persistence. It did not re-run protected service requests at each step.

Authenticated editor capture on integrated revision 77c0b647d, cropped to the form with synthetic input and the secret field redacted: [view capture](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/183107bbb34fd9f94144c600d73b28c7b1eb4880/.pr-evidence/pr-12408-authenticated-secrets-editor.png).

prs.body:
## Summary





Base branch: `master`.





Add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse. Related #11867.





### What this does, simply





One logical task owns its transport pool. Healthy idle connections can be recreated; failed or unexpectedly dead transports remain unavailable until the task ends.





## Testing (required)





### How you can test (when useful)





Run `python3 scripts/ssh/test_ssh_task.py -v` and `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib task_ssh::tests`. Native Linux/OpenSSH lifecycle checks should cover process death, expiry and task cleanup.





### How I tested





Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 1add22e4e970f98fb1e018e0c07d9e56b4876515, including CLI-only artifact ratchet, parallel Runtime Test and Windows coverage. All 14 helper regressions and 20 native Linux/OpenSSH candidate checks passed. The integrated composition c67330cc221ffdee48494424071833f8b2165230 passed 13 follow-up validation groups: the actual opt-in helper steering test observed one task ID across both tool rounds; five streamed lifecycle tests, two task-scope tests, strict Clippy and release passed. Alias/effective-configuration isolation, per-key network setup, 8 KiB in-memory stderr and idle retirement/generation leases are covered. Earlier recommended maintainer commits retain their authorship. The Core ownership decision remains pending.





Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.





## Security & Privacy Impact (required)





The feature reuses existing SSH authentication and host-trust settings. No credential export or trust override is added. The failure-cache repair reclaims process/log/socket resources while retaining the task failure record. New transport access remains opt-in and task-scoped.





- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: No — existing configured SSH authority only.


- New external network calls: Yes — configured SSH destinations through the opt-in helper; no new trust source.


- Secrets/credentials handling changed: No — existing SSH agent and host-trust policy remain authoritative.


- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.


- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No





## Compatibility (required)





Backward compatible when disabled. The documented opt-in uses the ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER environment variable and helper/PATH contract; no new stored configuration field is added. No toolchain-floor change.





## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)





Disable the opt-in transport reuse or revert the feature. End the owning logical task before starting a new one after diagnosing a cached failure; task close reclaims remaining transports. Observe explicit transport-unavailable errors and leftover task processes.





## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)





None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.





## Pending Core Team decision





Pending the Core Team task-owner/configuration/runtime-entrypoint decision and any recorded bounded exception. Transport ownership remains in zeroclaw-tools. The proposed runtime wrapper destination is the planned kernel agent-loop owner, reviewed at extraction design review or before expanding transport, configuration or cleanup authority. The lifecycle repair does not grant that exception.



## Review follow-up - 2026-11-09



The sandbox finding is addressed in the current head. A shell command is refused before spawn when its turn owns a host SSH broker and an OS sandbox is active; stripping the environment alone would not prevent socket discovery through shared directories. The final safe/TUI environment overlay also removes all host-broker variables and injects the current task identity only for the native unsandboxed path. Two real child-process regressions cover environment stripping and stale-identity replacement. The exact shared shell source passed all 68 shell tests in the recovery integration worktree; task-helper lifecycle tests passed. Fresh exact-head CI is requested. The unrelated Telegram test delta was removed. The approved exception record #12266 still must land before this feature; approval is not being treated as a merged record.




SQLite follow-up: the workspace-only bridge from #12322 was removed from this independent PR after review identified the crates.io consumer limitation. Registry dependency compatibility is preserved. The shared security advisory remains tracked in #12320; #12322 is not a merge prerequisite for this PR.

## Foreground transport and runtime placement

The [isolated Linux/OpenSSH check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11869#issuecomment-6880479690) exercised an alias with `ForkAfterAuthentication=yes`, waited for the remote command, and checked cleanup after both normal shutdown and forced helper termination. The required CI gate passes on the current head. Depends on #12266 for the recorded runtime placement.

prs.title: feat(web): provision catalog credentials in external cloud vaults
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch: `master`. Depends on #12481. Related #12422 and #12373.
- Provide operator-only create and rotate for 1Password Connect, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and Google Secret Manager.
- Reuse the external reference form and provider-scoped editable defaults. Retain explicit linking, blank preservation on replacement, and catalog-only deletion.
- Use verified HTTPS, per-operation write authorization, and configured vault or name scope. Store only encrypted references. Existing read adapters still use their own identity.

### What this does, simply

An operator can provision a value from the same Secrets form regardless of which configured vault holds it. Azure and 1Password check for a name collision before creating. Their APIs provide no atomic conditional create by name, so configure a dedicated single-writer namespace. Google may create a resource before its first version fails. The UI directs the operator to check, link, and replace in that case.

## Testing

### How you can test

Enable one provider with a disposable prefix according to the WebUI guide. Use a scoped test identity. Add a synthetic value, verify the reference, replace it and confirm it advances, then delete the catalog alias. A blank replacement preserves the external value. Repeat with an existing name to see the conflict.

### How I tested

Added mock HTTP tests for all four providers. Tests cover expected request bodies, routes, AWS signing headers, scope validation, collision handling, 1Password IDs, and Google's partial-create recovery. `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib cloud_vault_write::tests` passed all five tests. The integrated WebUI passed TypeScript build and Vite production bundling. Real accounts are not available in this environment.

## Security and privacy

- New capability and external calls: yes, opt-in operator-only writes to a configured scope via verified HTTPS. Redirects and proxy environment routing are disabled.
- Secrets: transient write authority and value. Neither is included in catalog responses, audit output or persistent configuration.
- Personal data and untrusted model inputs: none added. Provider responses are never forwarded to the model.

## Compatibility and rollback

Remove the writer prefix to disable writes while preserving existing references. Reverting the code restores link-only behavior for these four providers. No migration is required. To remove an external resource, manage it in the vault.


### Integrated smoke test

The Linux release built with XMPP enabled. A disposable OpenBao KV v2 instance over verified TLS and an isolated gateway passed create, path denial, collision, versioned replacement, blank preservation, deletion of the alias and catalog-response redaction through the shared mutation route. After deployment to the Jarvis lab, the gateway, WebUI, OIDC and XMPP were healthy and the SSH helper remained Rust. The four cloud writers remain opt-in and unconfigured in that environment.

### Review and dependencies update

The branch inherits the catalog and manifest-validation corrections from #12408 and #12402 through the OpenBao work in #12481. The four cloud adapters are covered by mocked provider HTTP tests. The real OpenBao smoke test covers the shared mutation route. Live provider validation remains open for contributors with access.

prs.title: feat(web): provision scoped catalog credentials in OpenBao
prs.body:
## Summary

Base branch `master`. Depends on #12408. Related #12422 and #12373.

The external credential editor separates **Add**, **Link existing secret**, **Replace**, and **Delete**. OpenBao KV v2 writes support existing catalog credential types, including TOTP. An operator-configured mount and prefix supply an editable default identifier. The other external providers keep the same reference editor while their write adapters are pending.

### How to test

1. Configure an HTTPS OpenBao origin, a disposable KV v2 prefix and short-lived write authority. Sign in to the dashboard as an operator.
2. Add a synthetic TOTP entry. Check the prefilled identifier, save, and verify the remote KV entry and local metadata.
3. Try to add to the same destination. Confirm the CAS rejection.
4. Replace at the same path and verify its new version. Leave the value blank on a second replacement and verify the version stays the same.
5. Delete the catalog entry and verify the vault still owns its data.

### Validation

- `git diff --check` passed. Includes a regression test for prefix enforcement.
- The gateway typecheck, focused Rust prefix test, integrated Linux release build and WebUI build passed. An isolated gateway and OpenBao KV v2 server using TLS verified operator authentication, path confinement, creation, CAS collision, versioned rotation, blank replacement, catalog deletion and absence of secret values or write token from the local config. The integration test caught a duplicate Content-Type header during rotation, which is corrected and verified in 584d7f717. The integrated build was deployed on the Jarvis lab host with the OpenBao write prefix scoped to its own tree and the existing private CA verified. External write authority is supplied for each operation. Downstream use still requires the runtime read identity to have access to that path. Browser screenshots remain pending.

## Security and privacy

The gateway authorizes the operator and config mutation before contacting OpenBao. It uses verified HTTPS with redirects disabled, a constrained prefix, CAS zero for create, and a versioned patch for rotation. The operator supplies a short-lived vault token per write. The gateway persists only the encrypted reference. No credentials or personal data are included in fixtures. Remote failures are reported without printing response bodies. Agent-side vault access continues through the existing resolver.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive opt-in gateway configuration. Existing link-only requests remain supported. Unset `ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_PREFIX` to disable writes or revert the change to roll back. Manage existing remote secret versions in the vault.

### Review and dependencies update

The branch inherits the catalog and manifest-validation corrections from #12408 and #12402. The earlier live evidence covers OpenBao KV v2 over TLS. Please review the new CI on this head separately. The draft still depends on #12408 and the visual evidence listed above.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0â€“300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Latest functional/layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in#12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at1280px and390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.
